The source certificate has compact circuits, leaving a precise restricted-query question

12 September 2026 · Working source representation refinement · Circuit-restricted sufficient criterion · No survival estimate or new Frege proof · Symbolic source audit

Obligation and outcome. Determine whether the actual source-generated conflict trees have a proved restriction absent from the unrestricted moment-rank obstruction. A small query inventory alone does not help. The source's cofactors can, however, be retained as compact arithmetic circuits at logarithmic accuracy. This establishes a narrower class for a possible query argument; it proves no guarantee for that class.

1. The exact query and leaf inventory

Fix a completed degree-\(D\) NS certificate, common accuracy \(h\), \(S\ge1\) companions, and a scalar assignment \(b\) of every extension coefficient. Write \(C_E\) for a companion's cofactor and, after specialization, put

\[ T_E=C_E(b)\,g_{a,i}(b)\prod_{u=1}^h Q_{a,u,b}, \qquad Q_{a,u,b}=1-\sum_j b_{a,u,j}g_{a,j}(b). \]

For every base design, \(\omega(\sum_E T_E)=1\). This is an identity of design values derived from the NS certificate; the partial sum need not equal one as a formal polynomial.

The source conflict tree asks partial sums associated with a fixed balanced hierarchy on the \(S\) terms, then asks at most \(h\) factors of its selected term. If \(M\le S\) blocks have used companions, the number of distinct query polynomials is at most

\[ (S-1)+Mh. \tag{QUERY-inventory} \]

There are at most \(S(h+1)\) distinct leaf pairs: for each companion, one pair for every queried \(Q_{a,u,b}\), and one input-factor fallback. The complement is formed by omitting the chosen factor from the displayed product and retaining \(C_E(b)\). This uses no polynomial division, even if some factors vanish.

For the first count, each internal node of the balanced hierarchy contributes at most one partial-sum polynomial; nonzero values can lead to repeated copies of a subtree, but not new polynomials. Factor queries are shared by all used companions in one block. The original degree ledger bounds every term, query, and leaf product by \(D\). The scalar assignment is chosen before traversing the tree; it can depend on the candidate distribution, as in the source averaging proof.

This inventory does not exclude the full-space probe. That probe also has only \(O(pq)\) distinct queries and leaf pairs: after its first reply \(a\), it uses the fixed products \((f-a)g_s\). The issue is the descriptions of the polynomials, not merely their number.

2. A compact-circuit refinement of the direct source simulation

Use division-free arithmetic circuits with binary addition and multiplication gates and constants in \(\mathbb F_p\); sharing is allowed. Fix \(p\), the Frege presentation, and formula depth \(\ell\). Let \(T\ge2\) bound the actual symbol inventory of the balanced source proof, \(v\) be the number of original variables, and \(h\ge1\). The working direct simulation supplies \(T=(n+S_{\rm proof})^{O(1)}\), proof height \(O(\log S_{\rm proof})\), and constant formula-depth overhead.

Working representation refinement. Its NS certificate can be chosen so that all input, companion, and cofactor polynomials have a shared circuit representation of total size at most

\[ G_{\rm src}\le(v+T+h+1)^c\,2^{ch}, \tag{CIRCUIT-source} \]

for a constant \(c\) depending only on the fixed presentation, prime, and depth. The ordinary degree retains the form

\[ D\le(1+\log S_{\rm proof})(h+1)^{O(\ell+1)}. \]

A fixed constant in the majorant may be enlarged for the explicit domain witnesses below; no monomial-count bound is asserted. After the affine PHP boundary/clause substitution, the statement holds over the exact weak PHP base. In particular, if \(S_{\rm proof}\le n^K\) and \(h\le C\log(n+S_{\rm proof})\), the circuit size is \(n^{O_{p,\ell,K,C}(1)}\).

Approximation circuits. Keep each child approximation as a shared output. The defining operations are a complement, a sum followed by a fixed \((p-1)\)-st power, or \(h\) affine sums followed by their product. A deliberately coarse bound of \(T^2\) covers the total flattened OR-input inventory, including repeated subformula occurrences. Thus inputs, fresh coefficients, companions, and approximation circuits use polynomially many gates and variables in \(v,T,h\). No approximation is expanded in the original variables.

Domain and Booleanity witnesses. Frobenius identities can be certified gate by gate with compact cofactors. For a product gate, use

\[ (ab)^p-ab=(a^p-a)b^p+a(b^p-b); \]

for a sum gate, Frobenius is additive. At an original variable, use \(X^p-X=(X^2-X)\sum_{j=0}^{p-2}X^j\); at an extension variable use its field generator. Shared coefficient vectors make this polynomial in the circuit and generator inventories. These witnesses fit the structural degree majorants used for the approximation, with fixed-\(p\) constants.

Approximation Booleanity also has compact certificates. Complements preserve \(f^2-f\). For a MOD output \(a^{p-1}\), use

\[ (a^{p-1})^2-a^{p-1}=a^{p-2}(a^p-a). \]

For an OR approximation \(P=\prod_{u=1}^h Q_u\), \(Q_u=1-\sum_jr_{u,j}g_j\), use the explicit companion identity

\[ P(1-P)= \sum_{u=1}^h\sum_j r_{u,j}\!\left(\prod_{w<u}Q_w\right)(g_jP). \tag{CIRCUIT-Booleanity} \]

Prefix products and the companions \(g_jP\) are shared. This avoids treating an arbitrary high-degree function identity as if it automatically had a small certificate.

Local source certificates. In the audited BIKPRS Lemma 6.12, the formal logical-axiom certificates have bounded degree depending only on the presentation. Expand those coefficients in the formal arguments before substituting child approximations. Even for a variable-arity MOD schema, the number of formal arguments is bounded by \(T\), so bounded-degree expansion has polynomial size. Substitution then references the approximation circuits and the Booleanity witnesses just constructed.

For the congruence steps in Lemma 6.2(3,4), the formal degrees are the fixed numbers \(p-1\) and two. Their expansions have polynomially many terms in the argument inventory. The OR comparison in Lemma 6.9 expands products involving at most \(2h\) factors; retaining each inner affine sum as a circuit leaves at most \(2^{2h}\) outer terms. Select one nonempty factor in each term and use the displayed companion sums from Claims 1 and 3. This produces at most a polynomial inventory factor times \(4^h\) circuit gates, without expanding the child polynomials. The fixed-depth substitution induction of Lemma 6.11 preserves a bound of the form (CIRCUIT-source).

Global composition. For each generator \(F\), the exact MP recurrence is

\[ B_F=C_F+qA_F+W_F. \]

Refer to the two premise circuits and share the local multiplier \(q\), instead of copying or expanding them. Across \(T\) proof nodes and polynomially many generators, this adds polynomially many gates to the local constructions. The balanced-height degree recurrence is unchanged in form. Affine boundary substitution does not enlarge a circuit by more than a polynomial factor; the removed clause companions have explicit degree-two/three base certificates, and deleted field equations have the fixed-degree Boolean witness above. Collecting equal base generators uses additions. This completes the size and degree accounting.

The construction is a representation refinement of the existing simulation, not an assertion that every NS certificate of the same degree has compact cofactors. It also does not prove a constant-depth bound for all these cofactor circuits. The audited BIKPRS source, Lemmas 6.2 and 6.9–6.12 and Theorem 6.7, supplies the underlying local and balancing statements; the circuit count above is the new bookkeeping argument.

3. A narrower sufficient criterion, with its gap exposed

For a circuit bound \(G\), restrict both node queries and the two leaf polynomials to division-free circuits of at most \(G\) gates. Keep the original requirements on ordinary query degree, leaf-product degree, and height. Say one finite design distribution has survival \(\gamma\) if every such tree returns a non-conflict with probability at least \(\gamma\).

The preceding construction and inventory give a polynomially bounded \(G=G(n,S_{\rm proof},h)\) for every tree produced by the direct source certificate and every scalar specialization \(b\). Partial sums add polynomially many gates; factor complements are constructed by omission, not division. Therefore a distribution satisfying

\[ \gamma>S_{\rm ENS}(1-1/p)^h \quad\text{at height}\quad h+\lceil\log_2S_{\rm ENS}\rceil \tag{CIRCUIT-rate} \]

against this circuit-bounded class rules out the hypothetical source proof, by exactly the weighted ENS argument. The distribution must work for all trees within the stated bounds, including the tree and specialization selected after seeing it. The degree and circuit exponents may depend on the fixed proposed proof-size exponent \(K\), as usual in the quantified lower-bound target.

No such survival bound is established. The universal moment-rank argument averages over all polynomials in \(V_t\); it does not bound the circuit size of the resulting witness. Indeed, on \(v\) variables the space has dimension \(\binom{v+t}{t}\), while circuits with \(G\) gates have at most \(p^{O(G\log(v+G))}\) descriptions for fixed \(p\). For PHP's \(v=n(n+1)\), \(t=\Theta(\log n)\), and \(G=n^{O(1)}\), most full-space choices are not covered by that description bound. This observation does not prove that all successful probes are large or rule out compression modulo design relations. A succinct probe could still defeat the proposed criterion.

Upper-bound scope. The compact certificate constructed here is conditional on a short source Frege proof. It supplies no such proof of PHP. Moreover, the audited reverse BIKPRS simulation has size \((S+n+k)^{O(d_0+d)}\); even in its favorable bounded-input-degree setting, a polylogarithmic NS degree does not make that bound polynomial. No conversion eliminating this dependence is established here.

4. Research decision and evidence

The exact source ranges, local version provenance, and symbolic construction are retained in the audit record. No numerical experiment was needed for this operation count. No new third-party full text was acquired or committed.

Next step. Test whether compact products or sums of linear forms reproduce the covariance attack with the required probability budget. Stop at a sufficient attack, a concrete counterexample to the proposed probe bound, or a precise loss that prevents the argument. Test this actual query class before searching for another distribution.

Process assessment. The audit proved a representation restriction and kept its missing probability bound explicit; degree and query count alone would have given a false distinction, and no additional framework rule was needed.

A compact finite-field generator makes the covariance obstruction succinct

12 September 2026 · Working small-bias polynomial generator · Universal compact-query obstruction · Exhaustive small-field checks · The coarse circuit-size criterion fails; no final Frege bound

Obligation and outcome. Test the circuit-bounded query criterion against compact probes. A finite-field generator reproduces the needed full-space averaging with small error and polynomial-size prime-field circuits. In the PHP parameter regime, its queries have size \(O(n^2\log^3n)\), fitting the preceding source circuit budget. Thus that circuit-size restriction does not rescue the rate condition. Finer restrictions, such as a proved arithmetic-depth or source-syntax condition, are not addressed by this construction.

1. The first product sampler and its cost

One preliminary option is a sum of independent products of \(t\) random affine forms over \(\mathbb F_p\). For any nonzero linear functional \(\psi\) on \(\mathcal P_{\le t}\), its value on one such product is a nonzero multilinear tensor in the \(t\) independent coefficient blocks. Nonzeroness follows by selecting a product of variables and constants on which \(\psi\) is nonzero.

Condition on the first \(t-1\) blocks. Averaging a nontrivial additive character over the last block gives zero if the resulting linear form is nonzero, and one otherwise. By induction, a nonzero tensor in \(t-1\) blocks is nonzero with probability at least \(\theta_p^{t-1}\), where \(\theta_p=1-1/p\): choose a nonzero coefficient tensor and, when it survives, a nonzero linear form takes a nonzero value with probability \(\theta_p\). Thus the character average lies in \([0,1-\theta_p^{t-1}]\).

Summing \(L\) independent products multiplies these averages, giving error at most \(\exp(-L\theta_p^{t-1})\). It suffices to take \(L\ge\theta_p^{1-t}\log(1/\varepsilon)\), at circuit cost \(O(vtL)\). This is exponential in \(t\). The following construction removes that loss.

2. A small-bias generator with a compact polynomial representation

Let \(M_t\) be the space of multilinear polynomials in \(v\) variables of degree at most \(t\). Take \(E=\mathbb F_{p^k}\), \(Q=p^k\), with \(Q>t\). Choose independent uniform \(a_1,\ldots,a_v\in E\) and a uniform \(\mathbb F_p\)-linear functional \(\tau:E\to\mathbb F_p\). Define

\[ f_{a,\tau}(X)= \sum_{\substack{A\subseteq[v]\\|A|\le t}} \tau\!\left(\prod_{i\in A}a_i\right)X^A. \tag{SUCCINCT-generator} \]

The map \(\tau\) is applied coefficient-wise; it fixes the formal variables. In particular, \(f_{a,\tau}\) is a polynomial over the original prime field and has ordinary degree at most \(t\).

Working bias bound. For every nonzero linear test \(\psi:M_t\to\mathbb F_p\) and every nontrivial additive character \(\chi\) of \(\mathbb F_p\),

\[ 0\le \mathbb E_{a,\tau}\chi(\psi(f_{a,\tau})) \le\frac tQ. \tag{SUCCINCT-bias} \]

Proof. In the independent field variables \(a_i\), the polynomial

\[ P_\psi(a)= \sum_{|A|\le t}\psi(X^A)\prod_{i\in A}a_i \]

is nonzero and has total degree at most \(t\). Linearity gives \(\psi(f_{a,\tau})=\tau(P_\psi(a))\). Conditional on \(a\), this is uniform in \(\mathbb F_p\) if \(P_\psi(a)\ne0\), and zero otherwise. Hence the character average is exactly \(\Pr[P_\psi(a)=0]\).

The polynomial zero bound gives this probability at most \(t/Q\). For completeness, induct on the number of variables: if the last-variable degree is \(d\), its nonzero leading coefficient has total degree at most \(t-d\), and vanishes with probability at most \((t-d)/Q\); otherwise the resulting univariate polynomial has at most \(d\) roots. The two contributions sum to at most \(t/Q\).

Prime-field circuit and degree bound. Compute the first \(t\) homogeneous components of \(\prod_i(1+a_iX_i)\) by

\[ E_0^{(0)}=1,\quad E_j^{(0)}=0\ (j>0),\qquad E_j^{(i)}=E_j^{(i-1)}+a_iX_iE_{j-1}^{(i-1)}. \tag{SUCCINCT-DP} \]

Keep only \(0\le j\le t\), then output \(\tau(\sum_jE_j^{(v)})\). In a fixed \(\mathbb F_p\)-basis of \(E\), multiplication by the constant \(a_i\) is a \(k\times k\) scalar matrix. Every recurrence step therefore uses \(O(k^2)\) prime-field gates, giving

\[ \operatorname{CircuitSize}(f_{a,\tau})=O(vtk^2), \qquad \deg E_j^{(i)}\le j. \tag{SUCCINCT-size} \]

The output functional is just a scalar linear combination of the coordinate polynomials. It introduces no Frobenius powers of \(X\) and no new query variables. Truncation is part of the definition; the full product generally has degree \(v\). Sharing of intermediate components is used, and no constant-depth or polynomial formula-size bound is claimed.

Finite-field evaluation followed by a random linear functional is a classical small-bias method; compare the third construction in the introduction of Alon, Goldreich, Håstad, and Peralta's Simple Constructions of Almost \(k\)-wise Independent Random Variables, 14 June 1992 author copy. The multivariate coefficient version, its circuit implementation, and the application here are proved above and below.

3. Replacing uniform polynomials in the covariance probe

For a Boolean degree-\(D\) design with \(2t\le D\), Boolean reduction identifies the covariance on \(\mathcal P_{\le t}\) with the covariance on \(M_t\), preserving rank. Indeed, a polynomial minus its multilinear reduction is a Boolean-axiom combination through degree \(t\); multiplying by another degree-\(t\) polynomial stays within \(D\). The same holds for both factors. Thus the moment-rank lower bounds apply on \(M_t\).

Suppose a distribution \(\mathcal G\) on \(M_t\) has character bias at most \(\varepsilon\). For every subspace \(U\) of codimension \(r\), character orthogonality gives

\[ \Pr_{f\sim\mathcal G}[f\in U] \le p^{-r}+(1-p^{-r})\varepsilon. \tag{SUCCINCT-kernel} \]

To see this, average the character functions indexed by the \(p^r\) elements of the annihilator \(U^\perp\): the trivial test contributes one and every other average has absolute value at most \(\varepsilon\). Likewise, for a nonzero linear functional \(\psi\),

\[ \Pr[\psi(f)=0]\le p^{-1}+\theta_p\varepsilon. \tag{SUCCINCT-zero} \]

Use independent \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_q\sim\mathcal G\) in the same probe: query \(f\), get \(a=\omega(f)\), then query \((f-a)g_s\); a nonzero answer supplies the conflict pair. If every design's covariance rank on \(M_t\) is at least \(r\), put \(\alpha=p^{-r}\). Its non-conflict probability, averaged over the coefficient choices, is at most

\[ [\alpha+(1-\alpha)\varepsilon] +[1-\alpha-(1-\alpha)\varepsilon] (p^{-1}+\theta_p\varepsilon)^q. \tag{SUCCINCT-probe} \]

For any finite design distribution, averaging then fixes one deterministic tree with at most this non-conflict probability. It has height \(q+1\). After the first reply, each branch continues only on a zero product answer; a nonzero answer ends at a leaf. Consequently there are only \(1+pq\) internal query nodes and \(O(p^2q)\) leaves. If \(\mathcal G\) is (SUCCINCT-generator), every node and leaf polynomial has a prime-field circuit of size \(O(vtk^2)\).

4. The compact attack meets the ENS probability budget

Working compact obstruction. Let \(F\) be an unsatisfiable Boolean system with generators of degree at most two, in \(v\) variables. Let \(h\ge1\), \(S\ge2\), \(s=\lceil\log_2S\rceil\), and \(q=h+s-1\). If \(D\ge2h\), set \(t=h\). In the binary case \(D\ge h+1\) suffices, with \(t=\lceil h/2\rceil\). Take

\[ \alpha=p^{-h},\qquad \varepsilon=\frac{\alpha^2}{2(q+1)},\qquad k=2h+\left\lceil\log_p(2t(q+1))\right\rceil. \tag{SUCCINCT-parameters} \]

If the design space is nonempty, the rank theorem gives covariance rank at least \(h\) on \(M_t\), including the improved binary choice. The chosen \(Q=p^k\) has \(t/Q\le\varepsilon\), so the generator applies. If \(t>v\), Boolean reduction would make consecutive moment ranks flat before degree \(2t\); in that case no such design exists.

At zero bias, the right side of (SUCCINCT-probe) is at most \(2\alpha-\alpha^2\), because \(q\ge h\). Introducing bias \(\varepsilon\) increases the kernel term by at most \(\varepsilon\) and the \(q\)-th power term by at most \(q\varepsilon\); here \(x\mapsto x^q\) is \(q\)-Lipschitz on \([0,1]\). Therefore a fixed tree has non-conflict probability at most

\[ 2\alpha-\alpha^2+(q+1)\varepsilon =2p^{-h}-\frac12p^{-2h} < S(1-1/p)^h. \tag{SUCCINCT-ENS} \]

This is the forbidden side of the sufficient ENS rate, now with query and leaf circuits of size \(O(vtk^2)\). All queries still have ordinary degree at most \(D\). Extension-field constants are eliminated into prime-field coordinate circuits before any query is made.

Comparison with the source budget. For PHP, \(v=n(n+1)\). With \(h=O(\log n)\) and polynomial \(S\), we have \(t,k,q=O(\log n)\), so every query/leaf circuit has size \(O(n^2\log^3n)\), and even the full tree with separate circuit descriptions has size \(O(n^2\log^4n)\). The preceding coarse source budget is at least its balanced symbol inventory \(T\). For the stated clausal PHP presentation, the final formula alone contains \(n\binom{n+1}{2}=\Theta(n^3)\) collision clauses. Thus the compact attack fits that budget for all sufficiently large \(n\), with all fixed parameter constants retained.

The circuit-bounded criterion just justified therefore cannot supply the required survival probability with that budget. The earlier implication remains valid; its needed premise fails. We do not exclude every tighter per-query size bound, a constant-depth arithmetic class, or a source-specific factor/leaf condition. Each proposed restriction needs an actual source proof. This remains an obstruction to a lower-bound method, not an ENS upper bound or a polynomial-size Frege construction.

5. Exhaustive generator checks and the next question

The exact C++ checker uses \(\tau(w)=\operatorname{Tr}(zw)\), with uniform \(z\), and verifies the nondegenerate trace pairing in its two finite fields. It exhausts all seeds and every nonzero linear test of the coefficient space in four cases:

\((v,t,Q)\)SeedsNonzero testsMaximum character bias
\((2,1,4)\)647\(16/64=1/4\)
\((3,2,8)\)4096127\(960/4096=15/64\)
\((3,3,8)\)4096255\(1352/4096=169/512\)
\((4,2,4)\)10242047\(448/1024=7/16\)

All 2436 nonzero tests have nonnegative character sum and bias at most \(t/Q\). Across all seeds and Boolean assignments, all 82176 evaluations of the truncated-product recurrence agree with the independently formed coefficient polynomial. Fixing \(z=1\) gives a constant-coefficient test of absolute bias one in every case, so the negative control fails the promised bound as expected. These fixtures test the generator, not a sampled PHP design distribution.

Complete output frequencies, Fourier coefficients, controls, field encodings, reproduction commands, and source locators are retained in the evidence record. Compilation and execution succeeded under the shared resource controls; no dependency was installed.

Next step. Audit whether the actual source cofactors and queries have a polynomial-size bounded-depth arithmetic representation, and compare that exact class with the generator above. The dynamic program uses sharing and growing depth; neither a shallow implementation nor a shallow source restriction has been established here.

Process assessment. Testing the actual circuit-bounded class closed the proposed size workaround with a compact generator and a small exhaustive check; no additional framework rule was needed.

A degree-mixture sampler defeats the generic shallow-query criterion

12–13 September 2026 · Working shallow source representation · Working Boolean-quotient contraction and sampler theorems · Universal depth-four query obstruction · Exact F₂/F₃ checks · No final PHP bound

Obligation and decision. Test arithmetic depth as the proposed distinction between source-generated queries and the compact covariance attack. The source admits a stronger representation: fixed arithmetic depth and size polynomial in accuracy \(h\), not merely exponential in \(h\). A new degree-mixture sampler nevertheless gives depth-four query formulas of the required small size. Thus the generic query-distribution route is parked unless a new proof-specific mechanism is supplied; another broad query-complexity restriction is not currently justified.

1. Reusing prefix coefficients removes the exponential accuracy cost

Use the existing telescoping coefficients, not a new prefix identity. Let \(I_0=I_1\cup I_2\), with a common indexed input family \(f_i\), and let blocks \(b=0,1,2\) have products \(P_b\), companions \(E_{b,i}=f_iP_b\), and coefficients \(U_i^b\) satisfying

\[ 1-P_b=\sum_{i\in I_b}U_i^b f_i,\qquad \deg U_i^b\le1+(h-1)w,\qquad w=1+\max_i\deg f_i. \]

The source OR comparison has the explicit certificate

\[ \begin{aligned} P_0-P_1P_2={}& \sum_{i\in I_1}U_i^1E_{0,i} +\sum_{i\in I_2}P_1U_i^2E_{0,i}\\ &-\sum_{i\in I_1}P_2U_i^0E_{1,i} -\sum_{i\in I_2\setminus I_1}P_1U_i^0E_{2,i}. \end{aligned} \tag{SHALLOW-OR} \]

The first two sums equal \(P_0(1-P_1P_2)\); the last two equal \(-(1-P_0)P_1P_2\). This proves the identity, including overlapping index sets. Every term has ordinary degree at most \(3hw\), the source Lemma 6.9 ceiling. Each \(U_i^b\) is a sum of \(h\) prefix products. Writing those products directly gives formula size polynomial in \(h\) and the input inventory, and only a constant additional arithmetic depth above the inputs. No \(4^h\) expansion is needed.

2. Source cofactors have fixed arithmetic depth and polynomial accuracy cost

Arithmetic depth here counts unbounded-fan-in addition and multiplication gates over the prime field, with constants as leaves. Formula size counts the actual expression tree; sharing is not required. Fix \(p\), the Frege presentation, and formula depth \(\ell\), and let \(T\) be the balanced source proof's symbol inventory.

Working refinement. There are constants \(c,\Delta\), depending only on those fixed choices, such that the direct NS source certificate, its inputs and cofactors, and its scalar-specialized conflict queries and leaf factors have arithmetic formulas with total size at most

\[ (v+T+h+1)^c \]

and depth at most \(\Delta\). Their ordinary NS degree retains the bound \((1+\log S_{\rm proof})(h+1)^{O(\ell+1)}\). In particular \(c,\Delta\) do not grow when the constant multiplying \(h=\Theta(\log n)\) is increased.

Local accounting. The preceding source audit gives constant-depth approximation expressions: one complement, a fixed-power MOD expression, or a product of \(h\) affine sums per logical level. Fixed logical depth makes their formula size polynomial in \(T,h\), even after copying children. The bounded-degree formal axiom and congruence certificates likewise remain shallow after substituting these expressions. Replace their sole exponential-in-\(h\) OR expansion by (SHALLOW-OR).

The displayed approximation Booleanity certificates are already prefix sums and products. For Frobenius witnesses, an unbounded product can use

\[ \left(\prod_i a_i\right)^p-\prod_i a_i =\sum_i(a_i^p-a_i) \left(\prod_{j<i}a_j^p\right) \left(\prod_{j>i}a_j\right). \]

Addition is handled by Frobenius additivity. Induction through the fixed-depth approximation formula gives polynomially sized cofactor formulas of fixed depth. All copied prefix products and fixed powers retain the structural degree ceilings. This is an explicit construction for the local identities used by the source; it does not assume that arbitrary field-function identities have shallow certificates.

Global accounting. The naive MP coefficient recurrence \(B_F=C_F+qA_F+W_F\) follows proof height. Instead, unroll it on the balanced proof tree. Treat a leaf's local certificate as its contribution \(W_{u,F}\), and an internal node's correction as its contribution. Then

\[ C_F^{\rm root} =\sum_{u\in\pi} \left(\prod_{\substack{e\text{ on }u\to{\rm root}\\ e\text{ an antecedent edge}}}q_e\right) W_{u,F}. \tag{SHALLOW-paths} \]

There are at most \(T\) contributions, and each path has \(O(\log S_{\rm proof})\) factors. The \(q_e\) are explicit approximation/prefix polynomials, not recursively defined cofactor outputs. One unbounded product gate and one sum gate therefore add only two levels above the fixed-depth local formulas. Copying all local formulas along all paths and for all generators costs only a polynomial in \(v,T,h\). The degree is the same path-product degree counted in the original NS induction.

The affine PHP boundary/clause substitution and its constant-degree image certificates add only constant depth and polynomial size. Partial sums and omitted-factor leaf products do the same. This proves the refinement. The result uses unbounded arithmetic fan-in; no bounded-fan-in constant-depth claim is made.

3. A least-degree functional has a large contraction map

Let \(M_d\) be the space of multilinear polynomials of degree at most \(d\), with multiplication interpreted modulo \(X_i^2-X_i\). Suppose a linear functional \(\psi:M_d\to\mathbb F_p\) vanishes on \(M_{d-1}\), but not on \(M_d\), where \(d\ge1\). For a homogeneous linear form \(\ell\), define

\[ (\ell\mathbin{\lrcorner}\psi)(u) =\psi(\operatorname{ml}(\ell u)), \qquad u\in M_{d-1}. \]

Working contraction bound. The map from \(\ell\) to this functional has rank at least \(d\). A uniform linear form therefore annihilates it with probability at most \(p^{-d}\); every nonzero contraction has least nonzero degree \(d-1\).

Proof. Choose a \(d\)-set \(A\) with \(\psi(X^A)=c\ne0\). For columns \(\ell=X_j\), \(j\in A\), and tests \(u=X^{A\setminus\{i\}}\), \(i\in A\), the contraction matrix is \(cI_d\). The diagonal product is \(X^A\). Off the diagonal, Boolean reduction gives \(X^{A\setminus\{i\}}\), whose value is zero by the least-degree hypothesis. This proves rank at least \(d\). A contraction vanishes below degree \(d-1\) because multiplication by \(\ell\) increases degree by at most one.

For \(d\) independent uniform homogeneous linear forms, let

\[ \beta_d(\psi)= \mathbb E\chi\!\left( \psi(\operatorname{ml}(\ell_1\cdots\ell_d))\right), \]

where \(\chi\) is a nontrivial additive character of \(\mathbb F_p\). Conditional on the first \(d-1\) forms, averaging the last form gives zero for a surviving degree-one functional and one for the zero functional. Iterating the contraction bound gives

\[ 0\le\beta_d(\psi) \le1-\prod_{j=2}^{d}(1-p^{-j}) \le\sum_{j=2}^{d}p^{-j} \le\frac1{p(p-1)} \le\frac12. \tag{SHALLOW-contraction-bias} \]

The empty product for \(d=1\) gives zero bias. This proof works over every prime field. Boolean reduction and the least-degree hypothesis are essential, as the raw-power control below illustrates.

Retained preliminary tensor argument. The least-degree functional also defines a symmetric \(d\)-linear form that vanishes when \(p\) slots are equal, because \(\ell^p=\ell\) in the Boolean quotient. More generally, any nonzero symmetric form with that property has radical codimension at least \(\lceil d/(p-1)\rceil\): in a smaller quotient basis, every basis tuple repeats some vector at least \(p\) times. Contraction preserves the property, so random evaluation is nonzero with probability at least \(\prod_{j=1}^d(1-p^{-\lceil j/(p-1)\rceil})\ge(1-1/p)^p\). The last inequality follows by retaining the first \(p-1\) factors and bounding the remaining product by one minus the sum of its deficits. The diagonal-minor argument strengthens the bound for the Boolean-filtered functionals used here.

4. Mixing degrees gives a shallow small-bias sampler

Choose \(J\) uniformly from \(\{0,\ldots,t\}\). For \(J=0\), choose a uniform scalar. For \(J\ge1\), choose a product \(P_J\) of \(J\) independent uniform homogeneous linear forms. Analyze its image in the Boolean quotient, while retaining the original product as the query polynomial.

For every nonzero \(\psi:M_t\to\mathbb F_p\), let \(d\) be its least nonzero degree. The \(J=d\) component has character average at most \(1/2\), by (SHALLOW-contraction-bias), or zero when \(d=0\). Every other component has character average between zero and one: conditional averaging of the last linear form, or of the scalar when \(J=0\), has precisely those values. Hence

\[ 0\le\mathbb E\chi(\psi(\operatorname{ml}(P_J))) \le1-\frac1{2(t+1)}. \]

Sum \(L\) independent draws. Character averages multiply, so the resulting polynomial \(f\) has coefficient bias at most \(\varepsilon\) whenever

\[ L\ge2(t+1)\log(1/\varepsilon). \tag{SHALLOW-mixture} \]

The unreduced expression for \(f\) is a sum of products of linear forms. It has ordinary degree at most \(t\), arithmetic depth at most three, and formula size \(O_p(vtL)\). Scalar coefficients can be represented by repeated leaves in addition gates, costing only a fixed-\(p\) factor. No shared dynamic program, extension field, or explicit multilinear expansion is required.

The bias statement concerns the Boolean reduction, not the independent coefficients of unreduced powers. A degree-\(D\) Boolean design with \(D\ge2t\) sees the same values and pairings on the original formulas and their reductions, by the degree-preserving Boolean reduction argument. Thus this is exactly the bias property needed by the covariance probe.

5. Depth-four formulas already defeat the sufficient rate

Use the parameters of the compact obstruction: \(q=h+\lceil\log_2S\rceil-1\), \(t=h\) when \(D\ge2h\), or \(t=\lceil h/2\rceil\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) when \(D\ge h+1\), and

\[ \varepsilon=\frac{p^{-2h}}{2(q+1)},\qquad L=\left\lceil2(t+1) \log\!\left(2(q+1)p^{2h}\right)\right\rceil. \]

Use independent degree-mixture sums for \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_q\). The same rank and small-bias calculation gives, for any finite design distribution, a fixed tree of height \(h+\lceil\log_2S\rceil\) with non-conflict probability at most

\[ 2p^{-h}-\frac12p^{-2h} <S(1-1/p)^h \qquad(S\ge2). \tag{SHALLOW-ENS} \]

Each product query \((f-a)g_s\) has arithmetic depth at most four, ordinary degree at most \(2t\le D\), and formula size

\[ O_p(vtL) =O_p\!\left(vt(t+1)(h+\log(q+1))\right). \]

The leaf factors have depth at most three; the shift by \(a\) merges into the top sum. The tree has \(1+pq\) internal nodes. All these bounds are for prime-field formulas with their actual ordinary degrees.

For PHP with logarithmic \(h\) and polynomial \(S\), the per-query size is \(O(n^2\log^3n)\), and the full tree with separate descriptions has size \(O(n^2\log^4n)\). It fits the source's polynomial budget for the same reason as before: the clausal presentation alone has \(\Theta(n^3)\) collision clauses. It also fits any supplied arithmetic-depth bound at least four, including the source bound established above. The refined sufficient implication remains true, but its premise cannot be supplied by any design distribution in this class.

Research verdict. Degree, query height, polynomial description size, and a generic fixed arithmetic-depth bound at least four do not rescue the probability route. We will not keep weakening such bounds without a concrete proof-specific mechanism. The source's exact companion/cofactor relations could matter, but no usable guarantee based on them is established. These obstructions neither construct a short Frege proof nor imply the desired lower bound.

6. Exhaustive checks and the next source bridge

The exact checker enumerates the degree-mixture distribution in the Boolean quotient and every nonzero coefficient linear test:

\((p,v,t)\)Nonzero testsMaximum mixture biasProved upper bound
\((2,3,3)\)255\(107/128\)\(7/8\)
\((3,3,2)\)2186\(19/27\)\(5/6\)
\((3,3,3)\)6560\(569/729\)\(7/8\)

All 9001 tests satisfy both the mixture bound and the stronger least-degree bound \(1/[p(p-1)]\). Nonzero field values occur equally often in each tested component, so all character averages are computed with exact integers. Fixing the selected degree to a positive value leaves a constant-coefficient test of bias one. Separately, the raw coefficient of \(X_1^3\), before Boolean reduction, gives character bias \(3/4\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(5/9\) over \(\mathbb F_3\), violating the least-degree bound. These controls distinguish the actual hypotheses from stronger false statements.

Complete polynomial frequencies, test-value counts, controls, encodings, reproduction commands, and provenance are retained in the evidence record. The source identities and universal sampler proofs are analytic; no PHP moment suite was rerun. Compilation and execution succeeded. The marked reading and coding windows include the proof-development overlaps documented with the evidence.

Next step. Return to direct elimination of a polynomial-size, one-level affine-input ENS family over \(\mathbb F_2\), keeping the actual NS cofactor budgets. This contains every original level-one binary source block: with no earlier OR approximation, MOD2 and negation preserve affinity. Later blocks are not renumbered after pruning; their transformed inputs need not be affine. Test whether a simultaneous transfer can depend on \(\log M\) rather than charging all \(M\) blocks, against the existing assignment-tree and resistant-affine controls. Stop at a proved transfer or a concrete obstruction at that proposed scale.

13 September 2026 — Common vanishing polynomials exclude high-rank affine families

Status: working proofs and exact parameter checks. One-level binary ENS; explicit functional auxiliary base. This covers the earlier resistant high-rank family, not arbitrary affine source families or multiple levels.

Route obligation and stopping point. The first remaining obligation is simultaneous coverage of the actual source family without paying separately for every block. The original level-one binary source inputs are affine. This turn tests a global NS-to-PC argument on that class and stops at a proved high-rank criterion, its application to the recorded resistant family, and an explicit description of the ranks it leaves open. The generic query route remains parked.

The opening review revisited the historical degree-window construction and prefix certificate. They already contain the corresponding NS window and pebbling obstruction; those are reused controls, not new results. In particular the pebbling system's low-degree PC refutation prevents its NS obstruction from refuting the sufficient PC target.

1. Stable design extension identifies low-degree PC consequences

Write \(\mathcal P_{\le k}\) for ordinary polynomials of degree at most \(k\), and use the functional base \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\) over \(\mathbb F_2\). Let \(\mathcal I_k\) be its degree-\(k\) NS consequence space and \(\mathcal C_k\) its PC consequence space. The following strengthens the recorded quadratic extension theorem; the topological input is the same, already audited BLVZ connectivity theorem.

Working theorem. If \(B\ge1\) and \(N\ge2B-1\), every normalized degree-\(k\) design extends to degree \(B\), for every \(0\le k\le B\). Consequently

\[ \mathcal I_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le k}=\mathcal I_k,\qquad \mathcal C_B=\mathcal I_B,\qquad \mathcal C_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le k}=\mathcal I_k. \tag{AFF-stability} \]

Proof of extension. Boolean and same-row/column exclusions give the matching-monomial normal form. Its complete remaining design equations are the recorded matching marginals:

\[ z_\varnothing=1,\qquad \sum_{j\notin{\rm col}(T)}z_{T\cup\{(i,j)\}}=z_T \quad(i\notin{\rm row}(T)). \]

If only degree zero is prescribed, choose first moments summing to one in every row. Suppose moments through degree \(s-1\) have been assigned, with \(2\le s\le B\). On each specified set of \(s\) pigeon rows, their \((s-1)\)-matching moments form a reduced \((s-2)\)-cycle in \(\Delta_{s,N}\): for \(s=2\) the sum of the two row totals is \(1+1=0\); for \(s\ge3\), each boundary coefficient is the sum of two equal lower marginal sums. Since \(N\ge2s-1\), BLVZ gives \(\widetilde H_{s-2}(\Delta_{s,N};\mathbb F_2)=0\). A filling supplies all new \(s\)-matching moments and exactly their required marginals. Different \(s\)-row sets have disjoint new top moments and common, already fixed lower data. Fill them independently and iterate. This argument begins at any prescribed degree, not only degree two.

Proof of the consequence identities. Normalized degree-\(k\) designs exist and span the full annihilator of \(\mathcal I_k\): subtract a fixed normalized design from any other to obtain the zero-normalized directions. If a polynomial of degree at most \(k\) lies in \(\mathcal I_B\), every extended design annihilates it, so finite-dimensional annihilator duality puts it in \(\mathcal I_k\). The converse inclusion is immediate.

Every NS consequence is a PC consequence within the same ceiling. For the reverse inclusion, induct on a degree-\(B\) PC derivation. Linear combinations preserve \(\mathcal I_B\). At a legal multiplication step \(Xf\), the preceding nonzero \(f\) has degree at most \(B-1\); if \(f\in\mathcal I_B\), the just-proved identity puts it in \(\mathcal I_{B-1}\), so \(Xf\in\mathcal I_B\). Zero lines cause no difficulty. Thus \(\mathcal C_B=\mathcal I_B\), proving all three assertions.

This is an explicit exception to the general NS/PC distinction, with a field, encoding, and degree range. It does not assert equality on an augmented ENS system. The archived four-hole degree-three failure of full quadratic extension lies outside \(N\ge2B-1\) and remains unchanged.

2. Learn every polynomial vanishing on all block-zero spaces

Let \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb F_2[X_1,\ldots,X_v]\) contain the old Boolean equations. Adjoin \(M\) one-level affine-input ENS blocks, with common \(h\ge1\), complete companions, and fresh Boolean coefficient variables. Inputs use old \(X\) only. A block whose affine span contains one can be removed by a constant first-row specialization; a zero block can be discarded. For each remaining block \(b\), put

\[ Z_b=\{x\in\mathbb F_2^v:g_{b,i}(x)=0\text{ for every }i\}. \]

Then \(Z_b\) is a nonempty affine subspace of codimension \(r_b\), the rank of the block's linear parts. All nonzero inputs have degree one and their original companion degree is \(2h+1\).

Working learning lemma. Suppose the augmented system has a degree-\(D\) PC refutation, with \(D\ge2h+1\). If a multilinear polynomial \(f\) of degree at most \(k\ge1\) vanishes on every \(Z_b\), then

\[ f\in\mathcal C_{B}(\mathcal F),\qquad T=\max\{1,k-1\},\qquad B=TD+k. \tag{AFF-learning} \]

For a degree-\(D\) NS refutation, the stronger conclusion \(f\in\mathcal I_B(\mathcal F)\) holds. Neither bound has an additive \(M\) factor.

Low-degree affine ideal membership. For each block there are polynomials \(a_{b,i}\), of degree at most \(k-1\), such that

\[ f-H_b\in\mathcal I_k({\rm BOOL}),\qquad H_b=\sum_i a_{b,i}g_{b,i}. \tag{AFF-membership} \]

To see this, choose a basis of the block's inputs and complete it to an invertible affine coordinate system \(u_1,\ldots,u_v\), with \(Z_b\) given by \(u_1=\cdots=u_{r_b}=0\). Affine substitution and Boolean reduction preserve the degree ceiling. The reduced image of \(f\) contains no monomial using only the remaining coordinates, since its restriction there is zero on their entire Boolean cube. Factor one of \(u_1,\ldots,u_{r_b}\) from each monomial, obtaining coefficients of degree at most \(k-1\), and substitute back. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(u_j^2-u_j\) is a constant linear combination of the old Boolean equations, so the discarded Boolean reductions have certificates through \(k\). Express basis inputs as constant combinations of the displayed tuple to obtain (AFF-membership).

Global specialization and weighted replay. In every block simultaneously, set \(r_{b,1,i}=a_{b,i}(X)\), and set all coefficient rows numbered \(2,\ldots,h\) to zero. Multiply each specialized proof line by \(f\). A companion becomes the following old Boolean consequence:

\[ f\,g_{b,i}(1-H_b) =g_{b,i}\bigl[f(1-f)+f(f-H_b)\bigr] \in\mathcal I_{2k+1}({\rm BOOL}). \tag{AFF-weighted-companion} \]

Indeed \(f^2-f\) has a Boolean certificate through \(2k\), and (AFF-membership) handles the second summand. A fresh field equation becomes \(f(a^2-a)\), with a Boolean certificate through \(2T+k\). An old axiom becomes its multiple by \(f\). All these ceilings are at most \(B\): in particular \(D\ge3\) implies \(2k+1\le TD+k\).

Every substituted variable has degree at most \(T\). At a PC multiplication step, the original preceding line has degree at most \(D-1\); multiply its already derived weighted image by the substituted variable, one monomial at a time. Every intermediate degree is at most \(T(D-1)+k+T=B\). Linear-combination steps are immediate. The final weighted image of one is \(f\). This is the same weighted-specialization principle as historical one-block elimination, now using a common vanishing polynomial for every block, rather than learning an input separately from its peers.

For an NS certificate, a companion cofactor specializes to degree at most \(T(D-e)\), where its original degree is \(e=2h+1\ge3\). Inserting (AFF-weighted-companion) costs at most \(T(D-e)+2k+1\le TD+k\), because \(Te\ge k+1\). Field summands cost at most \(T(D-2)+2T+k=B\); an old degree-\(d\) axiom costs at most \(T(D-d)+d+k\le B\). This proves the NS conclusion without flattening a PC derivation. Original activity and cofactor budgets have not been enlarged after substitution.

3. A finite-parameter criterion for the whole family

Return to \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\), with \(v=N(N+1)\), and write

\[ b_k(w)=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(k,w)}\binom wj,\qquad m_j=\binom{N+1}{j}\binom Nj\,j!,\qquad u_k=\sum_{j=0}^k m_j,\qquad t_k=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(N+1-j)m_j. \]

Working exclusion theorem. For the consistent, nonzero affine blocks above, there is no degree-\(D\) augmented PC refutation, and hence no such NS refutation, if some integer \(k\ge1\) satisfies

\[ B=\max\{1,k-1\}D+k,\qquad N\ge2B-1,\qquad \boxed{\ \sum_{b=1}^M b_k(v-r_b)<u_k-t_k.\ } \tag{AFF-dimension} \]

The same exclusion follows for the weak base \(\mathcal F_N\) with these blocks: any weak-base refutation would still be a refutation after adjoining the functional axioms. This is the explicit auxiliary strengthening, not a derivation of those extra axioms from the weak base.

Proof. Let \(\mathcal M_k\) be the space of multilinear polynomials of degree at most \(k\), of dimension \(b_k(v)\). Restriction to \(Z_b\), followed by Boolean reduction in its \(v-r_b\) affine coordinates, has rank at most \(b_k(v-r_b)\). The common kernel \(K_k\), consisting of polynomials vanishing on every \(Z_b\), therefore has

\[ \dim K_k\ge b_k(v)-\sum_b b_k(v-r_b). \]

Before imposing row equations, the proper Boolean/exclusion quotient has exactly \(u_k\) matching monomials. Their independence follows by evaluation on partial-matchings: the inclusion matrix is triangular when ordered by matching size. A row equation multiplied by a \(j\)-matching is zero if that row is already used; otherwise it is one of \((N+1-j)m_j\) possible marginal equations. These span all remaining NS relations through degree \(k\). Some may be dependent, so

\[ q_k:=\dim(\mathcal P_{\le k}/\mathcal I_k)\ge u_k-t_k. \]

By (AFF-stability), the subspace \(\mathcal C_B\cap\mathcal M_k\) has dimension \(b_k(v)-q_k\). By (AFF-learning), an augmented refutation would put the entire \(K_k\) inside this subspace. The strict inequality in (AFF-dimension) makes \(\dim K_k>b_k(v)-q_k\), a contradiction. No explicit construction or efficient enumeration of the separating polynomial is needed for this degree lower bound.

4. Polynomially many high-rank blocks, including the resistant family

Asymptotic consequence. Fix \(0<\rho<1\). Suppose \(M\le n^a\), \(N\ge n^\varepsilon\), \(D=\operatorname{polylog}n\), and every remaining block has \(r_b\ge\rho v\). Then, for sufficiently large \(n\), the criterion holds with

\[ k=\left\lceil\frac{\log(8M)}{-\log(1-\rho)}\right\rceil =O_\rho(\log(M+1)),\qquad B=O_\rho(D\log(M+1)). \]

Quantitative proof. A uniformly chosen pair of distinct board cells shares a row or column with probability \((2N-1)/(v-1)\). A union bound over pairs in a \(k\)-set gives

\[ m_k\ge(1-\alpha)\binom vk,\qquad \alpha=\binom k2\frac{2N-1}{v-1}. \]

Also \(t_k\le(N+1)b_{k-1}(v)\), and consecutive binomial ratios imply \(b_{k-1}(v)/b_k(v)\le k/(v-k+1)\). Hence

\[ \frac{u_k-t_k}{b_k(v)} \ge1-\alpha-\frac{(N+2)k}{v-k+1} =1-O(k^2/N). \]

For \(s=v-\lceil\rho v\rceil\ge3k-1\), the lower binomial tail is bounded geometrically by \(b_k(s)\le2\binom sk\). Thus

\[ \frac{b_k(v-r_b)}{b_k(v)} \le2\,\frac{\binom sk}{\binom vk} \le2(1-\rho)^k. \]

Our choice of \(k\) makes the sum of these ratios at most \(1/4\). For sufficiently large \(n\), the quotient lower bound is at least \(b_k(v)/2\), and \(N\ge2B-1\). This proves (AFF-dimension). The argument allows arbitrary overlaps among the affine zero spaces.

The former resistant control is covered. In the recorded residual-rank construction, take \(M=n\), \(N=\lfloor\sqrt n/4\rfloor\), and \(r=\lfloor(N^2-1)/4\rfloor\). After every specified matching restriction, the linear parts retain rank \(r\) and the affine input spans do not contain one. Thus \(r/v\to1/4\), and \(\rho=1/5\) applies for large \(n\). At any polylogarithmic \(D\ge2h+1\), (AFF-dimension) excludes a refutation of the restricted one-level system. Restriction preserves any original proof's degree, so the original family is excluded as well.

The earlier rank/core calculation still correctly says that its own optimized ceiling is \(\Omega(n)\). The new argument bypasses that criterion and resolves this particular control positively. It establishes neither that these tuples occur essentially in a small PHP proof nor that all source tuples have comparable rank.

5. Exact checks and the remaining rank gap

The new C++ checker uses the existing Boost multiprecision integer library to retain every binomial term, matching count, row-relation count, dimension margin, and degree check for twelve parameter cases. It constructs no huge input matrices and uses no floating-point arithmetic.

CaseParametersResult
High-rank example\(N=200,M=1000,r=36000,h=2,D=10,k=6,B=56\)Both sufficient conditions hold
Insufficient vanishing degreeSame board and family bounds, \(k=1,B=11\)Dimension inequality fails
Insufficient board size\(N=40,M=1000,r=1476,h=2,D=10,k=6,B=56\)Dimension holds; stable-degree condition fails
Resistant-family scales\(n=2^q,\ N=2^{q/2-2},\ M=n,\ r=\lfloor(N^2-1)/4\rfloor,\ h=q,\ D=q^2\)Both hold at tested \(q=42,44,48,56,60\); at \(q=16,24,32,40\), at least one fails

For the scaled cases, \(k\) is the smallest integer satisfying \(8M\,4^k\le5^k\). At \(q=42\), the exact values are \(k=140\), \(B=245336\), and \(N=524288\). These verify the sufficient numerical criterion for any family with the stated ranks. They do not instantiate the resistant matrices or separately check its source existence union bound; that construction has its own asymptotic proof. A failed sufficient inequality is not an augmented refutation.

Complete outputs, commands, parameter encodings, and provenance are in the evidence record. The analytic argument proves the universal statements; the arithmetic checks test the parameter application and distinct failure conditions. Compilation and execution succeeded, with no installations.

What remains. Full affine coverage is still open. The high-rank theorem needs a positive fraction of the \(N(N+1)\) old-variable directions. Low-rank normalizers cover a different range, while intermediate ranks need not fit either bound. No rank dichotomy has been proved for the actual source family, and this proof uses one-level inputs over \(\mathbb F_2\). It does not cover transformed higher-level inputs or odd-prime MOD inputs.

Next step. Test the intermediate-rank range directly: determine whether actual affine source tuples admit a reduction to the covered classes, or exhibit a precise obstruction to that reduction. Use the completed high-rank theorem as a tool and retain the actual board and degree costs. Do not sharpen its already sufficient constants while that application remains unproved.

Process assessment. The first route obligation gains genuine coverage of the previously resistant class, and the index prevented the initial window/pebbling review from becoming rediscovery; keeping that review brief needs no additional framework rule.

13 September 2026 — Changing the residual size does not close the rank gap

Status: working existential construction and criterion obstruction, with exact finite parameter audits. This refines the earlier resistance template; it supplies no augmented refutation or proof-essential source family.

Route obligation. The new high-rank theorem covers a substantial affine subclass, but the first remaining obligation needs all actual source tuples. This cycle tests whether choosing a different matching-restriction size alone can put arbitrary polynomial-size affine inventories into the recorded rank ranges. The stopping point is an obstruction uniform over every usable residual size, with the precise methods it obstructs.

1. A polynomial-size inventory with a middle-rank class on every residual

Let \(n\) be sufficiently large, set \(L=\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil\), and work over \(\mathbb F_2\). For each dyadic rank \(r=2^j\le n\), make a class of \(n\) input tuples, each consisting of \(r\) homogeneous linear forms in the original \(n(n+1)\) PHP variables.

Working refinement of the residual-rank construction. The coefficients can be chosen so that, for every \(4L\le N\le n\), every matching restriction retaining an \((N+1)\times N\) board, and

\[ r_N=2^{\lfloor\log_2N\rfloor},\qquad N/2<r_N\le N, \]

the class of rank \(r_N\) has all its input ranks preserved. Any two of its spaces have zero intersection modulo the residual row-equation span \(H_N\), and their sum with \(H_N\) does not contain one. The entire inventory has \(O(n\log n)\) blocks, fewer than \(2n^2\) input forms, and \(O(n^4)\) binary coefficients.

Proof. Choose all coefficient rows independently and uniformly. Fix \(N\), a retained subboard \(U\), and two members of its selected dyadic class. The row-sum coefficient space on \(U\) has dimension \(N+1\), leaving \(N^2-1\) quotient directions. The same nonzero-combination argument as in the earlier construction bounds failure of full pair rank by

\[ (2^{2r_N}-1)\,2^{-(N^2-1)}. \]

Union-bound over the \(\binom n2\) pairs, the \(\binom{n+1}{N+1}\binom nN\) retained subboards, and all \(4L\le N\le n\). The logarithm of the summand for a fixed \(N\) is at most

\[ -N^2+2N(L+1)+3L+1\le-\frac{N^2}{8}. \]

For the inequality, use \(L\ge2\), \(L+1\le3L/2\), \(N\ge4L\), and \(3L+1\le2L^2\le N^2/8\). The full failure probability is therefore at most \(n\,2^{-2L^2}<2^{L-2L^2}<1\). One choice satisfies every required rank condition simultaneously.

A matching changes constant terms but leaves these surviving linear parts fixed. Full rank of the pair together with the row-sum coefficient vectors therefore implies the stated affine-span and nonconstant-one properties, for every matching on each subboard. The count does not need to enumerate matching bijections. Summing the dyadic ranks gives \(\sum_{2^j\le n}2^j<2n\), proving the description bounds.

Give all tuples common accuracy \(h\ge L\), with \(h=O(\log n)\) if logarithmic accuracy is desired. They are polynomial-size MOD2-compatible inputs with original companion degree \(2h+1\), and their Booleanity identities are sharply degree two. This verifies the coarse input syntax and counting conditions. It does not construct a Frege proof using them essentially.

2. Both recorded numerical tests fail on the surviving class

Fix \(D\ge2h+1\). Any residual usable for a degree-\(D\) transfer with target \(N/2\) must have \(N\ge2D>4h\ge4L\), so the preceding construction covers every such size. Its selected class has \(M=n\), rank \(r=r_N\in(N/2,N]\), and no constant-one span even after adjoining all affordable affine base consequences: filtration stability identifies those consequences with \(H_N\).

Older rank/core test. For this selected class, the recorded exact optimized ceiling is

\[ \min\{D+n,\ T(r)D\},\qquad T(r)=\max\{1,\lceil r/h\rceil-1\}. \]

The additive alternative exceeds \(N/2\), since \(n\ge N\). The other alternative satisfies \(T(r)D>2(r-h)>N-2h>N/2\). Thus that test cannot handle even the selected intermediate-rank class at any usable residual size. This is the same criterion as before, now with a rank class that adapts to every possible \(N\).

New dimension test. Put \(v=N(N+1)\). For every \(k\ge1\) whose learning budget \(B=\max(1,k-1)D+k\) obeys \(N\ge2B-1\), we have \(k\le(N+1)/2\). A uniformly chosen \(j\)-subset of \(v\) coordinates avoids a fixed \(r\)-set with probability at least \(1-jr/v\), by a union bound. Summing over \(j\le k\) gives

\[ b_k(v-r)\ge\left(1-\frac{kr}{v}\right)b_k(v) \ge\frac12\,b_k(v). \]

Two members of the selected class already make the left side of the dimension criterion at least \(b_k(v)\). Its right side \(u_k-t_k\) is at most \(b_k(v)\). The required strict inequality therefore fails for every feasible \(k\), and adding the other remaining blocks only enlarges its left side. Replacing the matching/row-relation lower bound by the exact base quotient dimension would not fix this particular inequality: that dimension is also at most \(b_k(v)\).

What this rules out. Merely selecting a different matching size does not turn all polynomial-size affine inventories into classes certified by these two rank tests. The selected class remains nonconstant and intermediate-rank on every usable board. Polynomial family count, affine MOD2 syntax, and sharp Booleanity alone do not justify the proposed rank dichotomy.

What it leaves open. This does not show that low-degree common vanishing polynomials are absent. The estimate subtracting the sum of separate restriction ranks can underestimate the dimension of their common kernel. Nor does the construction rule out more informative substitutions, mixed proof transformations, new base consequences derived using peers, or properties of the actual source certificate. No short augmented proof has been supplied.

3. Exact parameter audit and the next substantive test

The compiled checker evaluates the full rational union bound, without logarithmic estimates or floating point, for two fixtures. It then checks every \(2D\le N\le n\) and every \(k\) with \(N\ge2(\max(1,k-1)D+k)-1\), at \(h=\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil,\ D=2h+1\).

Original \(n\)Existence rangeUsable boards checkedFeasible degree cases checked
64\(28\le N\le64\): exact union sum below one3566
128\(32\le N\le128\): exact union sum below one95262

All 130 usable-board cases fail the older affordable-ceiling test, and all 328 feasible degree cases satisfy the two-block obstruction to the new dimension inequality. The control \(n=64,\ N_{\min}=8\) has an exact union sum at least one, so that enlarged range is not certified by the existence bound. This is a failed sufficient bound, not a proof that the family cannot exist there.

The evidence record retains every union summand, exact common-denominator sum, board budget, degree comparison, reproduction command, and provenance. These are parameter audits; no large affine matrices were constructed and no prior matrix suite was rerun. Compilation and execution passed under the existing resource limits, with no installations.

Next step. Test the actual common vanishing space on an intermediate-rank family. A low-degree construction there could improve the learning method despite this dimension-bound failure; a proved lower bound on its first nonzero degree would identify a deeper limitation. Keep the distinction between an absent polynomial and an insufficient dimension estimate explicit.

Process assessment. The residual-size audit closed a proposed shortcut without claiming source coverage, and checking all feasible parameters in two small fixtures kept the evidence focused; the existing workflow needs no additional rule.

13 September 2026 — An intermediate-rank family has no affordable common vanishing class

Status: working exact Boolean-kernel calculation, existential uniform family, and method obstruction; complete finite kernel certificates. No augmented proof-size or degree upper bound is constructed.

Route obligation and stopping point. The preceding audit only obstructed a dimension estimate. This cycle determines an actual common vanishing space and tests whether its first nonzero degree can fit the current learning method on every usable residual. The stopping point is an exact degree obstruction with a matching-independent construction, while keeping Boolean-ideal membership distinct from membership using additional PHP relations.

1. The exact kernel for independent affine input groups

Work in the Boolean function ring \(\mathbb F_2[X]/(X_i^2-X_i)\), using each class's canonical multilinear polynomial and its degree. There are \(M\) nonempty affine input groups \(G_b\), of sizes \(r_b\), whose combined linear parts are independent; put \(R=\sum_b r_b\le v\). Let \(Z_b\) be the common-zero affine space of group \(b\), and let \(K_k\) be the degree-at-most-\(k\) classes vanishing on every \(Z_b\).

Working exact calculation. Complete all group inputs together to affine coordinates \(u_1,\ldots,u_v\), with disjoint coordinate groups. A basis of the common vanishing space consists of squarefree \(u\)-monomials meeting every group. In particular

\[ K_k=0\quad(k<M),\qquad \min\{\deg f:0\ne f,\ f|_{Z_b}=0\ \forall b\}=M. \tag{JOINT-first-degree} \]

The exact number of basis monomials of each degree has the integer generating polynomial

\[ (1+z)^{v-R}\prod_{b=1}^{M}\bigl((1+z)^{r_b}-1\bigr); \tag{JOINT-Hilbert} \]

the sum of its coefficients through degree \(k\) is \(\dim K_k\). These coefficients count dimensions over \(\mathbb F_2\); the generating polynomial itself is over the integers.

Proof. Invertible affine coordinate maps over \(\mathbb F_2\) are bijections of the Boolean cube. Substitution followed by Boolean reduction preserves the degree filtration; applying the inverse shows that a nonzero Boolean class's degree is unchanged. In \(u\)-coordinates, setting the variables of group \(b\) to zero leaves exactly the monomials missing that group. The restricted multilinear polynomial is zero on its full remaining cube if and only if all those coefficients are zero. Imposing this condition for every group leaves exactly the stated monomial basis. Each surviving monomial needs at least one variable from each of the \(M\) disjoint groups. Choosing one from every group attains degree \(M\). Independent choices of nonempty subsets in each group and arbitrary subsets of the free coordinates give (JOINT-Hilbert).

“Nonzero” here means nonzero as a Boolean function. A formal polynomial such as \(X_i^2-X_i\) vanishes on all these spaces at degree two, but is already a base consequence and cannot supply a separating class for the learning argument.

Why pairwise independence is insufficient. Take three two-dimensional spaces

\[ \langle u_1,u_2\rangle,\qquad \langle u_3,u_4\rangle,\qquad \langle u_1+u_3,u_2+u_4\rangle. \]

Any pair is independent, but all six displayed inputs have joint rank four. The nonzero quadratic \(u_1u_4+u_2u_3\) vanishes on every block-zero space. Thus the pairwise condition used in the preceding rank-test audit does not establish (JOINT-first-degree). The construction below enforces full joint independence instead.

2. Joint independence on every usable matching residual

Let \(L=\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil\), with \(n\) sufficiently large. For every integer \(1\le r\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1\), form a class of \(r\) blocks, each with \(r\) homogeneous linear inputs in the original PHP cells. Choose all coefficient rows independently and uniformly.

Working refinement. There is a choice such that, after every matching restriction retaining \(4L\le N\le n\) holes, the class

\[ r=r_N=\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1 \]

retains all its \(r^2\) input linear parts jointly independent modulo the residual row-sum coefficient space. In particular they are affine coordinates, every block has rank \(r\), no pair exposes a constant-one span modulo row equations, and the selected class has exactly \(M=r\) groups. The whole original inventory has \(O(n^2)\) blocks, \(O(n^3)\) input forms, and \(O(n^5)\) coefficients.

Proof. For a fixed retained subboard \(U\) of size \((N+1)\times N\), apply the earlier nonzero-combination argument to the full stack of \(r^2\) random rows. The probability of a rank loss modulo the \(N+1\) row-sum vectors is at most

\[ (2^{r^2}-1)\,2^{-(N^2-1)}. \]

There is one designated full stack for each \(N\); there is no pair-count factor. Union-bound over retained subboards and over \(4L\le N\le n\). Since \(r\le N/2+1\), the logarithm of a fixed-\(N\) summand is at most

\[ -\frac34N^2+2NL+N+L+2\le-\frac18N^2. \]

Indeed \(2NL\le N^2/2\) for \(N\ge4L\), while \(N+L+2\le N^2/8\) for \(N\ge\max(4L,12)\). This last condition holds throughout our range for large \(n\). The total failure probability is less than \(2^{L-2L^2}<1\). Matching-dependent constants do not affect the full linear-part certificate, so it covers every matching with the same surviving vertices. Summing \(r\) blocks and \(r^2\) inputs over \(O(n)\) ranks gives the description bounds.

This refines the dyadic pair-rank inventory, using all integer ranks and fewer blocks within the selected class to obtain a full-stack certificate. It remains a polynomial-size, one-level MOD2-compatible inventory, with sharp degree-two input Booleanity and original companion degree \(2h+1\) at common accuracy \(h\).

3. The actual kernel is trivial in the affordable range

Take \(h\ge L\), \(D\ge2h+1\). Every usable residual \(N\ge2D\) lies above \(4L\). For its selected class, full joint independence and (JOINT-first-degree) show that the first nonzero common Boolean vanishing class has degree

\[ M=r_N=\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1. \]

Thus there is no such class through the target degree \(\lfloor N/2\rfloor\). The full inventory's common kernel is contained in the selected class's kernel and obeys the same vanishing statement. This is a statement about the actual kernel, not just an unsuccessful dimension estimate.

13 September 2026 — Full-base relative learning and an exact quadratic obstruction

1. Relative ideal membership is sufficient for learning

Let \(\mathcal F\) be an old system over \(\mathbb F_2\) containing all old Boolean equations. Use a one-level affine ENS family with common \(h\ge1\), all companions and fresh Boolean coefficient variables, after zero/unit-span cleanup. Write \(G_b\) for block \(b\)'s input tuple. Suppose an augmented degree-\(D\) PC or NS refutation exists, with \(D\ge2h+1\).

Working extension of common-vanishing learning. If an old polynomial \(f\), of degree \(s\le c\), satisfies

\[ f\in\bigcap_b\mathcal I_c(\mathcal F\cup G_b), \qquad c\ge1, \]

then it is an old-base consequence through

\[ B=TD+s,\qquad T=\max(1,c-1): \quad f\in\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F) \quad\text{or respectively}\quad f\in\mathcal I_B(\mathcal F). \tag{REL-learning} \]

The coefficient-certificate ceiling \(c\) and the actual target degree \(s\) are separate. The earlier \(TD+c\) bound follows by using \(s\le c\).

Proof. By the definition of ordinary NS membership, for every block there are coefficients of degree at most \(c-1\) such that

\[ f-H_b\in\mathcal I_c(\mathcal F),\qquad H_b=\sum_i a_{b,i}g_{b,i}. \]

Set the first coefficient row of every block to \(a_{b,i}\), all other rows to zero, and weight the specialized proof by \(f\). The companion identity is unchanged:

\[ f g_{b,i}(1-H_b) =g_{b,i}\bigl[f(1-f)+f(f-H_b)\bigr]. \]

Its first term has an old Boolean certificate through \(2s+1\), and its second has an old-base certificate through \(c+s+1\). Since \(s\le c\), both fit \(c+s+1\). Fresh field images have certificates through \(2T+s\). The inequalities \(c+1\le3T\le TD\) and \(D\ge3\) put these ceilings within \(TD+s\); old-axiom multiples also fit because \(T\ge1\). Weighted polynomial substitution replays every PC inference through \(TD+s\), ending with \(f\).

For an NS certificate, a companion's original degree is \(e=2h+1\ge3\). Its specialized cofactor costs at most \(T(D-e)\), so the inserted old certificate costs at most \(T(D-e)+c+s+1\le TD+s\), using \(c+1\le Te\). Field terms cost at most \(T(D-2)+2T+s\); an old degree-\(d\) generator costs at most \(T(D-d)+d+s\). This proves the NS statement without closing a truncated NS space under multiplication. All activity and cofactor bounds remain tied to the original degrees.

This uses ordinary membership in each augmented old-input system, not a certificate in the full unrestricted ideal. The earlier target-annihilator theorem has a different, nested-span hypothesis; its supplied annihilator products are not assumed here.

13 September 2026 — Pair compatibility supplies a simultaneous NS-to-PC transfer

Status: working conditional transfer throughout the first mixed-support band, an exact pair-duality criterion, and certified finite applications. The input is an NS derivation; no augmented PC lower bound is inferred.

Route obligation. A global common class was only a sufficient method hypothesis. This cycle examines the actual NS cofactor supports beyond the automatic window. It stops at a pair-compatibility construction, an application to the prior independent fixture, and an explicit remaining source-overlap and higher-degree gap.

1. In this degree band, only pair components are needed

Over \(\mathbb F_2\), let the old system \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb F_2[Y]\) contain all old Boolean equations. Use a complete same-level family of nonconstant affine input tuples \(G_b=(g_{b,i})_i\) in \(\mathbb F_2[Y]\), with disjoint fresh coefficient variables, their Boolean equations, and common accuracy \(h\ge1\). Keep original companion degree \(e=2h+1\). Write

\[ D=3h+u,\quad 1\le u\le h,\qquad L=D-h=2h+u,\qquad H=D-2h=h+u. \tag{PAIR-band} \]

The historical automatic window covers \(D\le3h\). Here an allowed companion cofactor has degree at most \(h+u-1<2h\), so at most one foreign block can have all its \(h\) factor rows represented.

Specialize the historical sufficient mixed-moment system. Keep an old root functional \(\lambda\), singleton components \(\mu_{b,j}\) on \(\mathcal P_{\le L}\), and pair components \(\phi_{ab,jk}\) on \(\mathcal P_{\le H}\). They annihilate the old NS spaces through their respective domains. The required equations are

\[ \lambda(qg_{b,i})=\sum_j\mu_{b,j}(qg_{b,i}g_{b,j}) \quad(\deg q\le h+u-1), \tag{PAIR-root} \]
\[ \mu_{b,j}\bigl(qg_{b,i}(1-g_{b,j})\bigr)=0 \quad(\deg q\le u-1), \tag{PAIR-own} \]
\[ \begin{aligned} \mu_{a,j}(qg_{b,i})&=\sum_k\phi_{ab,jk}(qg_{b,i}g_{b,k}),\\ \mu_{b,k}(qg_{a,i})&=\sum_j\phi_{ab,jk}(qg_{a,i}g_{a,j}) \end{aligned} \quad(\deg q\le u-1). \tag{PAIR-cross} \]

There are no additional constraints indexed by two or more complete blocks in a cofactor: the next multiplier ceiling is \(D-e-2h=u-h-1<0\). All components on three or more blocks may be set to zero. This reduction concerns the stated diagonal coefficient-operator construction; it is not asserted to characterize every possible joint design.

2. The exact compatibility condition for one pair

Put \(Q_H=\mathcal P_{\le H}/\mathcal I_H(\mathcal F)\), and define

\[ U_b=\left\{\sum_i q_i g_{b,i}:\deg q_i\le u-1\right\},\qquad W_b=\operatorname{span}\{ [qg_{b,i}g_{b,j}]_{Q_H}:\deg q\le u-1\}. \tag{PAIR-spaces} \]

Members of \(U_b\) have degree at most \(u\), and the displayed products have degree at most \(u+1\le H\). Fix the singleton components. Pair components satisfying (PAIR-cross) exist if and only if the following condition holds:

\[ \begin{gathered} A_j\in U_b,\quad B_k\in U_a,\qquad A_jg_{b,k}+B_kg_{a,j}\in\mathcal I_H(\mathcal F) \quad\text{for all }j,k\\ \Longrightarrow\quad \sum_j\mu_{a,j}(A_j)+\sum_k\mu_{b,k}(B_k)=0. \end{gathered} \tag{PAIR-dual} \]

Proof. The unknown \(\phi_{ab,jk}\) are arbitrary linear functionals on copies of \(Q_H\). Take an arbitrary linear combination of the equations in (PAIR-cross). Collecting its coefficients yields some \(A_j\in U_b\), \(B_k\in U_a\); the coefficient of the unknown functional \(\phi_{ab,jk}\) is the class of \(A_jg_{b,k}+B_kg_{a,j}\). Such a combination is a consistency obstruction precisely when all these classes are zero but its prescribed right side is nonzero. Finite-dimensional linear separation gives exactly (PAIR-dual). No common class across all blocks occurs in this criterion.

This is necessary and sufficient for the displayed pair-component equations with the chosen singletons. Simultaneous selection of compatible singletons can still matter when the input product spaces overlap.

3. Pairwise separation is a sufficient simultaneous transfer condition

Working theorem. In (PAIR-band), assume

\[ W_a\cap W_b=0\quad(a\ne b). \tag{PAIR-separation} \]

Every functional on old \(\mathcal P_{\le D}\) annihilating \(\mathcal C_D(\mathcal F)\) extends to a functional annihilating the complete augmented degree-\(D\) NS space, preserving its old values. A normalized old functional therefore extends to an ordinary degree-\(D\) design. Consequently, with \(\mathcal R\) denoting all fresh Boolean equations,

\[ \mathcal I_D(\mathcal F\cup\mathcal E\cup\mathcal R) \cap\mathbb F_2[Y]_{\le D} \subseteq\mathcal C_D(\mathcal F). \tag{PAIR-transfer} \]

In particular an augmented degree-\(D\) NS refutation yields an old-base degree-\(D\) PC refutation. The degree bound has no family-count or fan-in factor. No corresponding conclusion is asserted for an augmented PC derivation.

Construct the singletons. This specializes the historical PC-based supported construction. For each block, seek functionals \(\nu_{b,j}\) through degree \(L+1\), annihilating \(\mathcal C_{L+1}(\mathcal F)\), with

\[ \sum_j\nu_{b,j}(Gg_{b,j})=\lambda(G),\qquad G=\sum_i q_i g_{b,i},\quad \deg q_i\le h+u-1. \]

The consistency kernel has every \(Gg_{b,j}\in\mathcal C_{L+1}\). Since \(\deg G\le h+u\), PC reuse gives

\[ G^2=\sum_i q_i(Gg_{b,i})\in\mathcal C_D, \qquad L+1\le D,\quad 2(h+u)\le D. \]

The same degree bound handles \(G^2-G\), so \(G\in\mathcal C_D\) and \(\lambda(G)=0\). Finite-dimensional separation supplies the \(\nu_{b,j}\), independently for every block, from the same root \(\lambda\).

Define \(\mu_{b,j}(P)=\nu_{b,j}(g_{b,j}P)\) on \(\mathcal P_{\le L}\). These annihilate \(\mathcal I_L\). Boolean reduction gives (PAIR-root): the extra support factor replaces \(g_{b,j}^2\) by \(g_{b,j}\) within degree \(h+u+2\le L+1\). It also gives (PAIR-own), since the supported expression contains \(g_{b,j}(1-g_{b,j})\). All witnesses lie in the stated old domains.

Construct each pair. Consider a kernel in (PAIR-dual). The class of \(A_jg_{b,k}\) lies in \(W_b\), while that of \(B_kg_{a,j}\) lies in \(W_a\). Separation forces both classes to be zero. Write \(A_j=\sum_i q_i g_{b,i}\) with \(\deg q_i\le u-1\). Then

\[ A_j^2=\sum_i q_i(A_jg_{b,i}) \in\mathcal I_{H+u-1}(\mathcal F). \]

Boolean reduction of \(A_j^2-A_j\) costs at most \(2u\le H+u-1\). Thus \(A_j\in\mathcal I_{h+2u-1}\subseteq\mathcal I_L\), because \(u\le h\). The same holds for every \(B_k\). Both sums in (PAIR-dual) are therefore zero, regardless of the already chosen singleton components. Each pair is feasible, and different unordered pairs have disjoint unknown functionals.

Assemble the extension. Choose these pair solutions, set all higher components to zero, and apply the mixed-system construction:

\[ \Lambda(P)=\lambda(P(Y,0)) +\sum_{b,j}\mu_{b,j}(T_{b,j}P) +\sum_{a<b}\sum_{j,k}\phi_{ab,jk}(T_{ab,jk}P). \]

Here the linked coefficient operators first make the selected auxiliary variables Boolean, extract their complete diagonal groups, and set other fresh variables to zero. The established root, own-block, and pair equations cover all allowed cofactors; no higher equation is required in this band. Old-axiom multiples lie in the component annihilation domains, and new Boolean equations reduce to zero. Every nonempty coefficient operator vanishes on old-only polynomials, so old values and normalization are preserved.

The construction also works for unnormalized \(\lambda\); normalization was never used in its consistency arguments. Therefore every old functional annihilating \(\mathcal C_D\) annihilates any augmented NS consequence that is old-only. Annihilator duality proves (PAIR-transfer).

Functional-PHP consequence. When \(N\ge2D-1\), base filtration stability gives \(\mathcal C_D=\mathcal I_D\) and normalized old designs. The old-only augmented NS intersection is then exactly \(\mathcal I_D(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun})\), and no augmented degree-\(D\) NS refutation exists under (PAIR-separation). At \(u=1\), all product polynomials have degree at most two; the separation test may use \(\mathcal I_2\), since \(\mathcal I_{h+1}\cap\mathcal P_{\le2}=\mathcal I_2\) in this range.

Their product spaces are nested as well, so full pairwise separation fails whenever the smaller space is nonzero. A completed-certificate support argument could still matter, but no general removal of these interactions has been proved.

The separation test is also restrictive beyond \(u=1\): for \(u\ge2\), choosing \(q=g_{b,j}\) in a diagonal generator of \(W_a\) shows that \([g_{a,i}g_{b,j}]\) lies in both \(W_a\) and \(W_b\), using the degree-three Boolean reduction. Separation would force every such cross product into \(\mathcal I_H\). The exact compatibility criterion is more general; our finite applications are at \(u=1\). Source degree budgets can also exceed \(4h\); at \(D=4h+1\), cofactors may contain two complete blocks and higher mixed components are no longer optional.

Next step. Test (PAIR-dual) on the actual nested OR/MP interactions, and determine whether singleton components can be chosen coherently for them. Stop at a local construction with its needed old-base proofs, or a precise obstruction to that source interface. Keep the separate higher-support and multilevel gaps explicit.
