13 September 2026 — Nested and overlapping affine spaces can be coordinated

Status: working first-boundary transfer under faithful quadratic relations, a certificate-specific extension, and exact finite controls. Full source faithfulness and higher-support coverage remain open.

Route obligation. The source can contain nested or overlapping input spaces, so pair separation is too restrictive. This cycle classifies the exact first-boundary kernel, coordinates the surviving equal-span condition, and tests a family where the earlier separation and global shared-class tests both fail.

1. The Boolean pair kernel is zero except for equal spans

Start at \(D=3h+1\), \(h\ge1\), with the previous one-level binary affine setup. Ignore zero inputs and remove spans containing one by their existing scalar specialization. Let \(V_a,V_b\) be the nonzero polynomial input spans, with \(1\notin V_a,V_b\). Redundant generators are allowed.

In the Boolean function space through degree two, put

\[ \widehat W_b=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_2} \{g_{b,i}g_{b,j}\}\pmod{\mathcal I_2({\rm BOOL})}. \]

Faithful-pair hypothesis. The natural map

\[ \rho_{h+1}:\widehat W_a+\widehat W_b \longrightarrow \mathcal P_{\le h+1}/\mathcal I_{h+1}(\mathcal F) \tag{FAITH-pair} \]

is injective. This allows the product spaces to overlap, provided the old base introduces no extra quadratic relation in their sum. It compares Boolean function classes with a bounded old NS quotient, not with the unrestricted ideal.

Working classification. Under (FAITH-pair), a kernel from (PAIR-dual) has

\[ \begin{cases} A_j=B_k=0\text{ for all }j,k,&V_a\ne V_b,\\ A_j=\alpha g_{a,j},\quad B_k=\alpha g_{b,k},\quad \alpha\in\mathbb F_2,&V_a=V_b. \end{cases} \tag{FAITH-kernel} \]

This is a classification of polynomial arrays. Redundant tuple coordinates can add coefficient-representation kernels whose polynomial arrays are zero.

Proof. At this first boundary, \(A_j\in V_b\) and \(B_k\in V_a\) are affine. Faithfulness turns their kernel relation into the Boolean identity

\[ A_jg_{b,k}=B_kg_{a,j}. \]

Write \(A_j=\sum_k c_k g_{b,k}\). Summing the identities with coefficients \(c_k\) gives \(A_j^2=g_{a,j}\sum_k c_kB_k\). Since \(A_j\) is Boolean, it vanishes on the affine hyperplane \(g_{a,j}=0\). An affine function vanishing on that hyperplane is either zero or \(g_{a,j}\): make \(g_{a,j}\) the first affine coordinate and inspect the remaining coefficients. Hence \(A_j\in\{0,g_{a,j}\}\); symmetrically \(B_k\in\{0,g_{b,k}\}\).

Two nonzero affine functions in a span excluding one have a nonzero Boolean product. Otherwise one vanishes on the other's one-hyperplane, so they are complements and their sum is one. If some \(A_j=g_{a,j}\ne0\), then \(g_{a,j}\in V_b\), and its product with every nonzero \(g_{b,k}\in V_b\) is nonzero. The kernel equation forces \(B_k=g_{b,k}\) for every \(k\), so \(V_b\subseteq V_a\). Reversing the argument forces every \(A_j=g_{a,j}\) and \(V_a\subseteq V_b\). If all \(A_j=0\), the identities \(B_kg_{a,j}=0\) imply \(B_k^2=0\), hence \(B_k=0\). Conversely the common identity array is a kernel whenever the spans are equal. This proves (FAITH-kernel), including strict nesting and non-nested overlap.

2. One scalar can be chosen consistently for each equal-span class

The surviving condition is

\[ \theta_a=\theta_b,\qquad \theta_b:=\sum_j\mu_{b,j}(g_{b,j}) \quad\text{when }V_a=V_b. \tag{FAITH-theta} \]

Working coordination lemma. For a fixed old functional \(\lambda\) annihilating \(\mathcal C_{3h+1}(\mathcal F)\), singleton components can be chosen with one common feasible \(\theta_V\) for all tuples spanning the same \(V\), without increasing any degree ceiling.

Proof. Use the supported components \(\mu_j(P)=\nu_j(g_jP)\), with \(\nu_j\) defined through \(B_0=2h+2\) and annihilating \(\mathcal C_{B_0}\). The root constraints concern

\[ U(V)=\left\{\sum_i q_i g_i:\deg q_i\le h\right\}. \]

This polynomial space depends only on \(V\), not on its displayed generators. Extend the root-coupling domain by the constant polynomial, and consider

\[ \Phi_{(g_i)}:U(V)+\mathbb F_2\,1 \longrightarrow\bigoplus_i \bigl(\mathcal P_{\le B_0}/\mathcal C_{B_0}\bigr), \qquad G\longmapsto([Gg_i])_i. \]

All products fit because \(\deg G\le h+1\). Its kernel is the tuple-independent condition \(GV\subseteq\mathcal C_{B_0}\). Prescribing a scalar \(\theta\) means prescribing a linear functional on \(U(V)+\mathbb F_2\,1\) that agrees with \(\lambda\) on \(U(V)\), takes value \(\theta\) on one, and annihilates this kernel. Such a prescription is feasible exactly when that linear functional descends to the image of \(\Phi\).

The original supported construction supplies at least one feasible prescription: take any of its \(\nu_i\), and evaluate \(\sum_i\nu_i(Gg_i)\) on the enlarged domain. The set of possible \(\theta\) therefore is nonempty and depends only on \(V\). Choose one value per equal-span class; finite-dimensional separation supplies the corresponding \(\nu_i\) for every tuple in that class. Finally \(\sum_i\mu_i(g_i)=\sum_i\nu_i(g_i^2)=\sum_i\nu_i(g_i)=\theta\), using degree-two Boolean reduction. This proves the claim without assuming arbitrary independent singleton choices are compatible.

The discussion concerns the chosen diagonal component construction. The scalar is an algebraic component value; no positivity or multiplicativity is assumed.

3. Simultaneous transfer at the first boundary

Working theorem. In the one-level setup of Section 1, suppose (FAITH-pair) holds for every distinct pair. Then every old functional annihilating \(\mathcal C_D(\mathcal F)\), \(D=3h+1\), extends to a functional annihilating the augmented degree-\(D\) NS space and preserving all old values. In particular,

\[ \mathcal I_D(\mathcal F\cup\mathcal E\cup\mathcal R) \cap\mathbb F_2[Y]_{\le D} \subseteq\mathcal C_D(\mathcal F). \tag{FAITH-transfer} \]

Here \(\mathcal R\) consists of the fresh Boolean equations. The input is an NS consequence; this is not an augmented-PC transfer theorem. There is no family-count degree charge.

Proof. Choose supported singletons by Section 2, with one feasible scalar for each equal-span class. For different spans, Section 1 says the polynomial-array kernel in (PAIR-dual) is zero. For equal spans, its only potentially nonzero value is \(\theta_a+\theta_b=0\). Thus each pair system is feasible. Solve the pairs independently, set higher components to zero, and apply the mixed-system construction exactly as in the preceding transfer proof. Normalization was not needed to select the components. Annihilator duality gives (FAITH-transfer); a normalized root gives an ordinary joint design.

The same proof permits an edge-by-edge choice: each pair may satisfy either the preceding separation hypothesis or (FAITH-pair). Separation works for every choice of singletons, while the common scalars handle all faithful equal-span edges at once. For a supplied old-target certificate, only the edges of its complete-diagonal cofactor graph need these hypotheses.

For binary functional PHP with \(N\ge2D-1\), base filtration stability supplies normalized old designs and \(\mathcal C_D=\mathcal I_D\). The theorem therefore excludes augmented NS refutations through \(D\). Faithfulness can be checked in the old degree-two quotient because \(\mathcal I_{h+1}\cap\mathcal P_{\le2}=\mathcal I_2\). Strictly nested tuples are covered when this hypothesis holds; nesting itself is no longer an obstruction.

4. A certificate-specific extension through the first band

There is also a useful refinement for \(D=3h+u\), \(1\le u\le h\), with \(H=h+u\) and \(L=2h+u\). Consider an actual degree-\(D\) NS certificate for an old target, and its extracted arrays

\[ A^{a\to b}_j=\sum_i T_{a,j}(C_{b,i})g_{b,i}, \qquad \deg A^{a\to b}_j\le u. \]

Working corollary. Suppose that, on every required pair, (FAITH-pair) holds with quotient \(\mathcal I_H\), and each displayed array polynomial Boolean-reduces to an affine polynomial. Then that certificate's old target belongs to \(\mathcal C_D(\mathcal F)\). Alternatively, a pair may satisfy the earlier separation test, without the affine-reduction assumption on that pair. This statement concerns the supplied certificate; for \(u>1\) it does not assert a full joint-design extension.

Proof. The scalar argument of Section 2 applies with \(U(V)=\sum_i\mathcal P_{\le h+u-1}g_i\), and supported \(\nu_i\) through \(L+1\). The kernel and its feasible scalar set still depend only on \(V\). The preceding root construction remains valid since \(2(h+u)\le D\). Choose common feasible scalars for equal spans.

Let \(\widetilde A_j\) be the affine reduction of \(A_j\). It vanishes wherever every input of block \(b\) vanishes. Since \(1\notin V_b\), this nonempty affine zero space has vanishing affine ideal exactly \(V_b\); hence \(\widetilde A_j\in V_b\). Also \(A_j-\widetilde A_j\in\mathcal I_u({\rm BOOL})\). The actual coefficient identity

\[ A_jg_{b,k}+B_kg_{a,j}\in\mathcal I_H(\mathcal F) \]

therefore gives the same identity for the affine representatives, because \(u+1\le H\). Section 1 classifies that reduced kernel, and the chosen scalars give

\[ \sum_j\mu_{a,j}(A_j)+\sum_k\mu_{b,k}(B_k)=0. \]

The replacement by affine representatives does not affect these values: the singletons annihilate \(\mathcal I_L\), and \(u\le L\). On a separated pair, the earlier square argument instead puts every array polynomial in \(\mathcal I_L\), giving the same cancellation.

Apply just the root-plus-singleton functional \(\Lambda_0(P)=\lambda(P(Y,0))+\sum_{a,j}\mu_{a,j}(T_{a,j}P)\) to the whole certificate. Old-axiom and fresh-field multiples vanish. Root cofactors cancel by the root equations. Cofactors with nonempty own support cancel by supported Booleanity, while incomplete or non-diagonal foreign supports contribute zero. Its remaining extension contribution is exactly \(\sum_{a\ne b,j}\mu_{a,j}(A^{a\to b}_j)\), which cancels pairwise as just proved. Thus every \(\lambda\) annihilating old \(\mathcal C_D\) annihilates the target, proving the corollary by duality.

Affine reduction of these actual extracted arrays is an additional source obligation. It cannot be inferred merely from affine inputs: the cofactor coefficients have degree up to \(u-1\). Likewise a local OR/MP tuple pattern does not establish the support or cancellation pattern of a completed source certificate.

5. A finite family beyond separation and shared-class learning

Use the six affine inputs \(U_1,\ldots,U_6\) from group zero of the eleven-hole independent fixture. The ambient certificate records their exact coefficients and extracts the following facts from the previously saved complete rank certificates. No old large matrix computation was repeated.

First quotient only by Boolean and row equations, obtaining a free Boolean cube with \(d=132-12=120\) coordinates. The six \(U_i\) are independent modulo rows and can be completed to affine coordinates. Let \(J_{U,2}\) be the degree-two ideal of their common zero space in this cube, and put

\[ M=\mathcal P_{\le1}+J_{U,2},\qquad \dim J_{U,2}=6(120+1)-\frac{6\cdot7}{2}=705, \quad \dim M=121+705-6=820. \]

The old functional-PHP degree-two quotient has dimension \(5995\). The saved relative-input elimination has additional rank \(705\), exactly six affine pivots, and the old quotient has affine dimension \(121\). Thus the image of \(M\) has dimension \(705+121-6=820\), so its map to the full old quotient is injective. Highest-pivot monomial order is degree-compatible: the affine pivots measure precisely the intersection with the affine subspace. The independent saved square-space certificate also gives rank \(21\) for \(\operatorname{span}\{U_iU_j\}\) and puts the unit outside that span. In particular the unital degree-two Boolean space

\[ A_{U,2}=\operatorname{span}\{1,U_i,U_iU_j:i<j\} \]

has dimension \(22\) and embeds in the old quotient. Here “degree-two space” is a truncated vector space, not an assertion that it is closed under arbitrary multiplication.

Take all \(64\) tuples \(G_c=(U_1+c_1,\ldots,U_6+c_6)\), \(c\in\mathbb F_2^6\), and add the nested tuple \((U_1,\ldots,U_5)\) and a prefix-basis change of \(G_0\). This gives \(66\) complete ENS blocks. Each input span excludes one, and all pair-product sums lie in \(A_{U,2}\); hence every pair is faithful. The exact small-space audit finds one equal-span pair and three strict nestings. Its square-space intersections are:

Thus none of the \(2,145\) pairs satisfies the previous separation test. Nevertheless, at \(h=1,D=4,N=11\), (FAITH-transfer) supplies a normalized augmented degree-four design and excludes an NS refutation through degree four.

The global shared-class tests also fail here. Every old Boolean assignment has some value \(U=c\), so it lies in the zero space of the corresponding translated tuple. The union of these zero spaces is the whole cube; its common Boolean vanishing space is zero at every degree. This observation alone does not settle relative membership in the full PHP base, so use the certified injectivity of \(M\).

In the row cube, let \(J_{c,2}\) be the degree-two ideal generated by \(U_i+c_i\). It is exactly the space of degree-at-most-two functions vanishing on the fiber \(U=c\), by an affine coordinate change. Expanding \((U_i+c_i)q=U_iq+c_iq\), \(\deg q\le1\), shows \(J_{c,2}\subseteq M\). The fibers cover the row cube, hence \(\bigcap_c J_{c,2}=0\). Injectivity on their common ambient space gives

\[ \bigcap_c \frac{\mathcal I_2(\mathcal F_{11}^{\rm fun}\cup G_c)} {\mathcal I_2(\mathcal F_{11}^{\rm fun})}=0. \]

Indeed equal images from different \(J_{c,2}\) must have the same preimage in \(M\). Adding the two extra tuples cannot enlarge this intersection. No individual translated tuple has a degree-two NS unit either: \(1\in M\), but \(1\notin J_{c,2}\). The degree-one common relative space is also zero by the old stable inclusion into degree two. For the currently available relative-learning ledger, \(c\ge3\) already costs at least \(2D=8\), whereas the stable ceiling on this board is at most six. Thus all affordable shared-class premises fail, while the new moment construction succeeds.

A cheaper necessary test does not already dispose of this example. More generally, setting all fresh variables to zero in a degree-\(D\) augmented NS refutation gives

\[ 1-P\in\mathcal I_D(\mathcal F),\qquad P=\sum_{b,i}q_{b,i}g_{b,i},\quad \deg q_{b,i}\le D-(2h+1),\quad\deg P\le d_0:=D-2h. \]

Whenever \(\mathcal I_D\cap\mathcal P_{\le d_0}=\mathcal I_{d_0}\), this gives an NS refutation of \(\mathcal F\cup\bigcup_b G_b\) through \(d_0\). Its absence would be a cheap exclusion of the augmented endpoint. The translated family passes this necessary test: the aggregate inputs already have the linear identity \(U_1+(U_1+1)=1\). This calibration does not claim that every earlier random fixture was tested by this cheaper criterion.

This is a finite, fully specified application, not a full source-family theorem. Enumerating every translation uses \(2^r\) tuples for ambient rank \(r\), so the construction does not by itself supply a polynomial-size asymptotic family with \(r\) proportional to the board size. No full eleven-hole joint moment array or augmented PC lower bound was computed.

6. Exact kernel and singleton-coherence controls

The new compiled checker solves seven pure-Boolean pair kernels and one failed-hypothesis column control, retaining all equations, elimination traces, and kernel vectors. The seven cases are separated spaces, strict nesting, proper overlap, identical tuples, an invertible basis change, affine offsets, and a redundant equal-span tuple. Their polynomial-array kernel dimensions are respectively \(0,0,0,1,1,0,1\). The redundant case has coefficient-kernel dimension three, with two zero-representation directions, as required by the distinction in Section 1.

Old quadratic relations can matter without preventing transfer. In the control \(V_a=\langle a\rangle\), \(V_b=\langle a,b\rangle\), with the old equation \(ab=0\), the array \(A=a\), \(B_a=a\), \(B_b=0\) is an extra nonzero kernel for distinct spans. The domain consists of \(00,01,10\); the checker obtains dimension one. Faithfulness fails. This particular new relation is harmless for compatible components: the root equations give \(\lambda(a)=\mu_{a,a}(a)=\mu_{b,a}(a)\), since \(\mu_{b,b}(ab)=0\). Its dual value is therefore zero. Failure of the sufficient hypothesis is not itself failure of transfer; the known column normalizers also cover this simple structure.

Equal-span choices really require coordination. For a separate satisfiable Boolean control, take three old variables \(x_0,x_1,x_2\), root evaluation at \(000\), two identical tuples \((x_0,x_1,x_2)\), and \(h=1,D=4\). Define \(\nu_j\) as the sum over the nonzero three-bit points whose first set bit is \(j\), and put \(\mu_j(P)=\nu_j(x_jP)=\nu_j(P)\). The combined sum over all seven nonzero points annihilates every nonconstant monomial of degree at most two: the relevant counts are four or two, both even. These components satisfy the root and own-block equations and have \(\theta=1\). All-zero components also satisfy them and have \(\theta=0\).

Choosing different scalars in the two blocks gives dual value one on the common identity-array kernel, so no pair components can repair those fixed singleton choices. Equal zero choices work with zero pairs; equal one choices work with \(\phi_{jk}=\delta_{jk}\nu_j\) restricted through degree two. The latter cross equations follow from the support identity \(\nu_j(x_ix_j)=\nu_j(x_i)\).

7. Contribution and remaining source obligation

The first-boundary overlap issue is reduced to old quadratic relations: strict nesting, arbitrary overlap, affine offsets, and repeated spans are compatible under faithfulness, with the last case requiring one coherent scalar. The translated PHP example distinguishes this method from both pair separation and global relative learning. However, no proof yet shows that the actual source spaces satisfy faithfulness or that all additional old quadratic relations are harmless. The affine-reduction requirement for larger first-band cofactors, higher supports at \(D>4h\), odd-prime inputs, and multilevel propagation remain open.

Next obligation. Analyze the old quadratic relations induced by actual affine input coefficients on the PHP board. Stop at a checkable structural condition or an explicit obstruction, and identify what it proves for the OR/MP tuples rather than treating another conditional example as full source coverage.

13 September 2026 — Quadratic PHP relations localize affine input directions

Status: working structural criteria for quadratic faithfulness, a conditional source MP extension, and exact coefficient-space certificates. Universal source coverage and compatibility in the presence of extra relations remain open.

Route obligation. The preceding transfer needs the old PHP base to add no quadratic relation in the relevant pair spaces. This cycle replaces that assumption by explicit tests on affine input coefficients, explains where a relation must be supported, and treats the actual nested MP input pattern with an arbitrary independent affine antecedent.

1. Every old quadratic relation satisfies rectangle equations

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) with the explicit functional base \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\), \(N\ge4\). Let \(U=(U_1,\ldots,U_r)^{\mathsf T}\) be affine inputs, written

\[ U=c+\sum_{i=0}^{N}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} A_{ij}x_{ij}, \qquad A_{ij}\in\mathbb F_2^r. \]

Assume the within-row coefficient differences span \(\mathbb F_2^r\):

\[ \operatorname{span}\{A_{ij}+A_{ik}:i,j,k\}=\mathbb F_2^r. \tag{RECT-linear} \]

This says precisely that the input linear parts are independent modulo the span of the row vectors. Consequently \(1,U_1,\ldots,U_r\) have no nonzero affine relation modulo the old row equations. The old degree-two space has no additional affine consequences, by filtration stability at \(B=2\).

Write a Boolean polynomial in the inputs through degree two as

\[ Q(U)=q_0+\ell^{\mathsf T}U+ \sum_{s<t} C_{st}U_sU_t, \qquad C_{ts}=C_{st},\quad C_{ss}=0. \]

Here \(C\) is its alternating Hessian matrix; over \(\mathbb F_2\) it is symmetric with zero diagonal. If \(Q(U)\in\mathcal I_2(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun})\), then for different rows \(i,a\) and four pairwise distinct columns \(j,k,b,d\),

\[ (A_{ij}+A_{ik})^{\mathsf T}C(A_{ab}+A_{ad})=0. \tag{RECT-equations} \]

Proof. Reduce Boolean squares and the row/column exclusions. The coefficient of the legal matching monomial \(x_{ij}x_{ab}\), \(i\ne a,j\ne b\), is \(A_{ij}^{\mathsf T}CA_{ab}\). Every remaining degree-two NS consequence is a sum of row equations multiplied by affine polynomials. On a fixed row pair \(i,a\), its matching coefficients therefore have the form \(s_j+t_b\): only the two corresponding row generators can contribute. Summing around a rectangle using disjoint column pairs cancels these potentials. All four monomials are legal matchings, giving (RECT-equations). Boolean and exclusion generators contribute no matching coefficient. This uses original degree-two NS generators, not closure under multiplication of previously derived equations.

Direct sufficient test. Solve (RECT-equations) as a homogeneous linear system on the \(\binom r2\) entries of \(C\). If its kernel is zero, the map

\[ A_{U,2}:=\operatorname{span}\{1,U_s,U_sU_t:s<t\} \longrightarrow\mathcal P_{\le2}/\mathcal I_2(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}) \tag{RECT-map} \]

is injective. Indeed an old relation must have \(C=0\); its remaining affine part is zero by (RECT-linear), old affine stability, and \(1\notin\mathcal I_2\). The input coordinates themselves are independent, so the source space has dimension \(1+r+\binom r2\). Nonzero rectangle kernels are only candidates for old relations: lower-degree terms and the other NS consistency conditions still have to be matched. No converse is asserted.

2. A quadratic relation must use directions supported on a few rows and columns

For one pigeon \(i\) and two holes \(J=\{j,k\}\), define

\[ S_{i,J}=\operatorname{span}\{A_{ab}+A_{ad}: a\ne i,\ b,d\notin J\},\qquad L_{\rm loc}=\operatorname{span}_{i,J}S_{i,J}^{\perp} \subseteq\mathbb F_2^r. \tag{RECT-local} \]

Working localization theorem. Under (RECT-linear), the Hessian of every old quadratic input relation satisfies

\[ \operatorname{im}C\subseteq L_{\rm loc}. \tag{RECT-image} \]

Every nonzero vector \(w\in S_{i,J}^{\perp}\) gives a nontrivial input combination \(w^{\mathsf T}U\) whose nonconstant support, modulo row equations, is contained in row \(i\) and the two columns \(J\). In particular:

  • If \(\dim L_{\rm loc}\le1\), (RECT-map) is injective.
  • A sufficient special case is \(S_{i,J}=\mathbb F_2^r\) for every \(i,J\): deleting any one row and two columns retains full coefficient rank modulo the remaining row vectors.
  • A nonzero quadratic relation forces at least two independent localized directions. The existence of those directions does not itself prove that a relation exists.

Proof. Apply (RECT-equations) with \(u=A_{ij}+A_{ik}\). It says \(Cu\in S_{i,J}^{\perp}\), using symmetry of \(C\). The vectors \(u\) span the entire input-coordinate space by (RECT-linear), so their images span \(\operatorname{im}C\), proving (RECT-image).

If \(w\in S_{i,J}^{\perp}\), the coefficient \(w^{\mathsf T}A_{ab}\) is constant in \(b\notin J\) for every \(a\ne i\). Call it \(\beta_a\). Subtracting \(\sum_{a\ne i}\beta_a(\rho_a-1)\) from \(w^{\mathsf T}U\) leaves only an affine constant and coefficients on the stated row and columns. A nonzero \(w\) cannot become constant modulo all rows, by (RECT-linear). This proves the support assertion with degree-one row witnesses.

A nonzero alternating matrix has rank at least two: any nonzero off-diagonal entry supplies an invertible \(2\times2\) principal submatrix. Thus \(\dim L_{\rm loc}\le1\) forces \(C=0\), and the affine argument from Section 1 finishes injectivity. This also proves the necessity of two independent localized directions.

More explicitly, choose a matrix \(W\) whose columns are a basis of \(L_{\rm loc}\), and a left inverse \(K\). From (RECT-image) and symmetry, \(C=W(KCK^{\mathsf T})W^{\mathsf T}\). Hence the quadratic part of any relation can be expressed using only the affine combinations \(W^{\mathsf T}U\), up to an affine remainder. This statement localizes the quadratic part; it does not say that all lower-degree terms of the relation involve only those combinations.

3. A robust conclusion space permits any independent affine antecedent

Working source-pattern theorem. Let \(N\ge6\) and let \(G=(G_1,\ldots,G_r)\) be affine conclusion inputs. Assume that deleting any two pigeon rows and four hole columns leaves full coefficient-difference rank \(r\) modulo the remaining rows. Let \(a\) be any affine polynomial independent of \(1,G_1,\ldots,G_r\) modulo the old row equations. Then the unital degree-two Boolean space on \((G,a)\) embeds in the old degree-two functional-PHP quotient.

Proof. The enlarged inputs satisfy (RECT-linear). Apply Section 2 to them and write a localized coefficient direction as \(w=(v,t)\in\mathbb F_2^r\oplus\mathbb F_2\). If \(t=0\), then \(v^{\mathsf T}G\) is supported, modulo rows and a constant, on one row and two columns. Pad these deletions to two rows and four columns. Full remaining rank forces \(v=0\).

Thus every nonzero localized direction has \(t=1\). If \(w=(v,1)\) and \(w'=(v',1)\) are two such directions, perhaps from different deletions, their sum is a combination of \(G\) supported on the union of at most two rows and four columns, modulo rows and a constant. The same rank hypothesis gives \(v+v'=0\). Therefore all nonzero localized directions coincide, and their span has dimension at most one. Section 2 proves injectivity. No coefficient-distribution assumption is imposed on \(a\).

Precise source implication. In an original binary level-one MP-A interaction, the nested tuples are \(G\) and \((a,G)\). Under the stated conclusion-rank and antecedent-independence hypotheses, their pair-product sum lies in the faithfully embedded degree-two space just proved. For \(D=3h+1\), \(N\ge2D-1\), old filtration stability upgrades the quotient to \(\mathcal I_{h+1}\), certifying the faithful-pair transfer hypothesis on this interaction. The pair's singletons can therefore be coupled without a degree increase. This is a conditional application to the actual nested source pattern, not merely a comparison of unrelated random spaces.

The test uses more than is necessary: a source pair needs faithfulness only on its within-block product sum, whereas the theorem embeds an entire unital degree-two space. It also does not cover a conclusion that fails the rank hypothesis, an antecedent dependent modulo rows, other edges of the completed certificate, larger first-band cofactor arrays, or higher support. No whole-source transfer follows from certifying one MP edge. Literal and row/column normalizers retain their separate scope.

The condition is not vacuous at large boards. If the coefficient vectors of \(G\) at different cells are independent and uniform in \(\mathbb F_2^r\), a fixed two-row/four-column deletion leaves \((N-1)(N-5)\) independent uniform differences after choosing a reference column in each retained row. For each nonzero dual vector the probability all its pairings vanish is \(2^{-(N-1)(N-5)}\). A union bound gives

\[ \Pr[\text{some deletion loses rank}] \le \binom{N+1}{2}\binom N4(2^r-1) 2^{-(N-1)(N-5)}. \]

This proves existence when the displayed bound is below one and strong probability bounds for many low-rank dense spaces. Actual source coefficients are proof-dependent and need not be random; this calculation does not supply their missing hypothesis.

4. Exact checks and controls

The new compiled checker uses the six previously certified eleven-hole inputs and their first five as the conclusion tuple. It performs coefficient-space elimination only, without rebuilding the large old NS quotient. Full input words, independent-generator witnesses, elimination traces, dual bases, and explicit row-equation localization witnesses are retained.

Every fixture has full global rank modulo row equations. Separately, all \(\binom{12}{2}\binom{11}{4}=21{,}780\) two-row/four-column deletions of the five-input conclusion retain rank five. Its direct rectangle matrix has rank ten out of ten. The source-pattern theorem therefore permits any independent affine antecedent on this board; the cell antecedent is an explicit checked instance. The archived sixth input also meets the independence assumption, already certified by the prior joint-rank evidence.

Controls distinguish the conclusions. For a single cell the full deletion-rank test fails, but \(\dim L_{\rm loc}=1\) correctly proves faithfulness. The two cells in one row or column have the actual old quadratic relation \(U_1U_2=0\), so global affine independence alone does not suffice. In contrast \(U_1=x_{00},U_2=x_{11}\) have \(\dim L_{\rm loc}=2\) but no old quadratic relation: use rows zero and one, column pairs \(\{0,2\}\) and \(\{1,3\}\) in (RECT-equations) to force \(C_{12}=0\), then use affine independence. Thus even a two-dimensional localized space need not obstruct faithfulness. These are algebraic controls, not claims that functional PHP itself has a satisfying assignment.

The reproduction record links the exact deletion certificates, rectangle certificates, inherited input data, and code hashes. A full-rank certificate stops after finding a basis; a deficient one includes a complete dual basis checked against every generator. No separate joint moment array, full NS quotient, or actual Frege proof was computed.

5. What changed in the route

The quadratic-faithfulness obligation is now checkable in input-coordinate spaces and has a proved support explanation. Robust conclusion spaces tolerate an arbitrary independent affine antecedent in the actual MP-A nesting pattern. This removes the need to assume pair faithfulness without a coefficient-level justification for that subclass. It does not show that the complete source inventory lies in the subclass.

The next question is whether the remaining quadratic relations really prevent coupling. Begin with nested source tuples involving row/column-supported directions: determine whether root constraints force their pair-kernel values to cancel, or produce an explicit incompatible system. Faithfulness is sufficient; its failure should not be mistaken for an obstruction. Higher cofactor supports, odd primes, and multilevel propagation remain open.

Process assessment. Small coefficient certificates avoided a full old-quotient elimination; an entry-placement slip was corrected before review and motivates a narrow placement guard in the timing helper, without adding workflow rules.

13 September 2026 — One restriction can remove a family's shared localized relations

Status: working first-boundary NS exclusion for affine families with a common removable support, and an exact mixed-family application. Universal pair coupling without faithfulness remains open.

Route obligation and actual outcome. The question was whether old row/column relations can be handled when the faithful-pair hypothesis fails. Pure single-column tuples are already covered by the existing normalizer; that case is not new. For mixed inputs, this cycle proves a family-wide restriction criterion and tests a family whose original blocks all have quadratic relations. It does not prove universal cancellation in the exact pair system.

1. Affine changes modulo row equations preserve the original ENS budget

Let \(g_i,g'_i\) be affine inputs over \(\mathbb F_2\), with \(g_i-g'_i\) a constant linear combination of old row equations. Use the same coefficient variables and accuracy \(h\), retaining original companion ceiling \(e=2h+1\). Then

\[ E_i(g)-E_i(g')\in \mathcal I_e(\{\rho_a-1\}_a) \]

in the joint old/coefficient-variable polynomial ring. Thus replacing all such input tuples preserves a supplied NS or PC derivation through its original degree ceiling. This is a specialized affine row-replacement statement, not an extension of the earlier general stable-ideal reduction theorem to arbitrary full-PHP ideal membership.

Proof. Write \(F_u=1-\sum_jr_{uj}g_j\), and similarly \(F'_u\). Telescope:

\[ E_i(g)-E_i(g')=(g_i-g'_i)\prod_uF_u +g'_i\sum_u(F_u-F'_u) \prod_{v<u}F'_v\prod_{v>u}F_v. \]

The first summand has a row-generator certificate through \(1+2h=e\). In the other summands, \(F_u-F'_u=-\sum_jr_{uj}(g_j-g'_j)\); each row generator has a coefficient of degree at most \(1+1+2(h-1)=2h\), including the outside input and the selected fresh variable. These certificates also fit \(e\). Coefficient-field equations and old axioms are unchanged.

For an NS certificate multiply the replacement proof by its original cofactor of degree at most \(D-e\). For PC, derive each original companion from its replacement and the displayed old-row certificate, then replay the original proof. Do not use a smaller specialized companion degree to enlarge original cofactor spaces. The replacements may be performed simultaneously, without a block-count charge.

2. A sufficient family-wide restriction theorem

Use the binary functional base on \(n+1\) pigeons and \(n\) holes. Consider any finite complete one-level affine ENS family of common accuracy \(h\), at

\[ D=3h+1. \]

Suppose there is a \(q\)-matching restriction \(\rho\), leaving \(N=n-q\) holes, and common affine polynomials \(U_1,\ldots,U_r\), such that every input has a representation

\[ g_{b,i}\equiv c_{b,i}+\sum_s a_{b,i,s}U_s+z_{b,i} \pmod{\operatorname{span}\{\rho_a-1\}_a}. \tag{STAR-inputs} \]

Each \(z_{b,i}\) is affine and its nonconstant support lies on rows or columns covered by the selected matching. Consequently \(z_{b,i}|_\rho\) is a constant. Assume also that the actual Boolean degree-two space

\[ \operatorname{span}\{1,U_s|_\rho,(U_sU_t)|_\rho\} \longrightarrow \mathcal P_{\le2}/\mathcal I_2(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}) \tag{STAR-core} \]

is injective, and \(N\ge2D-1\). Then the original augmented family has no NS refutation through degree \(D\). This also excludes such refutations over the weaker source base, by the explicit functional strengthening.

Proof. First use Section 1 to choose the displayed affine representatives in (STAR-inputs). An assumed NS refutation retains degree \(D\). Apply the matching restriction: old axioms become zero or residual functional-PHP axioms, and the remaining inputs all belong to \(\operatorname{span}\{1,U_s|_\rho\}\).

Remove zero inputs. If a tuple's polynomial span contains one, constant coefficients make its first ENS factor identically zero, so all its companions vanish; set its other coefficient rows to zero. An all-zero tuple also disappears. Set unused coefficient variables to constants, preserving field images and the original degree ceiling. Every retained nonzero input is affine and nonconstant, with companion degree \(2h+1\), and its span excludes one.

For every remaining pair, its raw Boolean within-block product sum lies in the space (STAR-core). Old filtration stability identifies \(\mathcal I_{h+1}\cap\mathcal P_{\le2}=\mathcal I_2\), so every pair satisfies (FAITH-pair). The simultaneous theorem supplies an ordinary degree-\(D\) joint design and rules out the restricted NS refutation. This contradicts its assumed origin.

A single such branch suffices for the lower-bound goal: every restriction preserves an assumed refutation. There is no need here to extend a prescribed original-board functional, recombine all column states, or pay a degree cost for every block. The cost is the actual loss of \(q\) holes. The final step is an NS exclusion; the preceding degree-preserving operations do not turn it into an augmented PC lower bound.

(STAR-core) can be certified by the rectangle test on the residual coefficients. The localized-direction theorem helps recognize candidate supports in (STAR-inputs), but does not guarantee a small common cover or preserve core faithfulness after an arbitrary restriction. Both hypotheses remain explicit.

3. A 192-block family whose original faithfulness tests all fail

Take the first five affine inputs \(U_0,\ldots,U_4\) from the inherited eleven-hole fixture. For each \(c\in\mathbb F_2^5\) and \(k=0,\ldots,5\), use the tuple

\[ G_{c,k}=(U_0+c_0,\ldots,U_4+c_4, x_{2k,0},x_{2k+1,0}). \tag{STAR-example} \]

There are \(32\cdot6=192\) complete blocks, each with seven inputs, at \(h=1,D=4\). These are affine tuples mixing dense old-variable inputs with a common column. They are not pure single-column tuples.

The original coefficient differences have rank seven for every column pair, so every translated tuple has input span excluding one. Each raw within-block product space contains the nonzero Boolean function \(x_{2k,0}x_{2k+1,0}\), which is an old column-exclusion generator. Thus every block has a nontrivial old quadratic relation, and the faithful-pair hypothesis fails on every pair of original blocks.

The older separation test also fails on every pair. The common core's unital quadratic space has certified dimension \(16\). For each translation \(c\), the within-core product span has dimension \(15\): in affine core coordinates it is the space of degree-at-most-two functions vanishing at \(U=c\). Any two such subspaces intersect in dimension at least \(15+15-16=14\). Each full block contains its core subspace. This is a dimension argument from the inherited faithful core, not a claim that all \(\binom{192}{2}\) full-block intersections were separately computed.

A common Boolean vanishing witness cannot give a new old consequence here. On any Boolean assignment satisfying the single column's exclusions, that column has at most one occupied cell. Choose \(c=U(x)\) and a pair \(k\) containing no occupied cell; at least five pairs are available if the column is occupied, and all six otherwise. Then every input of \(G_{c,k}\) is zero. Hence the union of the block-zero sets covers the entire proper single-column state domain. A polynomial vanishing on all block-zero sets vanishes on that domain. Boolean reduction in the other variables and degree-complete column division put a degree-\(t\) such polynomial in the old \(\mathcal I_t\). It is therefore not a nonzero class for the Boolean common-vanishing learning method. This does not settle all higher relative memberships using the full PHP base.

Covering restriction. Match pigeon eleven to hole zero. The residual board has \(N=10\) holes and eleven pigeons. For \(k=5\), the input \(x_{11,0}\) becomes one, so the corresponding \(32\) blocks disappear. For \(k<5\), both column inputs become zero. The remaining \(160\) blocks are five copies of the \(32\) translated core tuples on the actual restricted \(U_s|_\rho\).

The restricted core has coefficient rank five and rectangle rank ten out of ten. Thus its unital quadratic space embeds in the residual old quotient, and \(10\ge2\cdot4-1\). Section 2 excludes an NS refutation of the original 192-block family through degree four. No original-board joint functional was extended and no augmented PC lower bound is claimed.

Wrong-column control. Instead match pigeon eleven to hole one. The restricted dense core still has full rank five and rectangle rank ten. However, none of the local inputs becomes one, and \(160\) blocks retain two different cells of column zero and their nontrivial old collision relation; the other \(32\) retain one local cell. Thus faithful core survival alone does not suffice: the chosen restriction must also remove the localized directions. This is a failed hypothesis of the present criterion, not a refutation of the original family's lower bound.

4. Evidence, scope, and next obligation

The shared coefficient checker now has a separate --column-family mode. It preserves the full affine input words, six original tuple-rank certificates, both residual core certificates, all residual tuple ranks, and all \(384\) block images across the covering and wrong-column restrictions. It records each original column relation with a Boolean nonvanishing witness. All arithmetic is exact over \(\mathbb F_2\); it does not build a full NS quotient or a joint moment array.

The reproduction record explains the complete restriction output and inherited evidence. Compilation and the exact run passed. One preliminary source lookup used a nonexistent anchor and was corrected immediately; this was a navigation error, not a failed mathematical computation.

What changed. The first-boundary criterion now covers a whole mixed affine family with shared removable localized relations, even when original pair faithfulness, original pair separation, and nontrivial Boolean common vanishing all fail. The exact original pair system was not solved universally. A small shared support, faithful residual core, one-level affinity, and the first-boundary degree are still required; no theorem says the completed source family has them.

Proposed next obligation. Return to the actual MP cofactor identity and track its first mixed coefficient terms, including the contribution of the antecedent proof. Determine whether the completed source forces the relevant kernel cancellation, with a degree ledger for composition. This addresses a source-specific dependency that geometric sufficient conditions have not settled.

Process assessment. The claim-index check identified the pure-column case as already solved, and using one goal-sufficient restriction kept the new proof bounded; no further framework change was needed.

13 September 2026 — The actual MP pair coefficient carries an antecedent term

Status: exact source-identity refinement and a degree/composition audit, with finite ordinary-polynomial checks. No new PHP lower bound or universal mixed-moment construction is established.

Route obligation. The affine first-band criteria concern completed NS certificates. This cycle checks whether the actual MP-A correction supplies their needed pair relations, including the antecedent contribution. It refines the existing prefix identity, MP identity, and cofactor recurrence; those identities themselves are not new results.

1. Exact diagonal coefficients of the source prefixes

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) with nonzero affine old inputs \(a,g_1,\ldots,g_m\), common accuracy \(h\ge1\), and distinct fresh coefficient blocks. Let \(B\) have inputs \(g_i\), coefficient variables \(s_{v,i}\), product \(b\), and prefixes \(V_i\). Let \(U\) have inputs \(f_0=a,f_i=g_i\), coefficient variables \(r_{v,j}\), product \(c\), and prefixes \(U_j\). In particular,

\[ U_i=\sum_{v=1}^h r_{v,i} \prod_{w<v}\left(1-\sum_jr_{w,j}f_j\right), \qquad V_i\text{ is the corresponding prefix for }B. \]

Use the historical diagonal coefficient operators, setting all other fresh variables to zero. They satisfy the following exact ordinary-old-polynomial identities:

\[ T_{U,j}(U_i)=\delta_{ij}f_j^{h-1},\qquad T_{B,k}(V_i)=\delta_{ik}g_k^{h-1},\qquad T_{B,k}(b)=g_k^h,\quad T_{U,j}(c)=f_j^h. \tag{MP-diagonals} \]

Proof. Only the last prefix summand, \(v=h\), can contain all \(h\) selected factor rows. Its last variable must have index \(i=j\), and the earlier factors supply \(f_j^{h-1}\). The product formulas follow by selecting the nonconstant term in every row. Signs disappear over \(\mathbb F_2\). No old-variable Boolean reduction is used here, including at \(h=1\), where the zero-th power is one.

2. The local correction is not an old-target pair kernel by itself

Write the actual local identity as

\[ b=c+qa+R,\qquad q=bU_0,\qquad R=\sum_{i=1}^m U_iE_{B,i}+\sum_{i=1}^m V_iE_{U,i}. \]

The omitted coefficient of \(E_{U,0}=ac\) is zero in this local correction; the companion remains in the complete family. Apply the joint operator \(T_{U,j;B,k}\). Then

\[ T_{U,j;B,k}(R)=T_{U,j;B,k}(qa) =\begin{cases}a^hg_k^h,&j=0,\\0,&j\ge1,\end{cases} \qquad T_{U,j;B,k}(b-c)=0. \tag{MP-mixed-residual} \]

Proof. For \(j\ge1\), the first correction sum contributes \(g_j^hg_k^h\), and the second contributes the same polynomial, so they cancel. At \(j=0\), the first sum contributes nothing; the second contributes \(a^hg_k^h\). Also the fresh blocks of \(b\) and \(U_0\) are disjoint, so \(T_{U,j;B,k}(bU_0a)=g_k^h\delta_{j0}a^{h-1}a\). The two product targets each use only one block, proving their zero joint coefficient.

The cofactor arrays of the companion correction alone are

\[ A_0=0,\qquad A_j=g_j^h\ (j\ge1),\qquad B_k=g_k^h. \]

They Boolean-reduce to affine arrays \(A_0=0,A_j=g_j,B_k=g_k\). At the local ceiling \(D=4h\), their coefficient multipliers have degree \(h-1\), fitting the first-band parameter \(u=h\). But their reduced pair relation at the antecedent coordinate is \(A_0g_k+B_ka=ag_k\), not automatically zero in the old bounded NS quotient. The term \(qa\) supplies exactly the missing contribution. In particular a local correction with affine-reducing arrays is not by itself the completed old-target certificate required by the certificate-specific transfer.

This is compatible with the earlier boundary-elimination theorem, which explicitly requires both full premise proofs. It is an extraction-level explanation of that dependency, not a correction to the earlier theorem.

3. Inserting the antecedent proof can leave the first band

In this affine setup the ordinary prefix and product degrees give

\[ \deg b=\deg c=2h,\qquad \deg U_0=2h-1,\qquad \deg q=4h-1,\qquad \deg(qa)=4h. \]

Every displayed local companion multiple has degree at most \((2h-1)+(2h+1)=4h\). These bounds precede all field reductions. The degree of \(q\) is exact for the stated nonzero affine inputs: the fresh factor rows give nonzero highest homogeneous terms, and multiplication in the ordinary polynomial ring adds degrees.

Suppose the supplied antecedent certificate is \(a=\sum_F A_FF\), of NS degree \(d_a\). The existing recurrence inserts \(qA_F\) into the completed cofactor of \(F\). Every nonzero such term has degree

\[ \deg(qA_FF)=4h-1+\deg(A_FF). \tag{MP-antecedent-ledger} \]

Thus the displayed antecedent certificate, multiplied before any cross-contribution collection, has ceiling \(4h-1+d_a\). It fits \(D=4h\) only when \(d_a\le1\), unless a different certificate or actual cofactor cancellations improve the ledger. A nonzero earlier companion term already has \(\deg(A_FF)\ge2h+1\) when its accuracy and affine degree are the same, giving at least \(6h\).

These are statements about the supplied construction, not lower bounds on all NS proofs or on the degree after arbitrary global cancellation. The implication premise and other path contributions may use the same axiom, so the final coefficient \(C_F+qA_F+W_F\) must be examined before claiming any unavoidable support. Conversely, cancellation cannot be assumed merely because the local MP identity has degree \(4h\).

PC keeps a different ledger. Once \(a\) has an augmented PC proof through \(d_a\), final-line reuse derives \(qa\) through \(\max\{d_a,4h\}\). This is the already recorded NS/PC distinction. It does not let an ordinary joint NS design annihilate an arbitrary augmented PC derivation, nor does it make a completed NS cofactor fit the first band.

For a concrete old antecedent certificate, take additional old variables \(z,w\) and \(F_1=a+zw,F_2=zw\). Then \(a=F_1+F_2\) has degree two. The two displayed terms \(qF_1,qF_2\) each have degree \(4h+1\), although their sum is the final polynomial \(qa\) of degree \(4h\). This finite ledger control is not an assertion about minimum certificate degree for a completed source proof.

4. A third complete block can enter an antecedent contribution

Let a distinct fresh block \(C\) have one old affine input \(z\), accuracy \(h\), and companion \(E_C=z\prod_v(1-t_vz)\). A prospective antecedent-certificate term \(qE_C\) has ordinary degree \(6h\). Its selected three-block coefficient is

\[ T_{U,0;B,k;C,0}(qE_C) =a^{h-1}g_k^h z^{h+1}. \tag{MP-third-support} \]

This follows by separate extraction in the three disjoint blocks, and is nonzero for nonzero old affine inputs in the ordinary ring. It gives a concrete possible complete-support pattern after antecedent multiplication. It does not assert that this term occurs essentially in an actual completed PHP certificate, or that its mixed coefficient survives collection. The first-band construction sets higher components to zero because of a cofactor-degree restriction; that justification does not extend to this term.

5. Exact checks and actual progress

The targeted checker uses coordinate inputs at \(h=1,2,3\), and affine inputs with offsets at \(h=1,2\). All \(300\) diagonal equations pass. In each case two antecedent-coordinate omission controls are nonzero, for ten controls in total. The displayed local, degree-two-antecedent, and third-companion degrees are respectively \((4,5,6)\), \((8,9,12)\), and \((12,13,18)\) at the three accuracies. The offset fixtures give the same first two triples.

The reproduction record describes the full ordinary-polynomial output, including the prefixes, products, companions, extracted arrays, premise terms, and three-block controls. Arithmetic is exact over \(\mathbb F_2\). These are local identity and degree checks, not PHP refutations, full source certificates, or lower bounds on minimum NS degree.

What changed in the route. The local prefix arrays do have the affine reductions hoped for, but their antecedent coordinate is balanced by a premise contribution, and ordinary NS composition can introduce larger degree and support. Therefore the new first-band theorems still lack an application to the completed source endpoint. The source-specific task is to control the collected premise/path contributions at their actual degree, or construct the required higher mixed components. More geometry within the first band alone does not discharge that obligation.

Proposed next step. Use the exact path-product representation to determine which complete-block supports remain in collected source coefficients, with sharing and scope conventions explicit. Seek a restriction that supports a valid transfer at the actual source degree; do not infer it from a local prefix or a generic formula-depth bound.

Process assessment. The existing MP identities and sparse-polynomial checker were reused, and the new run tested only the missing extraction and composition claims; no framework change was needed.

13 September 2026 — The affine MP boundary is removable in the theorem simulation

Status: proved scope audit and correction of a proposed source application. The earlier conditional algebraic theorems and finite examples remain valid; their application to the hard retained source family has not been established.

Question and change of direction. This cycle began by checking collected source path supports and their sharing conventions. The selected direct NS endpoint is an assumption-free theorem simulation. That hypothesis exposes an earlier issue: the original level-one affine MP boundary pattern considered in recent cycles is already semantically constant and removable. This scope check takes priority over refining its path coefficients.

1. A binary theorem with no OR gates has zero affine approximation

In the audited source convention, TRUE is represented by zero. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), negation and MOD gates are affine operations, and without an OR gate the approximation introduces no ENS coefficients and computes the exact Boolean value. Thus an original structural-level-zero formula has an affine polynomial in the original Boolean variables.

If such a formula is a theorem, its polynomial is zero on every Boolean assignment. It is therefore the zero ordinary affine polynomial: evaluation at zero determines the constant coefficient, and evaluation at the coordinate vectors determines each linear coefficient. In particular a level-zero antecedent line in an assumption-free proof has \(a=0\), not an arbitrary nonzero affine polynomial.

This uses binary exactness and theorem validity on the entire Boolean cube. It does not apply to a derivation with assumptions, to higher original ENS levels, or merely because a later polynomial happens to become affine after a substitution.

2. Constant original level-one OR formulas have scalar cleanup

Let an original level-one OR cluster have affine inputs \(g_i\), the complements of the approximations of its maximal non-OR children. These children have original structural level zero, so their values are exact. The OR is true on an old Boolean assignment exactly when some \(g_i\) is one.

Scope corollary of the existing unit-span cleanup. If the OR formula is a tautology, then

\[ 1\in\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_2}\{g_i\}. \tag{THEOREM-unit-span} \]

Proof. Otherwise choose a linear functional on \(\operatorname{span}\{1,g_i\}\) taking value one on the constant and zero on every input, and extend it to the affine polynomial space. Set each old variable to its functional value. Since the field is \(\mathbb F_2\), this is a Boolean assignment, and evaluation agrees with the functional on every affine polynomial. All inputs vanish there, contradicting the tautology.

Thus some constant coefficient vector \(\beta\) satisfies \(\sum_i\beta_i g_i=1\) as an ordinary polynomial identity. Put \(\beta\) in the first ENS coefficient row and zero in the remaining rows. The product and every companion vanish identically, and all fresh field images vanish. This preserves any supplied NS or PC ceiling and every original cofactor budget.

If the OR formula is instead identically false, every affine input is zero on the Boolean cube and hence is the zero polynomial. Its product is identically one and its companions are already zero. Therefore a proved formula with leading negations and an original level-one OR boundary is also covered: even parity of leading negations gives the unit-span case, and odd parity gives the all-zero-input case.

The argument applies to every copy of a semantically constant original level-one OR formula, including a proper occurrence of the same formula. Its level-zero inputs have no copy-specific ENS variables. Scalar assignments can be made simultaneously and all later inputs can be specialized, with no family-count degree cost. Such identities survive the final affine PHP boundary substitution.

For example, \((u,v,1+u+v)\) has the unit certificate given by summing all three inputs; no complementary pair is required. In contrast \((u,v)\) has the common zero \(u=v=0\), so it is not a tautological OR tuple and has no constant unit certificate.

3. Scope correction for the recent MP applications

In an actual literal implication \(\neg\varphi\vee\psi\) at original structural level one, the antecedent \(\varphi\) has level zero: its occurrence is under the new outer OR, and negation does not increase the structural level. In the assumption-free theorem proof, Section 1 gives \(a=0\). The implication itself is a theorem, so Section 2 removes its level-one OR block. If \(\psi\) begins directly with OR at that level, its theorem boundary is likewise removable.

Consequently the recent independent-affine-antecedent theorem is a valid conditional algebraic statement, but its nonzero independent antecedent hypothesis is not realized by these original level-one MP boundaries in the selected direct theorem simulation. Its suggested source application is vacuous for that subclass. The mixed coefficient identity is also correct for its stated formal inputs; the nonzero affine-antecedent examples must not be described as essential instances of those theorem boundaries.

This is not a retraction of the faithful-pair theorem, the coefficient-space criteria, the shared-support restriction theorem, or their exact finite applications. They remain potential tools for other retained objects. What is withdrawn is the inference that covering this particular MP pattern advances coverage of the hard original level-one theorem boundaries.

The scope agrees with the earlier nonboundary source reduction and highest-OR-level support theorem, whose precise endpoint and leaf hypotheses must be retained. The latter results concern their constructed PC/signed simulations; they are not silently imported as NS conversions. The scalar cleanup proved here applies directly to either NS or PC because its polynomial substitution is degree-preserving.

4. The retained level-one objects are proper subspace indicators

A nonconstant proper original level-one OR subformula need not be a theorem. Its affine common-zero set

\[ Z_G=\{x:g_i(x)=0\text{ for every }i\} \]

is a nonempty proper affine subspace, after zero/unit cleanup. With the source's TRUE-by-zero convention, its exact Boolean value is the indicator of \(Z_G\). Its ENS product is the algebraic approximation of that value, not automatically the same polynomial function on arbitrary coefficient assignments. It does not prove that these particular blocks must survive every normalization of a completed PHP proof; equal-span batching may handle them. The line-scoped NS simulation permits independent copies but explicitly adds their comparison certificates. 13 September 2026 — A retained proper OR comparison has a genuine NS degree-six boundary

Status: source-support refinement using existing reductions, exact proper-OR cofactor formulas, and a computer-assisted local degree theorem. No global PHP lower bound follows.

Route obligation. Following the preceding scope correction, this cycle targets proper original level-one OR blocks that survive the stated binary scalar, span-sharing, and rank-packing passes. 1. Binary Booleanity need not use companions

The existing binary Booleanity argument applies to every current polynomial \(P\), since all original and coefficient variables have Boolean domains:

\[ P^2-P\in\mathcal I_{2\deg P}({\rm BOOL}). \]

Frobenius cancels cross terms, and ordinary monomial Boolean reduction supplies the certificate without increasing degree. For an unmodified affine-input OR product, \(\deg P=2h\), so this uses degree \(4h\), matching the existing prefix/companion Booleanity ceiling. The same comparison uses \(2h(\delta+1)\) for a general nonzero input-degree ceiling \(\delta\).

Source-support consequence. In the binary direct NS construction, replace an OR-Booleanity module \(P^2-P=-\sum_iU_iE_i\) by its domain-only certificate. Multiplying either module by its source context preserves the same degree budget. Thus companion contributions arising solely from Booleanity can be omitted without increasing the supplied NS ceiling. This is a new use of the recorded domain argument, not a new Booleanity theorem. It does not remove companions used for value or comparison statements.

For compact source circuits the existing Frobenius witness construction also uses only domains: \(\Phi(A+B)=\Phi(A)+\Phi(B)\) and \(\Phi(AB)=B^2\Phi(A)+A\Phi(B)\), where \(\Phi(T)=T^2-T\). Its structural degree bounds fit the source majorants. Ordinary Boolean division gives the sharper actual-degree existence statement above; a cancellation in an arbitrary circuit is not by itself a bound on its formal degree.

2. Use the existing affine normal form on the NS endpoint

For original level-one affine inputs, the merge-first and binary packing operations have direct original-axiom image certificates, so their affine specializations preserve an already supplied NS certificate as well as PC. Here are the relevant budgets, keeping the selected NS endpoint explicit.

Equal-span sharing. For a common affine basis \(F\), write each tuple as \(G_b=L_bF\). Choose a constant matrix \(M_b\) with \(L_b^{\mathsf T}M_b=I\), and send its coefficient vector in each row to \(M_bS\), using common canonical coefficients \(S\). All nonzero affine companions retain their ceiling \(2h+1\); field images fit degree two. The whole map is affine, including when applied to later inputs. This is the affine special case of the existing quotient operation, not elimination of the canonical block.

For a span of rank \(r\le2h\) excluding one, pack at most two basis elements per coefficient row. For a pair \(F_s,F_t\), coefficients \(1,1-F_s\) make that factor exactly \((1-F_s)(1-F_t)\); an unpaired element uses coefficient one. Empty rows contribute one. The resulting product is \(H=\prod_{j=1}^r(1-F_j)\). If \(g_i=\sum_j a_{ij}F_j\), then

\[ g_iH=-\sum_j a_{ij}(F_j^2-F_j) \prod_{k\ne j}(1-F_k). \]

Each affine \(F_j\) has its domain proof through two, so the companion image costs at most \(r+1\le2h+1\). The coefficient images are affine and their field proofs cost two. Constant input-span changes return the assignment to the original tuple. This verifies the original-degree NS image bound; the zero and unit-span cases retain scalar cleanup.

After these selected passes, the remaining original level-one spans are distinct, exclude one, and have rank \(r>2h\). They correspond to nonempty proper affine zero spaces. Because a consistent affine zero set determines its affine vanishing span, equal-flat level-one copies can use the same canonical product. Their equality target is then identically zero, so the source can omit that entire known comparison module, including its contextual multiples. This does not assert that arbitrary input differences vanish or that all comparison contributions disappear.

Other PHP-specific normalizers or restrictions may remove more blocks. The statement describes the passes just specified, not essential survival under every possible transformation. Later inputs are always the actual specialized polynomials; they are not renumbered and declared affine.

The source's OR comparison is an already proved identity, not a new formula. Take disjoint index sets \(I_1,I_2\), \(I_0=I_1\cup I_2\), affine inputs \(f_i\), and independent coefficient blocks with products \(P_0,P_1,P_2\), prefixes \(U_i^b\), and companions \(E_{b,i}=f_iP_b\). \[ \begin{aligned} P_0-P_1P_2={}&\sum_{i\in I_1}U_i^1E_{0,i} +\sum_{k\in I_2}P_1U_k^2E_{0,k}\\ &-\sum_{i\in I_1}P_2U_i^0E_{1,i} -\sum_{k\in I_2}P_1U_k^0E_{2,k}. \end{aligned} \tag{PROPER-union} \]

It expresses intersection of the affine zero spaces: the exact Boolean indicator for the combined input span is the product of the two child indicators. Unlike equal-flat comparison, the three spans can be distinct and all three formulas nonconstant.

\[ T_{0,i;2,k}(-P_2U_i^0)=f_i^{h-1}f_k^h, \qquad T_{0,i;1,i;2,k}(-P_2U_i^0E_{1,i})=f_i^{2h}f_k^h. \tag{PROPER-support} \]

The cofactor has degree \(4h-1\), the original companion has degree \(2h+1\), and the term has degree \(6h\). The cofactor contains two complete foreign blocks. For independent nonconstant affine inputs the displayed extracted polynomials are nonzero, and the second remains nonzero after old Boolean reduction.

Then \(P_0=1,P_1=0,P_2=1\), while every variable is Boolean. The comparison has value one, so it is outside the full domain ideal. Companions or another justified transformation are required.

Its cost counts all deleted vertices, including union vertices.

\[ \left\lceil\frac{2m}{3}\right\rceil. \]

13 September 2026 — An exact weighted selector representation for the binary source

Status: working ordinary-degree embedding over every field and a binary modular NS source construction with an old-target endpoint. Global elimination of the resulting relations remains open.

Route obligation. The preceding wide-family example concerns a selector-valued target. This cycle returns to the old target one: it identifies an exact degree ledger for selector expressions and constructs the binary source proof with selector-valued external multipliers. Individual ENS coefficients remain inside explicitly supplied local witness certificates.

1. Substituting genuine selector products reflects ordinary degree exactly

Let \(K\) be any field. Start with old variables \(X\), and introduce formal variables \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) in an order compatible with the block dependencies. Block \(b\) has positive accuracy \(h_b\) and formal input polynomials \(\widehat g_{b,i}(X,Z_{

\[ \Phi(Z_b)=P_b=\prod_{u=1}^{h_b} \left(1-\sum_i r_{b,u,i}\Phi(\widehat g_{b,i})\right), \qquad \Phi(X)=X. \]

Give old variables weight one. Having assigned the earlier weights, put

\[ \delta_b=\max_i\deg_w\widehat g_{b,i},\qquad w_b=h_b(\delta_b+1),\qquad \deg_w Z_b=w_b. \tag{SEL-weights} \]

All degrees here are ordinary collected polynomial degrees, with no field or Boolean reduction. Zero input polynomials are ignored in the maximum.

Working theorem. For every nonzero formal polynomial \(F(X,Z)\),

\[ \deg\Phi(F)=\deg_w F. \tag{SEL-reflection} \]

In particular \(\Phi\) is injective, every nonzero formal input stays nonzero, and the weights are the actual degrees of the genuine products.

Proof. Induct on the number of selectors. The old-variable case is immediate. For the new block write \(F=\sum_jF_jZ_b^j\), and let \(D=\max_j(\deg_wF_j+jw_b)\). The substitution upper bound gives \(\deg\Phi(F)\le D\).

Choose \(k\) attaining this maximum, and an input \(g_*=\Phi(\widehat g_{b,i_*})\) of degree \(\delta_b\), using the induction hypothesis. Set other coordinates of the new coefficient block to zero and write \(\rho_u=r_{b,u,i_*}\). The ordinary coefficient of \(\rho_1^k\cdots\rho_{h_b}^k\) is

\[ \sum_{j\ge k}\binom jk^{h_b}(-g_*)^{h_bk}\Phi(F_j). \]

This extraction does not reduce fresh powers and is different from the earlier Boolean-diagonal operator. The \(j=k\) summand is nonzero and has old-variable degree

\[ \deg_wF_k+h_bk\delta_b=D-h_bk. \]

For \(j>k\), its degree is at most

\[ D-jw_b+h_bk\delta_b =D-h_bk-(j-k)w_b<D-h_bk. \]

Thus the leading old part of the \(j=k\) summand cannot cancel, regardless of binomial coefficients vanishing in \(K\). Restoring the fresh monomial adds degree \(h_bk\), so the image has degree at least \(D\). This proves equality and injectivity. The argument also covers \(k=0\), nonlinear earlier inputs, unequal accuracies, and constant nonzero inputs. All-zero tuples are excluded because their product is constant.

2. The field quotient and raw coefficients require separate treatment

The theorem is not an embedding of Boolean or field quotients. For \(G=(x,y)\), let \(Z\) name its product and set \(\chi=(1-x)(1-y)\). The nonzero formal polynomial

\[ \chi(Z-1) \]

is nonzero at the formal domain point \(x=y=Z=0\), but its concrete image vanishes after old Boolean reduction: where \(\chi=1\), both inputs are zero and the genuine product is one. Similarly \(Z^p-Z\) has a nonzero ordinary image of degree \(p\,w_Z\), although that image vanishes on the concrete field domain. No identification of formal and concrete bounded domain ideals follows from (SEL-reflection).

Distinct formal selectors must represent distinct genuine blocks with disjoint own coefficients. If two products are assigned the same coefficient family, \(Z_1-Z_2\) can map to zero. A removed constant product must likewise be replaced by its known expression rather than retained as a free formal variable.

Nor is every concrete cofactor in the selector subring. When all retained selector weights exceed one, a fresh coefficient variable has degree one and cannot be \(\Phi(F)\): reflection would force \(\deg_wF=1\), so \(F\) could use only the old variables. At accuracy one a source prefix can be exactly such a coefficient. This is why the next construction changes the source composition instead of assuming an arbitrary collected NS coefficient has a selector expression.

3. The exact binary source expressions at the chosen stage

Use the coherent, genuine direct theorem construction, with one value for each chosen formula representation and all required OR subgroup products. Before optional polynomial normalization, binary negation and MOD evaluation are affine operations on child values, while an OR contributes one named product. Therefore every value and every original block input has an affine formal expression in old variables and the appropriate selectors. Block inputs use only strictly earlier selectors; same-level OR brackets are bypassed.

This is the binary specialization of the structural argument behind the recorded selector-dependency claim, applied here explicitly to the direct NS constructor. It is not an inference from the earlier PC endpoint alone.

Apply only the standard affine PHP boundary/clause map and any needed constant-product cleanup. Deleted products become \(1\), \(1-\rho_i\), \(x_{aj}x_{a'j}\), or constants. Replace their formal variables by those polynomials. At this stage every remaining value and input has the literal form

\[ q(X)+\sum_b\alpha_bZ_b,\qquad \deg q\le2,\quad \alpha_b\in\mathbb F_2, \tag{SEL-binary-profile} \]

with only earlier \(Z_b\)'s in an input. Retained own coefficient blocks remain fresh and their products genuine, so (SEL-reflection) applies with their actual new weights. The profile is stage-specific: optional packing can replace a selector by a product of earlier expressions and destroy the affine-in-selector assertion. A further normalization requires its own representation and degree audit.

4. Genuine OR interfaces have selector-valued NS targets

Before the boundary map, let \(L\ge1\) bound all source values and the required OR subgroup values. For a binary OR interface with actual values \(a,b,c\), the relation

\[ R=c-ab \]

has an NS witness through \(3L\). This is an ordinary-NS statement, proved directly from the source prefix comparison; it does not import the earlier PC reuse bound as an NS claim.

Degree proof. For three genuine products of degrees \(s_0,s_1,s_2\), the prefix of block \(b\) has degree at most \(s_b-\delta_b\). Each term of the union certificate therefore fits \(s_0+s_1+s_2\le3L\). For a non-OR child value \(a\), use the algebraic singleton data \(g=1-a,P=a,U=1\). Its companion \(a(1-a)\) has the domain-only NS witness through \(2\deg a\). Inserting that witness into the same identity preserves the bound \(s_0+\deg a+s_2\). This adds no artificial unary OR occurrence. Constant and empty cases reduce directly.

All three values have formal selector expressions, so the witness target is \(\widehat R=\widehat c-\widehat a\,\widehat b\). Its proof may use individual coefficients, but its target does not. Booleanity modules \(B_v=v^2-v\) similarly have selector-valued targets and binary domain-only witnesses through \(2\deg v\le2L\).

For MP, apply the OR interface to the implication and write

\[ R_{\rm MP}=c-(1-a)b,\qquad b=c+ab-R_{\rm MP}. \tag{SEL-MP} \]

The external antecedent multiplier is \(b\), of degree at most \(L\). Prefixes are confined to the supplied witness for \(R_{\rm MP}\). This differs from the original flattened MP coefficient \(bU_0\); it is a new modular source construction, not a claim that the old coefficient was selector-valued.

5. A binary source derivation with selector-valued outer coefficients

Let the balanced assumption-free \(F(\mathrm{MOD}_2)\) proof have height \(H_\pi\). Let \(M_{\rm fr}\) be the maximum leaf-occurrence count of its fixed Boolean axiom frames, counting repeated and constant leaves, and put

\[ C=\max\{M_{\rm fr}+2,12\}. \]

Choose coherent values and any required OR subgroup blocks, of polynomial total inventory and without increasing the maximum structural level. The usual source bound can be used for \(L\), enlarged to cover all these values and MOD prefix sums; for fixed depth it has the form \((\ell'+1)h^{\ell'}\).

Working source theorem. The theorem value has a formal identity

\[ \widehat\tau=\sum_\alpha Q_\alpha\,H_\alpha, \qquad \deg_wQ_\alpha+\nu_\alpha \le (C+H_\pi)L, \tag{SEL-source} \]

where \(H_\alpha\) are the chosen OR-interface and Booleanity targets, and \(\nu_\alpha\le3L\) or \(2L\) is their supplied concrete NS witness ceiling. Every \(Q_\alpha\) is a polynomial in old variables and selectors. Expanding the local witnesses gives an ordinary NS source derivation with the same bound. Polynomially many factored coefficient expressions suffice; no monomial-count bound is asserted.

Boolean axiom leaves, using NS accounting. Evaluate a fixed Boolean frame formally with negation \(1-z\) and OR multiplication. If node \(t\) has \(m_t\) leaf occurrences, its formal polynomial \(F_t\) has degree at most \(m_t\). Using the actual value \(a_t\), expand

\[ a_t-F_u(b)F_v(b) =(a_t-a_ua_v)+(a_u-F_u(b))a_v +F_u(b)(a_v-F_v(b)). \]

This is the earlier frame expansion, but multiply the entire child NS certificates. Inductively a child difference costs at most \((m_u+2)L\); its multiplier \(a_v\) costs at most \(L\), while the other multiplier \(F_u(b)\) costs at most \(m_uL\). Since both child leaf counts are at least one, all terms fit \((m_t+2)L\), including the \(3L\) local gate witness. Negation adds no cost. At the root, the formal tautology polynomial has its degree-\(m\) Boolean-domain certificate; substituting the representative values and their \(2L\) Booleanity witnesses costs at most \(mL\). Thus the actual axiom value costs \((m+2)L\), and all external multipliers remain selector polynomials.

MOD leaves. The recorded recursion has a ten-leaf outer Boolean frame. In characteristic two its MOD values are affine polynomials in the last argument value \(a\) and the common prefix sum \(t\); the interpolation relation is literal. The resulting frame polynomial in \(a,t\) has degree at most ten and vanishes on their Boolean domain. Formal Boolean division and substitution cost at most \(10L\), while the NS frame-comparison calculation costs \(12L\). The empty cases have value zero. This proves the claimed uniform leaf ceiling without a MOD-arity charge and without using a PC-only proof as an NS certificate.

MP composition. In (SEL-MP), multiply the antecedent's complete modular NS certificate by the known selector-valued \(b\). If the premise ceilings are \(d_a,d_c\), the new ceiling is

\[ d_b\le\max\{d_c,d_a+L,3L\}. \]

Induction on the balanced tree gives (SEL-source). All leaf and gate expressions are polynomials in selector-valued actual nodes. Unrolling follows at most \(H_\pi\) antecedent edges, with external factors \(b\), so the factored representation remains polynomial in the source inventory. Coherence is an explicit choice; independently scoped copies require their actual comparison modules and witness ceilings.

The original direct MP expression can also be sharpened to \(\deg(bU_0)\le2L\) for a genuine nonconstant implication product. Thus the point of the new construction is the selector-valued external interface, together with its stated recurrence; it is not a claimed factor-\(h\) improvement over every sharper analysis of the old source.

6. The old PHP target and the remaining elimination problem

Apply the standard global affine boundary/clause substitution to the constructed source proof. Its target becomes one, and each original axiom image has the original-degree NS image certificate. Re-express each removed selector by its known old polynomial, and name only the remaining genuine products. The diagram between formal substitution and concrete substitution commutes. Reflection therefore gives the exact degree of every surviving formal coefficient and target.

The resulting ordinary formal identity is

\[ 1=\sum_\alpha \widetilde Q_\alpha\,\widetilde H_\alpha, \qquad \deg_{\widetilde w}\widetilde Q_\alpha+\nu_\alpha \le (C+H_\pi)L. \tag{SEL-old-target} \]

Each \(\Phi(\widetilde H_\alpha)\) has the supplied NS witness from the exact weak PHP base, retained ENS companions, and domains, through the carried ceiling \(\nu_\alpha\). Here \(L\) and those witness ceilings are inherited from the pre-substitution construction. They are not silently reset to the smaller degree of a specialized target. At the specified stage, relation targets have selector degree at most two and old-variable degree at most four, by (SEL-binary-profile). Optional packing can change that profile.

Exact module interface. More generally, if formal relations \(H_\alpha\) have concrete NS witnesses through \(\nu_\alpha\), then an identity \(t=\sum Q_\alpha H_\alpha\) satisfying \(\deg_wQ_\alpha+\nu_\alpha\le D\) gives a concrete degree-\(D\) NS derivation of \(\Phi(t)\). Conversely a concrete identity already presented with such selector-valued outer factors lifts to the formal identity by injectivity. This is not a statement about arbitrary NS coefficients or a projection of the entire concrete field ideal.

Witness ceiling and polynomial degree are different data. For example the preceding OR-union relation at \(h=1\) has formal weighted degree four but minimum concrete NS witness degree six in its Boolean-domain presentation. Treating it as a supplied degree-four witness would lose that distinction.

The old-target source interface is now proved in the binary case, with polynomially many relations and polylogarithmic weighted degree under the usual hypothetical small-Frege-proof parameters. The remaining theorem would transfer (SEL-old-target) to a forbidden base PC refutation with a suitable degree bound. Neither the injective ordinary substitution nor the source compilation establishes that elimination theorem. The degree embedding is field-general; the source compiler and affine-in-selector profile stated here are binary.

7. Exact checks and process assessment

The degree checker uses three genuine selectors, including nonlinear old inputs and a later input depending polynomially on earlier selectors. Four cases over \(\mathbb F_2,\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\), with two accuracy choices in the binary case, verify all \(28\) ordinary weighted-degree equalities. The field, zero-fiber, shared-coefficient, constant-product, and bare-coefficient controls behave as described in Section 2. Their full formal polynomials and concrete images are saved.

Separate binary gate tests use child ranks \(2h+1\), with a parent input containing a genuine earlier selector. They verify complete NS witnesses, including the domain-only antecedent Booleanity coefficients:

These are proper gate-interface tests, not claims that the nonconstant child is a proved original level-one theorem. The witness ceilings are upper bounds for the displayed certificates, not minimum-degree assertions. The reproduction record explains the complete degree/control output and NS gate certificates. All checks passed in compiled exact arithmetic; no full PHP proof or global eliminator was computed.
