13 September 2026 — Independent targets after conditioning the compact bit base

Status: working quotient-injection and dimension proofs, exact Boolean multiplication and coefficient-dual checks, and an explicit old-relation control; no second source-level elimination.

Question and stopping point. The highest-risk obligation is removal of the remaining nonlinear source family. The previous turn added \(1-f\) to remove the affine bottom level, but nonzero Boolean factors can have zero product. This turn asks whether that conditioning leaves a large space of separated targets. Stop at a degree-controlled dimension bound or a product obstruction; dimension alone is not a nonlinear membership certificate.

1. Bounded degree within each pigeon row gives a larger injective space

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\), with \(n=2^\ell,\ \ell\ge2\), \(m=n+1\), and the compact transported class \(\mathcal J\). For \(1\le a\le\ell,\ K\ge1\), let \(\mathcal A_{a,K}\) span squarefree bit monomials of total degree at most \(K\) and degree at most \(a\) in each row.

\[ \boxed{4^a(K-1)<n\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal A_{a,K}\cap\mathcal J_K=\{0\}.} \tag{CQ-row-degree} \]

This extends row-linear injection, the case \(a=1\). Degree zero is immediate as well. The constant \(4^a\) is sufficient, with no optimality claim.

Proof. For \(u\in\mathcal A_{a,K}\cap\mathcal J_K\), write \(u=c+\sum_{S\ne\varnothing}F_S\) by exact occupied row set. Let \(s\le K\) be the largest occupied row count. The matching-normal-form argument reduces \(\tau u\) to degree at most \(s\) with an NS certificate through \(K\). Our hypothesis implies \(n\ge2K-1\), so functional-base stability drops membership to \(\mathcal I_s\). The coefficient on a top row set \(S\) satisfies

\[ F_S((z_i)_{i\in S}) =\sum_{i\in S}\psi_i((z_j)_{j\in S\setminus\{i\}}) \qquad\text{on pairwise distinct labels.} \]

Each unrestricted function on the right omits one row. This follows from original degree-\(s\) row-equation cofactors after matching reduction, not from the unrestricted ideal.

If \(F_S\ne0\), choose a monomial of maximum total degree, with nonempty axis sets \(T_i\) of sizes \(d_i\le a\). Greedily choose translates of these coordinate subspaces. Previously chosen cubes contain at most \((s-1)2^a\) points, whereas the next direction has \(n/2^{d_i}\) cosets. Since

\[ (s-1)2^a\le(K-1)2^a<n/2^a\le n/2^{d_i}, \]

and each occupied point forbids at most one coset, disjoint cubes exist. Sum the coefficient identity over their product, which consists entirely of legal matching tuples. Missing-row terms occur evenly and vanish. The mixed finite difference on the left kills every monomial missing a selected axis; maximal total degree leaves only the chosen monomial, with sum one. This contradiction eliminates every nonzero top row set. The remaining constant is zero by old stability, proving the claim.

2. The conditioned kernel on row-linear targets is Boolean annihilation

Let \(f\in\mathcal L_d\) be nonzero of actual degree \(d\), and \(t\ge0\). Assume \(d+t\ge1\) and

\[ 16(d+t-1)<n. \tag{CQ-product-range} \]

Write \({\rm ml}(u)\) for the squarefree Boolean representative. For \(g\in\mathcal L_t\), the product representative \({\rm ml}(fg)\) has degree at most \(d+t\) and row degree at most two. Boolean division certifies \(fg-{\rm ml}(fg)\) through \(d+t\). Applying the preceding injection with \(a=2\),

\[ \boxed{g\in\mathcal J_t^f \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad{\rm ml}(fg)=0.} \tag{CQ-exact-kernel} \]

The Boolean difference lies in \(\mathcal J_{d+t}\), so membership of \(fg\) equals that of its representative, and a nonzero representative cannot belong. For \(t\le B,\ B+d\le n/2\), conditioned stability replaces \(\mathcal J_t^f\) by \(\mathcal J_B^f\) in this equivalence. The same hypotheses ensure \(f\notin\mathcal J_{n/2}\), by injection and original stability. If \(d=t=0\), then \(f=1\) and the result is immediate. Only the kernel on \(\mathcal L_t\) is identified, not the full intrinsic NS or PC quotient.

3. Avoiding one leading monomial's rows retains many targets

Choose a degree-compatible monomial order. The leading monomial \(M_f\) of row-linear \(f\) occupies exactly \(d\) rows \(S_f\). Set

\[ \mathcal V_{f,t}=\operatorname{span}\left\{ \prod_{i\in S}b_{i,t_i}:S\subseteq[m]\setminus S_f,\ |S|\le t \right\}. \]

Boolean multiplication lemma. The map \(g\mapsto{\rm ml}(fg)\) is injective on \(\mathcal V_{f,t}\), without a board-size hypothesis. For nonzero \(g\), the ordinary leading monomial of \(fg\) is \(M_fM_g\). Its factors occupy disjoint rows, so it is squarefree of degree \(d+\deg g\). Boolean reduction of a nonsquarefree term strictly lowers total degree and cannot create or cancel this leading term. Thus the reduced product is nonzero. Distinct basis multipliers equivalently have distinct leading reduced products.

Only the rows of the chosen leading monomial are excluded. Other terms of \(f\) may use multiplier rows and produce Boolean reductions; the proof still applies.

Combining this with the kernel identity, for \(t\le B\), \(B+d\le n/2\), and (CQ-product-range),

\[ \mathcal V_{f,t}\cap\mathcal J_B^f=0,\qquad \boxed{\dim(\mathcal P_{\le t}/\mathcal J_t^f) \ge\sum_{j=0}^{\min(t,m-d)}\binom{m-d}{j}\ell^j.} \tag{CQ-dimension} \]

The same number bounds the image dimension of \(\mathcal L_t\). The subspace is explicit once \(f\) and a monomial order are given; this does not construct the earlier existential common-vanishing \(f\). At \(d,t=O(\sqrt{n\log n})\), the row-degree condition holds for large \(n\). Properness still requires the separately tracked \(B+d\le n/2\).

On \(n=8,\ \ell=3\), take three rows and \(T=E_{12}+E_{13}+E_{23}\). Every nonconstant monomial confined to one row appears in two equalities and cancels. Remaining nonconstant terms use two rows, with degree at most two in either row and total degree at most three. The total degree is three and the constant coefficient is one, so \(T\ne0\). Thus \(T\in\mathcal A_{2,3}\cap\mathcal J_3\), certified through degree three by those three old axioms. Here \(16(3-1)=32\not<8\), although old degree-three stability holds. This refutes omission of all range restrictions, not sharpness of the constant sixteen.

With both parameters of order \(\sqrt{n\log n}\), that ceiling exceeds the linear barrier. 13 September 2026 — Unary affine queries survive as a second-level label subfamily

Status: working source-normalization proof and conditioned-rank control; reuse of earlier unary-family obstructions, not a new general lower bound.

Question and stopping point. The active obligation is the actual remaining nonlinear source family. The previous turn supplied separated conditioned targets but neither nonlinear membership nor a composition theorem. This audit asks which familiar unary queries remain inside the compact source, and whether earlier rank estimates survive conditioning. Stop at a certified reduction or a precise import obstruction.

1. Label blocks and their parity parents survive the relevant preprocessing

Let \(n=2^\ell,\ \ell\ge2\), and define the Boolean label functions

\[ \eta_z(b_i)=\prod_{t=1}^{\ell}(1-b_{it}-z_t), \qquad z\in\mathbb F_2^\ell. \]

A label bottom block has affine inputs \(b_{it}+z_t\). Its rank is \(\ell\), its common zero set is the label \(z\), and its genuine product \(P_{i,z}\) has original degree \(2h\). At \(h\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), the existing pair packing sends \(P_{i,z}\) exactly to \(\eta_z\) using affine coefficient images. It certifies bottom companions through \(\ell+1\le2h+1\) and coefficient Booleanity through two. Every such label block is low in the earlier hybrid partition and its virtual image remains this indicator.

For unary affine tuples

\[ L_{a,s}(X)=c_{a,s}+\sum_{i,z}a_{a,s;i,z}x_{i,z}, \]

make parent inputs \(\widehat g_{a,s}=c_{a,s}+\sum_{i,z}a_{a,s;i,z}P_{i,z}\), with their own fresh parent coefficients and all companions. Nonconstant formal inputs have original degree \(2h\), so their parent companions have original degree \(2h^2+3h\). After bottom packing their inputs are precisely \(\theta L_{a,s}=c_{a,s}+\sum_{i,z}a_{a,s;i,z}\eta_z(b_i)\).

Signed parities of label predicates realize this syntax with two structural OR levels: the literal label test supplies the first, and its parity parent supplies the second; residue or negation choices give the required constants. The description is polynomial for a polynomial unary inventory. Repeated label occurrences can have separate fresh bottom blocks and receive the same packing map; no unsupported sharing assumption is necessary.

The earlier indicator-basis characterization already proves that these are sums of arbitrary functions of individual pigeon labels, not generally affine bit functions. This is its application to the retained compact source stage, not a new characterization.

2. A label indicator decodes to its unary variable through degree \(\ell\)

Use the affine decoder \(\tau(b_{it})=\sum_{z:z_t=1}x_{i,z}\), and the local functional axioms of row \(i\): its row sum, Booleanity, and same-row exclusions. Then

\[ \boxed{\tau(\eta_z)-x_{i,z} \in\mathcal I_\ell(\text{local functional axioms of row }i).} \tag{LABEL-decode} \]

Explicit certificate. Write \(l_t=1-\tau(b_{it})-z_t\), so \(\tau\eta_z=\prod_tl_t\), and let \(q_t=\sum_{w:w_1=z_1,\ldots,w_t=z_t}x_{i,w}\). The first difference \(l_1-q_1\) is zero or \(1-\rho_i\). For \(t\ge2\), \(l_tq_{t-1}-q_t\) is a sum of Booleanity generators and same-row exclusion monomials through degree two: expand the two linear sums, retain the diagonal terms, and cancel their linear parts. This holds for either desired bit value; complementing the literal cancels the extra \(q_{t-1}\) terms. Therefore

\[ \prod_{t=1}^{\ell}l_t-q_\ell =\left(\prod_{t=2}^{\ell}l_t\right)(l_1-q_1) +\sum_{t=2}^{\ell} \left(\prod_{u=t+1}^{\ell}l_u\right) (l_tq_{t-1}-q_t). \]

The first witness costs \(\ell\), and each later one costs \(\ell-t+2\le\ell\). Since \(q_\ell=x_{i,z}\), this proves the claim. In particular, \(\tau\theta L-L\) has an NS certificate through \(\ell\) for every unary affine \(L\). This refines the use of the existing functional-row interpolation to the exact original source budget; it does not interpret weak modular rows as one-hot rows.

3. The two-level label source returns to the unary affine family without degree increase

Working transfer. Consider \(\mathcal Q_n\) with the label bottom blocks and the parent tuples above, at common \(h\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil\). A degree-\(D\) NS or PC refutation of that system gives a degree-\(D\) refutation of \(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}\) with the one-level affine tuples \(L_{a,s}\), their original parent coefficients, complete companions, and fields.

Map and witnesses. Send each old bit to its affine decoder and each label coefficient to its affine packing image, then leave parent coefficients unchanged. This is one global affine variable map. The compact base image certificates fit each original base degree. Bottom companion images cost \(\ell+1\le2h+1\); their coefficient fields cost two.

A parent input becomes \(A_s=\tau\theta L_s\), with \(\deg A_s\le\ell\) and a certificate \(A_s-L_s\) through \(\ell\). Telescope the parent companion from tuple \(A\) to tuple \(L\). The outside input replacement costs at most \(\ell+h(\ell+1)\). Replacing a product row contributes a factor \(r_{u,s}(A_s-L_s)\), the other \(h-1\) factors, and an outside affine input, costing at most \(\ell+2+(h-1)(\ell+1)\). Both fit

\[ C_{\rm parent}=(h+1)\ell+h \le2h^2+3h=e_{\rm parent}^{\rm original}. \tag{LABEL-parent-budget} \]

The image thus equals the canonical affine parent companion modulo old functional axioms through the original source degree. The new companion's own degree is only \(2h+1\); its smaller degree is not used to enlarge the original cofactor space. Apply the affine map to the supplied NS identity or PC proof, then substitute these certified axiom images. Original NS cofactors and PC multiplication steps stay within \(D\).

This is a certified reduction of the displayed subfamily. It does not normalize the other possible sums of flat indicators, does not assert that an arbitrary conditioned system still has the required ranks, and does not manufacture a refutation of the unary family. In the label-only bottom family one may use \(f=1\), so there is no necessary conditioning loss in this particular reduction.

4. The earlier multiscale inventories remain relevant, with their original limitations

Take the existing polynomial multiscale unary inventory. Its proof certifies full rank of residual linear parts modulo row sums, uniformly over the required subboards and pairs of blocks. Altering the constant of each input does not change that event. Set each constant so that its value is zero at the assignment sending every pigeon to label zero.

The corresponding label-parent tuple now has a common zero on the full bit cube. Its nonzero linear part modulo rows also makes every input nonconstant on the product of one-hot row states, by the indicator-basis characterization. Hence the parent OR is nonconstant: it is false at the common-zero assignment and true somewhere else. It is not a constant source object removed by scalar cleanup. The label bottom objects are nonconstant as well.

All residual rank, pair-intersection, and nonconstant-one properties from the original linear-part proof survive these constant changes. The two earlier unary numerical tests therefore retain their recorded failure on the normalized unary family. The degree-preserving source reduction shows why those families remain pertinent inside the compact second level.

This is still a source-syntax and method-scope statement. No Frege proof uses the inventory essentially here, no short augmented refutation is supplied, and the old criteria's failure is not an impossibility theorem for other transformations or for a new nonlinear criterion.

5. Conditioning can halve an actual label-input span

Let \(n=2^\ell\ge8\), choose one pigeon row \(i\) and one bit \(t\), and put \(f=b_{it}\). For any \(\ell\le B\le n/2-1\), consider the \(n\)-dimensional label span \(\mathcal W_i=\operatorname{span}\{\eta_z(b_i):z\in\mathbb F_2^\ell\}\). Then

\[ \dim\bigl(\mathcal W_i/(\mathcal W_i\cap\mathcal J_B)\bigr)=n, \qquad \boxed{\dim\bigl(\mathcal W_i/(\mathcal W_i\cap\mathcal J_B^f)\bigr)=n/2.} \tag{LABEL-conditioned-rank} \]

Proof. Without conditioning, a label combination decodes, through degree \(\ell\), to \(\sum_z a_zx_{i,z}\). Old stability reduces its \(\mathcal I_B\) membership to the affine row-equation span. No nonzero linear combination supported on this one row and having zero constant term is in that span: a nonzero multiple of its row equation has a constant term, and other row equations introduce their own variables. Thus the \(n\) indicators remain independent.

Modulo bit Booleanity, \(f\eta_z=0\) for \(z_t=0\), and \(f\eta_z=\eta_z\) for \(z_t=1\). These reductions have certificates through \(\ell+1\). Membership of \(fg\) is tested in \(\mathcal J_{B+1}\), with \(B+1\le n/2\); the same decoder and affine-stability argument makes the surviving \(n/2\) label indicators independent there. The other half are zero, proving the displayed rank.

This is an input-rank control inside the actual label subfamily. It does not contradict the preceding row-linear target-space theorem, which chooses its candidates differently. It prevents importing unconditioned unary rank hypotheses unchanged merely because the conditioned old base still has a large PC barrier.

13 September 2026 — One degree cost for row-supported multilevel coefficient profiles

Status: working support-dependent NS and PC normalization over every prime, with complete three-level certificates over \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(\mathbb F_3\); unrestricted source coverage remains open.

Question and stopping point. The active obligation is normalization of actual nonlinear source inputs without multiplying the cost once per level. The preceding audit retained wide unary-query parents. This turn tests whether bounded pigeon support permits direct old-variable coefficient choices across a whole dependency-closed package. Stop at a certified support-dependent transfer or a counterexample, and do not infer the support hypothesis from depth or inventory.

1. The functional row-state ideal has certificates through the target degree

Over any \(\mathbb F_p\), let \(U_{\rm row}\) consist of \(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij}\), same-row exclusions \(x_{ij}x_{ik}\) for \(j\ne k\), and \(\rho_i-1\), on \(m\) rows with \(n\ge2\) labels. There are no column collisions in this satisfiable subsystem. Its state space \(\Gamma\) assigns exactly one label to each row. Then

\[ q|_\Gamma=0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in\mathcal I_{\deg q}(U_{\rm row}). \tag{RS-degree-complete} \]

This extends the existing state-algebra reduction to products of functional row states, using the affine row-pivot coordinates. It is a statement about the displayed satisfiable row ideal, not automatic degree completeness of full PHP or a conditioned base.

Proof. First reduce every monomial by Booleanity and same-row exclusions, preserving its original degree. The remainder uses at most one variable from each row. Fix a reference label zero and replace every \(x_{i0}\) by \(1-\sum_{j\ne0}x_{ij}\). A replacement in a degree-\(d\) monomial has a row-equation certificate through \(d\). Since that monomial has no other variable from row \(i\), replacement preserves the one-variable-per-row property.

The final basis consists of products with at most one nonreference variable from each row. The local functions \(1,x_{i1},\ldots,x_{i,n-1}\) are linearly independent on the \(n\) one-hot states. Their tensor products are therefore independent on \(\Gamma\). If \(q\) vanishes there, its final normal form is zero, and all recorded reductions fit \(\deg q\). The reverse implication is immediate. Constants and affine targets require no artificial homogenization to the total number of rows.

2. Define the coefficient choices before interpolating them

Consider any finite strictly leveled ENS family over a unary PHP base, with arbitrary positive accuracies. Fix the listed order of inputs in each block. On each old row state \(\gamma\in\Gamma\), process the blocks by dependency order. Evaluate the current input tuple after the already selected earlier coefficient values. If all values vanish, choose every own coefficient to be zero. Otherwise let \(j_*\) be the first nonzero input value and put

\[ w_{a,j}(\gamma)= \begin{cases} g_{a,j_*}(\gamma)^{-1},&j=j_*,\\ 0,&j\ne j_*. \end{cases} \]

Use these values in the first coefficient row and zero in every other row. The block product is one at a common zero and zero otherwise; every companion and every coefficient field equation vanishes. This defines deterministic old-state functions \(w_{a,j}\) for the whole package.

Inputs may be nonlinear and can use earlier raw coefficients. In that generality their evaluated profiles refer to the fixed recursive choice just defined. For the source's selector-only dependencies, evaluating each earlier genuine product by its common-zero indicator gives the same input functions independently of the particular valid coefficient choice.

If all evaluated inputs of a block depend on one common set \(S_a\) of at most \(s\) pigeon rows, its coefficient choices depend on that set too. Interpolation gives

\[ \beta_{a,j}(X)= \sum_{z\in[n]^{S_a}}w_{a,j}(z) \prod_{i\in S_a}x_{i,z_i}, \qquad \deg\beta_{a,j}\le |S_a|\le s. \tag{RS-profile} \]

Empty supports give constants. More generally it suffices to have any old polynomial representatives of all coefficient profiles through degree \(T\ge1\); bounding the support of the whole input tuple is a convenient sufficient condition, not a necessary condition on every useful normalizer. These interpolants may have \(n^{|S_a|}\) terms. This is a degree theorem, with no assertion that the large truth tables have been computed efficiently.

3. One simultaneous map, with original axiom budgets

Working theorem. If all coefficient profiles have old representatives of degree at most \(T\ge1\), then

\[ \mathcal F_n+\mathcal E\vdash_{\rm NS/PC}^{D}1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}\vdash_{\rm NS/PC}^{TD}1. \tag{RS-transfer} \]

The source base can already be functional. A common row-support bound \(s\) for every evaluated input tuple supplies \(T=\max(1,s)\). There is no factor for the number of blocks or levels. This is an explicit extension of the old state-profile normalizer to products of row states; it is distinct from the earlier column-statistic freezing.

Proof. Fix every old incidence variable and simultaneously replace the first own coefficient row by \((\beta_{a,j})_j\), with the other rows zero. Every image depends only on old variables. Consequently the global variable map has degree at most \(T\), regardless of dependency depth; these are not nested polynomial substitutions into earlier coefficient formulas.

On \(\Gamma\), induction by level shows that the assigned polynomials evaluate to the prescribed coefficient choices. Thus each substituted companion is zero on \(\Gamma\). An original companion of degree \(e\) has image degree at most \(Te\), and (RS-degree-complete) certifies that image through its actual degree, hence through \(Te\). Likewise \(\beta^p-\beta\) vanishes on \(\Gamma\) and has an old row-ideal certificate through \(pT\), matching \(T\) times the original field degree. Coefficients need not be Boolean when \(p\) is odd.

All original weak-base generators remain available in the explicitly strengthened \(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}\), without changing their degrees. An original NS cofactor of degree at most \(D-e\) maps to degree at most \(T(D-e)\); multiplying the image certificate stays within \(TD\). Polynomial substitution and the same certified axiom images replay PC through \(TD\) as well. Only active original axioms require these preludes. The functional auxiliary bridge and audited base lower bound justify the final contradiction whenever

\[ TD\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor. \tag{RS-exclusion} \]

For a selected dependency-closed package, the same proof removes that package and retains every other block as a genuine ENS block on its actual transformed inputs. Dependencies into an unremoved earlier block cannot simply be ignored. Degree is still charged once to the entire selected package.

4. Compact and conditioned applications retain their incoming budgets

For a binary compact source, first send old bits through the affine decoder and define the row profiles on the decoded one-hot states. All bit strings are represented by these states. The compact primitive axioms have their original-degree certificates, so the same argument transfers the current degree \(D_{\rm in}\) through \(T D_{\rm in}\) to the functional unary base.

If the current base also has \(1-f\) from bottom conditioning, it maps to \(1-\tau f\). For \(f\notin\mathcal J_{n/2}\), \(\deg f=d\), the conditioned unary base retains PC degree at least \(n/2-d+1\): the same multiplication-and-stability argument applies to \(\tau f\notin\mathcal I_{n/2}\). The normalizer's companions vanish on the full row-state space, so no unproved degree completeness of the conditioned ideal is used.

In that application the incoming degree is already \(D_{\rm in}=kD\). The new bound is \(TkD\), not \(TD\) for the original proof and not \(\max(T,k)D\). Small \(T\), for example polylogarithmic support at a square-root incoming degree, can still fit the asymptotic barrier. Another square-root-sized factor generally cannot. No support bound for the complete remaining source family has been proved.

5. Individual-input support is insufficient

For \(r\) different rows take \(g_j=x_{j,1}\), \(1\le j\le r\). Each input individually depends on one pigeon. Under the fixed first-success rule, however,

\[ w_j=x_{j,1}\prod_{i<j}(1-x_{i,1}). \]

This is already in the row-pivot normal form, with nonzero degree-\(j\) monomial \((-1)^{j-1}\prod_{i\le j}x_{i,1}\). Degree-preserving reduction implies that no polynomial representative of this particular profile has degree below \(j\). A common support bound of one for the whole tuple would therefore be false. This uses the usual first-success prefix, not a new lower bound on all coefficient assignments; other packing choices can exploit multiple accuracy rows.

Dense unary parities can also depend on many pigeon rows at fixed formula depth and polynomial inventory. Conversely, a wide-support profile may have a low-degree polynomial representation. The useful hypothesis concerns actual coefficient degree, not support size by itself. The theorem covers a nonlinear multilevel subclass over every prime, not all wide inputs or the unrestricted odd-prime source.

6. Complete three-level image certificates

The compiled checker uses three two-label functional rows, without column collisions. Its three blocks have evaluated tuple supports of sizes \(2,3,3\), with nonlinear later inputs and a common-zero state in every block. It assigns all coefficients directly as row-state interpolants of degree at most three. These test the general leveled ENS theorem; their input syntax is not asserted to be a literal retained Frege source instance.

Over each of \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(\mathbb F_3\), the checker preserves six complete companion certificates, six coefficient-field certificates, and three affine row-equation controls. All 30 NS identities are verified as ordinary polynomial sums. Original companion degrees reach eleven; actual image and witness degrees reach nineteen, within the global ceiling \(3\cdot11=33\). Coefficient field witnesses reach six and nine respectively. The map has degree three although the product of the three support bounds is eighteen; this compares two supplied ledgers, not optimal normalizer degrees.

All sixteen old-state profiles, original blocks, coefficient maps, target polynomials, and cofactor/axiom pairs are retained in source-certificates.jsonl, with commands and scope in the result note. The degree-one row controls verify that interpolation does not need an artificial degree-three homogenization.

Omitting a row equation leaves a Boolean, same-row-exclusive point with nonzero mapped companion, demonstrating the role of the full row domain for the chosen map. In the ternary fixture a coefficient has value two: its Boolean equation fails while its field equation holds. These are controls on the displayed construction, not impossibility results for alternative maps. Compilation and every computation passed; these satisfiable local fixtures are not full PHP refutations.

Question and stopping point. The active obligation concerns the retained source, beyond the preceding support theorem. Identify a dependency-closed row-local package, replace its products by canonical unary values through original budgets, and stop at the exact remaining input class.

1. The compact boundary terms can be removed from the old part

Start with the coherent binary NS source after the compact boundary map and scalar cleanup, before optional polynomial or hybrid normalization. The structural source proof gives more than the bound \(\deg q\le\ell\): each value and input has the form

\[ c+\sum_{i,t}\beta_{it}b_{it} +\sum_{i<j}\gamma_{ij}E_{ij} +\sum_a\alpha_aP_a, \qquad c,\beta,\gamma,\alpha\in\mathbb F_2, \tag{RL-source} \]

with only earlier products in inputs. Negation and MOD2 are affine in their child values; each OR supplies a named product. The compact map introduces only equality products and constants as new old values. This is the chosen NS constructor's input structure, not a property inferred from every PC endpoint or from an arbitrary old polynomial of degree \(\ell\).

Decode bits affinely to \(\tau(b_{it})\) in \(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}\). Each \(\tau E_{ij}\) has an old NS certificate through \(\ell\). A nonzero linear combination of the \(E_{ij}\) has degree exactly \(\ell\): for each pair, a degree-\(\ell\) monomial using both of its rows occurs in no other pair equality. Affine bit terms cannot cancel that monomial for \(\ell\ge2\).

It follows that deleting equality terms from an old part fits that part's original degree. An input's degree is at least the weights of its occurring selectors and its old-part degree, by ordinary weighted reflection. Thus the equality deletions fit the original input budgets as well.

Propagation of a certified input change. Suppose each changed input differs from its actual image by an old certificate through its original degree \(d_i\), and neither input version exceeds that degree. Telescoping the \(h\) product factors gives a product-comparison certificate through \(w=h(\delta+1)\), where \(\delta=\max_i d_i\). Telescoping the outside input then gives each companion comparison through \(d_i+w=e_i\). Induction by source level therefore removes every old equality term while preserving the original companion budgets. The result has affine unary old parts plus genuine earlier selectors. All remaining coefficients stay fresh.

2. Pigeon support must be propagated through dependencies

In the resulting presentation, assign an old incidence variable its pigeon row. For each block \(a\), let \(R_a\) be the union of rows occurring in its affine old input parts and the sets \(R_b\) of every earlier selector that actually occurs in those inputs. Use collected formal inputs, or a conservative circuit support computation; do not discard a dependency merely because it does not appear as a raw old variable.

The package

\[ \mathcal K=\{a:|R_a|\le1\} \]

is dependency-closed: an earlier selector used by \(a\) has \(R_b\subseteq R_a\). This is a concrete syntactic sufficient criterion. Semantic cancellations may admit a larger package, and a tuple with a wide literal support may still have cheap coefficient choices; maximality among all possible normalizers is not asserted.

For \(a\in\mathcal K\), its evaluated inputs under the recursive first-success policy depend on one row or are constant. The row-profile theorem assigns every removed coefficient an affine old unary polynomial, simultaneously across the package. The global map is affine regardless of how many levels occur inside a row.

3. Each removed product has a canonical affine row-state value

For a selected block supported on row \(i\), let \(Z_a\subseteq[n]\) be the labels at which all its evaluated inputs vanish. Set

\[ v_a(X)=\sum_{z\in Z_a}x_{i,z}. \]

When the value is constant, use the corresponding constant representative instead. Under the affine profile map \(\sigma\), the actual product \(\sigma P_a\) agrees with \(v_a\) on the functional row states. It has degree at most its original weight \(w_a\). The row-state division theorem gives

\[ \boxed{\sigma P_a-v_a \in\mathcal I_{w_a}(U_{\rm row}).} \tag{RL-selector} \]

A nontrivial product has \(w_a\ge1\), so the affine comparison term fits; an all-zero tuple has product and canonical value both one and needs no witness. Removed companions and coefficient fields already have the original-degree image certificates from the profile theorem.

Now replace a selected selector by \(v_a\) in every later input, and rebuild each unselected genuine product on its changed input tuple. The same input/product/companion telescoping induction used above keeps the comparisons within the old \(d_i,w_a,e_i\) budgets. Multipliers can involve other rows and remaining fresh coefficients; the underlying certificates still use old axioms only. This also explains why an actual product cannot simply be replaced by an arbitrary affine function sharing a convenient rank.

4. The canonical retained class and complete proof transfer

Working source pass. A supplied degree-\(D\) NS refutation in the stated compact source presentation yields a degree-\(D\) refutation over \(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}\) and the unselected ENS blocks, whose inputs now have the form

\[ L_{a,s}(X)+\sum_{b\notin\mathcal K}\alpha_{a,s;b}P'_b, \qquad L_{a,s}\text{ affine unary}, \tag{RL-retained} \]

with the original dependency order and only earlier products in inputs. The same transfer applies to a supplied PC proof of a family satisfying these input hypotheses; the source-profile premise is not asserted for an unrelated PC extraction.

NS and PC budgets. The bit decoder and all removed coefficient images are affine. Each primitive old image and each removed or replaced companion has a certificate within its original source degree. An original NS cofactor of degree at most \(D-e\), including one containing raw removed coefficients, therefore multiplies a replacement through \(e\) without exceeding \(D\). No selector-only restriction on arbitrary cofactors is needed. Affine PC substitution with these axiom-image proofs has the same ceiling.

The number of retained blocks only decreases. Row-state values and coefficient tables have at most \(n\) entries per selected row-local object; no added ENS inventory is required. This is a degree transfer, without a claimed polynomial bound on all expanded NS certificate monomials.

Dependency-minimal retained blocks have affine unary inputs. They need not have affine bit inputs: arbitrary row-state functions have become unary linear forms. The normalized multiscale label parents remain available among these wide inputs. The pass is therefore real preprocessing of the source, but it does not settle the retained family.

5. Keep the two preprocessing orders distinct

This pass starts before the optional compact hybrid map. It gives a functional-unary presentation at degree \(D\). The earlier compact-first route instead uses a weight and a degree-\(kD\) conditioned endpoint, whose remaining old inputs include nonlinear flat indicators. Its smaller bit variable space and the present affine unary input form are not simultaneously guaranteed by either theorem.

In particular, this entry is not another level eliminated from the already conditioned system, nor permission to apply the affine-bit exclusion to newly affine-unary tuples. Combining the two orders would need an additional map, image certificates, and its full degree ledger.

6. A selector-linear source fixture and complete image evidence

The compiled checker uses two four-label rows over \(\mathbb F_2\), with \(\ell=2,\ h=1\). There are two local bottom blocks, two local second-level blocks, and a retained third-level parent whose inputs are affine in old bits, earlier selectors, and one compact equality term. Thus its input syntax matches the specific source profile tested here; no complete Frege proof is instantiated.

The four local products become the unary label indicators \(x_{0,0},x_{1,0},x_{0,2},x_{1,2}\), with comparison witnesses through their original weights two and three. The retained parent becomes an affine-unary ENS tuple after the old equality term is certified away. Every removed coefficient image is affine.

The complete output retains all sixteen row states, original blocks, maps, canonical values, and thirty NS certificates: four selector comparisons, eight removed companions, eight removed fields, four bit domains, one compact equality, two retained companions, two retained fields, and one raw-cofactor multiple. Commands and schema are in the result note.

The retained companion witnesses use degree seven, exactly their original budgets, although the canonical companion degree is three. Multiplying one original companion by a raw bottom coefficient squared gives a nonzero mapped certificate through the original budget nine. This tests the cofactor ledger as well as the input syntax.

A wrong canonical label replacement fails at a state satisfying all the displayed local row and column axioms. A separate input with a literal old variable from row zero changes when only row one changes, exposing its earlier-selector dependency. These are controls on the local image construction; the two-row subsystem is satisfiable and is not the full \(n+1\)-pigeon base. Compilation and all computations passed.

Route assessment. Row-local source structure now has a canonical degree-preserving removal pass, but no new unrestricted lower-bound coverage is claimed. Wide affine-unary parents remain, and the two preprocessing presentations must not be counted as cumulative eliminations.

Process assessment. The source-shaped fixture closed the previous syntax gap, but next-step speculation leaked into checkpoint preparation; the accompanying framework revision makes the preparation marker start an already-prepared sequential batch.

14 September 2026 — Formal source cofactors as matrix programs, and the realization gap

Status: working source refinement and exact algebraic construction; source-shaped fixed-order obstruction; scoped literature audit and finite checks. The full PHP lower-bound goal remains open.

Question and stopping point. Does the retained source identity constrain cofactors beyond polynomial inventory, degree, and shallow arithmetic formulas? We test the row-local-first binary NS presentation, stop at an explicit additional representation constraint and a source-compatible test of its survival, and retain the carried concrete witness costs. This refines the existing proof-path expansion and selector-valued interface; their shallow representation is not a new discovery here.

1. The outer cofactors are sums of logarithmically many affine factors

Let \(T\) include the symbol inventory of the balanced binary source proof and its coherent local modules, and let \(H_\pi=O(\log S_{\rm proof})\) be its height. Work before expanding the supplied concrete NS witnesses of those modules. After the row-local-first pass, let \(u\) consist of the unary old coordinates \(X\) and the formal names \(Z_a\) of retained products. Every actual formula value, MOD prefix sum, and node value is affine in these formal coordinates.

Formal specialization and its cost. Apply a ring homomorphism to the original formal identity while the original product names are still present: the goal selector goes to one, packed clause selectors to zero, row-local selectors to their affine unary state values, old bits to their affine decoder, and retained selectors to their new formal names. This is a legitimate substitution into a free polynomial ring. It is not an assertion that an old collision polynomial is literally zero after unary decoding.

To justify the concrete witnesses, use the boundary certificates and the compact-equality comparisons, then the canonical row-local comparisons. Each replaced product agrees with its virtual value modulo the retained base and companions through its original weight. For a local target, telescope its constant-degree expression in those values: replacing a factor uses its comparison certificate multiplied by the other factors. This costs no more than the target's original structural weighted bound, hence no more than its carried witness ceiling. The transformed local target therefore retains its original supplied witness. Zero targets may be discarded; retained coordinate weights can be kept at their original upper bounds.

\[ 1=\sum_\alpha Q_\alpha(u)H_\alpha(u),\qquad \deg_w Q_\alpha+\nu_\alpha\le D=(C+H_\pi)L,\qquad \deg H_\alpha\le2. \tag{MATRIX-source} \]

Here \(L=(d+1)h^d\), \(C=\max(M_{\rm fr}+2,12)\), and \(\nu_\alpha\le3L\) or \(2L\) is the concrete NS witness ceiling inherited from the source. Formal ordinary degree two does not replace \(\nu_\alpha\).

Working refinement. There are constants \(C_0,C_1\), depending only on the fixed axiom frames and presentation, such that

\[ Q_\alpha=\sum_{r\in R_\alpha}c_r \prod_{j=1}^{t_r}\ell_{r,j}(u),\qquad t_r\le H_\pi+C_0,\qquad \sum_\alpha |R_\alpha|\le C_1T, \tag{MATRIX-factors} \]

where every \(\ell_{r,j}\) is affine. No polynomial bound on the fully expanded monomial count is claimed.

Proof. At an MP node with antecedent value \(a\), implication value \(c\), and conclusion value \(b\), the local relation is \(c-b+ab\). Its certificate vector satisfies \(Q_b=Q_c+bQ_a-e_{\rm MP}\). Unrolling the balanced tree multiplies a contribution by \(b\) at each antecedent edge and by one at each implication edge, hence adds at most \(H_\pi\) affine factors. A fixed Boolean frame has a bounded number of leaf occurrences. Its formal expansion and Boolean-domain division give a bounded number of monomials of bounded degree in its actual node values, each now affine in \(u\). The fixed outer MOD frame uses its last argument and affine prefix sum and has the same property, independent of MOD arity. Thus every local contribution is a bounded sum of bounded products of affine forms. There are at most a constant times \(T\) such contributions, proving the formula. This argument deliberately leaves the internal NS cofactors of the \(H_\alpha\)-witnesses unexpanded.

2. An explicit read-once matrix representation

A read-once oblivious algebraic branching program (ROABP) computes a polynomial as an initial row vector, a product of matrices univariate in successive distinct coordinates, and a terminal column vector. Its width is the largest intermediate matrix dimension. This is the standard model used in Forbes–Shpilka–Tzameret–Wigderson (2021); the elementary construction below is included to make the source application and its accounting explicit.

Consider \(q(u)=\prod_{j=1}^t(c_j+\sum_{i=1}^N a_{ji}u_i)\) over any field. In the auxiliary algebra

\[ A=\mathbb F[\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_t]/(\epsilon_1^2,\ldots,\epsilon_t^2) \]

use the \(2^t\) basis vectors \(\epsilon_S\), \(S\subseteq[t]\). The initial row is \(v_S=\prod_{j\in S}c_j\). The terminal column selects \(S=[t]\). For coordinate \(u_i\), take multiplication by \(\prod_j(1+a_{ji}\epsilon_j u_i)\); its matrix is

\[ M_i[S,U]= \begin{cases} \displaystyle\left(\prod_{j\in U\setminus S}a_{ji}\right) u_i^{|U\setminus S|},&S\subseteq U,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \tag{MATRIX-subsets} \]

For any coordinate order \(\pi\), \(q=vM_{\pi(1)}\cdots M_{\pi(N)}e_{[t]}\). Indeed, obtaining the coefficient of \(\epsilon_1\cdots\epsilon_t\) assigns each factor \(j\) exactly once, either its constant term or one of its variable terms. Nilpotence removes multiple assignments to the same factor. All multiplication operators commute, so every order works. Each layer has at most \(3^t\) nonzero entries and univariate degree at most \(t\). Direct sums represent sums of \(R\) such products with width at most \(\sum_r2^{t_r}\le R2^t\).

3. Polynomial width for the costed formal module certificate

Add one formal placeholder \(Y_\alpha\) for each target and define

\[ \mathscr C(u,Y)=\sum_\alpha Q_\alpha(u)Y_\alpha,\qquad \mathscr C(u,0)=0,\qquad \mathscr C(u,H(u))=1. \tag{MATRIX-certificate} \]

Working corollary. In every order of all the \(u\)- and \(Y\)-coordinates, this certificate has a ROABP of width at most

\[ \sum_{\alpha,r}2^{t_r+1} \le C_1T\,2^{H_\pi+C_0+1}. \tag{MATRIX-width} \]

This is polynomial in the hypothetical proof and source sizes; its exponent does not grow with the chosen accuracy \(h\). The number of variables, matrix entries, and univariate degrees are polynomial as well. Assigning \(Y_\alpha\) weight \(\nu_\alpha\) gives \(\deg_w\mathscr C\le D\).

Proof. Adjoin \(Y_\alpha\) as one more affine factor to each contribution in (MATRIX-factors), and apply (MATRIX-subsets). The two displayed certificate identities follow from (MATRIX-source); the weight bound follows from \(\deg_wQ_\alpha+\nu_\alpha\le D\).

This is an IPS-style certificate for the supplied formal module equations. The equations and their witnesses depend on the hypothetical source proof. It is not yet a small-width refutation in the original PHP variables, nor an application of a lower bound for a different CNF. Genuine substitution and the witness expansion still need their own representation analysis.

4. Booleanization preserves width, with explicit weighted corrections

Fix an order and any chosen set of coordinates to reduce modulo \(u_v^2-u_v\). In a univariate matrix, replace \(M_v(u_v)\) by \(M_v(0)+u_v(M_v(1)-M_v(0))\). This performs the ordinary Boolean remainder in that coordinate without increasing width. In (MATRIX-subsets), a nonempty transition changes \(u_v^d\) to \(u_v\), while the constant diagonal stays one.

The quotient \((u_v^d-u_v)/(u_v^2-u_v)\) is \(\sum_{e=0}^{d-2}u_v^e\) for \(d\ge2\), and zero for \(d=0,1\). Telescoping the ordered matrix product, with earlier chosen layers reduced and later ones unreduced, therefore supplies

\[ Q_\alpha-\operatorname{ml}(Q_\alpha) =\sum_v A_{\alpha v}(u)(u_v^2-u_v),\qquad \deg_w A_{\alpha v}+2w_v\le\deg_wQ_\alpha. \tag{MATRIX-Boolean} \]

Each quotient cofactor is represented in the same order and width as its starting program. The weighted bound follows from the univariate division on collected monomials; it does not require the factored expression to have no cancellations. Hence

\[ 1=\sum_\alpha\operatorname{ml}(Q_\alpha)H_\alpha +\sum_v B_v(u)(u_v^2-u_v),\qquad B_v=\sum_\alpha A_{\alpha v}H_\alpha,\qquad \deg_wB_v+2w_v\le D. \]

The quadratic formal targets have polynomial-width programs in the same order. A product of two programs is represented by tensoring their corresponding layers, and a sum by direct sums. Thus the correction cofactors remain polynomial width. In the binary source, an old coordinate's Booleanity and a genuine selector's Booleanity have concrete witnesses through \(2w_v\): expand Frobenius additivity and the product identity over the primitive Boolean domains, with product degree at most \(w_v\). This certifies the added terms through \(D\). Domain-only Booleanity of an arbitrary selector is not asserted over odd primes.

These are ordinary polynomial identities with explicit domain correction terms. Merely replacing every coordinate by its Boolean remainder inside the source identity without those terms would be incorrect.

5. A two-level realization with superpolynomial width at one cut

The formal width bound need not survive replacing a selector by its genuine polynomial. Work over \(\mathbb F_2\). For \(b,j\in[h]\), use independent old variables \(x_{bj},y_{bj}\) and one modifier \(z\). Child block \(b\), of accuracy \(h\), has inputs \(g_{bj}=1+x_{bj}+y_{bj}\). Give the parent, also of accuracy \(h\), inputs \(1-P_b+z\). These are affine in old bits and earlier selectors. A nonconstant MOD\(_2\) wrapper around each child realizes this intervening affine value; it prevents collapsing contiguous ORs into one cluster. Thus this is a legitimate two-level selector pattern, not an artificial extra OR level produced by unflattened OR-of-OR syntax.

Specialize every block's coefficient matrix to the identity and then \(z=0\). Put \(s_{bj}=x_{bj}+y_{bj}\) and \(\chi_b=\prod_{j\le h}s_{bj}\). The children become \(\chi_b\), and the parent becomes

\[ P_{\rm parent}\longmapsto \prod_{b=1}^h\chi_b =\prod_{b,j\le h}(x_{bj}+y_{bj}). \tag{MATRIX-realization} \]

Each child product has original degree \(2h\). The original parent product has degree \(h(2h+1)\), and its companions have degree \(2h^2+3h\). These original costs are retained.

Companion-image certificates. For a child, \(g_{bj}\chi_b=-(s_{bj}^2-s_{bj})\prod_{k\ne j}s_{bk}\), and \(s_{bj}^2-s_{bj}=(x_{bj}^2-x_{bj})+(y_{bj}^2-y_{bj})\). This is a Boolean NS certificate through \(h+1\le2h+1\). For a parent input, after the displayed specialization,

\[ (1-\chi_b)\prod_c\chi_c =-(\chi_b^2-\chi_b)\prod_{c\ne b}\chi_c,\qquad \chi_b^2-\chi_b =\sum_j(s_{bj}^2-s_{bj}) \prod_{k<j}s_{bk}^2\prod_{k>j}s_{bk}. \]

The resulting witness costs at most \(h^2+h\), within \(2h^2+3h\). All coefficient field images are zero under the \(0/1\) map. The modifier restriction is itself Boolean. Thus the example includes companion and domain checks, not just an arbitrary polynomial substitution.

Cut-rank proof. Index rows of the coefficient matrix by squarefree \(x\)-monomials \(x_A\), and columns by squarefree \(y\)-monomials \(y_B\), where \(A,B\subseteq[h]\times[h]\). The entry for (MATRIX-realization) is one exactly when \(B\) is the complement of \(A\). The matrix is a permutation matrix of rank \(2^{h^2}\). A width-\(w\) ROABP reading all \(x\)'s before all \(y\)'s factors at that cut into at most \(w\) products of a left polynomial and a right polynomial, so its coefficient-matrix rank is at most \(w\). Scalar restrictions cannot increase width. Therefore any program respecting this cut for the genuine parent must have width at least \(2^{h^2}\), although its formal selector coordinate alone has width one.

At \(h=\Theta(\log n)\), this lower bound is superpolynomial in \(n\), with only polynomially many source variables and blocks. Assign the old pairs to distinct pigeon rows to keep the children nonlocal when \(h\ge2\); their propagated support survives the row-local pass. Unary decoding does not remove the obstruction: set one unary variable representing each displayed bit to that bit and other row variables to zero, an affine restriction that recovers the same polynomial. This last restriction concerns polynomial representation and need not be a PHP model.

Scope. Interleaving \(x_{bj},y_{bj}\) makes this particular product easy. This is a fixed-order obstruction, not an all-order lower bound. Nor does the example show an essential occurrence in any complete PHP certificate. It tests source-eligible selector realization; it does not prove that every possible normalizer or complete cofactor identity must retain the same complexity. The initial one-level control only gives \(2^h\), still polynomial at logarithmic accuracy; the nested control was added specifically to test the relevant superpolynomial scale.

6. Literature scope: a small-characteristic gap in a subset-sum step

Hakoniemi–Limaye–Tzameret, “Hard CNF Instances for Ideal Proof Systems,” v1 (6 May 2026) studies roABP-IPS and states CNF lower bounds. Its Proposition 21 gives a functional-PHP upper-bound argument using the Boolean equations for \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\) and \(n+1-\sum_k y_k=0\), treating that subsystem as unsatisfiable. We checked the displayed statement and proof on PDF pages 27–28. Their main CNF lower-bound proof was not audited or applied here.

Exact field check. On Boolean inputs the sum is an integer Hamming weight \(r\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\), interpreted in the field. In characteristic zero, or prime characteristic \(p>n+1\), \(n+1-r\) cannot vanish. If \(p\le n+1\), take \(r\) to be the least nonnegative residue of \(n+1\) modulo \(p\); then \(r\le n\), and any vector with \(r\) ones is a model. Thus the displayed subset-sum step does not establish the upper bound over fixed small prime fields. This countermodel is for that intermediate subsystem, not for FPHP. It neither disproves every possible roABP upper bound nor challenges the paper's main CNF theorem.

The exact v1 record permits CC BY 4.0 redistribution; the unchanged PDF, extracted text, version/license evidence, and reading limits are preserved with attribution. The 2021 algebraic-proof-complexity paper and Elbaz–Govindasamy–Lu–Tzameret (2025), v1 were screened for model/background definitions only; no PHP lower-bound theorem was imported from them.

7. Complete finite evidence and the remaining obligation

The compiled checker uses exact sparse polynomial arithmetic. For each of \(p=2,3\), a height-three MP tree has fifteen nodes and fourteen module targets, with two leaves sharing a target. Its fifteen factored contributions give a formal certificate on three old coordinates and fourteen placeholders. The old weights are \(1,2,4\); module costs are declared as their weighted target degrees plus two. These are formal test costs, not claimed concrete ENS witnesses.

There are eighteen complete matrix programs in total: in each field, three ordinary programs, three Boolean-remainder programs, and three correction programs. Orders are increasing, decreasing, and the permutation \(i\mapsto5i\bmod17\). Every direct-sum width is eighty and the weighted certificate budget is ten. Complete matrices, initial/terminal vectors, polynomials, and corrections are retained. At the ternary point with old values \((2,0,0)\), first placeholder one, and the others zero, ordinary certificate minus Boolean remainder is two, providing a non-Boolean control.

Three one-level selector controls use \(h=4,6,8\) and preserve eighteen full companion certificates. Two nested controls use \(h=2,3\), have cut ranks sixteen and 512, and preserve eighteen further complete companion certificates. Twelve full Hamming-weight tables use \(p=2,3,5,7\) and \(n=4,8,16\), including both small-field models and an unsatisfiable large-characteristic control.

The initial run and strengthened run are both preserved. Reproduction and schema, source hashes, version evidence, timing, and complete command logs accompany the checkpoint. All builds and computations passed; finite MP fixtures do not instantiate a full Frege/PHP refutation.

Route assessment. The proof-specific mechanism obligation now has a sharper formal input class with a full width construction. Its preservation under genuine realization remains open, and one natural fixed-order guarantee is refuted at the relevant accuracy scale. No additional augmented-PHP lower bound or odd-prime source coverage is claimed.

Next bounded question. Test whether choosing an old-variable order repairs the two-level realization gap, stopping at a polynomial-width construction or an ordering-independent obstruction; retain the distinction between a hard selector and essential use in the complete certificate.

Process assessment. The claim-index search prevented rebranding the old shallow path argument and the nested control resolved a concrete accuracy concern; a failed draft-tool parse wasted context, so the retry separates the HTML from its small insertion controller without adding a framework rule.

14 September 2026 — Every-order selector hardness, with a degree-preserving elimination control

Status: working every-order obstruction for source-shaped selector realization; explicit degree-preserving normalizer for the same family; exact matrix and certificate checks. No new augmented-PHP lower bound.

Question and stopping point. Can choosing the old-variable order repair the preceding fixed-order realization gap? We stop at an every-order counterexample, while checking whether it is actually an obstruction to our degree-elimination route. The construction below uses elementary linear-code and matrix-rank arguments; its research application is to the retained source class, without a claim that those general methods are new.

1. Exact cut rank of a binary affine-flat indicator

Let \(A\in\mathbb F_2^{r\times v}\) have row rank \(r\), let \(b\in\mathbb F_2^r\), and let \(f_b\) be the unique multilinear polynomial agreeing on Boolean inputs with the indicator of \(Ax=b\). For a partition \([v]=S\sqcup T\), put \(r_S=\operatorname{rank}A_S\) and \(r_T=\operatorname{rank}A_T\).

Working lemma. Both the Boolean evaluation matrix and the multilinear coefficient matrix across this cut have rank

\[ \operatorname{rank}M_{S,T}(f_b)=2^{r_S+r_T-r}. \tag{CODE-cut} \]

Proof. Put \(U=\operatorname{im}A_S\), \(W=\operatorname{im}A_T\). Full row rank gives \(U+W=\mathbb F_2^r\). Group left assignments by their syndrome \(u\in U\), and right assignments by \(w\in W\). The evaluation entry is one exactly when \(u+w=b\). Choose \(u_0+w_0=b\). The nonzero syndrome pairs are indexed by the affine space \(u_0+(U\cap W)\), of cardinality \(2^{r_S+r_T-r}\). Distinct pairs give disjoint nonzero row/column blocks, each an all-ones matrix of rank one. Selecting one row and column per block gives an identity submatrix, proving the exact rank over \(\mathbb F_2\).

The Boolean evaluation matrix is obtained from the multilinear coefficient matrix by multiplying on the left and right by the respective subset-incidence matrices. These are triangular with diagonal one in subset order and hence invertible over \(\mathbb F_2\). The coefficient rank is therefore the same. Any ROABP respecting this cut has width at least that rank: split the program at the cut into a sum of at most its width many left/right polynomial products.

2. A short binary code whose every half retains almost all rank

Take even \(v\). Suppose every nonzero row combination of \(A\) has Hamming weight between \(3v/8\) and \(5v/8\). Then \(A\) has full row rank, and every \(v/2\)-column submatrix has rank at least \(r-1\).

Proof. The positive weight lower bound first excludes a nonzero left kernel. If \(A_S\), \(|S|=v/2\), had rank at most \(r-2\), choose independent \(\lambda,\mu\) annihilating its columns. Write \(w_\lambda,w_\mu,w_{\lambda+\mu}\) for the three codeword weights. The number of columns on which both forms vanish is

\[ v-\frac{w_\lambda+w_\mu+w_{\lambda+\mu}}2 \le \frac{7v}{16}<\frac v2, \tag{CODE-common-zero} \]

contradicting that all columns of \(S\) lie there. The count follows because a nonzero pair of binary form values contributes exactly two to the sum of the three Hamming weights.

Existence with \(v=64(r+1)\). Choose each column independently and uniformly from \(\mathbb F_2^r\). For each fixed nonzero \(\lambda\), its codeword consists of independent fair bits. If \(\epsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}\) are their signed versions, then \(\mathbb E e^{t\sum_i\epsilon_i}=(\cosh t)^v\le e^{vt^2/2}\). The inequality follows by integrating \(\tanh t\le t\). Markov's inequality with \(t=1/4\), in both tails, bounds the chance that the weight lies outside the required interval by \(2e^{-v/32}\). A union bound over nonzero \(\lambda\) gives failure probability at most

\[ 2^{r+1}e^{-v/32} =\exp\big((r+1)(\log2-2)\big)<1. \tag{CODE-existence} \]

Thus a suitable matrix exists with \(O(r^2)\) bits of description. This is a probabilistic existence proof, not a claim of a deterministic polynomial-time verifier for arbitrary large \(r\). The finite witnesses below explicitly enumerate their codeword weights.

Only the lower codeword-weight bound is used in the half-rank argument; the upper bound is a convenient symmetric sampling convention.

Every variable order has a middle cut into two sets of \(v/2\) variables. Combining this lemma with (CODE-cut) gives ROABP width at least \(2^{r-2}\) for \(f_b\) in every order.

3. A retained two-level source value with width \(2^{h^2-2}\) in every order

Let \(h\ge2\), \(r=h^2\), \(v=64(r+1)\), and choose the matrix above. Write its linear forms as \(L_{bj}(x)\), \(b,j\in[h]\). Replace the separated forms \(x_{bj}+y_{bj}\) in the preceding source pattern by these dense linear forms: child block \(b\) has inputs \(1+L_{bj}\), accuracy \(h\), and product \(P_b\); the parent has inputs \(1-P_b+z\) and accuracy \(h\). As before, nonconstant MOD\(_2\) wrappers provide the intermediate values, so the two OR levels do not flatten into a single cluster.

Specialize each coefficient matrix to the identity and then \(z=0\). The genuine parent becomes

\[ q(x)=\prod_{b,j\le h}L_{bj}(x). \tag{CODE-selector} \]

Its Boolean remainder is \(f_{\mathbf1}\), the indicator of \(Ax=\mathbf1\). The univariate matrix reduction does not increase ROABP width. Therefore any ROABP for the ordinary polynomial \(q\), in any variable order, has width at least \(2^{h^2-2}\). The same lower bound holds before the scalar restrictions, since restricting coordinates to constants cannot increase width, whatever their positions in the order. The formal parent selector alone has width one.

The description has \(O(h^4)\) bits for \(A\) and polynomial total source size. At \(h=\Theta(\log n)\), width is superpolynomial in \(n\), while the number of old variables is \(O(\log^2 n)\). Choose one bit from each of \(v\) distinct pigeon rows, requiring \(v\le n+1\), which holds eventually. Each input form involves at least \(3v/8\) rows, so these blocks survive the row-local support pass. Unary decoding also preserves the representation obstruction: restrict one suitable unary variable per selected row to the corresponding bit and all other unary variables to zero. Any unary variable order induces an order on those surviving bits. This restriction is an algebraic representation test, not a satisfying PHP assignment.

The result is source-shaped and remains after the specified row-local pass. It does not assert essential occurrence in a hypothetical PHP proof, or survival under every other admissible normalization.

4. The same family still has a degree-preserving normalizer

The width obstruction is not a degree-elimination obstruction. Keep \(z\) free and set only the coefficient matrices to the identity. Put \(\chi_b=\prod_jL_{bj}\), \(F_b=1+\chi_b+z\), and \(Q=\prod_b(\chi_b+z)=\prod_b(1+F_b)\).

A child companion has the ordinary identity

\[ (1+L_{bj})\chi_b =(L_{bj}^2-L_{bj})\prod_{k\ne j}L_{bk}, \qquad L_{bj}^2-L_{bj} =\sum_i A_{(b,j),i}(x_i^2-x_i). \]

Its old Boolean NS certificate costs at most \(h+1\), within its original \(2h+1\) companion degree. For the parent,

\[ F_bQ=(F_b^2-F_b)\prod_{c\ne b}(\chi_c+z),\qquad F_b^2-F_b=(\chi_b^2-\chi_b)+(z^2-z), \]
\[ \chi_b^2-\chi_b =\sum_j(L_{bj}^2-L_{bj}) \prod_{k<j}L_{bk}^2\prod_{k>j}L_{bk}. \tag{CODE-normalizer} \]

The inner certificate costs \(2h\), and its outside multiplier has degree at most \(h(h-1)\). Thus parent companions have Boolean NS certificates through \(h^2+h\), within their original \(2h^2+3h\) degrees. Child products originally have degree \(2h\), and the parent product originally has degree \(h(2h+1)\). All coefficient field equations map to zero.

The global variable substitution is affine, fixing old variables and sending fresh coefficients to constants. Every companion image has an old certificate within its original degree. Hence any degree-\(D\) NS or PC refutation of a Boolean old base augmented by exactly this package transfers to the old base through \(D\), including NS cofactors containing raw coefficient variables. No multiplication of degree costs across the two levels is needed. For a package inside a larger family, the other blocks must still be transformed and retained; no elimination of those blocks follows automatically.

This strengthens the scope control: every-order-hard old selector values coexist with inexpensive elimination. A route demanding polynomial width for every realized selector is stronger than what the degree lower-bound strategy needs.

5. Exact checks, full evidence, and contribution

The compiled checker saves all of its evidence. For the rank-three matrix with columns the eight vectors of \(\mathbb F_2^3\), it checks all seventy balanced coordinate cuts and all eight targets: 560 full evaluation matrices and corresponding multilinear coefficient matrices, with exact \(\mathbb F_2\) ranks. A rank-four repeated-basis control has a half of rank two and cut rank one, violating the proposed \(r-1\) half-rank conclusion when the code-weight hypothesis is dropped.

Three deterministic seeded searches supply complete balanced-code witnesses:

All \(15\), \(511\), and \(65{,}535\) nonzero codeword weights respectively are retained, along with every matrix column, generator seed, and trial number. Each search accepted its first candidate. The every-order conclusion uses the proved half-rank lemma; these large instances do not enumerate all their coordinate orders.

Thirty-eight complete NS certificates verify the child and parent identities, with \(z\) free, in independent formal variables \(t_{bj},z\) for \(h=2,3,4\). The saved linear substitutions \(t_{bj}=L_{bj}(x)\), together with the displayed Frobenius identity, specify the full composed old-variable certificates without expanding products of dense forms. This preserves the complete factored evidence and degree ledger; it is not a claim to have stored an exponentially expanded monomial list. These checks use ordinary polynomial arithmetic, so Boolean-only evaluations cannot make the certificate test vacuous.

The complete output, commands and schema, hashes, timing, and execution evidence are preserved. All compilation and computation checks passed.

The same examples are eliminated without degree loss, so this does not add PHP lower-bound coverage or justify abandoning the degree route. Further individual-selector hardness refinements would not address the remaining obligation; a useful matrix argument must concern the complete companion/cofactor certificate.

14 September 2026 — The complete retained OR witness can have hard collected cofactors

Status: working obstruction for the supplied source witness, with explicit source syntax, normalization, and original-degree accounting. No lower bound for all alternative witnesses or a full PHP certificate.

Question and stopping point. Does collection or Boolean reduction rescue the formal polynomial-width certificate when its actual OR-module witnesses are expanded? We test the existing proper-union witness on the preceding code family, including the admissible child normalization. This is an application of the already established collected coefficient formula, not a new OR identity.

1. A proper source module with a wide retained side

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(h\ge2\), \(r=h^2\). Take the \(v=64(r+1)\) old bit variables and full-rank matrix \(A\) from the balanced-code construction, with forms \(L_{bj}\). Add \(a=2h+1\) independent old signals \(t_1,\ldots,t_a\), using distinct additional pigeon rows. Require \(v+a\le n+1\), which holds eventually at logarithmic accuracy. The modifier \(z\) can use another bit in an existing row.

For each \(b\in[h]\), let the lower block \(C_b\) have accuracy \(h\), inputs \(1+L_{bj}\), and genuine product \(V_b\). The three blocks in the proper comparison, all of accuracy \(h\), use

\[ I_1=\{t_1,\ldots,t_a\},\qquad I_2=\{f_b=1-V_b+z:b\in[h]\},\qquad I_0=I_1\sqcup I_2. \tag{ORCODE-inputs} \]

Write their products as \(P_1,P_2,P_0\), respectively, with fresh disjoint coefficient scopes. The \(f_b\) are nonconstant MOD\(_2\)-wrapped lower values, so the source has two genuine OR levels. Every selected package has support on more than one pigeon row. The affine side has rank \(2h+1\), above the standard rank-\(2h\) affine packing threshold. This family survives the row-local-first preprocessing. We do not assume survival under every further possible normalization or essential occurrence in a PHP proof.

The lower products and \(P_1\) have original degree \(2h\). The nonlinear inputs \(f_b\) have original degree \(2h\); hence \(P_0,P_2\) have degree \(h(2h+1)\). The supplied three-value NS budget is

\[ \nu=s_0+s_1+s_2=4h^2+4h. \tag{ORCODE-budget} \]

The old source theorem may carry a larger ceiling such as \(3L\); this local calculation does not reset any smaller formal target degree to a supplied witness cost.

2. The actual collected witness has every-order-hard cofactors

For \(E_{k,i}=g_iP_k\), let \(U_i^k\) be the usual prefixes satisfying \(1-P_k=\sum_i U_i^k g_i\). The supplied complete certificate is

\[ P_0-P_1P_2 =\sum_{i\in I_1}U_i^1E_{0,i} +\sum_{j\in I_2}P_1U_j^2E_{0,j} -\sum_{i\in I_1}P_2U_i^0E_{1,i} -\sum_{j\in I_2}P_1U_j^0E_{2,j}. \tag{ORCODE-witness} \]

Collection by the original companion generators gives exactly \(-P_2U_{t_1}^0\) for \(E_{1,t_1}\). Consider the following scalar restriction for testing the polynomial representation: set the lower coefficient matrices and block-two coefficients to identity matrices; set \(z=0\); in block zero set the first row's \(t_1\)-coefficient to one and every other coefficient to zero. Its prefix is then literally \(U_{t_1}^0=1\). Thus

\[ -P_2U_{t_1}^0\longmapsto q(x)=\prod_{b,j\le h}L_{bj}(x). \tag{ORCODE-isolation} \]

By the every-order code lemma, the restricted cofactor needs ROABP width at least \(2^{h^2-2}\) in every order. Scalar restrictions preserve width and induce some order on the remaining old variables, so the original genuine cofactor has that lower bound in every order as well.

Introduce separate placeholders for the actual companion generators in (ORCODE-witness). Setting only the placeholder for \(E_{1,t_1}\) to one, and the others to zero, extracts this cofactor. Consequently the complete supplied IPS-style witness also requires width at least \(2^{h^2-2}\) in every order. This is a statement about the collected supplied witness, not a minimum over all possible NS certificates for its target.

Boolean remainder commutes with the displayed \(0/1\) restrictions. The resulting cofactor is the affine-flat indicator of \(Ax=\mathbf1\), whose middle-cut rank has the same lower bound. Thus Booleanizing the cofactors does not help. If the associated domain corrections are added to obtain an ordinary certificate, setting their placeholders to zero still isolates this hard reduced cofactor.

3. The obstruction survives the inexpensive child normalization

Now apply an actual source-preserving normalization, leaving \(z\) free: set only the lower matrices and block-two matrix to identity, while retaining all block-zero and block-one coefficients. The preceding complete companion certificates remove that lower-plus-block-two package. Put

\[ \chi_b=\prod_jL_{bj},\qquad q_z=\prod_b(\chi_b+z). \]

The remaining module target is \(P'_0-P_1q_z\), with union inputs \(t_i\) and \(1-\chi_b+z\). The global coefficient map is affine. Removed child companions have old witnesses through \(h+1\); removed block-two companions through \(h^2+h\), both within their original degrees. Hence the complete transformed witness retains (ORCODE-budget), including the cost of its raw internal cofactors. The removed witnesses use only old Boolean axioms; they introduce no new contribution to \(E_{1,t_1}\). Its collected coefficient remains exactly \(-q_z(U_{t_1}^0)'\), and the block-zero restriction and \(z=0\) again give (ORCODE-isolation).

The retained comparison is not a Boolean-domain identity. Choose old Boolean values with \(t_1=1\), set block one's first row to select \(t_1\), and set every block-zero coefficient to zero. Then \(P_1=0\), \(P'_0=1\), and the target is one. This is a domain control, not a satisfying assignment of the full pigeonhole base.

An old-quotient nonzero check. With one chosen bit per code row, \(\operatorname{ml}(q)\) is a nonzero row-linear bit polynomial of degree at most \(r\): full rank of \(A\) supplies Boolean solutions to \(Ax=\mathbf1\). Under \(4(r-1)<n\), the row-linear injection gives \(\operatorname{ml}(q)\notin\mathcal J_r\). If \(B\ge r\) and \(n\ge2B-1\), transported stability then gives \(\operatorname{ml}(q)\notin\mathcal J_B\). Thus the old-base filtration does not simply identify the extracted cofactor with zero at these budgets. This is nonvanishing in the quotient, not a rank lower bound for all quotient-equivalent representatives.

4. What this rules out, and what it leaves open

The binary formal outer certificate had polynomial width because it treated local relations as costed module placeholders. Expanding these placeholders using the supplied proper-OR witnesses can produce every-order superpolynomial width at \(h=\Theta(\log n)\), even after collection, Boolean reduction, and the specified inexpensive child normalization. Thus the formal width theorem cannot be promoted to the same width bound for those fully expanded witnesses by this procedure.

There is no claim that every alternate witness for \(P'_0-P_1q_z\) is hard, that a complete PHP certificate cannot cancel such terms across modules, or that every admissible source transformation preserves this coefficient. These are different obligations. In particular the scalar restriction used to prove a representation lower bound need not preserve an unsatisfiable proof system. The actual normalization used in Section 3 has separate companion-image certificates.

Evidence. No new numerical run is needed for this composition. It uses the exact proper-union identity and collected coefficient, the proved cut-rank formula, and the preceding complete code matrices and NS templates. The substitutions and budget calculations are stated above in full; this entry does not relabel those archived checks as new computations. Dependency and provenance notes accompany the measured record.

Route assessment. The easy expansion of the formal matrix certificate is now ruled out for an actual supplied source-module witness. A better witness or a global coupling argument remains possible. No additional PHP lower-bound coverage follows.

Next bounded question. Try to replace the retained union value by \(P_1q_z\) using the remaining child coefficients, then reconstruct the source modules within their original budgets. Stop at a valid source transfer or an explicit cost obstruction; a nonlinear map on raw coefficient variables cannot be treated as automatically degree preserving.
