14 September 2026 — Fold eligible OR unions by rebuilding their costed source witnesses

Status: working binary modular-NS source transfer, with an application to the retained code comparison and complete finite certificates. It is not an arbitrary NS/PC substitution theorem or a full PHP lower bound.

Question and stopping point. Can the retained union be replaced by the product of its children without inheriting the hard collected cofactors of its supplied witness? We prove a sufficient cost test, apply it to that actual source pattern, and check a second comparison using the folded value. This develops the existing structural NS prefix/companion bounds and modular source interface; it does not infer NS bounds from the older PC-only virtual-interface results.

1. Costed value data must include prefix errors

Fix one retained polynomial system \(\Gamma\). For a value \(v\), indexed inputs \(g_i\), input bounds \(\deg g_i\le\mu_i\), and cost \(s\), use the following data:

\[ \deg v\le s,\qquad R_v=1-v-\sum_iU_i g_i\in\mathcal I_s(\Gamma),\qquad \deg U_i+\mu_i\le s, \tag{FOLD-prefix} \]
\[ g_iv\in\mathcal I_{s+\mu_i}(\Gamma),\qquad v^2-v\in\mathcal I_{2s}(\Gamma). \tag{FOLD-companions} \]

Every membership includes a supplied ordinary NS certificate. Bounds on nonzero prefixes are understood individually. The cost \(s\) is not automatically the smaller collected degree of \(v\).

A genuine binary ENS product has such data with its structural product weight: its prefix residual is zero, companions are axioms, and Booleanity has the usual domain certificate. A non-OR value can use the singleton input \(1-v\), prefix one, and its Booleanity certificate, taking \(\mu=s\). Literal negation and binary MOD sums retain their costed Booleanity bounds.

The prefix residual matters after canonical substitutions. If an affine source map supplies \(\Phi(P)-v\) through \(s\), input differences \(\Phi(g_i)-g'_i\) through \(\mu_i\), and \(\deg\Phi(U_i)+\mu_i\le s\), then

\[ 1-v-\sum_i\Phi(U_i)g'_i =(\Phi(P)-v)+\sum_i\Phi(U_i)(\Phi(g_i)-g'_i) \in\mathcal I_s. \]

Thus the earlier canonical source comparisons retain costed prefix data through their original weights, even where the virtual value lacks a literal exact prefix identity. Their companion and Booleanity witnesses retain the same structural ceilings. A constant or affine canonical value does not justify lowering this proof cost by itself.

2. Products add profile costs, and local OR witnesses still work

Working closure lemma. If \(a,b\) have the displayed data at costs \(s_a,s_b\), their product \(v=ab\) has the data for the concatenated input tuple at cost \(s=s_a+s_b\).

Proof. Set the new prefixes to \(U_i^a\) on the first tuple and \(aU_j^b\) on the second. Then \(R_v=R_a+aR_b\), with an NS certificate through \(s\). Their individual input-weight inequalities also fit \(s\). Multiply each first-child companion witness by \(b\), and each second-child witness by \(a\); these fit \(s+\mu_i\). Finally

\[ (ab)^2-ab=b^2(a^2-a)+a(b^2-b) \]

has an NS certificate through \(2(s_a+s_b)\). This is ordinary NS multiplication of complete witnesses, with its full degree cost, not PC final-line reuse.

Local module lemma. Suppose \(c,a,b\) have these data for an input tuple and its two indexed parts, with costs \(s_0,s_1,s_2\). The proper source relation \(c-ab\) has an NS witness through \(s_0+s_1+s_2\). The existing prefix certificate acquires exactly the residual correction

\[ \begin{aligned} c-ab={}& \sum_{i\in I_1}U_i^1(g_ic) +\sum_{j\in I_2}aU_j^2(g_jc)\\ &-\sum_{i\in I_1}bU_i^0(g_ia) -\sum_{j\in I_2}aU_j^0(g_jb)\\ &+cR_1+caR_2-abR_0. \end{aligned} \tag{FOLD-OR} \]

Substituting \(1-v_k=\sum_iU_i^kg_i+R_k\) proves the identity. Each prefix cancels the matching input weight in the supplied companion bound; the remaining value multipliers give at most the sum of the three costs. The residual terms have the same bound. This supplies ordinary NS witnesses for the OR and MP modules used by the binary source.

3. A source fold is valid when the replacement fits its original weight

Start with the coherent binary modular source identity

\[ 1=\sum_\alpha Q_\alpha H_\alpha,\qquad \deg_wQ_\alpha+\nu_\alpha\le D, \]

using the supplied structural OR/Booleanity ceilings. Suppose a retained union selector \(Z_0\), of original weight \(w_0\), has two coherent subgroup values with costed data at \(s_1,s_2\) over the intended remaining system. The subgroup inputs must be the actual indexed partition of the union's inputs. Require

\[ s_1+s_2\le w_0. \tag{FOLD-eligibility} \]

Replace \(Z_0\) everywhere by the product of those child expressions, delete its fresh coefficient block, and rebuild every later genuine product on its actual changed inputs. Require the dependency order to remain acyclic. A single proper union with children independent of its own coefficients has this property; for several folds, process an acyclic graph of strict ENS dependencies and proper subgroup inclusions and check the cost inequality at each fold.

Working modular-NS transfer. If the starting values have their supplied costed data within the original structural weights, these folds preserve the source degree ceiling \(D\), provided the rebuilt local witnesses fit the carried \(\nu_\alpha\). For the standard binary source ceilings, this last condition follows from the nonincreasing value costs and (FOLD-OR); any separately sharpened cost labels must be checked individually.

Proof. A folded value has cost at most its original weight by the product lemma. A remaining genuine product keeps fresh coefficients and has rebuilt input degrees no larger than their original bounds; its original structural product weight is therefore still an upper bound for its costed data. Existing earlier canonical values retain their supplied certificates. This gives a simultaneous interpretation over one final retained system, in the stated acyclic order. In the row-local-first application, a nonlocal fold does not alter the earlier dependency-closed row-local certificates or the old boundary/clause certificates.

The formal replacement is a ring homomorphism on the old variables and named selectors, fixing the target one. Each replaced formal coordinate has weighted degree at most its original weight; remaining coordinates may keep their old upper bounds or a proved smaller bound. Hence every transformed outer coefficient has degree at most \(\deg_wQ_\alpha\). The new module targets receive freshly reconstructed NS witnesses through their carried ceilings: use (FOLD-OR) for OR/MP, the costed Booleanity data for Boolean modules, and literal binary negation/MOD identities for the associated values. Multiplying those witnesses by the transformed outer coefficients proves one through \(D\).

This uses the established binary formal source composition; it does not recompile a PC-only conditional interface into NS. The number of retained blocks and ENS levels does not increase, and the folded coefficient block disappears. Expressions can be retained as factored acyclic data; no bound on expanded NS monomial counts or ROABP width is asserted.

Scope. This is a transfer for the supplied costed modular source certificate, with its original weights. It is not a claim about an arbitrary NS certificate over the specialized system. Raw internal coefficients of the old module witnesses are replaced by new witnesses, not silently substituted through a nonlinear map. Nor does it automatically give a PC replay theorem for arbitrary intermediate lines.

4. The hard code comparison satisfies the cost test

In the audited family, after the certified child normalization, let \(A=P_1\), \(\chi_b=\prod_jL_{bj}\), and \(q_z=\prod_b(\chi_b+z)\). The wide affine side has genuine cost \(s_A=2h\). The normalized nonlinear side has cost \(s_B=h^2\): its exact prefixes have degree at most \(h^2-h\), its companions have NS witnesses through \(h^2+h\), and its Booleanity through \(2h^2\). These are proved costs, not just the product's degree.

\[ s_A+s_B=h^2+2h \le 2h^2+h=w_0\qquad(h\ge2). \]

Thus the union can be folded to \(P_1q_z\) within its original source weight. Its designated comparison becomes literally zero. Other comparisons using the same union value need not become zero; (FOLD-OR) reconstructs their witnesses. Later ENS inputs use the new product value and must be rebuilt. This is an additional removal in the original costed binary source, not elimination of the remaining wide affine side or an application of the original affine-coordinate matrix theorem to the changed inputs.

The existing paired-factor assignment gives a concrete realization of the same value. With \(r^1_{u,i}\) the affine-side coefficients, set union coefficients on the old signals to \((\chi_u+z)r^1_{u,i}\), and coefficients on the nonlinear inputs \(1-\chi_b+z\) to \(\delta_{ub}\). Each union factor becomes \((\chi_u+z)(1-\sum_i r^1_{u,i}t_i)\). Its product is \(P_1q_z\).

That assignment has coefficient degree \(h+1\). Its coefficient-field images can have degree \(2h+2\), exceeding their original degree-two budgets. Therefore it does not prove degree-preserving substitution for arbitrary raw NS cofactors. The source transfer instead uses the costed formal replacement and reconstructed witnesses.

The original weights matter even after child normalization: the intermediate genuine union has degree \(h(h+1)\), whereas its folded value can have degree \(h^2+2h\). The latter fits the original \(2h^2+h\) source weight, but not the smaller intermediate product degree. The theorem retains that source provenance; it does not grant the same conclusion for an arbitrary newly chosen refutation of the intermediate system.

Limit of the mechanism. Two untouched affine child products each cost \(2h\), while their untouched affine union originally weighs \(2h\). Their sum \(4h\) fails (FOLD-eligibility). The old terminal-product obstruction remains active. The present gain comes from a proved cost reduction before folding, not from making all wide OR products exact for free.

5. A nonzero affected comparison and full certificates

The compiled checker uses \(h=2\), five independent affine-side signals, four formal linear-form variables, and a free modifier. The folded union has cost eight within its original weight ten. A second partition of its seven inputs defines two retained genuine blocks \(D,E\), each of current cost six. The affected target \(P_1q_z-P_DP_E\) is nonzero. Its complete rebuilt witness fits \(8+6+6=20\), within the original source ceiling thirty.

The test deliberately changes one affine-side prefix by \(t_2^2-t_2\). This creates the nonzero certified residual \(t_1(t_2^2-t_2)\). Omitting the residual correction in (FOLD-OR) gives an incorrect ordinary polynomial identity; adding it restores the target. This checks the new costed-prefix issue rather than only the trivial designated comparison.

Eleven full NS certificates are saved: seven virtual companions, the prefix residual, folded Booleanity, the nonzero affected comparison, and one coefficient-field image. The last has degree six, contradicting a proposed degree-two image budget. Complete original generators, current products, prefixes, cofactor polynomials, and the paired coefficient map are retained. The ordinary polynomial calculations use exact \(\mathbb F_2\) arithmetic; the local system is not a complete PHP refutation. Dense code linear substitutions can be composed using the previous Frobenius certificates without expanding or rerunning their archived code enumeration.

The complete output, reproduction and schema, source hashes, timing, and command evidence accompany this checkpoint. All compilation and certificate checks passed.

Route assessment. We have a new degree-preserving operation on the actual binary modular source and an application eliminating the union responsible for the preceding supplied-witness obstruction. The wide child and general nonlinear source remain; ordinary untouched affine unions fail the cost test. This is concrete preprocessing progress, not a superpolynomial lower bound.

Next bounded question. Determine which further unions in the retained source become eligible after the existing canonical and affine packing passes, and whether repeated costed folds reduce a previously unhandled source class. Stop at an explicit application or a retained family whose cost inequalities still fail.

14 September 2026 — Sparse selector dependence collapses the compiled binary source to one affine level

Status: working modular-NS source reduction and restricted-source exclusion, using the earlier one-level theorem. No unrestricted Frege lower bound or unaudited preservation claim for proof conversion/balancing.

Question and stopping point. Does repeated costed folding cover a larger actual source class? We give a sufficient condition on the retained input lists, reduce the entire such source to one-level affine-bit ENS, and apply the existing exclusion theorem. We also identify the limitation of ordinary affine packing. The condition is imposed on the chosen compiled source, not silently on the original proof's syntax.

1. Keep compact bits by using virtual clause values

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), with the compact base \(\mathcal Q_n=\{E_{ii'}\}\cup{\rm BOOL}_b\). Start with the coherent binary source while the original clause products still have formal names. A compact clause has inputs \(g_t=b_{it}+b_{i't}\) and \(E_{ii'}=\prod_{t\le\ell}(1-g_t)\).

Give this clause the virtual value zero. Taking \(U_t=\prod_{s<t}(1-g_s)\) supplies

\[ 1-0-\sum_t U_tg_t=E_{ii'}\in\mathcal I_\ell(\mathcal Q_n). \tag{SPARSE-clause} \]

Its companions and Booleanity are zero; the input-weighted prefix inequalities fit cost \(\ell\le2h\) when \(h\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil\). Thus it has the required costed NS profile within its original clause weight. The final PHP product has value one and, after this replacement, its input clause values are zero, so its profile is immediate. Other constant boundary products are treated consistently.

Assign the formal clause names zero and the goal name one by a ring homomorphism. This retains the costed source identity with target one and yields all other retained inputs in the form

\[ g_{a,i}(b,Z)=L_{a,i}(b)+\sum_{c<a}\alpha_{a,i;c}Z_c, \qquad L_{a,i}\text{ affine in bits}. \tag{SPARSE-inputs} \]

The structural source profile follows from literal negation/MOD2 and named OR values. Unlike assigning a value to a formal clause name, replacing the old polynomial \(E_{ii'}(b)\) by zero while fixing all bits is not a ring homomorphism; we do not do that. The costed prefix residual (SPARSE-clause) supplies the needed old-base certificate. No functional-unary decoding, row-local projection, or hybrid conditioning is used in this presentation.

2. Retain the affine part and make the remaining input product exact

For a retained block \(a\), call an input position dependent if its collected expression in (SPARSE-inputs) has a nonzero coefficient of a retained earlier selector. Let \(J_a\) be those positions and \(m_a=|J_a|\). This counts input positions, not the number of selectors mentioned by one input. Let \(I_a\) contain the other positions, whose inputs are old affine bit forms.

Introduce, if needed, a fresh accuracy-\(h\) ENS block \(A_a\) only on the affine tuple indexed by \(I_a\). Its product has cost \(s(A_a)\le2h\). An empty affine tuple has value one and cost zero; an entirely constant tuple can use its actual smaller structural cost. All these new blocks depend only on old bits and have mutually disjoint coefficients.

Suppose the earlier source selectors already have interpreted values \(V_c\). Let \(G_{a,i}=g_{a,i}(b,V)\), and choose certified degree bounds \(\deg G_{a,i}\le\mu_{a,i}\). Define

\[ T_a=\prod_{i\in J_a}(1-G_{a,i}),\qquad V_a=A_aT_a,\qquad s_a=s(A_a)+\sum_{i\in J_a}\mu_{a,i}. \tag{SPARSE-value} \]

The exact product \(T_a\) has a costed profile of weight \(\sum_{i\in J_a}\mu_{a,i}\): its usual prefixes satisfy the individual input-weight bounds, and

\[ G_{a,i}T_a =-(G_{a,i}^2-G_{a,i}) \prod_{\substack{j\in J_a\\j\ne i}}(1-G_{a,j}) \]

has an NS certificate through \(\sum_{j\in J_a}\mu_{a,j}+\mu_{a,i}\). Here every primitive remaining variable is Boolean, so \(G_{a,i}^2-G_{a,i}\) has its direct domain certificate through \(2\mu_{a,i}\). Product Booleanity fits twice the total cost. Combining this with the affine block by profile multiplication proves all required data for \(V_a\).

The affine subgroup need not already be a named source block. Adding \(A_a\) and discarding the original block replaces at most one block by one; its tuple is a subset of the original input list. It adds no level beyond the single old-affine level. The exact tail introduces no fresh ENS block. This is an interpretation of the costed modular source, with freshly proved witnesses, not a substitution theorem for arbitrary raw coefficients.

3. Fewer than \(h\) dependent positions suffice at every block

Retain each block's original input degrees \(d_{a,i}\), \(\delta_a=\max_i d_{a,i}\), and product weight \(w_a=h(\delta_a+1)\). Use the already certified scalar/constant cleanup, and omit zero input positions where they do not affect the product. The ordinary weighted source reflection ensures that an input with a retained nonconstant selector has original degree at least that selector's original product weight, hence at least \(h\).

Working source theorem. Suppose

\[ m_a\le h-1\quad\text{for every retained block }a. \tag{SPARSE-condition} \]

Then the supplied binary costed modular NS certificate of degree \(D\) yields an NS refutation through \(D\) of \(\mathcal Q_n\) plus a one-level affine-bit ENS family, with no more blocks or input positions than the original retained family.

Proof. Interpret blocks in their original strict dependency order by (SPARSE-value). Inductively suppose each earlier \(V_c\) has a proved cost \(s_c\le w_c\). Since (SPARSE-inputs) is affine in named earlier selectors, each transformed input can be bounded by its original degree: choose \(\mu_{a,i}\le d_{a,i}\). This is a structural upper bound; cancellations can only improve it.

If \(m_a=0\), the block is already old-affine, and its fresh affine realization has cost at most \(w_a\), including constant cases. If \(m_a>0\), then \(\delta_a\ge h\), and

\[ s_a\le2h+(h-1)\delta_a \le h(\delta_a+1)=w_a. \tag{SPARSE-budget} \]

This proves the induction. More generally the exact sufficient test is \(s(A_a)+\sum_{i\in J_a}\mu_{a,i}\le w_a\); the uniform count bound is only a convenient sufficient condition. When \(I_a\) is empty, \(m_a\le h\) already suffices by the same estimate without the affine-block cost.

In the final system all \(A_a\) are old-affine blocks at one level. The interpreted values may depend on many of them, but these are polynomials, not additional extension axioms. Their profile witnesses are valid over the same final system: the construction uses only its genuine affine companions and primitive Boolean domains, along with the old compact clauses for the boundary profiles.

The interpretation is a degree-contracting homomorphism on the source's formal coordinates. The modular NS reconstruction therefore transforms the complete source identity through its original degree \(D\), retaining the carried standard local ceilings. Fresh affine input lists and coefficient scopes form a valid one-level ENS family of polynomial inventory when the original source has polynomial inventory. This does not assert a low-degree replay of an arbitrary NS certificate in raw extension variables or of arbitrary PC lines.

4. The existing one-level theorem excludes this compiled source class

Take logarithmic \(h\ge2\ell\), polynomial retained inventory \(M\), and \(D=\operatorname{polylog}n\). The proved one-level affine-bit exclusion forbids the endpoint produced above, for sufficiently large \(n\). Its parameter choice \(k=\lceil\sqrt{(n+1)\log(4M)}\rceil\) gives old degree \(k(D+1)<n/2\). An empty final family is ruled out by the compact base's own PC degree barrier.

Restricted-source consequence. A valid costed binary modular NS source refutation in this parameter range cannot satisfy (SPARSE-condition). At least one retained OR block must have \(h\) or more input positions genuinely depending on retained earlier selectors, after the specified virtual clause/constant boundary treatment.

The hypothetical polynomial-size bounded-depth ordinary-PHP proof supplies the required degree and inventory through the chosen balanced compact compiler. Thus the conclusion applies to that compiled source. We have not proved that Boolean label conversion, its auxiliary equivalence proofs, or proof balancing preserves a corresponding sparsity property of the original Frege proof. This is not yet an unrestricted Frege lower bound, nor a new lower bound for a named proof fragment based only on its surface syntax.

5. Coverage examples and the remaining dense case

A three-level ledger. At \(h=3\), start with two affine blocks, each with seven old affine inputs and weight six. Two second-level blocks each have seven affine inputs and two dependent inputs, using the two earlier values. Their original weights are \(3(6+1)=21\), while (SPARSE-value) costs \(6+2\cdot6=18\). A third-level block with seven affine inputs and two inputs using those second-level values has original weight \(3(21+1)=66\) and new cost \(6+2\cdot18=42\). The final family consists of five one-level affine blocks. This is an exact symbolic ledger illustrating the proved construction, not a new numerical run or an instantiated PHP refutation.

The count threshold is sufficient, not necessary. With a nonempty affine part, \(m=h\), and untouched dependent inputs of degree \(2h\), the estimate gives \(2h+2h^2>h(2h+1)\), failing by \(h\). The preceding code family has \(m=h\) but its child normalization reduces each dependent input's cost to \(h\); its union does pass the more precise cost test. Conversely the count theorem permits a single dependent input to mention polynomially many earlier selectors; its degree is bounded by their maximum cost, not their sum.

Ordinary affine packing alone adds no proper affine unions using its standard costs. For consistent affine spans, assign packed rank-\(r\le2h\) indicators cost \(r\), and untouched higher-rank selectors cost \(2h\). A retained parent span of rank \(r_0>2h\) cannot pass the sum-of-child-cost test: if one child is retained and the other has positive rank, the sum exceeds \(2h\); if both are packed, their rank sum is at least \(r_0>2h\). A zero-rank child leaves an equal-span comparison, already handled by sharing. This is a statement about those standard cost labels, not a lower bound against all possible old-base profiles.

Evidence and limits. No historical numerical suite was rerun. This cycle composes the fully proved and finitely checked costed interface with the earlier affine-bit theorem; the boundary profile, global interpretation, and parameter ledger are stated here in full. Dependency and provenance notes identify the reused complete certificates.

Route assessment. The binary multilevel source gap is now narrowed by a sufficient class that collapses all remaining levels without degree loss. The unrestricted source may contain much denser dependent input lists. Whether this condition describes a useful natural proof restriction survives neither translation nor balancing automatically.

Next bounded question. Audit the actual Boolean proof conversion and balancing step for how they change selector-dependent input counts. Stop at a justified original-proof restriction to which the exclusion applies, or a concrete construction showing why the compiled-source condition does not follow from that restriction.

Process assessment. Keeping formal clause names avoided an invalid old-polynomial substitution and preserved the bit endpoint; applying the existing one-level result directly avoided spending another cycle only on conditional degree estimates.

14 September 2026 — Unbalanced PC compilation and the label-substitution gap

Status: working application of the existing PC compiler; restricted unbalanced compact-source exclusion; refutation of general sparsity preservation under literal label substitution. No unrestricted Frege or Res(\(\oplus\)) size lower bound is claimed here.

Question and stopping point. Does the new sparse-source exclusion require an unaudited preservation theorem for proof balancing or Boolean label conversion? We remove the balancing requirement by choosing the already available PC endpoint, and exhibit a direct failure of the label-substitution preservation claim. The exact transfer for a named affine-clause proof system is left for a separate complete rule audit.

1. The existing PC compiler handles the original proof DAG

Let a binary Frege proof have formula-value interpretations over one fixed retained system \(\Gamma\), with all value costs at most \(L\), using the costed prefix, companion, and Booleanity data. Keep literal negation and MOD2 definitions and coherent copies, or use the established copy interfaces.

A profile of cost \(s\le L\) gives companion proofs through \(s+\mu_i\le2L\). Under its input assumptions \(g_i=0\), the prefix identity with its certified residual proves \(1-v\) through \(s\le L\). Thus the common-system PC interface has \(A_*\le2L\), \(U_*\le L\), and copy/Booleanity ceiling \(2L\). Its OR relation ceiling is \(3L\).

The fixed Boolean-frame compiler and recorded MOD-recursion compiler therefore prove each instantiated logical axiom value through

\[ K=cL,\qquad c=\max\{M_{\rm fr},10\}. \tag{UNBAL-axioms} \]

The MOD argument uses its aligned prefix scalars, not arbitrary independent Boolean gate values; the earlier controls remain applicable.

Proof-height-free MP step. Let \(a,c,b\) be antecedent, implication, and conclusion values. The local relation is \(R=c-(1-a)b\), with a PC proof through \(3L\). From completed proofs of \(a,c\), use

\[ b=c+ab-R. \]

To derive \(ab\), multiply the final line \(a\) by the known polynomial \(b\), monomial by monomial. This does not require that \(b\) has already been proved: it is an allowed polynomial multiplier. Intermediate degrees are at most \(\deg a+\deg b\le2L\), while the existing proof ceiling for \(a\) remains \(K\). Hence the conclusion also fits \(\max\{K,3L\}=K\). Induction on the proof DAG adds no factor for height or number of inferences. Separately supplied assumption-value proofs are included in the maximum.

This is an application of the existing PC value compiler, not a new PC reuse principle. It does not convert the resulting PC proof to NS at the same degree. The important point is that the one-level affine-bit exclusion accepts PC as well as NS, so the present route does not need that conversion.

2. Sparse source exclusion applies before balancing

Take an unbalanced bounded-depth proof of the compact tautology \(\Theta_n\), or a refutation from its compact collision clauses. Give those clauses the virtual zero profiles with old residual \(E_{ii'}\); the theorem target has value one, or the refutation target FALSE has value one. Assumption clause values are literally zero.

Suppose every retained OR block, including the coherent subgroups needed by the compiler, has at most \(h-1\) selector-dependent input positions. The preceding local interpretation constructs costed profiles for every value over one final old-affine ENS family, each within its original structural source weight. This construction of the profiles does not use a balanced NS identity; it only uses the strict input dependency order and the cost inequalities.

Apply (UNBAL-axioms) directly to the original proof DAG. For fixed formula depth, its source bound \(L=(d+1)h^d\) is polylogarithmic at logarithmic accuracy. Polynomial proof size gives polynomial family inventory. At \(h\ge2\ell\), the resulting degree-\(cL\) one-level affine-bit PC refutation is excluded for sufficiently large \(n\).

Working corollary. Such an unbalanced compact proof must already have a retained block with at least \(h\) dependent input positions, unless it fails another stated source-interface hypothesis. No balancing-preservation theorem is required. The earlier NS theorem remains valid; this argument uses a different sufficient endpoint.

This condition concerns the compact bit proof and its specified virtual boundary. It still does not automatically follow from a structural restriction on an ordinary incidence-variable PHP proof before Boolean label substitution.

3. Literal label substitution can make an affine disjunction dense

Take \(m\) incidence propositions \(u_i\) from distinct pigeon rows and consider \(F_m=\bigvee_{i\le m}u_i\). Under the source's TRUE-by-zero convention, \(u_i^{\rm ap}=x_i\), so the original OR inputs \(1-x_i\) are old affine forms and have zero selector-dependent positions.

Substitute the Boolean label predicate \(\Lambda_{i,z_i}\) for \(u_i\), using the sign convention of the existing label-parent construction. Its approximation is \(1-P_{i,z_i}\), where the lower label product has affine inputs \(b_{it}+z_{it}\). The new top OR inputs are therefore

\[ (\neg\Lambda_{i,z_i})^{\rm ap}=P_{i,z_i}, \qquad i=1,\ldots,m. \tag{LABEL-dependent} \]

There are exactly \(m\) dependent positions. The label products have distinct row supports and fresh scopes, their input spans are proper, and they are not the compact pair-collision clauses assigned virtual zero. The top union is nonlocal for \(m\ge2\). Thus the specified virtual boundary and scalar cleanup do not turn this back into the original affine-bit list. One can take \(m=\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), far above logarithmic \(h\). Choosing distinct labels also permits both truth values of \(F_m\) on injective assignments to these \(m\) rows; this is a partial-row control, not a model of the full PHP base.

This is a counterexample to general preservation of the sparse-input property by the actual literal substitution. It does not construct a short PHP proof. It refines the already recorded label-parent source embedding by counting the specific parameter used in the new exclusion.

4. Packing removes label selectors but changes the old input class

At \(h\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), the existing affine coefficient map sends \(P_{i,z_i}\) to

\[ \eta_{z_i}(b_i)=\prod_{t\le\ell}(1-b_{it}-z_{it}). \]

These are old polynomials of degree exactly \(\ell\), not affine bit inputs when \(\ell\ge2\). Counting zero remaining selectors after this packing therefore does not satisfy (SPARSE-inputs): its old-affine premise has changed. Unary decoding restores affine incidence variables, but then the terminal problem is the general unary affine family, not the affine-bit family excluded earlier.

A scoped degree control. The exact old product \(\prod_{i\le m}(1-\eta_{z_i})\) is multilinear of degree \(m\ell\), because its factors use disjoint rows and its top monomial has coefficient one. More generally, any old-only value with the costed profile for this tuple over Boolean domains alone must agree with that product at every Boolean assignment: a nonzero input forces value zero by its companion, while all-zero inputs force value one by the prefix condition. Unique multilinear representation then forces ordinary degree at least \(m\ell\).

This exceeds the original top weight \(h(2h+1)\) when \(m\ell>h(2h+1)\). It explains why simply making every substituted label input exact does not satisfy the folding budget. The control is over Boolean domains alone; the old compact PHP equations or other retained companions can change the profile problem. It is not a general lower bound on profiles over the full unsatisfiable PHP system.

5. Audit scope and the next direct proof-system test

The concluding proof of BIKPRS Theorem 6.7(1) cites Krajíček's 1995 Lemma 8.4.8 for polynomial-size, logarithmic-height tree conversion with constant formula-depth overhead. We reread that passage and Definition 6.8. The passage supplies no selector-input count bound. Author and publisher links did not supply the full cited book proof; a targeted excerpt request was withdrawn once the PC compiler removed that dependency.

A prefix conjunction \(D_t=\bigwedge_{j\le t}C_j\), under the recorded flat DeMorgan convention, contains the OR of the complements of its conjuncts. When their current values are retained selectors \(Z_j\), that OR has \(t\) dependent input positions, regardless of balanced binary bracketing. This formula-pattern check illustrates why a height/depth bound alone cannot supply the desired count; it is not a claim that every balancer must retain such a block or a verification of the unread book implementation.

The source audit records primary locators, exact reading coverage, and access limits. No new third-party full text was downloaded or published, and no historical numerical suite was rerun. The previously audited bit-PHP Res(\(\oplus\)) paper was screened again at its abstract: its stated results concern bounded proof-DAG depth. No broader size lower bound is imported or claimed here.

Route assessment. The sparse-source result now applies before balancing by PC compilation; literal label substitution remains a concrete obstacle to transferring a sparsity condition from ordinary incidence-variable proofs. This makes a direct audit of an affine-clause proof system on the bit encoding a better next test than another balancing lookup.

Next bounded question. Check whether affine-clause resolution and semantic weakening have a degree-\(O(h+\ell)\) PC simulation using only one-level affine-bit ENS, including the original-degree initial-clause witnesses. Stop at a complete rule-by-rule transfer or a concrete obstruction before asserting a result for Res(\(\oplus\)).

Process assessment. Choosing the already sufficient PC endpoint removed an unnecessary balancing dependency; the accompanying small framework revision makes the required compiler stages and preservation hypotheses explicit in task selection.

14 September 2026 — A direct one-level PC simulation of Res(\(\oplus\)) and a working bit-PHP lower bound

Status: working complete rule simulation and lower-bound corollary, with exact PC traces and explicit internal dependencies. The corollary has no proof-DAG-depth restriction; the next cycle is a focused audit of its lower-bound dependency chain. The full \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege goal remains open.

Question and stopping point. Can affine-clause proofs reach the one-level affine-bit endpoint directly? We give ordinary-PC derivations for resolution, semantic weakening, both published binary rule conventions, and the original compact clauses. We then apply the existing one-level theorem. This direction is from an affine-clause proof to algebraic degree; it does not require extracting a clause proof from an arbitrary algebraic source identity.

1. Clause values and the fixed one-level system

Represent a linear clause as \(C=\bigvee_i(g_{C,i}=1)\), where \(g_{C,i}\) are affine forms over \(\mathbb F_2\). An equation \(f=\alpha\) has true-indicator \(g=1+f+\alpha\). The falsifying set \(Z(C)=\{g_{C,i}=0\ \forall i\}\) is an affine subspace or empty.

For each nonempty clause used in the proof, introduce one fresh accuracy-\(h\) block, with all companions and coefficient Booleanity:

\[ P_C=\prod_{u=1}^{h}\left(1-\sum_i r_{C,u,i}g_{C,i}\right), \qquad E_{C,i}=g_{C,i}P_C. \]

All inputs are old affine forms, so this is one level. Different blocks have disjoint coefficient scopes. Write \(P_\varnothing=1\), without introducing a block for the empty clause. The standard prefixes satisfy

\[ 1-P_C=\sum_iU_{C,i}g_{C,i},\qquad \deg P_C\le2h,\quad \deg U_{C,i}\le2h-1,\quad \deg E_{C,i}\le2h+1. \tag{RPC-prefix} \]

Zero literals can be removed; constant/tautological cases obey these upper bounds and are handled below. The fixed algebraic system contains the old base, all these companions, and all old/coefficient Boolean domains. It does not contain \(P_C=0\) as an axiom for every proof line. Those values are proved in the original proof order.

Gryaznov–Ovcharov–Riazanov, Section 2.1 uses complementary-parity resolution and one-premise semantic weakening. The Byramji–Impagliazzo presentation also describes arbitrary two-premise semantic consequences. Section 4 below covers that convention explicitly.

2. Complementary-parity resolution costs at most \(4h+1\)

Suppose the premises have input lists \((a_i)_i,u\) and \((b_j)_j,1-u\), with \(u\) affine. The conclusion \(T\) has the union of the context lists \((a_i),(b_j)\). Assume the premise values \(P_A,P_B\) have already been derived through degree \(K\). Every context companion \(a_iP_T,b_jP_T\) is available among the conclusion block's axioms; repeated literals may share that axiom.

The exact prefix identities give PC derivations through \(\max(K,4h)\) of

\[ R_A=P_T-U_{A,u}uP_T =P_AP_T+\sum_iU_{A,i}(a_iP_T), \]
\[ R_B=P_T-U_{B,1-u}(1-u)P_T =P_BP_T+\sum_jU_{B,j}(b_jP_T). \tag{RPC-resolution} \]

For example, an existing line \(P_A\) is multiplied by the known polynomial \(P_T\), giving degree at most \(4h\); a context companion of degree \(2h+1\) is multiplied by a prefix of degree at most \(2h-1\). These use completed PC lines, not multiplication of entire preceding derivations.

Since \(u\) is affine over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(u^2-u\) is a linear combination of old Booleanity axioms and has a degree-two proof. Consequently

\[ (1-u)R_A-U_{A,u}P_T(u^2-u)=(1-u)P_T \]

is derivable through \(\max(K,4h+1)\). Multiply this completed line by \(U_{B,1-u}\) and add \(R_B\). The resulting polynomial is \(P_T\), and the final multiplication has degree at most \((2h+1)+(2h-1)=4h\). Thus resolution preserves the global ceiling \(\max(K,4h+1)\), irrespective of proof height or reuse.

Every polynomial multiplication here expands into monomial-by-monomial variable multiplications and linear combinations at the stated degree. No implicit Boolean reduction or additional inference rule is used.

3. Semantic weakening costs at most \(4h\)

Suppose \(C\models D\). If \(Z(D)\ne\varnothing\), then \(Z(D)\subseteq Z(C)\), and every affine \(g_{C,i}\) vanishes on \(Z(D)\). Elementary affine linear algebra gives constants \(\lambda_{ij}\in\mathbb F_2\) with

\[ g_{C,i}=\sum_j\lambda_{ij}g_{D,j}. \]

Hence \(g_{C,i}P_D\) is a constant linear combination of the \(D\)-companions, through degree \(2h+1\). The identity

\[ P_D=P_CP_D+\sum_iU_{C,i}(g_{C,i}P_D) \tag{RPC-weakening} \]

derives \(P_D\) through \(\max(K,4h)\) from a completed degree-\(K\) proof of \(P_C\). If \(Z(D)=\varnothing\), then \(1\) is in the affine span of its input forms, so a constant combination of its companions derives \(P_D\) directly through \(2h+1\). This includes tautological clauses. Deriving an empty clause means that the proved value is already one.

4. General two-premise semantic inference has the same simulation

Affine-cover lemma. Suppose linear clauses \(A,B,D\) satisfy \(A\wedge B\models D\). Put \(W=Z(D)\). Then \(W\subseteq Z(A)\cup Z(B)\). An empty \(W\) is the tautology case, and if \(W\) lies in one of the two sets, one-premise weakening suffices.

Otherwise \(W\cap Z(A)\) and \(W\cap Z(B)\) are proper affine subspaces covering \(W\). Each has at most half its points. Therefore both have exactly half, are disjoint affine hyperplanes of \(W\), and are parallel. There is an affine parity \(u\), extended from \(W\) to the whole old variable space, that is zero on the first half and one on the second.

It follows that

\[ A\models D\vee(u=1),\qquad B\models D\vee(u=0). \]

Two semantic weakenings and one complementary-parity resolution yield \(D\), with duplicate context literals identified. An affine constant in \(u\) only switches the two parity labels. Thus this rule convention adds at most two auxiliary clause blocks per binary inference, still old-affine and at one level. The PC ceiling remains \(4h+1\). This argument uses \(\mathbb F_2\); no other-field rule equivalence is inferred.

For size accounting, clauses can be replaced by bases of their falsifying affine systems, of at most \(v+1\) equations on \(v\) old variables. Semantic equivalence preserves binary semantic consequences; the reduction above then supplies bounded-width basic-rule derivations with constant line overhead. Fresh propositional variables, if present, may first be set to constants: semantic implication survives restriction, and a resolution with a constant pivot becomes a weakening. Thus polynomial line count can be treated with polynomial total clause descriptions over the original bit variables.

5. Initial compact clauses and the complete DAG transfer

For \(n=2^\ell\), let

\[ C_{ii'}=\bigvee_{t\le\ell}(b_{it}+b_{i't}=1),\qquad E_{ii'}=\prod_{t\le\ell}(1-b_{it}-b_{i't}). \]

The old compact system \(\mathcal Q_n\) contains these \(E_{ii'}\) and bit Booleanity. Set \(g_t=b_{it}+b_{i't}\) and \(T_t=\prod_{s<t}(1-g_s)\). The ordinary identity

\[ P_{C_{ii'}}=E_{ii'}P_{C_{ii'}} +\sum_tT_t(g_tP_{C_{ii'}}) \tag{RPC-initial} \]

is an NS, hence PC, derivation through \(2h+\ell\), using the original degree-\(\ell\) old axiom. No equality polynomial has been treated as an affine axiom.

Working simulation theorem. A size-\(S\) DAG-like Res(\(\oplus\)) refutation of these linear clauses yields a one-level affine-bit ENS family of polynomial inventory and an ordinary-PC refutation over \(\mathcal Q_n\) through

\[ D=\max\{2h+\ell,\;4h+1\}. \tag{RPC-transfer} \]

Introduce all proof-clause blocks, and the constant number of auxiliary blocks for general binary semantic inferences, in one fixed family. Follow the original proof DAG: initial values follow from (RPC-initial), each rule derives its conclusion value at the same global ceiling, and the empty clause has value one. Conditional premise-value lines in the local rule proofs are replaced by their actual earlier derivations, not added as new algebraic axioms. No balancing, proof-depth restriction, or higher extension level is introduced.

The usual bit-PHP CNF has one clause for each pair \(i,i'\) and label \(z\), forbidding both labels from being \(z\). The stronger linear clause \(C_{ii'}\) semantically implies every such CNF clause: equality to the same \(z\) falsifies \(C_{ii'}\). Algebraically each \(b_{it}+b_{i't}\) is the sum of the two corresponding label-disagreement forms in that CNF clause. Therefore one semantic weakening obtains each needed CNF axiom from \(C_{ii'}\). A polynomial-size refutation of the usual CNF would give a polynomial-size refutation of the linear-clause system, so the lower-bound consequence below covers that standard encoding as well.

6. A working superpolynomial lower-bound corollary for DAG-like Res(\(\oplus\))

Working corollary. For every fixed \(K\), sufficiently large \(n=2^\ell\) admit no size-\(n^K\) DAG-like Res(\(\oplus\)) refutation of bit PHP with \(n+1\) pigeons and \(n\) holes, under either rule convention above. This includes the usual CNF encoding. No proof-DAG-depth restriction is assumed.

Proof from the internal one-level theorem. Suppose a polynomial-size refutation exists. Choose \(h=2\ell\). After the preceding constant-overhead rule/encoding transformations, (RPC-transfer) supplies a polynomial-inventory one-level affine-bit family with a PC refutation through \(D=8\ell+1\). This contradicts the one-level affine-bit exclusion.

To expose the parameter and dependency chain, if \(M\) is the resulting number of blocks, choose \(k=\lceil\sqrt{(n+1)\log(4M)}\rceil\). The simultaneous hybrid lemma and dimension estimate produce a nonzero row-linear bit polynomial \(f\) that a putative PC refutation would derive from the old compact base through

\[ B=k(D+1)=O\!\left(\sqrt n\,(\log n)^{3/2}\right)<n/2. \]

For sufficiently large \(n\), \(4(k-1)<n\). The row-linear quotient injection, transported PC inclusion, and functional matching-moment stability then forbid this old consequence. All inputs of the new family are affine in the original bit variables; all companions and coefficient domains are present; no augmented NS/PC equality is used.

This is a new working consequence of our internal lower-bound chain, not an imported theorem from the cited depth-restricted literature. The rule simulation has now been checked directly, and the cited lower-bound arguments were reread for the composition. The next focused audit will examine whether the matching-moment extension and weighted replay cover every required old constraint and PC step. The conclusion should retain its working-proof status while that audit proceeds.

This does not prove the full \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege goal, an odd-prime analogue, or a unary Res(\(\oplus\)) bound via unproved Boolean substitution. The label-conversion obstruction remains relevant to those broader transfers.

7. Complete ordinary-PC traces and falsifying controls

The compiled checker uses the existing ordinary-PC kernel and replay verifier. Every saved inference is an axiom introduction, a two-term field-linear combination, or multiplication by one variable. Polynomial multiplication in the mathematical argument is expanded into these primitive steps.

The initial run has ten complete traces at \(h=1,2\): resolution, proper semantic weakening, tautology handling, a two-row initial clause with \(\ell=2\), and a composed two-hole refutation. The strengthened run adds two genuinely binary semantic inferences, proving \(x+y=0\) from \(x=1\) and \(y=1\) via the affine-cover construction. It has twelve traces and 3,172 primitive PC lines.

14 September 2026 — A second derivation of the lower-bound chain and complete sparse moment witnesses

Status: second internal correctness audit; an alternative dual separation proof and an ordinary-restriction proof recover the working bit-PHP Res(\(\oplus\)) size consequence. No gap was found in this pass. This is not external peer review or a full \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege lower bound.

Question and stopping point. Check whether the matching-moment argument omits any truncated old constraints or couples row sets incorrectly, then verify its use in the new size consequence. We rederive completeness and old PC closure, construct a different separating functional, and recover the needed one-level exclusion with slightly larger logarithmic accuracy. The finite audit checks the complete sparse moment system, including a case with \(k>\ell\).

1. The matching marginals are the complete ordinary-NS constraints

Use the functional unary system on \(m\) rows and \(N\ge1\) columns, over \(\mathbb F_2\): Booleanity, same-row and same-column exclusions, and \(\rho_i-1\), \(\rho_i=\sum_jX_{ij}\). Let \(\mathcal I_B\) use the degree of each ordinary generator multiple. Cancellation between larger-degree multiples does not make them members of \(\mathcal I_B\).

Booleanity reduces powers, and row/column exclusions kill every nonmatching squarefree monomial, without increasing degree. Thus a functional annihilating their multiples is specified by matching moments \(z_T\), \(|T|\le B\); conversely assigning matching moments and extending by this normal form annihilates every such multiple.

For a row-equation multiplier \(q\) of degree at most \(B-1\), replacing \(q\) by its matching normal form changes \(q(\rho_i-1)\) by Booleanity/exclusion consequences through \(B\). It therefore suffices to test a matching monomial \(X_T\). If row \(i\) is already occupied, \(X_T(\rho_i-1)\) reduces to zero. Otherwise its reduction is the sum of legal one-cell extensions in row \(i\), minus \(X_T\). Hence the complete remaining equations are exactly

\[ \sum_{j\notin{\rm col}(T)}z_{T\cup\{(i,j)\}}=z_T, \qquad |T|<B,\quad i\notin{\rm row}(T). \tag{AUD-marginals} \]

Normalization adds \(z_\varnothing=1\); zero-normalized annihilator directions instead have \(z_\varnothing=0\). There are no multiplicativity or positivity constraints on these finite-field linear functionals. This verifies the completeness premise of the earlier moment extension argument.

2. Row-set extension and old PC closure

The same extension argument works for any \(m\ge B\), not only \(m=N+1\), when \(N\ge2B-1\). Starting from any consistent moments through degree \(k\le B\), fill the degrees \(s=k+1,\ldots,B\). At degree one each row total can equal the prescribed constant moment because \(N\ge1\).

For \(s\ge2\), fix an \(s\)-row set \(S\). Its prescribed \((s-1)\)-matching moments form a reduced \((s-2)\)-cycle in the chessboard complex \(\Delta_{s,N}\). At \(s=2\), the augmentation is the sum of two equal row totals and is zero. At larger \(s\), a face missing two rows has boundary coefficient equal to the sum of their two already prescribed marginal sums, \(z_T+z_T=0\).

The already audited BLVZ connectivity theorem gives \(\widetilde H_{s-2}(\Delta_{s,N};\mathbb F_2)=0\) for \(N\ge2s-1\). A filling supplies all degree-\(s\) moments on \(S\), and its boundary equation is precisely (AUD-marginals). A top matching has exactly one occupied row set. Therefore different \(S\)'s have disjoint new unknowns; every shared lower face has its single previously assigned value, which each filling respects. This accounts for cross-row-set consistency rather than assuming it.

Thus every prescribed normalized degree-\(k\) design extends through \(B\). Normalized designs exist and their linear span is the full annihilator of \(\mathcal I_k\): subtracting one fixed normalized design generates the zero-normalized directions. Finite-dimensional duality gives

\[ \mathcal I_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le k}=\mathcal I_k. \]

At an ordinary-PC multiplication \(f\mapsto Xf\) within degree \(B\), nonzero \(f\) has degree at most \(B-1\). If \(f\in\mathcal I_B\), stability puts it in \(\mathcal I_{B-1}\), so \(Xf\in\mathcal I_B\). Linear combinations preserve \(\mathcal I_B\). Conversely NS multiples have PC derivations within their own degree. This proves \(\mathcal C_B=\mathcal I_B\), restating the old stability theorem with its needed arbitrary-row-count scope. It does not assert augmented ENS stability or use an implicit multilinear multiplication rule.

3. A separate dual witness for row-linear bit polynomials

Let \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), \(m=n+1\), \(1\le k\le B\), \(4(k-1)<n\), and \(n\ge2B-1\). Take nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\), the space using at most one bit from each occupied row in any monomial. If \(f\) is constant, a normalized degree-\(B\) design separates it. Otherwise choose a nonzero monomial on a maximum occupied row set \(S\), \(|S|=t\), and let \(a_i\) be its selected bit coordinate in row \(i\).

Choose pairwise disjoint two-point coordinate lines \(C_i=\{c_i,c_i+e_{a_i}\}\) among the hole labels. Each direction has \(n/2\) cosets; the previously chosen lines forbid at most \(2(t-1)<n/2\) of them, so greedy selection works. Let \(F=\bigcup_{i\in S}C_i\), \(|F|=2t\).

On the remaining \(m-t\) rows and \(n-2t\) columns outside \(F\), choose a normalized matching design \(\lambda\) through degree \(B-t\). Section 2 supplies it because

\[ n-2t\ge2(B-t)-1. \]

The remaining column set is nonempty under the present line-selection hypotheses; degree zero is the trivial normalized constant functional.

Define \(\mu\) on matching monomials of degree at most \(B\). It is zero unless the matching occupies every row in \(S\) at a column in that row's line, and every other occupied row uses a column outside \(F\). In the remaining case, let \(U\) be the matching on rows outside \(S\) and set

\[ \mu(X_T)=\lambda(X_U). \tag{AUD-tensor} \]

Extend to ordinary monomials by Boolean power reduction and zero on collisions. This is a zero-normalized functional, not a probability distribution.

Marginal check. If \(T\) is missing at least two selected rows, one extension cannot make its value nonzero. If it misses exactly one selected row and the marginal adds that row, its two allowed line endpoints contribute the same residual moment twice, giving zero, as does the right side. Any already forbidden column or wrong selected-row label keeps all terms zero. If all selected rows are present, a marginal for another row is exactly a marginal of \(\lambda\) on columns outside \(F\). These exhaust (AUD-marginals), so \(\mu\) annihilates the full old \(\mathcal I_B\), hence \(\mathcal C_B\).

Under the affine decoder \(\tau(b_{ia})=\sum_{z:z_a=1}X_{iz}\), every monomial of \(\tau f\) occupies at most \(t\) rows after collision reduction. Only the chosen set \(S\) can contribute to \(\mu(\tau f)\). The residual matching is empty and \(\lambda(1)=1\), so this value is the sum of the top row coefficient over \(\prod_{i\in S}C_i\). That sum is the mixed one-bit finite difference isolating the selected monomial's coefficient, namely one. Therefore

\[ \mu(\tau f)=1,\qquad \tau f\notin\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}). \tag{AUD-separation} \]

This provides a different proof of the row-linear separation used in the lower bound. It directly constructs the separating direction, without the earlier top-coefficient description of an NS certificate. The affine decoder's original-degree axiom witnesses still transfer any old compact PC consequence into the functional system.

4. A second one-level argument using ordinary polynomial restrictions

For this audit, take \(h=3\ell\), slightly more accuracy than the earlier \(2\ell\) proof. Let \(M\ge1\) be the number of proper one-level affine blocks, set \(v=(n+1)\ell\), and choose \(k=\lceil\sqrt{(n+1)\log(4M)}\rceil\). Low blocks have rank at most \(h(k+1)\); high blocks have rank at least \(r_*=3\ell(k+1)+1\).

Restrict \(\mathcal L_k\) to a high block's zero flat using affine free coordinates, as ordinary polynomials rather than Boolean remainders. The image dimension is at most \(\binom{v-r+k}{k}\). With \(m=n+1\), for sufficiently large boards in the polynomial-\(M\) regime,

\[ \frac{\binom{v-r_*+k}{k}}{\binom mk\ell^k} =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1} \left(1-\frac{r_*-1-(\ell+1)j}{v-\ell j}\right) \le e^{-k^2/m}. \tag{AUD-ordinary-dimension} \]

Indeed the numerator of each subtracted fraction is at least \(\ell k\), while its denominator is at most \(m\ell\). Thus the sum of the high restriction dimensions is at most \(\frac14\binom mk\ell^k<\dim\mathcal L_k\). A nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\) restricts to the zero ordinary polynomial on every high flat.

In affine coordinates whose first coordinates are a basis of that block's inputs, every monomial of \(f\) has one of those coordinates as a factor. Consequently \(f=\sum_i a_i g_i\) literally, with \(\deg a_i\le k-1\). Assign these coefficients to the first factor row and zero to the others, making the high product \(1-f\). Its weighted companion \(fg_i(1-f)=-g_i(f^2-f)\) has an old Boolean NS certificate through \(2k+1\).

For low rank \(r\le h(k+1)\), distribute the affine basis complements among \(h\) bins of size at most \(k+1\). Factor telescoping assigns old-only coefficients of degree at most \(k\) and makes the exact zero-flat indicator. Each companion image has a Boolean certificate through \(r+1\), so multiplication by \(f\) costs at most \(r+1+k\le k(2h+1)+k\). Coefficient-field images times \(f\) cost at most \(3k\), and old axioms keep their standard multiplied witnesses.

Multiply every substituted PC line by \(f\). At a source multiplication the preceding ordinary degree is at most \(D-1\); its substituted variable has degree at most \(k\). Every primitive replay step therefore fits \(B=k(D+1)\). The final old consequence is \(f\). For polynomial \(M\) and polylogarithmic \(D\), \(B<n/2\) and \(4(k-1)<n\) eventually, contradicting (AUD-separation). Zero/unit spans are handled by the already available scalar cleanup.

This recovers the needed one-level exclusion through an ordinary-restriction kernel and literal affine ideal membership. It does not change the earlier \(h\ge2\ell\) statement; it supplies a separate sufficient argument at \(h=3\ell\).

5. The concrete Res(\(\oplus\)) consequence survives this audit

The direct clause simulation works at every accuracy. Set \(h=3\ell\); a hypothetical polynomial-size proof yields polynomial block/input inventory and ordinary-PC degree \(D=12\ell+1\). Section 4 excludes that endpoint. Thus this second derivation recovers the same working superpolynomial size lower bound for DAG-like Res(\(\oplus\)) on bit PHP.

The checked chain keeps the following distinctions explicit: matching moment equations describe NS annihilation, while old PC closure needs the extension argument; the hybrid replay uses one simultaneous old-only map and pays \(k(D+1)\); the clause simulation adds only affine-input blocks and reuses completed PC lines; the usual CNF follows by semantic weakening from the compact pair-difference clauses. No balancing, augmented NS/PC equality, unary proof substitution, or bound on expanded PC monomial count is required. Family inventory is the polynomial quantity.

No mathematical correction to the working size consequence was identified in this pass. The imported BLVZ theorem is reused with its audited statement; this is a second algebraic derivation and internal audit, not a new proof of its topology or external verification of the research.

6. Complete sparse moment evidence, including \(k>\ell\)

The independent compiled checker constructs (AUD-tensor) with residual design degree two. On the residual board choose distinct columns \(q,a,b\). Every first row moment is concentrated at \(q\); for each ordered pair of rows the only nonzero pair moments are at \((q,a),(b,a),(b,q)\). Their row/column sums are exactly the required first moments over \(\mathbb F_2\).

\((8,3,2,4)\)2846489

The first board tests the old degree range near its boundary. The second has \(k>\ell\) and repeats a bit direction on different rows, addressing the regime needed by the new row-linear argument. In both cases the functional selects exactly the prescribed row-bit monomial and vanishes on all other degree-at-most-\(k\) row-linear basis elements. For other row sets or lower degrees this follows from the support of the complete moment table; all bit-axis choices on the selected rows are evaluated explicitly.

The checker forms every marginal with a nonzero left contribution or right moment. Each nonzero moment contributes every one of its faces, and every nonzero lower moment contributes every missing-row right side. Therefore an unlisted marginal has only zero entries on both sides. This is a complete sparse representation of 184,041 possible row equations in the first case and 1,903,909,999,986,644,001 in the second; those enormous zero portions were not enumerated. Booleanity/exclusion annihilation is supplied by the ordinary normal-form definition.

Deleting one top moment gives exactly four and eight violated marginal equations respectively. This control preserves the support convention but breaks the required cross-row constraints, so an isolated nonzero bit evaluation alone would not pass the audit. The complete output is 45,569,198 bytes and is retained as sparse moment tables, every nontrivial marginal, basis evaluations, and corruption witnesses. Commands and schema, source hashes, timing, and full command output accompany it. The final build and all mathematical checks passed; a preliminary indentation warning was corrected before the run.

14 September 2026 — All-prime affine exclusion, complete power-input transfer, and the two MOD polarities

Status: working proofs extending the binary affine-family argument to every fixed prime, with an actual nonlinear one-level application and exact finite checks over \(\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\). General complemented MOD inputs and the full Frege source remain open.

Question and stopping point. Does the odd-prime obstruction come from the lower-bound engine or from the shape of actual modular inputs? We first check the signs and field domains in the engine, then test both source polarities. The result is a complete all-prime affine theorem and a factor-two transfer for entire systems with inputs \(L_i^{p-1}\). A large-zero-set example limits the complementary-predicate rank argument, but that example itself also admits a degree-preserving transfer.

1. Matching extension and old PC stability over every field

Use the functional unary system on \(m\) rows and \(N\) columns over an arbitrary field \(\mathbb K\): Booleanity, same-row and same-column exclusions, and \(\rho_i-1\). Assume \(m\ge B\), \(N\ge1\), and \(N\ge2B-1\). The ordinary matching normal form works in every characteristic. Its complete remaining constraints are

\[ \sum_{j\notin{\rm col}(T)}z_{T\cup\{(i,j)\}}=z_T, \qquad |T|<B,\quad i\notin{\rm row}(T). \tag{OP-marginals} \]

To extend prescribed moments from degree \(k\) to \(B\), perform the earlier row-set construction with orientations. For an \(s\)-row set \(S=\{i_0<\cdots<i_{s-1}\}\), orient each matching by increasing row order. Give a prescribed \((s-1)\)-matching missing row \(i_j\) the chain coefficient \((-1)^jz_T\). This is the boundary that the new top matching moments must realize.

For a face missing rows \(i_a,i_b\), \(a<b\), the two boundary contributions have signs \((-1)^{a+b}\) and \((-1)^{a+b-1}\). Their marginal sums are the same previously assigned moment, so they cancel. At \(s=2\), the reduced augmentation is the difference of the two equal row totals. Thus the prescribed chain is a reduced cycle, including outside characteristic two.

The primary BLVZ Theorem 1.1 gives \((s-2)\)-connectivity of the \(s\times N\) chessboard complex when \(N\ge2s-1\). Consequently its reduced homology in degree \(s-2\) vanishes over every field. A filling supplies exactly (OP-marginals): the top boundary and the prescribed chain have the same \((-1)^j\) factors. New top matchings belong to unique row sets, so independent fillings respect all shared lower moments. Degree one is filled by assigning each row its prescribed total. This is a field extension of our earlier argument, not a new topological theorem.

Every normalized degree-\(k\) design therefore extends. Normalized designs span the annihilator once one normalized design is fixed. Duality, followed by the ordinary-PC multiplication argument, gives

\[ \mathcal I_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le k}=\mathcal I_k,\qquad \mathcal C_B=\mathcal I_B. \tag{OP-stability} \]

For the second equality, a nonzero predecessor multiplied by a variable within degree \(B\) has degree at most \(B-1\); the first equality places it in \(\mathcal I_{B-1}\). Its multiplication stays in \(\mathcal I_B\). The converse follows by deriving each NS multiple within its ordinary degree. These are statements about the old functional system, with no augmented ENS equality.

2. The compact encoding and signed row-linear separation

For a prime \(p\), \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), and \(m=n+1\), define the appropriate compact base over \(\mathbb F_p\) by

\[ \mathcal Q_{n,p}=\{E^{(p)}_{ii'}\}\cup{\rm BOOL}_b,\qquad E^{(p)}_{ii'}=\prod_{t=1}^{\ell} \left(1-(b_{it}-b_{i't})^{p-1}\right). \tag{OP-base} \]

These collision equations have original degree \(\gamma=(p-1)\ell\). On Boolean labels each factor tests equality of the corresponding bits. The binary polynomial is recovered at \(p=2\); it must not simply be reused unchanged at odd primes.

The decoder remains \(\tau(b_{it})=\sum_{z:z_t=1}X_{iz}\). Boolean images have degree-two certificates using unary Booleanity and same-row exclusions. For a collision image, work first in the two involved rows with their Booleanity, exclusions, and row equations. Any polynomial of degree \(d\) in those rows reduces to its row-state interpolation through degree at most \(\max(d,2)\). Indeed powers collapse, conflicting same-row cells vanish, and a constant or one-row term can be completed to two occupied rows using the missing row sums, at cost at most two. The interpolation coefficient at states \(z,w\) is the value of the polynomial on those states.

For \(\tau E^{(p)}_{ii'}\), that coefficient is one exactly when \(z=w\). Thus its difference from \(\sum_zX_{iz}X_{i'z}\) has an ordinary NS certificate through \(\gamma\ge2\), and column exclusions kill the latter sum through degree two. All original-degree axiom images are certified. Affine PC replay therefore sends compact consequences through \(B\) to old functional consequences through \(B\).

3. Signs preserve the separating functional

Let \(\mathcal L_k\) consist of bit monomials with at most one coordinate from each occupied pigeon row, and suppose \(1\le k\le B\), \(4(k-1)<n\), and \(n\ge2B-1\). Its dimension is \(\sum_{j\le k}\binom{n+1}{j}\ell^j\) over every field. For a nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\), choose a monomial of maximum row degree \(t\), with rows \(S\) and selected coordinate \(a_i\) in row \(i\).

As in the binary dual construction, choose disjoint coordinate edges \(C_i\) of the Boolean label cube. There are \(n/2\) edges in each direction and at most \(2(t-1)\) forbidden ones at a greedy step. Orient each edge from bit \(a_i=0\) to bit \(a_i=1\), giving its endpoints weights \(-1,+1\). Delete their \(2t\) columns and take a normalized residual design \(\lambda\) through \(B-t\); Section 1 applies because \(n-2t\ge2(B-t)-1\).

Define the moment of a matching to be zero unless it contains every selected row on its assigned edge and its other rows avoid the deleted columns. In the remaining case set

\[ \mu(X_T)= \left(\prod_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i(T(i))\right) \lambda(X_{T|_{\overline S}}), \qquad \varepsilon_i\in\{-1,+1\}. \tag{OP-signed-tensor} \]

Boolean power reduction and collision zeroes extend this to ordinary polynomials. If a marginal is missing one selected row, its two endpoint terms cancel; if more are missing, all terms are zero. Incorrect selected labels or forbidden columns remain zero after extension. Once all selected rows are present, the marginal is exactly that of \(\lambda\), multiplied by the fixed edge signs. Hence \(\mu\) annihilates all of \(\mathcal I_B=\mathcal C_B\).

Only the chosen top row set can contribute to \(\mu(\tau f)\). The signed sum on its edges is the mixed finite difference isolating the chosen nonzero coefficient. Rescale \(\mu\) if a value of one is desired. Constant \(f\) is separated by a normalized design. Thus every nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\) is excluded from the compact PC consequences through \(B\), with the same degree and line-selection conditions as before.

4. One-level affine-bit exclusion for every fixed prime

Working theorem. Fix a prime \(p\). Let \(n=2^\ell\), choose accuracy \(h=3(p-1)\ell\), and take polynomially many complete one-level ENS blocks over \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\), all inputs affine in the old bits. For sufficiently large \(n\), this system has no ordinary-PC refutation of polylogarithmic degree \(D\). Its coefficient domains are \(r^p-r\), not Boolean equations when \(p\ne2\).

Proof. Remove zero/unit spans by scalar cleanup and let \(M\ge1\) count the remaining blocks. Put \(v=(n+1)\ell\) and \(k=\lceil\sqrt{(n+1)\log(4M)}\rceil\). A block is low if \((p-1)r\le h(k+1)\), and high otherwise. Every high block has rank at least \(r_*=3\ell(k+1)+1\).

Restrict \(\mathcal L_k\) as ordinary polynomials to each high zero flat in \(\mathbb F_p^v\). The image dimension is at most \(\binom{v-r+k}{k}\). The same dimension computation is field-independent:

\[ \frac{\binom{v-r_*+k}{k}}{\binom{n+1}{k}\ell^k} =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1} \left(1-\frac{r_*-1-(\ell+1)j}{v-\ell j}\right) \le e^{-k^2/(n+1)}. \]

The sum over high blocks is smaller than \(\dim\mathcal L_k\). Therefore a nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\) is identically zero as an ordinary polynomial on every high flat. Affine coordinates give literal expressions \(f=\sum_i a_i g_i\), \(\deg a_i\le k-1\), for each high tuple.

Use \(p-1\) coefficient rows \((\alpha a_i)_i\), one for every nonzero \(\alpha\in\mathbb F_p\), and zero remaining rows. The high product becomes

\[ \prod_{\alpha\ne0}(1-\alpha f)=1-f^{p-1}. \]

Weight by \(f\) itself, retaining row-linear separation. A weighted companion is \(fg_i(1-f^{p-1})=g_i(f-f^p)\), with an old Boolean NS certificate through \(pk+1\). The identity \(t^p-t\) has a Boolean certificate through \(p\deg t\): use Frobenius on its monomials and \(b^p-b=(b^2-b)\sum_{j=0}^{p-2}b^j\). Weighting by \(f^{p-1}\) is unnecessary.

For low rank, use the historical factor-packing lemma on all \((p-1)r\) factors \(1-\alpha F_j\), where \(F_j\) is an affine basis. Distribute them into \(h\) bins of size at most \(k+1\). Prefix telescoping gives coefficient degree at most \(k\) and exact product \(Z=\prod_j(1-F_j^{p-1})\). Since \(F_jZ=(F_j-F_j^p)\prod_{t\ne j}(1-F_t^{p-1})\), every companion image has a Boolean NS certificate through \((p-1)r+1\).

There is one simultaneous old-only substitution \(\sigma\). The needed weighted axiom ceilings are

\[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{image multiplied by }f&\text{old NS ceiling}\\ \hline \text{high companion}&pk+1\\ \text{low companion}&(p-1)r+1+k\le h(k+1)+1+k\\ \text{coefficient field}&(p+1)k\\ \text{old axiom }F&\deg F+k . \end{array} \]

Each fits \(k(e+1)\), where \(e\) is its original axiom degree: affine companions have \(e=2h+1\), coefficient fields \(e=p\), and old degrees are retained. For instance \(h(k+1)+1+k\le k(2h+2)\) for \(k\ge1\), and \(pk+1\le k(2h+2)\) here.

Replace each PC line by \(f\sigma(\text{line})\). At multiplication, the source predecessor degree is at most \(D-1\); multiplying its already derived weighted image by the variable's degree-at-most-\(k\) image stays within \(B=k(D+1)\). Expand polynomial multiplications into primitive PC steps. The putative refutation ends at the old polynomial \(f\). Polynomial \(M\) and polylogarithmic \(D\) give \(B=\sqrt n\,\operatorname{polylog}n<n/2\) and \(4(k-1)<n\) eventually, contradicting Section 3. If no proper blocks remain, old stability already excludes the refutation. No augmented NS/PC equality or expanded-monomial size bound is used.

5. A complete coefficient transfer for nonlinear power inputs

Consider an entire one-level family whose inputs in each block are \(g_i=L_i^{p-1}\), with \(L_i\) affine in the old Boolean bits. Its original product weight is \(hp\), companions have degree \(hp+p-1\), and coefficient fields degree \(p\), after constant cases are cleaned up. Introduce one fresh affine block on the \(L_i\)'s, with coefficients \(R_{ui}\) and product \(P_A\). Map every old coefficient by

\[ \Phi(r_{ui})=R_{ui}L_i. \tag{OP-power-map} \]

This degree-two map sends the original factor to \(1-\sum_iR_{ui}L_i^p\). Its difference from the affine factor \(1-\sum_iR_{ui}L_i\) has an old Boolean NS certificate through \(p+1\). Telescoping the \(h\) factors gives

\[ \Phi(P)-P_A\in\mathcal I_{h(p+1)}({\rm BOOL}_b). \]

Consequently the companion image is the sum of \(L_i^{p-1}(\Phi(P)-P_A)\) and \(L_i^{p-2}(L_iP_A)\). Its certificate degree is at most \(h(p+1)+p-1\), bounded by twice its original degree. For every coefficient domain,

\[ (R_{ui}L_i)^p-R_{ui}L_i =L_i^p(R_{ui}^p-R_{ui})+R_{ui}(L_i^p-L_i), \]

which has an NS certificate through \(2p\). Old axioms remain unchanged. All blocks use disjoint fresh coefficient sets, so these maps are simultaneous. Every original axiom image has its required certificate through twice its original degree; hence ordinary NS and PC replay send a degree-\(D\) refutation to one of degree at most \(2D\). This covers arbitrary use of the original coefficients, not only a preselected modular witness.

Working corollary. Polynomial-inventory one-level families of affine-power inputs \(L_i^{p-1}\), at \(h=3(p-1)\ell\), have no polylogarithmic-degree PC refutation over \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\). Affine blocks may coexist with these blocks. Section 4 excludes the resulting affine family at degree \(2D\). A constant factor is sufficient for the endpoint; no degree-preserving global map is needed.

6. Actual negative MOD children have profiles within their original source weight

Under the recorded source convention, formula approximations are zero for truth and an OR block uses inputs \(1-A^{\rm ap}\). A first-layer MOD child has approximation \(L^{p-1}\); its negation has \(1-L^{p-1}\). Thus an OR of negative MOD children has exactly the power inputs in Section 5. The affine \(L\) comes from its literal children and source offset. This matches the earlier signed source audit.

There is also stronger local cost information. Let \(P_A\) be the new affine product, with exact prefixes \(1-P_A=\sum_iU_iL_i\), \(\deg U_i\le2h-1\). For the actual inputs \(g_i=L_i^{p-1}\), choose value \(P_A\), prefixes \(V_i=U_iL_i\), input bounds \(\mu_i=p-1\), and cost \(s=2h+p-1\). Then

\[ 1-P_A-\sum_iV_ig_i=\sum_iU_i(L_i-L_i^p) \in\mathcal I_s,\qquad g_iP_A=L_i^{p-2}(L_iP_A)\in\mathcal I_s. \]

Furthermore \(\deg V_i+\mu_i\le s\), and \(P_A^2-P_A=-\sum_iU_i(L_iP_A)\) has a certificate through \(4h\le2s\). For odd \(p\) and \(h\ge2\), \(s\le hp\), the original product weight. These are complete costed NS profiles in the sense of the existing definition. Their identities hold with the necessary companion axioms; a general ENS product is not Boolean over its coefficient domains alone at odd primes. Section 5 separately supplies the complete-system transfer.

7. Complementary modular predicates: a rank obstruction that is itself removable

Positive MOD children instead produce inputs \(1-L_i^{p-1}\). Their common zero set says every \(L_i\ne0\); it is not a single affine zero flat. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), take independent old Boolean bits \(x,b_1,\ldots,b_m\) and

\[ L_i=1+x+b_i,\qquad g_i=1-L_i^2=xb_i-(x^2-x)-(b_i^2-b_i). \tag{OP-positive-example} \]

The \(L_i\) have affine rank \(m\), witnessed by their identity minor on the \(b_i\) columns. On the Boolean cube, their complementary predicates have \(2^m+1\) common zeroes out of \(2^{m+1}\): all points with \(x=0\), and the single point with \(x=1\), every \(b_i=0\). Thus underlying affine rank alone gives no shrinking-codimension estimate for this source polarity. Using the unchanged affine product on the \(L_i\)'s also fails: wherever all \(L_i=0\), its value is one and every \(g_i=1\).

A complete transfer for this example

The example is not a hardness claim. Introduce an affine block on \(b_1,\ldots,b_m\), with product \(P_A\), prefixes \(U_i\), and companions \(b_iP_A\). Put \(V=1-x+xP_A\), \(s=2h+1\), and \(\mu_i=2\). With \(B_x=x^2-x\), \(B_i=b_i^2-b_i\), the exact witnesses are

\[ 1-V-\sum_iU_ig_i=\sum_iU_i(B_x+B_i), \]
\[ g_iV=x(b_iP_A)+B_x\bigl(b_i(P_A-1)-V\bigr)-B_iV, \]
\[ V^2-V=B_x(P_A-1)^2+x(P_A^2-P_A). \]

The respective NS ceilings are \(s\), \(s+2\), and \(2s\), and \(\deg U_i+2\le s\le3h\) for \(h\ge1\). This gives a costed profile within the original positive-MOD product weight.

Here even the entire raw coefficient system transfers without degree loss. Rename its coefficients to those of the affine block. On old Boolean inputs, its product is \(\prod_u(1-x\sum_iR_{ui}b_i)=1-x+xP_A\), as an identity modulo old Booleanity. Degree-nonincreasing reduction of old bits therefore certifies the product difference through original degree \(3h\); coefficients \(R\) need no reduction. Multiply this difference by \(g_i\) and use the companion witness above: the original companion image has an NS certificate through \(3h+2\). Coefficient domains are just renamed. Ordinary NS/PC replay preserves \(D\).

Accordingly these common-bit blocks can coexist with the other handled one-level classes at \(p=3\). The general positive-MOD tuple and later dense nonlinear source still require new arguments. A large common zero set by itself does not imply a large proof degree.

8. Complete finite evidence and what changed

The moment checker now accepts an explicit prime while preserving its default binary output. The new \(\mathbb F_3\) run uses endpoint signs \((-1,+1)\) and residual pair coefficients \((1,-1,1)\) on the earlier three-cell path. It verifies 69,468 nonzero moments and 299,784 potentially nonzero marginal rows over the two fixtures \((n,k,B)=(8,2,4),(32,6,8)\), including every selected bit-axis evaluation. Unlisted constraints have zero on both sides by complete sparse support construction. Removing a top moment breaks four/eight marginals; replacing all nonzero moments by one also fails. The \(k>\ell\) fixture retains repeated directions on different rows.

The ordinary-polynomial checker saves all axioms, products, coefficient maps, targets, and NS cofactors. The initial run verified 51 certificates; the strengthened run verifies 72 across six local cases: negative MOD profiles and high-factor maps over \(\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\), low-rank packing over \(\mathbb F_3\), and the positive-MOD common-bit family. It checks the original degree ceilings and every raw source companion and field image.

Nonvacuous controls include a missing high factor, an omitted low-rank residue factor, a non-Boolean coefficient assignment showing that companion axioms are needed for product Booleanity, and a valid affine-core model refuting the naive complementary-input replacement. A complete 64-point table for \(m=5\) has the predicted 33 common zeroes. The finite cases verify the local algebra and moment witnesses; they do not instantiate the asymptotic rank threshold or prove a finite PHP size lower bound.

Both accepted NS outputs and the complete signed moment output are retained with commands, schema, source scope, hashes, and timing evidence. All mathematical checks passed. Preliminary indentation warnings were corrected before the corresponding runs.

Route assessment. Odd primes are no longer missing from the one-level affine lower-bound engine, and a complete nonlinear source class reaches that endpoint with affordable degree. This does not cover unrestricted MOD polarities, the dense multilevel Frege family, or the ordinary-unary proof conversion. The existing binary bit-PHP Res(\(\oplus\)) consequence is unchanged.

Next bounded question. Test an actual odd-prime clause calculus whose lines are disjunctions of affine disequalities. Include Boolean-domain clauses explicitly, audit a \(p\)-premise affine cover, and derive its rule and initial-value PC costs. Keep its scope separate from standard disjunctions of affine equations and from Boolean-semantic inference. Stop at a complete forward simulation or a concrete obstruction.

Process assessment. Checking a complete coefficient transfer exposed an affordable factor-two route beyond the local profiles; the existing endpoint-first guidance handled this adjustment, so no additional framework rule is needed.
