14 September 2026 — Eligible shared-bit parents become old-bit source values

Status: working binary source-profile and projected-rank criterion, with exact third-level controls. Eligible affine cores may be constrained to zero; the original shared-bit parents then become their old probe bits, not zero.

Question and stopping point. The previous complete transfer left the parent value \(x+(1-x)A\). We combine its fresh affine core with the joint-zero theorem and check the actual source interface, including later input offsets and original degree bounds. This cycle stops at a precise projected-source criterion and a third-level witness.

1. Canonical pair profiles can be used consistently

Work in the coherent compact binary source with common accuracy \(h\ge2\), retaining its original weights. For a designated bottom tuple \((x,y)\), use the old value

\[ z=(1-x)(1-y) \]

at its original cost \(2h\). The consistent scalar specialization already proves the complete map. Its source profile has exact prefix

\[ 1-z=x+(1-x)y. \]

The companions have old Boolean certificates through three, and

\[ z^2-z=(1-x)^2(y^2-y)+(1-y)(x^2-x) \]

has a certificate through four. These fit the original input, companion, and Booleanity ceilings. Choose one canonical value for each reused bottom block; all later uses see that same value.

The value \(z\) is old-only but is generally quadratic, not old-affine. Its mixed difference in two distinct bits is one, whereas every affine function has mixed difference zero. Therefore its formal selector column must remain in the subsequent rank calculation unless another justified step removes it.

2. A constrained affine core gives the original parent value \(x\)

For a shared-bit parent \(s\), the interpreted inputs are \(G_{s,i}=(1-x_s)(1-y_{s,i})\), with original individual bounds \(d_{s,i}=2h\) and original parent weight \(w_s=h(2h+1)\). Introduce the affine core \(A_s\) on \(1-y_{s,i}\), with exact prefixes \(U_{s,i}\). Suppose its zero equation \(A_s=0\) is included in the retained system.

Give the original parent the value \(v_s=x_s\), keeping cost \(w_s\). Its exact prefix residual is

\[ 1-x_s-\sum_iU_{s,i}G_{s,i} =(1-x_s)A_s \in\mathcal I_{2h+1}(\Gamma). \tag{CORE-old-bit-prefix} \]

The original input bounds, rather than their reduced degree two, give

\[ \deg U_{s,i}+d_{s,i} \le4h-1\le h(2h+1)=w_s. \tag{CORE-original-prefix-cost} \]

Companions have particularly short old Boolean witnesses:

\[ G_{s,i}x_s =-(x_s^2-x_s)(1-y_{s,i}), \tag{CORE-old-bit-companion} \]

through degree three. Booleanity of \(v_s\) is the old bit equation through two. Thus all prefix, companion, value-degree, and Booleanity requirements of the costed source interface hold within the original ceilings.

This also compares the actual mapped parent polynomial with the old bit. From the previous product difference,

\[ \Phi(P_s)-x_s =\bigl(\Phi(P_s)-[x_s+(1-x_s)A_s]\bigr) +(1-x_s)A_s \in\mathcal I_{3h}(\Gamma). \tag{CORE-actual-parent-comparison} \]

No inference \(P_s=0\) follows: even with \(A_s=0\), the parent is one whenever \(x_s=1\). The source assignment is an old-bit value with a certified prefix residual.

3. A multilevel criterion after the correct affine projection

Use the exact binary source stage and original degree conventions of the adapted-rank compiler, including every required subgroup and coherent copy. Fix source depth \(d\), take \(h=3\ell\), and choose in advance a polynomial upper bound \(M\ge1\) for the final affine inventory. Put

\[ k=\left\lceil\sqrt{(n+1)\log(4M)}\right\rceil,\qquad r_*=3\ell(k+1)+1. \]

Select a set \(S\) of shared-bit parents whose proper affine cores \(A_s\) have rank at least \(r_*\). Canonicalize their pair-bottom blocks by Section 1. Optionally also select a set \(H\) of original proper affine bottom blocks of rank at least \(r_*\), using their zero-value profiles. Retain the corresponding affine blocks and add all equations \(A_s=0\), \(s\in S\), and \(P_c=0\), \(c\in H\).

For every other nonbottom source block, replace its formal inputs by

\[ L_{a,i}(b)+\sum_{c<a}\alpha_{a,i;c}Z_c \ \longmapsto\ \underbrace{L_{a,i}(b)+ \sum_{s\in S,\ s<a}\alpha_{a,i;s}x_s}_{\text{new old-affine part}} +\sum_{\substack{c<a\\c\notin H\cup S}} \alpha_{a,i;c}Z_c . \tag{CORE-source-projection} \]

The columns in \(H\) disappear with value zero; the columns in \(S\) disappear only after their old-bit contribution is added to the affine part. Canonical pair-bottom columns remain in the final sum: being old-only does not make their quadratic values affine.

Working source criterion. If every remaining nonbottom block has selector-matrix rank at most \(h-1\) after (CORE-source-projection), then the entire source has costed profiles within its original weights over a complete one-level affine family with these eligible core constraints. A hypothetical polynomial-size proof of fixed source depth satisfying this criterion is excluded for sufficiently large \(n\).

Proof. Assign the canonical pair values first, the selected original high-bottom zero values as before, and the selected shared-bit parent values from Section 2. All use one common retained system and respect strict source order. For every unselected block, apply the old-affine intersection and degree-ordered original-input basis construction to the projected formal tuple. Interpret its remaining selector names only after this basis choice, so their formal cancellation gives genuinely old-affine core inputs.

The old-affine offset in (CORE-source-projection) has degree at most one. Every interpreted earlier value stays within its original weight. The adapted construction therefore retains all original individual \(d_i\)'s and yields cost at most \(2h+r_a^{\rm rem}\delta_a\). If a remaining selector direction occurs, the original \(\delta_a\) is at least \(h\), even if that direction's current value has smaller collected degree. Hence \(r_a^{\rm rem}\le h-1\) gives the original \(w_a=h(\delta_a+1)\) bound. Affine, zero, and unit cases have their established profiles. Prefix pullbacks, companions, and Booleanity retain the previous original-degree bounds.

Canonicalized pair bottoms require no retained block; every other original bottom is retained at most once. Each selected star or unselected later block contributes at most one fresh affine core. Thus the final inventory is at most one affine block per source registry block. The chosen \(M\) remains valid, and the designated core ranks are old-affine ranks in that final family.

The joint-zero theorem excludes a degree-\(D\) refutation of this endpoint whenever its usual multiplier and old-board bounds fit. The existing source reconstruction preserves its supplied modular NS degree, or the logical-DAG compiler gives

\[ D\le\max(M_{\rm fr},10)(d+1)h^d. \]

For fixed \(d\), polynomial \(M\), and \(h=3\ell\), this is polylogarithmic, while \(k(D+1)=o(n)\) and \(4(k-1)<n\). The forbidden affine endpoint follows, completing the criterion.

The criterion must hold for the full retained registry, including mixed auxiliary unions. It is not automatically satisfied by the displayed logical formulas alone. This is a source-profile theorem; it does not assert a raw degree-preserving map of arbitrary later coefficient proofs. General surviving selector dependence and the ordinary unary conversion gap remain open.

4. Exact original-input checks at the next level

The new checker uses the shared NS witness helper introduced after the preceding checkpoint. Its binary fixture has two shared-bit parents with different old probes, four actual pair-bottom blocks, two constrained affine star cores, and a third-level affine core on \(b_0+x_0,b_1+x_1,b_2+x_0\).

Fifteen complete NS certificates check both actual parent-to-bit comparisons through six, old-bit prefix residuals through five, star companions through three, and bit Booleanity through two. The output retains 288 complete canonical models satisfying both core constraints. In 36 the third value is one; each original star parent is one in 144 models and always equals its own probe. A wrong-zero-projection control changes a later input from one to zero if the old-affine offset is omitted. Removing the first core constraint gives a retained-system model where a claimed third-level companion is nonzero.

The small cores have rank two and are not instances of the asymptotic high-rank eligibility threshold. These are conditional-profile and degree-accounting checks over an old Boolean base, not finite PHP lower bounds. All checks passed with a clean compilation. 14 September 2026 — Mixed auxiliary unions fit their original source weight

Status: working affine-core profile for covered mixed OR groups, valid algebraically over every prime, with a binary source-compiler application. Exact overlapping-input and corrected-OR controls pass. General uncovered source groups remain open.

Question and stopping point. The preceding projected-rank criterion could fail on an auxiliary OR union containing many canonical quadratic bottom values. We build the profile for that actual flattened input tuple. A fresh affine core on the old truth bits of its eligible star subgroups avoids a cost proportional to the number of grouped bottom literals. This is a source-profile construction; no raw union-coefficient map is claimed.

1. Keep the actual flattened tuple and its original degree

Let selected shared-bit subgroups \(s\) cover the original union input index set \(I\). Their index sets \(I_s\) may overlap. After the consistent pair-bottom specialization, each occurrence in subgroup \(s\) has

\[ G_i=(1-x_s)L_{s,i},\qquad L_{s,i}=1-y_{s,i}, \qquad i\in I_s. \]

A shared input must have the same polynomial in every occurrence. For example \((1-x_0)(1-x_1)\) can occur in stars with either probe \(x_0\) or probe \(x_1\). The source convention flattens an OR cluster into its maximal non-OR children. Thus the union still reads the original bottom products, with original bounds

\[ \mu_i=2h,\qquad w_U=h(2h+1). \tag{UNION-original-weight} \]

The union and its proper OR subgroups can be at the same ENS level. We do not insert another level or replace the input tuple by the subgroup products to obtain a larger weight.

For each subgroup retain its affine core \(A_s\) on the \(L_{s,i}\)'s, with prefixes \(U_{s,i}\), and assume the eligible equation \(A_s=0\) is present. Put \(\chi_s=1-x_s\). The old-bit profile supplies the exact relation

\[ \chi_s-\sum_{i\in I_s}U_{s,i}G_i =\chi_s A_s,\qquad \deg U_{s,i}\le2h-1. \tag{UNION-subgroup-prefix} \]

The hypotheses concern the actual tuple, its cover, and the supplied core equations. A general collection of low-rank bottom blocks need not admit such a cover.

2. Compress the old truth inputs into one affine core

Introduce one fresh complete accuracy-\(h\) affine block on the old bits \((\chi_s)_s\), with product \(B\) and prefixes \(V_s\), so \(1-B=\sum_sV_s\chi_s\) and every \(\chi_sB\) is a companion axiom. Give the original union value \(B\). For its original input position \(i\), put

\[ W_i=\sum_{s:i\in I_s}V_sU_{s,i}. \tag{UNION-original-prefix} \]

Every overlapping occurrence contributes to this sum. Substitution of (UNION-subgroup-prefix) gives the exact residual

\[ 1-B-\sum_{i\in I}W_iG_i =\sum_sV_s\chi_s A_s \in\mathcal I_{4h}(\Gamma). \tag{UNION-residual} \]

Each displayed generator multiple costs at most \((2h-1)+1+2h=4h\). The original input-weighted prefix bound is

\[ \deg W_i+\mu_i \le(2h-1)+(2h-1)+2h=6h-2. \tag{UNION-prefix-cost} \]

For a companion, choose any subgroup \(s\) containing \(i\). Its factorization gives the particularly direct witness

\[ G_iB=L_{s,i}(\chi_sB) \in\mathcal I_{2h+2}(\Gamma). \tag{UNION-companion} \]

There is no need to sum over all groups for this step. Booleanity of the new value has the ordinary identity

\[ B^2-B=-\sum_sV_s(\chi_sB) \in\mathcal I_{4h}(\Gamma). \tag{UNION-Booleanity} \]

Working profile theorem. These data form a complete profile of cost \(s_U=6h-2\), with the original \(\mu_i=2h\), for every \(h\ge2\). It fits the original union weight because

\[ h(2h+1)-(6h-2)=(2h-1)(h-2)\ge0. \tag{UNION-budget} \]

The value degree is at most \(2h\), the residual ceiling \(4h\) is at most \(s_U\), and the companion and Booleanity ceilings fit \(s_U+\mu_i\) and \(2s_U\). All equations are ordinary NS identities and work over every prime. No bound on the number of subgroups or grouped bottom literals appears in these degree estimates. Witness size and input inventory are still retained; no small expanded-monomial-size claim is made.

All affine blocks use only old inputs and have disjoint own coefficients. The union value does not recursively depend on same-level subgroup values. Its NS witnesses use the supplied subgroup coefficients in one fixed retained system, which is permitted by the source interface.

In the binary source criterion of the preceding entry, handle a remaining flattened union of selected star tuples by Section 2, even if its formal selector matrix has rank much larger than \(h\). Keep its resulting affine-core value as the interpretation of its original selector name. Apply the adapted-rank condition only to the other remaining nonbottom blocks after the previously justified old-bit and zero projections.

\[ c-ab=c(1-a)+ca(1-b)-ab(1-c). \]

The binary checker uses \(h=2\), three star cores, five actual pair-bottom inputs, and two union cores. The star index sets are \(\{0,1\}\), \(\{0,2\}\), and \(\{3,4\}\): the first input is shared by stars with different probes. The two union tuples are \(\{0,1,2\}\) and \(\{0,1,2,3,4\}\).

14 September 2026 — Publication audit of the bit-PHP Res(\(\oplus\)) candidate

Status: positive internal audit and provisional novelty assessment; standard encoding clarification. Cycle 132.

Question and stopping point. Determine whether the working unrestricted DAG-like Res(\(\oplus\)) bound is a distinct publication candidate, check the dependency interfaces most likely to invalidate it, and explain its relationship to ordinary PHP. This cycle stops at that verdict. The next cycle will give the linked end-to-end theorem and proof requested by the user; an expanded whitepaper is deferred.

1. Bit PHP is established territory; the missing restriction is the distinction

Primary sourceScope relevant to the candidate
Efremenko, Garlík, and Itsykson, Lower Bounds for Regular Resolution over Parities, ECCC TR23-187, revision 2; STOC 2024 and SIAM Journal on Computing 54(4), 2025.For \(n+1\) pigeons and \(n\) holes, regular Res(\(\oplus\)) requires \(2^{\Omega(n^{1/3}/\log n)}\) size. The report also gives an unrestricted DAG-like affine-width lower bound, which is not a superpolynomial size bound.
Byramji and Impagliazzo, Lower Bounds for Bit Pigeonhole Principles in Bounded-Depth Resolution over Parities, arXiv v1, 25 November 2025.Bit-PHP size bounds retain a restriction on proof-DAG depth. This includes the \(n+1\)-pigeon instance; the family itself is not new.
Bhattacharya, Byramji, Chattopadhyay, and Impagliazzo, Lower Bounds for Near-Quadratic-Depth Resolution over Parities, STOC 2026, pp. 955–966, DOI 10.1145/3798129.3800809.The official proceedings abstract includes exponential lower bounds for depth \(O(n^{2-\varepsilon})\) Res(\(\oplus\)) refutations of bit PHP with \(n+1\) pigeons and \(n\) holes. This is the merged conference publication, not a separate unrestricted size theorem.
Itsykson, Podolskii, and Shekhovtsov, Resolution Width Lifts to Near-Quadratic-Depth Res(\(\oplus\)) Size, ECCC TR26-018, 12 February 2026, Introduction, p. 2.The paper explicitly identifies general superpolynomial Res(\(\oplus\)) size lower bounds as open. Its unrestricted size consequence is quadratic. This paper is distinct from the preceding STOC publication.

The potential contribution is therefore a superpolynomial size lower bound with neither regularity nor proof-DAG-depth restrictions. “Bounded depth” in this literature concerns paths in the proof DAG, not the constant formula-depth parameter in the broader Frege goal. The primary-source search found no earlier result with the claimed unrestricted scope. That is a provisional literature assessment as of this audit, not a guarantee that all published or unpublished work has been located.

For historical scale, the STOC 2026 abstract credits the introduction of Res(\(\oplus\)) to Itsykson and Sokolov at MFCS 2014. The unrestricted superpolynomial-size benchmark has therefore remained open for roughly twelve years from the system's introduction to the explicit 2026 open-problem statement.

2. Focused correctness and scope audit

The review used the shorter sufficient route at \(h=3\ell\), rather than requiring the sharper earlier accuracy bound or later source-profile developments. These are the interfaces checked:

  1. Source calculus. The rule definition in TR26-018, p. 2 is complementary-parity resolution plus one-premise semantic weakening. These are exactly the resolution and weakening simulations. The two-premise semantic bridge covers the alternate convention without a proof-height cost. Fresh unrelated propositional variables can be fixed first; no extension rule is being admitted.

Initial algebraic values are derived using degree-\(\ell\) collision polynomials. Clause values are completed PC lines, not extra axioms, and multiplying those lines incurs the displayed local degree cost rather than multiplying their entire earlier derivations.

The resulting PC/NS equality is used only for the old functional system.

Its zero normalization is allowed. It separates the nonzero row-linear polynomial supplied by the ordinary restriction-kernel argument. That argument gives literal affine ideal membership, uses one simultaneous old-only coefficient map, includes every coefficient field equation, and replays primitive PC multiplication through \(k(D+1)\).

3. What does transfer from bit PHP to ordinary PHP?

Standard reduction, clarified. Let \(n=2^\ell\), and let \(X_{ij}\) be the variables of ordinary unary PHP. In a depth-\(d\) \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege refutation, substitute

\[ X_{ij}\longmapsto \Lambda_{ij} :=\bigwedge_{t=1}^{\ell} \begin{cases}b_{it},&j_t=1,\\ \neg b_{it},&j_t=0.\end{cases} \tag{PUB-label-substitution} \]

This is the familiar bit-label substitution, also used explicitly by Bonacina and Bonet, On the strength of Sherali-Adams and Nullstellensatz as propositional proof systems, Definition 4.11 and the proof of Corollary 4.12, p. 18. Its use here is a clarification of the route, not a claim of a new encoding lemma.

Argument. A unary collision clause \(\neg X_{ij}\vee\neg X_{i'j}\) becomes exactly the bit-PHP clause forbidding rows \(i,i'\) from both encoding \(j\), after De Morgan expansion. A pigeon axiom becomes the tautology \(T_i=\bigvee_{j

Uniform substitution preserves the Frege inference rules, including MOD\(_p\) occurrences, with polynomial size overhead and formula depth \(d+O(1)\). Replace each substituted pigeon axiom by the preceding derivation and each substituted collision axiom by its bit-PHP clause. Therefore a polynomial-size ordinary-PHP refutation at fixed depth would yield a polynomial-size bit-PHP refutation at another fixed depth. Consequently, bit-PHP lower bounds at every fixed \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege depth suffice for the ordinary-PHP goal.

The powers-of-two restriction does not obstruct that implication. For a general \(N\), let \(n\le N<2n\) be a power of two. Assign the \(N-n\) extra pigeons to distinct extra holes and set surviving-pigeon variables in those holes to zero. Restricting unary PHP on \(N+1\) pigeons and \(N\) holes leaves unary PHP on \(n+1\) pigeons and \(n\) holes. Restriction preserves proof size and bounded depth.

Why the present subsystem bound is insufficient. Under (PUB-label-substitution), an affine parity \(\bigoplus X_{ij}\) becomes a parity of bit conjunctions, generally a nonlinear polynomial in the bits. That is outside the affine-query language of Res(\(\oplus\)). No polynomial-size Res(\(\oplus\)) conversion follows from this substitution. Likewise, the existing source obstruction concerns preservation of a restricted selector-rank hypothesis, not absence of the standard Frege reduction. Earlier references to an “ordinary-unary conversion gap” should be read with this distinction; this dated clarification leaves their original statements intact.

14 September 2026 — An end-to-end bit-PHP lower bound for unrestricted Res(\(\oplus\))

Status: working publication theorem, composed from linked dependencies; no external verification claimed. Cycle 133.

Purpose. Following the positive internal audit, formulate the result proposed for publication and give its complete logical chain and parameter closure in one place. As requested, dependency statements and proofs are referenced rather than restated. This entry consolidates the earlier working corollary and its second derivation; it is not another stronger lower bound or an expanded whitepaper.

1. Encoding, proof system, and size convention

Let \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), and \(m=n+1\). There are \(v=m\ell\) Boolean variables \(b_{it}\), with \(i\in[m]\), \(t\in[\ell]\). Write \(b_i=(b_{i1},\ldots,b_{i\ell})\). For a label \(z\in\{0,1\}^{\ell}\), the literal \([b_{it}\ne z_t]\) means \(b_{it}\) if \(z_t=0\), and \(\neg b_{it}\) if \(z_t=1\). Define the usual CNF bit pigeonhole principle by

\[ {\rm BPHP}_n^{n+1} =\bigwedge_{\substack{1\le i<i'\le m\\z\in\{0,1\}^{\ell}}} \left( \bigvee_{t=1}^{\ell}[b_{it}\ne z_t] \ \vee\ \bigvee_{t=1}^{\ell}[b_{i't}\ne z_t] \right). \tag{PUB-BPHP} \]

Each row already encodes one of the \(n\) labels, so no separate pigeon or range axiom is needed. There are \(n\binom m2\) clauses, each of width \(2\ell\).

A Res(\(\oplus\)) line is a disjunction of affine equations over \(\mathbb F_2\), evaluated on the Boolean variables. In the basic presentation the rules are

\[ \frac{A\vee(u=0)\qquad B\vee(u=1)}{A\vee B}, \qquad \frac{C}{D}\quad\text{when }C\models D, \tag{PUB-rules} \]

where \(u\) is affine. A refutation is a finite acyclic derivation from the CNF clauses to the empty clause. Earlier lines may be reused arbitrarily; there is no regularity or proof-height condition. Its size \(S\) is the number of nodes, including initial nodes, in this proof DAG. The theorem also covers the presentation allowing every semantically sound inference from at most two linear-clause premises. Auxiliary free propositional variables are harmless by restriction; extension axioms defining new predicates are not part of this system.

2. The proposed publication theorem

Theorem (working proof). For every fixed real \(K>0\), there is \(\ell_0(K)\) such that for every integer \(\ell\ge\ell_0(K)\), every unrestricted DAG-like Res(\(\oplus\)) refutation of \({\rm BPHP}_{2^\ell}^{2^\ell+1}\) has more than \((2^\ell)^K\) nodes. This holds under either rule presentation in Section 1.

Equivalently, the minimum refutation line count is \(n^{\omega(1)}\), along \(n=2^\ell\). In particular, total proof-description size is superpolynomial as well. Since the CNF family has size polynomial in \(n\), the conclusion is also superpolynomial in its input-description length.

The theorem concerns the concrete binary proof system and encoding above. It makes no claim of a full \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege lower bound, of a unary Res(\(\oplus\)) lower bound, or of a general odd-prime equation-clause lower bound. The standard Frege encoding reduction does not itself supply any of those missing stronger-system statements.

3. End-to-end proof using the recorded dependencies

Fix the alleged polynomial bound. Fix \(K>0\), and suppose that for an arbitrarily large \(n=2^\ell\) there is a refutation \(\pi\) of (PUB-BPHP) with \(S\le n^K\). All choices below are made after fixing this proof; no uniform construction of a separating functional is required.

Step 1: put the actual CNF proof into the audited clause presentation. Apply the rule and clause-description normalization, including restriction of any unrelated variables. Prepend the compact pair-difference clauses

\[ C_{ii'}=\bigvee_{t=1}^{\ell}(b_{it}+b_{i't}=1) \]

and use the recorded semantic-weakening bridge to obtain each initial CNF clause that \(\pi\) uses. The resulting basic-rule proof can be chosen with at most \(3S+\binom m2\) nodes: the semantic-rule conversion adds at most two auxiliary clauses per original node, and there are at most \(\binom m2\) compact initial nodes. Its clause descriptions have polynomial length in \(v\). Thus the number of clause blocks and input positions needed below is polynomial in \(n\), even if the original size convention counted only lines.

Step 2: obtain the complete one-level algebraic endpoint. Set \(h=3\ell\). Apply the direct ordinary-PC transfer to this proof. In the notation of the fixed clause system, it gives a family \(\Gamma\) over the old compact base

\[ \mathcal Q_n =\left\{ E_{ii'}=\prod_{t=1}^{\ell}(1-b_{it}-b_{i't}) \right\}_{i<i'} \cup\{b_{it}^2-b_{it}\}_{i,t}. \]

Each added block has old-affine inputs, fresh own coefficients, all its companions \(g_{a,j}P_a\), and all its coefficient Booleanity equations. Every block is at the same extension level. The transfer derives one in ordinary PC through

\[ D=\max\{2h+\ell,4h+1\}=12\ell+1. \tag{PUB-D} \]

The source proof's initial clause values and subsequent line values are derived within this fixed system. They are not inserted as additional axioms. The PC degree is the ordinary joint-variable degree; no Boolean quotient degree or bound on expanded PC monomial count is substituted for it. The transfer has no proof-DAG-height factor.

Step 3: close the quantitative hypotheses. Let \(M\) be at least one and at least the number of proper affine blocks after the scalar cleanup included in the one-level argument. We may take

\[ M\le 3S+\binom m2+1\le 3n^K+n^2+1, \qquad k=\left\lceil\sqrt{m\ln(4M)}\right\rceil, \qquad B=k(D+1). \tag{PUB-parameters} \]

Here \(\ln\) is the natural logarithm. Since \(K\) is fixed,

\[ k=O_K\!\left(\sqrt{n\log n}\right),\qquad B=O_K\!\left(\sqrt n\,(\log n)^{3/2}\right)=o(n). \]

Consequently, after increasing \(\ell_0(K)\) if necessary, all required board and degree inequalities hold simultaneously:

\[ D\ge2h+1,\qquad 1\le k\le B\le n/2,\qquad m\ge B,\qquad n\ge2B-1,\qquad 4(k-1)<n. \tag{PUB-room} \]

This choice also lies in the polynomial-inventory regime of the ordinary restriction-dimension estimate. No restriction on the ranks of the actual proof clauses is being assumed: the linked one-level argument handles both sides of its rank partition.

Step 4: remove the affine extensions at a controlled old degree. Apply the ordinary restriction-kernel and weighted-PC argument with exactly these \(h,M,k,D\). Its construction and original-degree ledger yield a nonzero polynomial \(f\) in \(\mathcal L_k\), the space spanned by products of at most \(k\) bits on distinct rows, and an ordinary-PC derivation

\[ f\in\mathcal C_B(\mathcal Q_n),\qquad f\ne0. \tag{PUB-old-consequence} \]

The hypotheses for this application were verified in Step 3. We use the simultaneous map from that dependency; we do not eliminate blocks one at a time, assume augmented PC equals NS, or replace formal ideal membership by pointwise vanishing.

Step 5: contradict the old separating functional. Apply the decoder transfer to (PUB-old-consequence), with the same degree \(B\). It puts \(\tau f\) in the ordinary degree-\(B\) PC consequence space of the functional unary PHP system on \(m=n+1\) rows and \(n\) columns. But the cube-residual separation lemma, whose hypotheses are precisely included in (PUB-room), excludes that membership for this nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\). Its old-PC premise is justified by the complete matching constraints and old row-set extension and closure proof. This is the contradiction.

The argument applies to every sufficiently large \(n=2^\ell\) for the chosen \(K\). Hence no refutation of at most \(n^K\) nodes exists there. Since \(K\) was arbitrary, the theorem follows. \(\square\)

5. Supplement prompted by the user: the Dvořák work and subsequent bounds

Bhattacharya, Chattopadhyay, and Dvořák, Exponential Separation Between Powers of Regular and General Resolution over Parities, CCC 2024, give formulas exponentially hard for bottom-regular Res(\(\oplus\)) but with short proofs even in general ordinary Resolution. This is a separation from the regular subsystem; those formulas cannot witness a lower bound for unrestricted Res(\(\oplus\)). Their published abstract explicitly distinguishes the still-open unrestricted size problem. This comparison was missing from the preceding audit table and is added here.

Bhattacharya and Chattopadhyay's Exponential Lower Bounds on the Size of ResLin Proofs of Nearly Quadratic Depth, ECCC TR25-106, 30 July 2025, reaches nearly quadratic proof depth using lifted Tseitin formulas. It retains a depth restriction, and identifies ideas originating in the earlier three-author paper. Chattopadhyay and Dvořák's Super-critical Trade-offs in Resolution over Parities Via Lifting, ECCC TR24-132, concerns tree-like proofs with width restrictions. These are relevant advances, not unrestricted superpolynomial DAG-size theorems.

Together with the Efremenko–Garlík–Itsykson and 2025–26 comparison, these additional primary sources leave the provisional novelty verdict unchanged. They also show why simply obtaining another regular or shallow-proof result would not resolve the stated benchmark. The candidate above explicitly removes those restrictions.

14 September 2026 — Two-bit-per-row multipliers: dimension and board estimates

Status: working component arguments; the constant-accuracy endpoint assembly is deferred for the requested whitepaper. Cycle 134.

Question and interruption. Test whether the affine exclusion can use constant accuracy \(h=2(p-1)\). The following dimension and old-board arguments were developed before the user requested the expanded publication draft. They are preserved here without claiming a completed constant-accuracy theorem or a numerical verification. The publication proof continues to use its audited \(h=3\ell\) route.

1. A larger multiplier space has the required restriction dimension

Let \(v=m\ell\), and let \(\mathcal A_{2,k}\) be the homogeneous degree-\(k\) space of squarefree bit polynomials using at most two bits in each row. Suppose \(1\le k\le v\), and put

\[ \varepsilon= m\binom{\ell}{3}\frac{\binom{v-3}{k-3}}{\binom vk}, \]

with \(\varepsilon=0\) if \(k<3\) or \(\ell<3\). Every excluded \(k\)-set of bits contains a triple from one row. A union bound over these triples therefore gives

\[ \dim\mathcal A_{2,k}\ge(1-\varepsilon)\binom vk. \tag{CA-dimension} \]

For an affine flat of codimension \(r\), ordinary polynomial restriction has image dimension at most \(\binom{v-r+k}{k}\). If \(r\ge2k+3\), then

\[ \frac{\binom{v-r+k}{k}}{\binom vk} =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\left(1-\frac{r-k}{v-j}\right) \le \exp\!\left(-\frac{k(r-k)}v\right) \le e^{-k^2/v}. \tag{CA-restriction} \]

Thus, if \(k=\lceil\sqrt{v\ln(4M)}\rceil\), \(\varepsilon\le1/2\), and there are at most \(M\) such flats, the sum of their restriction-image dimensions is at most \(\frac14\binom vk<\dim\mathcal A_{2,k}\). A common nonzero kernel polynomial exists over every field. The restrictions here are ordinary polynomials, so the existing affine-coordinate argument supplies literal ideal representations with coefficient degree at most \(k-1\). If no such flats exist, the kernel assertion is immediate.

2. Its top monomials fit the residual-board detector

Take \(n=2^\ell\), \(m=n+1\), \(k\le B\), and assume

\[ 16(k-1)<n,\qquad n\ge2B+k-1. \tag{CA-board} \]

A nonzero monomial of \(f\in\mathcal A_{2,k}\) occupies \(u\) rows with axis counts \(d_i\in\{1,2\}\). Each required coordinate cube has at most four points. At each greedy placement, at most \(4(u-1)\) previously used labels forbid cosets, out of at least \(n/4\) cosets, so (CA-board) gives disjoint cubes.

The number of removed labels is \(F=\sum_i2^{d_i}=2k\). Since \(k\le2u\),

\[ n-F\ge2B-k-1\ge2(B-u)-1. \]

The residual label set is nonempty: (CA-board), with \(B\ge k\), gives this for \(k\ge2\), and \(\ell\ge2\) handles \(k=1\). The signed multi-axis cube detector therefore separates every nonzero \(\tau f\) from old degree-\(B\) PC consequences, over each prime field. This uses the earlier detector rather than a new matching-moment construction.

3. Candidate assembly and what remains to check

At \(h=2(p-1)\), the existing low-rank packing threshold \((p-1)r\le h(k+1)\) becomes \(r\le2(k+1)\), matching the high-rank cutoff in Section 1. The existing simultaneous weighted map suggests the same replay ceiling \(B=k(D+1)\), now using \(f\in\mathcal A_{2,k}\). For polynomial \(M\), the proposed \(k\) is \(O(\sqrt n\log n)\), \(\varepsilon=O((\log n)^3/\sqrt n)=o(1)\), and polylogarithmic \(D\) makes (CA-board) eventually available.

Before stating the assembled theorem, check the complete original-degree axiom ledger at this constant \(h\), including every coefficient field equation, and review the changed multiplier space in the weighted replay. A planned focused finite check would exercise genuine rank-\(2k+3\) high tuples, a fully packed low tuple, and within-row quadratic terms, with controls showing why unweighted high images are invalid. No checker was written and no numerical run was performed in this interrupted cycle.

2. Inline homological background added for the manuscript

This is an exposition of the classical BLVZ chessboard bound, not a new connectivity theorem. Work with reduced homology over \(\mathbb F_2\). Call a complex \(q\)-acyclic when its reduced homology vanishes from degree \(-1\) through \(q\); \((-1)\)-acyclic means it has a vertex, and conditions below \(-1\) are vacuous.

Homological cover lemma. Suppose a finite complex \(K\) is covered by subcomplexes \(L_1,\ldots,L_t\), their nerve is \(q\)-acyclic, and every nonempty intersection of \(s\) members is \((q-s+1)\)-acyclic, where \(q\ge0\). Then \(K\) is \(q\)-acyclic.

Proof. Use the finite double complex

\[ D_{a,b}= \bigoplus_{\substack{J\subseteq[t],\ |J|=a+1\\L_J\ne\varnothing}} C_b(L_J;\mathbb F_2), \qquad L_J=\bigcap_{j\in J}L_j,\quad a,b\ge0. \]

The vertical differential is simplicial boundary; the horizontal differential omits a cover index. Their sum squares to zero in characteristic two. Augment horizontal rows to \(C_b(K)\). For any fixed simplex of \(K\), the indices of cover members containing it form a nonempty simplex, whose augmented chain complex is exact. Taking the direct sum over simplices shows that the horizontal rows are exact after augmentation. Computing horizontally first therefore recovers the homology of \(K\).

Vertically first, the first page is \(\bigoplus_{|J|=a+1}H_b(L_J)\). Its groups with \(b>0\), \(a+b\le q\), vanish by the intersection hypotheses. For \(b=0\), \(a\le q\), every nonempty intersection is connected, so the remaining horizontal groups and maps are the nerve chain complex. At \(a=q+1\), the augmentation \(H_0(L_J)\to\mathbb F_2\) is still onto; hence the incoming boundaries contain all nerve boundaries needed in degree \(q\). The second page has zero reduced groups in total degrees at most \(q\). Later pages cannot create nonzero groups from zero entries, and the finite filtration converges. Augmenting degree zero gives the asserted reduced-homology vanishing. \(\square\)

Homological chessboard bound. For \(a,b\ge1\), define

\[ \nu(a,b)=\min\left\{a,b, \left\lfloor\frac{a+b+1}{3}\right\rfloor\right\}. \]

The chessboard complex \(\Delta_{a,b}\) is \((\nu(a,b)-2)\)-acyclic. In particular \(b\ge2a-1\) implies \(\widetilde H_{a-2}(\Delta_{a,b};\mathbb F_2)=0\).

Proof by the standard star cover. Transpose so \(a\le b\) and induct on \(a\). If \(\nu=1\), nonemptiness suffices. Otherwise \(q=\nu-2\ge0\) and \(a\ge2\). Cover by the closed stars of the row-one vertices \((1,j)\). They are cones. A matching avoiding row one uses at most \(a-1<b\) columns, so it belongs to some star. An intersection of \(s\ge2\) stars is \(\Delta_{a-1,b-s}\), on the remaining rows and columns. Every proper subfamily has a vertex in its intersection, while the full intersection does not. The nerve is the boundary of a \((b-1)\)-simplex, a sphere of dimension \(b-2\).

Here \(\nu\le b-1\), so the nerve is \(q\)-acyclic. For a nonempty \(s\)-fold intersection, \(s\ge2\), let \(\mu=\nu(a-1,b-s)\). Each entry in this minimum is at least \(\nu-s+1\):

\[ a-1\ge\nu-s+1,\qquad b-s\ge\nu-s+1,\qquad a+b-s\ge3\nu-s-1\ge3(\nu-s+1). \]

Thus \(\mu\ge\nu-s+1\). Induction, transposing the smaller board if needed, gives \((q-s+1)\)-acyclicity of the intersection. Apply the cover lemma. Finally \(b\ge2a-1\) makes \(\nu=a\), giving the exact consequence used by the matching-moment argument. \(\square\)

1. Complete one-level exclusion at \(h=2(p-1)\)

Working theorem. Fix a prime \(p\), let \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), \(m=n+1\), \(v=m\ell\), and use the correct compact base \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\), of collision degree \(\gamma=(p-1)\ell\). Adjoin any complete one-level old-affine ENS family of common accuracy \(h=2(p-1)\), with fresh disjoint coefficient scopes and every coefficient equation \(r^p-r\). Let \(M\ge1\) bound the number of proper blocks after scalar cleanup, and put

\[ k=\left\lceil\sqrt{v\ln(4M)}\right\rceil,\qquad B=k(D+1),\qquad \varepsilon=m\binom{\ell}{3} \frac{\binom{v-3}{k-3}}{\binom vk}. \tag{CA-full-parameters} \]

As before set \(\varepsilon=0\) if \(k<3\) or \(\ell<3\). A sufficient finite set of hypotheses is

\[ D\ge\max\{\gamma,2h+1\},\qquad 1\le k\le v,\quad \varepsilon\le\tfrac12,\qquad 16(k-1)<n,\qquad n\ge2B+k-1. \tag{CA-full-room} \]

Under these conditions the augmented system has no ordinary-PC refutation of degree at most \(D\). Consequently, for polynomially many blocks and sufficiently large \(n\), every polylogarithmic degree is excluded at this constant accuracy.

Proof. Remove zero and unit spans by constant coefficient assignments, which preserve degree. Proper affine spans have the same rank as their linear parts and nonempty zero flats. Split the family at

\[ (p-1)r\le h(k+1) \iff r\le2(k+1). \]

The higher ranks are at least \(2k+3\). By the recorded dimension argument, there is a nonzero homogeneous \(f\in\mathcal A_{2,k}\), using at most two bits per row, that is the zero ordinary polynomial on every high flat. Its dimension estimate uses \(\binom vk\), rather than the smaller row-linear top layer. On each high block, affine coordinates give literal

\[ f=\sum_i a_i g_i,\qquad \deg a_i\le k-1. \]

Use \(p-1\) coefficient rows \((\alpha a_i)_i\), \(\alpha\in\mathbb F_p^\times\), and set the remaining rows to zero. This is permitted because \(h=2(p-1)\). The high product becomes \(1-f^{p-1}\). Weight every substituted proof line by \(f\). A high companion has image \(g_i(f-f^p)\), with an old Boolean NS certificate through \(pk+1\).

On a low block, partition the \((p-1)r\) factors \(1-\alpha F_j\) from an affine basis among \(h\) bins of size at most \(k+1\). The existing telescoping map has coefficient degree at most \(k\) and produces the exact flat indicator \(Z=\prod_j(1-F_j^{p-1})\). Its companion images have Boolean certificates through \((p-1)r+1\), hence weighted certificates through \((p-1)r+1+k\).

The full original-degree ledger is

\[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{source axiom}&\text{original degree }e& \text{weighted NS ceiling}\\ \hline \text{high companion}&2h+1&pk+1\\ \text{low companion}&2h+1&(p-1)r+1+k\\ \text{coefficient field}&p&(p+1)k\\ \text{old axiom}&e&e+k. \end{array} \tag{CA-full-ledger} \]

Every row fits \(k(e+1)\). For companions, \(2h+2=4p-2\), so \(pk+1\le k(4p-2)\), while

\[ (p-1)r+1+k \le h(k+1)+1+k \le k(2h+2). \]

The last inequality is \((k-1)(h+1)\ge0\). For a coefficient image \(\beta\), Boolean reduction certifies \(\beta^p-\beta\) through \(p\deg\beta\le pk\), giving the displayed field row after multiplication by \(f\). This uses the actual field equation, not Booleanity of a general \(\mathbb F_p\)-valued coefficient. Old axioms retain their original degrees.

All maps use only old bits, so they are simultaneous. In a primitive source multiplication, the predecessor degree is at most \(D-1\) and the mapped variable has degree at most \(k\). The same weighted replay therefore derives \(f\) from \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\) through \(B=k(D+1)\). This step does not use the earlier one-bit-per-row restriction: its algebraic requirements are the stated degree bounds and old Boolean equations.

The recorded two-bit-row board lemma now excludes that consequence. Its disjoint cubes delete exactly \(2k\) labels, and (CA-full-room) gives the residual design needed by the signed detector. The degree-preserving decoder and old PC stability over \(\mathbb F_p\) give the contradiction. If there are no high blocks, the joint-kernel choice is unrestricted and the same proof works.

For polynomial \(M\), \(k=O(\sqrt n\log n)\) and \(\varepsilon=O((\log n)^3/\sqrt n)=o(1)\). Any polylogarithmic \(D\) gives \(B=\sqrt n\,\operatorname{polylog}n=o(n)\), so all finite conditions hold eventually. A smaller proposed degree can first be enlarged to \(\max\{\gamma,2h+1\}\), which remains polylogarithmic. \(\square\)

Larger accuracies. The qualitative exclusion also holds when individual blocks have any accuracies \(h_a\ge2(p-1)\): set coefficient rows beyond \(2(p-1)\) to zero in each block. The resulting complete system is covered by the theorem, and this constant substitution does not increase PC degree. No minimality of \(2(p-1)\) is asserted.

All checks passed with no compiler warning. These are local complete-image and dimension controls; their small boards are outside the combined asymptotic PHP hypotheses. 14 September 2026 — Accuracy one: affine exclusion and the complete shared-bit source

Status: working all-prime refutation theorem and complete two-level source transfer, with exact local controls. Cycle 137.

Obligation and stopping point. Apply the stronger affine endpoint to the actual dense shared-bit family at the remaining positive accuracy \(h=1\). The preceding theorem used \(2(p-1)\) coefficient rows, and the earlier bottom map used two. Separate coefficient degree from multiplier degree, verify every source axiom image, and stop at the resulting source exclusion. This cycle reaches that endpoint; general rank-two bottoms and later nonlinear inputs remain open.

1. Complete one-level affine exclusion at accuracy one

Working theorem. Fix a prime \(p\), write \(a=p-1\), and let \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), \(m=n+1\), \(v=m\ell\). Adjoin a complete one-level old-affine ENS family of accuracy one to the compact base \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\), with fresh disjoint coefficients and their genuine field equations \(r^p-r\). Let \(M\ge1\) bound the number of proper blocks after scalar cleanup. Put

\[ k=\left\lceil\sqrt{v\ln(4M)}\right\rceil,\quad T=2a(k+1)-1,\quad \delta=ak,\quad A=2a,\quad B=TD+\delta, \qquad \varepsilon=m\binom{\ell}{3} \frac{\binom{v-3}{k-3}}{\binom vk}. \tag{UA-parameters} \]

Set \(\varepsilon=0\) if \(k<3\) or \(\ell<3\). A sufficient finite hypothesis is

\[ D\ge\max\{a\ell,p,3\},\quad 1\le k\le v,\quad\varepsilon\le\tfrac12,\quad 4^A(\delta-1)<n,\quad n\ge2B+(2^A-2)\delta-1. \tag{UA-room} \]

Then the complete augmented system has no ordinary-PC refutation through degree \(D\). In particular, for each fixed prime, polynomially or quasipolynomially many such blocks admit no polylogarithmic-degree refutation for sufficiently large \(n\).

Common kernel. Remove zero and unit spans by the existing constant restrictions. Divide the remaining proper affine ranks into \(r\le2(k+1)\) and \(r\ge2k+3\). The row-cap-two restriction argument supplies nonzero homogeneous \(f\in\mathcal A_{2,k}\): it is squarefree of degree \(k\), uses at most two bits per row, and restricts to the zero ordinary polynomial on every high flat. Indeed its domain has dimension at least \((1-\varepsilon)\binom vk\), while the sum of high restriction-image dimensions is at most \(M e^{-k^2/v}\binom vk\le\binom vk/4\). On each such block affine coordinates give literal

\[ f=\sum_i a_i g_i,\qquad \deg a_i\le k-1. \]

One-row maps. On a high block send its sole coefficient row to \(\beta_i=a_i f^{p-2}\), whose degree is at most \(\delta-1\le T\). Its product becomes \(1-f^{p-1}\). On a low block take an affine basis \(L_1,\ldots,L_r\) and telescope all \(ar\) factors \(1-\alpha L_j\), \(\alpha\ne0\), into one coefficient row. The resulting product is the exact full-field flat indicator

\[ Z=\prod_{j=1}^r(1-L_j^{p-1}), \qquad \deg\beta_i\le ar-1\le2a(k+1)-1=T. \]

The coefficients on basis forms pull back by constant linear combinations to the original tuple. This is the same telescoping construction, with a larger allowed coefficient degree and only one bin. Every map uses only old variables, so all blocks are handled simultaneously.

Weighted original-degree ledger. Set \(F=f^{p-1}\) and weight every substituted proof line by \(F\), of degree \(\delta\). It takes values zero or one on every old Boolean point. Thus high weighted companions \(g_iF(1-F)\) have old Boolean NS certificates through \(2\delta+1\). Low unweighted companions \(g_iZ\) vanish on every full-field point and have Boolean certificates through \(ar+1\). For a coefficient image \(\beta\), the actual field polynomial \(\beta^p-\beta\) has a Boolean certificate through \(pT\). Boolean reduction here retains every ordinary generator multiple; it does not silently replace coefficient field equations by Boolean ones.

\[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{source axiom}&\text{original degree }e& \text{weighted old NS ceiling}\\ \hline \text{high companion}&3&2\delta+1\\ \text{low companion}&3&ar+1+\delta\le T+2+\delta\\ \text{coefficient field}&p&pT+\delta\\ \text{old axiom}&e&e+\delta \end{array} \tag{UA-ledger} \]

Every row fits \(Te+\delta\): \(2\delta+1\le3T+\delta\), \(T+2\le3T\), and \(T\ge1\). A primitive nonzero multiplication predecessor of degree \(d\) has \(d+1\le D\). Its weighted image has degree at most \(Td+\delta\); multiplying by the variable image, of degree at most \(T\), stays within \(T(d+1)+\delta\le B\). Expand polynomial variable images into monomial multiplications. Certified axiom images and linear combinations therefore replay the entire PC proof and derive \(F\) from \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\) through \(B\).

Booleanization and separation. Let \(H\) be the squarefree Boolean remainder of \(F\). The difference \(F-H\) has an old Boolean certificate through \(\delta\), so \(H\) is also an old degree-\(B\) consequence. Since nonzero squarefree \(f\) is nonzero at some Boolean point, \(H\ne0\). Every term of \(H\) has total degree at most \(\delta\) and uses at most \(A=2(p-1)\) bits per row: it comes from a product of \(p-1\) row-cap-two monomials followed by Boolean power reduction.

Select a nonzero top monomial of \(H\), of degree \(\kappa\le\delta\), with \(u\) occupied rows and axis counts \(1\le d_i\le A\). Greedily place a coordinate cube for each row, avoiding earlier cubes. For the next \(d_i\)-axis cube there are \(n/2^{d_i}\) disjoint cosets, while fewer than \((u-1)2^A\le(\delta-1)2^A<n/2^A\) labels have been used. Each used label forbids at most one coset, so a placement exists. Let \(N_{\rm del}=\sum_i2^{d_i}\). Then

\[ N_{\rm del}-2u \le(2^A-2)u\le(2^A-2)\delta,\qquad n-N_{\rm del}\ge2(B-u)-1. \]

The residual board has enough rows because \(m\ge B\). It also has a remaining label: for \(\delta\ge2\), \(N_{\rm del}\le2^A\delta\le4^A(\delta-1)<n\); if \(\delta=1\), the only case is \(p=2,k=1\), and the selected cube has two labels while \(n\ge4\). The signed multi-axis detector, the decoder, and old PC stability now exclude \(H\). A nonzero constant target is excluded by the normalized old design directly. This contradicts the replayed proof.

For \(\ln M=\operatorname{polylog}n\) and polylogarithmic \(D\), the quantities \(k,T,\delta,B\) are \(\sqrt n\,\operatorname{polylog}n=o(n)\), and \(\varepsilon=o(1)\). Since \(A\) is fixed, all conditions hold eventually. Smaller proposed proof degrees can be enlarged to the displayed base threshold. This proves the qualitative assertion. The same assertion holds for any individual accuracies \(h_b\ge1\): set every coefficient row after the first to zero. \(\square\)

Scope. Accuracy one is the minimum positive accuracy. The theorem concerns refutations; it does not establish the older target-preservation or joint-selector claims at this new accuracy. Allowing quasipolynomial inventory is a sufficient degree-only endpoint, not a claim of polynomial-size proof simulation. Its usefulness follows from the existing logarithmic dependence on inventory.

2. The actual dense shared-bit source at accuracy one

Use actual old Boolean bits \(x,y_i\) over \(\mathbb F_p\). A bottom block \(B_i\) has input tuple \((x,y_i)\), accuracy one, product degree two, and companions of degree three. Each parent \(j\) reads the actual products \(P_{B_i}\), \(i\in I_j\), for an arbitrary nonempty list of distinct bottom blocks; different lists may overlap. Its product has original degree three and its companions have degree five. Every bottom and parent coefficient has its field equation. This is the actual unflattened shared-bit source, now at \(h=1\); no negation boundary is erased.

Working complete-transfer theorem. Over any old Boolean base, this system maps to one complete old-affine accuracy-one core per parent, with every NS/PC degree \(D\) preserved. Additional old-affine blocks may remain. The map covers arbitrary uses of raw coefficients and all overlaps.

Bottom images. Write \(\chi=1-x\), \(L_i=1-y_i\), and set

\[ r_{i,x}\longmapsto1,\qquad r_{i,y}\longmapsto\chi, \qquad P_{B_i}\longmapsto1-x-(1-x)y_i=\chi L_i. \tag{UA-bottom} \]

This single affine assignment is made once per bottom, even if many parents reuse it. With \(B_x=x^2-x\) and \(B_{y_i}=y_i^2-y_i\), its companion images are

\[ x\chi L_i=-B_xL_i,\qquad y_i\chi L_i=-\chi B_{y_i}, \]

both certified through the original degree three. The first coefficient field equation maps to zero; the second maps to \(\chi^p-\chi=-(x^p-x)\), which is a multiple of \(B_x\) through degree \(p\). All variable images have degree at most one. At odd primes the assumption that \(x,y_i\) are Boolean bits matters; arbitrary affine field-valued probes are outside this statement.

Parent images. Introduce a fresh affine core on \((L_i)_{i\in I_j}\), with product \(A_j=1-\sum_iR_{j,i}L_i\), companions \(L_iA_j\), and all \(R_{j,i}^p-R_{j,i}\). Rename the original parent coefficients to these core coefficients. Its product has the literal image

\[ \Phi(P_j)=1-\chi\sum_iR_{j,i}L_i =x+\chi A_j=:V_j. \tag{UA-parent} \]

For each parent companion the exact ordinary identity is

\[ \Phi(P_{B_i}P_j) =\chi L_iV_j =\chi(L_iA_j)+B_xL_i(A_j-1). \tag{UA-parent-companion} \]

The first generator multiple costs four, the second at most five, fitting the original companion degree five. Parent field equations are simply renamed, and old axioms are fixed. Thus every source axiom has a complete NS image within its own original degree. Affine substitution preserves cofactor degree in NS and primitive multiplication degree in PC, proving the complete \(D\mapsto D\) transfer. \(\square\)

Composing this map with Section 1 excludes polylogarithmic-degree refutations over \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\) for polynomially or quasipolynomially many blocks in this family. The earlier map covers \(h\ge2\), and this fills its missing accuracy-one case. Parent values remain \(x+(1-x)A_j\), so general later blocks still require a justified interface; no new target or clamping guarantee is inferred.

14 September 2026 — General rank-two bottoms with few conditioning coordinates

Status: working binary source-transfer and refutation-exclusion theorem, with complete exact branch controls. Cycle 138.

Obligation and stopping point. Move beyond the shared-bit two-level family by identifying the actual endpoint left by general rank-two affine bottoms. A maximal collection of jointly independent pairs gives a small set of conditioning coordinates when that collection is small. This cycle proves and checks the resulting complete source application, and stops there. Large independent-pair counts and their combination with branching remain open.

1. What the actual bottom layer leaves

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) and any old base \(\mathcal G\) containing all old Boolean equations. Use a common accuracy \(h\ge1\). Each bottom \(B_i\) has a proper rank-two old-affine tuple \((L_i,M_i)\), with independent homogeneous linear parts. A parent reads a nonempty tuple of actual products \(P_{B_i}\); different parents may overlap. Include all companions and every coefficient Boolean equation. Additional one-level old-affine blocks may remain.

Working normalization lemma. This complete system maps, without NS/PC degree increase, to \(\mathcal G\) plus one-level accuracy-\(h\) blocks on the old quadratic inputs

\[ q_i=(1-L_i)(1-M_i)=a_i b_i. \tag{QB-inputs} \]

Proof. At \(h=1\), send the bottom coefficients to \((1,1-L_i)\); the product is literally \(q_i\). At \(h\ge2\), send the first two rows to \((1,0)\), \((0,1)\), and every later row to zero. This is the canonical pair map, extended from bits to binary affine forms. For any such form \(L=c+\sum_jc_jx_j\),

\[ L^2-L=\sum_jc_j(x_j^2-x_j). \]

Consequently \(L_iq_i=-(L_i^2-L_i)(1-M_i)\) and \(M_iq_i=-(M_i^2-M_i)(1-L_i)\) have old Boolean certificates through three, within the original bottom companion degree \(2h+1\). Coefficient Boolean images have certificates through two at \(h=1\) and are zero for the scalar maps at larger \(h\). The assignment is made once per reused bottom.

Retain each parent's coefficients. Its product and companions map literally to the quadratic-input block's product and companions. Their new companion degree \(3h+2\) is at most the actual original degree \(h(2h+1)+2h=2h^2+3h\). All variable images have degree at most one, and every axiom image fits its original degree, proving the complete \(D\mapsto D\) transfer. \(\square\)

The result identifies the remaining source explicitly. In general the \(q_i\) have no common factor, so the shared-bit parent identity alone does not cover them.

2. A maximal independent-pair collection gives affine branches

Fix one parent tuple \((a_i b_i)_i\), and regard the homogeneous parts of its factors as vectors in the old linear-form space. Greedily select whole pairs whose two vectors increase the span dimension by two, until no pair can be added. If \(r\) pairs were selected, their \(2r\) vectors are jointly independent. Let \(U\) be their span, choose a basis \(u_1,\ldots,u_t\), \(t=2r\), and extend it to a full old linear-coordinate basis.

Working coordinate lemma. On each Boolean affine flat \(u=\sigma\in\mathbb F_2^t\), every \(a_i b_i\) agrees with an old-affine polynomial \(g_{\sigma,i}\). The greedy collection need only be maximal, not maximum.

Proof. Maximality says that the images of the two homogeneous factors in the quotient by \(U\) span at most one dimension. After setting \(u=\sigma\), either both factors are constant, only one is nonconstant, or their homogeneous parts equal the same remaining linear form \(w\). Only the last case needs reduction:

\[ (w+c)(w+d)\equiv(1+c+d)w+cd \pmod{{\rm BOOL}_{\rm old}},\qquad c,d\in\mathbb F_2. \tag{QB-branch} \]

Each right-hand side extends to an affine polynomial in the original old variables, by the chosen complementary coordinates. Thus the claim holds for every input simultaneously. A selected pair itself becomes constant. \(\square\)

This is a sufficient coordinate criterion; it does not bound \(r\) for an arbitrary dense tuple. The next construction also applies to any supplied \(t\)-dimensional linear subspace with this affine-on-each-branch property, regardless of how it was found.

3. Complete interpolation, with its degree and inventory costs

For a parent with conditioning coordinates \(u_1,\ldots,u_t\), define

\[ \chi_\sigma(u)=\prod_{j=1}^t \begin{cases}u_j,&\sigma_j=1,\\1-u_j,&\sigma_j=0.\end{cases} \qquad \sum_\sigma\chi_\sigma=1. \]

For every branch introduce a fresh complete affine block on \((g_{\sigma,i})_i\), of the same accuracy \(h\), with coefficients \(R_{\sigma,v,i}\), product \(A_\sigma\), all companions \(g_{\sigma,i}A_\sigma\), and all \(R_{\sigma,v,i}^2-R_{\sigma,v,i}\). Map the original quadratic block's coefficients by

\[ r_{v,i}\longmapsto\beta_{v,i} =\sum_\sigma\chi_\sigma R_{\sigma,v,i}, \qquad V=\sum_\sigma\chi_\sigma A_\sigma . \tag{QB-map} \]

Coefficient images have degree at most \(T=t+1\). This extends the existing residue-selector construction to several binary coordinates and applies it to the actual quadratic source identified above. The old coordinates need not be individual bits or independent of each input.

Old Boolean comparisons. At every old Boolean assignment exactly one selector is one. Keeping all new coefficients as formal indeterminates, that branch's inputs agree with \(q_i\). Old Boolean division therefore gives complete ordinary NS certificates

\[ E_{\sigma,i}:=\chi_\sigma(q_i-g_{\sigma,i}) \in\mathcal I_{t+2}({\rm BOOL}_{\rm old}),\qquad \Delta:=\Phi(P)-V \in\mathcal I_{h(t+3)}({\rm BOOL}_{\rm old}). \tag{QB-comparisons} \]

Each mapped factor has degree at most \(t+3\), while \(\deg V\le t+2h\le h(t+3)\). Divide only by old Boolean equations. The remainder is zero as a polynomial in the still-free \(R\)'s, because it vanishes at every old Boolean assignment. This argument does not use any new coefficient-domain or companion equation.

Companions. The exact identity

\[ q_i\Phi(P)=q_i\Delta+ \sum_\sigma\chi_\sigma(g_{\sigma,i}A_\sigma) +\sum_\sigma E_{\sigma,i}A_\sigma \tag{QB-companion} \]

has certificates through the maximum of \(h(t+3)+2\), \(t+2h+1\), and \(t+2+2h\), hence through \(h(t+3)+2\). The quadratic source companion has original degree \(e=3h+2\), and

\[ h(t+3)+2\le(t+1)(3h+2)=Te. \]

Coefficient domains. Frobenius gives the ordinary identity

\[ \beta_{v,i}^2-\beta_{v,i} =\sum_\sigma\chi_\sigma^2 (R_{\sigma,v,i}^2-R_{\sigma,v,i}) +\sum_\sigma(\chi_\sigma^2-\chi_\sigma)R_{\sigma,v,i}. \tag{QB-fields} \]

The second sum has old Boolean certificates. Every generator multiple in the first costs at most \(2t+2=2T\), and those in the second at most \(2t+1\). This fits \(T\) times the source field degree two. Old axioms stay fixed.

Working complete-transfer theorem. Suppose each quadratic parent \(j\) admits such coordinates of dimension \(t_j\), and put \(t=\max_jt_j\). With disjoint fresh branch coefficients, all maps are simultaneous and fix the old variables. A degree-\(D\) ordinary NS or PC proof transfers to the old base plus \(\sum_j2^{t_j}\) complete affine blocks through degree at most \((t+1)D\). Any already retained old-affine blocks remain. For NS, substituted cofactors cost at most \(T(D-e)\) and axiom-image certificates at most \(Te\). For PC, a nonzero multiplication predecessor has degree at most \(D-1\); its image and the degree-\(T\) variable image stay within \(TD\). Thus arbitrary raw coefficient uses are covered. \(\square\)

Branch tuples containing one or consisting of zeroes can be cleaned up afterward by the existing constant maps. The exponential branch count is charged explicitly; it is not declared polynomial. There is no additional factor for overlaps, parent count, or proof height.

4. A new two-level source exclusion

Working corollary. Over the binary compact base \(\mathcal Q_n\), consider the actual rank-two-bottom system from Section 1, with polynomially many bottom, parent, and additional old-affine blocks. Suppose each parent has a maximal jointly independent-pair collection of size at most \(R(n)=\operatorname{polylog}n\). Then, at any common accuracy \(h\ge1\), the system has no polylogarithmic-degree ordinary-PC refutation for sufficiently large \(n\).

Proof. The two maps send a proposed degree-\(D\) refutation to a complete affine family at degree \(D'\le(2R+1)D\). If \(M_0\) old-affine blocks and \(M\) parents were present, its inventory is bounded by

\[ M_{\rm aff}=M_0+\sum_j2^{t_j}\le M_0+M\,4^R. \]

For polylogarithmic \(R\), this is quasipolynomial, and \(D'\) is polylogarithmic. Apply the accuracy-one affine exclusion, first restricting each affine core to one coefficient row. That theorem permits this inventory and every larger individual accuracy, so it yields a contradiction. \(\square\)

The exact finite test can use \(k=\lceil\sqrt{(n+1)\ell\ln(4\max\{1,M_{\rm aff}\})}\rceil\),

\[ B=(2k+1)(t+1)D+k, \quad\varepsilon\le\tfrac12,\quad 16(k-1)<n,\quad n\ge2B+2k-1, \]

along with the range and base-degree hypotheses of that affine theorem. This records the actual degree cost before considering any larger \(R\). The corollary also excludes NS refutations in the same range, since their certificates replay as PC proofs.

Scope. No common bit or common polynomial factor is required, and the formal selector rank may be arbitrarily large. For example, the products \(ab,(a+z_i)(b+z_i)\) have no common affine factor and become affine after fixing \(a,b\), independently of the number of \(z_i\)'s. Large independent-pair counts are still uncovered. The present result does not supply a joint elimination theorem mixing these branch cores with other unhandled quadratic blocks, and it does not handle general later nonlinear inputs or settle the full Frege goal.

5. Exact noncommon-factor and overlap controls

The compiled exact checker uses five old bits \(a,b,c,d,e\), products \(ab,(a+c)(b+c),(a+d)(b+d),(a+e)(b+e)\), and parents on product lists \((0,1,2)\) and \((1,2,3)\). Their selected coordinate pairs are \((a,b)\) and \((a+c,b+c)\). Each whole factor span has rank four, while each selected pair is maximal and every remaining quotient pair has rank at most one. Neither parent tuple has a common affine polynomial factor.

At \(h=1\), the checker constructs the actual complete two-level source, all eight affine branch cores, and one simultaneous map of every coefficient. It retains 59 complete NS certificates, including all 33 original source axiom images. At \(h=2\), it checks the quadratic intermediate family, with 49 certificates including all 23 source images. The remaining certificates are the 24 branch-input comparisons and two parent-product comparisons in each fixture. All degree ceilings and every ordinary generator multiple are checked.

All 32 old Boolean assignments per fixture lift to complete source models. Removing a selected branch companion gives a target model violating the corresponding source image; using branch zero unconditionally instead of selecting the actual branch also fails. Adding the extra pair \(cd\) to coordinates \((a,b)\) gives quotient rank two and a nonzero quadratic branch input, detecting the missing hypothesis. These controls do not claim that this larger tuple has no other useful coordinate set.

All 108 exact certificates, 64 canonical models, two missing-companion models, and the additional branch controls passed. Two initial compiler indentation warnings were corrected before the mathematical run; the final compilation was clean. These are complete local Boolean-interface checks, not numerical PHP instances in the corollary's asymptotic regime. Full output, reproduction instructions, source hashes, and timing are retained.

Route assessment. The actual two-level application now covers general binary rank-two bottoms whenever each parent's conditioning dimension is polylogarithmic, including dense tuples without a common factor. This discharges the bounded-coordinate part of the proposed decomposition. The next unresolved source obligation is a parent with many jointly independent pairs; combining any future high-pair argument with this branching map requires its own degree accounting.

Process assessment. The existing residue-selector proof supplied the interpolation template, leaving the new work focused on actual source coverage and its complete ledger; shared NS verification was sufficient, so no additional framework rule is needed.

14 September 2026 — Combining independent pairs and affine branches

Status: working complete binary two-level source theorem, with exact mixed-map, quotient, cube, and parameter controls. Cycle 139.

Obligation. Handle parents with many jointly independent quadratic pairs and audit how they coexist with the bounded-coordinate branch construction. A direct simultaneous map adds the branch-selector and coefficient degrees. This avoids the larger product obtained by separately applying two generic whole-proof degree bounds. The resulting working argument covers the complete binary two-level rank-two-bottom family.

1. A large multiplier space with affordable row cubes

Let \(n=2^\ell\), \(m=n+1\), \(v=m\ell\). For a squarefree degree-\(k\) old-bit monomial \(z\), let \(d_i(z)\) be its degree in pigeon row \(i\), and set

\[ W(z)=\sum_{i=1}^m(4^{d_i(z)}-1),\qquad \mathcal S_k=\operatorname{span} \{z:\deg z=k,\ z\text{ squarefree},\ W(z)\le n/16\}. \tag{IQ-space} \]

Working dimension and separation lemma. Put

\[ \theta=\frac{16m}{n} \left[\left(1+\frac{3k}{v}\right)^\ell-1\right]. \]

Then \(\dim\mathcal S_k\ge(1-\theta)\binom vk\). If \(1\le k\le n/16\) and \(k\le B\le n/4\), every nonzero \(f\in\mathcal S_k\) is excluded from the old compact degree-\(B\) PC consequences.

Counting proof. Choose a uniform \(k\)-subset of the \(v\) bits. Expanding \(4^{d_i}=(1+3)^{d_i}\) and writing falling factorials gives

\[ \mathbb E W =m\sum_{s=1}^{\ell} 3^s\binom{\ell}{s}\frac{(k)_s}{(v)_s} \le m\left[\left(1+\frac{3k}{v}\right)^\ell-1\right]. \]

Terms with \(s>k\) are zero. The inequality uses \((k)_s/(v)_s\le(k/v)^s\). Markov's inequality bounds the fraction with \(W>n/16\) by \(\theta\), proving the dimension bound. In particular, \(\theta=o(1)\) whenever \(k=o(n)\), since the bracket is at most \(e^{3k/m}-1\).

Cube proof. Select a nonzero top monomial of \(f\), with \(u\) occupied rows and axis counts \(d_i\). Order these rows by decreasing \(d_i\). For the next cube of dimension \(d\), the number of labels already used satisfies

\[ 2^d N_{\rm used} \le\sum_{\text{earlier }i}4^{d_i} \le W+u\le n/16+k\le n/8<n. \]

There are \(n/2^d\) cosets with the required axes, and each used label forbids at most one, so a disjoint cube exists. The final deleted-label count is

\[ N_{\rm del}=\sum_i2^{d_i} \le\tfrac12\sum_i4^{d_i} =\tfrac12(W+u)\le n/16. \]

Hence \(n-N_{\rm del}\ge15n/16\ge2(B-u)-1\), with positive residual room and \(m\ge B\). Apply the signed residual detector, the compact decoder, and old PC stability. This proves separation. \(\square\)

This replaces the fixed row cap in the earlier multiplier space by a bound on the cost of the selected cubes. Individual rows may contain more than two selected bits; the complete record of the older detector remains its dependency.

2. The filtered quotient for independent quadratic pairs

Suppose a tuple contains \(R\) products \(a_jb_j\) whose \(2R\) homogeneous linear parts are jointly independent over \(\mathbb F_2\). Use the affine forms \(a_j,b_j\) as the first \(2R\) coordinates \(y_1,\ldots,y_{2R}\), and complete an invertible affine coordinate change. Booleanity of these coordinates has ordinary degree-two certificates from old Booleanity in either direction.

Working quotient lemma. The degree-at-most-\(k\) image modulo the selected products and old Booleanity has dimension

\[ J(v,R,k)=\sum_{j=0}^k[z^j](1+2z)^R(1+z)^{v-2R}. \tag{IQ-quotient} \]

In particular this bounds the image dimension of \(\mathcal S_k\). A kernel element \(f\in\mathcal S_k\) has an ordinary NS identity

\[ f=\sum_{j=1}^R a'_j(a_jb_j)+E,\qquad \deg a'_j\le k-2,\qquad E\in\mathcal I_k({\rm BOOL}_{\rm old}). \tag{IQ-membership} \]

Proof. In the \(y\)-coordinates, reduce Boolean powers and then remove every squarefree monomial containing both members of a selected pair. The remaining monomials choose neither or one of each pair and freely choose the other variables, giving (IQ-quotient). Their evaluations are independent on the product domain \(\{00,01,10\}^R\times\{0,1\}^{v-2R}\), so they form a basis. Every removed pair monomial is a selected product times a cofactor of degree at most \(k-2\). Boolean reductions also stay through \(k\). Pulling back by the affine coordinate change preserves these bounds and proves (IQ-membership). This is Boolean-ideal membership, not ordinary vanishing on an affine flat.

For \(1\le k\le v/2\), put \(z=k/(v-k)\). Since \(z\le1\), the sum of coefficients through \(k\) is at most \(z^{-k}\) times the full generating polynomial. The degree-\(k\) probability in the binomial distribution with parameter \(k/v\) is a mode, hence at least \(1/(v+1)\). Therefore

\[ \frac{J(v,R,k)}{\binom vk} \le(v+1)\left(\frac{1+2z}{(1+z)^2}\right)^R =(v+1)\left(1-\frac{k^2}{v^2}\right)^R \le(v+1)e^{-Rk^2/v^2}. \tag{IQ-dimension-ratio} \]

This explicitly accounts for the nonlinear quotient, whose dimension cannot be replaced by an affine-codimension formula. \(\square\)

3. One kernel handles both kinds of parent

Consider one-level accuracy-one blocks over \(\mathcal Q_n\), with quadratic tuples \((a_i b_i)_i\) as above and, optionally, old-affine tuples. Let \(M\ge1\) bound the total number of blocks. Choose \(1\le R\le v/2\). For each quadratic tuple, greedily select independent pairs until reaching \(R\) or becoming maximal. Call the first case high-pair. In the other case the coordinate lemma supplies \(t_j\le2(R-1)\) coordinates and at most \(2^{t_j}\) affine branch tuples.

Count these branch tuples and the original affine tuples together by \(N\le M4^R\). Scalar-clean zero and unit spans. In every other affine tuple call ranks at least \(2k+3\) high-affine and ranks at most \(2k+2\) low-affine. Suppose

\[ \theta\le\tfrac12,\qquad M(v+1)e^{-Rk^2/v^2}\le\tfrac18,\qquad M4^R e^{-k^2/v}\le\tfrac18. \tag{IQ-joint-dimension} \]

The high-pair quotient maps have total image dimension at most \(\binom vk/8\) by Section 2. The high-affine ordinary restrictions have total image dimension at most \(\binom vk/8\), by the existing restriction-image estimate; that estimate applies to any subspace of degree-\(k\) squarefree polynomials. Meanwhile \(\dim\mathcal S_k\ge\binom vk/2\). Thus a nonzero homogeneous \(f\in\mathcal S_k\) lies in every kernel simultaneously.

The two kinds of kernel have different meanings: high-pair tuples give (IQ-membership) modulo Booleanity, while a high-affine tuple gives literal \(f=\sum_i c_i g_i\), \(\deg c_i\le k-1\), by ordinary affine coordinates. Both are used with their stated meanings below.

4. A complete old-only map and the source theorem

Working finite theorem. In addition to (IQ-joint-dimension), assume

\[ D\ge\max\{\ell,5\},\quad 2\le k\le\min\{v/2,n/16\},\quad T=2k+2R-1,\quad B=TD+k\le n/4. \tag{IQ-degree-room} \]

Then the complete accuracy-one affine/quadratic family has no ordinary-PC refutation of degree at most \(D\).

High-pair maps. Use the cofactors \(a'_j\) from (IQ-membership) as the coefficients of selected inputs and zero for all other inputs. The product becomes \(1-f+E\), with \(E\) an old Boolean consequence through \(k\). At every old Boolean point where \(f=1\), this product is zero. Coefficient images have degree at most \(k-2\).

Affine maps. For a high-affine tuple use its literal coefficients \(c_i\), giving product \(1-f\). For a proper low-affine tuple of rank \(s\le2k+2\), the one-bin telescoping map gives the exact flat indicator \(\prod_{j=1}^s(1-L_j)\), with coefficient degree at most \(s-1\le2k+1\). Zero tuples take zero coefficients; unit spans use a constant representation of one. Consequently every affine tuple has old-only coefficients \(\gamma_i\), of degree at most \(2k+1\), whose companions vanish on all old Boolean points with \(f=1\).

Low-pair maps. For the branches of a low-pair parent, substitute these old-only \(\gamma_{\sigma,i}\) directly into the branch interpolation:

\[ \beta_i=\sum_\sigma\chi_\sigma\gamma_{\sigma,i}, \qquad \deg\beta_i\le t_j+2k+1\le T. \tag{IQ-direct-map} \]

At an old Boolean point with \(f=1\), the selector chooses its actual branch, on which \(q_i=g_{\sigma,i}\); the affine companion property therefore gives \(q_i(1-\sum_j\beta_jq_j)=0\). All source coefficients now have old-only images. The branch tuples index their construction; no branch axioms are assumed in the final old-base proof. The degrees in (IQ-direct-map) add because the affine map fixes the old variables appearing in \(\chi_\sigma\).

Full original-degree ledger. Weight the simultaneously substituted proof by \(f\). Every weighted companion vanishes on the full old Boolean cube: the weight is zero where \(f=0\), and the mapped companion is zero where \(f=1\). Old Boolean division certifies it through its actual ordinary degree. The resulting bounds are

\[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{source axiom}&\text{original degree }e& \text{weighted old NS ceiling}\\ \hline \text{affine companion}&3&T+k+2\\ \text{quadratic companion}&5&T+k+4\\ \text{coefficient Booleanity}&2&2T+k\\ \text{old axiom}&e&e+k . \end{array} \tag{IQ-ledger} \]

Each row fits \(Te+k\). Coefficient Boolean images vanish at every old Boolean point, and old axioms retain their original generators. A primitive multiplication with predecessor degree \(d\le D-1\) has weighted image degree at most \(Td+k\), and its variable image costs at most \(T\). The complete proof therefore replays over \(\mathcal Q_n\) through \(B=TD+k\), deriving \(f\). Section 1 excludes that old consequence, proving the finite theorem. \(\square\)

Working actual-source corollary. Every polynomial-inventory complete binary two-level family whose bottoms are proper rank-two old-affine tuples and whose parents read their actual products has no polylogarithmic-degree PC refutation over \(\mathcal Q_n\), for sufficiently large \(n\), at any common accuracy \(h\ge1\). Additional old-affine blocks may remain. No bound on the parents' independent-pair counts or formal selector ranks is required.

Parameters and source proof. The complete bottom normalization first gives quadratic parent inputs without degree loss. Restrict every parent and additional affine block to its first coefficient row, also without degree loss. For the resulting one-level family set

\[ L=\ln(8M(v+1)),\qquad R=\left\lceil\sqrt{vL}\right\rceil,\qquad k=\left\lceil\max\left\{ \sqrt{v\ln(8M4^R)},\ v\sqrt{L/R}\right\}\right\rceil . \tag{IQ-choice} \]

For polynomial \(M\), \(R=O(\sqrt n\log n)\), \(k=O(n^{3/4}\log n)\), and \(\theta=o(1)\). Both image-sum bounds hold by construction. With polylogarithmic \(D\), \(B=n^{3/4}\operatorname{polylog}n=o(n)\), so the remaining finite conditions hold eventually. Applying the theorem gives the contradiction. NS refutations in that range are also excluded by their PC replay. \(\square\)

Scope. This closes the complete binary two-level rank-two-bottom class, including arbitrary overlaps and arbitrary raw coefficient uses. The potentially \(M4^R\) branch count is used only in the dimension argument; it is not claimed polynomial and is not enumerated in a computation. General higher-rank bottoms, later nonlinear levels, and odd-prime affine probes remain outside this theorem. The publication draft and the full ordinary-PHP \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege goal retain their separate status.

5. Focused evidence

The compiled exact checker treats three quadratic blocks together: a high-pair tuple, a low-pair tuple with a high-affine branch, and a low-pair tuple with a low-affine branch. The high inputs are \((a+b)(a+c)\) and \((d+e)(d+f)\). Their chosen homogeneous squarefree kernel is

Its ordinary restriction to \(b=a,e=d\) is \(a^2d+ad^2\ne0\), although both selected products vanish there. This checks the necessary Boolean residual in (IQ-membership). The combined old-only map has actual coefficient degree four: two from the selector plus two from the high-affine coefficients. Exact finite parameter controls. For \(M=n^2\), \(D=\ell^2\), let \(q=\lceil\log_2\ell\rceil\), \(H=3\ell+q+4\), \(R=\lceil\sqrt{vH}\rceil\), and choose integer \(k\) so that \(k^2\ge v(2\ell+2R+3)\) and \(Rk^2\ge v^2H\), taking the least value satisfying both.
