14 September 2026 — Rank-three bottoms and closure under conditioning

Status: working complete binary source theorem through rank three, with exact normalization, branch-closure, mixed-map, and parameter controls. Cycle 140.

Obligation and stopping point. Extend the actual two-level source from rank-two to rank-three affine bottoms, first checking that conditioning preserves a usable input class. The necessary closure is into individual lower-rank flat indicators, including zero and one. This cycle does not assert closure for the arbitrary sums of flat indicators occurring in the broader compiled source; that is a separate application obligation.

1. The complete source becomes cubic flat indicators

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\), with an old Boolean base, and common accuracy \(h\ge1\). Each bottom tuple is old-affine with proper rank at most three, and each parent reads actual bottom products; arbitrary overlaps and additional old-affine blocks are allowed. Zero and unit spans can be handled by their existing constant maps. Choose an affine basis \(L_1,\ldots,L_r\), \(r\le3\), for a remaining bottom span.

Working normalization lemma. The complete system transfers to one level on old inputs \(q=\prod_{j=1}^r(1-L_j)\), preserving degree for \(h\ge2\), and with degree factor at most two for \(h=1\).

Proof. Pack the \(r\) factors into \(h\) bins and telescope each bin into its own coefficient row, pulling basis coefficients back to the original tuple by constant combinations. At \(h=1,r=3\), the basis coefficients can be

\[ 1,\qquad1-L_1,\qquad(1-L_1)(1-L_2). \]

At \(h=2\), put two factors in one bin and the third in the other; all coefficient images are affine. At \(h\ge3\), all images can be constant. In every case the bottom product is literally \(q\). Each companion vanishes on the old Boolean cube and has an old Boolean NS certificate through \(r+1\le4\). This fits twice the original degree \(2h+1\) at \(h=1\), and that original degree itself when \(h\ge2\). Coefficient Boolean images fit twice the image degree, giving ceilings four and two, respectively. Lower-rank bottoms obey the same bounds.

Keep all parent coefficients. Their images are exactly the complete blocks on the new inputs \(q\). The global variable map has degree at most two, and at most one when \(h\ge2\); its axiom images fit the corresponding original-degree budgets. Ordinary NS and PC therefore transfer with those factors, including arbitrary coefficient uses. Finally restrict each parent and additional affine block to its first coefficient row, without further degree increase. Write \(D_0\le2D\) for the resulting incoming degree. \(\square\)

2. A conditioned indicator stays a lower-rank indicator

Let \(q=\prod_{j=1}^s a_j\), \(s\le3\), be a product of binary affine forms. Suppose that after fixing some independent linear coordinates, the remaining homogeneous parts span at most \(r\). Then, on that branch, \(q\) agrees with either zero or a product of at most \(r\) affine forms with independent homogeneous parts; the empty product one is allowed.

Proof. The product is one exactly when every equation \(a_j=1\) holds. Gaussian elimination on these affine equations either finds inconsistency, giving the zero function, or gives an equivalent affine basis \(F_1=\cdots=F_t=0\), \(t\le r\). The indicator is then \(\prod_{\nu=1}^t(1-F_\nu)\). This equality is on the old Boolean cube. It extends to an ordinary Boolean NS comparison after multiplication by the branch selector: a selector of degree \(u\) gives a certificate through \(u+s\), by degree-preserving old Boolean division. \(\square\)

Greedily selecting whole independent triples until maximal supplies the relevant coordinates: if fewer than \(R_3\) triples are selected, their span has dimension at most \(3(R_3-1)\), and every remaining triple has quotient rank at most two. Existing rank-two or rank-one inputs already obey that bound. Thus each branch tuple consists of indicators of rank at most two. Applying the pair argument inside such a tuple similarly yields affine branch inputs. No assumption that a product remains literally multilinear is made.

3. Three kinds of kernel constraints

The independent-pair quotient proof extends to \(R_3\) products of three jointly independent affine factors. In affine Boolean coordinates, remove monomials containing all three members of any selected triple. The filtered quotient dimension is

\[ J_3(v,R_3,k)=\sum_{j=0}^k[z^j] \bigl((1+z)^3-z^3\bigr)^{R_3}(1+z)^{v-3R_3}. \]

For \(1\le k\le v/2\), the same generating-function and binomial-mode argument gives

\[ \frac{J_3(v,R_3,k)}{\binom vk} \le(v+1)\left(1-(k/v)^3\right)^{R_3} \le(v+1)e^{-R_3k^3/v^3}. \tag{RT-triple-quotient} \]

A kernel polynomial has an ordinary NS representation by the selected cubic products and old Booleanity through \(k\), with product cofactors through \(k-3\). This follows from the explicit monomial reduction and the affine Boolean coordinate change, exactly as for pairs.

Let \(M\ge1\) bound the original one-level block count. At each root tuple, stop triple selection at \(R_3\), or branch on a maximal smaller selection. At each resulting rank-at-most-two tuple, stop pair selection at \(R_2\), or branch on a maximal smaller selection. Count pair-stage tuples by \(N_2=M2^{3R_3}\) and affine-stage tuples by \(N_1=M2^{3R_3+2R_2}\). These are upper bounds; zero/unit tuples and smaller coordinate sets only reduce them.

Use the cube-volume space \(\mathcal S_k\), with its parameter \(\theta\). In affine-stage tuples use the earlier rank threshold \(2k+3\). If

\[ \begin{aligned} \theta&\le\tfrac12,\\ M(v+1)e^{-R_3k^3/v^3}&\le\tfrac18,\\ N_2(v+1)e^{-R_2k^2/v^2}&\le\tfrac18,\\ N_1e^{-k^2/v}&\le\tfrac18, \end{aligned} \tag{RT-joint-dimension} \]

the three families of restriction/quotient maps have total image dimension at most \(3\binom vk/8\), below \(\dim\mathcal S_k\ge\binom vk/2\). A common nonzero homogeneous \(f\in\mathcal S_k\) therefore exists. Triple and pair membership is modulo old Booleanity; high-affine membership is literal ordinary flat vanishing.

4. The complete map and final parameters

Working finite theorem. Consider complete accuracy-one blocks whose old inputs are individual flat indicators of rank at most three, with their own coefficient Boolean equations. Allow zero inputs and arbitrary mixtures of ranks inside a tuple. Suppose (RT-joint-dimension) holds, \(3R_3\le v\), \(2R_2\le v\), \(k\ge3\), and

\[ k\le\min\{v/2,n/16\},\quad T=2k+1+3(R_3-1)+2(R_2-1),\quad B=TD_0+k\le n/4,\quad D_0\ge\max\{\ell,7\}. \tag{RT-degree-room} \]

Then the system has no ordinary-PC refutation through \(D_0\).

Coefficient construction. High-triple tuples use the selected-product NS cofactors through \(k-3\), giving product \(1-f+E\) with an old Boolean residual. High-pair tuples use the corresponding cofactors through \(k-2\). At affine leaves, high ranks use the literal coefficients for \(f\); low proper ranks use exact one-bin flat indicators with coefficient degree at most \(2k+1\). Zero tuples and spans containing one have their constant maps.

Interpolate these old-only coefficients upward along the pair branches, then the triple branches. Each interpolation multiplies by an old selector, so the degrees add. At a root the coefficient degree is at most

\[ 3(R_3-1)+2(R_2-1)+(2k+1)=T. \]

At every old Boolean point with \(f=1\), the actual branch is selected, the current input indicators agree with their branch representatives, and the mapped companions vanish. This proves the conditional companion property at every root. All original coefficients receive one simultaneous old-only image; no virtual branch axiom is assumed in the final old proof.

Mixed original degrees. In a root tuple write \(d_i=\deg g_i\) and \(\delta=\max_i d_i\). Nonzero companions have original degree \(e_i=d_i+\delta+1\). Constant-one inputs can be removed by their unit map; zero companions are immaterial. The weighted companion's ordinary degree is at most

\[ k+d_i+(T+\delta) \le k+T(d_i+\delta+1)=k+Te_i. \]

It vanishes on the old Boolean cube and hence has an old Boolean NS certificate within that ceiling. Weighted coefficient domains cost \(2T+k\); old axiom images cost \(e+k\). The complete weighted PC replay therefore derives \(f\) over \(\mathcal Q_n\) through \(B=TD_0+k\). The cube-volume separation theorem contradicts this consequence. The same argument covers NS proofs by PC replay. \(\square\)

Working actual-source corollary. Polynomially many complete binary two-level blocks with proper rank-at-most-three affine bottoms and arbitrary overlapping parent tuples have no polylogarithmic-degree PC refutation over \(\mathcal Q_n\), for sufficiently large \(n\), at any common accuracy. Additional old-affine blocks are allowed.

Proof of the asymptotic regime. Apply Section 1 and enlarge the incoming degree to \(\max\{2D,\ell,7\}\), still polylogarithmic. Put \(L=\ln(8M(v+1))\), and choose

\[ R_3=\left\lceil(v^3L^4)^{1/7}\right\rceil,\qquad R_2=\left\lceil4(v^5L^2)^{1/7}\right\rceil,\qquad k=\left\lceil4(v^6L)^{1/7}\right\rceil . \tag{RT-choice} \]

For polynomial \(M\), \(L=\Theta(\log n)\). The triple exponent is at least \(64L\) to leading order. The pair exponent is \(64(v^3L^4)^{1/7}\) to leading order, while its required logarithm is \(L+3R_3\ln2\). The affine exponent is \(16(v^5L^2)^{1/7}\) to leading order, while its required logarithm is \(\ln(8M)+(3R_3+2R_2)\ln2\), whose leading term is \(8\ln2\,(v^5L^2)^{1/7}\). The strict constant margins absorb ceilings for sufficiently large \(n\). Thus all image-count conditions hold.

Moreover \(R_3=O(n^{3/7}\log n)\), \(R_2=O(n^{5/7}\log n)\), and \(k=O(n^{6/7}\log n)\). Hence \(\theta=o(1)\), all coordinate ranges fit, and \(B=n^{6/7}\operatorname{polylog}n=o(n)\). The finite theorem applies. \(\square\)

Scope. This is a binary theorem for individual bounded-rank flat indicators and the specified actual two-level source. Arbitrary sums of these indicators do not inherit the factor-selection or branch-closure hypotheses. Higher-rank bottoms growing with \(n\), later nonlinear levels, and odd-prime affine probes are also outside the claim. No general bounded-rank induction or full Frege lower bound is asserted here.

5. Focused evidence

The existing combined-source checker now accepts --rank-three. The new mode preserves all systems, coefficient maps, targets, ordinary NS cofactors, and model assignments. Its default rank-two output remains byte-identical to the recorded cycle-139 output.

Normalization and closure. Fifteen exact certificates cover every bottom companion and coefficient-domain image at \(h=1\) and \(h=2\), with degree factors two and one, respectively. Another 512 certificates check every ordered triple of affine factors on two Boolean variables, reconstructing its indicator by affine Gaussian elimination. There are 301 inconsistent triples; the consistent indicators have ranks zero, one, and two in 1, 42, and 168 cases. Two further certificates check the conditional identity \(ab(a+b+u)=0\) on \(u=0\) and \(ab(a+b+u)=ab\) on \(u=1\), modulo old Booleanity. The unreduced cubic at \(u=0\) is not the zero ordinary polynomial, guarding the distinction.

One nested map. The eighteen-bit fixture combines a high-triple tuple, a low-triple parent with a high-pair branch, and two further low-triple parents with high- and low-affine leaves. The kernel is \(zwF\), where \(F\) is the cubic kernel in the preceding cycle. The high triples are \(z(a+b)(a+c)\) and \(w(d+e)(d+f)\). The affine leaf has thirteen independent coordinates, exactly \(2k+3\) for \(k=5\). The maximum coefficient degree is nine: three from the outer selector, two from the inner selector, and four from the affine coefficient.

Sixty-six complete weighted original axiom images and one explicit triple-kernel Boolean residual give 67 certificates for this joint system. All 14,336 old Boolean assignments with nonzero kernel produce complete conditional source models. An unweighted high-triple companion fails where the kernel is zero; omitting the outer unit-branch coefficient fails even at a nonzero-kernel point. These are local Boolean-domain controls, not a finite PHP instance satisfying the asymptotic theorem.

Quotients and parameters. Three complete generating-function coefficient tables are cross-checked by an independent multinomial formula; the two small cases additionally enumerate all Boolean monomials. For \(v=60,R_3=20,k=30\), the quotient through thirty has dimension \(75{,}041{,}971{,}313{,}315{,}926\), below the homogeneous domain dimension \(118{,}264{,}581{,}564{,}861{,}424\). The rational bound preceding (RT-triple-quotient) is checked with exact integers.

For \(M=n^2\), source degree \(D=\ell^2\), and \(D_0=2D\), exact parameter controls use \(H=3\ell+\lceil\log_2\ell\rceil+4\), \(R_3=\lceil(v^3H^4)^{1/7}\rceil\), \(R_2=4\lceil(v^5H^2)^{1/7}\rceil\), and \(k=4\lceil(v^6H)^{1/7}\rceil\). Integer inequalities bound the required logarithms by \(H\), \(H+3R_3\), and \(2\ell+3+3R_3+2R_2\), respectively. The checks \(6k\le n+1\) and \(192k\le n\) certify \(\theta\le1/2\), as in the preceding cycle. At \(\ell=256,512\) all sufficient conditions pass; at \(\ell=128\) the range, space, and image-count conditions pass but \(4B\le n\) fails. Branch inventories remain symbolic.

14 September 2026 — Treating sums directly through bounded affine probes

Status: working binary bounded-probe source theorem and actual bounded-sum application, with complete exact controls. Cycle 141.

Obligation and stopping point. Audit the sums of indicators in the actual residual source. Such sums need not remain individual indicators or retain product generators in their input span. The replacement criterion below uses the number of independent affine probes needed by each input function, and handles a bounded number of bounded-rank summands directly. Unbounded sums remain a separate gap.

1. The previous factor hypothesis is genuinely lost

Over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(q=ab+cd\) is a sum of two rank-two flat indicators, but it is one at six of the sixteen assignments. A nonzero affine-flat indicator has support of power-of-two size, so \(q\) is not an individual flat indicator of any rank.

The failure persists for an arbitrarily large input span. Take \(q_i=a_ib_i+c_id_i\) on disjoint four-variable groups. In a nonzero sum of \(t\) such inputs, each group has bias \(1/4\), so the support on those \(4t\) variables has size

\[ \frac{2^{4t}}2\left(1-4^{-t}\right) =2^{2t-1}(2^{2t}-1), \]

which is not a power of two. Unused coordinates multiply this by another power of two. Thus the nonzero input span contains no affine-flat indicator. Its nonzero quadratic forms also have polar rank at least four, whereas a product of two affine forms has polar rank at most two.

This is a boundary of the previous argument, not a hardness theorem. A single-input block on \(q\) has the constant coefficient choice one and companion \(q-q^2\), certified by old Booleanity through four. The input ideal may also contain useful higher-degree products even when the linear span does not. A valid extension must preserve the actual sums and their coefficient interfaces.

2. A reduction map for nonfactorable input functions

Call an old polynomial \(g\) an \(r\)-probe input if its function on the old Boolean cube depends on at most \(r\) affine forms with independent homogeneous parts. We also retain its actual ordinary degree bound \(\deg g\le s\). In affine coordinates extending the probes, its unique multilinear representative is supported on those probe coordinates and has degree at most \(s\): affine substitution and Boolean reduction do not increase degree.

Suppose a tuple contains \(R\) nonconstant inputs, each supplied with \(j\) probes, whose \(jR\) homogeneous probe vectors are jointly independent. Use these as disjoint coordinate groups. Let \(F_i\) be each input's multilinear representative, choose a fixed graded lexicographic order, and let \(m_i\) be its leading monomial. Its degree \(d_i\) satisfies \(1\le d_i\le a_j:=\min(s,j)\), and the \(m_i\)'s use disjoint variable groups.

Working reduction lemma. There is a linear reduction map on degree-at-most-\(k\) polynomials whose image is spanned by squarefree monomials avoiding every \(m_i\). For \(1\le k\le v/2\), its image dimension is at most

\[ \binom vk\,(v+1) \prod_{i=1}^R\left(1-(k/v)^{d_i}\right) \le\binom vk\,(v+1)e^{-R(k/v)^{a_j}}. \tag{BP-reduction-bound} \]

If \(f\) lies in its kernel, then

\[ f=\sum_{i=1}^R c_i g_i+E,\qquad \deg c_i\le k-1,\qquad E\in\mathcal I_{k+s-1}({\rm BOOL}_{\rm old}), \tag{BP-membership} \]

assuming \(k\ge s\). In particular, the selected source coefficients can make the product zero on every old Boolean point with \(f=1\).

Proof. Use the divisors \(y_\nu^2-y_\nu\) and \(F_i\), with a fixed priority among applicable leading monomials. Define reduction on a monomial by replacing its first divisible leading monomial and recursively reducing the smaller resulting monomials; extend linearly. Graded lexicographic order decreases at every replacement, and total degree does not increase. This gives a linear map even without asserting that the divisors form a Gröbner basis. Every reduction has an explicit ordinary certificate through the starting degree, with \(F_i\)-cofactors of degree at most \(k-d_i\).

A normal monomial is squarefree and avoids the mutually disjoint supports \(m_i\). Its generating function is

\[ (1+z)^{v-\sum_i d_i} \prod_i\bigl((1+z)^{d_i}-z^{d_i}\bigr). \]

Evaluate at \(z=k/(v-k)\) and apply the same binomial-mode bound as in the pair quotient argument. This proves (BP-reduction-bound); it is an image-dimension upper bound, not an assertion that all these normal monomials are independent in the quotient.

For a kernel element, pull the reduction certificate back to old affine coordinates. Each coefficient still has degree at most \(k-d_i\le k-1\). The representative \(F_i\) agrees with the actual \(g_i\) on the old Boolean cube. Their difference has a Boolean certificate through \(s\), so replacing \(F_i\) by \(g_i\) gives (BP-membership) through \(k+s-1\). The conditional product conclusion uses this Boolean identity, with every unselected coefficient set to zero. \(\square\)

The selected generators remain the actual input functions \(g_i\). No replacement of \(ab+cd\) by the separate inputs \(ab,cd\) is used.

3. A complete one-level theorem for bounded probe dimension

Working finite theorem. Over \(\mathcal Q_n\), let \(M\ge1\) bound the number of complete accuracy-one blocks, all of whose old inputs have degree at most \(s\) and are \(r\)-probe inputs. Keep every coefficient Boolean equation. Fix integers \(R_j\ge1\), \(j=1,\ldots,r\), with \(jR_j\le v\), and put

\[ a_j=\min(s,j),\qquad N_j=M\,2^{\sum_{u>j}uR_u},\qquad T=k-1+\sum_{j=1}^r j(R_j-1),\qquad B=TD+k. \]

Assume \(k\ge\max\{2,s\}\), \(k\le\min\{v/2,n/16\}\), \(D\ge\max\{\ell,2s+1\}\), and

\[ \theta\le\tfrac12,\qquad B\le n/4,\qquad N_j(v+1)e^{-R_j(k/v)^{a_j}}\le\frac1{4r} \quad(1\le j\le r), \tag{BP-finite-conditions} \]

where \(\theta\) is the cube-volume dimension parameter. Then the complete system has no ordinary-PC refutation through degree \(D\).

Branch construction. At a stage-\(j\) tuple, each current input is a function of at most \(j\) affine probes and still has Boolean degree at most \(s\). Handle constant-one functions by choosing their coefficient one, and constant-zero functions by coefficient zero. Greedily select nonconstant inputs with \(j\)-dimensional probe spaces until reaching \(R_j\) jointly independent groups or becoming maximal. In the first case retain the reduction-map constraint from Section 2.

In the second case, condition on the span of the selected probes, of dimension at most \(j(R_j-1)\). Every unselected \(j\)-probe space then has quotient dimension at most \(j-1\); inputs using fewer probes already satisfy that bound. On each branch, represent every input by its multilinear function in complementary coordinates. Degree remains at most \(s\). Thus each child is a stage-\((j-1)\) tuple. At stage zero the inputs are constants and the companion property has a constant coefficient assignment.

This recursive tree is finite and has at most \(N_j\) stage-\(j\) nodes. Its construction depends on the input functions and chosen probe spaces, before choosing \(f\). By (BP-reduction-bound) and (BP-finite-conditions), all high-node maps together have image dimension at most \(\binom vk/4\). The space \(\mathcal S_k\) has dimension at least \(\binom vk/2\), so a common nonzero homogeneous \(f\in\mathcal S_k\) lies in every kernel.

One old-only coefficient map. At a high node use (BP-membership), with coefficients through \(k-1\). At a low node interpolate its children's coefficients using the old Boolean selectors of its conditioning coordinates. The selector degrees add along a path, giving the displayed bound \(T\). Every root coefficient is now an old-only polynomial. At every old Boolean point with \(f=1\), the actual branches are selected and the current input functions agree with their representatives; all mapped root companions vanish.

Weight the entire substituted proof by \(f\). If an actual root input has degree \(d_i\) and the tuple's maximum input degree is \(\delta\), its nonzero companion has original degree \(e_i=d_i+\delta+1\). Its weighted image is Boolean-zero and has ordinary degree at most

\[ k+d_i+T+\delta\le k+Te_i. \]

It therefore has a complete old Boolean NS certificate through that ceiling. Weighted coefficient Booleanity costs \(2T+k\); old axiom images cost \(e+k\). The complete weighted PC replay derives \(f\) through \(TD+k=B\), contradicting cube-volume separation. This includes arbitrary raw coefficient uses. NS refutations are excluded by PC replay. \(\square\)

Fixed-parameter consequence. Fix \(r,s\), put \(S=\sum_{j=1}^r\min(s,j)\), and let \(M\) be polynomial in \(n\). Any polylogarithmic proof degree is excluded for sufficiently large \(n\). To see this, set

\[ L=\ln(4rM(v+1)),\qquad k=\left\lceil(v^S L)^{1/(S+1)}\right\rceil, \]

and, from \(j=r\) down to one, choose

\[ R_j=\left\lceil(v/k)^{a_j} \left(L+\ln2\sum_{u>j}uR_u\right)\right\rceil. \tag{BP-thresholds} \]

These choices give the required image-count inequalities. With \(A=v/k\to\infty\), backward induction gives \(R_j=O(A^{\sum_{u\ge j}a_u}L)\), with constants depending only on \(r,s\). Since \(A^SL=O(k)\), every \(R_j=O(k)\), and \(T=O(k)\). Here \(k=O(n^{S/(S+1)}\log n)=o(n)\), so \(\theta=o(1)\), all ranges fit, and \(B=O(kD)=o(n)\). Smaller proposed degrees can be enlarged to the fixed/base threshold. Larger individual accuracies reduce to one by setting later coefficient rows to zero.

4. Application to actual bounded sums of bottom products

Working source corollary. Fix positive integers \(b,c\). Consider a complete binary two-level system in which every bottom tuple is proper old-affine of rank at most \(b\), and every parent input is a fixed linear combination of at most \(c\) actual bottom products. Parent tuples may have arbitrarily many inputs and overlap arbitrarily. With polynomial block inventory, no polylogarithmic-degree PC refutation exists over \(\mathcal Q_n\) for sufficiently large \(n\), at any common accuracy.

Complete transfer. Telescope a bottom affine basis into one coefficient row and set the other rows to zero. Its exact product is the associated rank-at-most-\(b\) flat indicator. Coefficient degree is at most \(b-1\), and a companion has an old Boolean certificate through \(b+1\). With \(T_0=\max(1,b-1)\), these fit \(T_0\) times the original companion and field degrees; all other axiom images are the actual substituted source axioms. Thus the complete normalization costs at most \(D_0=T_0D\), with sharper earlier maps available in special cases.

Every parent input becomes the actual sum of at most \(c\) indicators, of degree at most \(b\), depending on at most \(bc\) affine probes. Apply Section 3 with \(r=bc,s=b\), after restricting parent coefficient rows to accuracy one. The constants \(b,c\) keep \(D_0\) polylogarithmic. Every bottom is assigned once, all sums remain intact, and every source coefficient equation is included. \(\square\)

An additional old-affine summand is also allowed by taking \(r=bc+1\), \(s=\max\{b,1\}\). In the simplest new case, \(b=c=2\) and no extra affine summand, \(r=4,s=2,S=7\), giving old degree \(n^{7/8}\operatorname{polylog}n=o(n)\). This directly covers sums such as \(ab+cd\), regardless of whether the input span contains factorable polynomials.

Remaining gap. The full residual source allows the number of summands and the probe dimension to grow with \(n\), and may include old terms outside the stated affine-offset class. The fixed-parameter theorem does not cover those cases or further nonlinear levels. Bounded polynomial degree alone does not imply bounded affine-probe dimension: a sum of many disjoint quadratic terms can have large polar rank. No full Frege lower bound is claimed.

5. Focused evidence

The compiled exact checker verifies the reduction for the actual nonfactorable generators \(y_0y_1+y_2y_3\) and \(y_4y_5+y_6y_7\). It reduces all 495 ordinary monomials through degree four in eight old variables after an invertible affine coordinate change, including a constant shift. Every certificate is pulled back to the old variables and reconstructed using old Booleanity and the two actual input polynomials, within the original monomial degree.

The normal output space has 120 monomials. Its full evaluation matrix on the 100 common-zero points has rank 100, with the matrix, reduced matrix, and pivots retained. A polynomial already in the input ideal has a nonzero normal remainder, whose degree-three ideal certificate is also saved. This guards the distinction between the linear reduction map used for the dimension bound and a full quotient normal form.

Seven nonzero combinations of three disjoint quadratic sums have support sizes 1536, 1920, or 2016 on twelve bits, and polar ranks four, eight, or twelve. All are outside the affine-flat indicator class. Four ordinary Boolean certificates also check restrictions of \(ab+cd\), including the nonfactorable intermediate \(b+cd\) and the two-probe function \(1+cd\).

Actual complete sum-source map. Three bottom blocks have values \(ab,cd,ef\), and one parent reads the actual sums of bottom products giving \(ab+cd\) and \(ab+ef\). Map both parent coefficients to \(a\), consistently with the affine bottom maps. The parent product becomes \(1-F\), where \(F=a(cd+ef)\). All 22 weighted original source axiom images, including every bottom and parent coefficient equation, have complete old Boolean NS certificates through their original degree plus three. All twelve old assignments with \(F\ne0\) give complete conditional source models. An unweighted companion fails when \(F=0\).

A separate expanded-input model has \(ab=1,cd=0\) and both expanded coefficients equal to one. Summing those coefficients to represent the original input \(ab+cd\) gives coefficient zero and a violated original companion, while the expanded companions hold. This refutes that proposed coefficient map, without claiming that every transfer from an expanded system is impossible.

In total, 522 exact NS certificates passed: 495 basis reductions, one extra ideal relation, 22 complete weighted source images, and four restriction comparisons. For \(r=4,s=2,M=n^2,D=\ell^2\), integer parameter checks choose \(H=3\ell+\lceil\log_2\ell\rceil+5\), \(k=\lceil(v^7H)^{1/8}\rceil\), and recursively \(R_j=\lceil v^{\min(2,j)}(H+\sum_{u>j}uR_u)/k^{\min(2,j)}\rceil\). These upper-bound the logarithms in (BP-thresholds). At \(\ell=256,512\), all sufficient inequalities hold; at \(\ell=128\), the range, space, and image-count conditions hold but the old-degree bound fails. The branch inventory is never materialized.

Compilation and all checks passed. Complete polynomials, certificates, and matrices, reproduction and scope, source hashes, and timing accompany the result. The local fixtures test the interfaces; the large integer cases test the finite inequalities, not an instantiated large PHP proof.

Route assessment. The working criterion addresses actual sums through a sufficient probe bound and preserves their full source interfaces. It replaces a lost factor hypothesis without asserting that the arbitrary compiled residual family has bounded probes.

Process assessment. The input-span counterexample prevented an invalid summand expansion, and a monomial-reduction image bound supplied the needed coefficient witnesses directly; no additional framework rule is needed.

14 September 2026 — Disjoint leading pairs and shared quadratic tails over every prime

Status: working all-prime source theorem with exact multi-field controls. Cycle 142.

Obligation and stopping point. Test an actual unbounded-sum source outside the fixed-probe theorem. The initial private bilinear example also has an arity argument in its balanced regime, so it is retained as a control. The main application below has linear arity and shared dense quadratic tails, where the displayed arity bound no longer closes. Disjoint leading monomials replace independent full probe groups.

1. Why the first example is not the decisive test

For \(I\) old inputs of degree at most two over \(\mathbb F_p\), write \(a=p-1\). The telescoping coefficients

\[ \beta_i=g_i^{p-2}\prod_{j<i}(1-g_j^{p-1}) \]

give the exact product \(\prod_i(1-g_i^{p-1})\). Each companion vanishes on the old Boolean cube and has an ordinary Boolean certificate through \(2aI+2\). Coefficient degree is at most \(2aI-2\), with \(T_0=\max(1,2aI-2)\); companion and field images fit \(T_0\) times their original accuracy-one degrees. Thus the usual complete old-only replay gives degree \(T_0D\).

In the balanced private-matrix example \(g_i=\sum_{j\le t}a_jb_{ij}\), \(I=t=O(\sqrt v)\), this is already \(\sqrt n\,\operatorname{polylog}n\) for fixed \(p\) and polylogarithmic \(D\). This is a reuse of telescoping and the old Boolean image ledger, not new asymptotic coverage. It motivates a test with both larger arity and growing probe dimension.

2. Leading pairs suffice without disjoint probe groups

Work over any prime field, in the original \(v\) old Boolean coordinates. Let a quadratic input tuple \((g_i)_i\) have \(R\) constant linear combinations \(q_j=\sum_i\lambda_{ji}g_i\) whose multilinear Boolean representatives have pairwise disjoint squarefree quadratic leading monomials under a supplied degree-compatible monomial order. Rescale them to be monic. Require \(2R\le v\).

Working reduction lemma. There is a linear reduction map on degree-at-most-\(k\) polynomials with image dimension at most

\[ J(v,R,k)=\sum_{d=0}^k[z^d](1+2z)^R(1+z)^{v-2R}. \]

For \(1\le k\le v/2\),

\[ J(v,R,k)\le\binom vk\,(v+1)e^{-Rk^2/v^2}. \tag{LP-image} \]

A degree-\(k\) kernel polynomial has

\[ f=\sum_i c_i g_i+E,\qquad \deg c_i\le k-2,\qquad E\in\mathcal I_k({\rm BOOL}_{\rm old}). \tag{LP-membership} \]

Proof. Apply the fixed monomial-reduction construction to old Booleanity and the monic representatives of the \(q_j\)'s. It uses only a decreasing degree-compatible order and the disjoint leading supports. Lower terms may involve any old variables and may overlap arbitrarily. The normal monomials are squarefree and avoid the \(R\) leading pairs, giving the displayed generating function. The binomial-mode estimate gives (LP-image).

All divisors have degree two, so every source-generator cofactor has degree at most \(k-2\). Replacing a representative by its \(q_j\), and then its given linear combination of the actual inputs, preserves ordinary degree through \(k\); the representative difference has an old Boolean certificate through two. This gives (LP-membership). No exact quotient-dimension or Gröbner-basis assertion is needed. \(\square\)

The order here is on the original Boolean variables. Arbitrary affine changes over an odd prime field are not included in this hypothesis: such changes need not preserve the Boolean-coordinate domain. The private leading pairs in the application below require only a variable order.

3. Complete exclusion with the existing all-prime row-cube bounds

Let \(n=2^\ell\), \(m=n+1\), \(v=m\ell\), and use the compact base \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\). Consider complete accuracy-one blocks, each either old-affine or old-quadratic with the leading-pair property of Section 2. Include every coefficient equation \(r^p-r\). Let \(M\ge1\) bound the total block count and \(R\) be a common lower bound on the available disjoint leading pairs in each quadratic block. Put

\[ a=p-1,\quad L=\ln(8M(v+1)),\quad k\ge\max\left\{3,\left\lceil v\sqrt{L/R}\right\rceil\right\}, \quad \delta=ak,\quad A=2a,\quad T=2a(k+1)-1,\quad B=TD+\delta. \]

Working finite theorem. There is no ordinary-PC refutation through degree \(D\) if \(D\ge\max\{a\ell,p,5\}\), \(1\le R\le v/2\), \(k\le v/2\), and

\[ \varepsilon=m\binom{\ell}{3} \frac{\binom{v-3}{k-3}}{\binom vk}\le\tfrac12,\qquad 4^A(\delta-1)<n,\qquad n\ge2B+(2^A-2)\delta-1. \tag{LP-finite} \]

As before take \(\varepsilon=0\) if \(\ell<3\). These are the existing row-cap-two/power-multiplier conditions, with a new class of high-kernel constraints.

Common kernel. The homogeneous row-cap-two space \(\mathcal A_{2,k}\) has dimension at least \((1-\varepsilon)\binom vk\). The quadratic reduction maps have total image dimension at most \(\binom vk/8\), by the choice of \(k\). Among affine blocks, scalar-clean zero and unit spans, then use ordinary restrictions for proper ranks at least \(2k+3\). Their total image dimension is at most \(M e^{-k^2/v}\binom vk\le\binom vk/8\): since \(R\le v/2\), \(k^2/v\ge2L\). Thus one nonzero homogeneous \(f\in\mathcal A_{2,k}\) lies in all high kernels.

Coefficient maps. For a quadratic block use the coefficients \(c_i f^{p-2}\) from (LP-membership). Their degree is at most \(ak-2\), and the product is \(1-f^{p-1}+Ef^{p-2}\). A high-affine block uses its literal kernel coefficients times \(f^{p-2}\), of degree at most \(ak-1\). On a proper low-affine block, pack the \((p-1)r\) factors of its flat indicator into one bin; since \(r\le2k+2\), coefficient degree is at most \(T\). All images use only old variables.

Weight every substituted line by \(F=f^{p-1}\), of degree \(\delta\). On every old Boolean point \(F\) is zero or one. Where it is one, each high product is zero and each low-affine companion vanishes. Hence every weighted companion is Boolean-zero. If its original input has degree \(d_i\) and its tuple has maximum degree \(\Delta\), its image has ordinary degree at most \(\delta+d_i+T+\Delta\le\delta+T(d_i+\Delta+1)\), fitting its original degree. Weighted coefficient fields have old Boolean certificates through \(pT+\delta\), and old axioms cost \(e+\delta\).

The complete weighted PC replay therefore derives \(F\) over \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\) through \(B=TD+\delta\). Its Boolean remainder \(H\) is also an old consequence through \(B\), since \(F-H\) has a Boolean certificate through \(\delta\). It is nonzero: nonzero multilinear \(f\) is nonzero at some Boolean point over every field. Each monomial of \(H\) has total degree at most \(\delta\) and row degree at most \(A=2(p-1)\). The separation step of the accuracy-one theorem applies under (LP-finite), giving the contradiction. \(\square\)

Dense leading-pair regime. For each fixed prime, polynomial \(M\), polylogarithmic \(D\), and \(R=\Theta(v)\), we have \(k=O(\sqrt n\log n)\), \(\varepsilon=o(1)\), and \(B=\sqrt n\,\operatorname{polylog}n=o(n)\). All finite conditions hold eventually. Larger individual accuracies reduce to one by constant restriction. NS refutations are excluded by PC replay. No general fixed-probe hypothesis is required.

4. A source family with large arity and shared dense tails

Within each parent, choose old bits \(u_i,v_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,t\), all distinct and disjoint from a shared set of tail variables \(w\). Consider the actual quadratic inputs

\[ g_i=u_iv_i+Q_i(w),\qquad \deg Q_i\le2. \tag{LP-shared-tail} \]

Place all \(u_i\)'s ahead of all other variables in graded lexicographic order. The leading monomial of \(g_i\) is \(u_iv_i\), so the tuple has \(t\) disjoint leading pairs, even though all tail variables may be shared. Different parents may reuse old variables; their coefficient scopes remain disjoint, and their reduction maps may use different orders.

An explicit unbounded-sum family takes \(t=\lfloor v/4\rfloor\), uses \(4t\) distinct old bits \(u_i,v_i,a_j,b_j\), and sets

\[ Q_i=\sum_{j=0}^{t-1}a_jb_{j+i\bmod t}, \qquad 0\le i<t. \tag{LP-cyclic-tail} \]

There are \(t\) inputs and \(t+1\) quadratic summands per input. In the binary case each \(g_i\) has polar rank \(2t+2\), so it requires that many independent affine probes. Its full probe groups overlap on the \(2t\) tail variables. Thus the fixed-probe theorem does not apply. The straightforward arity bound also charges \(\Theta(tD)\), above the old degree barrier in this regime; this is a statement about that displayed bound, not an impossibility for every alternative normalizer.

Working actual-source corollary. For every fixed prime, polynomially many complete two-level sources of type (LP-shared-tail), with \(\Theta(v)\) private leading pairs per parent, have no polylogarithmic-degree refutation over \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\). Use a common accuracy \(h\ge1\). Express each multilinear \(Q_i\) as an old-affine part plus scalar-weighted products of two distinct old bits. Represent these products by actual rank-two bottom blocks, retain the old-affine part directly in the parent input, and allow additional old-affine blocks. The number of summands can grow polynomially with \(n\).

Source transfer. For a bottom tuple \((1-x,1-y)\) on old bits, use coefficients \((1,x)\) at accuracy one, giving the literal product \(xy\). At larger accuracy use the two scalar rows selecting the inputs separately and set later rows to zero. The companion images have old Boolean certificates through three; coefficient fields have certificates through their original prime-field degree. These are complete degree-preserving maps over every prime, and each reused bottom is assigned once.

Parent inputs become their actual sums of the corresponding products. Their companion degree after normalization is at most \(3h+2\), within the original \(2h^2+3h\), and all parent coefficient fields are retained. Thus the full NS/PC degree is preserved. Restrict parent accuracies to one and apply Section 3 with \(R=\Theta(v)\). In the cyclic-tail example, only \(O(v^2)\) distinct bottom products per parent are needed, so the source inventory is polynomial. \(\square\)

Scope. This handles an explicit source with unbounded sums and growing probe dimension over every fixed prime. It does not show that arbitrary quadratic input spaces possess disjoint leading pairs, that the required private products occur in every compiled Frege source, or that general later nonlinear levels can be removed. Adding private old variables to an arbitrary source would require its own justified source and PHP transfer.

5. Focused evidence

The evidence and reproduction note links the complete exact output. One twelve-bit cyclic-tail fixture, with three private heads and three shared tail pairs, was checked over \(\mathbb F_2,\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\).

For each field, all 455 ordinary monomials through degree three were reduced with ordinary NS witnesses. The normal space has 266 monomials; this is not asserted to be the functional quotient dimension. The kernel \(f=u_1g_0\) has degree three and row cap two, and its extracted reduction coefficients supply the actual parent map \(c_i f^{p-2}\).

The complete source has twelve reused rank-two bottoms and one three-input parent, on 39 variables. There are 66 weighted original-axiom certificates per field: twelve old Boolean equations, 27 companions, and 27 genuine coefficient field equations. Including basis reductions, kernel membership, and Booleanization of \(F=f^{p-1}\), the output retains 1,569 exact NS certificates. Every identity was reconstructed and every ordinary generator multiple charged.

All nonzero-weight old points give complete source models: 960 over \(\mathbb F_2\), 1,304 over \(\mathbb F_3\), and 1,400 over \(\mathbb F_5\). An unweighted companion fails at old point 9 in all three fields. At old point 587, the first parent coefficient is two over \(\mathbb F_3\) and three over \(\mathbb F_5\): its genuine field equation holds, while its Boolean equation fails. The Booleanized powers have maximum row degrees two, three, and five respectively, directly checking the need for the enlarged odd-prime row cap.

For \(M=n^2,D=\ell^3,R=\lfloor v/4\rfloor\), exact integer parameters use \(H=3\ell+\lceil\log_2\ell\rceil+4\ge\ln(8M(v+1))\) and \(k=\lceil\sqrt{\lceil v^2H/R\rceil}\rceil\). All sufficient conditions hold at \(\ell=64,128\) for each tested prime. At \(\ell=40\), the range, image, and domain bounds hold, but the old-degree bound fails in all fields; the cube-packing bound also fails for \(p=5\). Full integers and flags are retained. These large parameter cases and the local algebra fixture check different interfaces; they are not one instantiated PHP refutation.

Compilation and the exact run passed. The coding interval includes a compaction/restoration interruption.

Route assessment. The working criterion supplies an explicit unbounded-sum source application beyond the fixed-probe theorem, and covers every fixed prime. General source coverage still requires the leading-pair hypothesis or a replacement for it.

14 September 2026 — Cyclic sums without private heads via costed Boolean pair relations

Status: working binary cyclic-source theorem with exact field-component and complete source controls. Cycle 143.

Obligation and stopping point. Remove the private heads from the preceding cyclic-tail example. The input functions remain the actual dense cyclic sums. The proposed endpoint is complete two-level exclusion at a sublinear old degree for a growing family of cyclic lengths, with every auxiliary field computation expressed in binary coordinates.

1. A controlled ideal certificate can replace a leading input monomial

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) with \(v\) old Boolean variables. For a quadratic tuple \(g=(g_i)\), suppose an invertible binary affine coordinate change \(y=y(b)\) supplies \(R\) disjoint coordinate pairs \(M_j=y_{\alpha_j}y_{\beta_j}\), and explicit identities

\[ M_j=\sum_i a_{ji}g_i+E_j,\qquad \deg a_{ji}\le c-2,\qquad E_j\in\mathcal I_c({\rm BOOL}_b),\qquad c\ge2. \tag{CP-witness} \]

For \(k\ge2\), there is a linear map from degree-at-most-\(k\) old polynomials into the span of squarefree \(y\)-monomials avoiding these pairs. Its image dimension is at most \(J(v,R,k)\) from the leading-pair lemma. Every kernel element has

\[ f=\sum_i c_i g_i+E,\qquad \deg c_i\le k+c-4,\qquad E\in\mathcal I_{k+c-2}({\rm BOOL}_b). \tag{CP-kernel} \]

Proof. Express \(f\) in the independent \(y\)-coordinates, Boolean-reduce through degree \(k\), and retain only monomials avoiding every selected pair. Assign each removed monomial to its first contained pair. It is that pair times a monomial of degree at most \(k-2\). Substituting (CP-witness) gives the coefficient and ordinary NS bounds. Boolean equations in the new coordinates pull back through degree two: over \(\mathbb F_2\), an affine form \(L\) satisfies \(L^2-L=\sum_{i\in{\rm supp}(L)}(b_i^2-b_i)\). Hence the coordinate change does not increase these degrees. \(\square\)

This uses the supplied tuple only to construct kernel witnesses. The tuple equations and their pair consequences are not added to the old PHP base. It also does not require the pairs to belong to the tuple's constant linear span.

2. Small-field multiplication gives the required pair certificates

Let \(K=\mathbb F_{2^d}\), choose a binary basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1}\), and write \(A=\sum_r e_r x_r\), \(B=\sum_r e_r z_r\). Let \(C_\lambda(x,z)\) be the binary coordinate polynomials of \(AB\). All \(x_r,z_r\) are Boolean variables, and all polynomial equations and coefficient maps remain over \(\mathbb F_2\).

For \(1\le u\le d-1\), define the literal linear form \(L_u(x)=\sum_r e_r^{2^u}x_r\) with values in \(K\), and put

\[ V(x)=\prod_{u=1}^{d-1}L_u(x),\qquad h_{ij\lambda}(x)=x_i\,{\rm coord}_j\!\left(V(x)e_\lambda\right). \tag{CP-inverse} \]

For \(d=1\) the empty product is one. We have \(\deg h_{ij\lambda}\le d\), and

\[ x_i z_j-\sum_{\lambda=0}^{d-1}h_{ij\lambda}C_\lambda \in\mathcal I_{d+2}({\rm BOOL}_{x,z}). \tag{CP-field} \]

Proof. At every Boolean \(x\), \(L_u(x)=A^{2^u}\), so \(V(x)=A^{2^d-2}\). If \(A\ne0\), then \(V(x)AB=B\). If \(A=0\), every \(x_i=0\). Consequently \(x_iV(x)(AB)=x_iB\) in both cases. Taking the \(j\)-th coordinate proves Boolean vanishing of (CP-field). Its ordinary degree is at most \(d+2\); full Boolean reduction supplies an ordinary NS certificate within that degree. \(\square\)

The coefficient maps are the explicit polynomial products (CP-inverse), defined also at \(A=0\).

Why the ideal step matters. When \(d\ge2\), no coordinate product \(x_i z_j\) lies in the constant span of the \(C_\lambda\)'s. A nonzero combination is \(\Lambda(AB)\) for a nonzero binary functional \(\Lambda:K\to\mathbb F_2\). Its bilinear pairing is nondegenerate, since multiplication by any nonzero \(A\) is bijective and \(\Lambda\ne0\); its polar rank is \(2d\). A coordinate product has polar rank two. This also rules out obtaining such a product by an invertible binary linear coordinate change of one nonzero component combination. The higher-degree Boolean certificates are doing real work.

3. The actual cyclic inputs have small field components

Take \(t=2^s-1\), \(s\ge1\), and distinct old bits \(a_0,\ldots,a_{t-1},b_0,\ldots,b_{t-1}\). The parent tuple is

\[ g_i=\sum_{j=0}^{t-1}a_jb_{j+i\bmod t},\qquad 0\le i<t. \tag{CP-cyclic} \]

In \(\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^t-1)\), these are the coefficients of \(A^-(X)B(X)\), where \(A^-=\sum_j a_jX^{-j}\) and \(B=\sum_jb_jX^j\). The polynomial \(X^t-1\) is squarefree because \(t\) is odd. The identity \(X(X^t-1)=X^{2^s}-X\) shows that every irreducible factor has degree dividing \(s\), hence at most \(s\).

The Chinese remainder decomposition gives

\[ \mathbb F_2[X]/(X^t-1) \cong\prod_{\nu}K_\nu,\qquad K_\nu=\mathbb F_{2^{d_\nu}},\quad d_\nu\le s,\quad\sum_\nu d_\nu=t. \tag{CP-CRT} \]

These standard algebra facts are recorded in Milne, Fields and Galois Theory, finite fields, Corollary 4.22, and Theorem 8.1 on the Chinese remainder map. The research application here uses their binary coordinate maps: residues of \(A^-\) and \(B\) give separate invertible linear changes on their \(t\) old bits, and the coordinates of the products \(A_\nu B_\nu\) are constant binary combinations of the actual \(g_i\)'s.

For each component select its \(d_\nu\) diagonal pairs \(x_{\nu,r}z_{\nu,r}\). The pairs are jointly disjoint in the full binary coordinate system, and Section 2 certifies each through \(d_\nu+2\le s+2\). Pullback of Boolean equations under the binary coordinate changes costs two. Thus (CP-witness) holds with

\[ R=t,\qquad c=s+2. \]

This is a binary change of basis and a list of binary polynomial identities. It does not extend the coefficient domains of any ENS block to \(K_\nu\), and no old variables are added. The other \(v-2t\) old coordinates are unchanged.

4. Complete source exclusion and the finite budget

Let \(n=2^\ell\), \(m=n+1\), \(v=m\ell\), and use \(\mathcal Q_{n,2}\). Consider at most \(M\) complete accuracy-one blocks, each old-affine or old-quadratic with (CP-witness), common parameters \(R,c\), and genuine Boolean coefficient equations. Choose

\[ k\ge\max\!\left(3,\left\lceil v\sqrt{\ln(8M(v+1))/R}\right\rceil\right), \quad T=\max(2k+1,k+c-4),\quad B=TD+k. \]

Working finite theorem. There is no ordinary-PC refutation through \(D\) when \(D\ge\max(\ell,5)\), \(1\le R\le v/2\), \(k\le v/2\), and

\[ \varepsilon=m\binom{\ell}{3} \frac{\binom{v-3}{k-3}}{\binom vk}\le\tfrac12,\qquad 16(k-1)<n,\qquad n\ge2B+2k-1. \tag{CP-finite} \]

Proof. Use the same row-cap-two homogeneous space and simultaneous dimension argument as the preceding theorem. The costed-pair maps have the same image bound \(J(v,R,k)\), and the high-affine restriction maps are unchanged. Their joint kernel contains a nonzero homogeneous \(f\) of degree \(k\), with at most two bits per old pigeon row.

On each high quadratic block use the coefficients from (CP-kernel), of degree at most \(k+c-4\le T\). The product becomes \(1-f+E\), where \(E\) is old-Boolean zero through \(k+c-2\). The high-affine and low-affine maps remain those of the accuracy-one affine theorem and fit \(2k+1\le T\). Weight every substituted line by \(f\). On an old Boolean point with \(f=1\), all mapped high products vanish; all other high weighted companions vanish because \(f=0\). Low companions vanish directly.

A weighted companion with original input degree \(d_i\le2\) has ordinary degree at most \(k+d_i+T+2\le k+T(d_i+3)\), fitting its original companion degree, and every coefficient Booleanity image has a certificate through \(k+2T\). Affine companions and old axioms fit their original \(Te+k\) ceilings as before. The complete replay therefore derives \(f\) over the old base through \(B=TD+k\). Its row-cap-two separation follows from (CP-finite), a binary instance of the power-detector theorem. This is a replay of arbitrary source coefficients and every source axiom, not merely the existence of conditional models. \(\square\)

Actual cyclic-source corollary. Choose \(t=2^s-1\) to be the largest such length with \(2t\le v\). Then \(t=\Theta(v)\) and \(s=O(\log v)\). Any polynomial family of complete cyclic tuples (CP-cyclic), each on \(2t\) selected old bits, together with old-affine blocks, has no polylogarithmic-degree refutation over \(\mathcal Q_{n,2}\). Distinct parents may reuse old bits; their own coefficient scopes remain disjoint.

Indeed Section 3 gives \(R=t,c=s+2\), so \(k=O(\sqrt n\log n)\), \(T=O(k)\), \(\varepsilon=o(1)\), and \(B=\sqrt n\,\operatorname{polylog}n=o(n)\). All finite conditions hold eventually. For an actual common-accuracy two-level source, represent each summand by a rank-two bottom with tuple \((1-a_j,1-b_k)\), normalize it to the literal product \(a_jb_k\) using the preceding complete bottom map, and preserve every parent sum and field equation. This costs no degree increase. Restrict remaining parent rows to accuracy one. Only \(t^2\) distinct bottom products are needed per parent. NS refutations are also excluded by PC replay.

Scope. This removes the private heads for a genuine growing family of dense cyclic sums. Arbitrary bilinear coefficient tensors need not admit this small-field decomposition; cyclic lengths with large irreducible factors and repeated factors are not covered by the stated corollary. General later nonlinear levels and full odd-prime source compilation remain open.

5. Focused evidence

The reproduction note and complete exact output retain 80 ordinary NS certificates. Thirty certify every cross pair \(x_i z_j\) for fields of dimensions one through four, within degree \(d+2\). All multiplication tables and inverse-coordinate polynomials are saved. Twenty-six nonzero scalar-component combinations have full polar rank \(2d\), and all 56 field-product zeroes are retained. A two-dimensional countermodel has \(C_0=0\), \(C_1=1\), and \(x_0z_0=1\), showing why one cannot omit a product component.

For \(t=3,7,15\), the checker verifies the complete polynomial factorization, invertibility of both binary CRT maps, and every literal quadratic component identity. Forward and inverse matrices, the actual cyclic inputs, and all component products are retained. These checks enumerate coefficient identities, not the exponentially many assignments at \(t=15\).

The actual source fixture has seven old bits, nine reused bottoms, and a three-input cyclic parent, on 28 variables. Its cubic multiplier is an extra old bit times one transformed diagonal pair. Its parent coefficients have degree at most three. The saved kernel identity has a nonzero old-Boolean correction through degree five, so the mapped parent product is \(1-f+E\), not literally \(1-f\). Forty-nine complete weighted source-image certificates include every companion, coefficient equation, and old Boolean equation. Their budgets are at most ten, within each original \(3e+3\) ceiling. Exact parameter controls use \(M=n^2,D=\ell^3\), the largest \(t=2^s-1\) with \(2t\le v\), \(R=t,c=s+2\), and the integer logarithm bound from the preceding entry. 14 September 2026 — Pair consequences are not a universal quadratic interface

Status: working ideal-level obstruction and interface clarification with exact evaluation checks. Cycle 144.

Obligation and stopping point. Audit the missing step from the latest structured source families to arbitrary quadratic tuples. The costed-pair method succeeds for cyclic multiplication, but one must not silently promote its pair consequences to a universal property. The stopping point is an explicit obstruction and a precise statement of the weaker compression obligation that remains.

1. The earlier disjoint-sum example has no hidden quadratic pair consequences

Over \(\mathbb F_2\), take \(q_i=a_ib_i+c_id_i\), \(1\le i\le r\), on disjoint four-variable groups, with any further unused Boolean variables. Let \(S\) be the common Boolean zero set of the \(q_i\)'s. This is the same family as the earlier input-span obstruction; the new claim concerns its full Boolean vanishing ideal.

Working refinement. Every multilinear polynomial \(h\) of degree at most two that vanishes on \(S\) is a constant linear combination of \(q_1,\ldots,q_r\). Consequently no product \(LM\) of affine forms with independent linear parts belongs to \((q_1,\ldots,q_r,{\rm BOOL})\), at any certificate degree.

Proof. The zero assignment lies in \(S\), so the constant coefficient of \(h\) is zero. Every single-one assignment also lies in \(S\), killing every linear coefficient. Every two-one assignment lies in \(S\) except the pairs \(a_i,b_i\) and \(c_i,d_i\). Thus every other quadratic coefficient, including cross-group and unused-variable coefficients, is zero. Write \(h=\sum_i(\alpha_i a_ib_i+\beta_i c_id_i)\). The assignment with all four variables of group \(i\) equal to one and all others zero lies in \(S\); it gives \(\alpha_i=\beta_i\). This proves the classification.

The Boolean remainder of a product \(LM\) of independent affine forms has polar rank two. Each nonzero combination of \(u\) of the \(q_i\)'s has block-diagonal polar rank \(4u\). Such a product therefore cannot vanish on \(S\). Every polynomial in the full input-plus-Boolean ideal does vanish on \(S\), independently of certificate degree, proving the obstruction. \(\square\)

This excludes the pair premise even after an arbitrary invertible binary affine change of old coordinates: two distinct coordinate forms have independent linear parts. Allowing higher-degree cofactors cannot repair a false consequence.

2. These sources remain covered, and cubic products illustrate the scope

The same tuple has \(r\) disjoint leading pairs \(a_ib_i\), under a variable order giving those terms priority within each group. Its generators have shared terms only within their own four-variable groups. Thus the ordinary leading-term reduction works directly, although the actual pair polynomials are not input-ideal consequences.

For \(r=\lfloor v/4\rfloor\), polynomial inventory and polylogarithmic source degree, this is already an application of the leading-pair theorem, in its binary case. Complete actual two-level parents use sums of the two corresponding rank-two bottom products, with no source-degree increase. This is reuse of existing coverage, not a new lower bound.

The obstruction is specifically quadratic. There are explicit cubic products in the Boolean ideal, for example

\[ a_ib_i(1-c_i)=(1-c_i)q_i+d_i(c_i^2-c_i). \tag{QP-cubic} \]

This is an ordinary identity through degree three. It does not rescue the false quadratic-pair assertion; it shows why the earlier record's possibility of useful higher-degree products remains consistent with the present refinement. No cubic-product detour is needed for this already-covered family.

3. The sufficient obligation is kernel compression, not pair vanishing

Here is a restatement of the existing binary weighted-replay mechanism, rather than a new source-coverage theorem. Use \(\mathcal Q_{n,2}\), with \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), \(v=(n+1)\ell\), and \(D\ge\max(\ell,5)\). Fix a homogeneous row-cap-two space \(A=\mathcal A_{2,k}\), \(k\ge1\), a coefficient budget \(T\ge1\) with \(k\le T+2\), and complete accuracy-one old quadratic tuples. For each tuple \(g^{(a)}\) not already assigned an old-only coefficient map of degree at most \(T\) whose every companion is Boolean-zero, define the linear subspace

\[ K_a(k,T)=\left\{f\in A: f=\sum_i c_i g^{(a)}_i+E,\quad \deg c_i\le T,\quad E\in\mathcal I_{T+2}({\rm BOOL}) \right\}. \tag{QP-kernel} \]

If

\[ \sum_a {\rm codim}_{A}K_a(k,T)<\dim A, \tag{QP-compression} \]

then there is a common nonzero \(f\) with all the required witnesses. On each such block the coefficient map gives \(P_a=1-f+E_a\), so weighting by \(f\) kills every mapped companion on the old Boolean cube. Unconditionally normalized blocks need no kernel constraint. All coefficient Booleanity images also vanish. For an input of original degree \(d_i\) in a tuple of maximum degree \(\Delta_a\le2\), the weighted companion has degree at most \(k+d_i+T+\Delta_a\le k+T(d_i+\Delta_a+1)\); coefficient equations cost \(k+2T\), and old axioms cost \(k+e\). Hence complete PC replay derives \(f\) through \(B=TD+k\), exactly as in the preceding ledger.

Provided the row-cap domain is nonempty and the old separation conditions \(16(k-1)<n\), \(n\ge2B+2k-1\), hold, that replay contradicts old separation. This gives a sufficient endpoint. It does not prove (QP-compression) for the general source.

The leading-monomial maps and the costed-pair maps provide different upper bounds on these codimensions. An image map whose kernel is contained in \(K_a\) bounds \({\rm codim}\,K_a\) by its image dimension. The disjoint-sum example proves that literal pair vanishing cannot be demanded of every such map. Conversely, the cyclic example proves that inexpensive Boolean ideal consequences can help when a literal input-span description is insufficient. Pair extraction, a particular coordinate order, and an exact quotient normal form are conveniences of specific constructions.

Remaining route. For actual retained quadratic tuples, establish enough compression at an affordable coefficient budget, or provide complete unconditional normalizers for the difficult blocks. Even an unrestricted quadratic theorem would still need to meet the source normalization and later-level obligations of the main Frege route. No progress on those remaining universal hypotheses is claimed in this audit.

4. Focused evidence

The reproduction note and complete exact output retain four full degree-two evaluation matrices, their RREFs, pivots, and reconstructed kernel bases.

For one, two, and three disjoint two-pair sums, the common zero sets have 10, 100, and 1,000 points. The degree-two feature spaces have 11, 37, and 79 columns, and their exact ranks are 10, 35, and 76. In every case the entire kernel is precisely the original input span. All eleven nonzero input combinations have the predicted polar ranks \(4u\). A separate single-product control \(ab=0\) has three zeroes, four features, rank three, and the genuine rank-two pair in its kernel; the obstruction correctly fails there.

Six reconstructed ordinary NS witnesses verify (QP-cubic) through degree three, with every generator multiple retained and charged. Compilation and all checks passed. These are local Boolean-ideal fixtures, not PHP models; the universal proof is the argument in Section 1.

Route assessment. This refutes a proposed universal pair interface while preserving the weaker compression route. It adds no new excluded source family; its contribution is preventing an invalid strengthening from becoming the next research target.

Process assessment. Reusing the earlier disjoint-sum family gives a short ideal-level obstruction, avoiding further specialized cyclic calculations; no additional framework rule is needed.

Some preliminary interface reasoning overlapped the preceding checkpoint and remains included in preparation time.

14 September 2026 — Large binary field products through conjugate-coordinate reduction

Status: working binary large-field source theorem with exact extension-coordinate and complete descent controls. Cycle 145.

Obligation and stopping point. Remove the small field-dimension restriction from the preceding multiplication-source method. The inverse witness costs degree \(d\) in a field of dimension \(d\), which is unaffordable when \(d=\Theta(v)\). The proposed replacement is a degree-preserving reduction over an auxiliary field, with the correct transformed old domain equations and binary descent of every coefficient witness.

1. Conjugate coordinates and their actual domain equations

Let \(K=\mathbb F_{2^d}\), choose a binary basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1}\), and use old Boolean bits \(x_r,z_r\). Write \(A=\sum_r e_rx_r\), \(B=\sum_re_rz_r\), and let \(C_\lambda(x,z)\) be the binary coordinate polynomials of \(AB\). In the scalar-extended ordinary polynomial ring define

\[ X_j=\sum_r e_r^{2^j}x_r,\qquad Z_j=\sum_r e_r^{2^j}z_r,\qquad 0\le j<d. \tag{LF-coordinates} \]

The coordinate matrix is invertible over \(K\). Indeed a nonzero row relation would give a nonzero linearized polynomial \(\sum_{j<d}\alpha_j U^{2^j}\) vanishing on the binary basis, and hence on all \(2^d\) elements of \(K\). Its degree is at most \(2^{d-1}\), contradicting the root bound. Other old coordinates are unchanged.

With indices interpreted cyclically modulo \(d\), the exact ordinary identities are

\[ X_j^2-X_{j+1} =\sum_r e_r^{2^{j+1}}(x_r^2-x_r),\qquad Z_j^2-Z_{j+1} =\sum_r e_r^{2^{j+1}}(z_r^2-z_r), \tag{LF-domain} \]
\[ X_jZ_j=\sum_\lambda e_\lambda^{2^j}C_\lambda. \tag{LF-product} \]

The product identity conjugates coefficients, without raising the old variables to powers. The domain identities follow from characteristic two and \(e_r^{2^d}=e_r\). They have degree two throughout. In general \(X_j\) is not Boolean on old Boolean points, so \(X_j^2-X_j\) is not an available old-domain equation.

2. A small reduction image and binary witness descent

Use the monic divisors \(X_j^2-X_{j+1}\), \(Z_j^2-Z_{j+1}\), \(X_jZ_j\), and the ordinary Boolean equations of unused coordinates. Any degree-compatible monomial order makes their heads the squares and the disjoint pairs. The fixed linear monomial reduction therefore has image over \(K\) of dimension at most

\[ J(v,d,k)=\sum_{u=0}^k[t^u](1+2t)^d(1+t)^{v-2d}. \tag{LF-image} \]

Repeated square reductions strictly lower total degree, including across the cyclic wraparound. No quotient normal-form assertion or Booleanity of the \(X_j,Z_j\) is needed. Pulling the degree-\(k\) reduction identities back using (LF-domain) and (LF-product) expresses every kernel element through ordinary degree \(k\) in the actual \(C_\lambda\)'s and old Boolean equations.

Restrict the map to the binary multiplier space \(\mathcal A_{2,k}\). Its binary image dimension is at most \(dJ(v,d,k)\), since each output coefficient in \(K\) has \(d\) binary coordinates. Thus its binary kernel has codimension at most that quantity.

Binary descent. For \(f\) in this kernel, first pull back the full identity to binary original generators:

\[ f=\sum_\lambda a_\lambda C_\lambda+\sum_r b_r{\rm BOOL}_r, \qquad a_\lambda,b_r\in K[b],\qquad \deg a_\lambda,\deg b_r\le k-2. \tag{LF-extension-witness} \]

Choose a binary linear functional \(\pi:K\to\mathbb F_2\) with \(\pi(1)=1\), and apply it coefficientwise. Since \(f\), every \(C_\lambda\), and every original Boolean generator have binary coefficients, this gives

\[ f=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda C_\lambda+E,\qquad c_\lambda\in\mathbb F_2[b],\quad\deg c_\lambda\le k-2,\quad E\in\mathcal I_k({\rm BOOL}_b). \tag{LF-binary-witness} \]

Use the descended coefficients to define the ENS map, taking every subsequent product over the binary field. Linearity commutes with multiplication by the binary original generators, which is all that descent needs. The functional is not asserted to be multiplicative. In a basis starting with one, taking the constant coordinate supplies a suitable functional; the ordinary field trace would kill one when \(d\) is even and must not be used indiscriminately.

3. Complete source exclusion at growing field dimension

Let \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), \(v=(n+1)\ell\), and use \(\mathcal Q_{n,2}\). Adjoin at most \(M\ge1\) complete accuracy-one blocks. Each non-affine block is the full binary coordinate tuple of a field product on \(2d_a\) selected old bits, where \(R\le d_a\le v/2\); the other blocks are old-affine. Coefficients have their original binary field equations. Set

\[ L=\ln(8Mv(v+1)),\qquad k\ge\max\!\left(3,\left\lceil v\sqrt{L/R}\right\rceil\right), \qquad T=2k+1,\qquad B=TD+k. \tag{LF-parameters} \]

Working finite theorem. There is no ordinary-PC refutation through \(D\) if \(D\ge\max(\ell,5)\), \(1\le R\le v/2\), \(k\le v/2\), and

\[ (n+1)\binom{\ell}{3} \frac{\binom{v-3}{k-3}}{\binom vk}\le\tfrac12,\qquad 16(k-1)<n,\qquad n\ge2B+2k-1. \tag{LF-finite} \]

Proof. The row-cap-two domain has dimension at least \(\binom vk/2\). By the binomial image bound, the sum of the binary image dimensions of the field-product reductions is at most

\[ \sum_a d_aJ(v,d_a,k) \le Mv(v+1)e^{-Rk^2/v^2}\binom vk \le\tfrac18\binom vk. \]

High-affine proper ranks at least \(2k+3\) add at most \(\binom vk/8\), as in the accuracy-one affine argument. Hence a common nonzero binary \(f\in\mathcal A_{2,k}\) survives all kernel constraints. Each field block has the descended coefficients (LF-binary-witness), of degree at most \(k-2\); each affine block has its previous old-only map through \(2k+1=T\).

After weighting by \(f\), every companion vanishes on the old Boolean cube. A quadratic companion has ordinary degree at most \(k+T+4\le k+5T\); coefficient Booleanity costs \(k+2T\), and old axioms cost \(k+e\). The complete weighted replay derives \(f\) over the old base through \(B=TD+k\), contradicting the row-cap-two separation under (LF-finite). \(\square\)

Actual-source corollary. For \(d_a=\Theta(v)\), polynomial block inventory, and polylogarithmic \(D\), the theorem has \(k=O(\sqrt n\log n)\), \(T=O(k)\), and \(B=\sqrt n\,\operatorname{polylog}n=o(n)\); every finite condition holds eventually. Each coordinate of \(AB\) is an actual binary sum of old-bit products \(x_rz_s\). Represent those products by reused rank-two bottom blocks and apply the complete degree-preserving bottom map, preserving all parent sums and coefficient equations. At most \(d_a^2\) distinct bottom products per parent are needed. Restrict the remaining parent rows to accuracy one. The result excludes polylogarithmic-degree NS and PC refutations for this complete two-level family, with arbitrary original common accuracy and all original degrees retained.

The proof does not pay for enumerating the \(2^{d_a}\) field elements. It is an existence and ordinary-degree argument; the auxiliary image dimension carries only the extension degree \(d_a\). Neither a polynomial-size construction of the common multiplier nor a new coefficient domain is claimed or required.

Scope. This removes the large component-dimension obstruction for binary field-product inputs. It does not diagonalize arbitrary bilinear tensors, prove general quadratic compression, or remove later nonlinear levels. The transformed domain argument is specific to characteristic two as stated.

14 September 2026 — Arbitrary binary cyclic lengths through local truncated products

Status: working arbitrary-length binary cyclic-source theorem with exact weighted-reduction and complete mixed-source controls. Cycle 146.

Obligation and stopping point. Remove the special-length restriction from the cyclic-source theorem, including repeated factors. The actual inputs remain cyclic sums of products. The proposed endpoint is a complete two-level theorem for every growing cyclic length, with correct old-domain pullbacks and binary coefficient descent.

1. Local coefficient coordinates at arbitrary cyclic length

Write \(t=eu\), with \(e=2^s\) and \(u\) odd. Choose \(d_\ast\ge1\) with \(u\mid2^{d_\ast}-1\) and \(d_\ast\le u\), taking \(d_\ast=1\) for \(u=1\). Such a choice exists by the finite multiplicative order of two modulo odd \(u\). Put \(K=\mathbb F_{2^{d_\ast}}\). The \(u\)-th roots of unity all lie in \(K\): \(X^u-1\) divides \(X^{2^{d_\ast}-1}-1\), whose roots are the nonzero elements of \(K\). They are distinct, and

\[ X^t-1=(X^u-1)^e=\prod_{\zeta^u=1}(X-\zeta)^e. \tag{CY-local-factorization} \]

For \(A^-=\sum_{i<t}a_iX^{(-i\bmod t)}\) and \(B=\sum_{i<t}b_iX^i\), take the coefficients of \(\epsilon^r\), \(0\le r<e\), after substituting \(X=\zeta+\epsilon\). Call them \(A_{\zeta,r}\) and \(B_{\zeta,r}\). These are linear forms over \(K\) in the original operand coordinates; binomial coefficients are reduced modulo two.

Each operand's local coefficient map is invertible. If a polynomial of degree below \(t\) has every such coefficient zero, it is divisible by every \((X-\zeta)^e\), hence by their degree-\(t\) product; it must be zero. The source and target dimensions are both \(t\). This argument handles repeated factors directly and uses no division by factorials.

The cyclic inputs \(g_i=\sum_j a_jb_{j+i\bmod t}\) are the coefficients of \(A^-B\) modulo \(X^t-1\). Their local images are the exact quadratic polynomials

\[ C_{\zeta,k}=\sum_{r+q=k}A_{\zeta,r}B_{\zeta,q} =\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}\binom{i}{k}\zeta^{\,i-k}g_i, \qquad 0\le k<e. \tag{CY-local-products} \]

Terms with \(i<k\) are zero in the last sum. Evaluation modulo \(\epsilon^e\) annihilates \(X^t-1\), so the cyclic wraparound is preserved. No summand is replaced by a separate parent input.

2. Frobenius domains and disjoint weighted leading pairs

Frobenius permutes the roots by \(\zeta\mapsto\zeta^2\) and leaves the local coefficient index \(r\) fixed. If \(A_{\zeta,r}=\sum_i\alpha_{\zeta,r;i}a_i\), then coefficient conjugation gives \(\alpha_{\zeta,r;i}^2=\alpha_{\zeta^2,r;i}\). Consequently

\[ A_{\zeta,r}^2-A_{\zeta^2,r} =\sum_i\alpha_{\zeta^2,r;i}(a_i^2-a_i), \tag{CY-local-domain} \]

and similarly for \(B\). These are degree-two pullbacks of the old domain equations. Squaring a whole local power series would also square \(\epsilon\); that is a different operation from the coefficient conjugation used here.

Select \(C_{\zeta,2r}\) for \(0\le r<\lceil e/2\rceil\). Order monomials first by total degree, then by the additive variable weights \(-r^2\) on \(A_{\zeta,r}\) and \(B_{\zeta,r}\), and finally by any fixed lexicographic tie break. This is a degree-compatible monomial order. Within \(C_{\zeta,2r}\), the weight of the term with indices \(i,2r-i\) is

\[ -i^2-(2r-i)^2=-2r^2-2(i-r)^2. \]

Its unique maximum is the central term \(A_{\zeta,r}B_{\zeta,r}\). The selected leading pairs are mutually disjoint, with total count

\[ R_t=u\lceil e/2\rceil\ge t/2. \tag{CY-pair-count} \]

The domain divisors have square leading terms, since their other terms are linear. Thus the weighted monomial reduction, using only these local product equations and the actual domain divisors, preserves ordinary degree and has auxiliary-field image dimension at most \(J(v,R_t,k)\). The variable weights affect the reduction order, not the ordinary degree charged in the proof.

3. Original Boolean coordinates and witness descent

The operand coordinates may be \(2t\) binary affine probes with jointly independent linear parts, rather than selected individual old bits. Extend them to a binary affine coordinate system only for the reduction construction. Each probe's Boolean equation has an old-Boolean certificate through two. Compose this with the local coefficient map and (CY-local-domain); unused coordinate equations also pull back through two.

The multiplier space remains \(\mathcal A_{2,k}\) in the original pigeon-bit coordinates, and the old base \(\mathcal Q_{n,2}\) is unchanged. Every reduction identity is pulled back before use. This is not an invariance claim for PHP under arbitrary affine changes.

Restricting the local reduction to binary multipliers gives binary image dimension at most \(d_\ast J(v,R_t,k)\). A kernel element \(f\) has an ordinary degree-\(k\) identity in the original cyclic inputs and old Boolean generators over \(K\). Apply the unital coefficient descent after this pullback to obtain

\[ f=\sum_i c_i g_i+E,\qquad c_i\in\mathbb F_2[b],\quad\deg c_i\le k-2,\quad E\in\mathcal I_k({\rm BOOL}_b). \tag{CY-binary-kernel} \]

Only constant combinations of original inputs are used in the generator pullbacks. Every ENS coefficient map is then defined over \(\mathbb F_2\), with its original binary field equation retained.

4. The complete arbitrary-length source theorem

Let \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), \(v=(n+1)\ell\), and use \(\mathcal Q_{n,2}\). Consider at most \(M\ge1\) complete accuracy-one blocks, each old-affine or an actual cyclic tuple on \(2t_a\) independent binary affine probes, with \(2t_a\le v\). Let \(R\ge1\) be a common lower bound on \(R_{t_a}\). Choose

\[ k\ge\max\!\left(3,\left\lceil v\sqrt{\ln(8Mv(v+1))/R}\right\rceil\right), \qquad T=2k+1,\qquad B=TD+k. \]

Working finite theorem. There is no ordinary-PC refutation through \(D\) if \(D\ge\max(\ell,5)\), \(R\le v/2\), \(k\le v/2\), and

\[ (n+1)\binom{\ell}{3} \frac{\binom{v-3}{k-3}}{\binom vk}\le\tfrac12,\qquad 16(k-1)<n,\qquad n\ge2B+2k-1. \tag{CY-finite} \]

Proof. Each auxiliary extension degree is at most \(u_a\le t_a\le v\). Therefore the sum of binary local-reduction image dimensions is at most

\[ Mv(v+1)e^{-Rk^2/v^2}\binom vk\le\tfrac18\binom vk. \]

High-affine constraints contribute at most another eighth, as in the large-field theorem. The row-cap-two domain has dimension at least half of \(\binom vk\), so a common nonzero binary multiplier exists. Use (CY-binary-kernel) on every cyclic block and the previous accuracy-one maps on affine blocks, then weight by \(f\). Every cyclic companion has ordinary degree at most \(k+T+4\le k+5T\), every coefficient Booleanity costs \(k+2T\), and an old axiom \(F\) costs \(k+\deg F\). The complete original-degree replay derives \(f\) through \(B\), contradicting old separation under (CY-finite). \(\square\)

Actual two-level corollary. For arbitrary lengths \(t_a=\Theta(v)\), polynomial inventory, and polylogarithmic source degree, \(R=\Theta(v)\), \(k=O(\sqrt n\log n)\), and \(B=\sqrt n\,\operatorname{polylog}n=o(n)\); the finite conditions eventually hold. Represent each summand \(a_jb_k\) by its actual rank-two bottom on \((1-a_j,1-b_k)\). The binary bottom map gives the literal product and complete Boolean certificates through three, including when the probes are affine. It preserves the parent sums and every original joint degree; at most \(t_a^2\) distinct bottoms per parent are needed. Restrict remaining parent rows to accuracy one. Thus the full common-accuracy two-level source has no polylogarithmic-degree NS or PC refutation.

Scope. This covers arbitrary cyclic lengths, including repeated factors and independent affine operand probes. It remains a structured multiplication family. General bilinear tensors, dependencies among operand probes, and later nonlinear source levels are not handled by this theorem.
