15 September 2026 — An adaptive query attempt returns to the existing quantifier gap

Status: unsuccessful attempt to supply active source feasibility; elementary old-query budget recorded, no new Frege or source-extension bound. Cycle 156.

Question. Could an adaptive old-design strategy choose compatible answers as source queries arrive, avoiding the need to construct the whole joint functional first? The old query argument works within its degree budget. The application fails to produce the fixed distribution required by the existing ENS averaging bridge. This returns to an already recorded gap, rather than advancing its solution.

1. An elementary degree budget for old polynomial queries

Let \(F\) be a system over \(\mathbb F_p\) containing the Boolean equations in its old variables, and let \(q\) be an old polynomial of degree \(s\ge1\). If every branch \(F\cup\{q-a\}\), \(a\in\mathbb F_p\), has an ordinary NS refutation through \(B\ge s\), then \(F\) has one through \(B+(p-1)s\).

Proof. Write \(1=U_a+(q-a)V_a\), where \(U_a\in\mathcal I_B(F)\) and \(\deg V_a\le B-s\). Put \(\delta_a(q)=1-(q-a)^{p-1}\). The degree-\((p-1)\) Lagrange polynomials satisfy \(\sum_a\delta_a(q)=1\) identically, and \((q-a)\delta_a(q)=q-q^p\). Therefore

\[ 1=\sum_a\delta_a(q)U_a+(q-q^p)\sum_aV_a. \]

The first terms have ordinary NS cost at most \(B+(p-1)s\). The recorded Boolean Frobenius certificate puts \(q^p-q\) in \(\mathcal I_{ps}({\rm BOOL})\); multiplying by \(V_a\) gives the same ceiling. This proves the claim. Constant queries need no branching.

The contrapositive allows an answer \(a\) that leaves a nonrefutable branch, spending at most \((p-1)s\) degree. By finite-dimensional duality, that branch has a normalized design at the remaining degree. Successive designs may change, but the previous answer equations remain among the axioms.

In particular, consider any adaptive old-polynomial query tree of height at most \(H\), with query degrees at most \(D\), whose leaf outputs \(f,g\) with \(\deg(fg)\le D\). If

\[ 1\notin\mathcal I_K(F),\qquad K=\bigl((p-1)H+p\bigr)D, \]

there is a normalized old degree-\(D\) design that follows one path of the tree and has no conflict at its leaf. Answer the \(H\) queries by the preceding rule, reserving degree \(pD\). At the selected leaf, also condition on \(f=a\) and \(g=b\); their total degree is at most \(D\), so degree \(D\) remains. The identity

\[ fg-ab=g(f-a)+a(g-b) \]

fits that degree and forces \(\omega(fg)=\omega(f)\omega(g)\). If a leaf factor is zero, non-conflict is automatic. The final design retains all path answers. This is only a favorable-design existence statement for each fixed tree; no literature novelty is claimed.

2. Why this does not supply the source implication

Scalar specialization of all ENS coefficients already makes the source's queries and leaf factors old polynomials within the original degree \(D\). For polylogarithmic \(H,D\), the old PHP barrier supplies the much larger degree \(K\) above. Thus one can find a favorable design after each specialized tree is given.

The actual averaging bridge requires a different order of choices. One probability distribution \(\nu\) on old designs must satisfy

\[ \Pr_{\omega\sim\nu} [T\text{ has no conflict on }\omega] >S(1-1/p)^h \]

for every permitted tree of height \(h+\lceil\log_2S\rceil\). The scalar assignment, and hence the resulting tree, may be chosen after \(\nu\). The construction in Section 1 gives \(\forall T\,\exists\omega_T\); it does not give the required single \(\nu\) and quantitative lower bound. The earlier bridge entry explicitly warned against choosing a favorable design after seeing the tree, and the shallow-query obstruction rules out the proposed guarantee for the coarse query class.

Trying instead to commit values of whole input spaces before the fresh coefficient choices does not yet repair this. Querying a basis of rank \(r\) with degrees at most \(s\) costs up to \((p-1)rs\) under the case-split argument. No sufficient bound on the accumulated cost is available for the full source. This reproduces a rank-control obligation, not a new source invariant.

Outcome. No active source solution, new admissible distribution, or sufficient full-source cost bound was obtained. The active-window reduction remains a valid description of the construction problem; this attempt does not establish its feasibility. The next work must test an actual source-dependent invariant rather than add another equivalent endpoint.

2026-09-10 / import_20260910_01 — focused audit and zero-cofactor pruning

Question. After importing the manuscript, what refutation-dependent reduction is already justified, without assuming the missing global compression theorem?

Status. Focused proof audit; elementary working pruning lemma local:zero-cofactor-pruning. This is a local clarification of the unused-block observation in Theorem 8.1, not a novelty claim or the missing affordable theorem. No old claim is superseded.

Objects and quantifiers. Fix any prime \(p\), any Boolean/field old base \(F\), and any finite leveled ENS system with fresh coefficient-variable groups \(R_a\), all companions \(E_{a,i}\), and all required extension field equations. Fix an actual ordinary-polynomial NS certificate

\[ 1=\sum_{f\in F}q_f f+\sum_{a,i}q_{a,i}E_{a,i} +\sum_{r}s_r(r^p-r), \qquad \deg(q_FF)\le D \]

for every nonzero summand. Cofactors are collected within each axiom's coefficient; their possible sharing of extension variables is unrestricted.

Lemma. If every companion coefficient \(q_{a,i}\) of a block a is zero, its fresh variables may all be set to zero throughout the certificate. The resulting identity has degree at most \(D\), uses no axioms of a, and has the same ENS form on the surviving blocks after updating their inputs by the same substitution. Zero input coordinates and blocks can be cleaned up by further constant substitutions. Iterating zero-cofactor deletion and this cleanup terminates. Consequently, a block with zero companion coefficients need not be retained merely because its variables occur in other cofactors or in later inputs.

Proof. Let \(\sigma\) fix the original variables and all surviving fresh variables, and send \(R_a\) to zero. Apply this ring homomorphism to the entire identity. The left side remains one, the base axioms are fixed, and each removed field axiom becomes zero. There were no nonzero companion summands for a. For a surviving block b, its fresh variables are fixed and its companion becomes

\[ \sigma(E_{b,i})=\sigma(g_{b,i}) \prod_{u=1}^{h_b}\left(1-\sum_j r_{b,u,j}\sigma(g_{b,j})\right). \]

No surviving input acquires a dependence on a later level, and no fresh coefficient variable enters an input of its own block. Each surviving field axiom remains \(r^p-r\). This establishes the identity and structural claim.

There is one syntax detail: if a surviving input becomes identically zero, its coefficient variables may disappear from that block's polynomial companions while still occurring in later inputs or cofactors. Set these now-unneeded coefficient variables to zero everywhere as well. Drop identically zero companions, remove all-zero blocks, recompute the identity, and repeat. This preserves the strict convention that surviving new variables are introduced in an earlier nonzero block, rather than silently treating unintroduced field variables as original Boolean variables. Each cleanup removes variables or blocks, so the process is finite. Complete the companion list of every retained nonzero tuple with zero coefficients where needed.

Constant substitution is degree-nonincreasing on every entire original summand. Therefore every nonzero image summand still has degree at most \(D\). This proves the lemma. In particular, we have constructed a new certificate; we have not enlarged the original certificate's permissible cofactor space.

Degree accounting and a candidate quantity. Let \(\pi'\) be the resulting pruned certificate, with surviving maximum input degrees \(\delta'_a\). Converting \(\pi'\) to PC and applying thm:additive gives the certified bound

\[ B_{\rm support}(\pi)=D+(p-1)\sum_{a\in A(\pi')}\delta'_a. \]

This quantity depends on the actual certificate and its specialization, not just on the originally supplied collection of extension spaces. Where nested/core-residual hypotheses hold, replace the sum by the corresponding certified batch compositions. For one affine level, the exact subset recurrence of lem:subsetdp can be applied to the pruned family. These are sufficient bounds only; the recurrence need not be computationally affordable and no uniform upper bound in \(D,h,\log M\) is established.

  • Append any number of spread blocks that carry zero companion cofactors in a certificate. Pruning removes them without a degree charge. Their appearance solely in other cofactors is harmless under the substitution argument.
  • The prefix-pebbling certificate contains genuinely used blocks and long adjacent-block propagation. The lemma does not declare that propagation cheap merely from sparse support. Its prefix spans are nested, so the existing thm:nested yields \(D+(p-1)\) (input degree one). Its base also has PC degree at most three. This is consistent with the ordinary-design counterexample and does not transfer that counterexample to high-PC-degree PHP bases.
  • The static spread family without a certificate remains data only. If many such blocks survive with essential nonzero coefficients, the present pruning lemma supplies no reason for a small charge. Proving that actual translations admit a cheaper representation is precisely the unresolved task.

15 September 2026 — Finite Boolean covers have a total degree barrier

Status: working all-field cover obstruction and ordinary NS combination bound; scope audit of a bounded-arity extension theorem. No new main-route lower bound. Cycle 157.

Question. Could a short menu of coefficient assignments replace the failed single Boolean-domain normalization map? At every old input, at least one menu entry would satisfy the complete source. A product of the resulting branch certificates would then eliminate the menu. The approximate-majority example forces the total degree budget of such a complete cover to be linear in the old bit count. This rejects the proposed universal preprocessing mechanism before constructing a generator or further examples.

1. Polynomial covers of an approximate-majority graph

Let \(C:\{0,1\}^v\to\{0,1\}\) be zero on weights at most \(a\), and one on weights at least \(v-a\). Work over any field. For \(j=1,\ldots,t\), let \(G_j\) be a finite system of old polynomials and let \(V_j\) be an old polynomial. Assume

\[ \forall x\in\{0,1\}^v\ \exists j:\ G_j(x)=0, \qquad G_j(x)=0\Longrightarrow V_j(x)=C(x). \]

If every polynomial in \(G_j\), and \(V_j\), has degree at most \(b_j\ge1\), then

\[ \sum_{j=1}^t b_j\ge a+1. \tag{FC-degree} \]

Proof. Introduce a Boolean output coordinate \(z\), and choose a point \((x_0,z_0)\) with \(z_0\ne C(x_0)\). For each \(j\), the equations \(G_j(x)=0\) and \(z-V_j(x)=0\) cannot all hold there. Choose one polynomial \(F_j(x,z)\) from that system which is nonzero at \((x_0,z_0)\), and put \(P(x,z)=\prod_jF_j(x,z)\).

The product is nonzero at the chosen point. At every true graph point \((x,C(x))\), some \(j\) is a valid cover entry; all its equations, including the output equation, vanish. Thus \(P\) vanishes on the graph. The old polynomial \(P(x,z_0)\) is Boolean-nonzero, has degree at most \(\sum_jb_j\), and vanishes on the entire output class \(C^{-1}(z_0)\). That class contains one of the two Hamming balls. The all-field certifier argument therefore gives (FC-degree).

The number of equations inside each \(G_j\) is unrestricted. The proof chooses only one witness from each menu entry at a wrong graph point. It does not require low-degree indicator polynomials for the cover domains.

2. Application to complete coefficient menus

Use the complete three-level approximate-majority source, with \(a=\lfloor v/3\rfloor\). For each fixed scalar assignment to all its extension coefficients, let \(G_j(x)\) contain all specialized companions and field equations, and let \(V_j(x)\) be the specialized top product. On the common zero set of \(G_j\), the complete evaluation semantics gives \(V_j=C\).

Consequently, any menu whose good domains cover the whole old Boolean cube obeys (FC-degree), with \(b_j\) bounding its specialized equations and output. The same argument permits old-only polynomial coefficient maps, provided their complete image degrees and output are included in \(b_j\). It is not enough to inspect only a subset of the source equations and assume the top output remains correct.

If a generator has \(s\) prime-field seed variables and every seed gives one such assignment with degree ceiling \(b\), then its at most \(p^s\) choices can cover the cube only if

\[ p^s b\ge a+1. \]

This is a coverage-degree condition, not a general impossibility of pseudorandom generators. In particular, a logarithmic seed is not ruled out. The issue for the proposed route is the total degree spent enumerating its choices.

3. What the branch-product elimination actually costs

Let \(F\) include the old Boolean equations. Suppose the systems \(G_1,\ldots,G_t\) cover the whole old Boolean cube, and \(F\cup G_j\) has an ordinary NS refutation through degree \(D_j\). Then

\[ 1\in\mathcal I_{\sum_jD_j}(F). \tag{FC-NS} \]

Proof. Separate each certificate as \(1=A_j+B_j\), with \(A_j\in\mathcal I_{D_j}(F)\) and \(B_j=\sum_u q_{ju}G_{ju}\), each displayed product of degree at most \(D_j\). The telescoping identity

\[ 1-\prod_jB_j =\sum_j A_j\prod_{i<j}B_i \]

has an old NS certificate through \(\sum_jD_j\). Expand \(\prod_jB_j\). In each summand, the factor \(\prod_jG_{j,u_j}\) vanishes on the old Boolean cube: at every old point one cover entry has all its equations zero. Boolean division certifies that factor through its ordinary degree. Multiplying by \(\prod_jq_{j,u_j}\) keeps the summand within \(\sum_jD_j\). Thus the product has an old Boolean NS certificate at the same ceiling, proving (FC-NS). The expansion may be large; no polynomial certificate-size bound is asserted.

For complete scalar specializations of a source whose full axiom and output degrees fit \(D\), use \(D_j=D\). The menu must satisfy \(tD\ge a+1\). More generally the same conclusion holds for a proposed branch budget with \(D_j\ge b_j\). In the compact PHP regime \(v=(n+1)\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\),

\[ \sum_jD_j\ge\lfloor v/3\rfloor+1>n/2. \]

Thus this generic product-combination accounting cannot place the complete approximate-majority menu below the old PHP barrier. This does not exclude a different proof-specific combination with additional cancellations or another certified cost saving.

4. Covers exist; their degree cost is the obstacle

For calibration, a complete leveled ENS family with \(S\) companions and accuracy \(h\) has failure probability at most \(\varepsilon=S(1-1/p)^h\) at every fixed old Boolean input under independent uniform coefficient rows. Condition on earlier levels: a nonzero input vector makes each factor nonzero with probability \(1-1/p\); a union bound handles all companions. Field equations already hold for scalar coefficients.

If \(\varepsilon<1\), independently choosing \(t\) complete scalar assignments gives a covering menu with positive probability whenever \(2^v\varepsilon^t<1\). This is only a nonuniform existence control. It neither constructs a sufficiently cheap menu nor evades (FC-degree).

The cover obstruction concerns the complete evaluation source throughout the Boolean domain. Essential occurrence of that source in a short PHP proof has not been proved. Pruning unused modules, exploiting explicit PHP residuals, or controlling only a justified proof-specific interface can escape these hypotheses and still needs its own argument. Active feasibility for the actual compiler remains open.

5. A related published theorem needs different source bounds

A targeted primary-source check of Dahiya–Mahajan–Mouli (SAT 2024) found a finite-field extension bound with at most \(N^{1+\varepsilon(1-\delta)}\) extensions, original-variable arity at most \(N^{1-\varepsilon}\), and polynomial size. Its hard family is an XORification of generalized PHP. Definition 2.2 uses equations \(z_j-Q_j(x)\) in the original variables; Definition 4.1 defines support from those variables. Replacing a large defining polynomial by a chain of auxiliary gates does not automatically meet that model. Our full source has no proved matching inventory, arity, or conversion bound. No theorem from the paper is applied here.

The evidence note records the cover proof review, source scope, and literature locators. No new numerical suite or generator implementation was needed.

15 September 2026 — Existing pruning and a matrix normalization control

Status: reuse audit with no new pruning coverage; working necessary degree bounds for complete Boolean-domain matrix normalization. Cycle 158.

Question. Can proof-specific abstraction remove the auxiliary evaluation circuits that obstruct universal normalization? The first proposed cases were already covered by the record. A separate test of matrix-valued coefficients shows that matrix dimension alone does not bypass the Boolean-domain degree obstruction. Neither observation constructs the missing PHP-relative active functional.

1. The proposed pruning was already available

The original zero-cofactor lemma already removes a block when all its collected companion cofactors vanish, even if its variables occur in other cofactors or later inputs. Its coefficient variables are set to zero throughout the identity; retained inputs are rebuilt and the zero-coordinate cleanup preserves the introduction convention. This is reuse, not a new pruning theorem.

The Booleanity-port theorem handles isolated proof uses under its stated constant substitution and information-flow conditions. In the binary source, domain-only Booleanity witnesses already remove companion contributions that arose solely from Booleanity. A copied value requires its actual copy interface; it is not automatically an isolated Booleanity use.

The proper OR-union comparison retains nonzero collected companion cofactors for independent nonconstant affine inputs. Its domain-only countermodel shows that the comparison cannot simply be discarded with the Booleanity subproofs. This is evidence about the supplied local witness, not a claim that its term survives every global certificate rewrite.

Thus the complete approximate-majority evaluation gadget is harmless to a given certificate when the existing pruning hypotheses hold, but those hypotheses have not been established for every complex circuit occurring in a short PHP proof. No new coverage or sufficient support bound was found in this audit.

2. Matrix dimension does not remove the flat degree

Over any field, take independent old Boolean variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_r\), interpreted as scalar matrices \(x_iI_s\), \(s\ge1\). Let \(R_{u,i}(x)\) be arbitrary \(s\times s\) polynomial matrices, each entry of degree at most \(T\), and define the ordered product

\[ P(x)=\prod_{u=1}^h \left(I_s-\sum_{i=1}^rR_{u,i}(x)x_i\right). \]

If every complete companion \(x_iP(x)\) is zero entrywise on the old Boolean cube, then

\[ h(T+1)\ge r. \tag{MX-flat} \]

Proof. At the all-zero point, every factor is \(I_s\), so \(P=I_s\). At any other Boolean point, some \(x_i=1\), and its companion forces \(P=0\). Thus every diagonal entry has the Boolean function

\[ \prod_{i=1}^r(1-x_i). \]

Its unique multilinear representative has degree \(r\). Each entry of the ordered matrix product has ordinary degree at most \(h(T+1)\), proving (MX-flat). In particular, \(h=1,r=3\) requires \(T\ge2\), for every matrix dimension.

This necessary condition does not even need commutation or coefficient-field assumptions. A valid matrix interpretation of a commutative polynomial proof would need those additional conditions; dropping them in this lower-bound test only makes its hypothesis weaker. The claim concerns complete Boolean-domain companion images, not images certified using PHP residuals.

3. The complete evaluation obstruction also persists

For the three-level approximate-majority source, interpret old bits as scalar matrices and its extension coefficients as polynomial matrices, evaluating each displayed product in its given order. Let \(W(x)\) be a scalar polynomial with nonzero Boolean remainder. Suppose multiplying every complete matrix companion image by \(W\) makes it zero entrywise on the old cube. Let \(Z(x)\) be the top matrix product.

At a point with \(W(x)\ne0\), the bottom inputs are scalar zeros or ones. Their companion equations make each bottom product its correct scalar Boolean value times \(I_s\). The same argument applies successively to the middle and top products, giving \(Z(x)=C(x)I_s\). Hence \(Z_{11}\) agrees with \(C\) wherever \(W\ne0\). The partial-representation bound yields

\[ \deg W+\deg Z\ge\lfloor v/3\rfloor+1, \]

where matrix degree is the nonnegative entry-degree ceiling \(\max(0,\max_{i,j}\deg Z_{ij})\), so zero entries cause no degree-convention issue. This statement uses a scalar weight; no claim about arbitrary matrix-valued weights is made. Matrix dimension alone therefore does not rescue that complete Boolean-domain strategy. A PHP-relative or proof-specific interpretation remains a different problem.

4. What remains

The next useful source result must go beyond the existing pruning conditions and control nonzero companion contributions in a full proof context, or directly solve the active PHP-relative equations. 15 September 2026 — Compressing comparison components through exposed products

Status: working affine boundary-type certificates and a proof-specific component-compression theorem; the full-source boundary bound remains open. Cycle 159.

Question. Can a whole certificate use less information than the complete evaluation source? The answer is yes for an isolated comparison component. Its internal product values can be replaced by functions of the products whose genuine interfaces remain exposed. With one exposed product the replacement is affine and preserves the original source degree budget. It does not claim that every compiled PHP source has such a small exposed boundary.

1. Grouping a block does not by itself give a smaller ENS tuple

For an ordinary NS certificate, group a block's summands as \(P_aA_a\), where \(A_a=\sum_iq_{a,i}g_{a,i}\). This is a valid polynomial identity. The aggregate can depend on other blocks' coefficients and is not automatically a valid earlier input for a new ENS block.

For the actual proper OR-union witness, let the parent be 0 and its two children be 1 and 2. Put \(A=\sum_{i\in I_1}U_i^0f_i\), \(B=\sum_{i\in I_2}U_i^0f_i\), so \(A+B=1-P_0\). The three grouped contributions are

\[ P_0(1-P_1P_2),\qquad -P_1P_2A,\qquad -P_1P_2B. \]

The parent's aggregate depends on the child coefficients, while the first child's aggregate \(-P_2A\) depends on the parent's coefficients. For independent nonconstant inputs these dependencies are nonzero. They already form a cycle among blocks that originally had old-affine inputs at one level. Grouping does not justify applying a triangular input-elimination theorem to those aggregates. The construction below instead changes the values used by certified interfaces.

2. Unrealizable boundary types have short complete witnesses

Work over \(\mathbb F_p\). Let \(P_1,\ldots,P_k\) be complete old-affine ENS products of common accuracy \(h\), with nonconstant affine inputs \(g_{j,i}(x)\), and write \(w=2h\), \(W=kw\). Retain their companions and all their own field equations, together with old Booleanity. For a bit vector \(\eta\in\{0,1\}^k\), define

\[ \delta_\eta(P)= \prod_{\eta_j=1}P_j\prod_{\eta_j=0}(1-P_j). \]

Call \(\eta\) feasible if there is a point \(x\in\mathbb F_p^v\) at which the zero-set indicators of the \(k\) affine tuples have precisely these values. The point need not satisfy the old PHP equations or be an old Boolean input; it will only define a consistent comparison character.

Lemma. If \(\eta\) is infeasible, then \(\delta_\eta(P)\) has an ordinary NS certificate through \(W+1\) from the retained boundary system and old Booleanity. If the positive affine equations are consistent, the ceiling improves to \(W\).

Proof. Let \(J_+=\{j:\eta_j=1\}\) and \(J_-=\{j:\eta_j=0\}\). If the positive input equations are inconsistent over \(\mathbb F_p\), a constant linear combination of them equals one. Multiply it by \(\prod_{J_+}P_j\) and use one positive companion in every summand. This costs at most \(\sum_{J_+}w+1\); multiplication by the remaining negative factors gives \(W+1\).

Otherwise let \(L\) be their nonempty affine zero flat, and put \(q=|J_-|\). Infeasibility says that the negative zero flats cover \(L\). For every choice of one input \(g_{j,i_j}\) from each negative tuple, the polynomial \(R=\prod_{J_-}g_{j,i_j}\), of degree at most \(q\), vanishes on \(L(\mathbb F_p)\). Ordinary affine coordinates, followed by division by the free-coordinate equations \(y^p-y\), give an NS certificate for \(R\) from the positive affine equations and old Booleanity through degree \(q\). The pullback of \(y^p-y\) is a linear combination of \(x_i^p-x_i\), and each has a Boolean certificate through degree \(p\). Such terms only occur when \(q\ge p\); if \(q<p\), the reduced polynomial is identically zero. This retains the stated degree \(q\).

Now expand each negative factor using its literal prefix identity \(1-P_j=\sum_iU_{j,i}g_{j,i}\), with \(\deg U_{j,i}\le w-1\). In each summand use the preceding certificate for \(R\). Old Boolean terms cost at most \(W\). A positive input term is absorbed by that input's companion, with its product \(P_j\) supplied by the positive factors; its cost is also at most \(W\). These are complete ordinary generator-multiple witnesses, proving the lemma. No boundary rank bound is used.

3. Replace internal values by boundary interpolation

Let \(\mathscr A\) be a same-level family of old-affine products of common weight \(w=2h\). Its internal ports are union relations \(Z_c-Z_aZ_b\), where the parent tuple is the union of the child tuples, and copy relations for equal affine zero flats. Choose \(k\) products to retain as a boundary \(\mathscr B\). These products keep their complete original ENS blocks.

For every feasible boundary type \(\eta\), choose one field point \(x_\eta\) realizing it and give every component node its zero-flat value at \(x_\eta\). For an infeasible type choose arbitrary Boolean internal values, while giving each boundary node its prescribed bit \(\eta_j\). Denote the resulting bit for node \(a\) by \(c_a(\eta)\), and put

\[ v_a(Z_{\mathscr B})=\sum_{\eta\in\{0,1\}^k} c_a(\eta)\delta_\eta(Z_{\mathscr B}). \]

Every boundary value is fixed literally: \(v_j=Z_j\). Every other \(v_a\) has weighted degree at most \(W\). After interpreting boundary names by their genuine products, all internal union, copy, and Booleanity ports have ordinary NS witnesses through \(2W\).

Proof. For \(k\ge1\), a union port \(R=v_c-v_av_b\) has weighted degree at most \(2W\). Its Boolean remainder in the boundary names is \(\sum_\eta R(\eta)\delta_\eta\). Feasible types contribute zero because affine-zero-set indicators multiply under union. Thus only infeasible types remain. Weighted Boolean division costs at most \(2W\), and the preceding lemma certifies every remaining type through \(W+1\le2W\). Boundary Booleanity itself has the literal prefix certificate

\[ P_j^2-P_j=-\sum_iU_{j,i}(g_{j,i}P_j) \in\mathcal I_{2w}. \]

Substituting these witnesses into the Boolean-division terms preserves \(2W\). Copy ports have the same argument with equal point values. Each \(v_a\) is Boolean on the formal boundary cube, so its Booleanity is certified through \(2W\) as well. All retained coefficient-field equations remain available.

For an empty boundary, choose one field point and use its constant character; every internal port vanishes literally. Truth-table expressions can have \(2^k\) terms. These are degree and retained-block bounds, not a polynomial running-time or expanded-size claim for growing \(k\).

4. One boundary product gives an affine replacement at no degree loss

Suppose the one retained boundary tuple has a nonempty proper affine zero flat. Choose \(x_0\) outside it and \(x_1\) inside it, and write \(c_a^i\) for node \(a\)'s zero-flat value at \(x_i\). Then

\[ v_a=c_a^0+(c_a^1-c_a^0)Z_\star \in\{0,1,Z_\star,1-Z_\star\}. \]

The boundary is fixed. For a union port, put \(d_a=c_a^1-c_a^0\), \(d_b=c_b^1-c_b^0\). The exact polynomial identity is

\[ v_c-v_av_b=-d_ad_b(Z_\star^2-Z_\star). \tag{BC-one} \]

A copy port vanishes literally, and \(v_a^2-v_a=d_a^2(Z_\star^2-Z_\star)\). Consequently the new witnesses cost at most \(2w=4h\), fitting the original union cost \(3w=6h\) and copy/Booleanity cost \(2w\). This uses a genuine retained boundary block; it does not give prefix or companion certificates for the removed tuples.

5. Proof-specific transfer and its interface condition

Use an explicit costed modular NS identity for an old target, as in the audited source interface. Its outer polynomials use old variables and whole-product names. A discarded product may be a genuine OR/copy root only in the internal union/copy ports. A direct companion or input-prefix use outside those port witnesses, or outside a separately reconstructed Booleanity port, forces that product to remain on the boundary. The condition is checked on the given modular proof; it is not inferred from an arbitrary flattened certificate.

Outside the component, removed values may occur in outer coefficients, in later input expressions, and as Boolean parameters of the standard source templates. A parameter use means that its template remains valid after replacing that value by any Boolean polynomial with the stated degree bound. The singleton-value OR template and isolated Booleanity ports have this property. Mere absence of a named companion from an arbitrary flattened certificate does not establish this condition: a domain-only identity can still encode a particular product's input behavior.

Working transfer. Charge internal union ports \(3w\) and copy/Booleanity ports \(2w\), keeping every outer cofactor's original declared weight. Under these interface conditions and costs, one can remove the internal coefficient blocks, retain the boundary blocks completely, and rebuild every later input and source witness. For \(k\) boundary products, the ordinary NS degree is at most \(\max(1,k)D\). For one boundary it remains \(D\), and the affine-in-earlier-selector input grammar is preserved.

Proof. Substitute the \(v_a\)'s in the free formal identity, fixing boundary names and the old target. Rebuild retained products in level order on the substituted inputs, keeping their fresh coefficients and all own field equations. Component roots had the same level and weight, so the one-boundary substitution introduces no same-level input dependence and does not increase any original weighted bound.

More generally, with \(T=\max(1,k)\), each original product has a rebuilt or virtual value of degree at most \(T\) times its original weight. For a retained block, the induction uses \(\delta'\le T\delta\) and \(h(\delta'+1)\le T h(\delta+1)\). This is one uniform scaling, not one factor per later level. The original input and generator costs remain upper bounds after scaling; smaller collected images do not reset those costs.

Internal union/copy/Booleanity ports use the interpolation witnesses through \(2kw\), within \(T\) times their original costs. Outside genuine-root ports keep their roots by the isolation hypothesis, and the standard prefix/copy identities are rebuilt on their new inputs. Boolean-parameter ports use the new Booleanity witnesses. Each outer cofactor and its port certificate therefore fit \(TD\). Summing gives the old target from the new system. Apply the usual zero-input and unused-coefficient cleanup to preserve the strict source introduction convention.

The source-wide application here is to the audited binary OR/Booleanity compiler; an odd-prime full Frege compiler is not supplied by this result. The component identities and boundary-type certificates themselves hold over every prime. For \(k>1\), later inputs can become nonlinear in boundary products, so the original affine-input grammar must not be assumed to survive.

6. Source-shaped checks and remaining gap

The focused check uses a component with all four affine boundary-value types and a later two-input ENS block. The later inputs originally use two distinct component products \(P_\star,P_-\): \(g_1=P_\star\), \(g_2=1-P_-\). Interpolation sends \(P_-\) to \(1-P_\star\), so both rebuilt inputs are \(P_\star\). The formal nonlinear input rank drops from two to one.

The later interface has Boolean child values \(a=1-P_\star\), \(b=P_-\) (the non-OR syntax can be \(\neg A\lor\neg\neg B\)). Its original certificate is

\[ P_Q-ab=E_{Q,1}+aE_{Q,2} +U_{Q,1}b(a^2-a)+U_{Q,2}a(b^2-b). \tag{BC-later} \]

Thus it uses the removed value through Booleanity rather than its full input-prefix interface. Replacing that Booleanity by the boundary witness rebuilds the certificate. With \(w_Q=h(w+1)\), its original ceiling \(w_Q+2w\) is retained.

The compiled checker passed 264 complete NS certificate checks over \(p=2,3,5\), with \(h=1,2\) and retained boundary rank \(2h+1\). Each component has four basic old-affine tuples and sixteen union tuples. Nineteen product blocks are removed and one is retained. The output preserves all original factored block definitions and field domains, all virtual values, and the complete rebuilt axiom tables and NS cofactors.

Each case checks sixteen union ports, four copies, twenty Booleanity ports, one rebuilt later port, and three infeasible-type witnesses. The latter include inconsistent positive flats, containment in a negative flat, and all \(p\) affine hyperplanes covering one field coordinate. The later port keeps ceiling seven at \(h=1\) and eighteen at \(h=2\). The general \(k\)-boundary interpolation is proved above; these executable checks focus on its one-boundary source transfer and its type-certificate ingredients.

All eighteen complete retained-system models satisfy the old Boolean equations, every retained companion, and the actual coefficient fields \(r^p-r\). Odd-prime models include non-Boolean coefficient values. Controls show that changing the retained boundary or hiding an exposed internal companion/prefix use invalidates the proposed transfer. Four odd-field controls retain all fields and the later companions but omit boundary companions; boundary Booleanity then fails, as expected.

These are satisfiable local source checks, not finite PHP lower-bound instances. The full JSONL output and reproduction note retain the complete evidence. Compilation and the exact run succeeded without a retry.

Remaining gap. This is a new source-interface compression mechanism, not a proof that the full PHP source has a small exposed boundary. The next audit must measure or bound the genuinely exposed products in the actual compiler. It must also distinguish those uses from appearances inside Boolean parameters and later inputs; counting variable occurrences alone would miss the permitted compression.

Process assessment. Grouping raw companion contributions revealed cyclic dependencies; keeping the certified port structure instead produced a boundary-based compression with explicit original-degree reconstruction. No further conditional refinement is needed before testing that boundary condition on the full source.

15 September 2026 — Ordinary PC and NS foundations for the publication formalization

Status: formalized definitions and elementary interface lemmas; R01. No equality of PC and NS spaces is asserted.

Ordinary polynomial proof foundations

Question and stopping point. Supply the common ordinary-polynomial interface needed by the remaining bit-PHP route, before formalizing completed-line reuse, substitution, or matching reduction. The source is paper §2, together with the functional base and compact base. Stop with a checked shared interface and a local checkpoint so independent workers can import it.

Over a field \(K\), use the ordinary ring \(K[V]\). Applications have finite \(V\); the elementary interface also permits arbitrary variable types. Write \(\deg 0=0\), following Mathlib's natural total degree. A derivation through \(B\) is a finite tree whose leaves are zero or axioms of degree at most \(B\), and whose rules are addition, scalar multiplication, and multiplication by a single variable when its output has degree at most \(B\). Trees may reuse their premise derivations; reading the premises in order gives concatenated ordinary PC derivations. No polynomial-multiplication or NS rule is built into this definition.

\[ \mathcal C_B(\mathcal F)=\{f:\mathcal F\vdash_B f\},\qquad \mathcal I_B(\mathcal F)=\operatorname{span}_K\{qF:F\in\mathcal F,\ \deg(qF)\le B\}. \]

Interface facts and proof. Every derived polynomial has degree at most \(B\): induct on the tree, using the supplied bounds for axioms and variable multiplication, \(\deg(f+g)\le\max(\deg f,\deg g)\), and \(\deg(af)\le\deg f\). The zero, addition, and scalar rules make \(\mathcal C_B\) a subspace. Enlarging the axiom set or the ceiling preserves every tree, by the same induction. The bounded-degree space is Mathlib's ordinary total-degree submodule. Every spanning generator of \(\mathcal I_B\) lies in it, hence so does its span. Enlarging the axiom set or ceiling enlarges the set of legal products and therefore the span; each individually legal product belongs to that span. These statements include zero generators and zero degree bounds.

The file also defines Boolean axioms \(X_v^2-X_v\), the weak unary base consisting of Booleanity, row sums minus one, and different-row same-column products, and the functional base adding different-column same-row products. The binary compact base on \(m\) rows and \(\ell\) bits consists of Booleanity and \(\prod_t(1+b_{it}+b_{i't})\) for \(i<i'\). All these are ordinary polynomials; no quotient reduction is implicit, and each NS product is charged before summing.

Verification and remaining route. PolynomialCalculus.lean records the exact definitions and checked interface declarations. The verification report preserves theorem types and transitive axiom reports; the scope map separates R02–R04 and the later publication obligations. The initial check exposed constructor syntax, a Mathlib argument-order mismatch, and a missing field-instance import; these were corrected without changing the mathematics. No mathematical discrepancy was identified. Process assessment: agreeing on exact shared names before dependent proofs avoids competing PC and NS definitions; Mathlib's existing bounded-degree space is linked rather than rebuilt.

15 September 2026 — Completed-line reuse and the ordinary NS-to-PC bridge

Status: Lean formalization of the full reuse lemma and elementary NS inclusion; R02.

Completed-line multiplication versus flattened certificates

Question and scope. Formalize historical Lemma 1.3 and the elementary inclusion used in Lemma 1.2, using the primitive ordinary PC interface. The stopping point is a reusable checked multiplication interface for substitution and Boolean reduction; it is not an identification of all bounded PC consequences with NS certificates.

Over any field, if \(f\in\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F)\), then for every ordinary polynomial \(q\),

\[ qf\in\mathcal C_{\max\{B,\deg q+\deg f\}}(\mathcal F). \qquad q\mathcal I_B(\mathcal F)\subseteq\mathcal I_{B+\deg q}(\mathcal F), \qquad \mathcal I_B(\mathcal F)\subseteq\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F). \]

Proof of reuse. Expand \(q=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha X^\alpha\) over its actual support. Starting from the completed line \(f\), scale by \(c_\alpha\) and multiply by each variable occurrence of \(X^\alpha\). Every intermediate new line has degree at most \(|\alpha|+\deg f\le\deg q+\deg f\). The original derivation still costs \(B\); taking the linear combination of these completed products adds no degree. The Lean proof implements this monomial construction by induction under multiplication by a variable. A nonzero monomial gains exactly one in ordinary degree; a zero intermediate multiplier is handled directly by the zero rule. This includes \(q=0\), \(f=0\), constants, and degree-zero derivations. Earlier derivation lines are never multiplied by \(q\).

Proof of the NS bound. If \(p=\sum_i a_i r_iF_i\) is an ordinary NS certificate with each \(\deg(r_iF_i)\le B\), then \(qp=\sum_i a_i(qr_i)F_i\). Each new generator multiple has degree at most \(\deg q+B\). Formally this is induction on the spanning submodule, with the generator, zero, addition, and scalar cases explicit. Cancellation among larger-degree terms does not authorize any generator.

Proof of inclusion. Consider one legal generator multiple \(qF\), of degree at most \(B\). If it is zero, the zero PC rule suffices. Otherwise the field polynomial ring is a domain, so \(\deg(qF)=\deg q+\deg F\). Thus \(F\) itself is an eligible degree-\(B\) axiom and completed-line reuse derives \(qF\) through \(B\). Closure under linear combinations proves the inclusion for the entire NS span. The converse remains a separate, system-specific theorem.

Verification and process. PolynomialCalculusReuse.lean and the verification report expose all three statements and their checked dependencies. The scope map records the source and excluded downstream claims. Verification retried after correcting a tactic-module import and one linter warning; these were operational issues. The proof follows the source; the local monomial helper is kept in the same file because it serves this construction. Process assessment: the shared primitive derivation interface makes the degree distinction between reuse and flattening explicit without adding stronger inference rules. Substitution and duality remain R03 and R04.

15 September 2026 — Formal row-linear dimensions and ordinary affine restrictions (R13)

Status: complete Lean formalization of two extracted supporting claims; quotient injection, PC separation, and the common-kernel theorem are separate obligations.

Assignment and endpoint. The parallel formalization assignment selects R13 and R15 of the bit-PHP route. This cycle releases R13: the ordinary row-linear space, its exact dimension and top coefficient, and the ordinary affine restriction image bound required by the later common-kernel comparison. R15 still requires affine-coordinate and duality prerequisites. The statements are extracted from the paper's row-linear dimension equation and ordinary-restriction audit, with the broader quotient-injection claim left distinct. These are supporting interfaces adapted from the recorded arguments, with no novelty claim.

Row-linear polynomial space and exact dimension

Claim lem:row-linear-polynomial-space. Let \(K\) be any field and \(m,\ell,k\) any natural numbers. In the ordinary polynomial ring \(K[b_{ia}:i\in[m],a\in[\ell]]\), let \(\mathcal L_k\) be the span of monomials of degree at most \(k\) containing at most one variable from each row. Then

\[ \dim_K\mathcal L_k=\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom mj\ell^j, \qquad \deg p\le k\quad(p\in\mathcal L_k). \]

Every nonzero \(p\in\mathcal L_k\) has a nonzero coefficient on a monomial using exactly \(\deg p\) rows. The formal definition uses natural total degree, with \(\deg0=0\), and counts ordinary coefficients; it is not a Boolean quotient.

Full proof. Index a monomial by \(0\le j\le k\), a \(j\)-element subset \(S\) of the rows, and a function \(a:S\to[\ell]\). Its variable set is the graph \(\{(i,a(i)):i\in S\}\), and its exponent vector assigns one to each graph element and zero elsewhere. This indexing is injective: projecting the graph to rows recovers \(S\), the unique variable in each selected row recovers \(a\), and its cardinality recovers \(j\). Conversely every allowed monomial has exactly this description. Ordinary monomials form a coefficient basis, so the allowed exponent subset gives a basis of \(\mathcal L_k\).

There are \(\binom mj\) row subsets and \(\ell^j\) coordinate functions on each, proving the dimension formula. An indexed exponent has total sum \(j\le k\), so every supported exponent of \(p\) has sum at most \(k\); their maximum is \(\deg p\). If \(p\ne0\), its finite support is nonempty, so choose an exponent attaining that maximum. Its coefficient is nonzero by support membership, and its index uses exactly \(\deg p\) rows. This includes constants through the empty row set. It also covers \(k>m\), since \(\binom mj=0\) for \(j>m\), and \(m=0\) or \(\ell=0\), when only the constant monomial remains. \(\square\)

Ordinary affine restriction image dimension

Claim lem:ordinary-restriction-dimension. For any field \(K\) and natural \(d,k\), the subspace \(K[z_1,\ldots,z_d]_{\le k}\) has dimension at most \(\binom{d+k}{k}\). Let \(U\) be any subspace of ordinary source polynomials, all of degree at most \(k\), and substitute each source variable by an ordinary polynomial of degree at most one in these \(d\) variables. Then degree does not increase and

\[ \dim_K\operatorname{res}(U)\le\binom{d+k}{k}. \]

In particular this applies to \(U=\mathcal L_k\) and to affine free coordinates on a codimension-\(r\) flat, taking \(d=v-r\). The formal theorem allows an arbitrary source variable type and requires only the stated degree bounds.

Full proof. The coefficient basis of the target degree space is indexed by nonnegative exponent vectors \(e\) with \(\sum_i e_i\le k\). Add a dummy symbol with multiplicity \(k-\sum_i e_i\), keeping the original \(d\) multiplicities. The result is a multiset of exactly \(k\) symbols from \(d+1\) choices. The encoding is injective because ignoring the dummy recovers every original exponent. Stars and bars counts these multisets as \(\binom{(d+1)+k-1}{k}=\binom{d+k}{k}\), giving the bound. The encoding is in fact bijective, but injectivity suffices here; equality of the full target dimension is not needed.

If a variable \(x_i\) is replaced by \(g_i\) with \(\deg g_i\le1\), a monomial with exponent \(e\) becomes its scalar coefficient times \(\prod_i g_i^{e_i}\), of degree at most \(\sum_i e_i\). Addition cannot increase the largest term degree, so substitution cannot increase the source polynomial's degree. Thus its image on \(U\) is a subspace of the target degree space, and dimension monotonicity proves the result. This works over finite fields without identifying pointwise vanishing with the zero ordinary polynomial. For \(d=0\) or \(k=0\) the target consists of constants and the binomial bound is one. \(\square\)

Formalization and evidence. RowLinearPolynomialSpace.lean provides the explicit monomial index, its cardinality, the polynomial subspace and finite-dimensional instance, the exact dimension theorem, degree bound, and maximal coefficient theorem. OrdinaryRestrictionDimension.lean provides the independent reusable target-dimension and affine-restriction interface. Their separate row-linear and restriction reports retain exact theorem types and transitive axiom audits. The reproduction record links the pre-proof scope map, pinned dependencies, and complete measured command evidence.

Review and remaining route. These seven theorem declarations discharge R13, including constants and empty dimension cases. They do not establish literal affine-ideal membership or the strict common-kernel inequality of R15, and do not formalize the larger quotient-injection or PC-separation claims. The main Frege status and existing mathematical-gap list were reviewed and are unchanged; the coordinator owns their living-section updates. No new mathematical discrepancy was found.

Process assessment. Separating ordinary restriction dimension from row-specific counting produced a reusable dependency; the small indexing and cardinality helpers remain local. 15 September 2026 — Degree-controlled substitution and weighted PC replay

Status: full Lean formalization of the polynomial substitution lemma, including weighted replay; R03.

Polynomial substitution through the actual predecessor degree

Question and stopping point. Formalize historical Lemma 1.4, retaining the exact primitive multiplication budget needed by later affine removal. Stop at the general replay theorem; constructing the source-specific weighted axiom-image proofs is a downstream obligation.

Let \(\phi:K[V]\to K[W]\) substitute \(v\mapsto g_v\), with \(\deg g_v\le T\), over a field. If \(\mathcal F\vdash_D f\), then \(\phi(\mathcal F)\vdash_{TD}\phi(f)\). More generally, fix an ordinary polynomial \(w\) and a target system \(\mathcal G\). Suppose every source axiom \(a\in\mathcal F\) of degree at most \(D\) has a supplied derivation

\[ \mathcal G\vdash_{TD+\deg w}w\phi(a). \qquad\text{Then}\qquad \mathcal G\vdash_{TD+\deg w}w\phi(f). \]

The supplied images are actual PC derivations, not extra axioms silently adjoined to \(\mathcal G\). The Lean statement permits arbitrary variable types and every natural \(T\), including \(T=0\); finite-variable applications with \(T\ge1\) recover the source statement.

Degree bound. For an actual-support monomial \(c_\alpha X^\alpha\), its substituted polynomial is \(c_\alpha\prod_v g_v^{\alpha_v}\). Its degree is at most \(\sum_v\alpha_v\deg g_v\le T|\alpha|\). Taking the finite sum over the support gives \(\deg\phi(p)\le T\deg p\), without reducing any ordinary powers.

Weighted proof. Induct on the source primitive derivation. Zero maps to zero; an axiom uses its supplied image proof; addition and scalar multiplication commute with substitution and multiplication by \(w\). Consider the step \(p\mapsto X_vp\). If \(p=0\), its image is zero. Otherwise the ordinary polynomial ring is a domain and \(\deg(X_vp)=\deg p+1\le D\). By the preceding degree bound,

\[ \deg g_v+\deg(w\phi(p)) \le T+\deg w+T\deg p \le TD+\deg w. \]

The inductive image line \(w\phi(p)\) is already derived through \(TD+\deg w\). Apply completed-line multiplication by \(g_v\); the displayed inequality keeps its maximum ceiling unchanged. Commutativity identifies the result with \(w\phi(X_vp)\). This proves weighted replay. For ordinary substitution take \(w=1\), the target system \(\phi(\mathcal F)\), and use each axiom image directly; its degree is at most \(TD\).

15 September 2026 — Binary Boolean reduction with ordinary-degree certificates

R05 formalization · verified binary specialization of degree-controlled field reduction

Statement and assigned endpoint

Let \(V\) be a finite variable set and work in the ordinary polynomial ring \(\mathbb F_2[X_i:i\in V]\). Put \(\mathrm{BOOL}=\{X_i^2-X_i:i\in V\}\), and let \(\mathcal I_d\) charge the ordinary degree of every individual generator multiple. For an exponent vector \(e\), put \(M_S=\prod_{i\in S}X_i\) and define

\[ \operatorname{red}(P)=\sum_{e\in\operatorname{supp}(P)}[X^e]P\,M_{\operatorname{supp}(e)}. \]

The verified statement is that \(\operatorname{red}(P)\) has individual degrees at most one and total degree at most \(\deg P\), agrees with \(P\) at every Boolean point, and satisfies

\[ P-\operatorname{red}(P)\in\mathcal I_{\deg P}(\mathrm{BOOL}). \]

Consequently a polynomial \(P\) vanishing at all Boolean points belongs to \(\mathcal I_d(\mathrm{BOOL})\) whenever \(\deg P\le d\), and

\[ \deg q\le k\quad\Longrightarrow\quad q^2-q\in\mathcal I_{2k}(\mathrm{BOOL}). \]

This extracts the binary portion of historical Lemma 1.5 needed by the bit-PHP paper's Boolean-reduction lemma. It does not mark that broader all-prime, mixed-domain historical claim fully formalized.

Full certificate argument

For every \(n\ge1\), \(X_i^n-X_i\in\mathcal I_n(\mathrm{BOOL})\). At \(n=1\) the polynomial is zero. Induct using

\[ X_i^{n+1}-X_i=X_i^{n-1}(X_i^2-X_i)+(X_i^n-X_i). \]

The new generator multiple has ordinary degree at most \(n+1\), and the earlier witness remains legal at this larger ceiling. To reduce a product of positive powers, induct over its variables with

\[ AB-ab=A(B-b)+(A-a)b, \qquad A=X_i^{e_i},\quad a=X_i,\quad B=\prod_{j\in S}X_j^{e_j},\quad b=M_S. \]

The first error has certificate cost at most \(e_i+\sum_{j\in S}e_j\). The second has cost at most \(e_i+|S|\), which is no larger because all exponents indexed by \(S\) are positive. Here multiplying an existing ordinary NS witness uses the already verified R02 multiplication closure, which multiplies each legal generator multiple and charges its actual degree. Therefore \(X^e-M_{\operatorname{supp}(e)}\) has certificate cost at most \(\sum_i e_i\). Scalar combination over the monomials of \(P\) gives the stated witness through \(\deg P\). No Boolean quotient degree replaces an original polynomial degree.

Each \(M_S\) has individual degrees at most one and total degree at most \(|S|\). Since \(|\operatorname{supp}(e)|\le\sum_i e_i\), the remainder has the asserted total-degree bound. At a point of \(\mathbb F_2^V\), every positive power of a coordinate equals that coordinate, proving pointwise agreement.

Grid injectivity and boundary cases

The formal proof reuses Mathlib's checked finite-field evaluation injectivity. A complete argument for that step is as follows. For \(v=|V|\), the squarefree polynomial space has the \(2^v\) squarefree monomials as a basis. The space of functions on \(\mathbb F_2^V\) also has dimension \(2^v\). Evaluation is onto, since the point \(a\) has the squarefree indicator

\[ \delta_a(X)=\prod_{i:a_i=0}(1-X_i)\prod_{i:a_i=1}X_i. \]

Thus evaluation between these equal-dimensional spaces is an isomorphism. A zero-evaluating squarefree polynomial is zero. Applied to the remainder, this proves the vanishing certificate. Finally \(q^2-q\) vanishes at every Boolean point and has ordinary degree at most \(2\deg q\); monotonicity gives the version with a supplied ceiling \(k\). This includes zero and constant polynomials. For an empty variable set there is one assignment, both spaces above have dimension one, and the empty indicator product is one. Lean uses its natural total-degree convention \(\deg0=0\).

Verification and dependencies. BooleanReduction.lean uses the checked R01 ordinary NS definitions and R02 multiplication closure, plus pinned Mathlib polynomial and finite-field facts. The targeted incremental audit prints the full theorem types and transitive axiom reports. Scope, proof design and reproduction evidence retain all checks. No custom axiom or unproved dependency is introduced.

15 September 2026 — Bounded-degree duality and compatible annihilator extension

Status: full Lean formalization of historical separation and a reusable standard linear-algebra dependency; R04.

Separation and annihilator extension

Question and stopping point. Complete historical Lemma 1.2 and provide the compatible-extension interface needed by matching moments. The general linear-algebra result below is standard, with basis extension supplied by pinned Mathlib; neither its statement nor a different implementation is claimed as project novelty. Stop before proving any matching-filtration or source-specific compatibility hypothesis.

Let \(M\) be a vector space over a field \(K\), and \(S\le M\). For \(v\in M\), there exists a linear functional \(L\) with \(L(v)=1\) and \(L(S)=0\) if and only if \(v\notin S\). Necessity follows immediately by applying \(L\). For sufficiency, extend a basis of \(S\) by \(v\), prescribe zero on \(S\) and one on \(v\), and extend linearly to an ambient basis. Mathlib's LinearMap.exists_extend_of_notMem supplies this construction. Finite dimension is unnecessary for existence.

More generally, let \(U,S\le M\) and \(\lambda:U\to K\) be linear, with \(\lambda(x)=0\) whenever \(x\in U\cap S\). Then \(\lambda\) extends to an ambient linear \(L:M\to K\) annihilating \(S\).

Complete extension argument. Define \(h(u+s)=\lambda(u)\) on \(U+S\). If \(u+s=u'+s'\), then \(u-u'=s'-s\in U\cap S\), so \(\lambda(u)=\lambda(u')\); hence the definition is independent of the decomposition. Addition and scalar multiplication show that \(h\) is linear. It agrees with \(\lambda\) on \(U\) and vanishes on \(S\). Extend \(h\) to an ambient basis of \(M\), assigning arbitrary values on a complement. The resulting \(L\) has both required properties. The Lean proof uses LinearPMap.sup to glue the compatible partial maps and LinearMap.exists_extend for the final extension.

Application to actual bounded-degree polynomial functionals

Let \(P_B=K[V]_{\le B}\) be the ordinary polynomial subspace, with \(\deg0=0\). The formal definition HasNormalizedFunctional(S,B) asks for \(\lambda:P_B\to K\), normalized by \(\lambda(1)=1\), which annihilates every member of \(S\) lying in \(P_B\). Apply separation inside \(P_B\) to the inverse image of \(S\) under its subtype inclusion. The constant polynomial one belongs to \(P_B\), including when \(B=0\); its membership in that inverse image is exactly \(1\in S\). Therefore

\[ \exists\text{ degree-}B\text{ NS design for }\mathcal F \iff 1\notin\mathcal I_B(\mathcal F), \qquad \exists\text{ normalized annihilator of }\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F) \iff \mathcal F\not\vdash_B1. \]

Both NS and PC spaces lie in \(P_B\) by the foundation lemmas. Their functionals are linear only: no positivity, multiplicativity, or point-evaluation representation is assumed. The remaining assertion of historical Lemma 1.2, \(\mathcal I_B\subseteq\mathcal C_B\), is precisely the already checked R02 inclusion and is reused rather than re-proved.

Statement and complete proof

Let \(S\) be a finite variable set, let \(x,y\in S\) be distinct, and suppose the polynomial system \(\mathcal F\) explicitly contains \(X_xX_y\). Over \(\mathbb F_2\), write \(M_S=\prod_{i\in S}X_i\). Then

\[ M_S=M_{S\setminus\{x,y\}}(X_xX_y) \quad\text{and}\quad M_S\in\mathcal I_{|S|}(\mathcal F). \]

For the identity, remove the factor \(X_x\) from the finite product. Because \(x\ne y\), the remaining product still contains \(X_y\); remove that factor as well and commute the factors. The displayed product is one legal NS generator multiple: its polynomial is exactly \(M_S\), whose ordinary total degree is at most \(|S|\). Thus the supplied forbidden-pair equation alone gives the stated certificate. No Boolean quotient calculation or inferred exclusion equation is used. The membership hypotheses exclude the empty and singleton sets automatically.

15 September 2026 — Affine-system witnesses and an ordinary polynomial bridge (R07 release)

Status: complete Lean formalization of two extracted supporting claims; this is an intermediate R07 release, not completion of all scalar cleanup or companion-degree obligations.

Assignment and stopping point. The assigned branch formalizes R07, R08 and R16. This cycle releases the affine linear-algebra witnesses required by R15 and semantic weakening: proper-span consistency, constant linear-combination certificates, independent linear parts, and a faithful ordinary polynomial representation. The source is the affine setup of common vanishing learning, the semantic weakening argument, and the paper's scalar-cleanup discussion. Their larger learning and PC claims remain separate. No new mathematical novelty is asserted.

A faithful finite affine-form interface

Claim lem:affine-form-polynomial-interface. Let \(K\) be any field and \(n\ge0\). Represent an affine form by a constant \(a_0\) and linear coefficients \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\), collected as a function on an extra constant coordinate together with \([n]\). Define

\[ E_a(x)=a_0+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i, \qquad P_a=C(a_0)+\sum_{i=1}^n a_iX_i\in K[X_1,\ldots,X_n]. \]

The map \(a\mapsto P_a\) is linear and injective, \(\deg P_a\le1\), and evaluation gives \(P_a(x)=E_a(x)\). The unit constant form maps to the polynomial one. Every affine map \(F:K^n\to K\) has such a representation, obtained by taking \(a_0=F(0)\) and \(a_i=F^{\rm lin}(e_i)\), and the resulting polynomial evaluates to \(F\).

Full proof. The polynomial assignment is linear because constants and scalar multiples of variables distribute over addition and scalar multiplication. Each summand has degree at most one, so the whole polynomial does too. Evaluation sends each variable to its coordinate and the constant polynomial to its scalar, proving the evaluation identity. Equality of affine values at zero gives equality of constant coefficients. Equality at each coordinate vector \(e_i\), after subtracting the common constant, gives equality of each linear coefficient. Thus equality of affine values implies equality of forms, and polynomial equality implies form equality. For an affine map, \(F(x)=F(0)+F^{\rm lin}(x)\); expand \(x=\sum_i x_i e_i\) and apply linearity. This proves the claimed representation, including \(n=0\). The argument is valid over finite fields because it concerns affine forms specifically, not arbitrary polynomial functions. \(\square\)

Proper spans, zero-flat witnesses and linear parts

Claim lem:affine-system-linear-algebra. Let \(S\) be a subspace of the coefficient space just defined, and let \(u\) denote the constant unit form. If \(u\notin S\), there exists \(x_0\in K^n\) with \(E_a(x_0)=0\) for every \(a\in S\). If such an \(x_0\) exists and an affine form \(f\) vanishes at every common zero of \(S\), then \(f\in S\).

Consequently, for a finite input family \((g_i)\), a common zero together with vanishing of \(f\) on the common zero set gives constants \((c_i)\) such that

\[ f=\sum_i c_i g_i. \]

If the input family has no common zero, there instead exist constants with \(u=\sum_i c_i g_i\). These are equalities of forms, hence literal equalities of their ordinary polynomials under the linear map above.

For a proper span \(S\), projection to linear coefficients is injective on \(S\). It therefore preserves the dimension of \(S\), and sends every independent family spanning a proper subspace to an independent family of linear parts. Every nonzero \(a\in S\) has \(\deg P_a=1\).

Full proof by finite-coordinate duality. For a linear functional \(L\) on the affine coefficient space, write \(t=L(u)\) and \(v_i=L(u_i)\), where \(u_i\) is the unit vector at the \(i\)-th linear coordinate. Expanding any coefficient vector in the coordinate basis gives

\[ L(a)=a_0t+\sum_i a_iv_i. \]

The vector-space annihilator theorem says that an element lies in a subspace exactly when every functional vanishing on the subspace kills that element. If \(u\notin S\), choose such a functional \(L\) with \(t\ne0\). Set \((x_0)_i=v_i/t\). The displayed identity gives \(E_a(x_0)=L(a)/t=0\) for every \(a\in S\), proving consistency of a proper span.

Next fix a common zero \(x_0\), and suppose \(f\) vanishes at all common zeros. Let \(L\) be any functional annihilating \(S\); its constant value \(t\) may now be zero. Put \(y_i=v_i+(1-t)(x_0)_i\). Direct expansion yields, for every form \(a\),

\[ E_a(y)=L(a)+(1-t)E_a(x_0). \]

For \(a\in S\), both terms on the right vanish. Thus \(y\) is another common zero, so \(E_f(y)=E_f(x_0)=0\), and the identity forces \(L(f)=0\). Since every annihilator kills \(f\), the same vector-space theorem gives \(f\in S\). This argument avoids dividing by \(t\) in the vanishing step and therefore includes direction functionals with \(t=0\).

For a finite family, membership in its span is equivalent to a finite constant linear combination, giving the first certificate. If there is no common zero but \(u\) were outside its span, the consistency argument would supply a contradiction; therefore \(u\) belongs to the span and gives the unit certificate. To prove injectivity of linear-part projection on a proper span, take \(a,b\in S\) with equal linear coefficients and evaluate at the common zero. Their constant coefficients must agree as well, hence \(a=b\). Restricting this injective linear map to \(S\) gives equal domain and image dimensions and preserves linear independence.

Finally, \(\deg P_a\le1\) is already proved. If its degree were zero, the ordinary polynomial would be constant. Its value at the common zero is zero, so it would be the zero polynomial. Injectivity of the coefficient representation would force \(a=0\), contrary to the hypothesis. Thus every nonzero proper input has exact degree one. Empty input families, zero forms, constant forms and zero-dimensional ambient spaces are covered without excluding them implicitly. \(\square\)

The separate representation and system reports preserve fifteen checked theorem types and their transitive axiom audits. The reproduction record includes the source/dependency scope and complete measured outputs.

15 September 2026 — Exact degree-controlled interpolation on two functional rows

Status: full Lean formalization of the indexed two-row interpolation lemma; R11.

Two-row interpolation with ordinary NS certificates

Question and scope. Formalize the indexed two-functional-row interpolation statement, needed for the compact decoder. Relabel its two distinct rows by \(0,1\), retaining the same \(n\) columns in each, and work over \(\mathbb F_2\). The polynomial depends only on these two rows, exactly as in the indexed statement; no outside coefficient variables or unequal state domains are asserted. Let \(U\) contain their Booleanity equations, same-row exclusions, and \(\rho_r-1\), with \(\rho_r=\sum_jX_{rj}\). It contains no cross-row collision equations. For every ordinary polynomial \(P\),

\[ P-\mathcal T(P)\in\mathcal I_{\max\{\deg P,2\}}(U),\qquad \mathcal T(P)=\sum_{j,k}P(e_j,e_k)X_{0j}X_{1k}. \]

The Lean theorem also includes \(n=0\): the sums are empty and the row equations then contain \(-1\). Constants, zero polynomials, and degree-one targets retain the same maximum-with-two bound. The stopping point is this complete local identity; its global decoder application is R12.

Squarefree reduction. By the checked Boolean reduction, \(P-\overline P\) has a Boolean NS certificate through \(\deg P\), and \(\overline P\) has the same values at every Boolean point. Hence \(\mathcal T(\overline P)=\mathcal T(P)\). Write \(\overline P\) as the sum of its original monomial coefficients times squarefree support monomials \(M_S=\prod_{x\in S}X_x\). For each original support, \(|S|\le\deg P\).

Forbidden supports. If \(S\) contains distinct cells \((r,a),(r,b)\) in one row, factor out \(X_{ra}X_{rb}\). The independently checked forbidden-pair certificate puts \(M_S\) in \(\mathcal I_{|S|}(U)\). Its evaluation at every pair of one-hot row states is zero, since two distinct cells of one row cannot both be one. Therefore \(\mathcal T(M_S)=0\), with no cross-row equation used.

Remaining supports. Otherwise the row projection is injective on \(S\), so \(|S|\le2\). An empty support is the constant one; a singleton is one variable; a two-element support has one variable in each row. Direct evaluation gives

\[ \mathcal T(1)=\rho_0\rho_1,\qquad \mathcal T(X_{0j})=X_{0j}\rho_1,\qquad \mathcal T(X_{1k})=\rho_0X_{1k},\qquad \mathcal T(X_{0j}X_{1k})=X_{0j}X_{1k}. \]

The required constant and linear errors have explicit degree-two row-generator certificates:

\[ 1-\rho_0\rho_1=-(\rho_0-1)-\rho_0(\rho_1-1),\qquad X_{0j}-X_{0j}\rho_1=-X_{0j}(\rho_1-1),\qquad X_{1k}-\rho_0X_{1k}=-X_{1k}(\rho_0-1). \]

The bilinear error is zero. Thus every squarefree support error has a certificate through \(\max\{|S|,2\}\). Taking the original coefficient-weighted sum costs at most \(\max\{\deg P,2\}\). Adding the Boolean-reduction certificate proves the displayed identity. This follows the source argument; the generic forbidden-pair dependency was extracted collaboratively rather than duplicating matching-specific machinery.

15 September 2026 — Complete affine coordinates and exact free parametrization

Status: complete Lean formalization of an extracted R07 dependency; fresh-companion degrees and scalar PC cleanup remain.

Obligation and endpoint. Continue R07 from the verified proper-span witnesses by making the paper's affine coordinate completion explicit. The endpoint supplies actual inverse affine coordinates and a parametrization of precisely the common zero set, with the correct number of free coordinates for R15's ordinary restriction bound.

Claim: affine coordinate completion

Let \(K\) be a field and let \((g_i)_{i\in I}\) be linearly independent affine forms on \(K^n\), with the constant one outside their span. There exist an injection \(e:I\hookrightarrow[n]\) and an affine equivalence \(E:K^n\simeq K^n\) satisfying

\[ (E(x))_{e(i)}=g_i(x)\qquad(i\in I,\ x\in K^n). \]

Write \(J=[n]\setminus e(I)\), and let \(z:K^J\to K^n\) extend coordinates by zero at all selected indices \(e(i)\). Then \(P=E^{-1}\circ z\) is an injective affine map with

\[ P(K^J)=\{x\in K^n:g_i(x)=0\text{ for all }i\}. \]

If \(I=[r]\), then \(|J|=n-r\). Thus these are exactly the required free affine coordinates, and both coordinate changes remain ordinary affine maps. The formal completion theorem even permits any index type \(I\); the resulting injection into \([n]\) certifies its finiteness.

Full proof. By the preceding proper-span theorem, the linear coefficient vectors of the \(g_i\) are independent and they have a common zero \(x_0\). Map a coefficient vector \(a\) to the linear functional \(x\mapsto\sum_j a_jx_j\). This map is injective, since evaluation on coordinate unit vectors recovers every coefficient, so the resulting functionals \(L_i\) are independent. Extend them to a basis \((B_j)\) of the dual of \(K^n\), using the vector-space basis-extension theorem. Reindex that basis by \([n]\); the selected functionals occupy distinct positions \(e(i)\), with \(B_{e(i)}=L_i\).

The map \(T:x\mapsto(B_j(x))_{j\in[n]}\) is a linear equivalence: the canonical finite-dimensional identification with the double dual followed by coordinates in the dual basis gives precisely this map. Set \(E(x)=T(x-x_0)\). Since \(g_i(x_0)=0\), its constant coefficient is minus its linear part at \(x_0\). Therefore \((E(x))_{e(i)}=L_i(x-x_0)=g_i(x)\), proving the designated coordinate identity.

Zero-extension \(z\) is linear and injective; composing with \(E^{-1}\) gives an injective affine map \(P\). Every \(P(y)\) satisfies all equations because the selected coordinates of \(E(P(y))=z(y)\) are zero. Conversely, if every \(g_i(x)=0\), the selected coordinates of \(E(x)\) vanish. Its remaining coordinates give \(y\in K^J\) with \(z(y)=E(x)\), hence \(P(y)=x\). Finally the image of an injection from \([r]\) has cardinality \(r\), so its complement in \([n]\) has cardinality \(n-r\). This includes an empty selected family, when all coordinates are free, and \(r=n\), when the zero flat is a single point. \(\square\)

15 September 2026 — The compact decoder preserves every ordinary PC degree

Status: full Lean formalization of the extracted publication decoder lemma and its coordinate dependency; R12.

An explicit linear polynomial left inverse

Question and scope. Formalize the degree-preserving old-base transfer in paper §4, using the decoder certificate proof and the ordinary coordinate argument. The coordinate map below is valid for all \(m,\ell\ge0\); transfer of compact collision axioms requires \(\ell\ge2\), as the source explicitly states. The known \(\ell=1\) exception is not a new gap. Stop at arbitrary ordinary PC consequences, not the downstream transported-filtration or lower-bound claims.

Fix a bijection between \(\{1,\ldots,2^\ell\}\) and binary labels \(z\in\mathbb F_2^\ell\). In ordinary polynomial rings define

\[ \tau(b_{it})=s_{it}=\sum_{z:z_t=1}X_{iz}. \]

The source proves independence by completing these linear forms to coordinates. Here is the full equivalent left-inverse proof used in Lean. For each bit position \(t\), let \(e_t\) be its unit label. Define a second polynomial substitution

\[ \sigma(X_{iz})=\sum_t[\,z=e_t\,]b_{it}. \]

Then \(\sigma(s_{it})=b_{it}\): interchange the two finite sums, and observe that among unit labels only \(e_t\) has its \(t\)-th bit equal to one. Equality on every polynomial generator, together with preservation of constants, gives \(\sigma\tau=\mathrm{id}\) on the entire ordinary polynomial ring. Thus \(\tau\) is injective. Every variable image under either substitution has degree at most one, so the checked substitution degree bound gives

\[ \deg\tau(P)\le\deg P =\deg\sigma\tau(P)\le\deg\tau(P). \]

Consequently \(\deg\tau(P)=\deg P\), including zero and constants. Empty bit sets cause no exception: there are then no bit variables and both maps agree on constants. This coordinate claim is isolated in its own file and index entry because injectivity and degree preservation are used independently of proof-system transfer.

Original axiom-image certificates and arbitrary-consequence replay

For \(\ell\ge2\), let \(\mathcal Q\) contain bit Booleanity and the compact collision polynomials \(E_{ii'}=\prod_t(1+b_{it}+b_{i't})\), \(i<i'\). Let \(\mathcal F^{\mathrm{fun}}\) be the functional unary base on \(m\) rows and \(2^\ell\) columns. The precise transfer is

\[ \mathcal Q\vdash_B P\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal F^{\mathrm{fun}}\vdash_B\tau(P) \qquad\text{for every }B\ge0. \]

There is no extra assumption \(B\ge\ell\). Every eligible source axiom is treated at its own original degree before primitive replay.

Boolean images. Each \(s_{it}\) is a linear ordinary polynomial. At every Boolean assignment, its value lies in \(\mathbb F_2\), so \(s_{it}^2-s_{it}\) vanishes. The checked degree-two Boolean certificate theorem puts it in \(\mathcal I_2(\mathrm{BOOL})\), hence in \(\mathcal I_2(\mathcal F^{\mathrm{fun}})\). Equivalently, expansion in characteristic two gives the source's explicit identity \(s_{it}^2-s_{it}=\sum_{z:z_t=1}(X_{iz}^2-X_{iz})\). The formal proof uses the former already verified reduction. The original polynomial \(b_{it}^2-b_{it}\) has exact degree two, since its quadratic coefficient is nonzero.

Collision images. First use two local rows. The ordinary degree of \(R=\tau(E_{01})\) is at most \(\ell\). At the one-hot states \((e_z,e_w)\), each decoded bit is the corresponding label bit. The factor \(1+z_t+w_t\) is one when those bits agree and zero otherwise. Thus \(R(e_z,e_w)=[z=w]\). The R11 interpolation identity, with \(\ell\ge2\), yields

\[ R-\sum_zX_{0z}X_{1z}\in\mathcal I_\ell(U). \]

Each remaining summand is a degree-two column-exclusion generator, so \(R\in\mathcal I_\ell(\mathcal F^{\mathrm{fun}}_{2,2^\ell})\). Relabel these local rows injectively as any distinct \(i,i'\). This substitution maps each Boolean, row-sum, same-row, and same-column generator into the corresponding global functional generator. It does not increase ordinary degree. Mapping each legal NS product separately therefore preserves its original degree budget, proving \(\tau(E_{ii'})\in\mathcal I_\ell(\mathcal F^{\mathrm{fun}})\).

Original collision degree. For distinct \(i,i'\), every factor \(1+b_{it}+b_{i't}\) has degree exactly one: the coefficient of \(b_{it}\) is one, and its degree is at most one. The ordinary polynomial ring over a field is a domain, so these nonzero factors multiply with additive total degree. Therefore \(\deg E_{ii'}=\ell\). This proof includes the empty product degree convention, although the transfer theorem still requires \(\ell\ge2\).

Primitive replay. A source Boolean axiom eligible at ceiling \(B\) has \(2\le B\), and a source collision axiom eligible there has \(\ell\le B\), by the exact degrees just proved. Their NS image certificates thus lie within \(B\), and the checked NS-to-PC inclusion supplies actual PC image proofs. Apply weighted substitution with weight one and variable-image bound one. Its primitive multiplication argument uses the actual predecessor degree, so the ceiling remains \(B\) throughout. This proves the stated transfer for every target polynomial and every original proof ceiling.
