15 September 2026 — A binary row cube isolates the selected coefficient

Status: verified independent coefficient-isolation dependency for R14; board/PC separation remains separate.

Exact coefficient isolation with unrestricted outside images

Statement and scope. Let \(P\in\mathcal L_k\) be an ordinary binary row-linear polynomial. Choose a row monomial \(x\), with selected row set \(S\), one bit direction \(d_i\) in each selected row, and \(t=|S|\), such that \(\deg P\le t\). Choose any base label \(c_i\) for each \(i\in S\). For every binary choice \(\varepsilon:S\to\mathbb F_2\), let \(\Phi_\varepsilon\) substitute old bit variables by ordinary polynomials in an arbitrary variable type \(W\). On selected rows require

\[ \Phi_\varepsilon(b_{ia})= \bigl(c_i+\varepsilon_i e_{d_i}\bigr)_a, \]

as a constant polynomial; outside \(S\), require only that each variable image is independent of \(\varepsilon\). There is no degree bound on those outside images, no finiteness condition on \(W\), and no disjoint-pair, packing, nonzero, or \(\ell\ge2\) assumption. Then

\[ \sum_{\varepsilon:S\to\mathbb F_2}\Phi_\varepsilon(P) =\operatorname{C}\!\left([x]P\right). \]

This isolates the coefficient used in the source cube-separation argument, before its board-specific realization. The weaker degree bound allows \(\deg P<t\), in which case the coefficient and sum are zero.

Proof. Expand \(P\) over its actual monomial support. Row-linearity represents each term as \(c_y\prod_{i\in T}b_{i,a_i}\), with one bit per occupied row and \(|T|\le\deg P\le|S|\). If a selected row \(r\in S\) is absent from \(T\), flip only \(\varepsilon_r\). Every factor is unchanged: other selected-row images depend only on their own choice, and outside images are choice-independent by hypothesis. Pairing each cube assignment with this fixed-point-free involution cancels the sum in characteristic two. Such a term cannot be the selected monomial.

Otherwise \(S\subseteq T\). The cardinality bound forces \(T=S\), so no outside polynomial factor remains. Distributing the independent binary sums over the product yields

\[ c_y\prod_{i\in S}\left((c_i)_{a_i}+(c_i+e_{d_i})_{a_i}\right) =c_y\prod_{i\in S}[a_i=d_i]. \]

It equals \(c_y\) exactly when every chosen bit agrees with the selected monomial, and zero otherwise. The checked injectivity of the row-monomial exponent representation identifies this condition with equality to \(x\). Summing the original coefficients therefore gives exactly \([x]P\). If \(S\) is empty, the degree bound makes \(P\) constant, the cube has one assignment, and the empty product is one; the same argument applies.

Verification. RowCubeCoefficientIsolation.lean and its verification report give the exact generic theorem. The scope map separates it from full R14. Previously proved row-monomial support, cardinality, degree, and injectivity facts were exposed in a separate API checkpoint without changing their proofs; its verification is included in this cycle. Retries concerned dependent indices and equivalent finite cube enumerations, not a mathematical gap. Process assessment: the isolated generic coefficient theorem lets the board-specific worker supply only the concrete selected/outside substitution identities. No additional audit or optional generalization was performed after verification passed.

2026-09-15 — Concrete row-cube restrictions and residual NS transport

Status: Lean-verified supporting claim. This discharges the concrete generator-image obligation for R14; coefficient isolation and final separation are separate.

Claim: concrete residual restriction

Let \(S\subseteq[m]\), \(F\subseteq[N]\), and let \(p_i(0),p_i(1)\in F\) for \(i\in S\). Assume every choice \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb F_2^S\) gives an injective assignment \(i\mapsto p_i(\varepsilon_i)\). Map selected-row variables by \(x_{ij}\mapsto[ j=p_i(\varepsilon_i)]\); map remaining rows and columns outside \(F\) to the corresponding variables of the \((m-|S|)\times(N-|F|)\) board, and all other variables to zero. Write this algebra map as \(\rho_\varepsilon\), and \(\Delta=\sum_\varepsilon\rho_\varepsilon\). Then

\[\deg\Delta P\le\deg P-|S|,\qquad \Delta(\mathrm{NS}_B(\mathrm{fPHP}_{m,N}))\subseteq \mathrm{NS}_{B-|S|}(\mathrm{fPHP}_{m-|S|,N-|F|}),\]

where subtraction is truncated at zero. Every source generator has an image independent of the cube choice, equal to zero or an actual residual generator.

Proof. A Boolean generator at a selected cell evaluates to zero; at a retained cell it is precisely its residual Boolean generator, and at a deleted cell it is zero. A selected row sum is one minus one. An unselected row sum retains exactly the complement of \(F\), hence becomes its residual row equation. For a collision generator, two nonzero selected cells cannot violate a row or column exclusion: the former would be the same chosen cell, and the latter contradicts injectivity. A selected and an unselected retained cell cannot collide in a column because their column sets are disjoint. Two retained cells preserve distinctness and every common row or column under the complement bijections. Any remaining collision product contains a zero factor. This proves the complete fixed-image assertion for the original functional-unary encoding, including both sorts of exclusions.

Apply the verified cube degree-drop lemma: unselected images have degree at most one, and selected images are constants depending only on their own row choice. If a generator has fixed image \(g\), then \(\Delta(qf)=(\Delta q)g\). The actual-degree argument in that lemma gives the displayed NS budget, including zero products and degrees below \(|S|\). No generator-image hypothesis remains unproved in this application.

For binary labels \(N=2^\ell\), the compact decoder sends a bit \((i,t)\) to the sum of columns whose label has bit \(t\) equal to one. At a selected row, exactly its chosen column survives, so

\[\rho_\varepsilon(\tau(z_{it}))= \operatorname{bit}_t(p_i(\varepsilon_i)).\]

At every other row the image is independent of \(\varepsilon\). Algebra-map composition proves the same substitution identity for all polynomials, rather than only coordinates. These are exactly the hypotheses needed by the separate coefficient-isolation lemma. Finally the disjoint coordinate pairs construct the stipulated data with \(|F|=2|S|\): disjointness makes every endpoint choice injective. All complement relabelings are actual finite equivalences, not just cardinality correspondences.

2026-09-15 — Full cube/residual dual separation in Lean

Status: The entire indexed claim lem:cube-residual-dual-separation is Lean-verified with its dependencies, using the alternative operator proof below. The row count is generalized to arbitrary \(m\); the paper's \(m=2^\ell+1\) follows immediately.

Exact statement and proof

Set \(n=2^\ell\), with \(\ell\ge2\), \(1\le k\le B\), \(4(k-1)<n\), and \(2B-1\le n\). Let \(P\ne0\) belong to the degree-at-most-\(k\) row-linear bit space: its monomials contain at most one bit from each row. Then there is a binary linear functional \(\mu\) on all unary polynomials satisfying

\[\mu(\mathrm{PC}_B(\mathrm{fPHP}_{m,n}))=0, \qquad \mu(\tau P)=1.\]

Moreover \(\mu(1)=0\) when \(\deg P>0\), and \(\mu(1)=1\) when \(\deg P=0\). Consequently \(\tau P\notin\mathrm{PC}_B(\mathrm{fPHP}_{m,n})\) and \(P\notin\mathrm{PC}_B(\mathrm{compactBitPHP}_{m,\ell})\). These are memberships in the actual bounded PC derivation spaces, not an assumed abstract ideal or functional interface.

Construction. Choose a nonzero top-degree coefficient of \(P\), at a row monomial with selected rows \(S\), \(|S|=t=\deg P\le k\), and bit direction \(a_i\) in row \(i\). The verified packing lemma supplies pairwise disjoint coordinate lines \(\{c_i,c_i+e_{a_i}\}\). Let \(F\) be their union, so \(|F|=2t\). Their cube choices define the concrete restrictions \(\rho_\varepsilon\) onto the residual \((m-t)\times(n-2t)\) board, and put \(\Delta=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\mathbb F_2^S}\rho_\varepsilon\).

The parameter ledger is essential. Since \(n\) is divisible by four, \(4(k-1)<n\) implies \(4k\le n\), so \(n-2t\ge1\). Also

\[n-2t\ge 2(B-t)-1.\]

The latter includes the boundary \(t=B\), where its right side is interpreted as the nonnegative truncated bound zero. These inequalities, including \(t=0\) and \(t=1\), are already proved in cube_residual_parameters. The verified matching extension theorem therefore provides a residual functional \(L\), normalized by \(L(1)=1\), annihilating residual NS through \(B-t\). Its arbitrary-row-count scope imposes no additional condition on \(m-t\).

Define \(\mu=L\circ\Delta\). The concrete restriction theorem proves, for every original generator, a cube-independent image equal to zero or a residual generator. Hence \(\Delta\) carries original NS through \(B\) into residual NS through \(B-t\). In detail, if a generator has fixed image \(g\), then \(\Delta(qf)=(\Delta q)g\); the cube cancels all terms missing a selected row and lowers the actual multiplier degree by \(t\). The previously checked ordinary-degree ledger bounds the resulting product by \(B-t\). Thus \(\mu\) annihilates original NS through \(B\), and the proved stable-filtration identity \(\mathrm{PC}_B=\mathrm{NS}_B\) makes it annihilate actual PC.

On a selected bit coordinate, \(\rho_\varepsilon\tau\) evaluates to the corresponding bit of \(c_i+\varepsilon_i e_{a_i}\); outside \(S\), it is independent of \(\varepsilon\). The verified coefficient-isolation identity now gives

\[\Delta(\tau P)=\operatorname{coeff}_{\prod_{i\in S}z_{i,a_i}}P=1.\]

For clarity, its cancellation has no hidden degree hypothesis on the outside images: a row-linear monomial missing a selected row cancels in that cube coordinate. A surviving monomial must use all \(t\) selected rows; the top-degree bound allows no other row. Multiplying the coordinate bit differences leaves one precisely for the chosen directions and zero otherwise. A nonzero binary coefficient is one, so \(\mu(\tau P)=L(1)=1\). This is an operator proof of the same separation, replacing the original explicit tensor-of-moments presentation.

If \(t>0\), cube cancellation gives \(\Delta1=0\), yielding the claimed zero normalization. If \(t=0\), the nonzero binary polynomial is the constant one, so the already proved separator value yields \(\mu(1)=1\). No constant case was omitted. Finally, membership of \(\tau P\) in unary PC would contradict its functional value. Membership of \(P\) in compact-bit PC would imply unary membership by the verified decoder PC transfer, giving the second exclusion.

15 September 2026 — The affine-family exclusion is formally assembled

Status: full R17 formalization, including finite parameters and polynomial-inventory/polylogarithmic-degree exclusion; the publication size theorem remains R25.

Finite-parameter exclusion

Let \(m>0\), \(\ell\ge2\), \(h=3\ell\), and let a finite family of affine input tuples over \(\mathbb F_2\) extend the actual compact bit base \(\mathcal Q\). Retain every companion and every Boolean domain equation. Suppose \(M,k\ge1\), \(k\le m\), \(m\log(4M)\le k^2\), \(D\ge2h+1\), \(4(k-1)<2^\ell\), and \(2k(D+1)-1\le2^\ell\). If at most \(M\) high-rank blocks have proper spans, there is no ordinary-PC refutation through \(D\). Counting all proper blocks suffices. In particular the original choice \(k=\lceil\sqrt{m\log(4M)}\rceil\) recovers the indexed audit's finite interface.

Proof. Apply the common-kernel theorem to obtain a nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\). For each block of rank greater than \(h(k+1)\), it supplies either a constant unit-span witness or a literal identity \(f=\sum_i a_i g_i\), \(\deg a_i\le k-1\). The verified removal theorem with unit blocks consequently turns a hypothetical complete-family refutation into \(\mathcal Q\vdash_{k(D+1)}f\). The cube separator forbids precisely this consequence for nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\). Here \(k\le k(D+1)\), and the displayed board hypotheses are exactly the separator's hypotheses. This is a contradiction. Unit and zero spans therefore require no implicit proper-family assumption or additional global pruning argument. The proof works for arbitrary \(m\), specializing to \(m=2^\ell+1\) in the publication.

A uniform parameter proof for polynomial inventories

The asymptotic proof uses a convenient larger parameter instead of repeating the exact ceiling-of-square-root-log argument. For fixed natural numbers \(a,A,d\), put \(n=2^\ell\), \(t=\ell+1\), \(q=\sqrt2\), and \(k=\lceil tq^\ell\rceil\). For sufficiently large \(\ell\), this parameter has \(1\le k\le n+1\), satisfies the square condition for \(M=A2^{a\ell}+1\), and leaves room for every \(D\le At^d\):

\[ (n+1)\log(4M)\le k^2,\qquad 4(k-1)<n,\qquad 2k(At^d+1)-1\le n. \]

Full parameter argument. Since \(q>1\), \(1\le q^\ell\), and the ceiling inequality gives \(tq^\ell\le k\le2tq^\ell\). Also \(M\le(A+1)2^{a\ell}\), so \(\log(4M)\le C+a\ell\), where \(C=\log(4(A+1))\); this uses \(\log2\le1\). Eventually \(\ell\ge2a\) and \(\ell\ge C\), whence \(2\log(4M)\le t^2\). As \(n+1\le2n\) and \(q^{2\ell}=n\), we obtain \((n+1)\log(4M)\le nt^2\le k^2\).

For the remaining room, \(At^d+1\le(A+1)t^d\), and therefore \(4k(At^d+1)\le8(A+1)t^{d+1}q^\ell\). The checked standard geometric-growth limit \(t^e/q^\ell\to0\), for every fixed \(e\), makes the latter strictly smaller than \(q^{2\ell}=n\) eventually. The shifted limit follows from the ordinary \(\ell^e/q^\ell\to0\) limit at \(\ell+1\), multiplying by \(q\). This single strict inequality gives both the packing and degree-room conditions above. The Lean lemma proves these eventual inequalities directly, not as an assumed asymptotic estimate.

For the full indexed consequence, let the proper-block count be at most \(A2^{a\ell}+1\), and let the proposed degree be \(D\le A(\ell+1)^d\). Enlarge it to \(D'=\max(D,6\ell+1)\). Then \(D'\le(A+7)(\ell+1)^{d+1}\). Apply the parameter lemma with \(A+7,d+1\), and apply the finite theorem to this raised ceiling. A degree-\(D\) refutation would also be a degree-\(D'\) refutation, contradiction. Natural exponents and constants here cover any fixed polynomial inventory and polylogarithmic degree after increasing those bounds; \(\ell=\log_2 n\). No publication-size conclusion is claimed until R25 composes this with the actual proof translation.

15 September 2026 — The publication's bit-PHP lower bound is formally proved

Status: complete R25 Lean formalization of the actual usual-CNF superpolynomial node lower bound; all H01–H13 and R01–R25 route obligations are complete.

Exact publication theorem

For every real \(K>0\), there is a bit-length threshold \(L\) such that, for every \(\ell\ge L\), every refutation of the usual bit-PHP CNF with \(n=2^\ell\) holes and \(m=n+1\) pigeons in the formal affine DAG calculus has more than \(n^K\) nodes. The actual initial clauses and empty final clause are part of the statement. The calculus includes both recorded rule conventions, retains DAG sharing, and imposes no height restriction.

Full proof. Fix \(K>0\), and choose the natural exponent \(a=\max(\lceil K\rceil,2)\). Apply the verified asymptotic affine-family exclusion with parameters \(a,13,1\), taking the bit length large enough also to have \(\ell\ge2\). Suppose a refutation has \(S\le n^K\) nodes. Since \(n\ge1\) and \(K\le a\), we have \(S\le n^a\).

The actual usual-CNF transfer, at accuracy \(h=3\ell\), constructs one complete affine registry with

\[ N\le3S+\binom{n+1}{2},\qquad D=\max(2h+\ell,4h+1)=12\ell+1. \]

It supplies an actual ordinary-PC derivation of one through \(D\) from that registry over the compact base, including all companion and Boolean domain axioms. The checked registry/family identity identifies this system with the exact input of the exclusion theorem; no generic initial-value assumption remains.

For the inventory estimate, \(\binom{n+1}{2}\le(n+1)^2\le4n^2\le4n^a\), hence

\[ N\le7n^a\le13n^a+1=13\,2^{a\ell}+1, \qquad D=12\ell+1\le13(\ell+1). \]

The number of proper blocks is at most \(N\). These are precisely the inventory and degree bounds excluded by R17 at \(a,13,1\). The produced refutation is therefore impossible. Thus \(S>n^K\), with one threshold valid for every proof at every sufficiently large bit length. The generous constant thirteen simplifies this final comparison without changing the claimed lower bound. All analytic growth work is reused from R17; it is not assumed anew here.

15 September 2026 — Mixed comparisons prevent a depth-only boundary bound

Status: working all-prime boundary and old-degree obstruction for actual mixed OR interfaces; no new PHP lower bound or global proof-support theorem. Cycle 160.

Question and stopping point. The first remaining-route obligation needs a proof-specific general step. The preceding component compression supplies a conditional step, but leaves its exposed boundary uncontrolled. This cycle tests whether the actual compiler's fixed depth makes that boundary small. A family of mixed OR interfaces disproves that inference. The local interpolation theorem remains valid under its stated isolation condition.

1. A one-level source with mixed prefix comparisons

Fix a prime \(p\), accuracy \(h\ge1\), and \(r\ge2\) old Boolean variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_r\). For \(2\le j\le r\), take independent complete ENS blocks on the affine input tuples \((x_1,\ldots,x_j)\):

\[ P_j=\prod_{u=1}^h\left(1-\sum_{i=1}^j r_{j,u,i}x_i\right), \qquad E_{j,i}=x_iP_j,\qquad w=2h. \]

Keep all own equations \(r_{j,u,i}^p-r_{j,u,i}\) and old Booleanity. Put \(P_1=1-x_1\) as a virtual literal value, without adding a unary OR block. All genuine blocks have original product degree \(w\), input degree one, and companion degree \(w+1\). The input inventory is \(O(r^2)\), and the coefficient inventory is \(O(hr^2)\).

The actual OR template, splitting the prefix tuple at its last input, supplies

\[ R_2=P_2-(1-x_1)(1-x_2),\qquad R_j=P_j-P_{j-1}(1-x_j)\quad(3\le j\le r). \tag{MIX-prefix} \]

These are source comparison targets, not equations invented by treating an arbitrary polynomial as an ENS value. In the binary compiler, a flat disjunction and a literal give exactly the proper-OR/non-OR split in \(R_j\). Each required split has bounded syntactic depth; its flattened input tuple bypasses the same-level OR child. Listing all prefixes does not require a formula nested to depth \(r\). The algebraic identities below hold over every prime; no new odd-prime full Frege compiler is asserted.

For clarity, these local interfaces are not claimed to be indispensable parts of a short PHP proof. They test a bound inferred from compiler templates and depth alone. A proof-specific deletion or cancellation argument would need additional information from the whole certificate.

2. Complete ordinary NS witnesses keep constant source ceilings

Write the literal prefix identity \(1-P_j=\sum_{i\le j}U_{j,i}x_i\), where \(\deg U_{j,i}\le w-1\). For \(j\ge3\), the actual mixed comparison has the certificate

\[ \begin{aligned} R_j={}&\sum_{i

Verification. The first two terms before expansion equal \(P_j(1-P_{j-1})+P_{j-1}x_jP_j\). The remaining terms equal \(-(1-P_j)P_{j-1}(1-x_j)\), using \(x_j(1-x_j)=-(x_j^2-x_j)\). Their sum is \(R_j\). The first sum costs at most \(2w\); each other generator multiple costs at most \(2w+1=4h+1\). These are ordinary NS costs, charging each original generator multiple.

At \(j=2\), put \(a_i=1-x_i\). The two-singleton instance is

\[ R_2=E_{2,1}+a_1E_{2,2} +U_{2,1}a_2(x_1^2-x_1) +U_{2,2}a_1(x_2^2-x_2). \tag{MIX-base} \]

The same prefix expansion verifies it through \(w+2\le2w+1\). All coefficient-field equations remain present, although these particular witnesses do not need them. Thus the number of mixed comparisons can grow while their structural level and supplied witness ceilings stay fixed at a chosen \(h\).

3. Boundary-only reconstruction must retain every prefix

Let \(K\subseteq\{2,\ldots,r\}\), and let \(\Gamma_K\) contain old Booleanity and precisely the complete original blocks \(P_i\), \(i\in K\). Retained products are fixed. For every omitted index \(j\), propose a value depending only on the retained product values. Allow an arbitrary function of those values; the obstruction does not rely on a polynomial degree bound. Keep the old literal value \(v_1=1-x_1\).

Proposition. If every reconstructed relation \(v_j-v_{j-1}(1-x_j)\) vanishes on all models of \(\Gamma_K\), then \(K=\{2,\ldots,r\}\). In particular, ordinary NS witnesses for all reconstructed ports cannot exist over a smaller \(\Gamma_K\) under this replacement rule.

Proof. Every old Boolean assignment extends to a model of \(\Gamma_K\). A retained prefix with all inputs zero has product one. Otherwise choose a first-row coefficient selecting a nonzero input and set the other coefficients to zero, making its product zero. All coefficients lie in \(\mathbb F_p\), so their field equations hold. Hence, on every such model,

\[ P_i=N_i(x):=\prod_{t=1}^i(1-x_t). \]

The reconstructed relations, starting with \(v_1=1-x_1\), force \(v_j=N_j(x)\) by induction. Suppose an index \(j\ge2\) is omitted. Compare the old points \(e_j\) and \(e_{j+1}\), using the zero point instead of \(e_{r+1}\) when \(j=r\). Every retained prefix has the same value at these two points: the only prefix indicator that changes is \(N_j\). Any function of the retained product values therefore agrees at the two points, but the required \(v_j\) is zero at the first and one at the second. This contradiction proves the claim.

The controls use complete satisfiable systems, including actual coefficient fields. Adding Booleanity of virtual values cannot repair the contradiction: the recurrence already forces those values to be Boolean.

4. Allowing old variables gives an explicit tradeoff

Now let omitted values be formal polynomials \(V_j(x,Z_K)\), still fixing \(V_i=Z_i\) for retained \(i\), and \(V_1=1-x_1\). Here \(\deg_x\) counts powers of old variables only, treating the formal boundary names as parameters. Suppose all reconstructed ports vanish on every model of \(\Gamma_K\).

Working degree bound. If \(j\notin K\) and \(a\) is the largest retained index below \(j\), or zero if none exists, then

\[ \deg_x V_j\ge j-a. \tag{MIX-gap} \]

Consequently, if every omitted value has old-variable degree at most \(\delta\), with \(\delta\ge1\), and \(k=|K|\), then

\[ r\le k+(k+1)\delta, \qquad k\ge\frac{r-\delta}{\delta+1}. \tag{MIX-tradeoff} \]

Proof. Fix \(x_1,\ldots,x_a\) to zero, and leave \(x_{a+1},\ldots,x_j\) free. If there is a next retained index \(b>j\), fix \(x_b=1\); fix all other coordinates to zero. Every retained prefix at or below \(a\) now has value one, and every retained prefix at or above \(b\) has value zero, independently of the free coordinates. There are no retained indices between them.

This is a complete cube of retained-system models with constant coefficient choices: set all coefficients to zero in blocks at or below \(a\), and in each block at or above \(b\) set its first-row coefficient on \(x_b\) to one and all others to zero. Every retained companion and field equation holds throughout the cube. If no next retained index exists, the second group is empty.

After this restriction the boundary names are constants. The reconstructed recurrence forces \(V_j\) to agree on the cube with \(\prod_{t=a+1}^j(1-x_t)\). Its unique multilinear representative has degree \(j-a\) over every field, while Boolean reduction cannot increase degree. This proves (MIX-gap). Between successive retained indices, every run of omitted indices therefore has length at most \(\delta\). The same holds before the first and after the last retained index. The possible initial literal index 1 has degree one and is covered by \(\delta\ge1\). There are at most \(k+1\) runs and \(k\) retained indices, proving (MIX-tradeoff).

This lower bound concerns old-variable dependence even if boundary-name degree is unrestricted. It also applies to an alleged costed reconstruction whose value bounds imply the displayed old-degree bound. It is not, by itself, the accumulated degree bound for an entire multilevel source transformation.

5. What this audit rules out and what it leaves open

The preceding pure comparison interpolation chose a comparison character separately on each feasible boundary type. Mixed ports impose additional agreement with the current old input. Two old assignments with the same boundary type can require different internal values, as the explicit models show. They cannot be assigned one common character while preserving those ports. The isolation hypothesis correctly excludes this case; the new result does not retract it.

A non-OR child is a Boolean parameter of the singleton template, but that does not make a genuine parent or proper-OR child into a Boolean-only parameter. The mixed certificate still uses their original companions. Thus fixed source depth and cheap local witnesses do not imply a small exposed boundary. Compared with the earlier unchanged-comparison support obstruction and prescribed-product degree bound, the present argument allows arbitrary boundary-value replacements and quantifies the old dependence needed to repair them.

Main-route status. No small-boundary theorem for the actual PHP certificate was obtained. A useful application must establish that its relevant mixed interfaces can be removed or reconstructed using the old PHP equations and the whole costed identity. The satisfiable Boolean-domain models above do not rule out PHP-relative certificates, changing the chosen modular proof, additional retained source information, or global cancellation. In particular they establish no lower bound on indispensable support in every short PHP proof.

Evidence and process. The checks here are the displayed exact prefix expansions and parameterized complete model families; no numerical job or old test suite was run. The audit record preserves source locators and review scope. Testing the actual mixed-child interfaces before refining the conditional compression found its missing coverage immediately; the existing task-selection guidance already requires this, so no additional framework rule is needed.

15 September 2026 — Nonzero masks help locally, but the first application was already covered

Status: reuse audit with an explicit ordinary NS mask calculation; no new source coverage or Frege lower bound. Cycle 161.

Question. Can a mixed comparison be compressed after multiplication by its actual outer cofactor, even when its unweighted version needs a retained boundary? This tests the first remaining-route obligation at the level of the whole costed source identity. Nonzero masking can remove a local obstruction, but the concrete axiom-frame application below is already covered by the earlier virtual-interface argument.

1. The nonzero mask calculation

Use a mixed prefix port \(H=c-ab\), with \(a=P_{j-1}\), \(c=P_j\), \(b=1-x_j\), and \(j\ge3\). Both genuine products have weight \(w=2h\). Suppose its outer coefficient contains \(1-a\), and replace the internal value \(c\) by zero while keeping \(a\) genuine. In the formal product-value ring,

\[ (1-a)\bigl(0-ab\bigr)=b(a^2-a). \tag{MASK-mixed} \]

The mask \(1-a\) is nonzero. The right-hand side has an ordinary NS witness through \(2w+1\), using the complete retained block's prefix certificate for \(a^2-a\). In the binary source its domain-only Booleanity witness is also available. The supplied mixed port originally costs \(2w+1\), and its outer mask costs at most \(w\), so the replacement fits the carried ceiling \(3w+1\). An additional cofactor multiplies both budgets in the usual way.

Thus an unweighted need for a genuine product does not imply that the same product is needed by every weighted occurrence. This is the existing costed-module substitution principle applied to a Booleanity identity. It supplies neither a raw coefficient substitution for the deleted block nor permission to ignore its other uses. Later inputs and every surviving source use must share one consistent replacement.

2. The actual tautology-frame application is reuse

Consider the source frame \(\neg A\vee(A\vee B)\), with values \(a\) for \(A\), \(b\) for \(B\), \(c\) for the inner disjunction, and \(t\) for the whole frame. Its two OR targets are

\[ H_{\rm inner}=c-ab,\qquad H_{\rm outer}=t-(1-a)c. \]

The exact frame identity is

\[ t=H_{\rm outer}+(1-a)H_{\rm inner}-b(a^2-a). \tag{MASK-frame} \]

This produces precisely the nonzero mask in (MASK-mixed), rather than assigning an arbitrary coefficient to a source port. With virtual values \(c=t=0\), the outer target vanishes, and the remaining two terms cancel. Each required weighted inner image has the Booleanity certificate just described.

However, the earlier pure-disjunct virtual-interface application already treats \(A\vee\neg A\vee C\) by using \(A\)'s unit interface and ignoring the irrelevant disjunct root. The ordinary NS frame construction already provides its selector-valued coefficients and degree accounting. The displayed calculation makes the mask explicit; it does not establish a new class of PHP source proofs to which elimination applies.

3. The unresolved condition is still global

The unweighted prefix obstruction remains valid. It does not cover cofactor-masked uses, as (MASK-mixed) illustrates. Conversely, one successful mask does not show that every essential mixed comparison in a hypothetical short PHP proof has such a mask, or that the same choices remain compatible across its occurrences, later inputs, and old boundary.

Independent choices for individual summands do not preserve a polynomial identity: even the cancellation \(Z-Z=0\) is lost if its two occurrences are evaluated differently. A legitimate construction must act consistently on the old-target identity, or supply a linear functional satisfying its joint equations. The existing certificate-support refinement addresses this in its stated first mixed degree band; it does not cover the full source merely because its conclusion is proof-specific. The relative interfaces already allow old PHP residuals, but do not provide the missing witnesses.

Outcome. This attempt obtained no new coverage of the general source. Further local mask identities would refine an already available mechanism while leaving its main hypothesis unproved. The next task returns to construction of a source-dependent joint functional for the actual cofactor family, with the complete coupled equations and original witness costs as constraints. An equivalent reformulation alone will not discharge that obligation.

15 September 2026 — A joint extension needs correlations even for literal copies

Status: working obstruction to a scalar-component extension ansatz, with an explicit correlated extension for a complete affine copy source; the general source-extension problem remains open. Cycle 162.

Question. The first remaining-route obligation is to construct a normalized joint functional for the source. The active-window reduction already fills unused moments after the queried components agree. A tempting first construction is to make each selector component a scalar multiple of one old matching functional. The following test rules this out even when the old functional is freely chosen and the source itself has an immediate complete elimination.

1. Complete copy blocks and their carried costs

Fix a prime \(p\), \(\ell\ge2\), \(n=2^\ell\), \(m=n+1\), and \(\gamma=(p-1)\ell\). Use the compact bit-PHP base \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\), with Boolean bits \(b_{it}\) and collision polynomials

\[ E_{ii'}=\prod_{t=1}^{\ell} \left[1-(b_{it}-b_{i't})^{p-1}\right]. \]

For every bit \(b=b_{it}\), introduce a complete accuracy-\(h\) ENS block on the two identical inputs \(1-b,1-b\). Its product \(P_{it}\) has weight \(w=2h\), and it keeps both companions and every own coefficient-field equation. In the binary source this is the duplicate-literal OR template, not an artificial unary OR occurrence. Optional duplicate-input reduction gives the equivalent one-input notation.

Write \(1-P=U(1-b)\) for the combined literal prefix, with \(\deg U\le w-1\), and \(E=(1-b)P\) for either companion. Then

\[ P-b=E+U(b^2-b). \tag{COPY-link} \]

This is an ordinary NS witness through \(w+1\). Give the formal copy module \(Z_{it}-b_{it}\) a carried cost \(\nu\ge w+1\); using the existing conservative gate ceiling \(\nu=3w\) is permitted. The argument below uses that declared cost, not the smaller formal degree of the relation. The local identities hold over every prime; the full source compiler remains the previously audited binary one.

2. Scalar copies of one old functional cannot suffice

Let \(\lambda\) be a normalized ordinary degree-\(D\) functional for \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\), and let \(\Lambda\) extend it to the formal source with selector weights \(w\). Assume

\[ D\ge\nu+\max(1,\gamma-1). \tag{COPY-budget} \]

The proposed scalar-component ansatz would choose constants \(c_{it}\) such that, even just on the queried old window,

\[ \Lambda(q(b)Z_{it})=c_{it}\lambda(q(b)) \quad\text{for every }\deg q\le D-\nu. \tag{COPY-scalar} \]

Working obstruction. No choice of the old normalized \(\lambda\), the constants \(c_{it}\), or the higher selector components can make (COPY-scalar) compatible with every legal copy-module multiple. This holds over any extension field of characteristic \(p\) as well.

Proof. The copy equations and (COPY-scalar) give

\[ \lambda(qb_{it})=c_{it}\lambda(q) \quad(\deg q\le D-\nu). \tag{COPY-eigen} \]

Taking \(q=1\) gives \(\lambda(b_{it})=c_{it}\). Taking \(q=b_{it}\), and using old Booleanity, gives \(c_{it}^2=c_{it}\). Thus every \(c_{it}\) is zero or one, without a positivity assumption. The budget also allows \(q\) through degree \(\gamma-1\). Induction on monomial degree in (COPY-eigen) therefore gives

\[ \lambda(f(b))=f(c) \qquad\text{for all }\deg f\le\gamma. \]

The \(n+1\) vectors \(c_i\in\{0,1\}^{\ell}\) cannot all be distinct. For an equal pair \(i,i'\), the old collision polynomial satisfies \(E_{ii'}(c)=1\). The displayed equality then gives \(\lambda(E_{ii'})=1\), contrary to its required value zero. Higher selector moments cannot repair this contradiction because only the single-selector active components were used.

The obstruction is not a lack of old designs. For \(n\ge2D-1\), normalized old designs in this range follow from the functional matching theorem and the affine bit decoder, which preserves the Boolean and collision witness costs. In particular, fixed \(h\) or polylogarithmic \(h\) gives arbitrarily large parameters satisfying both the budget and old existence conditions.

3. The source has a direct correlated extension

For each copy block, set one coefficient in its first row to one and every other coefficient to zero. The product becomes \(P_{it}=b_{it}\), every own field equation vanishes, and each companion becomes \((1-b_{it})b_{it}\), an old Boolean consequence through degree two. This complete constant coefficient map does not increase any original degree budget.

Consequently every normalized old degree-\(D\) functional extends to the complete concrete copy source by pullback. In the formal product notation its moments are

\[ \Lambda(q(b)Z_U) =\lambda\left(q(b)\prod_{(i,t)\in U}b_{it}\right). \tag{COPY-correlated} \]

The right-hand side is defined whenever the original weighted moment is: \(\deg q+|U|\le\deg q+w|U|\le D\). Copy modules vanish after this substitution, old generator multiples retain their budgets, and selector Booleanity pulls back to old Booleanity. The underlying coefficient map also checks every original companion and field equation, so this is not a construction that tests only the formal link polynomials.

These components are conditioned old functionals, rather than scalar copies of the same functional. A first moment can be zero while the corresponding functional on nonconstant queries is nonzero. This agrees with the earlier zero-mean versus zero-functional warning and does not require universal degree-extension sections commuting with conditioning.

4. Consequence for the current construction attempt

The general joint extension was not constructed. The rejected ansatz would have removed precisely the old/selector correlations needed even by a harmless affine source. The successful copy pullback is a control and a reuse of complete substitution; it does not solve the higher-level input problem. A correlated construction must still satisfy the source equations jointly, including the active old matching indices and carried cofactor costs.

The universal-section obstruction does not rule out source-dependent correlated components, while the factorial-family counterexample prevents ignoring source size. Both remain checks on the next candidate. A common polynomial-density representation might organize correlations, but an invertible reparameterization alone would leave source feasibility unchanged and would not count as a solution.

Evidence and process assessment. Verification consists of the exact link identity, the scalar-component contradiction, and the full constant coefficient map; no numerical run was needed. The audit record preserves the source locators and review scope. Testing the ansatz on a completely eliminable source identified its lost correlations before any large linear-system computation; the remaining task is a correlated construction with an actual source-size bound.

15 September 2026 — A common density representation, and a failed projection rule

Status: working characteristic-two moment-pairing and density-representation lemmas; exact finite counterexample to the orthogonal-unit projection recipe. Joint source feasibility remains open. Cycle 163.

Question. After the scalar-component obstruction, can polynomial densities organize the necessary old/selector correlations? Yes: one suitably chosen old functional can represent all active components with bounded old-degree densities. This solves a representation problem. A natural rule for choosing those densities, tested below on an actual mixed OR port, fails even though the required pairings are nondegenerate.

1. A normalized old design with a nondegenerate pairing

Work first over \(\mathbb F_2\) with the functional matching base. Put \(V_t=\mathcal P_{\le t}/\mathcal I_t\), assume \(t\ge1\), \(m\ge2t\), and \(N\ge4t-1\), and write \(d=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}V_t\). The old stable-filtration theorem gives a surjective restriction from degree-\(2t\) annihilators to \(V_t^*\), and \(1\notin\mathcal I_t\).

Working lemma. Over some finite extension \(\mathbb K/\mathbb F_2\), there is a normalized \(\lambda_*\in{\rm Ann}(\mathcal I_{2t})\) for which

\[ B_{\lambda_*}([f],[g])=\lambda_*(fg) \quad(f,g\in\mathcal P_{\le t}) \tag{DEN-pairing} \]

is nondegenerate on \(V_t\otimes\mathbb K\). Any extension field of size greater than \(d\) contains a suitable specialization of the family in the proof.

Proof. The pairing is well defined: multiplying a degree-\(t\) old NS consequence by a polynomial through \(t\) gives an old consequence through \(2t\). Choose an \(\mathbb F_2\)-basis \(e_0=1,e_1,\ldots,e_{d-1}\) of \(V_t\), with representatives through \(t\). Booleanity gives \(e_i^2-e_i\in\mathcal I_{2t}\).

By surjectivity choose an affine family of degree-\(2t\) old functionals \(\lambda_u\), over indeterminates \(u_1,\ldots,u_{d-1}\), satisfying \(\lambda_u(e_0)=1\) and \(\lambda_u(e_i)=u_i\). Every Gram entry \(G_{ij}(u)=\lambda_u(e_ie_j)\) is affine in \(u\). The matrix is symmetric and its diagonal is \(1,u_1,\ldots,u_{d-1}\).

In the determinant expansion in characteristic two, permutations containing a cycle of length at least three cancel with the permutation obtained by reversing one such cycle. The remaining terms correspond to disjoint transpositions and fixed points. Every transposition contributes a square \(G_{ij}(u)^2\), whose variable exponents are even. The identity permutation contributes \(\prod_{i=1}^{d-1}u_i\). Any nonempty transposition set contains a nonzero index \(j\), removing its diagonal factor \(u_j\); squared off-diagonal factors cannot restore exponent one in that variable. Hence the coefficient of this squarefree monomial in \(\det G(u)\) is exactly one.

Thus \(\det G\) is nonzero, with total degree at most \(d\). A polynomial of degree less than the field size in each variable cannot vanish on the entire field grid. Specialize in any finite extension of size greater than \(d\) to obtain an invertible Gram matrix. Normalization and all old annihilator equations are retained. The argument is elementary linear algebra; no novelty claim about that general technique is made.

The extension field is used for functional values. It changes no source coefficient domain: a binary source still has the equations \(r^2-r\). One cannot simply promise the pairing over \(\mathbb F_2\) itself. Already for one Boolean bit, the normalized Gram matrix on \(1,x\) is

\[ \begin{pmatrix}1&a\\a&a\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \det=a+a^2. \]

It is singular for both \(a\in\mathbb F_2\), but nonsingular when \(a=\theta\in\mathbb F_4\) and \(\theta^2+\theta+1=0\).

2. What the pairing supplies

Every \(\mu\in{\rm Ann}(\mathcal I_t)\), extended to \(\mathbb K\), now has a unique density class \(f_\mu\in V_t\otimes\mathbb K\) satisfying

\[ \mu(q)=\lambda_*(f_\mu q)\qquad(\deg q\le t). \tag{DEN-represent} \]

This follows by solving the invertible Gram system. A functional given only through \(a\le t\) can first be extended by old filtration, then represented in this way. Its density is not unique until that extension is chosen.

Consequently, for active source windows \(a_U\le t\), all components can be represented over one \(\lambda_*\) by densities \(f_U\) of degree at most \(t\), with products queried only through old degree \(2t\). The empty component can have its own density \(f_\varnothing\), with \(\lambda_*(f_\varnothing)=1\); prescribing an old functional does not force it to equal the chosen common \(\lambda_*\). Taking \(t=D\) covers the prescribed empty degree-\(D\) component as well; smaller cutoffs represent only their stated windows.

This does not solve the source equations. After \(\lambda_*\) is fixed they are still joint linear conditions on the \(f_U\)'s. In particular \(f_{U\cup V}\) is not required to be \(f_Uf_V\), and \(f_U\) is a density for a functional, not a polynomial value assigned to a Boolean selector. Matrix dimensions and density inventories may be large; no efficient general construction is claimed.

3. A natural orthogonal-unit recipe fails

A candidate recipe for an affine input ideal was to take the orthogonal projection of \(1\) onto its annihilator in the truncated old pairing. Its output \(p\) satisfies \(1-p\) in the truncated input ideal and \(p\) orthogonal to that ideal. Those are attractive local conditions, but they do not choose the right unnormalized component masses or enforce mixed source comparisons.

Here is a counterexample with every required Gram restriction nonsingular. Let \(r\ge3\), \(t=r-1\), \(\mathbb K=\mathbb F_4\), and \(\bar\theta=\theta+1=\theta^2\). On the Boolean \(r\)-cube define a normalized functional by the point weights

\[ \omega_0=\theta,\qquad \omega_{e_1}=\bar\theta,\qquad \omega_x=1\quad(x\ne0,e_1),\qquad \lambda(F)=\sum_x\omega_xF(x). \tag{DEN-weights} \]

All old inputs are Boolean. The weights are elements of the functional's value field, not probabilities or assignments of non-Boolean source coefficients. Let \(V\) be the multilinear polynomials through \(r-1\), and let \(U_A,U_C\subset V\) be the degree-truncated ideals of \((x_1,\ldots,x_{r-1})\) and \((x_1,\ldots,x_r)\), respectively.

Nondegeneracy. In the full function space on the cube, the pairing is diagonal with nonzero weights. The subspace \(V\) is characterized by \(\sum_xF(x)=0\), since that sum is the coefficient of the full monomial. Its orthogonal normal has entries \(\omega_x^{-1}\), with squared norm \(\sum_x\omega_x^{-1}=1\). Thus the restriction to \(V\) is nonsingular.

Likewise, \(U_C\) consists of the functions in \(V\) vanishing at \(0\), while \(U_A\) consists of those vanishing at both \(0\) and \(e_r\). On the remaining points their defining hyperplane normals have squared norms \(\theta\) and \(\bar\theta\), respectively. Both are nonzero, so both ideal restrictions are nonsingular.

The corresponding orthogonal-unit projections are

\[ p_A=\prod_{i=1}^{r-1}(1-x_i),\qquad p_C=\bar\theta+\theta\prod_{i=2}^{r}(1-x_i). \tag{DEN-projections} \]

For \(p_A\), the pointwise annihilator and unit identities prove this directly. For \(p_C\), its value is one at \(0,e_1\) and \(\bar\theta\) elsewhere. Hence, for every \(q\in V\),

\[ \lambda(p_Cq)= \bar\theta\sum_xq(x)+q(0)=q(0). \tag{DEN-evaluation} \]

Also \(1-p_C\in U_C\). This proves the orthogonality and, by nonsingularity, identifies the projection uniquely.

Take complete accuracy-one ENS products \(A,C\) on the two input tuples above. Their weights are both two, and their actual mixed port is \(C-A(1-x_r)\), with the ordinary NS witness ceiling five. If their singleton component densities are \(p_A,p_C\), the constant-cofactor source equation fails:

\[ \lambda(p_C)-\lambda(p_A(1-x_r)) =1-\theta=\bar\theta\ne0. \tag{DEN-port-failure} \]

Choose \(r=6\), \(t=D=5\). Then the ambient density cutoff covers the source degree budget, and the failed port is a legal degree-\(D\) constraint. This is not an artifact of testing an unavailable query or a singular Gram matrix.

4. Correct densities need not be unit projections or multiply as values

The true complete-source value of \(C\) on an old point is \(N_C=\prod_{i=1}^{r}(1-x_i)\). Its singleton component on queries through \(t\) has density

\[ f_C=\theta p_C,\qquad \lambda(f_Cq)=\theta q(0)=\lambda(N_Cq) \quad(q\in V). \tag{DEN-corrected} \]

Thus \(p_A,f_C\) satisfy the mixed port, and the latter density matches every old query through \(t\), although \(N_C\) itself has degree \(t+1\). This is the distinction the density representation was intended to permit.

However, multiplying density polynomials as if they were selector values is also invalid. In this example

\[ \lambda(f_C)=\theta,\qquad \lambda(f_C^2)=\theta^2=\bar\theta,\qquad \lambda(f_C^2-f_C)=1. \tag{DEN-square-control} \]

The Boolean-support convention instead uses the same component for \(C^2\) and \(C\). There is no contradiction: a density need not be Boolean or multiplicative.

For completeness, every old Boolean point has a complete genuine source model: at each nonzero input tuple select one nonzero coordinate with a first-row coefficient one, and otherwise set coefficients zero. Both products have their correct zero-flat values, every companion vanishes, and every original coefficient satisfies \(r^2-r=0\). Taking the weights (DEN-weights) gives a genuine normalized joint functional. Thus the counterexample rejects the proposed projection recipe, not existence of a joint extension.

5. Exact checks and the remaining task

The compiled GF(4) checker verifies the three-bit illustration and the six-bit budget-eligible case. It preserves all six nonsingular Gram matrices, pivot data for the full matrices, both ideal projections, the corrected densities, and 72 complete source models. It checks the expected nonzero mixed-port errors and the density-squaring errors, as well as three one-bit field-size controls. All calculations use exact finite-field arithmetic.

The complete JSONL evidence and reproduction note record the fields, bases, polynomials, models, and budgets. Compilation and execution succeeded without retries. These are satisfiable Boolean-source controls, not PHP instances; they show that nondegeneracy and projection alone are insufficient, not that every specially chosen PHP-relative construction must fail.

Main-route status. We have a common bounded-degree density representation of active old functionals, but still no construction satisfying the actual source equations at the required family-size bound. The failed recipe imposed a value-like unit condition on a density and chose the wrong component mass. Further work must choose the correlated support-indexed densities jointly, using the old PHP structure rather than treating orthogonal projection as an automatic lift.

Process assessment. The determinant argument removed a real representation issue, and a budget-eligible mixed-port control prevented mistaking that issue for the source-feasibility problem; no additional workflow rule is needed.

15 September 2026 — The full PHP row space repairs the local density projection

Status: working prescribed-row pairing refinement and a complete degree-preserving correction in a PHP-based source; the row-local normalization mechanism is reused. General source coverage remains open. Cycle 164.

Question. Can the density method repair a mixed comparison while retaining the actual PHP base and all source costs? The previous counterexample used a truncated space of bit polynomials. In the corresponding functional-unary source, the existing old row coordinates supply additional degree-one queries and the correct indicator densities. This repairs the complete local source, without changing the chosen row-state weights.

1. Keep prescribed row masses while making the old pairing nondegenerate

Use \(\mathcal F^{\rm fun}_{m,N}\) in characteristic two, with \(t\ge2\), \(m\ge2t\), and \(N\ge4t-1\). Write \(V_t=\mathcal P_{\le t}/\mathcal I_t\), and distinguish row zero. Its cell classes \(e_j=X_{0j}\) are linearly independent in \(V_t\), sum to one, and satisfy \(e_je_k=\delta_{jk}e_j\) modulo old consequences through degree two. Independence follows already at degree one, then from old stability.

Fix nonzero masses \(\omega_j\) in a finite characteristic-two field \(\mathbb K_0\), with \(\sum_j\omega_j=1\). For a Boolean row predicate \(g_i=\sum_{j\in S_i}e_j\), let \(U_G\subseteq V_t\) be the span of \([qg_i]\) for ordinary products through degree \(t\). Consider finitely many such predicate tuples.

Working refinement. Over a finite extension \(\mathbb K/\mathbb K_0\), one can choose a normalized old degree-\(2t\) functional \(\lambda_*\) with \(\lambda_*(e_j)=\omega_j\), whose pairings on \(V_t\) and all the specified \(U_G\)'s are nondegenerate.

Proof. Extend the cell classes to an \(\mathbb F_2\)-basis of \(V_t\). Old stability allows arbitrary functional values on the remaining basis classes, while fixing the cell masses. The cell block of the Gram matrix is the constant diagonal matrix \({\rm diag}(\omega_j)\). All other diagonal entries are independent parameters, because the basis representatives are Boolean modulo old Booleanity.

The same characteristic-two determinant argument now has squarefree coefficient \(\prod_j\omega_j\ne0\): a surviving nonidentity involution must involve a free index, since off-diagonal entries between distinct cells vanish. Its squared factor cannot restore that index's missing parameter to exponent one. Thus the full Gram determinant is nonzero.

For an input tuple \(G\), let \(Z_G\) be its zero-label set and \(W=\operatorname{span}\{e_j\}\). Then

\[ U_G\cap W=\operatorname{span}\{e_j:j\notin Z_G\}. \tag{ROW-ideal-intersection} \]

For a forbidden state \(j\), choose an input \(g_i\) with \(g_i(e_j)=1\). The degree-two row identities give \(g_i e_j-e_j\in\mathcal I_2\), so \(e_j\in U_G\). Conversely \(g_i e_j\in\mathcal I_2\) for a zero state \(j\). Multiplying by a cofactor through \(t-1\) gives a consequence through \(t+1\le2t\). Hence every admissible \(\lambda_*\) pairs \(U_G\) to zero against that \(e_j\). For an element of \(W\), the diagonal cell pairing and \(\omega_j\ne0\) force its coefficient at \(e_j\) to vanish. This proves (ROW-ideal-intersection).

Choose a basis of \(U_G\) beginning with those forbidden cell classes and with its other elements independent modulo \(W\). Their diagonal values can again vary freely. The identical determinant argument gives a nonzero polynomial for the restricted Gram determinant. The product of all these finitely many determinant polynomials and the full one is nonzero; specialization in a sufficiently large finite extension makes them all nonsingular. All old annihilator equations and the prescribed normalization remain unchanged. This refines the previous pairing lemma; it does not numerically construct the large global matrix.

2. The full old input ideal has the correct projection

For the same tuple set

\[ v_G=\sum_{j\in Z_G}e_j. \]

The forbidden cell calculation and the row sum give \(1-v_G\in U_G\). Moreover \(g_i v_G\) has an old row certificate through degree two. Thus \(v_G\) is orthogonal to every \(qg_i\) through degree \(t\), using old certificates through \(t+1\le2t\). When the restriction to \(U_G\) is nondegenerate, \(v_G\) is therefore exactly the orthogonal-unit projection of one onto \(U_G^\perp\) in the full \(V_t\).

This is where the PHP row structure changes the earlier calculation. The input ideal is taken in the actual old matching quotient, not only in the span of low-degree bit monomials. The value \(v_G\) and its costed input replacement are already supplied by the canonical row-local selector theorem; the present observation identifies the corresponding density projection.

3. A complete PHP-based correction at the original degree

Take \(N=64\), \(m=65\), \(t=5\), and source degree \(D=6\). Use the functional-unary old base, whose quadratic row and collision constraints are active at this degree. For row zero set

\[ L_i=\sum_{z:z_i=1}X_{0z}\quad(1\le i\le6),\qquad \omega_0=\theta,\quad\omega_1=\bar\theta,\quad \omega_z=1\ (z\ne0,1). \tag{ROW-example} \]

Here \(\bar\theta=\theta+1\) in \(\mathbb F_4\). The preceding refinement gives an old functional through ten with these row masses and the required nonsingular pairings. The matching range holds. Its empty degree-six component is simply its restriction, so density one suffices even though the pairing cutoff is five.

Introduce complete accuracy-one ENS blocks \(A,C\) on \((L_1,\ldots,L_5)\) and \((L_1,\ldots,L_6)\). Keep every companion and coefficient equation \(r^2-r\). The original product weights are two, companion costs three, field costs two, and the mixed port \(C-A(1-L_6)\) has its carried NS cost five. The corrected densities are

\[ f_\varnothing=1,\qquad f_A=X_{0,0}+X_{0,32},\qquad f_C=f_{\{A,C\}}=X_{0,0}. \tag{ROW-densities} \]

They give all source-supported old moments through the required windows by \(\Lambda(qZ_U)=\lambda_*(qf_U)\). Products and repeated powers reduce to these intersection indicators with their old row certificates. In particular

\[ f_C-f_A(1-L_6)\in\mathcal I_2(\mathcal F^{\rm fun}), \]

so the mixed comparison and all its degree-six legal old multiples vanish under \(\Lambda\). The old marginal and collision conditions are retained, rather than replaced by satisfiable Boolean-domain conditions.

Complete coefficient map. This also comes from the existing first-success row profile. For each block and each input coordinate \(i\), map its coefficient to the sum of \(X_{0z}\) over labels whose first nonzero input coordinate is \(i\). These coefficient images are old affine polynomials. At a one-hot row state the product becomes exactly the appropriate zero-label indicator.

The row-state NS theorem certifies every coefficient-field image through two, every companion image through three, and the actual product's difference from its canonical value through two. The actual substituted mixed port has a certificate through three, while its canonical density version costs two; both fit the original supplied cost five. Thus the full concrete source, including all original fields and companions, has a normalized degree-six joint functional by pulling back \(\lambda_*\) through the coefficient map. This verifies more than the single comparison equation.

The values \(L_i\) are the justified affine decoder predicates in the functional-unary presentation. The correction uses that presentation and its explicit image bounds; it does not combine the small compact-bit variable space with an unrelated conditioned or unary degree guarantee. The earlier preprocessing-order caveat remains in force.

4. The previously missing query detects the difference

On the distinguished row, the bit-only density from the earlier counterexample was \(\theta p_C\), where \(p_C\) has value one at labels \(0,1\) and \(\bar\theta\) elsewhere. It agreed with the true parent component on bit queries through five. The old unary variable \(X_{0,0}\), however, is an additional degree-one query, and

\[ \lambda_*\bigl((\theta p_C-X_{0,0})X_{0,0}\bigr)=1. \tag{ROW-new-query} \]

The unscaled old projection \(p_C\) also fails orthogonality to the full input ideal: pairing \(p_C L_1X_{0,1}\) gives \(\bar\theta\ne0\). Replacing it by \(X_{0,0}\) repairs these tests and the mixed port. No row-state mass was changed. The earlier counterexample is still valid in its original bit-only space; the corrected old space contains more low-degree information.

5. Evidence, reuse, and the remaining gap

The compiled checker passed 34 complete ordinary NS image certificates and all 64 local row-state checks. It preserves the original blocks and coefficient domains, the affine decoder and coefficient maps, the complete local row-axiom table, every NS cofactor, and the nonzero missing-query controls. All eleven source coefficient fields are checked. These local states are not satisfying assignments of the full PHP base; the global old design and full pairing are supplied by the mathematical existence proof.

The full output and reproduction note retain the evidence. An initial compile used the wrong polynomial-library method call; after correcting it, compilation and the exact run passed. This was a tooling error, not a failed mathematical test.

Main-route status. The requested correction works for this complete PHP-based source and its full old query space. Its normalization coverage is already part of the row-local source pass, so it is not a new unrestricted source class. The new pairing refinement shows that prescribed row masses and the projection interpretation can coexist. The general problem still needs compatible densities for inputs depending on unboundedly many pigeons; the existing multirow profile theorem already charges the row-support factor, which can exceed the desired budget.

Process assessment. Testing the correction in the actual old quotient exposed the missing row-state direction, while the prior claim lookup kept a reused normalizer from being presented as new source coverage; another small-row example is not the next general step.

15 September 2026 — Few written cofactors do not give a small old query space

Status: working support lower bound for Boolean-point realizations of old designs and a source-cofactor specialization-span bound; no cofactor-specific lift or new Frege lower bound. Cycle 165.

Question. The actual source normal form has polynomially many factored cofactor terms. Can that description make the joint construction small enough by using few old evaluation points or a small space of scalar-specialized queries? Neither conclusion follows. The first has an exponential support obstruction; one actual cofactor factor can already span a large space modulo the old matching consequences.

1. A full old design needs exponentially many Boolean support points

Let \(F\) be an unsatisfiable polynomial system on a Boolean cube over a field, with generator degrees at most \(\gamma\). Let \(\lambda\) be a normalized degree-\(D\) ordinary NS design, \(D\ge\gamma\), and suppose

\[ \lambda(f)=\sum_{a\in S}w_a f(a)\qquad(\deg f\le D), \qquad w_a\ne0, \tag{SUP-realization} \]

where the points \(a\) are distinct Boolean assignments. Weights may have either sign where that terminology applies, or lie in an extension field; no positivity is assumed.

Working support bound.

\[ |S|\ge2^{D-\gamma+1}. \tag{SUP-bound} \]

Proof. Any nonempty set of \(K\) Boolean points contains a point isolated within that set by a conjunction of at most \(\lfloor\log_2K\rfloor\) literals. Repeatedly choose a coordinate that splits the current set and keep a nonempty smaller side. Each step at least halves its size, and the product of the chosen coordinate literals isolates the final point.

If \(K<2^{D-\gamma+1}\), the isolator \(q\) has degree at most \(D-\gamma\). At the isolated point \(a\), some generator \(F_i\) is nonzero because the system is unsatisfiable. Then \(\deg(qF_i)\le D\), but

\[ \lambda(qF_i)=w_aF_i(a)\ne0, \]

contrary to the design property. This elementary argument bounds every point realization, not only the earlier Boolean-poset inversion construction.

Binary refinement. If the system is defined over \(\mathbb F_2\), even extension-field weights require \(|S|\ge2^{D-\gamma+1}+1\). Indeed project the finite \(\mathbb F_2\)-span of the weights to \(\mathbb F_2\) by a linear map sending one to one. The resulting nonzero weights are all one and have odd support size, while still realizing a normalized degree-\(D\) design over \(\mathbb F_2\). Apply (SUP-bound) to that support subset.

For the functional or weak linear-row PHP base, \(\gamma=2\). For compact bit-PHP the characteristic-correct bound is \(\gamma=(p-1)\ell\). Support size is not moment-matrix rank; no circuit-width or Gram-rank lower bound is inferred here.

2. A sharp degree-two control

For four pigeons and three holes, take the following three one-hot row assignments with weights one in \(\mathbb F_2\). Each table entry is that row's chosen hole, indexed from zero.

Support pointRow 0Row 1Row 2Row 3
01212
11012
20212

The total weight is one. Booleanity, row sums, and same-row exclusions vanish pointwise, so all their degree-two allowed multiples vanish. The only nonzero column-collision evaluations are \(X_{0,1}X_{2,1}\), with values \((1,1,0)\), and \(X_{1,2}X_{3,2}\), with values \((1,0,1)\). Both sums are zero. Hence this is a complete degree-two design for both displayed PHP bases, attaining the binary lower bound of three points.

It is not a degree-three design: \(X_{1,0}X_{0,1}X_{2,1}\) has weighted value one. The support assignments are not PHP models; their collision violations cancel only within the permitted degree-two tests.

3. Optimizing support cannot rescue the same union bound

The earlier pointwise lift attempt chooses constant ENS coefficients that make every companion vanish at every support point. At a fixed nonzero input vector, \(h\) independent coefficient rows all miss the required value one with probability \((1-1/p)^h\). Its support-count certificate therefore requires

\[ K(1-1/p)^h<1. \tag{SUP-union} \]

The choice can be made block by block after earlier choices, so this comparison does not need an extra inventory factor. In the binary case, (SUP-bound) forces \(h>D-\gamma+1\) whenever (SUP-union) is to certify success. For the unary PHP bases this requires \(h\ge D\). At that accuracy a nonconstant affine block has original companion degree \(2h+1>D\), so its companions are already inactive. For other primes the same miss probability is larger, making this support-count requirement no better.

The earlier failure used a coarse upper bound on support. The new lower bound shows that merely finding an optimally small point realization does not put this particular certificate of success into the active unary regime. In general the necessary condition is \(h>(D-\gamma+1)\log2/[-\log(1-1/p)]\). For binary compact bit-PHP this is \(h>D-\ell+1\). It fails in the recorded scale \(h=3\ell\), \(D=(C+H_\pi)L\): with \(d\ge1\) and \(C\ge12\), the source bound \(L=(d+1)h^d\) already gives \(D\ge24h\).

This is a limitation of the support-only union-bound guarantee, not an impossibility theorem for all constant coefficient assignments. The literal-copy map, for example, succeeds pointwise with one coefficient row regardless of the number of old support points. Structure-specific assignments and genuinely correlated functionals remain possible.

4. One source factor already has many old specializations

Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_r\) be distinct old coordinate variables, and consider the genuine accuracy-\(h\) product

\[ P(R,X)=\prod_{u=1}^h \left(1-\sum_{i=1}^r R_{u,i}g_i\right). \tag{SUP-factor} \]

Its written arithmetic size is \(O(hr)\). The coefficient of a fresh monomial \(R_{1,i_1}\cdots R_{s,i_s}\), with all other fresh coordinates absent, is \((-1)^s g_{i_1}\cdots g_{i_s}\). Conversely every coefficient is a scalar times such a product. Since the fresh variables occur multilinearly, Boolean-parameter inversion expresses these coefficients as linear combinations of scalar specializations, and specializations are linear combinations of the coefficients.

Consequently the old polynomial span of all scalar specializations is exactly the products of at most \(h\) inputs. Before old Boolean reduction its dimension is \(\binom{r+h}{h}\); after Boolean reduction it is

\[ \sum_{s=0}^{\min(h,r)}\binom rs. \tag{SUP-span} \]

For \(1-P\), omit the constant product and subtract one from the dimension. The actual frame \(\neg A\vee(A\vee B)\) supplies precisely the cofactor \(1-P_A\), so this is a source-template example rather than an arbitrary mask assigned to a module.

5. The growth can persist in the old PHP quotient

In \(\mathcal F^{\rm fun}_{m,N}\), take \(g_i=X_{i,i}\) for \(r\le\min(m,N)\) distinct rows and columns. Let \(B\ge h\), \(m\ge B\), and

\[ N\ge\max\{2B-1,\,2h+1\}. \tag{SUP-old-range} \]

Then all the squarefree diagonal products through degree \(h\), including one, are independent modulo \(\mathcal I_B\). Thus (SUP-span) remains the dimension of the specialization span in the old degree-\(B\) quotient.

Proof. Take a nonzero combination and a maximal-degree monomial on \(k\le h\) diagonal cells. If \(k=0\), an old normalized design separates its nonzero constant. Otherwise choose, for each selected row, its diagonal column and one alternate column, with all \(2k\) columns distinct. Give the diagonal state weight one and the alternate state weight minus one. Delete all these columns from the unselected rows and choose a normalized residual old design through \(B-k\). It exists because \(N-2k\ge2(B-k)-1\), and at least one residual column remains.

Use the signed row-cube construction: a matching moment is zero unless all selected rows occur on their chosen two-point sets and all other rows avoid the deleted columns; otherwise multiply the signs by the residual moment. The same row-marginal verification makes this an old degree-\(B\) annihilator. A diagonal monomial missing a selected row has value zero. The chosen maximal monomial has value one, and no other monomial of the same or smaller degree contains all its selected rows. The functional therefore detects its nonzero coefficient. This proves independence.

For \(h\) of logarithmic size in \(r\), this dimension is already superpolynomial in \(r\). Counting factored expressions alone cannot replace a bound on their old specialization space. The example does not prove that this space is indispensable in every globally rewritten PHP certificate: the displayed tautology frame itself has the previously recorded cheap normalization.

6. What remains of the proof-specific route

No functional for the actual cofactor family was constructed. A method that insists on a full degree-\(D\) old design cannot make its point support small merely because the certificate has few written terms. Likewise, a guarantee over all scalar coefficient choices can involve a large old specialization span even for one factor. A functional defined only on the actual required tests may avoid those hypotheses, but then its normalization, closure, and annihilation properties need their own proof; they do not follow from the expression count.

The symbolic density representation remains available and does not require a small point support. The remaining task is still a compatible construction using the source's particular equations and polynomial inventory. The fixed-distribution quantifier issue is not resolved by choosing a different favorable old functional after each coefficient assignment.

Evidence and process assessment. The evidence is the isolating-literal proof, the complete three-point degree-two control, the coefficient-extraction identity, and the old row-cube separator; no numerical run was needed. The audit record retains the exact scope and dependencies. Testing both the support budget and the actual parameterized query span avoided replacing the open construction by an unjustified small-description argument.

16 September 2026 — General consequence transfer and the exponential bit-PHP parameter range

Status: working corollaries of the recorded and formalized component theorems; the new generic assembly and exponential conclusion are not separately formalized.

Question and stopping point. Assess the author's supplied Fable feedback that Sections 5–6 contain a general Res(\(\oplus\))-to-PC tradeoff and permit \(2^{\Omega(n/\log^2 n)}\) bit-PHP lower bounds. This is a bounded publication-scope assessment, not a restart of Spin or a new attack on the main Frege obligation. Stop after stating the exact generic conclusion, checking a basic short-proof control, and closing the finite bit-PHP parameters with explicit conservative constants. Do not alter the preprint or start an unassigned formalization.

A generic dimension-budget consequence theorem

Let \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_v]\) contain all old Boolean equations. Let \(\Gamma\) adjoin a finite complete one-level affine ENS family with accuracy \(h\ge1\), all companions and fresh coefficient Boolean equations, and old-affine inputs only. Suppose \(\Gamma\) has a degree-\(D\) ordinary-PC refutation, \(D\ge2h+1\). Fix \(k\ge1\) and a linear subspace \(U\subseteq\mathcal P_{\le k}\). Let \(H\) be the blocks with input span not containing one and rank \(r_a>h(k+1)\). Define

\[ B=k(D+1),\qquad R=\sum_{a\in H}\binom{v-r_a+k}{k}. \]

Then

\[ \dim\bigl(U\cap\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F)\bigr)\ge\dim U-R. \]

In particular, \(\dim U>R\) forces a nonzero member of \(U\) to be derivable through \(B\). Conversely, if \(U\cap\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F)=\{0\}\), no such refutation exists whenever the dimension inequality holds. For \(r_*=h(k+1)+1\le v\), one may replace \(R\) by \(|H|\binom{v-r_*+k}{k}\). If \(r_*>v\), then \(H\) is empty and \(R=0\).

Proof. For every \(a\in H\), choose affine coordinates on its nonempty common zero flat and let \(\rho_a\) be ordinary polynomial restriction to those coordinates. The ordinary restriction dimension bound gives \(\operatorname{rank}(\rho_a|_U)\le\binom{v-r_a+k}{k}\). The joint restriction map on \(U\) consequently has rank at most \(R\), so its kernel \(K\) has dimension at least \(\dim U-R\). For each \(f\in K\), literal affine-ideal membership supplies \(f=\sum_i a_{a,i}g_{a,i}\) with \(\deg a_{a,i}\le k-1\) for every proper high block. Each other high block has one in its span. The weighted removal theorem therefore derives every \(f\in K\) from \(\mathcal F\) through \(B\). Thus \(K\subseteq U\cap\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F)\), proving the inequality. The rank-threshold specialization follows by monotonicity of the binomial count. These are ordinary restriction maps, not pointwise evaluation maps.

This abstracts the existing common-kernel argument rather than discovering a new elimination mechanism. Its dependencies are indexed as lem:ordinary-restriction-dimension, lem:proper-affine-block-restriction, and lem:affine-family-removal-with-unit-blocks. Their Lean files verify those ingredients; the displayed arbitrary-\(U\) dimension inequality is a new paper-level assembly, not an additional exported Lean theorem.

What is generic, and what still depends on the source

The finite DAG registry theorem is generic but requires actual bounded-degree derivations of the supplied initial clause values. For a CNF with \(t\) initial clauses of width at most \(w\), take the old base to contain its ordinary clause polynomials \(F_C=\prod_i(1-g_i)\) and Boolean equations, with \(g_i\) the literal true-indicators. The telescoping identity gives

\[ P_C=F_CP_C+\sum_i\left(\prod_{j<i}(1-g_j)\right)g_iP_C. \]

Each term has a PC/NS certificate through \(w+2h\): the clause product has degree at most \(w\), the block product at most \(2h\), and each prefix-companion product at most \(w+2h\). The empty initial clause directly supplies one. Hence an \(S\)-node source refutation gives a registry with at most \(3S+t\) slots and a refutation through \(D=\max\{4h+1,w+2h\}\). Applying the preceding theorem gives a generic subspace-consequence bound. For another old encoding, an analogous initial-value bridge must be supplied; \(D=O(\log n)\) is not free for arbitrary wide clauses or arbitrary encodings. The publication uses its specific compact bit-PHP bridge.

The conclusion is not in general a degree-\(B\) PC refutation: the resulting polynomial is some nonzero \(f\), not necessarily one. Nonzero ordinary polynomials can be valid low-degree consequences. For instance, the satisfiable system \(\{x,x^2-x\}\) derives the nonzero polynomial \(x\) but cannot derive one. Thus this argument alone does not establish a conventional universal size-versus-PC-refutation-degree theorem or a Res(\(\oplus\)) size–width relation. A useful application needs a sufficiently large space \(U\) with the additional separation property \(U\cap\mathcal C_B=\{0\}\). In bit PHP that is the substantial row-linear separation theorem, not a consequence of mere absence of a PC refutation.

Short-proof control. For any affine \(L\), the old system \(\{L,1-L\}\cup\mathrm{BOOL}\) derives one through degree one. It has a short complementary-parity refutation as well. Consequently, for every \(B\ge k\ge1\), all degree-at-most-\(k\) polynomials are in \(\mathcal C_B\), by multiplying the completed unit line. The generic consequence theorem is compatible with this whole family of easy parity contradictions: its conclusion is already satisfied, while the required separated space does not exist. This is a basic analytic control, not a comprehensive audit of known Res(\(\oplus\)) upper bounds. The latter remains worthwhile before advertising a general tradeoff.

The stronger bit-PHP parameter consequence

For all sufficiently large \(n=2^\ell\), the recorded finite-parameter exclusion and actual clause transfer imply that every usual-CNF bit-PHP refutation has

\[ S>\exp\!\left(\frac{n}{32768\ell^2}\right) =2^{\Omega(n/(\log n)^2)}. \]

Proof. Put \(c=1/32768\), \(m=n+1\), \(h=3\ell\), and \(D=12\ell+1\). Suppose \(S\le\exp(cn/\ell^2)\). The actual usual-CNF transfer supplies at most \(N\le3S+\binom{n+1}{2}\) blocks. Put \(M=\max\{1,N\}\). For all sufficiently large \(\ell\), \(n^2\le\exp(cn/\ell^2)\) and \(\ln20\le cn/\ell^2\); therefore \(M\le5\exp(cn/\ell^2)\) and \(\ln(4M)\le2cn/\ell^2\). Both eventual comparisons follow from \(2^\ell/\ell^3\to\infty\).

Choose \(k=\lfloor n/(32\ell)\rfloor\). For sufficiently large \(\ell\), \(n\ge64\ell\), hence \(n/(64\ell)\le k\le n/(32\ell)\), in particular \(1\le k\le m\). Since \(m\le2n\),

\[ m\ln(4M)\le4c\frac{n^2}{\ell^2} =\frac{n^2}{8192\ell^2} \le\frac{n^2}{4096\ell^2}\le k^2. \]

Moreover \(D\ge2h+1\), and

\[ B=k(D+1)\le\frac{n(12\ell+2)}{32\ell}\le\frac{7n}{16}, \qquad 2B-1\le n,\qquad 4(k-1)\le4k\le\frac{n}{8\ell}<n. \]

These are exactly the hypotheses of affine_family_exclusion_of_square in the verified finite exclusion theorem. The number of proper high blocks is at most \(N\le M\). The transferred degree-\(D\) refutation is therefore impossible, proving the bound. No optimization of the constant is claimed.

This uses the existing finite square-condition theorem with a new parameter choice. The already exported final theorem bitPHP_superpolynomial states only the superpolynomial conclusion; the exponential corollary has not been formalized or inserted into the preprint. Its dependence on the same core proof means that the stronger asymptotics are neither independent confirmation of that core nor a contradiction in themselves.

Outcome and remaining work. Fable's observation identifies a useful general subspace-consequence theorem and a stronger quantitative corollary. It does not, without additional hypotheses, produce a general low-degree PC refutation. Independent specialist review of the encoding, fixed-registry simulation and weighted removal remains appropriate. If the author requests an extension, isolate the generic theorem, test it against substantive known short-proof families, and formalize the exponential parameter closure before changing the publication's headline. The main Frege goal, remaining route and proposed main research step are unchanged; only the publication-side summary is refreshed. No numerical experiment, Lean rerun, or claim of new literature priority was needed. Initial rules reading preceded timing.

17 September 2026 — Lean formalization of the exponential bit-PHP bound, with an explicit threshold

Status: full Lean formalization of cor:bit-PHP-exponential-parameter-bound, strengthened to every bit length \(\ell\ge32\); a parameter corollary of already verified theorems, with no new elimination mechanism. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1, medium effort).

Assignment, obligation, and stopping point. The user assigned the Formalize prompt to the exponential parameter corollary of the 16 September assessment, as a prerequisite for stating it in the publication-side preprint. This does not touch the main Frege route.
