18 September 2026 — Below size \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\) every role-separated mixed reader has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds, with arbitrary light tails; above it, multi-row tails switch when no light row carries light-host mass above \(n^{2-\varepsilon}/\mathrm{polylog}\)

Status: working theorem with full proof (role-separated readers of pinned rows with light tails on any rows: few labels with a large light union, or bounded light mass per light row), containing the pattern-bounded theorem with \(H_{\max}\) halved; corollary: every such reader of size below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\) has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds and switches when its tails lie in the light range. Spin cycle 200. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Verification gate. The exact proofs of the pattern-bounded theorem (host setting, steps (H1) to (H4), scope), the activated union lemma, the both-endpoints rule, the matched-first preference, the two-role correction, the height budget, and the statement of the light lemma were re-read from the notebook; the recorded counterexample readers of the adaptive-rule gap, the hole-only sparse failure, the pigeon-only refutation, the q-skip refutation, the two-role example, the alive-pair obligation, and the falsification families of the general column claim were checked against the conclusion (they concern other trees or fall in case (H3) with at most one round each); no rule or encoding changed, and the both-endpoints decoder was exercised on readers with three-row tails (2255 rich bad paths, 0 round-trip failures); a fresh-context reviewer confirmed facts (a) and (b) and steps (H1) to (H4) and reported four findings, all resolved here: the switching clause lacked the light lemma's per-row range, the size corollary needs no width or mass hypothesis because case (H4) cannot occur below size \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\), the upper bound on \(N\) and the probability constant of the containment were misstated, and three wordings (the bound on \(|B|\) in the corollary, "at most \(|B|\)", the two-stage exposure) were imprecise.

Question and stopping point. The task was the multi-row extension of the pattern-bounded theorem: a host becomes a tail on several light rows, and step (H4) must handle hosts with overlapping row sets. Writing the theorem's hypothesis as a bound on the light-host mass carried by a light row, instead of a count of hosts, makes the multi-row proof a greedy choice of row-disjoint matched hosts. The fresh-context review then showed that, since the total light mass of a reader is at most its number of terms, the mass step is never needed below size \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\): there the rank step alone bounds the rounds, for tails of any shape. The stopping point was this theorem with its gate.

1. Hosts on several rows

A reader consists of at most \(n^c\) terms \([i\to x]\wedge\bigwedge_{j\in J}[j\in p_j]\) with \(i\in A\), \(J\subseteq B\), \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\), and each \(p_j\) a pattern of literals on the bits of row \(j\); the tail \(J=\varnothing\) is allowed. It is read by the both-endpoints tree with the matched-first preference: the current term is the earliest term not falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi\) whose pinned pair is matched by \(\mu'\), or the earliest such term if none has a matched pair; its uncovered tail rows are queried in order, and then, if its pinned pair is unkilled with a residual row and a hole in \(Q\), a heavy round follows. A host \(h\) is a tail: a row set \(J_h\) with patterns \(p_{h,j}\). Its pair set \(P_h\), mass \(m_h\), the sets \(I_{h,x}\), the heavy hosts (\(m_h\ge2N(n+1)\)) and light hosts, \(U^{\rm L}_x=\bigcup_{h\text{ light}}I_{h,x}\), and \(D_2^\ast=n/(800e(N+1))\) are as in the host setting. Given the light assignment \(\zeta\), a host is activated if every \(j\in J_h\) is residual or has \(\zeta(j)\in C(p_{h,j})\), that is, if its tail is not falsified by \(\rho'\). New are the set \(X_{\rm L}=\{x:\ |U^{\rm L}_x|\ge D_2^\ast\}\) of labels with a large light union, the light mass of a light row, \(m^{\rm L}_j=\sum\{m_h:\ h\text{ light},\ j\in J_h\}\), and its maximum \(M_{\rm row}\) over \(B\); all are fixed by the reader. For a fixed \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) put \(d_\varepsilon=\lceil(c+1)/\varepsilon\rceil+1\), and when the tails have at most \(t\) rows and total width at most \(W\) (at most \(W\) literals per term outside the pinned row) put \[J_0=2t\bigl(2^{W+4t}(c+1)\ln n+N+1\bigr),\qquad M_\varepsilon=\frac{n^{2-\varepsilon}}{1600e(N+1)J_0}.\]

The two facts about a bad path (at least \(N/48\) rounds, no 1-leaf) transfer to several rows. (a) By the both-endpoints lemma its trigger pairs form a matching of pairs \((i,x)\in P_h\) with \(x\in Q\) and \(i\in R'\); at a round the current term's tail is satisfied by \(\rho'\cup\pi\), hence not falsified by \(\rho'\), so \(h\) is activated. (b) A host with a matched pair, \(\mu'(i)=x\) for some \((i,x)\in P_h\), contributes no trigger pair: if a round's term \(T'\) had tail \(h\), then at the node where \(T'\) is chosen \(T=[i\to x]\wedge h\) would be falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi\), since otherwise the preference chooses a term with a matched pinned pair, whose pinned row is not residual, so that no round follows from it; the pinned part of \(T\) holds under \(\rho'\), so its tail \(h\) is falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi\), and so is \(T'\), which is not falsified at that node.

2. Theorem

Theorem. Fix \(c\ge1\) and \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\). Let \(N\ge2^{d_\varepsilon+6}(c+1)\log_2n\) with \((Nn^{-\varepsilon})^{d_\varepsilon+1}\le n^{-c-1}\), which polylogarithmic \(N\) and large \(n\) give, and let \(n\) be large. A reader as in Section 1 has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds on every path before any 1-leaf, with probability at least \(1-3n^{-c-1}\) over \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\), if (i) \(|X_{\rm L}|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\); and with probability at least \(1-4n^{-c-1}\) if (ii) its tails have at most \(t\) rows and total width at most \(W\), \(J_0\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\), and \(M_{\rm row}\le M_\varepsilon\). In either case, when the light part satisfies the hypotheses of the light lemma (rows per term and per-row width in its range, per-row width \(2^w\le n^{1/3}\) up to polylogarithmic factors), the reader switches under one restriction within the height budget.

Proof. (H1) Heavy hosts have a matched pair. Unchanged from step (H1): given \(Q\), for the labels \(x\notin Q\) of \(P_h\) the events "the occupant of \(x\) lies outside \(I_{h,x}\)" are decreasing on distinct columns, each of probability \(1-|I_{h,x}|/(n+1)\), while the labels in \(Q\) have no occupant and carry mass at most \(N(n+1)\le m_h/2\); so a heavy host has no matched pair with probability at most \(e^{-m_h/(2(n+1))}\le e^{-N}\le n^{-2c-3}\), and over at most \(n^c\) hosts this costs \(n^{-c-3}\). Outside this event, by fact (b), the trigger pairs of a bad path come from light hosts, so every trigger pair \((i,x)\) has \(i\in U^{\rm L}_x\).

(H2) Labels with a small light union. The rounds of a bad path at labels outside \(X_{\rm L}\) are triggered by a matching in \(\{(i,x):\ x\in Q\setminus X_{\rm L},\ i\in R_A\cap U^{\rm L}_x\}\), where \(R_A=R'\cap A\). The proof of the activated union lemma uses only that, given \(Q\) and \(\zeta\), \(R_A\) is a uniform subset of \(A\) of size at most \(N+1\), \(|A|\ge n/2+N+2\), and the rows of a \(k\)-matching are chosen from sets of fewer than \(D_2^\ast\) elements; it applies verbatim to the fixed sets \(U^{\rm L}_x\), \(x\notin X_{\rm L}\), and gives fewer than \(N/192\) such rounds outside probability \(2^{-N/192}\le n^{-c-1}\).

(H3) Few labels with a large light union, \(|X_{\rm L}|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\): by the rank lemma in its independent-points form with \(d=d_\varepsilon\), \(\Pr[|X_{\rm L}\cap Q|\ge2^{d}]\le(n^{1-\varepsilon}N/n)^{d+1}=(Nn^{-\varepsilon})^{d+1}\le n^{-c-1}\). Outside this event a bad path, whose rounds have distinct labels, has fewer than \(N/192+2^{d}\le N/192+N/128<N/48\) rounds, as \(N\ge2^{d+7}\). This proves (i).

(H4) Many labels with a large light union under (ii), \(|X_{\rm L}|>n^{1-\varepsilon}\): then \(\Omega_{\rm L}=\sum_x|U^{\rm L}_x|\ge|X_{\rm L}|D_2^\ast>n^{2-\varepsilon}/(800e(N+1))\). (H4a) For a set \(J\) of fewer than \(J_0\) light rows put \(V_x(J)=\bigcup\{I_{h,x}:\ h\text{ light},\ J_h\cap J=\varnothing\}\). Since \(U^{\rm L}_x\subseteq V_x(J)\cup\bigcup\{I_{h,x}:\ h\text{ light},\ J_h\cap J\ne\varnothing\}\) and a light host meeting \(J\) is counted in the light mass of a row of \(J\), \(\sum_x|V_x(J)|\ge\Omega_{\rm L}-\sum_{j\in J}m^{\rm L}_j\ge\Omega_{\rm L}-J_0M_\varepsilon\ge n^{2-\varepsilon}/(1600e(N+1))\), and the labels in \(Q\) contribute at most \(N(n+1)\), so \(\sum_{x\notin Q}|V_x(J)|\ge N(n+1)J_0\): indeed \(N(n+1)(J_0+1)\le2(n+1)n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^3\le n^{2-\varepsilon}/(1600e(N+1))\) once \(N^2\ge3200e(N+1)(n+1)/(Nn)\), which \(N\ge95\) gives. Given \(Q\), the event that no light host disjoint from \(J\) has a matched pair is the intersection over \(x\notin Q\) of the decreasing events "the occupant of \(x\) lies outside \(V_x(J)\)" on distinct columns, of probability at most \(\prod_{x\notin Q}(1-|V_x(J)|/(n+1))\le e^{-NJ_0}\). Over fewer than \(n^{J_0}\) sets \(J\) this costs at most \(e^{-J_0(N-\ln n)}\le e^{-J_0N/2}\le n^{-c-1}\), as \(N\ge2\ln n\) and \(J_0\ge2(c+1)\ln n\). (H4b) Outside that event let \(\mathcal M\) be the set of light hosts with a matched pair, determined by \(Q\) and the images of the pinned rows. If some \(h\in\mathcal M\) has \(J_h=\varnothing\), its term is satisfied by \(\rho'\) and the tree is a 1-leaf. Otherwise choose greedily a maximal \(\mathcal M'\subseteq\mathcal M\) of hosts with pairwise disjoint row sets and put \(J'=\bigcup_{h\in\mathcal M'}J_h\). Every host of \(\mathcal M\) meets \(J'\), so \(|J'|\ge J_0\), since otherwise \(J=J'\) would have a matched light host disjoint from it; hence \(|\mathcal M'|\ge J_0/t\), and \(|B|\ge|J'|\ge J_0\). (H4c) Expose \(Q\) and \(R_A\). The set \(\mathrm{rem}\) of labels outside \(Q\) not taken by pinned rows is then a uniform subset of \(Q^c\) of size \(|B|-s_B\), where \(s_B=N+1-|R_A|\le N+1\) is the number of slots left for \(B\), so \(|\mathrm{rem}|\ge|B|-N-1\ge J_0-N-1\ge2t2^{W+4t}(c+1)\ln n\). For each pattern \(p\) of the reader, of width \(w_p\), \(|C(p)\cap Q^c|\ge n2^{-w_p}-N\ge n2^{-w_p}/2\) because \(2^{w_p}\le2^{W}\le J_0\le n/(2N)\), so \(\mathbb E|C(p)\cap\mathrm{rem}|\ge|\mathrm{rem}|2^{-w_p}/2\ge16(c+1)\ln n\), using \(t2^{4t}\ge16\) and \(W\ge w_p\); sampling without replacement is negatively associated, so the Chernoff bound gives \(|C(p)\cap\mathrm{rem}|\ge2^{-w_p}|\mathrm{rem}|/4\) outside probability \(e^{-2(c+1)\ln n}=n^{-2c-2}\), and over at most \(tn^c\) patterns this costs at most \(tn^{-c-2}\le n^{-c-1}\). Given also the images of the pinned rows, which fix \(\mathcal M'\), the light rows form a uniform bijection of \(B\) onto \(\mathrm{rem}\) and the slots. Fix \(h\in\mathcal M'\) with rows \(j_1,\dots,j_k\), \(k\le t\), and its matched pair \((i,x)\), and let \(E_h\) be the event that \(\mu'(j_r)\in C(p_{h,j_r})\cap\mathrm{rem}\) for every \(r\). Row by row, the \(r\)-th row has at least \(|C(p_{h,j_r})\cap\mathrm{rem}|-(r-1)\ge2^{-w_{h,j_r}}|\mathrm{rem}|/8\) admissible labels among at most \(|B|\) remaining targets, because \(2^{-w_{h,j_r}}|\mathrm{rem}|/8\ge t\); so \(\Pr[E_h]\ge2^{-W}8^{-t}(|\mathrm{rem}|/|B|)^t\). Here \(|\mathrm{rem}|/|B|\ge1-(N+1)/|B|\ge1-(N+1)/J_0\ge1-1/(2t)\) because \(J_0\ge2t(N+1)\), and \((1-1/(2t))^t\ge1/2\), so \(\Pr[E_h]\ge2^{-W-4t}\). On \(E_h\) the term \([i\to x]\wedge h\) is satisfied by \(\rho'\). The events \(E_h\), \(h\in\mathcal M'\), are increasing and depend on pairwise disjoint sets of rows of the light bijection, so negative association gives \(\Pr[\text{no }E_h]\le\prod_{h\in\mathcal M'}(1-\Pr[E_h])\le\exp(-(J_0/t)2^{-W-4t})\le n^{-2c-2}\). A term satisfied by \(\rho'\) prevents every round.

Under (ii) the cases \(|X_{\rm L}|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\) and \(|X_{\rm L}|>n^{1-\varepsilon}\) are exclusive and fixed by the reader; the excluded events total at most \(n^{-c-3}+n^{-c-1}+\max(n^{-c-1},\ 2n^{-c-1}+n^{-2c-2})\le4n^{-c-1}\). The switching conclusion is the composition recorded in the height budget, with the both-endpoints decoder for role-separated readers and the light lemma for the tails, which supplies the per-row width range. \(\square\)

3. Corollary: every role-separated mixed reader of size below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\)

Corollary. Under the theorem's conditions on \(N\), if \(1\le c<2-\varepsilon\) and \(800e(N+1)\le n^{2-\varepsilon-c}\), every reader as in Section 1 with at most \(n^c\) terms, whatever its tails, has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds on every path before any 1-leaf with probability at least \(1-3n^{-c-1}\), and switches within the height budget when its tails lie in the light lemma's range.

Proof. Each term contributes one pair to one host, so \(\Omega_{\rm L}=\sum_x|U^{\rm L}_x|\le\sum_{h\text{ light}}m_h\le n^c\), and \(|X_{\rm L}|\le\Omega_{\rm L}/D_2^\ast\le800e(N+1)n^{c-1}\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\); apply (i). \(\square\)

Beyond size \(n^{4/3}/\mathrm{polylog}\), up to which the general random-flat theorem covers all readers, this is the first switching statement in the window that assumes nothing about the reader's pinned pairs, labels, hosts, or tail shape: the recorded column and host theorems each restrict one of them, and the final clause of the pattern-bounded theorem covers single-row tails of width up to \(\ell/(2\log_2(2\ell+1))\) at every polynomial size. The only width restriction is the light lemma's, on each tail row separately; a tail of total width above \(\tfrac13\log_2n\) must therefore spread over several rows, which the corollary allows.

4. Scope

For \(t=1\), \(\varepsilon=1/3\), and integer \(c\), \(d_\varepsilon=3c+4\) and the threshold \(2^{3c+10}(c+1)\log_2n\) are those of the pattern-bounded theorem, whose (H3) needs the same bound \((Nn^{-1/3})^{3c+5}\le n^{-c-1}\), and \(J_0\) exceeds that theorem's \(J_0\) by \(N+1\), hence by at most a factor two. A reader with at most \(H_{\max}/2\) patterns per light row has \(M_{\rm row}\le2N(n+1)H_{\max}/2\le M_{1/3}\), so part (ii) contains the pattern-bounded theorem with \(H_{\max}\) halved, with the probability constant \(4\) in place of \(3\), and through it the role-separated column theorems; the hypothesis is on the mass of light hosts, so heavy hosts, which block their rows, cost nothing however many share a row. The multi-row step is the greedy family \(\mathcal M'\), which loses the factor \(t\) in \(|\mathcal M'|\) and the factor \((|\mathrm{rem}|/|B|)^t\) in the satisfaction probability, absorbed by \(J_0\ge2t(N+1)\); no hypergraph matching bound beyond maximality is needed. The rank step with \(|X_{\rm L}|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\) replaces the \(n^{2/3}\) convention of the earlier entries at the price of \(2^{d_\varepsilon}\) rounds, which the polylogarithmic \(N\) absorbs. Part (ii) matters only for readers with more than \(n^{2-\varepsilon}/(800e(N+1))\) terms in light hosts, since below that part (i) applies with any tails.

What remains in the window for the literal frontier: at sizes \(n^c\), \(c\ge2-\varepsilon\), a light row whose light hosts carry mass above \(n^{2-\varepsilon}/\mathrm{polylog}\), the multi-row form of the crowded-row case (the random-subset blocking argument, where the matched hosts of a row are a random subset of its hosts, remains the proposed way); the encoding for rows with two roles, which the theorem excludes by role separation; and parity terms.

Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. In the literal window, the constant-factor heavy-round bound now holds for every role-separated mixed reader of size below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\), with light tails of any shape, and above that size for tails on boundedly many rows when no light row carries light-host mass above \(n^{2-\varepsilon}/\mathrm{polylog}\); open are heavier rows at larger sizes, the two-role encoding, and parity terms, the open core.

Process assessment. The gate again changed the result before commit: the reviewer's second finding turned a mass-conditioned corollary with a spurious total-width condition into the unconditional size statement, and its first finding restored a hypothesis the draft had dropped, at the cost of one review round of about seventeen minutes; the three-row-tail round trips were cheap and ran before the review. One framework line follows: the reviewer is also asked which hypotheses the argument never uses.

18 September 2026 — Few light rows need no mass hypothesis: exposing the light rows, whose residual ones are few, bounds the heavy rounds of every role-separated reader with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows, of any size

Status: working theorem with full proof (role-separated readers with light tails of any shape on at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows, any pinned pairs, any size): fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds on every path, hence switching within the height budget when the tails lie in the light range; it contains the crowded single light row when the light rows are few. Spin cycle 201. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question and stopping point. The task was a light row carrying light hosts of mass above \(n^{2-\varepsilon}/\mathrm{polylog}\), where the multi-row theorem stops. The intended general claim, fewer than \(N/48\) rounds for every role-separated reader, was first tested against the natural crowded reader, one light row hosting a term \([i\to x]\wedge[j\in p_i]\) for every row \(i\) and label \(x\): the adversary would need an answer at \(j\) that activates exactly the hosts of the residual rows, and there are only \(n\) answers against \(\binom{n}{N}\) residual sets. This is the mechanism of the proof: expose the light rows; only a bounded number of them are residual; take a union bound over their answers; then the activated hosts are a fixed family, matched with high probability when their mass is large and otherwise concentrated on few labels, which the rank lemma keeps out of the flat. The stopping point was this theorem with its gate; the combination with the multi-row theorem is the next step.

1. Exposing few light rows

A reader consists of any number of terms \([i\to x]\wedge\bigwedge_{j\in J}[j\in p_j]\) with \(i\in A\), \(J\subseteq B\), \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), and \(b=|B|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\), for a fixed \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\); tails may be empty, have any number of rows, and any patterns. It is read by the both-endpoints tree with the matched-first preference, as in the multi-row setting; hosts are tails, \(P_h\), \(I_{h,x}\), and \(D_2^\ast=n/(800e(N+1))\) are as there, and no host is called heavy or light. Write \(\zeta\) for the restriction of \(\mu'\) to \(B\) (which light rows are residual, \(R_B\), and the labels of the others). For a labeling \(y\) of \(R_B\) by labels, let \(\zeta_y=\zeta\cup y\), a labeling of all of \(B\); call a host consistent with \(\zeta_y\) if \(\zeta_y(j)\in C(p_{h,j})\) for every \(j\in J_h\), let \(\mathcal H_y\) be the set of consistent hosts, \(U_x(y)=\bigcup_{h\in\mathcal H_y}I_{h,x}\subseteq A\), \(m(y)=\sum_x|U_x(y)|\), and \(X(y)=\{x:\ |U_x(y)|\ge D_2^\ast\}\); given \(\zeta\) and \(y\) these are fixed. Put \[r_0=\lceil(c+2)/\varepsilon\rceil+1,\qquad c'=c+2+r_0,\qquad d=\lceil c'/\varepsilon\rceil+2.\]

Residual light rows are few. Given \(Q\), a fixed set of \(r\) light rows is residual with probability \(\prod_{k<r}(N+1-k)/(n+1-k)\le((N+1)/(n+1))^r\), so \(\Pr[|R_B|\ge r]\le\binom br((N+1)/(n+1))^r\le(eb(N+1)/(r(n+1)))^r\le n^{-\varepsilon r}\), using \(b\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) and \(e(N+1)\le N^4\); with \(r=r_0\) this is at most \(n^{-c-2}\).

Two facts about a bad path (at least \(N/48\) rounds, no 1-leaf). Let \(y\) be the path's final partial matching restricted to \(R_B\), the labels it assigns to residual light rows by pigeon queries or by moves at hole queries, extended by arbitrary labels to the residual light rows it leaves unassigned. (a) Every trigger pair of the path belongs to a host of \(\mathcal H_y\): at a round the current term's tail is satisfied by \(\rho'\cup\pi\), so each of its rows is matched with a consistent label or was assigned a consistent label by the path, which is consistency with \(\zeta_y\). By the both-endpoints lemma the trigger pairs form a matching of pairs \((i,x)\) with \(x\in Q\) and \(i\in R_A\cap U_x(y)\), where \(R_A=R'\cap A\). (b) No host of \(\mathcal H_y\) has a matched pair: if \(h\in\mathcal H_y\) had a matched pair \((i,x)\), then at the node where the first round's term is chosen \(T=[i\to x]\wedge h\) is not falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi\), because its pinned part holds under \(\rho'\), its matched tail rows carry labels of \(\zeta_y\), its residual tail rows assigned so far carry labels of \(y\), and unassigned rows falsify nothing; so the preference chooses at that node a term with a matched pinned pair, whose pinned row is not residual, and no round follows from it.

2. Theorem

Theorem. Fix \(c>0\) and \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\). Let \(N\ge2^{d+7}c'\log_2n\) with \((Nn^{-\varepsilon})^{d+1}\le n^{-c'}/2\), which polylogarithmic \(N\) and large \(n\) give, and let \(n\) be large. Every reader as in Section 1, of any size, has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds on every path before any 1-leaf, with probability at least \(1-4n^{-c-2}\) over \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\); when its light part satisfies the hypotheses of the light lemma it switches under one restriction within the height budget.

Proof. Condition on \(\zeta\). If \(|R_B|\ge r_0\) the bound above applies, so assume \(|R_B|<r_0\). By the two facts, a bad path determines a labeling \(y\) of \(R_B\), one of fewer than \(n^{r_0}\), such that (b) no host of \(\mathcal H_y\) has a matched pair and (a) the alive pairs \(\{(i,x):\ x\in Q,\ i\in R_A\cap U_x(y)\}\) contain a matching of size \(N/48\). Fix \(y\); \(\mathcal H_y\), \(m(y)\), and \(X(y)\) are now fixed. Given \(Q\) and \(\zeta\), the pinned rows form a uniform bijection of \(A\) onto the labels outside \(Q\cup\zeta(B)\) and the \(N+1-|R_B|\) remaining slots, and \(R_A\) is a uniform subset of \(A\) of size at most \(N+1\); given \(\zeta\) alone, \(Q\) is uniform among the flats disjoint from \(\zeta(B)\), a set of at most \(b\) labels, which the uniform flat avoids with probability at least \(1-bN/n\ge1/2\).

(K1) Large consistent mass, \(m(y)\ge(4N+b+3)(n+1)\). The event (b) is contained in the intersection over the labels \(x\notin Q\cup\zeta(B)\) of the events "the occupant of \(x\) lies outside \(U_x(y)\)", which are decreasing on distinct columns of the pinned bijection, each of probability \(1-|U_x(y)|/|A|\); since the labels in \(Q\cup\zeta(B)\) carry at most \((N+b)(n+1)\) of \(m(y)\), negative association gives \(\Pr[\text{(b)}\mid Q,\zeta]\le\exp(-3(N+1)(n+1)/|A|)\le e^{-3(N+1)}\le n^{-c'}\).

(K2) Small consistent mass, \(m(y)<(4N+b+3)(n+1)\). Then \(|X(y)|\le(4N+b+3)(n+1)/D_2^\ast\le810e(N+1)(4N+3)+810e(N+1)n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\) for \(N\ge20\) and \(n\) large. Rounds at labels of \(Q\) outside \(X(y)\): the proof of the activated union lemma, which uses only that \(R_A\) is uniform of size at most \(N+1\) in \(A\) given \(Q\) and \(\zeta\), that \(|A|\ge n/2+N+2\), and that the rows of a \(k\)-matching are chosen from fixed sets of fewer than \(D_2^\ast\) elements, gives fewer than \(N/192\) of them outside probability \(2^{-N/192}\le n^{-c'}\). Rounds at \(X(y)\cap Q\): these have distinct labels, and by the rank lemma in its independent-points form, conditioned on \(\zeta\), \(\Pr[|X(y)\cap Q|\ge2^{d}\mid\zeta]\le2(|X(y)|N/n)^{d+1}\le2(Nn^{-\varepsilon})^{d+1}\le n^{-c'}\), the factor \(2\) paying for the conditioning on \(Q\cap\zeta(B)=\varnothing\). Outside these events the path has fewer than \(N/192+2^{d}\le N/192+N/128<N/48\) rounds, as \(N\ge2^{d+7}\).

Given \(\zeta\) with \(|R_B|<r_0\), the bad event is therefore contained in a union over fewer than \(n^{r_0}\) labelings \(y\) of events of conditional probability at most \(3n^{-c'}=3n^{-c-2}n^{-r_0}\); with the residual-row bound the total is at most \(4n^{-c-2}\). The switching conclusion is the composition recorded in the height budget, with the both-endpoints decoder for role-separated readers. \(\square\)

3. Scope

The theorem has no hypothesis on the hosts or on the size: no heavy or light distinction, no bound on the mass of a row, on the number of terms, patterns, or their widths beyond the light lemma's range for switching, or on the pinned pairs; \(c\) only names the probability. For readers with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows it contains the crowded single light row of any size, hence the case of wide patterns crowded on one row that the pattern-bounded scope named, and readers of unary and mixed terms together, since empty tails are consistent with every labeling. Its cost is the union over the answers at the residual light rows, which is why the light rows must be few: with \(b\) light rows the number of residual ones is bounded by \(r_0\) only when \(bN/n\le n^{-\varepsilon}\), and \(b\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) also keeps the conditioning of the flat on the light rows' labels harmless and the dormant mass at those labels below the mass threshold of (K1). The constants are large (\(d\) is of order \(c/\varepsilon^2\)) and only \(N\) polylogarithmic matters for the route.

The multi-row theorem covers the opposite regime, many light rows of bounded light mass; this one covers few light rows of any mass. The combination is the proposed next step: expose only the crowded light rows, those of light mass above \(M_\varepsilon\), whose number is at most \(n^c/M_\varepsilon\); when this is at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\), which holds for every reader of size \(n^c\) with \(c<3-2\varepsilon-o(1)\), only a bounded number of them are residual, the union bound over their answers costs \(n^{r_0}\), and the hosts consistent with the crowded rows' labels form a reduced reader on the uncrowded rows to which steps (H1) to (H4) apply with the constants raised by \(r_0\), the heavy threshold raised to \(2(N+b_c)(n+1)\) to absorb the mass at the labels the crowded rows occupy, and the rank step conditioned on those labels. That would extend the size corollary from \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\) to \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\). Until then a crowded row among more than \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows at size at least \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\) is covered by neither theorem; the two-role encoding and parity terms remain open.

Verification gate. The exact statements and proofs of the multi-row setting and theorem, the both-endpoints rule, the matched-first preference, the activated union lemma, the rank lemma's independent-points form, the height budget, and the light lemma were re-read from the notebook; the recorded readers of the pigeon-only refutation, the hole-only sparse failure, the adaptive-rule gap, the q-skip refutation, and the two-role example, and the code and window obstructions, were checked against the theorem (they fall in case (K2) with one round or concern other trees or encodings); no rule or encoding changed and no computation was run; the standing reviewer confirmed every step and reported three findings, all applied here: the labeling \(y\) must be the path's final matching on the residual light rows, because a hole query can move a light row without a pigeon query; the reader's size is never used, so the theorem holds at any size with \(c\) a free exponent; and the crowded-row case is closed only for readers with few light rows.

Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. In the literal window, the constant-factor heavy-round bound now also holds for every role-separated mixed reader with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows at every polynomial size, with tails of any shape, which closes the crowded single row in that regime; open are a crowded row among more light rows at sizes at least \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\), the two-role encoding, and parity terms, the open core.

Process assessment. The reviewer was continued from the previous cycle instead of being spawned afresh, as the user asked, and reviewed with the dependency context already loaded; its findings removed an unused size hypothesis and an overclaim before commit. The user also asked for short status lines, so the gate record now sits in its own paragraph here and in the two previous entries, and both preferences are recorded in CLAUDE.md.

18 September 2026 — Crowded rows exposed, spread rows matched: every role-separated reader with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) crowded light rows has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds, hence every one of size below \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\)

Status: working theorem with full proof (role-separated readers of pinned rows with light tails on at most \(t\) rows, any pinned pairs, at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows of light mass above \(M_\varepsilon\)), combining the multi-row theorem and the few-light-rows theorem; corollary: every such reader of size \(n^c\), \(c<3-2\varepsilon\), has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds and switches when its tails lie in the light range. Spin cycle 202. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question and stopping point. The task was the combination proposed last cycle: a crowded light row among many light rows at size at least \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\). The two theorems fit together as planned: the crowded rows are exposed and only a bounded number of them are residual, so a union bound over their assignment fixes which hosts survive, and the survivors, with the crowded rows deleted from their tails, form a reader on the uncrowded rows to which the multi-row steps apply. Three details needed care: hosts that differ only on crowded rows merge, the labels the crowded rows occupy carry mass that a heavy host must dominate, and those labels must not eat a pattern's cube. The stopping point was this theorem with its gate.

1. Crowded rows, the raised heavy threshold, and the reduced reader

A reader is as in the multi-row setting: terms \([i\to x]\wedge\bigwedge_{j\in J}[j\in p_j]\), \(i\in A\), \(J\subseteq B\), \(|J|\le t\), total tail width at most \(W\), \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\), at most \(n^c\) terms. Fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) and \(c>0\), and put \[b_{\max}=\frac{n^{1-\varepsilon}}{N^4},\quad \theta=2(N+b_{\max})(n+1),\quad r_0=\Bigl\lceil\frac{c+2}{\varepsilon}\Bigr\rceil+1,\quad c'=c+2+r_0,\quad d=\Bigl\lceil\frac{c'}{\varepsilon}\Bigr\rceil+2,\] \[J_0=2t\bigl(2^{W+4t}c'\ln n+N+1\bigr),\qquad M_\varepsilon=\frac{n^{2-\varepsilon}}{1600e(N+1)J_0}.\] A host is heavy if \(m_h\ge\theta\) and light otherwise; this threshold replaces \(2N(n+1)\). The light mass of a light row \(j\) is \(m^{\rm L}_j=\sum\{m_h:\ h\text{ light},\ j\in J_h\}\); a light row is crowded if \(m^{\rm L}_j>M_\varepsilon\). Let \(B_{\rm c}\) be the set of crowded rows, \(b_{\rm c}=|B_{\rm c}|\), and \(B_0=B\setminus B_{\rm c}\); all of this is fixed by the reader. Write \(\zeta_{\rm c}\) for the restriction of \(\mu'\) to \(B_{\rm c}\) and \(R_{\rm c}\) for the residual crowded rows.

The reduced reader. For a labeling \(y\) of \(R_{\rm c}\), let \(\zeta_y=\zeta_{\rm c}\cup y\) on \(B_{\rm c}\), and call a host consistent with \(\zeta_y\) if \(\zeta_y(j)\in C(p_{h,j})\) for every \(j\in J_h\cap B_{\rm c}\). The reduced reader \(F_y\) consists of the terms of the consistent hosts with their crowded rows deleted from the tails. Its hosts are the reduced tails, on rows of \(B_0\): a reduced host \(h'\) is the union of the consistent hosts with the same tail on \(B_0\), its pair set \(P_{h'}\) is the union of theirs, and its mass is at most the sum of theirs. A reduced host is heavy or light by the same threshold \(\theta\); if it is light, each of its constituents is light, so the light mass of a row \(j\in B_0\) in \(F_y\) is at most \(m^{\rm L}_j\le M_\varepsilon\). Given \(\zeta_{\rm c}\) and \(y\), \(F_y\) is fixed.

Two facts about a bad path (at least \(N/48\) rounds, no 1-leaf). Let \(y\) be the path's final partial matching restricted to \(R_{\rm c}\), extended by arbitrary labels to the crowded rows it leaves unassigned. (a) Every trigger pair of the path is a pair of a reduced host of \(F_y\) whose reduced tail is satisfied by \(\rho'\cup\pi\) at the round: the round's term's tail is satisfied there, its crowded rows carry labels of \(\zeta_{\rm c}\) or of \(y\), so its host is consistent, and its uncrowded rows are consistent. By the both-endpoints lemma the trigger pairs form a matching of pairs \((i,x)\) with \(x\in Q\) and \(i\in R_A=R'\cap A\). (b) A reduced host with a matched pair contributes no trigger pair, and if moreover all its uncrowded rows are matched with consistent labels there is no round at all: let \((i,x)\) be the matched pair, belonging to a constituent \(h_1\), and let \(T=[i\to x]\wedge h_1\). At the node where a round's term \(T'\) with the same reduced tail is chosen, \(T\) is not falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi\): its pinned part holds under \(\rho'\), its uncrowded rows are those of \(T'\), which is not falsified, and its crowded rows are matched with labels of \(\zeta_{\rm c}\), assigned by the path with labels of \(y\), or unassigned, all consistent with \(\zeta_y\); so the preference chooses a term with a matched pinned pair, whose row is not residual, and no round follows from it. If all uncrowded rows of \(h_1\) are matched consistently, \(T\) is never falsified on the path and the same argument forbids every round.

Residual crowded rows are few. As in the few-light-rows setting, if \(b_{\rm c}\le b_{\max}\) then \(\Pr[|R_{\rm c}|\ge r_0]\le n^{-\varepsilon r_0}\le n^{-c-2}\).

2. Theorem

Theorem. Let \(N\ge2^{d+7}c'\log_2n\) with \((Nn^{-\varepsilon})^{d+1}\le n^{-c'}/2\), let \(J_0\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\), and let \(n\) be large. Every reader as in Section 1 with at most \(b_{\max}\) crowded rows has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds on every path before any 1-leaf, with probability at least \(1-6n^{-c-2}\) over \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\); when its light part satisfies the hypotheses of the light lemma it switches under one restriction within the height budget.

Proof. Condition on \(\zeta_{\rm c}\) and assume \(|R_{\rm c}|<r_0\). By the two facts, a bad path determines a labeling \(y\) of \(R_{\rm c}\), one of fewer than \(n^{r_0}\), such that the alive pairs of the reduced hosts of \(F_y\) without a matched pair, activated on \(B_0\), contain a matching of size \(N/48\). Fix \(y\); \(F_y\) is fixed. Two events independent of \(y\) are excluded first. (E1) Given \(Q\), the labels of the matched crowded rows form a uniform subset of \(Q^c\) of size at most \(b_{\rm c}\); for a pattern \(p\) of width \(w_p\), \(|C(p)\cap\zeta_{\rm c}(B_{\rm c})|\) is a sum of negatively associated indicators with mean at most \(2b_{\rm c}2^{-w_p}\), and \(2^{w_p}\le2^W\le J_0\le n/(8N)\), so the Chernoff bound gives \(\Pr[|C(p)\cap\zeta_{\rm c}(B_{\rm c})|\ge n2^{-w_p}/4]\le(8eb_{\rm c}/n)^{n2^{-w_p}/4}\le n^{-\varepsilon n2^{-w_p}/4}\le n^{-2c'}\), and over at most \(tn^c\) patterns this costs at most \(n^{-c-2}\). Outside (E1), \(|C(p)\setminus(Q\cup\zeta_{\rm c}(B_{\rm c}))|\ge n2^{-w_p}-N-n2^{-w_p}/4\ge n2^{-w_p}/2\) for every pattern. (E2) \(|R_{\rm c}|\ge r_0\), of probability at most \(n^{-c-2}\).

The remaining steps follow the proof of the multi-row theorem for \(F_y\), with \(c'\) in place of \(c+1\) and these changes. Given \(Q\) and \(\zeta_{\rm c}\), the rows of \(A\cup B_0\) form a uniform bijection onto the labels outside \(Q\cup\zeta_{\rm c}(B_{\rm c})\) and the remaining slots, so the occupant of such a label is uniform on \(A\cup B_0\) and lies in a set \(V\subseteq A\) with probability at least \(|V|/(n+1)\); the labels in \(Q\cup\zeta_{\rm c}(B_{\rm c})\) number at most \(N+b_{\rm c}\le N+b_{\max}\) and carry at most \((N+b_{\max})(n+1)=\theta/2\) of any host's mass.

(H1) Heavy reduced hosts have a matched pair. Given \(Q\) and \(\zeta_{\rm c}\), for a heavy reduced host the product over the columns outside \(Q\cup\zeta_{\rm c}(B_{\rm c})\) of the decreasing events "the occupant lies outside \(I_{h',x}\)" is at most \(\exp(-(m_{h'}-\theta/2)/(n+1))\le e^{-(N+b_{\max})}\le n^{-c'-c}\); over at most \(n^c\) reduced hosts (each contains a term) this costs \(n^{-c'}\). Outside it, by fact (b), the trigger pairs come from light reduced hosts; let \(U^{\rm L}_x=\bigcup_{h'\text{ light}}I_{h',x}\) and \(X_{\rm L}=\{x:\ |U^{\rm L}_x|\ge D_2^\ast\}\), fixed given \(\zeta_{\rm c}\) and \(y\).

(H2) Labels outside \(X_{\rm L}\). Given \(Q\) and the whole light assignment \(\zeta\), \(R_A\) is a uniform subset of \(A\) of size at most \(N+1\) and \(|A|\ge n/2+N+2\), so the count of the activated union lemma gives fewer than \(N/192\) rounds at labels outside \(X_{\rm L}\) outside probability \(2^{-N/192}\le n^{-2c'}\), as \(N\ge384c'\log_2n\).

(H3) \(|X_{\rm L}|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\). Given \(\zeta_{\rm c}\), \(Q\) is uniform among the flats disjoint from \(\zeta_{\rm c}(B_{\rm c})\), which the uniform flat avoids with probability at least \(1-b_{\rm c}N/n\ge1/2\), so \(\Pr[|X_{\rm L}\cap Q|\ge2^d\mid\zeta_{\rm c}]\le2(Nn^{-\varepsilon})^{d+1}\le n^{-c'}\); outside this event a bad path has fewer than \(N/192+2^d<N/48\) rounds, as \(N\ge2^{d+7}\).

(H4) \(|X_{\rm L}|>n^{1-\varepsilon}\), so \(\Omega_{\rm L}=\sum_x|U^{\rm L}_x|>n^{2-\varepsilon}/(800e(N+1))\). (H4a) For \(J\subseteq B_0\) with \(|J|<J_0\), the light reduced hosts disjoint from \(J\) have \(\sum_x|V_x(J)|\ge\Omega_{\rm L}-J_0M_\varepsilon\ge n^{2-\varepsilon}/(1600e(N+1))\), since the light mass of \(F_y\) at a row of \(B_0\) is at most \(M_\varepsilon\); the labels in \(Q\cup\zeta_{\rm c}(B_{\rm c})\) carry at most \(\theta/2\le2n^{1-\varepsilon}(n+1)/N^4\) (as \(N<J_0\le b_{\max}\)), and \(N(n+1)J_0\le(n+1)n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^3\), so \(\sum_{x\notin Q\cup\zeta_{\rm c}(B_{\rm c})}|V_x(J)|\ge N(n+1)J_0\) once \(N^3\ge1600e(N+1)(n+1)(2/N+1)/n\), which \(N\ge100\) gives. Given \(Q\) and \(\zeta_{\rm c}\), the product over these columns bounds the probability that no light reduced host disjoint from \(J\) has a matched pair by \(e^{-NJ_0}\), and the union over fewer than \(n^{J_0}\) sets \(J\) costs at most \(e^{-J_0N/2}\le n^{-c'}\), as \(N\ge2\ln n\) and \(J_0\ge2c'\ln n\). (H4b) Outside it, among the light reduced hosts with a matched pair, one with an empty reduced tail forbids every round by fact (b); otherwise a maximal row-disjoint family \(\mathcal M'\) has \(|\mathcal M'|\ge J_0/t\) and \(|B_0|\ge J_0\), exactly as before. (H4c) Expose also \(R_A\) and the images of the pinned rows. The set \(\mathrm{rem}\) of labels outside \(Q\cup\zeta_{\rm c}(B_{\rm c})\) not taken by pinned rows is a uniform subset of \(Q^c\setminus\zeta_{\rm c}(B_{\rm c})\) of size \(|B_0|-s_0\), where \(s_0\le N+1\) is the number of slots left for \(B_0\), so \(|\mathrm{rem}|\ge|B_0|-N-1\ge J_0-N-1\); outside (E1), \(\mathbb E|C(p)\cap\mathrm{rem}|\ge|\mathrm{rem}|2^{-w_p}/2\ge16c'\ln n\) for every pattern, and the Chernoff bound with a union over at most \(tn^c\) patterns gives \(|C(p)\cap\mathrm{rem}|\ge2^{-w_p}|\mathrm{rem}|/4\) for all of them outside probability \(n^{-c'}\). Given all exposed data the rows of \(B_0\) form a uniform bijection onto \(\mathrm{rem}\) and the slots; for \(h'\in\mathcal M'\) with its matched pair \((i,x)\) in a constituent \(h_1\), the event \(E_{h'}\) that every row \(j\) of the reduced tail has \(\mu'(j)\in C(p_{h',j})\cap\mathrm{rem}\) has probability at least \(2^{-W-4t}\) by the row-by-row count of the multi-row proof, with \(|\mathrm{rem}|/|B_0|\ge1-1/(2t)\) because \(J_0\ge2t(N+1)\); on \(E_{h'}\) all uncrowded rows of \(h_1\) are matched consistently, which by fact (b) forbids every round. The events \(E_{h'}\) are increasing on disjoint row sets, so \(\Pr[\text{no }E_{h'}]\le\exp(-(J_0/t)2^{-W-4t})\le n^{-2c'}\).

For fixed \(y\) the excluded events total at most \(3n^{-c'}+2n^{-2c'}\le4n^{-c'}\); over fewer than \(n^{r_0}\) labelings this is \(4n^{-c-2}\), and with (E1) and (E2) the total is at most \(6n^{-c-2}\). The switching conclusion is the composition recorded in the height budget, with the both-endpoints decoder for role-separated readers. \(\square\)

3. Corollary: size below \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\)

Corollary. Under the theorem's conditions on \(N\) and \(J_0\), every reader as in Section 1 with \(1600e\,t(N+1)N^4J_0\,n^c\le n^{3-2\varepsilon}\) has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds on every path before any 1-leaf with probability at least \(1-6n^{-c-2}\), and switches within the height budget when its tails lie in the light lemma's range.

Proof. A host with \(k\le t\) rows is counted in the light mass of \(k\) rows, so \(\sum_jm^{\rm L}_j\le t\sum_hm_h\le tn^c\), and the crowded rows number at most \(tn^c/M_\varepsilon=1600e\,t(N+1)J_0n^{c-2+\varepsilon}\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4=b_{\max}\). \(\square\)

With \(N\) and \(J_0\) polylogarithmic the condition reads \(c\le3-2\varepsilon-o(1)\), against \(2-\varepsilon\) for the previous corollary; the tails must still satisfy \(J_0\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\), that is \(W+4t+\log_2t\le(1-\varepsilon)\log_2n-O(\log\log n)\), and the light lemma's per-row range for switching.

4. Scope

The theorem contains part (ii) of the multi-row theorem for readers whose \(\theta\)-light mass exceeds \(M_\varepsilon\) on at most \(b_{\max}\) rows, in particular for every reader below size \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}/\mathrm{polylog}\); not in general, since a host of mass between \(2N(n+1)\) and \(\theta\) is heavy there and light here, and a reader with \(n/4\) light rows each hosting one such host has \(M_{\rm row}=0\) there but \(n/4\) crowded rows here. For readers all of whose light rows are crowded the proof reduces to the few-light-rows argument plus the mass step (H1); that theorem's hypotheses are weaker (no bound on rows per term, width, or size), so neither contains the other. The raised threshold \(\theta\) costs nothing in the corollary, since the corollary counts crowded rows through the total light mass, which only shrinks when more hosts are heavy. The exponent \(3-2\varepsilon\) comes from two uses of \(n^{1-\varepsilon}\): the rank step tolerates \(n^{1-\varepsilon}\) labels of large light union, which puts the crowded threshold at \(n^{2-\varepsilon}/\mathrm{polylog}\), and the exposure tolerates \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) crowded rows. Both are the same limitation: a set of size \(n^{1-\varepsilon}\) (labels in one case, light rows in the other) is what the rank lemma and the residual-row count keep away from the flat and the slots with polynomially small failure.

What remains in the window: readers of size \(n^c\), \(c\ge3-2\varepsilon\), with more than \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) crowded rows, where neither exposing the crowded rows nor spreading their mass applies; a second level of the same dichotomy (crowded rows whose union of pinned rows is large versus small) is the natural continuation but is not attempted here. The two-role encoding and parity terms remain open.

Verification gate. The exact statements and proofs of the multi-row theorem and the few-light-rows theorem (setting, steps, scope), the both-endpoints rule, the matched-first preference, the activated union lemma, the rank lemma's independent-points form, the height budget, and the light lemma were re-read from the notebook; the recorded readers of the pigeon-only refutation, the hole-only sparse failure, the adaptive-rule gap, the q-skip refutation, and the two-role example, and the code and window obstructions, were checked against the theorem (no crowded rows, case (H3) with at most one round, or other trees, encodings, or roles); no rule or encoding changed and no computation was run; the standing reviewer confirmed every definition, fact, and step, found every hypothesis used, and reported four findings, all applied here: the per-labeling total needed the sharper bound of step (H2); the containment of the multi-row theorem holds only below size \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}/\mathrm{polylog}\), and neither theorem contains the few-light-rows theorem; the corollary must carry the bound on \(|B|\); and step (H4a) uses \(N\le b_{\max}\).

Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. In the literal window, the constant-factor heavy-round bound now holds for every role-separated mixed reader of size below \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\) with tails on boundedly many rows of total width below \((1-\varepsilon)\log_2n\), and for readers of any size with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) crowded rows; open are larger sizes with more crowded rows, the two-role encoding, and parity terms, the open core.

Process assessment. The standing reviewer returned in a few minutes with the context of both earlier entries loaded, and its findings were a constant slip, an overclaimed containment, and two wordings, none in the argument; the combination was drafted directly from the two committed proofs without a computation. No framework change is needed.

18 September 2026 — The complete-term rule closes the two-role encoding gap: rounds before tails, every row of a current term assigned, a decoder for rows pinned in one term and light in another, and switching for two-role readers with few light rows

Status: working tree rule with a decoder lemma (verified by exhaustive round trips, including the recorded two-role counterexample), a transfer lemma for every recorded round bound, and a working theorem with full proof (two-role readers with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows switch within the height budget when their light part satisfies the light lemma's hypotheses with sparse pinning). Spin cycle 203. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question and stopping point. The task was the two-role encoding. The gap is a pinned row of a current term left unassigned when the term's tail fails, then moved by a later term as a light row, so that the decoder sees the earlier term falsified. The obvious repair, assigning the pinned row by its pigeon query before the tail is examined, was dismissed there as costing a heavy query with no gain; on the both-endpoints tree every round already contains that pigeon query, so the repair is only a change of order plus the rule that the tail rows are queried whatever the round's outcome. The round-trip tool, extended with this rule, decodes the recorded two-role counterexample and random two-role readers without failure. The stopping point was the rule, its decoder, the transfer of the round bounds, and the two-role form of the few-light-rows theorem, whose probabilistic steps tolerate two-role rows because the light rows are exposed.

1. The complete-term rule

Readers are as in the multi-row setting except that a row may be pinned in one term and light in another: \(A\) is the set of rows pinned in some term, \(B\) the set of rows light in some term, and \(C=A\cap B\) may be nonempty; \(X_i\) denotes the set of labels to which row \(i\) is pinned in some term. Rule. At a node, the current term is chosen by the matched-first preference. If its pinned pair \((i,x)\) is alive (\(i\) residual and unassigned, \(x\in Q\) unkilled), the heavy round of the both-endpoints rule comes first: query the pigeon \(i\), and on a branch \(i\mapsto y\ne x\) query the hole \(x\). Then, whatever the round's outcome, query the term's uncovered tail rows in the term's order; a 1-leaf is a node where some term is satisfied by \(\rho'\cup\pi\), and a term whose pinned pair is killed with its row unassigned (its hole used by another row or emptied) counts as falsified. So every row of a current term is assigned at its node, except in a round cut by the height bound. Encoding. The extension encoding of the light lemma with the round's answers recorded in \(\delta\) before the node's light answers, \(\beta\) marking the moved rows and the round's length, and the code label of a moved row \(j\) with pattern \(p\) chosen in \(E(\rho)\cap C(p)\setminus X_j\), the free outside labels consistent with \(p\) to which \(j\) is pinned nowhere. Call \(\rho\) \(s\)-rich' if \(|E(\rho)\cap C(p)\setminus X_j|\ge s\) for every light row \(j\) and pattern \(p\) of a term on \(j\).

Lemma 1 (rounds). On every path the trigger pairs of the rounds are pairwise disjoint pairs \((i,x)\) with \(i\in R'\), \(x\in Q\), whose host is not falsified by \(\rho'\) and has no matched pair; so the rounds number at most \(\nu(B_{\rm t})\le N\), the heavy queries at most twice that, and each round's answers take at most \((N+e)(N+2)\) values. Proof. Disjointness as in the both-endpoints lemma: after the round \(i\) is assigned and \(x\) is used or emptied. At the node the current term is not falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi\), so its host is not falsified by \(\rho'\); and if its host had a matched pair \((i',x')\), the term \([i'\to x']\wedge h\) would be falsified there (otherwise the preference chooses a term with a matched pinned pair, which has no residual pinned row and makes no round), its pinned part holds, so its tail, the current term's tail, would be falsified, a contradiction. \(\square\)

Lemma 2 (transfer). Every recorded round bound holds on the complete-term tree: those of the multi-row theorem and its predecessors as stated, since their proofs use of the tree only Lemma 1; those of the few-light-rows theorem and the combined theorem with fewer than \(r_0\) rounds added, absorbed by their thresholds. Proof. In the latter two, fact (a) placed every round's host in the family \(\mathcal H_y\) consistent with the exposed rows' final labels, using that the tail was satisfied at the round. On the complete-term tree a round precedes its tail, so its host may instead be falsified by the path's answer at an exposed residual row \(j\) assigned later in the same node; the rows a cut last node leaves unassigned belong to its current term alone, and \(y\) is extended to them consistently with that term, so no other host leaves \(\mathcal H_y\). Such a round is charged to \(j\), assigned at that node and at no other, so these rounds number at most \(|R_B|\), respectively \(|R_{\rm c}|\), fewer than \(r_0\) outside the excluded event; all other rounds have hosts in \(\mathcal H_y\) and are counted as before, and fact (b) is unchanged, as it argues at the node where the round's term is chosen. The final counts \(N/192+2^d+r_0\) stay below \(N/48\) because \(N\ge2^{d+7}c'\log_2n\ge256r_0\). \(\square\)

2. The decoder for two-role readers

Lemma 3 (decoder). For every reader, two-role rows allowed, the encoding of a rich' bad path of the complete-term tree is decodable, with the count of the light lemma's encoding lemma and the round costs of Lemma 1. Proof. The decoder starts from \(\alpha=\rho^\ast\) and processes the nodes of the path in order; at each node it applies the preference with falsification tested on \(\alpha\) and a pinned pair counted as matched when \(\rho^\ast\) matches its row to its label, reads the round's answers from \(\delta\) if \(\beta\) says there was one, identifies the moved rows from \(\beta\), and reassigns them to their holes from \(\delta\). At node \(m\), \(\alpha\) agrees with \(\rho'\cup\pi_{<m}\) on matched rows and on rows assigned before \(m\), and additionally matches rows moved at or after \(m\) to code labels. Three claims. (i) The matched status computed from \(\rho^\ast\) is that of \(\mu'\): a row matched by \(\rho'\) has the same label in \(\rho^\ast\); a residual row that is moved carries a code label outside \(X_i\), so no pinned pair at it counts as matched, as in \(\rho'\); every other row is residual in \(\rho^\ast\), as in \(\mu'\). (ii) Every term preceding the current term \(T_m\) in the preference is falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi_{<m}\), through a row on which \(\alpha\) agrees, or through a killed pair recorded in \(\rho'\) or \(\delta\), so it is falsified by \(\alpha\). (iii) \(T_m\) is not falsified by \(\alpha\): its rows assigned before \(m\) are consistent, its tail rows moved at node \(m\) carry consistent code labels, a tail row assigned at node \(m\) by the round's hole query is unassigned in \(\alpha\) when \(T_m\) is identified and receives its hole from \(\delta\) afterwards, its pinned row, if alive at \(m\), is queried at \(m\) as a pigeon, hence never moved, and is unassigned in \(\alpha\), and it has no other rows, because the rule assigns every row of a current term at its node (a cut last round leaves rows unassigned in both). So the decoder finds \(T_m\), whether it is the earliest matched-pair term or the earliest term, then its round and its moved rows; after the last node it deletes the moved rows and recovers \(\rho'\). \(\square\)

Lemma 4 (richness'). If \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\), \(e\ge2^{w+3}s\), and the reader is sparsely pinned, \(|X_j\cap C(p)|\le|C(p)|/4\) for every light row \(j\) and pattern \(p\) of a term on \(j\), then \(\Pr_{\rho\in\Phi_e}[\rho\text{ not }s\text{-rich'}]\le Mr\,e^{-e2^{-w-5}}\). Proof. As in the richness lemma, \(|C(p)\cap O|\ge n2^{-|p|-1}\), so \(|(C(p)\setminus X_j)\cap O|\ge n2^{-|p|-2}\); \(E(\rho)\) is a uniform \(e\)-subset of \(O\), so \(|E(\rho)\cap C(p)\setminus X_j|\) is hypergeometric with mean at least \(e2^{-w-2}\ge2s\), and the Chernoff bound gives \(\Pr[\cdot<s]\le e^{-e2^{-w-5}}\); there are at most \(Mr\) pairs \((j,p)\). \(\square\) A role-separated reader has \(X_j=\varnothing\) on its light rows and is sparsely pinned; so is any reader whose rows are pinned to at most \(n2^{-w-2}\) labels each.

Consequently the light lemma, the both-endpoints round costs, and the composition of the height budget hold for every sparsely pinned reader on the complete-term tree, and a two-role reader switches within the height budget as soon as its rounds are fewer than \(N/48\) on every bad path.

3. Theorem: two-role readers with few light rows

Theorem. Let \(\varepsilon\), \(c\), \(r_0\), \(c'\), \(d\), and \(N\) be as in the few-light-rows theorem, and let a reader have light rows \(B\) with \(b=|B|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\), two-role rows allowed, tails of any shape, any pinned pairs, any size. On the complete-term tree it has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds on every path before any 1-leaf with probability at least \(1-4n^{-c-2}\); if it is sparsely pinned and its light part satisfies the light lemma's hypotheses with \(e\ge2^{w+3}s\), it switches under one restriction within the height budget.

Proof. Write \(A_0\) for the rows outside \(B\). Condition on \(\zeta=\mu'|_B\), which fixes the labels and the residual status of every row of \(B\), including \(C\); outside the event \(|R_B|\ge r_0\), of probability at most \(n^{-c-2}\), fewer than \(r_0\) light rows are residual. Given \(Q\) and \(\zeta\), the rows of \(A_0\) form a uniform bijection onto the labels outside \(Q\cup\zeta(B)\) and the remaining slots, and \(R_{A_0}=R'\cap A_0\) is a uniform subset of \(A_0\) of size at most \(N+1\), with \(|A_0|=n+1-b\ge n/2+N+2\). For a bad path let \(y\) be its final matching on \(R_B\), extended to the rows a cut last node leaves unassigned consistently with that node's current term and arbitrarily otherwise, and \(\mathcal H_y\), \(U_x(y)\subseteq A\), \(m(y)\), \(X(y)\) as in the few-light-rows setting. Its rounds are of three kinds: (1) rounds whose host is falsified by the path at a residual light row assigned at the round's node, fewer than \(r_0\) by the charging of Lemma 2; (2) rounds whose pinned row lies in \(C\), hence in \(C\cap R_B\), fewer than \(r_0\), one per row; (3) rounds with host in \(\mathcal H_y\) and pinned row in \(R_{A_0}\). Fact (b) holds as before: a host of \(\mathcal H_y\) with a matched pair has a term never falsified on the path, so the preference forbids every round; for a pair at a row of \(C\) the matched status is fixed by \(\zeta\), and on a bad path no such pair of a host of \(\mathcal H_y\) is matched. Fix \(y\), one of fewer than \(n^{r_0}\) labelings. (K1) If \(m(y)\ge(4N+2b+3)(n+1)\): the pairs at rows of \(C\) carry at most \(b(n+1)\) of \(m(y)\), the labels in \(Q\cup\zeta(B)\) at most \((N+b)(n+1)\), so the rows of \(A_0\) carry at least \(3(N+1)(n+1)\) at labels outside \(Q\cup\zeta(B)\), and the product over those columns of the \(A_0\)-bijection gives \(\Pr[\text{no host of }\mathcal H_y\text{ matched}\mid Q,\zeta]\le e^{-3(N+1)}\le n^{-c'}\). (K2) Otherwise \(|X(y)|\le(4N+2b+3)(n+1)/D_2^\ast\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\) for \(N\ge25\); rounds of kind (3) at labels outside \(X(y)\) are fewer than \(N/192\) outside probability \(2^{-N/192}\) by the union-lemma count over \(R_{A_0}\), and \(|X(y)\cap Q|<2^d\) outside probability \(2(Nn^{-\varepsilon})^{d+1}\le n^{-c'}\) by the rank lemma conditioned on \(\zeta\). In all, at most \((N/192-1)+(2^d-1)+2(r_0-1)<N/48\) rounds outside a total probability of \(4n^{-c-2}\), as \(2^d\le N/128\) and \(2r_0\le N/128\) for \(N\ge2^{d+7}\) and \(N\ge256r_0\). The switching clause is Lemma 3 with Lemma 4 and the height budget. \(\square\)

4. Verification

The round-trip tool gained --rule complete (runs and parameters). On eight-label boards with \(N=2\) and \(e=3\): the recorded two-role counterexample, 6640 rich bad paths, 0 failures under the complete-term rule against 1800 of 6380 under the both-endpoints rule rerun as the control; two random two-role readers, 5759 and 1076 rich bad paths, 0 failures; two role-separated readers, 1851 and 4978, 0 failures. Every path had at most four heavy queries.

5. Scope

The rule removes the encoding obstacle recorded in the two-role correction for every sparsely pinned reader, at the price of rounds that the tail-first tree avoided (a term whose tail fails after its round); Lemma 2 shows these cost nothing in the recorded bounds. What the rule does not give is a two-role round bound for readers with many light rows. Steps (H1) to (H3) and (H4a) of the multi-row and combined theorems are role-independent (the residual rows are a uniform set of all rows given \(Q\), and the occupant products run over all rows), but step (H4c) is not: after the pinned images are exposed the labels of the rows of \(C=A\cap B\) are fixed, the light bijection is of \(B\setminus C\) only, and the events \(E_h\) of hosts that use rows of \(C\) are determined rather than random, while (H4a) and (H4b) would have to take \(J\supseteq C\). The few-light-rows theorem avoids this because it exposes all light rows and charges their fewer than \(r_0\) residual ones. Sparse pinning fails for a row pinned to more than a quarter of some pattern's cube; such rows need code labels chosen otherwise or a recorded answer. The remaining open cases in the window are therefore: two-role readers with more than \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows, where step (H4c) loses the two-role rows, densely pinned rows, sizes at least \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\) with many crowded rows, and parity terms.

Verification gate. The exact statements and proofs of the two-role correction, the both-endpoints rule, the matched-first preference, the light lemma with its encoding, richness, and decoder arguments, the height budget, the few-light-rows setting and theorem, the multi-row setting and theorem, and the combined setting and theorem were re-read from the notebook; the recorded readers and obstructions (the q-skip refutation, the code obstruction, the two-role example, the recording-rule cost argument, the pigeon-only and hole-only refutations) were checked against the rule and the theorem; the rule changed the tree, so the exhaustive checker was extended and run (six runs, two controls, all as recorded in Section 4); the standing reviewer confirmed Lemmas 1, 2, 4 and the theorem and reported six findings, all applied here: the decoder's matched test must run on the code, not on the running assignment, as the tool does; the term-identification claims needed the hole-move case, the preference order, and the killed-pair convention; the rows outside the light rows are all rows outside \(B\), not only pinned ones; a cut last node needs the labeling extended consistently with its term; the two-role obstruction for many light rows lies in step (H4c), not in the residual pinned rows; and the final count needed its slack stated.

Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. In the literal window, the encoding now covers two-role readers with sparse pinning, so switching for a two-role reader reduces to its round bound; that bound is proved for two-role readers with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows at every size, and remains open for two-role readers with many light rows, alongside large sizes with many crowded rows, dense pinning, and parity terms, the open core.

Process assessment. The cycle followed the gate's order for a rule change: the candidate rule was tested with the round-trip tool on the recorded counterexample before any proof was written, and the standing reviewer, with the encoding lemma freshly re-read, caught that the draft's decoder differed from the tool's in its matched test. No framework change is needed.

18 September 2026 — Two-role readers with many light rows: the combined theorem on the complete-term tree when the two-role rows outside the exposed set carry bounded light mass, hence every two-role reader of size below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\) switches under sparse pinning

Status: working theorem with full proof (two-role readers with tails on at most \(t\) rows, an exposed set of at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows containing the crowded ones, and light mass at most \(n^{2-\varepsilon}/(3200e(N+1))\) on the two-role rows outside it), with corollaries for sizes below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\) (no further hypothesis) and below \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\) (few or light two-role rows). Spin cycle 204. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question and stopping point. The task was the obstruction named last cycle: in step (H4c) of the multi-row theorem, exposing the pinned images fixes the labels of the rows of \(C=A\cap B\), which then drop out of the light bijection, so the greedy family's events at those rows are no longer random. The intended statement, the round bound for every two-role reader of bounded per-row mass, was tested first against a reader all of whose rows are two-role (terms \([i\to x]\wedge[i+1\in p]\) for every row and label): there every host whose pinned row is matched has a matched pair, and one of them is satisfied by the light bijection with high probability, so the reader is not a counterexample, but the test showed no way to keep the rows of \(C\) in the greedy family in general. The proof therefore keeps the greedy family off the rows of \(C\), which costs their light mass in step (H4a); two-role rows that are few are exposed instead, like crowded rows. The stopping point was this theorem with its gate.

1. Setting

A reader is as in the combined setting (tails on at most \(t\) rows, total width at most \(W\), at most \(n^c\) terms; the combined setting's bound on \(|B|\) is not needed) except that \(A\), the rows pinned in some term, may meet \(B\), the rows light in some term; \(C=A\cap B\). It is read by the complete-term tree. Fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), \(c>0\), and take \(b_{\max}\), \(r_0\), \(c'\), \(d\), \(J_0\), \(M_\varepsilon\) as in the combined setting, but with the heavy threshold \[\theta=2(N+2b_{\max})(n+1)\qquad\text{and}\qquad M_C=\frac{n^{2-\varepsilon}}{3200e(N+1)}.\] Light hosts, the light mass \(m^{\rm L}_j\) of a light row, and crowded rows (\(m^{\rm L}_j>M_\varepsilon\)) are defined with this \(\theta\). An exposed set is a set \(B_{\rm e}\subseteq B\) of at most \(b_{\max}\) light rows containing every crowded row; write \(B_0=B\setminus B_{\rm e}\), \(C_0=C\cap B_0\), \(\zeta_{\rm e}=\mu'|_{B_{\rm e}}\), \(R_{\rm e}\) for the residual exposed rows, and \(A_{\rm out}\) for the rows outside \(B_{\rm e}\). The reduced reader \(F_y\) for a labeling \(y\) of \(R_{\rm e}\), its hosts, and the two facts about a bad path are as in the combined setting, with \(y\) the path's final matching on \(R_{\rm e}\) extended as in Lemma 2 of the complete-term rule; on the complete-term tree the rounds whose host is falsified at an exposed row assigned at the round's node are fewer than \(r_0\), and so are the rounds whose pinned row lies in \(R_{\rm e}\), one per row. Every other round of a bad path has its host in \(F_y\), without a matched pair, and its pinned row in \(R'\cap A_{\rm out}\).

2. Theorem

Theorem. Let \(N\ge2^{d+7}c'\log_2n\) with \((Nn^{-\varepsilon})^{d+1}\le n^{-c'}/2\), let \(J_0\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\), and let \(n\) be large. A reader as in Section 1 with an exposed set \(B_{\rm e}\) such that \(\sum_{j\in C_0}m^{\rm L}_j\le M_C\) has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds on every path of the complete-term tree before any 1-leaf, with probability at least \(1-6n^{-c-2}\); if it is sparsely pinned and its light part satisfies the light lemma's hypotheses with \(e\ge2^{w+3}s\), it switches under one restriction within the height budget.

Proof. The proof of the combined theorem is followed step by step with \(B_{\rm e}\) in place of \(B_{\rm c}\); the exposure of \(B_{\rm e}\), the bound \(\Pr[|R_{\rm e}|\ge r_0]\le n^{-c-2}\), the union over fewer than \(n^{r_0}\) labelings \(y\), the event (E1), and the reduced reader are unchanged, and the following points are where two-role rows enter. Given \(Q\) and \(\zeta_{\rm e}\), the rows of \(A_{\rm out}\), of which there are \(n+1-|B_{\rm e}|\ge n/2+N+2\), form a uniform bijection onto the labels outside \(Q\cup\zeta_{\rm e}(B_{\rm e})\) and the remaining slots; the occupant of such a label is uniform on \(A_{\rm out}\), and \(R'\cap A_{\rm out}\) is a uniform subset of \(A_{\rm out}\) of size at most \(N+1\). A pair \((i,x)\) with \(i\in A\cap B_{\rm e}\) has its matched status fixed by \(\zeta_{\rm e}\); these pairs are excluded from the products below, and their mass, at most \(|B_{\rm e}|\,n\le b_{\max}n\) of any host's, is subtracted. Two-role rows in \(B_0\), the set \(C_0\), are pinned rows whose labels the pinned images fix; their light mass is at most \(M_C\) in total by hypothesis.

(H1) A heavy reduced host has, at rows of \(A_{\rm out}\) and labels outside \(Q\cup\zeta_{\rm e}(B_{\rm e})\), mass at least \(m_{h'}-(N+b_{\max})(n+1)-b_{\max}n\ge\theta/2\), so the product over those columns of the \(A_{\rm out}\)-bijection bounds the probability of no matched pair by \(e^{-(N+2b_{\max})}\le n^{-c'-c}\), and the union over at most \(n^c\) reduced hosts costs \(n^{-c'}\). Outside it every trigger pair of a bad path, other than the fewer than \(2r_0\) charged to exposed rows, belongs to a light reduced host and has its row in \(R'\cap A_{\rm out}\); \(U^{\rm L}_x\) and \(X_{\rm L}\) are as before, fixed given \(\zeta_{\rm e}\) and \(y\).

(H2) The count of the activated union lemma, over rows of \(U^{\rm L}_x\cap A_{\rm out}\) with \(R'\cap A_{\rm out}\) uniform of size at most \(N+1\) in a set of at least \(n/2+N+2\) rows, gives fewer than \(N/192\) such rounds at labels outside \(X_{\rm L}\) outside probability \(2^{-N/192}\le n^{-2c'}\). (H3) If \(|X_{\rm L}|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\), the rank step conditioned on \(\zeta_{\rm e}\) gives \(|X_{\rm L}\cap Q|<2^d\) outside probability \(n^{-c'}\). Both steps are role-independent.

(H4) If \(|X_{\rm L}|>n^{1-\varepsilon}\), so that \(\Omega_{\rm L}>n^{2-\varepsilon}/(800e(N+1))\). (H4a) For \(J\subseteq B_0\) with \(|J|<J_0\), the light reduced hosts whose reduced tails avoid \(J\cup C_0\) have, over all labels, union mass at least \(\Omega_{\rm L}-J_0M_\varepsilon-\sum_{j\in C_0}m^{\rm L}_j\ge n^{2-\varepsilon}/(1600e(N+1))-M_C=M_C\), since a light reduced host meeting \(J\cup C_0\) is counted in the light mass of a row of \(J\) or of \(C_0\), and the light mass of \(F_y\) at a row is at most that of the reader; the labels in \(Q\cup\zeta_{\rm e}(B_{\rm e})\) carry at most \((N+b_{\max})(n+1)\) of it and the rows of \(A\cap B_{\rm e}\) at most \(b_{\max}n\), so over the labels outside \(Q\cup\zeta_{\rm e}(B_{\rm e})\) and the rows of \(A_{\rm out}\) at least \(M_C-(N+2b_{\max})(n+1)\ge N(n+1)J_0\) remains, because \(N<J_0\le b_{\max}\) and \(N^3\ge3200e(N+1)(n+1)(3/N+1)/n\), which \(N\ge128\) gives. The product over those columns bounds the probability that no such host has a matched pair by \(e^{-NJ_0}\), and the union over fewer than \(n^{J_0}\) sets \(J\) costs at most \(n^{-c'}\). (H4b) Outside it, expose the residual status and the images of all rows outside \(B_0\setminus C_0\), which fixes the set \(\mathcal M\) of light reduced hosts with a matched pair and the labels of \(C_0\). A host of \(\mathcal M\) with an empty reduced tail forbids every round by fact (b). Otherwise choose greedily a maximal family \(\mathcal M'\) of hosts of \(\mathcal M\) whose reduced tails avoid \(C_0\) and are pairwise disjoint, and put \(J'=\bigcup_{h'\in\mathcal M'}J_{h'}\subseteq B_0\setminus C_0\). Every host of \(\mathcal M\) meets \(J'\cup C_0\), so \(|J'|\ge J_0\): otherwise (H4a) with \(J=J'\) gives a matched light reduced host avoiding \(J'\cup C_0\), which \(\mathcal M'\) could contain. Hence \(|\mathcal M'|\ge J_0/t\) and \(|B_0\setminus C_0|\ge J_0\). (H4c) The set \(\mathrm{rem}\) of labels outside \(Q\cup\zeta_{\rm e}(B_{\rm e})\) not taken by pinned rows has size \(|B_0\setminus C_0|-s_0\ge J_0-N-1\), with \(s_0\le N+1\) the slots left for \(B_0\setminus C_0\), and is a uniform subset of \(Q^c\setminus\zeta_{\rm e}(B_{\rm e})\) given \(Q\), \(\zeta_{\rm e}\), and the residual rows among the rows whose images are exposed; the Chernoff step for \(|C(p)\cap\mathrm{rem}|\) is as before, using (E1). Given all exposed data the rows of \(B_0\setminus C_0\) form a uniform bijection onto \(\mathrm{rem}\) and the slots, the events \(E_{h'}\), \(h'\in\mathcal M'\), concern pairwise disjoint sets of those rows, each has probability at least \(2^{-W-4t}\) by the row-by-row count with \(|\mathrm{rem}|/|B_0\setminus C_0|\ge1-1/(2t)\), each forbids every round by the strengthened fact (b), and negative association gives \(\Pr[\text{no }E_{h'}]\le\exp(-(J_0/t)2^{-W-4t})\le n^{-2c'}\).

For fixed \(y\) the excluded events total at most \(4n^{-c'}\); with the union over labelings, (E1), and the residual-row event, at most \(6n^{-c-2}\). Outside them a bad path has fewer than \(N/192+2^d+2r_0<N/48\) rounds, each summand strict, as \(2^d\le N/128\) and \(2r_0\le N/128\). The switching clause is the two-role decoder with its richness lemma and the height budget. \(\square\)

3. Corollaries

Corollary 1 (size below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\)). Under the multi-row theorem's conditions on \(N\), if \(1\le c<2-\varepsilon\) and \(800e(N+1)\le n^{2-\varepsilon-c}\), every two-role reader with at most \(n^c\) terms, whatever its tails, has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds on every path of the complete-term tree before any 1-leaf with probability at least \(1-3n^{-c-1}\), and switches within the height budget under sparse pinning when its tails lie in the light lemma's range. Proof. Steps (H1) to (H3) of the multi-row theorem are role-independent, as the complete-term scope records: given \(Q\) alone the residual rows form a uniform set of at most \(N+1\) of all rows and the occupant products run over all rows, so the union lemma of (H2) applies to \(R'\cap U^{\rm L}_x\) with all \(n+1\) rows in place of \(A\). Hence part (i) of that theorem holds for two-role readers, on the complete-term tree by Lemma 2 with no added rounds, as no light row is exposed; and \(|X_{\rm L}|\le800e(N+1)n^{c-1}\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\) as in the multi-row size corollary, since each term contributes one pair to one host whatever the roles of its rows. \(\square\) The theorem above gives the same conclusion with probability \(1-6n^{-c-2}\) for tails on at most \(t\) rows with \(J_0\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/(2N^4)\) and \(3200e\,t(N+1)n^c\le n^{2-\varepsilon}\), taking \(B_{\rm e}\) to be the crowded rows: \(\sum_jm^{\rm L}_j\le tn^c\), so there are at most \(tn^c/M_\varepsilon=1600e\,t(N+1)J_0n^{c-2+\varepsilon}\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) of them, and \(\sum_{j\in C_0}m^{\rm L}_j\le tn^c\le M_C\).

Corollary 2 (size below \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\)). Under the same conditions, every reader as in Section 1 with \(3200e\,t(N+1)N^4J_0\,n^c\le n^{3-2\varepsilon}\) and either at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/(2N^4)\) two-role rows or \(\sum_{j\in C}m^{\rm L}_j\le M_C\) has the same conclusion. Proof. The crowded rows number at most \(tn^c/M_\varepsilon\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/(2N^4)\). In the first case take \(B_{\rm e}\) to be the crowded rows together with \(C\), so \(C_0=\varnothing\); in the second take the crowded rows, so \(C_0\subseteq C\). \(\square\)

4. Scope

Corollary 1 is the two-role form of the multi-row size corollary, with arbitrary tails; it rests on the role-independent steps of the multi-row theorem rather than on the theorem here, which reaches it only for tails on boundedly many rows. Corollary 2 is the two-role form of the combined size corollary. For role-separated readers (\(C=\varnothing\)) the theorem is the combined theorem with the threshold \(\theta\) enlarged. What remains for two-role readers is the case the hypothesis excludes: more than \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/(2N^4)\) two-role rows carrying light mass above \(n^{2-\varepsilon}/\mathrm{polylog}\) in total, possible only at sizes at least \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\), where the greedy family would have to use two-role rows whose labels the pinned exposure fixes. Sparse pinning remains the encoding's hypothesis. Beyond size \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\) the crowded-row case is open as before, and parity terms remain the open core.

Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. In the literal window, the constant-factor heavy-round bound and switching now hold for every sparsely pinned two-role reader of size below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\), and below \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\) when its two-role rows are few or light; open are heavy two-role rows at larger sizes, dense pinning, the crowded case beyond \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\), and parity terms, the open core.
