18 September 2026 — The window's switching clauses rest on an unproved composition: the round bounds are proved on the compact family, the light encoding lives on the slack family, and the mixed tree is not defined on the slack family at pins with free holes

Status: correction with an obstruction (every "switches within the height budget" clause of the mixed-term window theorems is conditional on an unproved composition lemma; the round bounds stand). Spin cycle 205. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question and stopping point. This cycle set out to consolidate the window theorem as it now stands and to check its composition with the height budget and the weight step with the current constants. The check found that the composition is recorded only as a sketch, and that the sketch composes objects that live on different restriction families. The stopping point is the exact statement of the gap, the list of what stands and what becomes conditional, and the repair routes with their obstacles; no repair is proved here.

1. What is recorded

The light lemma lives on the slack family \(\Phi_e\): \(\rho=(R,\mu)\) has \(N+1+e\) residual rows and \(e\) free outside labels \(E(\rho)\), the canonical tree \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\) queries residual rows over the holes \(Q\cup E(\rho)\), a moved row is encoded by matching it to a code label in \(E(\rho)\cap C(p)\), which places the code in \(\Phi_{e-s}\), and the bound \(A^s\) is the family ratio times the cost of \(\beta\) and \(\delta\). Its transfer to the compact family \(\Phi_0\) of the weight step restricts \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\) by a uniform filling \(\rho''\) of the \(e\) free labels: the restricted tree is a tree for \(\rho'=\rho\cup\rho''\) over \(Q\) of no greater height.

The mixed-term round bounds, from the single-row full-class theorem to the two-role theorem, are proved for \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\): "given \(Q\), \((R',\mu')\) is a uniform bijection of the rows onto \(Q^c\) and \(N+1\) residual slots", every outside label has an occupant, the residual rows number \(N+1\), and the tree is the complete-term tree (earlier the both-endpoints tree) on the residual instance of \(\rho'\), whose holes are \(Q\). Each of them ends with "the switching conclusion is the composition recorded in the height budget". That composition is the observation of the height-budget entry: on the slack tree the rounds are keyed to the holes of \(Q\), so at most \(N\) of them occur, each answer is recorded in \(\delta\), and the light answers are paid by the extension encoding, giving \(\Pr[\text{height}\ge s+2N+1]\le\sum_k\binom{s+k}{k}A^s(2r(N+e+2))^k+Mr\,e^{-e2^{-w-4}}\); with a round bound \(\nu<N/48\) in place of \(N\) the height is to be below \(N/8\). The round-trip tool research/tools/check_mixed_term_encoding.py enumerates \(\Phi_e\) and treats a pinned pair \((i,x)\) as alive whenever \(i\) is residual and \(x\) is an unused, unemptied hole of \(Q\cup E\).

2. The gap

(a) Two families. The round bounds are statements about \(\Phi_0\) and use its structure throughout: the products over columns run over occupied outside labels, the residual set has exactly \(N+1\) rows, the union lemma's probability that \(k\) given rows are residual is \(((N+1)/(n/2))^k\), and the light bijection of the exposed steps is onto \(Q^c\) and \(N+1\) slots. The extension encoding needs \(e\ge2^{w+3}s\) free outside labels and does not exist on \(\Phi_0\). No recorded argument applies a round bound to the slack tree \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\), \(\rho\in\Phi_e\), or the encoding to the compact tree \(\mathcal T(F,\rho')\), or relates the two trees: the restriction of \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\) by \(\rho''\) is a tree for \(\rho'\), but it is not \(\mathcal T(F,\rho')\), since the matched-first preference and the falsification tests of \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\) are evaluated on \(\rho\), which matches \(e\) fewer rows.

(b) The compact proofs do not survive on the slack family, and the slack tree is not defined at pins with free holes. The round-bound proofs use \(|R'|=N+1\) essentially: the sparse count of the union lemma sets \(((N+1)/(n/2))^k\) against \((D_2^\ast)^k\) choices of rows, which on \(\Phi_e\), with \(N+1+e\) residual rows and \(e=n^\theta\), becomes about \((n^{\theta}/(400k))^k\); the residual-row bound of the exposed steps, \(((N+1)b/n)^{r}\), becomes \((eb(N+1+e)/(rn))^{r}\), useless for \(\theta\ge\varepsilon\); and the products over columns lose the \(e\) unoccupied labels as dormant mass. So no recorded round bound is a statement about the slack tree, at any size. Moreover, for \(\rho\in\Phi_e\) a term \([i\to x]\wedge h\) with \(i\in R(\rho)\) and \(x\in E(\rho)\) is neither falsified nor satisfied. Under the recorded rule its pinned pair is not alive, because \(x\notin Q\); the node queries the uncovered tail rows, and at the next node the same term is current with no uncovered tail row and no alive pair, so the node has no query. On \(\Phi_0\) the case does not arise, which is why the theorems are stated there. The tool resolves it by treating the pair as alive, with a round whose pigeon answer is a hole of \(Q\cup E\) and whose hole answer is a residual row; then even the trivial count fails, since trigger holes may lie in \(E\) and the rounds number up to \(N+e\). For a reader of \(n^c\) terms with spread pinned pairs, a pair has \(i\in R(\rho)\) and \(x\in E(\rho)\) with probability \(((N+1+e)/(n+1))(e/(n-N))\), so about \(n^{c-2}e^2\) pairs are alive at free holes, and for \(c>2-2\theta\) their matching number exceeds \(N\); below that size they are negligible in expectation and the residual count alone is the obstruction.

(c) The arithmetic of the sketch. Even for rounds at holes of \(Q\), the slack tree's pigeon answer ranges over \(Q\cup E\), and its hole answer over the \(N+1+e\) residual rows of \(\rho\), so a round costs \((N+e)(N+e+2)=n^{2\theta+o(1)}\) in \(\delta\) (the recorded count \((N+e)(N+2)\) of the both-endpoints lemma and Lemma 1 pairs a slack pigeon count with a compact hole count, an instance of the same mix), while a moved row gains \(A=2r(N+e)e(N+e+1)/(n-N-e+1)=n^{-(1-3\theta)+o(1)}\). With \(\nu<N/48\) rounds and height \(s+2\nu\le N/8-r\) the sum is below \(n^{-c}/8\) only if \((1-3\theta)s\ge2\theta\nu+c+o(N)\) with \(s\le N/12\), that is \(\theta<2/7\); the observation's arithmetic, \(A^s=n^{-s/3+o(s)}\) against a heavy factor \(n^{k/3+o(N)}\), takes \(e\le n^{2/9}\) for the first and \(e\le n^{1/3}\) for the second. So the sketch, where it applies, covers per-row widths up to \((2/7-o(1))\log_2n\), not the light lemma's \(\tfrac13\log_2n\). On the compact tree the answers of a round take \(N(N+2)\) values, polylogarithmic; the width range would be the light lemma's if the composition were carried out there.

3. What stands and what becomes conditional

Unaffected: the light lemma and its transfer for readers without pinned rows; the heavy-term dichotomy and with it the complete regime up to size \(n^{4/3}/\mathrm{polylog}(n)\), since its light part has no pinned rows and its tree comes through the light lemma's transfer; the unary theorem, whose tree is built on \(\Phi_0\) with no encoding, and its corollary on separate light and unary terms in its recorded order (order fix: the light tree first, by the transfer, then at each 0-leaf the cover of the alive graph of \(\rho'\cup\pi\), a compact object; two compact trees concatenated, with no encoding over a tree with rounds); every recorded round bound as a statement about the complete-term or both-endpoints tree of \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\), from the single-row full-class theorem through the two-role theorem, including their probability bounds and size corollaries; and the decoder lemmas, as statements about the slack tree in the tool's definition, with the verified round trips. Conditional on a composition lemma that is not proved: every clause "switches within the height budget" attached to those round bounds, and the observation that every literal reader of the window switches with height \(4N+3c+o(N)\), which counts rounds keyed to \(Q\) on a slack tree that is not defined at pins with free holes. The obligation, fewer than \(N/48\) rounds on every path before a 1-leaf, remains the right target for the compact tree; what is missing is the lemma that turns it into a height bound.

4. Repair routes and their obstacles

(R1) Compose on the slack family, moving pinned rows. Define the slack tree at a term whose pin \((i,x)\) has \(x\in E(\rho)\) by a pigeon query on \(i\) alone (an answer \(x\) satisfies the pin, any other answer falsifies the term); restricted by \(\rho''\), the query is answered by the filling when \(i\) is filled and is a real query into \(Q\) otherwise. Encode the pinned row of every such pigeon query as a moved row with its pin \(x\) as code label, free in \(\rho\), and the pinned row of a round at a hole of \(Q\) whose pigeon answer \(y\) lies in \(E(\rho)\) as a moved row with code label \(y\): the family ratio then pays the answer as for a light row, each such round costs a factor \(A\), no bound on their number is needed, and the rounds whose answers lie in \(Q\) cost \(N(N+2)\) each, polylogarithmic, so the width range is the light lemma's. Obstacle: the decoder's matched test on \(\rho^\ast\) sees a moved pinned row as a matched pair; a term whose pinned row is moved at a later node is a fake matched-pair term at every earlier node and, when it precedes the true current term in the reader's order, the matched-first preference chooses it. A light answer \(j\mapsto x\) recorded in \(\delta\) may also collide with a pin \(x\) used as a code label, so that a term killed in reality shows a satisfied pin in \(\alpha\); a collision rule (a row at its pin in \(\rho^\ast\) while that label is a hole of \(\delta\) counts as killed) is needed. Under the plain earliest-term rule with that collision rule the decoder is correct, because a fake term earlier than the current term would itself be current, but fact (b), which every round bound uses through the preference, is lost. A preference that the decoder can compute and that keeps fact (b) is the missing device.

(R2) Compose on the compact family by a swap. Fix an auxiliary decomposition \(\rho'=\rho\cup\rho''\); move \(j\) to \(y\in E(\rho)\cap C(p)\setminus X_j\) and make the occupant of \(y\) residual, so the code stays in \(\Phi_0\); counting pairs \((\rho,\rho'')\), the family ratio is \(\binom{n-N}{e-s}/\binom{n-N}{e}\le(e/(n-N-e+1))^s\), the displaced row is one of \(N+1\) residual rows of the code, and the light answers are holes of \(Q\), so a moved row costs about \(2rN^2e/n\), which would widen the light range. Obstacle: before the moved row's node the decoder sees the displaced row as residual, while in \(\rho'\) it is matched at \(y\), and a term falsified only through that row is misjudged; recording the displaced row's label costs \(n\) per row, and the set \(E(\rho)\) is not known to the decoder. If the count held with a decoder, the light range would pass the recorded intrinsic bound (code obstruction, window structure), whose argument covers extension codes with free pools; the displaced row's invisible label is where that entropy reappears, so the route is recorded as an obstacle, not a prospect.

(R4) Narrow tails on the slack family. For tails of polylogarithmic cube size, \(2^w\) and hence \(e\) polylogarithmic, the compact proofs use \(|R'|\) only through factors \((N+1)/n\) and the mass at unoccupied labels, so re-running them on \(\Phi_e\) with \(N+1+e\) residual rows, \(D_2^\ast\) reduced by the factor \((N+1+e)/(N+1)\), and \(e(n+1)\) extra dormant mass looks routine; the free-hole pins then have expected count \(n^{c-2}(N+1+e)e\), negligible below size \(n^{2-o(1)}\), and a slack round costs polylogarithmically. With a restriction-by-filling argument for trees with hole queries, also unwritten, this would recover switching for narrow tails below size \(n^2\) without moving pinned rows; it does not reach the light lemma's width range.

(R3) Bound the extra rounds on the slack family directly. Rounds at free holes have unbounded matching number for \(c\ge2-2\theta\) by Section 2(b), and rounds at holes of \(Q\) whose pinned row is filled cost \(n^{\theta}\) each; neither can be absorbed without moving the pinned row.

A per-node mark of whether the current term's pin is matched is not enough for (R1): a term whose pinned row is moved at a later node, with its pin free and its tail alive, is unmatched in reality, never preferred, and can precede a marked current term in the reader's order. The device to test first records instead, at each node whose current term has a matched pin, the rank of that pin among the \(\rho^\ast\)-matched pins carrying a term not falsified by \(\alpha\), in the order of their first terms: the fake pins are pins of rows moved at later nodes, at most one per later round, so the rank is at most \(\nu+1\le N+1\), and among the terms with the identified pin the earliest one not falsified by \(\alpha\) is the current term, since an earlier term unfalsified in reality with the same matched pin would itself be current. With the collision rule this is a candidate preference, not a proof; the round-trip tool, extended to move pinned rows, decides it on small boards before any proof.

Verification gate. The exact statements and proofs of the light lemma with its family definitions and transfer, the height-budget observation and its Section 3, the both-endpoints rule and transfer, the complete-term rule with Lemmas 1 and 2, the two-role decoder lemmas, the unary theorem with its separate-terms corollary and recorded order fix, and the statements of the single-row full-class, multi-row, few-light-rows, combined, and two-role theorems were re-read from the notebook, and the round-trip tool's definitions were read; the claim of a gap was tested against the recorded intrinsic-range obstruction and the mixed-terms decomposition of the unary entry; no rule, tree, or encoding changed, so no checker run was needed; the standing reviewer, asked to break the claim of a gap, confirmed it (no recorded argument applies a round bound to the slack tree or the encoding to the compact tree, and the recorded per-round cost itself mixes the families) and reported six findings, all applied here: the separate-terms corollary stands in its recorded order; a slack round costs \((N+e)(N+e+2)\), so the sketch's width bound is \(2/7\), not \(4/13\); the residual count, not the free-hole pins, is the primary reason the compact proofs fail on the slack family; route (R1) needs a collision rule, the code label of a round at a hole of \(Q\) is its answer, and a mark-only preference fails, with a rank device proposed instead; the swap count of (R2) had to be reconciled with the intrinsic-range obstruction; and the dichotomy stands because its light part has no pinned rows, with narrow tails on the slack family added as route (R4).

Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. On the literal frontier the recorded state regresses: the constant-factor round bounds for the recorded classes of mixed readers stand on the compact tree, but their conversion into switching within the height budget is unproved, so the window is closed for no class of mixed readers; unary readers, readers of light terms, and readers of separate light and unary terms are unaffected. Parity terms remain the open core.

Process assessment. Question and stopping point. After the composition correction, the task was route (R1). Before building it, this cycle asked which of the conditional switching clauses need a composition at all. A pinned row \([i\to x]\) has all \(\ell\) bits fixed, so it is a heavy row in the sense of the heavy-term dichotomy, and that theorem switches every source of total size below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\) with single-label pins outright, with no round bound. The stopping point is that lemma, the observation that it restores less than the corollaries claim, and the pair-counting form of the composition, whose remaining obligations are a decoder and a round bound at compact rows.

1. Switching by the dichotomy for total size below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\)

Lemma. Let \(F\) be a reader whose terms are \([i\to x]\wedge\bigwedge_{j\in J}[j\in p_j]\), with tails of any width, or pin-free light terms with at most \(w\) literals per row, \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\), at most \(r\) rows per term of either kind, \(e\ge2^{w+2}s\), and at most \(M\) terms of which \(M_h\) have a pin; rows may be pinned in one term and light in another, and no sparse-pinning hypothesis is made. Then with probability at least \[1-A^s-Mr\,e^{-e2^{-w-4}}-\frac{M_h\,r\,(N+1)(N+2r)}{n^2},\qquad A=\frac{2r(N+e)e(N+e+1)}{n-N-e+1},\] a uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) admits a matching decision tree over \(Q\) of height below \(s\) whose 1-leaves contain a term satisfied by \(\rho'\) and the leaf and whose 0-leaves falsify every pin-free term while every pinned term is falsified or lies in the residual Boolean ideal at degree at most its number of literals. If every term has a pin, the tree has height \(0\) outside probability \(M_hr(N+1)(N+2r)/n^2\), with no hypothesis on \(w\), \(e\), or \(s\): the reader is satisfied by \(\rho'\), or every term is falsified or vanishing. For a source of \(S\) readers with \(S_{\rm tot}\) terms in all, the failure summed over the readers is at most \(SA^s+S_{\rm tot}r\,e^{-e2^{-w-4}}+S_{\rm tot}r(N+1)(N+2r)/n^2\), which is below \(3/8\) with \(s=\lceil\log_2(8S)\rceil\), \(A\le\tfrac12\) (that is \(e\le(n/48r)^{1/3}\), the light lemma's parameters), \(e\ge2^{w+6}s\), and \(S_{\rm tot}\le n^2/(8r(N+1)(N+2r))\); so every source of total size \(n^c\), \(c<2\), switches under one restriction with height \(O(\log S)\).

Proof. Follow the proof of the dichotomy with \(w_0=\ell\), not its statement, whose hypothesis \(w=w_0-1\le\ell-\ell_2-1\) the choice violates: the heavy bound and the light step decouple. The heavy rows are exactly the pinned rows, a pinned term is a heavy term, \(F_{\rm light}\) is the set of pin-free terms, and \(2^{-w_0}=1/n\); the bound on \(B_1\cup B_2\) in the refined form is \(M_hr(N+1)(N+2r)/(2^{w_0}n)\), and it uses of a heavy row only \(|C(p_i)|\le n2^{-w_0}\), here a single label, and of the other rows of a heavy term only their number. Outside \(B_1\cup B_2\) every pinned term is satisfied, falsified, or vanishing, whatever its tail rows carry; the light step is the light lemma for the canonical tree of \(F_{\rm light}\), a pin-free reader, so a row pinned elsewhere is an ordinary light row of that tree and no decoder sees a pin, and a vanishing term stays vanishing under every extension of the assignment. When \(F_{\rm light}\) is empty its tree is one 0-leaf. The summed bound adds the three terms over the readers, \(SA^s\le1/8\) at \(s=\lceil\log_2(8S)\rceil\) and \(A\le\tfrac12\), and \(S_{\rm tot}r\,e^{-e2^{-w-4}}\le1/8\) once \(e2^{-w-4}\ge4s\), as in the light lemma's parameters. \(\square\)

What this restores is less than the corollaries claim. The multi-row size corollary and Corollary 1 of the two-role entry are statements about one reader with at most \(n^c\) terms failing with probability \(3n^{-c-1}\), sized for a union over \(n^c\) readers of a source of \(n^c\) readers with \(n^c\) terms each; the lemma's failure for such a reader is \(n^{c-2}r(N+1)(N+2r)\), essentially tight (a column class of \(n\) terms at one label fails with probability about \(N/n\)), which exceeds \(n^{-c}/8\) for every \(c>1\) and sums to \(n^{2c-2}\) polylog over the source. So the dichotomy switches sources of total size below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\), per-reader size below \(n^{1-\varepsilon/2}\) in that convention, and the corollaries' switching clauses at per-reader size \(n^c\), \(c\ge1\), remain conditional on the composition; the per-reader failure \(n^{-c-1}\) of the round bounds is exactly the content the dichotomy lacks. The recorded parameters of the dichotomy write \(8Sr(N+1+e)(N+2r)/n\) for a source of \(S\) readers with at most \(S\) terms each, where the summed heavy count is \(S^2\); the lemma above separates \(S\) from \(S_{\rm tot}\). In the total-size convention, single-label pins lie inside the window exactly from total size \(n^2\) on, where \((c-1)\log_2n\ge\ell\) (structure); the recorded pigeon-only refutation, a bad reader in every restriction at total size \(n^2\), shows the lemma's heavy bound essentially tight.

2. Toward the composition lemma: the pair count on the restricted slack tree

This section is analysis, not a result. A uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) is \(\rho\cup\rho''\) with \(\rho\in\Phi_e\) uniform and \(\rho''\) a uniform filling of \(e\) rows of \(R(\rho)\) onto \(E(\rho)\), each \(\rho'\) arising from \(\binom{n-N}{e}\) pairs. Encode the pairs \((\rho,\rho'')\) whose restricted tree \(\mathcal T'=\mathcal T(F,\rho)|\rho''\) has a long path by \((\rho^\ast,\sigma,\beta,\delta)\), with \(\rho^\ast\in\Phi_{e-s}\) the code restriction and \(\sigma\) the filling written as a bijection from \(e\) rows of \(R(\rho)\), the residual rows of the code together with the moved rows named by their order on the path, onto \(E(\rho^\ast)\) together with the \(s\) code labels in path order; the fillings number the same on both sides, \(\binom{N+1+e}{e}e!=(N+1+e)!/(N+1)!\), so the probability that \(\mathcal T'\) has a long path is at most \(|\Phi_{e-s}|/|\Phi_e|\) times the cost of \((\beta,\delta)\), provided the code determines the pair. On a path of \(\mathcal T'\) the real queries are those of \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\) at rows residual in \(\rho'\); a query at a filled row is answered by the filling. Modify the slack tree so that a round queries its hole only when the pigeon answer lies in \(Q\), and resolve a pin at a free hole by the pigeon query alone. Then, along a path of \(\mathcal T'\): a light query at a residual row is paid by moving the row, with its hole among \(N\), at the factor \(A'=2rNe(N+e+1)/(n-N-e+1)\); a light query answered by the filling is paid by the same move at the factor \(A\); a pigeon query at a filled pinned row \(i\), answered by \(\rho''(i)\in E(\rho)\), is paid by moving \(i\) to that answer, a label free in \(\rho\), at the family ratio and a mark in \(\beta\) that the round was answered by the filling; and the unpaid answers are pigeon answers in \(Q\) and hole answers, at most \(N\) each per path since a round with its pigeon answer in \(Q\) uses or empties its hole, each among at most \(N+2\) values. Rounds with pigeon answers in \(E(\rho)\) leave their hole free, so they are not a matching, but they cost nothing. Hence, if a decoder exists, \(\Pr_{\rho'}[\mathcal T'\text{ has height}\ge s+2\nu_0]\) is at most the probability that some path carries \(\nu_0\) rounds with pigeon answers in \(Q\), plus \(2\sum_{\nu<\nu_0}\binom{s+2\nu}{2\nu}(N+2)^{2\nu}A'^{s}\), plus the richness' term, the factor \(2\) summing the filling-answered moves, each of which costs at most \(A\le\tfrac12\) beyond the \(s\) real ones. With \(\nu_0=N/48\) the unpaid factor \((N+2)^{N/24}\) is \(n^{o(N)}\), so the width range would be at least the light lemma's; and since \(A'\) is about \(2rNe^2/n\), it would reach about \(\tfrac12\log_2n\), beyond the intrinsic bound of the window-structure entry, whose argument assumes light answers over \(Q\cup E\). That bound must therefore reappear in the decoder obligation below, and no width claim beyond the light lemma's is made.

Two obligations remain. (i) The decoder. A moved pinned row sits at its filling label in \(\rho^\ast\), which the code shows as a matched pair \((i,\rho''(i))\) that \(\rho\) does not have; the fake pairs are those of pinned rows moved at later nodes. At a node whose current term has a pin matched under \(\mu\), record in \(\beta\) the rank of the current term's pin among the fake pins, at most \(P\), the number of pinned moves later on the path, and let the decoder take the earliest term with that pin not falsified by \(\alpha\): every true matched-pin term preceding the current one is falsified in reality through a row on which \(\alpha\) agrees, and a matched pin is never killed. The count is by pins, not terms, since a pin may carry \(n^{c-2}\) terms at size \(n^c\). The cost, a factor \(1+P\) at each of the \(s'\le s\) marked nodes, is not absorbed by the gain of the pinned moves, which is paid once per move: for \(P=1\) it is \(2^{s'}\) against one family ratio. Charging the marks to the pinned moves is part of the open decoder step. What this device also does not settle is the pins at free holes: a light row moved later may take a hole \(y\in E(\rho)\) of a pin \((i,y)\) as its code label, so a term alive in reality looks killed in \(\alpha\), and avoiding every pinned label in the code needs the pinned labels sparse in every pattern cube, which a reader with \(n^c\) pins need not satisfy. Deferring the pins at free holes to the end of every path, after all other terms are falsified, removes later light moves but leaves the identification of the deferred term when its pinned row is filled; this is the open decoder step. (ii) The round bound. The rounds counted are at pairs \((i,x)\) with \(i\in R'\) and \(x\in Q\) of hosts whose tail is assigned at the node by the path or the filling, with no matched pair under \(\mu\), where the filled rows do not count as matched. Steps (H1) to (H3) of the multi-row theorem transfer to this structure with the heavy threshold raised to \(2(N+e)(n+1)\), since the mass at the \(N+e\) unoccupied labels is at most \((N+e)(n+1)\), the occupant of an occupied label is uniform over all rows, the union lemma runs over \(R'\), which is a uniform set of \(N+1\) rows given \(Q\), and the rank step over \(Q\); the steps that use a satisfied term or the exposure of light rows do not, since a term satisfied by \(\rho'\) whose pinned row is filled is an unresolved pin on the slack tree and prevents no round there, while the exposure steps do transfer when \(\varepsilon>\theta\): a light row is residual in \(\rho\) with probability \((N+1+e)/(n+1)\), so at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows leave about \(n^{\theta-\varepsilon}/N^4\) residual ones, and the residual-row bound becomes \((eb(N+1+e)/(rn))^r\le n^{-(\varepsilon-\theta)r}\), with \(\varepsilon-\theta\) in place of \(\varepsilon\) in \(r_0\). So the composition would recover the round bound wherever only (H1) to (H3) and the exposure of light rows are used, and the cases that use a satisfied term, the mass steps (H4) of the multi-row and combined theorems, need that step redone on the pair space, or a preference under which a filled satisfied term resolves before any round, which the decoder cannot compute.

Verification gate. The exact statements and proofs of the heavy-term dichotomy with its parameters and refined bound, the light lemma with its families and transfer, the multi-row setting, theorem (steps (H1) to (H3)) and size corollary, Corollary 1 of the two-role entry, the complete-term rule with Lemma 1, and the window structure were re-read from the notebook; the lemma was tested against the recorded pigeon-only refutation (consistent: it shows the heavy bound tight) and the intrinsic-range obstruction (named in Section 2); no rule, tree, or encoding changed, so no checker run was needed; the standing reviewer confirmed the lemma and reported seven findings, all applied here: the corollaries are per-reader statements with failure \(n^{-c-1}\), which the dichotomy's tight per-reader failure \(n^{c-2}\) cannot give, so the restoration is for total size only and the corollaries' clauses stay conditional; the tail-width hypothesis was unused and the pin-only case has height \(0\) with no light lemma; the lemma follows the dichotomy's proof, not its statement, and the summed bound needs \(A\le\tfrac12\); the light accounting of the pair count had to be made consistent and reconciled with the intrinsic-range obstruction; the fake-pin device must count pins, not terms, and its marking cost is not absorbed; the residual light rows of the slack restriction number \(n^{\theta-\varepsilon}/N^4\), so the exposure steps transfer and only the satisfied-term steps do not; and the filling's domain is the slack residual set, with a mark for filling-answered rounds.

Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. On the literal frontier, sources of total size below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\) with single-label pins switch by the dichotomy, with a shorter tree than the height budget and without role or pinning hypotheses; the recorded round bounds, whose per-reader failure \(n^{-c-1}\) the dichotomy cannot match, stand, and their composition is reduced to a decoder for pins at free holes, with the cost of marking fake pins still to be charged, and to the satisfied-term steps on the pair space, both unproved. Parity terms remain the open core.

Process assessment. The cycle's question, which conditional clauses need a composition at all, was the right one, but the first draft read the corollaries as total-size statements and claimed a restoration the reviewer cut to its true scope; checking the failure-probability convention of a claim before restating it is now the first item of the reviewer's brief.

18 September 2026 — The composition on the pair space: a filling on rows outside every tail, an encoding that pays only for the compact residual rows, and switching within the height budget for sparsely pinned role-separated readers with tails far beyond the light range

Status: working theorem (composition on the pair space for sparsely pinned role-separated readers); obstruction for dense pinning. Spin cycle 207. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question and stopping point. The task was the composition lemma of the correction: a proof, on one probability space and for one tree, that the compact-family round bounds and the light lemma's encoding together give a matching decision tree of height below \(N/8-2r\) for a uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\). The stopping point is such a lemma for role-separated readers whose pinned labels are sparse in every tail pattern cube, with a decoder verified by exhaustive round trips; the pair space of the previous entry is used with the filling placed on rows outside every tail, which turns out to be what makes the encoding cheap: it pays for the \(N+1\) residual rows of the compact restriction only, so its light range is \(2^w\lesssim e/s\) with \(e\) up to \(n^{2-\varepsilon-c}/4400\), far beyond the light lemma's \(n^{1/3}\). Dense pinning remains the obstruction, and the tool exhibits the decoder failing there.

1. The pair space and the restricted slack tree

Readers are role-separated as in the multi-row setting: at most \(M\le n^c\) terms \([i\to x]\wedge\bigwedge_{j\in J}[j\in p_j]\) with \(i\in A\), \(J\subseteq B\), \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\), at most \(r\) rows per term, at most \(w\) literals per tail row with \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\), pin-free terms allowed; \(A\) is taken to be every row outside \(B\), so \(|A|\ge n/2+N+2\), and \(X\) is the set of labels pinned by some term. The reader is sparsely pinned if \(|X\cap C(p)|\le|C(p)|/4\) for every pattern \(p\) of a tail row; a reader with \(|X|\le n2^{-w-2}\) is sparsely pinned whatever its pins.

The pair space. Fix an \(e\)-set \(S\subseteq A\) of rows outside every tail. Let \(\Phi_e(S)=\{\rho\in\Phi_e:\ S\subseteq R(\rho)\}\) and let a pair be \((\rho,\rho'')\) with \(\rho\in\Phi_e(S)\) and \(\rho''\) a bijection of \(S\) onto \(E(\rho)\); \(\rho'=\rho\cup\rho''\) then lies in \(\Phi_0^S=\{\rho'\in\Phi_0:\ S\cap R'=\varnothing\}\), the compact family with \(S\) matched, and the map is a bijection from pairs onto \(\Phi_0^S\), since \(\rho'\) determines \(\rho''=\rho'|_S\) and \(\rho\). So the uniform pair gives the uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0^S\), and given \(S\) the slack restriction has \(R(\rho)=R'\sqcup S\) with \(R'\) a uniform \((N+1)\)-subset of the rows outside \(S\), \(E(\rho)\) a uniform \(e\)-subset of \(O\), and \(\mu\) a uniform bijection of the other rows onto \(O\setminus E(\rho)\). Write \(b=|A|\).

Lemma A0 (uniform \(\rho'\)). If \(e(N+1)\le n/8\), then for every event \(\mathcal E\) on \(\Phi_0\), \(\Pr_{\rho'\in\Phi_0}[\mathcal E]\le\tfrac75\,\mathbb E_S\Pr_{\rho'\in\Phi_0^S}[\mathcal E]\), the expectation over a uniform \(e\)-subset \(S\) of \(A\). Proof. \(|\Phi_0^S|=q|\Phi_0|\) with \(q=\binom{n+1-e}{N+1}/\binom{n+1}{N+1}\le1\) for every \(S\), and a given \(\rho'\) lies in \(\Phi_0^S\) for \(\binom{b-|A\cap R'|}{e}\ge\binom{b-N-1}{e}\) sets \(S\). Hence \(\mathbb E_S\Pr_{\Phi_0^S}[\mathcal E]=\sum_{\rho'\in\mathcal E}\binom{b-|A\cap R'|}{e}/(\binom be\,q|\Phi_0|)\ge\Pr_{\Phi_0}[\mathcal E]\binom{b-N-1}{e}/\binom be\), and \(\binom{b-N-1}e/\binom be\ge(1-(N+1)/(b-e))^e\ge1-e(N+1)/(b-e)\ge5/7\), as \(b-e\ge7n/16\). \(\square\)

The slack tree. \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\) is the complete-term tree on the residual instance of \(\rho\), pigeons \(R\) and holes \(Q\cup E(\rho)\), with three changes. The current term is chosen by the matched-first preference among the terms not falsified by \(\rho\cup\pi\) and not killed. If its pin \((i,x)\) is alive (\(i\) unassigned, \(x\) unused and not emptied) and \(x\in Q\), the round queries the pigeon \(i\) over the unused holes of \(Q\cup E(\rho)\) and, on every answer other than \(x\), the hole \(x\) over the unassigned rows of \(R\) and the empty branch (the hole after every answer, not only after answers in \(Q\)). If its pin is alive and \(x\in E(\rho)\), a pin test follows: two branches, "\(i\mapsto x\)", which assigns \(i\) to \(x\), and "not", which kills the term; a killed term is skipped by the preference from then on and its node is left at once, without tail queries. Otherwise every uncovered tail row is then queried in order. As on the complete-term tree, a term whose pin's hole is used or emptied while its row is unassigned counts as falsified, and a 1-leaf is a node where some term is satisfied by \(\rho\cup\pi\). Lemma 1 of the complete-term rule holds verbatim for the rounds: the trigger pairs of a path are pairwise disjoint pairs \((i,x)\) with \(i\in R\), \(x\in Q\), whose host is not falsified by \(\rho\) and has no \(\mu\)-matched pair, so the rounds number at most \(N\); a pin test triggers no round.

Lemma A (restriction by filling). Restrict \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\) by \(\rho''\): at a pigeon query of a row of \(S\) follow the branch of its filling label; at a pigeon query of another row keep the branches into \(Q\); at a hole query keep the branches of the rows of \(R'\) and the empty branch; at a pin test \((i,x)\) follow "\(i\mapsto x\)" if \(i\in S\) and \(\rho''(i)=x\), and "not" otherwise. The result \(\mathcal T'\) is a matching decision tree for \(\rho'\) over \(Q\), with pigeon and hole queries at rows of \(R'\) and holes of \(Q\), whose 1-leaves contain a term satisfied by \(\rho'\) and the leaf and whose 0-leaves falsify every term; its height is the largest number of real queries, the queries of \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\) at rows of \(R'\) and at holes, along a path. Proof. Along a surviving path the labels of \(E(\rho)\) are used only by rows of \(S\), each at its filling label, which is unused when the row is queried, so the followed branches exist; a row of \(R'\) receives a hole of \(Q\); a hole query keeps only rows residual in \(\rho'\). A surviving path together with \(\rho''\) is a path of \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\) on which every killed term is falsified by \(\rho'\), since its pinned row is either in \(R'\), and then cannot reach the filled label \(x\), or in \(S\) with \(\rho''(i)\ne x\); so a 0-leaf falsifies every term under \(\rho'\cup\pi_{\rm real}\) and a 1-leaf contains a satisfied term. A pigeon query of a row of \(R'\) at which every hole of \(Q\) is used or emptied keeps no branch: a dead leaf, whose leaf term vanishes modulo the row axiom and the column exclusions, as in the light lemma's Section 1. Hole-query nodes are admissible. \(\square\)

Two remarks. A pin test costs nothing in \(\mathcal T'\), and rows of \(S\) are queried only as pigeons: they lie in no tail. This is what the choice \(S\subseteq A\) buys; with a filling on arbitrary residual rows the slack tree passes through nodes whose only queries are at filled tail rows, of which a path may have of order \(e\), and the encoding below has to pay for them (Section 5 records the failure).

2. The encoding and its decoder

Call \(\rho\) \(s\)-rich' if \(|E(\rho)\cap C(p)\setminus X|\ge s\) for every pattern \(p\) of a tail row, the richness' of the two-role decoder with the global pinned set \(X\) in place of the row's own; for a sparsely pinned reader, \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\) and \(e\ge2^{w+3}s\), \(\Pr[\rho\text{ not }s\text{-rich'}]\le Mr\,e^{-e2^{-w-5}}\) by the same proof, since \(E(\rho)\) is a uniform \(e\)-subset of \(O\) on \(\Phi_e(S)\) and \(|C(p)\cap O\setminus X|\ge n2^{-w-2}\). A move is a real query of a tail row; a real light query moves the row to a hole of \(Q\).

Fix a pair with \(\rho\) rich' whose restricted tree has a path with at least \(s\) moves and fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds before its \(s\)-th move, and take the lexicographically first such path, cut after its \(s\)-th move. Its code is \((\rho^\ast,\sigma,\beta,\delta)\): \(\rho^\ast\in\Phi_{e-s}(S)\) is \(\rho\) with each moved row taken out of \(R\) and matched to the smallest unpicked label of \(E(\rho)\cap C(p)\setminus X\), \(p\) its pattern in the node's term, the code labels; \(\sigma\) is the filling written as a bijection from \(S\) onto \(E(\rho^\ast)\sqcup\{1,\dots,s\}\), the index \(k\) standing for the code label of the \(k\)-th moved row; \(\beta\) lists, in path order, one bit per round, whether the node moves a row, and per moved row its position among the at most \(r\) tail rows of its term and one bit marking the last move of its node; and \(\delta\) lists, in path order, the moves' holes and the rounds' answers, a hole of \(Q\) for the pigeon when the pinned row lies in \(R'\), and a row of \(R'\) or the empty branch for the hole. Rows of \(S\) are recorded by nothing: a pin test is decided by the decoder, and a pigeon query of a row of \(S\) at a round has answer \(\rho''(i)\), which the decoder reads off \(\sigma\) when it lies in \(E(\rho^\ast)\) and replaces by a mark "outside \(Q\), at no pinned label" when it is a code label, which is at no pinned label.

Lemma B (decoder). The code determines the pair. Proof. The decoder starts from \(\alpha=\rho^\ast\) with no term killed, knows \(S\), \(E(\rho^\ast)\) and \(\sigma\), and processes nodes until it has found \(s\) moved rows. At a node it chooses the current term by the preference with falsification tested on \(\alpha\), killed terms skipped, and a pin counted as matched when \(\rho^\ast\) matches its row to its label. Claims: (i) the matched pins of \(\rho^\ast\) are those of \(\mu\), since moved rows lie in \(B\) and pinned rows are never moved; (ii) every term preceding the real current term in the preference is killed in both, or falsified by \(\rho\cup\pi_{<m}\) through a row assigned before \(m\), on which \(\alpha\) agrees (matched rows; rows moved earlier, reassigned to their holes; rows of \(S\) assigned at earlier rounds or pin tests, whose labels the decoder knows or has marked as outside \(Q\) at no pinned label, which decides every pin at them; rows assigned by hole answers), or through a killed pin, whose hole is used or emptied in \(\alpha\) as in reality: holes of \(Q\) are used only by recorded assignments, and a pin at a code label does not exist; (iii) the current term is not falsified by \(\alpha\): its rows assigned before \(m\) agree, its tail rows moved at \(m\) carry consistent code labels, its other tail rows are unassigned in both (a row of \(B\) moved later is unassigned in reality and, were it in this term's tail, would be queried now), and its pin is alive in \(\alpha\) exactly when alive in reality, the pinned row's status agreeing as in (ii) and its hole being a hole of \(Q\), used or emptied in \(\alpha\) as in reality, or a label of \(E(\rho^\ast)\), used or free in both since rows of \(S\) assigned before \(m\) are in \(\alpha\), or a label of \(O\setminus E(\rho)\), used in both, since a pinned label is never a code label. So the decoder finds the current term. If its pin is alive at \(x\in E(\rho^\ast)\), the decoder decides the pin test: "\(i\mapsto x\)" exactly when \(i\in S\) and \(\sigma(i)=x\), which agrees with reality because a row of \(R'\) never reaches \(x\) and a slot value of \(\sigma(i)\) is a code label, not \(x\). If its pin is alive at \(x\in Q\), it resolves the round: the pigeon answer from \(\delta\) when \(i\in R'\), from \(\sigma\) or the mark when \(i\in S\); the hole answer from \(\delta\) whenever the pigeon answer differs from \(x\); then it reads the round's bit of \(\beta\). If the node has moves, by the bit or because the node has no round and the path continues, it reads the positions from \(\beta\) up to the last-of-node bit, and for each the hole from \(\delta\); a node with neither a round nor a move does not occur before the cut, since a current term with an unassigned tail row makes a move, a killed term is left at once, and a pin test "\(i\mapsto x\)" whose tail is covered is a 1-leaf. After the \(s\)-th move it returns the moved rows to the residual set, which gives \(\rho\), and reads \(\rho''\) off \(\sigma\), the code labels now being known. \(\square\)

Lemma C (count). Let \(\theta_A=(N+1)e/(n-N-e+1)\) and \(A''=2rN\theta_A\). Among the pairs of \(\Phi_e(S)\) with \(\rho\) rich', the fraction whose restricted tree has a path with at least \(s\) moves and fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds before its \(s\)-th move is at most \(A''^{\,s}(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\). Proof. The codes number at most \(|\Phi_{e-s}(S)|\) times \(e!\) for \(\sigma\), times \((2r)^s2^{\nu}\) for \(\beta\), \(N^s\) for the moves' holes and \((N(N+2))^{\nu}\) for the rounds' answers, summed over \(\nu<\nu_0\); the pairs number \(|\Phi_e(S)|\,e!\); Lemma B makes the code injective. Counting \(\Phi_k(S)\) as the choice of the \(N+1+k-e\) residual rows outside \(S\), of \(E\), and of the matching, \(|\Phi_k(S)|=\binom{n+1-e}{N+1+k-e}\binom{n-N}{k}(n-N-k)!\), so \[\frac{|\Phi_{e-s}(S)|}{|\Phi_e(S)|}=\prod_{i=0}^{s-1}\frac{(N+1-i)(e-i)}{n-N-e+1+i}\le\theta_A^{\,s},\] and \(\sum_{\nu<\nu_0}(2N(N+2))^\nu\le(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\). \(\square\)

The formula for \(|\Phi_k(S)|\) and the ratio were checked by enumeration on boards with \(n\le9\), \(N\le3\), \(e\le3\) (research/results/pair_space_20260918_207/count_check.txt).

The ratio is the light lemma's \(|\Phi_{e-s}|/|\Phi_e|\) with the residual-row factor \(N+1+e-i\) replaced by \(N+1-i\): a moved row is one of the \(N+1\) rows of \(R'\), not one of the \(N+1+e\) residual rows of the slack restriction, because the rows of \(S\) are never moved; and a move's answer is one of \(N\) holes of \(Q\), not of \(N+e\) holes. Both savings come from encoding the restricted tree rather than the slack tree. This narrows the scope of the recorded observation that the \((1/3)\log_2n\) limit is intrinsic to extension encodings in flat families: its counting keeps the residual factor \(N+e+1-i\) because its encodings move any residual row of the slack tree in \(\Phi_e\), and for those the limit stands, as does its point that a fixed free pool cannot help; the pair-space code moves rows of \(R'\) only, keeps the free-set entropy \(e/n\) per label, and pays \(2rN(N+1)\) per move instead of \(2r(N+e)^2\), so \(e\) may grow to \(n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\) before \(A''\) reaches \(1/(4\sqrt N)\). The observation's claim-index row records the narrowing.

3. The round bound on the slack tree and the composition

Lemma E (steps (H1) to (H3) on \(\Phi_e(S)\)). Fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), \(d_\varepsilon=\lceil(c+1)/\varepsilon\rceil+1\), \(N\ge2^{d_\varepsilon+6}(c+1)\log_2n\) with \((Nn^{-\varepsilon})^{d_\varepsilon+1}\le n^{-c-1}\), and \(e\le n/16\). Call a host heavy if \(m_h\ge2(N+2e)(n+1)\), light otherwise, let \(U^{\rm L}_x\) be the union of the \(I_{h,x}\) over light hosts, \(D_2^{(e)}=n/(1600\,\mathrm e\,(N+1+e))\) with \(\mathrm e\) Euler's number, and \(X^{(e)}_{\rm L}=\{x:\ |U^{\rm L}_x|\ge D_2^{(e)}\}\), all fixed by the reader. If \(|X^{(e)}_{\rm L}|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\), then, for a uniform \(e\)-subset \(S\) of \(A\) and a uniform \(\rho\in\Phi_e(S)\), every path of \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\) before a 1-leaf has at most \(N/48-1\) rounds except with probability \(3n^{-c-1}\). In particular this holds for a reader with at most \(n^c\) terms when \(1600\,\mathrm e\,(N+1+e)\le n^{2-\varepsilon-c}\), since \(|X^{(e)}_{\rm L}|\le\sum_x|U^{\rm L}_x|/D_2^{(e)}\le n^c/D_2^{(e)}\).

Proof. Follow the multi-row theorem, part (i). (H1) Given \(Q\), \(S\) and \(E(\rho)\), the occupants of the labels of \(O\setminus E(\rho)\) form a uniform injection of a uniform subset of the rows outside \(S\), so the occupant of a label is uniform over the \(n+1-e\) rows outside \(S\) and the events "the occupant of \(x\) lies outside \(I_{h,x}\)" are decreasing on distinct columns, each of probability at most \(1-|I_{h,x}\setminus S|/(n+1)\). The labels of \(Q\cup E(\rho)\) carry mass at most \((N+e)(n+1)\) and the rows of \(S\) at most \(e(n+1)\), so for a heavy host \(\sum_{x\notin Q\cup E}|I_{h,x}\setminus S|\ge m_h/2\), and the host has no \(\mu\)-matched pair with probability at most \(e^{-m_h/(2(n+1))}\le e^{-N}\le n^{-2c-3}\); over at most \(n^c\) hosts this costs \(n^{-c-3}\). Outside this event, by Lemma 1 the trigger pairs of a bad path come from light hosts at holes of \(Q\), so they form a matching in \(\{(i,x):\ x\in Q,\ i\in R\cap U^{\rm L}_x\}\) with \(R=R'\sqcup S\). (H2) The sets \(U^{\rm L}_x\) are fixed by the reader. Given \(Q\), \(S\) is a uniform \(e\)-subset of \(A\) and, given also \(S\), \(R'\) is a uniform \((N+1)\)-subset of the rows outside \(S\). For \(k\) given rows of \(A\), the probability that all lie in \(R=R'\sqcup S\) is at most \(\sum_{T_1\sqcup T_2}(e/(b-k))^{|T_1|}((N+1)/(n+1-e-k))^{|T_2|}\le(4(N+1+e)/n)^k\), as \(b\ge n/2+N+2\), \(e\le n/16\) and \(k\le N/192\). So the expected number of \(k\)-matchings at labels outside \(X^{(e)}_{\rm L}\), \(k=N/192\), is at most \(\binom Nk(D_2^{(e)})^k(4(N+1+e)/n)^k\le(4\mathrm eN(N+1+e)D_2^{(e)}/(kn))^k=0.48^k\), as in the activated union lemma, and Markov's inequality gives fewer than \(N/192\) such rounds outside probability \(2^{-N/192}\le n^{-c-1}\). (H3) \(X^{(e)}_{\rm L}\) is fixed by the reader, so by the rank lemma in its independent-points form, \(\Pr[|X^{(e)}_{\rm L}\cap Q|\ge2^{d_\varepsilon}]\le(Nn^{-\varepsilon})^{d_\varepsilon+1}\le n^{-c-1}\); outside this event a path before a 1-leaf, whose rounds have distinct holes, has fewer than \(N/192+2^{d_\varepsilon}\le N/192+N/128\le N/48-1\) rounds, as \(N\ge2^{d_\varepsilon+7}\ge256\). \(\square\)

Theorem D (composition). Let \(F\) be sparsely pinned, \(s=\lfloor N/12\rfloor-2r\ge1\), \(\nu_0=\lfloor N/48\rfloor\), \(2^{w+3}s\le e\le n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\), and suppose that, for a uniform \(e\)-subset \(S\) of \(A\) and a uniform \(\rho\in\Phi_e(S)\), every path of \(\mathcal T(F,\rho)\) before a 1-leaf has fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds except with probability \(p_R\). Then a uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) admits a matching decision tree over \(Q\), with pigeon and hole queries, of height below \(N/8-2r\), whose 1-leaves contain a term satisfied by \(\rho'\) and the leaf and whose 0-leaves falsify every term, except with probability at most \[\tfrac75\Bigl(Mr\,e^{-e2^{-w-5}}+p_R+2^{-N/8+(2r+1)(2+\frac12\log_2N)}\Bigr).\] Proof. By Lemma A0 it suffices to bound the failure for a fixed \(S\) and average. Take the pair uniform and \(\mathcal T'\) of Lemma A; it is the required tree unless some path has at least \(s+2\nu_0\) real queries. A round contributes at most two real queries and a pin test none, so such a path has at least \(\nu_0\) rounds or at least \(s+2\) moves with fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds before its \(s\)-th move; the first is the event of probability \(p_R\) (at most \(N/48-1\) rounds means fewer than \(\nu_0\)), and the second, with \(\rho\) rich', has probability at most \(A''^{\,s}(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\) by Lemma C, the richness' failure costing the first term. The height bound is \(s+2\nu_0\le N/12-2r+N/24=N/8-2r\). For the numeric bound, \(N+e\le n/2\) gives \(\theta_A\le2(N+1)e/n\), so \(A''\le4rN(N+1)e/n\le1/(4\sqrt N)=2^{-2-\frac12\log_2N}\), and with \(s\ge N/12-2r-1\) and \(2N(N+2)\le4N^2\), \[A''^{\,s}(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\le2^{-(N/12-2r-1)(2+\frac12\log_2N)+(N/48)(2+2\log_2N)}=2^{-N/8+(2r+1)(2+\frac12\log_2N)}.\ \square\]

Theorem F (switching for sparsely pinned role-separated readers). Let \(F\) be a sparsely pinned role-separated reader as in Section 1 with at most \(n^c\) terms and \(|X^{(e)}_{\rm L}|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\), in particular any such reader when \(1600\,\mathrm e\,(N+1+e)\le n^{2-\varepsilon-c}\); let \(N\) be as in Lemma E with \(N\ge8(c+1)\log_2n+(2r+1)(16+4\log_2N)\) and \(s\ge4((2c+1)\ln n+\ln r)\), and let the tails satisfy \(2^{w+3}s\le e\le n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\). Then a uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) admits a matching decision tree over \(Q\) of height below \(N/8-2r\), with the leaf properties of Theorem D, except with probability at most \(7n^{-c-1}\). Proof. Theorem D with Lemma E's \(p_R=3n^{-c-1}\); the richness' term is at most \(n^{-c-1}\) because \(e2^{-w-5}\ge s/4\ge(2c+1)\ln n+\ln r\), and the count term is at most \(n^{-c-1}\) by the bound on \(N\). \(\square\)

Scope. The per-reader failure \(7n^{-c-1}\) is what a union over \(n^c\) readers of a source needs, so this is the composition that the correction found missing, for sparsely pinned role-separated readers. What is new per reader is the tails' width beside a pin of width \(\ell\): with \(|X^{(e)}_{\rm L}|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\) given directly, \(e\) may be as large as \(n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\), so tails of width up to \(\log_2n-\log_2(2^8rN^{5/2}s)\) are admitted; through the size route, \(e\le n^{2-\varepsilon-c}/4400-N-1\) and the width is up to \((2-\varepsilon-c)\log_2n-\log_2(2^{16}s)\), at \(c=1\) up to \((1-\varepsilon)\log_2n-O(\log N)\). This is a per-reader statement and makes no claim on the window of the window structure, whose upper end \((c-1)\log_2n\) is a total-size statement of the dichotomy; per reader, the dichotomy covers rows of width at least \((2c-1)\log_2n+O(\log N)\), and for a reader of size \(n^c\) with failure \(n^{-c-1}\) nothing, so rows of width between \((2-\varepsilon-c)\log_2n\) and \(\ell\) remain open per reader. The recorded light lemma's range \(2^w\lesssim n^{1/3}/(rNs)\) is the case of arbitrary pins; sparse pinning is the price of the pair space, and every column class at one label, and every reader with at most \(n2^{-w-2}\) pinned labels, pays it.

4. What remains: dense pinning, two-role rows, the satisfied-term steps

Dense pinning. If some tail pattern cube \(C(p)\) is pinned on more than a quarter of its labels, the code labels for \(p\) may have to be pinned labels, and then the decoder cannot tell a pin at a code label, alive in reality because the label is free, from a pin at an occupied label, dead: the code shows every code label as occupied. This is the failure of the tool's first design (Section 5, batch 3 off \(G\)). Naming the code labels costs \(n/s\) per move against a gain of \(\theta_A\approx(N+1)e/n\), and recording, for each pin test at a code label, which slot the pinned row's filling occupies costs \(s\) per such test with no bound on their number. Readers whose pins cover a pattern cube, such as a class pinning one row to every label, remain without a composition; the dichotomy switches them below total size \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\).

Two-role rows. The filling avoids every tail row, so a row pinned in one term and light in another lies outside \(S\) and is moved like any light row; the two-role decoder's device (code labels outside the moved row's own pinned labels) is then needed for it, and richness' with both exclusions holds under the two conditions together. The transfer is not written here.

The satisfied-term steps (H4) of the multi-row theorem, the few-light-rows and combined theorems' exposure steps, and the two-role theorems are not transferred to \(\Phi_e(S)\); the previous entry's remark that exposure transfers for \(\varepsilon>\theta\) stands, and the pair space's uniformity given \(S\) is what those proofs would use.

5. The tool and the runs

research/tools/check_pair_space_encoding.py enumerates every pair on small boards, builds the restricted slack tree, encodes the lexicographically first path with at least \(h\) real queries, and decodes it. Its modes record the design's history (records, all runs under ./compute.sh, \(n=8\), \(N=4\)): the first design (filling on any residual row, a per-node record, \(G=\{E(\rho)\cap X=\varnothing\}\)) decoded every rich bad pair on \(G\) in twelve runs and failed off \(G\) on 895 of 4770, 637 of 4193, 216 of 1508 and 1257 of 1806; the entry's encoding without positions, tried first, failed on \(G\) on 966 of 9834 pairs, the decoder skipping a moved row that sits at a code label in the code as if it were matched, which is why \(\beta\) carries positions; the entry's encoding with the filling on rows outside every tail (batch 3, seven runs, hole after every answer) decoded every rich bad pair on \(G\), 5034, 152, 580, 432, 4762 and 114 of them, and failed off \(G\) on 433 of 2135, 197 of 713, 116 of 300 and 55 of 154; the same encoding with the filling on any residual row failed on \(G\) on 20 of 3062 (the nodes at filled tail rows); and the encoding of Section 2, with the pin test and code labels outside \(X\) (batch 4, nine runs), decoded every rich bad pair on and off \(G\): 1006, 78, 40 and 795 rich bad pairs off \(G\) with no failure, where batch 3 had failed. Richness' is checked by the encoder (a run counts only pairs where every code label exists), so batch 4 verifies Lemma B on the pairs where its hypothesis holds; the probability bounds are not tested, the boards being too small.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the multi-row setting and theorem (steps (H1) to (H4), facts (a) and (b)), the light lemma's families, encoding lemma and richness lemma, the two-role decoder's richness', the complete-term rule (Lemmas 1 and 2), the activated union lemma, the rank lemma, hole-query nodes, the window structure's Section 3, and the composition-gap and pair-count entries. Recorded obstructions checked: the pigeon-only refutation, the hole-only failure, the q-skip refutation, the two-role example and the adaptive-rule counterexample concern other trees or readers excluded here; the intrinsic light-range observation is narrowed in scope, not contradicted, and its claim-index row says so. Checks run: the count formula and family ratio by enumeration, and the round-trip tool's batches 3 and 4 with their negative controls (Section 5). The standing reviewer, given the draft and the anchors, confirmed Lemmas A0, A, B, C and E and Theorems D and F and reported eleven findings, all applied: a consequence sentence claiming that the window closes below size \(n^{3/2-\varepsilon}\) mixed the per-reader and total-size conventions and was removed; the narrowing of the recorded observation is recorded as such; the round count of Lemma E was off by one when 48 does not divide \(N\), and the floor in \(s\) was dropped in Theorem D's exponent, both repaired at the cost of constants; \(c\ge1\) and a conditioning on the light assignment were unused and are dropped; the tree rule's two conventions, dead leaves, the notation \(\Phi_0^S\) and the status line were wording.

Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. On the literal frontier the composition that the correction found missing is now proved for sparsely pinned role-separated readers, with per-reader failure \(7n^{-c-1}\) and tails up to width \((2-\varepsilon-c)\log_2n-O(\log N)\) beside the pin; densely pinned readers and two-role readers remain, the former on the pin at a code label, and per reader the rows of width between \((2-\varepsilon-c)\log_2n\) and \(\ell\) beside a pin remain open. Parity terms remain the open core.

Process assessment. The cycle's first two encodings failed the round-trip tool before any draft reached the reviewer, and each failure named the design that works (positions in \(\beta\); the filling outside every tail; the pin test), so the tool did the design work and the reviewer's findings concerned a consequence and constants, not the argument; the one false sentence was again a mixing of probability conventions, which the gate's item (1) names, caught by the reviewer. No framework change.

18 September 2026 — The composition without a slack tree: the pair-space count applies to the compact complete-term tree itself, code labels avoid only their own filling row's pins, and every recorded round bound on role-separated readers becomes a switching theorem in the pair-space light range

Status: working theorem (composition on the compact family for role-separated readers under column-sparseness); obstruction for dense pattern cubes above size \(n^{5/3}\). Spin cycle 208. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question and stopping point. The task was to weaken the sparse-pinning hypothesis of the previous entry. The attempt to make the filled-pigeon nodes free by skipping the tail after a killed pin failed the round-trip tool at once (a row moved later can sit in the tail of an earlier current term, which the complete-term rule forbids), and the failure showed what the slack tree was for: nothing. The decoder can simulate the recorded compact complete-term tree of \(\rho'\) itself from the code, once the code labels are chosen so that no filling row is pinned to its own code label. The stopping point is a composition lemma on \(\Phi_0\) for one tree, the recorded one, with the recorded round bounds as its only input, so that every recorded round bound on role-separated readers becomes a switching theorem; the pinning hypothesis reduces to a column-sparseness that holds automatically for readers of size \(n^c\) whose tails have width below \((2-c)\log_2n-10\). The slack tree, the pin test and the transferred round bound of the previous entry stand but are no longer needed.

1. The compact tree and the pair space

Readers are role-separated as in the multi-row setting: at most \(M\le n^c\) terms \([i\to x]\wedge\bigwedge_{j\in J}[j\in p_j]\) with \(i\in A\), \(J\subseteq B\), \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\), at most \(r\) rows per term, at most \(w\) literals per tail row, \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\), pin-free terms allowed; \(A\) is every row outside \(B\), so \(b=|A|\ge n/2+N+2\); \(A_y\) is the set of rows pinned to the label \(y\). The tree is the complete-term tree \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) on the residual instance of \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\), pigeons \(R'\) and holes \(Q\): the current term is chosen by the matched-first preference among the terms not falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi\), a term whose pin's hole is used or emptied while its row is unassigned counting as falsified; if its pin \((i,x)\) is alive, \(i\in R'\) unassigned and \(x\in Q\) unused and not emptied, the round queries the pigeon \(i\) over the unused holes of \(Q\) and, on every answer other than \(x\), the hole \(x\) over the unassigned rows of \(R'\) and the empty branch; then every uncovered tail row is queried in order. This is the tree of every recorded round bound after Lemma 2 of the complete-term rule; a move is a light query, at a row of \(R'\cap B\), and the height of a path is its moves plus at most two per round.

The pair space is that of the previous entry: an \(e\)-set \(S\subseteq A\), \(\Phi_e(S)=\{\rho\in\Phi_e:\ S\subseteq R(\rho)\}\), a pair \((\rho,\rho'')\) with \(\rho''\) a bijection of \(S\) onto \(E(\rho)\), and \(\rho'=\rho\cup\rho''\), a bijection from pairs onto \(\Phi_0^S=\{\rho'\in\Phi_0:\ S\cap R'=\varnothing\}\); given \(S\), \(R'\) is a uniform \((N+1)\)-subset of the rows outside \(S\), \(E(\rho)\) a uniform \(e\)-subset of \(O\), \(\mu\) a uniform bijection of the other rows onto \(O\setminus E(\rho)\), and \(\rho''\) a uniform bijection given the rest. Lemma A0 gives \(\Pr_{\Phi_0}[\mathcal E]\le\tfrac75\mathbb E_S\Pr_{\Phi_0^S}[\mathcal E]\) for every event when \(e(N+1)\le n/8\). Nothing else of the previous entry is used: the tree is the compact tree of \(\rho'\), and the slack restriction \(\rho\) appears only inside the code. This is the swap encoding on \(\Phi_0\) that the correction listed as a repair route and found blocked because "the displaced row's label must be visible to the decoder": the displaced row is the row filling the code label, \(\sigma\) makes its label visible as a value in \(E(\rho^\ast)\) or a slot, and the own-row rule removes the one pin the slot leaves undecided.

2. The code and its decoder

Code labels. For a pattern \(p\) of a tail row call a label \(y\in E(\rho)\cap C(p)\) valid if the row filling it is not pinned to it, \(\rho''^{-1}(y)\notin A_y\), and call the pair \(s\)-rich if every tail pattern has at least \(s\) valid labels. Fix a rich pair whose compact tree has a path with at least \(s\) moves and fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds before its \(s\)-th move, and take the lexicographically first such path, cut after its \(s\)-th move. Its code is \((\rho^\ast,\sigma,\beta,\delta)\): \(\rho^\ast\in\Phi_{e-s}(S)\) is \(\rho\) with each moved row taken out of \(R\) and matched to the smallest unpicked valid label of its pattern in the node's term, its code label; \(\sigma\) is \(\rho''\) written as a bijection of \(S\) onto \(E(\rho^\ast)\sqcup\{1,\dots,s\}\), the index \(k\) standing for the \(k\)-th code label; \(\beta\) lists, in path order, one bit per round, whether the node moves a row, and per moved row its position among the term's tail rows and a last-of-node bit; \(\delta\) lists, in path order, the moves' holes and the rounds' answers, a hole of \(Q\) for the pigeon and a row of \(R'\) or the empty branch for the hole.

Lemma B (decoder). The code determines the pair. Proof. The decoder simulates \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) node by node from the assignment \(\alpha\) that extends \(\rho^\ast\) by \(i\mapsto\sigma(i)\) for the rows of \(S\) whose value lies in \(E(\rho^\ast)\), and by a mark "at the \(k\)-th code label" for the others; it evaluates a term as follows: a tail row is consistent or not by its label in \(\alpha\), or uncovered if unassigned; a pin \((i,x)\) with \(x\in Q\) is satisfied, dead or alive by \(\alpha\) and the emptied holes as in the tree; a pin \((i,x)\) with \(x\notin Q\) is satisfied if \(\alpha(i)=x\) and dead otherwise, a marked row satisfying no pin, since by validity the row at the \(k\)-th code label is not pinned to it. The preference counts a pin as matched when \(\rho^\ast\) or \(\sigma\) matches its row to its label. Claims, at a node \(m\) with real current term \(T\): (i) the terms with a matched pin are the same in \(\alpha\) and in \(\rho'\), by validity; (ii) every term before \(T\) in the preference is falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi_{<m}\) through a row assigned there, on which \(\alpha\) agrees (matched rows; rows of \(S\), whose pins the decoder decides exactly; rows moved earlier, reassigned to their holes; rows assigned by pigeon answers or hole answers, recorded in \(\delta\)), or through a pin at a hole of \(Q\) used or emptied, which \(\alpha\) shows, or through a pin at an outside label to which its row is not matched, which the decoder's rule shows; (iii) \(T\) is not falsified in \(\alpha\): its rows assigned before \(m\) agree, its tail rows moved at \(m\) carry consistent code labels, its other tail rows are unassigned in both, since a row of \(B\) moved later is unassigned in reality and, were it in \(T\)'s tail, would be queried at \(m\) by the complete-term rule, and its pin's status agrees as in (ii). So the decoder finds \(T\); if its pin is alive it reads the pigeon answer and, when that differs from the pin's hole, the hole answer from \(\delta\), then the round's bit of \(\beta\); if the node has moves, by the bit or because the node has no round and the path continues, it reads the positions from \(\beta\) up to the last-of-node bit and their holes from \(\delta\). After the \(s\)-th move it returns the moved rows to the residual set, which gives \(\rho\), and reads \(\rho''\) off \(\sigma\), the code labels now being known. \(\square\)

Lemma C (count). With \(\theta_A=(N+1)e/(n-N-e+1)\) and \(A''=2rN\theta_A\), among the rich pairs of \(\Phi_e(S)\) the fraction whose compact tree has a path with at least \(s\) moves and fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds before its \(s\)-th move is at most \(A''^{\,s}(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\). Proof. As in Lemma C of the previous entry: \(e!\) values of \(\sigma\), \((2r)^s2^\nu\) of \(\beta\), \(N^s(N(N+2))^\nu\) of \(\delta\), the ratio \(|\Phi_{e-s}(S)|/|\Phi_e(S)|\le\theta_A^{\,s}\) checked by enumeration there, and Lemma B. \(\square\)

3. Richness with the own-row rule

Call a label \(y\) heavy if \(|A_y|>b/64\), and the reader column-sparse if, for every flat \(Q\) and every tail pattern \(p\), at most a quarter of the labels of \(C(p)\cap O\) are heavy. A reader with at most \(n^c\) terms has fewer than \(n^c/(b/64)\le128n^{c-1}\) heavy labels, and \(|C(p)\cap O|\ge n2^{-w-1}\) by the richness lemma's count, so it is column-sparse, for every flat, whenever \(2^w\le n^{2-c}/1024\).

Lemma R. If the reader is column-sparse, \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\) and \(2^{w+4}s\le e\), then, for a uniform \(e\)-subset \(S\) of \(A\) and a uniform pair over \(\Phi_e(S)\), the pair fails to be \(s\)-rich with probability at most \(n2^{-e/29}+2Mr\,e^{-s/3}\). Proof. For a label \(y\) that is not heavy, \(|A_y\cap S|\) is hypergeometric with mean at most \(e/64\), so \(\Pr[|A_y\cap S|>e/16]\le(\mathrm e/4)^{e/16}\le2^{-e/29}\); over at most \(n\) labels this costs \(n2^{-e/29}\), and outside it every non-heavy label has \(|A_y\cap S|\le e/16\). Fix a tail pattern \(p\) and let \(L\) be the non-heavy labels of \(C(p)\cap O\), \(|L|\ge\tfrac34|C(p)\cap O|\ge\tfrac38n2^{-w}\). Given \(S\), the set \(E(\rho)\) is a uniform \(e\)-subset of \(O\), so \(|E(\rho)\cap L|\) is hypergeometric with mean at least \(\tfrac38e2^{-w}\ge6s\), and \(|E(\rho)\cap L|\ge4s\) outside probability \(e^{-e2^{-w}/48}\le e^{-s/3}\). Given \(S\) and \(E(\rho)\), list the first \(m=\min(|E(\rho)\cap L|,\lceil e/2\rceil)\ge4s\) labels of \(E(\rho)\cap L\) and reveal their filling rows one at a time; the \(t\)-th is uniform over the \(e-t+1\ge e/2\) rows of \(S\) not yet revealed, so it lies in \(A_{y_t}\) with conditional probability at most \((e/16)/(e/2)=1/8\), and the number \(Z\) of the \(m\) labels whose filling row is pinned to them is dominated by a binomial with parameters \(m\) and \(1/8\): \(\Pr[Z\ge m/2]\le2^m8^{-m/2}=2^{-m/2}\le2^{-2s}\). Outside these events the pattern has at least \(m/2\ge2s\) valid labels, of which at most \(s-1\) are picked. Over \(Mr\) patterns the two terms cost at most \(Mr(e^{-s/3}+2^{-2s})\le2Mr\,e^{-s/3}\). \(\square\)

4. The composition and the restored switching clauses

Theorem G (composition on \(\Phi_0\)). Let \(F\) be a column-sparse role-separated reader, \(s=\lfloor N/12\rfloor-2r\ge1\), \(\nu_0=\lfloor N/48\rfloor\), and let the tails satisfy \(2^{w+4}s\le e\le n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\). If every path of \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) before a 1-leaf has at most \(\nu_0-1\) rounds except with probability \(p_R\) over \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\), then \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) has height below \(N/8-2r\), and \(F\) switches within the height budget, except with probability at most \[p_R+\tfrac75\Bigl(n2^{-e/29}+2Mr\,e^{-s/3}+2^{-N/8+(2r+1)(2+\frac12\log_2N)}\Bigr).\] Proof. A path of height at least \(s+2\nu_0\) has at least \(\nu_0\) rounds or at least \(s+2\) moves with fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds before its \(s\)-th move. The second is an event on \(\Phi_0\); by Lemma A0 its probability is at most \(\tfrac75\) times its average over \(S\) of its probability on \(\Phi_0^S\), which is at most the richness failure of Lemma R plus the count of Lemma C, and \(e(N+1)\le n/8\) holds. The bound \(A''\le1/(4\sqrt N)\) and the exponent are as in Theorem D of the previous entry. \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) is a matching decision tree for \(\rho'\) with the leaf properties of the switching lemmas, as recorded, a pigeon query at which every hole of \(Q\) is used or emptied being a dead leaf whose term vanishes modulo the axioms as in the light lemma's Section 1, and \(s+2\nu_0\le N/8-2r\). \(\square\)

Corollary (switching clauses restored). Let \(N\) and \(J_0\) satisfy the hypotheses of the cited round bound, \(N\ge8(c+1)\log_2n+(2r+1)(16+4\log_2N)\), \(s\ge3((2c+1)\ln n+\ln(2r))\) and \(e\ge29(c+2)\log_2n\), so that the three terms in the bracket are each at most \(n^{-c-1}\); and let the tails satisfy \(2^{w+4}s\le e\le n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\). Then a uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) switches, within the height budget, except with probability at most \(p_R+5n^{-c-1}\): (a) every role-separated reader with at most \(n^c\) terms, \(1\le c<2-\varepsilon\), \(800\,\mathrm e\,(N+1)\le n^{2-\varepsilon-c}\), and \(2^w\le n^{2-c}/1024\), with \(p_R=3n^{-c-1}\) (the multi-row size corollary, part (i) of the multi-row theorem transferred to the complete-term tree by Lemma 2 as stated); (b) every column-sparse role-separated reader with tails on at most \(t\) rows, total width \(W\), \(J_0\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) and \(1600\,\mathrm e\,t(N+1)N^4J_0n^c\le n^{3-2\varepsilon}\), with \(p_R=6n^{-c-2}\) (the crowded size corollary); (c) every column-sparse role-separated reader with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows and at most \(n^c\) terms for any \(c>0\), with \(p_R=4n^{-c-2}\) (the few-light-rows theorem), and every column-sparse role-separated reader of the combined theorem with its \(p_R\); in (b) and (c) the fewer than \(r_0\) rounds that Lemma 2 adds are absorbed by the thresholds, as recorded. Proof. Theorem G with the recorded round bound, which lives on \(\Phi_0\) and on this tree; the recorded proofs bound the rounds of a good path by \(N/192+2^{d}+r_0\le5N/384+r_0\le\lfloor N/48\rfloor-1\) once \(N\ge128(r_0+2)\), which their bounds on \(N\) give, so their events are Theorem G's hypothesis with \(\nu_0=\lfloor N/48\rfloor\); in (a) the reader is column-sparse by the count of Section 3. \(\square\)

Scope. These are per-reader statements, failure \(p_R+5n^{-c-1}\), the convention of the round bounds, so a union over the \(n^c\) readers of a source costs \(n^c\) times that. The light range is \(2^w\le e/(16s)\) with \(e\) up to \(n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\), so width up to \(\log_2n-\log_2(2^9rN^{5/2}s)\), for every size; the light lemma's \(n^{1/3}/(rNs)\) is exceeded at every \(c\). The one hypothesis beyond the round bound's is column-sparseness, automatic below width \((2-c)\log_2n-10\) for readers of size \(n^c\); it covers the light lemma's whole range for \(c\le5/3-o(1)\), and above that a reader pinning every row to every label of one pattern cube of width \(\tfrac13\log_2n\) (about \(n^{5/3}\) terms) is not column-sparse and is not covered, though its tree is short for other reasons (a matched tail row satisfies a term). The previous entry's slack tree, pin test and transferred round bound are superseded: they were the detour that hid the compact tree.

5. What remains

Two-role readers: the filling avoids every tail row, so a row pinned in one term and light in another is moved like a light row, and in \(\alpha\) it sits at a code label while in reality it is unassigned, which changes the status of its own pins; the recorded two-role decoder handles this on the slack tree by the complete-term rule and code labels outside the row's pinned labels, and the combination with the own-row rule is the next step. Dense pattern cubes: readers above size \(n^{5/3}\) whose pins fill a tail pattern cube of width in the light range are not column-sparse; for them the count of Lemma R has no valid labels, and a different argument, for instance one that treats such a cube's terms as heavy terms of the dichotomy, is needed. Per reader, tails of width between \((2-c)\log_2n\) and \(\ell\) beside a pin remain open without column-sparseness.

6. The tool and the runs

research/tools/check_pair_space_encoding.py --tree compact builds \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) for every pair on small boards, encodes the first path with at least \(h\) queries with the own-row rule (--code-rule own) and decodes it by simulating the compact tree from \(\rho^\ast\) and \(\sigma\), exactly as in Lemma B (records, all runs under ./compute.sh, \(n=8\), \(N=4\)). Eleven runs, six with every label pinned or three pinned labels and rows pinned to several labels each: no decoder failure on \(G\) (5094, 136, 492, 450, 5264, 296, 368 rich bad pairs) or off \(G\) (1567, 459, 176, 2, 516, 1303, 206, 103), where \(G\) is the event of the previous entry that no free label is pinned. Controls: with code labels chosen freely in \(E(\rho)\cap C(p)\) the decoder fails off \(G\) on 184 of 1816 and 181 of 1498 rich bad pairs, the pin at a filling row's own code label; with the previous entry's rule (code labels outside every pinned label) it decodes 734 rich bad pairs off \(G\) where the own-row rule admits 1303. The skip-the-tail variant that started the cycle failed on \(G\) on 120 of 302 (recorded in the results of this session's first invocations); the failing pair is traced in the README.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the multi-row setting, theorem and size corollary, the crowded theorem and corollary, the few-light-rows theorem, the complete-term rule (rule, Lemmas 1 and 2), the both-endpoints rule and matched-first preference, the height-budget observation, hole-query nodes, the light lemma's families, richness count and encoding, the composition-gap entry's routes, and the previous entry's Lemma A0 and Lemma C with its count check. Recorded obstructions checked: the composition correction's routes (this is its swap-encoding route, now unblocked), the narrowed intrinsic light-range observation, the two-role gap (role separation is assumed), and the round-trip counterexamples, which concern other trees. Checks run: the round-trip tool's batch 5 with its three controls, including the failing variant that started the cycle (Section 6). The standing reviewer, given the draft and the anchors, confirmed Lemmas B, C and R and Theorem G, the tree's identity with the recorded complete-term tree, the tool's agreement with Lemma B and the runs' agreement with the text, and reported ten findings, all applied: the off-by-one between "fewer than \(N/48\)" and \(\nu_0-1\) rounds, settled by the slack of the recorded proofs; a binomial tail written as its middle term; the pigeon answers missing from claim (ii)'s list; column-sparseness to be required for every flat; an unused bound on \(e\) in Lemma R; dead leaves; the corollary's size and \(J_0\) hypotheses; the composition correction's route to be named; the results README, which the reviewer found not yet written; and the status line's scope.

Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. On the literal frontier the composition lemma is now proved on the compact family for the recorded tree, so the switching clauses of the multi-row size corollary (below size \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\), tails below width \((2-c)\log_2n-10\)), the crowded corollary, the few-light-rows theorem and the combined theorem are restored for role-separated readers under column-sparseness, with a light range up to width \(\log_2n-O(\log N)\); two-role readers and dense pattern cubes above size \(n^{5/3}\) remain. Parity terms remain the open core.

Process assessment. The cycle's result came from a failed variant: the round-trip tool rejected the skip-the-tail rule within minutes, and tracing the one failing pair showed that the complete-term rule is what the decoder needs and that the slack tree contributed nothing, which turned a weakening of one hypothesis into the removal of the whole detour; the reviewer's findings were constants, wording and the record. Rule for the framework, not yet a rule: when a device is introduced to make a decoder work, ask what the decoder would do without it before building on it.
