18 September 2026 — Two-role readers on the compact composition: code labels outside the moved row's own pins and outside its filling row's pins, and the two-role round bounds regain their switching clauses

Status: working theorem (composition on the compact family for two-role readers under sparse pinning and column-sparseness). Spin cycle 209. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question and stopping point. The task was the two-role case of the compact composition: a row pinned in one term and light in another is moved to a code label in the code while unassigned in reality, which changes the status of its own pins in the code. The recorded two-role decoder on the slack family handled this by the complete-term rule (the current term's pinned row is assigned at its node by the round, so it is never a row moved later) and by code labels outside the moved row's own pinned labels. The stopping point is the same device on the compact composition: a code label must avoid the pins of two rows, its own filling row and the moved row, and with that rule Lemma B, Lemma R and Theorem G of the previous entry go through for two-role readers, so the recorded two-role round bounds, all on the complete-term tree, regain their switching clauses.

1. Setting

Readers are as in the complete-term rule's setting: \(A\) is the set of rows pinned in some term, \(B\) the set of rows light in some term, \(C=A\cap B\) may be nonempty, \(X_j\) is the set of labels to which row \(j\) is pinned; at most \(M\le n^c\) terms, at most \(r\) rows per term, at most \(w\) literals per tail row, \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\). Two hypotheses are added. The rows outside every tail, \(A_0\), number \(b=|A_0|=n+1-|B|\ge n/2+N+2\), that is \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\), the multi-row setting's bound, which the two-role settings had dropped; the pair space of the previous entry places its filling set \(S\) in \(A_0\), and Lemma A0 needs \(b\). And the reader is sparsely pinned, \(|X_j\cap C(p)|\le|C(p)|/4\) for every light row \(j\) and every pattern \(p\) of a term on \(j\), the recorded two-role hypothesis, and column-sparse as in Section 3 of the previous entry, with \(A_y\) the rows of \(A_0\) pinned to \(y\) and a label heavy if \(|A_y|>b/64\); the count there gives column-sparseness for every flat when \(2^w\le n^{2-c}/1024\). The tree is the compact complete-term tree \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\), the tree of the recorded two-role round bounds.

2. Code labels and the decoder

For a move of row \(j\) with pattern \(p\) a label \(y\in E(\rho)\cap C(p)\) is valid if the row filling it is not pinned to it, \(\rho''^{-1}(y)\notin A_y\), and \(j\) is not pinned to it, \(y\notin X_j\); the pair is \(s\)-rich if every pair \((j,p)\) of a light row and a pattern of a term on \(j\) has at least \(s\) valid labels. The code \((\rho^\ast,\sigma,\beta,\delta)\) is that of the previous entry with this validity.

Lemma B (decoder). The code determines the pair. Proof. The decoder and its evaluation rule are those of Lemma B of the previous entry; its three claims are re-examined where a two-role row \(j\) moved later, at its code label \(c_j\) in \(\alpha\) and unassigned in reality, has pins. (i) Matched pins agree: \(\rho^\ast\) matches \(j\) to \(c_j\notin X_j\), so it matches no pin of \(j\), and \(\mu'\) matches none, \(j\) being residual. (ii) A pin \((j,x)\) with \(x\notin Q\) is dead in both: in \(\rho'\) the label \(x\) is occupied by a row other than \(j\), and \(\alpha(j)=c_j\ne x\). A pin \((j,x)\) with \(x\in Q\) unused is alive in reality and dead in \(\alpha\); a term \(T'\) carrying it that precedes the current term \(T\) is falsified in reality, and not through its pin, so through a tail row assigned before \(m\), on which \(\alpha\) agrees, and \(T'\) is falsified in \(\alpha\) as well; \(T\) itself never carries such a pin, since an alive pin of the current term is resolved by the round at \(m\), which assigns \(j\) at \(m\), so that \(j\) is not moved later. Pins at \(c_j\) of other rows are dead in both, \(c_j\) being occupied in \(\rho'\) by its filling row, which by validity is not pinned to it, and \(\alpha(i)\ne c_j\) for every row \(i\ne j\). (iii) The current term's rows assigned before \(m\) agree, including a pinned row assigned by an earlier round or moved earlier and reassigned to its hole; its tail rows moved at \(m\) carry consistent code labels; a row of \(B\) moved later is not in its tail by the complete-term rule and, by the argument of (ii), not its pinned row. Everything else is as before, rows of \(S\) lying outside \(B\). \(\square\)

Lemma C of the previous entry, the count \(A''^{\,s}(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\) with \(A''=2rN(N+1)e/(n-N-e+1)\), is unchanged: validity only restricts the encoder's choice.

3. Richness with both exclusions

Lemma R. If the reader is sparsely pinned and column-sparse, \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\) and \(2^{w+6}s\le e\), then, for a uniform \(e\)-subset \(S\) of \(A_0\) and a uniform pair over \(\Phi_e(S)\), the pair fails to be \(s\)-rich with probability at most \(n2^{-e/29}+2Mr\,e^{-s}\). Proof. As in Lemma R of the previous entry, outside probability \(n2^{-e/29}\) every non-heavy label \(y\) has \(|A_y\cap S|\le e/16\). Fix \(j\) and a pattern \(p\) of a term on \(j\), and let \(L\) be the non-heavy labels of \(C(p)\cap O\setminus X_j\): \(|C(p)\cap O|\ge|C(p)|/2\), at most a quarter of it is heavy, and \(|X_j\cap C(p)|\le|C(p)|/4\), so \(|L|\ge\tfrac38|C(p)|-\tfrac14|C(p)|=n2^{-w-3}\). Then \(|E(\rho)\cap L|\) is hypergeometric with mean at least \(e2^{-w-3}\ge8s\), so it is at least \(4s\) outside probability \(e^{-e2^{-w-3}/8}\le e^{-s}\), and the sequential revelation of the filling on the first \(m=\min(|E(\rho)\cap L|,\lceil e/2\rceil)\ge4s\) of its labels gives at least \(m/2\ge2s\) valid labels outside probability \(2^{-m/2}\le2^{-2s}\), as before. Over at most \(Mr\) pairs \((j,p)\) this costs \(Mr(e^{-s}+2^{-2s})\le2Mr\,e^{-s}\). \(\square\)

4. The composition and the restored two-role clauses

Theorem G (two-role form). Let \(F\) be a sparsely pinned, column-sparse reader as in Section 1, \(s=\lfloor N/12\rfloor-2r\ge1\), \(\nu_0=\lfloor N/48\rfloor\), with tails satisfying \(2^{w+6}s\le e\le n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\). If every path of \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) before a 1-leaf has at most \(\nu_0-1\) rounds except with probability \(p_R\) over \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\), then \(F\) switches within the height budget except with probability at most \(p_R+\tfrac75\bigl(n2^{-e/29}+2Mr\,e^{-s}+2^{-N/8+(2r+1)(2+\frac12\log_2N)}\bigr)\). Proof. That of Theorem G with Lemmas B and R above; Lemma A0 applies with \(b=|A_0|\ge n/2+N+2\). \(\square\)

Corollary (two-role switching clauses restored). Let \(N\ge8(c+1)\log_2n+(2r+1)(16+4\log_2N)\), \(s\ge(2c+1)\ln n+\ln(2r)\), \(e\ge29(c+2)\log_2n\), the tails as in the theorem, and the reader sparsely pinned with \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\). Then a uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) switches within the height budget except with probability \(p_R+5n^{-c-1}\) for: (a) every two-role reader with at most \(n^c\) terms, \(1\le c<2-\varepsilon\), \(800\,\mathrm e\,(N+1)\le n^{2-\varepsilon-c}\) and \(2^w\le n^{2-c}/1024\), with \(p_R=3n^{-c-1}\) (Corollary 1 of the two-role many-rows entry); (b) every column-sparse reader of that entry's Corollary 2, with \(p_R=6n^{-c-2}\); (c) every column-sparse two-role reader with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows, which makes the bound on \(|B|\) automatic, and at most \(n^c\) terms for any \(c>0\), with \(p_R=4n^{-c-2}\) (the two-role few-rows theorem); (d) every column-sparse reader of the two-role exposed theorem with its \(p_R=6n^{-c-2}\); each with the cited result's own hypotheses on \(N\), \(J_0\), the exposed set and, in (d), the mass condition \(\sum_{j\in C_0}m^{\rm L}_j\le M_C\). Proof. The theorem with the cited round bound, which lives on \(\Phi_0\) and on the complete-term tree; the cited proofs bound the rounds of a good path by \(N/192+2^{d_\varepsilon}\le5N/384\le\lfloor N/48\rfloor-1\) in (a), for \(N\ge256\), and by \(N/192+2^d+2r_0\le\lfloor N/48\rfloor-1\) in (b) to (d), once \(N\ge128(2r_0+2)\), which their bounds on \(N\) give; in (a) column-sparseness follows from the count of the previous entry. \(\square\)

Scope. The recorded clauses read "under sparse pinning when the tails lie in the light lemma's range"; they now hold with the pair-space light range, width up to \(\log_2n-\log_2(2^{11}rN^{5/2}s)\), and with column-sparseness, automatic below width \((2-c)\log_2n-10\), at the price of \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\), which the two-role settings had not needed for their round bounds but which the pair space needs for its filling set. Per-reader statements, as before.

5. What remains

The two-role part of the dense-pinning obstruction and of the dense-cube obstruction is closed under sparse pinning; their dense-cube part remains, and the claim index says so. The window's open cases are now those of the round bounds themselves: two-role readers with more than \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows beyond the exposed theorem's mass condition (step (H4c) of the multi-row proof loses the two-role rows, as the complete-term scope records), more than \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) crowded rows at sizes at least \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\), and, for the composition, the dense pattern cubes above size \(n^{5/3}\) and rows pinned to more than a quarter of a pattern cube, both failures of richness rather than of the decoder. Per reader, rows of width between \((2-c)\log_2n\) and \(\ell\) beside a pin remain open without column-sparseness.

6. The tool and the runs

research/tools/check_pair_space_encoding.py --tree compact --two-role --code-rule own-two-role draws tails from all rows, so a row may be pinned in one term and light in another, and excludes from a moved row's code labels its own pinned labels as well as the filling row's; --two-role-example is the recorded two-role counterexample of the mixed-term tool, the reader on which the first two-role encoding failed (records, all under ./compute.sh, \(n=8\), \(N=4\)). Batch 6, 12 runs with both exclusions: the recorded two-role example decoded on all its rich bad pairs (2100, 1560, 1320; its pins lie in \(Q\), so every pair is on \(G\)); the outside-pin example, whose two-role row is pinned at an outside label consistent with its light pattern, decoded on 2660 on and 1800 off \(G\) and 1520 on and 720 off \(G\); the random two-role readers decoded on every rich bad pair (0/13, 322/304, 106/65, 0/35, 0/0, 0/0, 64/282 on/off \(G\); one run had no pair, its tails covering all but one row). Control without the moved row's exclusion: the outside-pin example fails off \(G\) on 880 of 1800 and 520 of 1320 rich bad pairs, the two-role row moved to the outside label it is pinned to, whose pin then looks matched and satisfied in the code while the label is filled by another row in reality; on the recorded example, whose pins lie in \(Q\), and on the random readers, whose two-role rows are pinned outside \(Q\) only at labels inconsistent with their light patterns, the two rules admit the same code labels and the control passes, as it should.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the compact composition's Lemmas B, C and R, Theorem G and corollary as committed; the two-role decoder's Lemmas 3 and 4; the two-role few-rows theorem, the two-role many-rows setting, theorem and corollaries; the complete-term rule and scope; the two-role gap correction. Recorded obstructions checked: the two-role gap (its mechanism, the round assigning the pinned row before the tail, is what claim (iii) uses), the complete-term scope's open cases, the dense-cube obstruction (narrowed here). Checks run: batch 6 with both exclusions on the recorded two-role counterexample, an outside-pin example built for the second exclusion and random two-role readers, and the control without the moved row's exclusion, which fails on the outside-pin example (Section 6). The standing reviewer, given the draft and the anchors, confirmed Lemmas B and R, Theorem G in its two-role form and the corollary, the citations' hypotheses and their slack for the off-by-one, and the tool's agreement with the rule and the runs, and reported four findings, all applied: a sentence of the run report wrongly said the random readers' two-role rows are pinned in \(Q\) only (they are pinned outside \(Q\) at labels inconsistent with their light patterns, which is why the control coincides there); the off-by-one slack differs between (a) and (b) to (d); the exposed theorem's mass condition and the automatic \(|B|\) bound in (c) were to be named; and the two obstruction rows of the claim index were to be narrowed. The inherited \(c\ge1\) of Corollary 1 is unused, as in the cited corollary.

Main-route assessment. The first obligation is unchanged. On the literal frontier every recorded round bound, role-separated or two-role, now composes into switching within the height budget on the compact family, under column-sparseness and, for two-role rows, sparse pinning; the open cases of the window are those of the round bounds and of richness (dense pattern cubes above size \(n^{5/3}\)). Parity terms remain the open core.

Process assessment. A short cycle: the recorded two-role decoder's device transferred as expected, and the tool's first control was uninformative (the two rules coincided on the readers at hand), which the added outside-pin example repaired before the draft went out; the reviewer caught a factual slip in the run report that the record itself contradicted, a reminder to read the jsonl, not the summary, when describing runs. 2026-09-18: Column-sparseness is unnecessary: code labels outside the pin labels of the path's current terms

Working theorem: the compact composition holds for every recorded round bound without column-sparseness, so the dense-cube obstruction is closed. Spin cycle. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question. The proposed next step was to attack the dense pattern cubes of the dense-cube obstruction: readers above size \(n^{5/3}\) whose pins fill a tail pattern cube, for which the own-row rule of the compact composition leaves no valid code label, and to test the intended mechanism on the all-pairs reader first. The test showed that the heavy-term mechanism has the wrong convention (the per-reader failure of the heavy count is \(n^{c-2}\), not \(n^{-c-1}\)), and the examination of what the own-row rule actually protects against showed that it protects against a divergence that only the current terms of the encoded path can cause. Excluding their pin labels, at most \(s+\nu_0-1\) of them, is enough, and it needs nothing of the reader. This entry records the modified code, its decoder, the resulting richness lemma, which is a count on \(E(\rho)\) alone, the theorem and its corollaries, and the exhaustive checks, including the all-pairs reader, on which the own-row rule encodes no move at all.

1. What the own-row rule protects against

The setting, the pair space, Lemma A0 and the code \((\rho^\ast,\sigma,\beta,\delta)\) are those of the compact composition, and for two-role readers those of its two-role form. The decoder simulates \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) from \(\alpha\), which shows every row of \(S\) at its label except the rows filling code labels, marked "at the \(k\)-th code label". Before the \(k\)-th move is decoded the decoder does not know the \(k\)-th code label \(y_k\), so it cannot decide the pins \((f_k,y_k)\) of the filling row \(f_k=\rho''^{-1}(y_k)\), which are matched in reality. The own-row rule removed those pins by choosing a label to which the filling row is not pinned, and that is what required column-sparseness. But the pins \((f_k,y_k)\) can change the decoder's selection at a node \(m\) only if a term carrying one of them is the current term of \(m\): a term carrying such a pin that is not falsified at \(m\) is a pin-matched term, and the matched-first preference selects the first pin-matched term that is not falsified, so such a term either is the current term or comes after it in the reader's order, and a term that comes after the current term plays no part at \(m\). Once the \(k\)-th move is decoded, \(y_k=\rho^\ast(j_k)\) is known and the decoder decides the pins of \(f_k\) exactly. So the code label of the \(k\)-th move only has to avoid the pin labels of the current terms of the nodes up to and including the node of the \(k\)-th move, and there are at most \(s+\nu_0-1\) such nodes on the encoded path.

2. The current-term rule and its decoder

Code labels. Fix a pair whose compact tree has a path with at least \(s\) moves and fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds before its \(s\)-th move, take the lexicographically first such path, cut after its \(s\)-th move, and let \(m_k\) be the node of its \(k\)-th move. Let \(X_{\le k}\) be the set of pin labels of the current terms of the nodes up to and including \(m_k\); \(|X_{\le k}|\le(k-1)+(\nu_0-1)+1\le s+\nu_0-1\), every node having a move or a round. The code label of the \(k\)-th move, of a row \(j_k\) with pattern \(p_k\) in the current term of \(m_k\), is the smallest label of \(E(\rho)\cap C(p_k)\) that is not a code label of an earlier move and not in \(X_{\le k}\); for a two-role reader also not in \(X_{j_k}\), the set of labels \(j_k\) is pinned to, as in the two-role form. The code is \((\rho^\ast,\sigma,\beta,\delta)\) as before with these code labels.

Decoder. The decoder of Lemma B of the compact composition with one change to its evaluation rule: a row marked "at the \(k\)-th code label" satisfies no pin while the \(k\)-th move is undecoded; when the \(k\)-th move is decoded, its row \(j_k\) being read from \(\beta\) and \(y_k=\rho^\ast(j_k)\) from \(\rho^\ast\), the marked row \(f_k\), which \(\sigma\) names, is assigned \(y_k\) in \(\alpha\), and from then on it satisfies the pin \((f_k,y_k)\) and no other, and the preference counts that pin as matched.

Lemma B (decoder). The code determines the pair. Proof. The decoder simulates \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) node by node. At a node \(m\) with real current term \(T\), let \(K_m\) be the set of \(k\) with \(m_k\ge m\), the slots undecoded when the decoder selects at \(m\); a marked row of a slot \(k\notin K_m\) is assigned its label in \(\alpha\) and behaves as a row of \(S\) with a value in \(E(\rho^\ast)\). Three claims. (i) A term not falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi_{<m}\) whose pin is not \((f_k,y_k)\) for a \(k\in K_m\) has the same pin-matched status in \(\alpha\) and in \(\rho'\): its pinned row \(i\) lies in \(A\), so it is not moved, and \(\alpha(i)=\rho^\ast(i)=\rho'(i)\) for \(i\notin S\), \(\alpha(i)=\sigma(i)=\rho'(i)\) for \(i\in S\) with a value in \(E(\rho^\ast)\) or with a decoded slot, while a marked row of an undecoded slot \(k\) is matched in reality only to \(y_k\), and the pin \((i,y_k)\) is excluded; the preference counts only pins matched by \(\rho'\), as recorded. (ii) A term falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi_{<m}\) is falsified in \(\alpha\): through a tail row assigned in reality, on which \(\alpha\) agrees as in the recorded proof (matched rows, rows moved earlier and reassigned to their holes, rows assigned by round answers), or through its pin, a hole of \(Q\) used or emptied, which \(\alpha\) shows, or an outside label \(x\) with \(\rho'(i)\ne x\) or \(i\) residual, where \(\alpha(i)\ne x\), or \(\alpha(i)\) is undefined, or \(i\) is a marked row of an undecoded slot, whose real label differs from \(x\) and which satisfies no pin by the rule: dead in both. (iii) A term \(T'\) carrying a pin \((f_k,y_k)\) with \(k\in K_m\) and not falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi_{<m}\) comes after \(T\) in the reader's order: it is pin-matched in reality, so if it preceded \(T\) the preference would select it or an earlier pin-matched term, and \(T'=T\) is excluded because \(m\le m_k\) and \(y_k\notin X_{\le k}\), which contains the pin label of \(T\). Now the decoder scans the terms in order as the preference does. Every term before \(T\) is falsified in reality, hence in \(\alpha\) by (ii), or is not falsified and not pin-matched in reality; the latter has, by (iii), no pin \((f_k,y_k)\) with \(k\in K_m\), so by (i) it is not pin-matched in \(\alpha\) either, and the scan passes it whether or not \(\alpha\) shows it falsified through the code label of a row moved later. \(T\) is not falsified in \(\alpha\): its rows assigned before \(m\) agree, its tail rows moved at \(m\) carry consistent code labels, its other tail rows are unassigned in both by the complete-term rule, and its pin agrees by (i), since \(T\)'s pin is not \((f_k,y_k)\) with \(k\in K_m\). If \(T\) is pin-matched in reality it is pin-matched in \(\alpha\) by (i) and the scan stops at \(T\); otherwise no term is pin-matched and not falsified in reality, and none is in \(\alpha\): a term not falsified in \(\alpha\) is not falsified in reality by (ii), and a pin matched in \(\alpha\) is matched in reality, since \(\alpha\) agrees with \(\rho'\) wherever it assigns a pinned row of \(A\), and for a two-role reader a moved row's code label lies outside its pinned labels; so the scan returns the first term not falsified in \(\alpha\), which is \(T\). The rest, the reading of the round answers and the moves from \(\delta\) and \(\beta\), the return of the moved rows to the residual set and of \(\rho''\) from \(\sigma\), is as recorded. For a two-role reader the additional points of the two-role form's Lemma B, the pins of a row moved later, are unchanged, since a moved row's code label lies outside its own pinned labels and outside every other code label. \(\square\)

Lemma C of the compact composition, the count \(A''^{\,s}(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\) with \(A''=2rN(N+1)e/(n-N-e+1)\), is unchanged: the code has the same format and the rule only restricts the encoder's choice.

3. Richness is a count on \(E(\rho)\)

Call the pair \(s\)-rich if \(|E(\rho)\cap C(p)|\ge3s\) for every pattern \(p\) of a tail row, and for a two-role reader \(|E(\rho)\cap C(p)\setminus X_j|\ge3s\) for every pair \((j,p)\) of a light row and a pattern of a term on \(j\). If \(s\ge\nu_0\), the encoder always has a label: at the \(k\)-th move at most \(k-1\le s-1\) labels are picked and at most \(s+\nu_0-1\) excluded, and \(3s-(s-1)-(s+\nu_0-1)=s-\nu_0+2\ge2\).

Lemma R. If \(2^{w+4}s\le e\le n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\) (which implies the recorded \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\)), and for a two-role reader the reader is sparsely pinned, then, for every \(e\)-set \(S\) and a uniform pair over \(\Phi_e(S)\), the pair fails to be \(s\)-rich with probability at most \(Mr\,e^{-s}\). Proof. Given \(S\), the set \(E(\rho)\) is a uniform \(e\)-subset of \(O\), \(|O|=n-N\). For a pattern \(p\) of width at most \(w\), \(|C(p)\cap O|\ge n2^{-w}-N\ge n2^{-w-1}\), as \(N\le n2^{-w-2}\) in the stated range; under sparse pinning \(|X_j\cap C(p)|\le|C(p)|/4\), so \(|C(p)\cap O\setminus X_j|\ge n2^{-w}-N-n2^{-w-2}\ge n2^{-w-1}\). Hence \(|E(\rho)\cap C(p)|\), or \(|E(\rho)\cap C(p)\setminus X_j|\), is hypergeometric with mean at least \(e2^{-w-1}\ge8s\), and it is below \(3s\le\tfrac38\cdot8s\) with probability at most \(e^{-(5/8)^2\cdot8s/2}\le e^{-s}\), by the Chernoff bound for a hypergeometric variable. There are at most \(Mr\) patterns of tail rows, or pairs \((j,p)\). \(\square\)

4. The composition without column-sparseness

Theorem G (composition on \(\Phi_0\), current-term rule). Let \(F\) be a role-separated reader as in Section 1 of the compact composition, or a sparsely pinned two-role reader as in Section 1 of its two-role form, with \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\); let \(s=\lfloor N/12\rfloor-2r\ge\nu_0=\lfloor N/48\rfloor\), and let the tails satisfy \(2^{w+4}s\le e\le n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\). If every path of \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) before a 1-leaf has at most \(\nu_0-1\) rounds except with probability \(p_R\) over \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\), then \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) has height below \(N/8-2r\), and \(F\) switches within the height budget, except with probability at most \[p_R+\tfrac75\Bigl(Mr\,e^{-s}+2^{-N/8+(2r+1)(2+\frac12\log_2N)}\Bigr).\] Proof. The proof of Theorem G of the compact composition, with Lemma B and Lemma R above in place of its Lemmas B and R: a path of height at least \(s+2\nu_0\) has at least \(\nu_0\) rounds or at least \(s\) moves with fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds before its \(s\)-th move; the second event, on \(\Phi_0\), has probability at most \(\tfrac75\) times its average over \(S\) of its probability on \(\Phi_0^S\) by Lemma A0, which is at most the failure of richness plus the count of Lemma C among rich pairs, and \(e(N+1)\le n/8\) holds; \(A''\le1/(4\sqrt N)\) and the exponent are as recorded; Lemma A0 applies with \(b=|A|\ge n/2+N+2\), or \(b=|A_0|\) in the two-role form. \(\square\)

Corollary (switching clauses without column-sparseness). Let \(N\) and \(J_0\) satisfy the hypotheses of the cited round bound, \(N\ge8(c+1)\log_2n+(2r+1)(16+4\log_2N)\) and \(s\ge(2c+1)\ln n+\ln r\), so that the two terms in the bracket are each at most \(n^{-c-1}\), and let the tails satisfy \(2^{w+4}s\le e\le n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\). Then a uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) switches, within the height budget, except with probability at most \(p_R+3n^{-c-1}\), for: (a) every role-separated reader with at most \(n^c\) terms, \(1\le c<2-\varepsilon\), \(800\,\mathrm e\,(N+1)\le n^{2-\varepsilon-c}\), with \(p_R=3n^{-c-1}\) (the multi-row size corollary, transferred to the complete-term tree by Lemma 2 of the complete-term rule); (b) every role-separated reader with tails on at most \(t\) rows, total width \(W\), \(J_0\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) and \(1600\,\mathrm e\,t(N+1)N^4J_0n^c\le n^{3-2\varepsilon}\), with \(p_R=6n^{-c-2}\) (the crowded size corollary); (c) every role-separated reader with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows and at most \(n^c\) terms for any \(c>0\), with \(p_R=4n^{-c-2}\) (the few-light-rows theorem), and every role-separated reader of the combined theorem with its \(p_R\); and, under sparse pinning with \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\), (d) every two-role reader with at most \(n^c\) terms, \(1\le c<2-\varepsilon\), \(800\,\mathrm e\,(N+1)\le n^{2-\varepsilon-c}\), with \(p_R=3n^{-c-1}\) (Corollary 1 of the two-role many-rows entry); (e) every reader of that entry's Corollary 2, with \(p_R=6n^{-c-2}\); (f) every two-role reader with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) light rows, which makes the bound on \(|B|\) automatic, and at most \(n^c\) terms for any \(c>0\), with \(p_R=4n^{-c-2}\) (the two-role few-rows theorem); (g) every reader of the two-role exposed theorem with its \(p_R=6n^{-c-2}\); each with the cited result's own hypotheses on \(N\), \(J_0\), the exposed set and, in (g), the mass condition \(\sum_{j\in C_0}m^{\rm L}_j\le M_C\). Proof. Theorem G with the cited round bound, which lives on \(\Phi_0\) and on this tree; the cited proofs bound the rounds of a good path below \(\nu_0\) with the slack recorded in the corollaries of the compact composition and its two-role form, whose bounds on \(N\) give it; \(s\ge\nu_0\) holds for \(N\ge16(2r+1)\), which the bound on \(N\) gives; and \(n^cr\,e^{-s}\le n^{-c-1}\) for \(s\ge(2c+1)\ln n+\ln r\). The width conditions \(2^w\le n^{2-c}/1024\) of the recorded clauses (a) and (d) were only the automatic column-sparseness, and are gone. \(\square\)

Scope. Per-reader statements, failure \(p_R+3n^{-c-1}\), the convention of the round bounds, so a union over the \(n^c\) readers of a source costs \(n^c\) times that. The light range is \(2^w\le e/(16s)\) with \(e\) up to \(n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\), width up to \(\log_2n-\log_2(2^8rN^{3/2}(N+1)s)\), for every size. The only hypotheses beyond the round bound's are the tail range and, for two-role readers, sparse pinning, a hypothesis on the pins of the light rows, and \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\), which the pair space needs for its filling set; for role-separated readers nothing is assumed about the pins. The recorded conditions \(e\ge29(c+2)\log_2n\) and \(s\ge3((2c+1)\ln n+\ln(2r))\) came from Lemma R of the compact composition and are not needed.

5. What this closes and what remains

The dense-cube obstruction and the dense-pinning obstruction are closed: both concern the filling rows of a role-separated reader, and the reader pinning every row outside its tails to every label of one pattern cube, which has no valid label under the own-row rule, is covered by Theorem G with the round bound of clause (a) or (b), its tree being short by the count of Section 4, not only by the satisfied-term argument of the scope note. The own-row rule and its richness lemma stand but are superseded. For role-separated readers the pins are no longer among the window's open cases; a two-role reader still needs sparse pinning, so a tail row pinned to more than a quarter of its own pattern cube remains open, as the two-role form recorded. What remains otherwise is, per reader, tail rows of width above the pair-space light range, between \(\log_2n-O(\log N)\) and \(\ell\), where neither the count (the light range of every extension encoding, code obstruction) nor the dichotomy (whose per-reader failure is \(n^{c-2}\), lemma) applies; and the round bounds' own open cases, more than \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) crowded rows at sizes at least \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\) and many heavy two-role rows. Terms containing parities remain open.

6. Exhaustive checks

The checker (check_pair_space_encoding.py) gained the code rules current and current-two-role, which exclude the pin labels of the current terms of the nodes up to the move, and --reveal-slots, the decoder's assignment of a marked row once its move is decoded; a diagnostic splits the failures of a run by whether the code used a current term's pin label. Batch 7 (runs, README, provenance): the eleven role-separated configurations of batch 5 under current --reveal-slots decode every rich pair, 0 failures, with at least as many rich pairs as under the own-row rule on every configuration and more on seven (for instance 1641 against 1567, 1360 against 1303, 167 against 103 off \(G\)); the recorded two-role counterexample, the outside-pin example and six random two-role readers with the tool's default term counts, under current-two-role --reveal-slots, 0 failures; batch 7b re-runs the six random two-role readers of batch 6 in their exact configurations, 0 failures, again with at least as many rich pairs as the own rule (322 against 304, 106 against 65, 64 against 282 off \(G\), among others). Controls: current without --reveal-slots fails on 9 of 1641 rich pairs off \(G\) (seed 4), so the decoder must learn the slot's label; any --reveal-slots fails on 175 of 1816 and 181 of 1498 rich pairs off \(G\) (seeds 4 and 10), and every failing code used a current term's pin label (the diagnostic counts 0 failures without one and 16 decoded pairs with one), which is the rule's content. Batch 7c, the all-pairs reader of the obstruction, rows \(0\) to \(5\) pinned to every label of the cube of one literal and tails of that literal on rows \(6\), \(7\), \(8\): on flats of two holes (378000 pairs per run) the own-row rule encodes no path with a move on any flat (rich pairs with moves 0 in every run, only round-only paths being encodable), while the current-term rule encodes and decodes every rich pair: 20856 and 19680 paths with moves on the flat \(\{2,6\}\) inside the cube, 42336 on the flat \(\{0,1\}\) meeting the cube in one hole, 7418 on the flat \(\{1,3\}\) missing the cube, 0 failures. On the latter two flats the control any --reveal-slots fails on 21504 of 71208 and 14680 of 26352 rich pairs with moves, every failure through a current term's pin label (11100 and 4254 pairs used such a label and still decoded; none failed without one). Flats of four holes and thresholds of three queries gave no encodable path on this reader (the flat inside the cube leaves no outside cube label; no path reaches three queries) and are recorded as uninformative.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the compact composition's setting, Lemmas B, C and R, Theorem G, corollary and scope; the two-role form's decoder, richness, theorem and corollary; Lemma A0; the matched-first preference and the complete-term rule; the statements of the seven cited round bounds (none uses column-sparseness or a width condition beyond the light lemma's range in its switching clause). Recorded obstructions checked: the dense-cube and dense-pinning obstructions (closed for the filling rows they concern), the composition gap (discharged), the code obstruction (the light range remains), the two-role gap (its mechanism is unchanged by the rule). Checks run: batches 7, 7b, 7c and 7d of the exhaustive checker, with the two negative controls and the all-pairs reader (Section 6). The standing reviewer, given the draft and the anchors, confirmed Lemmas B and R, Theorem G and the corollary, the tool's agreement with the rule and the records with the text, and reported four findings, all applied: the scope sentences claimed no hypothesis on the pins for two-role readers too, which still need sparse pinning on their light rows; Lemma B's last case needed the contrapositive of (ii) and the one-directional agreement of matched pins; the hypothesis \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\) is implied by the tail range and the heavy-label notation was no longer used; and the batch-7 two-role runs were not the batch-6 configurations, which batch 7b re-runs. The inherited \(c\ge1\) of clauses (a) and (d) is unused, as in the cited corollaries.

Assessment. The named obligation, the composition of the recorded round bounds into switching within the height budget, is now discharged for every recorded round bound with tails in the pair-space light range, with no hypothesis on the pins of a role-separated reader and sparse pinning for a two-role one; the window's open cases are the tail widths above that range and the round bounds' own cases. The consolidation of Working mathematical context that the next step asked for is done in this cycle: the window theorem is stated once, with its hypotheses, and the round-bound paragraph is condensed.

Process assessment. The next step's instruction to test the intended mechanism on the all-pairs reader before drafting paid off twice: the heavy-term mechanism failed the test at once, and asking what the own-row rule actually protected against, rather than how to satisfy it, gave the simpler rule; the tool then settled the question in one batch before any writing, and the two negative controls plus the diagnostic split of failures by cause made the run report checkable. One wasted run: the first all-pairs example left a spare unpinned row, which hid the own rule's failure until the reader was fixed. No framework change.

2026-09-18: Wide tail rows: unplaced moves compose under a wide-move bound, and the complete-term tree needs hole queries for shared wide cubes

Conditional result (composition under a wide-move bound) and obstruction (long complete-term paths for a shared wide cube), with finite checks. Spin cycle. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question. The window's next case is, per reader, the tail rows wider than the pair-space light range, above \(\log_2n-O(\log N)\) literals (remaining). The proposed next step was to skip the terms with a residual wide row whose pattern cube misses the flat, to check that the recorded round bounds survive that change, and to encode the remaining wide-row moves at their answer holes. Testing the plan on simple readers before drafting changed it in two ways. Placing a moved row at a hole of \(Q\) gains nothing: the flat is recoverable from the code, so the family ratio is above one; a wide row can, however, be moved without being placed at all, at the price of naming its answer, and the pair-space count absorbs a bounded number of such moves (Section 1). The bound on the number of wide moves cannot come from the complete-term tree: a pin-free reader whose rows share one wide pattern has, with probability about \(N/n\), a path querying every residual row of the pattern without ever resolving the one hole of the flat that the pattern contains, so the tree needs hole queries for wide rows (Section 2). This entry records the conditional composition, the obstruction, and the finite checks; the wide-round bound for a tree with hole queries is the named obligation.

1. Composition with unplaced wide moves

Setting. A reader as in Section 1 of the compact composition, role-separated, or two-role and sparsely pinned with \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\) as in its two-role form, except that a tail row of a term may be wide: more than \(w\) literals, up to \(\ell\). The tree is the complete-term tree \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) as recorded: at the current term, after its round if its pin is alive, every uncovered tail row, light or wide, is queried in order over the unused holes of \(Q\). A move of a wide row is a wide move. Nothing else changes: the pair space, Lemma A0, and the code \((\rho^\ast,\sigma,\beta,\delta)\) of the current-term rule, with one addition: a wide row moved on the encoded path is not matched to a code label; it stays in the residual set of \(\rho^\ast\), its entry in \(\beta\) carries its kind (wide) with its position among the term's tail rows and the last-of-node bit, and its answer is recorded in \(\delta\) like any move's. So \(\rho^\ast\in\Phi_{e-m_{\rm l}}(S)\), \(m_{\rm l}\) the number of light moves, and \(\sigma\) is a bijection of \(S\) onto \(E(\rho^\ast)\sqcup\{1,\dots,m_{\rm l}\}\), the \(k\)-th slot standing for the \(k\)-th light move's code label.

Lemma B (decoder). The code determines the pair. Proof. The decoder of the current-term rule, which simulates \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) from \(\alpha\) node by node. A wide row moved later is unassigned in \(\alpha\) and unassigned in reality, so \(\alpha\) agrees with \(\rho'\) on it, and claims (i) to (iii) of that lemma hold verbatim; at the node of a wide move the decoder has found the current term \(T\), reads from \(\beta\) that the move is wide and its position, which names the row, and reads the answer from \(\delta\), after which \(\alpha\) agrees with reality on the row, as for a light move. For a two-role reader a wide row may carry pins; unassigned in both, its pins have the same status in \(\alpha\) and in reality, which is more than the two-role form's Lemma B needs for a placed row. At the end the placed rows are returned to the residual set, where the wide rows already are, giving \(\rho\), and \(\rho''\) is read off \(\sigma\). \(\square\)

Lemma C (count). Let \(\theta_A=(N+1)e/(n-N-e+1)\) and \(A_{\rm w}=4rN\theta_A\). Among the pairs of \(\Phi_e(S)\) that are \(s\)-rich for their light patterns, the fraction whose compact tree has a path with at least \(s\) moves, fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds and at most \(\nu_1\) wide moves before its \(s\)-th move is at most \((\nu_1+1)A_{\rm w}^{\,s-\nu_1}(4rN)^{\nu_1}(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\). Proof. As in Lemma C of the compact composition with the code above: for a path with \(m_{\rm w}\le\nu_1\) wide moves and \(m_{\rm l}=s-m_{\rm w}\) light moves, \(\rho^\ast\) ranges over \(\Phi_{e-m_{\rm l}}(S)\), whose size is at most \(\theta_A^{\,m_{\rm l}}|\Phi_e(S)|\) by the recorded ratio, \(\sigma\) over \(e!\) values, \(\beta\) over at most \((4r)^s2^{\nu}\) (kind, position and last bit per move, one bit per round) and \(\delta\) over \(N^s(N(N+2))^{\nu}\) for a path with \(\nu<\nu_0\) rounds, the sum over \(\nu\) being absorbed by \(\sum_{\nu<\nu_0}(2N(N+2))^{\nu}\le(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\) as in the recorded Lemma C; Lemma B makes the code injective, and summing over \(m_{\rm w}\) gives \(\sum_{m_{\rm w}\le\nu_1}\theta_A^{\,s-m_{\rm w}}(4rN)^s(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\le(\nu_1+1)(4rN\theta_A)^{s-\nu_1}(4rN)^{\nu_1}(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\). \(\square\)

Theorem G (composition with wide rows). Let \(F\) be a reader of the setting, \(s=\lfloor N/12\rfloor-2r\ge\nu_0=\nu_1=\lfloor N/48\rfloor\), \(r\le N^6/16\), and let the light tails satisfy \(2^{w+4}s\le e\le n/(32rN^4(N+1))\). If, except with probability \(p_R+p_W\) over \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\), every path of \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) before a 1-leaf has at most \(\nu_0-1\) rounds and at most \(\nu_1\) wide moves, then \(\mathcal T_c(F,\rho')\) has height below \(N/8-2r\), and \(F\) switches within the height budget, except with probability at most \[p_R+p_W+\tfrac75\Bigl(Mr\,e^{-s}+2^{-N/8+(2r+2)(2+3\log_2N)}\Bigr).\] Proof. A path of height at least \(s+2\nu_0\) has at least \(\nu_0\) rounds, or at least \(s\) moves with fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds before its \(s\)-th move; the first is the round bound's event, and the second with more than \(\nu_1\) wide moves before the \(s\)-th move is the wide-move bound's. The remaining event is on \(\Phi_0\); by Lemma A0 its probability is at most \(\tfrac75\) times its average over \(S\) of its probability on \(\Phi_0^S\), at most the richness failure \(Mr\,e^{-s}\) of Lemma R of the current-term rule for the light patterns plus the count of Lemma C, and \(e(N+1)\le n/8\) holds. The bound on \(e\) gives \(A_{\rm w}\le4rN(N+1)e/(n/2)\le1/(4N^3)\), so \(A_{\rm w}^{\,s-\nu_1}\le2^{-(N/16-2r-1)(2+3\log_2N)}\), while \((4rN)^{\nu_1}(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}(\nu_1+1)\le2^{(N/48)(3\log_2N+\log_2r+4)+\log_2N}\) as \(N+2\le2N\); the exponent is at most \(-N/8-(N/8)\log_2N+(N/48)(\log_2r+4)+(2r+1)(2+3\log_2N)+\log_2N\le-N/8+(2r+2)(2+3\log_2N)\), using \(6\log_2N\ge\log_2r+4\) for \(N^6\ge16r\). The tree is a matching decision tree for \(\rho'\) with the leaf properties of the switching lemmas, as recorded, and \(s+2\nu_0\le N/8-2r\). \(\square\)

Scope. The theorem is conditional on two bounds for the same tree: the recorded round bound \(p_R\), proved for the complete-term tree for tails of any shape by clauses (a), (c), (d) and (f) of the corollary of the current-term rule and for bounded total width by (b), (e) and (g), so that it is available for readers with wide rows, and a wide-move bound \(p_W\), proved for no reader yet; Section 2 shows that for the complete-term tree the wide-move bound fails on a simple reader, so the bound must come with a change of tree, and then the round bound must be re-proved for the changed tree. The light range is the current-term rule's up to the factor \(N^{5/2}\) in the bound on \(e\), width up to \(\log_2n-O(\log N)\) still. The heavy-term dichotomy's per-reader failure \(n^{c-2}\) (lemma) is what the wide-move bound must beat.

2. A shared wide cube defeats the complete-term tree

Lemma (long complete-term paths). Let \(p\) be a pattern of \(\ell-1\) literals, \(C(p)=\{z_0,z_1\}\), let \(B\) be a set of \(\lfloor(n-2N-2)/2\rfloor\) rows, the setting's bound, and let \(F_p\) be the pin-free reader with the \(|B|\) terms \([j\in p]\), \(j\in B\). For \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) with \(|C(p)\cap Q|=1\) and no row of \(B\) matched into \(C(p)\), the complete-term tree \(\mathcal T_c(F_p,\rho')\) has a path of length \(\min(|R'\cap B|,N-1)\), and the probability of that event together with \(|R'\cap B|\ge N/8\) is at least \(N/(4n)\) for \(N\ge8\) and \(n\ge8N\). Proof. Let \(C(p)\cap Q=\{x_0\}\). No term is satisfied by \(\rho'\): a matched row of \(B\) lies outside \(C(p)\), and its term is falsified. The current term at the root is the first term \([j\in p]\) with \(j\in R'\cap B\), pin-free and not falsified; it queries \(j\) over the unused holes. Follow the branch of an answer other than \(x_0\): it lies outside \(C(p)\), so the term is falsified, no other term changes status, \(x_0\) stays unused, and the next current term is the next residual row of \(B\). The branch continues while an unused hole other than \(x_0\) and an unqueried row of \(R'\cap B\) remain, so its length is \(\min(|R'\cap B|,N-1)\). For the probability: \(Q\) is a uniform flat of dimension \(\ell_2\), so \(\Pr[z_0\in Q]=N/n\) and, given \(z_0\in Q\), \(z_1=z_0+v\) lies in \(Q\) with probability \((N-1)/(n-1)\), the direction space being uniform; hence \(\Pr[|C(p)\cap Q|=1]=2(N/n)(1-(N-1)/(n-1))\ge3N/(2n)\) for \(n\ge4N\). Given that, the label of \(C(p)\) outside \(Q\) is occupied by a uniform non-residual row, outside \(B\) with probability at least \((n-|B|-N)/(n-N)\ge2/5\) for \(n\ge8N\), and \(|R'\cap B|\), hypergeometric with mean \((N+1)|B|/n\ge(N+1)/2-N(N+1)/n-1\ge N/8+2\) for \(N\ge8\) and \(n\ge8N\), is at least \(N/8\) with probability at least \(1/2\), its median lying within one of its mean, the three events being independent given \(Q\) up to the conditioning on the occupant, which only removes one row. So the probability is at least \(\tfrac32(N/n)\cdot\tfrac25\cdot\tfrac12\ge N/(4n)\). \(\square\)

The reader \(F_p\) has about \(n/2\) terms, size \(n^1\), and the failure \(N/(4n)\) is the dichotomy's per-reader failure \(n^{c-2}\) at \(c=1\) up to the factor \(N\); the per-reader target of the composition is \(n^{-c-1}=n^{-2}\). The tree, not the reader, is at fault: for every \(\rho'\) with \(|C(p)\cap Q|\le1\) a tree of height at most one exists, the hole query at \(x_0\) when \(C(p)\cap Q=\{x_0\}\), whose answer, a row of \(R'\) or the empty branch, satisfies the term of that row if it lies in \(B\) and otherwise falsifies every term of a residual row modulo the axioms, exactly as a round's hole query does for a pin whose hole is used or emptied; when \(C(p)\cap Q=\varnothing\) every term of a residual row vanishes and the root is a 0-leaf. Two further readers locate the other failures of the complete-term tree on wide rows. (a) With distinct patterns \(p_j\) of \(\ell-1\) literals on the rows \(j\in B\), the tree queries every residual row of \(B\) whether or not its cube meets \(Q\), so its height is at least \(|R'\cap B|-|\{j\in R'\cap B: C(p_j)\cap Q\ne\varnothing\}|\), about \(N/2\), for almost every \(\rho'\); skipping the terms with a residual row whose cube misses \(Q\) (the sub-reader \(F_{Q,R'}\), which vanishes term by term modulo the axioms) removes these queries, and is necessary. (b) The pinned reader \([i\to x]\wedge[j\in p]\), \(j\in B\), one pin and one shared pattern, has, after the round at an alive pin, the path of the lemma with probability about \(N^3/n^3\); with \(n^{c-1}\) such pins, size \(n^c\), the failure is about \(N^3n^{c-4}\), above \(n^{-c-1}\) from \(c=3/2\) on. So a wide row must be resolved by a hole query at the holes of its cube when several residual rows share the cube, and by a pigeon query when one row carries several cubes (the reader with the \(n\) terms \([j=z]\), \(z\) a label, on one row \(j\) is resolved by one pigeon query and by \(N\) hole queries), which is the smaller-side rule of the recorded hole-query trees for unary terms (theorem).

3. What remains

The named obligation for wide tail rows is a wide-round bound on a tree that treats a wide row as a generalized pin: at the current term, for an uncovered wide row \(j\) with pattern \(p\), let \(H\) be the unused, not emptied holes of \(Q\) in \(C(p)\); if \(H=\varnothing\) the term counts as falsified (it vanishes modulo the axioms, as a term whose pin's hole is used or emptied); otherwise a wide round queries \(H\) by hole queries, or \(j\) by a pigeon query, by a fixed smaller-side rule, and the term is resolved. A wide round costs the count \(N\) or \((N+2)^{|H|}\) with no family gain, as a round does, and \(|H|\le|C(p)\cap Q|\), which is at most one for almost every flat when \(p\) has more than \(\log_2n-\log_2N\) literals. Theorem G above then applies with wide rounds in place of wide moves once every path has fewer than \(\nu_1\) of them except with probability \(p_W\), and the recorded round bounds must be re-proved for the changed tree, since the wide rounds assign rows and resolve holes that the recorded proofs' alive-pair counts do not see; the natural route is to add the pairs \((j,x)\), \(x\in C(p_j)\cap Q\), to the pinned pairs of the union-lemma counts, at a mass of at most \(n2^{-w'}\) per wide row of \(w'\) literals. Lemma B and Lemma C need no change for wide rounds: a hole query's answer is a row of \(R'\) or the empty branch, recorded in \(\delta\) as in a round. The dichotomy's per-reader failure \(n^{c-2}\) remains the bound to beat, and the reader \(F_p\) shows the complete-term tree does not beat it.

4. Checks

The checker (check_pair_space_encoding.py) gained --wide-w W: tail rows with more than \(W\) literals are moved without a code label, their kind recorded in \(\beta\). Batch 8 (runs, README, provenance): seven batch-5 configurations with every move unplaced (--wide-w 0), four two-literal configurations with one-literal rows placed and two-literal rows unplaced (--wide-w 1), and three two-role configurations with every move unplaced, all under the current-term rule with slot revelation: every rich pair decodes, 0 failures in 14 runs; with every move unplaced no pair fails richness, as the theorem says. The tree heights of Section 2 were computed exhaustively by wide_rows_tree_check.py over every \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) for every flat of \(\mathbb F_2^3\) of dimension one and two, for the three readers of Section 2 with \(A=\{0,1,2\}\) and \(B=\{3,\dots,8\}\), with and without the static skip; three deviations from Section 2: \(B\) has six of the nine rows rather than the setting's bound, the reader with distinct cubes has only the four two-literal cubes of \(\mathbb F_2^3\) for its six rows, so two pairs of rows share a cube, and the split by whether the flat meets the cube refers to the shared cube \(\{0,4\}\) for all three readers, which for that reader is the cube of its first row. On the four-hole flats (\(N=4\), \(N+1=5\) residual rows, 33264 restrictions whose flat meets the cube \(\{0,4\}\) of the pattern), the shared-pattern reader has a path of length at least \(3\) in \(48.3\) percent of them and a satisfied term at the root in \(48.5\) percent, so almost every restriction without a satisfied term has the lemma's long path, and the static skip changes nothing there (identical counts), while on the flats missing the cube it reduces the height from \(|R'\cap B|\) to \(0\); the reader with distinct cubes has a path of length at least \(3\) in \(39.7\) percent of the restrictions whose flat misses the shared cube, reduced to \(2.4\) percent by the skip; the one-pin reader keeps its long paths under the skip when the cube meets the flat (\(24.2\) percent with length at least \(3\)) and loses them otherwise (maximum height \(2\), the round). On the two-hole flats the same pattern holds with the lemma's length \(\min(|R'\cap B|,N-1)=1\) plus the forced last answer. The exact counts are in the results directory.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the current-term rule's Lemmas B and R, Theorem G and corollary; the compact composition's setting and Lemma C with its family ratio; Lemma A0; the complete-term rule; the random-flat family's definition and flat probabilities; the hole-query nodes; the dichotomy's restoration lemma; the unary theorem's statement. Recorded obstructions checked: the code obstruction (the light range is respected; wide rows are not placed), the window structure (hole queries necessary, now per reader at size \(n\)), the composition gap (unchanged for light rows), the pigeon-only refutation (the shared-cube lemma is its per-reader analogue for one wide pattern). Checks run: batch 8 of the exhaustive checker with unplaced and mixed moves, and the exhaustive tree-height census of Section 4. The standing reviewer, given the draft and the anchors, confirmed Lemmas B and C, the conditional Theorem G with its arithmetic, the obstruction lemma with its constants, the height-one tree, that \(F_p\) lies outside every recorded switching result, and the finite-check numbers, and reported six findings, all applied: the lemma's reader had more light rows than the setting allows (now \(\lfloor(n-2N-2)/2\rfloor\), with \(n\ge8N\)); \(N\ge16\) was unused; the scope misdescribed which round bounds allow wide tails; Lemma C's per-round factors needed the recorded geometric sum; the finite check's three deviations from Section 2 were to be stated; the hypergeometric median needed its half-sentence. The equality \(\nu_0=\nu_1\) is notational.

Assessment. The named obligation, the window's wide tail rows per reader, is now split: the composition half is done conditionally (Theorem G with a wide-move bound), and the tree half is identified precisely, with an obstruction showing the complete-term tree cannot supply the bound and a finite check confirming the obstruction; the wide-round bound on the generalized-pin tree, with the recorded round bounds re-proved for it, is the remaining obligation.

Process assessment. Testing the planned mechanism on the simplest readers before writing again paid for itself: the plan to place wide rows at their answer holes died in a five-line count (the flat is recoverable), and the shared-cube reader was found by asking what the static skip cannot fix rather than by running the tool, which then confirmed it exhaustively in minutes; the cycle's cost was the search for a positive result before accepting that the tree, not the encoding, is the obstacle, and the record now states that with a lemma instead of a hunch. No framework change.
