2026-09-18: The wide-round tree: a static vertex cover bounds the wide queries, the wide matching number is small by degrees and rank, and readers whose rows split into light and wide switch below size \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\)

Working proof: composition on the wide-round tree, unconditional for readers with split rows of size below \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\). Spin cycle. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question. The named obligation was a wide-round bound on a tree that treats a wide row as a generalized pin (remaining), with the recorded round bounds re-proved for that tree. The proposed rule, a per-node smaller-side choice between hole queries and a pigeon query, was replaced before drafting: an adaptive choice can be driven to many queries by one hole (adaptive-rule counterexample), while a choice fixed at the root gives a deterministic bound. The wide-round tree \(\mathcal T_w\) computes at the root a canonical minimum vertex cover of the wide graph, the bipartite graph of residual wide rows and the holes of their cubes inside the flat, and resolves a wide row of the cover by a pigeon query and every other wide row by hole queries at its cube's holes; the wide queries of a path then number at most the cover's size, which is the wide matching number by König's theorem (Section 2), and that matching number is bounded by a degree split and the rank lemma exactly as the rounds of the multi-row theorem (Section 3). The round bounds whose proofs use of the tree only Lemma 1 of the complete-term rule transfer to \(\mathcal T_w\) (Section 4), the composition goes through with the current-term rule and wide queries paid in \(\delta\) alone (Section 5), and two corollaries follow: pin-free readers with split rows switch at every size in their range, and role-separated readers with split rows switch at size below \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\), where the light and wide ranges overlap (Section 6). The stopping point was these results with their gate; the transfer of the remaining round bounds and the sizes from \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\) on are named in Section 7.

1. The wide-round tree

Setting. A reader \(F\) as in Section 1 of the compact composition, role-separated with \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\) and pin-free terms allowed, or a two-role reader as in its two-role form, sparsely pinned on its light rows and with \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\), with one change: the tail rows split, \(B=B_{\rm l}\sqcup B_{\rm w}\), a partition fixed by the reader. A light row \(j\in B_{\rm l}\) carries, in every term, a pattern of at most \(w\) literals (the recorded \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\) is implied by the light range of Theorem W); a wide row \(j\in B_{\rm w}\) carries patterns of any width up to \(\ell\). A pair \((T,j)\) of a term and a wide row of its tail, with pattern \(p_{T,j}\), is a wide incidence. The tree lives on the residual instance of \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\), pigeons \(R'\) and holes \(Q\), all \(N\) holes unused at the root.

The wide graph. For \(\rho'\) let \(G=G(F,\rho')\) be the bipartite graph with the residual wide rows \(R'\cap B_{\rm w}\) on one side and the holes of \(Q\) on the other, and an edge \((j,x)\) whenever \(x\in C(p_{T,j})\) for some term \(T\) on \(j\), whatever the status of \(T\). It depends on \(Q\) and \(R'\cap B_{\rm w}\) only. Let \(C=C_{\rm rows}\sqcup C_{\rm holes}\) be its canonical minimum vertex cover: among the vertex covers of least size one with the fewest rows, and among those the lexicographically first; the tie-breaks only make the choice determinate for the decoder, and any fixed rule would do. By König's theorem \(|C|=\tau(G)=\nu(G)\), the matching number of \(G\).

Rule. A hole of \(Q\) is resolved on a path once it is used by a row assigned on the path or emptied by a hole query. The statuses of the terms at a node are those of the complete-term tree with one more way of counting as falsified: a term with an uncovered tail row \(j\in B_{\rm w}\) of pattern \(p\) none of whose holes in \(C(p)\cap Q\) is unresolved counts as falsified. The current term is chosen by the matched-first preference among the terms neither falsified nor counting as falsified; a 1-leaf is a node where some term is satisfied by \(\rho'\cup\pi\), and a node without a current term is a 0-leaf. At the current term, if its pin is alive, the round of the complete-term rule comes first; then its uncovered tail rows are handled in the term's order. A light row is queried as a pigeon over the unused holes of \(Q\), a light move as before. A wide row \(j\in C_{\rm rows}\) is queried as a pigeon over the unused holes of \(Q\), a wide pigeon query. A wide row \(j\notin C_{\rm rows}\) with pattern \(p\) is sought by hole queries at the unresolved holes of \(C(p)\cap Q\) in increasing order, each with branches over the unassigned rows of \(R'\) and the empty branch as in a round, until an answer is \(j\) or no unresolved hole of \(C(p)\cap Q\) remains, in which case \(j\) stays uncovered. Wide pigeon queries and these hole queries are the wide queries. So every tail row of the current term is assigned at its node or left uncovered with all of its cube's holes in \(Q\) resolved, and after its node the term is satisfied, falsified, or counts as falsified, except at a cut. Any row of \(R'\) may be assigned by the answer of a hole query; \(\mathcal T_w\) differs from \(\mathcal T_c\) only at wide rows, and on a reader without wide rows the two trees coincide.

Lemma W0 (annihilation at a wide row). Let \(T\) be a term with a wide row \(j\in R'\) of pattern \(p\), and let a path leave \(j\) unassigned while every hole of \(C(p)\cap Q\) is resolved on it. Then the product of the image of \(T\) under \(\rho'\) and the path's leaf factor lies in the ideal of the residual axioms at degree two (row axioms, row and column exclusions, Boolean axioms), the ideal the switching lemmas' image step works modulo, which contains the ideal of the hole-query nodes lemma. Proof. The restriction confines the label of the residual row \(j\) to \(Q\), so the image of \([j\in p]\) equals, modulo the row axiom and the row exclusions of \(j\), \(\sum_{x\in C(p)\cap Q}X_{jx}\), the sum of the residual unary variables of \(j\) at the labels of its cube inside the flat, as the image of a pin \([i\to x]\) is \(X_{ix}\); it is a factor of the image of \(T\). Every hole of \(Q\) is unused at the root, so a used \(x\in C(p)\cap Q\) is used by a row \(j'\ne j\) of \(R'\) assigned on the path, the leaf factor contains \(X_{j'x}\), and \(X_{jx}X_{j'x}\) is a column exclusion; for \(x\) emptied at a node with matching \(\pi_0\) the leaf factor contains \(u_x(\pi_0)\), and \(j\) is uncovered by \(\pi_0\), so \(X_{jx}u_x(\pi_0)\) lies in the ideal by the hole-query nodes lemma. \(\square\)

If \(C(p)\cap Q=\varnothing\) the image of \(T\) is zero outright, so the terms with a residual wide row whose cube misses the flat vanish at the root: the static skip of the wide-rows entry is built in. Hence a 0-leaf of \(\mathcal T_w\) falsifies or annihilates every term, a 1-leaf contains a satisfied term, and its nodes are pigeon queries over unused holes and hole-query nodes of the recorded kind; the tree has the leaf properties the switching lemmas use, with leaf degrees at most the height, as recorded for the complete-term tree. The q-skip refutation does not apply: it broke the encoding because a moved row's code label, consistent with its pattern, revived a skipped term for the decoder, while here the skip tests only wide rows, which are never placed at code labels, so the decoder sees them exactly as reality does (Lemma W4).

2. Wide queries are bounded by the cover

Lemma W1. On every path of \(\mathcal T_w(F,\rho')\) the wide queries number at most \(|C|=\nu(G)\); a wide pigeon query has at most \(N\) answers and a hole query at most \(N+2\). Proof. A wide pigeon query is at a row of \(C_{\rm rows}\), which its answer assigns, so each row of \(C_{\rm rows}\) is queried at most once. A hole query is made for an uncovered wide row \(j\notin C_{\rm rows}\) of the current term, with pattern \(p\), at an unresolved hole \(x\in C(p)\cap Q\). An uncovered row is residual, so \((j,x)\) is an edge of \(G\); \(C\) covers it and \(j\notin C_{\rm rows}\), so \(x\in C_{\rm holes}\); the query resolves \(x\), so each hole of \(C_{\rm holes}\) is queried at most once. The answers are the unused holes of \(Q\), respectively the unassigned rows of \(R'\) and the empty branch. König's theorem gives \(|C|=\nu(G)\). \(\square\)

The bound is deterministic: on the pin-free reader \(F_p\) of the shared-cube lemma, \(G\) is the complete bipartite graph between \(R'\cap B\) and \(C(p)\cap Q\), the cover is \(C(p)\cap Q\) when \(|C(p)\cap Q|\le|R'\cap B|\), and the tree makes at most two hole queries where the complete-term tree made \(\min(|R'\cap B|,N-1)\) pigeon queries; on the single-row reader with the \(n\) terms \([j=z]\) the graph is a star at \(j\), the cover is \(\{j\}\), and the tree makes one pigeon query, the smaller-side rule of the hole-only sparse failure without a per-node decision.

3. The wide matching number

For a label \(x\) let the wide degree \(d_{\rm w}(x)\) be the number of wide incidences \((T,j)\) with \(x\in C(p_{T,j})\), and let \(m_{\rm w}=\sum_xd_{\rm w}(x)=\sum_{(T,j)}|C(p_{T,j})|\) be the wide mass; both are fixed by the reader. For \(D>0\) let \(\mathrm{Heavy}=\{x:\ d_{\rm w}(x)>D\}\), so that \(|\mathrm{Heavy}|\le m_{\rm w}/D\).

Lemma W2. For integers \(k\ge2\) and \(t\ge1\), with \(d=\lceil\log_2k\rceil\), \[\Pr_{\rho'\in\Phi_0}\bigl[\nu(G)\ge k+t-1\bigr]\le\Bigl(\frac{|\mathrm{Heavy}|N}{n}\Bigr)^{d+1}+\Bigl(\frac{eDN(N+1)}{t(n+1)}\Bigr)^{t}.\] Proof. A matching of \(G\) uses distinct holes, so at most \(|\mathrm{Heavy}\cap Q|\) of its edges have a heavy hole and the others form a matching of the subgraph \(G_{\rm light}\) of the edges at holes outside \(\mathrm{Heavy}\); so \(\nu(G)\le|\mathrm{Heavy}\cap Q|+\nu(G_{\rm light})\), and \(\nu(G)\ge k+t-1\) forces \(|\mathrm{Heavy}\cap Q|\ge k\) or \(\nu(G_{\rm light})\ge t\). By the rank lemma in its independent-points form, \(\Pr[|\mathrm{Heavy}\cap Q|\ge k]\le(|\mathrm{Heavy}|N/n)^{d+1}\). For the second event condition on \(Q\). A matching of size \(t\) in \(G_{\rm light}\) consists of \(t\) holes \(x_1<\dots<x_t\) of \(Q\) outside \(\mathrm{Heavy}\), at most \(\binom Nt\le(eN/t)^t\) choices, and distinct rows \(j_1,\dots,j_t\in R'\cap B_{\rm w}\) with \((j_i,x_i)\) an edge; the rows adjacent to \(x_i\) number at most \(d_{\rm w}(x_i)\le D\), at most \(D^t\) choices, and a fixed set of \(t\) rows is residual with probability \(\prod_{i<t}(N+1-i)/(n+1-i)\le((N+1)/(n+1))^t\), since \(R'\) is a uniform \((N+1)\)-subset of the \(n+1\) rows independent of \(Q\). The union bound gives \(\Pr[\nu(G_{\rm light})\ge t]\le(eDN(N+1)/(t(n+1)))^t\). \(\square\)

Polynomial form. Fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) and \(c'>0\); put \(d=\lceil c'/\varepsilon\rceil+2\), \(t=\lceil c'/\varepsilon\rceil+1\), \(D=n^{1-\varepsilon}/(N+1)\). If \(m_{\rm w}\le n^{2-2\varepsilon}/(N+1)\), then \(|\mathrm{Heavy}|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\), the first term is at most \((Nn^{-\varepsilon})^{d+1}\le N^{d+1}n^{-c'-3\varepsilon}\) and the second at most \((eNn^{-\varepsilon}/t)^t\le(eN)^tn^{-c'-\varepsilon}\); so for \(n\) large enough that \(N^{d+1}\le n^{3\varepsilon}/2\) and \((eN)^t\le n^{\varepsilon}/2\), which polylogarithmic \(N\) gives, \(\Pr[\nu(G)\ge2^d+t-1]\le n^{-c'}\). A reader with at most \(n^c\) terms, at most \(r\) wide rows per term and every wide pattern of at least \(w_1\) literals has \(m_{\rm w}\le rn^{c+1}2^{-w_1}\), so the mass condition holds when \(2^{w_1}\ge r(N+1)n^{c-1+2\varepsilon}\): the wide range begins at \((c-1+2\varepsilon)\log_2n+\log_2(r(N+1))\) literals. A pattern of fewer than \(w_1\) literals on a wide row adds at most \(n\) to \(m_{\rm w}\), so with \(2^{w_1}\ge2r(N+1)n^{c-1+2\varepsilon}\) up to \(n^{1-2\varepsilon}/(2(N+1))\) such incidences are absorbed by the same condition.

4. Rounds on the wide-round tree

Lemma W3. Lemma 1 of the complete-term rule holds on \(\mathcal T_w\): on every path the trigger pairs of the rounds are pairwise disjoint pairs \((i,x)\) with \(i\in R'\), \(x\in Q\), whose host is not falsified by \(\rho'\) and has no matched pair. Proof. As recorded, with the new way of counting as falsified added. After a round \(i\) is assigned and \(x\) is used or emptied, and wide queries only assign further rows and resolve further holes, so the pairs are disjoint. At the node the current term neither is falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi\) nor counts as falsified, so its host \(h\) is not falsified by \(\rho'\). If \(h\) had a matched pair \((i',x')\), the term \(T'=[i'\to x']\wedge h\) would be pin-matched; were it neither falsified nor counting as falsified at the node, the preference would choose a pin-matched term, whose pinned row is matched and not residual, and no round would follow; so \(T'\) is falsified or counts as falsified there, its pinned part holds under \(\rho'\), and so its tail \(h\) is falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi\) or has an uncovered wide row with every hole of its cube in \(Q\) resolved, which makes the current term, with the same tail, falsified or counting as falsified, a contradiction. \(\square\)

By Lemma 2 of the complete-term rule the round bounds of the multi-row theorem and its predecessors use of the tree only Lemma 1, so they hold on \(\mathcal T_w\) with their probabilities. The re-reading of the multi-row theorem's proof for this entry confirms it: its facts (a) and (b) are Lemma 1; steps (H1) to (H3) count the trigger pairs of rounds through them and the activated union lemma and the rank lemma, which concern \(\rho'\) alone; and (H4) exhibits a term satisfied by \(\rho'\), which makes the root a 1-leaf of \(\mathcal T_w\) as of every tree with the 1-leaf rule. So the multi-row size corollary holds on \(\mathcal T_w\): a role-separated reader with at most \(n^c\) terms, \(1\le c<2-\varepsilon\), \(800\,\mathrm e\,(N+1)\le n^{2-\varepsilon-c}\), under that theorem's conditions on \(N\), has fewer than \(N/48\) rounds on every path of \(\mathcal T_w\) before a 1-leaf except with probability \(3n^{-c-1}\), whatever its tails. The recorded multi-row setting pins every term, while Section 1 allows pin-free terms: a pin-free term triggers no round and contributes no pair to any host, mass or union, and when satisfied it only makes a 1-leaf, so the bound holds with them, the extension that clause (a) of the current-term corollary already makes. The few-light-rows theorem, the combined theorem and the two-role bounds are not transferred here: Lemma 2 charges a round whose host is falsified at its own node to the residual light row assigned there, and on \(\mathcal T_w\) a host can also leave the family consistent with the exposed rows' labels when a wide row of the current term is left uncovered with its holes exhausted and later assigned elsewhere by a hole query; that accounting is left to the next cycle (Section 7).

5. Composition on the wide-round tree

Code. For a pair \((\rho,\rho'')\) of \(\Phi_e(S)\) whose tree \(\mathcal T_w(F,\rho')\) has a path with at least \(s\) light moves, fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds and at most \(\nu_1\) wide queries before its \(s\)-th light move, take the lexicographically first such path, cut after its \(s\)-th light move, and let \(m_k\) be the node of its \(k\)-th light move. The code is \((\rho^\ast,\sigma,\beta,\delta)\) of the current-term rule: \(\rho^\ast\in\Phi_{e-s}(S)\) places the \(s\) moved light rows at code labels chosen by that rule, the \(k\)-th in \(E(\rho)\cap C(p_k)\), unpicked, outside \(X_{\le k}\), the pin labels of the current terms of the nodes up to and including \(m_k\), and for a two-role reader outside \(X_{j_k}\); now \(|X_{\le k}|\le k+(\nu_0-1)+\nu_1\le s+\nu_0+\nu_1-1\), every node having a light move, a round or a wide query. Wide rows are never placed. \(\sigma\) is as before; \(\beta\) lists, in path order, one bit per node, whether the node has a light move, and per light move its position among the term's tail rows and a last-of-node bit; \(\delta\) lists, in path order, the rounds' answers, the light moves' holes and the wide queries' answers, a hole of \(Q\) for a wide pigeon query and a row of \(R'\) or the empty branch for a hole query. Richness is that of the current-term rule for the light patterns: \(|E(\rho)\cap C(p)|\ge3s\) for every pattern \(p\) on a light row, and for a two-role reader \(|E(\rho)\cap C(p)\setminus X_j|\ge3s\) for every pair \((j,p)\) of a light row and a pattern of a term on \(j\); with \(s\ge\nu_0+\nu_1\) the encoder always has a label, since at the \(k\)-th move at most \(k-1\le s-1\) labels are picked and at most \(s+\nu_0+\nu_1-1\) excluded, and \(3s-(s-1)-(s+\nu_0+\nu_1-1)=s-\nu_0-\nu_1+2\ge2\). Lemma R of the current-term rule, a statement about \(E(\rho)\) alone, bounds the failure of richness by \(Mr\,e^{-s}\) under \(2^{w+4}s\le e\le n/(16rN^{3/2}(N+1))\) and, two-role, sparse pinning.

Lemma W4 (decoder). The code determines the pair. Proof. The decoder first recovers \(G\) and \(C\): \(Q\) is the flat of \(\rho^\ast\), and \(R'\cap B_{\rm w}\) is the set of residual wide rows of \(\rho^\ast\), because \(S\subseteq A\) is disjoint from \(B\) and only light rows are placed. It then simulates \(\mathcal T_w(F,\rho')\) node by node from \(\alpha\) as in Lemma B of the current-term rule, whose claims (i) to (iii) hold verbatim: they concern the pins and the statuses of terms, and use of the tree only that every uncovered light row of the current term is moved at its node, which \(\mathcal T_w\) keeps. Three additions. The rows assigned in reality on which \(\alpha\) agrees now include the rows assigned by wide queries, read from \(\delta\). The unresolved holes agree in \(\alpha\) and in reality: \(\alpha\) uses no hole of \(Q\) beyond those the path uses, the code labels and the values of \(\sigma\) lying outside \(Q\), and the emptied holes are read from \(\delta\); with the wide rows unplaced, a term counting as falsified through a wide row does so in \(\alpha\) exactly when it does in reality, so claim (ii) extends to this way of being falsified and the current term's uncovered wide rows are unassigned in both. At the current term the decoder reads the round from \(\delta\) if the pin is alive in \(\alpha\), then handles the tail rows in the term's order: a light row is moved at this node exactly when \(\beta\) lists its position, its hole coming from \(\delta\), and otherwise it is assigned in reality as in \(\alpha\); an unassigned wide row of \(C_{\rm rows}\) takes its hole from \(\delta\); for an unassigned wide row outside \(C_{\rm rows}\) it reads from \(\delta\) one answer per unresolved hole of the row's cube, in increasing order, updating \(\alpha\) with each, until the answer is the row or the holes are exhausted, as the tree does. After the \(s\)-th light move it returns the moved rows to the residual set, which gives \(\rho\), and reads \(\rho''\) off \(\sigma\). For a two-role reader a wide row may carry pins; unplaced, and assigned only through \(\delta\), its pins have the same status in \(\alpha\) and in reality. \(\square\)

Lemma W5 (count). Let \(\theta_A=(N+1)e/(n-N-e+1)\) and \(A_{\rm w}=4rN\theta_A\). Among the \(s\)-rich pairs of \(\Phi_e(S)\), the fraction whose tree has a path with at least \(s\) light moves, fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds and at most \(\nu_1\) wide queries before its \(s\)-th light move is at most \(2A_{\rm w}^{\,s}(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}(2(N+2))^{\nu_1}\). Proof. As in Lemma C of the compact composition with the code above. \(\rho^\ast\) ranges over \(\Phi_{e-s}(S)\), of size at most \(\theta_A^{\,s}|\Phi_e(S)|\) by the recorded ratio, and \(\sigma\) over \(e!\) values. A path with \(\nu<\nu_0\) rounds and \(m_{\rm w}\le\nu_1\) wide queries has at most \(s+\nu+m_{\rm w}\) nodes, so \(\beta\) takes at most \(2^{s+\nu+m_{\rm w}}(2r)^s\) values, and \(\delta\) at most \(N^s(N(N+2))^{\nu}(N+2)^{m_{\rm w}}\) by Lemma W1 and the recorded round costs. Lemma W4 makes the code injective, so the fraction is at most \(\sum_{\nu<\nu_0}\sum_{m_{\rm w}\le\nu_1}A_{\rm w}^{\,s}(2N(N+2))^{\nu}(2(N+2))^{m_{\rm w}}\le A_{\rm w}^{\,s}(2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\cdot2(2(N+2))^{\nu_1}\), since \(\sum_{\nu<\nu_0}x^{\nu}\le x^{\nu_0}\) and \(\sum_{m\le\nu_1}y^m\le2y^{\nu_1}\) for \(x,y\ge2\). \(\square\)

Theorem W (composition on the wide-round tree). Let \(F\) be a reader of Section 1, \(\nu_0=\nu_1=\lfloor N/48\rfloor\), \(s=\lfloor N/12\rfloor-2r-\nu_1\), \(N\ge48(2r+1)\), and let the light patterns satisfy \(2^{w+4}s\le e\le n/(32rN^4(N+1))\). Suppose that, over \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\), every path of \(\mathcal T_w(F,\rho')\) before a 1-leaf has at most \(\nu_0-1\) rounds except with probability \(p_R\), and \(\nu(G(F,\rho'))\le\nu_1\) except with probability \(p_W\). Then \(\mathcal T_w(F,\rho')\) has height below \(N/8-2r\), and \(F\) switches within the height budget, except with probability at most \[p_R+p_W+\tfrac75\Bigl(Mr\,e^{-s}+2^{-N/8+(2r+2)(2+3\log_2N)}\Bigr).\] Proof. The height of a path is its light moves plus at most two per round plus its wide queries. A path of height at least \(s+2\nu_0+\nu_1\) has at least \(\nu_0\) rounds, or more than \(\nu_1\) wide queries, or at least \(s\) light moves with fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds and at most \(\nu_1\) wide queries before its \(s\)-th light move. The first is the round bound's event; the second is contained in \(\nu(G)>\nu_1\) by Lemma W1; the third is an event on \(\Phi_0\), and by Lemma A0, applicable as \(e(N+1)\le n/8\) and \(b=|A|\ge n/2+N+2\), or \(b=|A_0|\) in the two-role form, its probability is at most \(\tfrac75\) times its average over \(S\) of its probability on \(\Phi_0^S\), at most the richness failure \(Mr\,e^{-s}\), Lemma R's range holding, plus the count of Lemma W5. The bound on \(e\) gives \(\theta_A\le2(N+1)e/n\), as \(N+e-1\le n/2\), hence \(A_{\rm w}\le8rN(N+1)e/n\le1/(4N^3)\); and \(N\ge48(2r+1)\) gives \(s\ge N/16-2r-1\ge\nu_0+\nu_1\), since \(\nu_0+\nu_1\le N/24\). With \(N+2\le2N\) the count is at most \(2^{1-(N/16-2r-1)(2+3\log_2N)+(N/48)(2+2\log_2N)+(N/48)(2+\log_2N)}\), whose exponent is \(-N/24-(N/8)\log_2N+(2r+1)(2+3\log_2N)+1\le-N/8+(2r+2)(2+3\log_2N)\), because \((N/8)\log_2N\ge N/12\) for \(N\ge2\). Outside the three events every path has height below \(s+2\nu_0+\nu_1=\lfloor N/12\rfloor+2\nu_0-2r\le N/8-2r\); the tree is a matching decision tree for \(\rho'\) with pigeon queries over unused holes and hole-query nodes, with the leaf properties of Section 1, so the conclusion is the composition recorded in the height budget. \(\square\)

Scope. The theorem replaces the wide-move composition: no wide-move bound, no factor \((4rN)^{\nu_1}\), no hypothesis \(r\le N^6/16\); the wide queries cost \((2(N+2))^{\nu_1}\) in \(\delta\) and the node bits alone, and the range \(e\le n/(32rN^4(N+1))\) is kept as recorded, although \(N^3\) in place of \(N^4\) would do at the cost of the constant in the exponent. The light range is the current-term rule's up to the factor \(N^{5/2}\), width up to \(\log_2n-\log_2(2^9rsN^4(N+1))\). A reader without light rows needs neither the pair space nor the bound on \(|B|\): outside the two bounds' events its tree has height at most \(2(\nu_0-1)+\nu_1<N/8-2r\).

6. Two corollaries

Corollary 1 (pin-free readers with split rows). Let \(F\) be a pin-free reader with at most \(M\le n^c\) terms \(\bigwedge_{j\in J}[j\in p_j]\), at most \(r\) rows per term, on rows \(B=B_{\rm l}\sqcup B_{\rm w}\) with \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\) when \(B_{\rm l}\ne\varnothing\) (the Scope note), light patterns of at most \(w\) literals with \(2^{w+4}s\le e\le n/(32rN^4(N+1))\), and wide mass \(m_{\rm w}\le n^{2-2\varepsilon}/(N+1)\), which holds when every wide pattern has at least \(w_1\) literals with \(2^{w_1}\ge r(N+1)n^{c-1+2\varepsilon}\). Let \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), \(d=\lceil(c+1)/\varepsilon\rceil+2\), \(t=\lceil(c+1)/\varepsilon\rceil+1\), \(N\ge\max\bigl(48(2r+1),\ 48(2^d+t),\ 8(c+1)\log_2n+(2r+2)(16+24\log_2N)\bigr)\), \(s\ge(2c+1)\ln n+\ln r\), and \(n\) large enough that \(N^{d+1}\le n^{3\varepsilon}/2\) and \((eN)^t\le n^{\varepsilon}/2\). Then a uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) switches \(F\) within the height budget except with probability at most \(4n^{-c-1}\). Proof. \(F\) has no pins, so no rounds: \(p_R=0\). The polynomial form of Lemma W2 with \(c'=c+1\) gives \(\Pr[\nu(G)\ge2^d+t-1]\le n^{-c-1}\), and \(\nu_1+1=\lfloor N/48\rfloor+1\ge2^d+t-1\) by \(N\ge48(2^d+t)\), so \(p_W\le n^{-c-1}\). In Theorem W, \(Mr\,e^{-s}\le n^{-c-1}\) for \(s\ge(2c+1)\ln n+\ln r\), and \(2^{-N/8+(2r+2)(2+3\log_2N)}\le n^{-c-1}\) for \(N\ge8(c+1)\log_2n+(2r+2)(16+24\log_2N)\); the total is \(n^{-c-1}+\tfrac75\cdot2n^{-c-1}\le4n^{-c-1}\). \(\square\)

Widths. The light range ends at \(\log_2n-\log_2(2^9rsN^4(N+1))\) literals and the wide range begins at \((c-1+2\varepsilon)\log_2n+\log_2(r(N+1))\); they overlap when \(n^{2-2\varepsilon-c}\ge2^9r^2sN^4(N+1)^2\), which holds for \(c<2-2\varepsilon\) and \(n\) large. Then every row whose patterns all have at most \(w\) literals, or all have at least \(w_1\) literals, is covered, with \(w_1\le w\), so every width is covered per row; a row carrying both a pattern of fewer than \(w_1\) literals and one of more than \(w\) literals goes to \(B_{\rm w}\) and is covered as long as such incidences number at most \(n^{1-2\varepsilon}/(2(N+1))\), by the absorption remark of Section 3 with \(2^{w_1}\ge2r(N+1)n^{c-1+2\varepsilon}\). From \(c=2-2\varepsilon\) on, the widths between the two ranges are open per reader.

Corollary 2 (role-separated readers below size \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\)). Let \(F\) be a role-separated reader of Section 1 with at most \(n^c\) terms, \(1\le c<2-\varepsilon\) as the multi-row corollary states (a reader with fewer terms has at most \(n\) terms), whose rows split with the light range and the wide mass condition of Corollary 1 with the same \(\varepsilon\), under Corollary 1's conditions on \(N\), \(s\) and \(n\), the multi-row theorem's conditions on \(N\), and \(800\,\mathrm e\,(N+1)\le n^{2-\varepsilon-c}\). Then a uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) switches \(F\) within the height budget except with probability at most \(7n^{-c-1}\). In particular, for \(c<2-2\varepsilon\) and \(n\) large, every role-separated reader of size \(n^c\) whose tail rows split into rows of patterns of at most \(w\) literals and rows of patterns of at least \(w_1\) literals switches, whatever the widths. Proof. The multi-row size corollary on \(\mathcal T_w\) (Section 4) gives fewer than \(N/48\) rounds on every path before a 1-leaf except with probability \(3n^{-c-1}\), and below \(\nu_0\) with the slack recorded in the current-term corollary, since its count \(N/192+2^{d_\varepsilon}\le5N/384\) is at most \(\lfloor N/48\rfloor-1\) for \(N\ge256\); so \(p_R=3n^{-c-1}\), \(p_W\le n^{-c-1}\) as in Corollary 1, and Theorem W gives \(3n^{-c-1}+n^{-c-1}+\tfrac{14}5n^{-c-1}\le7n^{-c-1}\). The width clause is the overlap of the two ranges for \(c<2-2\varepsilon\). \(\square\)

Corollary 2 closes, for role-separated readers with split rows, the window case of the current-term rule at sizes below \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\): the per-reader failure \(7n^{-c-1}\) is the convention of the round bounds, a union over the \(n^c\) readers of a source costing \(n^c\) times that, against the dichotomy's per-reader failure \(n^{c-2}\) (lemma), which the complete-term tree could not beat on \(F_p\).

7. What remains

(1) The round bounds of the few-light-rows theorem, the combined theorem and the two-role theorems on \(\mathcal T_w\): a round whose host leaves the consistent family through a wide row of the current term left uncovered with its holes exhausted must be charged; the natural charge is to the resolution of the last hole of that row's cube, one per (row, pattern), and the union over the exposed rows' labels must then include the wide rows assigned by hole queries. With them, clauses (b), (c), (e), (f) and (g) of the current-term corollary would transfer, and sizes up to \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\) would follow for readers whose light and wide ranges overlap; from \(c=2-2\varepsilon\) on they do not, and the widths between \(\log_2n-O(\log N)\) and \((c-1+2\varepsilon)\log_2n+O(\log N)\) are open per reader. (2) Two-role readers: Theorem W is conditional on a round bound for \(\mathcal T_w\); Corollary 2 is role-separated. (3) Rows carrying many patterns on both sides of the split beyond the absorbed number. (4) Terms containing parities, the open core.

8. Checks

The checker (check_pair_space_encoding.py) gained the wide-round tree: --tree wide builds the wide graph and its canonical minimum vertex cover at the root, queries wide rows as Section 1 does, encodes with the current-term rule for light moves, one bit per node and the wide answers in \(\delta\), and the decoder recomputes the cover from \(\rho^\ast\); --wide-rows K makes the last \(K\) rows of \(B\) wide, --wide-example builds the three readers of the wide-rows entry. Batch 9 (runs, README, provenance): the three readers of the wide-rows entry on two-hole and four-hole flats, 120960 and 1512 pairs each, and eight random mixed readers with one to three wide rows of two-literal patterns among light rows and pins, 3024 to 7560 pairs each, all with the current-term rule and slot revelation: every rich pair decodes, 0 failures in 14 runs, and on every pair the wide queries of the encoded path are at most the cover's size (wide_gt_cover 0). Two controls with --code-rule any, code labels allowed inside the excluded pin labels, fail on 106 and 20 pairs, all through such labels (xcur_fail), as the current-term rule predicts. The exhaustive census of the wide-rows entry was repeated with the wide tree (wide_rows_tree_check.py --tree wide) over every \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) for every flat of \(\mathbb F_2^3\) of dimension one and two, with the same three deviations from Section 2 of that entry: on the four-hole flats the shared-pattern reader, which had a path of length at least \(3\) in \(48.3\) percent of the restrictions whose flat meets the cube, now has maximum height \(2\), the two hole queries at the cube's labels, with a path of length \(2\) in \(27.3\) percent; the reader with distinct cubes keeps paths of length at least \(3\) in \(27.6\) percent, its cover having mean size \(1.27\) and size up to \(4\), as its six rows share only four cubes, and its height never exceeding the cover; the one-pin reader has maximum height \(4\), the round plus two hole queries; the flats missing the cube give height \(0\) for the shared-pattern reader and at most the round for the one-pin reader; and in every restriction the wide queries are at most the cover's size. The exact counts are in the results directory.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the wide-rows entry (setting, Lemmas B and C, Theorem G, the shared-cube lemma, Section 3); the current-term rule's code labels, Lemma B with its claims (i) to (iii), Lemma R, Theorem G and corollary; the complete-term rule with its Lemmas 1 and 2; the compact composition's setting, code, and Lemma B; the multi-row host setting, theorem (proof steps (H1) to (H4)) and size corollary; the rank lemma in its independent-points form and the dense-labels lemma; the hole-query nodes lemma; the few-light-rows theorem. Recorded obstructions checked: the q-skip refutation (the skip here tests only unplaced rows), the hole-only sparse failure and the adaptive-rule counterexample (the cover gives the smaller side statically), the pigeon-only refutation and the shared-cube lemma (resolved by the cover's holes), the code obstruction (wide rows are not placed; the light range is unchanged). Checks run: batch 9 of the exhaustive checker on the wide tree with two negative controls, and the tree-height census with the wide tree. The standing reviewer, continued from the previous cycles with the draft and the new anchors, re-read the multi-row theorem's proof independently and confirmed Lemmas W0 to W5, Theorem W with its arithmetic, both corollaries with their constants, the tool's implementation of the tree and decoder, and every quoted number; it reported six findings, none breaking a statement, all applied: the ideal of Lemma W0 is that of the residual axioms at degree two (the image identity holds modulo the row axiom); the transfer of Section 4 needed the one-line justification for pin-free terms; the census sentence on the distinct-cube reader overstated by one; \(w\le\ell-\ell_2-1\), the cover's tie-breaks, the bound on \(|B|\) for readers without light rows and \(c\ge1\) were unused or inherited and are now marked as such; one \(\varepsilon\) serves both corollaries; the status line had two clauses of scope.

Assessment. The named obligation, the wide-round bound with the recorded round bounds re-proved for the changed tree, is discharged for the multi-row round bound and open for the exposed-row bounds: with Lemmas W1 to W3 and Theorem W, every role-separated reader of size below \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\) whose rows split into light and wide switches under one restriction, whatever the widths, the first unconditional switching statement in the window for tail rows above the light range; sizes from \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\) on need the transfer of the exposed-row bounds and a treatment of the widths between the two ranges.

Process assessment. The static cover replaced the planned adaptive smaller-side rule before any code was written, by checking the plan against the recorded adaptive-rule counterexample, and the census then confirmed the deterministic bound in minutes; the cycle's waste was one decoder bug (light rows placed at code labels are invisible at nodes without moves), fixed by the per-node bit before drafting, and a second lost shell from a kill command naming the tool file, now a shell-hygiene rule in CLAUDE.md; the reviewer's findings were precision and wording only.

2026-09-18: The wide-round tree reordered: wide rows before the round, every recorded round bound transfers, and readers with few tail rows or few wide rows switch at every width

Working proof: every recorded round bound holds on the reordered wide-round tree, and readers with few tail rows switch at every size and width. Spin cycle. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question. The named obligation was the transfer of the exposed-row round bounds to the wide-round tree (remaining, item (1)): on that tree as defined, the round of a node precedes the node's wide queries, so a round's host can leave the family of hosts consistent with the exposed rows' final labels when a wide row of the current term is left uncovered with its holes exhausted and is later assigned elsewhere, and the charging of Lemma 2 of the complete-term rule, one charge per residual light row moved at the round's node, does not cover it. The plan was to charge such rounds to the exhaustion of a cube; the count of exhaustions on a path is not bounded by anything small, and the plan was dropped before drafting. Instead the node is reordered: the current term's wide rows are resolved first, the round is made only if the term is still alive, and the light rows are moved last. Then a round's host has every wide row assigned consistently at the round, the only inconsistency a round's node can produce is at a light row assigned after the round, by its move or by the round's own hole answer, which Lemma 2's charging covers, and one further convention on the labels of rows the path never assigns makes the second fact of the exposed-row proofs, that a consistent host with a matched pair forbids the round, robust against terms that count as falsified through an exhausted cube. Everything of the previous entry survives the reordering (Section 1); the two facts hold on the reordered tree for any exposed set (Section 2); the four exposed-row theorems and the two-role size corollary transfer (Section 3); and one observation, that the wide matching number is at most the number of residual wide rows, gives switching at every size and width for readers with few tail rows, and at every width below size \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\) for readers with few wide rows (Section 4). The stopping point was these results with their gate and the checker re-run on the reordered tree.

1. The reordered node

Definition. The wide-round tree \(\mathcal T_w(F,\rho')\) is that of the previous entry (the setting with split rows, the wide graph \(G\) and its canonical minimum vertex cover \(C\), the statuses, the preference, the leaves) with the order inside a node changed. At the current term \(T\), chosen at the start of the node: first its uncovered wide rows are handled in the term's order, a row of \(C_{\rm rows}\) by a wide pigeon query over the unused holes of \(Q\) and a row outside \(C_{\rm rows}\) by hole queries at the unresolved holes of its cube in \(Q\) in increasing order until found or exhausted; then, if \(T\) is still neither falsified nor counting as falsified and its pin is alive, the round of the complete-term rule; then its uncovered light rows are moved in the term's order, whatever the term's status. The order of the previous entry, the round first and the tail rows in the term's order, is called round-first below; from here on \(\mathcal T_w\) is the reordered tree. On a reader without wide rows the node has no wide phase and the round is made exactly when the pin is alive at the start, so \(\mathcal T_w\) coincides with the complete-term tree \(\mathcal T_c\).

Lemma R0 (the previous entry survives). Lemmas W0 to W5, Theorem W and Corollaries 1 and 2 of the previous entry hold for the reordered tree with the same proofs. Proof. Lemma W0 and Lemma W2 do not mention the order inside a node. Lemma W1 counts the wide queries of a path by the rows of \(C_{\rm rows}\) and the holes of \(C_{\rm holes}\) they consume, in any order. Lemma W3 argues at the start of the round's node, where the preference is applied, and uses only that assignments and resolutions are never undone; the trigger pair is alive at the round, as before. Lemma W4's decoder processes the node in the reordered order: after the wide phase, read from \(\delta\) as before, it makes the round exactly when \(T\) is alive with an alive pin in \(\alpha\), which agrees with reality, because the rows assigned by the wide phase and the resolved holes agree, the status of the pin agrees, its row lying in \(A\) for a role-separated reader and, for a two-role reader, being assigned by the round when alive and hence never a row moved later, the two-role form's point, and the light rows of \(T\) moved later are consistent in \(\alpha\) and unassigned in reality, so they falsify nothing in either; claims (i) to (iii) are unchanged. Lemma W5 counts nodes, moves, rounds and wide queries, not their order, and Theorem W and the corollaries use only these lemmas and the multi-row transfer. \(\square\)

2. The two facts of the exposed-row proofs on the reordered tree

Setting. A reader of the previous entry's setting, role-separated or two-role, with rows split into \(B_{\rm l}\) and \(B_{\rm w}\). Let \(B_{\rm e}\subseteq B\) be any set of exposed tail rows fixed by the reader and \(B_0=B\setminus B_{\rm e}\); the exposed-row theorems take \(B_{\rm e}=B\) (the few-light-rows and two-role few-rows theorems), the crowded rows (the combined theorem) or an exposed set containing them (the two-role exposed theorem). A host \(h\) is a tail, rows \(J_h\subseteq B\) with patterns \(p_{h,j}\); its reduced tail is its restriction to \(B_0\). Write \(\zeta=\mu'|_{B_{\rm e}}\) and \(R_{\rm e}=R'\cap B_{\rm e}\). For a path \(P\) of \(\mathcal T_w(F,\rho')\) with at least one round let \(x_{\rm last}\) be the trigger hole of its last round, unresolved at the start of that round's node, and define the labeling \(y_P\) of \(R_{\rm e}\): a row assigned on \(P\) gets its label; if \(P\) is cut inside its last node at or after that node's round, an unassigned tail row of that node's current term gets a label of the term's pattern on it, and such a row is light, the term's wide rows having been assigned before the round; every other unassigned row gets \(x_{\rm last}\). Call a host consistent (with \(\zeta_{y_P}=\zeta\cup y_P\)) if \(\zeta_{y_P}(j)\in C(p_{h,j})\) for every \(j\in J_h\cap B_{\rm e}\). Every label a path assigns is a hole of \(Q\), a pigeon query ranging over unused holes of \(Q\) and a hole query assigning its hole.

Lemma X (exposed-row facts). Let \(P\) be a path of \(\mathcal T_w(F,\rho')\) before any 1-leaf with at least one round. (a) The host of every round of \(P\) is consistent, except for rounds at whose node a light row of \(B_{\rm e}\) in the host is assigned, by its move or by the round's hole answer, to a label outside its pattern's cube; these rounds number at most \(|R_{\rm e}|\). (b) Let \(h_1\) be a consistent host with a matched pair \((i',x')\), so that \(T=[i'\to x']\wedge h_1\) is a term of the reader with \(\mu'(i')=x'\). Then no round of \(P\) has a host with the same reduced tail as \(h_1\); and if every row of \(h_1\) in \(B_0\) is matched by \(\rho'\) to a label of its pattern's cube, \(P\) has no round at all.

Proof. (a) Let the round be at node \(m\) with current term \(T''\) and host \(h\), and let \(j\in J_h\cap B_{\rm e}\). If \(j\) is matched by \(\rho'\), its label is consistent, since \(T''\) is not falsified by \(\rho'\cup\pi\). If \(j\) is residual and assigned before \(m\), or during the wide phase of \(m\) as the answer of a query, its label is consistent, since \(T''\) is neither falsified nor counting as falsified at the round, which comes after the wide phase; and this label is \(y_P(j)\). If \(j\) is wide and uncovered at the start of \(m\), the wide phase assigns it, at a hole of its cube when found by a hole query, or by a wide pigeon query or as a bystander with a label that is consistent because \(T''\) is alive at the round; so it falls under the previous case. If \(j\) is light and uncovered at the round, it is assigned at \(m\) by the round's hole query, whose answer ranges over the unassigned rows of \(R'\), or by its move after the round: to a consistent label, or to an inconsistent one, in which case the round is charged to \(j\); a residual row is assigned at one node only, so at most \(|R_{\rm e}|\) rounds are charged; if \(P\) is cut before \(j\) is assigned, \(y_P(j)\) is consistent by the convention. No other case arises: after the wide phase the node assigns only the round's pigeon, the round's hole answer and moved light rows, a wide row of \(h\) is assigned before the round, and every row of \(h\) is assigned by the end of \(m\) unless \(P\) is cut there. (b) Suppose a round of \(P\) at node \(m\) has current term \(T''\) whose host has the reduced tail of \(h_1\). At the start of \(m\), \(T''\) is neither falsified nor counting as falsified, and \(T\)'s pinned part holds under \(\rho'\). The rows of \(T\) in \(B_0\) are those of \(T''\) with the same patterns, so they contribute the same status. A row \(j\) of \(h_1\) in \(B_{\rm e}\) matched by \(\rho'\) is consistent, since \(h_1\) is consistent; one assigned before \(m\) carries \(y_P(j)\in C(p_{h_1,j})\); one unassigned at the start of \(m\) can make \(T\) count as falsified only if it is wide and every hole of \(C(p_{h_1,j})\cap Q\) is resolved before \(m\), but \(y_P(j)\in C(p_{h_1,j})\) is a hole of \(Q\) unresolved at the start of \(m\): the label \(j\) receives later, a hole unused until then, or \(x_{\rm last}\), unresolved at the start of the last round's node, which is at or after \(m\); the third convention concerns light rows, which never make a term count as falsified. So \(T\) is neither falsified nor counting as falsified at the start of \(m\), and it is pin-matched; the preference then selects a pin-matched term, whose pinned row is matched and not residual, and no round follows at \(m\), a contradiction. If every row of \(h_1\) in \(B_0\) is matched consistently, the status of \(T\) at the start of any node of \(P\) up to the last round's depends on its rows in \(B_{\rm e}\) alone, which by the same argument never falsify it; so \(T\) is alive and pin-matched at the start of every round's node, and there is no round. \(\square\)

On the round-first tree fact (a) fails: the pinned reader with the terms \([a\to x]\wedge[j\in p]\) for the pins \((a,x)\), \(x\in C(p)\cap Q\), and the rows \(j\in B\) makes a round at a term whose wide row \(j\) then has its cube exhausted by the round's own hole query, and \(j\) is later assigned outside the cube; the reordered node makes no round there, because the hole query at \(x\) for \(j\) comes first and either satisfies the tail or kills the pin (Section 6).

3. Every recorded round bound holds on the wide-round tree

Theorem T (transfer). The following hold on \(\mathcal T_w\) with the probabilities recorded: the few-light-rows theorem (\(4n^{-c-2}\)), the combined theorem with its size corollary (\(6n^{-c-2}\)), the two-role few-rows theorem (\(4n^{-c-2}\)), the two-role exposed theorem with its Corollary 2 (\(6n^{-c-2}\)), and the two-role Corollary 1 for sizes below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\) (\(3n^{-c-1}\)); with the multi-row size corollary of the previous entry, every round bound cited in clauses (a) to (g) of the current-term corollary holds on \(\mathcal T_w\). Proof. Each proof was re-read for this entry. The four exposed-row proofs use of the tree exactly the two facts about a bad path stated in their settings, the disjointness of the trigger pairs (Lemma 1 of the complete-term rule, on \(\mathcal T_w\) by Lemma W3 and Lemma R0), and the 1-leaf rule, which the reordering keeps; their probabilistic steps ((K1) and (K2), (H1) to (H4c), (E1) and (E2), the residual-row count) concern \(\rho'\) and the family of hosts consistent with a fixed labeling, not the tree. Lemma X supplies the two facts: its (a) is their fact (a) with the charging of Lemma 2 of the complete-term rule, fewer than \(r_0\) charged rounds outside the excluded event \(|R_{\rm e}|\ge r_0\), with \(R_{\rm e}\) the residual light rows, crowded rows or exposed rows respectively; its (b) is their fact (b), including the strengthened form the combined and two-role exposed proofs use in (H4b) and (H4c), and the form of the two-role few-rows proof, in which a host of \(\mathcal H_y\) with a matched pair has a term never falsified on the path. The labelings \(y_P\) are labelings of \(R_{\rm e}\) by labels, fewer than \(n^{r_0}\) of them, as the union bounds count. The charged rounds are absorbed as in Lemma 2: the final counts \(N/192+2^d+r_0\) for the few-light-rows and combined theorems and \(N/192+2^d+2r_0\) for the two-role theorems stay below \(N/48\), because \(N\ge2^{d+7}c'\log_2n\ge256r_0\). The two-role Corollary 1 rests on steps (H1) to (H3) of the multi-row theorem, role-independent, and on Lemma 1 with no exposed row, which Lemma W3 gives on \(\mathcal T_w\). \(\square\)

Scope. With wide rows, clauses (b), (e) and (g) add nothing to (a) and (d): their hypothesis \(J_0\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) caps every tail's total width below \((1-\varepsilon)\log_2n\), so their wide patterns satisfy the wide mass condition of the previous entry only when \(r(N+1)n^{c-1+2\varepsilon}\le n^{1-\varepsilon}\), that is for \(c<2-3\varepsilon\), where the multi-row bound applies; and Lemma W2's mass condition itself fails for a reader of size \(n^c\), \(c\ge2-2\varepsilon\), whose every term has a wide row. What the transfer adds is the few-rows theorems, clauses (c) and (f), which bound the rows, not the widths or the size, and the two-role Corollary 1, clause (d), which Corollary B's two-role form uses.

4. Few tail rows, or few wide rows: switching at every width

Lemma Y (few wide rows). \(\nu(G)\le|R'\cap B_{\rm w}|\), and for \(b_{\rm w}=|B_{\rm w}|\) and \(r\ge1\), \(\Pr[|R'\cap B_{\rm w}|\ge r]\le\binom{b_{\rm w}}r\bigl(\tfrac{N+1}{n+1}\bigr)^r\le\bigl(\tfrac{eb_{\rm w}(N+1)}{r(n+1)}\bigr)^r\); for \(b_{\rm w}\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) this is at most \(n^{-\varepsilon r}\). Proof. A matching of \(G\) uses distinct rows of \(R'\cap B_{\rm w}\). A fixed set of \(r\) rows is residual with probability \(\prod_{k<r}(N+1-k)/(n+1-k)\), and \(e(N+1)\le N^4\), as in the few-light-rows setting. \(\square\) So a reader with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) wide rows has \(\nu(G)<r_0=\lceil(c+2)/\varepsilon\rceil+1\) except with probability \(n^{-c-2}\), whatever its wide patterns and its size; by Lemma W1 its wide queries number fewer than \(r_0\) on every path, and Theorem W applies with \(p_W\le n^{-c-2}\) as soon as \(\nu_1=\lfloor N/48\rfloor\ge r_0-1\), which \(N\ge48r_0\) gives.

Corollary A (few tail rows, every size and width). Let \(F\) be a role-separated reader of the previous entry's setting with at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) tail rows, light and wide together, at most \(M\le n^c\) terms for any \(c>0\), light patterns with \(2^{w+4}s\le e\le n/(32rN^4(N+1))\), wide patterns of any width; let \(r_0,c',d\) be as in the few-light-rows theorem, \(N\ge2^{d+7}c'\log_2n\) with \((Nn^{-\varepsilon})^{d+1}\le n^{-c'}/2\), \(N\ge48(2r+1)\), \(N\ge8(c+1)\log_2n+(2r+2)(16+24\log_2N)\), \(s\ge(2c+1)\ln n+\ln r\), and \(n\) large enough for the cited theorems' own conditions. Then a uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) switches \(F\) within the height budget except with probability at most \(4n^{-c-1}\); the bound \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\) of the setting is automatic. The same holds for a two-role reader with those rows under sparse pinning on its light rows. Proof. The few-light-rows theorem on \(\mathcal T_w\) (Theorem T) gives at most \(\nu_0-1\) rounds on every path before a 1-leaf except with probability \(4n^{-c-2}\), its count being below \(\lfloor N/48\rfloor-1\) with the slack recorded; Lemma Y with \(b_{\rm w}\le n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) gives \(p_W\le n^{-c-2}\), as \(N\ge256r_0\); Theorem W (Lemma R0) with \(Mr\,e^{-s}\le n^{-c-1}\) and \(2^{-N/8+(2r+2)(2+3\log_2N)}\le n^{-c-1}\) gives the total \(5n^{-c-2}+\tfrac{14}5n^{-c-1}\le4n^{-c-1}\) for \(n\ge5\). The two-role form uses the two-role few-rows theorem on \(\mathcal T_w\), \(4n^{-c-2}\), and Theorem W's two-role form; \(|B|\le(n-2N-2)/2\) is automatic. \(\square\)

Corollary B (few wide rows, size below \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\)). Let \(F\) be a role-separated reader of the previous entry's setting with at most \(n^c\) terms, \(1\le c<2-\varepsilon\) as the multi-row corollary states, at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) wide rows and any number of light rows, light patterns in the range above and wide patterns of any width, under the multi-row theorem's conditions on \(N\), \(800\,\mathrm e\,(N+1)\le n^{2-\varepsilon-c}\), \(N\ge48r_0\) with \(r_0=\lceil(c+2)/\varepsilon\rceil+1\), and the conditions on \(N\), \(s\) and \(n\) of Corollary A's last three clauses. Then a uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) switches \(F\) within the height budget except with probability at most \(7n^{-c-1}\); the same holds for a two-role reader under sparse pinning. Proof. The multi-row size corollary on \(\mathcal T_w\), or its two-role Corollary 1 by Theorem T, gives \(p_R=3n^{-c-1}\); Lemma Y gives \(p_W\le n^{-c-2}\); Theorem W gives \(3n^{-c-1}+n^{-c-2}+\tfrac{14}5n^{-c-1}\le7n^{-c-1}\). \(\square\)

Against Corollary 2 of the previous entry, Corollary B reaches \(c<2-\varepsilon\) instead of \(2-2\varepsilon\), needs no wide mass condition and covers every wide width, at the price of few wide rows; Corollary A is the first switching statement of the window at every polynomial size with tail rows of every width, for readers whose tails live on \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) rows. Both keep the light range for the light rows, the range intrinsic to extension encodings (code obstruction).

5. What remains

Every recorded round bound now lives on the wide-round tree, so for wide rows the sole remaining restriction is the bound on the wide matching number: Lemma W2 needs wide mass at most \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}/(N+1)\), and Lemma Y needs few wide rows. Open per reader are therefore readers with more than \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) wide rows and wide mass above \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}/(N+1)\), possible only at sizes from \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\) on; the natural route is a wide-mass dichotomy, in which a hole of large wide degree forces, by negative association over the rows matched into the cubes at it, a satisfied term or a matched wide row that removes the incidences from the wide graph, as step (H1) of the multi-row theorem does for pinned pairs. The round bounds' own open cases are as before: more than \(n^{1-\varepsilon}/N^4\) crowded rows at sizes at least \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}\), many heavy two-role rows, dense pinning of two-role rows. Terms containing parities remain the open core.

6. Checks

The checker (check_pair_space_encoding.py) gained --wide-order: wide-first, the default, is the reordered node of Section 1 (the encoder and the decoder process a node as a plan, wide rows, then the round if the term is still alive with an alive pin, then light rows), and round-first is the previous entry's order; the path search reports the largest number of rounds on a path. Batch 10 (runs, README, provenance) repeats batch 9 on the reordered tree: the three readers of the wide-rows entry on two-hole and four-hole flats and the eight random mixed readers with wide rows, all with the current-term rule and slot revelation: every rich pair decodes, 0 failures in 14 runs, the wide queries of the encoded path never above the cover, at most two rounds on a path; the two controls with --code-rule any fail on 106 and 12 pairs, all through excluded pin labels. The census (wide_rows_tree_check.py --tree wide --wide-order) was run in both orders over every \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) for every flat of \(\mathbb F_2^3\) of dimension one and two, for the three readers of the wide-rows entry and a fourth, the pinned reader of Section 2 with the pins \((a,x)\), \(a\in\{0,1,2\}\), \(x\in C(p)=\{0,4\}\), and the wide row \(j\in\{3,\dots,8\}\) with the shared pattern \(p\), 36 terms, on which a round-first node can exhaust its wide row through the round's own hole query. For the three readers of the wide-rows entry the two orders give identical heights and wide-query counts in every restriction (the one-pin reader's single round cannot touch its wide row's cube, whose labels are not the pin's), and the wide queries never exceed the cover. The pinned reader separates the orders. On the four-hole flats meeting the cube (\(33264\) restrictions, no term ever satisfied) the round-first tree has a path of length at least \(2\) in \(73.6\) percent, maximum height \(4\) and up to \(2\) rounds on a path, these being rounds followed by the exhaustion of the host's cube through the round's own hole query; the reordered tree has such a path in \(38.0\) percent, maximum height \(3\) and at most \(1\) round, the hole queries for the wide row coming first and killing the pin or satisfying the tail before any round. On the two-hole flats the shares are \(56.3\) and \(26.1\) percent with at most one round in either order, and on the flats missing the cube both trees have height \(0\). The exact counts are in the results directory.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the previous entry in full (setting, Lemmas W0 to W5, Theorem W, corollaries); the complete-term rule with its Lemmas 1 and 2 and its Section 3 (the two-role few-rows theorem); the few-light-rows setting and theorem with facts (a) and (b) and steps (K1) and (K2); the combined setting, theorem with steps (E1), (E2), (H1) to (H4c), and size corollary; the two-role exposed setting, theorem and both corollaries; the multi-row setting, theorem and size corollary. Recorded obstructions checked: the q-skip refutation (the skip still tests only unplaced rows), the adaptive-rule counterexample (the cover is still static), the hole-only sparse failure and the shared-cube lemma (unchanged by the order), the (H4c) obstruction of the complete-term scope (the two-role transfers keep the greedy family off the two-role rows as recorded). Checks run: batch 10 of the exhaustive checker on the reordered tree with two negative controls, and the census in both orders with the new pinned reader. The standing reviewer, continued from the previous cycles with the draft and the new anchors, re-read every cited proof against its anchor and confirmed Lemma R0, Lemma X (b) in both forms, the transfer of each theorem, Lemma Y and both corollaries with their constants, and the tool's implementation of the reordered node; it reported five findings, one a gap, all applied: Lemma X (a) omitted the light exposed rows of the host that the round's own hole answer assigns inconsistently, now included in the charged rounds with the same bound, which is Lemma 2's recorded charge; the reader of Section 2 is pinned, not pin-free; Lemma R0's agreement on the pin's status needed the two-role form's point; the Scope omitted clause (d); and \(1\le c\), the bound on \(|B|\) in Corollary A and the largeness of \(n\) are inherited or automatic and are now marked so.

Assessment. The named obligation, the exposed-row round bounds on the wide-round tree, is discharged: every recorded round bound holds on the reordered tree, so the composition of the previous entry is unconditional wherever its wide bound holds, and readers with few tail rows switch at every size and width while readers with few wide rows switch at every width below size \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\); what remains for wide rows is the wide matching number of readers with many wide rows of large wide mass, at sizes from \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\) on.

Process assessment. The charging plan of the proposed next step was tested against the tree before drafting and dropped in favour of the reordering, which was verified by the exhaustive checker before the proofs were written; the reviewer's one gap, the round's own hole answer at a light row of the host, is the kind of case a fresh reading catches and a writer's re-reading does not, and its repair changed no count. No framework change.

2026-09-18: The wide-mass dichotomy, base case: pin-free readers of single-row terms of any width switch at every size by row mass, and the pinned case needs the alive wide graph with a matched-mass concentration

Working proof: pin-free readers of single-row terms of any width switch at every size; the pinned case is analysed and left open. Spin cycle. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Question. The named obligation was the wide matching number of readers with many wide rows of large wide mass, possible only from size \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\) on (remaining), by a dichotomy in the manner of step (H1) of the multi-row theorem: a hole of large wide degree should force a satisfied term. The intended general claim was tested first against pinned readers, where the terms \([a\to y]\wedge[j\in p]\) of one pinned row \(a\) with all labels \(y\) share the fate of one matched pin, and it failed as stated: the wide graph of the previous entries counts the incidences of every term, alive or dead, so for a reader whose pins are mostly dead it is large while its tree is a leaf, and the count of Lemma W2 applied to the alive incidences of the light pins hits the same barrier \(c<2-2\varepsilon\), because the light pins' total mass is \(n^{c+1}\) while only about \(n\) of them are matched. What holds cleanly is the base case, the mechanism the dichotomy rests on: for a pin-free reader whose terms are single tail literals, of any width and in any number, the row mass \(\sum_j|S_j|\), \(S_j\) the union of the cubes on row \(j\), either forces a satisfied term at the root or is below \(4N(n+1)\), where Lemma W2, restated by rows, bounds the wide matching number (Section 2). This closes the shared-cube family at every size and contains the unary readers. The pinned and multi-row cases are analysed in Section 4: they need the alive wide graph, whose cover the code can carry at no cost to the count, a refined preference, and a concentration of the matched row mass over the pinned images, which is the named obligation. The stopping point was the base theorem with its gate and this analysis.

1. Lemma W2 by rows

For a wide row \(j\in B_{\rm w}\) let \(S_j=\bigcup_{T\ni j}C(p_{T,j})\) be the union of the cubes of its patterns over the terms on it; the wide graph \(G\) of the wide-rounds entry has the edges \((j,x)\), \(j\in R'\cap B_{\rm w}\), \(x\in Q\cap S_j\). For a label \(x\) let the row degree \(d_{\rm r}(x)=|\{j\in B_{\rm w}:\ x\in S_j\}|\) and the row mass \(m_{\rm r}=\sum_xd_{\rm r}(x)=\sum_j|S_j|\); \(d_{\rm r}\le d_{\rm w}\) and \(m_{\rm r}\le m_{\rm w}\), with equality when no two patterns on a row overlap. Lemma W2 (rows). Lemma W2 and its polynomial form hold with \(d_{\rm r}\), \(\mathrm{Heavy}=\{x:\ d_{\rm r}(x)>D\}\) and \(m_{\rm r}\) in place of \(d_{\rm w}\), \(\mathrm{Heavy}\) and \(m_{\rm w}\). Proof. The recorded proof uses the wide degree once, to bound the number of rows adjacent to a hole \(x_i\) of a matching; that number is \(d_{\rm r}(x_i)\). \(\square\)

2. Single-row pin-free readers switch at every size

Setting. A reader \(F\) whose terms are single tail literals \([j\in p]\), \(j\in B\), \(p\) a pattern of any width from \(0\) to \(\ell\), any number of terms and of patterns per row; every row of \(B\) is wide, \(B_{\rm w}=B\), \(B_{\rm l}=\varnothing\), and there are no pins. The wide-round tree \(\mathcal T_w(F,\rho')\) of the previous entry makes neither rounds nor light moves, so every query on a path is a wide query. A term \([j\in p]\) is satisfied by \(\rho'\) when \(j\) is matched and \(\mu'(j)\in C(p)\).

Theorem V (row-mass dichotomy). Fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)\) and \(c'>0\); put \(d=\lceil c'/\varepsilon\rceil+2\) and \(t=\lceil c'/\varepsilon\rceil+1\). Let \(N\ge8(2^d+t-1)\), and let \(n\) be large enough that \(4N(N+1)(n+1)\le n^{2-2\varepsilon}\), \(N^{d+1}\le n^{3\varepsilon}/2\) and \((eN)^t\le n^{\varepsilon}/2\). Then for every reader of the setting and a uniform \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\), except with probability at most \(e^{-N}+n^{-c'}\), the tree \(\mathcal T_w(F,\rho')\) has height at most \(2^d+t-2\le N/8-1\), and \(F\) switches under \(\rho'\) within the height budget. With \(N\ge(c+1)\ln n\) and \(c'=c+1\) the failure is at most \(2n^{-c-1}\), whatever the number of terms.

Proof. Two cases by the row mass \(m_{\rm r}=\sum_{j\in B}|S_j|\), fixed by the reader. (D1) \(m_{\rm r}\ge4N(n+1)\). Given \(Q\) and \(R'\), \(\mu'\) is a uniform bijection of the rows outside \(R'\) onto the labels outside \(Q\), and for a matched row \(j\) the event \(E_j\) that \(\mu'(j)\in S_j\), which satisfies a term on \(j\), has probability \(|S_j\setminus Q|/(n-N)\ge(|S_j|-N)/n\). The events \(E_j\) are increasing and depend on pairwise disjoint rows of the bijection, so negative association gives \(\Pr[\text{no }E_j]\le\prod_{j\notin R'}(1-\Pr[E_j])\le\exp\bigl(-\sum_{j\notin R'}(|S_j|-N)/n\bigr)\), as in step (H4c) of the multi-row theorem. The residual rows carry at most \((N+1)n\) of \(m_{\rm r}\) and the subtracted \(N\) per row totals at most \((n+1)N\), so the exponent is at least \((4N(n+1)-(N+1)n-N(n+1))/n=(2Nn+3N-n)/n\ge N\) for \(N\ge1\). So some term is satisfied by \(\rho'\) except with probability \(e^{-N}\), and then the root of \(\mathcal T_w(F,\rho')\) is a 1-leaf. (D2) \(m_{\rm r}<4N(n+1)\le n^{2-2\varepsilon}/(N+1)\). The polynomial form of Lemma W2 (rows) with the row mass in place of the wide mass gives \(\Pr[\nu(G)\ge2^d+t-1]\le n^{-c'}\). Outside this event every path has at most \(2^d+t-2\) wide queries by Lemma W1, hence that height, and \(2^d+t-2\le N/8-1\) by the bound on \(N\). In both cases the tree is a matching decision tree for \(\rho'\) with pigeon queries over unused holes and hole-query nodes whose 1-leaves contain a satisfied term and whose 0-leaves falsify or annihilate every term (Lemma W0), of height at most \(N/8-r\) with \(r=1\), which is what the height budget asks of a switched reader; no pair space enters, the reader having no light rows (the scope of Theorem W). The last clause: \(e^{-N}\le n^{-c-1}\) for \(N\ge(c+1)\ln n\). \(\square\)

3. Scope

The theorem has no hypothesis on the number of terms, the widths, the number of patterns per row or the number of rows, and its failure is per reader; a source of \(n^c\) such readers costs \(n^c\) times \(2n^{-c-1}\). It contains the pin-free reader \(F_p\) of the shared-cube lemma at every size: its row mass \(2|B|\) is below \(4N(n+1)\), its heavy holes are the two labels of \(C(p)\), and case (D2) gives at most two hole queries, as the census of the wide-rounds entry showed. It contains the unary readers, the terms \([j=z]\) of width \(\ell\), on the wide-round tree, where the recorded unary theorem used its own hole-query trees; and it contains the reader with every pattern of \(\ell-1\) literals on every row of \(B\), of row mass \(n|B|\), which case (D1) satisfies at the root except with probability \(e^{-N}\) when \(|B|\ge4N+1\) and case (D2) covers otherwise; that reader has a term satisfied at the root as soon as some row of \(B\) is matched, its \(S_j\) being the whole label set (Section 5). It is not implied by an earlier result: Corollary 1 of the wide-rounds entry needs the wide mass condition, which fails for this family from size \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\) on; Corollary A of the previous entry needs few rows; the dichotomy does not apply to pin-free terms of width above \(\ell-\ell_2-1\); and the recorded unary theorem's height grows with the source size. Case (D1) needs no hypothesis on \(N\) beyond \(N\ge1\), and case (D2) is Lemma W2; the split at \(4N(n+1)\) is where the two meet, and \(\varepsilon<\tfrac12\) serves only to make \(4N(N+1)(n+1)\le n^{2-2\varepsilon}\) satisfiable for large \(n\).

4. The pinned and multi-row cases

The alive wide graph. Let \(G_{\rm a}\) be the wide graph restricted to the incidences of terms not falsified by \(\rho'\) at the root (pin matched or alive, matched tail rows consistent). Lemma W1 holds with a vertex cover of \(G_{\rm a}\): a term falsified at the root is never current, so every hole query is at an edge of \(G_{\rm a}\). The decoder of Lemma W4 cannot compute \(G_{\rm a}\) at the root, because the pins at the filling rows of undecoded slots are undecided there; but the cover can be written into the code. Remark (the cover in the code). A cover with at most \(\nu_1=\lfloor N/48\rfloor\) elements, each a row of \(R'\cap B_{\rm w}\) or a hole of \(Q\), takes at most \((2N+2)^{\nu_1}\le2^{(N/48)(2+\log_2N)}\) values, and adding this factor to the count of Lemma W5 changes the exponent of Theorem W to \(-(5N/48)\log_2N+(2r+1)(2+3\log_2N)+1\), which is at most \(-N/8+(2r+2)(2+3\log_2N)\) for every \(N\ge1\); so Theorem W holds with the cover of any decoder-independent graph containing the queried edges written into the code, at no cost to its bound. This is not implemented in the checker.

Single-wide-row pinned terms. Let the terms be \([a\to y]\wedge[j\in p]\), one wide row and no light row; the hosts are the pins \((a,y)\), with row mass \(\mu_{(a,y)}=\sum_j|S^{(a,y)}_j|\), \(S^{(a,y)}_j\) the union of the cubes of the patterns on \(j\) in the terms with that pin. Three steps are available and one is missing. (i) A heavy pin, \(\mu_{(a,y)}\ge4N(n+1)\), has a matched wide incidence except with probability \(e^{-N}\), by the argument of (D1) applied to its rows; if the pin is matched the term is satisfied, and if the pin is alive the term with the matched wide row is alive with no uncovered wide row. With the preference refined to prefer, among alive terms of the same pin status, those without an uncovered wide row, which the decoder can apply since wide rows are never placed, such a term is current before any term of its host with an uncovered wide row and resolves the host by its round, so the host contributes no wide query; hence the queried edges lie in \(G'_{\rm a}\), the alive incidences of hosts without an alive wide-satisfied term. (ii) Among light pins, the edges of \(G'_{\rm a}\) at alive pins, \(a\in R'\cap A\) and \(y\in Q\), need a count of their own: an edge is charged per pin, with the incidence degree over pins at \((j,x)\) rather than the row degree, the pinned rows' residual events cost \((N+1)/(n+1)\) each only for distinct pinned rows, and the events \(y\in Q\) of the pins are events of the flat, the rank lemma's territory, not residual events; this count is to be written out. (iii) The edges at matched light pins are the obstacle. Counting them as in Lemma W2 with the matched status costing \(1/(n-N)\) per pin bounds the heavy holes by \(\bigl(\sum_{\text{light pins}}\mu\bigr)(N+1)/n^{2-\varepsilon}\), which is at most \(n^{1-\varepsilon}\) only when the light pins' total row mass is at most \(n^{3-2\varepsilon}/(N+1)\), that is for \(c<2-2\varepsilon\) when there are \(n^c\) light pins of mass up to \(4N(n+1)\); the count charges every light pin although only one pin per pinned row is matched. The repair is a dichotomy on the matched row mass \(M_{\rm m}=\sum_{a\notin R'}\mu_{(a,\mu'(a))}\): given \(Q\) and \(R'\) its expectation is \(\sum_{\text{pins}}\mu/(n-N)\) up to the residual pinned rows, above \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}/(N+1)\) exactly when the count fails, and when \(M_{\rm m}\) is large the wide bijection, given the pinned images, satisfies a term by the argument of (D1) with the unions \(S^{\rm m}_j=\bigcup_aS^{(a,\mu'(a))}_j\) in place of \(S_j\), except that the probabilities are \(|S^{\rm m}_j\cap\mathrm{Rem}|/|\mathrm{Rem}|\), with \(\mathrm{Rem}\) the labels outside \(Q\) not taken by pinned rows, while the edges use \(S^{\rm m}_j\cap Q\). What is missing is the concentration of \(M_{\rm m}\), and of its part in \(\mathrm{Rem}\), over the pinned images: both are sums over the pinned rows of terms bounded by \(4N(n+1)\) that depend on a uniform injection of \(A\setminus R'\) into the labels outside \(Q\), and the rank lemma does not apply to them, their label sets depending on the images. The natural tool is the Azuma inequality for the sequential exposure of the images, whose martingale differences are bounded by twice the largest term through the transposition coupling, giving failure \(\exp(-\Omega(n^{1-4\varepsilon}/N^4))\) for \(|B|\) of order \(n\), useful only for \(\varepsilon<\tfrac14\), where Theorem V and the barrier are stated for \(\varepsilon<\tfrac12\); this concentration, together with the alive-pin count of (ii), is the named obligation of the pinned case.

Multi-row wide terms. The wide graph of all incidences is the wrong graph for terms with several wide rows: for the terms \([j\in p]\wedge[j'=z]\) with \(|C(p)|=n/2\) on disjoint pairs of rows, \(G\) joins every residual row \(j\) to half of \(Q\), so \(\nu(G)\) is of order \(N\), while a term is alive only if \(j'\) is residual or matched at \(z\), which leaves few alive incidences. The extension therefore starts from \(G_{\rm a}\) with the cover in the code, and the satisfaction step needs the greedy row-disjoint families of steps (H4b) and (H4c) of the multi-row theorem, because the satisfaction events of terms sharing rows are positively correlated.

5. What remains, and checks

For wide rows the open cases are, per reader, pinned terms with a wide row at sizes from \(n^{2-2\varepsilon}\) on when the wide rows are many, whose route is Section 4 with the matched-mass concentration as the obligation, and terms with several wide rows, which need the alive wide graph; light rows enter through the exposed-row mechanism once these are done. The round bounds' own open cases and parity terms are as before.

Checks. The census tool (wide_rows_tree_check.py) gained the reader all-patterns, every pattern of \(\ell-1\) literals on every row of \(B\), \(72\) terms for \(n=8\), of row mass \(n|B|=48\), which for \(n=8\) lies below the split \(4N(n+1)\) and so falls under case (D2) by the theorem's own division while exhibiting the satisfaction mechanism of (D1), every row of \(B\) having \(S_j\) equal to the whole label set and \(|B|>N+1\); batch 11 (runs, README, provenance) ran the census of the wide-round tree over every \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) for every flat of \(\mathbb F_2^3\) of dimension one and two on it and on the shared-pattern reader, the small-mass case. In every one of the \(1693440\) restrictions of the two-hole flats and the \(42336\) of the four-hole flats the all-patterns reader has a term satisfied by \(\rho'\) at the root (the census's satisfied share is \(1.000\)), every matched row satisfying the three terms whose cubes contain its label and some row of \(B\) being matched in every restriction, and its tree has height \(0\); the shared-pattern reader, of row mass \(2|B|=12\), keeps the heights of the wide-rounds census, at most \(2\), the two hole queries of case (D2) at the cube's labels. The exact counts are in the results directory. No rule, tree or encoding changed, so the round-trip checker was not rerun.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the wide-rounds entry's Lemmas W0, W1 and W2 with its polynomial form and Theorem W's scope note; the previous entry's Lemma R0; the multi-row theorem's step (H4c) for negative association over disjoint rows of the bijection; the rank lemma's independent-points form; the height-budget observation; the shared-cube lemma; the unary theorem's statement. Recorded obstructions checked: the shared-cube lemma (contained, at every size), the pigeon-only refutation (the single-target reader is a unary reader, resolved by one hole query in the cover), the hole-only sparse failure (the star reader, resolved by one pigeon query), the code obstruction (no light rows, nothing placed). Checks run: the census of batch 11. The standing reviewer, continued from the previous cycles with the draft and the anchors, confirmed Theorem V in both cases with its arithmetic and its composition, Lemma W2 by rows against the recorded proof, the containment claims and the absence of an earlier result with fewer hypotheses (the unary theorem's height grows with the source size), the Remark's count and exponent, and the analysis of Section 4 as analysis; it reported five findings, none breaking a statement, all applied: the census instance has row mass \(48\), below the split for \(n=8\), so it exhibits the satisfaction mechanism rather than case (D1); the dichotomy lemma does not apply to this family, so the non-implication rests on the width; the Azuma route needs \(\varepsilon<\tfrac14\) and step (ii) needs a per-pin count with the pins' labels in the flat as flat events, both now in the stated obligation; \(N\ge8(2^d+t-1)\) suffices and the Remark's inequality holds for every \(N\ge1\); the multi-row example's matching number is of order \(N\), not \(N/2\).

The named obligation, the wide matching number of readers with many wide rows, is discharged for pin-free readers of single-row terms, at every size and width and with no hypothesis, by the row-mass dichotomy, which closes the shared-cube family and contains the unary readers; for pinned single-wide-row terms the dichotomy is reduced to a concentration of the matched row mass over the pinned images and a per-pin count of the alive pins' edges, with the alive wide graph and its cover in the code as the tree and encoding to use, and multi-row wide terms are routed through the same graph.
