1. The induction is a composition of recorded results

Cycle 174 already records the alternatives at every level on the support of the weight: a block whose purely affine part has rank at least \(r_{\rm high}=\lceil v\ln(16M)/k\rceil\) is clamped, a block reading at most polylogarithmically many low indicators is packed exactly, and what is left at every level is a wide disjunction of narrow terms, on whose union, that entry asserts without proof, no weight vanishes. Cycle 173 states the same zone for the row-linear weight. The collapse of the previous entries fits into this list as one more removable case, and it is the recorded removal of an input span that contains one, applied after the images of the lower level:

Collapse step. Let a block \(R\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) have inputs whose images, after the substitutions of the lower levels, are old polynomials \(q_1,\dots,q_a\) of degree at most \(w\), and suppose \(1+\sum_ic_iq_i\) reduces to zero by Booleanity for some constants \(c_i\in\mathbb F_2\). Assign the first coefficient row of \(R\) the constants \(c_i\) and the other rows zero. The product of \(R\) has the image \(1+\sum_ic_iq_i\), which is zero with a Boolean certificate of degree at most \(w\); all companions and field equations of \(R\) have zero images. No degree is spent beyond the images of the inputs. For a generic reader of \(a\ge2^w(D_w\ln2+\ln(1/\eta))\) terms of rank \(w\) on the residual bit space, Lemma C supplies the hypothesis with \(q_i\) the flat indicators, whose coefficient images have degree at most \(w-1\) by the one-bin telescoping map. A slightly more general form costs nothing either: if constants \(c_i\) exist with \(q_j(1+\sum_ic_iq_i)\equiv0\) for every \(j\), then \(\hat P=1+\sum_ic_iq_i\) is an exact image of the product. Example: terms that all contain one common form \(L_0\) and are otherwise generic never cover the space, yet the reader has the exact image \(L_0\).

This is a restatement, not a new lemma: the normal form removes a block whose literal input span contains one, and the step applies it to the images of the inputs instead of the literal inputs.

2. Attempts to break the induction, and what survives

Mixed blocks. A block one level up that reads a collapsed reader and a surviving one sees a constant in place of the first, so it is the same block on the surviving inputs only. Constants propagate upwards and never help with the surviving inputs.

Shared forms. Lemma C needs independent forms. Terms sharing forms are handled exactly when the shared part factors out as in the example above; a family of terms whose forms are shared in a less regular way has a smaller span and no covering certificate with constant coefficients, and the step does not apply.

Survivors. For a generic reader of \(a=n^c\) terms of rank \(w\) on the residual bit space of dimension \(v\), the step applies for \(w\le w_1\approx c\log_2n/\log_2(2v+2)\) and the weight clamps the terms for \(w\ge r_{\rm high}\). The expected number of uncovered points is \(2^v(1-2^{-w})^a\), so the covering threshold is \(a\ln(1/(1-2^{-w}))=v\ln2\) (for \(w=1\) this is \(a=v\); for large \(w\) it is \(a2^{-w}\approx v\ln2\)). Two zones survive. Between \(w_1\) and the threshold the reader is constant with high probability, but only a covering certificate with constant coefficients is excluded and the cost of a certificate with polynomial coefficients is open (the second row of the table of the dense-forms entry). Beyond the threshold, with a margin (by the variance bound of Lemma B the probability of no uncovered point is at most the reciprocal of the mean), the reader is not constant as a function; this zone contains the balanced rank. In both zones exact packing costs about \(aw\), and the count of cycle 174, which is what produces a weight, needs \(k\ge v\ln(16a)/w\) for a weight of degree \(k\) vanishing on all \(a\) flats, more than \(0.69\,v\) at the balanced rank against \(k\le v/4\) (that no weight exists is expected for generic flats but is not proved, here or in cycle 174). These survivors are the frontier recorded in cycles 173 and 174. A block reading a surviving reader has no input image to which the step could apply, so the induction stops at its first step for every source that contains one such reader, and the question of dependence between levels is not reached. The proposal of the previous entry is withdrawn as a route: it handles a generic source only if the source has no reader in these zones.

3. What a generic source needs instead: a joint choice of term values

The weight is one way to make a design give every high product the value zero. Nothing forces a design to be of weight form. Let \(\mathcal F\) be a base containing the Boolean equations, let \(T\) be a set of first-level blocks with exact flat indicators \(Z_c=\prod_i(1+L_{c,i})\) of degree at most \(w\), and let \(e\in\mathbb F_2^T\).

Reduction. Call a source pure over \(T\) if it consists of the blocks of \(T\) and of higher blocks each of whose inputs is an \(\mathbb F_2\)-affine combination of earlier products, with no old variables, no raw coefficients and no products of products. If \(\mathcal F\cup\{Z_c+e_c:c\in T\}\) has no polynomial-calculus refutation of degree \(B\), then no source pure over \(T\) has a refutation of degree \(B/\max(1,w-1)\). Any accuracy is allowed. The statement uses of the base only its Boolean equations and of \(T\) only the exactness of the flat indicators; it extends the recorded constant-value profiles of eligible zero clamps (zero-value profile, shared core) from zero clamps supplied by the weight to arbitrary constants under a hardness hypothesis. Proof: the telescoping substitution gives each block of \(T\) the product image \(Z_c\) with coefficient images of degree at most \(w-1\). A reader of products of \(T\) has inputs congruent to constants modulo the added axioms. If some input \(g\) is congruent to 1, the first coefficient row that selects this input alone gives the product image \(1+g\), a constant combination of the added axioms, hence congruent to 0, and every companion image is a multiple of it. If all inputs are congruent to 0, the zero coefficient rows give the product image 1, and each companion image is an input, again a combination of the added axioms. Either way the reader's product is congruent to a constant, and the same argument applies one level up. The images of the axioms of the source have certificates within \(\max(1,w-1)\) times their original degrees (companions of \(T\): \(w+1\) against \(3(w-1)\) for \(w\ge2\); field equations: \(2(w-1)\); reader companions: at most \(2w\) against \(5(w-1)\)). Every line of a refutation of the source maps to a consequence of the enlarged base of degree at most \(\max(1,w-1)\) times its own. \(\square\) (A reader that also has a nonconstant affine part becomes a first-level block of the quotient and joins \(T\) with its own value; this case is not needed below.)

So for a generic pure source the general step would follow, with the factor \(w-1\), from a statement in the old variables about the base with the first-level terms of the source adjoined: some assignment of values to the terms keeps the PHP hard. For every reader both outcomes are acceptable, since a reader with one true term is 0 and a reader with no true term is 1; the signs \(e_c\) are ours to choose.

Lemma S (the recorded case split, in polynomial-calculus form). The Nullstellensatz form over every \(\mathbb F_p\), with loss \((p-1)s\) for a query of degree \(s\), its contrapositive and its iteration along a query tree are recorded in the case-split budget; the polynomial-calculus proof and the phrasing for term values are the only additions. Let \(Z\) be an old polynomial of degree \(w\le B\) with \(Z^2-Z\) in the Boolean ideal through \(2w\). If \(\mathcal F\cup\{Z\}\) and \(\mathcal F\cup\{1+Z\}\) both have refutations of degree \(B\), then \(\mathcal F\) has one of degree \(B+w\). Proof: multiply every line of the first refutation by \(1+Z\) and of the second by \(Z\). The axiom \(Z\) becomes \(Z(1+Z)\), a Boolean consequence through \(2w\le B+w\); the old axioms and the rules stay within \(B+w\). The two derivations end at \(1+Z\) and \(Z\), whose sum is 1. \(\square\)

Hence for any \(a\) flats some sign vector keeps the base hard through \(D_0-1-aw\), where \(D_0\) is its refutation degree. This loss is additive in the number of terms. The same conclusion is recorded: committing the values of whole input spaces by case splits costs up to \((p-1)rs\) and reproduces a rank-control obligation. A loss linear in the number of terms up to a logarithmic factor does occur for adversarial terms: the \(r\log_2N\) parity constraints that fix the labels of \(r\) rows lower the refutation degree of the PHP by about \(r/2\). The question left by the generic model is whether independent generic terms lose almost nothing:

Question H. The new content is whether generic terms lose less than the case-split ceiling. Let \(Z_1,\dots,Z_a\) be independent uniform flats of codimension \(w\) in the residual bit space, \(a\le n^c\), below the covering threshold with a margin: \(a\ln(1/(1-2^{-w}))\le(1-\delta)v\ln2\), and for \(w=1\) also \(v-a\ge CN\) (for \(w=1\) the constraints leave an affine subspace of dimension \(v-a\), and a search over its free bits refutes within about \(v-a\); for \(a>v\) the linear system is inconsistent and there is a refutation of degree one). Is \(\mathrm{PHP}_N\cup\{Z_c\}\) without refutations of degree \(N/8\), with high probability? And near and above the covering threshold, is there always either a covering certificate of affordable degree or a hard sign vector?

The recorded mechanisms do not answer it. The counting argument for a weight fails as above. A restriction fails by Lemma I: a generic form stays uniform under every restriction, and a sub-board on which \(a\) chosen dense forms are constant exists only for \(a\) up to about \(\log n/\log\log n\) (a row is usable with probability \(N'^{-a}\) per direction space). Lemma S loses \(w\) per term. The rank-cutoff failure does not apply, because values are imposed as axioms and hardness is asked of the whole system, so all relations among the terms are respected; but it shows that the values cannot be chosen block by block without the joint hardness statement. Question H is also not a statement about actual sources: for the terms "row \(i\) has label \(z\)" every sign vector contradicts the row axiom or a hole axiom at once, and such terms belong to the switching side. A hybrid (values for generic-looking terms, switching for literal terms) is not formulated here.

4. Finite check: tolerance of low-degree closures to generic axioms

Design. The tool research/tools/term_avoidance_check.py adds random axioms \(Z_c=0\) one at a time to the exact degree-\(d\) polynomial-calculus closure over \(\mathbb F_2\) and reports the first count \(a^*\) at which 1 enters. Boards: the functional PHP with \(N+1\) rows and \(N\) holes (refutation degree \(N/2+1\)); as controls the satisfiable bijective board with \(N\) rows, and the labelings of \(N+1\) rows without hole axioms. Forms are dense: every row contributes a uniform subset of the holes, or for \(N=8\) the zero set of a uniform affine function of the label. For \(w=1\) the axiom is a random parity constraint with multipliers of degree \(d-1\); for \(w=2\) a random clause of two parities with multipliers of degree \(d-2\). Nonvacuous range: \(d\) at most the refutation degree minus one, that is \(d\le3\) on six holes and \(d\le4\) on eight; sizes 673 to 45385 monomials. Eight holes at degree four (241993 monomials with up to 30313 low-degree elements to multiply) is beyond this Python tool and was not run. Three seeds per case.

The column "axiom of the first jump" is the first axiom whose increment of the closure dimension exceeds the previous increment; "quotient left" is the codimension of the closure after the axiom before the tipping one. If 1 is in the closure, the closure is the whole space, so the dimension at tipping carries no information and is not reported. Full increment sequences are in the archived records.

Reading. Every run has the same shape. The closure first grows by increments that decrease slowly (63, 62, 61, ... for parity constraints on eight holes at degree two; 1477, 1415, 1354, ... at degree three; a constant 62 for rank-two terms at degree three). These increments are generic ranks: they are the same for every seed, so the three seeds are not independent evidence. For parity constraints at degree two and for rank-two terms they coincide for the PHP and the labelings; for parity constraints at degree three they do not (400 against 526 on six holes, 1477 against 1765 on eight). Then a jump ends the counting regime. On the PHP the tipping is at the jump or within five axioms after it (eight holes, degree two, affine forms: jump at 19 to 20, tipping at 21; rank-two terms on eight holes: jump at 91, tipping at 96), and 1 enters while the quotient still has dimension 36 to 4953. On the bijective control a jump of the same kind occurs slightly earlier than on the PHP (axiom 5 against 6 on six holes at degree three; 12 against 15 and 14 against 17 on eight holes; 34 against 50 and 69 against 91 rank-two terms), and on the labelings with affine forms at the same axiom as on the PHP (15 for parity constraints at degree three, 91 for rank-two terms, 19 to 20 at degree two). Against the labelings with uniform forms the PHP tips earlier: 6 against a jump at 15 to 16 on six holes at degree three, 15 against 21 to 23 at degree two, 50 rank-two terms against none within 120, and on eight holes 32 against 44 and 17 against 31; after division by the last column of the table the PHP is at about 0.7 to 0.85 of that control. Whether this gap is the smaller quotient of the PHP or an effect of the hole axioms is not decided by these runs.

Where models survive the jump it leads to their vanishing ideal, quotient one to four; after it single models are removed, and \(a^*\) is a semantic count (10 to 11 against \(\log_2720=9.5\); 15 to 17 against \(\log_240320=15.3\); 18 to 20 against 18.1; 26 to 31 against 27). Where no model survives (all rank-two controls, the labelings with uniform forms at degree three, and the degree-two controls except the labelings with affine forms) the control tips at or near its jump with a quotient left, in the same way as the PHP: 98 rank-two terms with quotient 11333 on the labelings, which have had no model since about 65 axioms, against 96 with 4953 on the PHP. For rank-two terms the jump comes long before the counting increments would exhaust the quotient (91 times 62 against 17584), so it is a saturation of the space reachable with the available multipliers; on eight holes at degree two rank-two terms have no multipliers and nothing happens within 120 axioms.

What may be concluded. The experiment is nonvacuous (no base closure contains 1) and the controls separate semantic tipping from dimension tipping. At these degrees the tipping of the PHP is governed by dimension counting, the quotient against the number of multipliers (last column), and it coincides with a saturation jump that the controls also show. The PHP never tipped before the jump of the bijective control or of the labelings with affine forms; it did tip earlier than the labelings with uniform forms, by a factor of about 0.7 to 0.85 after normalisation, and the runs do not say why. For comparison, the case split guarantees at degree three on eight holes a hard sign vector for a single parity constraint only (\(D_0-1-a\ge3\) with \(D_0=5\)), while random signs survived 14 and 16 constraints; at this scale generic axioms lose far less than the worst case. The tolerance seen here is small for a trivial reason and says nothing about degree \(N/8\) or growing rank: there the same count would be of order \(c_B/c_{B-w}\) with \(c_t\) the quotient dimension at degree \(t\), and whether 1 stays out of the closure throughout the counting regime is exactly the open question. The check has low power: ranks one and two, degrees two and three.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the records listed in the route check, and after the review the case-split budget with its source comparison and the two clamped-profile lemmas. The standing reviewer confirmed the collapse step with its generalisation and example, the proof of the Reduction line by line (any accuracy, affine combinations of products, the factor \(\max(1,w-1)\) and the three certificate budgets), the polynomial-calculus proof of Lemma S with its corollary and the adversarial example, the quoted values of \(w_1\) and \(r_{\rm high}\), the sub-board count, and that the rank-cutoff failure does not apply (inconsistent signs make the enlarged base refutable at low degree, which the hardness hypothesis excludes). It reported eight findings, all applied: Lemma S and its additive-loss reading were already recorded and unlinked, and two clamped-profile lemmas were unlinked (now linked and presented as restatements); the covering threshold was wrong for small rank and Question H ill-posed near it (exact threshold, margin, and the condition for rank one added; the two survivor zones separated); a regularity first noted in the data, that 1 enters only when the closure is full, is a tautology, and the table now reports the quotient before the tipping axiom; the reading of the counts was reduced to what dimension counting allows; the purity hypothesis of the Reduction was pinned down; two quotations of cycle 174 were corrected (the unproved assertion about weights, and the constant 16 in the count). Unused hypotheses, as the reviewer lists them: the collapse step uses nothing about genericity or the PHP, and Lemma S nothing of the PHP. A second pass recomputed the table from all 27 records (every cell agrees) and reported four further findings on the reading of the counts, all applied: the comparison with the labelings with uniform forms, where the PHP tips earlier, was missing; the increments of the PHP and the labelings coincide only in some cases; two PHP runs tip a few axioms after the jump; the list of controls without surviving models was incomplete. The sentence comparing the observed tolerance with the case-split guarantee was added after the second pass and is elementary arithmetic. The reviewer did not rerun the tool.

Main-route assessment. General step: unchanged. The level-by-level collapse proposed in the previous entry is withdrawn as a route; its survivors are the frontier already recorded in cycles 173 and 174. What the cycle adds is a formulation for generic sources: the step would follow from a joint choice of term values that keeps the PHP hard, where the recorded case split loses the rank of every term and Question H asks whether generic terms lose less. In the exact counts at degrees two and three the PHP tips at a saturation jump that the controls also show, never before the jump of the bijective control or of the labelings with affine forms, though earlier than the labelings with uniform forms; the check has low power. Estimate that Question H leads to a mechanism for generic sources: about 10 percent; its bearing on structured sources is not established, since literal terms admit no sign vector at all.

Process assessment. Reading the named records first showed within the first part of the cycle that the proposed induction was a composition of recorded results, which is what the opening rule is for; but Lemma S was drafted mid-cycle and the index was not searched under its technique name, so a recorded lemma was restated as new until the reviewer found it, and CLAUDE.md now requires that search for every lemma formulated during a cycle. The next entry is a route review of the five dense-form entries.

2026-09-18: Route review of the dense-forms line: its general claim, a test against the recorded universal obstruction in dense coordinates, and the selection of one hardness question

Review turn with no new theorem: the general claim of the line is stated, the recorded approximate-majority obstruction is used as a falsification test, and one continuation is selected. Spin cycle 221. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Purpose. Route item: the general step. Five research entries followed the review of the literal line: dense forms on the compact family, PHP-relative images, the augmented PHP on small boards, the feasibility count and the literature, and the collapse induction. The framework allows six before a review; this one is made at five because the last entry withdrew its own proposal. For this review the universal obstruction (cycle 149) was read in full.

1. What the five entries produced, against the route

For generic dense terms on the compact family: the restriction changes nothing (Lemma I), readers of low restricted rank are packed (Lemma P), wide readers of rank up to about \(c\log n/\log\log n\) are removed at no cost (Lemma C with the input-span normal form), and everything between that rank and the high threshold survives, the balanced rank included. Exact computation on small boards found no PHP-relative image of a dense-form block that Booleanity does not already give, no loss for level-one blocks at the one reachable degree, and cannot reach the recorded second-level loss. The published bounds for polynomial calculus with extension variables stop before dense or nested extension variables. The last entry reduced a pure generic source to one statement in the old variables, a joint choice of term values that keeps the PHP hard, and recorded that the known case split loses the rank of every term. None of this moved the general step for an actual source. The entries did not grow a case list; they closed four directions (restriction, PHP-relative images on small boards, exact tests of the second level, the collapse induction) and left one question.

2. The general claim of the line, stated once

Claim G (image or value). Let a source compiled from a proof of polynomial size over the compact bit base have \(n^c\) first-level terms, flats of codimension at most \(r\) in the bit space, and readers over them through a fixed number of levels. Then there are value axioms \(E\), each a linear equation in the bits or an equation \(Z_c=e_c\) for a term of the source, chosen with knowledge of the source, such that (i) the base with \(E\) adjoined has no polynomial-calculus refutation of degree \(B\), and (ii) modulo \(E\) every block of the source has an old image of degree \(s\), certified by consequences of the base and \(E\), with \(s\) and the accumulated substitution factors within \(B\) over the needed proof degree. The design for the source is then a design of the enlarged base composed with the images, so everything the source can derive is derived from the enlarged base. The claim is stated for compiled sources only, which is all the goal needs. For arbitrary sources of the same shape it has an untested candidate counterexample, found by the reviewer: the disjoint union of a wide literal reader, which needs a restriction to a residual board of polylogarithmic dimension, and the row-mixing twisted source of Section 4, which needs about \(0.7v\) generic linear equations; the two systems of equations are inconsistent with each other, and under the compact restriction alone the twisted part becomes about \(v^{3.75}\) generic flats of codimension \(3\log_2v\) on polylogarithmically many bits, far above the covering threshold, whose readers have no low-degree images. No property of compiled sources is known that excludes such a union, so this is the first falsification target for the claim, and it arises without any mixed term.

The two lines of the last weeks are its extreme cases. For literal terms \(E\) is a matching restriction of the compact family, (i) is the preservation of the compact base, and (ii) is switching (Conjecture L). For generic dense terms in a pure source \(E\) consists of term values, (ii) is trivial by the reduction of the last entry, and (i) is Question H. The recorded structure of the base fits the same language: the compact bit base is itself a system of \(\binom{n+1}2\) avoidance axioms for flats of codimension \(\ell\), the collision flats \(\{\mathrm{label}_i=\mathrm{label}_{i'}\}\), of total density about \(n/2\), which is below the generic covering threshold \(v\ln2\) of the last entry although the structured flats do cover the space. Part (i) asks that further avoidance axioms or linear equations, generic or chosen from a proof, leave this system hard.

3. What the main goal needs from it

The goal needs Claim G for every source compiled from a small proof, with \(B\) and \(s\) polylogarithmic and the factors multiplied along a fixed number of levels. The line has not touched three parts of this. First, (i) has a recorded proof only for structured \(E\): axioms that confine every label to one flat, or that fix rows by a matching, leave a compact base with fewer holes, which is hard by the recorded decoder and bridge (Section 4). For generic \(E\) the notebook has no technique: the weight gives hardness only for avoiding flats above the high threshold, restrictions do not act on dense forms, the case split loses total rank, and a complete affine block never imposes a value. Second, different parts of one source may need incompatible axioms, as in the union above, and mixed terms, with a literal part and a dense part, need both kinds at once; no statement for either exists. Third, the choice of \(E\) must work for all readers of a source simultaneously; for generic terms this is automatic, for structured terms it is a combinatorial problem that has not been posed. What the line does supply is a formulation in which the universal obstruction does not apply, since images are certified relative to the enlarged base and not on the Boolean cube; Section 4 checks this on the obstruction's own source.

4. Falsification attempt: the approximate-majority source in dense coordinates

The recorded obstruction is a three-level evaluation source for an approximate majority \(C\) of the \(v=(n+1)\ell\) old bits: \(v\) sampled DNFs with \(r=\lceil4v(3/2)^t\rceil\) terms of \(t=\lceil3\log_2v\rceil\) positive literals, and their conjunction. Any old-only map certified on the Boolean cube needs \(\deg W+\deg\sigma(Z)\ge\lfloor v/3\rfloor+1\). For \(p=2\), an invertible affine map \(u=Ay+c\) of the bit space is a bijection of the cube that preserves the degree of multilinear representatives and nonzero Boolean remainders, and a map \(\sigma\) for the twisted source \(C(u)\) transports to one for \(C\) with the same degrees; so the same barrier holds for the twisted source with \(A\) a generic invertible matrix. (For odd \(p\) a parity of bits is not affine and the twist leaves the grammar.) Its bottom blocks have the inputs \(1-u_i\), dense affine forms, and its terms are flats of codimension about \(t\). The twisted source is the natural hard instance for Claim G on the dense side: no restriction simplifies it, since its forms are generic, and no Boolean-certified image exists.

The original coordinates, and twists row by row. Here Claim G holds in full with recorded hardness (the reviewer's observation, checked against the records). Let \(J\) consist of the same \(\ell'=\lfloor0.3\ell\rfloor\) bit positions of every label, fixed before the circuit is sampled, and let \(E\) set all other bit positions of every label to zero. By the count below, which applies to any fixed set of at most \(0.3v\) coordinates, every term of a suitable circuit contains a zeroed bit, so (ii) holds with constant images. The fixed positions contribute the factor 1 to every collision polynomial, so the base with \(E\) adjoined is the compact bit base of \(n+1\) rows and \(2^{\ell'}\) holes. It has no refutation through \(2^{\ell'}/2\), about \(n^{0.3}/2\): the decoder transfer holds for every number of rows and every ceiling when \(\ell'\ge2\), and the imported bound for the functional PHP holds whenever there are more rows than holes. The same is true for a twist that applies one affine bijection of \(\mathbb F_2^\ell\) to every label, since the base is invariant under relabelling the holes. So the recorded obstruction source does not resist value axioms; this is the escape that the obstruction entry itself names, a justified restriction that preserves a sufficient old barrier, with the indicator of the subspace, a weight of degree about \(0.7v\), replaced by adjoined axioms and a hardness statement. What is open is exactly a twist that mixes rows.

Values for the row-mixing twist. Fix a set \(J\) of at most \(0.3v\) coordinates and let \(I\) be its complement. A term of the recorded construction is a sample of \(t\) independent uniform coordinates, so it lies inside \(J\) with probability exactly \((|J|/v)^t\le0.3^t\), and the expected number of the \(vr\) terms inside \(J\) is at most \(v(4v(3/2)^t+1)\,0.3^t\le4v^2(0.45)^t+v\,0.3^t\le4v^{-1.45}+v^{-4}\), since \(t\ge3\log_2v\). Adding this event to the recorded existence argument keeps the total failure probability below one for \(v\ge8\), so there is an approximate-majority circuit of the recorded form every term of which contains a coordinate of \(I\). Take \(E=\{u_i=0:i\in I\}\). Modulo \(E\) every bottom product has the telescoping image \(\prod u_i\equiv0\), every middle block has all inputs congruent to 0 and the image 1, and the top block has an input congruent to 1 and an image congruent to 0, by the two cases of the recorded reduction; the substitution factor is \(t-1\) once. Part (ii) of Claim G holds for the twisted obstruction source, and the barrier does not apply because the image of the top block is certified modulo \(E\), not on the cube.

What this leaves. Part (i) for this \(E\): the compact base restricted to the generic affine subspace \(\{u_i=0,i\in I\}\) of codimension about \(0.7v\) must have no refutation of degree \(B\). This is Question H for parity constraints at linear codimension, before any restriction to a small board. It cannot be moved to the residual board of the compact family: there \(0.7v\) generic equations meet a space of polylogarithmic dimension and are inconsistent. So the attempt does not falsify Claim G, and for row-mixing twists it does not support it either: it shows that, for \(p=2\), the claim escapes the twisted obstruction exactly if the PHP stays hard on a generic affine subspace of linear codimension. The finite counts of the last entry do not bear on it: on eight holes, in the unary encoding, random parity constraints on the label bits were tolerated up to 20 of \(v=27\) at degree two and up to 14 at degree three, so codimension \(0.7v=19\) was tolerated at degree two only, and the free dimension \(v-a^*\) needed to stay unrefuted grew with the degree, from 6 to 12. That agrees with refutation by search over the free bits and says nothing about \(0.3v\) free dimensions at polylogarithmic degree.

5. Estimate, alternatives, and the selection

Estimate for the line. That the dense-forms line, continued through part (i) of Claim G, advances the general step: about 10 percent. Part (i) is a lower-bound problem of a kind for which the notebook has no tool, and a positive answer would still leave mixed terms and the simultaneous choice of \(E\). The estimate concerns this line only.

Alternatives. (A) Question H for parity constraints: the polynomial-calculus degree of the compact base on a generic affine subspace of codimension up to \(0.7v\). The hardness part of Claim G now has three levels: axioms confining all labels to one flat (recorded), axioms confining each row to its own flat, which is a PHP on a bipartite graph and should be covered by published expansion bounds (not read), and generic row-mixing equations (open). The last is the single statement on which both the generic model and the test of Section 4 depend, it is sharp (a refutation strategy of low degree would end the value method for dense terms), and cheap exact experiments exist. (B) The dual target, the parked level-one conjecture. Cycle 173 already judged that it does not move the obligation, and nothing since has changed that. (C) Mixed terms and the simultaneous choice of \(E\) for structured sources. Premature: without part (i) for the simplest axioms there is nothing to combine. (D) The alternatives of the earlier reviews (active-window reduction, density coordinates, PHP-relative interfaces, virtual clause source); their placement is unchanged. (E) Extending the published methods for polynomial calculus with extension variables (quadratic degree, restrictions with cleanup) towards dense arity. Not selected now: both papers need a formula that survives their cleanup restrictions (an XOR lift of a generalised PHP in one, selector variables over a family whose large subsets stay hard in the other), and the PHP of the main goal is not of that kind; it stays the fallback if (A) fails, because a failure of (A) would say that hardness under generic linear constraints is the wrong invariant and that size-based measures should be looked at.

Selection. (A), with a bound of two research entries. First entry: an honest retrieval of what is known about polynomial-calculus degree or Res(\(\oplus\)) width of the PHP under affine restrictions and linear substitutions, and the scaling experiment stated in the next step. Second entry: one proof attempt by duality, a design of the compact base supported on the subspace. If neither yields a lemma or a usable source, Question H is parked as a conjecture next to Conjecture L and the following review takes up (E).

Verification gate. No lemma is claimed beyond the reduction of Section 4. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the universal obstruction entry in full, the reduction of the previous entry, and after the review the decoder transfer and the functional bridge with its imported bound for more rows than holes. The standing reviewer confirmed the invariance of the barrier over \(\mathbb F_2\), the hitting count with its arithmetic and the total failure probability below one from \(v=8\), the constant images modulo \(E\) (the flat indicators lie in the ideal of \(E\) at degree \(t\), so hardness with \(E\) implies the hypothesis of the reduction with zero values; rank above accuracy causes no issue), the inconsistency on the residual board, the description of the compact base as avoidance axioms of total density \((n+1)/2\), the fairness of alternatives (B) and (E) after one rewording, and that neither the affine-clause transfer nor the one-affine-level theorem gives hardness of the base with linear equations. It reported six findings, all applied: Claim G was stated for arbitrary sources and has a candidate counterexample (now stated for compiled sources, with the union source recorded as the first falsification target); the original coordinates could be examined and satisfy the claim with recorded hardness (added, and the statement that the notebook has no tool qualified); a sentence read the toy counts as consistent with the hardness question although codimension \(0.7v\) was refuted at degree three (reworded); the twist needs \(p=2\); "pure" was missing once; one description of the published methods fitted only one of the two papers. Not checked by the reviewer: whether the union source admits some other choice of axioms.

The review states the line's general claim (image or value) for compiled sources, records a candidate counterexample for arbitrary sources, shows that the recorded universal obstruction source satisfies the claim in its original coordinates and under row-by-row twists with recorded hardness, and that for \(p=2\) a row-mixing twist escapes exactly if the PHP stays hard on a generic affine subspace of linear codimension; it selects that hardness question for at most two entries. 2026-09-18: The PHP under linear constraints: safe systems of rank up to a quarter of the holes keep the base hard by the recorded detector, the technique read in the literature stops at rank of order n, and three exact data points on the tolerated free dimension

Working proof of a corollary of a recorded detector (safe linear systems lose one degree per equation), with imported statements, a finite check of low power and a conjecture. Spin cycle 222. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Route check. Route item: the general step. First of at most two entries on Question H for parity constraints, selected by the route review: is the compact base hard on a generic affine subspace of the bit space, up to codimension \(0.7v\)? The claim index was searched for "affine subspace", "linear substitution", "parity constraint", "affine restriction", "Res(", "two-label", "coordinate edge", "safe" and "pivot"; no entry states hardness of the base with linear equations adjoined, but that search missed the recorded top-monomial detector, from which the reviewer derived the lemma of Section 2 in a few lines; the lemma is therefore recorded as a corollary. Estimate for the line as given by the review: about 10 percent. Stopping point as announced: the literature position and the scaling table; the corollary below came out of the literature reading.

1. What is published

Locators and hashes are in the source audit; the statements are imported as context, and only the definition of a safe system is used below, with its attribution.

Mikša and Nordström, A generalized method for proving polynomial calculus degree lower bounds (CCC 2015; arXiv 1505.01358v1 read). Theorem 4.9: if a bipartite graph \(G\) is an \((s,\delta)\)-boundary expander with left degree at most \(d\), then refuting the graph functional PHP over \(G\) (pigeon, hole and functionality axioms on the variables \(x_{u,v}\), \((u,v)\in E\)) in polynomial calculus requires degree greater than \(\delta s/(2d)\). Theorem 4.5 gives \(\delta s/2-\xi\) for the graph PHP with onto axioms under a matching condition, after Alekhnovich and Razborov. For the middle level of the review, value axioms that confine each row to its own flat, this would give at most \(n/(2d)\), since \(\delta s\le n\): at most \(n^{0.7}/2\) for flats of \(n^{0.3}\) labels, and only if the graph of flat neighbourhoods is a boundary expander, which has not been checked. The transfer from the bit encoding to the graph formula (restrictions \(x_{i,z}=0\) are derivable in degree two from a bit equation and the functional axioms) has not been written out either.

Byramji and Impagliazzo, Lower bounds for bit pigeonhole principles in bounded-depth resolution over parities (arXiv 2511.20023v1 read: abstract and proof overview). For the bit PHP with \(n+1\) pigeons, every Res(\(\oplus\)) refutation of depth \(N^{2-\varepsilon}\) has size \(\exp(\tilde\Omega(N^{\varepsilon}))\), \(N\) the number of variables; general Res(\(\oplus\)) is described as open beyond such depth. The overview and Section 3.1 recall from Efremenko, Garlík and Itsykson (not retrieved) the notions used to handle linear systems over the label bits: a system of rank \(r\) is safe if it can be rewritten as fixing \(r\) variables from distinct blocks as affine functions of the other variables, equivalently (their Theorem 3.1) if its coefficient matrix has \(r\) independent columns no two of which belong to the same block; then, as long as \(r\) is not too large, the \(r\) pigeons can be sent to \(2r\) holes without collisions, each to a pair of holes differing in one bit. Every system \(\Phi\) has a closure \(\mathrm{Cl}(\Phi)\), a set of blocks, with \(\Phi\) equivalent to a part on the closure, of rank at least \(|\mathrm{Cl}(\Phi)|\), and a part that is safe once the closure is fixed. Their probability estimates for safe systems are stated for rank \(r\le cn\) with a small constant \(c\). So the technique, as far as this one overview shows it, handles linear systems of rank of order \(n\), the number of holes, and Question H at linear codimension asks for rank of order \(v=(n+1)\ell\); a system of rank above the number of blocks cannot be safe.

2. Safe systems keep the base hard: a corollary of the recorded detector

Let \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), \(m=n+1\), let \(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}\) be the functional unary base and \(\mathcal Q=\mathcal Q_{n,2}\) the compact base, with the affine decoder \(\tau\). A linear system \(\Phi\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) in the label bits is safe of rank \(a\) (definition of Efremenko, Garlík and Itsykson, as quoted above) if it is equivalent to equations \(L_i=0\), \(L_i=b_{i,j_i}+w_i+c_i\), \(i\in I\), with \(|I|=a\) distinct rows, one pivot position \(j_i\) in each, constants \(c_i\), and linear forms \(w_i\) in the non-pivot variables.

Corollary SL. Let \(\Phi\) be safe of rank \(a\) with \(4(a-1)<n\). Then every polynomial-calculus refutation of \(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}\cup\tau\Phi\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), and hence every refutation of \(\mathcal Q\cup\Phi\), has degree at least \(n/2-a+1\). The right-hand sides \(c_i\) are arbitrary.

Proof (the reviewer's derivation, checked against the records). Let \(R=\prod_{i\in I}(1+L_i)\), the indicator of the solution space, of degree \(a\). Its monomial \(\prod_ib_{i,j_i}\) has coefficient one, because no \(w_{i'}\) contains a pivot, and it uses one bit in each of \(a\) distinct rows. Suppose \(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}\cup\tau\Phi\) has a refutation of degree \(B\); a refutation of \(\mathcal Q\cup\Phi\) gives one by the decoder transfer, since the images \(\tau L_i\) are axioms of the target. Multiply every line by the weight \(\tau R\), using the recorded weighted replay. An old axiom \(g\) costs \(\deg g+a\). For the axiom \(\lambda=\tau L_i\) the weighted line is \(\tau\bigl(\prod_{i'\ne i}(1+L_{i'})\bigr)(\lambda^2+\lambda)\), and in characteristic two \(\lambda^2+\lambda=\sum_e(x_e^2-x_e)\) over the cells of \(\lambda\), a Boolean consequence of degree two; the cost is \(a+1\le B+a\). So \(\tau R\in\mathcal C_{B+a}(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun})\). By the recorded top-monomial detector, with \(u=a\) and ceiling \(B+a\), this is impossible when \(4(a-1)<n\) and \(n\ge2(B+a)-1\). Hence \(2(B+a)-1>n\), that is \(B\ge n/2-a+1\). \(\square\)

This is the weight step of the one-affine-level theorem with the weight equal to the indicator of the subspace, which is affordable exactly because the rank is small. In the language of the literature: \(\Phi\) is safe if and only if the top-degree part of that indicator contains a monomial with one bit in each of \(a\) rows (the coefficient of a squarefree monomial of degree \(a\) is the corresponding minor, which is the criterion of their Theorem 3.1), and the detector's disjoint coordinate edges are the pairs of holes of Efremenko, Garlík and Itsykson.

A direct restriction shows what is left of the PHP. Choose labels \(h_i\), \(i\in I\), one after another so that the \(2a\) labels \(h_i^0,h_i^1\) (the two ends of the edge through \(h_i\) in direction \(j_i\), with pivot bit 0 and 1) are distinct, which is possible because before the \(i\)-th choice at most \(2(i-1)<n/2\) of the \(n/2\) edges of direction \(j_i\) are blocked. In unary variables send \(x_{i,h_i^1}\mapsto u_i\), \(x_{i,h_i^0}\mapsto1+u_i\) and the other cells of row \(i\) to zero, where \(u_i\) is \(\tau(w_i+c_i)\) with \(\tau(b_{i',t})\) replaced by the constant \((h_{i'})_t\) for every \(i'\in I\), the row \(i\) itself included, at \(t\ne j_{i'}\) (both ends of an edge agree there, so this is what the map gives), and with the reserved cells of the other rows set to zero; and send \(x_{k,h}\mapsto0\) for every row \(k\notin I\) and every reserved label \(h\). The row axioms of \(I\) go to zero, Booleanity and same-row products of \(I\) to \(u_i^2+u_i\) of degree two, the column exclusions that involve a row of \(I\) to zero by disjointness of the pairs, and \(\tau L_i\) to zero; what remains is exactly the functional PHP with \(n+1-a\) rows and \(n-2a\) holes, at ceiling \(\max(B,2)\). The imported bound for more rows than holes gives the same \(n/2-a+1\). (The reviewer checked every image of this map; the first draft carried out the same restriction in the bit variables, which needed the label-decoder certificate and an extra hypothesis \(n-2a>2\ell\) that the unary form does not need.)

Several pivots in one row. If the reduced system has pivot sets \(T_i\) in \(u\) rows, \(a=\sum_i|T_i|\), the indicator has the squarefree top monomial \(\prod_i\prod_{t\in T_i}b_{it}\), and the recorded multi-axis cube detector applies with ceiling \(B+a\) whenever pairwise disjoint coordinate cubes with free axes \(T_i\) exist (packing): with \(F=\sum_i2^{|T_i|}\) reserved labels, every refutation has degree at least \((n-F)/2-(a-u)+1\) (the lemma's other hypotheses, \(m\ge B+a\) and a residual label, are harmless: if they fail, \(B\) already exceeds the stated bound or the bound is at most one). Since \(2^p\ge2p\), one has \(F\ge2a\), so \(F\le n/2\) gives \(a\le n/4\) exactly, and a nonvoid bound needs \(a<n/2\) in any case: several pivots in a row never buy more rank than single pivots.

Generic systems. A uniformly random system of \(a\le n/4\) equations, with any right-hand sides, is safe except with probability at most \(a\,2^{-(m-a+1)\ell}\): reduce the equations one at a time; the reduced \(r\)-th equation is uniform on the non-pivot coordinates, so it has a nonzero coefficient in a block not used before except with probability \(2^{-(m-r+1)\ell}\); back-substitution then removes the pivots from the forms \(w_i\) and keeps the pivots. So Question H for parity constraints has the answer yes for up to \(n/4\) generic equations, with degree \(n/2-a+1\).

What the corollary is worth. Its loss, one degree per equation, equals that of the recorded case split; the gain over the case split is that it holds for every right-hand side and every safe system, not for some sign vector. It does not reach what the value method needs: the row-mixing twist of the review needs rank about \(0.7v\), far above the number of blocks, where no system is safe, the cubes cannot be packed, and any bound of the form \(n/2-a\) is void.

3. Scaling of the tolerated free dimension

Design. The tool of the previous finite check, parity constraints in the affine family (forms linear in the label bits, which correspond to linear equations on the compact base through the decoder), now also on sixteen holes at degree two: 17 rows, \(v=68\), 32913 monomials, refutation degree at least nine, three seeds, with the bijective and labelings controls. Sixteen holes at degree three (about 2.3 million monomials) is out of reach of the tool.

Reading. The columns for the controls give \(a^*\). The free dimension \(v-a^*\) at which the PHP with random parity constraints first becomes refutable is 6 on eight holes and 7 on sixteen at degree two, although \(v\) grows from 27 to 68, and 12 at degree three on eight holes. Two points at degree two cannot separate the hypothesis stated with the experiment, that \(v-a^*\) does not depend on \(v\), from the prediction of the conjecture below, that it is proportional to \(\ell\) at a fixed degree (\(6/3=2.0\) against \(7/4=1.75\)); the two are in tension and the data do not decide. At degree two nothing in the table is specific to the PHP: the bijective control tips at the same free dimension (5 to 6 of its 24 bits against 6, and 7 of 64 against 7), far beyond its semantic threshold \(\log_2N!\) (15.3 and 44.3), so both boards are refuted at degree two only when about two rows' worth of bits remain. Only the degree-three row shows the PHP tipping (15) at or below the control's semantic threshold. The labelings tip at about their semantic count \(v\). Corollary SL accounts for a small part of the tolerance: on sixteen holes it excludes refutations through degree four at \(a=4\) (and through degree seven at \(a=1\)), while 60 equations were tolerated at degree two.

Conjecture H1. For a uniformly random affine subspace \(W\) of the bit space, the polynomial-calculus refutation degree of \(\mathcal F_n^{\rm fun}\) with the decoded equations of \(W\) adjoined is at least \(c\min(n,\dim W/\ell)\) for a constant \(c>0\), with high probability. It is stated on the unary board, where the experiment lives; the compact form follows by the decoder. An upper bound of this order is elementary: for a fixed set of \(r\) rows with \(r\ell\ge\dim W+t\) the projection of \(W\) to the labels of those rows is injective except with probability \(2^{-t}\); then the sum of the label indicators \(X_y\) of these rows is one at degree \(r\), an indicator outside the image is refuted at degree \(r+1\), and one inside the image determines all labels and meets a collision at degree \(r+2\). So the refutation degree is at most \(\lceil\dim W/\ell\rceil+O(1)\) in unary degree, and at most \(n/2+1\) in any case, so that \(c\le1/2\). For the row-mixing twist of the review, \(\dim W=0.3v\) and the conjecture gives degree linear in \(n\).

4. What remains

Between rank \(n/4\), where the pair-of-holes argument stops, and rank \(0.7v\). For rank above the number of blocks every block loses several bits; with \(p\) pivots in a block its pigeon needs a reserved cube of \(2^p\) holes (Section 2, the multi-axis detector), which is affordable only for few blocks or small \(p\), so the recorded detectors cannot reach linear codimension, and the closure of a generic system of rank above \(m\) is everything. The second entry attempts a design supported on \(W\) that does not reserve holes: the local structure is favourable, since on a generic \(W\) of dimension \(0.3v\) every set of \(r\) rows with \(r\le0.3m-(\log_2\binom mr+t)/\ell\) has jointly free labels, except with probability \(2^{-t}\), so the system looks locally like an unrestricted PHP, and the global information is carried by linear relations of large row support.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the decoder transfer, the label-decoder certificate, the functional bridge with its imported bound, and after the review the top-monomial detector, the multi-axis cube detector and the weighted replay. The standing reviewer found no error in the first draft's direct proof (reserved pairs and the four-cycle claim, every axiom image, the substitution at ceiling \(\max(B,\ell+1)\), the decoding step, the arithmetic, generic safety) and reported six groups of findings, all applied. The main one: the lemma follows in a few lines from the recorded top-monomial detector by weighted replay, under fewer hypotheses, so it is recorded as a corollary with the reviewer's derivation, which was checked here against the detector's statement and range; the direct restriction is kept in the unary form that the reviewer verified image by image, and the hypothesis \(n-2a>2\ell\) of the draft, an artifact of working in bit variables that made the statement empty on eight holes, is gone. Further: the claimed elementary upper bound in Conjecture H1 was wrong as written (free coordinates of a generic subspace need slack; corrected with the reviewer's degree count) and the conjecture is now stated on the unary board; the reading of the table overstated what two points show and ignored that the bijective control tips at the same free dimension at degree two; the sentence on the graph PHP bound overstated its reach (at most \(n/(2d)\), expansion unchecked); smaller corrections to the imported statements. In the previous entry's gate the reviewer confirmed that the one-affine-level theorem as stated gives no hardness with linear equations; that remains true of the theorem as stated and at linear codimension, while its weight step does give the small-rank corollary above. A second pass confirmed the corollary's proof, the multi-pivot bound and the images of the restriction, and found four wording defects, all fixed: the definition of \(u_i\) left the cells of row \(i\) itself unsubstituted; the loss was called the worst-case rate without a matching upper bound; the reason given for the rank limit of several pivots was wrong (\(F\ge2a\), not \(F\ge2u\)); two hypotheses of the cube detector were omitted. Unused hypotheses named by the reviewer: \(m=n+1\) (the restriction needs only more rows than holes after the reservation); \(\ell\ge2\) is used by the decoder and the detector's statement only. Not checked: the paper of Efremenko, Garlík and Itsykson (not retrieved), expansion of flat-neighbourhood graphs, safety of the random systems used in the runs, and the ECCC report number in the source audit (taken from the ECCC page, absent from the arXiv text); the reviewer compared the sixteen-hole records with the table but did not rerun them.

Main-route assessment. General step: unchanged. Question H for parity constraints is settled for safe systems of rank up to \(n/4\), by a corollary of a recorded detector with the loss of one degree per equation, the same rate as the recorded case split (whether a safe system can really lose that much is open); the literature read stops at rank of order \(n\) as well. What the value method needs, rank of order \(v\) on a generic subspace, is now Conjecture H1, with three exact data points that do not decide its scaling. Estimate for the line as in the review: about 10 percent.

Process assessment. The literature retrieval was productive within the hour (a definition that turns the question into a statement the recorded detectors answer), but the lemma was again drafted in full before anyone checked whether the record already gives it, the third restatement caught by the reviewer in one day; CLAUDE.md now requires sending the one-paragraph statement of a new lemma to the standing reviewer with that single question before drafting the proof.

2026-09-18: The PHP on a generic subspace in residual coordinates: the linear equations are eliminated exactly, exact bit degrees stay within two of the generic dimension count for dimensions up to seventeen on sixteen and thirty-two holes, no design was found, and Conjecture H1 is parked untested

Working proof of a composition lemma (exact elimination of linear equations over \(\mathbb F_2\)) and a finite check; the proof attempt at Conjecture H1 failed and the conjecture is parked. Spin cycle 223. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Route check. Route item: the general step. Second and last entry on Question H for parity constraints under the bound of the route review: one proof attempt at Conjecture H1 beyond Corollary SL, preceded by the planned attempt to break it, which turned out to be vacuous for the conjecture on every board within reach (Section 3). Read in full first, as the plan required: the signed two-point construction, the row-trade lemma, the row-linear quotient injection and the cube detector. The claim index was searched for "design", "moment extension", "locally consistent", "Hilbert", "Koszul", "regular sequence", "invertible affine", "change of coordinates" and "affine substitution". Relevant hits: the recorded design-extension theorems (all on the unrestricted functional base), the occupancy-probe theorem (linear equations in the unary variables that empty all holes but one; they are not linear in the label bits and do not bear on a subspace of the bit space), and the ingredients of the lemma of Section 1. Before drafting, the statement of that lemma was sent to the standing reviewer with the single question whether the record implies it; the answer (not recorded, but a composition of four recorded results) shaped the statement. Estimate for the line as given by the review: about 10 percent. Stopping point: a lemma with its degree ledger or the obstruction, then the parking decision.

1. The linear equations are eliminated exactly

Setup: \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), rows \(i\in[n+1]\), label bits \(b_{i,t}\), \(v=(n+1)\ell\), the compact base \(\mathcal Q_{n,2}\) (Booleanity and the collision polynomials \(E_{ii'}=\prod_t(1+b_{i,t}+b_{i',t})\)), polynomial calculus over \(\mathbb F_2\) with the recorded degree convention (a multiplication is charged the degree of its predecessor plus one). Let \(\Lambda=\{\Lambda_1,\dots,\Lambda_a\}\) be affine forms in the bits, linearly independent with the constant one outside their span, \(W\) their common zero flat, \(k=v-a\), and \(P:\mathbb F_2^k\to\mathbb F_2^v\) an injective affine map with image \(W\). Write \(\mathcal S_P=\{E_{ii'}\circ P:i<i'\}\cup{\rm BOOL}_y\), a system in the variables \(y_1,\dots,y_k\); its axiom \(E_{ii'}\circ P\) is the product of the \(\ell\) affine forms \(1+(P_{i,t}+P_{i',t})(y)\), the indicator of the collision flat \(\{y:P_i(y)=P_{i'}(y)\}\), of codimension \(e_{ii'}\le\ell\) in \(\mathbb F_2^k\) when it is not empty.

Lemma R (residual coordinates). Write \(D_b\) for the refutation degree of \(\mathcal Q_{n,2}\cup\Lambda\) and \(D_y\) for that of \(\mathcal S_P\). Then \(D_y\le D_b\le\max(D_y,\ell)\), and \(D_b\ge\ell\); hence \(D_b=\max(D_y,\ell)\). The same holds with the multilinear quotient ring \(\mathbb F_2[y]/(y_j^2+y_j)\) in place of ordinary polynomial calculus with \({\rm BOOL}_y\).

Proof. The coordinate-completion lemma gives an affine equivalence \(E\) of \(\mathbb F_2^v\) with \((E(b))_{e(c)}=\Lambda_c(b)\) and a parametrization \(P_0=E^{-1}\circ z\) of \(W\) by the free coordinates; any other injective affine \(P\) with image \(W\) is \(P_0\circ A\) for an affine bijection \(A\) of \(\mathbb F_2^k\), so \(P\) has an affine left inverse \(\lambda:\mathbb F_2^v\to\mathbb F_2^k\) (take \(A^{-1}\) of the free coordinates of \(E\)), and \(P(\lambda(b))=b+\sum_c\Lambda_c(b)\,h_c\) for fixed vectors \(h_c\in\mathbb F_2^v\): in the coordinates of \(E\) the map \(P\circ\lambda\) sets the designated coordinates to zero and keeps the others.

First inequality: apply the substitution replay with \(T=1\), \(w=1\) to \(b\mapsto P(y)\), at the ceiling \(D_b\). A Boolean axiom \(b^2+b\) goes to \(g^2+g\) for an affine form \(g=\sum_jg_jy_j+g_0\), which over \(\mathbb F_2\) equals \(\sum_jg_j(y_j^2+y_j)\), a combination of Boolean axioms of degree two (the cross terms cancel in characteristic two; this is the certificate used in the decoder). Each \(\Lambda_c\circ P\) is an affine polynomial that vanishes on all of \(\mathbb F_2^k\), hence the zero polynomial. Each \(E_{ii'}\) goes to an axiom of \(\mathcal S_P\). So every axiom image is derived within the ceiling and \(\mathcal S_P\) is refuted within \(D_b\).

Second inequality: apply the replay to \(y\mapsto\lambda(b)\) at the ceiling \(\max(D_y,\ell)\). Boolean axioms go to combinations of Boolean axioms as before. The axiom \(E_{ii'}\circ P\) goes to \(E_{ii'}(b+\sum_c\Lambda_ch_c)=\prod_t\bigl(1+b_{i,t}+b_{i',t}+\sum_c\eta_{t,c}\Lambda_c\bigr)\) with \(\eta_{t,c}=(h_c)_{i,t}+(h_c)_{i',t}\). Expanding the product, every term other than \(E_{ii'}(b)\) contains a factor \(\sum_c\eta_{t,c}\Lambda_c\), so the image is \(E_{ii'}+\sum_c\Lambda_cq_c\) with \(\deg q_c\le\ell-1\), derived from the axioms \(E_{ii'}\) and \(\Lambda_c\) within degree \(\ell\). This costs \(\ell\) even when the collision flat has smaller codimension, which is why the ceiling is \(\max(D_y,\ell)\).

Lower bound \(\ell\): \(\Lambda\cup{\rm BOOL}_b\) has the common zeros \(W\ne\varnothing\), so a refutation uses a collision axiom, a line of degree \(\ell\). Quotient ring: reduce an ordinary proof line by line as in the functional bridge (an ordinary multiplication with nonzero predecessor has \(\deg P+1\le D\), so the quotient inference has the same charge); conversely a quotient inference \(P\mapsto\overline{y_jP}\) is the ordinary product \(y_jP\) of degree \(\deg P+1\) minus multiples \(m'(y_j^2+y_j)\) of the same degree. The quotient-ring axiom is the multilinear reduction of \(E_{ii'}\circ P\), of degree \(e_{ii'}\), while the ordinary product can have degree up to \(\ell\) when its forms are dependent; passing between the two costs at most \(\ell\), inside the ceiling, so \(D_y^{\rm quot}\le D_y^{\rm ord}\le D_b\le\max(D_y^{\rm quot},\ell)\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses. The proof uses \(\mathbb F_2\) (affine forms are Boolean, cross terms cancel) and \(W\ne\varnothing\); \(\ell\ge2\) only to keep the Boolean images within the ceiling. It does not use \(m=n+1\), \(n=2^\ell\), genericity of \(W\), or the product form of the collision polynomials: the same argument gives \(D_y\le D_b\le\max(D_y,\ell)\) for any system over \(\mathbb F_2\) with Boolean axioms whose other axioms \(f\) have degree at most \(\ell\), since \(f(b+\sum_c\Lambda_ch_c)-f(b)\in\sum_c\Lambda_c\mathcal P_{\le\deg f-1}\). It is stated for the compact base because that is where it is used.

So the PHP on \(W\) is, exactly and in bit degree, the statement that the \(\binom{n+1}2\) collision flats of the \(n+1\) affine maps \(P_i:\mathbb F_2^k\to\mathbb F_2^\ell\) cover \(\mathbb F_2^k\). For a uniform \(W\) the maps are generic, the flats have codimension \(\ell\) once \(k\ge\ell\) (up to rank defects of probability about \(2^{\ell-k}\) each), and their total density \((n+1)/2\) is far below the covering threshold \(k\ln2\) of independent flats as soon as \(k\) exceeds a constant times \(n\): the covering is a pigeonhole fact, not a density fact. Through the decoder the bit degree is at least the unary degree, so Conjecture H1 implies \(D_b\ge c\min(n,k/\ell)\); this bit form is what the value method of Claim G uses. No upper relation between the two degrees is recorded, so the bit-degree counts below are not comparable with the unary tipping counts of the two previous entries.

Remark (dual picture, Nullstellensatz only, not used below). A functional on polynomials of degree at most \(d\) in \(y\) is a sum of evaluations over a set \(S\subseteq\mathbb F_2^k\). It is normalized exactly if \(|S|\) is odd, and it annihilates the multiples of the indicator of a collision flat \(A\) of codimension \(e_A\) through degree \(d\) exactly if every subflat of \(A\) of codimension at most \(d-e_A\) in \(A\) contains an even number of points of \(S\) (equivalently the restriction of the indicator of \(S\) to \(A\) has degree at most \(k-d-1\)). So a Nullstellensatz design of degree \(d\) for the PHP on \(W\) is an odd set that meets all these subflats evenly. No equality of polynomial-calculus and Nullstellensatz closures is recorded for this system (the recorded \(\mathcal C_B=\mathcal I_B\) concerns the unrestricted functional base), so such a set would not by itself exclude a polynomial-calculus refutation.

2. The proof attempt: why the recorded constructions do not extend

The plan was a design of the compact base that annihilates the multiples of the equations of \(W\), built from the recorded signed constructions and the local freedom of a generic subspace. It did not produce a design. What stops it, stated as far as it is proved:

(a) Weights supported on \(W\). Corollary SL uses the functional \(\mu(\tau R\,\cdot)\) with \(R\) the indicator of \(W\). A nonzero function on \(\mathbb F_2^v\) that vanishes outside \(W\) has multilinear degree at least \(a\): in the coordinates of \(E\) it is \(\prod_c(1+u_c)\,g(y)\) with \(g\ne0\), whose multilinear form contains \(u_1\cdots u_a\) times the top monomial of \(g\), and an invertible affine map over \(\mathbb F_2\) preserves multilinear degree (recorded remark). A polynomial of unary degree \(r\) is, on the labelings, a sum of functions of at most \(r\) labels each, of bit degree at most \(r\ell\). So a weight that vanishes outside \(W\) as a function on the labelings has unary degree at least \(a/\ell\), which for \(a=0.7v\) is \(0.7(n+1)\), above the barrier \(n/2+1\) of the base. This excludes pointwise weights at linear codimension. It does not exclude a weight \(f\) with \(f\Lambda_c\) in the old ideal only through the working degree; no such weight was found. For a single partial-matching monomial \(f=X_T\) with \(|T|<n/2\), \(B\ge|T|+1\) and \(n-|T|\ge2B-1\) the condition holds for all \(c\) exactly if every \(\Lambda_c\) has all its bits in the rows of \(T\) and vanishes at the labels of \(T\) (the restriction that sets \(T\) maps \(X_T\tau\Lambda_c\) to a polynomial of degree at most one on the residual board, the recorded \(\mathcal I_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le1}=\mathcal I_1\) makes it a combination of row axioms, and a nonzero linear functional of the label is not constant on the more than \(n/2\) free holes); this forces \(a\le|T|\ell\) and fails for a generic \(W\).

(b) Product sets. For a uniform \(W\) of codimension \(a\) with direction space \(W_0\), a fixed nonzero vector lies in \(W_0\) with probability \((2^k-1)/(2^v-1)<2^{-a}\). Hence, except with probability \(\binom{n+1}r2^{r\ell-a}\), any two points of \(W\) differ in more than \(r\) rows; for \(a=0.7v\) this holds with \(r=\lfloor0.7(n+1)\rfloor-\lceil(n+1+t)/\ell\rceil\) except with probability \(2^{-t}\). In particular \(W\) contains no product of label sets with more than one point once \(a\ge\ell+\log_2(n+1)+t\). The recorded designs (signed two-point, cube, row trades \(\bigotimes_i(\mathbf e_{a_i}-\mathbf e_{b_i})\)) are tensor products over rows: their marginal identities cancel row by row inside a product of label sets. The one recorded device that is not of product form, the affine restriction behind Corollary SL, reserves a pair of holes for each equation and so stops at rank of order \(n\). The local freedom of \(W\) is of another kind: the projection of \(W\) to fewer than about \(k/\ell\) rows is onto, but the \(2^r\) labelings in the support of a trade on \(r\) rows have different completions in \(W\), so the cancellation of one row's two labels changes all other rows. No replacement for the row-by-row cancellation was found.

(c) Locality. The published expander method read in the previous entry needs axioms whose variables lie in few groups. A generic equation of \(W\) has variables in every row, and in residual coordinates every collision axiom involves \(\ell\) forms that are generic in all \(k\) coordinates; no choice of coordinates was found that makes the system local, and nothing is proved about this.

So the obstruction is the type of the problem: a degree bound for a dense system of flat-avoidance axioms without product structure and without locality, for which neither the recorded detectors nor the methods read so far give a handle. This is the same wall as the generic-flats form of Question H.

3. Exact bit degrees in residual coordinates, and why they do not test the conjecture

Design. By Lemma R the refutation bit degree of the compact base with the equations of \(W\) can be computed in the \(k\) residual coordinates, where a closure needs \(\sum_{j\le d}\binom kj\) monomials instead of the \(10^4\) to \(10^6\) monomials of the unary board. The new tool subspace_flat_cover_closure.cpp draws a uniform \(v\times60\) matrix \(G\) of full column rank and a uniform \(c\), takes the nested subspaces \(W_k=c+\) span of the first \(k\) columns (refutability at a fixed degree is monotone along the chain, since \(W_k\subseteq W_{k+1}\)), and computes the degree-\(d\) closure of the multilinear collision axioms in \(\mathbb F_2[y]/(y_j^2+y_j)\) by an echelon basis with degree-major pivots, multiplying every basis element of degree below \(d\) by every variable until nothing new appears or 1 is derived. For each seed it scans \(k\) upward and stops at the first \(k\) that is not refuted; only \(d\ge\ell\) is run, as Lemma R requires. Checks of the tool: on four holes with \(k=v=10\) the identity parametrization and a random one both refute at degree three and not at degree two, as Lemma R and the recorded unary bound \(n/2+1=3\) require; a brute-force count of the points of \(W_k\) with pairwise distinct labels gives the semantic status of the control runs; the standing reviewer rebuilt the tool and reproduced five tipping points and the full eight-hole base (refuted at degree five, not at four).

Yardstick. The generic count for \(m\) axioms of degree \(\ell\) in \(k\) Boolean variables is the first \(d\) at which the coefficient of \(t^d\) in \((1+t)^k(1+t^\ell)^{-m}\) is not positive: the dimension count that results when the multiples of the axioms are as independent as the relation \(f^2=0\) of the graded Boolean ring allows. In the literature on Boolean polynomial systems this is the degree of regularity of a semi-regular system; no source was read for it in this cycle and nothing is imported, it serves only as a yardstick. Computed values for sixteen holes (\(m=136\)): the count is 7, 11, 16, 26, 42, 54 at \(k=20,40,60,100,160,200\), so \(k/d\) stays below four. The column "count" is the largest \(k\) for which the count is at most \(d\).

Reading. (1) What the computation can test. The bit form of Conjecture H1, \(D_b\ge c\min(n,k/\ell)\) with \(c\le1/2\), exceeds the unconditional bound \(D_b\ge\ell\) of Lemma R only for \(k>2\ell^2\), that is \(k\ge33\) on sixteen holes and \(k\ge51\) on thirty-two, far beyond the dimensions a closure can reach; and by monotonicity along the chain the tipping points below give \(D_b(W_k)\ge7\) for every \(k\ge17\) on the sixteen-hole chains, which is at least \(\tfrac12\min(n,k/\ell)\) for every \(k\le56\). On eight holes the conjectured bound is at most 4 and the observed degree is the largest possible from \(k=12\) on (from \(k=11\) for seeds 2 and 3). So the conjecture could not have failed on any board within reach: the planned attempt to break it was vacuous, and the conjecture is recorded as not tested. What the data do test is a stronger hypothesis, that \(D_b(W_k)\) stays within two of the generic count until it meets the degree of the full base. (2) Sixteen and thirty-two holes. Every completed scan gives the same largest refuted dimension for the three seeds, and it is the count or one to two below it: 9, 12, 16 against 9, 13, 18, and 11, 15 against 11, 16. The system is never easier than the count in these scans. The degree-seven scans with seed 1 were stopped by hand shortly before their time limit while still refuting (through \(k=17\) on sixteen holes and \(k=18\) on thirty-two; counts 22 and 20); the other seeds were not run at that degree. (3) The control. The bijective control differs from the PHP by one row (120 against 136, and 496 against 528, collision flats of the same kind), so it controls for the pigeonhole principle, not for the collision structure. On these subspaces it is unsatisfiable as well (a brute-force count finds no point with distinct labels for \(k\le18\) on sixteen and thirty-two holes; the first appears at \(k=19\) or 20 on sixteen) and tips at the same dimension or one below, in step with its own count: the pigeonhole principle plays no visible role in the range reached. Independent random flats were not run; the count is the only proxy for them. (4) Four and eight holes, where the structure shows. On eight holes degrees three and four stay within one of the count (7 and 10 to 11 against 7 and 11), and the control becomes satisfiable at \(k=10,7,8\) for the three seeds, which is where its scans stop. The full base is refuted at degree five in the original coordinates, against a count of 15 at that degree, and on four holes at degree three against a count of 9: the full base beats the generic count. With the recorded lower bound \(n/2+1\) for the compact base its bit degree is exactly three on four holes and exactly five on eight, and by monotonicity every subspace is refuted at that degree. On eight holes \(D_b(W_k)\) is at least the minimum of the count and five and within one of it (at \(k=11\) seeds 2 and 3 need degree five where the count gives four). (5) Summary. No refutation below the generic count appeared for \(k\le17\). If the full base has bit degree of order \(n\), as on four and eight holes, and the stronger hypothesis held throughout, the degree at \(k=0.3v\) would be the smaller of about \(0.08\,n\ell\) (the count, with the computed ratio) and the degree of the full base; nothing computed here reaches that regime. Eight holes is already a test of the stronger hypothesis where only the pigeonhole principle makes the system unsatisfiable (item 4); the next such test beyond eight holes: sixteen holes, degree seven, \(k=19\) to 22, with 94,184 to 280,600 monomials, that is dense closures of 1.1 to 9.8 GB and, at the cubic growth observed (six minutes at 41,226 monomials), about one hour at \(k=19\) and about thirty at \(k=22\) with the present tool. The counts are in bit degree and are not comparable with the unary tipping counts of the two previous entries.

4. Decision and what remains

The bound set by the review is reached: two entries produced Corollary SL (rank up to \(n/4\), a corollary of a recorded detector), the literature position (rank of order \(n\)), Lemma R, two finite checks that do not test the conjecture, and neither a lemma at rank of order \(v\) nor a usable published tool. Conjecture H1 is therefore parked next to Conjecture L, with this record: proved for safe systems of rank up to \(n/4\) at one degree per equation; not tested: on every board within reach its bit form is implied by \(D_b\ge\ell\) and the computed tipping points; the stronger hypothesis that the bit degree stays within two of the generic count up to the degree of the full base holds for \(k\le17\) on sixteen and thirty-two holes and says nothing yet about the regime the conjecture is needed for (\(k\) a constant fraction of \(v\) on large boards); the recorded proof methods fail for the reasons of Section 2. The following entry is a route review that takes up alternative (E) of the last review. Open besides the conjecture itself: whether the full compact base has bit degree of order \(n\) or of order \(n\ell\) (on four and eight holes it is exactly the recorded unary bound \(n/2+1\), three and five), and whether a weight in the weaker sense of Section 2(a) exists.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the four items named in the route check, the coordinate-completion lemma, the substitution replay, the Boolean reduction of the functional bridge, the affine remark of the last review, and the statement of Conjecture H1 with its upper bound. No rule, tree or encoding changed; the tool was checked as described in Section 3. Before drafting, the standing reviewer answered that Lemma R is not recorded and is a composition of four recorded results, and that the odd-set dual is not recorded; both were written accordingly. On the full draft the reviewer confirmed Lemma R (the left inverse, the identity \(P\lambda(b)=b+\sum_c\Lambda_ch_c\), the expansion with \(\deg q_c\le\ell-1\), the quotient-ring simulation), the closing paragraph of Section 1, the dual remark, the degree bound of 2(a), the arithmetic of 2(b), every table cell against the records and the count column against the series, monotonicity along the chain, and the tool's code; it rebuilt the tool and reproduced five tipping points, the four-hole check, the brute-force counts and the full eight-hole base (refuted at degree five, not at four). It reported seven findings, all applied. (1) The computation could not have broken Conjecture H1 in any range reached, because the conjectured bound is there below the unconditional bound \(\ell\); the draft said the attempt to break the conjecture had failed and called the conjecture supported. The section, the reading, the decision and the assessments now say that the conjecture is not tested and name the stronger hypothesis that the data do test. (2) The claim that a single monomial weight is impossible was false as worded (an equation system supported in the rows of \(T\) is a counterexample); it is replaced by the exact condition with its board-size hypothesis. (3) The sentence that every recorded restriction lives on a product of label sets contradicted the affine restriction behind Corollary SL; reworded. (4) The asymptotic formula for the generic count was wrong (the computed ratio \(k/d\) stays below four); replaced by computed values, and the statement about \(k=0.3v\) made conditional. (5) The control differs by one row and controls only for the pigeonhole principle; the eight-hole degree is within one of the minimum, not equal to it; the full base beats the count on four and eight holes; the title now names the range. (6) A one-sentence gap in the quotient-ring form of Lemma R (the multilinear axiom can have smaller degree than the ordinary product) is closed, the unused hypotheses are named, and the recorded lower bound for the compact base is cited. (7) Wording on the runs that were stopped, and the results README. A second pass on the changed passages found six small defects, all fixed (an inequality that is an equality at \(k=56\), the eight-hole bound 4 instead of 4.5, the hypothesis \(B\ge|T|+1\) in 2(a), eight holes as an existing test in the pigeonhole regime, the description of the stopped runs, and a premature statement about CLAUDE.md). Not checked by the reviewer: the occupancy-probe description beyond its index row, full scans beyond the reproduced cells, the degree-seven runs, the descriptive sentences on recorded designs beyond the counterexample of finding (3), that Claim G uses the bit form, any literature on the generic count, and a direct numerical test of Lemma R in bit coordinates (no tool exists for that side).

Main-route assessment. General step: unchanged. The hardness part of Claim G for generic linear value axioms remains a conjecture; this entry makes it exactly computable (Lemma R), finds that no board within reach can test it, records a stronger count-tracking hypothesis that holds in the small range computed, and records why the recorded detectors cannot prove it. Estimate for the line as in the review: about 10 percent; the review that follows decides whether the line continues.

Process assessment. The pre-draft question to the standing reviewer worked as intended and Lemma R was written as a composition from the start, but the computation was designed, coded and run before anyone compared the bound that Conjecture H1 predicts at the reachable dimensions with the trivial bound \(\ell\), a one-line count that would have shown at once that no outcome could contradict the conjecture; the reviewer found it after the fact. The existing rule on nonvacuous parameters was applied to the tool and not to the statement under test; the framework commit that follows this entry makes that comparison explicit for computations designed inside a cycle.

2026-09-18: Route review of the value method: both of its hardness inputs and the union source meet one wall, the PHP on a generic subspace of linear codimension; the published extension-variable methods do not apply; parity decision trees bound the bit degree, which is of order \(n\) for the full base; one bounded step on the weakest form of the wall
