Route check. Route item: the general step. This review was fixed by the bound of the last review: two entries on Question H for parity constraints ended with Conjecture H1 parked untested (decision), and the fallback (E), the published methods for polynomial calculus with extension variables, was to be taken up. The claim index was searched for "lift", "selector", "size", "quadratic degree", "unary affine", "multiscale" and "truth-table"; nothing on size-based measures is recorded, and the hits on unary affine families are used in Section 2. Read for this review: the proof outline and Section 5 of Dahiya, Mahajan and Mouli in full (the restriction lemma, the cleanup, Theorem 5.5), the recorded literature section, the alternatives of the three earlier reviews, the middle-rank frontier, and the label-parent normalization with the multiscale family.

1. What the line produced since the last review

Two entries: Corollary SL (safe linear systems of rank up to \(n/4\) keep the base hard, a corollary of a recorded detector), the literature position (the technique for linear systems on the bit PHP stops at rank of order \(n\)), Lemma R (the equations of a subspace are eliminated exactly over \(\mathbb F_2\)), a finite check that cannot test the conjecture at reachable sizes, and the reasons why weights and tensor-product designs do not reach linear codimension (attempt). Nothing moved in the general step.

2. The general claim, and what the main goal needs from it

The line's claim is Claim G (image or value): for a compiled source there are value axioms \(E\), linear equations in the bits or term values, such that the base with \(E\) stays hard and modulo \(E\) every block has an old image. The main goal needs the general step for the sources that short proofs produce, not for generic ones. Two facts from the record fix what that means at the first MOD level. A parity of the variables of the ordinary PHP becomes, in the bit encoding, a sum of arbitrary within-row functions \(a_0+\sum_if_i(b_i)\), a class of dimension \(1+m(n-1)\) against \(1+m\ell\) for affine bit forms (recorded characterization); so the simplest gate that an \(\mathrm{AC}^0[2]\)-Frege proof of the ordinary PHP uses is already a sum of low flat indicators, outside the class of the all-ranks one-level theorem. And a two-level source of this kind reduces without degree loss to the one-level unary affine family (normalization), for which the record has an inventory on which both recorded rank tests fail (multiscale family, criterion gap) and an exclusion at high rank only, with intermediate ranks open (high-rank coverage); the all-ranks theorems are for affine-bit families. The record's own caveat stands: the failure of the two tests is not an impossibility theorem, and no proof is known to use the inventory. The generic dense bit forms studied in the last eight entries are therefore a model of the frontier (stated for bit forms), not the simplest recorded unexcluded class; the simplest is one OR over parities of PHP variables at middle rank. For both, the value method asks the same thing of the base: hardness under linear constraints of rank far above \(n\), with right-hand sides of our choice. For bit-linear constraints that is Conjecture H1; for parities of unary variables the constraints are \(\sum_if_i(b_i)=e\) with arbitrary \(f_i\), a larger class. Recorded for it: the case split, which covers arbitrary old polynomial queries with right-hand sides of our choice at one degree per query, hence rank up to about \(n/2\), and the occupancy-probe theorem, an example where unary linear equations with the wrong right-hand sides drop the PHP to degree two.

3. Falsification attempt on the union source

The recorded candidate counterexample to Claim G for arbitrary sources is the union of a wide literal reader and the row-mixing twisted approximate-majority source. The statement of the claim already notes that the two systems of equations are inconsistent with each other; the corollary below is the uniform, quantitative form of that sentence. The two recorded choices of value axioms are a restriction \(\rho'\) of the compact family \(\Phi_0\) for the reader (family: a flat \(Q\) of dimension \(\ell_2\), \(N=2^{\ell_2}\), \(N+1\) live rows, the other rows matched bijectively to the labels outside \(Q\)) and \(a=0.7v\) generic linear equations for the twisted source.

Corollary U (incompatibility). Let \(W\) be a uniform affine subspace of \(\mathbb F_2^v\) of codimension \(a\ge(N+1)\ell+\log_2\binom{n+1}{N+1}+t\). Except with probability \(2^{-t}\), every restriction \(\rho'\in\Phi_0\) leaves at most one point of \(W\).

Proof. By the recorded observation, except with probability \(\binom{n+1}{r}2^{r\ell-a}\) no two points of \(W\) differ in at most \(r\) rows. A restriction of the compact family fixes every row outside its \(N+1\) live rows to one label, so two assignments that it leaves differ in at most \(N+1\) rows. Take \(r=N+1\); the event does not depend on \(\rho'\), so no union over the family is needed. \(\square\)

For \(a=0.7v\) and polylogarithmic \(N\) the hypothesis holds with room to spare. So on the union source the two recorded mechanisms cannot be combined by intersecting their axioms: whatever restriction serves the reader leaves at most one point of the subspace that serves the twisted source, and on a point the base is refuted at degree at most \(\ell\) (Lemma T below; on an empty intersection at degree one), so hardness is lost outright. The claim itself, which quantifies over all \(E\), is not refuted. With the equations of the twisted source alone, the general form of Lemma R (its Hypotheses paragraph: the substitution acts on the old variables only, with \(\ell\) replaced by the largest axiom degree) puts the whole system into the residual coordinates of \(W\), where every pin \([a\to y]\) of the reader is a flat indicator of codimension at most \(\ell\) in forms that are generic for a generic twist; the reader is then a reader of dense-form terms and falls under the term-value form of Question H. With a restriction alone, the twisted source becomes a reader of generic flats on the polylogarithmic residual space, as in the recorded invariance (which is stated for uniform forms; the rows of a uniform invertible matrix are only approximately uniform). Either way the union source leads back to the same hardness question, on one of the two spaces. Over \(\mathbb F_2\) the distinction between literal and dense terms depends on the coordinates; the hardness question does not.

4. Alternative (E): what the published methods need

Read in the second paper (locators in the source audit; statements imported as context). Theorem 5.5: a refutation of Razborov's \(\mathrm{PHP}^{m,r}_n\) over \(\mathbb F_p\), \(p>2\), with \(M\) extension variables \(z=Q\), each \(Q\) a polynomial of degree at most \(k\) in at most \(\kappa\) original variables, \(r>2pk\), has size \(\exp(\Omega(n^2/((M+mn)\kappa k)))\). The proof removes the pairs of terms of high quadratic degree in rounds. A round picks a variable by averaging; for an extension variable it applies an assignment of Hamming weight at most \(pk\) that sets \(Q\) to zero or to \((b-a)x+a\) (Lemma 5.3: set the variables of one minimal monomial to one and the other variables of \(Q\) to zero), removes every hole touched by \(\mathrm{vars}(Q)\), at most \(\kappa\) holes, and then splits the lines. The fractional pigeons are what makes the cleanup sound: an assignment of weight below \(r/2\) commits no pigeon to a hole. At the end the definitions are substituted, which multiplies the degree by \(k\), and Razborov's degree bound is applied to the surviving \(\mathrm{PHP}^{m,r}_{n'}\), \(n'\ge n/2\). Theorem 1.2 adds an XOR lift of the formula so that a random restriction brings extension axioms of polynomial size down to logarithmic degree.

What this needs, against a compiled source of the ordinary PHP: (1) definitions in the original variables only, where the source is nested to the depth of the proof and the final substitution would cost \(k\) per level, the recorded multiplicative cost; (2) \((M+mn)\kappa k=o(n^2)\), where a source has \(n^c\) blocks for arbitrary \(c\) and dense blocks have \(\kappa\) of order \(mn\), so that the bound is void already for one dense block; (3) a formula that survives assignments of weight \(pk\) and the loss of \(\kappa\) holes per round; the ordinary PHP is falsified by two ones in a hole (the paper does not discuss it; this is my reading of why the fractional variant is used), and dense arity removes all holes in one round; (4) an XOR lift of the formula, which is not available when the formula is the fixed target; (5) \(p>2\); for \(p=2\) both papers point to the size-degree tradeoff, which needs degree above the square root of the number of variables and is void once the number of extension variables reaches about \(n^2\), the same limit as in (2). None of the five holds for the source of the general step, and (1) to (3) fail independently. The one idea with no counterpart in the notebook is the size measure itself (quadratic degree, removal of extension variables one at a time). It does not help here: every round spends holes in proportion to the arity, and the notebook's endpoint is a degree statement with the inventory entering only through a logarithm.

5. One wall, and its weakest form

Image methods stop at the universal obstruction; the value method needs the PHP to stay hard on a subspace cut out by linear constraints of rank of order \(v\); the union source and the unary parities lead to the same requirement. Every technique on record or read stops at rank of order \(n\): the recorded detectors at \(n/4\), where they reserve holes (Corollary SL), the case split at about \(n/2\), where its additive loss meets the barrier, the closure technique for Res(\(\oplus\)) at \(cn\) (literature), the expander method at locality. Rank \(n\) is where a system can still be solved for one bit in each of distinct rows; above it every row is touched and all but a \(2^{-t}\) fraction of the linear forms on \(W\) have no representation by bits of \(r\) rows or fewer when \(r\ell+n+1+t\le\dim W\) (there are at most \(\binom{n+1}r2^{r\ell}\) such representations), so an accounting that charges a bounded number of rows to a query stops.

Lemma T (parity decision trees give polynomial-calculus degree). Let \(W\), \(P\) and \(\mathcal S_P\) be as in Lemma R. Suppose a parity decision tree of depth \(d\ge\ell\) solves the collision search on \(W\): every query is a linear form that is not constant on the current subspace, and every leaf, an affine subspace \(U=\{q_1=a_1,\dots,q_s=a_s\}\) of \(W\) with \(s\le d\), lies inside the collision flat of some pair \(p(U)\). Then \(\mathcal S_P\) has a refutation of degree at most \(d\) in the multilinear quotient ring, in fact the Nullstellensatz certificate \(1=\sum_UE_{p(U)}\prod_{j\in J_U}(1+q_j+a_j)\) with \(|J_U|=\operatorname{codim}U-e_{p(U)}\). Hence \(D_b(W)\) is at most the larger of \(\ell\) and the parity-decision-tree depth of the collision search on \(W\), and at most \(\max(\ell,\dim W)\), by querying all coordinates (a point lies in a collision flat because there are more rows than holes).

Proof. Fix a leaf \(U\) with pair \(p\), let \(R_p\) be the span of the forms of the collision flat of \(p\) (dimension \(e_p\le\ell\)) and \(Q_j\) the span of the first \(j\) queries on the path. Since \(U\) is nonempty and lies in the flat, \(R_p\subseteq Q_s\), so \(\dim(R_p+Q_j)\le s\le d\) for every \(j\). The reduced line \(E_p\prod_{i\le j}(1+q_i+a_i)\) is the indicator of the flat cut out by \(R_p+Q_j\) with the given values, of degree \(\dim(R_p+Q_j)\), or zero. If \(q_{j+1}\) is constant on that flat, the next line is the same line or zero and no inference is made; otherwise the dimension is below \(d\) before the multiplication, the predecessor has degree at most \(d-1\), and multiplying by the affine form \(1+q_{j+1}+a_{j+1}\) (a sum of variable multiplications) stays within \(d\). The last line is the indicator of \(U\), which is obtained from \(E_p\) by the factors \(j\in J_U\) that raised the dimension. The leaves partition \(W\), so their indicators sum to the constant 1 as multilinear polynomials. \(\square\)

Position in the record. The recorded case-split lemma gives \(\ell+d\) by induction on the tree (each parity query costs one degree); the bound \(\max(d,\ell)\) without the additive \(\ell\) and the general fact behind it are new. Recorded analogues, none of which implies it: the hole-query trees on the unary board, the branch closure for products of at most three affine forms, and the affine-clause transfers of the publication branch, which go through extension variables. The containment \(R_p\subseteq Q_s\) is the argument of the recorded paragraph on parity decision trees at the end of the unary-query section (a leaf inside a flat of codimension \(r\) has queried rank at least \(r\)). The lemma uses \(\mathbb F_2\) (a linear query is a polynomial of degree one) and nothing about the PHP beyond the axioms being flat indicators; genericity of \(W\) and the non-constancy of the queries (constant queries can be skipped) are not used, and \(d\ge\ell\) only keeps the axiom within the ceiling and gives the passage to \(D_b\) through Lemma R.

Corollary (the compact base has bit degree of order \(n\)). \(n/2+1\le D_b(\mathcal Q_{n,2})\le2n-2+\ell\), and \(D_b(W)\le\min(\max(\ell,\dim W),\,2n-2+\ell)\) for every affine subspace \(W\). The lower bound is the recorded one. For the upper bound use the halving tree: query the first bit of all \(n+1\) rows and keep the \(n/2+1\) rows of the majority side, which share \(n/2\) holes; query the second bit of those rows, and so on; level \(j\) makes \(n/2^{j-1}+1\) queries, \(2n-2+\ell\) in all, and after level \(\ell\) two rows agree in every bit, so the leaf lies in their collision flat. The tree restricted to \(W\) solves the search on \(W\). This settles the question left open in the previous entry (order \(n\), not order \(n\ell\)); the exact values three and five on four and eight holes equal the lower bound. For the bit form of Conjecture H1 it means that at \(\dim W=0.3v\) the degree lies between \(c\,n\), if the conjecture holds, and \(2n-2+\ell\).

A depth lower bound of order \(n\) for parity decision trees on a generic subspace of linear codimension is therefore a necessary condition for the bit form of the conjecture, and it is the simplest question on which all the techniques above fail for the same reason. For the full space such a bound is published (the abstract of Byramji and Impagliazzo, read in the previous literature entry, states depth \(\Omega(n)\); imported context, not used).

6. Estimates and selection

Estimates, for the lines named only. That the value method (Claim G) advances the general step: about 5 percent, down from 10, because its hardness input turned out to have neither a proof method nor a test within reach (that its two mechanisms do not combine on the union source was known when the 10 percent was set). That an extension of the published extension-variable methods advances it: about 2 percent. The parked lines are unchanged (Conjecture L is not sufficient; the level-one conjecture does not move the obligation).

Selection. One bounded step, at most two research entries, on the weakest form of the wall: the parity-decision-tree depth (up to an additive \(\ell\) the depth of tree-like Res(\(\oplus\)) refutations, a standard fact that is not in the record) of the bit PHP on a generic subspace of codimension \(0.7v\). It is selected because it is sharp in both directions and cheap to state: a prover strategy of depth \(o(n)\) that exploits the linear relations of the subspace refutes the bit form of Conjecture H1 by Lemma T, and one of depth below the working degree of the recorded framework (\(B=k(D+1)\) with \(k\) of order \(\sqrt{n\log M}\)) ends the value method for dense forms, while a delayer strategy that survives \(cn\) queries would be the first technique on record that crosses rank \(n\); the motivation, a heuristic only, is that designs are often built from delayer strategies. First entry: try to build the prover strategy (queries that read one parity of many rows at once, using the relations of \(W\)); then the delayer, starting from the recorded closure technique and the observation that a pair is separated as soon as one form of its span is answered against its target. No computation is proposed: by the rule on nonvacuous tests, the conjectured depth \(cn\) exceeds the trivial bound \(\ell\) only on boards where the game tree over affine subspaces of \(\mathbb F_2^k\), \(k\ge n\), is out of reach. If neither strategy results, the value method is parked as a whole and the following review reconsiders the form of the general step rather than its mechanisms, starting from the simplest recorded unexcluded class of Section 2.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read from the notebook: the compact family (preservation lemma), the observation of the previous entry used for Corollary U, Lemma R with its Hypotheses paragraph, the unary-query characterization, the label-parent normalization, the multiscale family, the middle-rank frontier, the statement of Claim G, and the literature section; from the paper, the passages listed in the source audit. Before drafting, the standing reviewer answered that the incompatibility statement follows in one line from the recorded observation with \(r=N+1\) (my own route, a union bound over the family, needed \(a>v/2\) and its claimed range \(\ell\ge4\) was wrong), that the record gives only \(\ell+d\) for parity trees, and pointed out the halving tree, which gives the corollary on the full base. On the full draft the reviewer confirmed Lemma T step by step, the halving count, the restriction of the tree to \(W\), Corollary U against the definition of the family, the counting sentence of Section 5, every statement of Section 4 against the paper text, and the presence of the five elements of a review; it found no error in the lemma or the corollaries and reported seven findings, all applied. (1) The inconsistency of the two axiom systems on the union source is already stated with Claim G; Corollary U is now presented as its quantitative form, and the reason given for lowering the estimate no longer counts it. The review finds that the value method's two hardness inputs, the union source and the unary parities of the simplest recorded unexcluded class all require the PHP to stay hard under linear constraints of rank of order \(v\), that every available technique stops at rank of order \(n\), and that the published extension-variable methods need five properties none of which the compiled source has. Route check. Route item: the general step. First of at most two entries selected by the route review: the parity-decision-tree depth of the collision search for the bit PHP on a generic affine subspace \(W\) of codimension \(0.7v\), the weakest form of the hardness question behind Conjecture H1 (by Lemma T the bit degree is at most the depth). Estimate for the value-method line as set by the review: about 5 percent. The claim index was searched for "delayer", "prover", "decision tree", "adversary", "anti-concentration", "Fourier" and "bias"; nothing of the kind used below is recorded (the bias lemmas on record concern coefficient generators). Both lemmas were sent to the standing reviewer before drafting. Stopping point as announced: a prover strategy, a delayer lemma with its range, or the obstruction.

1. The prover: what cannot help

Notation: \(W\) a uniform affine subspace of \(\mathbb F_2^v\) of dimension \(k\), \(W^\perp\) the space of linear forms vanishing on its direction space (uniform of dimension \(a=v-k\)), \(R_p\) the span of the \(\ell\) forms \(b_{i,t}+b_{i',t}\) of a pair \(p=(i,i')\). A tree solves the collision search on \(W\) if every leaf subspace lies in the collision flat of some pair.

Lemma L (every prover must touch many rows). Let \(r\ell+\log_2\binom{n+1}r+t\le k\). Except with probability \(2^{-t}\) over \(W\), the following holds for every parity decision tree that solves the collision search on \(W\) and every assignment, to each query node, of a form in the label bits that agrees with the query on \(W\): on some path the assigned forms jointly touch more than \(r-2\) rows. In particular a tree whose queries touch at most \(\omega\) rows each has depth more than \((r-2)/\omega\).

Proof. A fixed nonzero linear form annihilates the direction space of \(W\) with probability \((2^a-1)/(2^v-1)<2^{-k}\), and at most \(\binom{n+1}r2^{r\ell}\) nonzero forms are supported on \(r\) rows or fewer. So except with probability \(2^{-t}\) no nonzero form supported on at most \(r\) rows is constant on \(W\); equivalently, for every set \(S'\) of at most \(r\) rows the projection of \(W\) to the label bits of \(S'\) is onto. This is the event that every set of \(r\) rows has jointly free labels on \(W\), stated without proof in the earlier entry. Note \(r\le k/\ell\le n+1\). Assume the event, fix a tree and an assignment, and suppose that on every path the assigned forms jointly touch at most \(r-2\le n-1\) rows. A delayer walks down the tree and keeps the set \(S\) of rows touched so far and a point \(x\) of the whole bit space that satisfies the answers given so far and is injective on \(S\). At a node with assigned form \(\tilde q\) it adds the rows of \(\tilde q\) to \(S\), changes \(x\) on the new rows to distinct labels not used on the old rows (possible because \(|S|\le n\), and harmless because the earlier forms do not involve the new rows), and answers \(\tilde q(x)\). Let the walk end at a leaf \(U\) with pair \(p\). If a row of \(p\) lies outside \(S\), change \(x\) there so that the two labels of \(p\) differ; otherwise they differ already, because \(x\) is injective on \(S\). As \(|S\cup p|\le r\), some \(w\in W\) agrees with \(x\) on the rows of \(S\cup p\). The assigned forms agree with the queries on \(W\) and are supported on \(S\), so \(w\) gives the delayer's answers and lies in \(U\); but \(w\) does not lie in the collision flat of \(p\). So the tree does not solve the search. (The same argument at an inner node shows that every answer of the delayer is realised on the current subspace of \(W\), so the walk never enters an empty branch.) \(\square\)

The proof uses the uniformity of \(W\) only for the probability of the free-rows event; the statement holds for every affine subspace on which every \(r\) rows are jointly free, and it uses of the board only that there are \(n\) labels.

For \(k=0.3v\) the condition reads \(r\le0.3(n+1)-(\log_2\binom{n+1}r+t)/\ell\), which allows \(r\) about \((0.3-0.88/\ell)n\), at least \(0.3n-n/\ell\): vacuous for \(\ell\le4\) (at \(\ell=4\) the condition allows \(r=2\) only), about two rows at \(\ell=5\), and a fraction of \(n\) that tends to \(0.3\) as \(\ell\) grows. So on a generic subspace of codimension \(0.7v\) every tree whose queries touch at most \(\omega\) rows each has depth more than \((r-2)/\omega\): ordinary decision trees on the bits need depth of order \(n\). This is the standard adversary argument, run on \(W\) through the free rows; it is a bound at rank of order \(v\), but only for the weakest kind of query. A prover that does better must use queries that touch many rows in every representation; all but a \(2^{-t}\) fraction of the forms on \(W\) are of this kind (counting sentence of the review). I found no strategy that uses such queries (two wide queries whose sum is a pair form give one narrow form for two queries, and are available on the whole space as well), and no proof that none exists. The attempt to build a prover of depth \(o(n)\) ends here.

2. A density delayer

Lemma D (density delayer). Let \(G\) be a nonempty set of points of an affine subspace \(W\). If a parity decision tree of depth \(d\) solves the collision search on \(W\), there are a pair \(p\) and an affine subspace \(U\) of \(W\) inside the collision flat of \(p\), of codimension \(s\le d\) in \(W\), with \(|U\cap G|\ge2^{-s}|G|\); equivalently the density of \(G\) in \(U\) is at least its density in \(W\).

Proof. The delayer answers every query that is not constant on the current subspace by the side containing at least half of the points of \(G\) in it. After \(s\) such queries the subspace \(U\) has codimension \(s\) and \(|U\cap G|\ge2^{-s}|G|>0\). The path ends at a leaf, which lies in a collision flat. \(\square\)

Use on the whole space. Let \(W\) be the whole bit space and \(G=G^{[j]}\) be the points whose \(n+1\) labels take exactly \(n+1-j\) values (\(j=1\): one colliding pair), and \(\bar c_j\) the average number of colliding pairs of a point of \(G\). All pairs are equivalent, so \(|G\cap F_p|=\bar c_j|G|/\binom{n+1}2\), and the density of \(G\) inside a collision flat is smaller than in the whole space by the factor \(\beta_j=(n+1)/(2\bar c_j)\). Inside the flat of \(p\), with the two rows of \(p\) merged, \(G\cap F_p\) is the set \(S_{j-1}\) of labelings of \(n\) rows by \(n\) labels with image size \(n-j+1\). So on the full space a tree of depth \(d\) exists only if some affine subspace of codimension at most \(d-\ell\) of \(\mathbb F_2^{n\ell}\) carries \(S_{j-1}\) at density at least \(\beta_j\) times its average, a density boost \(\beta_j\). The depth is thus at least \(\ell\) plus the least codimension at which near-injective labelings can be concentrated by the factor \(\beta_j\) on an affine subspace. For an affine subspace \(H\) with annihilator \(A\) (a space of characters, \(|A|=2^s\)) the boost is \(\sum_{\chi\in A}\pm\hat S(\chi)/\hat S(0)\), at most \(1\) plus the sum of the \(2^s-1\) largest values of \(|\hat S(\chi)|/\hat S(0)\), \(\chi\ne0\) (the spectral bound of the table below), hence at most \(1+(2^s-1)\max_{\chi\ne0}|\hat S(\chi)|/\hat S(0)\). On a generic \(W\) the factor \(\beta_j\) holds only on average over the pairs, and the identification with \(S_{j-1}\) is not available; Lemma D itself holds for every \(W\) and every \(G\). The record already gives a depth bound on the whole space by another route: by Lemma T the depth is at least the bit degree, which is at least \(n/2+1\) (recorded); the interest of Lemma D is its use on \(W\), where the bit degree is unknown.

3. Spectra of near-injective labelings

Here \(S_j\) is a set of labelings of \(n\) rows, the rows of the board with the two rows of \(p\) merged. Two closed forms. For bijections (\(S_0\)) the character with the same nonzero functional \(z\) on every row has coefficient exactly 1: its value on a bijection is \(\prod_x(-1)^{\langle z,x\rangle}\) over all labels, which is 1 because \(n/2\) is even for \(\ell\ge2\). All bijections lie in the subspace where the sum of the \(n\) labels is zero, of codimension \(\ell\): boost \(n\), above \(\beta_1=(n+1)/2\). On the board this is the subspace of the collision flat of \(p\) on which the labels of all rows except one row of \(p\) sum to zero; it contains every point whose only collision is \(p\). With \(G^{[1]}\) the delayer of Lemma D therefore guarantees only depth \(2\ell\). For \(S_1\) the same characters have coefficient \(-1/(n-1)\): the labels are all labels with one label \(x^\circ\) missing and one label \(x^*\) doubled, the sum of all labels is \(x^\circ+x^*\), and by the symmetry of \(S_1\) under permutations of the labels this is uniform over the nonzero vectors, so the coefficient is \(2\frac{n/2-1}{n-1}-1\).

Exact computation. The new tool near_injective_spectrum.py computes the Walsh transforms of the indicators of \(S_0,S_1,S_2\) on \(\mathbb F_2^{n\ell}\) for \(n=4\) and \(n=8\) (\(2^{24}\) points), lists the largest coefficients, and searches the 24 characters of largest coefficient for the best boost at codimension up to four (a lower bound on the maximal boost; the spectral bound above is an upper bound). Nonvacuity, checked before the run: the question is whether a boost \(\beta_j\) is reachable at codimension below \(\log_2\) of what the trivial bound \(2^s\) allows; on eight holes \(\beta_2=2.0625\) and \(\beta_3=1.243\) (from \(\bar c_2=1008/462\), \(\bar c_3=9576/2646\)), so codimensions two to four decide something.

\(S_0\) (bijections)403201 (the seven uniform characters), then \(1/7\)2, 4, 8, 9.142, 4, 8, at most 9.14\(\beta_1=4.5\)
\(S_1\) (image size 7)1128960\(1/7\) (the seven uniform characters), then \(0.102\)1.14, 1.27, 1.44, 1.621.14, 1.43, 2.00, 2.82\(\beta_2=2.0625\)
\(S_2\) (image size 6)5362560\(1/19\)1.05, 1.11, 1.18, 1.251.05, 1.16, 1.37, 1.79\(\beta_3=1.243\)

On four holes the largest coefficients are 1 for \(S_0\) and \(1/3\) for \(S_1\), as the closed forms say. Consequences. On eight holes no affine subspace of codimension at most three boosts \(S_1\) to \(2.0625\) (spectral bound 2.00), so by Lemma D every parity decision tree for the full bit PHP on eight holes (nine rows) has depth at least \(\ell+4=7\), against 5 from Lemma T and the recorded degree bound; the halving tree has depth 17. With \(S_2\) the bound is 6, and \(j=3\) cannot give more than 7, because the boost 1.2531 found at codimension four exceeds \(\beta_3\). If the largest coefficient of \(S_1\) is \(1/(n-1)\) for every \(n\), as on four and eight holes (not proved), the weaker form of the spectral bound gives depth at least \(\ell+\log_2\bigl(1+(n-1)(\beta_2-1)\bigr)\), about \(3\ell-2\): logarithmic, below the \(n/2+1\) that the record already gives on the whole space. The spectral bound wastes almost everything: the best boosts found grow by a factor of about 1.13 per codimension, not 2.

4. What remains

Question A (concentration of near-injective labelings). For \(j\ge2\) fixed, what is the least codimension \(s_j(n)\) of an affine subspace of \(\mathbb F_2^{n\ell}\) on which \(S_{j-1}\) has density \(\beta_j\) times its average? The needed boost is not a constant: \(\beta_2=(n+1)(3n-2)/(12n)\), about \(n/4\). An upper bound, the birthday subspace. Prescribe distinct \(t\)-bit prefixes on \(m\le2^t\) rows: codimension \(mt\). Under a uniform bijection the labels of the \(m\) rows are a uniform injective tuple, so the subspace has probability \(\prod_{i<m}(n/2^t)/(n-i)\) against \(2^{-tm}\) under the uniform measure: boost \(n^m(n-m)!/n!\), which is \(\exp(m^2/(2n)+O(m^3/n^2))\). For \(S_1\) the labels of the \(m\) rows are a uniform injective tuple given that the colliding pair does not lie inside them, so the boost is \(\bigl(1-\binom m2/\binom n2\bigr)n^m(n-m)!/n!\). It exceeds \(\beta_2\) at \(m\) about \(\sqrt{2n\ln(n/4)}\), codimension \(m\lceil\log_2m\rceil\) (or \(m(\lceil\log_2m\rceil-1)+1\), prescribing only the pair conditions of the prefix tree, which changes the constant only): 742 for \(n=2^{10}\), 5200 for \(n=2^{14}\) (below \(n/2+1=8193\)), 66456 for \(n=2^{20}\). Balanced halving is much weaker: fixing the first bit on \(m\) rows, half each way, boosts bijections by \([2^m/\binom m{m/2}]\binom{n/2}{m/2}^2/\binom nm\), about \((1-m/n)^{-1/2}\) for \(m<n\) and \(\sqrt{\pi n/2}\) at \(m=n\). The birthday characters are visible in the spectrum: the second coefficient \(0.102\) of \(S_1\) on eight holes belongs to the characters \((-1)^{\langle z,\mathrm{label}_i+\mathrm{label}_{i'}\rangle}\) of two rows, with value \(\frac1{28}-\frac{27}{28}\cdot\frac17=-20/196\). Consequence. With \(G^{[2]}\) Lemma D cannot prove more than depth \(O(\ell\sqrt{n\log n})\) on the whole space, where the record gives \(n/2+1\): the density criterion loses at least a square root there, and the same subspace limits \(G^{[j]}\) for other fixed \(j\) (not computed). Compare with the working degree of the recorded framework, \(B=k(D+1)\) with \(k\) of order \(\sqrt{n\log M}\) (review): the ceiling is of the same order up to logarithmic factors, so through \(G^{[2]}\) Lemma D can at best match the working degree, and even a complete answer to Question A with the transfer would not exclude provers of depth between about \(\ell\sqrt{n\log n}\) and \(B\); a depth bound is in any case only a necessary condition for degree hardness. So \(s_2(n)\) lies between about \(2\ell-2\) (spectral bound, given the largest coefficient) and \(O(\ell\sqrt{n\log n})\). The transfer to a generic \(W\) is the part that concerns the wall: one needs that on \(W\) no subspace concentrates \(G^{[j]}\cap W\) more than the subspaces of the whole space do. I tried the moment method and it does not reach this (an account of a failed attempt, not a claim): for one fixed subspace \(H\) of the whole space the second moment shows that \(W\cap H\cap G\) has about the expected size as long as \(k-\operatorname{codim}H\) exceeds \(\log_2(2^v/|G|)\), about \(1.44n\) for small \(j\); but there are about \(2^{sv}\) subspaces \(H\) of codimension \(s\), so a union bound over them needs failure probabilities below \(2^{-sv}\), and in the higher moments that I computed the events that the parameter subspace of \(W\) falls into a structured \(H\) dominate once \(s\) exceeds about \(\ell/2\). So after this entry the delayer side has a criterion (Lemma D), its first obstruction (the linear invariant of bijections, avoided by \(j\ge2\)), a logarithmic bound from spectra, a ceiling of order \(\ell\sqrt{n\log n}\) from the birthday subspace (no higher than the working degree of the value method, up to logarithmic factors), and two open statements: Question A on the whole space and the transfer. 1. A sequential bound for subspaces defined on few rows

Labels are the points of \(\mathbb F_2^\ell\), \(n=2^\ell\), and there are \(\rho\le n\) rows. For a set \(S\) of labelings and an affine subspace \(H\) of codimension \(s\) the boost is \(\Pr_{x\in S}[x\in H]/2^{-s}\). Let \(A\) be the space of linear forms that are constant on \(H\) (dimension \(s\)) and \(T\) the set of rows touched by \(A\), \(\tau=|T|\). Fix an ordering of \(T\) as positions \(1,\dots,\tau\), let \(A_i\) be the forms of \(A\) supported on positions at most \(i\) and \(c_i=\dim A_i-\dim A_{i-1}\), so \(\sum_ic_i=s\); call \(i\) a pivot position if \(c_i>0\).

Lemma N (sequential boost bound). (a) For \(S\) the injective labelings of \(\rho\le n\) rows, \(\mathrm{boost}(H)\le\prod_{i\ \mathrm{pivot}}\frac n{n-i+1}\le\frac{n^\tau(n-\tau)!}{n!}\) for every ordering of \(T\), with equality on the birthday subspace of the previous entry. (b) For \(S=S_1\), the labelings of \(n\) rows with exactly one colliding pair, \(\mathrm{boost}(H)\le\prod_{i\ \mathrm{pivot}}\frac{n+3}{n-i+1}\) for every ordering of \(T\) (the proof gives \(n+2\)).

Proof. A form of \(A_i\) whose component on position \(i\) vanishes lies in \(A_{i-1}\), so \(A_i/A_{i-1}\) injects into the functionals of the label of position \(i\). Hence for \(x\in H\) and given \(x_1,\dots,x_{i-1}\) the label \(x_i\) lies in a coset \(K_i(x_{<i})\) of codimension \(c_i\), with \(n2^{-c_i}\) labels, and \(H\) is the set of \(x\) with \(x_i\in K_i(x_{<i})\) for all \(i\). Reveal the rows of \(T\) in order; \(\Pr[x\in H]\) is the product over \(i\) of the conditional probabilities of \(x_i\in K_i\) given that the earlier conditions hold, each of which is at most the largest value of \(\Pr[x_i\in K_i\mid x_{<i}]\). (a) Given \(x_{<i}\), the label \(x_i\) is uniform on the \(n-i+1\) unused labels, so the probability is at most \(n2^{-c_i}/(n-i+1)\); non-pivot positions contribute at most 1. On the birthday subspace (distinct \(t\)-bit prefixes on \(m\) rows) every position of \(T\) is a pivot and \(K_i\) never contains a used label, so equality holds throughout. (b) The number of ways to complete an injective labeling of the first \(i-1\) rows to an element of \(S_1\) is \(f(i)=(n-i+1)!\sum_{k=i}^n(k-1)\), by the recursion \(f(i)=(i-1)(n-i+1)!+(n-i+1)f(i+1)\), \(f(n+1)=0\) (for \(i=1\) read \(q_1=0\); either row \(i\) repeats one of the \(i-1\) used labels and the rest is injective into the \(n-i+1\) unused ones, or it takes an unused label); in particular \(|S_1|=n!\,n(n-1)/2\). So before the collision \(x_i\) equals a given used label with probability \((n-i+1)!/f(i)\), in total \(q_i=2(i-1)/((n-i+1)(n+i-2))\), and is uniform on the unused labels otherwise; after the collision it is uniform on the \(n-i+2\) unused labels. In both cases \(\Pr[x_i\in K_i\mid x_{<i}]\le\frac{n2^{-c_i}}{n-i+1}+q_i\min\bigl(1,\frac{n2^{-c_i}}{i-1}\bigr)\le2^{-c_i}\Bigl(\frac n{n-i+1}+\frac{2n}{(n-i+1)(n+i-2)}\Bigr)\le2^{-c_i}\frac{n+2}{n-i+1}\), since the second term occurs only for \(i\ge2\). \(\square\)

Finite check. The new tool sequential_boost_check.py draws random affine subspaces whose forms live on at most \(\tau\) rows, computes the exact boosts of bijections and of \(S_1\) by enumeration, and compares them with the bound minimised over all orderings. On four holes (2000 subspaces, \(\tau\le4\)) and eight holes (400 subspaces, \(\tau\le5\), codimension up to eight) there is no violation. For bijections the bound is attained, also nontrivially (571 and 120 of the subspaces touch at least two rows and have boost above one, and 282 and 43 of these attain the bound exactly), so the test has power for part (a) and for the pivot count: an error there would show as a ratio above one. For the constant of part (b) it has none: the largest ratios for \(S_1\), 0.57 and 0.73, come from one-row subspaces (boost 1 against \((n+3)/n\)), with two or more rows they are 0.48 and 0.70, and in no sample does the boost of \(S_1\) exceed even the bound with constant \(n\). Part (b) rests on its proof; the reviewer checked the conditional law of \(S_1\) by brute force on four holes (\(f(i)=144,36,10,3\), \(q_i=0,1/6,2/5,1\)). Outputs: results directory.

What the lemma gives and what it does not. The bound depends on the rows touched, not on the codimension: with \(\tau\) rows the boost of \(S_1\) is at most \((1+3/n)^\tau n^\tau(n-\tau)!/n!\), about \(\exp(\tau^2/2n)\), so the birthday subspace is optimal among subspaces defined on few rows, and a boost \(\beta_2\approx n/4\) needs \(\tau\) at least about \(\sqrt{2n\ln(n/4)}\) rows. For forms of large row width the bound says nothing, and for bijections it cannot: the sum-zero subspace has boost \(n\) at codimension \(\ell\), every ordering has a pivot at the last position with ratio \(n\), and (a) is attained there as well. In the application of Lemma D the subspace lives inside a collision flat on the \(n\) merged entities, \(T\) counts entities, and a query that touches a row of the pair touches the merged entity. There the lemma gives depth at least \(\ell\) plus about \(\sqrt{2n\ln(n/4)}/\omega\) on the whole space for queries of row width \(\omega\), which is weaker than the injective-point adversary of Lemma L (order \(n/\omega\)). So Lemma N adds no depth bound; it shows that Question A is entirely a question about forms of large row width, the same place where the prover side stopped.

2. Forms of large row width: what was tried

Absolute values lose the signs. The boost is a signed sum of normalised coefficients over the characters of \(A\), and the spectral bound of the previous entry replaces it by the sum of absolute values. Take \(H\) the subspace that fixes the labels of \(m\) rows to distinct values (\(s=m\ell\)). For bijections the character that applies one functional \(z\ne0\) to two rows has coefficient exactly \(-1/(n-1)\) (the sum of two distinct uniform labels is uniform on the nonzero vectors), and \(A\) contains \((n-1)\binom m2\) of them: absolute sum \(\binom m2\), signed sum \(\binom m2/(n-1)\) (for each pair, \(\sum_{z\ne0}-(-1)^{\langle z,a_i+a_{i'}\rangle}/(n-1)=1/(n-1)\)), which is the first-order term of the true \(\ln\) boost \(m^2/2n\). Likewise for \(S_1\), where the two-row coefficient is \(1/\binom n2-(1-1/\binom n2)/(n-1)\), about \(-(1-3/n)/n\) (previous entry), and the absolute sum is \(\binom m2(1-O(1/n))\). So no argument through absolute values can show a boost below \(1+\binom m2\) at codimension \(m\ell\), that is, it cannot answer Question A beyond codimension about \(\ell\sqrt{n/2}\); counting also the characters on \(j\) disjoint pairs (about \((m^2/2)^j(n-1)^j/j!\) of them with coefficients about \(n^{-j}\); heuristic, not proved) the absolute sum is about \(\exp(m^2/2)\) and the method stops near \(1.2\,\ell^{3/2}\), barely above the \(2\ell-2\) of the spectra.

A closed form for one functional on \(w\) rows. For bijections the character that applies one functional \(z\ne0\) to \(w\) rows has coefficient \((-1)^{w/2}\binom{n/2}{w/2}/\binom nw\) for even \(w\) and zero for odd \(w\): the labels of the \(w\) rows form a uniform \(w\)-subset of the labels, half of which satisfy \(\langle z,x\rangle=1\), and \(\sum_j(-1)^j\binom{n/2}j\binom{n/2}{w-j}\) is the coefficient of \(x^w\) in \((1-x^2)^{n/2}\). It gives \(-1/7\) at \(w=2\) and \(w=6\) on eight holes, as in the computed spectrum, and about \(2^{-n/2}\) at \(w=n/2\): single characters of middle width are negligible, and only a subspace with very many of them, with aligned signs, could matter.

A mixed programme and its ceiling (heuristic, no claim). Split \(A\) into the part \(A_0\) generated by characters of row width below \(w_0=4s/\ell\) and the rest. The boost of \(H\) is the boost of the larger subspace \(H_0\) defined by \(A_0\) plus a signed sum over \(A\setminus A_0\), all of whose characters have width at least \(w_0\); if coefficients of width \(w\) are at most \((Cw/n)^{w/2}\) (true for the closed form above, not proved for \(S_1\) in general), the \(2^s\) characters of the rest contribute little as long as \(s\) is below about \(\ell\,n^{1/2-\delta}\). The subspace \(H_0\) touches at most \(w_0s=4s^2/\ell\) rows and has at most \(s\) pivots, so by Lemma N its boost is at most about \(\exp(4s^3/(\ell n))\), below \(\beta_2\) only for \(s\) up to about \((\ell^2n)^{1/3}\). The programme would therefore end at depth of order \((\ell^2n)^{1/3}\), below the birthday ceiling and below the working degree.

The transfer, reformulated. The account in the previous entry counted the \(2^{sv}\) subspaces of codimension \(s\); the better count is over characters. Let \(W=c+W_0\) with \(W_0\) a uniform subspace of dimension \(k\) and \(c\) uniform, \(G\) a point set and \(f(\varphi)=|G|^{-1}\sum_{x\in G}\varphi(x)\). Expanding the indicator of \(W\) gives, for every character \(\chi\), \(\sum_{x\in G\cap W}\chi(x)=2^{-a}|G|\sum_{\psi\in W_0^\perp}\psi(c)f(\chi\psi)\): the coefficient of \(G\cap W\) at the class of \(\chi\) is \(f(\chi)\) plus the noise \(N(\chi)=\sum_{\psi\ne0}\psi(c)f(\chi\psi)\), normalised by \(1+N(1)\). The average over \(c\) gives \(\mathbb E N(\chi)=0\) and \(\mathbb E N(\chi)^2=\sum_{\psi\ne0}\Pr[\psi\in W_0^\perp]f(\chi\psi)^2<2^{-k}2^v/|G|\) by Parseval, about \(2^{-k+1.44n}\) for \(G^{[2]}\). This controls one character, not all \(2^v\) of them; a simultaneous bound needs moments of order above \(v/(k/2-0.72n)\), in which the average over \(c\) leaves the tuples of characters with trivial product, and the characters with large coefficients (small row width, and their products with the uniform characters) have to be separated as main terms, which is where the free-rows event of Lemma L would enter. I did not carry this out: its outcome would be that the coefficients of \(G\cap W\) are those of \(G\) up to a small error, after which the transfer inherits exactly the problem of the whole space, signed sums over characters of large row width.

Route review; one lemma (constant-row clamp) and two remarks with working proofs; the general step is unchanged. Spin cycle 227. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), reasoning effort xhigh (user setting)).

Route check. Route item: the general step. This is the review prescribed by the previous review after the parity-tree step ended without a strategy (decision). 1. The forms on record are of one type

Thesis. Every form of the general step that has produced a polynomial-calculus exclusion at a degree not tied to the accuracy of the blocks is of one type: a design of an enlarged old base \(\mathcal F\cup E\) composed with old images of the blocks modulo \(E\). The forms differ only in \(E\): a weight \(w\) (over \(\mathbb F_2\), for \(\mathcal F\) containing the Boolean equations and \(\deg w\le B\), \(w\notin\mathcal C_{B+\deg w}(\mathcal F)\) implies that \(\mathcal F\cup\{1+w\}\) has no refutation of degree \(B\), which implies \(w\notin\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F)\); so the one-affine-level theorem, the learning lemma and the relative interfaces are of this type with \(E=\{1+w\}\)), matching restrictions (the literal line, Conjecture L), linear value axioms and term values (Claim G, the reduction). Each needs a hardness statement \(H(E)\) about the old base alone, and the proof techniques on record for \(H(E)\) are four: counting a common weight, restrictions that preserve the base, the top-monomial detectors (rank at most \(n/4\), Corollary SL), and the case split (additive loss). The standing reviewer, asked for recorded forms outside this type, named three, with their recorded status: (a) source-module moment designs, in which the selector moments are free unknowns (coupled marginals, active-window reduction, pair-separated transfer): this form does have unconditional Nullstellensatz extensions with no charge for the number of blocks or their rank, but only in the band \(3h<D\le4h\) tied to the accuracy and for bit-affine families (first boundary, coherent band, faithful pairs), coverage at rank at most \(4h\) in the band \(6h\le D<8h\) (corollary), no feasibility theorem beyond, and three recorded obstructions to simple ansätze (statuses from the index rows; these entries were not re-read for this review); (b) fresh-block conservativity through the coefficient criterion and its dual: open at level one (conjecture), refuted at the same degree over second-level bases, with loss at most \(\min(D+k\delta,2D-w)\) per block (loss bound) and total rank under sequential application (placement); (c) proof-specific forms, in which \(E\) is chosen after the refutation is given: escapes are named (obstruction entry, published extension-variable methods), local pruning exists, and no theorem uses the structure of the source of a short proof. The generic query route is parked by its own obstruction.

Lemma K (constant-row clamp). Work over \(\mathbb F_p\). Let a source over an old base \(\mathcal F\) have complete first-level blocks \(b\le M\) with old inputs \(g_{b,1},\dots,g_{b,r_b}\) and accuracies \(h_b\), \(P_b=\prod_{u\le h_b}(1-\sum_jr_{b,u,j}g_{b,j})\). Choose constants \(c_{b,u,j}\) and put \(\lambda_{b,u}=\sum_jc_{b,u,j}g_{b,j}\), \(Q_b=\prod_{u\le h_b}(1-\lambda_{b,u})\). (i) If \(\mathcal F\cup\{g_{b,i}Q_b:b,i\}\) has no polynomial-calculus refutation of degree \(D\), then \(\mathcal F\) with the blocks has none. (ii) Over \(\mathbb F_2\): if the source has, above the first level, only pure readers in the sense of the recorded reduction, and \(\mathcal F\cup\{Q_b:b\le M\}\) has no refutation of degree \(D\), then the source has none of degree \(D\).

Proof. Substitute \(r_{b,u,j}=c_{b,u,j}\); this is the degree-zero case of the substitution rule. The product \(P_b\) maps to \(Q_b\), each companion \(g_{b,i}P_b\) to \(g_{b,i}Q_b\), each coefficient field equation to \(c^p-c=0\), and old axioms to themselves; no degree changes. This proves (i). For (ii), modulo the axioms \(Q_b\) every first-level product is congruent to 0, so every input of a reader is congruent to a constant, and the two cases of the recorded reduction give the reader a constant image with constant coefficient rows (an input congruent to 1 is selected by the first row, image congruent to 0; if all inputs are congruent to 0 the zero rows give the image 1), and the same one level up. All images use constants, so the factor \(\max(1,w-1)\) of that reduction does not occur. \(\square\)

Scope, as the reviewer pointed out. Part (i) uses nothing about \(\mathcal F\); (ii) and the remarks (b), (c) below are written for \(\mathbb F_2\) (for odd \(p\) the reader cases select an input congruent to \(c\ne0\) with \(c^{-1}\), and flat indicators need powers \(p-1\); not written out). The lemma is not in the record in this form; the nearest records are the constant first-row specialization at the end of the learning lemma, the zeroing of surplus rows in the relative old-target theorem, and the recorded reduction with its nonconstant telescoping images. (a) Part (ii) needs the stronger axioms \(Q_b\); with \(g_{b,i}Q_b\) alone the product is not constant, the axioms only exclude the flat of \(\lambda\) minus the zero set \(Z_b\) of the block. (b) Since \(Z_b=Z_bQ_b\) modulo Booleanity, hardness of \(\mathcal F\cup\{Q_b\}\) at \(B+h\) implies hardness of \(\mathcal F\cup\{Z_b\}\) at \(B\): the hypothesis of (ii) is stronger than the zero-value hypothesis of the recorded reduction, and what it buys is the removal of the factor \(w-1\) at every rank above \(h\). It is Question H at rank \(h\) with total density \(M2^{-h}\). (c) For a block of rank at most \(h\), taking the \(\lambda_u\) a basis makes the companions Boolean consequences; this is the recorded packing. So for first-level blocks the accuracy is the width of the avoidance axiom the block needs, whatever its rank, and the choice of the \(\lambda\) is ours.

2. What the goal needs at the simplest unexcluded class

The simplest recorded unexcluded class is one OR over parities of PHP variables: the one-level unary affine family over \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\) (Section 2 of the previous review; in the bit base it is the two-level class with second-level inputs that are sums of low flat indicators, and the normalization returns to the unary family). A superquasipolynomial \(\mathrm{AC}^0[2]\)-Frege lower bound for the ordinary PHP would have to cover proofs that use such gates (the translation of such a proof into this source is the recorded telescoping substitution, a sketch and not a formal implication). The one-affine-level theorem does not cover it (its blocks are affine in the bits). What the record has, with the further items the reviewer listed: exact packing up to rank about \(hN/(2D)\) (ceiling \(T(r)D\)); the dimension criterion at rank at least \(\rho v\), \(v=N(N+1)\), and more generally where \(M\,b_k(v-r)<u_k-t_k\) for some \(k\le N/(2D)\); old-target NS exclusions for jointly independent middle-rank groups on eleven and thirteen holes only (pair-separated transfer); the degree gap of the common-vanishing method for \(\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1\) independent blocks; and the failure of a unary weight by the ambient dimension. My first formulation of the uncovered window, \(hN/(2D)<r<2D(N+1)\ln(4M)\), was corrected by the reviewer at its upper edge: in the recorded criterion the matching monomials are only a fraction of about \(e^{-k^2/N}\) of \(b_k(v)\) (and the term \(t_k\) makes the criterion vacuous once \(e^{-k^2/N}<k/N\)), so the requirement is about \(r>v\ln(4M)/k+(N+1)k\), smallest near \(k=\sqrt{N\ln4M}\), and the upper edge is about \(2(N+1)\sqrt{N\ln4M}\) once \(N\) exceeds about \(4D^2\ln4M\) (computed by the reviewer for three parameter sets; not gated further). The qualitative statement is the recorded one: ranks around \(N\) lie inside the window on every usable board (criterion gap), and the multiscale family has a class there.

So every recorded cost is either additive in the number of blocks or linear in the inverse relative codimension, and nothing covers \(M\ge N/2\) blocks of window rank. The reviewer found the elimination row, which my draft had missed together with a product-weight row that it makes moot. The record also shows that the dependence on \(M\) cannot be removed: with exponentially many literal blocks the ordinary PHP has one-level refutations through \(4h+1\) and \(4h+2\) (exponential family, matching-tree refutation). In the language of Lemma K this is the regime \(M2^{-h}\gg1\). What the simplest class needs is therefore a method whose cost is logarithmic in \(M\) and is governed by the accuracy \(h\) and not by the relative codimension \(r/v\): by Lemma K it suffices that, for a suitable choice of the \(\lambda\),

(HW) \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\cup\{g_{b,i}Q_b\}\) has no polynomial-calculus refutation of degree \(D\), where \(Q_b\) is the indicator of a flat of codimension \(h\) cut out by forms in the span of block \(b\), \(M\le N^c\), \(h\ge c'\log_2N\) with \(M2^{-h}<1\), \(D\) polylogarithmic.

This is Question H at rank \(h\) in the unary base, in the regime of small total density, with no substitution factor. There is no finite evidence in the regime itself: the recorded check of the same entry has \(h=2\), where \(M2^{-h}<1\) allows three axioms. What it shows at larger density: on six holes at degree three, with general unary forms, the closure grows by the constant increment 34 per clause of two parities until 1 enters at axiom 50; on eight holes, with decoded bit-affine forms, by 62 until a jump at axiom 91, with 28 percent of the quotient left, and 1 enters at axiom 96 (\(M2^{-h}=24\)). The jump is a cancellation effect of polynomial calculus, which a Nullstellensatz design does not see. No recorded technique proves it: the weight fails by the ambient dimension, restrictions do not act on dense forms, and the case split pays per block.

Remark (few blocks are conservative in the stable range; a corollary of two records). Over \(\mathbb F_2\), let \(N\ge2B-1\), and adjoin to \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\) fresh complete blocks \(1,\dots,M\) whose inputs are old polynomials of degree at most \(\delta\), of any rank and accuracy. If an old polynomial \(t\) of degree \(k\) has a polynomial-calculus derivation of degree \(d\) from the enlarged system and \(d+M\max(\delta,k)\le B\), then \(t\in\mathcal I_k(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun})\). Proof: eliminate the blocks one at a time by the transfer lemma, whose base may contain the other blocks, at the cost \(\max\{d+\delta,d+k,2k\}\) each; the result is a derivation from \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\) within \(B\), and \(\mathcal C_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le k}=\mathcal I_k\) brings \(t\) down to its own degree. \(\square\) So the difficulty of the simplest class lies only in the number of blocks: whatever their ranks, \(M\) blocks give no refutation and no old consequence of degree \(k\) while \(d+M\max(\delta,k)\le(N+1)/2\).

3. Falsification attempts

(1) Do term values weaken the wall on the twisted approximate-majority source? In the test of Claim G the value axioms were the \(0.7v\) linear equations \(u_i=0\), \(i\in I\), and that entry records that every term then lies in their ideal, so hardness with those equations gives the zero-value hypothesis \(E'=\{Z_c=0\text{ for every term }c\}\). Conversely \(E'\) is a weaker sufficient hypothesis, so the sentence there that the claim escapes "exactly if" the PHP stays hard on a generic subspace of codimension \(0.7v\) holds for that \(E\) only. Does \(E'\) avoid linear codimension? The points on which every (positive) term vanishes are the union of the coordinate subspaces \(\{u_S=0\}\) over the hitting sets \(S\) of the terms. For the recorded parameters (\(v\) DNFs of \(\lceil4v(3/2)^t\rceil\) terms, \(t=\lceil3\log_2v\rceil\) uniform coordinates each) a set of density \(\sigma\) misses a given term with probability \((1-\sigma)^t\); the expected number of missed terms is at least \(4v^{2}(1.5(1-\sigma))^t\), which exceeds \(v\) by a power of \(v\) exactly when \(\sigma<1-2^{-1/3}/1.5=0.4709\) (at \(\sigma=0.47\) it is at least \(3.2\,v^{1.007}\)), and a union bound over the sets of size \(\lfloor0.47v\rfloor\) suffices because supersets of hitting sets are hitting sets (failure probability at most \(0.09^v\), reviewer's arithmetic). So with high probability every hitting set has more than \(0.47v\) elements, a sharpening of the \(v/3\) that the approximate-majority property gives by itself. Every point allowed by \(E'\) lies on a coordinate subspace of codimension above \(0.47v\), a generic subspace after the twist. Random sets are hitting sets from density about \(0.58\) (equivalently, a complement fixed beforehand may have density up to about \(0.42\); reviewer). The only recorded route to hardness with \(E'\) is one such subspace, so term values move the instance of Conjecture H1 from dimension \(0.3v\) to at most about \(0.53v\): the wall stays. The source has many narrow terms of total density about \(4v^{0.75}\gg1\); this is the opposite regime to (HW).

(2) Is (HW) false for structured blocks? For some choices of the \(\lambda\), yes: if every block is a row clause \(\bigvee_jx_{ij}\) and every \(Q_b\) keeps the same \(h\) holes, the axioms \(g_{b,i}Q_b\) give \(x_{ij}=0\) outside the kept holes at degree about \(h+1\), and what is left is a PHP with \(h\) holes, refutable in degree about \(h/2+1\) (the upper bound is recalled from the literature and matches the recorded closures on six and eight holes; not retrieved). This example has \(M2^{-h}<1\), so the density condition is meaningful only for generic dense blocks, and (HW) can only hold for suitable choices of the \(\lambda\). For row clauses the suitable choice is trivial (\(\lambda_1\) the row sum, which is 1 modulo the row axiom); for other literal blocks it would have to make the kept cells expanding, where published bounds for graph PHP apply (imported context recorded in the literature section, not checked against this base). For exponentially many literal blocks the recorded families refute the PHP. I found no refutation of (HW) for polynomially many generic blocks with \(M2^{-h}<1\).

(3) Is (HW) within reach for generic blocks? On the design side the count is favourable: a design must annihilate the multiples of the \(Q_b\) of degree up to \(B\), about \(M\) times the quotient dimension at degree \(B-h\) against the quotient dimension at degree \(B\), and the recorded closures behave exactly by this count until a saturation jump; the jump is a polynomial-calculus effect outside the reach of a Nullstellensatz design, so a design-side proof could at best cover the counting regime. A proof needs that the only relations among these multiples modulo the matching marginals are those forced by the base axioms. Statements of this kind for dense random systems are, as far as I remember the literature on semi-regular sequences over \(\mathbb F_2\), conjectures and not theorems (from memory, not retrieved); what makes the present case different is that the base has an explicit design theory (fillings by the stable filtration, row trades) in which the statement becomes linear algebra on zero-marginal arrays. This is a reason to try a bounded step, not evidence that it will succeed.

4. Estimates and selection

Estimates, for the lines named only. The value method with linear equations at linear codimension: parked, about 3 percent (previous entry). Block-by-block conservativity: it would settle the simplest class if the level-one conjecture held over the PHP base for many blocks, but every recorded argument is additive in the number of blocks (the transfer lemma, the loss bound) and the same-degree statement is refuted at the second level: about 3 percent. Source-module moment designs: no feasibility theorem after the recorded reductions; unchanged, and not re-estimated here because this review did not re-read those entries beyond their index rows. Proof-specific forms: no mechanism on record: about 2 percent. (HW), the hardness input that Lemma K isolates: about 5 percent that a proof for generic blocks is found and extends to the structured blocks of compiled sources; its merits are that it is the input of the simplest unexcluded class at all ranks at once, that its cost would be logarithmic in \(M\), that the recorded closures at larger density show no early failure in the counting regime (there is no finite evidence in the regime itself), and that it lies in a regime (wide axioms of small total density) that no entry has attacked: the previous review went to linear equations at linear codimension because its test source has narrow terms of large total density.

Selection. One bounded step, at most two research entries, on (HW) for generic blocks at the Nullstellensatz level in the unary base: construct a design of \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\) that annihilates every multiple of every \(Q_b\) through degree \(B\), level by level through the recorded fillings, and identify the exact linear-algebra statement that the construction needs at each level (consistency of the new equations with the matching marginals on zero-marginal arrays). Stopping point: a proof of consistency for all levels up to \(B\) of order \(N/\operatorname{polylog}N\); or an exact rank computation in which the relations among the multiples exceed those forced by the base axioms; or a named obstruction. If two entries give none of these, (HW) is parked next to Question H and the next review takes up the forms outside the type, (a) and (c) of Section 1. The Nullstellensatz level is a convenience of the method, not what the goal needs: the goal needs polynomial calculus, where the stability identity \(\mathcal C_B=\mathcal I_B\) of the base is not available for the enlarged base and where the recorded closures show a saturation jump that a design does not see; that gap is recorded here so that a Nullstellensatz result is not mistaken for the input of Lemma K.

Route check. Route item: the general step. This is the first of at most two entries that the route review allotted to (HW) (statement): the functional unary base with polynomially many avoidance clauses \(Q_b=\prod_{u\le h}(1+\lambda_{b,u})\) of logarithmic width and total density below one has no polynomial-calculus refutation of polylogarithmic degree; by Lemma K this is the hardness input of the simplest unexcluded class. Estimate that completing the line advances the general step: about 5 percent, as in the review. The computation was designed there with its nonvacuity count: the first level at which the working prediction can fail is level two for clauses of two parities, at degree four on seven holes (\(N=2B-1\)); the prediction is also the forced upper bound, so a rank below it refutes it. Read in full before the design: the stability theorem with its truncated-closure induction, Lemma K and (HW), and the recorded finite check of polynomial-calculus closures with generic axioms. Stopping point for the two entries: a proof of consistency, a rank that contradicts the prediction, or a named obstruction.

1. Setting, a no-fall criterion and the forced fall

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) with the base \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\) (rows \(i\le N+1\), holes \(j\le N\), \(\rho_i=\sum_jx_{ij}\)) in matching normal form, as in the stability theorem: \(\mathcal P_{\le e}\) is the span of the matching monomials of size at most \(e\), \(m_e\) is the number of matchings of size \(e\), and the normal form of the degree-\(e\) Nullstellensatz space of the base is \(\mathcal I_e=\operatorname{span}\{x_T(1+\rho_i):|T|\le e-1,\ i\notin\operatorname{row}(T)\}\). For affine forms \(\lambda_{b,u}\) put \(Q_b=\prod_{u\le h}(1+\lambda_{b,u})\) (in normal form), \(b\le M\), and \[ G_e=\mathcal I_e+\sum_{b\le M}Q_b\,\mathcal P_{\le e-h}\qquad(G_e=\mathcal I_e\text{ for }e<h), \] the degree-\(e\) Nullstellensatz space of the base with the clauses. Let \(\mathcal C_B\) be the normal-form closure: the least subspace of \(\mathcal P_{\le B}\) that contains the normal forms of the axioms of degree at most \(B\) (the \(1+\rho_i\) and the \(Q_b\)) and is closed under \(f\mapsto\operatorname{nf}(xf)\) for \(f\) of degree at most \(B-1\). It contains the normal form of every line of a degree-\(B\) polynomial-calculus derivation, so \(1\notin\mathcal C_B\) implies that there is no refutation of degree \(B\); it may be larger than the set of those normal forms. A degree fall at level \(e\) is an element of \(G_e\cap\mathcal P_{\le e-1}\) outside \(G_{e-1}\).

Lemma E (no-fall criterion). (i) If \(G_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le B-1}=G_{B-1}\), then \(\mathcal C_B=G_B\). (ii) If \(G_e\cap\mathcal P_{\le e-1}=G_{e-1}\) for every \(1\le e\le B\), then \(1\notin G_B=\mathcal C_B\), and the base with the clauses \(Q_b\) (hence with the weaker axioms \(g_{b,i}Q_b\) of Lemma K (i)) has no polynomial-calculus refutation of degree \(B\).

Proof. \(G_B\subseteq\mathcal C_B\) because every Nullstellensatz consequence is a consequence within the same ceiling. Conversely \(G_B\) is a subspace that contains the axioms, and for \(f\in G_B\) of degree at most \(B-1\) the hypothesis puts \(f\) in \(G_{B-1}\); since \(\operatorname{nf}(x\cdot x_T(1+\rho_i))\) is zero or \(x_{T'}(1+\rho_i)\) with \(|T'|\le B-1\) and \(i\notin\operatorname{row}(T')\), and \(\operatorname{nf}(xQ_bm)=Q_b\operatorname{nf}(xm)\), one has \(\operatorname{nf}(xG_{B-1})\subseteq G_B\). This is (i). For (ii), the chain of hypotheses gives \(G_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le0}=G_{B-1}\cap\mathcal P_{\le0}=\dots=G_0=\mathcal I_0=0\), as \(h\ge1\). \(\square\)

This is the general one-level form of the truncated-closure induction that the record carries out three times for specific classes (unary base, transported bit class, conditioned class); the stability entry explicitly does not assert equality for an augmented system, and Lemma E says what would have to be shown there. No relation between \(N\) and \(B\) is used; for \(M=0\) the hypothesis is the recorded stability, valid for \(N\ge2B-1\). Part (i) uses only level \(B\); the lower levels are used for \(1\notin G_B\) alone. The proof uses neither the field nor the PHP, only \(\operatorname{nf}(xG_{B-1})\subseteq G_B\) and \(G_0=0\).

Observation F (forced fall). Let \(X\subseteq Y\subseteq\mathcal P_{\le e}\) be subspaces and \(\operatorname{top}_e(Y)=Y/(Y\cap\mathcal P_{\le e-1})\). Then \(\dim X-\dim(X\cap\mathcal P_{\le e-1})\le\dim\operatorname{top}_e(Y)\). Hence, if \(X\subseteq G_e\) and \(\dim X-\dim(X\cap G_{e-1})>\dim\operatorname{top}_e(Y)\), there is a degree fall at level \(e\). (a) With \(X=G_e\), \(Y=\mathcal P_{\le e}\): a fall is forced once \(\dim G_e-\dim G_{e-1}>m_e\). (b) If all forms lie in a space \(L\) of affine forms containing the constants, \(e=h+1\), \(X=\mathcal I_e+\sum_bQ_bL\) and \(Y=\mathcal I_e+L^{h+1}\) (products of \(h+1\) elements of \(L\)): a fall is forced once \(\dim X-\dim G_h>\dim\operatorname{top}_{h+1}(\mathcal I_{h+1}+L^{h+1})\). The proof is the rank inequality for the projection to the top-degree component. The recorded reading of the jump as "a saturation of the space reachable with the available multipliers" (term values) and the generic Hilbert-series count in the bit ring (cycle 223) are instances without the count; that yardstick, \((1+t)^k(1+t^\ell)^{-m}\), treats the collision flats as generic polynomials of degree \(\ell\), and the clause series \((1+t)^k(1-t^\ell/(1+t)^\ell)^m\) has a later first nonpositive coefficient (on sixteen holes, \(m=136\): degree 8 against 7 at \(k=20\), 14 against 11 at \(k=40\); noted by the reviewer, recomputed in series_compare.py).

The count under test. The relations \(\lambda_{b,u}Q_b=0\) and \(Q_bQ_{b'}=Q_{b'}Q_b\) hold identically. If they generate all relations among the multiples, then with \(H_R(t)=\sum_k\gamma_kt^k\), \(\gamma_k=\dim\mathcal P_{\le k}/(\mathcal I_k+\mathcal P_{\le k-1})\) (in the stable range \(\gamma_k=c_k-c_{k-1}\) for \(c_k=\dim\mathcal P_{\le k}/\mathcal I_k\)), the graded dimensions of the quotient by \(M\) clauses are the coefficients of \[ H_R(t)\Bigl(1-\frac{t^h}{(1+t)^h}\Bigr)^{M} \tag{SR-series} \] up to the first coefficient that is not positive: the multiples of one clause are a copy of the quotient by its \(h\) forms, shifted by \(h\). For \(h=1\) this is \(H_R(t)/(1+t)^M\). It is the series of a semi-regular sequence over \(\mathbb F_2\) in the sense of Bardet, Faugère and Salvy (cited from memory, not read in this cycle), taken relative to the base ring instead of the Boolean ring. Level by level: a clause of \(h\) forms adds \(c_1-h\) at degree \(h+1\); at degree \(h+2\) the \(b\)-th clause of two forms adds \(c_2-2c_1+3-(b-1)\). At level one the count is an upper bound for \(\dim G_B\) when the forms of a clause are independent modulo \(\mathcal I_1\) and the constants; at level two it is an upper bound if moreover \(\lambda_1R_{\le1}\cap\lambda_2R_{\le1}\) is spanned by \(\lambda_1\lambda_2\) and each \(\lambda_uR_{\le1}\) has dimension \(c_1-1\) (\(R_{\le k}=\mathcal P_{\le k}/\mathcal I_k\)), as the review noted: a rank below the count refutes the count, a rank above it refutes that claim. If the count holds for the dimensions, a negative coefficient in degree \(B\) forces a fall by Observation F (a).

2. Exact computation

Tool and runs. research/tools/hw_unary_ns_rank.cpp builds \(\mathcal I_B\) from the marginal relations and adds the multiples \(x_\sigma Q_b\), \(|\sigma|\le B-h\), clause by clause, by dense elimination over \(\mathbb F_2\) with monomials ordered by degree; it reports the increment of \(\dim G_B\), whether \(1\in G_B\), and the number of pivots by the degree of the leading monomial, whose partial sum through \(e\) is \(\dim(G_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le e})\). The clause generator does not depend on \(B\), so the run at degree \(e\) gives \(\dim G_e\) for the same clauses, and analyze.py finds the first clause and level with \(\dim(G_B\cap\mathcal P_{\le e})\ne\dim G_e\). Forms: uniform affine forms in the \(x_{ij}\) ("general"), or on eight holes the unary images of bit-affine forms ("label": every row contributes the zero set of a uniform affine function of the three-bit hole label; these span a space \(L\) of dimension 37 with the constants, 28 modulo the row sums). The quotient dimensions 435, 2080, 1540, 17584 agree with the recorded closures. Sizes: up to 71793 monomials (seven holes, degree four), about four minutes per run; all outputs with provenance in research/results/hw_unary_design_20260918_228/.
