Label parity constraints. For \(h=1\) with label forms on eight holes (three seeds, 40 clauses): at degree two the increments are \(64-b\) up to the first fall, which is at clause 19, 19, 20 (amount 1, 2, 7), and irregular after it (1 enters at clause 24, 24, 26 with 327 to 331 of the quotient left); count (b) with multipliers from \(L\) gives \(27M-\binom{M+1}2\) against \(\dim\operatorname{top}_2(L^2)=864-540=324\), forced at \(M=20\) (\(330>324\)) with slack one at \(M=19\) (323): again a fall at slack one in two of three seeds. At degree three the increments are 1477, 1415, 1354, ... up to the first fall, at clause 15 for all seeds (amounts 179, 182, 187), and 1 enters at clause 17 with about 600 left; the reviewer's count with multipliers from \(L^2\) (top part \(\binom{27-b}2-27\) per clause, \(2300>2268\) first at clause 15; not rerun here) forces a fall at clause 15 with excess 32, so the amount of a fall equals the excess only in the runs with \(h=2\). The recorded closure jumps for these families are 19, 19, 20 and 15.

The recorded jumps are forced falls. The recorded polynomial-calculus closures (table) have their first jump at axiom 50 on six holes (clauses of two general parities, degree three) and at axiom 91 on eight holes (decoded bit-affine forms): these are the clauses 50 and 91 of the table above, so the jump of the closure is the first degree fall of the Nullstellensatz spaces, and through the clause before it \(\mathcal C_B=G_B\) by Lemma E (at clause 50 on six holes the closure already contains 1, which enters \(G_3\) only at clause 62) (the closure increments 34 and 62 are the Nullstellensatz increments). The recorded jumps for parity constraints follow from (SR-series) with \(h=1\) by hand: at degree two a fall is forced once \((c_1-1)M-\binom{M+1}2>\gamma_2\), which first holds at \(M=15\) on six holes (\(405>399\)) and at \(M=32\) on eight (\(1488>1476\)), the recorded jumps with general forms; at degree three on eight holes \(\gamma_3-M\gamma_2+\binom{M+1}2\gamma_1-\binom{M+2}3\) is 180 at \(M=16\) and \(-378\) at \(M=17\), the recorded jump. The review's sentence that the jump "is a cancellation effect of polynomial calculus, which a Nullstellensatz design does not see" stands for the design, and is sharpened: the jump is visible in the Nullstellensatz spaces as the first fall, and its position is a count.

3. Reading, conjecture, and what it would give

Conjecture SR (finite evidence only). Let the forms be uniform in a space \(L\) that is either all affine forms or the unary images of bit-affine forms. Then with probability \(1-o(1)\): \(\dim G_B\) follows (SR-series); no degree fall occurs at any level \(e\le B\) before the first clause at which Observation F forces one for a pair of the fixed family \(X=\mathcal I_e+\sum_bQ_bL^{d}\), \(Y=\mathcal I_e+L^{d+h}\) with \(d+h\le e\) (for all affine forms this is count (a)), up to a bounded number of clauses; and 1 does not enter \(G_B\) before \(\mathcal I_B+L^B\subseteq G_B\). All degrees are unary degrees: the top part of \(L^3\) for the label forms is spanned by the products of three label bits on three distinct rows, \(\binom93\cdot3^3=2268\), and the bit degree plays no role (in pure bit degree the base itself falls early, as the reviewer notes from the record). Evidence: every run above and every recorded jump; the deviation for general forms is a fall of amount one at slack 0 or 1, in four of the six boundary events, the behaviour of a square or nearly square uniform matrix over \(\mathbb F_2\) (singular with probability about 0.71, rank deficient at slack one with probability about 0.42); for label parity constraints at degree two the fall comes at slack one in two of three seeds with amounts 1 and 2 (a corank of two has probability about 0.04 for a uniform matrix, so this comparison is less apt there). The third clause was checked directly for label forms only, where it has content: after clauses 123 to 126 of width two (70, 44, 18, 0) and after clauses 16, 17 of label parity constraints at degree three (88, 0); at degree two the reviewer's scratch check gives 10, 11, 2 before and 0 at the clause where 1 enters (not rerun here). All statistics except those boundary events are the same for all seeds (generic ranks), so the seeds are not independent evidence, and the evidence is at degrees two to four with \(h\le3\).

What it would give. With Lemma E, Conjecture SR implies polynomial-calculus hardness of the base with generic clauses up to the forced clause. For general forms the fall at degree \(B\) is forced, to first order in (SR-series), at \(M^*\approx\gamma_B/\gamma_{B-h}\) clauses, which is of order \((N^2/B)^h\) for \(B\ll\sqrt N\) (\(\gamma_1=N^2-1\), \(\gamma_2=\binom{N+1}2((N-1)(N-2)-1)\), exact in the three computed cases, and \(\gamma_k\) is of order \(N^{2k}/k!\) for \(k\ll\sqrt N\)), and for label forms the pair with multipliers from \(L^{B-h}\) gives, heuristically, about \(((N+1)\log_2N/B)^h\); this is the count of one pair, another pair may force a fall earlier, so it is an upper estimate. Both are superpolynomial for \(h\ge c'\log_2N\) and \(B\) polylogarithmic, so under Conjecture SR, and by extrapolation from \(h\le3\), \(B\le4\), the statement (HW) would hold for generic clauses with room to spare, also at total density above one. For the decoded forms the count has to be made in the subalgebra generated by the forms: count (a) is off by a factor of three there (91 against 264).

What suffices, and what is a convenience. (HW) needs \(1\notin\mathcal C_B\) only; the absence of every fall is stronger, and it is the route that Lemma E offers, not a necessity. It is also the kind of statement that is open in simpler settings: semi-regularity of generic sequences is a conjecture already over the Boolean ring (recollection of the literature, not checked here). What the goal needs is more than the generic case: clauses chosen by a proof. One precision from the falsification attempts below belongs to the statement of (HW): the codimension \(h\) of a clause has to be counted modulo the row sums.

Falsification attempts. (1) The standing reviewer pointed to the recorded jump at axiom 91 with decoded forms as a counter-instance to "falls only when forced": count (a) forces a fall only from clause 264. The subalgebra count (b) explains it exactly (2268, amount 7), and also the entry of 1 at clause 126. (2) Wide forms inside a small subalgebra: the column sums \(\kappa_j=\sum_ix_{ij}\) satisfy \(\sum_i(1+\rho_i)+\sum_j(1+\kappa_j)=1\) identically, because \(\sum_i\rho_i=\sum_j\kappa_j\) and \(2N+1\) is odd: the \(N\) onto axioms \(1+\kappa_j\), which are avoidance clauses of width one with wide forms and total density \(N/2\), give a Nullstellensatz refutation of degree one over \(\mathbb F_2\) (the classical mod 2 counting argument; \(N\) literal clauses of width one cost nothing). This agrees with the pattern of the data: the subalgebra generated by the \(\kappa_j\) has dimension \(N\) in degree one modulo the base, and 1 enters when it is exhausted. In the regime of (HW) the attack needs a cover: the same identity makes the form \(\sum_j\kappa_j\) constant modulo \(\mathcal I_1\), so a parity decision tree that first queries it has \(2^{h-1}\) leaves of nominal codimension \(h\) whose clauses sum to 1 at degree \(h\), at nominal density one half; modulo the row sums the clauses have codimension \(h-1\) and density one, outside the regime. (3) A tempting shortcut fails, as the reviewer showed: if all forms span \(\ell_0\) dimensions modulo the row sums and the clauses are satisfiable as a formula in these parities, one may fix a satisfying value \(y^*\) and replace the clauses by \(\ell_0\) linear equations, from which every \(Q_b\) follows within degree \(h+1\); but the record has no hardness of the base with linear equations at a chosen right-hand side outside the safe bit-linear systems of Corollary SL (the case split keeps the base hard for some sign vector only, and a fresh block never imposes a value), and the clauses \(1+x_{11}\), \(1+x_{21}\) are satisfiable in their two parities while the base with \(x_{11}=x_{21}=1\) is refuted at degree two. So no bound in the dimension of the form space is claimed. Attempts (1) and (2) do not contradict Conjecture SR or (HW) with the precision on the codimension.

Remark S (the recorded support bound, applied to clauses). By the recorded point-support lemma, every set \(T\subseteq\mathbb F_2^v\) of Boolean points that realizes a normalized degree-\(B\) design of the base has at least \(2^{B-1}\) points (axioms of degree at most two). The exact condition for the design to annihilate the multiples of \(Q_b\) is that the evaluations at \(T\cap A_b\) (\(A_b\) the flat of the clause) vanish on all polynomials of degree at most \(B-h\), so \(T\cap A_b\) is empty or a nonzero word of the dual Reed and Muller code on the flat, with at least \(2^{B-h+1}\) points. Heuristically, a fixed \(T\) meets a random flat in about \(|T|2^{-h}\ge2^{B-h-1}\) points that are not of this form, so a design cannot be chosen before the clauses; \(T\) is not unique (it can be changed by any codeword of the dual Reed and Muller code), so this is a heuristic and not a statement about the design.

4. Outcome and remaining gap

The prediction of the review is confirmed at the first level where it could fail (seven holes, degree four, 766 and one less per clause), and beyond: exact Nullstellensatz spaces follow (SR-series) until exhaustion, the first fall is where counting forces it, and the recorded polynomial-calculus jumps are these falls. No rank contradicts the count, and no proof of consistency was found: the entry does not prove (HW) for any family beyond the recorded additive range, and the two construction principles examined do not give one: a design fixed before the clauses (Remark S), and a linear restriction to a satisfying value of the forms (attempt (3), for which the record has no hardness at a chosen right-hand side). The gap is a proof technique for the absence of falls with many wide forms at once. The smallest instance is parity constraints at degree two: no fall for \(M\) random parity constraints up to the forced count (\(M=15\) and 32 on six and eight holes, against \(N/2-2\) from the additive bound). There the statement is about two-forms: with \(V=\mathcal P_1/\text{constants}\), \(W\) the span of the forms with the row sums, and \(K\subseteq\Lambda^2V\) the span of the products of conflicting cells, a fall is a nonzero element of \(K\) (modulo the forced ones) that vanishes on the annihilator \(W^\perp\), and a first-moment bound over \(K\) by rank would need a count of the low-rank elements of \(K\); the count of all elements, \(2^{\dim K}\) with \(\dim K\approx N^3\), against the probability \(2^{-\binom{\dim W^\perp}2}\) for a nondegenerate form gives the heuristic range \(M\le N^2-O(N^{3/2})\). This is not carried out here.

1. The two-form criterion

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) with \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\) in matching normal form, \(N\ge3\). Let \(V'\) be the span of the variables \(x_c\), \(c\) a cell, \(\Theta=\operatorname{span}\{\theta_i\}\) with \(\theta_i=\sum_jx_{ij}\) the linear part of \(1+\rho_i\), and \(V=V'/\Theta\), \(n=\dim V=N^2-1\). Elements of \(\Lambda^2V\) are alternating forms on \(V^*=\{\varphi\in\mathbb F_2^{\rm cells}:\sum_j\varphi_{ij}=0\text{ for all }i\}\). Let \(K_0\subseteq\Lambda^2V'\) be the span of the \(x_c\wedge x_{c'}\) over conflicting cells (same row or same column) and \(\bar K\) its image in \(\Lambda^2V\). The degree-two component of the normal form of a product of two affine polynomials with linear parts \(\alpha,\beta\) is the class of \(\alpha\wedge\beta\) modulo \(K_0\). One has \(\dim\bar K=(N+1)(2N^2-3N+2)/2\) (196, 316, 477 on six, seven, eight holes, equal to \(\binom n2-\gamma_2\) with \(\gamma_2\) from the previous entry): \(K_0\) has the \(N(N+1)(2N-1)/2\) conflicting pairs as a basis, and \(K_0\cap(\Theta\wedge V')=\operatorname{span}\{\theta_i\wedge x_{ij}\}\), of dimension \(N^2-1\). Indeed, if \(\sum_i\theta_i\wedge\alpha_i\in K_0\), its coefficient on a compatible pair \((i,j),(i',j')\) is \(\alpha_i(i',j')+\alpha_{i'}(i,j)=0\); for \(N\ge3\) this makes \(\alpha_i(i',j')\) independent of \(j'\) and symmetric in \(i,i'\), so \(\alpha_i\) is its own-row part plus \(\sum_{i'}e_{ii'}\theta_{i'}\) with \(e\) symmetric, and the second part cancels in \(\sum_i\theta_i\wedge\alpha_i\). Parity constraints are axioms \(a_b=\ell_b+c_b\), \(\ell_b\in V'\), \(c_b\in\mathbb F_2\), \(b\le M\); \(G_1=\mathcal I_1+\operatorname{span}\{a_b\}\), \(G_2=\mathcal I_2+\sum_ba_b\mathcal P_{\le1}\). Let \(\bar W\subseteq V\) be the span of the images \(\bar\ell_b\), \(U=\bar W^\perp\subseteq V^*\), \(d=\dim U\).

Theorem T2 (criterion). (The constants \(c_b\) play no role below.) Suppose the \(\bar\ell_b\) are linearly independent in \(V\) (so \(d=n-M\)) and

\[ \text{no nonzero element of }\bar K\text{ vanishes on }U. \tag{*} \]

Then \(G_2\cap\mathcal P_{\le1}=G_1\) and \(G_1\cap\mathcal P_{\le0}=0\); hence \(1\notin\mathcal C_2=G_2\), and the base with the parity constraints has no polynomial-calculus refutation of degree two.

Proof. If \(\sum_ic_i(1+\rho_i)+\sum_be_ba_b\) is a constant, its linear part \(\sum c_i\theta_i+\sum e_b\ell_b\) vanishes, so \(e=0\) by independence in \(V\), then \(c=0\), and the constant is 0. Let \(f\in G_2\) have degree at most one, \(f=\operatorname{nf}(\sum_ip_i(1+\rho_i)+\sum_bg_ba_b)\) with \(p_i,g_b\in\mathcal P_{\le1}\) and linear parts \(\alpha_i,\beta_b\). The degree-two component of \(f\) is the class of \(\kappa=\sum_i\alpha_i\wedge\theta_i+\sum_b\beta_b\wedge\ell_b\), so \(\kappa\in K_0\). Its image \(\bar\kappa=\sum_b\bar\beta_b\wedge\bar\ell_b\) lies in \(\bar K\) and vanishes on \(U\), because every term has a factor in \(\bar W=U^\perp\). By \((*)\), \(\bar\kappa=0\). Extending the independent \(\bar\ell_b\) to a basis of \(V\) and comparing coefficients (Cartan's lemma), \(\bar\beta_b=\sum_{b'}s_{bb'}\bar\ell_{b'}\) with \(s\) symmetric, so \(\beta_b=\sum_{b'}s_{bb'}\ell_{b'}+\tau_b\) with \(\tau_b=\sum_it_{bi}\theta_i\in\Theta\). The normal-form ring is a quotient of a Boolean ring, so every element is idempotent; with \(\ell_{b'}=a_{b'}+c_{b'}\), \[ \sum_{b,b'}s_{bb'}\ell_{b'}a_b=\sum_b\Bigl(s_{bb}+\sum_{b'}s_{bb'}c_{b'}\Bigr)a_b, \] the terms with \(b\ne b'\) cancelling in pairs. With \(\theta_i=(1+\rho_i)+1\), \(\tau_ba_b=\sum_it_{bi}(1+\rho_i)a_b+(\sum_it_{bi})a_b\). Hence \(f=\operatorname{nf}(\sum_ip_i'(1+\rho_i))+a'\) with \(p_i'=p_i+\sum_bt_{bi}a_b\in\mathcal P_{\le1}\) and \(a'\in\operatorname{span}\{a_b\}\). Then \(f-a'\in\mathcal I_2\cap\mathcal P_{\le1}=\mathcal I_1\) by the stability theorem (\(B=2\), \(N\ge3\)), so \(f\in G_1\). The last assertion is Lemma E (ii). \(\square\)

Remarks. (a) The criterion is sufficient, not necessary: in the finite check below \((*)\) fails without a fall in a few instances on four holes (a relation among the multiples instead of a fall). (b) If \(\binom d2<\dim\bar K\), the restriction \(\bar K\to\Lambda^2U^*\) has a kernel and \((*)\) fails; reading the proof backwards, a nonzero \(\bar\kappa\in\bar K\cap(\bar W\wedge V)\) lifts to multipliers whose combination has degree at most one, which is a fall or, if it lies in \(G_1\), a relation among the multiples beyond the forced ones. This is the forced count of the previous entry in the form \(\binom d2<\dim\bar K\) (\(M=15\) on six holes, \(190<196\le210\); \(M=32\) on eight, \(465<477\le496\)). (c) \((*)\) is a condition on the subspace \(\bar W\) alone. It fails for the structured families on record: for a form \(\ell\) supported in one row and a cell \(x_{ij}\) of that row, \(\bar\ell\wedge\bar x_{ij}\in\bar K\) vanishes on \(U\); for a column sum \(\kappa_j=\sum_ix_{ij}\), \(\kappa_j\wedge x_{ij}\) is a sum of column conflicts, which is how the recorded column-occupancy equations bring the degree down to two; and all \(N\) column sums are dependent in \(V\) (the onto axioms of the previous entry). (d) Theorem T2 is the analogue, for arbitrary multipliers (\(\bar W\wedge V\)), of the recorded quadratic-faithfulness statements, which treat relations whose two factors are both inputs (\(\bar W\wedge\bar W\)) by the same top-coefficient argument and a deterministic localization (rectangle test, localized directions); as the reviewer notes, for uniform forms that line would cover the \(\bar W\wedge\bar W\) part down to \(d\) of about \(3N\), and the forced fall at \(\binom d2<\dim\bar K\) shows that \(\bar W\wedge V\) is the real constraint.

2. Three lemmas on alternating forms over \(\mathbb F_2\)

Lemma R1. Let \(\kappa\) be an alternating form of rank \(2\rho\) on \(X=\mathbb F_2^n\) and \(U\) a uniform subspace of dimension \(d\). Then \(\Pr[\kappa|_U=0]\le2.39\cdot2^{\rho(\rho+1)/2-\rho d}\).

Proof. Let \(\pi:X\to S\) be the quotient by the radical; \(S\) is a nondegenerate symplectic space of dimension \(2\rho\). \(\kappa|_U=0\) means that \(\pi(U)\) is totally isotropic, hence contained in a Lagrangian \(\Lambda\) (dimension \(\rho\)). There are \(\prod_{i=1}^\rho(2^i+1)\le2.39\cdot2^{\rho(\rho+1)/2}\) Lagrangians, and \(\pi^{-1}(\Lambda)\) has codimension \(\rho\), so \(\Pr[U\subseteq\pi^{-1}(\Lambda)]=\prod_{i<d}(2^{n-\rho-i}-1)/(2^{n-i}-1)\le2^{-\rho d}\). \(\square\)

Lemma R2. If moreover \(\rho\ge d\) and \(d\le n-1\), then \(\Pr[\kappa|_U=0]\le6\cdot2^{(\log_2d)^2/6}\,2^{-\binom d2}\).

Proof. Let \(u_1,\dots,u_d\) be independent uniform vectors of \(X\); conditioned on their independence, which has probability at least \(1-2^{d-n}\ge1/2\), their span is a uniform \(d\)-subspace, so it suffices to bound the probability of \(E=\{\kappa(u_k,u_l)=0\ \forall k<l\}\) by \(3\cdot2^{(\log_2d)^2/6-\binom d2}\). Expose the vectors in order and let \(t\) be the dimension of \(T=\pi(\operatorname{span}(u_1,\dots,u_k))\); while \(E\) holds, \(T\) is isotropic. Given the past, \(u_{k+1}\) is orthogonal to the earlier vectors with probability \(2^{-t}\), and then \(\pi(u_{k+1})\) is uniform on \(T^\perp\supseteq T\), of dimension \(2\rho-t\), so it lies in \(T\) with probability \(2^{2t-2\rho}\). Thus a step either raises \(t\) (probability at most \(2^{-t}\)) or keeps it (probability \(2^{t-2\rho}\)), or \(E\) fails. A history with \(j\) stays ends at \(t=d-j\), its raises contribute \(2^{-\binom{d-j}2}\), each stay at most \(2^{(d-j)-2\rho}\le2^{-(d+j)}\), and there are at most \(\binom dj\) such histories: \[ \Pr[E]\le\sum_j\binom dj2^{-\binom{d-j}2-j(d+j)}=2^{-\binom d2}\sum_j\binom dj2^{-j(3j+1)/2}\le2^{-\binom d2}\sum_j2^{j\log_2d-3j^2/2}, \] and the last sum is at most \(2^{(\log_2d)^2/6}\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}2^{-\frac32(j-j^*)^2}\le3\cdot2^{(\log_2d)^2/6}\). \(\square\)

Lemma R3 (few conflict two-forms of low rank). \(\bar K\) has at most \(\binom n{2\rho}2^{2\rho(3N-2)}\) elements of rank \(2\rho\).

Proof. Use the basis \(\bar x_{ij}\), \(j\le N-1\), of \(V\) (eliminating \(x_{iN}=\theta_i+\sum_{j<N}x_{ij}\)). A lift in \(K_0\) has same-row coefficients \(r_{i,jj'}\) and same-column coefficients \(c_{ii',j}\), \(j\le N\). After the elimination the matrix \(A\) of the form has arbitrary entries inside a row of the board, and between rows \(i\ne i'\) the entries \(A_{(i,j),(i',j')}=\delta_{jj'}c_{ii',j}+c_{ii',N}\). So the row of \(A\) indexed by \((i,j)\) is determined by \(N-2\) bits inside the board row and by the two bits \(c_{ii',j},c_{ii',N}\) for each of the \(N\) other board rows: at most \(2^{3N-2}\) possibilities. A symmetric matrix of rank \(r\) whose rows indexed by \(C\), \(|C|=r\), span its row space satisfies \(A=YA_{C\cdot}\) with \(Y_{C\cdot}=I\), hence \(A=A_{\cdot C}Y^{\mathsf T}\) and \(A_{C\cdot}=A_{CC}Y^{\mathsf T}\), so \(A_{CC}\) is nonsingular and \(A=A_{\cdot C}A_{CC}^{-1}A_{C\cdot}\) is determined by \(C\) and the rows in \(C\). \(\square\)

3. Uniform forms

Theorem U. Let \(a_1,\dots,a_M\) be independent uniform affine forms in the variables of \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\), \(d=N^2-1-M\ge1\), \(s\ge1\). If \[ \binom d2\ge\dim\bar K+\tfrac16(\log_2d)^2+s\qquad\text{and}\qquad d\ge12N+8\log_2N+2s, \] then with probability at least \(1-2^{-d}-7\cdot2^{-s}\) the spaces \(G_1,G_2\) have no degree fall and \(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\cup\{a_b\}\) has no polynomial-calculus refutation of degree two. For large \(N\) this is the range \(M\le N^2-\sqrt2N^{3/2}(1+o(1))\), and by Remark (b) a fall or a relation is forced when \(\binom d2<\dim\bar K\), that is from \(M\ge N^2-\sqrt2N^{3/2}(1-o(1))\).

Proof. The images \(\bar\ell_b\) are independent uniform vectors of \(V\); they are dependent with probability at most \(2^{M-n}=2^{-d}\), and conditioned on independence \(U\) is a uniform \(d\)-subspace of \(V^*\). By Theorem T2 it suffices to bound the expected number of nonzero \(\kappa\in\bar K\) with \(\kappa|_U=0\). Elements of rank \(2\rho\), \(\rho\le d-1\): by R3, \(\binom n{2\rho}\le2^{4\rho\log_2N}\), R1 and \((\rho+1)/2\le d/2\), their contribution is at most \(2.39\sum_{\rho\ge1}2^{-\rho(d/2-6N-4\log_2N+4)}\le2.39\cdot2\cdot2^{-(s+4)}\). Elements of rank at least \(2d\): at most \(2^{\dim\bar K}\) elements, each with probability at most \(6\cdot2^{(\log_2d)^2/6-\binom d2}\) by R2, together at most \(6\cdot2^{-s}\). \(\square\)

The second hypothesis needs \(\sqrt2N^{3/2}>12N\), so the theorem is asymptotic (\(N\) above about 90 for \(s=5\)); on small boards the low-rank elements have visible probability, as the check shows (six holes, \(M=13\): 2 falls in 40 trials with slack 35 in the count).

4. Decoded bit-affine forms

Let \(N=2^\ell\), \(S_{i,t}=\sum_{j:\,{\rm bit}_t(j)=1}x_{ij}\), \(\bar L_i\subseteq V\) the span of the images of \(S_{i,t}\), \(t<\ell\) (dimension \(\ell\)), \(\bar L=\bigoplus_i\bar L_i\) (dimension \((N+1)\ell\)), and \(V_i\subseteq V\) the image of the cells of row \(i\) (dimension \(N-1\)). The unary image of a bit-affine form has its linear part in \(\bar L\) modulo \(\Theta\), and a multiple of \(\theta_i\) changes \(a_b\) by an element of \(\mathcal I_1\) and a constant, which changes neither \(G_1\) nor \(G_2\).

Structure lemma. For \(\ell\ge4\), \(\bar K\cap(\bar L\wedge V)=\bigoplus_i\bar L_i\wedge V_i\).

Proof. \(\bar L\wedge V\) is the set of forms that vanish on \(\bar L^\perp=\bigoplus_i{\rm RM}(\ell-2,\ell)\) (per row, the vectors orthogonal to all affine functions of the label). Take a lift of \(\kappa\in\bar K\) with same-row parts \(R_i\) and same-column coefficients \(c_{ii',j}\). For \(\varphi\) on row \(i\) and \(\psi\) on row \(i'\ne i\), both of degree at most \(\ell-2\), \(\kappa(\varphi,\psi)=\sum_jc_{ii',j}\varphi_j\psi_j\). Every monomial of degree at most \(\ell\) is a product of two monomials of degree at most \(\ell-2\) when \(\ell\ge4\), so the products \(\varphi\psi\) span all functions and \(c_{ii'}=0\). The remaining same-row parts vanish on \({\rm RM}(\ell-2,\ell)=\bar L_i^\perp\cap V_i^*\) exactly when \(\bar R_i\in\bar L_i\wedge V_i\); conversely \(\Lambda^2V_i\subseteq\bar K\) because all pairs in a row conflict. \(\square\)

The part of the statement inside \(\Lambda^2\bar L\) is on record: bit polynomials of degree at most two inject into \(\mathcal P_{\le2}/\mathcal I_2\) (low-degree rigidity, first relation degree, exact ranks in the quadratic quotient checks), so \(\bar K\cap\Lambda^2\bar L\) is spanned by the same-row bit products; the new part is \(\bar L\wedge V\). The checker gives \(\dim\bar K\cap(\bar L\wedge V)=850=17\cdot50\) on sixteen holes, as the lemma says, and \(171=135+36\) on eight holes, where \(\ell=3\) leaves the \(\binom92\) constant cross terms \(\sum_jx_{ij}\wedge x_{i'j}\) (\({\rm RM}(1,3)\) is self-dual).

Theorem Lb. Let \(N=2^\ell\ge16\), let \(a_1,\dots,a_M\) be unary images of independent uniform bit-affine forms, \(d_L=(N+1)\ell-M\ge1\), \(s\ge1\). If \[ \binom{d_L}2\ge(N+1)\binom\ell2+\tfrac16(\log_2d_L)^2+s\qquad\text{and}\qquad d_L\ge\ell^2+\ell+4+2s, \] then with probability at least \(1-N^22^{-d_L}-9\cdot2^{-s}\) there is no degree fall and no polynomial-calculus refutation of degree two. In the language of Conjecture H1: for a uniform affine subspace \(W\) of the bit space of dimension \(d_L\ge\ell\sqrt{N+1}\,(1+o(1))\), the base with the decoded equations of \(W\) has no refutation of unary degree two. The statement is about unary degree and says nothing about bit degree (a unary monomial of degree two has bit degree up to \(2\ell\) on two rows; the recorded refutation of a sixteen-dimensional subspace on sixteen holes at bit degree six is compatible with it).

Proof. The linear parts are independent uniform vectors of \(\bar L\), dependent with probability at most \(2^{-d_L}\); otherwise \(\bar W\) is a uniform \(M\)-subspace of \(\bar L\) and \(U\supseteq\bar L^\perp\). Let \(\kappa\in\bar K\) vanish on \(U\). Then \(\kappa\in\bar L\wedge V\), so by the structure lemma \(\kappa=\sum_i(\pi_i+\mu_i)\) with \(\pi_i\in\Lambda^2\bar L_i\) and \(\mu_i=\sum_kS_{i,k}\wedge y_{i,k}\), where the \(y_{i,k}\) belong to a fixed complement of \(\bar L_i\) in \(V_i\) and are independent, and \(S_{i,k}\in\bar L_i\) is nonzero. For \(\varphi\in\bar L^\perp\) and \(\psi\in U\), \(\kappa(\varphi,\psi)=\sum_{i,k}S_{i,k}(\psi)y_{i,k}(\varphi)\); the functionals \(y_{i,k}\) are independent on \(\bar L^\perp\), so \(S_{i,k}(\psi)=0\) for all \(\psi\in U\), that is \(S_{i,k}\in\bar W\). A fixed nonzero vector lies in \(\bar W\) with probability at most \(2^{-d_L}\), and there are \((N+1)(N-1)\) nonzero single-row forms; outside this event \(\mu=0\) and \(\kappa=\pi=\sum_{i\in I}\pi_i\) is a form on \(\bar L^*\), block diagonal of rank \(2\rho\ge2|I|\), that vanishes on the annihilator of \(\bar W\) in \(\bar L^*\), a uniform \(d_L\)-subspace. There are at most \(\binom{N+1}t2^{t\binom\ell2}\) such forms with \(|I|=t\). The exponent in R1 does not increase in \(\rho\) on \([t,d_L-1]\), so the forms with \(\rho\le d_L-1\) contribute at most \(2.39\sum_t2^{-t(d_L/2-\binom\ell2-\ell-1)}\le2.39\cdot2^{-s}\), and those with \(\rho\ge d_L\) at most \(6\cdot2^{-s}\) by R2. Theorem T2 applies. \(\square\)

Not sharp for refutations. The recorded closures tip at degree two only at \(\dim W=6\) and 7 on eight and sixteen holes (data of Conjecture H1), while falls start near \(\binom{d_L}2=(N+1)\binom\ell2\), that is \(d_L\le7\) on eight holes and about \(\ell\sqrt N\) in general: for label forms the absence of falls is much stronger than the absence of a refutation, and Lemma E is a convenience there, as the previous entry warned. The case of Conjecture H1 that the record needs, \(\dim W=0.3v\), is inside the range of Theorem Lb, at degree two only.

5. Finite check of the criterion

research/tools/two_form_criterion_check.py computes for random instances, independently of the proofs, whether \((*)\) holds (rank of the restriction of the conflict two-forms to \(U\)), whether \(G_2\cap\mathcal P_{\le1}\ne G_1\), and whether \(\dim G_2\) equals the count. Instances: four holes (uniform and label forms, 200 per \(M\)), six holes uniform (40 per \(M\), \(M=11..17\)), eight holes uniform (20 per \(M\), \(M=29..34\)) and label (40 per \(M\), \(M=15..22\)), and sixteen holes label, the smallest board inside the range of the structure lemma (5 per \(M\), \(M=46,50,52,53,54,55\)); 3750 instances. In no instance with independent forms (all but 1 to 36 of 200 on four holes with label forms, all elsewhere) does \((*)\) hold together with a fall. On six, eight and sixteen holes \((*)\) fails exactly in the instances with a fall; on four holes it also fails without a fall in 2 to 23 of 200 instances per \(M\le4\). On sixteen holes no instance falls for \(M\le53\) (\(d_L\ge15\), \(\binom{15}2=105\ge102\)) and every instance falls for \(M\ge54\) (\(\binom{14}2=91<102\)), the forced count of Theorem Lb. With uniform forms every instance falls from the forced \(M\) (5, 15, 32 on four, six, eight holes) and none on eight holes before it; with label forms on eight holes 1, 2, 2, 7, 32 of 40 fall at \(M=15,\dots,19\) and all from 20. The falls before the forced count are the low-rank events of the first moment, as the reviewer computed: on eight holes the term \((N^2-1)2^{-d_L}\) of Theorem Lb (a single-row label form in \(\bar W\)) is 1.5 to 12 percent for \(M=15,\dots,18\), and on six holes at \(M=13\) the roughly \(2\cdot10^4\) elements of \(\bar K\) of rank two, each with probability about \(3\cdot2^{-22}\), account for 2 falls in 40; this is compatible with the conjecture of the previous entry, whose \(O(1)\) allowance concerns the forced clause, but it shows that on small boards falls before it are not rare. The power of the check is for Theorem T2 only; Theorems U and Lb are asymptotic and rest on their proofs. Lemmas R1 and R2 were compared with exact probabilities obtained by enumerating all \(d\)-subspaces of \(\mathbb F_2^n\) for \(4\le n\le8\), \(2\le d\le4\) and every rank (research/tools/isotropy_bounds_check.py, 40 cases): both bounds hold, with largest ratios 0.59 and 0.16.

6. Degree three and above: the named obstruction; decision

At level \(B\ge3\), with no fall below, the expected form of the statement (not proved here) is: a fall is an element \(\xi\) of the degree-\(B\) part \(\bar K_B=\bar K\wedge\Lambda^{B-2}V\) of the conflict ideal that vanishes on \(U\) and does not lie in \(\bar W\wedge\bar K_{B-1}\), the part that vanishes for the trivial reason. A first moment over \(\bar K_B\) cannot treat the event "\(\xi|_U=0\)" alone, because that event is dominated by the trivial one. For decomposable \(\xi=x\wedge a\wedge b\) with \(a\wedge b\in\bar K\) the two coincide under \((*)\): \(\xi|_U=0\) means that a nonzero combination \(\alpha x+\beta a+\gamma b\) lies in \(\bar W\); if \(\alpha=1\) then \(\xi=w\wedge a\wedge b\in\bar W\wedge\bar K\), and if \(\alpha=0\) then \(a\wedge b\in\bar K\) vanishes on \(U\), against \((*)\). For sums of decomposables one needs a bound on \(\Pr[\xi|_U=0\text{ and }\xi\notin\bar W\wedge\bar K_{B-1}]\) summable over \(\bar K_B\), which asks for a notion of rank of a \(B\)-form relative to the ideal and a count of the elements of low rank; there is no analogue of the principal-minor argument of R3 for \(B\ge3\) (a form of degree three is not determined by boundedly many of its slices), and I have none. This is the obstruction, named: the relative rank count for the conflict ideal in degree three.

Decision. The two entries allotted to (HW) have given: exact evidence that generic clauses do no harm before a count forces it, a criterion (Lemma E), and a proof of that pattern at degree two for parity constraints, with a method whose cost is not additive in the number of forms; they have not given a proof at any degree above two, nor anything for clauses of width above one or for forms chosen by a proof. (HW) is parked next to Question H, with the relative rank count as the recorded way back in. The next entry is the review of the forms outside the type (source-module moment designs, proof-specific forms), as the route review prescribed.

Verification gate. Re-read from the notebook: the stability theorem (used at \(B=2\)), Lemma E, the quadratic-faithfulness entries (rectangle test and localization in full), Conjecture H1 with its data, Corollary SL. Index searches by content words with tools/search-claims.py for the three theorems and the rank lemmas, and by phrase ("isotropic", "alternating", "Lagrangian", "first moment"): nothing implies them. Pre-draft questions to the standing reviewer (on the plan during the previous gate, on the statements before drafting): none of T2, U, Lb is in the record and no counterexample is; the part of the structure lemma inside \(\Lambda^2\bar L\) is recorded (cited), the column-occupancy equations are a recorded failure of \((*)\) (cited), and the statement has to be kept apart from bit degree (done). Checks run: the criterion against exact degree falls on 3750 random instances; the structure lemma on four, eight and sixteen holes; Lemmas R1 and R2 against exact enumeration in 40 cases. Full review: no error found in T2, U, Lb, R1 to R3, the structure lemma or the decomposable computation of Section 6, each step confirmed separately (the derivation of \(\dim\bar K\), Cartan's lemma with lifts modulo \(\Theta\), the idempotence step, the conditional law in R2, the count of histories, the constants 7 and 9, the monotonicity used in Lb); five low findings, all applied: a sixteen-hole label run inside the range of the structure lemma (rerun here: no fall for \(M\le53\), all from 54), two miscounted figures in Section 5 (3750 instances; 2 to 23), a sentence on the falls before the forced count, "about 90" for the asymptotic range with "asymptotically" in the title, and the scope of "first" in the assessment. Unused hypotheses, stated by the reviewer: the constants \(c_b\) (noted in T2), uniformity beyond the linear parts modulo \(\Theta\) in U, \(\ell\ge4\) outside the structure lemma, \(d\le n-1\) outside the factor two of R2. Not checked by the reviewer: the living sections, index rows and next step, the column-occupancy entry beyond its index row, the literature remarks.

Main-route assessment. General step: unchanged. New on the record: the first hardness statements for the unary base under order \(v\) wide linear constraints (uniform forms up to \(N^2-O(N^{3/2})\), decoded forms at every subspace dimension above about \(\ell\sqrt N\)), at unary degree two only, where the record had rank of order \(n\) at most for wide forms (Corollary SL); order \(v\) narrow constraints with recorded hardness exist (the matching restrictions of the compact family, the single-bit and row-by-row equations of the earlier test), and in bit degree Lemma R already gives the bound \(\ell\); and the form the same statement takes at higher degree, with the step that is missing. Degree two is far from the polylogarithmic degree the goal needs, and the forms are uniform. Estimate for the (HW) line after the two entries: about 3 percent; it is parked.

Process assessment. The estimate for the line is in the route check and in the assessment (5, now 3 percent; parked). What worked: the plan was checked by the reviewer before the cycle began, the reduction to two-forms turned a rank problem for a structured random matrix into counting by rank, and the label case came out of reading the recorded tipping data against the theorem, which also showed at once that the no-fall route is far from sharp for label forms. Waste: about a quarter of an hour on a degree-three first moment before noticing that the vanishing event is dominated by the trivial one, which is the content of Section 6 and could have been seen on the decomposable case first. The ranked index search committed after the previous cycle was used for every statement and found the records the reviewer also named.

19 September 2026 — Short second opinion on the current research route

Status: bounded strategic review of the latest route review and its follow-ups; no new theorem, computation, or independent certification of their proofs. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Scope. The user requested a short assessment, not an extended research attempt. Read the latest main-route review, the avoidance-space entry, and the degree-two parity entry, including passages restored in the preceding context-reading turn. The later preprint entry is a publication side task. This assessment does not audit all preceding research or rerun its checks.

Judgment. The progression makes sense: isolate the obstacle to treating many blocks together, inspect the cancellations in the augmented old system, and obtain a criterion and a rank-count argument that handle many wide constraints without an additive charge for each one. The degree-two argument is the most useful methodological development in these entries. The record also correctly distinguishes its unary-degree scope, generic inputs, and stronger no-fall condition from the main goal.

Claim versus need. The attempted route would keep PHP hard after adding suitably chosen avoidance clauses, at logarithmic width and polynomial inventory, so that block images yield a forbidden endpoint. Its current no-fall approach asks for much more than non-refutability. A theorem for random parity constraints at degree two does not yet supply polylogarithmic degree, logarithmic-width clauses, or a construction for the input spans of a structured proof source. These are separate missing implications; extrapolating the finite ranks does not close them.

Check against recorded obstructions. A naive transfer from generic forms to all input families fails the recorded same-row and column-sum tests; this refutes that shortcut, not the existential choice of suitable coefficients inside a block. Likewise, simply reusing the first moment at degree three counts relations that vanish for trivial ideal-theoretic reasons, as the last entry explains. These checks favor a change of immediate task over more instances of the same random experiment.

Recommendation on the highest-risk item, the general step. Follow the already scheduled review of direct source-module moment designs first. The recorded unconditional bands give a concrete starting point, although their exact proofs and transfer hypotheses must be read before developing them. Ask which compatibility equation first escapes those bands, and whether it can be controlled without paying separately for all blocks. A successful extension must reach a sufficient costed-source or polynomial-calculus endpoint; a wider Nullstellensatz band alone is not the goal. Stop that follow-up at an exact new compatibility mechanism, a counterexample, or an identified missing implication with its degree budget.

What to revisit. Preserve the degree-two method as a candidate tool. A bounded follow-up on genuine degree-three consequences after quotienting out the forced relations is worth considering, preferably if the moment-design review exposes that same obligation. This is a research question, not a proposed proof or an automatic degree-by-degree program. Keep the broad literal-switching, generic-subspace, and parity-tree lines parked until a new mechanism addresses their recorded obstruction. Proof-specific analysis remains an alternative only when it names an actual compiler property and how that property avoids a hard example.

Prospects and process. My short-review estimate for immediately extending the generic no-fall line to the full goal is low; this record does not justify calibrated percentages. Direct moment compatibility is the better next bounded investigation, not a prediction of success. Parking should preserve reusable mechanisms and reopening conditions, rather than treat an exhausted two-entry allocation as evidence that a conjecture is false. Existing guidance already permits this, so no new framework rule is needed.

State and timing. The main goal and formalization gaps are unchanged. The living sections were reviewed; the proposed next step retains its exact reading list with this prioritization. Initial instruction/status reading preceded this clock; earlier context restoration was separate. Spin remains paused, and this assessment is committed locally.

Minimal retrieval. tools/claim-index.py list --fields id,summary --format tsv lists every matching claim in registry order with no header, footer, scores, JSON framing or implicit result limit. Fields can be selected and reordered, filters can be applied, and limits are explicit. Diagnostics and omission notices use stderr. Backslash/control-character escaping and a distinct null marker preserve values; typed JSON projections remain available. The complete 866-claim output is saved as claim-inventory.tsv.

Review model. Schema version two preserves the original claim text and separates formalization artifacts, significance assessments, topic definitions and per-field reviews. Reviews record source revision, date, evidence, reasons and next actions. Source hashes cover exact notebook excerpts or whole referenced files; unrelated notebook appends do not invalidate an anchored review. Changed claim text, field values or cited sources flag it as stale. Missing reviews remain unreviewed, and pending questions are not silently counted as complete. Version-one imports and data remain readable.

First source-reviewed batch. The telescoping record now has partial coverage with separate artifacts for the verified identity/degree upper bounds and the counterexample to a loose-bound equality. The publication theorem and exponential corollary have explicit complete formalization scopes, declarations and links to their existing verification reports. This is reuse of recorded evidence, not a fresh kernel replay or new formalization assignment. Their significance records identify the independent publication result, retain provisional novelty and external-review limitations, and do not imply a new literature search.

Five relationships record the publication results' direct exclusion/transfer dependencies and the exponential bound's quantitative refinement of the superpolynomial conclusion. Refinement is not mislabelled as a dependency of the Lean module. Topic IDs have definitions rather than free-floating tags. The five seeded topics are a starting vocabulary, not a completed taxonomy of all research.

Checks and remaining work. Twenty registry tests, seven merge tests and six finalizer tests pass. Coverage reports three reviewed claims in each of the five metadata fields and 863 unreviewed claims in each; no sampled batch is presented as a full audit. All 1,326 current claim/evidence references resolve locally. Reproduction, the enrichment baseline and the complete coverage report are preserved in the evidence directory. The next batch will inventory existing Lean mappings and recorded scopes before continuing through the wider claim set.

Process assessment. Explicit field coverage prevents empty schema fields from looking like completed migration, while anchored source hashes avoid a full re-review after every append. The living mathematical sections and formalization gaps were reviewed and remain unchanged; only index navigation and metadata tooling change. Initial plan inspection preceded instrumentation. The checkpoint is local; Spin remains paused.

19 September 2026 — Parallel index curation exposes a false permutation-probability premise

Status: elementary counterexample and source correction; generic avoidance bound refuted, stronger reader conclusions not refuted. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and discovery. During user-authorized parallel index curation, a dependency reviewer identified a negative-association premise in the dense-label satisfaction proof. An independent source audit checked its actual use and the preceding generic matched-pair lemma. The latter had no own index record; it is now registered with retracted status and its historical text preserved. This entry gives the complete counterexample and limits its consequences precisely.

1. The permutation-matrix premise is false

Let \(\mu\) be a uniform bijection from two rows to two labels. Its only outcomes are the identity and swap, each with probability \(1/2\). Put \(X_{11}=\mathbf1_{\{\mu(1)=1\}}\) and \(X_{22}=\mathbf1_{\{\mu(2)=2\}}\). These are different matrix coordinates in different rows and columns. Both equal one for the identity and both zero for the swap. Therefore

\[ \Pr(X_{11}=1)=\Pr(X_{22}=1)=\tfrac12,\qquad \Pr(X_{11}=X_{22}=1)=\tfrac12>\tfrac14,\qquad \Pr(X_{11}=X_{22}=0)=\tfrac12>\tfrac14. \]

Thus the full matrix-entry family is not negatively associated: even two increasing coordinate functions have covariance \(1/4>0\). The decreasing-event product inequality actually used in the notebook fails as well.

More generally, fix distinct labels \(x,y\) in a uniform bijection of \(m\ge2\) rows and let \(S,T\) be allowed occupant sets. For \(A_x=\{\mu^{-1}(x)\in S\}\), \(A_y=\{\mu^{-1}(y)\in T\}\), there are \(|S||T|-|S\cap T|\) allowable ordered pairs of different occupants. Hence

\[ \Pr(A_x\cap A_y)=\frac{|S||T|-|S\cap T|}{m(m-1)},\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(\mathbf1_{A_x},\mathbf1_{A_y}) =\frac{|S||T|-m|S\cap T|}{m^2(m-1)}. \]

Disjoint nonempty sets give positive covariance, including large sets; transposition gives the same conclusion for row-specific label sets. The unary-reader setup permits arbitrary pair sets and does not impose a hypothesis that would make the asserted general negative association valid. This refutes the notebook's matrix/event interpretation. It does not assert that the cited Joag-Dev–Proschan paper contains that false statement; no new full-paper audit is claimed.

2. The stated generic exponential bound is false, even at large parameters

The old lemma claims, conditional on fixed \(Q,R'\), that every matched pair set \(P\) satisfies \(\Pr(\mu\cap P=\varnothing)\le\exp(-|P|/(n-N))\). Write \(m=n-N\). At \(m=2\), choose \(P\) to be the two diagonal pairs above. Avoidance has probability \(1/2\), whereas the claimed bound is \(e^{-1}<1/2\).

This is not merely a small-parameter failure. For any positive even \(m\), take \(P\) to be a fixed reference perfect matching of the \(m\) matched rows to the \(m\) outside labels. Avoiding \(P\) is the derangement event. Inclusion–exclusion, choosing the \(k\) fixed pairs and freely matching the other \(m-k\) rows, gives

\[ \Pr(\mu\cap P=\varnothing) =\sum_{k=0}^{m}(-1)^k\binom mk\frac{(m-k)!}{m!} =\sum_{k=0}^{m}\frac{(-1)^k}{k!}>e^{-1}. \]

For even \(m\), the difference from the absolutely convergent exponential series is

\[ \sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\left(\frac1{(m+1+2j)!}-\frac1{(m+2+2j)!}\right)>0. \]

Every summand is positive, while \(|P|/m=1\). This contradicts the exact claimed upper bound for arbitrarily large even \(m\).

Compatibility with the recorded random-flat model. Choose \(n=2^\ell\), \(N=2^{\ell_2}\) with \(1\le\ell_2<\ell\), an admissible affine flat \(Q_0\), and a residual row set \(R'_0\) of size \(N+1\). Their complements each have the positive even size \(m=n-N\). Fix a reference matching \(P\) between those complements before sampling \(\mu\), and condition on \((Q,R')=(Q_0,R'_0)\). The event has positive probability and the remaining map is exactly the uniform bijection above. There are \(m\) allowed unary pairs, giving polynomial reader size even when pins use \(O(\log n)\) bit literals. The construction also permits power-of-two polylogarithmic residual sizes at arbitrarily large \(n\).

3. What is and is not corrected

The generic avoidance lemma and the blanket matrix-entry premise are retracted. The dense-label proof has an unsupported product-bound step. Our reference-matching reader has label degree one and does not satisfy that theorem's dense-label thresholds, so it does not refute its final high-density conclusion. A valid replacement estimate with slack or extra hypotheses may exist; none is supplied by this audit.

The following directly identified passages use the same matrix/bijection inference. Their affected proof clauses must not be used unconditionally until replaced or independently justified. Unaffected subclaims, first/second-moment calculations and conditional composition statements retain their separate scope.

4. Additional direct use and the conditional-composition distinction

The final-range source review also identifies Lemma E, step (H1): decreasing events on distinct columns of a uniform injection are used to infer an exponential avoidance estimate. Disjoint columns alone do not justify that product bound. Lemma E's recorded proof therefore also requires a replacement probability argument; its final numerical statement is not refuted here. Theorem D in the same section is a conditional composition accepting a supplied round-failure bound pR; this audit does not invalidate that conditional implication. Its unconditional switching application must still justify the supplied round bound.

The pinned-wide proposal likewise imports (D1) after conditioning on pinned images. Its original concentration and alive-pin counting obligations remain, and the proposed probability step now also needs independent justification. This qualifies the proposed repair, without retracting the recorded obstruction or declaring the proposed extension impossible.

5. Correction-endpoint review

A further exact-source check identifies the two-role few-rows theorem, (K1) as another direct use: it obtains an exponential estimate by multiplying column-event probabilities of the restricted bijection. That step also needs a justified replacement. The current status of this proof is conditional, not a statement-level refutation.

The multirow, crowded-row and two-role size corollaries inherit affected round bounds. Their unconditional switching conclusions therefore also need the missing probability input. The pair-space section contains both a deterministic conditional decoder implication (Theorem D, with supplied round bound) and an unconditional application (Theorem F); the latter needs Lemma E's probability estimate. These parts must not be conflated. The per-claim scope review preserves the exact distinction, including earlier constant and tree-rule corrections. A revised constant or a correct decoder does not by itself repair a probability premise.

The other correction-endpoint review retains valid finite controls, revised support/degree statements, and conditional composition implications in their stated scopes. These are metadata clarifications of existing dated corrections, not new blanket retractions. Further descendants are an audit scope exposed by graph queries; this entry does not assert that every descendant is invalid.

19 September 2026 — Measure resume calls without confusing controls with behavior

Status: one historical observation and controlled command measurements; no demonstrated end-to-end recovery speedup. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question. Does the resume tool actually use fewer calls than the previous prose protocol? The user correctly challenged a deliberately optimized three-call simulation as insufficient evidence of normal agent behavior. This cycle separates an actual historical resume from scripted controls; the mathematical living sections and main research obligation remain unchanged.

Historical evidence. A privacy-filtered audit of this session's explicit post-compaction resume on 10 September found three tool calls, each containing one shell call, with some file reads combined. The completion response indicated readiness after about 22.3 seconds; no saved output contained a truncation marker. This was not a batching benchmark, but it is only one observation under an earlier guide/notebook. The detected reads did not include COMPUTATION_RULES.md, so its payload is not identical to the full-context simulation. It cannot establish an average or complete understanding.

Controlled results. Seven repetitions at pinned revisions gave six calls for separate old-style reads, three for deliberately batched old reads, and four for the new cached bundle. Old separate and batched output was identical: 52,863 bytes. The new tool emitted 55,105 bytes; reading the same current documents manually emitted 54,115, leaving 990 bytes of delivery overhead. Median subprocess times were 0.569 seconds for separate old reads, 0.563 for batched old reads and 0.481 for the new tool. These exclude model reasoning and tool-transport latency; they are not comparable to the historical 22.3-second full turn.

Conclusion. The earlier six-call description was an unbatched estimate, not a measured norm. Actual batching did occur, but neither one historical example nor an optimized control establishes typical performance. Bounded retryable delivery and explicit resume recording are demonstrated benefits; fewer natural tool calls, lower token use and faster overall recovery are not yet demonstrated. Future assessment should use ordinary resume observations rather than optimizing a benchmark and treating that as habitual behavior.

The evidence directory contains reproducible scripts, all trial measurements and the filtered historical counts. No transcript text, session IDs or duplicate source snapshots are committed. Initial planning/inspection preceded timing; a UTC-parsing compatibility retry is included among tool failures. No theorem or route change was produced.

20 September 2026 — Fossick: the generic subspace criterion and a narrow prose correction

Status: generalized criterion flagged for reuse; one explanatory sentence corrected, with no change to the verified theorem. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Generalization worth attention. The generic subspace-consequence theorem replaces the bit-PHP base and row-linear space by an arbitrary binary old base containing Boolean equations and an arbitrary bounded-degree polynomial subspace. Its CNF bridge and size criterion connect that broader statement to actual affine proof DAGs. Read both exact statements and the full rank-nullity/removal argument. This is more than a re-verification of the bit-PHP special case. Its application still requires a large subspace separated from old consequences at the precise degree ceiling; it is not a general size–degree or size–width theorem. No new family satisfying its hypotheses or independent novelty verdict is asserted.

A satisfiable base can have a separated subspace

Correction of explanatory prose only. The earlier criterion's Reading paragraph says that no such subspace exists for a satisfiable or easily refuted base. The satisfiable case of that sentence is false. Let the old base consist only of Boolean equations on any finite set of variables, and let U be the span of the constant polynomial one. Every PC consequence of this base evaluates to zero at the all-zero Boolean assignment: every axiom does, and evaluation respects linear combinations and variable multiplication. A nonzero constant evaluates to itself, so U intersects the old PC consequence space only in zero, at every degree ceiling. Thus U is a nonzero separated subspace over a satisfiable base.

The verified criterion assumes an actual refutation DAG and an initial-clause bridge. No such sound refutation exists for these satisfiable initials, so the implication is vacuous; the theorem and its proof are not refuted. For an old base already deriving one within the relevant degree ceiling, the separately recorded short-proof control does rule out a nonzero separated subspace. Preserve this distinction rather than silently rewriting the historical entry.

20 September 2026 — A valid matching-avoidance bound repairs dense-label satisfaction with slack

Status: working proof of a standard permanent-bound corollary and a corrected dense-label application; original false bounds remain retracted and downstream switching audits remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and endpoint. Repair the probability input exposed by the permutation audit, after the inventory-sensitive source detour found no new estimate. This cycle stops at a universal replacement and one correctly conditioned application. It does not prove the general switching conjecture or the Frege lower bound.

1. Imported permanent bound, with the entropy argument

Brégman's theorem. If a zero-one square matrix has positive row sums \(r_1,\ldots,r_m\), its number of supported permutations satisfies \(\operatorname{per}(A)\le\prod_i(r_i!)^{1/r_i}\). A zero row gives permanent zero. This is a classical theorem; the entropy proof is attributed to Radhakrishnan (1997). The publisher abstract and academy record were checked; the following argument is reconstructed here, not a claim of a full-paper audit or new theorem.

Entropy proof. If there are no supported permutations, the result is immediate. Otherwise choose a supported permutation \(\sigma\) uniformly, and independently choose a uniformly random order in which to expose its rows. For any fixed order, the entropy chain rule expresses \(\log\operatorname{per}(A)\) as the sum of conditional entropies of the images. At row \(i\), let \(K_i\) be the number of its allowed columns not used by earlier rows. The conditional entropy is at most the expected \(\log K_i\), since its conditional support is contained in those columns.

Now fix \(\sigma\) and average over the exposure order. The \(r_i\) allowed columns of row \(i\) have \(r_i\) distinct preimage rows, including \(i\). The rank of \(i\) in their random ordering is uniform; hence \(K_i\) is uniform on \(1,\ldots,r_i\). Therefore \(\mathbb E\log K_i=\log(r_i!)/r_i\). Sum over rows and exponentiate. This uses ordinary entropy of a finite distribution, not negative association of permutation entries.

2. Universal avoidance bound and sharp uniform constant

Lemma. Let \(m\ge1\), let \(\mu\) be a uniform bijection between two sets of size \(m\), and let \(P\) be any fixed set of forbidden pairs. Then

\[\Pr(\mu\cap P=\varnothing)\le 2^{-|P|/m}=\exp\!\left(-\frac{(\log 2)|P|}{m}\right).\]

Proof. Write \(d_i\) for the forbidden degree of row \(i\) and \(r_i=m-d_i\). If any \(r_i=0\), avoidance is impossible. Otherwise apply the permanent bound to the allowed matrix and divide by \(m!\). Put \(f(k)=\log(k!)/k\). For \(k\ge1\), arithmetic-geometric mean gives \(\exp f(k)\le(k+1)/2\), so

\[f(k+1)-f(k)=\frac{\log(k+1)-f(k)}{k+1}\ge\frac{\log2}{k+1}.\]

For \(1\le r\le m\), summing yields \(f(m)-f(r)\ge(m-r)\log2/m\). Consequently

\[\log\Pr(\mu\cap P=\varnothing)\le\sum_i f(r_i)-\log(m!)\le-\frac{\log2}{m}\sum_i d_i.\]

The empty forbidden set gives equality, including \(m=1\). For \(m=0\) the unique empty bijection avoids the empty set with probability one, treated separately without division. The constant \(\log2\) is best possible uniformly in positive \(m\): at \(m=2\), forbidding the two diagonal pairs gives probability \(1/2\) and \(|P|/m=1\). Thus a bound \(\exp(-c|P|/m)\) valid for every board requires \(c\le\log2\).

This replaces the retracted constant-one estimate; it does not validate that estimate or the false negative-association premise. Conditional use is valid whenever the remaining map really is a uniform bijection after the stated conditioning. Additional conditioning on avoidance or other matching-dependent events requires a new argument.

3. Corrected dense-label threshold

Use the unary-reader setting: \(F=\bigvee_{(i,x)\in P_F}[i\text{ pinned to }x]\), \(|Q|=N\), \(|R'|=N+1\), and, conditional on fixed \((Q,R')\), \(\mu'\) is a uniform bijection from the \(m=n-N>0\) matched rows to the labels outside \(Q\). Let \(S\ge1\), choose \(D^*\ge2(N+1)\), and let \(\mathcal D\) be the labels whose degree in \(P_F\) is at least \(D^*\). Define

\[\Delta_{\rm B}=N+\frac{2(n-N)\log(8S)}{(\log2)D^*}.\]

Corrected lemma. If \(|\mathcal D|\ge\Delta_{\rm B}\), some term of \(F\) is satisfied by \(\mu'\) with conditional probability at least \(1-1/(8S)\), for every fixed admissible \((Q,R')\).

Proof. At least \(|\mathcal D|-N\) dense labels lie outside \(Q\). Each has at least \(D^*-(N+1)\ge D^*/2\) pinned rows outside \(R'\). These are distinct pairs, even when their row sets overlap. Let \(P\) consist of all those remaining pairs. Then \(|P|\ge(|\mathcal D|-N)D^*/2\). A matching hitting any of them satisfies a unary term. Apply the preceding lemma to obtain failure probability at most

\[\exp\!\left(-\frac{(\log2)(|\mathcal D|-N)D^*}{2(n-N)}\right)\le\frac1{8S}.\]

The new threshold multiplies only the old threshold's logarithmic term by \(1/\log2\). Thus its previously used polylogarithmic size remains polylogarithmic under the same asymptotic parameter choices. For at most \(S\) fixed readers satisfying the corrected threshold, a union bound gives total failure at most \(1/8\); no independence between readers is assumed. This is not yet a renewed full unary switching theorem: its other concentration and decoder clauses must be checked with the changed threshold. The original dense-label statement at its smaller threshold remains conditional, not declared false or silently rewritten.

4. Evidence, scope and next obligation

The compiled checker exhausts all 66,066 forbidden boards for \(m=1,2,3,4\). If \(a\) permutations avoid the board, it checks \(a^m2^{|P|}\le(m!)^m\) in integers. Every case passes; the full board counts and comparisons, reproduction instructions, and source attribution are retained. The universal proof does not depend on finite enumeration. No Lean verification was run.

Main-route assessment. A shared probability input now has a valid replacement, and dense-label satisfaction has an unconditional corrected version. This repairs a usable part of the parked literal route, not its general reader bound or the source-compatibility obligation. Next audit the full unary switching theorem with the modified threshold, including its random-flat and decoder hypotheses, before propagating any status changes. The chance that this repair extends to additional affected estimates seems good; its chance of supplying the missing general Frege step remains low and unquantified.

Process assessment. Replacing a false dependence assertion by a permanent bound produced a concrete repair; test one application before expanding the audit. Keep the shared rules unchanged.

20 September 2026 — Unary switching survives the probability repair

Status: working corrected unary-only switching theorem and polynomial-family corollary; no mixed-tail composition or general literal/parity-reader theorem. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Task and endpoint. Check the full unary-reader application after the matching-avoidance repair. The endpoint is a correct probability and tree-height statement for unary readers, with every source-wide union bound counted. This repairs existing restricted work; it does not discharge the main Frege obligation.

1. Corrected finite-parameter theorem

Let \(n=2^\ell\), \(N=2^{\ell_2}<n\), and choose a uniform affine \(\ell_2\)-flat \(Q\subseteq\mathbb F_2^\ell\), an independent uniform \((N+1)\)-subset \(R'\) of the \(n+1\) pigeons, and a conditional uniform bijection \(\mu':R'^c\to Q^c\). A unary reader is the disjunction of the row-label pins in a fixed set \(P_F\), chosen before this restriction. Take integers \(1\le k_1<n\), \(k_2\ge2\), a real \(S\ge1\), and put

\[D^*=\frac{k_1(n-k_1)}{2e(N+1)N},\qquad \Delta_{\rm B}=N+\frac{2(n-N)\log(8S)}{(\log2)D^*},\qquad r_2=\lceil\log_2 k_2\rceil+1.\]

Assume \(D^*\ge2(N+1)\). Then, with probability at least

\[1-\frac1{8S}-2^{-k_1}-\Delta_{\rm B}^{k_2}(N/n)^{r_2},\]

the restricted reader has a pigeon-and-hole-query matching tree of height at most \(k_1+k_2\). Its 1-leaves contain a satisfied pin; on each 0-leaf all pins are falsified or annihilated by the functional residual Boolean/exclusion equations. Hole queries include the empty outcome. If the displayed lower probability bound is negative it is only a vacuous bound, not an extra hypothesis.

Proof: dense labels. Let \(\mathcal D\) contain the labels with pin degree at least \(D^*\). If \(|\mathcal D|\ge\Delta_{\rm B}\), the corrected satisfaction lemma, conditional on every \((Q,R')\), leaves failure probability at most \(1/(8S)\). On its success a single 1-leaf suffices. The remaining case has the deterministic bound \(|\mathcal D|<\Delta_{\rm B}\).

Sparse matching count. Let \(B_{\rm sp}\) consist of pins with a sparse label and both endpoints residual. If \(k_1>N\), it cannot have a matching of size \(k_1\). Otherwise fix \(Q\). For a set of \(k_1\) sparse labels in \(Q\), the number of choices of distinct pinned rows is at most the product of their degrees. For any such distinct row set, the independent uniform \(R'\) contains it with probability \((N+1)_{k_1}/(n+1)_{k_1}\le((N+1)/(n+1-k_1))^{k_1}\). Thus the expected number of these matchings is at most

\[\left(\frac{N+1}{n+1-k_1}\right)^{k_1}\binom N{k_1}(D^*)^{k_1}\le\left(\frac{eN(N+1)D^*}{k_1(n+1-k_1)}\right)^{k_1}\le2^{-k_1}.\]

Existence of a matching contributes at least one to the count, proving the failure bound. This is the existing argument; it uses neither independence of permutation entries nor concentration of a random affine flat.

Dense labels in the flat. For a fixed \(k_2\)-set \(X\subseteq\mathcal D\) of affine dimension \(d\), \(2^d\ge k_2\). If \(d>\ell_2\), inclusion in \(Q\) is impossible. Otherwise choose \(d+1\) affinely independent points in \(X\). Counting successive extensions of their affine spans gives

\[\Pr[X\subseteq Q]\le\frac Nn\prod_{t=0}^{d-1}\frac{N-2^t}{n-2^t}\le(N/n)^{d+1}\le(N/n)^{r_2}.\]

The first factor places the first point; at stage \(t\) the already spanned flat contains \(2^t\) points. This also makes the dimension convention explicit. Union over at most \(|\mathcal D|^{k_2}\) subsets proves \(\Pr[|\mathcal D\cap Q|\ge k_2]\le\Delta_{\rm B}^{k_2}(N/n)^{r_2}\). If \(k_2>N\), the event is empty. This is the recorded affine-rank estimate, with its counting spelled out.

The tree. Outside those events, the alive pin graph \(B\subseteq R'\times Q\) has matching number \(\nu(B)\le\nu(B_{\rm sp})+|\mathcal D\cap Q|<k_1+k_2\). It has a vertex cover of size \(\nu(B)\). For completeness, start from a maximum matching and follow alternating paths from unmatched row vertices. The nonreachable rows together with reachable columns form a cover: any edge from a reachable row reaches its column, while a matched edge couples reachability of its endpoints. No unmatched column is reachable, or an augmenting path would contradict maximality. Exactly one endpoint from every matched edge belongs to this cover and no unmatched vertex does, so its size is the matching size.

Query the cover vertices in a fixed order, skipping vertices already decided by the partial matching. A pigeon query either hits a pin, giving a 1-leaf, or disposes of all pins in that row. A hole query branches on its uncovered occupant rows and on the affine factor \(u_x=1-\sum_jX_{jx}\). A pin hit gives a 1-leaf; other occupant outcomes dispose of that column by exclusions, and the empty outcome annihilates each \(X_{ix}\), since \(X_{ix}u_x=X_{ix}-X_{ix}^2-\sum_{j\ne i}X_{ix}X_{jx}\). Already covered pigeons are handled by row exclusions. Branches inconsistent with earlier empty-hole outcomes have zero path product and may be pruned. Thus every remaining pin is disposed of by a cover vertex; all other pins were already falsified or annihilated by the restriction. The hole-node identities give the leaf partition and idempotence modulo the residual base without an onto axiom. Each path has at most the cover size queries and a product of that many affine factors. Union of the three failure events proves the theorem.

2. One restriction for every unary reader in a polynomial family

Corollary. Fix \(c>0\) and a fixed polylogarithmic upper bound on \(N\). For any at most \(S\le n^c\) fixed unary readers, choose

\[k_1=\lceil\log_2(16S)\rceil,\qquad k_2=2^{\lceil c\rceil+2}.\]

For all sufficiently large admissible \(n\), a common restriction gives every reader the preceding tree of height at most \(k_1+k_2\) with probability at least \(3/4\). The ceiling on \(c\) ensures an integer parameter.

Proof and budget. We have \(k_1=O(\log n)\) and \(D^*\ge2(N+1)\) eventually. Since \(\log(8S)/k_1\le\log2\),

\[\Delta_{\rm B}\le N+4e(N+1)N\frac{n-N}{n-k_1}\le N+8e(N+1)N\]

eventually, uniformly over \(1\le S\le n^c\). Therefore \(\Delta_{\rm B}=O(N^2)\) is polylogarithmic, and \(r_2=\lceil c\rceil+3\). Union over all readers costs at most \(1/8\) for dense satisfaction and \(S2^{-k_1}\le1/16\) for sparse matchings. The third term is at most

\[S\Delta_{\rm B}^{k_2}(N/n)^{r_2}\le n^{c-\lceil c\rceil-3}\operatorname{polylog}(n)=o(1),\]

hence at most \(1/16\) eventually. Total failure is at most \(1/4\). Reader events need not be independent. This restores the old unary-only qualitative polynomial-family conclusion with corrected finite-parameter constants.

3. Scope, verification and remaining gap

This corrects only the unary part of the earlier theorem and its grouped corollaries. It does not restore its smaller finite threshold, its separate-light-term decoder composition, or mixed pinned/light readers. In particular the two-role warning and composition correction remain relevant outside this unary-only result. Other matching-avoidance applications must check their own conditional distribution and constants.

Verification. Re-read the exact sparse-count, affine-flat, dense-label and hole-node arguments; the finite parameter proof above handles integer and empty-event cases explicitly. The prior exhaustive avoidance checks are reused as supporting evidence, not rerun or called fresh verification. No new computation or Lean proof was needed. The registry keeps the original combined claim conditional and adds the corrected unary statement separately.

Main-route assessment. A restricted but useful switching input is repaired for all fixed polynomial source sizes. The general-step obligation remains open: arbitrary mixed/parity readers and source-compatible composition are not supplied. Next inspect one mixed reader's use of matching avoidance after conditioning, to determine whether the same repair survives there; stop if its event is no longer a fixed forbidden board under a uniform bijection. The probability-repair line has now delivered its first complete restricted application, but its chance of reaching the missing general reader theorem is still low.

20 September 2026 — Mixed-reader loading estimates without negative association

Status: working repairs of out-loading and many-out-row satisfaction, plus a direct upper-tail count; full mixed-reader switching and decoder composition remain unaudited. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and stopping point. Does the repaired avoidance estimate apply after the actual conditioning used for full single-row mixed classes? Yes: a dummy-slot bijection preserves that distribution. This cycle proves the scoped satisfaction estimates and separately checks the positive row-hit bound used in the bounded-loading argument. No complete mixed-reader theorem is claimed.

1. Dummy slots give the corrected out-loading estimate

A full class \(\tau=(j_\tau,p_\tau,x_\tau)\) contains the terms \([i\mapsto x_\tau]\wedge[p_\tau\text{ on row }j_\tau]\) for every \(i\ne j_\tau\). Multiple classes may share a tail row. Write \(C(p)\) for the labels satisfying the pattern. As in the original setting, for fixed \(Q\) put

\[A_j(Q)=\left(\bigcup_{\tau:j_\tau=j,\ x_\tau\notin Q}(C(p_\tau)\setminus\{x_\tau\})\right)\setminus Q,\qquad E_Q=\sum_j|A_j(Q)|.\]

Corrected lemma. In the random-flat restriction, conditional on \(Q\) alone,

\[\Pr[\text{no term satisfied}\mid Q]\le 2^{-E_Q/(n+1)}.\]

Distribution and proof. Add \(N+1\) distinct dummy slots to the \(n-N\) real labels in \(Q^c\). A uniform bijection of all \(n+1\) rows to these \(n+1\) slots induces exactly the original conditional law: rows sent to dummy slots form a uniform \((N+1)\)-set \(R'\), and the remaining bijection to \(Q^c\) is uniform. Each original pair \((R',\mu')\) has exactly \((N+1)!\) dummy completions.

Forbid the pairs \((j,y)\) with \(y\in A_j(Q)\), and no dummy pair. The board is fixed after conditioning on \(Q\). If it is hit, row \(j\) receives a real label \(y\in C(p_\tau)\), with \(y\ne x_\tau\) and \(x_\tau\notin Q\), for some class. The real label \(x_\tau\) has an occupant \(i\ne j\). The full class contains that pin, so its term is satisfied. Therefore no satisfaction implies board avoidance; the universal bound at size \(n+1\) gives the result. No row-event product inequality is used.

For \(c>0\) and \(n>1\), the event that no term is satisfied and \(E_Q\ge(c+1)(n+1)\log n/\log2\) consequently has unconditional probability at most \(n^{-c-1}\). This is the precise joint-event assertion: it is not a claim about the distribution after additionally conditioning on no satisfaction. It replaces the logarithmic threshold in the old estimate by the factor \(1/\log2\).

2. Many out-rows still force satisfaction

Suppose each tail pattern has at most \(w\) consistent Boolean literals, so \(|C(p)|\ge n2^{-w}\), and assume \(N+1\le n2^{-w}/2\) and \(n\ge2\). Let \(J_{\rm out}(Q)\) be the rows hosting at least one class with label outside \(Q\). Every such row has \(|A_j(Q)|\ge n2^{-w}-N-1\ge n2^{-w}/2\). The preceding bound gives

\[\Pr[\text{no term satisfied}\mid Q]\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{(\log2)|J_{\rm out}(Q)|2^{-w}}3\right),\]

since \(n/(2(n+1))\ge1/3\). Thus \(|J_{\rm out}(Q)|\ge 3(c+1)2^w\log n/\log2\) suffices for failure at most \(n^{-c-1}\). This is the recorded implication with the corrected constant and explicit numerical hypothesis. Inconsistent patterns can be discarded as zero terms; they must not be counted among these out-rows.

3. Positive row events have a direct factorial-moment bound

Lemma. Let \(\pi\) be a uniform bijection of \(m\ge1\) rows to \(m\) slots. For fixed sets \(A_i\) of slots let \(X=|\{i:\pi(i)\in A_i\}|\), \(a_i=|A_i|\), and \(\lambda=\sum_i a_i/m\). For \(1\le k\le m\),

\[\Pr[X\ge k]\le\frac{e_k(a_1,\ldots,a_m)}{(m)_k}\le\frac{(m\lambda)^k}{k!(m)_k}.\]

Indeed \(\mathbb E\binom Xk\) sums the probabilities that each fixed \(k\)-set of rows hits its set. The restriction of a uniform bijection to these rows is uniform among \((m)_k\) injections, and at most the product of their \(a_i\)'s are admissible. Summing gives the first bound. Expanding \((\sum a_i)^k\) counts each product on distinct indices \(k!\) times and also nonnegative repeated-index terms, proving the second. Since \(\binom Xk\ge1\) on \(X\ge k\), it bounds the probability.

When \(k\le m/2\), use \((m)_k\ge(m/2)^k\) and \(k!\ge(k/e)^k\) to obtain \(\Pr[X\ge k]\le(2e\lambda/k)^k\). In particular \(k\ge4e\lambda\) gives \(\Pr[X\ge k]\le2^{-k}\). The factorial inequality follows by summing \(\log j\) and comparing with \(\int_1^k\log x\,dx\). For \(k>m\), the event is empty.

Scope of the bounded-loading repair. Conditional on \(Q\), take the dummy-slot model and \(A_j=U_j\setminus Q\), where \(U_j\) is the fixed union of consistent label sets on row \(j\). Then \(\lambda\le\Lambda(F)=\sum_j|U_j|/n\). For integer \(k\le(n+1)/2\) and \(k\ge4e\lambda_0\), the assumption \(\Lambda(F)\le\lambda_0\) gives \(2^{-k}\). This repairs step (ii) of the bounded-loading proof in that range. Choosing also \(k\ge(c+1)\log_2 n\) gives \(n^{-c-1}\). The residual-hosting-row estimate, parameter regime and decoder in that theorem still need their own checks; this lemma does not silently reinstate the whole theorem.

4. What has changed

The out-loading and out-row arguments now use the correct conditional law, and the positive-event estimate has an elementary counting substitute. These results allow arbitrary overlap between row sets of admissible labels; they do not assume negative association. For non-full classes, a tail hit need not make its pinned class satisfied, and an additional occupancy argument is required. Conditioning on already exposed assignments preserves uniformity on the remaining slots, but conditioning on arbitrary events about the same matching does not.

The old statements retain their original statuses and constants; these are separate scoped replacements. No numerical or Lean verification was needed: the exact dummy-completion count and factorial moment argument provide the evidence. The next cycle audits the complete single-row full-class heavy-round bound with the corrected out-row constant, while retaining the separate decoder-composition warning. Stop at the round bound or a precise failure, not a claim for all literal readers.

Main-route assessment. More shared probability inputs have been repaired, but the general source/Frege step remains open. The prospect of repairing the full-class round estimate is good; that is a restricted intermediate result, not an estimate that the general reader problem is solved.

Process assessment. Separating negative events (permanents) from positive events (injection counts) avoided another blanket dependence assertion. No additional framework guidance is needed.
