20 September 2026 — Repair the full single-row heavy-round bound, without claiming a decoder

Status: working repaired heavy-round theorem; two proof-bookkeeping gaps isolated. No automatic switching composition, non-full classes or multi-row tails. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Task. Audit the single-row full-class estimate after repairing matching probabilities. The argument can be repaired with explicit slack and nonempty survivor bookkeeping. The resulting theorem concerns rounds of the both-endpoints tree, not a decoder or a new Frege lower bound.

1. Empty good pairs cannot be charged to a surviving label

The old proof calls \((j,z)\) light-good if \(L_j(z)\cap X_L\setminus\{z\}\subseteq Q\), including the empty set, then charges every such pair to a light label of \(Q\). This pointwise assertion is false. Take one full class on row \(j\), with light pattern containing its label \(x\), and a flat omitting \(x\). The only light label is \(x\). At answer \(z=x\), the pair is good and small but has no surviving label, while \(u_{\rm s}(Q)=0\). The pattern may be one bit at all sufficiently large parameters; this is not an inconsistent-pattern example. It refutes that bookkeeping assertion, not the full theorem's final probability conclusion.

The repair below uses \(M_j(z)=L_j(z)\cap X_L\setminus\{z\}\) and counts only \(M_j(z)\ne\varnothing\). Such answers are exactly the possible contributors of new light trigger holes.

2. A separate small-label corollary has an insufficient union budget

The small-label-set corollary uses \(|X|\le n^{2/3}\) and claims \(|X|^{c+4}(N/n)^{c+4}\le n^{-c-1}\). Substituting its stated maximum gives \(N^{c+4}n^{-(c+4)/3}\), which does not imply the claimed bound when \(c>1/2\); for \(c=1\) even \(N\ge1\) leaves \(N^5n^{-5/3}>n^{-2}\). This identifies a proof-budget gap, not a counterexample to the final probability statement. The deterministic trigger-label observation remains valid for the corrected both-endpoints rule. The proof below uses only fixed polylogarithmic-sized label sets in its analogous union bounds, and does not import that corollary.

3. Corrected theorem and parameters

Fix \(c>0\). Use the uniform random-flat restriction with \(n=2^\ell\), \(N=2^{\ell_2}<n\), and \(N\) bounded by a fixed power of \(\log n\). Classes are full: \((j,p,x)\) contains every term \([i\mapsto x]\wedge[p\text{ on }j]\) for \(i\ne j\). Tail patterns are consistent and have width at most \(w\), with \(2^w\le n^{1/3}\); arbitrary classes may share a row. Set

\[K=2^{\lceil c\rceil+4},\quad r=\log_2K+1=\lceil c\rceil+5,\quad \lambda=\frac{3(c+3)\log n}{\log2},\quad q_0=\lceil2c+6\rceil,\quad \theta=\frac1{2048eK}.\]

Assume \(N\ge2048eK^2\lambda+128(q_0+2)K\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), depending on the fixed parameters and polylogarithmic bound, with probability at least \(1-8n^{-c-1}\), every path of the canonical both-endpoints tree with matched-first preference has fewer than \(N/48\) heavy rounds, hence fewer than \(N/24\) heavy queries, before its first 1-leaf. The same conclusion holds simultaneously for any at most \(n^c\) fixed readers with failure at most \(8/n\). The required lower bound on \(N\) is polylogarithmic and nonvacuous.

Definitions. Retain the old label loading \(u(x)=\sum_j|U_{x,j}|/n\). Heavy labels have \(u(x)\ge\lambda\), the others are light. Let \(M_j(z)=L_j(z)\cap X_L\setminus\{z\}\). Call a pair small if \(0<|M_j(z)|<K\), and define the deterministic quantities

\[\Lambda=\frac{|\{(j,z):M_j(z)\ne\varnothing\}|}{n},\quad v(x)=\frac{|\{(j,z)\text{ small}:x\in M_j(z)\}|}{n},\quad V=\sum_{x\in X_L}v(x).\]

Then \(v(x)\le u(x)<\lambda\) for light labels and \(V\le K\Lambda\). Write \(v(Q)=\sum_{x\in Q\cap X_L}v(x)\). These definitions exclude the self-only answers responsible for the earlier gap.

Fixed-set fact. If a deterministic label set \(A\) meets \(Q\) in at least \(K\) points, that intersection contains \(r\) affinely independent points. The affine inclusion count therefore bounds its probability by \(|A|^r(N/n)^r\). If \(A\) has polylogarithmic size this is at most \(n^{-c-2}\) eventually. A fixed set of at least \(K\) points being wholly contained in \(Q\) has probability at most \((N/n)^r\), without a union over its subsets.

(1) Heavy labels. For a heavy \(x\notin Q\), forbidding the pairs \((j,z)\) with \(z\in U_{x,j}\setminus(Q\cup\{x\})\) forces satisfaction whenever hit, by fullness. Each nonempty \(U_{x,j}\) has size at least \(n2^{-w}\ge2(N+1)\) eventually. The dummy-slot avoidance argument gives failure at most \(\exp(-(\log2)u(x)/3)\le n^{-c-3}\). Union over at most \(n\) labels costs \(n^{-c-2}\). Outside that event, a reader with no satisfied term has every heavy label in \(Q\). If there are at least \(K\) heavy labels, that containment is a fixed-set event of probability at most \((N/n)^r\). Hence fewer than \(K\) heavy labels can contribute, apart from two exceptional events.

(2) Good answers are small. A pair with \(|M_j(z)|\ge K\) has \(M_j(z)\subseteq Q\) with probability at most \((N/n)^r\). Union over \(n(n+1)\) pairs costs at most \(n^{-c-2}\) eventually. Outside that event every nonempty good pair is small.

(3) Effective loading. Apply the out-loading bound only to light classes. Except with probability \(n^{-c-2}\), if no term is satisfied its outside-pair count is at most \((c+2)(n+1)\log n/\log2\). Each pair counted by \(n\Lambda\) either has \(z\in Q\), is nonempty good, or belongs to that outside board. There are at most \(N(n+1)\) pairs of the first kind, and, on event (2), at most \(nv(Q)\) of the second, since each is charged to at least one \(x\in M_j(z)\subseteq Q\). Thus, eventually,

\[\Lambda\le v(Q)+\frac{n+1}{n}\left(N+\frac{(c+2)\log n}{\log2}\right)\le v(Q)+3N.\]

(4) The light loading of the flat. If \(V\le8NK\), the deterministic set \(A_\theta=\{x:v(x)\ge\theta\}\) has size at most \(8NK/\theta\), hence polylogarithmic. Outside its fixed-set event it meets \(Q\) in fewer than \(K\) labels, giving \(v(Q)\le N\theta+\lambda K\). If \(V>8NK\), then \(\Lambda\ge V/K>8N\), so (3) forces \(v(Q)\ge V/(2K)\). The deterministic set \(A=\{x:v(x)\ge V/(4KN)\}\) has size at most \(4KN\). Its complement contributes at most \(V/(4K)\) to \(v(Q)\), while each label of \(A\) contributes less than \(\lambda\). Consequently \(|A\cap Q|>V/(4K\lambda)>2N/\lambda\ge K\), another fixed-set exceptional event. The cases depend on deterministic \(V\), so one such event suffices. On their complements, a reader with no satisfaction obeys \(v(Q)\le N\theta+\lambda K\).

(5) Matched contributing rows. For fixed \(Q\), let \(G_j=\{z\in Q^c:\varnothing\ne M_j(z)\subseteq Q\}\). On (2), \(\sum_j|G_j|/n\le v(Q)\). Use the row-hit tail in the dummy-slot bijection with \(a=\lceil N/(192K)\rceil\). Eventually \(a\le(n+1)/2\); when \(v(Q)\le N\theta+\lambda K\),

\[\frac{2e\,v(Q)}a\le384eK\theta+\frac{384eK^2\lambda}{N}\le\frac38<\frac12.\]

Also \(a\ge(c+2)\log_2n\), so the chance of at least \(a\) matched contributing rows is at most \(n^{-c-2}\). This conditional estimate is applied only to deterministic conditions on \(Q\), then integrated; it is not conditioned on no satisfaction or on a matching-dependent event.

(6) Residual contributing rows. A residual tail row contributing a light trigger hole hosts a light label in \(Q\). These rows lie in a fixed-given-\(Q\) set of size at most \(N\lambda\,2^w\), since \(|J_x|\le2^wu(x)\). Independence of \(R'\) and \(Q\) bounds the probability of at least \(q_0\) such residual rows by

\[\left(\frac{eN\lambda n^{1/3}(N+1)}{q_0(n+1-q_0)}\right)^{q_0}=\operatorname{polylog}(n)n^{-2q_0/3}\le n^{-c-2}\]

eventually. This uses uniform-subset counting, not permutation-entry association.

Counting rounds. If a term is already satisfied by the initial restriction, matched-first preference prevents any heavy round before a 1-leaf: that matched term remains available. Otherwise the preceding bad-event analysis applies. Immediately before a heavy round, matched-first preference excludes any already satisfied full-class term. Every assigned tail row that can contribute a new trigger hole therefore has its nonempty survivor set contained in \(Q\): an outside surviving label has a different matched occupant and would yield a preferred satisfied term. A new trigger cannot be the row's own assigned label, which is already used or outside \(Q\). Each contributing row thus supplies fewer than \(K\) light holes by (2). The both-endpoints rule makes trigger holes distinct. Hence every path before its first 1-leaf has fewer than

\[K+K(a+q_0)\le\frac N{192}+(q_0+2)K\le\frac N{192}+\frac N{128}<\frac N{48}\]

rounds. There are seven exceptional events, each at most \(n^{-c-2}\) eventually; the stated \(8n^{-c-1}\) bound has slack. This counting is simultaneous over paths; no union over paths is used. Union over at most \(n^c\) fixed readers gives the final assertion.

4. Scope and review

The theorem repairs a restricted heavy-round estimate at enlarged parameters and with corrected definitions. It does not assert the invalid adaptive-tree count, the original numerical constants, or automatic switching for rows with two roles. The separate composition obligation remains. The older small-label-set probability corollary is now qualified for its union-budget gap; its deterministic trigger observation survives. The empty-good-pair example corrects a proof clause, not a mathematical refutation of all full-class conclusions.

Review and evidence. The complete proof above checks nonempty charging, fixed-versus-matching-dependent conditioning, integer thresholds, all seven exception budgets and both-endpoints query accounting. Source inputs were read directly: the six-event argument, loading definitions, matched-first preference, corrected tree rule, and the three repaired probability estimates. No new computation or Lean verification was needed.

Main-route assessment. The full single-row restricted round bound is repaired. General source compatibility, arbitrary non-full/multi-row readers and the decoder remain open. Before another application audit, the next cycle reviews which remaining general obligation this repair can realistically advance; a growing list of repaired subclasses is not the main lower bound.

Process assessment. Explicitly defining the counted pairs exposed a gap that changing a probability constant alone would have missed. Keep this practice in the existing hypothesis-and-cost review; no additional framework rule is warranted.

Status: route review, correction of a rediscovery assessment, and working rank-one relative cubic-kernel exclusion; no degree-three hardness theorem. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Thus another list of subclass repairs is not the selected main task. Preserve these tools and return only for a concrete required use.

Correction to the preceding audit's assessment. The small-label exponent issue recorded in the last entry is a rediscovery of the earlier rank-step correction. That correction already gives the label-set corollary with its larger threshold. I missed the link in the existing index assessment and incorrectly marked the corrected reading conditional. The index now restores the corrected scope and labels my audit as a rediscovery. The original smaller constant is still unsupported, and the new full-class proof is unchanged. This corrects my attribution and status handling, not its mathematics.

Test a rank stratification by the number of linear-times-conflict-quadratic summands. The first stratum admits the bound below using existing two-form estimates. This is a nontrivial test of the proposed counting method, not a declaration that (HW) or all degree-three falls are handled.

1. Random restriction does not collapse a high-rank conflict form to rank two

Use the exact two-form setup over \(\mathbb F_2\): \(V=V'/\Theta\), \(v=\dim V=N^2-1\), and \(\bar K\subseteq\Lambda^2V\) is the image of the span of conflicting cell pairs. Write

\[k=\dim\bar K=\frac{(N+1)(2N^2-3N+2)}2.\]

An element of \(\Lambda^2V\) is an alternating form on \(V^*\). Let \(N\ge3\), let \(U\subseteq V^*\) be uniform of integer dimension \(2\le d\le v\), and let \(s\ge1\). Assume

\[d\ge12N+8\log_2N+2s,\qquad \binom{d-1}2\ge k+d+\frac{(\log_2(d-1))^2}{6}+s.\]

Working lemma. With probability at least \(1-8\cdot2^{-s}\), every nonzero \(\kappa\in\bar K\) remains nonzero on \(U\), and every \(\kappa\in\bar K\) of original rank at least four has restricted rank at least four.

Reduce small restricted rank to an isotropic hyperplane. If \(\kappa|_U\) has rank at most two, \(U\) has an isotropic hyperplane of dimension \(d-1\): at rank two take its radical plus a line in the two-dimensional symplectic quotient; at rank zero take any hyperplane. There are \(2^d-1\) hyperplanes in \(U\). A uniform one inside a uniform \(U\) is itself a uniform \((d-1)\)-subspace of \(V^*\), by invariance under invertible linear maps. Therefore, for fixed \(\kappa\),

\[\Pr[\operatorname{rank}(\kappa|_U)\le2]\le(2^d-1)\Pr[\kappa|_L=0],\qquad \dim L=d-1.\]

Low original ranks. Put \(A=6N+4\log_2N-4\). The recorded R3 count gives at most \(2^{A\rho}\) conflict forms of rank \(2\rho\), since \(\binom v{2\rho}\le v^{2\rho}\le2^{4\rho\log_2N}\). R1 at dimension \(d-1\), multiplied by the hyperplane count, bounds the contribution from \(2\le\rho\le d-2\) by

\[2.39\sum_{\rho=2}^{d-2}2^{f(\rho)},\qquad f(\rho)=d+A\rho+\frac{\rho(\rho+1)}2-\rho(d-1).\]

Terms outside the ambient rank range are simply absent. Now \(f(2)=2A+5-d\le-3-2s\), and

\[f(\rho)-f(2)=(\rho-2)\left(A-d+\frac{\rho+5}2\right)\le-(\rho-2)(s+5/2),\]

using \(d\ge2A+8+2s\) and \(\rho\le d-2\). The geometric sum is at most \(2\), so this contribution is at most \(4.78\cdot2^{-3-2s}\le2^{-s}\).

High original ranks. At \(\rho\ge d-1\), apply R2 to \(L\) of dimension \(d-1\), which is at most \(v-1\). There are at most \(2^k\) such forms in total. The contribution is at most

\[6\cdot2^{k+d+(\log_2(d-1))^2/6-\binom{d-1}2}\le6\cdot2^{-s}.\]

Thus original rank at least four collapses to rank at most two with probability at most \(7\cdot2^{-s}\). Finally, original rank-two forms vanish with probability at most \(2.39\cdot2^{A+1-d}\le2^{-s}\), by R3 and R1 directly at dimension \(d\). These exhaust all nonzero ranks and prove the lemma. The R1–R3 statements and proofs were reread; this argument reuses them, not a fresh verification of the historical finite runs.

2. All linear-times-conflict-quadratic kernels are trivial on that event

Let \(W=U^\perp\subseteq V\), and let \(W\wedge\bar K\) denote the span of \(w\wedge\kappa\), \(w\in W\), \(\kappa\in\bar K\). On the preceding lemma's good event, for every \(a\in V\) and \(\kappa\in\bar K\),

\[(a\wedge\kappa)|_U=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad a\wedge\kappa\in W\wedge\bar K.\]

Proof. If \(\kappa=0\), the conclusion is immediate. An alternating two-form of rank at least four has zero linear exterior annihilator: if a nonzero \(b\) obeys \(b\wedge\eta=0\), extend \(b\) to a basis; comparison of terms not containing \(b\) gives \(\eta=b\wedge t\), of rank at most two. Hence when \(\kappa\) has original rank at least four, its restriction still has rank at least four and the premise forces \(a|_U=0\). Thus \(a\in W\), as required.

If \(\kappa\) has rank two, write \(\kappa=b\wedge c\). Its restriction is nonzero, so \(b|_U,c|_U\) are independent. The premise implies \(a|_U\) lies in their span. Choose \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb F_2\) such that \(w=a-\alpha b-\beta c\in W\). Then \(a\wedge\kappa=w\wedge\kappa\in W\wedge\bar K\). This covers every \(a\) simultaneously, without union-bounding over its \(2^v\) possible choices.

Why this is a relative count. The earlier decomposable calculation handles a cubic with a decomposable conflict two-form. Here the quadratic factor may have arbitrary rank; the rank-collapse estimate removes the new cases uniformly. The conclusion excludes the first stratum of the unwanted event, not all cubic forms. A sum \(\sum_i a_i\wedge\kappa_i\) may vanish by cancellation even though none of its summands does. Injectivity on this generating class is not injectivity on its linear span.

Parameter scope. Taking \(s\) of order \(\log N\), the displayed sufficient conditions permit \(d=\sqrt2N^{3/2}(1+o(1))\), with a suitable positive lower-order margin, the same leading scale as the existing degree-two estimate. No sharp threshold for cubic kernels is claimed. The calculation concerns a uniform subspace and the recorded conflict ideal; it gives neither degree-three PC hardness nor structured-source avoidance without the remaining multi-summand argument.

20 September 2026 — A uniform growing range of relative cubic ranks

Status: working deterministic lifting criterion and probabilistic exclusion through a growing factor-rank range; unrestricted cubic kernels and degree-three hardness remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question. Can the preceding single-product argument control cancellation uniformly, rather than treating ranks one, two, three separately? The answer below covers a growing range by one estimate. It still leaves arbitrary-rank cubic kernels uncontrolled, so the stopping point is the explicit range and its remaining counting cost.

1. A deterministic criterion over any field

Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional over any field, \(K\subseteq\Lambda^2V\), and \(\pi:V\to E\) a linear map with kernel \(W\). Write \(\pi_j=\Lambda^j\pi\). The support of a two-form is the image of its contraction map \(V^*\to V\); its dimension is its alternating rank and the form belongs to the exterior square of that support. For \(\xi\in V\wedge K\), define its K-factor rank as the least number of summands \(a_i\wedge\kappa_i\), \(a_i\in V\), \(\kappa_i\in K\), in a representation of \(\xi\).

Lemma. Fix an integer \(R\ge1\). Suppose:

  1. If \(\kappa\in K\) has rank greater than \(2R\), then \(\pi_2\kappa\) also has rank greater than \(2R\).
  2. For every tuple of at most \(R\) elements of \(K\), each of rank at most \(2R\), the map \(\pi\) is injective on the sum of their supports.

Then every \(\xi\) of K-factor rank at most \(R\) with \(\pi_3\xi=0\) lies in \(W\wedge K\). The latter denotes a linear span; the conclusion is not merely that each summand vanishes separately.

Proof. Choose a tensor \(T=\sum_{i=1}^R a_i\otimes\kappa_i\in V\otimes K\) whose exterior product is \(\xi\), padding by zeros if needed. Factor \((\pi\otimes1)T\) as \(\sum_{i=1}^t b_i\otimes\eta_i\), \(t\le R\), with both lists linearly independent. This is an ordinary rank factorization of a tensor. Choose lifts of the \(b_i\) to \(V\). The difference from \(T\) lies in \(W\otimes K\), so its exterior product lies in \(W\wedge K\). If \(t=0\) we are done.

Let \(S=\operatorname{span}\{b_i\}\). The relation \(\sum_i b_i\wedge\pi_2\eta_i=0\), projected onto the component with one S-coordinate and two coordinates in a complement of S, shows that every \(\pi_2\eta_i\) belongs to \(S\wedge E\). Such a two-form has rank at most \(2t\): in an adapted basis its complementary-complementary block is zero and its matrix has rank at most twice \(\dim S\). By hypothesis 1 each \(\eta_i\) has original rank at most \(2R\).

Let \(H\) be the sum of their supports. Hypothesis 2 makes \(\pi\) injective on \(H\), so \(\pi_2\) is injective on \(\Lambda^2H\), and the forms \(\pi_2\eta_i\) are linearly independent. Decompose \(E=\pi(H)\oplus E'\). In the same cubic relation, the component with one E'-coordinate and two \(\pi(H)\)-coordinates is \(\sum_i(b_i)_{E'}\otimes\pi_2\eta_i=0\). Independence forces all \((b_i)_{E'}=0\). Thus every \(b_i\) lifts to an \(h_i\in H\). Now \(\sum_i h_i\wedge\eta_i\in\Lambda^3H\) restricts to zero, so it is zero by injectivity of \(\pi_3\) on \(\Lambda^3H\). Changing the previous lifts to the \(h_i\)'s changes the exterior product only by \(W\wedge K\). This proves the claim. All the decompositions are vector-space decompositions; no positivity, generic basis, or characteristic assumption is used.

2. Simultaneous probability bounds for the conflict space

Return to the binary unary-PHP conflict space \(K=\bar K\), with \(v=N^2-1\), \(k=\dim K=(N+1)(2N^2-3N+2)/2\), \(N\ge3\). Take uniform \(U\subseteq V^*\) of dimension \(d\le v\), let \(\pi:V\to U^*\) be restriction, and put \(W=\ker\pi\). Define

\[A=6N+4\log_2N-4,\qquad L=d-R.\]

Theorem. Let \(R\ge1\) be an integer, \(L\ge2\), and \(s\ge1\). If

\[\begin{aligned} d&\ge 2A+2R+3,\ d&\ge A(R+1)+\frac{R^2+5R+2}{2}+s+5,\ d&\ge(A+2)R^2+R\log_2(R+1)+s,\ \binom L2&\ge k+RL+\frac{(\log_2L)^2}{6}+s+5, \end{aligned}\]

then, with probability at least \(1-3\cdot2^{-s}\), every cubic \(\xi\in V\wedge K\) of K-factor rank at most \(R\) that vanishes on \(U\) belongs to \(W\wedge K\).

Prevent high-rank collapse. If \(\pi_2\kappa\) has rank at most \(2R\), it has an isotropic subspace of dimension at least \(d-R=L\). A d-dimensional binary space has at most \(4\cdot2^{R(d-R)}\) codimension-R subspaces. Indeed the Gaussian binomial product is bounded by \(2^{R(d-R)}/\prod_{j\ge1}(1-2^{-j})\), and that denominator is at least \((1/2)(3/4)(1-\sum_{j\ge3}2^{-j})=9/32>1/4\). A uniform L-subspace inside uniform U is uniform in the ambient space. Therefore a union bound costs at most \(4\cdot2^{RL}\) times the isotropy probability at dimension L.

For original rank \(2\rho\), \(R+1\le\rho\le L-1\), R3 gives at most \(2^{A\rho}\) choices, and R1 gives contribution at most

\[4\cdot2.39\sum_{\rho=R+1}^{L-1}2^{F(\rho)},\qquad F(\rho)=RL+A\rho+\frac{\rho(\rho+1)}2-\rho L.\]

Empty rank ranges contribute zero. The first exponent is

\[F(R+1)=-d+A(R+1)+\frac{R^2+5R+2}{2}\le-s-5.\]

Moreover \(F(\rho)-F(R+1)=(\rho-R-1)(A-L+(\rho+R+2)/2)\le-(\rho-R-1)\), by \(\rho\le L-1\) and the first hypothesis. The geometric sum is at most two; the low-rank contribution is below \(19.12\cdot2^{-s-5}<2^{-s}\).

For \(\rho\ge L\), use R2 and the total count \(2^k\), obtaining at most \(24\cdot2^{k+RL+(\log_2L)^2/6-\binom L2}\le24\cdot2^{-s-5}<2^{-s}\). Here \(L\le v-1\), as required by R2. Thus hypothesis 1 of the deterministic lemma fails with probability at most \(2^{1-s}\). These are the same R1–R3 estimates used in the first-stratum proof, now with a codimension-R isotropic subspace.

Preserve every low-rank tuple's joint support. There are at most \((R+1)2^{AR}\) forms in K of rank at most \(2R\), including zero. Ordered R-tuples, with zeros padding shorter tuples, therefore number at most \(2^{AR^2+R\log_2(R+1)}\). Each has joint support dimension at most \(2R^2\). For a fixed nonzero vector \(x\), uniform W of dimension \(v-d\) contains x with probability \((2^{v-d}-1)/(2^v-1)\le2^{-d}\). Union over the nonzero vectors of a fixed support, then over every tuple, bounds the failure of hypothesis 2 by

\[2^{(A+2)R^2+R\log_2(R+1)-d}\le2^{-s}.\]

The tuple family is fixed before U is chosen. Its simultaneous coverage is what allows the deterministic proof to choose its tensor factorization after restriction. Adding the two failures and applying the lifting criterion proves the theorem.

3. A growing range at the old leading dimension scale

Corollary. For all sufficiently large N, take

\[R=\left\lfloor\frac{N^{1/4}}4\right\rfloor,\qquad d=\left\lceil\sqrt2N^{3/2}+N\right\rceil,\qquad s=2\log_2N.\]

Then every relative cubic kernel of K-factor rank at most R is trivial, simultaneously, with probability at least \(1-3/N^2\). This is a uniform growing-rank statement, not a list of finitely many cases.

Parameter check. Eventually \(R\ge1\), \(d\le v\) and \(L\ge2\). The joint-support condition's leading term is at most \((6/16)N^{3/2}+o(N^{3/2})\), below \(d\). The other two lower bounds on d are \(O(N)\) and \(O(N^{5/4})\). Finally \(k=N^3+O(N^2)\), while \(\binom{d-R}2=N^3+\sqrt2N^{5/2}+O(N^2+N^{7/4})\), and \(R(d-R)=O(N^{7/4})\); the last condition follows. The error probability is \(3\cdot2^{-s}=3/N^2\). The retained dimension is \(\sqrt2N^{3/2}(1+o(1))\), with explicit positive margin.

4. Remaining gap and review

The theorem controls cancellation in any representation with at most R factors. It does not show that all cubic kernels have such a representation: the ambient bound can be of order \(\dim V\), much larger. Nor has this entry established a degree-three no-fall theorem from a complete kernel criterion. The general relative-rank obligation remains open. The new bottleneck is explicit: tuple-support union costs roughly \(NR^2\) bits against d. Extending that argument naively beyond \(R\asymp\sqrt{d/N}\) loses its bound; this is a limitation of the estimate, not a lower bound on kernel existence.

Next falsification test. Before proposing a high-rank first moment, check whether K-factor rank controls the probability of nontrivial vanishing at all. A cubic may have a short factorization by a linear form and a quadratic not in K even when its K-factor rank is large; ordinary vanishing of that linear form may then dominate. Determine whether quotienting by W wedge K removes this obstruction. Seek a bound uniform in the remaining rank range or a counterexample to the proposed parameter, not another isolated rank increment.

Assessment. This advances the named relative cubic-count subproblem through a growing range and supplies a reusable deterministic criterion. It does not close the main general-step obligation or establish degree-three hardness. The new range supports continuing one bounded test of this stratification, with modest confidence and the high-rank obstruction explicit.

Verification and process. Reviewed the tensor-rank reduction, both exterior components, the quantifier order of the support union, the Gaussian-binomial constant and every exponent. No new numerical or Lean verification was required. Early derivation was accidentally left under the preparation phase before the marker was corrected; that category contains mixed mathematics and is not retrospectively split.

20 September 2026 — Cubic kernels are forced at the degree-two dimension scale

Status: working exact dimension formula and universal symbolic-kernel obstruction; not an actual degree-three fall or PC refutation. The low-rank exclusion remains valid. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and stopping point. Test whether high K-factor rank makes the remaining relative cubic kernels rare. Before estimating that probability, count their ambient dimensions. The count already forces nontrivial kernels at the retained dimension used in the preceding two cycles. This resolves the proposed high-rank exclusion negatively at that dimension, while leaving the actual degree-fall question separate.

1. Exact degree-three dimension of the conflict ideal

Let there be m rows and N columns, \(N\ge5\), and work in the exterior algebra over any field. Quotient the cell space by its row-sum vectors, writing \(V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m R_i\), \(\dim R_i=N-1\). Let K be the image of the span of conflicting cell wedges, and \(K_3=V\wedge K\). Then

\[\dim K_3=\binom{m(N-1)}3-\binom m3(N^3-6N^2+8N-1).\]

Proof. Put \(t=N-1\), eliminate the final coordinate in each row, and order the row spaces. K contains each \(\Lambda^2R_i\). Between two distinct rows it is the t-dimensional diagonal span together with the all-ones tensor, a space of dimension \(t+1=N\). The final-column conflict gives the all-ones tensor; these descriptions follow directly from the row-sum substitution.

Modulo the ideal generated by same-row wedges, degree three has only tensors on three distinct rows, independently for each row triple. For one triple its ambient dimension is \(t^3\). The three pair modules each have dimension \(t(t+1)\). To count their sum, write a relation as

\[\delta_{ij}P_{ik}+B_k+\delta_{ik}Q_{ij}+D_j+\delta_{jk}T_{ji}+F_i=0\quad(1\le i,j,k\le t).\]

Each module's parameterization is unique: its off-diagonal entries determine the all-ones coefficient, then its diagonal entries determine the remaining coefficients. On triples of distinct indices, \(B_k+D_j+F_i=0\). Since \(t\ge4\), any two choices of k admit the same distinct i,j avoiding them, so all B-coordinates coincide; the same holds for D and F. Write the constants b,d,f with \(b+d+f=0\), giving two parameters. At \(i=j\ne k\), and cyclically, the off-diagonal entries of P,Q,T vanish. At \(i=j=k\), the remaining diagonal entries satisfy \(P_{ii}+Q_{ii}+T_{ii}=0\), giving two parameters per i. Thus the relation space has dimension \(2+2t=2N\).

The sum of pair modules has rank \(3N(N-1)-2N=3N^2-5N\), and its quotient has dimension \(t^3-(3N^2-5N)=N^3-6N^2+8N-1\). Sum over independent row triples and subtract from \(\binom{m(N-1)}3\). This proves the formula. The restriction \(N\ge5\) is substantive: the distinct-index argument is not valid at smaller t.

For the binary PHP setup \(m=N+1\), write \(v=N^2-1\), \(k=\dim K=(N+1)(2N^2-3N+2)/2\). The kernel dimension of the multiplication map \(V\otimes K\to K_3\) is therefore

\[\sigma=vk-\dim K_3=\frac{N(N^2-1)(5N-2)}3.\]

This gives a symbolic explanation consistent with the previously recorded finite quotient dimensions; those numerical dimensions are not new discoveries here. The general row-count exterior formula does not assert an odd-prime polynomial-calculus theorem.

2. A nontrivial relative kernel is unavoidable below the cubic threshold

For any finite-dimensional V and \(K\subseteq\Lambda^2V\), let \(U\subseteq V^*\) have dimension d and \(W=U^\perp\). Define

\[\mathcal H_3(U)=\frac{K_3\cap\ker(\Lambda^3V\to\Lambda^3U^*)}{W\wedge K}.\]

The denominator is contained in the numerator. With \(v=\dim V\), \(k=\dim K\), and \(\sigma=vk-\dim K_3\),

\[\dim\mathcal H_3(U)\ge\max\left\{0,\ dk-\sigma-\binom d3\right\}.\]

Proof. The numerator has dimension at least \(\dim K_3-\binom d3\), while \(\dim(W\wedge K)\le(v-d)k\). Subtract and use nonnegativity. No randomness or quadratic-faithfulness assumption is needed.

Conflict-space consequence. For \(N\ge5\), use the exact \(\sigma\) above. If \(d=(\alpha+o(1))N^{3/2}\), with fixed \(0<\alpha<\sqrt6\), then

\[dk-\sigma-\binom d3=\left(\alpha-\frac{\alpha^3}6+o(1)\right)N^{9/2}>0.\]

Thus every such U has a nontrivial relative cubic kernel. At the preceding choice \(d=\lceil\sqrt2N^{3/2}+N\rceil\), the lower bound is \((2\sqrt2/3+o(1))N^{9/2}\). With probability at least \(1-3/N^2\), the low-factor-rank theorem simultaneously says that none of these nonzero classes has a representative of K-factor rank at most \(\lfloor N^{1/4}/4\rfloor\). The forced kernels therefore occupy higher factor ranks. They are not collectively rare at this dimension.

Among the dimensions of order \(N^{3/2}\) relevant after quadratic faithfulness, excluding the entire symbolic cubic kernel requires a leading coefficient at least \(\sqrt6\), rather than \(\sqrt2\). Taking \(d\ge(\sqrt6+\varepsilon)N^{3/2}\) for fixed positive \(\varepsilon\) clears this particular necessary count; it does not prove exclusion. Nor does nonzero \(\mathcal H_3(U)\) itself prove an actual degree fall: lower-degree residues of leading relations may cancel or be consequences already present. The recorded higher-degree criterion was explicitly unproved, so that implication must not be assumed.

3. The support-injectivity method has the same rank-scale ceiling

A separate limitation explains why the preceding sufficient criterion cannot simply be iterated to all ranks. In the m-row exterior setup, \(N\ge3\), K contains every \(\Lambda^2R_i\). If a map \(\pi:V\to E\) is injective on the joint support of every at-most-R tuple of K-forms of rank at most \(2R\), then necessarily

\[\operatorname{rank}\pi\ge(N-1)\min\{R^2,m\}.\]

Proof. Otherwise select \(t=\min(R^2,m)\) row spaces. Their sum has dimension \(t(N-1)\), so it contains nonzero \(w\in\ker\pi\). Write its nonzero row components as \(w_i\). In each such row choose \(a_i\) independent of \(w_i\), possible since \(N-1\ge2\). Partition the used rows into at most R groups of at most R rows. For group J, let \(\kappa_J=\sum_{i\in J}w_i\wedge a_i\in K\). Disjoint row spaces give rank \(2|J|\le2R\), with support containing every \(w_i\) of that group. The joint support of these at-most-R forms contains w, contradicting the required injectivity.

At \(d\asymp N^{3/2}\) and \(m=N+1\), this necessary condition limits the criterion to \(R=O(N^{1/4})\). The proved growing range has the correct power of N for this particular sufficient method. Failure of joint-support injectivity does not imply a nontrivial cubic kernel; a weaker lifting condition could still work.

4. Checks, rejected shortcut and next obligation

The compiled exact binary checker constructs all three pair modules on a row triple for \(N=5,\ldots,12\), and independently wedges every quadratic conflict generator with every basis coordinate for the full \(N=5,6\) spaces. All ten checks agree. The full cubic ranks are 1744 and 4900, and the linear relation-space dimensions are 920 and 1960. Complete outputs and reproduction details are retained. The proof is symbolic; finite ranks are controls, not its justification.

An earlier attempted counterexample used \(\xi=\ell\wedge\sum_i a_i\wedge b_i\), with \(\ell,a_i\) in one row, and forced vanishing by putting \(\ell\in W\). That also kills the nonzero conflict quadratics \(\ell\wedge a_i\), violating the already required quadratic-faithfulness event. It was therefore discarded as a test of new cubic failures after degree two. The dimension obstruction above has no such conditioning defect.

Decision. Stop the attempted high-rank first moment at the degree-two dimension scale: its desired conclusion is false. Before choosing a larger d or a stronger exclusion condition, identify the actual lower-degree obstruction map from symbolic cubic relations to degree falls. The next task is a bounded test of whether those relations are harmless automatically under quadratic faithfulness, using the existing filtered setup and saved finite evidence before launching new experiments. If that implication fails, retain an explicit witness and the correct criterion; do not infer a PC refutation from the dimension count alone.

Main-route assessment. The full Frege step is still open. This cycle prevents extending a probabilistic claim into a dimensionally impossible regime and fixes the necessary cubic scale, but supplies no higher-degree hardness theorem. The rank-support lifting method is now bounded by a proved structural ceiling.

Process assessment. The dimension count should have preceded efforts to control all cubic ranks. The preceding partial bounds remain valid; the useful improvement is to apply the existing sufficient-versus-necessary endpoint check before imposing full symbolic-kernel exclusion. No additional framework rule is needed.

20 September 2026 — The filtered residue map, and an archived counterexample to automatic lifting

Status: working obstruction-map theorem and reuse of an exact finite counterexample; quadratic faithfulness alone does not prevent a cubic fall. No new elimination run or PC refutation claim. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Task. Determine what the forced symbolic cubic kernels say about actual lower-degree consequences. There is a well-defined surjection onto the fall space, not an implication from every nonzero symbolic class to a fall. Saved computations already refute the proposed automatic harmlessness of all such classes under quadratic faithfulness.

1. The correct obstruction map

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) in the Boolean polynomial ring \(B=\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_v]/(x_i^2-x_i)\), filtered by multilinear degree. Identify its degree-one vector space modulo constants with V, and its associated graded algebra with \(\Lambda V\). Let \(J_2\subseteq B_{\le2}\) be a quadratic relation space with \(J_2\cap B_{\le1}=0\), and let \(K=\operatorname{top}_2J_2\). For \(\kappa\in K\), write \(q_\kappa\) for its unique lift in \(J_2\). Assume old degree-three stability:

\[J_3=J_2+B_{\le1}J_2,\qquad J_3\cap B_{\le2}=J_2.\]

Impose independent affine linear equations with linear span \(W\subseteq V\). Their quotient is a Boolean polynomial ring \(B'\) on \(d=v-\dim W\) free affine coordinates. Let \(\sigma:B\to B'\) be the quotient, with linear part \(\pi:V\to E=U^*\), \(U=W^\perp\). Put \(q'_\kappa=\sigma(q_\kappa)\) and

\[J'_2=\operatorname{span}\{q'_\kappa\},\qquad J'_3=J'_2+B'_{\le1}J'_2,\qquad \mathcal F_3=(J'_3\cap B'_{\le2})/J'_2.\]

Each substituted generator retains original cost two, even if its image has smaller degree. Let \(K_3=V\wedge K\) and define \(\mathcal H_3(U)\) as in the symbolic-kernel entry.

Theorem. There is a well-defined linear surjection

\[\Delta_3:\mathcal H_3(U)\longrightarrow\mathcal F_3.\]

It depends on the actual quadratic lifts and affine right-hand sides, not only on the leading spaces. Level-three no-fall is equivalent to \(\Delta_3=0\); \(\mathcal H_3(U)=0\) is sufficient but is not required by this criterion. Under no falls at lower levels, the filtered closure lemma then gives the recorded degree-three no-refutation consequence.

Step 1: leading relation spaces. Define \(\mu_V:V\otimes K\to K_3\) by exterior product, and \(\mu_E:E\otimes K\to\Lambda^3E\) by \(b\otimes\kappa\mapsto b\wedge\pi_2\kappa\). Let \(S_V=\ker\mu_V\) and \(Z_E=\ker\mu_E\). Lifting a tensor \(z\in Z_E\) to \(T\in V\otimes K\) and taking \(\mu_VT\) gives an exact quotient description

\[Z_E/(\pi\otimes1)(S_V)\cong\mathcal H_3(U).\]

Changing the lift adds a tensor in \(W\otimes K\), hence changes its exterior product by \(W\wedge K\). Every numerator element has a lift because \(\mu_V\) is onto K_3. If a lifted product lies in \(W\wedge K\), subtract a tensor from \(W\otimes K\) with that product; the remainder lies in S_V and has the same projection z. This proves precisely the displayed kernel and surjectivity.

Step 2: take the lower-degree residue. For \(z=\sum_i b_i\otimes\kappa_i\in Z_E\), choose zero-constant linear polynomial representatives of the \(b_i\) in B' and set

\[\delta(z)=\left[\operatorname{nf}\sum_i b_iq'_{\kappa_i}\right]\in\mathcal F_3.\]

Its cubic part vanishes by definition of Z_E. Changing a representative by a constant adds an element of J'_2, so the coset is independent of that choice. Every element of \(J'_3\cap B'_{\le2}\), after discarding its constant-cofactor contribution in J'_2, arises this way. Thus \(\delta\) is onto the fall space.

Step 3: old relations map to zero. If \(T=\sum_i a_i\otimes\kappa_i\in S_V\), the polynomial \(\operatorname{nf}\sum_i a_iq_{\kappa_i}\) has degree at most two and lies in J_3. Old stability puts it in J_2. Apply \(\sigma\). Its affine image \(\sigma(a_i)\) differs from a chosen representative of \(\pi(a_i)\) only by a constant. The difference contributes only a linear combination of the \(q'_\kappa\). Consequently \(\delta((\pi\otimes1)T)=0\). Step 1 now makes \(\delta\) factor through the stated surjection \(\Delta_3\).

Relation to the original filtered presentation. Independent affine equations can be completed to an invertible affine coordinate change over \(\mathbb F_2\); such changes preserve the Boolean degree filtration in both directions. In those coordinates, every degree-at-most-e polynomial killed by the quotient is a sum of the eliminated coordinates times polynomials of degree at most \(e-1\). Thus quotienting the linear equations preserves the actual fall quotient: a lower-degree image can be lifted at that same degree, and the difference is an allowed original linear-equation consequence. Boolean normal reduction also preserves the original degree budgets. Hence \(\mathcal F_3\) is the degree-three fall space of the original system, modulo its degree-two consequences, not an enlarged closure using the smaller substituted degrees.

PHP hypotheses. For \(N\ge5\), eliminate each row equation by \(x_{iN}=1+\sum_{j<N}x_{ij}\). Same-row pairs and the N cross-row diagonal/all-ones relations have independent quadratic leading parts, as in the conflict-space setup; their quadratic lifts span J_2 with no affine element. The old filtration theorem at degree three supplies \(J_3\cap B_{\le2}=J_2\) after this degree-preserving elimination. Its matching-normal-form presentation and the Boolean-coordinate presentation give the same fall quotient. Quadratic faithfulness makes the substituted quadratic leading map injective, but is not needed to define the residue surjection itself.

Why whole-kernel exclusion was too strong. At \(d\asymp N^{3/2}\), the residue codomain has dimension at most \(1+d+\binom d2=O(N^3)\). At the earlier degree-two scale, the symbolic-kernel lower bound is of order \(N^{9/2}\). Therefore many symbolic classes must lie in \(\ker\Delta_3\). The \(\sqrt6\) threshold is a necessary threshold for eliminating all symbolic classes, not a proved necessary threshold for actual degree-three no-fall.

2. Archived exact counterexample to automatic harmlessness

The saved eight-hole label-form runs, seed 1, already contain a counterexample. They use the same constraint generator at degrees one, two and three. The following are extracted ranks, not a new elimination run:

Constraints Mddim G_1dim G_2dim(G_2 intersect degree at most 1)dim(G_3 intersect degree at most 2)Fall dimension
14492313402313400

There are nine old row equations and \(v=63\) row-quotient coordinates. The degree-one ranks show that the M additional linear parts are independent modulo those row equations, and the degree-two lower pivots show no fall to degree one. Here \(\dim K=477\). At M=15, the saved degree-two quotient dimension is 700; after affine elimination the ambient filtered degree-two space has dimension \(1+48+\binom{48}2=1177\). Therefore the substituted relation space has dimension \(1177-700=477\), and, since it has no lower-degree element, its quadratic leading map is injective. The same calculation at M=14 gives \(1+49+\binom{49}2-749=477\). Thus both systems are quadratically faithful.

Nevertheless, at M=15 the degree-three lower pivot count exceeds the degree-two rank by \(1568-1389=179\). This is a genuine finite degree fall, so the residue map is nonzero and has rank 179 in this instance. The stored constant pivot remains zero: this does not assert \(1\in G_3\) or a degree-three PC refutation. These are structured label forms, not evidence about a uniform subspace's typical behavior.

The bounded extraction script checks these arithmetic implications and records hashes of all three input logs in the witness report. The original generator, parameters and complete outputs remain in the historical run's reproduction package. No explicit polynomial fall certificate was extracted here, and no fresh numerical or Lean verification is claimed.

3. Next obligation and assessment

The general-step obligation remains open. We now have the correct level-three target, \(\Delta_3=0\), and a concrete rejection of the claim that quadratic faithfulness makes it automatic. The next bounded task is to analyze how the residue map changes with the affine right-hand sides at fixed W, beginning with its quadratic component. A leading-kernel dimension count cannot answer that question; the lifts' lower terms matter.

Process assessment. Saved data supplied the needed counterexample without rerunning large closures. Deriving the residue quotient prevented treating a stronger symbolic condition as necessary for the actual goal; no new framework rule is needed.

20 September 2026 — Right-hand sides act affinely on the quadratic residue

Status: working variation law and exact Boolean control; nonzero variation bounds the fraction of right-hand sides without a fall. No rank estimate for typical PHP subspaces. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Task and endpoint. Analyze the actual residue map at fixed W instead of counting all symbolic kernels. This cycle derives its quadratic variation and the exact affine solution-set consequence. It does not assume that the variation is nonzero, or small, for the PHP conflict space.

1. Intrinsic contraction formula

Use the hypotheses and notation of the residue-map theorem: a stable old Boolean quadratic lift space \(q_\kappa\), fixed \(W\subseteq V\), \(U=W^\perp\), \(E=U^*\), and restriction \(\pi:V\to E\). Vary the affine equations \(w=c(w)\), \(c\in W^*\), keeping the linear parts fixed. Write \(\mathcal H=\mathcal H_3(U)\), and set

\[Q_2=\Lambda^2E/\pi_2K.\]

The quadratic leading component of \(\Delta_{3,c}\) is a map \(D_c:\mathcal H\to Q_2\). It is well-defined even though the full residue codomain depends on c: every element of the substituted J'_2 has quadratic part in \(\pi_2K\).

Theorem. For \(t\in W^*\), any extension \(\widetilde t\in V^*\), and any representative \(\xi\in K_3\cap\ker\pi_3\),

\[D_{c+t}([\xi])-D_c([\xi])=[\pi_2(\iota_{\widetilde t}\xi)]\in Q_2.\]

Here \(\iota\) is exterior contraction. The right side is independent of c, of the extension of t and of the representative of the relative class. Thus \(c\mapsto D_c\) is affine-linear.

Independence checks. Choose \(V=W\oplus H\). Every element of \(\ker\pi_3\) has at least one W-factor. If two extensions of t differ by an element of U, its contraction cannot remove that factor, so its image under \(\pi_2\) is zero. Changing \(\xi\) by \(w\wedge\kappa\) changes its contracted image by \(t(w)\pi_2\kappa\), zero in Q_2. This proves the two required independences directly.

Variation proof. Use fixed affine quotient coordinates from H, and extend t by zero on H. For a quadratic Boolean lift \(q_\kappa\), changing c to c+t changes the linear part of its substituted image by \(\pi(\iota_{\widetilde t}\kappa)\). This follows by expanding each quadratic monomial after translation; the remaining change is constant and does not affect the quadratic part after multiplication by a linear coefficient. Old linear and constant terms add only constants to this difference.

Choose a cofactor tensor \(T=\sum_i a_i\otimes\kappa_i\) lifting the class, as in the residue construction. Its varying quadratic residue is consequently \(\sum_i\pi(a_i)\wedge\pi(\iota_{\widetilde t}\kappa_i)\), modulo \(\pi_2K\). Contracting \(\xi=\sum_i a_i\wedge\kappa_i\) gives this same expression together with \(\sum_i\widetilde t(a_i)\pi_2\kappa_i\), which vanishes in Q_2. This proves the formula. The calculation takes place after Boolean normal reduction and retains the original quadratic generator cost.

Uniform right-hand sides. Let \(L:W^*\to\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal H,Q_2)\) be this linear variation map, and let \(b=\operatorname{rank}L\). The equations \(D_c=0\) have either no solution or an affine solution space of codimension b. For uniform c, therefore,

\[\Pr_c[\text{no degree-three fall}]\le\Pr_c[D_c=0]\le2^{-b}.\]

If \(D_0\notin\operatorname{im}L\), every c has a nonzero quadratic residue. If b is zero and D_0 vanishes, lower linear or constant residues may still be nonzero, so the converse has not been asserted. This is an upper bound on the probability of no-fall, not a hardness lower bound. No assertion about the typical b for random W follows without another estimate.

2. Exact four-variable control

Take \(B=\mathbb F_2[a,b,u,v]/(a^2-a,b^2-b,u^2-u,v^2-v)\) and the single old relation \(q=ab+uv\). Its leading form \(\kappa=a\wedge b+u\wedge v\) has rank four. The linear exterior annihilator is zero, so the four linear multiples have independent cubic leading parts; hence old \(J_3\cap B_{\le2}=J_2=\langle q\rangle\), as required by the residue theorem.

Fix \(W=\langle a+u\rangle\) and impose \(a+u=t\), \(t\in\mathbb F_2\). Eliminating u leaves

\[q_t=a(b+v)+tv,\qquad \pi_2\kappa=a\wedge(b+v)\ne0.\]

The quadratic leading map is faithful for both right-hand sides. Its linear syzygies are spanned by the coefficients a and b+v, since these span the annihilator of that rank-two form. The two residues, subtracting q_t, are exactly

\[a q_t-q_t=t(av+v),\qquad (b+v)q_t-q_t=tbv.\]

For t=0 both vanish, so there is no degree-three fall. For t=1 their quadratic parts adjoin two independent classes \([av]\) and \([bv]\) modulo \(\langle ab+av\rangle\); hence the fall space has dimension two. The variation map L has rank one as a map from the one-dimensional right-hand-side space into the space of residue maps, even though the nonzero residue map itself has rank two. Exactly half the right-hand sides have no fall, attaining the stated probability bound.

This is a satisfiable Boolean quadratic model, not PHP and not a refutation example. It checks the variation, the distinction between the two ranks, and the fact that quadratic faithfulness does not remove right-hand-side dependence. All calculations are displayed; no numerical or Lean run was needed.

1. Quadratic faithfulness makes the symbolic dimension exact

Lemma. Over any field, let \(\pi:V\to E\) have kernel W and rank d, and suppose \(\pi_2\) is injective on \(K\subseteq\Lambda^2V\). Then exterior multiplication is injective on \(W\otimes K\). If \(\sigma=\dim\ker(V\otimes K\to V\wedge K)\), the relative cubic quotient has exact dimension

\[\dim\mathcal H_3= d\dim K-\operatorname{rank}(E\otimes K\to\Lambda^3E)-\sigma.\]

Replace E by the image of \(\pi\) if needed. For injectivity, expand a tensor as \(\sum_i w_i\otimes\kappa_i\) in a basis of W, and choose a complement of W in V. The component of its exterior product with one W-coordinate and two complementary coordinates is \(\sum_iw_i\otimes\pi_2\kappa_i\). If the product is zero, independence and quadratic faithfulness force every \(\kappa_i=0\). Thus the old syzygy space meets \(W\otimes K\) trivially, and its projection into \(E\otimes K\) remains injective. The leading-relation quotient description then gives the dimension formula. This is stronger than using only an upper bound on \(\dim(W\wedge K)\).

20 September 2026 — Semi-regularity does not supply the relative hardness theorem

Status: bounded source audit and elementary free-ring calculation; the relative conjecture and Frege goal remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and stopping point. On route item general-step, can the semi-regularity literature supply the missing hardness of the wide-companion system? We checked the three sources below, keeping their fields, rings, distributions and conclusions separate. The stopping point is an applicable theorem or a precise mismatch. This is not an exhaustive literature survey.

1. The checked sources and the missing implication

  • Hodges–Molina–Schlather, On the Existence of Semi-regular Sequences, arXiv:1412.7865v1 (2014). Their ring is homogeneous square-zero \(E=\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_v]/(x_i^2)\). Definition 2.2 imposes an annihilator condition below a cutoff; Theorem 2.4 characterizes the resulting truncated Hilbert series \([(1+t)^v/\prod_i(1+t^{d_i})]\). It does not establish that our clauses satisfy that condition. Theorem 7.14 rules out semi-regular sequences of a fixed degree vector, with some degree at least two, for sufficiently many variables. Neither the ring nor the quantifiers give a refutation of our growing-width, growing-inventory relative conjecture.
  • Bardet–Faugère–Salvy–Spaenlehauer, On the Complexity of Solving Quadratic Boolean Systems, arXiv:1112.6263v2 (2012). Definition 8 gives a strong semi-regularity hypothesis for a quadratic Boolean-system algorithm; Theorem 2 is conditional on it. Conjecture 1 concerns random quadratic coefficients with a linear number of equations. It is a conjecture supported by experiments, not a proved relative no-fall theorem for decomposable clauses over the matching base.
  • Bigdeli–De Negri–Dizdarevic–Gorla–Minko–Tsakou, Semi-regular sequences and other random systems of equations, arXiv:2011.01032v1 (2020). Their ordinary polynomial-ring cryptographic semi-regularity uses the truncated series \(\prod_i(1-t^{d_i})/(1-t)^v\); see Definitions 1.8 and 1.11. The generic assertion of Theorem 3.1 is over an infinite field. The finite-field Theorem 3.2 assumes cryptographic semi-regularity. Its conclusion is a Gröbner/solving-degree bound under the stated hypotheses, not the missing finite-field matching-relative PC lower bound.

Audit conclusion. None of these checked statements proves the desired implication. The earlier recollection that generic Boolean semi-regularity was simply an open conjecture was too broad: the definition and asymptotic regime matter, and there are nonexistence theorems. Our Conjecture SR remains a custom relative product-clause conjecture, with its recorded finite evidence and no imported theorem. This corrects the literature identification, not its mathematical status. Source versions and reading locators are saved in the source audit; third-party full texts are not included.

2. Exact free-ring baselines show why the definitions differ

Working proposition. All Hilbert polynomials below have integer dimension coefficients. In \(E\), let \(f=\lambda_1\cdots\lambda_h\), where the linear forms are independent and \(2\le h\le v\). Then \(\lambda_1f=0\) but \(\lambda_1\notin(f)\). Consequently the singleton \((f)\) fails the cited Definition 2.2 for every cutoff \(D>h+1\). This does not exclude semi-regularity at a smaller cutoff. Its exact quotient series is

\[ H_{E/(f)}(t)=(1+t)^v-t^h(1+t)^{v-h} =(1+t)^v\left(1-\frac{t^h}{(1+t)^h}\right). \]

Proof. Invertibly change linear coordinates so that \(\lambda_i=x_i\) for \(i\le h\). Such changes preserve the square-zero ideal in characteristic two. The squarefree monomials containing \(x_1\cdots x_h\) form a basis of \((f)\); their generating polynomial is \(t^h(1+t)^{v-h}\). Moreover \(x_1f=0\), while the degree-one element \(x_1\) is not in the degree-at-least-\(h\) ideal. This is exactly the prohibited annihilator at degree \(h+1<D\).

Now use the filtered Boolean function ring \(B=\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_v]/(x_i^2-x_i)\). Let \(S\) be an \(r\)-dimensional space of affine forms with \(1\notin S\), and choose independent \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_h\in S\), \(1\le h\le r\). Define

\[ Q=\prod_{i=1}^h(1+\lambda_i),\qquad J=(gQ:g\in S). \]

Write \(H\) for the associated-graded Hilbert polynomial of the ordinary polynomial-degree filtration. Then

\[ H_{B/(Q)}(t)=(1+t)^v-t^h(1+t)^{v-h},\qquad H_{B/J}(t)=(1+t)^v-t^h\big((1+t)^{v-h}-(1+t)^{v-r}\big). \]

Proof. Extend the selected forms to a basis \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_h,g_{h+1},\ldots,g_r\) of \(S\). Their linear parts are independent: a nonzero linear combination with zero linear part would give either a dependence or \(1\in S\). Complete them to affine coordinates, flipping the first \(h\) so that \(Q=x_1\cdots x_h\). Invertible affine Boolean substitutions preserve the filtration in both directions, as in the earlier common-kernel calculation. The selected companions \(\lambda_iQ\) vanish identically. The remaining companions are \(Qx_j\), \(h<j\le r\). Thus a basis of \(J\) consists of the squarefree monomials containing all first \(h\) variables and at least one of the next \(r-h\). Counting these monomials gives the second formula; counting only those containing the first \(h\) gives the first. Every degree-\(d\) monomial of \(J\) is a degree-\(d-h-1\) multiple of one generator of original cost \(h+1\); zero selected companions add nothing. Hence these counts also respect the original companion-cost filtration. For \(r=h\), \(J=0\), as the formula requires. \(\square\)

Scope. The one-clause factor in Conjecture SR already accounts for decomposable-clause annihilators; it is not the standard square-zero semi-regularity factor. Even that one-clause count differs from the count for its full companion block. Neither calculation multiplies across arbitrary overlapping blocks, passes through the PHP conflict quotient, or proves relative no-fall. These are elementary coordinate calculations; no novelty is claimed.

3. Route consequence

The required implication remains: for proof-chosen affine input spans, select suitable width-\(h\) projections so that the functional PHP base plus companions \(g_{b,i}Q_b\) has no degree-\(D\) PC refutation, with \(M\le N^c\), logarithmic \(h\), \(M2^{-h}<1\) and polylogarithmic \(D\). Random unrestricted polynomial coefficients do not give that quantifier. Imposing \(Q_b=0\) is stronger; controlling an ordinary NS space is weaker than the needed PC conclusion unless a valid closure argument is supplied.

Contribution and next action. No main-goal obligation is discharged. The audit removes an unjustified source shortcut and gives the correct free companion baseline. I estimate below 5% that a direct import from these particular generic semi-regularity results, without a new relative theorem, will advance the main goal; this is an assessment of that proposed shortcut only. Park it. Next test whether a source-specific occupancy-value specialization can preserve a sufficiently large hard functional PHP residual. Read the existing weak-base column-freezing map and its explicit functional-base limitation before proposing a new transfer; stop at a justified transfer or an algebraic obstruction, before any random-value counting.

20 September 2026 — Fixed occupancies expose a prime-power degree obstruction

Status: working certificate and transfer obstruction; a stronger functional normalization is unnecessary for the already solved column-statistic family. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and stopping point. On route item general-step, can the weak-PHP occupancy-freezing map be upgraded to the functional base as a route to chosen-value hardness? Test the original-degree certificates before random-value counts. The test produces a general obstruction. A dependency search also recovers the existing same-degree elimination theorem, which already solves the weak-base column-statistic family, so the proposed functional upgrade is not a missing goal obligation for that family.

1. A refutation degree controlled by the integer imbalance

Working lemma. Work over a field of characteristic \(p>0\), with \(m\) rows and \(n\) columns. The functional matching base has row equations \(\rho_i-1\), both row and column exclusions, and Boolean axioms. Add all column equations \(\kappa_j-c_j\), where \(\kappa_j=\sum_i x_{ij}\), \(c_j\in\{0,1\}\), and \(q=\sum_jc_j\) is counted as an integer. Suppose \(m>q\), and put

\[ \Delta=m-q,\qquad d=p^{v_p(\Delta)},\qquad u=\Delta/d. \]

There is an ordinary NS refutation of degree at most \(d\), and consequently a PC refutation through the same degree. This is an upper bound, not an exact degree assertion.

Proof, including the original degree ledger. Let \(e_k\) denote the elementary symmetric polynomial, with \(e_k=0\) when the list is too short. For every positive \(k\),

\[ e_k(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_m)-e_k(\kappa_1,\ldots,\kappa_n) \in\mathcal I_k(\text{row and column exclusions}). \tag{OC-matching} \]

For \(k=1\) the difference is identically zero. For \(k\ge2\), expand the first polynomial by choosing \(k\) distinct rows and a cell in each. A monomial with a repeated column is a multiple of a column exclusion, of total degree \(k\). What remains is the sum of all size-\(k\) matching monomials, each once. Expanding the second polynomial similarly removes repeated-row terms by row exclusions and leaves the identical matching sum. This proves (OC-matching) without division by \(k!\).

Telescoping the products in \(e_k(\rho)-e_k(1,\ldots,1)\) uses row equations with cofactors of degree at most \(k-1\). Telescoping \(e_k(\kappa)-e_k(c)\) uses occupancy equations with the same bound. Thus

\[ \binom mk-\binom qk\in\mathcal I_k(\text{augmented functional base}). \tag{OC-scalar} \]

For completeness, for an ordered set \(A=\{i_1,\ldots,i_k\}\), the first telescope is \(\prod_{a\in A}\rho_a-1=\sum_{t=1}^k(\rho_{i_t}-1)\prod_{s<t}\rho_{i_s}\). The column telescope inserts the constants on the remaining factors. Every displayed generator multiple has its original linear or quadratic cost and stays within \(k\).

In characteristic \(p\), Frobenius gives the formal-polynomial identity

\[ (1+T)^m-(1+T)^q =(1+T)^q\big((1+T^d)^u-1\big) =uT^d+\text{higher powers of }T. \]

Because \(p\nmid u\), the coefficient at degree \(d\) is nonzero. Equation (OC-scalar), divided by this field scalar, is the promised degree-\(d\) certificate. It also shows that all the lower scalar tests \(1\le k<d\) vanish; this only describes this symmetric-count test, not the full NS or PC space. An NS certificate gives a PC derivation by deriving its monomial multiples within the same degree. \(\square\)

Non-Boolean assigned occupancies. These are already refutable through degree two. Indeed \(\kappa_j^2-\kappa_j=\sum_i(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij})+2\sum_{i<i'}x_{ij}x_{i'j}\) is a degree-two base certificate, and subtracting \((\kappa_j-c_j)(\kappa_j+c_j-1)\) leaves \(c_j^2-c_j\). This is nonzero whenever \(c_j\notin\{0,1\}\), including over extension fields.

Checks and limitations. For \(p=2,m=7,q=3\), the first differing binomial coefficient is at \(k=4\); for \(q=5\) it is at \(k=2\). These are direct evaluations of the proof, not new computation runs. The recorded all-but-one-empty probe warns against calling the bound exact: at \(p=3,m=4,n=3,q=1\), the symmetric certificate is through degree three, whereas a degree-two PC refutation already exists for the weaker base with just the two zero occupancies. Adding the remaining occupancy equation and row exclusions cannot remove that refutation.

2. Necessary residual size for an affine functional upgrade

Working corollary. Suppose an affine polynomial map sends the preceding original functional base to a residual weak or functional PHP board with \(N+1\) rows and \(N\) holes, and certifies each original base-axiom image in the residual ordinary NS space through that axiom's original degree. Suppose it freezes all original column sums identically to the constants \(c_j\). If these constants are Boolean and \(m>q\), then necessarily

\[ N<2p^{v_p(m-q)}-1. \tag{OC-residual} \]

Proof. Apply the affine map to the degree-\(d\) certificate above. All added occupancy equations become zero. An original degree-\(a\) base axiom has a cofactor of degree at most \(d-a\); its affine image has the same upper degree bound and multiplies a replacement certificate through \(a\). The result is a residual NS refutation through \(d\). But if \(N\ge2d-1\), the all-field old matching theorem, starting from a normalized degree-zero functional, supplies a normalized degree-\(d\) design. The residual row count \(N+1\ge d\) satisfies its row hypothesis; a functional design also annihilates the weaker base. This contradicts the refutation and proves (OC-residual). \(\square\)

For the existing \(K\)-copy map, the matching prefix and copied occupied columns give exactly \(q=n-K\), while \(m=n+1\). Therefore \(d=p^{v_p(K+1)}\) and a functional upgrade with the same frozen pattern would require \(N\le2d-2\). Taking \(K=p-1\), as in the weak-base linear-residual theorem, would force \(N\le2p-2\). At a fixed prime this cannot retain an unbounded hard board. More generally, if \(n\ge2Kp^{v_p(K+1)}\), its recorded residual \(N=\lfloor n/K\rfloor-1\) is too large for such an upgrade. This does not rule out changing the pattern, the residual size, the map degree or its proof cost.

3. What this does and does not change

The missing row exclusions in the old map are a substantive limitation, not omitted bookkeeping. The new obstruction does not refute the old map: it was explicitly proved only for weak PHP. Nor does it refute (HW), whose selected projections are existential and whose companion equations are weaker than fixing all column values. A large prime-power part of \(m-q\) merely passes the symmetric test; it is not a hardness theorem.

Recover the sufficient endpoint. The existing weak-base theorem already eliminates any finite level-correct package polynomial in column sums and earlier package coefficients at the same NS/PC degree. The common-partition version retains a board controlled by the largest row class. These hypotheses do not cover arbitrary unary affine input spans, but no functional occupancy upgrade is needed to use their stated endpoints.

We have a reusable elementary counting certificate and an explicit obstruction to a stronger normalization, while the proposed column-statistic subcase was already solved in the appropriate weak base. Park this detour. I estimate below 5% that further functional upgrades of this fixed-pattern construction will advance the main goal; this judgment does not concern all occupancy methods or the whole program. Next review the actual coupled source-moment equations: can source-dependent row-set fillings meet them, without the already impossible universal conditioning-compatible sections? The review should identify a sufficient general compatibility claim and test it against the recorded source obstructions before developing more restricted cases.

Route item general-step remains the same: exclude the complete algebraic source of a hypothetical short ordinary-PHP Frege proof at its compiled cost. In the binary case the proved compiler interface supplies an identity \(1=\sum_\alpha Q_\alpha H_\alpha\) with \(\deg_w Q_\alpha+\nu_\alpha\le D\). The active-window theorem reduces its unknowns to weight \(E=D-L\), while retaining the original degree-\(D\) equation set and carried witness costs.

The desired compatibility statement is therefore simultaneous solvability of the complete coupled marginal equations for these fixed-depth, polynomial-inventory compiler sources at the supplied polylogarithmic degree. Old moments may be chosen after seeing the source; extending every prescribed old functional would be stronger. A normalized solution for a selected subsystem, a proper accuracy window, or the old coordinates alone does not suffice. The odd-prime source counterpart and fixed-depth recurrence remain additional obligations.

No compatibility follows by choosing those fillings separately. Trying to enforce universal naturality meets the exact conditioning-commutation obstruction: summing over a row would force a noninjective restriction map to be injective. Source-dependent choices are not ruled out.
  • Corrections using every coefficient row. I considered killing proper coefficient-row marginals, so that a foreign block contributes only when a cofactor touches all its \(h\) rows. The targeted index search recovered the stronger historical automatic-window theorem, with its full coefficient-operator proof. For original affine companion cost \(2h+1\), it already gives the \(D\le3h\) window, without restricting the number of blocks. This is a rediscovery of the mechanism, not a new theorem or an extension of its range.

Rewriting it as another linear system is not a proof of compatibility. The factorial-family example also prevents an inventory-independent elimination bound polynomial in the recorded degree parameters. The semi-regularity audit supplied no generic relative theorem. Neither detour closes the coupled source equations.

NS versus PC, with the endpoint fixed. The six-hole control remains a valid warning that an NS design does not establish PC hardness. That warning applies to invoking the sufficient (HW) specialization lemma in its stated PC form. It does not forbid using a direct NS functional to contradict an actual complete NS source identity. The two endpoints must not be conflated in either direction.

20 September 2026 — Private ENS coefficients do not give respectful expansion

Status: source-scope audit and exact Boolean satisfaction criterion; the natural block clustering fails in the unresolved rank range. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and stopping point. On route item general-step, test a published local-to-global PC criterion as a possible source of complete-system compatibility. A complete ENS block has many private variables; the question is whether these variables actually satisfy the criterion's local hypothesis. The stopping point is an applicable theorem or an explicit failed hypothesis, not a search over unrelated examples.

1. What the journal criterion requires

Source: Mikša–Nordström, A Generalized Method for Proving Polynomial Calculus Degree Lower Bounds, JACM 71(6), Article 37 (2024), Definitions 4.1–4.9, Theorem 4.11 and Corollary 4.14, pp. 37:19–37:23. The polynomial formulation uses Boolean partial assignments: satisfaction means vanishing for every completion. A respectful assignment also satisfies every background polynomial it touches. With respectful boundary expansion \((s,\delta,\xi)\), variable-cluster overlap \(\ell\), small-subfamily satisfiability, and \(|\operatorname{Vars}(f)|\le(\delta s-2\xi)/(2\ell)\) for each input polynomial, Theorem 4.11 gives degree greater than \((\delta s-2\xi)/(2\ell)\). The zero-slack corollary removes the separate local-satisfiability assumption, but retains its other stated conditions. This is a scope check of the statement and definitions, not a new proof of that theorem.

The older notebook discussion concerned the conference paper's graph-PHP application. It does not by itself verify these hypotheses for a dense affine ENS encoding. Source metadata and exact locators are in the audit record.

2. Exact threshold for satisfying a block by its private coefficients

Working lemma. In the Boolean function ring over \(\mathbb F_2\), let \(G=(g_1,\ldots,g_t)\) be affine forms in old variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_v\), let \(S=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_2}G\), and let \(r=\dim S\). For \(h\ge1\), form the complete companions

\[ g_iP,\qquad P=\prod_{u=1}^h\left(1-\sum_j a_{u,j}g_j\right), \]

with fresh Boolean coefficient variables \(a_{u,j}\). A constant Boolean assignment to all these coefficients makes every companion zero for every old Boolean point if and only if

\[ 1\in S\quad\text{or}\quad r\le h. \tag{RA-private} \]

Proof. If \(1\in S\), choose the first coefficient row to represent the constant one, so its factor is zero. If \(1\notin S\) and \(r\le h\), put a basis of \(S\) in the first \(r\) rows and zero in the rest. The product can equal one only at a common zero of that basis, where all inputs vanish. This is the recorded Boolean packing sufficiency.

For necessity assume \(1\notin S\) and \(r>h\). A basis \(s_1,\ldots,s_r\) of \(S\) has independent linear parts: a linear dependence among those parts would give a nonzero constant in \(S\), or a dependence among the affine forms. The affine map \(x\mapsto(s_1(x),\ldots,s_r(x))\) is therefore surjective onto \(\mathbb F_2^r\). Any fixed coefficient rows produce \(h\) linear combinations of these basis coordinates, say the rows of an \(h\)-by-\(r\) matrix \(A\). Choose a nonzero vector \(z\in\ker A\), and an old point mapping to \(z\). At that point every selected row form is zero, so \(P=1\), but some input \(g_i\) is nonzero since the inputs span \(S\). Its companion equals one. Thus the fixed coefficient assignment does not satisfy the block. \(\square\)

The threshold is semantic Boolean satisfaction, not ordinary polynomial identity before Boolean reduction. It refines the existing constant-row clamp and packing observation; the free companion ideal count also witnesses a nonzero ideal when independent selected rows leave unused input directions. No novelty is claimed.

A few assigned old variables do not always help. Still assume \(1\notin S\), \(r>h\), and define

\[ d_{\rm supp}(S)=\min_{0\ne g\in S}|\operatorname{supp}(\operatorname{lin}g)|. \]

This is positive. If a partial assignment fixes fewer than \(d_{\rm supp}(S)\) old variables, the restricted linear parts remain independent: any lost combination would have had its entire linear support in the assigned set. Hence the restricted span still has dimension \(r\) and excludes one. Applying (RA-private) proves that no further constant assignment to the coefficients can satisfy all companions for all remaining old points. Assigning only a subset of the coefficients cannot do so either, since a satisfying partial assignment would stay satisfying under every completion of those coefficients.

This support statement is on the free Boolean cube. It does not claim a lower bound relative to PHP equations, and it does not prohibit polynomial-valued coefficient substitutions or other proof interfaces.

3. Failed hypotheses and remaining scope

Take a complete block's companions as one left polynomial cluster and its private coefficient variables as a right cluster. For the unresolved spans \(r>h\) with \(1\notin S\), the right cluster cannot satisfy the left cluster, even before considering background respectfulness. It therefore contributes no respectful edge, no matter how many private coefficient variables it contains. The support-distance conclusion gives a sufficient obstruction even when the cluster also assigns a small old-variable set.

There are two further checks that cannot be omitted. First, in the slack theorem the background alone is among the required satisfiable small subsystems: putting all of the already unsatisfiable PHP base there fails the hypothesis immediately. A serious alternative representation would have to distribute suitable old constraints among the left clusters. Second, the polynomial theorem bounds each input's number of variables, not just its polynomial degree. Dense affine inputs and their full coefficient rows can have much larger support than the hoped-for degree threshold. The stated CNF variant has different hypotheses; replacing the encoding would require its own proof-transfer analysis.

Verdict. The natural private-coefficient clustering does not establish the needed general compatibility statement. This does not rule out other clusterings, restrictions, encodings, or algebraic extensions of the criterion. Enlarging clusters must be accompanied by actual respectful assignments, boundary and overlap estimates; ordinary incidence alone is insufficient. The complete-source NS endpoint remains sufficient, even though this audited theorem would have supplied the stronger PC conclusion.

Contribution and next step. No main-goal obligation is discharged. We now have an exact failed local hypothesis rather than an unsupported expansion analogy. The direct private-cluster proposal has no chance of covering the stated high-rank range, by the lemma; I assign no estimate to unexamined alternative clusterings. Next inspect the algebraic immunity criterion of Alekhnovich–Razborov referenced by the source, which does not start from this particular private-assignment proposal. Test its exact local requirements and variable-count loss on a complete affine block before attempting a global bound; stop on an explicit mismatch.

Process assessment. Reading the precise polynomial statement exposed both the local satisfaction failure and the support-size hypothesis, so a cluster search or numerical expansion experiment would have been premature; no new infrastructure is needed.
