20 September 2026 — Shared support defeats the checked immunity criterion

Status: version-qualified source audit and elementary overlap obstruction; no general lower-bound implication obtained. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and stopping point. On route item general-step, test whether the algebraic immunity method avoids the private-assignment obstruction. Compare its actual local and expansion parameters with complete affine ENS companions. Stop at a usable parameter bound or an explicit mismatch.

1. Source version and exact quantitative test

The readable source is Alekhnovich–Razborov, Lower Bounds for Polynomial Calculus: Non-Binomial Case, preprint dated 27 September 2000, Definition 2.3 and Theorem 3.8. In the Boolean function ring, \(f\) is \(\ell\)-immune if each nonzero semantic consequence has degree at least \(\ell\). An incidence matrix has row supports at most \(s\) and boundary at least \(c|I|\) for every set of at most \(R\) rows. The theorem requires common immunity \(\ell\) and

\[ s\le R\big(\ell/4-(s-c)\big), \]

and concludes PC degree greater than that right-hand side. This audit checks the statement and definitions; it does not reprove the theorem. It does not assert that this is the unchanged statement of the 2003 journal version. The author PDF timed out in the web tool and failed TLS verification in a protected download attempt; the journal full-text link redirected to its landing page. A comparison-copy request is in the ignored user request file. Bibliographic details, version and attempts are preserved in the source record.

2. Shared support makes the bound nonpositive

Working observation. Suppose two distinct rows of the proposed incidence matrix contain the essential variables of nonzero polynomials \(f_1,f_2\), and those polynomials share at least \(t\) essential variables. If the expansion range includes pairs, then

\[ s-c\ge t. \tag{IM-overlap} \]

If one of those polynomials has a nonzero semantic consequence of degree at most \(e\), any common immunity parameter satisfies \(\ell\le e\). Thus the checked theorem's threshold is at most \(R(e/4-t)\), and cannot be positive when \(t\ge e/4\).

Proof. Write \(J_1,J_2\) for the two incidence supports. Their pair boundary is their symmetric difference, whose size is \(|J_1|+|J_2|-2|J_1\cap J_2|\le2s-2t\). Pair expansion requires at least \(2c\), proving (IM-overlap). The immunity inequality follows directly from its definition. Padding incidence rows with additional variables cannot remove the shared essential variables, so it does not escape the bound. Nor does an expansion range \(R=1\) make this theorem applicable to a nonzero input: \(c\le s\) and \(\ell\le\deg f\le s\) would force the impossible \(s\le\ell/4\le s/4\). \(\square\)

Application to individual companions. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), take nonzero affine inputs \(g_1,\ldots,g_r\), with span excluding one and dimension greater than the accuracy \(h\). Zero or duplicate inputs may be removed; there are at least two independent inputs. Each nonzero Boolean companion \(g_iP\) has degree at most \(2h+1\), so it bounds common immunity by \(e=2h+1\).

Every one of the \(hr\) coefficient variables is essential in every companion. To see this for \(a_{u,j}\) in \(g_iP\), choose an old Boolean point with \(g_i=g_j=1\). Such a point exists: two nonzero affine forms from a span excluding one are either equal or have independent linear parts, and the latter map is surjective. Set all other coefficients to zero. The companion becomes \(1-a_{u,j}\). Hence two companions share at least \(t=hr\), and

\[ \ell/4-(s-c)\le(2h+1)/4-hr<0. \]

The raw individual-companion encoding therefore cannot satisfy the positive-threshold hypotheses of the checked criterion, even before the old PHP axioms are examined.

Grouping a whole block into a single polynomial. In the Boolean ring put \(Z_G=\prod_i(1-g_i)\) and \(F_G=P(1-Z_G)\). The equation \(F_G=0\) is equivalent on Boolean points to all the companions: if \(P=0\) they all vanish, and if \(P=1\) they vanish exactly when every input is zero. Therefore \(F_G\) semantically implies every \(g_iP\), and still has immunity at most \(2h+1\), regardless of its own larger degree or private-variable count.

Every old variable occurring in the affine input span is essential in \(F_G\). Indeed that span has a common-zero point because it excludes one. At zero coefficients, \(F_G=1-Z_G\); toggling an old variable appearing in an input takes the common-zero point to a nonzero input vector. Thus two such block polynomials with at least \(t\ge(2h+1)/4\) shared old variables have the same nonpositive bound. This addresses that particular Boolean grouping only; it is not a theorem about every possible regrouping, auxiliary encoding or relative normal form.

3. Decision

Outcome. The checked preprint criterion provides no direct general-step theorem for either the raw high-rank companions or the described dense, overlapping block polynomials. Private variables improve ordinary boundary counts, but shared variables incur a penalty that the available immunity cannot pay. This is a quantitative failed application, not a refutation of the source theorem or of the Frege program. The exact journal-version comparison remains pending; no unseen stronger version is ruled out.

Contribution and next action. No main-goal obligation is discharged. For these two specified representations the positive-threshold application is impossible under the checked criterion. Park that direct import. Return to a proof-specific escape: the retained-OR width audit only obstructs the supplied witnesses, not all alternative witnesses. The costed virtual fold is already available when child costs fit the parent weight. Next test whether an alternative original-budget witness can avoid the known collected-width obstruction outside that eligibility condition. Stop at a general admissible replacement, or a scoped obstruction for all witnesses in the specified budget; do not relabel the supplied-witness example as the latter.

Process assessment. The explicit overlap inequality settled the proposed application without an immunity enumeration; version-qualified reading and the existing user-request mechanism avoid spending further cycles on download retries.

The test below closes the latter escape for the exact recorded local example, but a full application check recovers that this example is already eligible for the former. 1. Isolate a cofactor in every local certificate

Use exactly the recorded code family: \(h\ge2\), code rank \(r=h^2\), \(v=64(r+1)\) independent old bits \(x\), independent old signals \(t_1,\ldots,t_{2h+1}\), modifier \(z\), lower blocks \(C_b\), and the three proper-union blocks \(P_0,P_1,P_2\). The old base in this statement consists of Boolean domains only. The generator set is the original companions of these blocks and the primitive Boolean equations. It does not include PHP axioms, other unrelated modules, or new derived generators.

Working theorem. In every ordinary NS identity for the target \(P_0-P_1P_2\) over that fixed generator set, the collected cofactor \(C_*\) of \(E_*=t_1P_1\) has ROABP width at least \(2^{h^2-2}\) in every variable order. The same holds for its Boolean remainder and for every local certificate of the child-normalized target \(P'_0-P_1q_z\) over the remaining original companions and Boolean domains. There is no degree restriction on this lower bound. The supplied witness shows nonvacuity within the original local ceiling \(4h^2+4h\).

Proof. Apply the following scalar specialization, leaving only the code bits \(x\) free:

  • Set every lower coefficient matrix and the block-two matrix to the identity, and set \(z=0\). Then \(V_b\) becomes \(\chi_b=\prod_jL_{bj}(x)\) and \(P_2\) becomes \(q(x)=\prod_{b,j}L_{bj}(x)\).
  • Set \(t_1=1\) and every other \(t_i=0\). Set every block-one coefficient to zero, so \(P_1=1\).
  • In block zero set the first row's \(t_1\)-coefficient to one and all other coefficients to zero. Its first factor is zero, so \(P_0=0\).

Modulo Booleanity, each lower companion becomes \((1+L_{bj})\chi_b=0\), and each block-two companion becomes \((1+\chi_b)q=0\). Every block-zero companion is zero because \(P_0=0\). Among block-one companions exactly \(E_*=t_1P_1\) becomes one; all others become zero. Every primitive Boolean equation becomes zero. The target becomes \(-q=q\).

Now apply this specialization to any ordinary certificate and take its Boolean remainder. Every generator term disappears except that of \(E_*\). Therefore, writing \(\rho\) for the specialization,

\[ \operatorname{ml}(\rho(C_*))=\operatorname{ml}(q) =\mathbf1[Ax=\mathbf1]. \tag{OR-all-witness-isolation} \]

For the child-normalized system the same proof simply omits the already removed lower and block-two generators, using \(q_z\mapsto q\). This is a scalar test of a polynomial identity; it is not a restriction preserving a satisfiable proof system.

The balanced-code lemma and cut-rank formula give rank at least \(2^{r-2}\) across every half of the code variables. Scalar restrictions do not increase ROABP width, and Booleanizing each univariate matrix does not increase width either. Every order on the surviving code bits has such a middle cut. Thus \(C_*\), in any original order, has width at least \(2^{h^2-2}\). A joint linear-in-generator-placeholders witness has the same lower bound: setting the \(E_*\) placeholder to one and all others to zero extracts \(C_*\). \(\square\)

Scope. This strengthens the supplied-witness statement to all witnesses in the specified fixed local basis. Adding a new target generator, folding away the parent, using other modules, or allowing old PHP generators changes the argument. In particular PHP generators need not vanish under \(\rho\), so their cofactors can contribute to the restricted identity. The recorded nonvanishing of \(q\) in an old quotient does not by itself give a cut-rank bound for all quotient representatives.

2. The admissible fold was already proved for this exact example

The targeted theorem excerpt was not enough to classify this fixture: its enclosing record contains the explicit code-union application. After child normalization it supplies complete profiles at costs \(s_1=2h\), \(s_2=h^2\), and original parent weight \(w_0=2h^2+h\). Hence

\[ s_1+s_2=h^2+2h\le2h^2+h=w_0. \]

The existing source-fold theorem already replaces the parent by \(P_1q_z\), making the designated comparison zero and rebuilding all affected comparisons at the carried costs. Thus the new theorem explains why a mere local cofactor rewrite cannot avoid the hard function while keeping this interface; it does not undermine the successful change of interface. The example is now explicitly linked in that theorem's index assessment so its solved status is visible during bounded retrieval.

3. An unfinished quotient-rank idea, retained for possible reuse

Open question; not an established extension of the theorem. For a polynomial in one selected bit from each of \(v\) distinct pigeon rows, can its cut-rank lower bound be preserved under addition of degree-\(B\) compact bit-PHP consequences? One possible construction is to leave a hard residual board entirely on one side of the chosen variable-order cut, and apply its normalized degree-\(B\) design on that side only. Such a linear contraction would preserve the rank upper bound supplied by a width-\(w\) program.

A candidate parameter choice is \(n=2^\ell\), \(N'=2^k\ge2B-1\), with \(k\le\ell/2\). Among unused rows, at least half have at least \(\ell/2\) bits on one side of the cut. Grouping by a selected \(k\)-subset of those bit positions suggests that

\[ n+1-v-a\ge2\binom{\ell}{k}(2^k+v+1) \]

could supply enough residual rows sharing free positions on that side, after excluding \(a\) additional signal rows. The code rows would use disjoint private two-label pairs, and the residual board would use \(2^k\) other labels with \(2^k+v+1\) rows; the extra \(v\) residual rows compensate for reserving two labels per code row. The remaining rows would be matched to the remaining labels.

This is an unfinished construction: the simultaneous label choices, the source restriction, old compact axiom images, and the one-sided contraction must all be proved with their degree budgets. It is not asserted for arbitrary unary-variable orders. No quotient-rank theorem or PHP-relative all-witness lower bound is claimed here. Since the local fixture is already foldable, this possible tool is parked rather than made the next main-goal task.

20 September 2026 — The modular NS source compiler extends to every prime

Status: working all-prime modular-source theorem, with exact small-prime certificates; PHP boundary conversion and general source exclusion remain separate. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Route review and selection. The recent audits and fixed-interface obstruction did not advance the highest-risk general-step implication. They also recovered solved cases. Rather than strengthen another convenient representation, this cycle addresses the explicitly missing field restriction in depth-prime-recurrence: extend the binary modular NS compiler to a general fixed prime without introducing a MOD-arity cost or importing PC line reuse as an NS argument. This is a required independent prerequisite, not a replacement for the general compatibility problem.

1. Statement and exact scope

Fix a prime \(p\) and work over \(\mathbb F_p\). Start with a coherent, balanced, assumption-free proof in the recorded presentation: a fixed Boolean axiom basis, the displayed MOD recursion and empty schemas, and MP. Use the same TRUE-by-zero approximation convention, complete fresh ENS companions and coefficient field equations, and polynomially many coherent OR subgroup values. Let \(H_\pi\) be proof height and \(M_{\rm fr}\) the largest leaf-occurrence count of a fixed Boolean axiom frame. Repeated and constant leaves count separately.

Assign structural value costs: old Boolean coordinates have cost one; constants cost zero; negation preserves cost; a MOD node on inputs of maximum cost \(\delta\) has cost \((p-1)\delta\); an OR product of accuracy \(h\) on inputs of maximum cost \(\delta\) has cost \(s=h(\delta+1)\). Keep each companion's original cost \(s+\mu_i\), with \(\mu_i\) the input cost. Let \(L\ge1\) bound all values, needed subgroup values and MOD prefix sums. These are upper costs, not assertions of equality with a collected degree.

Working theorem. Define

\[ C_p=\max\{M_{\rm fr}+2,12,10(p-1)\}. \]

The theorem value has a formal identity

\[ \widehat\tau=\sum_\alpha Q_\alpha H_\alpha, \qquad \deg_w Q_\alpha+\nu_\alpha\le(C_p+H_\pi)L, \tag{PS-source} \]

where the targets \(H_\alpha\) are the coherent OR-interface and value-Booleanity polynomials, with supplied concrete NS ceilings at most \(3L\) and \(2L\), respectively. Outer coefficients are polynomials in old coordinates and genuine selectors. Expanding their supplied witnesses gives an ordinary NS derivation through the same ceiling. For fixed \(p\), polynomial source/proof size yields polynomial-size factored coefficient circuits and polynomial module inventory; no expanded monomial bound or odd-prime ROABP-width theorem is asserted.

If the structural depth is \(d\), \(h\ge\max(1,p-1)\) permits \(L\le(d+1)h^d\), after including the same-level subgroup registry. Thus fixed depth and polylogarithmic accuracy/height give polylogarithmic source degree. The theorem starts from the stated coherent balanced proof setup; it does not itself audit the odd-prime ordinary-PHP-to-bit boundary conversion.

2. Booleanity through twice the structural value cost

Old Boolean coordinates and constants start the induction, and negation preserves the witness because \((1-v)^2-(1-v)=v^2-v\). For a genuine OR product \(P\), the ordinary prefix identity \(1-P=\sum_iU_i g_i\) gives

\[ P^2-P=-\sum_i U_i(g_iP). \]

The prefix satisfies \(\deg U_i\le s-\mu_i\), so each original companion multiple fits \(2s\). This proof is valid in every characteristic. At odd primes it uses companions; it is not the binary domain-only argument.

For a MOD node write \(T=\sum_jv_j-c\), \(c\in\mathbb F_p\), and \(v=T^{p-1}\). If the inputs have cost at most \(\delta\), Frobenius and a univariate telescoping identity give

\[ T^p-T=\sum_j(v_j^p-v_j) =\sum_j(v_j^2-v_j)\sum_{e=0}^{p-2}v_j^e. \]

Substituting the complete input Booleanity witnesses costs at most \(p\delta\). Now

\[ v^2-v=T^{p-2}(T^p-T) \]

has an ordinary NS witness through \((p-2)\delta+p\delta=2(p-1)\delta\), twice the MOD cost. A sum of any number of these certificates changes their count, not their maximum degree. This proves the induction, including prefix sums needed below.

3. The MOD recursion needs a field relation, not Booleanity of its prefix

Using the recorded coherent prefix convention, put

\[ t=\sum_{j=1}^k\varphi_j^{\rm ap}-(k-i),\quad a=\psi^{\rm ap},\quad b=t^{p-1},\quad c=(t-1)^{p-1},\quad m=(t+a-1)^{p-1}. \]

For two formal indeterminates \(t,a\), set

\[ l=a(1-b),\quad r=(1-a)(1-c),\quad q=(1-l)(1-r), \]\[ u=(1-m)q,\quad v=m(1-q),\quad F_p(t,a)=1-(1-u)(1-v). \]

This is precisely the algebraic value of the fixed outer Boolean frame. Its total degree is at most \(K_p=10(p-1)\). On \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(t\in\mathbb F_p\), the quantities \(b,c,m\) are Boolean, and \(m=q\): at \(a=1\) both equal \(b\), at \(a=0\) both equal \(c\). Hence \(F_p\) vanishes on that grid.

Divide first by \(a^2-a\), then by \(t^p-t\), using their monic leading terms. Neither division increases total degree. The remaining polynomial has \(a\)-degree below two and \(t\)-degree below \(p\). Its values at \(a=0,1\) are polynomials of degree below \(p\) vanishing on all \(p\) field elements, so both are zero. Consequently there is an exact identity

\[ F_p=A_p(t,a)(a^2-a)+B_p(t,a)(t^p-t),\qquad \deg A_p\le K_p-2,\quad \deg B_p\le K_p-p. \tag{PS-grid-certificate} \]

After substituting the actual selector-valued \(t,a\), the first term uses the Booleanity module of \(a\) at cost at most \(2L\). For the second, expand \(t^p-t\) by the preceding Frobenius identity into the Booleanity modules of the prefix argument values. Its extra cofactor factors have degree at most \((p-2)L\), so each term has carried cost at most

\[ (K_p-p)L+(p-2)L+2L=K_pL. \]

The first term has the same bound. This is an ordinary modular NS identity, with polynomially many factored terms and no arity factor in degree. The prefix \(t\) need not be Boolean when \(p>2\); replacing its field relation by \(t^2-t\) would be unjustified. Empty MOD schemas still have their literal zero values in the stated convention.

4. Gate, frame and proof composition

The three-product prefix identity is an ordinary ring identity in every characteristic. Its degree accounting gives the OR target \(c-ab\) a witness through the sum of the three value costs, at most \(3L\). For a non-OR child \(a\), the singleton profile with input \(1-a\) uses the Booleanity witness just proved; it need not be domain-only. Prefix residuals and products use the exact costed profile identities, so their budgets remain valid.

For a Boolean frame with \(m\) leaf occurrences, the same telescoping comparison as in the binary proof costs at most \((m+2)L\): at a binary node the child witness is multiplied by an actual value of cost at most \(L\), or by the other child's formal frame polynomial of degree at most its leaf count times \(L\). A fixed Boolean tautology has a Boolean-ideal certificate through its frame degree over any field, by multilinear division, giving the required leaf proof. For the MOD recursion the outer frame has ten leaves, so its actual-value comparison costs \(12L\); (PS-grid-certificate) gives the rest through \(K_pL\). These bounds establish the common leaf ceiling \(C_pL\).

For MP, let \(a\) be the premise value, \(c\) the implication value and \(b\) the conclusion value. The supplied target \(R=c-(1-a)b\) gives the literal identity \(b=c+ab-R\). Multiply the entire antecedent NS certificate by \(b\); if the two premise ceilings are \(d_a,d_c\), the new ceiling is at most \(\max\{d_c,d_a+L,3L\}\). Height induction proves (PS-source). All multipliers used above are polynomials in actual selector-valued expressions, so the identity exists in the formal coordinate ring as well. Sharing arithmetic subexpressions gives polynomial-size factored coefficient circuits; coherence and the original carried labels are retained.

Finally, for \(h\ge p-1\), a structural step increases the maximum cost by at most \(W\mapsto h(W+1)\); MOD costs at most \(hW\), and negation adds none. Induction from \(W_0\le1\) yields \(W_d\le(d+1)h^d\). This proves the claimed parameter bound. \(\square\)

The new compiled bivariate checker constructs \(F_p,A_p,B_p\) over \(p=2,3,5,7\), reconstructs each identity exactly, verifies all grid values and the degree bounds, and checks the recorded interpolation identity. Their actual frame degrees are 10, 16, 28 and 40, within bounds 10, 20, 40 and 60. Omitting the field relation leaves a nonzero remainder in every case, a nonvacuous control. All coefficients and targets are saved in the complete certificate output. These finite checks support the local arithmetic; the all-prime and proof-composition conclusions use the arguments above. A preliminary indentation warning was fixed and the final source compiled with warnings treated as errors.

Dropping the prefix field relation fails the exact control; omitting companions from odd-prime OR Booleanity would also lose the displayed proof. This does not establish a small-width odd-prime coefficient model, the ordinary-PHP-to-bit boundary audit, or general source exclusion. The strongest unresolved item remains complete source compatibility, whose current source-dependent filling approach I still estimate at roughly 5% without a new structural input. That estimate is about that approach only.

20 September 2026 — A one-sided residual board preserves cut rank modulo PHP

Status: working bounded-degree quotient-rank theorem and PHP-relative local-witness consequence; no full Frege lower bound. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Task and change of direction. The earlier inventory screen already rejected the simplest cofactor-count arguments. This cycle also checked the multiscale residual-rank control and recovered the existing full column-state normalizer; neither supplies the missing global estimate. Instead, the parked quotient-rank construction now has a concrete proof. It addresses the PHP-relative escape left by the local witness obstruction. The stopping point is the precise projection and its local application, without claiming that the already foldable fixture is an essential part of a short PHP proof.

1. A bounded-degree quotient cannot reduce the selected cut rank

Fix a prime \(p\), \(n=2^\ell\), and the compact Boolean-bit base \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\) on \(n+1\) pigeon rows, with collision degree \((p-1)\ell\). Select one bit from each of \(v\ge1\) distinct rows, writing these bits as \(x_1,\ldots,x_v\). Call them the code bits; no coding hypothesis is needed yet. Allow consistent prescribed Boolean values for other bits on these rows and on \(a\) additional rows, with at most \(g\ge0\) prescribed bits on each affected row. No code bit is prescribed. Let \(\mathcal G\) be these linear guard equations, and let \(\mathcal I_B\) mean the ordinary degree-\(B\) NS space of \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\cup\mathcal G\), retaining the original generator degrees.

Choose integers \(B\ge1\) and \(2\le k\le\lfloor\ell/2\rfloor\), and put \(N_0=2^k\), \(m_0=N_0+v+1\). Assume

\[ N_0\ge2B-1,\qquad n+1-v-a\ge2\binom{\ell}{k}m_0, \qquad \frac{n}{2^{g+1}}>N_0+2v+a. \tag{QC-room} \]

Working theorem. For every partition of all old bit variables into two sides, there is a linear map \(\mathcal T\) from degree-at-most-\(B\) polynomials to multilinear code-bit polynomials which:

  1. fixes every multilinear polynomial in the code bits of degree at most \(B\);
  2. annihilates \(\mathcal I_B\);
  3. does not increase coefficient-matrix rank across the given partition and its induced code-bit partition.

Consequently, if \(C-f\in\mathcal I_B\), with \(\deg C,\deg f\le B\) and \(f\) multilinear in the code bits, the cut rank of \(C\) is at least that of \(f\) across the induced cut. Any ROABP for \(C\) has at least that width at the cut. This concerns bounded-degree NS equivalence, not equivalence modulo the full unsatisfiable ideal or an augmented PC quotient.

2. Put every residual variable on one side

Exclude the code rows and the \(a\) additional guarded rows. In each remaining row, at least half of its \(\ell\) bits lie on one side of the partition. At least half the eligible rows choose the same side; call it the residual side. In each of those rows select \(k\) bit positions lying on that side. There are at most \(\binom\ell k\) possible position sets. The second inequality in (QC-room) therefore supplies \(m_0\) rows sharing a set \(J\) of \(k\) positions, all on the residual side. These will be the residual pigeons.

Fix their other positions to a common pattern, say zero. Their possible labels form a common axis-aligned subcube \(H\subseteq\{0,1\}^\ell\) of size \(N_0\). All their remaining variables lie on one side of the chosen cut.

For each code row choose a private two-label edge in the direction of its code bit, respecting its guards. At least \(n/2^{g+1}\) such edges are available before exclusions. At most \(N_0\) edges meet \(H\), and at most \(2(v-1)\) meet the vertices of previously chosen edges. The third inequality supplies an edge disjoint from all of them. Fix the other bits of that row to this edge's common values, leaving its original code bit free.

Assign each additional guarded row a distinct full label outside \(H\) and the \(2v\) private-edge vertices, respecting its prescribed bits. It has at least \(n/2^g\) candidate labels; excluding the reserved labels and earlier guarded labels still leaves a choice by (QC-room). Finally match all other rows bijectively to all remaining labels. The counts agree:

\[ (n+1)-m_0-v-a=n-N_0-2v-a. \]

This defines a partial constant assignment \(\sigma\), not an affine variable identification. It fixes no code bit. Reserving both labels of each code row is essential: the residual label set is independent of all code values. The price is that the residual board has \(N_0+v+1\) rows, rather than \(N_0+1\).

Two disjoint axis-aligned label subcubes have a coordinate fixed to opposite values on both. Thus every collision involving a fixed row or a code row has a literal zero factor after \(\sigma\). Only collisions between residual rows remain, and those become the compact collisions on their common \(k\) free positions. Their new degree \((p-1)k\) is at most the original \((p-1)\ell\). Boolean axioms become zero or Boolean axioms of a remaining bit, and guards become zero.

3. Contract a design on that side only

The residual compact system has \(m_0\) rows and \(N_0\) labels. It has a normalized ordinary degree-\(B\) design \(\mu\): use the old all-field matching extension on the functional \(m_0\)-by-\(N_0\) board and compose with the bit decoder. Here \(m_0\ge B\) and \(N_0\ge2B-1\). The decoder's two-row image certificates do not use an equality between the total row and column counts, so they apply to this board as well. The condition \(k\ge2\) ensures that the residual collision degree is at least two, as that original-degree interpolation argument requires.

Write \(Y\) for the residual free bits. Define

\[ \mathcal T(P)=\operatorname{ml}_x\big((\operatorname{id}_x\otimes\mu_Y)(\sigma P)\big). \tag{QC-projection} \]

For inputs of degree at most \(B\), every \(Y\)-coefficient lies in the design's domain. Normalization fixes every code polynomial. If \(P\) is a legal old collision multiple, its image is zero or a legal residual collision multiple through \(B\), so \(\mu\) kills it. Residual Booleanity is killed by the design; code-bit Booleanity is killed by \(\operatorname{ml}_x\); guards vanish. This proves that \(\mathcal T\) annihilates all of \(\mathcal I_B\).

For the rank assertion, a polynomial of cut rank \(w\) is a sum of \(w\) products of a left polynomial and a right polynomial. The constant assignment preserves such a decomposition. All residual variables are on one side, so contracting them changes only that side's factors; Booleanizing code variables also acts separately on the two sides. Thus the output still has a decomposition with at most \(w\) terms.

Individual factors in a chosen decomposition can have degrees above \(B\) because of cancellation. To make the preceding argument formal, extend \(\mu\) arbitrarily to all multilinear \(Y\)-monomials, for example assigning zero to the previously unspecified higher-degree monomials, and then to ordinary polynomials by Boolean reduction. This extension need not be a higher-degree design. It agrees with \(\mu\) on every coefficient of the actual degree-\(B\) input, and permits the linear rank argument on arbitrary factor polynomials. The decoder is used only to obtain \(\mu\); it is not substituted into the coefficient polynomial across the variable cut. This proves all three assertions. \(\square\)

Asymptotic room. For fixed \(g\) and \(v,a,B\le\ell^{O(1)}\), take \(k=\max(2,\lceil\log_2(2B-1)\rceil)\). Then \(N_0=O(B+1)\), \(k=O(\log\ell)\), and \(\binom\ell k\le\ell^k=\exp(O((\log\ell)^2))\). Both right-hand requirements in (QC-room) are eventually smaller than \(2^\ell\). Thus the theorem applies uniformly to polylogarithmic row support and degree for all sufficiently large boards. It is a compact-bit cut theorem; arbitrary orders on unary incidence variables are not covered.

Working corollary. Return to the binary code-union family, with \(r=h^2\), \(v=64(r+1)\) and independent old signal bits. Allow the original compact bit-PHP axioms as well as the fixed local companions and primitive Boolean domains in a certificate of \(P_0-P_1P_2\). Let its ordinary NS degree be at most \(B\), where \(B\ge4h^2+4h\). Under (QC-room), with at most \(a=2h+2\) additional guarded rows and \(g=2\), every such certificate has a collected cofactor of width at least \(2^{h^2-2}\) in every variable order. The same conclusion applies after the certified child normalization. In particular this holds for \(h=\Theta(\ell)\), any fixed polylogarithmic bound \(B\), and sufficiently large \(n\).

Proof. Repeat the coefficient isolation, but initially specialize only primitive coefficient variables: lower and block-two matrices become identity, all block-one coefficients become zero, and block zero selects \(t_1\) in its first row. Write \(C'_*\) for the resulting collected cofactor of \(t_1P_1\), before assigning the old signal bits.

The lower and block-two companion images have the already recorded Boolean-domain certificates within their original degrees. Add as guards \(t_1=1\), \(t_i=0\) for \(i>1\), and \(z=0\). Block-zero companions now belong to the guard ideal because their product is \(1-t_1\). All block-one companions except \(t_1\) are also guard equations; replacing \(C'_*t_1\) by \(C'_*\) costs a legal multiple of \(t_1-1\). Finally \(q_z-q_0\) is a multiple of \(z\) through degree at most \(h^2\). Therefore the original identity gives

\[ C'_* - \operatorname{ml}(q_0) \in\mathcal I_B(\mathcal Q_{n,2}\cup\mathcal G), \qquad q_0=\prod_{b,j}L_{bj}(x). \tag{QC-witness} \]

All image replacements used at most their original generator degrees, and Booleanizing \(q_0\) costs at most \(h^2\le B\). This is a bounded-degree NS equivalence, not a claim about an arbitrary PC consequence. The guards prescribe at most two bits on a row and never prescribe a code bit, including when the modifier uses a second bit of a code or signal row.

Fix any proposed ROABP order for the original cofactor, specialize its coefficient variables, and take the cut after half the code bits in the induced old-bit order. Apply the theorem to (QC-witness). The code half-rank bound and flat-indicator formula give cut rank at least \(2^{h^2-2}\) for \(\operatorname{ml}(q_0)\). Hence \(C'_*\), and therefore the original cofactor, has at least that width. The supplied local witness remains available within \(4h^2+4h\), so the statement is nonvacuous. \(\square\)

The unfinished projection question is answered in the explicit room regime, including the intended polylogarithmic regime. This is stronger than nonvanishing of a code function modulo the old base: it controls the cut rank of every representative at the allowed NS degree. It also closes the PHP-axiom escape for the stated local witness problem.

20 September 2026 — Named values preserve the formal source width

Status: working all-prime named-source representation and degree/width separation; no old-coordinate width transfer or Frege lower bound. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and stopping point. Audit a whole-source change of formal basis after the PHP-relative local witness bound. Can a useful small-width representation and the original degree ledger coexist after replacing values? The answer is yes in an explicitly enlarged named-value ring, but not as a width guarantee after eliminating those names. The stopping point is that distinction and its exact source construction.

1. Name MOD values, and keep their defining equations

Use the coherent balanced tree proof and structural costs of the all-prime modular compiler. Keep names for genuine OR values, and add a formal name \(M_v\) for each needed nonconstant MOD value. Empty or literal constant values can stay constants. A negated value is represented by one minus its underlying value. Every formula value is now affine in the old coordinates and this full collection of names.

For a MOD occurrence with argument values \(a_j\) and residue \(i\), include

\[ H_v^{\rm MOD}=M_v-\left(\sum_{j=1}^{k}a_j-(k-i)\right)^{p-1}. \]

Its weighted degree is at most its structural MOD weight, hence at most \(L\). Interpret \(M_v\) by that actual polynomial in the complete source, so the target has a literal zero concrete witness. Give it the uniform carried cost \(2L\). Keep OR targets at cost \(3L\), and Booleanity of each primitive value name at its justified individual cost \(2w_v\). The latter has a concrete witness from the preceding compiler proof. This is a forward formal interface with explicit definitions; its realization map is not asserted to be injective.

Working theorem. With the same \(C_p=\max(M_{\rm fr}+2,12,10(p-1))\), the theorem value has a formal modular identity through \(D=(C_p+H_\pi)L\). If \(T\) counts the balanced tree's symbol inventory and the coherent module registry, its outer coefficients have the form

\[ Q_\alpha=\sum_{r\in R_\alpha}c_r\prod_{j=1}^{t_r}\ell_{r,j}(u), \qquad t_r\le H_\pi+C_0(p),\qquad \sum_\alpha|R_\alpha|\le C_1(p)T, \tag{NV-factors} \]

where the factors are affine in the full named coordinates and the constants depend only on the fixed prime and proof frames, not on accuracy. Hence the linear-in-placeholders certificate \(\sum_\alpha Q_\alpha Y_\alpha\) has polynomial ROABP width in every order, with exponent independent of \(h\). The non-base module targets have ordinary formal degree at most \(\max(2,p-1)\). The already proved compact virtual boundary and affine decoder preserve this representation in their corresponding named rings.

2. Proof and active-window ledger

Boolean-frame comparison works verbatim with affine named values, using OR targets through \(3L\). For a MOD recursion leaf, let \(a,b,c,m\) denote its named values and let \(t\) be its affine named prefix sum. Compare the ten-leaf frame polynomial \(F(a,b,c,m)\) with the explicit grid polynomial \(F_p(t,a)\), replacing \(b,c,m\) by \(t^{p-1},(t-1)^{p-1},(t+a-1)^{p-1}\). Telescoping uses their three definition targets. Each replaced expression has weighted degree at most \(L\); the comparison cofactors have weight at most \(9L\), and the padded definition cost gives at most \(11L\). The actual frame comparison costs \(12L\).

The grid identity uses \(a^2-a\) and \(t^p-t\); expand the latter into the Booleanity modules of the named prefix arguments, exactly as in the all-prime proof. Its ceiling is \(10(p-1)L\). Thus the leaf ceiling remains \(C_pL\). MP multiplies the complete antecedent certificate by the conclusion value, now an affine expression in the names, and adds at most \(L\) per antecedent edge. This proves the degree statement.

For (NV-factors), the fixed Boolean frames give bounded sums of bounded products of affine named values. In the MOD proof, the frame comparison and the two-variable grid quotients have bounded degree depending only on \(p\); expand them as polynomials in the fixed list of affine expressions \(a,b,c,m,t\). The prefix field relation contributes at most a constant depending on \(p\) times the number of argument occurrences. Thus each leaf contribution is a bounded sum of bounded products of affine forms, and the total number of contributions is at most \(C_1(p)T\). Unrolling the balanced proof tree adds at most \(H_\pi\) affine factors. The any-field subset-state construction, with one extra placeholder factor, gives width at most \(C_1(p)T2^{H_\pi+C_0(p)+1}\). Active window. OR targets have weighted degree at most \(2L\) and cost \(3L\); MOD definitions have weighted degree at most \(L\) and cost \(2L\). Both leave at least \(L\) slack in a degree-\(D\) legal multiple. The complete active-window proof therefore still applies under its same old-board hypotheses with \(E=D-L\), now including every original legal MOD-definition equation at its cost \(2L\). Primitive named Booleanity has its individual \(2w_v\) witness; raw coefficient variables are still not Booleanized. No feasibility follows from this reduction. \(\square\)

3. Degree-conservative definitions need not preserve width

Working proposition. Give old coordinates positive weights and adjoin acyclic definitions \(D_j=y_j-F_j(u,y_{<j})\), with \(\deg_wF_j\le w_j=w(y_j)\). At definition cost \(w_j\), eliminating the names preserves bounded-degree NS consequences of the remaining coordinates, with all other generator costs carried along. This does not preserve ROABP width, even for quadratic definitions.

Degree proof. Recursive substitution \(\sigma\) fixes old coordinates, kills the definitions and does not increase weighted degree. Conversely \(P-\sigma P\) has a definition-ideal certificate through \(\deg_wP\). To see the latter, substitute names in reverse acyclic order and use

\[ y_j^e-F_j^e=(y_j-F_j)\sum_{q=0}^{e-1}y_j^{e-1-q}F_j^q. \]

Each cofactor has weight at most the replaced monomial's weight minus \(w_j\). Applying this to any other generator \(G_\alpha\) through its carried ceiling \(\nu_\alpha\) lifts a certificate using \(\sigma G_\alpha\) back to one using \(G_\alpha\) and the definitions without increasing the overall degree. Forward substitution proves the reverse direction. This is a weighted NS statement; it is not an additional PC theorem. If definition costs are padded above \(w_j\), forward elimination remains degree-nonincreasing, but this same-cost reverse reconstruction must account for the padding.

Width counterexample. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), use the recorded balanced-code forms \(L_1,\ldots,L_r\), with \(v=64(r+1)\), and introduce

\[ y_0=1,\qquad D_j=y_j-y_{j-1}L_j,\qquad w(y_j)=j. \]

Every definition is linear or quadratic in the formal variables and has weighted degree \(j\). Yet

\[ y_r-q=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\left(\prod_{k=j+1}^{r}L_k\right)D_j, \qquad q=\prod_{j=1}^{r}L_j, \tag{NV-width-control} \]

is a degree-\(r\) weighted certificate. The named polynomial \(y_r\) has width one; the code and cut-rank formula force width at least \(2^{r-2}\) for \(q\) in every old-variable order, also after Boolean reduction. If desired, named Booleanity has old-domain witnesses through twice each weight after elimination. Even padding every definition to cost \(2L\) with \(L=r\) leaves (NV-width-control) through \(3L-1\), inside the complete source degree scale. Hence a cut-rank projection fixing code functions and killing these added definitions cannot also be rank-nonincreasing. The PHP quotient theorem did not include such auxiliary definitions. \(\square\)

4. What a full source fold can retain

For an eligible costed fold, one may keep the former product name as a virtual name interpreted by the child product, rather than immediately substitute that product into every outer coefficient. The original formal coefficient identity and its affine-factor representation are then unchanged up to naming. The existing fold proof reconstructs all concrete local witnesses within their carried costs, including later inputs. Add the explicit virtual definition with its justified target degree and a carried cost, for example \(2L\) when its weighted degree is at most \(L\). Its concrete image is zero. If both children are affine in the retained names, this definition is quadratic; a more complicated profile needs its own named subexpressions or a separate target-degree bound.

This is a sound bookkeeping option for the full source under the already proved fold hypotheses. It does not enlarge the eligibility range, remove the need to reconstruct witnesses, or imply width preservation on eliminating virtual names. At cheap definition costs the degree-equivalence argument above explains the connection to the substituted system; with padded costs keep the actual legal cofactor set. The code example is a positive control for degree-preserving source folding and a negative control for coordinate-independent width transport.

Main-route assessment. The all-prime source now has a polynomial-width formal coefficient presentation in an explicitly enlarged ring, with constant formal target degree for each fixed prime and the original active-window slack. No small-width old-coordinate certificate follows, and no complete source-exclusion theorem has been proved. I estimate roughly 5% that a direct width-transport line resolves the main general step without an additional structural theorem; the new projection tool remains available, but arbitrary weighted definitions lie outside it.

20 September 2026 — Finite-field IPS results do not yet supply source compatibility

Status: bounded literature/model audit and an exact binary coefficient identity; no new complete-source exclusion. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For the fixed named-value source, test whether an existing finite-field IPS theorem supplies the missing compatibility/representation lower bound. Stop at a matched theorem or a concrete mismatch. The broader search below was an abstract-level screen, not an exhaustive literature review.

1. Match the proof model before importing a lower bound

The main source read was Elbaz–Govindasamy–Lu–Tzameret, Lower Bounds against the Ideal Proof System in Finite Fields, ECCC TR25-080. Coverage: introduction, Definition 9, the statements and surrounding arguments for Corollary 43, Theorem 46, and Section 5.4. Its constant-depth multilinear result concerns a knapsack variant, with prime \(p\ge5\) in the displayed theorem. Its ROABP lower bounds are explicitly placeholder bounds: their input polynomials are not small in the same ROABP model. Definition 9 measures the full certificate circuit and specifies which placeholder restrictions are multilinear; the introductory cofactor description must not be read as permission to ignore arbitrary Boolean-correction circuits.

Our fixed named presentation has small input generators. OR targets are differences of an affine expression and a product of two affine expressions. MOD definitions are an affine named value minus the \((p-1)\)-st power of an affine prefix. Their ROABP widths are bounded by constants depending on the fixed prime, in every order, using the subset-state construction. Primitive Booleanity is univariate. A compact collision axiom is a product of \(\ell\) factors \(1-\lambda_t^{p-1}\); expansion into at most \(2^\ell\) products of at most \((p-1)\ell\) affine factors gives width at most \(2^{p\ell}=n^p\). Thus all generators, and their polynomial-size list, are small ROABP inputs. A theorem for a different hard-input presentation is not automatically a theorem for this one.

Single-polynomial functional inverse test. For an equation \(f=0\) with no Boolean zero over our fixed \(\mathbb F_p\), \(f^{p-2}f=1\) on the Boolean cube. If \(f\) has width \(w\) in a given order, tensoring a fixed number of copies gives width at most \(w^{p-2}\) for that functional inverse; at \(p=2\) it is simply one. Booleanization preserves width as well. Thus a reduction to a single unsatisfiable polynomial that stays small in this model cannot yield the desired lower bound by proving its functional inverse hard. This is the obstruction discussed in the paper's Section 5.4. It does not prove that every multi-generator instance is easy or provide bounds for all Boolean-correction circuits.

No reduction from our named PHP source to the paper's hard instances was found or claimed. Its results remain useful context, but their field, multilinearity, representation and input hypotheses cannot be discarded.

2. Other recent primary-source screens

  • Lu–Santhanam–Tzameret (2025): the displayed hard DNF family expresses hardness of proving algebraic circuit lower bounds; the abstract explicitly leaves open whether those DNFs are tautologies. It is not an established explicit PHP lower bound.
  • Davis–Robere (2026), Res(log) Proves Bounded-Depth Frege Lower Bounds: formalizes lower bounds for ordinary bounded-depth Frege in a weak proof system. The abstract does not supply the required modular-gate compatibility theorem.
  • Alekseev (2026 journal version): proves an exponential bit-size lower bound over \(\mathbb Q\) for the binary value principle in polynomial calculus with extension and square-root rules. That is a different field, instance and measure from our fixed-prime source degree problem.

Exact URLs and reading coverage are retained in the source screen. No new theorem is imported from these abstract-only checks, and no third-party full text is published with this entry.

3. An exact coefficient description of binary flat indicators

Working lemma. Let \(A\in\mathbb F_2^{r\times v}\), \(b\in\mathbb F_2^r\), and let \(f_b(x)\) be the unique multilinear polynomial for \(\mathbf1[Ax=b]\). For every subset \(S\subseteq[v]\),

\[ [x_S]f_b= \begin{cases} 1,&\operatorname{rank}A_S=|S|\text{ and }b\in\operatorname{im}A_S,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \tag{BM-coefficient} \]

Proof. Write \(f_b=\sum_Uc_Ux_U\). Summing \(f_b(\mathbf1_T)\) over \(T\subseteq S\), each \(c_U\) appears \(2^{|S|-|U|}\) times, so in characteristic two only \(c_S\) survives. This sum counts solutions of \(A_Sz=b\) modulo two. If inconsistent it is zero; if consistent it equals \(2^{|S|-\operatorname{rank}A_S}\), which is odd exactly when the solution is unique. This proves (BM-coefficient).

Define the independence polynomial \(I_M(x)=\sum_{S\text{ independent in }M}x_S\) of the binary column matroid \(M=M(A)\). Then \(f_0=I_M\) over \(\mathbb F_2\). For \(b\ne0\), append a column \(e=b\) to obtain \(M_b\); contraction by \(e\) means taking the old columns modulo the line spanned by \(b\). An independent old set remains independent after contraction exactly when it does not span \(b\). Hence

\[ f_b=I_M+I_{M_b/e}\qquad(b\ne0). \tag{BM-contraction} \]

This also handles \(b\) outside the original column span: the two independence polynomials then agree and \(f_b=0\). The zero vector case is separate because an appended zero column is a loop.

If \(A\) has full row rank \(r\), the degree-\(r\) homogeneous component of every \(f_b\) is

\[ (f_b)_{[r]}=\det\big(A\operatorname{diag}(x)A^{\mathsf T}\big). \tag{BM-top} \]

Indeed, every independent \(r\)-set spans every \(b\), so its coefficient is one. Expanding the determinant by Cauchy–Binet gives coefficient \(\det(A_S)^2=\det(A_S)\) on \(x_S\), precisely the same basis indicator. This identity is over \(\mathbb F_2\).

Small symbolic control. For columns \((1,0),(0,1),(1,1)\), the formulas give

\[ f_0=1+x_1+x_2+x_3+x_1x_2+x_1x_3+x_2x_3, \qquad f_{(1,1)}=x_3+x_1x_2+x_1x_3+x_2x_3. \]

They agree directly with Boolean reductions of \((1+x_1+x_3)(1+x_2+x_3)\) and \((x_1+x_3)(x_2+x_3)\). This is a displayed symbolic check, not a new numerical experiment. The lemma gives an exact coefficient oracle by binary rank/span tests; producing all coefficients can still require exponentially many queries. No novelty is claimed.

Relevance and limit. The code-flat functions in the local cofactor bounds therefore have this precise matroid-polynomial interpretation. It does not provide a small circuit for the entire multilinear polynomial, a constant-depth multilinearization theorem, or source compatibility. In particular the determinant description of the top homogeneous component alone is not a representation of all lower components.

4. Route decision

The tested import does not give a sufficient compatibility condition for the complete named source, and no main-goal obligation is discharged. The fixed presentation's small generator complexity is now explicit, so a hard-input placeholder lower bound cannot simply be substituted for the missing theorem. The coefficient identity gives a concrete algebraic description of one relevant function family, not a new PHP lower bound.

Next bounded task. Test whether partial overlap of affine-flat row spaces supplies a usable gluing rule for their costed source moments, using the exact coefficient description and the recorded pair compatibility condition. State the proposed general gluing claim before testing it, and check whole-family consistency rather than independent pairs. Stop at a proof under a genuine structural hypothesis or a counterexample; do not infer such a hypothesis from polynomial inventory alone. The current unproved compatibility approach retains its roughly 5% assessment, not a verdict on the full program.

Process assessment. The primary definitions prevented a model mismatch that the abstracts alone could hide; the small coefficient calculation was worth retaining, but no new infrastructure or broad literature survey is warranted this cycle.

20 September 2026 — Free affine gluing does not enforce the PHP row equations

Status: filtered free-algebra gluing lemma and a PHP-relative local-to-global counterexample; the complete-source endpoint remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Tested claim and stopping point. Can pairwise overlap consistency of low-degree affine observable functionals, each locally compatible with PHP, supply simultaneous source moments? A useful theorem would have to respect the old PHP quotient and every original module cost. This cycle stops after separating the free-algebra statement from that required relative statement, rather than treating a free gluing theorem as source compatibility.

1. A sufficient gluing condition in the free Boolean algebra

Let \(R=\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_v]/(x_i^2-x_i)\), filtered by multilinear degree. For a space \(U\) of homogeneous linear forms, let \(A(U)\) be the subalgebra it generates, including constants. Affine offsets do not change this algebra. For two such spaces,

\[ A(U)_{\le b}\cap A(V)=A(U\cap V)_{\le b}. \tag{GL-intersection} \]

Proof. Take a basis of \(U\cap V\), extend it separately to bases of \(U,V\), then extend their union to an ambient basis. The resulting invertible binary linear coordinate change and its inverse preserve the Boolean degree filtration. Unique multilinear expansions show that membership in both algebras permits only monomials in the shared basis coordinates. This also proves the degree-truncated identity.

Working lemma. Give finitely many spaces \(U_a\) a rooted tree and cutoffs \(b_a\ge0\), with \(b_{\mathrm{parent}(a)}\ge b_a\). For each nonroot vertex require the linear-space running-intersection condition

\[ U_a\cap\sum_{c\notin\mathrm{subtree}(a)}U_c \subseteq U_{\mathrm{parent}(a)}. \tag{GL-tree} \]

Suppose \(\lambda_a:A(U_a)_{\le b_a}\to\mathbb F_2\) agree with their parent on \(A(U_a\cap U_{\mathrm{parent}(a)})_{\le b_a}\). Then they have a common linear extension to \(R_{\le b_{\mathrm{root}}}\). A shared normalization is preserved. This asserts neither multiplicativity nor positivity.

Proof. Remove a leaf \(a\), and inductively glue the other functionals on the sum of their domains. Put \(V=\sum_{c\ne a}U_c\). Every element of the intersection between the leaf domain and that sum lies, by (GL-intersection), in \(A(U_a\cap V)_{\le b_a}\). By (GL-tree) this is contained in the parent's domain. The leaf and the glued functional agree there by the parent-overlap assumption. They therefore define a functional on the enlarged sum: the value on a decomposition is independent of its choice. Removing leaves preserves the required inclusions because the outside sums only shrink. After all leaves have been added, extend from the sum to the ambient filtered vector space by a basis extension. No increase of the largest cutoff is needed. \(\square\)

The condition involves intersections with sums of spaces, not only intersections of pairs. For \(U_1=\langle x\rangle,U_2=\langle y\rangle,U_3=\langle x+y\rangle\), the pair intersections are zero. The normalized degree-one prescriptions \(\lambda_1(x)=\lambda_2(y)=\lambda_3(x+y)=1\) agree on all pair intersections but cannot glue, since \(x+y+(x+y)=0\) would have value one. No tree satisfies (GL-tree) for these spaces. This is the linear consistency issue already underlying the recorded warning about pairwise versus joint independence, not a new source lower bound.

2. Even every proper local PHP test can pass

Working obstruction. Work over any field with the functional unary PHP system \(\mathcal F^{\rm fun}_{m,N}\). Let \(B\ge1\), \(N\ge\max(3,2B)\), and \(m\ge B+1\); one may take the unsatisfiable board \(m=N+1\). Fix a row \(i\). Prescribe evaluation at zero on each algebra generated by one coordinate \(X_{ij}\), through degree \(B\). More strongly, prescribe evaluation at zero on the row-coordinate algebra generated by \(\{X_{ij}:j\in S\}\) for every proper subset \(S\subsetneq[N]\). These prescriptions agree wherever their domains overlap.

Each proper-subset prescription is the restriction of some normalized ordinary degree-\(B\) PHP design. Nevertheless no normalized degree-\(B\) PHP design realizes the full collection of singleton prescriptions.

Proof of local realizability with the original degrees. Given proper \(S\), choose \(j_0\notin S\). Restrict the old board by matching row \(i\) to column \(j_0\): put \(X_{ij_0}=1\), all other cells of row \(i\) to zero, and all other cells in column \(j_0\) to zero. The remaining board has \(m-1\) rows and \(N-1\) columns. Every old generator becomes zero or a generator of this board of no greater original degree. In particular the fixed row equation becomes zero; all other row equations are exactly their residual row equations. Boolean and exclusion generators are zero or retained generators. Thus every original NS multiple through \(B\) maps to a residual NS multiple through \(B\).

Here \(m-1\ge B\) and \(N-1\ge2B-1\). The old all-field matching theorem supplies a normalized degree-\(B\) design on this residual board. Pulling it back gives a normalized design on the original board and sends every polynomial in the coordinates of \(S\) to its constant term. This realizes precisely the prescribed zero evaluation. Different proper subsets may use different residual designs; the assertion does not require their unprescribed old moments to agree.

Global contradiction. A common design would satisfy \(\lambda(X_{ij})=0\) for every \(j\) and \(\lambda(1)=1\). But the original degree-one row equation gives

\[ 0=\lambda\left(\sum_{j=1}^N X_{ij}-1\right)=-1, \tag{GL-row-obstruction} \]

a contradiction over every field. This proof uses only a legal degree-one equation, not multiplication closure or a lowered cost for a canceled generator. In the binary free algebra, the singleton coordinate spaces are jointly independent and satisfy (GL-tree) for every tree; evaluation at the all-zero row gives a free gluing. It is precisely the PHP row relation that prevents a relative gluing. \(\square\)

Consequently no test restricted to a fixed number \(k<N\) of these domains can detect this inconsistency, even if it checks joint realizability rather than only pair intersections. The collection has only \(N\) singleton domains. Polynomial inventory therefore does not fix this generic local-to-global inference. This does not refute simultaneous moment feasibility for a compiled source with a common old root, and does not assert that its prescribed singleton components must be the bad ones above. A shared old root would already forbid these prescriptions.

3. What this does and does not change

The exact pair criterion was already formulated in the old quotient, and the first mixed band already requires one common root and singleton family. Nothing here replaces those requirements. The coherent one-level construction and full affine endpoint remain available; repeating free affine overlap cases would not extend them to multilevel source equations.

For a quotient-aware analogue of the leaf proof, one must control intersections of each domain's image modulo the original bounded NS space with the sum of earlier images, including relations that sum to a constant. Free input-space ranks do not provide that control. Nor has the compiler been shown to supply (GL-tree); proof-tree syntax alone does not prohibit reused old forms across branches. The new coefficient formula computes individual flat coefficients but does not remove either obstruction.

Route assessment. No required general-step implication is discharged. The generic free-overlap gluing shortcut is rejected; a source-dependent quotient gluing theorem remains possible, but no new structural hypothesis is supplied here. I put the chance that further work on this particular rank-only shortcut advances the main goal below 1%, and park it. This is not an estimate for the entire PHP program.

Test whether a compact-domain path can be encoded into a slack codomain while being exactly recoverable, so the heavy-round theorem is needed only on the compact domain. 20 September 2026 — Tail signatures let the compact decoder use filling rows anywhere

Status: working conditional switching theorem and an exact code collision; no general reader or Frege lower bound. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Recovered scope and target. The previous entry pointed back to the original compact/slack gap. The full index assessment and current-term composition theorem already close that gap for their stated reader classes; the old dense-filling-pin obstruction is superseded in that scope. This cycle instead tests removal of the hypothesis that the filling set avoids every tail row. Stop at an injective modified code with its full information cost, or a collision.

1. Statement and the extra information

Use the compact complete-term tree and its matched-first preference. There are \(n+1\) rows, \(n=2^\ell\) labels, a residual flat \(Q\) of size \(N\), and \(N+1\) residual rows. A reader has at most \(M\) terms, each with at most one pin and at most \(r\) rows in total; pin-free terms are allowed. Every tail pattern has at most \(w\) literals. Rows may be both pinned and used in tails, and the tail-row set may now be the whole board.

For each row \(f\), collect all distinct tail patterns occurring on it, and define its tail signature

\[ \kappa_f(y)=\big(\mathbf1[y\in C(p)]\big)_{p\text{ a tail pattern on }f}, \qquad K=\max_f|\{\kappa_f(y):y\in\{0,1\}^\ell\} |. \tag{TS-signature} \]

Empty lists have one signature. Fix a public ordering of the possible signatures for each row, so a signature can be recorded with at most \(K\) choices. Retain the own-row sparse-pinning hypothesis: with \(X_j\) the set of labels pinned on row \(j\), require \(|X_j\cap C(p)|\le|C(p)|/4\) for every tail pattern \(p\) on \(j\). This condition is automatic on rows with no pins. It is not removed by the new code.

Working theorem. Let \(r\ge1\), \(N\ge2\), \(n\ge4N\), and put

\[ s=\lfloor N/12\rfloor-2r\ge\nu_0=\lfloor N/48\rfloor\ge1, \qquad 2^{w+4}s\le e\le n/4,\qquad n2^{-w}\ge4N. \tag{TS-range} \]

Suppose the compact tree has fewer than \(\nu_0\) heavy rounds on every path before a 1-leaf except on an event of probability at most \(p_R\) in the same compact restriction distribution. Define

\[ A_K=\frac{2rK N(N+1)e}{n-N-e+1}. \tag{TS-cost} \]

Then the probability that the compact tree has height at least \(s+2\nu_0\) is at most

\[ p_R+Mr\exp(-s)+A_K^s\big(2N(N+2)\big)^{\nu_0}. \tag{TS-bound} \]

There is no hypothesis on the number of tail rows, and no transfer of a compact round bound to a slack tree. In particular, if also

\[ e\le\frac{n}{16KrN^{3/2}(N+1)}, \tag{TS-small} \]

then \(A_K\le1/(4\sqrt N)\), and the last term is at most \(2^{-N/8+(2r+1)(2+\frac12\log_2N)}\). Thus for \(M\le n^c\), \(s\ge(2c+1)\ln n+\ln r\), and \(N\ge8(c+1)\log_2n+(2r+1)(16+4\log_2N)\), the failure probability is at most \(p_R+2n^{-c-1}\). The resulting height is below \(N/8-2r\). This is a per-reader theorem; a source union and any further image-degree costs still have to be paid.

2. Pair space, decoder, and count

Uniformity without a tail-free reservoir. Choose \(S\) uniformly among all \(e\)-subsets of rows, and then choose uniformly a compact restriction \(\rho'\) in which every row of \(S\) is matched. Let \(\rho\) delete these matches and \(\rho''=\rho'|_S\); it is the same pair code as before. Averaging over \(S\) now gives the exact uniform compact distribution: every \(\rho'\) has exactly \(\binom{n-N}{e}\) admissible sets \(S\), and the conditional families have the same cardinality. This replaces the old reservoir comparison factor \(7/5\), rather than applying it outside its hypotheses.

Fix \(S,Q\). The free outside labels \(E(\rho)\) form a uniform \(e\)-subset of \(O=Q^c\). Call a pair rich if every row-pattern pair has at least \(3s\) labels in \(E(\rho)\cap C(p)\setminus X_j\). The explicit population condition \(n2^{-w}\ge4N\) in (TS-range) is automatic under (TS-small), the lower bound on \(e\), and \(s\ge1\). With this condition and sparse pinning, the available population is at least \(n2^{-w}/2\). Its sample mean is at least \(e2^{-w-1}\ge8s\). The same hypergeometric estimate bounds richness failure by \(Mr\exp(-s)\); it uses subset sampling, not the retracted permutation-entry association claim.

Encoding. On a rich pair with a compact path containing at least \(s\) moves and fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds before its \(s\)-th move, choose the first such path in the fixed order and cut it there. Use the current-term rule: the \(k\)-th moved row \(j_k\) receives the first unpicked code label \(y_k\in E(\rho)\cap C(p_k)\setminus X_{j_k}\) outside the pin labels of all current terms through its node. At most \(s-1\) previous code labels and \(s+\nu_0-1\) current labels are excluded, leaving a choice among the \(3s\) labels. Let \(f_k=\rho''^{-1}(y_k)\in S\).

Keep \((\rho^*,\sigma,\beta,\delta)\) exactly as in the compact code: move \(j_k\) to \(y_k\); in the filling permutation \(\sigma\), replace the value \(y_k\) at \(f_k\) by slot \(k\); record positions/end-of-node bits and the compact path answers. Add only

\[\eta_k=\kappa_{f_k}(y_k),\qquad k=1,\ldots,s.\]

The slot row \(f_k\) is already named by \(\sigma\). All rows of \(S\) were matched in \(\rho'\), so none is a moved or heavy-query row of the original compact path.

Decoder. A hidden slot row now evaluates every tail pattern using \(\eta_k\), while its pin evaluation follows the original current-term rule: it satisfies no pin until its slot is revealed. Once move \(k\) is recovered, \(j_k\) is known from the term and \(\beta\), its label \(y_k=\rho^*(j_k)\) is known, and the decoder restores that actual label to \(f_k\). Later tests use the label itself.

Here is the needed change in the old induction. A tail test on a row of \(S\) is now exactly its test in \(\rho'\), even before the slot is revealed. All other assigned tail rows still agree as before. Thus an earlier term falsified by an assigned tail remains falsified. A hidden pin \((f_k,y_k)\) that is not falsified in reality is matched in reality; the matched-first preference puts such a term after the real current term, unless it is that current term, which the current-term label exclusion forbids. A code on a moved two-role row creates no false matched pin because \(y_k\notin X_{j_k}\). The current term remains tail-consistent: its moved rows have consistent code labels, its already assigned rows have exact tests, and no later moved row occurs in its tail by the complete-term rule. These facts recover the current term, then its round and move answers, inductively. After \(s\) moves the decoder deletes their matches to recover \(\rho\) and restores \(\rho''\) from the revealed filling permutation. This proves injectivity. It never needs a tree on the slack domain.

Counting. For fixed \(S,Q\), adding \(s\) matches has the cardinality ratio

\[ \frac{|\Phi_{e-s}(S)|}{|\Phi_e(S)|} =\prod_{a=0}^{s-1}\frac{(N+1-a)(e-a)}{n-N-e+1+a} \le\left(\frac{(N+1)e}{n-N-e+1}\right)^s. \]

Here the codomain still requires all \(e\) rows of \(S\) to be residual; \(s\le N+1\) makes this possible. There are \(e!\) filling permutations in both the original pair denominator and the code count. The remaining advice has at most \((2r)^sN^sK^s\) choices for positions/bits, move answers and signatures, and at most \((2N(N+2))^{\nu_0}\) for all possible round records with fewer than \(\nu_0\) rounds. A round's hole answer can be indexed among the known rows \(R(\rho^*)\setminus S\), plus empty: a row assigned by a round cannot be a later moved row, so it remains in this known set. Thus its advice does not require naming an arbitrary old row. Summing the shorter round records is bounded by the displayed geometric power. Multiplying the ratio and advice bounds proves the encoding term of (TS-bound).

Average over all \(S\) by exact compact uniformity, add richness failure and the assumed round event, and use that height at least \(s+2\nu_0\) gives one of the two path events. Under (TS-small), \(n-N-e+1\ge n/2\) implies the bound on \(A_K\). Finally \(2N(N+2)\le4N^2\), \(s\ge N/12-2r-1\), and \(\nu_0\le N/48\) give exactly the displayed exponent. All factors, including \(K^s\), have been charged. \(\square\)

3. A collision if the filling-tail information is omitted

This is an explicit finite control of injectivity, not a test of the asymptotic probability regime. Use labels \(0,\ldots,7\), rows \(0,\ldots,8\), \(Q=\{0,4\}\), \(S=\{0\}\), and one move. Let the proposed common code restriction have residual rows \(\{0,3,4\}\) and matches

\[1\mapsto5,\quad2\mapsto6,\quad5\mapsto1,\quad6\mapsto2,\quad7\mapsto3,\quad8\mapsto7.\]

There are two original pairs. In pair A, remove the match \(1\mapsto5\) from this restriction and fill row \(0\) with \(5\). In pair B, remove \(2\mapsto6\) and fill row \(0\) with \(6\). Their compact residual sets are respectively \(\{1,3,4\}\) and \(\{2,3,4\}\). Consider the ordered pin-free reader

\[ T_A=[\operatorname{bit}_0(0)=1]\land[\operatorname{bit}_2(1)=1],\qquad T_B=[\operatorname{bit}_0(0)=0]\land[\operatorname{bit}_2(2)=1]. \]

Bit zero is the least significant bit, and notation \(\operatorname{bit}_t(i)\) refers to row \(i\)'s label. In pair A the current term is \(T_A\); in pair B it is \(T_B\), since the other term is falsified by row zero. The current term queries respectively row one or two. Both code labels, \(5\) and \(6\), satisfy its bit-two pattern, and both compact queries have the same first answer \(0\). The code restriction is the displayed one in both cases, \(\sigma\) maps row zero to slot one, \(\beta\) says the second row of the current term is the sole move, and \(\delta\) contains \(0\). There are no pin-label exclusions. Thus the old code without \(\eta\) is identical for two different pairs once filling rows are allowed in tails. The row-zero tail signatures distinguish the pairs. This does not contradict the historical decoder, whose filling rows were excluded from all tails.

4. Nonvacuity and the remaining general obligation

A row with just one distinct tail pattern has \(K_f\le2\), independently of the pattern's literal width. For a nonvacuous all-tail-row example, fix one pin label \(x_*\), give every row one pattern \(p_j\) with at least four satisfying labels, and allow any polynomial inventory of terms \([i\mapsto x_*]\land\bigwedge_{j\in J}p_j\) with \(i\notin J\), \(1\le|J|\le r-1\). Every row may occur in tails, and every row may be pinned. Here \(K\le2\), own-row sparsity holds, and every compact path has at most one heavy round because all rounds trigger the same hole \(x_*\), which is used or emptied at its first round. Thus \(p_R=0\) when \(\nu_0\ge2\). Fixed \(r\), polylogarithmic \(N\), and any fixed literal-width exponent below one leave a nonempty range for \(e\) for sufficiently large \(n\). This is a switching application, not a claimed new proof-system lower bound.

For general readers \(K\) can equal \(n\) even when every individual tail pattern is one literal: include all \(\ell\) coordinate tests on a row. Then this whole-signature code pays too much. Neither polynomial inventory nor small per-pattern width supplies the missing signature bound. In the regime \(K\le n^\kappa\) and \(2^w\le n^\theta\), fixed \(r\) and polylogarithmic \(N\) permit (TS-small) when \(\theta+\kappa<1\); the strict saving, not the existence of signatures, is the useful hypothesis.

Contribution and next step. This removes one actual reservoir hypothesis from the compact decoder at an explicit cost, while retaining own-row sparsity and a separately proved compact round bound. It does not solve general literal readers, parity-containing terms, or the full source-moment obligation. The next bounded test is whether the signatures can be replaced by cheaper path-dependent information while keeping exact recovery; start with the two-pair collision above and the full coordinate-test family. Stop at an injective code with a strictly smaller charge or a scoped information obstruction. I estimate a roughly 5% chance that this signature/compression line advances the main general-step obligation, not the whole program.
