20 September 2026 — Bound code multiplicity instead of recording whole tail signatures

Status: working trace-rank bound and conditional switching corollary; exact finite checks cover the pin-free core, not heavy-round decoding. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and stopping point. The signature code removes the tail-free filling reservoir but can charge \(K=n\) per move. Test whether the raw code's multiplicity can instead be bounded by low-degree trace polynomials. Stop at a proved bound with its retained pin hypotheses, or a collision defeating the argument. Initial planning occurred during the preceding cycle's preparation interval; this cycle measures the developed proof and checks.

1. Raw-code fibers have triangular low-degree witnesses

Use the compact pair-space encoder, current-term label exclusions, and complete-term tree of the previous proof, with arbitrary filling set \(S\). Retain the rule that a moved row \(j\)'s code label lies outside its own pin set \(X_j\). Do not record the signatures \(\eta\). A raw code is \((\rho^*,\sigma,\beta,\delta)\), for a path cut after \(s\) moves and with fewer than \(\nu\) heavy rounds. The argument also permits earlier termination when any term is already satisfied; the supplied round bound must use the same tree convention. There are exactly \(s\) hidden filling slots. Put \(m=s\ell\) and

\[ d=\min\{m,rw(s+\nu)\},\qquad L(m,d)=\sum_{a=0}^{d}\binom ma. \tag{TL-dimension} \]

Working theorem. Every fixed raw code has at most \(L(m,d)\) preimage pairs produced by this encoder, even when all rows occur in tails. This is a list-size bound; no unique decoder for the raw code is asserted. It uses no bound on the number of full row signatures. The own-row pin exclusion and current-term label exclusion are essential to the proof below.

What one code fixes. It fixes \(S,Q\), the slot rows \(f_k\) through \(\sigma\), and the assigned labels of \(\rho^*\). For a preimage \(a\), write \(y^a_k\) for slot \(k\)'s label and \(j^a_k\) for its moved row. Since \(\rho^*\) is an injection and \(\rho^*(j^a_k)=y^a_k\), the vector \(y^a\) identifies the moved rows, the slack restriction obtained by deleting them, and the filling. Distinct preimages therefore give distinct slot-label vectors. Round hole answers are indexed in the fixed set \(R(\rho^*)\setminus S\), plus empty, as in the preceding count; a row assigned by a round cannot be a later moved row.

Common-prefix observation. If two preimages have the same current terms up to some node, the raw marks and answers recover the same queries, moves, and revealed slots throughout that prefix. At the next node, each candidate current term's pin status is the same in both preimages:

  • A pin matched by an untouched code match or an explicit nonslot filling label is matched in every preimage. Its row cannot be a moved row in another preimage, since moving it to that code label would violate the own-row pin exclusion.
  • A pin on a previously queried row or revealed filling slot is decided by the common prefix.
  • An alive current pin must be on an unassigned row of the fixed set \(R(\rho^*)\setminus S\). If its row were a future coded move, this node's heavy round would assign it, contradicting its later occurrence as a light move.
  • A current pin cannot be on an unrevealed filling slot. Such a row is already matched outside \(Q\) in reality. A matching pin would equal that slot's code label, forbidden by the current-term exclusion up to its revealing move; every other pin on that row is dead.

These cases also cover used or emptied holes, which are determined by the common prefix. Thus matched-first priority for a candidate current term is fixed across all preimages sharing that prefix. If the next current term is the same, the next segment of marks and answers is decoded identically. Distinct preimages must therefore first differ at a current term, not solely at an unnamed row answer or a parsing choice.

Trace polynomial. For each preimage \(a\), introduce \(\ell\) formal Boolean bits for each slot label \(y_k\). At each node of its trace, form an augmented partial assignment: keep all code matches, restore all nonslot filling rows at their explicit sigma labels and its earlier query answers, put the already revealed filling labels to their known values, and use the formal slot bits for all unrevealed filling rows. Leave the still-unassigned rows of \(R(\rho^*)\setminus S\) unassigned. For the node's current term, multiply the indicators of its tail patterns on the assigned or formal rows; omit tail patterns on the remaining unassigned rows. Known consistent patterns contribute one. Patterns on an unrevealed slot contribute their literal indicator, of degree at most \(w\). Let \(P_a(y)\) be the product of these factors over the trace, reduced multilinearly over \(\mathbb F_2\).

Every diagonal value satisfies \(P_a(y^a)=1\). Tail rows already assigned when a term is chosen are consistent with it. Any row of that term that is a future coded move is moved at this very node, by the complete-term rule, so its code label is consistent too. Rows about to be assigned by the heavy round are still in the fixed unassigned set and are omitted; their later round answer need not satisfy the tail. This omission is necessary. All filling-row tests at \(y^a\) are their actual tests. Each node contributes at most \(rw\) degree; every visited node has a move or a round, so there are fewer than \(s+\nu\) such nodes. Hence \(\deg P_a\le d\).

Triangularity. Order preimages lexicographically by their current-term traces, using matched-first priority at each shared prefix. The preceding observation makes this order well-defined. For \(a\) earlier than \(b\), take their first different current term. The term selected by \(a\) has earlier priority in \(b\) as well, so it must be falsified in \(b\); otherwise \(b\)'s tree would select it. Its pin status agrees across the shared prefix, so the falsification must be through an assigned tail row. The augmented assignment used by \(P_a\), evaluated at \(y^b\), preserves this falsifier. It changes no assigned row of \(b\): differences are additional assignments to future coded moves, and these cannot undo an existing falsification. The corresponding factor is zero, so

\[ P_a(y^a)=1,\qquad P_a(y^b)=0\quad(a<b). \tag{TL-triangle} \]

The evaluation matrix is triangular with diagonal one over \(\mathbb F_2\). Thus its rows, and the polynomials \(P_a\), are linearly independent. The space of multilinear polynomials of degree at most \(d\) in \(m\) variables has dimension \(L(m,d)\), proving the bound. This is an algebraic counting argument, not an assertion that a polynomial-time decoder enumerates the list. \(\square\)

2. Conditional composition with no full-signature hypothesis

Retain the setting, own-row sparse pinning, population condition \(n2^{-w}\ge4N\), and other base parameters (TS-range) of the signature theorem. Put \(\nu=\nu_0\), and

\[ A_0=\frac{2rN(N+1)e}{n-N-e+1}. \]

Working corollary. If \(p_R\) bounds the same compact tree's event of at least \(\nu_0\) rounds before a 1-leaf, its probability of height at least \(s+2\nu_0\) is at most

\[ p_R+Mr\exp(-s)+L(s\ell,d)A_0^s\big(2N(N+2)\big)^{\nu_0}. \tag{TL-probability} \]

Proof. The old raw-code count is exactly the preceding signature-code count with the \(K^s\) advice factor removed. An encoder with at most \(L(s\ell,d)\) preimages per code bounds the rich bad pairs by that factor times the code count. Exact averaging over all filling sets gives the uniform compact distribution, and richness still follows from the same uniform-subset estimate. Add the independently supplied compact round event. Neither a slack-tree round estimate nor a permutation negative-association premise is used.

For \(0\le\alpha=d/(s\ell)\le1/2\),

\[ L(s\ell,d)\le2^{s\ell H_2(\alpha)}=n^{sH_2(\alpha)},\quad H_2(\alpha)=-\alpha\log_2\alpha-(1-\alpha)\log_2(1-\alpha). \tag{TL-entropy} \]

For \(0<\alpha\le1/2\), expand \((\alpha+(1-\alpha))^{s\ell}=1\). Every term of index at most \(d\), after removing its binomial coefficient, is at least \(\alpha^d(1-\alpha)^{s\ell-d}\). Summing gives (TL-entropy); \(d=0\) is immediate. Thus the effective cost per move is at most \(n^{H_2(\alpha)}\), regardless of \(K\). With fixed \(r\), polylogarithmic \(N\), and \(w\le\theta\ell\), feasibility follows whenever \(\theta+H_2(r\theta(1+\nu_0/s))<1\), in the range where that entropy argument applies.

A simple nonvacuous range. Fix \(r,c\), take sufficiently large polylogarithmic \(N\) satisfying the preceding height/tail-probability inequalities, and assume \(w\le\ell/(64r)\). Since \(s\ge\nu_0\), \(\alpha\le1/32\), and \(H_2(1/32)<7/32\): its first term is \(5/32\), and \(-(1-\alpha)\log_2(1-\alpha)\le\alpha/\ln2<2\alpha\). Choose \(e=\lceil n^{1/3}\rceil\). The richness and population inequalities hold eventually, and

\[ n^{H_2(\alpha)}A_0 \le n^{-43/96+o(1)}\le\frac1{4\sqrt N}. \]

The same elementary exponent calculation as in the signature theorem gives failure at most \(p_R+2n^{-c-1}\) and height below \(N/8-2r\). This conditional switching statement permits all rows to be tail rows and all coordinate tests to occur on them, even though those tests can have \(K=n\). It retains sparse own-row pins, fixed \(r\) in this displayed asymptotic range, and a valid round bound; no general source lower bound follows.

3. Exact finite controls and limitations

The bounded C++ checker fixes a code board at \(n=8,N=2\), uses one or two slots, and enumerates every ordered candidate moved-row tuple for each reader. It reconstructs the compact restriction, finds the first sufficiently long path, checks the encoder's greedy label choices, groups identical raw advice, constructs the multilinear trace polynomials, and checks diagonal one, triangular zeros, and exact \(\mathbb F_2\) matrix rank. Every reader, accepted preimage, polynomial and evaluation row is retained in the complete reviewed output.

The final run considered 2,340 candidate inputs for 130 readers. It accepted 31 preimages in 27 code fibers; the two nontrivial fibers have sizes two and four. All triangular and rank checks passed. The four-preimage control has two moves and independent choices of two hidden filling labels, so the check is not confined to a single slot. These are pin-free checks of the rank core; they do not test heavy-round decoding, large-parameter probabilities, or prove the general theorem. The pin-status argument is the separate proof in Section 1.

An initial run used selected-term stopping, as in the historical pair-space checker; it is retained as superseded diagnostic output, separate from the final checker's early-stop convention. The final code stops when any term is already satisfied. The triangular proof permits both conventions; the final finite counts refer only to the latter. The first compilation also failed on formatting warnings under -Werror; these were fixed before the accepted build. Reproduction and scope are in the run record.

Why the own-pin condition remains. Use the one-slot board of the previous two-pair control, with code matches \(1\mapsto5,2\mapsto6\), filling row zero, and residual flat \(\{0,4\}\). Replace its reader by

\[ [2\mapsto6]\land[\operatorname{bit}_2(1)=1],\qquad [1\mapsto5]\land[\operatorname{bit}_2(2)=1]. \]

Pair A moves row one, pair B moves row two; their current terms are respectively the first and second, with the other pin dead. The raw codes still coincide if own-row exclusions are dropped: each chosen code label differs from its current term's pin label. Filling row zero now has no tail patterns, so both tail trace polynomials are constant one. The missing distinction is whether a code-matched pinned row was actually moved in the other preimage. This is a concrete failure of (TL-triangle) after removing the own-pin rule, consistent with the historical two-role warning; it does not contradict the theorem just proved or exclude a different counting argument.

4. Contribution and next obligation

The general-step obligation remains open, but the literal-route decoder now has a proved alternative to the whole-signature cost: low-degree trace rank bounds ambiguity without requiring unique recovery or a tail-free reservoir. The full-coordinate signature example no longer blocks the stated small-literal regime. This is a constructive restricted improvement, not a general switching theorem or a Frege lower bound.

Next bounded task. Test whether the remaining own-row pin obstruction can be handled at acceptable code cost. Start from the crossed-pin two-pair control above, and distinguish information about which code matches were originally residual from hidden filling-tail bits. Stop at a proved counting/decoding mechanism preserving a positive exponent saving, or a scoped obstruction. Do not reintroduce a full-label cost without paying it. The current trace-counting line gets a roughly 10% assessment of advancing the main general-step obligation; the round bound and proof-source hypotheses are still independent gaps.

Process assessment. Counting a code's possible preimages avoided a more complicated decoder; the two-move control and the explicit terminal convention provided useful falsification checks, while no broad regression or new framework layer was needed.

20 September 2026 — Reveal false code matches to remove own-row pin sparsity

Status: working composition theorem for low-degree row predicates and a full-single-row switching corollary; no general-source or Frege lower bound. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and stopping point. The crossed-pin control defeats the preceding tail-only trace argument when a code match on a moved row creates a false matched pin. Can that event be resolved at less than a full-label cost? Stop at a proved correction protocol and charged list bound, or a counterexample. The construction below marks the offending row as originally residual and reveals its filling slot; it does not charge the row's name.

1. General row predicates and the bound

Use the compact complete-term tree and pair space of the preceding entries, with \(n=2^\ell\), residual flat \(Q\) of size \(N\), and \(N+1\) residual rows. A term has at most one pin and at most \(r\) rows total; pin-free terms are allowed. Its tail is a conjunction of one predicate on each of its tail rows. For every such predicate \(p\), assume

\[ |C(p)|\ge\beta n,\qquad \mathbf1_{C(p)}\text{ has a multilinear }\mathbb F_2\text{ polynomial of degree at most }k. \tag{PP-predicates} \]

Here \(0<\beta\le1\), and \(M\) bounds the number of terms. The predicates may be affine-flat indicators or other Boolean row predicates, not only literal conjunctions. There is no own-row pin-sparsity condition and no restriction on how many rows occur in tails. Different rows may have different predicate lists.

Put \(s=\lfloor N/12\rfloor-2r\ge\nu=\lfloor N/48\rfloor\ge1\), and assume \(n\ge4N\), \(\beta n\ge2N\), and \(16s/\beta\le e\le n/4\). Define

\[ A_0=\frac{2rN(N+1)e}{n-N-e+1},\quad W=(s+2)^{2s+\nu},\quad d=\min\{s\ell,rk(2s+\nu)\},\quad L=\sum_{a=0}^{d}\binom{s\ell}{a}. \tag{PP-costs} \]

Working theorem. Suppose \(p_R\) bounds the event that some compact-tree path has at least \(\nu\) heavy rounds before its first 1-leaf. Then the probability of height at least \(s+2\nu\) is at most

\[ p_R+Mr\exp(-s)+WL A_0^s\big(2N(N+2)\big)^\nu. \tag{PP-bound} \]

The round hypothesis refers to the same compact tree, including its chosen stopping convention. The slack restriction is used only for encoding. The theorem provides a probability/counting bound, not an efficient unique decoder for the raw code.

2. Correction protocol and its success

Choose the filling set \(S\) among all \(e\)-sets of rows. Use the exact compact averaging, raw code format and round-answer indexing from the signature proof. At each move choose the first unused label in \(E(\rho)\cap C(p)\) outside the pin labels of the original current terms through that node. Omit the own-row exclusion \(X_j\). No full tail signatures are recorded.

Each \(E(\rho)\cap C(p)\) has hypergeometric mean at least \(e\beta/2\ge8s\), since \(|C(p)\setminus Q|\ge\beta n/2\). With probability at least \(1-Mr\exp(-s)\), every such set has at least \(3s\) labels. Fewer than \(s\) previous labels and at most \(s+\nu-1\) current pin labels are excluded, so a choice exists. No permutation-entry association is used.

Auxiliary simulator. The encoder knows the original pair and its chosen compact path. For the proof, let a simulator know the true tail tests of all hidden filling slots; later those tests become the variables in a rank argument, so this knowledge is not free advice in the count. Initialize its working assignment with all code matches and explicit nonslot filling labels. An unrevealed slot evaluates tails at its true filling label but satisfies no pin. Keep a separate flag saying which matches are regarded as part of the initial matching; every replayed row query clears that row's initial-match flag, and path answers never acquire it. Retain used/emptied-hole information from the decoded prefix.

Before each original node, select a candidate term by the usual matched-first preference in this working state, ignoring artificial satisfaction caused by the code. If it is the actual current term, record advance and replay the node using the existing marks and answers. Each actual moved row reveals its slot as usual. Otherwise the candidate must have a false matched pin on an as-yet-unprocessed coded move row \(j_a\). Record peel(a), remove that artificial match so that \(j_a\) is again unassigned, mark it as originally residual, and reveal its filling row's label \(\rho^*(j_a)\). Do not assign \(j_a\) its future path answer at this point. Select a candidate again without advancing the original path.

Why the actual current term stays visible. Its already assigned tails are tested exactly. Extra code assignments on its other tails are consistent: any such future light move occurs at this node by the complete-term rule. A row assigned by the impending heavy round remains unassigned in the simulator. A genuinely matched current pin cannot be on an unrevealed filling slot, since its label would be one of the forbidden current-term labels for that slot's later code move. Its other matched pins are visible. An alive current pin cannot be on a future coded light move, because its heavy round assigns that row now. Pins satisfied or killed by earlier answers are decided by the common prefix and retain the correct initial-matching flag. Peeling a future move merely removes an extra assignment to an originally unassigned row; revealing a filling slot restores its actual initial label.

Why a misleading earlier candidate can be peeled. An assigned tail falsifier in the original path remains a falsifier: tail tests on filling rows are exact, all genuinely assigned old rows agree, and the remaining code assignments only fill originally unassigned rows. Hence a term that is dead in reality but selected by the simulator can become live only through its pin. Ignoring pins on hidden filling slots creates no false live pin. Used holes and prior answers are unchanged. The only remaining false positive is a code match \(j_a\mapsto y_a\) making an outside pin look initially matched although \(j_a\) was residual. Similarly, an earlier candidate cannot gain matched-first priority in any other way. Its row is named by the candidate's pin; the encoder need record only its slot index \(a\). Removing that match eliminates this false positive. A peeled row cannot cause a second such event, including after its later genuine query, because it remains flagged as originally residual.

There are at most \(s\) peeling events and fewer than \(s+\nu\) genuine nodes. The process therefore reaches and replays every original node, possibly revealing slots out of order, and finishes after fewer than \(2s+\nu\) events. This proof covers heavy nodes as well as move-only nodes; it does not infer a heavy-round estimate.

3. Advice and the new triangular argument

Record the event word, whose alphabet is advance, the \(s\) slot choices peel(a), and an end/padding symbol. Padding to length \(2s+\nu\) gives at most \(W\) words. The candidate terms themselves and the offending row names are not recorded.

Fix a raw code and this word. Two preimages with the same selected candidate terms through an event have the same simulated prefix. A peeling instruction names a slot; its candidate pin names the row, so its revealed label is the fixed code match. An advance uses the same original marks and answers. Therefore all pin tests and initial-match flags at the next event are fixed across these preimages: hidden filling pins are declared dead, revealed labels are known constants, and every other match, query answer and residual flag is determined by the prefix. The only remaining variable tests are the tails on unrevealed filling slots.

For each preimage, multiply the tail indicators of every selected candidate along this extended trace. Evaluate known assigned rows at their values, insert formal \(\ell\)-bit labels at unrevealed slots, and omit still-unassigned rows. Every selected candidate is not falsified in its simulator, so the diagonal product is one. Its degree is at most \(rk\) per event, hence at most \(d\) after Boolean reduction. Order preimages lexicographically by selected candidate terms with their simulated matched-first priority. At a first difference the earlier candidate has the same pin status in both simulators, so it must be falsified by a tail in the later one. Its factor is zero there. This gives a triangular matrix with diagonal one, exactly as in the preceding list-rank proof, now without requiring own-row pin exclusions.

Thus each raw-code/word pair has at most \(L\) preimages. The old raw-code count contributes \(A_0^s(2N(N+2))^\nu\); multiplication by \(W L\), exact averaging over filling sets, and the richness and round events prove (PP-bound). A fully known slot-label vector still determines all moved rows through the injective code matching, so identical complete traces cannot hide different preimages.

Nonvacuous asymptotics. For fixed \(r,c\), let \(N\) be sufficiently large and polylogarithmic, with the previous requirements \(s\ge(2c+1)\ln n+\ln r\) and \(N\ge8(c+1)\log_2n+(2r+1)(16+4\log_2N)\). Suppose \(\beta\ge n^{-1/3}\), \(k\le\ell/(96r)\), and take \(e=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil\). Then \(d/(s\ell)\le3rk/\ell\le1/32\). The proved entropy estimate gives \(L^{1/s}\le n^{7/32}\), while \(W^{1/s}\le(s+2)^3\). Consequently

\[ W^{1/s}L^{1/s}A_0\le n^{-9/32+o(1)}\le\frac1{4\sqrt N}. \]

Richness holds since \(e\beta\ge n^{1/6}\), and all other population/size conditions hold eventually. The same explicit exponent calculation yields failure at most \(p_R+2n^{-c-1}\) and height below \(N/8-2r\). This is a positive counting gain after paying for both the event word and the list size.

4. Application to complete single-tail classes

Working corollary. Fix \(c>0\). A reader of at most \(n^c\) terms is a union of full classes: a class \((j,p,x)\) contains every term \([i\mapsto x]\land p(j)\) for \(i\ne j\). Predicates may share rows arbitrarily. Assume each \(C(p)\) has at least \(n^{2/3}\) labels and its indicator has \(\mathbb F_2\) degree at most \(\ell/192\). For sufficiently large \(n\), a suitable power-of-two \(N=\operatorname{polylog}n\) gives a compact matching decision tree of height below \(N/8-4\), except with probability at most \(10n^{-c-1}\). Simultaneously for at most \(n^c\) such readers, failure is at most \(10/n\). No pin-sparsity or tail-row-reservoir hypothesis is needed.

Round-bound audit and proof. The repaired full-single-row proof uses the literal-width assumption only as a lower bound on the size of each nonempty row union \(U_{x,j}\), and hence in \(|J_x|\le n^{1/3}u(x)\). Its other steps concern fixed label sets, affine-flat inclusion probabilities, exact uniform-bijection hit bounds, and the fullness of a class. They do not use individual coordinate literals. Replacing cubes by the stated fixed predicate sets preserves both size uses. Thus the same proof and explicit threshold on \(N\) give its \(8n^{-c-1}\) exceptional probability. It applies to the complete-term ordering as well: its round count uses the matched-first property immediately before a heavy round, distinct trigger holes, and the charged contributing rows, not satisfaction of the tail before the round.

The proof's final count is strictly below \(N/192+N/128=5N/384\). Taking also \(N\ge256\) makes this less than \(\nu=\lfloor N/48\rfloor\), resolving the integer-threshold issue instead of replacing a strict real bound by a stronger integer bound. Apply the new theorem with \(r=2\), \(\beta=n^{-1/3}\), \(k\le\ell/192\), and \(e=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil\), enlarging the fixed polylogarithmic threshold as needed. Add its \(2n^{-c-1}\) to the round failure and union over the reader family. All hypotheses concern the same uniform compact-flat restriction.

This includes literal patterns with at most \(\ell/192\) literals, and consistent binary affine-flat predicates of codimension at most \(\ell/192\): their indicators are products of that many affine linear factors and their densities are \(2^{-k}\ge n^{-1/192}\). In particular rowwise parity tests are allowed. This does not cover arbitrary parities spanning many rows or arbitrary partial classes; it is not the complete multilevel source obligation.

5. Finite checks and scope

The new bounded C++ checker tests pins outside \(Q\), so there are no heavy rounds. It enumerates 2,370 candidate inputs for 131 small readers on \(n=8,N=2\), validates greedy current-term label choices, executes the peeling protocol, and groups equal raw codes plus event words. The accepted 37 preimages form 35 groups; two groups have size two. There are five peeling events, including one revealing a later slot before the first move. All exact triangular and rank checks pass. The maximum raw-code fiber before event advice has size four.

The three explicit controls are the crossed-pin collision, a combination of peeling with a nontrivial filling-tail list, and an early revelation of slot two before move one. These tests check both sides of the proposed repair, not just a code that was already injective. The complete output preserves every tested reader, accepted preimage, event trace, polynomial and evaluation row; reproduction and limitations are recorded separately. They do not verify heavy-round cases, the general probability bound, or a proof-system lower bound. Those claims rest on the full arguments above.

6. Contribution and next step

The literal-route composition now removes both the tail-free reservoir and own-row pin sparsity in the displayed low-degree/density regime. A previously repaired round estimate now composes to give the full-single-row switching statement, including rowwise affine predicates. The main goal is still open: arbitrary multilevel sources, general reader round counts, degree accounting for their normalization, and cross-row affine structure are not discharged by this class.

Next bounded task. Audit which exact compiled-source obligation this new switching statement can discharge. Compare the actual source input format and the retained-affine endpoint before extending the reader class again. Stop at a concrete costed transfer or an explicit missing hypothesis; do not substitute rowwise predicates for arbitrary cross-row inputs. I retain a roughly 10% assessment that the current counting route advances the main general-step obligation, not a verdict on the entire program.

Process assessment. Identifying an offending row from the already selected pin avoids paying its old-board name; the bounded controls test early revelation and nontrivial remaining lists, while the final application reuses the repaired probability proof with an explicit hypothesis audit.

20 September 2026 — Logarithmic reader height repairs the residual degree budget, not the source grammar

Status: corrected residual-ledger inference, logarithmic full-single-row switching, and a scoped costed profile; arbitrary compiled sources remain uncovered. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

General claim under audit. Does the new full-single-row switching theorem supply the missing complete-source step? It would need both an affordable algebraic image and a proved reduction of the actual source inputs into this reader class. This cycle checks those two requirements separately and stops at an explicit ledger and a precise remaining source hypothesis. The preceding paused clock contained checkpoint/pause handoff only; its separate journal is archived, and the research interval here starts at high reasoning.

1. A constant-fraction height is not the cited weight theorem's full hypothesis

The historical height-budget observation said that \(2t+r\le N/4\) suffices for the residual cube-volume weight step. That implication omitted conditions from the cited finite theorem. Its displayed choice is

\[ k'=\left\lfloor\frac{N/4-D'}{2D'+1}\right\rfloor,\quad T'=2k'+1,\quad B'=T'D'+k'\le N/4, \tag{WA-ledger} \]

where \(D'\) must cover the full incoming proof/witness ceiling, not only a collected value degree. The finite cube-volume theorem also requires \(k'\ge2\). For the sharpened affine threshold, its low-rank map must actually fit \(T'\); a sufficient extra inequality is

\[ r_{\rm high}-2\le T',\qquad r_{\rm high}=\left\lceil\frac{(N+1)\log_2N\,\ln(16M)}{k'}\right\rceil. \tag{WA-low-map} \]

These requirements do not follow from \(D'\le N/4\). For an exact arithmetic control, \(N=1024,D'=128\) obey that inequality and \(D'\ge\max(13,\log_2N)\), but \(k'=\lfloor128/257\rfloor=0\). In particular \(k'\ge2\) already requires \(D'\le N/20-2/5\). Even that is not the low-map condition. The old finite theorem is not refuted; its hypotheses were missing from the later application.

Correction scope. Withdraw the claim that the height inequality alone justifies this residual weight step. The original PT-choice calculation must retain \(k'\ge2\) and its asserted low-map fit, or a separately justified larger substitution budget. Its intended sufficiently-large regime with polylogarithmic degree in the old board remains available. The new switching theorems' tree-height and probability statements do not depend on this weight application and remain unchanged. No PC/NS identification for an augmented source is inferred.

A useful sufficient asymptotic regime is \((D')^2\log N\,\log(16M)=o(N)\), along with the displayed lower bounds: then \(k'=\Theta(N/D')\), \(r_{\rm high}=O(D'\log N\log M)=o(T')\), and the actual substitution ledger fits. If \(D'\le(\log n)^a\), \(M\le n^c\), and \(N\) is a power of two of order \((\log n)^A\), choosing \(A>2a+1\) supplies this room. This illustrates why image degree independent of \(N\), not merely a fixed fraction of it, is useful.

2. Full single-row classes actually have logarithmically many rounds

Keep the reader and row-predicate hypotheses of the new full-single-row theorem: fixed \(c>0\), at most \(n^c\) terms, full classes \((j,p,x)\), predicate density at least \(n^{-1/3}\), and indicator degree at most \(\ell/192\). Let \(N\) be polylogarithmic in \(n\), of an arbitrarily chosen fixed power, and sufficiently large compared with \(\log n\). Reuse

\[ K=2^{\lceil c\rceil+4},\quad \lambda=\frac{3(c+3)\ln n}{\ln2},\quad q_0=\lceil2c+6\rceil, \quad a=\left\lceil\max\{8\mathrm e(1+K\lambda),(c+2)\log_2n\}\right\rceil, \quad R=K(1+a+q_0). \tag{LH-parameters} \]

Sharper round bound. Every path of the same compact complete-term tree has fewer than \(R=O_c(\log n)\) rounds before its first 1-leaf, except with probability at most \(8n^{-c-1}\), for all sufficiently large \(n\). In particular the bound no longer grows linearly with the chosen residual size \(N\).

Proof, identifying the changed step. Use the deterministic quantities \(u(x),M_j(z),\Lambda,v(x),V\) and the seven-event decomposition in the repaired proof. Density supplies its two population uses exactly as audited in the preceding cycle. The heavy-label and large-good-pair events leave fewer than \(K\) contributing heavy labels and fewer than \(K\) light trigger labels per contributing row. The outside-pair estimate, on its good event and in the absence of a satisfied term, still gives \(\Lambda\le v(Q)+3N\); \(V\le K\Lambda\) and \(v(x)<\lambda\) for light labels are unchanged.

Change only the small-loading cutoff to \(\theta=1/N\). If \(V\le8NK\), the fixed set \(A_\theta=\{x:v(x)\ge1/N\}\) has size at most \(8KN^2\), still polylogarithmic. Outside its affine-flat inclusion event it meets \(Q\) in fewer than \(K\) labels, and

\[v(Q)<1+K\lambda.\tag{LH-loading}\]

If \(V>8NK\), the same outside-pair estimate forces \(v(Q)\ge V/(2K)\). The fixed set \(A=\{x:v(x)\ge V/(4KN)\}\) has size at most \(4KN\); its complement contributes at most \(V/(4K)\) to \(v(Q)\). Hence \(|A\cap Q|>V/(4K\lambda)>2N/\lambda\ge K\) once \(N\ge K\lambda\), another fixed-set exceptional event. A fixed polylogarithmic set contains \(K\) points of the random flat with probability at most \(n^{-c-2}\) eventually: \(K\) points contain \(\lceil c\rceil+5\) affinely independent points, and the recorded inclusion count applies. Thus (LH-loading) holds on the needed good event, with no additional matching-dependent conditioning.

Given a good \(Q\), the uniform-bijection row-hit bound for matched contributing rows is now

\[ \Pr(\text{at least }a\text{ matched contributing rows}\mid Q) \le\left(\frac{2\mathrm e(1+K\lambda)}a\right)^a \le4^{-a}\le n^{-2c-4}. \]

This is conditioned on \(Q\), not on absence of satisfaction. The residual-row bound is unchanged: with predicate density \(\beta\ge n^{-1/3}\), the relevant fixed-given-\(Q\) row set has size at most \(N\lambda/\beta\), and the probability of \(q_0\) such residual rows is \(\operatorname{polylog}(n)n^{-2q_0/3}\le n^{-c-2}\) eventually. The earlier heavy-label, outside-pair, and large-good-pair events keep their bounds because \(N\), \(|A_\theta|\), and \(|A|\) are still polylogarithmic. The same union bound is at most \(8n^{-c-1}\). The path charge is now strictly below \(K+K(a+q_0)=R\), using distinct trigger holes and the complete-term matched-first rule. This proves the sharper round statement.

Logarithmic switching height. The peeling/list proof, before its convenient choice of floor parameters, works for arbitrary integers \(1\le\nu\le s\le N+1\) and the same richness/denominator hypotheses: the ratio needs \(s\le N+1\), and the code-choice and word bounds use only \(\nu\le s\). Set

\[ \nu=R,\qquad s=\left\lceil\max\{R,(2c+1)\ln n+\ln2\}\right\rceil, \qquad e=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil, \qquad H=s+2\nu=O_c(\log n). \tag{LH-height} \]

Take \(N\ge2H\), increasing the chosen polylogarithmic residual if necessary. Its event word has \(W^{1/s}\le(s+2)^3\), and its trace-list root is at most \(n^{7/32}\), since \(r=2\) and \(k\le\ell/192\). The complete encoding term, including round advice, is

\[ WL A_0^s(2N(N+2))^\nu \le\left(n^{-9/32+o(1)}(2N(N+2))^{\nu/s}\right)^s =n^{-\Omega_c(\log n)}\le n^{-c-1}. \]

The richness failure is at most \(2n^c e^{-s}\le n^{-c-1}\). Add the round exception. The compact tree therefore has height below \(H=O_c(\log n)\), with failure at most \(10n^{-c-1}\), simultaneously with probability at least \(1-10/n\) for \(n^c\) readers. This is the same class as before with a stronger height conclusion and flexible polylogarithmic residual size, not an arbitrary-reader theorem. No new numerical experiment is claimed for these algebraic estimates.

3. An actual old-only profile for eligible inputs

Here is the source interface the switching result does supply. Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) and the functional unary PHP base on the residual board. Suppose the block inputs \(g_a\) have given ordinary NS expansions through an original carried cost \(\Delta\):

\[ g_a-\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal T_a}X_\tau\in\mathcal I_\Delta, \qquad\deg g_a\le\Delta, \tag{RP-inputs} \]

where each \(\mathcal T_a\) is a pairwise incompatible family of matching terms involving at most two rows. Assume their union is refined by the switched tree, and charge \(\Delta\ge2\). Inputs that are a pin times a row predicate meet this condition; an entire full single-tail class can also be one input, since its different pin rows conflict on the trigger column. Arbitrary sums of overlapping classes do not automatically meet it.

Working profile lemma. Let the tree height be \(t\). Take \(v\) to be the sum of zero-leaf polynomials and \(U_a\) the sum of full one-leaf polynomials assigned to input \(a\), as in the sum-input image lemma. Then \(\deg v,\deg U_a\le t\), and

\[ 1-v-\sum_aU_ag_a\in\mathcal I_{t+\Delta},\qquad g_av\in\mathcal I_{t+\Delta},\qquad v^2-v,\ U_a^2-U_a\in\mathcal I_{2t}. \tag{RP-profile} \]

Proof. For the matching-term expansions, the existing image lemma certifies prefix and companion identities through \(t+2\). Replacing each expansion by \(g_a\) multiplies its supplied error by \(U_a\) or \(v\), each of degree at most \(t\); hence the ceiling becomes \(t+\Delta\). Leaf partition, incompatibility and Booleanity give the final two identities. Empty hole branches use an affine factor and its degree-two orthogonality certificates, so they retain these costs and require no onto axiom.

Consequently this is a costed NOR profile of cost \(t+\Delta\), with input bounds \(\mu_a=\Delta\). The bounds on coefficient Booleanity also make the first-row coefficient substitution explicit; all other coefficient rows may be zero. A use at an earlier, smaller structural weight still needs a comparison with \(t+\Delta\); collected output degree is not permission to reset witness costs.

Decoder cost for predicates. A one-row polynomial of degree \(k\) has, under the affine bit decoder, the identity \(p(\tau b_j)=\sum_zp(z)X_{jz}\) through \(\max(k,1)\). Expand each monomial: same-row cross terms are exclusions, diagonal powers reduce by Booleanity, and the constant term uses the row equation. A bit pin has degree \(\ell\); multiplying it by the row predicate and discarding repeated-column choices gives the required pairwise-incompatible two-row expansion through \(\Delta=\ell+k\) when \(\ell\ge2\). An affine restriction of the bit coordinates does not increase this carried ceiling. Thus the new logarithmic-height theorem yields profile cost \(t+\Delta=O_c(\log n)\), independently of the selected power in \(N=\operatorname{polylog}n\).

4. The actual compiled source still has a different grammar

The named-value compiler guarantees affine expressions in old bits and earlier value names, fixed-degree named MOD definitions, and a complete cost ledger. It does not guarantee that each input is a row pin times one low-degree row predicate, that occurrences form full classes, or that summands within an input are pairwise incompatible. The recorded narrow-term frontier already identifies terms built from affine conditions spanning many rows as the missing general case. Rowwise parity predicates in the new theorem do not cover those cross-row conditions.

The input-span issue is substantive even before any probability estimate. An input \(x+y\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) vanishes at \(x=y=1\); replacing it by the two inputs \(x,y\), or by their disjunction, does not preserve that zero set. Row operations on the actual tuple preserve its span, but splitting arbitrary sums into separate Boolean tests need not. The incompatible-sum hypothesis is precisely what makes the valid profile construction avoid such cancellation. No such hypothesis is established for every compiled input.

Route verdict. The cycle supplies an affordable profile for a genuinely covered reader class, and repairs the residual-budget argument for that class by strengthening height to \(O(\log n)\). It does not discharge the main general-step obligation. Before additional reader subclasses, the next task must preserve the actual affine combinations of earlier values and test a common retained-system transfer. The retained-affine endpoint can handle affine pieces; it does not by itself extend compatible mixed moments through the nonlinear source. The probability that this current reader/profile line closes that remaining general implication is still modest, about 10%, not an assessment of the whole research program.

Next bounded task. Test a source-preserving combination of an affine input part and an eligible switched-predicate part. State the exact tuple and costed prefix/companion interface first, keep cancellations, and stop at a general transfer lemma or a counterexample. Do not replace a sum by an OR of its summands or assume the residual weight budget from tree height alone.

20 September 2026 — Preserve the input tuple by certified branch interpolation

Status: all-prime complete transfer under an explicit costed partition, with a shared-tree obstruction; existence of an affordable partition for general sources is open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. Combine an affine input part with switched old predicates without replacing sums by disjunctions. The quadratic branch theorem already supplies the interpolation pattern. The task here is to retain it over a relative old system using explicit ordinary NS certificates, with all coefficient domains and arbitrary proof uses accounted for. Stop at that transfer and test whether individual shallow trees imply its shared-partition hypothesis.

1. Certified partition data over the actual old system

Fix a prime \(p\), old variables \(x\), and an old system \(\Gamma\) over \(\mathbb F_p\). Consider one complete accuracy-\(h\) ENS block on old-only inputs \(q_i(x)\), with fresh coefficients \(r_{u,i}\), product \(P=\prod_{u=1}^h(1-\sum_i r_{u,i}q_i)\), all companions, and all coefficient equations \(r_{u,i}^p-r_{u,i}\). Let \(\delta\ge1\) be the actual maximum input degree and \(\mu_i=\deg q_i\) for nonzero inputs. Its nonzero companion has original degree

\[e_i=h(\delta+1)+\mu_i.\]

This equality uses a nonzero degree-attaining input and disjoint fresh coefficient rows. A loose degree ceiling is not substituted into it. All-constant or zero tuples instead admit the existing scalar cleanup.

Suppose a finite family of polynomials \(\chi_a\), affine old tuples \((g_{a,i})_i\), and an integer \(t\ge1\) are supplied with ordinary NS certificates over \(\Gamma\) for

\[ \deg\chi_a\le t,\qquad \sum_a\chi_a-1\in\mathcal I_t(\Gamma),\qquad \chi_a\chi_b\in\mathcal I_{2t}(\Gamma)\ (a\ne b),\qquad \chi_a^2-\chi_a\in\mathcal I_{2t}(\Gamma), \tag{CP-partition} \]
\[ \chi_a(q_i-g_{a,i})\in\mathcal I_{t+\delta}(\Gamma). \tag{CP-inputs} \]

The input comparisons are for the original positions, including their cancellations. If \(q_i=A_i+v_i\) and a leaf certifies \(v_i=c_{a,i}\), take \(g_{a,i}=A_i+c_{a,i}\). More generally the residual need only be affine, not constant. The old system may itself be unsatisfiable, as PHP is; merely agreeing on its full models would be vacuous and does not supply these certificates.

2. Complete map and original-degree ledger

For each branch introduce a disjoint fresh complete affine block, with the same accuracy \(h\), coefficients \(R_{a,u,i}\), and product \(A_a\). Put

\[ \Phi(r_{u,i})=\beta_{u,i}=\sum_a\chi_a R_{a,u,i},\qquad V=\sum_a\chi_a A_a,\qquad T=t+1. \tag{CP-map} \]

Working theorem. This map fixes the old variables, has degree at most \(T\), and sends every source axiom of original degree \(e\) to an ordinary NS consequence of the old system plus the new complete affine blocks through degree at most \(Te\). Consequently every ordinary NS or PC proof through degree \(D\) transfers through degree \((t+1)D\). For a family of old-only input blocks, use separate certified partitions and disjoint branch coefficients, with \(T=1+\max t_j\); the maps are simultaneous and the target has exactly the sum of the branch counts. There is no factor for block count or proof height.

Factor and product comparisons. From partition orthogonality and idempotence,

\[ \chi_a(\beta_{u,i}-R_{a,u,i})\in\mathcal I_{2t+1}(\Gamma). \]

Multiply this identity by \(q_i\) and use (CP-inputs) multiplied by \(R_{a,u,i}\). The selected mapped factor and its branch factor differ, after multiplication by \(\chi_a\), through degree \(2t+\delta+1\). Each mapped factor has degree at most \(t+\delta+1\), and each affine branch factor at most two. Telescope the \(h\) factors, and then use \(1-\sum_a\chi_a\) times the mapped product. This yields

\[ \Phi(P)-V\in\mathcal I_{B_0}(\Gamma),\qquad B_0=h(t+\delta+1)+t. \tag{CP-product} \]

All coefficients in these comparisons are still formal target variables. Only supplied old certificates have been multiplied and added; no Boolean-model argument replaces them.

Companions. The exact decomposition

\[ q_i\Phi(P)=q_i(\Phi(P)-V) +\sum_a\chi_a(g_{a,i}A_a) +\sum_a\chi_a(q_i-g_{a,i})A_a \]

has ceilings at most \(B_0+\mu_i\), \(t+2h+1\), and \(t+\delta+2h\). The first dominates when \(h,t,\delta\ge1\). Its original-degree comparison is

\[ (t+1)e_i-(B_0+\mu_i)=t(h\delta+\mu_i-1)\ge0. \tag{CP-companion-cost} \]

Thus every original companion position is covered through \(Te_i\), not merely a chosen input basis or its zero set.

Coefficient domains over every prime. Frobenius gives

\[ \beta_{u,i}^p-\beta_{u,i} =\sum_a\chi_a^p(R_{a,u,i}^p-R_{a,u,i}) +\sum_a(\chi_a^p-\chi_a)R_{a,u,i}. \]

The first sum uses target field generators through \(pt+p=pT\). For the second,

\[ \chi^p-\chi=(\chi^2-\chi)\sum_{j=0}^{p-2}\chi^j \]

has an old certificate through \(pt\), so multiplication by \(R\) costs at most \(pt+1\le pT\). This retains the original degree \(p\) of the source field axiom; odd-prime raw coefficients are not Booleanized. Old generators are fixed.

Proof replay. A source NS cofactor of degree at most \(D-e\) maps to degree at most \(T(D-e)\), which adds to the certified \(Te\) image cost. For PC, substitute each line; a nonzero multiplication predecessor has degree at most \(D-1\), and multiplying its image by a degree-\(T\) variable image stays within \(TD\). The certified axiom preludes fit that same bound. This completes the proof. \(\square\)

3. What a shared tree would supply, and what it would cost

A shared tree that makes every input affine on every leaf is a possible source of (CP-partition) and (CP-inputs). It is the certified selector degree and witness budget \(t\) that enters the theorem. A unary matching-query height is not automatically the same degree in compact-bit coordinates: a label indicator there can have degree \(\log_2N\), and dead/empty branches also need their actual certificates. The earlier old-only profile is over the functional unary base; changing that base or its coordinates requires a separate ledger.

On the \((N+1)\)-by-\(N\) matching board, a tree of height \(H\) has at most \((N+2)^H\) leaves. This is the actual branch inventory, not a claim of polynomial size. If \(H=O(\log n)\) and \(N=\operatorname{polylog}n\), its logarithm is \(O(\log n\log\log n)\), which can be affordable for an endpoint depending only on log inventory. That endpoint still needs the correct old system, actual affine input coordinates, certified value of \(t\), and the full proof-degree inequalities. The transfer theorem alone supplies none of these missing applicability facts.

4. Separate shallow trees do not give a cheap shared affine partition

Working sharp control. On the free Boolean cube \(\mathbb F_2^{2m}\), let \(q_j=x_jy_j\), \(j=1,\ldots,m\). Each polynomial becomes affine after the one query \(x_j\). But any tree of binary affine queries that makes all \(q_j\) affine on each nonempty leaf has height at least \(m\). Querying all \(x_j\) attains \(m\).

Proof. A leaf reached after \(d\) affine queries is an affine subspace with direction space \(W\) of dimension at least \(2m-d\). If \(q_j\) restricts to an affine function on that leaf, its polarization vanishes on \(W\):

\[ u_{x_j}v_{y_j}+u_{y_j}v_{x_j}=0\qquad(u,v\in W). \]

The projection of \(W\) to the coordinate pair \((x_j,y_j)\) therefore has dimension at most one; a two-dimensional projection would provide preimages of the two standard basis vectors with pairing one. The combined projection into all \(m\) pairs is injective, so \(\dim W\le m\). Hence \(d\ge m\) on every nonempty leaf. This remains an obstruction when the goal is affine residuals, not merely constant values.

This is a free-cube control of a shared-affinization inference, not a PHP lower bound or a counterexample to all low-degree transfers. Indeed the recorded rank-two theorem already handles its own large product families without demanding a cheap shared affine partition. The example is a reason to preserve that alternative, not to conclude that the main source endpoint is impossible.

5. Route verdict

The source-preserving transfer is now explicit over every prime and a genuinely relative old system; it keeps affine sums and covers all companions, field domains, and arbitrary raw coefficient uses. Its partition-existence premise is not supplied by the separate switching trees. Thus no main-goal implication is discharged, and treating a shared shallow tree as automatic would merely replace the missing general step by a stronger unproved convenience.

Next bounded task. Revisit the existing high-rank/low-branch alternative at the level of the actual input space, including affine sums of quadratic features. Check whether its product-tuple structural split survives those sums, or identify the exact failure. This directly tests an alternative to the expensive shared partition; do not expand a proof input into separate product generators unless its span is preserved. The shared-partition line alone has below a 5% chance of advancing the main general step without an additional structural theorem, not a verdict on the research program.

Process assessment. Reusing the existing interpolation pattern kept the work on the new relative certificates and original-degree ledger; the sharp free-cube control prevented mistaking separate shallow trees for a source-wide construction.

20 September 2026 — Preserve unbounded sums of independent quadratic features

Status: working complete binary source exclusion under a rank-or-leading-pairs condition; arbitrary quadratic input spaces remain outside it. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

General claim tested. The old product-tuple structural split cannot simply treat a sum as its separate product generators. The existing leading-pair criterion already works with constant combinations of the actual inputs. This cycle tests whether that high case can be combined with a low input-space rank map, keeping all original sums. Stop at a complete common-weight ledger and an actual source class it covers, not a claim about every quadratic space.

1. A finite criterion on the actual quadratic input spaces

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\), over the compact old base \(\mathcal Q_n\), with \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), and \(v=(n+1)\ell\) old bits. Consider at most \(M\ge1\) complete old-only ENS tuples of ordinary degree at most two, at any common accuracy. For a tuple let \(W\) be the span of its multilinear Boolean representatives, let \(K=W\cap\mathcal P_{\le1}\), and put \(r=\dim(W/K)\). This rank retains the actual input span; it is not the number of written monomials or summands.

Choose an integer \(k\ge2\). Require that every tuple with \(r\ge k\) supplies \(k\) constant combinations of its actual inputs whose multilinear representatives have disjoint squarefree quadratic leading monomials under a degree-compatible order, after a supplied invertible binary affine coordinate change if needed. Tuples with \(r<k\) need no factorization or common probe bound.

Working finite theorem. Put \(T=4k+1\), \(B=TD+k\), and

\[ \theta=\frac{16(n+1)}n\left[\left(1+\frac{3k}v\right)^\ell-1\right]. \]

Suppose

\[ D\ge\max(\ell,5),\quad k\le n/16,\quad \theta\le1/2,\quad B\le n/4, \quad M(v+1)e^{-k^3/v^2}\le1/8,\quad Me^{-k^2/v}\le1/8. \tag{RH-conditions} \]

Then the complete family has no ordinary NS or PC refutation through degree \(D\). Additional old-affine tuples are included as rank-zero cases. The theorem does not assert that every high-rank quadratic input space has the required leading pairs.

2. One weight for high quadratic rank and the remaining affine parts

First restrict every block to its first coefficient row, setting the other rows to zero. This preserves ordinary proof degree and all remaining coefficient domains. Use the cube-volume multiplier space \(\mathcal S_k\), of dimension at least \(\binom vk/2\) under (RH-conditions).

For every tuple with \(r\ge k\), use the leading-pair reduction map with \(R=k\). A binary affine coordinate change and its inverse have degree-two old Boolean certificates, so pulling back retains the ordinary degree-\(k\) kernel witness. Each image has dimension at most \(\binom vk(v+1)e^{-k^3/v^2}\). All such image dimensions sum to at most \(\binom vk/8\).

For each remaining tuple, keep its proper affine space \(K\); if it contains one, a constant coefficient map gives a Boolean-zero product image, and a zero space needs no restriction. Call \(K\) high-affine if its dimension is at least \(2k+3\). Ordinary restriction to its common-zero affine flat has image dimension at most

\[ \binom{v-\dim K+k}{k}\le\binom{v-k-3}{k} \le e^{-k^2/v}\binom vk. \]

The sum over these at most \(M\) maps is at most \(\binom vk/8\). Hence a nonzero \(f\in\mathcal S_k\) lies in every high-quadratic and high-affine kernel simultaneously. A high-quadratic tuple has

\[ f=\sum_i c_iq_i+E,\qquad\deg c_i\le k-2,\quad E\in\mathcal I_k({\rm BOOL}_{\rm old}), \tag{RH-high} \]

and a high-affine \(K\) has its ordinary affine-ideal representation of \(f\) with cofactors of degree at most \(k-1\). This uses only linear kernel intersections, not independent random choices of block normalizers.

3. Low quadratic rank is packed without splitting sums

For \(r<k\), choose a basis \(A_1,\ldots,A_a\) of \(K\) and extend it to a basis of \(W\) by \(G_1,\ldots,G_r\), each of degree at most two. Every original representative has a constant representation in this basis, and the basis has constant representations in the original inputs. Representatives and actual polynomials differ only by old Boolean consequences through two.

Use the existing old-only affine map on \(K\), and write its coefficients as \(\gamma_\nu\) and its value as \(A=1-\sum_\nu\gamma_\nu A_\nu\). If \(K\) is high-affine, choose \(\sum\gamma_\nu A_\nu=f\), so \(A=0\) wherever \(f=1\). If \(K\) is low-affine, telescope its at most \(2k+2\) basis forms, so \(A=\prod_\nu(1-A_\nu)\). In either case \(\deg\gamma_\nu\le2k+1\), \(\deg A\le2k+2\), and every affine-basis companion vanishes on the Boolean points where \(f=1\). Take \(A=1\) for \(K=0\).

Now set

\[ V=A\prod_{j=1}^r(1-G_j),\qquad 1-V=\sum_\nu\gamma_\nu A_\nu +\sum_{j=1}^r A\prod_{u<j}(1-G_u)G_j. \tag{RH-prefix} \]

The nonlinear basis coefficients have degree at most \(2k+2r\le4k-2\). Pull these coefficients back by the constant basis representations to the original input positions. Every coefficient image has degree at most \(T=4k+1\). On old Boolean points its product agrees with \(V\); any nonzero basis input makes \(V\) zero on \(f=1\), so every original companion vanishes there. This remains true if representative identities require degree-two Boolean corrections. Unit affine spans take a constant representation of one and value zero; zero tuples take all coefficients zero. A large number of summands in an original input is never split into extra generators.

For a high-quadratic tuple, simply use the coefficients \(c_i\) from (RH-high). Its product equals \(1-f\) on the old Boolean cube. Thus all tuples now have simultaneous old-only coefficient images of degree at most \(T\) whose companions vanish on \(f=1\).

4. Complete original-degree replay

Weight the substituted proof by \(f\). Over the binary field every old polynomial is Boolean-valued on Boolean inputs, so each weighted companion vanishes on the entire old Boolean cube: the weight is zero off \(f=1\), and the mapped companion is zero on it. Division only by old Boolean equations supplies ordinary certificates through the actual polynomial degree.

For a nonconstant accuracy-one source tuple let \(\delta\in\{1,2\}\) be its actual maximum degree and \(\mu_i\) a nonzero input's degree. Its original companion degree is \(e_i=\delta+1+\mu_i\); the weighted image has a Boolean certificate through

\[ k+T+\delta+\mu_i\le k+Te_i. \tag{RH-companion} \]

Each coefficient Boolean image has a certificate through \(2T+k\), matching \(T\) times its original degree two plus the weight. Old generators are fixed and multiplied by \(f\). Constant tuples use scalar cleanup. Thus NS cofactors and PC multiplications replay through \(TD+k=B\), exactly as in the previous common-weight theorem, deriving \(f\) in the old compact system. The cube separation lemma, with \(k\le B\le n/4\), excludes this nonzero \(f\). This proves the finite theorem for both calculi without assuming augmented PC equals NS.

Parameters. For polynomial \(M\), choose

\[ k=\left\lceil\max\left\{2, (v^2\ln(16M(v+1)))^{1/3}, \sqrt{v\ln(16M)}\right\}\right\rceil. \tag{RH-choice} \]

Then \(k=O(n^{2/3}\log n)\), the two image sums meet (RH-conditions), and \(\theta=o(1)\). For every polylogarithmic \(D\), \(B=O(n^{2/3}(\log n)D)=o(n)\), so the other finite conditions hold eventually. The displayed finite theorem also gives the explicit degree range \((4k+1)D+k\le n/4\) whenever its other conditions hold.

5. An unbounded-sum class that meets the criterion

Working source corollary. Consider complete binary two-level systems with proper rank-two old-affine bottom tuples. A parent input may be an arbitrary binary linear combination of their actual products, plus an old-affine offset. Assume that, for each parent separately, the homogeneous factor pairs of all distinct bottom products it uses are jointly independent. Different parents may overlap and reuse bottoms. With polynomial block inventory, there is no polylogarithmic-degree ordinary NS or PC refutation over \(\mathcal Q_n\), for sufficiently large \(n\), at any common accuracy.

Proof. Apply the complete degree-preserving bottom normalization once to every reused bottom. Literal images of the parent sums are preserved, so the same proof also handles the added sums and affine offsets. For one parent, use its jointly independent affine factors as coordinates. Every normalized input has the form

\[ L_i(y)+\sum_j C_{ij}y_{2j-1}y_{2j}. \tag{RH-diagonal-span} \]

Its quadratic input rank is \(\operatorname{rank}C\). Row-reduce \(C\) in the order of the pair monomials induced by any fixed degree-compatible monomial order. The pivot combinations have distinct leading pair monomials, and those pairs are disjoint. Thus when the rank is at least \(k\) the high criterion holds; otherwise the low-rank construction applies. All row operations are constant combinations of actual inputs, not the addition of individual feature generators. Each parent's coordinate change is used only to construct its reduction map; the common weight and all coefficient maps return to the original old coordinates. Apply the finite theorem and (RH-choice).

Compared with the fixed-summand source class, the number of summands may now grow without a fixed bound, under the new joint-independence hypothesis within each parent. It is not an extension to arbitrary overlapping quadratic tensors.

Small symbolic illustration. For three independent pairs \(z_j=x_jy_j\), the inputs \(z_1+z_2,z_2+z_3\) need not contain a nonzero factorable polynomial in their span: every nonzero binary combination has polar rank four, whereas a product of two affine forms has polar rank at most two. This is the already recorded factor-extraction obstruction. Nevertheless row reduction gives \(z_1+z_3,z_2+z_3\), with disjoint leading heads \(z_1,z_2\) in the indicated order. It illustrates why the existing leading-monomial tool, rather than splitting sums, is the correct high case. This is a symbolic control, not a numerical experiment or a new assertion of novelty.

6. Route verdict

The cycle closes a complete-source class with unbounded sums and no per-input probe bound, with an explicit \(n^{2/3}\operatorname{polylog}n\) old-proof ledger. It preserves actual input spans, overlaps between parents, all coefficient equations and arbitrary coefficient uses. The general-step obligation remains open because a large quadratic rank does not itself certify disjoint leading heads, and arbitrary compiled features need not form independent pairs.

Next bounded task. Test a quantitative structural alternative for overlapping quadratic input spaces: small rank, many disjoint leading heads, or an affordable certified affine partition. Start with the known common-factor and nonfactorable-sum controls; require the input span and the final degree/inventory budget to remain intact. Stop at a proved sufficient structural statement or a counterexample to the proposed alternative, not another list of specially factorable inputs. I estimate about 10% that this input-space line advances the main general step; it is not a likelihood for the full program.

20 September 2026 — A structural split for arbitrary binary quadratic input spaces

Status: working structural dichotomy using an imported additive-combinatorial theorem; the complete general-quadratic source consequence is the next audit, not yet claimed here. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. Supply a quantitative alternative for actual overlapping quadratic input spaces, rather than assuming product generators. Stop at a proved structural statement with branch/rank costs, or a counterexample. The split below gives either many disjoint leading pairs or a low-codimension input subspace made affine by relatively few binary probes. The latter leaves an explicitly bounded exceptional input rank.

1. Polar spaces and the imported additive theorem

Let \(\mathscr Q\) be a vector space of quadratic Boolean functions on \(\mathbb F_2^v\), represented by multilinear polynomials of degree at most two. For \(q\), write

\[ B_q(u,z)=q(u+z)+q(u)+q(z)+q(0). \]

This is an alternating bilinear form. The linear map \(q\mapsto B_q\) has exactly the affine functions as its kernel. Thus the polar space \(\mathscr B\) is the actual quadratic input space modulo its affine part. All ranks below are matrix ranks over the specified field; the original old variables remain binary.

Imported theorem. For a nonempty subset \(A\) of a finite binary vector space, of density \(\alpha\), the set \(4A=A+A+A+A\) contains a linear subspace of codimension at most \(C_{\rm BR}\log_2^4(2/\alpha)\), for an absolute constant. This is Sanders's quasipolynomial Bogolyubov–Ruzsa lemma, in the precise binary form of Theorem 4.7 of Ben-Sasson–Ron-Zewi–Tulsiani–Wolf; see also Sanders's original paper. The imported theorem concerns the additive coefficient space, not PHP assignments. No algorithmic efficiency or explicit value of the absolute constant is needed below.

2. High collective polar rank supplies disjoint heads

Working lemma. Suppose \(q_1,\ldots,q_a\) are binary quadratic functions and every nonzero combination of their polar matrices has rank at least \(4a^2\). Then an invertible binary linear change of old coordinates gives their multilinear representatives pairwise disjoint quadratic leading monomials under one degree-compatible monomial order. Their affine parts are unrestricted.

Proof. Construct independent directions \(u_1,\ldots,u_{2a}\) such that

\[ B_i(u_j,u_l)= \begin{cases}1,&j=2i-1,\ l=2i,\\0,&j<l\text{ otherwise},\end{cases} \tag{QR-diagonal} \]

while keeping all \(a j\) functionals \(B_i(u_b,-)\), \(i\le a,b\le j\), independent after step \(j\). At step \(j+1\), the required pairings with previous directions are \(aj\) independent linear constraints, hence define an affine set of size \(2^{v-aj}\). Let \(L\) be their span. Failure of the next \(a\) functionals to be independent modulo \(L\) means \(B_c(u,-)\in L\) for some nonzero \(c\in\mathbb F_2^a\). For a fixed \(c\), this set has size at most \(2^{v-4a^2+aj}\), because \(B_c\) has rank at least \(4a^2\). Even after conditioning on the required affine constraints, the union of all failures occupies a fraction at most

\[ (2^a-1)2^{2aj-4a^2}<2^{a+2aj-4a^2}\le2^{-a}<1 \qquad(j\le2a-1). \tag{QR-choice} \]

A valid direction therefore exists. It lies outside the span of the previous directions, since otherwise all its polar images would already lie in \(L\). Complete these \(2a\) directions to an old-coordinate basis.

In the first \(2a\) new coordinates, the quadratic part of \(q_i\) is exactly \(y_{2i-1}y_{2i}\). Diagonal square terms become affine after Boolean reduction. Use a monomial order that first compares total degree and then gives weight two to these \(2a\) variables and weight one to the others, followed by a fixed lexicographic tie break. The designated pair has weight four; every other quadratic term involves at least one remaining variable and has smaller weight. Thus the leading monomials are precisely the disjoint designated pairs. Binary linear changes preserve the old Boolean equations through degree two, so the existing leading-pair reduction applies to constant combinations of the actual inputs with its original-degree witnesses. \(\square\)

3. Bounded matrix rank gives common binary affine probes

Working lemma. Let \(\mathscr B\) be any space of alternating \(v\)-by-\(v\) binary matrices, each of rank at most \(R\), with \(v\ge1\). Put \(d=\lceil\log_2(v+1)\rceil\). There is a binary subspace \(U\) of codimension at most \(\min(v,d^2R)\) on which every form in \(\mathscr B\) vanishes. Hence every quadratic function with polar form in \(\mathscr B\) is affine on every coset of \(U\). Rank zero is the immediate affine case.

Generic rank and descent. Let \(r_*\) be the maximum rank in the scalar extension of \(\mathscr B\) to an algebraic closure. A nonzero \(r_*\)-minor is a polynomial of total degree at most \(v\) in the combination coefficients. Since \(|K|=2^d>v\) for \(K=\mathbb F_{2^d}\), it has a nonzero value at some point over \(K\). Thus a matrix \(F\in K\mathscr B\) reaches rank \(r_*\). Expand its coefficients in a binary basis of \(K\): \(F=\sum_{b=1}^d\omega_bF_b\) with \(F_b\in\mathscr B\). Rank subadditivity gives \(r_*\le dR\).

The radical is common isotropic over the extension. For any \(G\in K\mathscr B\), its restriction to \(\ker F\) must vanish. Otherwise choose two radical vectors with nonzero \(G\)-pairing. In coordinates putting \(F\) into a nonsingular \(r_*\)-block and a zero radical block, the corresponding \((r_*+2)\)-minor of \(F+zG\) has a nonzero coefficient of \(z^2\): it is the determinant of the nonsingular block times the determinant of that alternating two-by-two restriction. It is therefore nonzero for some \(z\) over the algebraic closure, contradicting maximality of \(r_*\). This argument needs maximum rank over the scalar extension, not merely over the binary coefficient points.

Set \(U=\ker F\cap\mathbb F_2^v\). A row basis of \(F\) contains \(r_*\) equations over \(K\). Expanding those equations into binary coordinates gives at most \(dr_*\le d^2R\) binary linear equations. Every \(G\in\mathscr B\) vanishes on \(U\times U\). For a quadratic function, vanishing polarization on a direction space means its restriction to any coset is affine. A basis of \(U^\perp\) is the promised probe list. No extension-field coefficients are needed in the resulting binary probes. \(\square\)

Why the extension step cannot be skipped. On three coordinate pairs let \(z_i=x_iy_i\), and take polar forms of \(z_1+z_3\) and \(z_2+z_3\). Each of the three nonzero binary combinations has rank four. The radical of the first contains the second coordinate pair, where the second form is nonzero. Over \(\mathbb F_8\), the combination with coefficients \(1,\alpha\), \(\alpha\notin\mathbb F_2\), has three nonzero pair coefficients and rank six. This explicit control refutes the tempting replacement of generic maximum rank by binary maximum rank.

4. The structural dichotomy

Working theorem. For any integer \(a\ge1\), every binary quadratic function space \(\mathscr Q\) has one of the following:

  • \(a\) actual input combinations with disjoint quadratic leading monomials after a binary linear coordinate change, supplied by an \(a\)-dimensional polar subspace of minimum nonzero rank at least \(4a^2\); or
  • a subspace \(\mathscr Q_0\subseteq\mathscr Q\) of codimension at most \(C_{\rm BR}(a+1)^4\), and at most \(16a^2\lceil\log_2(v+1)\rceil^2\) binary linear probes, such that every member of \(\mathscr Q_0\) becomes affine on every probe branch.

In the second case, after each branch the entire original input space has quadratic rank at most \(C_{\rm BR}(a+1)^4\) modulo its affine part. The bound may be capped by the actual input dimension, and the probe count by \(v\). It is a small exceptional input-space codimension, not a claim that all inputs become affine.

Proof. Work in the polar space \(\mathscr B\). Choose a maximal subspace \(C\) whose nonzero forms all have rank at least \(4a^2\). If \(\dim C\ge a\), apply the high-rank lemma to any \(a\)-dimensional subspace and lift its basis to the actual input functions.

Otherwise \(\dim C<a\). Put \(A=\{B\in\mathscr B:\operatorname{rank}B<4a^2\}\). Maximality implies \(\mathscr B=C+A\): any form outside \(C\) could be adjoined unless one of its translates by \(C\) had low rank, and a member of \(C\) differs from itself by zero. Hence \(|A|/|\mathscr B|\ge2^{-\dim C}\ge2^{-a}\). The imported theorem gives a subspace \(\mathscr B_0\subseteq4A\) of codimension at most \(C_{\rm BR}(a+1)^4\). Every member of \(4A\) has rank below \(16a^2\), by rank subadditivity. The preceding lemma supplies the common binary probes for \(\mathscr B_0\).

Take \(\mathscr Q_0\) to be the inverse image of \(\mathscr B_0\) under polarization. Its codimension is the same, and its functions become affine on each branch. Choose a complementary list of at most that many quadratic functions in the actual input space; together with the branch-affine images of \(\mathscr Q_0\), they span every original branch input. Thus its rank modulo affine functions is bounded by the same number. This preserves constant linear combinations and does not add separate product generators. \(\square\)

5. Exact controls and source scope

The bounded C++ checker constructs spaces \(q_c(x,y)=\operatorname{Tr}(cxy)\) over binary extension fields and checks every nonzero combination of the chosen \(a\) forms. The four cases have \((a,v)=(1,4),(2,16),(3,40),(4,64)\), with minimum ranks respectively \(4,16,40,64\), meeting \(4a^2\). It verifies irreducibility of each field polynomial, solves the prescribed affine constraints, checks all gradient independence and designated pairings, completes the coordinate basis, and records the transformed quadratic data. All four cases passed, with 20 sampled candidates in total. Replacing a selected direction by zero fails the designated-pair control as expected.

The same tool verifies the rank-four/rank-six extension control in Section 3. It does not test Bogolyubov–Ruzsa numerically, enumerate the exponentially many branches, or establish a full source lower bound. The first compilation failed on a C++ name collision and a formatting warning; both were corrected before the accepted build. Complete matrices, directions and checks, reproduction, and source coverage are retained.

The initial strength/regular-sequence screen included Ananyan–Hochster, whose maximal-rank discussion is relevant context. Ordinary regular-sequence conclusions alone are not imported as Boolean filtered-ideal bounds. The proof above instead uses the explicitly binary additive theorem and supplies its own matrix and descent arguments. No novelty claim has been established; comparison with quadratic regularity and bounded-rank matrix-space literature remains an attention item.

6. Candidate source ledger to check next

This structural result appears to remove the independence hypothesis from the preceding quadratic rank-or-heads criterion, but the complete source composition is deliberately the next checkpoint. The candidate ledger is explicit. With head count \(a\), put

\[ c_0=\lceil C_{\rm BR}(a+1)^4\rceil,\quad t_0=16a^2\lceil\log_2(v+1)\rceil^2, \quad k\ge\max\left\{2, v\sqrt{\frac{\ln(16M(v+1))}{a}}, \sqrt{v(\ln(16M)+t_0\ln2)}\right\}. \tag{QD-candidate} \]

The high case would use \(a\) leading heads. The low case has at most \(2^{t_0}\) branches per tuple, one affine input space per branch, and at most \(c_0\) exceptional quadratic directions to pack. The proposed simultaneous old-only coefficient budget is \(T=t_0+2k+2c_0+1\), with old proof ceiling \(TD+k\). For polynomial \(M\), choosing \(a=\lceil n^{2/9}\rceil\) makes this candidate ceiling \(n^{8/9}\operatorname{polylog}n\) when \(D\) is polylogarithmic. The branch count is charged through its logarithm, not called polynomial and not enumerated.

Current status. The high/low structural theorem is the result of this cycle.
