20 September 2026 — Complete binary ENS on arbitrary quadratic old inputs

Status: working end-to-end degree lower bound for complete old-only quadratic-input families, with an exact low-case certificate control; full multilevel Frege remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. Audit the complete source consequence of the new structural dichotomy. The required endpoint is an old proof below its degree barrier, with one common weight and actual maps of every source coefficient. This cycle supplies that ledger. It is a theorem about arbitrary quadratic inputs in the old bits, not about arbitrary later ENS inputs involving earlier coefficient variables.

1. Finite theorem and asymptotic consequence

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\), with \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), \(v=(n+1)\ell\), and the compact old base \(\mathcal Q_n\). Let \(\mathcal E\) contain at most \(M\ge1\) complete ENS blocks whose inputs are arbitrary polynomials of ordinary degree at most two in the old bits only. Input tuples may overlap arbitrarily and may contain arbitrary sums. Each block has fresh own coefficients, all companions and all coefficient Booleanity equations. Its positive accuracy may be chosen independently of the other blocks.

Let \(C_{\rm BR}\) be an absolute constant valid in the imported binary Bogolyubov–Ruzsa theorem. For integers \(a\ge1,k\ge2\), put

\[ d=\lceil\log_2(v+1)\rceil,\quad t_0=16a^2d^2,\quad c_0=\lceil C_{\rm BR}(a+1)^4\rceil, \quad T=t_0+2k+2c_0+1,\quad B=TD+k, \tag{GQ-costs} \]
\[ \theta=\frac{16(n+1)}n\left[\left(1+\frac{3k}v\right)^\ell-1\right]. \]

Working finite theorem. No ordinary NS or PC refutation of \(\mathcal Q_n\cup\mathcal E\) has degree at most \(D\), provided

\[ D\ge\max(\ell,5),\quad 2a\le v,\quad k\le n/16,\quad \theta\le1/2,\quad B\le n/4, \tag{GQ-room} \]
\[ M(v+1)e^{-ak^2/v^2}\le1/8,\qquad M2^{t_0}e^{-k^2/v}\le1/8. \tag{GQ-images} \]

Asymptotic corollary. For every fixed polynomial block-inventory exponent and every fixed polylogarithmic degree bound, such refutations are excluded for all sufficiently large \(n\). One parameter choice has \(T=O(n^{8/9}(\log n)^{3/2})\); the exact finite statement, rather than this asymptotic notation, owns the original-degree budget. This result is binary; no odd-prime extension is asserted.

2. A common weight for every high case and every low-case branch

Restrict all blocks to their first coefficient row, setting later rows to zero. This does not increase ordinary proof degree, regardless of their original accuracies. Constant tuples take scalar coefficient maps. For each remaining tuple apply the structural dichotomy to the span of its multilinear representatives, modulo the affine part.

High case. The dichotomy supplies \(a\) constant input combinations with disjoint quadratic leading pairs after a binary coordinate change. The leading-pair reduction, pulled back to the original old bits, has image dimension on degree-at-most-\(k\) polynomials bounded by

\[ \binom vk(v+1)e^{-ak^2/v^2}. \]

Its kernel gives an ordinary identity \(f=\sum_i c_iq_i+E\), with \(\deg c_i\le k-2\) and \(E\in\mathcal I_k({\rm BOOL}_{\rm old})\). Every selected generator is a constant combination of the actual input tuple.

Low case. There are \(t_j\le t_0\) independent binary linear probes and a subspace \(W_{j,0}\) of the actual input-function span of codimension \(s_j\le c_0\), all of whose functions become affine on each probe branch. Choose at most \(s_j\) exceptional quadratic functions completing that subspace to the full input span. For each \(\sigma\in\mathbb F_2^{t_j}\), let \(A_{j,\sigma}\) be the affine span of the restricted \(W_{j,0}\), extended as affine polynomials in the original old coordinates. Let \(G_{j,\sigma,1},\ldots,G_{j,\sigma,s_j}\) be the restricted exceptional functions, of degree at most two. They need not be independent after restriction. Together these functions span every original branch input, with constant representations in both directions modulo old Booleanity.

There are at most \(M2^{t_0}\) such affine spaces. A space containing one will be handled by a constant prefix; the zero space needs none. For every proper one of rank at least \(2k+3\), use ordinary restriction to its affine zero flat. Its degree-at-most-\(k\) image dimension is at most \(\binom vk e^{-k^2/v}\), by the same dimension calculation as before.

The cube-volume space \(\mathcal S_k\) has dimension at least \(\binom vk/2\). The two total image bounds in (GQ-images) consume at most \(\binom vk/4\). Thus a nonzero \(f\in\mathcal S_k\) lies in all high-quadratic and high-affine kernels. The weight remains a polynomial in the original pigeonhole bits. Coordinate changes used to construct individual reduction maps do not change the old PHP axioms or its separator space.

3. Simultaneous old-only coefficient maps

On a high tuple, use its kernel coefficients \(c_i\). Its accuracy-one product is \(1-f+E\), hence zero at every old Boolean point with \(f=1\).

For a low tuple and branch \(\sigma\), choose the affine coefficient map on \(A_{j,\sigma}\). A proper high-affine space uses its kernel representation of \(f\), giving affine-core value \(A=1-f\). A low-affine space of rank at most \(2k+2\) uses a telescoping flat indicator. These coefficients have degree at most \(2k+1\), and \(\deg A\le2k+2\). Take \(A=1\) for a zero affine space. A unit affine span gives a constant representation of one and value zero, as a Boolean-function identity.

For the remaining exceptional functions, use the exact basis-prefix expression

\[ V_{j,\sigma}=A\prod_{u=1}^{s_j}(1-G_{j,\sigma,u}),\qquad 1-V_{j,\sigma} =\sum_\nu\gamma_\nu A_\nu +\sum_{u=1}^{s_j} A\prod_{b<u}(1-G_{j,\sigma,b})G_{j,\sigma,u}. \tag{GQ-branch-prefix} \]

Pull the coefficients back to every original input position using the constant branch representations. Their degrees are at most \(2k+2s_j+1\), including the case \(s_j=0\). At Boolean points with \(f=1\), all branch companions vanish: a high-affine core is already zero, while in every other case a nonzero basis input forces the displayed product to zero. Working with representatives introduces only Boolean-function equalities here, which will be certified at the final actual degree.

Let \(\chi_{j,\sigma}\) be the product of the appropriate binary probe literals. Interpolate each original coefficient by

\[ \beta_{j,i}=\sum_\sigma\chi_{j,\sigma}\,\beta_{j,\sigma,i}. \tag{GQ-map} \]

Exactly one selector is one at every old Boolean point. Consequently the mapped original input tuple agrees there with the selected branch tuple, and every mapped original companion vanishes on \(f=1\). All these coefficient images are binary old-only polynomials of degree at most \(t_j+2k+2s_j+1\le T\). Different blocks use their own maps simultaneously; no coefficient image depends on another source coefficient. The potentially exponential branch count is charged in (GQ-images), while the degrees in (GQ-map) add. No repeated proof substitution or hidden factor for the number of branches is used.

4. Every original axiom and proof step is covered

Weight the substituted proof by the same \(f\). On the full old Boolean cube every weighted companion is zero, as proved above. Every coefficient image \(\beta\) also satisfies \(\beta^2-\beta=0\) there, since its coefficients and values are binary. Ordinary division by the old Boolean equations therefore supplies NS certificates through each polynomial's actual total degree. This argument uses the full Boolean cube, not the empty set of full PHP models.

For a nonconstant accuracy-one tuple let \(\delta\in\{1,2\}\) be the actual maximum input degree and \(\mu_i\) the degree of a nonzero input. Fresh coefficient variables make its original companion degree \(e_i=\delta+1+\mu_i\). The ledger is

\[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{source generator}&\text{original degree}&\text{weighted old NS ceiling}\\\hline q_iP & e_i & k+T+\delta+\mu_i\le k+Te_i\\ r_i^2-r_i &2&k+2T\\ F\in\mathcal Q_n&\deg F&k+\deg F\le k+T\deg F. \end{array} \tag{GQ-ledger} \]

Zero inputs contribute no companion; actual constant tuples use their exact scalar cleanup. Inputs whose Boolean representatives vanish or become affine are still charged at their actual original polynomial degree. Thus cancellations never lower a carried source cost without justification.

A source NS cofactor through \(D-e\) maps to degree at most \(T(D-e)\); adding the certified weighted generator gives ceiling \(TD+k\). For PC, represent every line \(p\) by \(f\Phi(p)\). Addition is linear, and a primitive multiplication is replayed by multiplying the previous weighted image by the corresponding degree-at-most-\(T\) variable image. Its predecessor degree is at most \(D-1\), so the total never exceeds \(TD+k\). All axiom preludes satisfy that bound. A refutation would therefore derive \(f\) in ordinary old PC through \(B\), or in old NS through the same bound.

But \(f\ne0\) belongs to \(\mathcal S_k\), and (GQ-room) gives \(k\le B\le n/4\). The cube-volume separation lemma excludes that old consequence. This proves the finite theorem. No equality between augmented PC and NS spaces has been assumed.

5. Parameter choice and the source corollary

For \(M\le n^c\) with fixed \(c\), choose \(a=\lceil n^{2/9}\rceil\), and

\[ k=\left\lceil\max\left\{2, v\sqrt{\frac{\ln(16M(v+1))}{a}}, \sqrt{v(\ln(16M)+t_0\ln2)}\right\}\right\rceil. \tag{GQ-choice} \]

The two image bounds then hold. As \(n\to\infty\),

\[ c_0=O(n^{8/9}),\quad t_0=O(n^{4/9}(\log n)^2),\quad k=O(n^{8/9}(\log n)^{3/2}),\quad T=O(n^{8/9}(\log n)^{3/2}). \]

In particular \(k=o(n)\), \(\theta=o(1)\), and \(TD+k=o(n)\) for every fixed polylogarithmic \(D\). All finite conditions hold for sufficiently large \(n\). Smaller proof ceilings can be enlarged to \(\max(D,\ell,5)\) before applying the statement.

Working actual-source corollary. A complete binary two-level family with old-affine bottoms of rank at most two and arbitrary parent sums of their actual products, with old-affine offsets allowed, has no polylogarithmic-degree ordinary NS or PC refutation over \(\mathcal Q_n\), at polynomial block inventory. Bottoms and parents may overlap arbitrarily, and no independence, fixed summand bound, special tensor shape, or common probe set is required. Positive accuracies may vary by block.

Proof. Apply the complete bottom map once per reused bottom. At rank two, the first-success coefficient map at accuracy one has degree one; at larger accuracy the two scalar rows produce the exact product of the two affine factors. Rank-one and scalar-clean cases have the corresponding constant/affine maps. Each bottom axiom image fits its original degree, so the whole substitution preserves NS/PC degree. Every parent input becomes its actual old quadratic sum plus affine offset. All parent coefficients and field equations remain until applying the theorem just proved. The restriction to first coefficient rows may then be made independently for every parent. This gives the contradiction without adding separate summand generators.

This removes the feature-independence condition from the preceding unbounded-sum source class, at a weaker exponent in the old-proof bound. Earlier stronger quantitative results on their narrower classes remain valid. Arbitrary-rank bottom affine tuples, later inputs depending on uneliminated coefficients, higher-degree old inputs, and odd primes remain outside the new theorem.

6. Exact low-case certificate control

The new bounded C++ checker uses seven Boolean old variables, four genuine quadratic inputs

\[ e=x_5x_6,\quad f=x_1+x_2,\quad g_i=x_0x_i+e\quad(i=1,2,3,4), \quad \beta_1=1+x_0+x_0f,\quad \beta_2=x_0,\quad \beta_3=\beta_4=0. \]

This is a hand-supplied low-case decomposition, not an execution of Bogolyubov–Ruzsa. At \(x_0=0\), all inputs reduce to the exceptional quadratic \(e\); at \(x_0=1\), the affine difference \(g_1+g_2=f\) supplies the weighted clamp. The coefficient map combines those branches. The checker expands ordinary polynomials before reduction and emits full NS cofactors for all four weighted companions and all four weighted coefficient-field equations. All eight reconstruct exactly, with zero Boolean remainder and the original-degree ceilings for \(T=2,\deg f=1\). Removing either the affine-branch contribution or the exceptional low-branch contribution gives a nonzero companion remainder.

All certificates and both controls, reproduction and encoding, and provenance are retained. This finite Boolean-base check does not prove the theorem or test a full PHP instance; it checks the new simultaneous interpolation and degree ledger. The preceding cycle's structural checks are reused without calling them fresh runs.

7. What changed on the main route

The binary quadratic old-input endpoint no longer needs the previously listed product-shape, leading-head or bounded-summand hypotheses. This is a substantive generalization of the first nonlinear source class, with a complete original-degree proof. It is not a proof of the full ordinary-PHP \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege goal: general earlier values are not quadratic old-only polynomials, and inserting their coefficient variables into the old base would invalidate the present separator argument unless a relative theorem were proved.

Next bounded task. Review the uniform extension actually needed for deeper sources, rather than proceeding through a list of degree-three, degree-four examples. Identify the precise relative old-system/target-separation condition required to reuse this structural argument over a retained lower level, and test it against the recorded mixed-moment and same-degree obstructions. Stop at a properly scoped sufficient relative lemma or a concrete obstruction to that formulation.

The complete quadratic theorem and its structural dependency are flagged for prior-art and independent-proof review before any publication claim. I estimate roughly 30% that this structural line supplies further useful progress on the main general step; that is not a probability assigned to the whole Frege program.

20 September 2026 — What a relative quadratic step would actually have to preserve

Status: sufficient relative rank criterion and explicit failures of two iteration shortcuts; no new lower bound for unrestricted multilevel sources. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. The quadratic endpoint is complete for old-only inputs. Can its argument be reapplied with an earlier ENS level retained in the old system? The main goal needs a costed step that composes on actual proof sources for every fixed depth and prime. This review isolates the target-separation hypothesis, tests automatic versions against existing obstructions, and stops before investigating further fixed polynomial degrees.

1. Count surviving target classes, not just nonzero polynomials

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\). Let \(\Gamma\subseteq\mathbb F_2[z_1,\ldots,z_V]\) be any retained system containing every \(z_i^2-z_i\). Let \(\mathcal E\) consist of at most \(M\ge1\) complete ENS blocks on degree-at-most-two polynomials in these retained variables, with fresh own coefficients and arbitrary positive accuracies. No input uses a coefficient of another block of \(\mathcal E\). An earlier level may be part of \(\Gamma\); all degrees here are actual ordinary degrees in its variables.

Fix an old target \(q\) of degree \(s\le D\), \(D\ge5\), integers \(1\le a\le V/2\) and \(2\le k\le V/2\), and any vector space \(S\) of multilinear polynomials of degree at most \(k\). With the same positive absolute Bogolyubov–Ruzsa constant as in the quadratic theorem, put

\[ d=\lceil\log_2(V+1)\rceil,\quad t_0=16a^2d^2,\quad c_0=\lceil C_{\rm BR}(a+1)^4\rceil,\quad T=t_0+2k+2c_0+1,\quad B=TD+k, \]
\[ R=\binom Vk\left[M(V+1)e^{-ak^2/V^2}+M2^{t_0}e^{-k^2/V}\right]. \tag{RQ-loss} \]

Choose either ordinary NS throughout, with \(J_B=\mathcal I_B(\Gamma)\), or PC throughout, with \(J_B=\mathcal C_B(\Gamma)\). These are subspaces of polynomials of degree at most \(B\), not the unrestricted ideal. Define

\[ \pi_{q,B}:S\longrightarrow\mathcal P_{\le B}/J_B, \qquad f\longmapsto fq+J_B. \tag{RQ-target} \]

Working sufficient criterion. If \(\operatorname{rank}\pi_{q,B}>R\), then \(q\) has no degree-\(D\) consequence proof in \(\Gamma\cup\mathcal E\) in the chosen system. More sharply, it suffices that this rank exceed the sum of the actual restricted image ranks of the high-quadratic and high-affine maps used below. This is a target-relative refinement of the existing kernel-compression criterion, not a proof of the required rank bound for general retained ENS systems.

Proof. Restrict every fresh block to its first coefficient row. Apply the structural dichotomy to each resulting input span. The quadratic proof's reduction maps are defined on all polynomials of degree at most \(k\); they do not depend on the PHP axioms. Each high-quadratic map has image dimension at most \(\binom Vk(V+1)e^{-ak^2/V^2}\). Each proper high-affine branch map has image dimension at most \(\binom Vk e^{-k^2/V}\), and there are at most \(M2^{t_0}\) such branches. Let \(K\subseteq S\) be their common kernel. Consequently \(\operatorname{codim}_S K\le R\). The induced map from \(S/K\) onto \(\pi_{q,B}(S)/\pi_{q,B}(K)\) gives

\[ \dim\pi_{q,B}(K)\ge\operatorname{rank}\pi_{q,B}-\operatorname{codim}_S K>0. \]

Choose \(f\in K\) with \(fq\notin J_B\). The same branch interpolation maps every fresh coefficient to a retained-variable polynomial of degree at most \(T\), fixes all \(z_i\), and makes every weighted fresh companion vanish on the full retained Boolean cube. It works for this possibly nonhomogeneous \(f\): only \(\deg f\le k\), its kernel memberships, and binary Boolean values are used. Every weighted fresh field equation is likewise Boolean-zero. For every fresh generator of original degree \(e\), old Boolean division gives a certificate through \(k+Te\), by the complete original-degree ledger. A retained generator \(F\in\Gamma\) has weighted certificate \(fF\) through \(k+\deg F\le k+T\deg F\).

For NS, substitute in each original cofactor: its degree bound \(D-e\) becomes \(T(D-e)\), so all terms remain through \(B\). For PC, replay each line as \(f\Phi(p)\); multiplication by a source variable uses its degree-at-most-\(T\) image, with the same original-line ledger. A proof ending at \(q\) would end at \(fq\in J_B\), a contradiction. This separates the PC and ordinary-NS conclusions without asserting their equality for \(\Gamma\). \(\square\)

For the old compact base and \(q=1\), the cube-volume multiplier space makes \(\pi_{1,B}\) injective, with dimension at least \(\binom Vk/2\), and the earlier image conditions give \(R\le\binom Vk/4\). Thus the preceding quadratic theorem is recovered. Over a retained lower level, however, neither that quotient injection nor a sufficient mixed-variable rank has been proved. Merely knowing \(1\notin J_B\) supplies one surviving class; it does not supply the large rank required here.

2. Existing obstructions identify the missing hypothesis

For a nonconstant target, two nonzero classes can multiply to zero. The recorded Boolean zero-divisor control, \(q=1-b\) and \(f=bz\), already shows why a statement about surviving multipliers alone is insufficient. Formula (RQ-target) explicitly asks for surviving target products. This is a reuse of that obstruction, not a new discovery.

The relative affine theorem preserves the transported old-bit target window under its finite conditions. It does not establish (RQ-target) on arbitrary polynomials involving retained raw coefficients. The rank-three helper fixture further shows that full retained-interface preservation can fail even for complete affine helpers: new degree-seven and degree-eight consequences enter the old base only one degree later. That finite example does not refute the present criterion, which asks for separation at the larger ceiling \(TD+k\), and it does not establish accumulating losses. It does refute using same-degree conservativity as a free inductive premise.

Likewise, replacing all mixed components by scalar multiples of one old functional is ruled out by the literal-copy obstruction. A rank bound needs the actual mixed quotient, or a justified source-specific replacement; choosing a normalized old root independently is insufficient. Formal selector names also require their costed definition translation. Treating a weighted high-degree value as an ordinary degree-one variable does not by itself satisfy the quadratic criterion's degree hypothesis.

3. Two failed shortcuts, with explicit controls

Old-only weights need not enter even one high kernel. Retain old bits \(x\) and extra Boolean coordinates \(y_{ju},z_{ju}\), for \(1\le j\le a\) and \(1\le u\le2a^2\). Take the quadratic tuple

\[ g_j=\sum_{u=1}^{2a^2}y_{ju}z_{ju}\quad(1\le j\le a). \tag{RQ-padding} \]

Its variable groups are disjoint, and each selected product has polar rank two. Every nonzero binary combination of the \(g_j\)'s has polar rank at least \(4a^2\), so this is a genuine high case of the structural dichotomy. Nevertheless a nonzero multilinear polynomial \(f(x)\) cannot belong to the ideal generated by these inputs and Booleanity alone: setting every auxiliary coordinate to zero leaves every \(g_j=0\) and would make \(f(x)\) a Boolean-zero polynomial. Hence every kernel witness of the form \(f=\sum c_jg_j+E_{\rm BOOL}\), with \(f\) old-only, is zero. This conclusion is independent of the coordinate choice or reduction order.

The same test works for degree-controlled relative membership. With \(\Gamma=\mathcal Q_n(x)\cup{\rm BOOL}_{y,z}\), specialization at auxiliary zero sends \(\mathcal I_L(\Gamma\cup\{g_j\})\) into \(\mathcal I_L(\mathcal Q_n)\), without increasing degree. Any old-only space separated from the latter therefore has zero intersection with that relative input ideal. This does not refute source hardness: a different normalization or a mixed multiplier can still work. Nor is (RQ-padding) claimed to be the input grammar of a compiled Frege source. It refutes the proposed automatic reuse of the old-only kernel space for arbitrary retained-variable quadratic inputs.

The unchanged ambient parameter scheme is not uniform in polynomial inventory. Suppose one copies the preceding theorem's fixed-fraction conditions using the full retained-variable count \(V\), in particular

\[ M(V+1)e^{-ak^2/V^2}\le1/8. \]

Then \(ak^2\ge V^2\ln(8M(V+1))\). Since \(T\ge2k\) and \(T\ge2C_{\rm BR}a^4\),

\[ V^2\ln(8M(V+1)) \le\frac{T^{9/4}}{4(2C_{\rm BR})^{1/4}},\qquad T\ge\left[4(2C_{\rm BR})^{1/4}V^2\ln(8M(V+1))\right]^{4/9}. \tag{RQ-ambient-loss} \]

Already this one image inequality forces \(T=\Omega(V^{8/9}(\ln V)^{4/9})\). If the retained-variable inventory grows as \(V\ge n^{9/8}\), the copied ceiling \(TD+k\) cannot lie below the old \(n/4\) barrier, even for bounded positive \(D\). Arbitrary polynomial-size source inventories are not restricted to a power below \(9/8\). The second image condition and the probe term can only add cost. This is an obstruction to the unchanged fixed-fraction parameter scheme, not a lower bound on every possible implementation of (RQ-target), every source-specific map, or every retained-system proof barrier. Actual restricted image ranks may be much smaller than the ambient estimates.

4. Route decision

General claim needed. A useful iteration would provide source-specific multiplier spaces with sufficiently many target products surviving at the next degree ceiling, together with small relative input-reduction losses, and a recurrence leaving a positive degree saving for every fixed depth and prime. The rank criterion states a sufficient local interface; it does not establish any of these quantitative premises for the full source. Simply calling lower coefficients old variables is inadequate both algebraically and quantitatively.

Contribution to general-step. This cycle does not discharge the main compatibility obligation. It converts an ambiguous relative-extension hope into an explicit quotient-rank test and rules out two shortcuts before further case development. The general quadratic old-input theorem remains a substantive restricted endpoint. Its prior-art and independent-proof review remain pending.

Next bounded task. Keep the structural tools, but shift from ambient-variable iteration to the actual retained source relations. Obtain a hand derivation of the known rank-three mixed-interface degree-seven gain and its degree-eight old certificate, retaining every companion and its original cost. Use it to test whether a source-specific relative correction can be charged to the participating interfaces rather than the total raw coefficient inventory. Stop at that exact explanation or an identified missing mechanism; do not infer a general recurrence merely from a small fixture.

I estimate about 15% that this relative structural line, with a source-specific replacement for ambient counting, yields further useful progress on the main general step. The unchanged ambient iteration is ruled out in the parameter regimes above; this assessment is not a verdict on the whole Frege program.

Checks and process. The rank inequality, specialization control and exponent ledger were checked symbolically; previously archived finite matrices were read for scope, not rerun. Existing bounded claim retrieval exposed the earlier kernel criterion and target obstruction before a duplicate lemma was named. No additional framework rule or numerical suite was needed.

20 September 2026 — Canonical OR identities explain the mixed-interface gain

Status: working uniform certificate construction explaining the archived rank-three loss; original-degree certificates checked exactly at ranks three through five. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question. The relative review asks for source-specific control of retained consequences. The known degree-seven gain was later given a tracked elimination witness, but its simple mechanism remained unidentified. This cycle supplies a hand construction, then checks it without repeating the matrix search. The task stops at that mechanism and its actual composition limitations.

1. A uniform family of certificates

Over \(\mathbb F_2\), fix \(r\ge3\) and Boolean variables \(x_i,y_i,a_i,b_i\) for \(1\le i\le r\), and \(u,v\). Put

\[ L=\sum_i a_ix_i,\quad K=\sum_i b_iy_i,\quad A=1+L,\quad B=1+K, \quad E=1+uL+vK. \]

The retained system \(\Gamma_0\) contains all Boolean equations and the complete companions \(x_iA,y_iB,LE,KE\). These are precisely the accuracy-one blocks on \(x\), on \(y\), and on \((1+A,1+B)=(L,K)\); their original companion degrees are three, three and five. Adjoin the complete accuracy-one helper with fresh Boolean coefficients \(s_i\), inputs \(g_i=x_i+y_i\), product \(G=1+\sum_i s_ig_i\), and degree-three companions \(g_iG\), obtaining \(\Gamma_1\).

\[ F_r=\prod_i g_i+\prod_i x_i+\prod_i y_i, \qquad t_r=EF_r. \]

Working certificate lemma. In ordinary NS, with original degrees charged before Boolean reduction,

\[ t_r\in\mathcal I_{r+4}(\Gamma_1),\qquad t_r\in\mathcal I_{r+5}(\Gamma_0). \tag{MP-certificates} \]

The certificates use only these participating blocks, so adding unrelated retained axioms or variables does not increase their cost. For \(r=3\), the target is the archived mixed cubic, and the earlier exact matrix separation proves that its retained minimum degree is eight. Thus the first certificate explains that strict seven-versus-eight gap. No lower bound or strict gap for \(r>3\) follows from (MP-certificates).

2. The corrected polynomial lies in the helper input ideal

Write \(C(z)=1+\prod_i(1+z_i)\), and abbreviate

\[ c=C(x),\quad d=C(y),\quad e=C(g),\quad U=\sum_i a_ig_i,\quad V=\sum_i b_ig_i,\quad S=u+v. \]

Use the following corrected representative:

\[ Q=c+d+e+S\bigl(e+BU+AV\bigr). \tag{MP-Q} \]

This is an ordinary polynomial, not a value chosen only on source models. Let

\[ H_i=\prod_{j<i}(1+x_j)\prod_{j>i}(1+y_j),\qquad J_i=\prod_{j>i}(1+g_j), \]
\[ q_i=H_i+J_i+S(J_i+a_iB+b_iA). \]

Telescoping gives the exact ordinary identities \(c+d=\sum_i g_iH_i\) and \(e=\sum_i g_iJ_i\). Therefore

\[ Q=\sum_iq_ig_i,\qquad \deg q_i\le\max(r,4),\qquad \deg Q\le\max(r+1,5). \tag{MP-input} \]

The correction is what allows low-cost annihilation by every helper input; the bare mixed target does not come with that certificate for free.

3. Every input annihilates the corrected polynomial cheaply

We claim

\[ g_jQ\in\mathcal I_{\max(r+3,6)}(\Gamma_0)\quad(1\le j\le r). \tag{MP-annihilate} \]

All Boolean-function equalities below have ordinary Boolean NS certificates through their displayed expansion degrees. In particular \(x_jc=x_j\), \(y_jd=y_j\), and \(g_je=g_j\) hold through \(r+1\); the last uses \(g_j^2+g_j=(x_j^2+x_j)+(y_j^2+y_j)\), with no assumption that an arbitrary nonbinary affine form is Boolean.

Multiplying (MP-Q) by \(g_j\) first leaves \(x_jd+y_jc\), plus \(S(g_j+g_jBU+g_jAV)\). The following reductions have retained certificates through five:

\[ g_jBU+x_jB =U(y_jB)+B(x_jA)+\sum_i a_ix_j(y_iB), \]
\[ g_jAV+y_jA =V(x_jA)+A(y_jB)+\sum_i b_iy_j(x_iA). \tag{MP-local} \]

These are exact ordinary identities: expand \(U=L+\sum_i a_iy_i\), \(V=K+\sum_i b_ix_i\). Hence, after multiplying by \(S\),

\[ g_jQ\equiv x_jd+y_jc+S(x_jK+y_jL) \pmod{\mathcal I_{\max(r+2,6)}(\Gamma_0)}. \]

Telescoping \(c=\sum_i x_i\prod_{b>i}(1+x_b)\) shows \(c+L\in\mathcal I_{r+2}(\Gamma_0)\): multiply the \(x_iA\)'s by those degree-at-most-\(r-1\) coefficients, and use \(Lc=L\) modulo Booleanity. Similarly \(d+K\in\mathcal I_{r+2}\). Thus the last display reduces through \(\max(r+3,6)\) to \((1+u+v)(x_jK+y_jL)\).

Finally \(y_jLE\) equals \((1+u+v)y_jL+vL(y_jB)\) modulo the Boolean correction \(u y_j(L^2+L)\); the analogous identity for \(x_jKE\) has correction \(v x_j(K^2+K)\) and companion term \(uK(x_jA)\). All cost at most six. Adding them proves (MP-annihilate) with complete ordinary witnesses.

4. Comparison with the target and the final ceilings

First,

\[ E(c+d+e)+Q\in\mathcal I_{r+3}(\Gamma_0). \tag{MP-compare} \]

Expand \(E\), use \(Lc=L\), \(Kd=K\) through degree \(r+3\), and group the terms as

\[ uL+vK+vKc+uLd+uAe+vBe+S(BU+AV). \]

The exact telescoping differences \(C(g)+C(y)\) and \(C(g)+C(x)\) belong respectively to \((x_i)_i\) and \((y_i)_i\), with cofactors of degree at most \(r-1\). Multiplication by \(A\) or \(B\), then by \(u\) or \(v\), uses retained companions through \(r+3\). Replace \(uAe\) by \(uAd\) and \(vBe\) by \(vBc\). The display becomes \(uL+vK+ud+vc+S(BU+AV)\). Replace \(d,c\) by \(K,L\) using their certificates through \(r+2\), with one additional coefficient. What remains is

\[ S(L+K+BU+AV)=S\sum_i\bigl(a_i(y_iB)+b_i(x_iA)\bigr), \]

which has cost five. This proves (MP-compare); the assumption \(r\ge3\) absorbs all constant ceilings.

The highest homogeneous part of \(c+d+e\) is \(F_r\), and its lower part has zero constant term and degree at most \(r-1\). The exact identities

\[ Ex_i=x_i(LE)+E(x_iA),\qquad Ey_i=y_i(KE)+E(y_iB) \tag{MP-old-kill} \]

give cost-six certificates. Applying one of them to each monomial of the lower part gives \(E(F_r+c+d+e)\in\mathcal I_{r+4}(\Gamma_0)\), and therefore

\[ t_r+Q\in\mathcal I_{r+4}(\Gamma_0). \]

Use the earlier gain mechanism, now with explicit hand-chosen data:

\[ Q=\sum_iq_i(g_iG)+\sum_j s_j(g_jQ). \]

The first sum costs \(\max(r,4)+3\le r+4\); the second costs \(\max(r+3,6)+1=r+4\). Together with the target comparison this proves the augmented part of (MP-certificates). Applying (MP-old-kill) directly to every degree-\(r\) monomial of \(F_r\) gives the retained ceiling \(r+5\). The ordinary generator costs, including five for \(LE,KE\), have not been replaced by multilinear image degrees. All coefficient Boolean equations remain present. \(\square\)

5. Exact controls and scope

The bounded checker constructs these cofactors directly for \(r=3,4,5\), expands ordinary polynomials with repeated exponents, divides the remaining Boolean-zero errors by all Boolean generators, and reconstructs the full ordinary identities. It checks each \(g_jQ\), the target comparison, and both target certificates: 21 identities in total. It charges each original companion degree plus its cofactor degree and emits every cofactor. All passed. Removing one input-annihilation contribution leaves a nonzero Boolean remainder, and charging the augmented construction one degree less than \(r+4\) fails its cofactor budget in all three cases.

Complete certificates and controls and the reproduction note are preserved. These are new checks of the hand construction, not fresh matrix lower bounds; the rank-three nonmembership assertion is reused from the historical computation. The preceding checkpoint's first archival attempt failed to reach user systemd from the sandbox; the escalated retry succeeded. That operational failure is separate from these successful mathematical checks.

6. What this says about the main route

The mechanism is local to the participating blocks, and its formula is uniform in rank; unrelated inventory does not enter its upper certificates. It shows why preserving only separate old-product terms misses a cheaper mixed relation. It does not prove that every helper-induced consequence admits this correction, that multiple such corrections compose without growth, or that their quotient losses have small rank. Increasing \(r\) increases the displayed source-degree budget; these are not uniform degree-seven witnesses of unbounded rank loss. Accuracy one, the binary field and this specific block template are essential stated restrictions.

Contribution to general-step. The known obstruction now has a short algebraic explanation and a uniform witness family. The main source-compatibility obligation is still open. I estimate roughly 15% that analyzing these source-specific relative corrections yields further useful progress on it; no probability for the whole research goal is intended.

Next bounded task. Try to falsify the general hope behind such corrections before proving more templates: can one complete level of fresh affine helpers always be eliminated into ordinary retained NS with a degree bound polynomial in the incoming degree, independent of helper count? Distinguish arbitrary retained bases from actual compiled sources, and NS from PC. Check the known coefficient criterion and proof-system separation controls; a counterexample or a precise surviving scope is the stopping point, not a conjectured recurrence.

Process assessment. Reading the later tracked witness exposed its canonical-OR structure; deriving symbolic cofactors before testing avoided another expensive elimination and produced a uniform statement instead of more isolated examples. No framework expansion was needed.

20 September 2026 — The historical prefix obstruction already rules out generic NS batching

Status: rediscovery and scope audit of an existing historical counterexample; no new theorem or finite computation. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and verdict. The previous cycle proposed testing whether a complete level of fresh affine helpers can always be eliminated into retained ordinary NS at degree polynomial in the incoming degree, independently of helper count. This is false for arbitrary retained bases. The counterexample was already proved in the handoff, including logarithmic accuracy and a stronger bound allowing logarithmic inventory. The useful outcome here is to close this proposed branch immediately and restore the precise NS-versus-PC distinction.

1. Existing counterexample, with its original costs

Use a topologically ordered single-sink DAG on \(N\) vertices, indegree at most two. Put \(b_i=1-x_i\), \(f_i=b_i\prod_{j\in\operatorname{pred}(i)}x_j\), and let \(\mathcal F_G\) contain all \(f_i\), the contradictory sink equation \(x_N\), and the old Boolean equations. For every prefix \([k]\), introduce one complete accuracy-\(h\) block on \((b_1,\ldots,b_k)\):

\[ A_k=\prod_{u=1}^{h}\left(1-\sum_{j\le k}r_{k,u,j}b_j\right), \qquad E_{k,j}=b_jA_k,\qquad A_0=1. \]

All blocks are in one level, their inputs are old affine polynomials, and all coefficients are fresh between blocks. Products have degree \(2h\), companions have degree \(2h+1\), and the full coefficient-domain equations can be included. There are \(N\) blocks and \(M=N(N+1)/2\) companions.

The historical lem:prefixcertificate supplies a degree-\(4h+2\) ordinary NS refutation over every field. For completeness, the local identities behind the audit are as follows. Choose the standard product-prefix coefficients \(U_{k,j}\) with

\[ 1-A_k=\sum_{j\le k}U_{k,j}b_j, \qquad \deg U_{k,j}\le2h-1. \]
\[ A_{k-1}-A_k =\sum_{j<k}U_{k,j}E_{k-1,j} +U_{k,k}b_kA_{k-1} -\sum_{j<k}U_{k-1,j}E_{k,j}. \]

For ordered predecessors \(p_1,\ldots,p_t\), \(t\le2\),

\[ b_kA_{k-1} =A_{k-1}f_k+ b_k\sum_{\ell=1}^{t}\left(\prod_{v<\ell}x_{p_v}\right)E_{k-1,p_\ell}. \]

The largest substituted summand has original degree \((2h-1)+2h+3=4h+2\). Sum all consecutive differences, and finish with \(A_N=A_Nx_N+E_{N,N}\). This is an exact ordinary certificate; no Boolean or fresh field reduction is used. Every summand involves at most two consecutive coefficient blocks. Thus sparse local block interaction does not prevent the collective shortening.

The audited imported pebbling family has old ordinary NS degree \(\Omega(N^{1/3})\), over every field, with the recorded Boolean-domain convention. With \(h=1\), the augmented degree is at most six while the old degree is unbounded. More strongly, choose \(h=\Theta(\log N)\). Then \(D=4h+2\) and \(\log M\) are logarithmic, whereas the old NS degree dominates \((D+h+\log M)^C\) for every fixed \(C\). This is exactly the historical cor:genericbatchfalse, not a new construction.

2. What is ruled out, and what survives

Ruled out: a universal ordinary-NS-to-ordinary-NS one-level transfer of degree polynomial in \(D,h,\log M\) for arbitrary retained Boolean bases, even with old-affine inputs and polynomial inventory. Preservation of all old NS designs through such a budget is equally impossible. The new local mixed-interface certificates do not avoid this obstruction merely because their formulas touch few blocks.

Not ruled out: a source-specific theorem for PHP, a transfer into old PC with suitable hypotheses, or a compatible ordinary source functional constructed by using stronger old-PC separation. The same pebbling base has a degree-three PC refutation, by the historical lem:pebblingpc. Its large NS degree supplies no old-PC obstruction. The direct complete-source ordinary NS functional remains sufficient for our compiled goal, but a sufficient output need not be obtainable from only ordinary-NS hardness of an arbitrary retained input system. Conversely, an NS output cannot silently be reused as a PC-stable input to another elimination.

The assignment-prefix tree control addresses a different escape: it works even over a PC-hard Boolean base, but has exponentially many blocks. It therefore refutes inventory-independent variants, not a bound explicitly charging \(\log M\). The actual compact-PHP factorial control has its own inventory ledger. These controls must be applied with their different old proof systems and counts intact.

3. Route decision and process repair

The broad NS-only batching line is closed; its chance of establishing the proposed general theorem is zero. This does not lower the status of the completed quadratic endpoint or establish a negative verdict on the main Frege goal. No remaining-route obligation was discharged in this cycle. The discovery was a retrieval failure corrected before any numerical search: the default current-registry search does not search the immutable historical index, and a direct lookup of its elimination chapter immediately supplied the stronger recorded theorem.

Next bounded task, general-step. Test an inventory-sensitive transfer into old PC, with a proposed ceiling polynomial in \(D,h,\log M\), before attempting an induction. Start with the recorded PC-hard assignment-tree and compact factorial controls and compute whether their inventories actually violate that proposed ceiling. Keep arbitrary retained bases distinct from matching/PHP bases, and do not infer augmented PC stability from ordinary NS compatibility. Stop at a genuine counterexample or a precise surviving hypothesis. I estimate about 15% that this more restricted investigation supplies useful progress; the estimate concerns this line only.

Checks and process assessment. Re-read the exact historical certificate, its imported degree statement and its PC-three proof; no historical suite was rerun and no literature novelty is claimed. Tighten the existing claim-search guidance to include a targeted historical-index lookup before extending a generic mechanism. This needs no new index, parser, or mandatory full-handoff read.

20 September 2026 — Inventory-sensitive PC transfer survives the prefix controls, but needs a sharper test

Status: scoped negative-control audit and imported ordering-principle test family; no general transfer theorem or new counterexample established. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question. After rejecting generic NS-only batching, test the stronger-input endpoint: could an ordinary degree-\(D\) refutation using one complete affine ENS level imply an old PC refutation at a ceiling polynomial in \(D,h,\log(M+1)\)? Here \(M\) bounds the actual block/slot inventory, all original degrees remain charged, and the retained base includes its Boolean axioms. A uniform theorem over arbitrary bases would be convenient; the main goal only needs an adequate PHP-relative or actual-source statement. This cycle checks existing controls and identifies the missing step in a new candidate test.

1. The known controls do not answer this version

ControlOld proof system and inventoryVerdict for the proposed PC ceiling
Historical pebbling prefixOld NS degree grows; old PC degree is three; polynomial inventory.Refutes the NS output, not the PC output.
Full Boolean assignment treeMay start from a PC-hard base on v variables; log inventory is Θ(v).The charged inventory already allows the general old truth-table degree bound.
Compact PHP factorial treev=(n+1)log₂n old bits; log inventory is Θ(n log n)=Θ(v).The same budget issue prevents it from refuting a polynomial log-inventory ceiling.

Why the latter verdict is stronger than comparing one lower bound. Any Boolean-unsatisfiable old system \(\Gamma\) on \(v\) variables, with maximum axiom degree \(\delta\), has an ordinary NS refutation through \(v+\delta\). For each Boolean assignment \(a\), choose an axiom \(F_a\) with \(F_a(a)\ne0\), and let \(\chi_a\) be its degree-\(v\) Boolean point indicator. The difference

\[ \chi_a-\chi_a F_a/F_a(a) \]

is Boolean-zero and has an ordinary Boolean certificate through \(v+\delta\). Sum over all assignments, using \(\sum_a\chi_a=1\). This proves the bound and hence the same old PC upper bound. It is only a degree argument; the certificate may be exponential in size. In both tree controls, \(\log(M+1)=\Theta(v)\), so a sufficiently large linear function of \(\delta+\log(M+1)\) already covers it. The old input degree must also be retained when specifying a general theorem; in the compact control it is \(\ell\), and is included in the incoming source ceiling.

For the compact tree specifically, \(M=\Theta(n\,n!)\), hence \(\log M=\Theta(n\log n)\), while its augmented degree is \(\max(4h+1,2h+\ell)\). Taking \(h=\Theta(\ell)\) makes the source degree logarithmic but does not make its inventory logarithmic in the old variable count. No new numerical check was needed.

2. A more discriminating imported test family

Galesi and Lauria's Optimality of size-degree trade-offs for Polynomial Calculus, Section 3, Lemma 1 and Theorems 1–2, provides bounded-degree expander graph ordering systems on \(\binom n2\) Boolean variables, with constant-degree axioms, PC degree \(\Omega(n)\), and polynomial-size resolution refutations, over every field. Use their specified total-order polynomial encoding, not an arbitrary ordering-principle variant. The degree statement is imported, not proved or independently re-audited here.

This supplies the old-PC-hard, short-proof contrast that pebbling lacks. It is only a candidate counterexample to the proposed transfer until the required augmented source is constructed.

3. A short proof is not the missing source certificate

To falsify the candidate using this family, we would need polynomially many one-level old-affine complete ENS blocks and an ordinary NS refutation through polylogarithmic degree, with the exact original costs. A polynomial-size resolution proof alone does not supply that premise. Local clause simulations may give a low-degree PC derivation while their ordinary NS flattening pays for proof height.

The available modular ordinary NS compiler explicitly charges \((C_p+H_\pi)L\) under its coherent balanced-presentation hypotheses. A size bound does not certify a logarithmic \(H_\pi\) or preserve a single old-affine source level during a balancing transformation. Introducing conjunctions of earlier clause values can instead create another ENS level. Neither a PC proof nor a multilevel NS source is the one-level ordinary certificate being tested.

Thus the graph-ordering facts do not currently refute the displayed one-level transfer hope. Conversely, passing the prefix controls is not evidence that a universal transfer is true. A sufficient target for the main goal may still require PHP geometry or actual proof-source restrictions.

4. Decision and next test

General-step remains open. The proposed PC-output bound survives the existing controls for explicit reasons. The next bounded task is to attempt the missing graph-ordering source construction: can its short ordering argument be expressed by polynomially many one-level affine blocks with polylogarithmic ordinary NS degree? Keep all parents, proof-height factors and coefficient equations visible. Stop at such a complete certificate, or at a precise point where the chosen construction requires another level or an unaffordable height cost. Do not call failure of that construction a proof that no such certificate exists.

I assign roughly 10% to this generic PC-transfer line yielding a usable positive transfer theorem, and regard the ordering family as a worthwhile falsification test before further positive development. This is a judgment about the line, not about the overall Frege goal.

Evidence and process assessment. The local tree and compiler proofs were read at their exact anchors; the author's accessible paper supplied the candidate family's statement and encoding scope. Source locations and reading scope are retained without redistributing the paper. No computation or theorem was manufactured to justify this audit. The prior historical-lookup fix was used; no further framework rule was needed.

20 September 2026 — Balanced minimum blocks refute the generic inventory-sensitive PC transfer

Status: working complete one-level source construction and generic-transfer counterexample; 60 exact ordinary certificates checked over three prime fields. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. The previous audit left a precise missing premise: a polynomial-inventory one-level affine ENS source of low ordinary NS degree for the graph-ordering control. A balanced minimum construction supplies it. This closes the proposed generic old-PC transfer, not the ordinary-PHP research program.

1. Complete source and theorem

Work over \(\mathbb F_p\), for any prime \(p\), with \(n\ge2\) ordered vertex labels and Boolean old variables \(x_{ij}\), \(i<j\). Write \(t_{ij}=x_{ij}\) if \(i<j\), and \(t_{ij}=1-x_{ji}\) if \(i>j\); thus \(t_{ij}+t_{ji}=1\). The old total-order system contains the two cyclic triangle polynomials for each unordered triple, equivalently every \(t_{ij}t_{j\ell}(1-t_{i\ell})\) for distinct vertices. For a simple graph of maximum degree \(\Delta\), its no-local-minimum axioms are \(F_i=\prod_{j\in N(i)}t_{ij}\). Include old Booleanity. This is the imported graph-ordering encoding.

Take a balanced binary partition tree of the vertex set, of height \(H=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\). At every nonsingleton node \(S\), and for every \(i\in S\), introduce a complete accuracy-\(h\) ENS block, \(h\ge1\), on the affine old inputs \(g_{i\ell}=1-t_{i\ell}\), \(\ell\in S\setminus\{i\}\). Denote its product by \(P_{S,i}\). Every block has fresh own coefficients and all coefficient field equations. Set \(P_{\{i\},i}=1\) as notation, without introducing an empty block. All genuine blocks are in one level, since all inputs are old literals.

Working theorem. This complete source has an ordinary NS refutation through

\[ D_{\rm ord}=\max\{(2H+4)h+2,\ 2h+\Delta\}. \tag{OM-degree} \]

There are at most \(nH\) blocks and \(2n(n-1)\) companions, and at most \(2hn(n-1)\) fresh coefficient variables. The certificates below use old Boolean equations but no fresh field equations; including all of the latter does not change the identity. Every nonempty block has product degree \(2h\), companion degree \(2h+1\), and prefix coefficients \(U_{S,i;\ell}\) of degree at most \(2h-1\), with the exact identity

\[ 1-P_{S,i}=\sum_{\ell\in S\setminus\{i\}}U_{S,i;\ell}g_{i\ell}. \tag{OM-prefix} \]

2. A local comparison has cost at most 6h+2

At a split \(S=A\sqcup B\), fix \(i\in A,j\in B\), and put \(X=P_{A,i}\), \(Y=P_{B,j}\), \(Z=P_{S,i}\), \(t=t_{ij}\). We prove

\[ ZY-tXY\in\mathcal I_{6h+2}. \tag{OM-comparison} \]

All memberships in this proof use only the old order/Boolean axioms and displayed complete companions. Start from the exact decomposition

\[ ZY-tXY=ZY(1-X)+XYZ(1-t)-tXY(1-Z). \]

Expand the first term by (OM-prefix) for \(X\). Every input belongs to \(Z\)'s tuple, so each term is a \(Z\)-companion with cofactor \(YU_{A,i;\ell}\), costing at most \(6h\). The second term is the \(j\)-companion of \(Z\) with cofactor \(XY\), costing at most \(6h+1\).

For the last term expand (OM-prefix) for \(Z\). We need witnesses for \(tXYg_{i\ell}\). If \(\ell\in A\setminus\{i\}\), it is an \(X\)-companion times \(tY\), through \(4h+2\). If \(\ell=j\), use \(t(1-t)=-(x_{\min(i,j),\max(i,j)}^2-x_{\min(i,j),\max(i,j)})\), with the coordinate interpreted by its unordered pair, and multiply by \(XY\); the degree is \(4h+2\). If \(\ell\in B\setminus\{j\}\), use the exact identity

\[ t_{ij}(1-t_{i\ell}) =t_{ij}(1-t_{i\ell})(1-t_{j\ell}) +t_{ij}t_{j\ell}(1-t_{i\ell}). \tag{OM-transitivity} \]

After multiplication by \(XY\), the first summand is a \(Y\)-companion times \(Xt_{ij}(1-t_{i\ell})\), and the second is an old cyclic-triangle axiom times \(XY\). Both cost at most \(4h+3\). Multiplication by the relevant prefix coefficient adds at most \(2h-1\), giving \(6h+2\). This proves (OM-comparison) with ordinary NS witnesses and their original degrees. Singleton children cause no difficulty: their products are one and their empty prefix sums vanish.

Interchanging \(A,i\) with \(B,j\) gives the corresponding identity with \(t_{ji}=1-t_{ij}\). Add them:

\[ P_{S,i}P_{B,j}+P_{S,j}P_{A,i}-P_{A,i}P_{B,j} \in\mathcal I_{6h+2}. \tag{OM-pair} \]

3. Balanced composition preserves a logarithmic height cost

Set \(\alpha=\sum_{i\in A}P_{A,i}\), \(\beta=\sum_{j\in B}P_{B,j}\), \(Z_A=\sum_{i\in A}P_{S,i}\), \(Z_B=\sum_{j\in B}P_{S,j}\). Summing (OM-pair) gives

\[ R=Z_A\beta+Z_B\alpha-\alpha\beta\in\mathcal I_{6h+2}. \]

Now use an exact polynomial identity, rather than assuming a semantic partition of the unsatisfiable old models:

\[ Z_A+Z_B-1 =R+(\alpha-Z_A)(\beta-1)+(1-Z_B)(\alpha-1). \tag{OM-recursion} \]

The two new multipliers have degree at most \(2h\). If child partition identities have ordinary NS ceilings \(d_A,d_B\), this identity has ceiling \(\max(6h+2,d_A+2h,d_B+2h)\). A singleton partition identity is exactly zero. Thus a node of positive height \(L\) satisfies

\[ \sum_{i\in S}P_{S,i}-1\in\mathcal I_{(2L+4)h+2}. \tag{OM-partition} \]

This is an ordinary-certificate recurrence: multiplying an already supplied child certificate increases its ceiling by \(2h\). It neither assumes truncated NS spaces are ideals nor silently reuses PC consequences. The degree depends on balanced tree height, not on the number of vertices, local comparison pairs or blocks.

At the root, write the graph neighbors of \(i\) in any order. Telescoping \(1-F_i\) gives

\[ P_{[n],i}=P_{[n],i}F_i+ \sum_{j\in N(i)}\left(\prod_{k\text{ before }j}t_{ik}\right) g_{ij}P_{[n],i}. \tag{OM-root} \]

Every term is an original old-axiom or root-companion multiple through \(2h+\Delta\). Sum the root equations and subtract (OM-partition). This yields one and proves (OM-degree).

4. Inventory and certificate representation

At each internal depth, the node sets partition the vertices; hence the total number of blocks is at most \(nH\). If \(C(n)\) counts companion slots, then \(C(1)=0\) and

\[ C(n)=n(n-1)+C(\lfloor n/2\rfloor)+C(\lceil n/2\rceil) \le2n(n-1). \]

For the induction, putting \(a+b=n\) with \(|a-b|\le1\), the difference between the substituted upper bound and \(2n(n-1)\) is \((a-b)^2-n\le0\). The coefficient-variable count is \(hC(n)\). These are actual source inventories, not counts of semantic input types after cancellation.

The displayed certificates also have polynomial-size factored coefficient representations in \(n,h\): each local comparison uses a polynomial number of prefixes and source multiples, the tree has \(O(n)\) nodes, and a local witness acquires only a product of at most \(H\) ancestor multipliers. This does not assert polynomial expanded monomial size, a particular ROABP width, or a cheap old-variable substitution for all coefficients.

5. Consequence for generic transfer, not for PHP

Apply the construction to the published bounded-degree expander ordering family, whose old PC degree is \(\Omega(n)\). The source degree is \(O(h\log n)\), and every source count is polynomial when \(h\) is polylogarithmic. Taking \(h=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\) gives \(D=O((\log n)^2)\) and \(\log(M+1)=O(\log n)\). Therefore no universal transfer from this ordinary one-level affine ENS source into old PC can promise a degree bounded by any fixed polynomial in \(D,h,\log(M+1)\). Its promised ceiling would be polylogarithmic and contradict the old degree lower bound.

This is a working counterexample to the proposed generic statement even with complete companions, fresh coefficient domains, polynomial inventory and polynomial-size factored witnesses. It supplies the missing premise of the preceding audit; it is not merely the observation that ordering has short resolution proofs. The previous exponential tree controls and the PC-easy pebbling prefix have different scopes.

The compact PHP base is not this ordering base. In particular this does not contradict the PHP old-quadratic endpoint, the one-affine-level matching argument, or the conditional target-rank criterion. It rules out replacing their PHP-specific separation by old PC hardness alone. A successful relative induction must preserve a stronger property or use justified restrictions on the actual proof source.

6. Exact checks and route assessment

The new checker uses four ordered vertices, a balanced tree and a path graph for the no-local-minimum axioms. For primes 2, 3 and 5 and accuracies 1 and 2, it constructs ordinary prefix, comparison, partition and root witnesses directly, without matrix search or assignment enumeration. All 60 emitted certificates reconstruct exactly at their original-degree budgets. Omitting all transitivity contributions makes the full identity fail in every case. Coefficient field equations are present and have zero cofactors throughout.

Complete certificate output and reproduction details are retained. The finite graph is a certificate control, not a test of the asymptotic expander lower bound. The first build rejected three misleading-indentation warnings; they were fixed before the accepted build and run.

General-step outcome. The generic inventory-sensitive old-PC transfer is false; that proposed positive line has no remaining chance in its stated scope. The main PHP-relative compatibility obligation remains open, now with a stronger adversarial control. The construction is flagged for prior-art and independent-proof review, without a novelty or publication claim.

Identify a precise matching/PHP property actually used by the available affine and quadratic separators that is absent from the ordering construction, and state the retained-level hypothesis an induction would have to preserve. Test that hypothesis against the existing same-degree and mixed-moment obstructions before developing further restricted examples. 20 September 2026 — Preserve matching corrections, not raw augmented filtration stability

Status: explicit harmless filtration failure over PHP and a scoped conditioning-defect identity; no retained-level compatibility theorem established. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

General claim under review. The ordering counterexample rules out generic low-degree transfer from old PC hardness and polynomial inventory alone. The remaining route needs a PHP-relative construction. This review asks which old matching properties supply the separator, whether full augmented filtration stability can be its invariant, and what freedom remains after the known failure of natural moment sections.

1. The old proof uses a family of geometric detectors

The signed residual detector reserves disjoint label cubes for selected pigeon rows, deletes all their labels, and fills the remaining matching board. If the cubes occupy \(u\) rows and \(F\) labels, its explicit room condition is \(n-F\ge2(B-u)-1\). The signed differences annihilate missing axes; the residual factor is independent of all reserved labels. This supplies many independently separated old targets, quantified by the cube-volume space. It is much more information than \(1\notin\mathcal C_B\).

That particular construction cannot simply be copied to the ordering base. On three order coordinates \(x=t_{12},y=t_{23},z=t_{13}\), the full signed cube takes the cubic coefficient of the old triangle axiom \(xy(1-z)\), which is \(-1\). Tensoring with a normalized residual functional independent of these coordinates still gives \(-1\), rather than zero. This is a failure of that proposed independent-coordinate detector, not a claim that no ordering separator exists below its degree bound.

For actual retained ENS systems, the required target-product rank is still unproved. The old matching theorem supplies extension and stable filtration for the old matching algebra. Neither its row-set argument nor its detector automatically annihilates all mixed source modules.

2. Full raw filtration stability fails even for a removable block

Over any \(\mathbb F_p\), take functional unary PHP with \(N+1\) rows and \(N\ge4h+1\) holes, \(h\ge1\). Choose the old cell \(x=X_{11}\). Add one complete accuracy-\(h\) block on the singleton input \(x\), with fresh coefficients \(r_1,\ldots,r_h\):

\[ P=\prod_{u=1}^h(1-r_ux),\qquad F=xP, \qquad q=x\prod_{u=1}^h(1-r_u). \]

The companion has original ordinary degree \(2h+1\), whereas \(q\) has degree \(h+1\). If \(\Gamma\) is the full augmented system, then

\[ q\in\mathcal I_{2h+1}(\Gamma)\cap\mathcal P_{\le h+1}, \qquad q\notin\mathcal I_{h+1}(\Gamma). \tag{SF-fall} \]

Proof of membership. Writing \(r_S=\prod_{u\in S}r_u\), expansion gives the exact identity

\[ F-q=(x^2-x) \sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq[h]}(-1)^{|S|}r_S \sum_{j=0}^{|S|-1}x^j. \]

Each displayed Boolean multiple has degree at most \(2h+1\), so this is an ordinary NS certificate at the original companion cost, without resetting that cost after reduction.

Proof of nonmembership. The companion is inactive at degree \(h+1\). Setting all \(r_u=0\) in a putative certificate would therefore derive \(x\) from the old base through \(h+1\); fresh field equations vanish. But pinning cell \((1,1)\), deleting its row and column, and using a normalized residual matching design through \(h+1\) gives an old design with value one on \(x\). The required residual bound \(N-1\ge2(h+1)-1\) follows from \(N\ge4h+1\). All old axiom images are residual matching axioms or zero. This proves nonmembership by duality.

This fall does not make the old problem easier. Set \(r_1=1\), all other coefficients zero. The sole companion maps to \(x(1-x)\), an old Boolean consequence through two; every coefficient field equation maps to zero. This is a degree-preserving elimination for old targets. It is an existing low-rank cleanup, not an obstruction to an algorithm that performs that cleanup. The example only refutes full raw-variable filtration stability as a necessary invariant. In the costed interface, the relation is still charged at \(2h+1\); the smaller collected degree does not authorize it earlier.

3. Noncommuting sections have precisely located defects

Use the notation of the existing no-natural-sections obstruction. Over any field, let \(\mathcal A_s\) be the old matching annihilator through \(s\), \(R_s:\mathcal A_s\to\mathcal A_{s-1}\) restriction, and \(M_e^{(s)}\) conditioning by cell \(e\). Assume \(d\ge1,m\ge d+1,N\ge2d+1\), and choose any linear sections \(E_{d-1},E_d\). Put \(K_d=\ker R_d\) and define

\[ \Delta_e=M_e^{(d+1)}E_d-E_{d-1}M_e^{(d)}: \mathcal A_d\longrightarrow\mathcal A_d. \]

Working defect identity.

\[ \Delta_e(\mathcal A_d)\subseteq K_d, \qquad \sum_{j=1}^N\Delta_{ij} =\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A_d}-E_{d-1}R_d \quad\text{for each row }i. \tag{CD-defects} \]

Indeed restrictions commute with conditioning, so \(R_dM_e^{(d+1)}E_d=M_e^{(d)}\), while \(R_dE_{d-1}M_e^{(d)}=M_e^{(d)}\). Their difference is zero. Summing before restriction uses the old row identity \(\sum_jM_{ij}^{(s)}=R_s\), giving the second formula. Its right-hand side is the projection onto \(K_d\), and equals the identity on \(K_d\).

A member of \(K_d\) has zero moments below \(d\). On each \(d\)-row set its top moments consequently have zero marginals. The disjoint two-label trade theorem, applicable since \(N\ge2d\), spans these arrays by signed trades. Thus each defect has a trade expansion. This refines the location of the previously identified obstruction; it does not remove it. In particular the defects cannot all vanish on every component of a whole row.

For clarity, changing sections by \(E_d'=E_d+L_d\) and \(E_{d-1}'=E_{d-1}+L_{d-1}\), with \(L_d\) valued in \(K_{d+1}\) and \(L_{d-1}\) valued in \(K_d\), changes the defect by

\[ \Delta_e'-\Delta_e=M_e^{(d+1)}L_d-L_{d-1}M_e^{(d)}. \tag{CD-change} \]

These formulas give a concrete correction space. They do not prove that any specified family of corrections solves the source equations. Different selector components may require different top-trade corrections even when their lower restrictions coincide; one fixed section need not encode those independent choices.

4. What is retained, and the next bounded question

The sufficient endpoint remains a normalized solution of the complete costed source equations, with the old root chosen after seeing the source. Full raw augmented stability is an unnecessary and false convenience. The matching geometry supplies explicit old detector and correction spaces; simultaneous annihilation of the mixed source modules is the unproved step. The scalar-copy and strict-naturality obstructions still apply.

Next task, general-step. Use (CD-defects) to write the source-dependent correction problem in zero-marginal trade coordinates at one weighted moment layer. Identify what an actual OR/MP overlap demands of those corrections, retaining all carried module costs and previously prescribed lower moments. The general hope is controlled simultaneous correction for the actual polynomial-inventory PHP source, not arbitrary commuting sections. Stop at a proved source-specific correction or an explicit dual obstruction; an abstract restatement of the full linear system alone does not discharge the task.

Assessment. No main-route obligation was discharged. The raw-stability shortcut is closed and the correction freedom is explicit, but there is no bound on its source-coupled obstruction. I estimate about 10% that this correction line yields a useful main-route advance. The two displayed algebraic arguments were checked symbolically; no numerical computation was warranted.

20 September 2026 — Row-bit predicates admit simultaneous trade corrections

Status: working one-row lifting theorem and local costed MP-fan correction; exact moment checks over three fields; multirow source compatibility remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question. The previous review located conditioning errors in zero-marginal trade spaces. This cycle identifies an explicit image of the conditioning map and uses it to solve a shared-variable family of actual MP-shaped equations. The result is uniform in the old degree and predicate count under a stated evaluation-rank condition; it does not construct the entire source functional.

1. Robust row evaluations give a joint lift

Work over a field \(\mathbb K\), on the functional matching board with \(m\) rows and \(N\) columns. Let \(\mathcal A_s\) be its ordinary degree-\(s\) annihilator, including unnormalized functionals, and let \(K_s=\ker(\mathcal A_s\to\mathcal A_{s-1})\). Fix \(d\ge1\), \(m\ge d+1\), \(N\ge2d+1\), and one distinguished row \(i\). Define

\[ K_d^{\neg i}=\{\eta\in K_d:\eta(X_T)=0 \text{ whenever the matching }T\text{ uses row }i\}. \]

For row-label functions \(f_1,\ldots,f_s:[N]\to\mathbb K\), \(s\ge1\), put \(a_t(X)=\sum_j f_t(j)X_{ij}\), and let \(M_{a_t}^{(d+1)}\) be conditioning by that affine old polynomial. Assume the evaluation matrix of \(1,f_1,\ldots,f_s\) has row rank \(s+1\) after deletion of any at most \(2d\) columns:

\[ \operatorname{rank}\begin{pmatrix} 1&\cdots&1\\ f_1(j)&\cdots&f_1(k)\\ \vdots&&\vdots\\ f_s(j)&\cdots&f_s(k) \end{pmatrix}_{j,\ldots,k\notin L}=s+1 \quad(|L|\le2d). \tag{RT-rank} \]

Working theorem. The map

\[ K_{d+1}\longrightarrow(K_d^{\neg i})^s, \qquad v\longmapsto(M_{a_1}^{(d+1)}v,\ldots,M_{a_s}^{(d+1)}v) \tag{RT-map} \]

is surjective and has a linear right inverse. Thus several predicate defects on one row can be corrected by one higher-degree trade, not independently chosen extensions of the shared component.

Proof: image and spanning. Conditioning commutes with restriction, so each image has zero lower moments. On a degree-\(d\) matching using row \(i\) at label \(j\), multiplication by \(a_t\) reduces to \(f_t(j)\) times that same matching, whose value under \(v\in K_{d+1}\) is zero. Hence the image lies in \(K_d^{\neg i}\).

The signed trade theorem spans \(K_d^{\neg i}\) by degree-\(d\) trades \(\eta\) on \(d\) rows other than \(i\), using \(2d\) distinct labels. Take one such trade, with label set \(L\), and any desired coefficient vector \(\alpha\in\mathbb K^s\). By (RT-rank), choose coefficients \(c_j\), supported outside \(L\), satisfying

\[ \sum_jc_j=0,\qquad \sum_jf_t(j)c_j=\alpha_t\quad(1\le t\le s). \tag{RT-factor} \]

Put the row factor \(c\) in row \(i\) and tensor it with \(\eta\), setting every other top row-set array to zero and every lower moment to zero. Disjoint label support makes all cells compatible. The new row marginal vanishes because \(\sum c_j=0\); every other marginal is a zero marginal of \(\eta\). Thus \(c\otimes\eta\in K_{d+1}\), and its \(t\)-th conditioned array is exactly \(\alpha_t\eta\).

Choose a basis from the finite spanning family of trades, expand all desired defects in that common basis, and use a fixed linear right inverse for each evaluation matrix in (RT-factor). Summing the resulting lifts proves surjectivity and linearity. One may take at most \(s+1\) nonzero labels in each row factor, so each elementary lift uses at most \(2d+s+1\) labels. This is a support bound for each term, not a bound on the number of terms in an arbitrary trade expansion. \(\square\)

2. All bits of one pigeon satisfy the rank condition

Let \(N=2^\ell\), label the columns by binary words, and take \(f_t(j)\) to be their \(t\)-th bits. Over every field, a nonzero affine combination of these bits and one is nonzero on at least \(N/2\) labels. For a nonconstant combination, pair labels differing in a bit with nonzero coefficient: the two values differ, so at most one is zero. A nonzero constant has full support.

Consequently (RT-rank) holds for all \(\ell\) bits whenever

\[ N>4d. \tag{RT-bit-room} \]

There is no division by the number of labels and no restriction on characteristic. Affine combinations of the bits can also be handled through this basis, provided their requested defects satisfy the same linear relations modulo constants; conditioning a constant on \(K_{d+1}\) is zero.

The robust-rank hypothesis has content. If a predicate is the indicator of a single label \(j\), then its conditioned top array must vanish on every matching already using column \(j\) in another row. Such a target need not be in its image even when it avoids row \(i\). A trade with a nonzero coefficient on a matching using column \(j\) gives an explicit failure. Our sufficient bit-predicate condition avoids this column obstruction.

3. Correct a shared literal-MP fan while preserving its lower data

Take the Boolean row predicates above and formal source values \(B,C_1,\ldots,C_s\) with actual supplied module targets

\[ H_t=C_t-(1-a_t)B. \tag{RT-MP} \]

This is the recorded literal-antecedent MP/OR form. Let \(\lambda,\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_s\in\mathcal A_d\) be already prescribed old-moment components for \(B,C_1,\ldots,C_s\). They need not be normalized. Assume:

  1. For every old polynomial \(q\) of degree at most \(d-1\), \(\nu_t(q)=\lambda((1-a_t)q)\).
  2. For every degree-\(d\) matching \(T\) using row \(i\) at label \(j\), \(\nu_t(X_T)=(1-f_t(j))\lambda(X_T)\).

The second condition is a necessary boundary condition involving only known moments: on that matching the old product \(a_tX_T\) collapses to \(f_t(j)X_T\).

Working local correction corollary. Under (RT-rank), there is \(\widetilde\lambda\in\mathcal A_{d+1}\) extending \(\lambda\), with

\[ \nu_t(q)=\widetilde\lambda((1-a_t)q) \quad(\deg q\le d,\ 1\le t\le s). \tag{RT-corrected} \]

The choice can be linear in the entire fan's prescribed data. It therefore preserves any homogeneous constant-coefficient relation between parallel fans when that relation holds simultaneously among their \(\lambda\)'s and among each corresponding \(\nu_t\).

Proof. Choose a linear old extension section \(E_d\), available by the matching extension theorem, and form

\[ z_t=\lambda-\nu_t-M_{a_t}^{(d+1)}E_d\lambda. \]

These are old annihilators through \(d\). Condition 1 says their restrictions through \(d-1\) vanish, and condition 2 says their top moments on matchings using row \(i\) vanish. Thus \(z_t\in K_d^{\neg i}\). Apply the linear lift of (RT-map) to find a single \(v\in K_{d+1}\) with \(M_{a_t}v=z_t\) for every \(t\). Then \(\widetilde\lambda=E_d\lambda+v\) preserves all old prescribed moments and satisfies (RT-corrected). All operations are linear, proving the assertion for relations between parallel fans.

Original-cost scope. If the module \(H_t\) carries witness cost \(\nu^{\rm cost}_t\), only cofactors with \(\deg q+w(R)+\nu^{\rm cost}_t\le D\) are being enforced, for a fixed spectator-selector support \(R\) disjoint from the displayed values. The degree-\(d\) conclusion requires \(d+w(R)+\nu^{\rm cost}_t\le D\); its formal target also requires \(w(C_t)\le\nu^{\rm cost}_t\) and \(w(B)+1\le\nu^{\rm cost}_t\), guaranteeing the needed component windows. Keep any larger carried cost from decoding or source compilation. Normal-form collapse in condition 2 does not lower that original multiplier charge.

This is an isolated fan or compatible parallel collection with the stated data. It does not promise to preserve unrelated higher moments, arbitrary pure-selector constraints not covered by the parallel-data relation, or other mixed modules already involving the same new top component. Those are simultaneous compatibility questions, not consequences of linearity alone. The construction depends on the source data and does not contradict the no-universal-commuting-sections theorem.

4. Exact matching-moment controls

The new bounded checker uses four rows, sixteen labels, \(d=2\), all four bits of row zero, and primes 2, 3 and 5. Three signed trades on different pairs of other rows generate nonzero target defects. Exact evaluation matrices supply zero-sum row factors, and a common higher trade corrects all four predicates. A point-matching functional supplies the initial \(B\) data; the prescribed \(C_t\) data contain the corresponding nontrivial zero-marginal adjustments.

Per field, all 3,860 old row-marginal checks, 6,020 contraction checks and 6,020 MP equations passed. The selected right inverse also passed linearity checks. Omitting the correction produces 24 MP failures. A singleton-label predicate whose support was deleted fails the evaluation-rank test; a saved matching using that label in another row certifies the genuine column obstruction. The case enumerates 14,945 matching monomials through degree three, not all assignments.

Complete sparse moments, row factors and controls and reproduction details are preserved. These are local formal moment checks, not a complete genuine-ENS source design or a numerical proof of the general theorem. One initial formatting warning was fixed before the accepted build.

5. Contribution and the next overlap

For general-step, there is now a source-dependent local correction covering all bit predicates of one pigeon row, with arbitrary compatible lower component data and no new old-degree loss beyond the single extension step. It uses the actual matching label geometry that generic PC hardness did not provide. It does not solve joint multirow compatibility or a full weighted source layer.

Next bounded test. Examine simultaneous correction for two different pigeon rows. The candidate general mechanism is a compatible multirow lifting theorem, not an accumulation of special degrees. Derive the necessary shared-contraction conditions and decide whether they suffice under an explicit robust-evaluation/deleted-label budget. Stop at a proof or a counterexample; carrying two independently chosen one-row corrections is not sufficient.

I estimate about 20% that the matching-correction line yields further useful progress on the main obligation. The current result is a local tool, not an end-to-end lower bound or a publication claim.
