20 September 2026 — Two-row correction is controlled by a product code

Working criterion and all-field proof; explicit failed-compatibility test and bounded exact checks. Higher-degree and complete-source compatibility remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For route item general-step, test whether the one-row correction theorem composes across two pigeon rows. The proposed mechanism is simultaneous lifting of compatible conditioning defects, not two independent choices. The bounded endpoint is an exact degree-one criterion plus a proof or counterexample to sufficiency of the obvious commuting-contraction equations. That test exposes a diagonal obstruction on eight labels, and an elementary product-code argument removes it on full bit cubes with at least four bits.

1. Exact criterion for degree one to two

Let \(\Omega\) have \(N\ge3\) labels and let \(\mathbb K\) be any field. Write \(U=\{v\in\mathbb K^\Omega:\sum_jv_j=0\}\). Choose predicates \(f_1,\ldots,f_s\) and \(g_1,\ldots,g_t\), with \(1,f_1,\ldots,f_s\) and \(1,g_1,\ldots,g_t\) each linearly independent as functions on \(\Omega\). The maps

\[ F:U\to\mathbb K^s,\quad F(v)_a=\sum_j f_a(j)v_j, \qquad G:U\to\mathbb K^t,\quad G(v)_b=\sum_jg_b(j)v_j \]

are surjective. Let \(C_F=\ker F\subset U\) and \(C_G=\ker G\subset U\), equivalently the kernels of the corresponding evaluation matrices including the constant row. Define the coordinatewise product-code space

\[ S=C_F*C_G=\operatorname{span}\{u\circ v:u\in C_F,\ v\in C_G\}\subseteq\mathbb K^\Omega. \]

For a fixed ordered pair of pigeon rows, a degree-two top matching trade is a matrix \(A=(A_{kl})\) with zero row sums, zero column sums and zero diagonal. The last condition enforces distinct columns for the two rows. Its two conditioning outputs are

\[ z_a(l)=\sum_k f_a(k)A_{kl},\qquad w_b(k)=\sum_l g_b(l)A_{kl}. \tag{TC-output} \]

Necessary conditions on the targets are \(z\in\mathbb K^s\otimes U\), \(w\in U\otimes\mathbb K^t\), and

\[ (\mathrm{id}\otimes G)z=(F\otimes\mathrm{id})w=:c, \quad\text{or}\quad \sum_l g_b(l)z_a(l)=\sum_k f_a(k)w_b(k). \tag{TC-compatible} \]

Working criterion. Choose any zero-row/column-sum matrix \(A_0\in U\otimes U\) realizing the compatible targets while allowing a diagonal. A matching-trade lift exists if and only if \(\operatorname{diag}A_0\in S\). Every compatible target lifts if and only if \(S=\mathbb K^\Omega\). The codimension of the actual conditioning image in the space of compatible targets is exactly \(N-\dim S\).

Proof. Fix linear right inverses \(r_F,r_G\) of \(F,G\). Every compatible pair has an unrestricted realization

\[ A_0=(r_F\otimes\mathrm{id})z+(\mathrm{id}\otimes r_G)w-(r_F\otimes r_G)c. \tag{TC-unrestricted} \]

Applying either conditioning map verifies the stated outputs. Two such realizations differ by the joint kernel \(C_F\otimes C_G\): decompose each copy of \(U\) as its evaluation kernel plus the image of its chosen right inverse, and check the four tensor summands. The diagonal image of that kernel is precisely \(S\). Thus a correction in the kernel deletes the diagonal exactly when the displayed criterion holds, independently of the chosen unrestricted realization.

Finally \(\operatorname{diag}:U\otimes U\to\mathbb K^\Omega\) is onto. For each \(j\), choose distinct \(a,b\ne j\); the matrix \((e_j-e_a)\otimes(e_j-e_b)\) has diagonal \(e_j\). Therefore the map from compatible targets to \(\mathbb K^\Omega/S\), sending a target to \([\operatorname{diag}A_0]\), is well defined and onto, with kernel exactly the matching image. This proves universality and the codimension formula. The compatible-target dimension is \(s(N-1)+t(N-1)-st\): the compatibility map to \(\mathbb K^s\otimes\mathbb K^t\) is onto. \(\square\)

This is an elementary tensor-kernel/diagonal argument. No prior-art or publication novelty claim is made. It is exact for one pair of rows at old degree one, not a theorem about arbitrary higher-degree source components.

2. Obvious compatibility and one-row robustness do not suffice

Take \(\Omega=\{0,1\}^3\), and use the three bit predicates on both rows, over any field. The one-row theorem's rank hypothesis for \(d=1\) holds: any nonzero affine bit function is nonzero on at least four labels, since a nonzero bit coefficient forces a nonzero value on at least one member of each pair along that coordinate; a nonzero constant is nonzero everywhere. Deleting any two labels cannot create an affine dependence.

Nevertheless prescribe \(w_1=w_2=w_3=0\), \(z_2=z_3=0\), and

\[ z_1(v_1,v_2,v_3)= \begin{cases}(-1)^{v_2+v_3},&v_1=1,\\0,&v_1=0.\end{cases} \tag{TC-bad-target} \]

The vector \(z_1\) is a signed square. Its total sum and all three bit moments are zero, over every field, including characteristic two. Hence (TC-compatible) holds. Each single-row target family separately has a lift by the preceding row theorem.

No common lift exists. Define the signed diagonal function

\[ P(u,v)=\prod_{a=1}^3(1-u_a-v_a). \]

It vanishes for distinct bit labels and equals \((-1)^{|u|}\) on the diagonal. Its expansion is

\[ P(u,v)=A(u)+B(v)+\sum_a u_a\alpha_a(v)+\sum_b\beta_b(u)v_b, \] \[ A(u)=u_1u_2+u_1u_3+u_2u_3-u_1u_2u_3,\quad B(v)=\prod_a(1-v_a), \] \[ \alpha_a(v)=-\prod_{b\ne a}(1-v_b),\qquad \beta_b(u)=-\prod_{a\ne b}u_a. \tag{TC-diagonal-dual} \]

Pair this identity with a hypothetical lift matrix. The left side is zero because the matrix has no diagonal; the pure-row terms vanish by the zero marginals. Thus every actual image satisfies

\[ \sum_a\langle\alpha_a,z_a\rangle+\sum_b\langle\beta_b,w_b\rangle=0. \]

For (TC-bad-target) the left side is \(-1\): only \(v=(1,0,0)\) contributes. This is nonzero in every field. The contradiction proves the obstruction without finite enumeration. It is an application of the previously studied first binary diagonal/collision layer, with this explicit signed witness valid also in odd characteristic; it is not a new discovery of the binary equality obstruction or an odd-characteristic extension of that full rigidity lemma.

Source interpretation and scope. With zero prescribed degree-one \(B\) component, use \(C_a=-z_a\) for a literal-MP fan at the first row and zero \(C\) components at the second row. The first defects are supported on the second row, and the second defects vanish. Lower and distinguished-row boundary conditions hold, as do the cross-contraction equations. Both fans separately admit the one-row correction, but no shared degree-two \(B\) extension satisfies both. These are local unnormalized moment data; this is neither a complete ENS source nor an asymptotic PHP refutation. Additional rows with zero target data cannot change the conflicting two-row matrix. A stronger sufficiently-large-board hypothesis is not refuted.

3. Full bit cubes with at least four bits satisfy the criterion

Corollary, over every field. For \(\Omega=\{0,1\}^\ell\), \(\ell\ge4\), and all \(\ell\) bit predicates on both distinguished rows, every target satisfying (TC-compatible) has a degree-two top matching lift.

Proof. Let \(C\) annihilate the constant and all bit evaluations. At each label \(j\), take the signed square \(c_j\) on coordinate directions 1 and 2 and the signed square \(d_j\) on directions 3 and 4. Both have coefficients \((1,-1,-1,1)\), with coefficient one at \(j\). Each belongs to \(C\): a bit is constant or depends on only one of the two square directions, and summing the other direction cancels it. The supports of the two squares meet only at \(j\), so \(c_j\circ d_j=e_j\). Consequently \(C*C=\mathbb K^\Omega\), and the criterion applies. The same proof works for every \(\ell\ge4\), not just the tested sixteen-label board. \(\square\)

The degree bookkeeping here is unary matching degree \(1\to2\). The bit predicates are affine unary row polynomials; the signed-square construction does not increase this degree. Neither this argument nor its finite check bounds coefficients or total certificate size, nor does it give compatibility with higher old moments or other source modules.

4. Exact checks and retained evidence

The bounded C++ checker builds the evaluation kernels, their coordinatewise products, the off-diagonal marginal system and both conditioning maps over \(\mathbb F_2,\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\). On eight labels the compatible-target dimension is 33, the actual image dimension is 32, and the product-code rank is 7. On sixteen labels these dimensions are 104, 104 and 16. In every case the measured image deficit equals \(N-\dim(C*C)\).

The full eight-label target and dual are saved; the dual annihilates every source column but evaluates to \(-1\) on the requested right side, and the augmented system's rank increases by one. For sixteen labels all coordinate-unit product witnesses are saved and verified. The matrices have at most 240 unknowns and 160 equation rows; there is no large assignment search. Complete certificates and reproduction details are retained. The initial compile rejected formatting warnings, fixed before the accepted run; they are not failed mathematical tests.

5. Contribution and higher-degree obligation

For general-step, the naive claim that one-row robustness plus commuting contractions suffices is false, but the degree-one obstruction has an exact quotient description and disappears on larger full bit cubes. The next obligation is to lift compatible two-row defects at arbitrary old degree \(d\), with a deleted-label budget that preserves zero marginals in every other row. Applying the degree-one matrix criterion separately after fixing the other labels need not preserve those marginals. The missing general claim must address that coherence explicitly; more checks at fixed bit counts would not do so.

A natural sufficient condition to test is robust coordinatewise-product spanning for the evaluation kernels after every relevant label deletion, combined with trade generation of the coupled targets. Establish or refute that coupled spanning implication before spending effort on a source-layer recurrence. Even a positive two-row theorem would still leave arbitrary source-module overlap and total degree costs to prove.

20 September 2026 — Coded trades give a simultaneous multirow correction theorem

Working all-field proofs and an exact full-image check beyond degree one. Complete source compatibility and the Frege lower bound remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and endpoint. The degree-one criterion left a coherence problem: separate matrix completions after fixing other labels need not preserve their marginals. For general-step, the bounded task is to prove or refute a trade-spanning mechanism that preserves all these marginals. A generalization of ordinary signed-trade spanning supplies such a mechanism. It yields joint correction for arbitrarily many designated rows, at every old degree in a robust evaluation range. It does not establish that the complete proof source supplies the required compatible data.

1. Disjoint codeword tensors span the constrained matching arrays

Let \(R\) be a set of \(r\ge1\) rows and \(\Omega\) a finite label set. For each \(i\in R\), let \(E_i\) be a \(q_i\)-by-\(|\Omega|\) matrix over any field \(\mathbb K\), with \(q_i\ge1\). Define

\[ L_R=\sum_{i\in R}(q_i+1)-1. \]

Assume every \(E_i\) retains row rank \(q_i\) after deletion of any at most \(L_R\) label columns. Let \(Z_R(E)\) be the arrays \(z\) on injections \(R\hookrightarrow\Omega\) with zero \(E_i\)-weighted marginal in every row: for every injection \(T\) of the other rows,

\[ \sum_{j\notin\operatorname{col}T}E_i(:,j)\,z(T+(i,j))=0. \tag{CT-marginal} \]

Working theorem. Every such array is a linear combination of pure tensors \(\bigotimes_{i\in R}c_i\), where \(c_i\in\ker E_i\), \(|\operatorname{supp}c_i|\le q_i+1\), and the row supports are pairwise disjoint. Conversely, these tensors belong to \(Z_R(E)\). In particular, each spanning tensor uses at most \(\sum_i(q_i+1)\) labels.

Proof by row induction. For one row, fix a basis of \(q_i\) evaluation columns. The vectors \(e_j\) minus their representations on that basis span \(\ker E_i\) and use at most \(q_i+1\) labels. Tensor products with disjoint supports clearly satisfy (CT-marginal).

For the induction step choose a row \(i_0\) of minimum \(q_i\), write \(q_0=q_{i_0}\), and choose a set \(B\) of \(q_0\) labels on which \(E_{i_0}\) is invertible. First remove all labels of \(B\) from the array, one label at a time. Suppose the set \(H\subset B\) has already been removed, and let \(b\in B\setminus H\) be next. For each row \(i\), the slice at \((i,b)\) is a constrained array on the other rows and label set \(\Omega\setminus(H\cup\{b\})\). The induction hypothesis applies: its own deletion allowance is

\[ L_{R\setminus\{i\}}=\sum_{j\ne i}(q_j+1)-1, \]

and \(|H|+1+L_{R\setminus\{i\}}\le q_0+L_{R\setminus\{i\}}\le L_R\). Hence write the slice as a sum of disjoint codeword tensors \(\eta\), each using at most \(\sum_{j\ne i}(q_j+1)\) labels. For each one, find a row-\(i\) codeword \(c\) whose coefficient at \(b\) is one and whose other support avoids \(H\cup\{b\}\cup\operatorname{supp}\eta\). This is possible because the excluded label count is at most

\[ |H|+1+\sum_{j\ne i}(q_j+1) \le q_0+\sum_{j\ne i}(q_j+1)\le L_R, \]

using \(q_0\le q_i\). Select an evaluation basis outside that excluded set and represent \(E_i(:,b)\) on it. The vector \(e_b\) minus this representation is the required codeword, with support at most \(q_i+1\). Subtract \(c\otimes\eta\) to cancel the slice. This introduces no \(b\) in another row and no label of \(H\). Repeating over the rows removes \(b\) everywhere; repeating over \(B\) leaves a constrained array \(z'\) avoiding all of \(B\).

Now slice \(z'\) at row \(i_0\) having label \(j\notin B\), giving \(z'_j\) on the other rows and labels outside \(B\cup\{j\}\). Row induction applies again, since

\[ q_0+1+L_{R\setminus\{i_0\}}=L_R. \]

Let \(h_j=E_{i_0}|_B^{-1}E_{i_0}(:,j)\), interpreted as a vector supported on \(B\). Then \(e_j-h_j\in\ker E_{i_0}\). Extend all slices by zero to a common array space. The row-\(i_0\) marginal identity gives \(\sum_{j\notin B}E_{i_0}(:,j)z'_j=0\), so \(\sum_j h_j\otimes z'_j=0\), and therefore

\[ z'=\sum_{j\notin B}(e_j-h_j)\otimes z'_j. \]

Each trade expansion of \(z'_j\) avoids \(B\cup\{j\}\), so every displayed tensor expands into the required disjoint codeword tensors. Together with the subtracted tensors, this proves the theorem. There is no division by a characteristic-dependent integer: only invertible evaluation minors are used. \(\square\)

Taking all \(E_i=(1,\ldots,1)\) gives \(q_i=1\), \(L_R=2r-1\), and precisely the earlier sufficient board size \(N\ge2r\). This is a generalization of that proof, not an assertion that arbitrary arrays are tensor products or that their trade expansions are short.

2. Pairwise-compatible predicate defects have a common lift

Return to a functional matching board with \(m\ge d+1\) rows, \(N\ge2d+1\) labels, and \(d\ge1\), over \(\mathbb K\). Let \(\mathcal A_t\) be its ordinary degree-\(t\) annihilator and \(K_t=\ker(\mathcal A_t\to\mathcal A_{t-1})\); put \(K_0=\mathcal A_0\). For a distinguished row \(i\), \(K_d^{\neg i}\) means the top arrays vanish on every row set using \(i\).

Choose \(k\ge1\) distinct rows \(I\), with \(s_i\) predicates \(f_{i,a}:\Omega\to\mathbb K\) on each, where \(1\le s_i\le s\). Write \(a_{i,a}=\sum_jf_{i,a}(j)X_{ij}\), and \(M_{i,a}\) for conditioning by this polynomial at the relevant degree. Set

\[ B=2d+s\min(d,k-1). \tag{CT-budget} \]

Assume every evaluation family \(1,f_{i,1},\ldots,f_{i,s_i}\) remains linearly independent after deletion of any at most \(B\) labels.

Working theorem. A tuple \(z_{i,a}\in K_d^{\neg i}\) has a common lift \(v\in K_{d+1}\) with \(M_{i,a}v=z_{i,a}\) if and only if, for every pair of distinct distinguished rows and their predicates,

\[ M_{j,b}z_{i,a}=M_{i,a}z_{j,b}\quad\text{in }K_{d-1}. \tag{CT-closed} \]

The joint map onto this compatible-target space has a linear right inverse. There is no factor depending on \(m\) in (CT-budget). Neither a short trade expansion nor compatibility with arbitrary additional source modules is asserted.

Necessity. Conditioning commutes, giving (CT-closed). A top trade conditioned at row \(i\) has zero lower moments, and it vanishes on degree-\(d\) matchings already using row \(i\): multiplication reduces to a scalar times a degree-\(d\) moment, which is zero. Thus the stated target space is necessary as well.

Sufficiency. Process the distinguished rows in any fixed order, initially with \(v=0\). Suppose the previous rows \(J\subset I\) are already correct and the next row is \(i\). For each predicate at \(i\), form the residual

\[ r_a=z_{i,a}-M_{i,a}v\in K_d^{\neg i}. \]

For every previous \(j,b\), commutation and (CT-closed) give

\[ M_{j,b}r_a=M_{j,b}z_{i,a}-M_{i,a}M_{j,b}v =M_{i,a}z_{j,b}-M_{i,a}z_{j,b}=0. \]

Consider the array of \(r_a\) on one \(d\)-row set \(S\) avoiding \(i\). Its ordinary row marginals vanish. For each \(j\in S\cap J\), all its predicate-weighted marginals also vanish. Apply the coded-trade theorem with \(q_j=s_j+1\) on these rows and \(q_j=1\) on the others. The required deletion allowance and the support size of each resulting tensor are, respectively,

\[ L_S=2d+\sum_{j\in S\cap J}s_j-1\le B-1, \qquad L_S+1\le B. \]

The robust hypotheses supply the nonconstant evaluation ranks; the constant rows retain rank because the same hypotheses imply \(N>B\). Expand all the residual predicates on \(S\) in one common basis selected from these disjoint tensors. For a basis tensor \(\eta\), let \(\alpha_a\) be its coefficient in residual \(r_a\). On labels outside its support, solve

\[ \sum_l c_l=0,\qquad\sum_l f_{i,a}(l)c_l=\alpha_a \quad(1\le a\le s_i). \]

The evaluation matrix has full row rank there, because at most \(B\) labels were removed. The tensor \(c\otimes\eta\), on row set \(S\cup\{i\}\), is a top matching trade. Its new-row contractions give \(\alpha_a\eta\). Its previous-row contractions vanish: if a previous row is absent, there is no relevant top row set; if present, the corresponding codeword factor annihilates its predicates. Thus summing these tensors over the common basis and all row sets corrects the whole new row without disturbing any previous row. Iteration gives \(v\).

Fix each finite trade basis and each linear right inverse of an evaluation matrix in advance. Residual formation, basis expansion and lifting are then linear at every stage, so the construction gives a linear right inverse on the compatible-target space. This is a source-data-dependent correction of top moments, not a universal old extension section commuting with every cell; the earlier obstruction is untouched. \(\square\)

3. Uniform bit-predicate range

Corollary, over every field. On the full \(\ell\)-bit label set, \(N=2^\ell\), take all bits on each of \(k\) designated pigeon rows. Pairwise-compatible top defects lift jointly whenever

\[ N>4d+2\ell\min(d,k-1). \tag{CT-bits} \]

In particular, \(N>2d(\ell+2)\) suffices uniformly for any number of designated rows. A nonzero affine bit function is nonzero on at least \(N/2\) labels, over every field, by pairing along a coordinate with nonzero coefficient (a nonzero constant has full support). Thus deleting fewer than \(N/2\) labels preserves evaluation rank. Condition (CT-bits) is exactly \(B<N/2\) in the theorem.

For one designated row this recovers the earlier \(N>4d\) bound. For two it gives \(N>4d+2\ell\). At \(d=1\), \(\ell\ge4\) satisfies this condition and agrees with the degree-one repair. The eight-label counterexample fails the stronger budget, so it remains a necessary warning against omitting the robustness hypothesis.

The extension consumes one unary old degree, \(d\to d+1\). It is not a conversion from source weight to old degree and cannot reset any original module cost. The bit-count factor occurs in the sufficient label room, not in the degree of the correction. No bound on the number of constructed terms follows.

4. Full-image verification beyond the first degree

The new exact checker uses three rows, sixteen labels, old degree two to three, and one predicate \(j\mapsto j\bmod2\) on each row. Here \(s=1,k=3,B=6\), while the minimum nonzero affine-predicate support is eight. Thus the theorem's hypotheses hold. Unlike constructing outputs from a prechosen lift, the check compares the entire actual image with the entire space satisfying the stated compatibility equations.

The source has 3,360 injective triples. Its zero-marginal matrix has rank 673. Adjoining all three predicate-contraction maps gives rank 1,256, so the actual image has dimension 583. The 720 target coordinates have ordinary zero-marginal and pairwise-contraction constraints of rank 137, also giving dimension 583. These values agree over \(\mathbb F_2,\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5\). The largest matrix is 1,440 by 3,360; exact compiled elimination stays far below the resource limits. All ranks and pivot lists and deterministic matrix definitions/reproduction are retained.

The previous eight-label target and dual remain the nonvacuous failed-hypothesis control; they were not rerun merely for this entry. The present finite check corroborates the higher-degree implication but does not prove its generality or assess source-layer consistency.

5. What changed on the main route

For general-step, the missing higher-degree coherence implication for this family of row-predicate corrections is now supplied, under an explicit robust deletion budget. The proof preserves other-row marginals by construction and handles any number of designated rows. The remaining issue is no longer how to combine already-compatible bit defects; it is whether the actual complete, costed source allows such defects to be chosen compatibly with every other component equation.

Next bounded step. Apply the theorem to a shared multirow literal-MP fan with prescribed component data, deriving the exact pairwise condition and its original degree cost. Then test whether that condition is forced by the source equations at the available cutoff or is a genuinely new consistency obligation. Stop at a precise source implication or obstruction before building a layer recurrence. OR, MOD, shared selector products and arbitrary mixed components remain outside the theorem's conclusion.

I estimate about 25% that the matching-correction line produces a further useful advance on the main goal. The coded spanning theorem merits independent review and a targeted prior-art comparison; no novelty or publication readiness is claimed. The Frege lower bound itself is still open.

Process assessment. Generalizing the existing row-induction proof resolved the coherence issue before further fixed-size examples were tried; the single full-image calculation then tested the actual sufficiency claim, so no additional framework machinery was needed.

20 September 2026 — A shared MP fan has an exact compatibility boundary

Working local projection theorem and an explicit large-board obstruction to automatic compatibility. No complete-source design is constructed. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question. For general-step, the new correction operator requires pairwise-compatible defects. Does a genuine-shaped literal-MP fan supply that condition at its original cost, or does it add a new consistency obligation? The bounded endpoint is an exact fan-projection statement and a direct test of whether already satisfied lower equations imply its hypotheses. The answer distinguishes a legal same-budget source consequence from a consequence already enforced by lower old-degree data.

1. Exact projection of a shared literal-MP fan

Use the field, matching board, degree \(d\), designated rows, predicates \(a_{i,a}\), and robust deletion budget of the joint lifting theorem. Let \(\alpha\) index a row-predicate pair and write \(i(\alpha)\) for its row. Formal component names \(B,C_\alpha\) are related by the actual module targets

\[ H_\alpha=C_\alpha-(1-a_\alpha)B. \tag{FC-module} \]

Prescribe ordinary old annihilators \(\lambda,\nu_\alpha\in\mathcal A_d\) for those components. They need not be normalized. The following conditions characterize the existence of \(\widetilde\lambda\in\mathcal A_{d+1}\) extending \(\lambda\) and satisfying \(\nu_\alpha(q)=\widetilde\lambda((1-a_\alpha)q)\) for every \(\deg q\le d\):

  1. Lower fan equations: \(\nu_\alpha(q)=\lambda((1-a_\alpha)q)\) for \(\deg q\le d-1\).
  2. Same-row boundary: if a degree-\(d\) matching \(T\) uses row \(i(\alpha)\) at label \(j\), then \(\nu_\alpha(X_T)=(1-f_\alpha(j))\lambda(X_T)\).
  3. Cross-row closure: for distinct distinguished rows,
    \[ M_\beta(\lambda-\nu_\alpha)=M_\alpha(\lambda-\nu_\beta) \quad\text{through old degree }d-1. \tag{FC-closed} \]

Working corollary. Under the robust rank hypotheses, these conditions are necessary and sufficient. A lift can be chosen linearly in the complete prescribed fan data. Thus this is an exact projection description for this local family, rather than just a list of necessary checks.

Proof. Necessity of the first two conditions follows from restriction and the matching identity \(a_\alpha X_T=f_\alpha(j)X_T\) on a row already used. If a lift exists, \(\lambda-\nu_\alpha=M_\alpha\widetilde\lambda\), so commuting conditioning gives the third condition.

Conversely choose a fixed linear old extension section \(E_d\), justified by old matching extension, and put

\[ z_\alpha=\lambda-\nu_\alpha-M_\alpha E_d\lambda. \]

The first two conditions put \(z_\alpha\) in \(K_d^{\neg i(\alpha)}\). Commutation cancels the section terms in the cross defect:

\[ M_\beta z_\alpha-M_\alpha z_\beta =M_\beta(\lambda-\nu_\alpha)-M_\alpha(\lambda-\nu_\beta)=0. \]

The joint lifting theorem supplies \(v\in K_{d+1}\) with \(M_\alpha v=z_\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\). Then \(\widetilde\lambda=E_d\lambda+v\) has the required properties. Fixed linear choices prove the linearity assertion. It preserves a homogeneous constant-coefficient relation between parallel complete fan tuples if that relation holds in every corresponding prescribed component; it does not preserve arbitrary unrelated equations merely because it is linear. \(\square\)

2. The pair obstruction is a legal same-budget source consequence

The closure condition is independent of the arbitrary old section. Algebraically it is precisely the vanishing, on the known component data, of

\[ K_{\alpha\beta}=a_\beta(B-C_\alpha)-a_\alpha(B-C_\beta) =a_\alpha H_\beta-a_\beta H_\alpha. \tag{FC-syzygy} \]

The terms \(a_\alpha a_\beta B\) cancel exactly. Hence multiplying this relation by an old \(q\) of degree at most \(d-1\) only queries \(\lambda,\nu_\alpha,\nu_\beta\) through degree \(d\), although its expression in the original fan generators uses multipliers of degree at most \(d\). Same-row pairs need no separate closure hypothesis: the row-boundary equations already make their weighted products symmetric.

Let \(\rho_\alpha\) be the original carried witness cost of \(H_\alpha\), and let a fixed spectator selector support \(R\) be disjoint from the displayed component names. Assume

\[ w(C_\alpha)\le\rho_\alpha,\quad w(B)+1\le\rho_\alpha, \qquad d+w(R)+\rho_\alpha\le D \quad\text{for every }\alpha. \]

Then (FC-syzygy) has a witness cost at most \(1+\max(\rho_\alpha,\rho_\beta)\), and a cofactor of degree \(d-1\) stays within

\[ (d-1)+w(R)+1+\max(\rho_\alpha,\rho_\beta)\le D. \]

Thus checking the projected pair relation introduces no degree beyond the already required degree-\(d\) fan equations. The same-row boundary is the old normal form of a legal \(X_TH_\alpha\); its charge is still \(d+w(R)+\rho_\alpha\). Keep any larger source/decoding cost carried by the original module. Cancellation does not authorize replacing it by the smaller degree of the displayed residual.

Crucial distinction. Pair closure is forced by the full degree-\(d\) fan constraints, because it is their linear combination. It is not necessarily forced by only the fan equations with multipliers through degree \(d-1\). The top degree-\(d\) equations are exactly those whose extension is being attempted. Treating their projected consequence as already satisfied would assume part of the desired extension.

3. The distinction persists on arbitrarily large robust boards

Here is an explicit obstruction over every field with no failure of the robust-rank hypothesis. Fix \(d\ge1\), a sufficiently large full bit cube \(N=2^\ell>4d+2\ell\), and \(m=d+1\) rows, including distinct rows \(i,j\). Use all bits on those two rows. Choose any complete injection \(P\) and let \(\mu_0\) be evaluation at \(P\) through degree \(d+1\). Put \(\lambda=\mu_0|_{\le d}\) and initially \(\nu_\alpha^0(q)=\mu_0((1-a_\alpha)q)\). This unperturbed fan is fully consistent and has \(\lambda(1)=1\).

Choose one bit predicate \(a\) on row \(i\), and one bit predicate \(b\) on row \(j\). Choose labels \(u,v\) on which \(b\) takes values zero and one, respectively. On the other \(d-1\) rows choose pairwise disjoint two-label differences, all disjoint from \(u,v\), and let their tensor be \(\eta\). For \(d=1\), take the empty tensor \(\eta=1\). The degree-\(d\) trade

\[ z=(e_u-e_v)_{j}\otimes\eta \]

has zero lower moments, is supported on row sets avoiding \(i\), and satisfies \(M_bz=-\eta\ne0\). Change only \(\nu_a\), setting \(\nu_a=\nu_a^0-z\); leave every other \(\nu_\alpha=\nu_\alpha^0\). All are still old annihilators through \(d\).

All lower fan equations remain true because \(z\) has zero moments through \(d-1\). All same-row boundary equations remain true because the sole perturbation avoids row \(i\). Each distinguished row's whole fan separately admits a lift by the one-row theorem. However the cross relation for \(a,b\) now has defect \(-\eta\), which is nonzero. No common higher \(B\) component exists, by necessity in the projection theorem. The available labels suffice for the disjoint trade since the displayed room condition is much stronger than \(N\ge2d\).

This is a symbolic, normalized-component example valid for arbitrarily large label sets and all fields, not a numerical search or a claim about a complete proof source. It can also be added as a top-trade perturbation to any available consistent fan on a larger matching board. Unlike the earlier eight-label example, this one deliberately violates cross closure while satisfying the robust rank budget; it tests the distinct, false assertion that lower fan equations imply closure automatically.

4. Route assessment and next decision

For general-step, the shared literal-MP fan can now be eliminated exactly at one old-degree boundary: its only extra conditions, beyond old annihilation and lower fan equations, are the stated row boundaries and pair relations. Those relations have explicit witnesses at the original target budget. This converts an implicit lifting issue into a concrete lower-component consistency obligation. It does not prove that all such obligations can be met simultaneously across the complete source.

The next step is a route review centered on that remaining issue: can projected boundary/pair relations be organized into a bounded-cost closure invariant for actual coupled source components, or do already-known mixed-interface obstructions defeat that invariant? State the invariant before iterating more local fan lemmas, and test the known counterexamples and original cost accumulation. OR/MOD products and overlapping spectator supports cannot be treated as independent parallel fans.

I estimate about 25% that the matching-correction line yields further useful progress on the main goal. The linear operator is stronger now, but source consistency remains the decisive unproved implication; this cycle does not move that implication to the proved column.

Process assessment. The direct source identity and a symbolic trade perturbation answered the cutoff question without another computation or literature lookup; the next review will test a general invariant before adding more local cases, so no framework change is needed.

20 September 2026 — Review the source closure, then test a wide parity

Route review and a conditional mixed-product closure lemma. Full-source feasibility and its cost recurrence remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

1. General claim, required endpoint and current gap

For general-step, the intended general claim is that the actual complete costed proof source admits jointly compatible matching/selector components below a separated old-base degree barrier. A normalized ordinary NS annihilator suffices. Arbitrary extension of every prescribed mixed component, raw augmented PC stability and same-degree preservation of every retained quotient are stronger statements and are not the endpoint.

The coded trade basis and joint row-predicate lift prove a genuine higher-degree coherence result: once top row-predicate defects avoid their own rows and have matching cross contractions, one common correction exists in the robust label range. The fan projection makes those conditions explicit for a source-shaped shared fan. What the goal still needs is a way to choose the entire coupled source data so those conditions, other modules and the normalization all hold. Repeated application of a conditional lift does not choose such data.

Falsification attempts. The large-board perturbation disproves automatic cross closure from lower fan equations alone. The mixed-helper counterexample independently rules out freely preserving arbitrary retained whole-product data at the same degree; it does not refute source-dependent choices with a buffer. The ordering source prevents replacing matching geometry by generic old PC hardness. None of these is a negative verdict on the whole PHP program.

2. Mixed products can force pair closure in an interior window

There is a concrete positive test of the stronger source-aware hypothesis. Let \(H_\alpha=C_\alpha-(1-a_\alpha)B\) have original witness cost \(\rho_\alpha\). Suppose the system also supplies the pure-selector absorption relation

\[ A_\alpha=BC_\alpha-C_\alpha \]

at cost \(\sigma_\alpha\). This must be supplied or proved. In the genuine ENS-parent case where \(1-B\) is literally one of the inputs of the block with whole value \(C_\alpha\), it is just the negative of that companion, with original cost \(w(B)+w(C_\alpha)\). The claim does not infer that syntactic parent-input condition for arbitrary renamed or flattened interfaces.

The exact diamond relation is

\[ J_{\alpha\beta}=C_\alpha C_\beta-(1-a_\beta)C_\alpha =C_\alpha H_\beta+(1-a_\beta)A_\alpha. \tag{DC-identity} \]

It has a carried witness cost at most \(\max(w(C_\alpha)+\rho_\beta,1+\sigma_\alpha)\). No Booleanity or division is hidden in this identity.

Conditional closure lemma. Fix a spectator support \(R\) disjoint from the displayed names. Suppose the known component data include \(\lambda\) for \(B\), \(\nu_\alpha\) for \(C_\alpha\), and \(\mu_\alpha\) for \(BC_\alpha\) through old degree \(d\), and \(\xi_{\alpha\beta}\) for \(C_\alpha C_\beta\) through \(d-1\). Suppose they satisfy the lower fan equations, the absorption equations \(\mu_\alpha=\nu_\alpha\) through \(d\), and the lower fan equations with spectator \(C_\alpha\):

\[ \xi_{\alpha\beta}(q)=\mu_\alpha((1-a_\beta)q) \quad(\deg q\le d-1). \]

Then all the fan cross-closure equations hold through \(d-1\). Indeed, these equations give \(M_\beta\nu_\alpha=\nu_\alpha-\xi_{\alpha\beta}\). The same mixed component appears in the reverse order. Together with \(M_\beta\lambda=\lambda-\nu_\beta\) from the lower fan equation,

\[ M_\beta(\lambda-\nu_\alpha) =\lambda-\nu_\beta-\nu_\alpha+\xi_{\alpha\beta} =M_\alpha(\lambda-\nu_\beta). \]

All quantities here are known components at the indicated windows. This is not an assumption of an already-extended \(B\) component.

Original-cost audit. These premises are legal at cutoff \(D\) when, for all relevant pairs,

\[ d+w(R)+\sigma_\alpha\le D,\qquad (d-1)+w(R)+w(C_\alpha)+\rho_\beta\le D, \]

together with the ordinary lower-fan and component-window requirements. In the coherent source with \(w(B),w(C_\alpha)\le L\), \(\rho_\alpha=3L\), supplied absorption cost at most \(2L\), and active cutoff \(E=D-L\), the sufficient common window is

\[ d+w(R)\le D-4L+1. \tag{DC-window} \]

All queried components then fit inside \(E\). In contrast, the new degree-\(d\) fan equations themselves can be legal up to \(d+w(R)\le D-3L\). Thus this proof of automatic mixed-data closure uses an interior reserve of \(L-1\) old degrees. For \(L=1\) this particular gap disappears; for larger \(L\) it must be charged. This is the cost of this argument, not a lower bound proving that every closure method must lose that amount.

Absorption is essential to the argument: it turns the component \(BC_\alpha\) in the spectator equation into the prescribed \(C_\alpha\) component. It is a pure-selector relation, so its assumed degree-\(d\) equations query no unknown degree-\(d+1\) old moment. Without a supplied absorption witness, deriving it from the fan and Booleanity can cost more and may query the very moments being extended; it cannot be silently treated as a prior constraint.

3. Why this is not yet an iterable source invariant

The mixed diamond lemma explains how a complete source may supply closure that an isolated fan lacks. It still assumes compatible mixed components and absorption at their required windows, leaves the fan's same-row boundary conditions to be enforced, and does not cover arbitrary OR/MOD overlaps or all changing spectator supports. To iterate it, one must prove a joint invariant specifying which components are already assigned, which equations hold, and how enough reserve survives every extension. A degree buffer is allowed if its full recurrence stays below the old barrier; neither failure nor success of that recurrence has been proved here.

The parked relative quadratic route faces a separate unproved target-rank bound and an ambient-cost problem. The single-row reader route still lacks arbitrary cross-row source coverage. These do not currently offer a proved general replacement. The useful next test for the present line should concern an actual cross-row MOD input, rather than another reformulation of independent row fans.

4. Next bounded test: one global old parity

On the full bit-label set \(N=2^\ell\), work in characteristic two and let \(a=\sum_{i\in I}a_i\) be one old parity, with each \(a_i\) a nonconstant bit-linear predicate on a different pigeon row. On top matching spaces, define \(D_a:K_{r+1}\to K_r\) by conditioning with \(a\). Two successive contractions give zero: distinct-row terms cancel in characteristic two, and a repeated-row product reduces to an old row polynomial, below the original top degree. Thus \(D_a^2=0\).

Candidate to prove or falsify next. If \(h=|I|>d\) and \(N>6d\), test whether

\[ \ker(D_a:K_d\to K_{d-1}) =\operatorname{im}(D_a:K_{d+1}\to K_d). \]

A possible proof mechanism uses the coded basis: choose one active row, lift the target part avoiding it, and subtract the resulting differential. The remaining part uses that row and annihilates its predicate, so it can be treated as a forced coded row in the next step. The deleted-label budget and the forced-row induction must be checked in full. This is a proposed argument, not a theorem established by this review.

The intended source payoff is a correction for one genuinely wide MOD2 antecedent. Its necessary annihilator condition may be supplied by an actual companion, instead of independently prescribing all separate row-bit contractions. The test will stop at a complete proof or an obstruction, including the thin active-row case; even a positive answer will not solve multiple overlapping parities or the odd-prime recurrence.

I estimate about 25% that the coded-matching line yields further useful progress toward the main goal. The recent operator theorem is substantial local progress, while the complete-source existence implication remains open. The current decision is to pause further local fan refinements and test this different cross-row mechanism.

20 September 2026 — Wide parity contractions are exact in the matching range

Working characteristic-two exactness theorem, a single-parity MP application and finite controls. Multiple overlapping parities and full-source consistency remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, prove or falsify the route review's candidate for one global old parity, using a coded-row induction and a thin active-row control. This tests an actual cross-row MOD2 input, rather than another independent-row fan. The candidate is proved below in a slightly more general robust-predicate form, with an explicit MP consequence. Its first proof outline was identified during the preceding measured review; the full induction, application and checks belong to this cycle.

1. The top matching contraction complex

Work over a field of characteristic two, on a functional matching board with \(m\) rows and \(N\) labels. As before, \(K_r\) is the space of ordinary degree-\(r\) annihilators with all lower moments zero; put \(K_0=\mathcal A_0\). Equivalently, for \(r\ge1\), it is the direct sum over \(r\)-row sets of injection arrays with every ordinary row marginal zero. A row function \(f_i\) defines \(a_i=\sum_jf_i(j)X_{ij}\). On top spaces, conditioning at row \(i\) is precisely its weighted marginal \(\delta_i\), and is zero on arrays not using that row.

Let \(I\) contain \(t\) active rows and let \(a=\sum_{i\in I}a_i\). Set \(D_I=\sum_{i\in I}\delta_i\), so \(D_I:K_{r+1}\to K_r\) is conditioning by \(a\). A repeated row cannot be removed twice, and distinct removals commute. Hence \(D_I^2=0\) in characteristic two. The same assertion follows algebraically: \(a^2\) reduces to a row-linear polynomial, whose moment vanishes on a top space two degrees higher.

Working theorem. Let \(d\ge1\), \(t>d\), and suppose for every \(i\in I\) the evaluation matrix of \(1,f_i\) has rank two after deletion of any at most \(3d\) labels. Then

\[ \ker(D_I:K_d\to K_{d-1}) =\operatorname{im}(D_I:K_{d+1}\to K_d). \tag{WP-exact} \]

The lift from the cycle space can be chosen linearly. In particular, for \(N=2^\ell\) full bit labels and nonconstant bit-linear \(f_i\), the sufficient condition is \(N>6d\), since every nonzero affine combination of \(1,f_i\) has support at least \(N/2\). There is no dependence on the total number of active rows beyond \(t>d\).

2. Forced coded rows give an elementary induction

The following strengthened statement keeps track of what is preserved. Fix a set \(F\) of forced rows, disjoint from a set \(J\) of active rows. Let \(V_r^F\) be arrays supported on \(r\)-row sets containing \(F\), with zero ordinary marginals and, additionally, zero \(f_i\)-weighted marginal for each \(i\in F\). On these spaces, \(D_J\) removes only rows of \(J\), preserves the forced constraints, and squares to zero.

We prove that every \(D_J\)-cycle in \(V_d^F\) lifts from \(V_{d+1}^F\) if \(|J|>d-|F|\), assuming the stated rank robustness for all predicates on \(F\cup J\). Induct on \(d-|F|\).

Choose \(i\in J\), and split a cycle \(z=z_0+z_1\) into row sets avoiding and using \(i\). The part \(z_0\) need not itself be a cycle. Nevertheless it has a lift \(v_1\in V_{d+1}^F\), supported on row sets using \(i\), with \(\delta_i v_1=z_0\). To see this, apply the coded-trade theorem to each \(d\)-row set of \(z_0\): forced rows have evaluation rank two, and the others have the constant row of rank one. Its deletion allowance and each spanning tensor's support bound are

\[ L_S=2d+|F|-1\le3d-1, \qquad |\operatorname{supp}\eta|\le2d+|F|\le3d. \]

For each such tensor \(\eta\), solve on labels outside its support for a row-\(i\) factor \(c\) with \(\sum c_j=0\) and \(\sum f_i(j)c_j=1\). Robust evaluation rank permits the solve, with at most two nonzero coefficients. Multiplying \(c\otimes\eta\) by the target tensor coefficient and summing constructs \(v_1\). This preserves all forced row codes and every ordinary marginal.

Put \(z'=z-D_Jv_1\). Its part avoiding \(i\) is zero, since only \(\delta_i v_1\) removes that row. It remains a cycle because \(D_J^2=0\). In

\[ 0=D_Jz'=\delta_i z'+D_{J\setminus\{i\}}z', \]

the first summand avoids \(i\), while the second uses it. They therefore vanish separately. Consequently \(z'\in V_d^{F\cup\{i\}}\) and is a cycle for the remaining active rows.

If \(|F|<d\), the induction hypothesis applies because

\[ |J|-1>d-|F|-1=d-|F\cup\{i\}|. \]

It gives \(u\in V_{d+1}^{F\cup\{i\}}\) with \(D_{J\setminus\{i\}}u=z'\). Its forced row-\(i\) condition says \(\delta_i u=0\), so \(D_J(v_1+u)=z\). If \(|F|=d\), the only possible target row set is \(F\); it avoids every active row. The constructed \(v_1\) uses just \(F\cup\{i\}\), so no other active contraction contributes, and it already lifts \(z\). This is the base case.

Every stage uses at most \(3d\) deleted labels; the degree does not grow further during the recursion. Starting with \(F=\varnothing,J=I\) proves (WP-exact). Choose fixed coded bases, evaluation inverses and a fixed order of active rows to make the construction linear. There is no claim that the resulting tensor expansion has polynomial size. \(\square\)

3. A wide old-parity MP target needs only its companion condition

Now let \(a\) be an actual binary affine parity on \(t>d\) pigeon rows, each with a nonzero bit-linear part; a constant bit offset is allowed. Assume \(N=2^\ell>6d\). Then \(a^2-a\) has a degree-two ordinary Boolean witness in the unary old variables. A constant offset does not affect its top contraction.

Consider the supplied targets \(H=C-(1-a)B\) and \(G=aC\), with their actual original witness costs \(\rho\) and \(\sigma\). Prescribe \(\lambda,\nu\in\mathcal A_d\) for \(B,C\). Suppose

\[ \nu(q)=\lambda((1-a)q),\qquad \nu(aq)=0 \quad(\deg q\le d-1). \tag{WP-data} \]

Working corollary. There is an old extension \(\widetilde\lambda\in\mathcal A_{d+1}\) of \(\lambda\) with \(\nu(q)=\widetilde\lambda((1-a)q)\) for every \(\deg q\le d\). A linear choice is possible. Unlike a single-row fan, this wide-parity case needs no separate same-row boundary hypothesis: the parity touches more rows than a degree-\(d\) top matching can occupy.

Proof. Choose a linear old extension section \(E_d\), available because \(m\ge t>d\) and \(N>6d\). Let \(z=\lambda-\nu-M_aE_d\lambda\). The first condition puts \(z\in K_d\). For \(\deg q\le d-1\), Booleanity at the original degree gives

\[ (D_I z)(q)=\lambda(aq)-\nu(aq)-E_d\lambda(a^2q) =-\nu(aq)=0. \]

The exactness theorem supplies \(v\in K_{d+1}\) with \(D_Iv=z\), and \(\widetilde\lambda=E_d\lambda+v\) proves the claim. \(\square\)

Source scope and costs. For spectator support \(R\) disjoint from the displayed values, require \(d+w(R)+\rho\le D\) for the extended fan, and \((d-1)+w(R)+\sigma\le D\) for the annihilator condition. Also retain \(w(C)\le\rho\) and \(w(B)+1\le\rho\) so the component windows exist. When \(C\) is literally a genuine ENS block with original input \(a\), \(aC\) is its companion. If a named MOD value was replaced by an affine old parity using a prior witness, keep that witness's larger carried cost; do not relabel the original source merely because its interpreted old polynomial is affine. The theorem does not supply this companion for an arbitrary formal interface lacking it.

The corollary corrects one shared pair of components. It preserves homogeneous relations between parallel complete data pairs under a common linear choice, but does not automatically preserve unrelated source equations or simultaneously solve several overlapping global parities. Odd-prime inputs are not covered by the characteristic-two differential argument.

4. Thin active rows and exact full-image checks

The width condition has a concrete purpose. Let the active set \(I\) have exactly \(d\) rows, and take each row predicate to be the first bit. On each active row choose two zero-bit labels, all \(2d\) labels distinct, and form their signed difference tensor \(z\) on row set \(I\). It is a nonzero top matching trade and every active weighted marginal vanishes, so \(D_Iz=0\). But the component on row set \(I\) of every \(D_Iv\), \(v\in K_{d+1}\), is zero: to produce it one would have to remove an active row outside \(I\), and none exists. Thus this cycle is not a boundary, even with many inactive rows and arbitrarily many labels. A large label budget alone is insufficient.

The bounded checker uses three rows, sixteen labels, \(d=2\) and the low bit on each active row. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), with three active rows the image and cycle-space dimensions are both 583. With two active rows they are 403 and 583, giving a 180-dimensional failure of exactness. It saves the explicit four-cell cycle on rows 0 and 1 with label pairs \((0,2),(4,6)\); a single target coordinate annihilates the entire image and evaluates to one on this cycle.

In each case all 10,080 two-deletion checks give \(D_I^2=0\). A characteristic guard records coefficient two from the two deletion orders over \(\mathbb F_3\), explaining why the same un-oriented operator is not automatically a differential there. For an actual zero-marginal example, the three-row trade with label pairs \((0,1),(2,3),(4,5)\) has a nonzero twice-contracted coefficient \(2\) at row 2, label 4 over \(\mathbb F_3\). This last assertion follows directly from its two contributing deletion orders; it is not an odd-prime analogue of the theorem.

Complete ranks, pivot lists and controls and matrix definitions/reproduction are retained. The full-image check uses matrices of at most 1,440 by 3,360 bytes, not a large assignment search. It tests the entire cycle-space claim, not merely outputs generated from a prechosen lift.

5. Contribution and the next overlap

For general-step, the coded method now handles one actual wide old MOD2 input. The companion condition supplies its exact compatibility equation, and the lift has one old-degree increment with no extra iteration over the parity width. This is a different mechanism from separately prescribing all row-bit outputs. Complete-source consistency, shared-component overlap, original cost accumulation and the odd-prime recurrence remain unproved.

The next bounded test is simultaneous correction for a family of global affine parities. State a collective active-row rank condition and the necessary Koszul/annihilator relations before attempting a proof, then test whether they suffice. A list of independent single-parity corrections is not a common component extension. Stop at a general implication or a counterexample to that collective condition.

I estimate about 30% that this coded-matching line yields further useful progress on the main obligation. The new exactness tool merits independent review and a comparison with weighted matching-complex homology; it is a working proof, not a novelty or publication-readiness claim, and it does not establish the Frege lower bound.

Process assessment. The forced-row induction turned the proposed wide-parity mechanism into a uniform proof before computation; one full-image test plus the thin-row and characteristic controls checked its actual scope, so no framework change was needed.

20 September 2026 — Collective row distance gives a common parity lift

Working projective lifting argument and binary matching application, with a full-image check and cancellation control. Full-source compatibility remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, identify a collective condition under which several global parity defects have one common higher component. The single-parity theorem cannot simply be applied independently. This cycle proves a sufficient condition using every nonzero combination and an explicit higher-degree buffer, then derives the source application and tests a cancellation counterexample. The family dimension enters the room bound; no dimension-free theorem is claimed.

1. From every projective combination to one joint lift

Let \(C_r\) be finite-dimensional spaces over a characteristic-two field \(k\), with commuting degree-minus-one operators \(D_1,\ldots,D_s\), each satisfying \(D_i^2=0\). For \(u=(u_1,\ldots,u_s)\), put \(D(u)=\sum_i u_iD_i\). Assume, after extending to an algebraic closure, that for every nonzero \(u\) the complex of \(D(u)\) is exact at all degrees

\[ r=d,d+1,\ldots,d+s-1. \tag{CP-fibers} \]

Lifting lemma. Every tuple \(z_i\in C_d\) satisfying

\[ D_i z_i=0,\qquad D_i z_j=D_j z_i\quad(i\ne j) \tag{CP-closed} \]

has a common \(v\in C_{d+1}\) with \(D_i v=z_i\) for every \(i\). A linear right inverse on the compatible tuple space exists.

Proof. For \(s=1\), this is the assumed exactness at \(d\). For \(s\ge2\), work first over the algebraic closure, on \(X=\mathbf P^{s-1}\). Let

\[ E_j=C_{d+j}\otimes\mathcal O_X(1-j),\qquad \partial_j=\sum_i u_iD_i:E_j\longrightarrow E_{j-1}. \]

Here \(E_{-1}=C_{d-1}\otimes\mathcal O_X(2)\); we need \(E_0,\ldots,E_s\). The operators make this a complex, and (CP-fibers) says it is exact on every fiber at \(E_0,\ldots,E_{s-1}\). The neighboring matrix ranks are constant: each is at most its generic rank, and exactness makes their sum the fixed dimension of the middle fiber, so neither can drop. Thus kernels and images give exact sequences of vector bundles (coherent kernels suffice below).

Put \(Z_j=\ker\partial_j\). For \(0\le j\le s-1\),

\[ 0\longrightarrow Z_{j+1}\longrightarrow E_{j+1} \longrightarrow Z_j\longrightarrow0. \]

The standard projective-space calculation says \(\mathcal O(-1),\ldots,\mathcal O(-(s-1))\) have zero cohomology on \(\mathbf P^{s-1}\). Also coherent cohomology vanishes in degrees at least \(s\), as the standard \(s\)-chart affine Čech cover shows. These facts follow from Stacks Project, Lemma 30.8.1 and its Čech calculation. Applying the long exact sequences for \(E_2,\ldots,E_s\) gives

\[ H^1(Z_1)\cong H^2(Z_2)\cong\cdots\cong H^s(Z_s)=0. \]

Consequently \(H^0(E_1)\to H^0(Z_0)\) is onto. The tuple defines the linear section \(z(u)=\sum_i u_i z_i\) of \(E_0\); (CP-closed) is exactly the coefficient condition \(\partial_0z(u)=0\). It therefore comes from a global section of \(E_1=C_{d+1}\otimes\mathcal O\), namely a constant vector \(v\). Coefficient comparison yields \(D_i v=z_i\). Finally, solvability of this finite linear system after a field extension implies solvability over \(k\), since matrix and augmented ranks are unchanged. Selecting a basis of its image gives a linear right inverse. \(\square\)

The cohomology input is standard; the displayed application is a working argument, not a claim of novelty in projective geometry. The higher-degree hypotheses are used: exactness only at \(C_d\) is insufficient for this abstract statement. For example, the pencil

\[ k^3\xrightarrow{\begin{pmatrix}u&v&0\\0&u&v\end{pmatrix}}k^2\longrightarrow0 \]

is onto at every nonzero \((u,v)\), while its three constant input coefficients cannot cover all four coefficients of a linear \(k^2\)-valued target. Taking all other graded spaces zero makes the two operators commuting and square-zero, but the joint lifting conclusion fails. We do not assert that the full \(s-1\) buffer is optimal for matching spaces.

2. A collective row-distance condition for matching moments

Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_s\) be binary affine parities in the old bits of \(m\) rows with \(N=2^\ell\) labels. Ignore their constant offsets when measuring row support. Write their coefficient block on row \(i\) as \(A_i\in\mathbb F_2^{\ell\times s}\), and define

\[ \delta=\min_{0\ne c\in\mathbb F_2^s} |\{i:A_i c\ne0\}|, \qquad q=d+s-1. \tag{CP-distance} \]

Thus the forms are independent modulo constants whenever \(\delta>0\). This minimum is unchanged over an algebraic closure: if a nonzero extension-field vector is supported on a row set \(S\), the stacked binary matrices outside \(S\) have a nontrivial kernel, hence already have a nonzero binary kernel vector supported on a subset of \(S\). The reverse inequality is immediate.

Working theorem. For \(d\ge1\), assume

\[ \delta>d+s-1,\qquad N>6(d+s-1). \tag{CP-room} \]

Then a tuple \(z_i\in K_d\) has a common lift \(v\in K_{d+1}\) with \(M_{a_i}v=z_i\) if and only if

\[ M_{a_i}z_i=0,\qquad M_{a_i}z_j=M_{a_j}z_i. \tag{CP-matching-closed} \]

There is a linear right inverse on this compatible space.

Proof. The top operators commute and square to zero in characteristic two. Every nonzero extension-field combination of the parities has more than \(q\) nonconstant row blocks. Each surviving row block is a nonconstant bit-linear function, whose constant/predicate evaluation pair survives any fewer than \(N/2\) label deletions. By the wide-row exactness theorem, that combination is exact at every degree \(r=d,\ldots,q\). The projective lifting lemma now applies with \(C_r=K_r\). Necessity is immediate from commutation and square-zero. Constant offsets act as zero on top spaces. \(\square\)

The output extends one old degree; the family dimension appears in the sufficient label and row-distance room, not as an extra output degree. Checking all binary combinations can be expensive for large \(s\); the theorem asserts a mathematical condition and does not provide a generally efficient minimum-distance algorithm. Source families whose span contains a thin parity do not meet it.

3. Shared MP components for a collectively wide family

Assume (CP-room). Let supplied targets be \(H_i=C_i-(1-a_i)B\) and \(G_i=a_iC_i\), with original carried costs \(\rho_i,\sigma_i\). Prescribe \(\lambda,\nu_i\in\mathcal A_d\). Suppose lower fan equations and the supplied companions hold through old cofactor degree \(d-1\), and

\[ M_{a_j}(\lambda-\nu_i)=M_{a_i}(\lambda-\nu_j) \quad\text{through }d-1. \]

Corollary. There is one \(\widetilde\lambda\in\mathcal A_{d+1}\) extending \(\lambda\) and satisfying every fan equation through old cofactor degree \(d\).

Proof. Choose one old section \(E_d\), and form \(z_i=\lambda-\nu_i-M_{a_i}E_d\lambda\). Lower fan equations put them in \(K_d\). The degree-two Boolean witnesses \(a_i^2-a_i\) give \(M_{a_i}z_i=-M_{a_i}\nu_i=0\), as in the single-parity application. The stated pair equations cancel the section terms in cross contractions. Apply the collective lift, then add it to \(E_d\lambda\). \(\square\)

For spectator support \(R\) disjoint from the displayed names, retain \(d+w(R)+\rho_i\le D\) and \(d-1+w(R)+\sigma_i\le D\), along with \(w(C_i)\le\rho_i\), \(w(B)+1\le\rho_i\). Any larger cost carried through a named MOD interpretation stays attached. The diamond lemma can supply pair closure from additional mixed and absorption data only in its stated interior window. This corollary neither chooses those data nor preserves arbitrary other overlapping source equations.

4. Individually wide forms can still fail jointly

On three rows and any sufficiently large full bit-label set, put \(a_1=b_{0,0}+b_{1,0}+b_{2,0}\) and \(a_2=a_1+b_{0,1}\). Both forms touch all three rows, but \(a_1+a_2\) touches only row zero. At \(d=1\), let \(z_1=0\) and let \(z_2=e_0-e_4\) on row zero, with every other row component zero; labels 0 and 4 have both displayed bits zero. All self and cross contractions in (CP-matching-closed) vanish.

A common lift would give \(M_{a_1+a_2}v=z_1+z_2=z_2\). But conditioning a top degree-two matching trade at row zero has no output on row zero itself, whereas \(z_2\ne0\) is supported there. Thus no common lift exists. This is an explicit counterexample to using only the widths of the listed parities; it does not refute the collective-distance hypothesis.

The exact binary checker compares entire images on three rows, sixteen labels and \(d=1\). The positive pair uses the first bit on every row for \(a_1\), and the second bit on every row for \(a_2\): the three nonzero combination widths are \(3,3,3\), satisfying (CP-room). Both the joint image and compatible space have dimension 87. For the negative pair above the widths are \(3,3,1\), the image has dimension 73 and the compatible space dimension 87. The full incompatible target and a two-coordinate separating dual are saved; the dual kills every source column and evaluates to one on the target.

Complete ranks, pivots, coefficient blocks and controls, reproduction details, and source-review provenance are retained. The largest matrix is 192 by 720 bytes. The standard cohomology source was read for its stated vanishings; no third-party full text was downloaded or republished.

5. Contribution and next risk

For general-step, several overlapping old parities can now be corrected simultaneously under a collective row-distance condition, with explicit source hypotheses and a single higher component. The projective argument also explains why separate fixed-combination checks at one degree are insufficient in an abstract operator family.

The unresolved route issue is how to handle an arbitrary source parity span, which may contain many thin combinations or have dimension too large for (CP-room), while preserving mixed-component consistency. The next bounded task is to test a decomposition into a collectively wide part and a controlled row-supported exceptional part, including the simultaneous correction costs. State a quantitative condition sufficient for the full source window before claiming that separate treatment of the two parts composes. No such decomposition/compatibility theorem is asserted here.

I estimate about 30% that this coded-matching line yields further useful progress on the main obligation. The collective theorem merits independent review, particularly its projective exactness and source scopes; no novelty or publication-readiness claim is made, and the Frege lower bound remains open.

20 September 2026 — Local and wide corrections compose, but not every span has that form

Working relative and hybrid lifting proofs; exact mixed-compatibility check and a structural limitation. A general source-span reduction remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and endpoint. For general-step, determine whether row-supported exceptions and a collectively wide parity family can be corrected together, and whether this covers arbitrary source spans. The answer is positive for genuine row-local exceptions under explicit mixed conditions, but a basis change alone does not put every span into that form. The bounded endpoint is the relative correction theorem, its exact compatibility conditions, and a concrete limitation of the proposed structural reduction.

1. Global correction inside prescribed row kernels

Work in characteristic two on full \(N=2^\ell\) bit labels. For each pigeon row \(i\), fix a space \(L_i\) of bit-linear forms of dimension \(u_i\le u\), and a basis of it. Let \(K_r(L)\subseteq K_r\) consist of top matching arrays annihilated by conditioning with every local basis form. On each row set, this is exactly the array space with weighted row marginals zero for the evaluation families \(1,L_i\).

For \(s\ge1\) global binary affine parities \(a_1,\ldots,a_s\), project each row's coefficient block into the quotient of bit-linear forms by \(L_i\). Let \(\delta_L\) be the minimum number of nonzero quotient blocks in any nonzero binary combination of these \(s\) columns. Set \(q=d+s-1\), with \(d\ge1\).

Working relative theorem. Assume

\[ \delta_L>q,\qquad N>2q(u+3). \tag{HY-room} \]

Then every tuple \(w_t\in K_d(L)\) with \(D_t w_t=0\) and \(D_t w_v=D_v w_t\), where \(D_t=M_{a_t}\) on top spaces, has a common lift \(v\in K_{d+1}(L)\) satisfying \(D_t v=w_t\). The choice can be linear. Thus all previously imposed row-local kernels are preserved.

Proof: one combination with base row codes. Fix a nonzero projective combination and any degree \(r\le q\). Its row function is inactive on \(K_r(L)\) when it belongs to \(L_i\) modulo constants; otherwise it adds one independent row evaluation. In the forced-row induction, retain the base codes \(1,L_i\) in every row from the start. A forced row acquires one extra independent predicate. Therefore the evaluation rank is \(u_i+1\) in an ordinary row and \(u_i+2\) in a forced row. For any \(r\)-row target set, the coded tensor support and required deletion allowance are bounded by

\[ \sum_{i\in S}(\operatorname{rank}E_i+1) \le r(u+3)\le q(u+3), \qquad L_S\le q(u+3)-1. \]

Every independent affine bit-evaluation family stays independent after fewer than \(N/2\) label deletions: any nonzero affine combination is nonzero on at least half the labels. Hence (HY-room) supplies every base, forced and insertion-row evaluation rank needed in that induction. The insertion factor now annihilates \(1,L_i\) and has weighted moment one for the active new predicate. Subtracting its differential again leaves a cycle on row sets using that row, with the extra predicate in its kernel. All other base row kernels commute with these contractions and remain zero.

The same induction consequently proves exactness for this combination on \(K_r(L)\) whenever its relative active-row count exceeds \(r\). The quotient-block minimum distance is unchanged by field extension, by the binary-kernel argument from the collective theorem. Thus every nonzero projective combination is exact for \(r=d,\ldots,q\). Apply the projective lifting lemma to \(C_r=K_r(L)\). \(\square\)

The output still gains one old degree. The local row-count is not charged, but the largest local dimension \(u\) and the global family dimension \(s\) are charged in label room. If no local forms are prescribed, this reduces to \(N>6(d+s-1)\). The case with no global family is already covered by the row-predicate theorem and needs no projective step.

2. Correct the two parts without undoing either

Suppose local targets are \(z_{i,b}\in K_d^{\neg i}\) for bases \(l_{i,b}\) of \(L_i\), and global targets are \(w_t\in K_d\). Under (HY-room), the following conditions are necessary and sufficient for a common \(v\in K_{d+1}\) with \(M_{l_{i,b}}v=z_{i,b}\) and \(D_t v=w_t\):

  1. All local cross contractions agree, as in the row-predicate theorem.
  2. The global targets satisfy self-annihilation and global cross closure.
  3. The mixed equations hold:
    \[ M_{l_{i,b}}w_t=D_tz_{i,b}. \tag{HY-mixed} \]

Proof. Necessity follows from commutation, square-zero and the own-row support condition. The label budget supplies the local theorem: its maximum required deletion count is at most \(d(u+2)\), below \(q(u+3)<N/2\). First choose a local lift \(v_0\). For each global predicate, set \(r_t=w_t-D_tv_0\). The mixed equations say every local contraction of \(r_t\) vanishes, so \(r_t\in K_d(L)\). The global self and cross conditions persist by commutation and square-zero. The relative theorem provides \(v_1\in K_{d+1}(L)\) with \(D_tv_1=r_t\). Then \(v_0+v_1\) is the required common lift. Fixed linear choices make the whole construction linear. \(\square\)

This is a genuine composition statement for prescribed defects. It does not infer their own-row, self, cross or mixed conditions from arbitrary source data. Any source application must still retain the original witnesses and charges used in the MP fan, including its companion and closure assumptions. The result does not impose extra local forms on a source and then assume their target components can be chosen freely.

3. A basis change cannot produce this form for every span

Let \(V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m V_i\), where \(V_i\cong\mathbb F_2^\ell\) is the bit-coefficient space of row \(i\), and take

\[ W=\{(v_1,\ldots,v_m):\sum_i v_i=0\}. \]

Then \(\dim W=(m-1)\ell\), \(W\cap V_i=0\) for every row, and its minimum nonzero row support is two. A basis consists of the bit differences between each of the first \(m-1\) rows and the last row, so its written inventory is polynomial.

If a decomposition inside the original span has the form \(W=(\bigoplus_iL_i)+H\) with each \(L_i\subseteq W\cap V_i\), all local parts vanish. Thus \(H=W\), with \(s=(m-1)\ell\) and relative distance two. For \(m\ge3,\ell\ge1,d\ge1\), the condition \(\delta_L>d+s-1\) fails. This refutes a universal basis-change-only reduction to the proved hybrid form. It does not refute the hybrid theorem, a source-specific restriction, or a separate elimination of locally contradictory inputs.

The limitation is concrete but narrow. Pinning one anchor row turns those differences into row-local affine forms on the remaining rows, so restrictions can genuinely change the structural problem. With all bits, their common zero condition forces the remaining rows to the pinned label and is locally incompatible with that used column. If only one bit per row is used, the same anchored difference span becomes one row-local bit constraint per remaining row, rather than a complete forced collision. These examples motivate testing a controlled restriction, not declaring every thin span hard or every low-support system inconsistent.

Conversely, enlarging \(W\) by all its rowwise projections would trivially make it row-local, but that introduces predicate targets not prescribed by the original source. Choosing those added targets with all compatibility conditions is precisely another lifting problem, not a proof of the desired normal form.

4. Full-image check and omitted-mixed-equation control

The binary checker uses three rows, sixteen labels and \(d=1\). Each row has its first bit as a local predicate; the single global parity is the sum of second bits on all three rows. Hence \(u=1,s=1,q=1,\delta_L=3\), and \(N=16>8\) meets the hybrid range.

The joint image and the space satisfying all local boundary, self, cross and mixed constraints both have dimension 128. Dropping only the mixed equations increases the candidate target dimension to 131. The saved control has every local target zero, and global target \(e_0-e_1\) on row zero: it satisfies the weakened conditions, but its first-bit local contraction is nonzero, violating exactly one mixed equation. This demonstrates that the composition hypothesis does actual work.

Complete exact ranks, pivots and control and reproduction details are retained. The largest matrix is 288 by 720 bytes. The general relative proof uses the already reviewed projective lemma; no new literature import or large computation was needed.

5. What remains to turn the tool into a general source step

For general-step, local and wide corrections now compose inside a precise common kernel, with a quantitative label budget. The unresolved part is structural and source-dependent: produce a suitable residual span and compatible source components for an arbitrary actual proof source. Polynomial inventory and a change of basis do not by themselves produce the proved form.

The next bounded task is to formulate and test a restriction/localization alternative: retain a sufficiently large functional-PHP residual board on which the parity span has a controlled row-local part and a collectively wide quotient, or identify a cheaply eliminable source input family. Charge the surviving holes, all original source weights and the family dimensions. Test the proposed general alternative on explicit coefficient spaces before using it in a recurrence. The equality-difference example is a control for how pinning can help, not evidence that it always helps enough.

I estimate about 30% that the coded-matching line yields further useful progress on the main goal. This cycle solves the conditional composition issue for the stated hybrid form, while a general source reduction and complete-source consistency remain open. The relative theorem merits independent review; no publication or novelty claim is made.

Process assessment. Testing the normal form independently from its correction theorem exposed a basis-change limitation before building a recurrence; the existing proof/index workflow sufficed, so no framework change was needed.
