20 September 2026 — Row selection and hole-bit restriction must be analyzed together

Working structural obstruction and a joint restriction for that family, with an original-cost block-value consequence. The general restriction theorem is open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, test whether selecting surviving rows can always produce the row-local plus collectively wide form while retaining a useful PHP board. A hierarchical parity span defeats row-coordinate puncturing alone. For the same family, a common hole-subcube restriction restores row-local structure and retains about the square root of the original holes. The endpoint is this scope distinction and its source-cost ledger, not a general restriction theorem.

1. The coefficient-space quantity to control

For a binary coefficient space \(W\subseteq\bigoplus_i V_i\), let \(W_S\) be its projection onto a surviving row set \(S\). Let \(A_i\subseteq W^*\) be the space of row-\(i\) coordinate functionals, and write \(r(S)=\dim\sum_{i\in S}A_i=\dim W_S\). The row-local part at \(i\) has dimension \(r(S)-r(S\setminus\{i\})\), by taking the kernel of projection to the other rows. Consequently the dimension left after removing all row-local parts is

\[ s(S)=r(S)-\sum_{i\in S}\bigl(r(S)-r(S\setminus\{i\})\bigr). \]

The collective theorem needs more than a small written basis: this quotient dimension and its minimum nonzero row support must meet the stated room bounds. Restricting the common hole bits changes the spaces \(A_i\) themselves; it is not captured by deleting row blocks while keeping every original bit direction.

2. A hierarchical span defeats every large row-only projection

Let \(N=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\). Index \(N\) pigeon rows by the leaves of a complete binary tree of height \(\ell\), and add one extra pigeon row \(*\). For each node \(u\) at depth \(j\), \(0\le j<\ell\), define the old parity

\[ g_u=\sum_{i\text{ below }u}b_{i,\ell-1-j}. \tag{HL-node} \]

Bit zero is the least significant label bit. Let \(W\) be the coefficient span of these \(N-1\) forms; the extra row has no coefficient in them. The generators have disjoint supports as sets of row/bit coordinates: nodes at the same depth use disjoint rows, and different depths use different bits. They are therefore independent.

Working obstruction. Retain any \(k\ge2\) leaf rows and keep all original bit directions in the formal coefficient space. After projecting onto those rows and quotienting by its entire row-local part, the remaining dimension is at least \(k-1\), and the minimum nonzero row support is exactly two. Thus for \(k\ge3\) and \(d\ge1\) it cannot satisfy the hybrid theorem's strict inequality \(\delta_L>d+s-1\), regardless of a change of basis.

Proof. Put \(k_u=|S\cap\operatorname{desc}(u)|\). Projected nonzero node forms remain independent with disjoint coordinate supports. Those with \(k_u=1\) span exactly the row-local part: a combination involving a generator on two or more rows cannot cancel any of its coordinate entries. The remaining generators, those with \(k_u\ge2\), form a basis of the quotient, and a combination has row support equal to the union of their row supports. Hence the quotient distance is \(\min_{k_u\ge2}k_u\).

The minimal binary subtree connecting \(k\) chosen leaves has \(k-1\) branching nodes, all with \(k_u\ge2\). A branching node of maximum depth has exactly one selected leaf below each child, so \(k_u=2\). This proves both claims. With \(k\ge3\), the quotient dimension \(s\ge2\), and therefore \(d+s-1\ge2=\delta_L\). Keeping the extra row does not alter these coefficient quantities; in particular, a row-only projection with at least four surviving pigeon rows still encounters this obstruction. \(\square\)

Scope. This is an obstruction to row-coordinate puncturing without using new affine identities among the surviving hole-bit functions. It is not an obstruction to arbitrary functional-PHP restrictions, which also remove holes and may make some old bit directions constant or dependent. The next construction uses exactly that freedom.

3. A common subcube restores locality and leaves a large PHP residual

Choose \(1\le t\le\lfloor\ell/2\rfloor\), let \(M=2^t\), and reserve the hole subcube \(Q=\{0,\ldots,M-1\}\), with all high bits zero. Let \(\operatorname{rev}_\ell\) reverse the \(\ell\) binary digits. Keep the \(M\) leaf rows

\[ S=\operatorname{rev}_\ell(Q) \]

and the extra row \(*\). Pin each other leaf row \(i\) to the hole \(\operatorname{rev}_\ell(i)\). This is an injection onto all \(N-M\) holes outside \(Q\). The functional-PHP residual has exactly \(M+1\) rows and \(M\) holes.

Working localization lemma. On this residual, every \(g_u\) becomes either zero or a row-local affine bit form. Their nonconstant parts span all \(t\) bits on each of the \(M\) surviving leaf rows and no bit of \(*\). There is no constant-one generator. With \(t=\lfloor\ell/2\rfloor\), the residual has \(M=2^{\lfloor\ell/2\rfloor}\) holes.

Proof: variable part. A node at depth \(j<\ell-t\) uses a high bit, fixed to zero on every surviving row. A deeper node has an interval of at most \(2^t\) leaf indices. The surviving leaf indices are spaced by \(2^{\ell-t}\ge2^t\), so such an interval contains at most one surviving leaf. Its nonconstant part is therefore one bit on at most one row. Conversely, each surviving leaf and each low bit has its unique ancestor at the corresponding depth; that generator supplies the bit. The variable-part rank is exactly \(Mt\).

Proof: constants. The complete assignment of the \(N\) leaf rows \(i\mapsto\operatorname{rev}_\ell(i)\) makes every (HL-node) zero, in characteristic two. Indeed, at depth \(j\), the label bit \(\ell-1-j\) is the leaf-index bit \(j\). If this index bit is fixed on the node's leaf interval, it occurs an even number of times. If free, half the leaves contribute; this is also even, since the free case cannot occur at depth \(\ell-1\) when \(\ell\ge2\). Reinstating the surviving leaf labels \(\operatorname{rev}_\ell(i)\in Q\) completes that assignment. Hence a restricted generator with no variable part has constant zero. A surviving bit form is exactly that bit minus its value at the corresponding reversed label. \(\square\)

This is a restriction of both the row set and the allowed hole-bit functions. It does not contradict the row-puncturing obstruction. Original source weights and carried module costs are not reset when the high bit directions disappear. The source bridge has polylogarithmic degree at fixed proof depth and size exponent; this family's square-root-size residual leaves ample room for such degrees. That parameter observation is not a claim that every source family admits this restriction simultaneously.

4. A bounded-cost consequence for a complete block on these inputs

For this particular restricted input family, there is also a direct old-functional refutation of the common zero equations through degree \(t+1\). Each surviving leaf row \(i\) is constrained bitwise to its distinct hole \(j_i=\operatorname{rev}_\ell(i)\), and those holes exhaust \(Q\).

Proof and degree ledger. The label indicator \(\Delta_{j_i}(b_i)\) is a product of \(t\) factors \(1+q_{i,v}\), where \(q_{i,v}=b_{i,v}-(j_i)_v\) is one of the resulting local input equations. The telescoping identity for \(1-\prod_v(1+q_{i,v})\) expresses \(1-\Delta_{j_i}\) in the input ideal with multiplier degree at most \(t-1\). In the unary functional row algebra, \(\Delta_{j_i}-X_{i,j_i}\) has an old witness through degree \(t\): replace a complemented bit by the sum of its matching row cells using the row equation, expand, kill unequal same-row cells, and reduce repeated cells by Booleanity. For \(t=1\), there are only two remaining labels, and this is the row equation or an exact identity. Therefore \(1-X_{i,j_i}\) has a witness through \(t\).

For the extra row, use

\[ X_{*,j_i}=X_{*,j_i}(1-X_{i,j_i})+X_{*,j_i}X_{i,j_i}. \]

The first term has a witness through \(t+1\), and the second is a column-exclusion axiom. Sum over all \(j_i\in Q\) and use the extra row sum to derive one. Input multipliers have degree at most \(t\).

Whole-value corollary. Suppose a complete ENS block has these original affine inputs (or its input span contains them), whole value \(P\), and original value-degree bound \(w\). Its original companions carry cost \(w+1\). Multiply the preceding refutation by \(P\), replacing each local-input multiple by the corresponding linear combination of original companion multiples. Then

\[ P\in\mathcal I_{w+t+1}(\text{old functional base plus the restricted block}). \]

The bound uses the original \(w\), not a degree reduced by restriction. If the supplied companion costs are instead bounded by a larger carried \(\rho\), use \(\max(w+t+1,\rho+t)\). This is a whole-value zero witness in the stronger functional base, not automatic elimination of every fresh coefficient or preservation of all other retained components.

5. Exhaustive small control and complete pinning data

The bounded C++ checker enumerates every one of the 65,536 row subsets of a height-four tree. For all 65,519 subsets with at least two leaves, the quotient dimension is at least \(k-1\) and its minimum support is two. This uses the independent-node support description proved above, not numerical rank guesses. Every subset record is retained in the complete output.

A height-five common-subcube fixture first checked coefficient rank ten on five surviving leaf rows, but its arbitrary pinning also produced fourteen constant-one generators. That output is retained as a structural projection check, not evidence of a hard surviving input family. The stronger canonical bit-reversal control keeps leaf rows 0, 8, 16 and 24 plus the extra row, reserves holes 0 through 3, and has coefficient rank eight, no nonlocal generator and no constant-one generator. It records every pin, every restricted affine generator and all constants, and verifies that the original node parities vanish under bit reversal. Reproduction details specify both runs. The general degree witness above is symbolic; this computation does not verify arbitrary source families.

6. Contribution and remaining general claim

For general-step, a proposed row-only structural reduction is now ruled out even on a linear-size hierarchical family, while a legitimate joint restriction resolves that example and has an explicit source-value cost. This narrows what a useful general theorem must control. It does not establish a restriction for an arbitrary input span, a common restriction for all polynomially many source families, or compatible complete-source moments.

The next bounded question is whether there is a general joint row/bit restriction alternative with enough residual holes for the supplied source degree: each relevant fan/input family must become a controlled local-plus-wide case or admit a certified low-cost reduction. Formulate the quantitative target for the actual polynomial-inventory source, including how a single restriction serves all families, before seeking a proof. In particular, a normal form for the union of all old parities is not automatically a normal form for each shared-component fan with prescribed targets.

Assessment. The coded lifting tools remain usable within their hypotheses. The main unresolved implication has shifted to a simultaneous structural restriction and source-data construction; the present example identifies a necessary feature of such a restriction, but supplies no evidence that the general alternative always holds. A further local example would not resolve it.

Process assessment. The symbolic tree analysis exposed the failure before a general row-only lemma was pursued, and the second fixture removed a constant-one shortcut from the first positive control. The user also identified unsupported numerical prospect estimates during this cycle; their separate correction is now the reporting rule. That administrative interval is marked as overhead in this cycle and measured separately in its correction entry.

20 September 2026 — Literal naming preserves the source but does not solve its consistency

Source-interface review and exact degree-preserving naming/completion argument. No new lower bound or full-source feasibility theorem. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

1. Audit the proposed structural target before strengthening it

For general-step, the required claim remains existence of a normalized functional for the complete costed source at its compiled degree. The preceding cycles proved conditional local, wide and hybrid correction tools. A general restriction theorem for parity spans would be one possible way to organize their use, but neither a syntactically simple coefficient span nor separate component lifts supplies the required compatible data.

This cycle tests that distinction against an allowed equivalent representation. Give every old bit a weight-one name. All genuine source-module targets then involve only named values; the only non-base equations coupling the names to matching cells are single-row affine literal definitions. This transformation preserves the full degree problem exactly. Therefore counting only visible old-parity interactions is not a sufficient feasibility invariant. The hard relations are transferred to the named-value components.

The underlying degree-preservation principle is already available as pure affine defining-extension replay, and the source already supports explicit named MOD values. The contribution here is the exact original-cost and active-window audit for literal names, and the resulting limitation of the planned structural criterion. Naming is not a new hardness theorem.

2. Costed source equivalence over every prime

Use the recorded compact-bit source before its matching normal-form expansion. Its old dependence is through bits \(b_{it}\), decoded as \(\beta_{it}(X)=\sum_{j:j_t=1}X_{ij}\), of old degree one. Let \(Z\) denote the genuine value names with their original positive weights. A source target \(H_\alpha(b,Z)\) has formal weighted degree at most its carried witness cost \(\rho_\alpha\). Keep the old functional matching base in \(X\).

Introduce \(Y_{it}\) of weight one, replace each target by \(H_\alpha(Y,Z)\) at the same cost \(\rho_\alpha\), and add

\[ F_{it}=Y_{it}-\beta_{it}(X)\quad\text{at cost }1. \tag{LN-definition} \]

Booleanity \(Y_{it}^2-Y_{it}\) may be included at cost two. It follows from (LN-definition) and old Booleanity/same-row exclusions, since

\[ Y^2-Y=(Y+\beta-1)(Y-\beta)+(\beta^2-\beta), \]

and \(\beta^2-\beta\) has the recorded old witness through degree two, also at odd primes. These names are bits, not fresh coefficient variables; no Booleanity is asserted for arbitrary \(\mathbb F_p\) coefficients.

Working equivalence lemma. At every weighted cutoff \(D\), normalized annihilators of the original and literal-named costed systems correspond bijectively. The original module costs and the degree ceiling are unchanged; the added inventory is \(O(m\ell)\).

Proof. Substitute \(Y_{it}\mapsto\beta_{it}(X)\), fixing \(X,Z\). This map, \(\pi\), does not increase weighted degree. It sends definitions to zero, renamed source targets to their original targets and new Booleanity to its degree-two old witness. Thus pulling an original annihilator back along \(\pi\) gives a named one at the same cutoff.

Conversely, for any polynomial \(F\) of weighted degree at most \(r\), telescoping one literal-name replacement at a time gives

\[ F-\pi(F)=\sum_{i,t}(Y_{it}-\beta_{it})Q_{it}, \qquad\deg_w Q_{it}+1\le r. \tag{LN-telescope} \]

For a legal original target multiple \(QH_\alpha\), the corresponding difference after naming is a definition combination through weighted degree at most \(\deg_w Q+\deg_w H_\alpha\le\deg_w Q+\rho_\alpha\le D\). Hence restriction of a named annihilator to \(X,Z\) annihilates the original costed system. Equation (LN-telescope) also says every named moment is determined by that restriction. The two maps are inverse and preserve the value of one. \(\square\)

This uses the compact-bit source before decoding/normal-form collection; it does not claim that arbitrary old-cell expressions can be represented by bit names at the same weight. It also does not substitute away genuine value names, lower their weights, or alter the supplied proof witnesses. Sparse expanded size preservation is not needed for this degree/moment equivalence.

3. The active window survives, but completion must use substitution

Use the all-prime active interface with \(D\ge3L\), \(E=D-L\), \(m\ge D\), \(N\ge2D-1\), OR costs \(3L\), OR target weights at most \(2L\), and the stated Booleanity costs. After literal naming, every full degree-\(D\) legal OR multiple still has target weight at most \(E\).

Working corollary. A full literal-named degree-\(D\) annihilator exists if and only if there is a normalized core through weight \(E\) satisfying old matching/Boolean relations, all literal-definition multiples whose total weight is at most \(E\), and all the original degree-\(D\) legal renamed OR equations. Every such core extends to a full named annihilator.

Proof. Restriction gives necessity. For sufficiency, restrict the named core to \(X,Z\). Telescope the literal names out of every legal OR multiple; all differences fit within \(E\) because its target weight, not its carried witness cost, is at most \(E\). The result is a valid original core. Complete that core to degree \(D\) by the existing active-window theorem, then pull the full functional back through \(Y=\beta(X)\). Equation (LN-telescope) through \(E\) shows that this full named functional agrees with all the given core moments, not just those without \(Y\). \(\square\)

The order matters. Definitions of cost one have legal multiples reaching degree \(D\), outside \(E\). Thus the old instruction to fill each unused selector component independently cannot be applied directly after adding literal names. Eliminate those names, complete the original core, then restore them by substitution.

Small exact guard. In the Boolean ring on old \(x_1,x_2\) and name \(y=x_1\), take \(D=3,E=2\). A core with value one on 1 and zero on all nonconstant monomials satisfies every definition multiple through degree two. Extend it as a squarefree functional by setting \(\Lambda(x_1x_2y)=1\) and keeping every other nonconstant squarefree moment zero. All Boolean relations still hold, but the legal degree-three definition multiple has

\[ \Lambda\bigl(x_1x_2(y-x_1)\bigr)=1. \]

The substitution completion instead gives \(\Lambda(x_1x_2y)=\Lambda(x_1x_2)=0\). This is a guard for the completion rule, not a PHP or genuine-ENS counterexample.

4. The actual remaining equations

Let \(U=(Y,Z)\) be the full name set, and write \(z_{T,R}=\Lambda(X_TU_R)\) for a partial matching \(T\) and Boolean name support \(R\). The core has \(|T|+w(R)\le E\). Besides old marginals, each literal definition gives, at its original legal cofactor weight \(|T|+w(R)+1\le E\),

\[ z_{T,R\cup\{Y_{it}\}}= \begin{cases} \displaystyle\sum_{j\notin\operatorname{col}T,\ j_t=1} z_{T+(i,j),R},&i\notin\operatorname{row}T,\\ (j_0)_t\,z_{T,R},&(i,j_0)\in T. \end{cases} \tag{LN-core} \]

The second line is the explicit row-used boundary condition. The first is a weighted marginal. If the name already belongs to \(R\), Boolean support reduction can lower the target's weight, but the original cofactor charge remains one; do not silently enlarge the equation set at the boundary.

All non-base OR targets are now polynomials in \(U\) alone. Thus their legal normal-form equations have the form

\[ \sum_S c_S^\alpha z_{T,R\cup S}=0, \qquad |T|+w(R)+3L\le D. \]

They keep the matching \(T\) fixed, but can couple many different name supports. That is where arbitrary parity combinations, products and proof-source structure now reside. Row-local literal syntax therefore does not remove the simultaneous component-selection problem. The hybrid theorem remains conditional on compatible data, and naming does not supply them.

5. Route decision and contribution

The general claim still needed is a normalized solution of these complete core equations for actual bounded-depth polynomial-inventory sources, with the original degree ledger. A theorem about restrictions of old parity coefficient spaces would be one possible method, but it is neither the endpoint itself nor a requirement forced by this equivalent interface.

The representation test falsifies the proposed shortcut “make all visible old couplings row-local, then the lifting theorem gives source feasibility.” Every source in this class already has such a representation at the same cutoff. A valid criterion must also control the named-value relations and the row-used boundaries. Conversely, this audit does not prove that the restriction approach is useless: naming moves its difficult relations rather than eliminating them.

Next bounded task. Inspect the first actual two-level source coupling in this literal-named interface. Identify a concrete sufficient rank or extension condition on its joint named-value components, retaining the old matching boundary and source weights, and test it against the existing mixed-interface obstruction. Stop if the condition merely restates full feasibility or assumes arbitrary prescribed components extend; do not pursue a general coefficient normal form solely because it is syntactically convenient.

Assessment. This cycle did not prove a new lower bound. It established the precise costed equivalence and completion rule and identified why the planned structural simplification alone would not discharge the main obligation. The conditional correction tools remain valid, but the needed construction of compatible source data is still absent.

Process assessment. Reading the existing affine-definition result before pursuing a simultaneous restriction theorem exposed a representation-dependent surrogate. The existing falsification guidance will be tightened to include allowed equivalent representations. No numerical estimate of the route's prospects is warranted.

20 September 2026 — One genuine parent is controlled by its input space

Working all-prime single-parent exclusion with complete companions and fields. Arbitrarily many coupled upper parents are not covered. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and endpoint. For general-step, inspect a genuine second-level parent whose input rank can exceed its accuracy, retaining every input and coefficient equation. The existing rank profile charges that rank; the present test asks for a sufficient condition using only the parent's input space. A one-parent criterion and a bounded-rank-bottom application are proved below. This concerns existence of a suitable annihilator, not extension of arbitrary previously chosen mixed moments.

1. A concrete two-cutoff test for one complete block

Work over \(\mathbb F_p\). Let \(\Gamma\) be a retained polynomial system whose variables have field equations, or certificates for them through their ordinary degrees. Thus a polynomial \(g\) of degree \(d\) has \(g^p-g\in\mathcal I_{pd}(\Gamma)\). This follows by Frobenius and telescoping monomials; old Boolean variables qualify because \(x^p-x\) has a witness through \(p\) from \(x^2-x\).

Add one complete ENS block with nonzero inputs \(g_i\), actual degrees \(d_i\), maximum \(\delta\), accuracy \(H\ge1\), fresh disjoint coefficient variables, and

\[ P=\prod_{u=1}^{H}\left(1-\sum_i r_{u,i}g_i\right), \qquad w=H(\delta+1),\qquad e_i=w+d_i. \]

When some input has actual degree \(\delta\), fresh coefficient rows make \(\deg P=w\) and \(\deg(g_iP)=e_i\) in the ordinary polynomial ring, before any field reduction. Zero inputs can be omitted. Constant cases are immediate or included by the same argument. Put \(B=D+(p-1)\delta\).

Working criterion. Assume \(1\notin\mathcal I_B(\Gamma)\) and, for every input,

\[ g_i\in\mathcal I_B(\Gamma)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad g_i\in\mathcal I_{e_i}(\Gamma). \tag{SP-input-test} \]

Then adjoining the complete block, including every \(g_iP\) and \(r_{u,i}^p-r_{u,i}\), gives no ordinary NS refutation through \(D\).

Proof: a surviving input. Suppose \(g_j\notin\mathcal I_B\). For \(a\in\mathbb F_p\), set \(\Delta_a(t)=1-(t-a)^{p-1}\). The exact interpolation identity \(t=\sum_{a\ne0}a\Delta_a(t)\) shows that some \(\Delta_a(g_j)\), \(a\ne0\), is outside \(\mathcal I_B\). Choose a linear functional \(\Lambda\) through \(B\) annihilating \(\mathcal I_B\) with \(c=\Lambda(\Delta_a(g_j))\ne0\); it need not initially be normalized.

Set \(r_{1,j}=a^{-1}\), all other parent coefficients to zero, and denote this constant substitution by \(\phi\). Then \(\phi(P)=1-a^{-1}g_j\). For polynomials through degree \(D\), define

\[ \widetilde\Lambda(F)=c^{-1}\Lambda\bigl(\Delta_a(g_j)\phi(F)\bigr). \]

This is defined through \(D\) and normalized. It annihilates retained generator multiples, since the extra factor costs at most \((p-1)d_j\le(p-1)\delta\). Parent coefficient equations map to zero. For a legal parent companion multiple \(Qg_iP\), use the exact identity

\[ \Delta_a(g_j)(1-a^{-1}g_j)=a^{-1}(g_j^p-g_j). \]

Its old witness, multiplied by \(\phi(Q)g_i\), has degree at most

\[ \deg Q+d_i+pd_j \le D-w+pd_j \le D+(p-1)\delta=B, \]

because \(w\ge d_j\). Every original input position is covered, regardless of parent rank or arity. Thus \(\widetilde\Lambda\) is a normalized annihilator of the full augmented system through \(D\).

Proof: all inputs vanish at the larger cutoff. If every \(g_i\in\mathcal I_B\), (SP-input-test) gives a witness through its original companion degree \(e_i\). Set every parent coefficient to zero, so \(P\) maps to one. A normalized degree-\(D\) annihilator of \(\Gamma\) exists by the first assumption. Each parent companion image is \(g_i\); multiplying its supplied witness by any legal cofactor still fits \(D\). Pulling back the old annihilator therefore completes this case. \(\square\)

This is a source-dependent version of the already recorded term-value conditioning/case-split mechanism. The new test isolates the needed input-window condition and charges the original complete block. It does not say that every retained system satisfies (SP-input-test), or that the choices for many parents can be made simultaneously. No PC extension claim is needed here.

2. Verify the criterion on an actual two-level family

Take the old functional PHP base on \(N+1\) rows and \(N\) columns over \(\mathbb F_p\). Let \(\Gamma_0\) adjoin any finite family of complete first-level blocks, each of common accuracy \(h\ge1\), with proper nonconstant old-affine input space of rank \(r_c\le R\), \(R\ge1\). Inputs may be affine in the old cells; decoded affine bit inputs are a special case. Each whole bottom value \(P_c\) has degree \(w_0=2h\), with disjoint own coefficients.

Add one complete parent of accuracy \(H\ge1\), whose original inputs are arbitrary \(\mathbb F_p\)-affine combinations of old affine forms and the actual \(P_c\)'s. Their arity, overlap and linear span rank are unrestricted. Assume at least one input uses a bottom value. Disjoint coefficient sets make every such input have actual degree \(\delta=w_0=2h\); an input using only old variables has degree at most one. Put

\[ S=(p-1)R,\quad T=\max\left(1,\left\lceil\frac{S}{h}\right\rceil-1\right),\quad w=H(2h+1),\quad B=D+(p-1)2h,\quad C=TB. \tag{SP-parameters} \]

Working theorem. Suppose

\[ S\le w,\qquad D\ge w+2h,\qquad N\ge2C-1. \tag{SP-range} \]

Then this complete two-level system has no ordinary NS refutation through \(D\). All bottom and parent coefficient field equations and every original companion are included. There is only one upper parent; an entire coherent compiler registry may contain many upper/subgroup blocks and is not covered.

3. Complete bottom normalization and cheap value comparison

First, normalize all bottoms at once. For a bottom affine basis \(L_1,\ldots,L_r\), set

\[ A=\prod_{j=1}^{r}(1-L_j^{p-1}) =\prod_{j=1}^{r}\prod_{a\in\mathbb F_p^*}(1-aL_j). \]

Partition these \((p-1)r\) linear factors into \(h\) bins of size at most \(q=\lceil S/h\rceil\). The ordinary telescoping prefix in each bin writes its product as \(1-\sum_i U_i g_i\), using the original affine inputs and coefficient degree at most \(\max(0,q-1)\le T\). Assign that bin's coefficient row accordingly. The whole product maps exactly to \(A\). All blocks have disjoint coefficients, so these assignments are simultaneous.

An original companion maps to \(g_iA\). Since each original input is a constant combination of the basis, the identity

\[ L_j(1-L_j^{p-1})=L_j-L_j^p \]

gives an old field/Boolean witness through \((p-1)r+1\). This fits \(T(2h+1)\): for \(q\le2\), the bound is at most \(2h+1\); for \(q\ge2\), \(qh+1\le(q-1)(2h+1)\). Coefficient field images have old witnesses through \(pT\), exactly the allowed multiple of their original degree \(p\). Old axioms are fixed. Therefore a degree-\(B\) ordinary NS consequence maps to an old functional consequence through \(TB=C\). This is the standard complete affine-bin normalization with its full degree ledger; it is not a substitution of semantic values without their certificates.

The old matching theorem supplies a normalized annihilator through \(C\), and \(\mathcal I_C\cap\mathcal P_{\le s}=\mathcal I_s\) for \(s\le C\), because \(N\ge2C-1\) and \(N+1\ge C\). It follows immediately that \(1\notin\mathcal I_B(\Gamma_0)\).

Second, compare each original whole value with its flat indicator inside \(\Gamma_0\). There is an ordinary NS certificate

\[ P_c-A_c\in\mathcal I_{w_0+(p-1)r_c}(\Gamma_0). \tag{SP-value-comparison} \]

Indeed, the bottom's exact prefix gives \(1-P_c=\sum_i U_i g_i\), \(\deg U_i\le w_0-1\). Multiplying by \(A_c\) and using the companion calculation above proves \(A_c(1-P_c)\) through \(w_0+(p-1)r_c\). Conversely, telescope \(1-A_c\) in the factors \(1-L_j^{p-1}\). Each term is a multiple of \(L_jP_c\), itself a constant combination of original companions, with remaining multiplier degree at most \((p-1)r_c-1\). Thus \(P_c(1-A_c)\) has the same ceiling. Subtract the two identities. This also explains why equality with a flat indicator is not freely available at the raw degree of \(P_c\).

4. Only the actual parent input window needs stability

Let \(g_i\) be a parent input, and let \(F_i\) be the old polynomial obtained by replacing every \(P_c\) in it by \(A_c\). Then \(\deg F_i\le S\), since \(S\ge1\). If \(g_i\in\mathcal I_B(\Gamma_0)\), the complete normalization maps its certificate to \(F_i\in\mathcal I_C(\mathcal F^{\rm fun})\). Old filtration stability gives \(F_i\in\mathcal I_S(\mathcal F^{\rm fun})\).

If the input uses bottom values, (SP-value-comparison) gives \(g_i-F_i\) through \(w_0+S\). Since \(S\le w\), both witnesses fit its original parent-companion degree \(e_i=w+w_0\). If the input is old-affine, the comparison is exact and the old witness through \(S\le w\) fits \(e_i=w+d_i\). Thus every input satisfies (SP-input-test). The one-parent criterion proves the theorem. \(\square\)

For fixed \(p\), common accuracies \(H=h=\Theta(\log N)\), bottom ranks may grow up to \(R\le h(2h+1)/(p-1)\). Then \(T=O(h)\), so polylogarithmic \(D\) still gives \(C=\operatorname{polylog}N\), well below the old barrier for large \(N\). Smaller target degrees follow by monotonicity from a ceiling satisfying \(D\ge w+2h\). This is not restricted to a bounded number of summands per parent input, unlike the earlier fixed-parameter corollary; in exchange, it has only one upper parent.

5. What the known mixed-interface obstruction does and does not refute

The mixed-helper example invalidates preserving arbitrary retained whole-product moments at the same cutoff. The present construction makes no such promise: in the surviving-input case it chooses a different retained functional, weights it by a nonzero input-value indicator, and normalizes it. This is permitted by the existence endpoint. The all-inputs-vanish branch instead requires actual witnesses at the original parent companion costs.

After one parent has been added, the retained system is no longer the normalized family of old-affine bottoms used in the proof of its input-window test. The raw filtration counterexample warns against simply assuming that test persists. For many upper parents, independently selected nonzero input slices may also be incompatible. Neither the new theorem nor the older term-clamping lemma proves a simultaneous choice at an affordable total degree.

No new finite computation was necessary for this cycle: the interpolation identity, complete affine coefficient substitution, input comparison and degree inequalities are explicit symbolic certificates. The parameters in (SP-range) are part of the theorem, not inferred from small-board experiments.

6. Contribution, remaining gap and queued source review

For general-step, there is now a concrete sufficient input-space test for one genuine parent and an all-prime two-level application with growing bottom rank and unrestricted parent sums. This handles one non-affine block without requiring arbitrary mixed-data preservation. It does not establish the multi-parent invariant required by the full source, and it does not prove the Frege lower bound.

Next cycle, as requested by the user. Audit the newly supplied Pitassi–Beame–Impagliazzo (1993), Krajicek–Pudlak–Woods (1995), and Alekhnovich–Razborov (2003) PDFs. Check the bipartite matching-switching hypotheses and parameters behind the earlier request, and compare the published AR criterion with the previously used preprint. Update source availability and the affected mathematical claims only after reading the relevant passages. None of these supplied PDFs was opened during the present cycle.

Assessment. The single-parent result supplies a proved existence step on an actual complete block family. Its proof exposes the next required premise precisely: cheap vanishing or survival of the later input spaces after prior parents have been installed. The present argument does not control that premise, so the full multi-parent route remains unresolved.

Process assessment. Using the sufficient existence endpoint avoided trying to preserve every prior mixed moment. The proof reused complete affine normalization and old matching stability, and no additional numerical suite or framework rule was needed. The user's supplied-source audit is queued immediately after this checkpoint.

20 September 2026 — Supplied sources settle the switching constants, but expose a base-system mismatch

Targeted source audit; imported bipartite switching statements, a scoped image-transfer correction, and comparison with the supplied March 2003 AR manuscript. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, resolve the source requests behind the literal switching import and the immunity audit. This cycle began only after the preceding single-parent cycle was committed and pushed. It stops at exact imported hypotheses, their application limits, and the resulting correction; it does not redo the full published lower-bound proofs.

1. The bipartite statements actually supplied by the papers

Pitassi–Beame–Impagliazzo. The supplied journal PDF is Exponential lower bounds for the pigeonhole principle, Computational Complexity 3 (1993), 97–140, DOI. Section 2 defines positive map disjunctions: each term is a partial injective matching, with at most \(r\) edges. On an \((n+1)\)-by-\(n\) board, the distribution \(Q\) chooses a spare pigeon uniformly, retains each of the other \(n\) pigeons independently with probability \(\theta\), chooses an equally sized uniform set of residual holes, and matches the complements uniformly. The spare pigeon remains free. Thus the residual board has \(K+1\) pigeons and \(K\) holes, \(K\) distributed as \(\operatorname{Bin}(n,\theta)\).

A 1–1 decision tree may query either a pigeon or a hole, branching over available partners on the other side. There is no empty-hole branch. Its representation condition concerns assignments that are 1–1 on the vertices covered by a leaf path. Let \(\delta(F\restriction_\rho)\) be the minimum height of such a representing tree. Lemma 5, printed p. 107 and proved from the balanced lemma in Section 6.1, pp. 137–138, states: for \(s\gt 0\), \(\theta\le 1/36\), and \(\theta n\ge 8(s+r)^2\),

\[ \Pr_Q[\delta(F\!\restriction_\rho)\ge s+1]<n\alpha^s, \qquad \left(1+\frac{36\theta^4n^3}{\alpha^2}\right)^r\le2. \tag{PBI-5} \]

Its stated sufficient choice is \(\alpha=8 \theta^2 n^{3/2} \sqrt{r}\). This is an existence/minimum-height statement for a binomial residual-size distribution, not the same assertion as the earlier fixed-residual canonical-tree bound. The extra factor \(n\) must not be dropped.

Krajicek–Pudlak–Woods. The supplied journal PDF is An exponential lower bound to the size of bounded depth Frege proofs of the pigeonhole principle, Random Structures and Algorithms 7 (1995), 15–39, DOI. Definition A, pp. 19–20, calls a family \(S\) of partial matchings \(k\)-complete when its members are pairwise incompatible, have size at most \(k\), and each partial matching \(a\) with \(|a|+k\le n\) is compatible with some member of \(S\). Refinement of \(H\) means each member of \(S\) either conflicts with every member of \(H\) or contains a member of \(H\). These are combinatorial conditions, not an ordinary polynomial partition identity.

Definition D, p. 24, retains each hole independently with probability \(\theta\) and chooses a uniform injection onto the removed holes. Lemma D2, p. 25, says that if the maps in \(H\) have size at most \(t\le s\), \(\theta\lt 1/100\) and \(\theta n\ge 40s\), then, with probability at least

\[ 1-e(16\theta^4n^3t)^s-2^{-c\theta n},\qquad c>0\text{ absolute}, \tag{KPW-D2} \]

there is a \(2s\)-complete family \(S\) on the residual board refining the restricted \(H\). The same bound includes the condition that at least \(\theta n/2\) holes remain. The paper notes the regime \(\theta=n^{\epsilon-1}\), \(t=s=n^\eta\), with \(0\lt \eta\lt \epsilon\lt 1/5\). This audit checked the definitions and statement, not the entire Section 4 proof. Neither source concerns arbitrary parity inputs.

2. A precise common-restriction consequence

Working corollary of the imported PBI statement. For \(M\) positive \(r\)-map disjunctions, \(r,M\ge 1\), take

\[ \theta=\frac{n^{-3/4}}{4r^{1/4}},\qquad \mu=\theta n=\frac{n^{1/4}}{4r^{1/4}},\qquad s=\lceil\log_2(4Mn)\rceil. \]

Assume \(\theta\le 1/36\) and \(\mu\ge \max(8(s+r)^2,8 \ln 8)\). Then a single restriction leaves \(\mu/2\le K\le 2\mu\) holes and gives every disjunction a PBI representing tree of height at most \(s\).

Proof. The sufficient \(\alpha\) is \(1/2\), and the union of the \(M\) bad-tree events has probability below \(Mn 2^{-s}\le 1/4\). For \(K\) binomial with mean \(\mu\), the usual exponential-moment bound gives \(\Pr[K\lt\mu/2]\le e^{-\mu/8}\) and \(\Pr[K\gt2\mu]\le e^{-\mu/3}\). For completeness, these follow from \(\mathbb E e^{tK}=(1-\theta+\theta e^t)^n\le e^{\mu(e^t-1)}\), using Markov with \(t=-\ln 2\) and \(t=\ln 2\) respectively and weakening the resulting constants. Their sum is below \(1/4\) under the stated lower bound on \(\mu\). Thus the union of all failures has probability below one. For a positive map disjunction, a 1-leaf path contains a term: assign exactly its path edges one and every other edge zero, then use the representation condition. Hence these trees also refine the disjunction. The corollary supplies these two-sided trees only. For polynomial \(M\) and polylogarithmic \(r\), its room conditions hold for large \(n\), \(s\) is logarithmic, and \(K\) is \(\Theta(n^{1/4}r^{-1/4})\).

3. Correction: a two-sided matching tree is not automatically a functional-PHP image

The original image lemma explicitly uses a point equation at every queried vertex, but then identifies the bipartite system with our functional PHP base. That identification is false for hole queries. Our base has pigeon row equations, Booleanity and exclusions; it has no equation asserting that a particular hole is occupied.

Exact counterexample to the claimed verbatim application. On an \((N+1)\)-by-\(N\) board, \(N\ge 2\), fix a hole \(q\) and let \(F\) be the disjunction of all \(X_{iq}\). A PBI tree querying \(q\) has height one, only branches \(X_{iq}\), and all leaves labeled one. It represents and refines \(F\) in the source's sense. The original image recipe gives zero for the sum of 0-leaves and coefficient one for each input \(X_{iq}\). Its asserted degree-one coefficient identity would require

\[ u_q=1-\sum_iX_{iq}\in\mathcal I_1(\mathcal F^{\rm fun}). \]

This is false over every field: the only degree-one generators are the pigeon row equations, and no linear combination of those has coefficient -1 in column \(q\) and zero in each other column. Equivalently, evaluate each row at the same different hole: this annihilates all degree-one row equations and gives \(u_{q}=1\). Exclusions have degree two and cannot enter a degree-one certificate. The failure concerns the claimed image recipe and its degree guarantee, not existence of some different image for this simple \(F\).

Adding all hole equations is not a harmless repair. The sum of the pigeon equations minus the sum of the hole equations is -1 on an \((N+1)\)-by-\(N\) board, giving a degree-one refutation. One cannot add them while retaining the old PHP barrier.

The existing empty-hole branch lemma correctly uses \(u_{q}\) as an additional branch factor. For this example, a zero-labeled empty branch repairs the tree. In general, however, an added empty branch must still compute the restricted reader; PBI's height guarantee and KPW's completeness definition provide no guarantee on those extra subtrees. Indeed \(S=\{\{(i,q)\}:i\in[N+1]\}\) is a 1-complete KPW family: its members conflict, and any matching of size at most \(N-1\) either already uses \(q\) or can be extended to it. Nevertheless its polynomial sum is \(\sum_{i} X_{iq}\), not one modulo the degree-one old ideal.

Scope of correction. Preserve the image argument when all queried point equations are actually available, and preserve applications using independently constructed, valid trees with empty-hole branches and the required partition certificates. Withdraw the unconditional passage from the imported two-sided trees to functional-PHP images. The locally proved fixed-size counting statement is not refuted by this example; its functional-image consequence has the same gap. Its counting proof and encoding tests are not rerun here. The sum-input image proof likewise needs the stated leaf-partition certificates. No blanket invalidation of the later, separately constructed empty-branch switching results is inferred.

4. The supplied AR manuscript preserves the checked immunity obstruction

The file named AR2003.pdf is a 31-page author-format manuscript dated 13 March 2003, with printed pages 1–31. It is not the journal typesetting at pp. 18–35. Its title is Alekhnovich–Razborov, Lower Bounds for Polynomial Calculus: Non-Binomial Case; the publication record identifies the journal version. The text encoding is broken, so the relevant rendered pages were inspected locally; previews and full text are not published.

Section 2, p. 4, works in the Boolean function ring over an arbitrary field. Definitions 2.2–2.3, pp. 5–6, use the same boundary-expansion and semantic-immunity conditions as the recorded 2000-preprint audit. Theorem 3.8, p. 13, again requires an \((R,s,c)\)-expander, common immunity \(\ell\), and

\[ s\le R\bigl(\ell/4-(s-c)\bigr), \]

and concludes PC degree strictly above that right-hand side. The theorem statement, ring conventions and application hypotheses therefore agree with the earlier recorded criterion. This is a targeted comparison, not a claim that every passage of the two versions agrees or that the journal typesetting has now been checked.

The shared-support calculation still defeats the raw high-rank binary ENS companions and the specified dense overlapping whole-block grouping for Theorem 3.8. The supplied version also states Theorem 3.13, p. 16: an \((R,s,c)\)-expander supports a degree lower bound \(Rc/2\) for equations that are individual assignment indicators on their incident variable sets. This more specialized result must not be omitted when describing the method's scope, but it does not automatically apply to ENS companions.

Direct check of that restriction. Take the same binary proper affine-span setting of the previous audit, with rank \(r\gt h\), \(h\ge 1\), and \(k\ge r\) nonzero inputs. A nonzero companion \(g_{i} P\) has Boolean degree at most \(2h+1\). Every one of its \(hk\) coefficient variables is essential by the earlier proof. Every old variable in the input span is essential as well: if it occurs in \(g_{i}\), set coefficients zero; otherwise choose an input \(g_{j}\) containing it, set a single first-row coefficient to one and the rest to zero, and choose \(g_{i}=1\). Toggling the variable then changes \(g_{i}(1-g_{j})\). Such an assignment exists since \(g_{i}\) is nonconstant and does not depend on that variable. Properness implies that the linear parts have rank \(r\), so there are at least \(r\) essential old variables. The companion therefore depends on at least \((h+1)r\gt 2h+1\) variables.

A nonzero scalar multiple of an assignment indicator on \(s\) variables has degree exactly \(s\) and depends on all \(s\) variables. Thus these raw companions cannot be the equations required by Theorem 3.13, even allowing nonzero scalar multiples. New encodings or regroupings remain outside this observation. The supplied March manuscript resolves the requested criterion comparison as far as this actual copy permits; an exact journal-copy comparison remains optional, with the version distinction recorded in the request note.

5. Outcome and next obligation

For general-step, the previously unavailable bipartite statements are now checked with exact constants and residual models. Their direct functional-PHP image application needs an additional bridge; the source audit exposed this rather than discharging it. The AR comparison preserves the earlier negative verdict for the two tested representations and adds the assignment-indicator scope check. None supplies the missing multi-parent existence invariant.

Next step. Return to the single-parent input-window result and test whether adding an upper parent preserves the cheap-vanishing-or-survival condition for later inputs. Begin by trying to falsify that general invariant against the augmented filtration obstruction; stop at a valid bounded invariant or an explicit failure before pursuing further special cases.

20 September 2026 — The cheap-input invariant fails even for a removable singleton child

Working binary counterexample with a degree-preserving positive control. Refutes persistence of the sufficient input test, not the single-parent theorem or complete-source nonrefutability. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, test the proposed iteration of the single-parent criterion: after adding a parent, must each later admissible input that vanishes at the larger cutoff already vanish at its own companion cost? The raw-coefficient example does not answer this for affine combinations of actual whole values. The construction below does: its later input is exactly one genuine whole parent value, and every bottom block has rank one. The stopping point is an explicit counterexample and a control showing that the rejected child is nonetheless removable.

1. Exact statement and source family

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) with old functional PHP on \(N+1\) pigeons and \(N=2^\ell\) holes. Choose \(K=2^t\lt N\) and let \(Q\) be the subcube of labels whose \(\ell-t\) high bits are zero. Select \(K+1\) pigeons \(A\). For \(i\) in \(A\) and each high bit \(v\), let \(\beta_{iv}=\sum_{j:\,j_v=1}X_{ij}\). Give each \(\beta_{iv}\) its own complete accuracy-\(h\) singleton block

\[ P_{iv}=\prod_{u=1}^{h}(1-a_{iv,u}\beta_{iv}),\qquad w_0=2h. \]

Every input is a decoded old bit, so each bottom has a proper affine input space of rank one. Include all companions \(\beta_{iv} P_{iv}\) and all coefficient Boolean equations. Add one complete accuracy-\(h\) parent

\[ P=\prod_{u=1}^{h}\left(1-\sum_{i\in A,\ v\text{ high}} b_{u,iv}(1-P_{iv})\right), \qquad W=h(2h+1). \]

Write \(\Gamma\) for this entire two-level system. Its upper companions are \((1-P_{iv})P\), each of original joint degree \(W+2h\). Fresh disjoint coefficient rows give \(\deg(P)=W\) before Boolean reduction. For a prospective complete accuracy-\(h\) child with sole input \(P\), define

\[ w_{\rm child}=h(W+1),\qquad e=w_{\rm child}+W, \qquad B=W+2h+K+2. \tag{WV-parameters} \]

Working counterexample. Assume \(h\ge 1\) and

\[ K\ge2e-1,\qquad N\ge2(B+2h)-1. \tag{WV-room} \]

Then all of the following hold:

\[ 1\notin\mathcal I_B(\Gamma),\qquad P\in\mathcal I_B(\Gamma),\qquad P\notin\mathcal I_e(\Gamma). \tag{WV-failure} \]

Thus, at \(D=B-W\), the single-parent criterion's larger cutoff is \(D+\deg(P)=B\), but its required implication for the input \(P\) fails. \(D\ge e\) under (WV-room). This is a failure within the allowed whole-value input class, with no raw coefficient polynomial used as an input.

2. A complete zero certificate at the larger cutoff

For each \(i,v\), combine the bottom and upper companions via the exact identity

\[ \beta_{iv}P=P(\beta_{iv}P_{iv})+ \beta_{iv}\bigl((1-P_{iv})P\bigr). \]

This gives \(\beta_{iv} P\) in \(\mathcal I_{W+2h+1}(\Gamma)\). If \(j\) is outside \(Q\), choose a high bit \(v(j)\) with \(j_{v(j)}=1\). The old same-row exclusions give \(X_{ij}\beta_{i,v(j)}-X_{ij}\) through degree two: the square term uses Booleanity and the other terms use same-row exclusions. Multiplying that identity by \(P\) and the previous certificate by \(X_{ij}\) yields

\[ PX_{ij}\in\mathcal I_{W+2h+2}(\Gamma)\qquad (i\in A,\ j\notin Q). \]

Consequently \(P\) times each confined row equation \(R_{i}-1\), where \(R_i=\sum_{j\in Q}X_{ij}\), has a certificate through \(W+2h+2\): subtract the outside-cell certificates from \(P\) times the original row equation. \(P\) times each column exclusion within \(A\)-by-\(Q\) has its original old certificate through \(W+2\).

The \((K+1)\)-by-\(K\) subsystem has an elementary ordinary NS refutation through \(K+1\). Indeed

\[ \prod_{i=1}^{K+1}R_i-1 =\sum_{i=1}^{K+1}(R_i-1)\prod_{j<i}R_j. \]

Every monomial in the expanded product repeats a hole on two distinct pigeons and is therefore a multiple of a column exclusion. Row multipliers have degree at most \(K\); exclusion multipliers have degree at most \(K-1\). Multiply this refutation by \(P\) and insert the certified weighted row equations above. The resulting degree is at most \(W+2h+2+K=B\), proving \(P\) in \(\mathcal I_B(\Gamma)\). This is a degree certificate; its full expansion can be large and is not an assertion of a small proof.

3. Why no zero certificate exists at the child's companion cost

Pin the \(N-K\) pigeons outside \(A\) bijectively to holes outside \(Q\). This is an ordinary matching restriction. The old functional system becomes the residual \((K+1)\)-by-\(K\) functional system, and every \(\beta_{iv}\) for \(i\) in \(A\) and high \(v\) becomes zero exactly. Set every bottom coefficient and every upper coefficient to zero. Then every \(P_{iv}\) and \(P\) becomes one; all bottom and upper companions become zero; all their coefficient field equations become zero.

This is a constant/variable restriction, so it does not increase ordinary NS degree. A hypothetical degree-\(e\) certificate for \(P=0\) would become a degree-\(e\) refutation of the residual old system. The normalized matching design through \(e\) exists because \(K\ge 2e-1\) and \(K+1\ge e\). It rules out that refutation. Hence \(P\) is not in \(\mathcal I_e(\Gamma)\). The same argument actually excludes zero certificates for \(P\) through any integer \(d\) with \(K\ge 2d-1\).

The larger retained system is still nonrefutable through \(B\). Apply the preceding two-level theorem at target \(B\). Here the prime is two, bottom rank bound \(R=1\), both accuracies are \(h\), \(S=1\) and its normalization factor \(T=1\). The required board inequality is exactly \(N\ge 2(B+2h)-1\); the other requirements \(B\ge W+2h\) and \(S\le W\) are automatic. Thus 1 is not in \(\mathcal I_B(\Gamma)\). The example therefore does not exploit an already-refuted retained base to falsify the input test.

4. The failing input test rejects a harmless child

Add the actual complete singleton child on input \(P\), with fresh coefficients \(c_{1},\ldots,c_{h}\) and product \(C=\prod_{u}(1-c_{u} P)\). Set \(c_{1}=1\) and all other \(c_{u}=0\). Then \(C\) maps to \(1-P\), and its companion \(PC\) maps to \(P(1-P)\). Every variable of \(\Gamma\) is Boolean, so Frobenius and monomial telescoping give

\[ P^2-P\in\mathcal I_{2W}(\Gamma). \]

Since \(2W\le e\), the companion image has a retained certificate within its original cost. Every child field equation maps to zero, and retained generators are fixed. Multiplying these witnesses by the images of legal cofactors proves degree-preserving elimination for old targets, in particular for a refutation. The child-augmented system therefore also has no degree-\(B\) ordinary NS refutation. This is the familiar singleton Boolean cleanup, applied as a positive control; it is not a new elimination mechanism.

Compatible asymptotic regime. Take \(h=\ell\) and choose \(K\) to be a power of two between \(4h^4\) and \(8h^4\). For sufficiently large \(\ell\), \(K\lt N=2^\ell\), \(K\ge 2e-1\) because \(e=O(h^3)\), and the second room condition holds because \(B=O(h^4)\). Both cutoffs and the number \((K+1)(\ell-t)\) of rank-one bottom blocks are polylogarithmic in \(N\). The lower bound on the degree of a zero witness for \(P\) grows as \(K/2\), while the child's original companion cost is \(O(h^3)\). Larger fixed polynomial choices of \(K\) produce still larger gaps. No exponentially large source inventory is hidden in this construction.

5. Route decision and significance

For general-step, the one-parent theorem remains valid, but its cheap-vanishing test is not a persistent invariant even for rank-one bottoms, decoded literal inputs, logarithmic accuracy and a singleton whole-value child. The raw filtration warning now has an actual whole-value counterpart with a tunable gap. This construction is related to the earlier whole-value zero certificate, but adds a residual-board lower bound and proves retained nonrefutability at the larger cutoff.

The control matters: failure of this test is not evidence that complete-source nonrefutability fails. It shows that forcing every semantically vanishing input to have a cheap zero certificate is stronger than the goal needs. The existing rank-one image already handles this child; clamping it to zero would discard useful structure. A successful iteration must allow such low-cost input images or another argument that does not require premature zero certificates.

Next step. Review the sufficient endpoint against this counterexample and the rank-dependent profile cost. Formulate a weaker multi-parent obligation that tolerates delayed whole-value zeros while still closing a fixed-depth degree recurrence. Check any proposed formulation against this confinement family and the generic ordering counterexample before testing further examples; neither conditional reformulation alone is progress on the general implication.

Process assessment. Testing the exact intended invariant produced a symbolic falsification without another finite enumeration. The removable-child control prevents confusing failure of a convenient criterion with failure of the sufficient lower-bound endpoint. No additional framework rule is needed: this follows the existing instruction to falsify the general claim before refining cases.

20 September 2026 — Historical PC elimination already supplies the stronger one-parent route

Route review and explicit corollaries of existing results. The single-parent proofs remain valid, but their application was narrower than an available historical PC argument. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and endpoint. For general-step, replace the failed persistent cheap-vanishing invariant by a sufficient argument that allows delayed zeros and ordinary PC reuse. The goal only needs a normalized complete-source NS functional. PC nonrefutability is a sufficient way to obtain one when it is already available; it need not be imposed as a universal extension property on every prospective construction.

1. An available result was missed in the one-parent comparison

The historical Theorem 7.6 (one-block additive elimination) says that a degree-\(D\) PC refutation after adjoining one complete ENS block, with maximum actual input degree \(\delta\), yields a retained PC refutation through \(D+(p-1)\delta\). The retained system may already contain other blocks and their field equations. The transformation has no rank or fan-in factor. Its output is a PC refutation, so the historical additive theorem composes it in reverse dependency order.

The proof was reread. Fix an input \(g_{j}\) and a nonzero \(a\), specialize its first coefficient to \(a^{-1}\) and all other fresh coefficients to zero, and weight the original proof by \(\Delta_{a}(g_{j})\). Companions become multiples of \(g_{j}^p-g_{j}\); field reduction handles them within \(D+(p-1)\delta\). The transformed conclusion derives \(\Delta_{a}(g_{j})\). Summing these derived polynomials with their field-value coefficients derives \(g_{j}\). Repeat for every used input, then zero-specialize the original proof and reuse the derived inputs as its starting lines. The inserted derivations need not be flattened and multiplied by every later cofactor: PC reuses their final polynomials. That is exactly the distinction the new cheap-NS-witness test unnecessarily tried to bypass.

Correction to the recent progress assessment. The conditional NS criterion remains correct and has a different premise for arbitrary retained systems. However, the bounded-rank application already follows more strongly from the historical PC transformation plus its own complete bottom normalization: the extra \(S\le w\) assumption is unnecessary. Its proof did not establish a previously missing one-parent endpoint. The whole-value counterexample remains correct, but refutes a convenience that the available PC transformation never required. It does not invalidate that transformation.

The historical result was also linked by the continued-research old-consequence transfer and explicitly used in the earlier few-block audit. The missed comparison is therefore a retrieval/process error, not a newly discovered elimination principle. The exact combinations with the current affine endpoints are recorded next to make the usable budget explicit.

2. Existing elimination plus the current affine endpoints

Let \(\Gamma_{0}\) contain an old base and an arbitrary family of complete old-affine bottom blocks. Above it, allow \(q\) complete ENS blocks in any acyclic dependency order, with all coefficient field equations and maximum actual input degrees \(\delta_{1},\ldots,\delta_{q}\). Earlier retained coefficients may occur in later inputs; the elimination statement only needs freshness in reverse order. Set

\[ A=(p-1)\sum_{a=1}^q\delta_a,\qquad E=D+A. \tag{RE-additive} \]

A degree-\(D\) PC refutation of the full system yields a degree-\(E\) PC refutation of \(\Gamma_{0}\). Ordinary degree-\(D\) NS refutations are included, since each original generator multiple has a PC derivation within its ordinary product degree. There is no unproved NS-to-PC closure identification here.

Endpoint A: bounded affine rank over the old unary functional base. Let the base have \(N+1\) rows and \(N\) holes over \(\mathbb F_p\); suppose the bottoms have common accuracy \(h\), proper nonconstant affine input spaces of ranks at most \(R\), and put

\[ T=\max\!\left(1,\left\lceil\frac{(p-1)R}{h}\right\rceil-1\right). \]

If \(N\ge 2TE-1\), the full system has no degree-\(D\) PC or NS refutation (take \(E\ge 1\)). There is no condition comparing \((p-1)R\) with the degree of an upper parent.

Proof. First eliminate every upper block by the historical additive transformation. Then apply the complete affine-bin normalization to all bottoms simultaneously. Its coefficient images have degree at most \(T\). Every companion image has an old Boolean/field certificate through \(T\) times its original companion degree, and every coefficient field image through \(pT\). Old axioms are fixed. A primitive multiplication step of the remaining degree-\(E\) PC proof has a predecessor of degree at most \(E-1\); its substituted predecessor has degree at most \(T(E-1)\), and multiplying by a variable image costs at most \(T\). Therefore the full replay, including its generator certificates, stays through \(TE\) and ends at one. The old matching design and PC stability exclude that refutation under \(N\ge 2TE-1\). This proves the endpoint and verifies the needed PC version of the normalization, not merely an NS substitution.

Endpoint B: arbitrary affine ranks in compact bits. Let \(\Gamma_{0}\) instead be the compact base \(\mathcal Q_{n,p}\), \(n=2^\ell\), \(m=n+1\), with at most \(M\ge 1\) complete old-bit-affine blocks of common accuracy \(h\ge 3(p-1)\ell\). Their ranks are unrestricted. If an integer \(k\) satisfies

\[ k\ge\max\{1,\lceil\sqrt{m\ln(4M)}\rceil\},\quad k\le m,\quad 4(k-1)<n,\quad n\ge2k(E+1)-1, \tag{RE-bit-range} \]

the full system has no degree-\(D\) PC or NS refutation. Indeed reverse elimination gives a degree-\(E\) refutation of \(\Gamma_{0}\), whereas the all-prime affine-level theorem at target degree \(t=0\) excludes one in its transported old space \(J_{0}\). No arbitrary-unary-affine assertion is imported from this bit-specific endpoint.

For polynomial \(M\), \(k=O(\sqrt{n \log n})\). Thus \(D+(p-1)\sum_{a} \delta_{a}=o(\sqrt{n/\log n})\) is a sufficient asymptotic range. In particular, polylogarithmically many upper blocks of polylogarithmic input degree are covered over every fixed prime, at any fixed depth with such an inventory bound. A single upper parent has no bottom-rank restriction under Endpoint B. These are applications of recorded results, not new elimination mechanisms or novelty claims.

3. Falsification and the actual remaining cost

The proposed persistent cheap-vanishing property is false by the preceding confinement example. The historical proof passes that test because it reuses PC consequences, and the explicit singleton-child image is consistent with it. The next tempting replacement, charging only a maximum degree or dependency depth for arbitrary upper blocks, is not supplied by (RE-additive). Balancing the transformations still adds their charges. The ordering-source counterexample also rules out a generic replacement depending only polynomially on \(D\), \(h\) and log inventory for arbitrary PC-hard old bases. Any successful large-batch theorem must use PHP geometry or the actual proof-source structure.

For the main goal, a polynomial-size Frege proof can produce polynomially many upper blocks. Their input degrees are polylogarithmic at fixed depth, but \(\sum_{a} \delta_{a}\) can already exceed \(\sqrt{n/\log n}\). Therefore neither endpoint above reaches arbitrary polynomial source inventory. This is the real outstanding obligation, rather than one-parent existence or a mandatory cheap-zero theorem.

The historical nested-span batches and core–residual batches already improve the sum for suitable input geometry. A core–residual batch changes a current degree bound \(d\) to \(T_{batch} d+(p-1)\gamma_{batch}\), with its recorded residual-rank and accuracy hypotheses. Composing those actual transformations requires the product-weighted additive ledger, not just the number of levels. No assertion that all compiler sources admit an affordable schedule follows from their existence.

4. Route review and next test

General claim under review. Complete fixed-depth polynomial-inventory PHP sources exclude their compiled polylogarithmic NS degree. The attempted cheap-input invariant was a stronger convenience and is rejected. A sufficient PC route remains available when reverse elimination reaches either affine endpoint within its explicit budget. A direct simultaneous NS functional remains another sufficient endpoint and does not require PC preservation.

Assessment of this line. Per-block and bounded-inventory PC elimination are already settled tools. Further one-parent examples will not address the polynomial-inventory gap. The source-specific batching direction has a precise remaining quantitative question, but no general compression theorem has been proved. This review recovers a stronger baseline and removes an unnecessary detour; it does not establish a new large-inventory lower bound.

Next mathematical task. Audit whether the actual coherent compiler imposes any sufficient nested-core or quotient-core structure on a same-level upper family. State an exact candidate geometric implication and its cost before testing it. Attempt to realize a large incomparable family through legitimate shared proof formulas; if the implication fails, record that failure and stop rather than subdividing the family into more examples. The required endpoint is a final degree below the affine barrier in (RE-bit-range), not a syntactically simpler source.

A bounded improvement is to surface historical matches in the ordinary claim-search display, using local historical statements without reimporting the handoff. 20 September 2026 — Coherent upper spreads defeat raw cores but have a cheap shared-bit image

Working compiler-geometry counterexample and complete shared-bit sum transfer. The costly raw criterion is not a lower bound on elimination or on proofs. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, test the claim that coherent fixed-depth formula syntax itself forces affordable same-level nested cores. The historical spread already refutes this for unrestricted affine data. Here it is realized on genuine whole bottom values in shallow formula syntax. The test also includes a complete, inexpensive normalization, so it does not mistake a raw-coordinate obstruction for a hard source. Stop at that distinction, not a claim that the blocks occur essentially in a short PHP refutation.

1. A spread among genuine upper input spaces

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\), with \(N=2^\ell\) large and \(N+1\) PHP pigeons. Put \(d=\ell\), \(q=\lfloor N/(2\ell)\rfloor\) and \(r=qd\), so \(2r\le N\). Select old label bits \(x,y_{1},\ldots,y_{2r}\), one from each of \(2r+1\) distinct pigeons. For each \(j\), make a complete accuracy-\(h\) bottom block on \((x,y_{j})\), with whole product \(P_{j}\) of original degree \(\delta=2h\), and disjoint fresh coefficient variables.

The map from \(\mathbb F_2^{2r}\) to the ordinary polynomial ring sending its jth coordinate to \(P_{j}\) is injective, even modulo the vector space of old-only polynomials. Indeed the top coefficient monomial using all \(h\) coefficients of \(x\) in block \(j\) has old coefficient \(x^h\) and occurs in no other \(P_{k}\). A nonzero linear combination therefore retains a fresh monomial and has actual joint degree exactly \(\delta\). This statement is before Boolean reduction and before using any bottom companions.

Identify \(\mathbb F_2^{2r}\) with \(K^q\oplus K^q\) for \(K=\mathbb F_{2^\ell}\). For each of the \(N\) distinct \(\alpha\) in \(K\), take the \(r\)-dimensional graph space

\[ V_\alpha=\{(u,\alpha u):u\in K^q\}. \]

Two such spaces meet only at zero: equality of \((u,\alpha u)\) and \((v,\beta v)\) gives \(u=v\) and \((\alpha-\beta)u=0\). Map a binary basis of each \(V_{\alpha}\) into the corresponding linear combinations \(g_{\alpha,i}\) of the \(P_{j}\), and give that tuple a complete accuracy-\(h\) upper block. Its maximum input degree is \(\delta=2h\). Pairwise intersections remain zero in the actual polynomial input spaces and modulo any old-only subspace.

Formula realization. Each \(P_{j}\) is the selector for the NOR formula \(\neg(x\lor y_j)\). Each \(g_{\alpha,i}\) is the parity of a specified subset of these NOR values, representable by a MOD2 gate. An upper OR of the \(r\) chosen parity formulas has exactly that selected input tuple in the coherent registry. There are \(N\) upper formulas, each using at most \(O(r^2)\) written child occurrences, hence polynomial total size and constant depth. Sharing the bottom formulas preserves coherence; intermediate OR subgroups do not remove the selected full tuples. Individual tautologies \(F_\alpha\lor\neg F_\alpha\) can contain these subformulas in legitimate proof syntax.

This realizes the geometry in shallow syntax; it does not show that it survives proof simplification, that every selected block is used by a compiled certificate, or that it occurs essentially in a short PHP refutation. Those stronger assertions would require separate evidence.

2. Exact cost of the raw nested-core criterion

Apply only the historical core–residual batch transformation to this selected upper family, without first rewriting its bottom values or quotienting by supplied relations involving them. Every nonzero input/core/residual direction has actual degree \(\delta\). Set

\[ T_r=\max\{1,\delta(\lceil r/h\rceil-1)\}. \]

For incoming degree \(D\), the best bound supplied by that criterion over all orders, batches and core choices is

\[ \min\{D+N\delta,\ T_rD\}. \tag{CS-raw-cost} \]

Proof. In a batch containing two selected spaces, the earlier core is contained in both and must be zero. Its residual then has rank \(r\), forcing a multiplicative factor at least \(T_{r}\). The same factor is forced by any zero-core selected singleton. If such a step occurs, all other steps are nondecreasing, so the final bound is at least \(T_rD\). Otherwise every selected block has a nonzero core and lies in a different batch from every other selected block. Each of the \(N\) batches pays at least \(\delta\) additively, so the bound is at least \(D+N \delta\). Full-core singleton batches attain the first expression; one zero-core batch attains the second. This is the historical spread-cost argument with nonlinear direction degree \(\delta\), not a new ordering principle.

For \(h=\Theta(\log N)\), \(r=\Theta(N)\), and \(D\) at least the original upper companion degree \(h(2h+1)+2h\) but polylogarithmic in \(N\), both choices exceed the affine endpoint's \(O(\sqrt{N/\log N})\) budget. Old-only quotient directions do not change the raw intersection calculation above. Quotients by actual retained bottom consequences and changes of source representation are deliberately outside this criterion audit; the next section supplies such a change.

3. Complete shared-bit normalization also permits arbitrary sums

Working transfer. Over any \(\mathbb F_p\) with old Boolean variables \(x,y_{j}\), take complete accuracy-\(h\) bottoms on \((x,y_{j})\), \(h\ge 1\). Allow arbitrarily many accuracy-\(h\) parents whose inputs are arbitrary homogeneous \(\mathbb F_p\)-linear combinations of these bottom whole products. There is an affine variable substitution into one complete old-affine core per parent that transfers every ordinary NS or PC proof through \(D\) to a proof through the same \(D\). All original companions, coefficient fields, sharing and overlaps are retained.

This extends the displayed direct-product inputs of the shared-bit transfer to arbitrary sums by the same common-factor identities. In the binary case it is also a special case of the broader rank-two-bottom theorem; no independent novelty claim is made.

Bottom map. Write \(\chi=1-x\) and \(L_{j}=1-y_{j}\). For \(h\ge 2\), set the coefficient of \(x\) in the first row to one, the coefficient of \(y_{j}\) in the second row to one, and all other bottom coefficients to zero. Then \(P_{j}\) maps exactly to \(\chi L_{j}\). For \(h=1\), use the existing affine assignment \(r_{x}=1\), \(r_{y}=\chi\), with the same exact product image. Both bottom companion images have old Boolean certificates through three, within their original degree \(2h+1\). Coefficient field images vanish or, for the affine coefficient \(\chi\), have a Boolean certificate through \(p\).

If a parent input is \(g_{i}=\sum_{j} a_{ij} P_{j}\), its image is \(\chi L_{i}\) with \(L_{i}=\sum_{j} a_{ij} L_{j}\) old-affine. Introduce a complete accuracy-\(h\) core on the original tuple of \(L_{i}\), with product \(A=\prod_{u}(1-V_{u})\), \(V_{u}=\sum_{i} R_{ui} L_{i}\), companions \(L_{i} A\), and coefficient fields. Rename the original parent coefficients to the \(R_{ui}\). Its product image is

\[ Q=\prod_{u=1}^h(1-\chi V_u). \]

Let \(B_{x}=x^2-x=\chi^2-\chi\). Expanding by subsets shows that

\[ Q-(x+\chi A) =\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq[h]}(-1)^{|S|} (\chi^{|S|}-\chi)\prod_{u\in S}V_u. \]

The right side is a multiple of \(B_{x}\) with a certificate through \(3h\), because \(\deg(V_{u})\le 2\); the size-one terms vanish. Further,

\[ \chi L_i(x+\chi A)=\chi(L_iA)+B_xL_i(A-1). \]

Thus the actual companion image \(\chi L_{i} Q\) has a certificate through \(\max(3h+2,2h+3)=3h+2\). Its original degree is \(h(2h+1)+2h=2h^2+3h\), which is at least \(3h+2\) for \(h\ge 1\). Parent field equations are simply renamed. Every variable image is affine and every generator image has a certificate at its own original cost. NS cofactors and primitive PC multiplication therefore replay without degree increase. Zero or redundant input positions cause no difficulty; the full original tuple is used, so no uncharged change of generators is hidden.

The spread family of Section 1 is a special case of this theorem. On the compact PHP base, with common \(h\ge 3(p-1)\ell\) and polynomial inventory, the resulting affine cores fall under the affine endpoint. The selected complete two-level spread system therefore has no polylogarithmic-degree NS or PC refutation for sufficiently large \(N\), despite its expensive raw core decomposition. This conclusion concerns the two-level system and its same-level subgroups, not unspecified later blocks reading the new parent values.

4. Outcome and next general obligation

For general-step, coherence alone does not force the affordable raw nested-core geometry. The historical spread can be realized on genuine formula values, and the expensive bound is entirely compatible with a degree-preserving alternative representation. This is a limitation of the raw criterion, not a new lower bound for Frege or an obstruction to every proof-informed batching method.

The shared-bit sum identity is a useful, explicitly costed tool, but its binary scope was already covered by the rank-two endpoint. Repeating more raw spread examples would not advance the goal. Any renewed core theorem must specify the permitted retained relations or semantic preprocessing, and prove their cost; formal input rank by itself is not a sufficient progress measure.

Next step. Return to the first unhandled nonlinear endpoint after the current quadratic theorem. Read the parked cubic residue and target-variation obstructions, then test a proposed degree-induction mechanism against them before specializing it to another low degree. The required implication is a source-relative or separated-old-target step with costs that compose, not a list of depth-specific examples.

The historical-search fix was implemented and passed all 24 focused registry tests before this mathematical test; it immediately recovered the spread result, so the current construction is labeled as its application. Search previews are bounded and do not replace source reading. The positive normalization control avoided interpreting a large raw criterion cost as evidence of source hardness.
