20 September 2026 — Finite-domain branch interpolation reaches a low-rank cubic endpoint

Working complete-transfer theorem and binary cubic source endpoint, using an imported cubic-space structure lemma. Unrestricted cubic spaces and retained multilevel inputs remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, test a degree-reduction mechanism that could extend the old-quadratic endpoint: represent a low-complexity input space using a small common set of lower-degree features, then replace each feature-value branch by a complete lower-degree source block. Unlike a sequence of isolated degree cases, the transfer lemma below works at arbitrary input degrees and over every prime. The endpoint application is binary and requires a uniform bound on the cubic rank of every combination in each input space. Stop at that exact condition and its budget; do not claim the high-rank or full multilevel case.

1. The relevant structural input

The parked cubic residue and RHS variation results concern degree-three falls after imposing affine equations on an old quadratic system. They do not give a structure theorem for cubic ENS input spaces. In particular, lack of full filtration stability is not itself failure of the sufficient NS endpoint.

Imported statement. Haramaty–Shpilka, On the Structure of Cubic and Quartic Polynomials, Definition 4.1 and Lemma 5.1, use \(\operatorname{rank}_3(f)=\min\{s:f=\sum_{j\le s}l_jQ_j+Q_0\}\), with linear \(l_{j}\) and quadratic \(Q_{j}\). For a vector space \(S\) of degree-at-most-three polynomial functions over \(\mathbb F_2\) with \(\operatorname{rank}_3(f)\le r\) for every \(f\) in \(S\), there are common quadratics \(Q_{1},\ldots,Q_{a}\) and common linears \(L_{1},\ldots,L_{b}\), where \(a\le r\) and \(b=2^{O(r)}\), such that

\[ f=\sum_{j=1}^a l_{f,j}Q_j+\sum_{j=1}^b L_jQ_{f,j}+Q_{f,0}. \tag{HS-space} \]

The coefficients \(l_{f,j}\) are linear and \(Q_{f,j}\) are quadratic. The statement and function-ring convention were checked; its proof is imported, not independently reproved. The retrieved PDF identifies arXiv v4, 1 January 2010, and also prints 15 June 2021 on its title page; the exact local copy and hash are recorded. No identification with an unchecked journal typesetting is made.

2. Complete transfer through a polynomial partition

Working theorem. Work over \(\mathbb F_p\). The retained old system \(\Gamma\) contains the domain equations for every old variable: Boolean equations or full field equations, defining their product domain \(\Omega\). Consider one level of complete ENS blocks on polynomials in those old variables only. In block \(a\) the accuracy is \(h_{a}\ge 1\), nonzero input \(i\) has actual degree \(d_{ai}\), the maximum is \(\delta_{a}\), and its original companion degree is

\[ e_{ai}=h_a(\delta_a+1)+d_{ai}. \]

Zero tuples and all-constant tuples may first be removed by the existing scalar cleanup. For each remaining block suppose a finite family of old polynomials \(\chi_{a,\sigma}\), of degree at most \(\kappa_{a}\), is exactly one-hot on \(\Omega\): at every old domain point one selector is one and all others are zero. Suppose branch input polynomials \(g_{a,\sigma,i}\) satisfy

\[ \deg g_{a,\sigma,i}\le d_{ai},\qquad q_{ai}(x)=g_{a,\sigma,i}(x)\quad \text{whenever }x\in\Omega,\ \chi_{a,\sigma}(x)=1. \tag{FB-compare} \]

Then the full system transfers to \(\Gamma\) plus one complete branch block per \(\sigma\), of the same accuracy and on the original ordered tuple of \(g_{a,\sigma,i}\), through degree \(D'=TD\), with \(T=1+\max_{a} \kappa_{a}\). The statement covers ordinary NS and PC, every coefficient field equation, all companions, arbitrary input overlap, and raw coefficient uses. Branches need not be nonempty or independent, and different blocks may use different features. No successor block depending on the replaced coefficients is silently treated as unchanged.

Map and companion certificates. Give every branch fresh coefficients \(R_{a,\sigma,u,i}\), product \(A_{a,\sigma}\), companions \(g_{a,\sigma,i}A_{a,\sigma}\), and their field equations. Fix every old variable and map

\[ r_{a,u,i}\longmapsto\beta_{a,u,i} =\sum_\sigma\chi_{a,\sigma}R_{a,\sigma,u,i}. \]

Each image has degree at most \(\kappa_{a}+1\). At an old point in \(\Omega\) this selects exactly one branch, while keeping all \(R\)'s as formal indeterminates. Therefore

\[ q_{ai}\Phi(P_a)-\sum_\sigma \chi_{a,\sigma}g_{a,\sigma,i}A_{a,\sigma} \]

vanishes coefficientwise in those indeterminates on the entire old product domain. Divide only by the monic old domain equations. The remainder is zero, and division does not increase total degree, including degrees in \(R\). Thus this difference has an ordinary old-domain certificate through \(e_{ai}+h_{a} \kappa_{a}\): its first term has at most that degree, and its branch terms have degree at most \(\kappa_{a}+e_{ai}\). The masked branch companion multiples have the same ceiling. Since \(e_{ai}\ge h_{a}\), this is at most \((\kappa_{a}+1)e_{ai}\le T e_{ai}\). Branch inputs of smaller collected degree do not reset the original cost.

Coefficient fields. Frobenius gives

\[ \beta^p-\beta= \sum_\sigma\chi_\sigma^p(R_\sigma^p-R_\sigma) +\sum_\sigma(\chi_\sigma^p-\chi_\sigma)R_\sigma. \]

The second sum has old-domain certificates because every selector is zero or one on \(\Omega\). All displayed certificates fit \(p(\kappa_{a}+1)\), which is \(T\) times the original field cost \(p\) or smaller. Old axioms are fixed. A substituted NS cofactor costs at most \(T(D-e)\), and its generator image costs at most \(Te\). For PC, a multiplication predecessor within degree \(D\) has degree at most \(D-1\); multiplication by its degree-at-most-\(T\) variable image stays through \(TD\). These observations prove the complete transfer. They use genuine certificates over the old domain, not vacuous semantic agreement on the unsatisfiable PHP system.

This is an extension of the existing branch interpolation and certified partition constructions to lower-degree polynomial branch tuples and nonlinear features. It is not a new case-splitting principle.

Feature realization. For features \(z_{1},\ldots,z_{t}\) over \(\mathbb F_p\), take all \(\sigma\) in \(\mathbb F_p^t\) and \(\chi_{\sigma}=\prod_{j}[1-(z_{j}-\sigma_{j})^{p-1}]\). These are one-hot on \(\Omega\), have degree at most \((p-1)\sum_{j} \deg(z_{j})\), and require \(p^t\) branch blocks. This explicitly charges both the degree factor and the inventory increase.

3. An unconditioned quadratic image for low-rank cubic spaces

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) with the compact PHP base \(\mathcal Q_n\), \(n=2^\ell\). Let a complete one-level family have at most \(M\) blocks, arbitrary positive accuracies, and inputs of ordinary degree at most three in old bits only. In each block, take the linear span \(S_{a}\) of the input functions after Boolean reduction. Assume every \(f\) in \(S_{a}\) has \(\operatorname{rank}_3(f)\le r\). Checking just the listed generators is not this hypothesis.

Use (HS-space) separately for each \(S_{a}\). Query the \(a_{a}\) common quadratic features and \(b_{a}\) common linear features. On a value branch \((u,v)\), replace an input \(f\) by

\[ g_{a,(u,v),f}=\sum_j u_j l_{f,j} +\sum_j v_j Q_{f,j}+Q_{f,0}, \]

which has degree at most two. For an original input already of ordinary degree at most two, simply keep that input on every branch, ensuring that no branch input exceeds its original individual degree. For a cubic whose Boolean reduction has smaller degree, that reduced representative also works. The comparisons hold on the whole old Boolean cube by the imported identity.

Put \(\kappa=\max_{a}(2a_{a}+b_{a})\), \(t=\max_{a}(a_{a}+b_{a})\), and

\[ D_*=(\kappa+1)D,\qquad M_*\le M2^t. \tag{LC-cost} \]

The complete-transfer theorem maps any degree-\(D\) NS or PC refutation to the unchanged compact base plus at most \(M_{*}\) complete old-quadratic blocks at degree \(D_{*}\). Apply the finite quadratic endpoint with these actual parameters. Whenever its inequalities hold, the cubic source has no degree-\(D\) refutation. The branch quadratics are all installed in the same target system; no feature values are imposed as new old-base axioms. Thus this argument does not assume a relative quadratic theorem for arbitrary conditioned PHP bases.

Asymptotic working consequence. For fixed exponents, polynomial \(M\), polylogarithmic \(D\), and \(r=O(\log \log n)\), the complete cubic family has no such refutations for all sufficiently large \(n\). Indeed \(\kappa,t\) are polylogarithmic, so \(D_{*}\) and \(\ln(M_{*})\) are polylogarithmic. The exponential number of branches is generally quasipolynomial, not declared polynomial.

Check against the finite quadratic inequalities. Let \(v=(n+1)\ell\), \(L=\ln(8M_{*}(v+1))\), choose \(a=\lfloor n^{2/9}\rfloor\), and \(k=\lceil v \sqrt{L/a}\rceil\). For sufficiently large \(n\), \(a\ge 1\) and \(k\ge 2\). The first image inequality is immediate from \(a k^2/v^2\ge L\). In the finite theorem, \(t_{0}=O(n^{4/9}(\log n)^2)\), \(c_{0}=O(n^{8/9})\), and \(k=n^{8/9}\operatorname{polylog}(n)\). Hence its total old degree \((t_{0}+2k+2c_{0}+1)D_{*}+k\) is \(o(n)\), while \(k\le n/16\) and \(\theta=o(1)\). Also \(k^2/v\ge vL/a\) grows as \(n^{7/9}\ell L\), dominating both \(t_{0} \ln 2\) and \(\ln(M_{*})\); the second image inequality holds eventually. The harmless condition \(D_{*}\ge \max(\ell,5)\) can be met by increasing the polylogarithmic target ceiling, and exclusion then implies exclusion at every smaller requested degree. This verifies the quasipolynomial-inventory use of the finite theorem rather than extrapolating its stated polynomial-inventory corollary.

4. What advanced and what did not

For general-step, there is now a complete, explicitly costed old-cubic endpoint for uniformly low-rank input spaces, obtained by a degree-reduction mechanism that applies beyond this particular degree. It allows arbitrary arity, overlap and block count within the stated inventory regime. The common feature bound depends on the rank of all input combinations, not on the number of written inputs.

The unrestricted cubic case is still open. The high-rank alternative would need a separated target or another affordable source image, and a general induction would have to control the growth of feature counts and branch inventories at every step. Actual deeper ENS inputs still involve retained coefficients; the present old-only theorem does not remove the relative surviving-rank premise. The ambient-cost obstruction also prevents declaring a free iteration by naming nonlinear features. No Frege lower bound follows yet.

Next step. Test the high-rank side of an input-space dichotomy at the level of the required general implication: does a sufficiently separated cubic family supply a common multiplier and a target that survive the PHP quotient at an affordable cost? State the rank notion and preservation requirement before any example. The low-rank branch is now a usable endpoint; a high-rank condition without a separated-target proof would not complete the step.

Reusing the existing partition map kept the algebraic work focused; no numerical enumeration or additional framework change was needed. The main source proof remains an imported dependency and the mathematical conclusions are working proofs, with no novelty or independent-review claim.

20 September 2026 — The quadratic budget permits logarithmic cubic rank

Working asymptotic refinement of the finite endpoint. The high-rank structural implication remains unproved; no quantitative universality theorem is imported. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, check the quantitative requirements of a high/low cubic-space dichotomy before trying to construct it. The first check reveals that the preceding low-rank endpoint used a smaller range than its finite inequalities permit. This cycle proves a larger branch budget, then records precisely what remains missing on the high-rank side. It ends before the user-requested presentation repairs.

1. A sufficient power-sized feature budget

Working corollary. Fix \(0<\varepsilon<1/13\). Suppose a complete binary old-only source over the compact PHP base admits the finite-domain branch transfer to quadratic branch inputs, with selector degree \(\kappa=O(n^\varepsilon)\), total branch inventory satisfying \(\ln M_*=O(n^\varepsilon)\), and original target degree \(D=\operatorname{polylog}n\). Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\), it has no ordinary NS or PC refutation through \(D\).

The constants in these asymptotic assumptions are fixed independently of \(n\). Every branch block is complete, and no constraints are added to the old PHP base. The exponent \(1/13\) is a sufficient range from the displayed estimates, not an asserted optimal threshold.

Proof. The transfer gives the unchanged compact base plus \(M_*\) complete old-quadratic blocks at degree

\[ D_*=(\kappa+1)D=O(n^\varepsilon\operatorname{polylog}n). \]

Choose a constant \(\alpha\) with

\[ 3\varepsilon<\alpha<\frac{1-\varepsilon}{4}. \tag{CB-alpha} \]

Such a choice exists because \(13\varepsilon<1\). In the finite quadratic theorem, write \(v=(n+1)\ell\), \(\ell=\log_2n\), and take

\[ L=\ln(8M_*(v+1)),\qquad a=\lfloor n^\alpha\rfloor,\qquad k=\left\lceil v\sqrt{L/a}\right\rceil. \tag{CB-choice} \]

For large \(n\), \(a\ge1\), \(k\ge2\), and its first image inequality follows immediately from \(ak^2/v^2\ge L\). Put \(\beta=1+(\varepsilon-\alpha)/2\). Then

\[ k=O(n^\beta\operatorname{polylog}n),\quad t_0=O(n^{2\alpha}(\log n)^2),\quad c_0=O(n^{4\alpha}). \]

Consequently the theorem's replay degree satisfies

\[ B=(t_0+2k+2c_0+1)D_*+k =O\!\left(n^{\max\{4\alpha+\varepsilon,\,\beta+\varepsilon\}} \operatorname{polylog}n\right)=o(n). \]

Both exponents are strictly below one by (CB-alpha). Also \(k=o(n)\), so \(k\le n/16\) and the theorem's cube-volume parameter obeys \(\theta=O(k/n)=o(1)\). The condition \(2a\le v\) is automatic.

For the second image inequality, use \(k^2/v\ge vL/a\), \(L\ge\ln M_*\), and \(L\ge\ln(8(v+1))\). Since \(\alpha<1/4\),

\[ \frac{t_0}{vL/a}=O(n^{3\alpha-1})=o(1),\qquad \frac{\ln M_*}{vL/a}\le\frac a v=o(1). \]

Thus \(\ln M_*+t_0\ln2-k^2/v\) tends to minus infinity, giving \(M_*2^{t_0}e^{-k^2/v}\le1/8\) eventually. All room inequalities, including \(B\le n/4\), now hold. Increase the original polylogarithmic ceiling if necessary to ensure \(D_*\ge\max(\ell,5)\); exclusion at that ceiling covers smaller requested degrees. The finite theorem proves the corollary. \(\square\)

2. Consequence for the common-feature cubic map

Working corollary. There is an absolute constant \(c_*>0\) such that complete binary ENS families on old-bit inputs of degree at most three, with polynomial block inventory and arbitrary positive accuracies, have no polylogarithmic-degree NS or PC refutations whenever

\[ \operatorname{rank}_3(f)\le c_*\log_2n \quad\text{for every }f\text{ in each block's input-function space}. \]

Proof. In the preceding imported common-feature bound, write the number of linear features as \(b\le C_1 2^{C_2r}\), with fixed positive constants \(C_1,C_2\), and the number of quadratic features as at most \(r\). Fix any \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/13)\), and choose \(c_*\) with \(C_2c_*<\varepsilon\). Then the prior branch construction has

\[ \kappa\le2r+C_1 2^{C_2r}=O(n^\varepsilon),\qquad t\le r+C_1 2^{C_2r}=O(n^\varepsilon),\qquad \ln M_*\le\ln M+t\ln2=O(n^\varepsilon). \]

Apply Section 1. This strengthens the earlier \(O(\log\log n)\) sufficient rank range; the earlier result remains valid. The common-feature identity and complete companion/field map are unchanged. The requirement still concerns all combinations in each input space, not only individual generators, and all inputs remain old-only. \(\square\)

3. The high-rank obligation is still substantive

The existing independent-triple quotient estimate asks for

\[ M(v+1)e^{-R_3k^3/v^3}\le\frac18. \]

Within its degree-room condition \(k\le n/16\), this particular estimate therefore requires

\[ R_3\ge(v/k)^3\ln(8M(v+1)) \ge4096\ell^3\ln(8M(v+1)). \]

For polynomial \(M\), that is an \(\Omega((\log n)^4)\) head count even at the largest permitted \(k\). This is a requirement of that sufficient counting argument, not a lower bound on all possible kernel constructions. Its \(R_3\) counts jointly independent cubic products; it is not the cubic rank \(r\) used by the low-rank theorem. No implication identifying those parameters has been proved.

A general cubic-space step must still produce an affordable structural split and a separated PHP target. Large rank of individual forms, a qualitative universality statement, or a change of coordinates alone would not establish the needed simultaneous hypotheses and costs. The screened high-rank-variety and slice-decomposition sources were not imported as supplying that theorem. In particular, the older rank-three-flat result remains about individual product inputs; it does not cover arbitrary sums automatically.

Outcome for the route. The quantitative low-rank branch is stronger than initially recorded, and its subexponential branch inventory is now justified directly. The high-rank branch and retained multilevel composition are unchanged open obligations. This is a parameter refinement, not completion of the cubic dichotomy or of the Frege lower bound.

Next research step. Formulate an exact input-space extraction theorem linking the high-rank alternative to a usable kernel map, with explicit loss and target-separation bounds. Test it against the existing independent-product scope and small-characteristic limitations before developing further examples. First perform the user's requested MathJax repairs between cycles.

20 September 2026 — High cubic rank does not force enough disjoint heads

Working structural counterexample and route review. The logarithmic-rank versus many-heads dichotomy fails; the counterexample itself has an affordable complete quadratic image. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

General claim and stopping point. For general-step, a sufficient cubic induction would reduce every complete old-cubic source to a separated old endpoint with degree below the PHP barrier. Test a concrete proposed analogue of the quadratic structural split: either the input space has uniformly small cubic rank, or actual input combinations have many disjoint cubic leading monomials after a binary affine change of coordinates. The low-rank branch is available only within its recorded budget; a high-rank assertion must meet the required head count. Stop at a proved implication or a counterexample, including a check that the obstruction is to the method rather than to source hardness.

1. An arbitrary-dimensional space with a head bottleneck

Working proposition. Let \(L,a\ge1\). Use distinct Boolean variables \(x_s,y_{js},z_{js}\), for \(s\le L\) and \(j\le a\), and let

\[ q_j=\sum_{s=1}^{L}x_s y_{js}z_{js},\qquad W=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_2}\{q_1,\ldots,q_a\}. \tag{CH-family} \]

This space has dimension \(a\). For the cubic function rank used in the common-feature lemma, every nonzero \(q\in W\) satisfies

\[ \left\lceil L/3\right\rceil\le\operatorname{rank}_3(q)\le L. \tag{CH-rank} \]

Nevertheless, after any invertible binary affine coordinate change, and for any degree-compatible monomial order, at most \(L\) nonzero members of \(W\) can have pairwise disjoint leading cubic monomials in their multilinear representatives. Adding unused old coordinates does not alter these conclusions. On the positive side, fixing the \(L\) common coordinates \(x_s\) makes every member of \(W\) quadratic, on every value branch.

Here a leading head belongs to an actual constant input combination; individual summands are not silently added as generators. The proposition concerns old polynomial functions, not retained ENS coefficients. It does not assert that the example is used essentially by a short PHP proof.

2. Lower rank bound by a self-contained diagonal-tensor argument

First consider \(q=\sum_{s=1}^{L}x_sy_sz_s\). Its mixed third additive derivative, in directions supported respectively on the three variable groups, is the trilinear form

\[ T(u,v,w)=\sum_{s=1}^{L}u_sv_sw_s. \]

If \(q=\sum_{i=1}^{r}\lambda_i Q_i+Q_0\) as Boolean polynomial functions, with each \(\lambda_i\) affine-linear and each \(Q_i,Q_0\) of degree at most two, this derivative is a sum of at most \(3r\) slices. Each product contributes a slice linear in \(u\), a slice linear in \(v\), and a slice linear in \(w\); its affine constant and the quadratic remainder contribute no third derivative. This argument works in characteristic two without division by a factorial.

We prove directly that the diagonal trilinear form needs at least \(L\) such slices. Suppose a slice expression uses \(r_x,r_y,r_z\) slices of the three types and \(r_x+r_y+r_z<L\). Let \(U,V,Z\subseteq\mathbb F_2^L\) be the common kernels of their respective linear factors. Then

\[ \dim U\ge L-r_x,\quad \dim V\ge L-r_y,\quad \dim Z\ge L-r_z, \]

and the supposed expression makes \(T\) vanish on \(U\times V\times Z\). A row-echelon basis of \(U\), summed over all its basis rows, gives a vector \(u\in U\) with every pivot coordinate equal to one. Hence its support has size \(m\ge L-r_x\). Multiplication by this vector coordinatewise maps \(V\) to a space of dimension at least

\[ \dim(operatorname{diag}(u)V) \ge\dim V-(L-m) \ge m-r_y \ge L-r_x-r_y >r_z. \]

But the annihilator \(Z^\perp\) under the ordinary nondegenerate coordinate dot product has dimension at most \(r_z\). Thus some \(v\in V\) has \(\operatorname{diag}(u)v\notin Z^\perp\), and some \(w\in Z\) gives \(T(u,v,w)\ne0\), a contradiction. Therefore \(3r\ge L\).

For a nonzero combination of the \(q_j\), choose an index with coefficient one and set the \(y,z\) variables belonging to all other indices to zero. The result is the preceding diagonal cubic. Restriction cannot increase the minimum number of linear-times-quadratic summands, proving the lower bound in (CH-rank). The displayed common \(x_s\) factors give its upper bound. Distinct \(y_{js}z_{js}\) terms also prove \(\dim W=a\). This is an elementary use of the diagonal slice argument, not a claimed new tensor-rank principle.

3. Why affine coordinate changes cannot remove the bottleneck

Every original cubic lies in the ideal generated by \(x_1,\ldots,x_L\). After an invertible binary affine change of old coordinates, let \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_L\) be the independent homogeneous linear parts of their images. The degree-three part of any transformed multilinear representative lies in

\[ J=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_L,\ t_1^2,\ldots,t_v^2) \subseteq\mathbb F_2[t_1,\ldots,t_v]. \tag{CH-top-ideal} \]

Indeed its unreduced highest-degree part is a sum of \(\ell_s\) times quadratics. Multilinear reduction changes that highest-degree part only by terms divisible by squares: repeated variables reduce to lower degree. The square-zero ideal in (CH-top-ideal) records this highest-degree operation; it is not a replacement of the old Boolean axioms.

Fix the chosen monomial order. Row-reduce the \(\ell_s\) to monic linear equations with \(L\) distinct pivot variables. Each pivot is expressed using smaller nonpivot variables. Together with the squares of the nonpivot variables, these equations form a reduction system whose standard monomials are the squarefree monomials in the nonpivot variables. To verify this, substitute the pivot expressions and reduce the remaining squares. These substitutions decrease the monomial order. In characteristic two a square of a linear expression is the sum of its squared terms, so every original square also reduces to zero. The resulting quotient is exactly the square-zero polynomial ring in the nonpivot variables, whose squarefree monomials are linearly independent. Thus the remainder is unique, and the initial ideal of \(J\) is generated by the pivot variables and nonpivot squares.

The degree-three part under consideration is squarefree and belongs to \(J\). Consequently its leading monomial must contain a pivot variable. A nonzero member of \(W\) still has degree three after the coordinate change: otherwise the inverse affine change would make the original cubic a function of degree at most two. Degree compatibility makes its full leading monomial the leading monomial of this cubic part. Pairwise disjoint heads must use different pivot variables, so there can be at most \(L\). This proves the head bound for every allowed coordinate change and order.

4. The proposed quantitative dichotomy fails, but this source is easy

Take a desired head count \(R\ge2\), set \(L=R-1\), and take \(a\ge R\). The space has enough independent inputs, but has no \(R\) disjoint cubic heads in any allowed coordinates. Every nonzero combination has cubic rank at least \(\lceil(R-1)/3\rceil\). Hence a universal implication from minimum nonzero cubic rank to \(R\) heads cannot use a threshold at or below this number. This is stronger than the trivial counterexample of a one-dimensional high-rank input space.

The recorded triple image estimate, even at its maximal permitted \(k\le n/16\), requires a head count at least

\[ R_{\rm req}=\left\lceil4096\ell^3\ln(8M(v+1))\right\rceil, \qquad v=(n+1)\ell,quad n=2^\ell. \]

For polynomial \(M\ge1\), this is \(\Theta((\log n)^4)\). Use \(R=R_{\rm req}\), \(a=R\) in (CH-family). It needs only \((R-1)(2R+1)=O((\log n)^8)\) old coordinates and therefore embeds into the compact PHP bits for all sufficiently large \(n\). Its nonzero cubic ranks exceed any fixed \(c\log n\), while it has fewer than \(R_{\rm req}\) disjoint heads. Therefore the naive alternative “the whole input space has cubic rank at most \(c\log n\), or it supplies the required number of heads” is false.

Allowing a low-rank subspace of codimension smaller than \(a\) does not rescue that rank threshold: such a subspace is nonzero and inherits the same lower bound on every nonzero rank. This does not rule out a more flexible structural alternative, other kernel maps, a better image-dimension estimate, or low-dimensional exceptional inputs handled at their full cost.

Complete-source positive control. The example already falls under the existing branch transfer, without using the exponential common-feature estimate. Query the \(L\) bits \(x_s\), and for \(\sigma\in\mathbb F_2^L\) use

\[ \chi_\sigma=\prod_{s=1}^{L}\bigl(1-(x_s-\sigma_s)\bigr), \qquad g_{j,\sigma}=\sum_{s=1}^{L}\sigma_s y_{js}z_{js}. \]

These selectors are exactly one-hot on the entire old Boolean cube, have degree \(L\), and give the original input values on their branches. Branch inputs have degree at most two, below the original degree three. Thus a complete block of any positive accuracy maps to \(2^L\) complete quadratic blocks at proof-degree factor \(L+1\), including every companion and coefficient field equation. For a polynomial family of such blocks, with potentially different overlapping coordinate choices, the total target inventory is at most \(M2^L\). At the logarithmic-power parameters above, \((L+1)D\) and \(\ln(M2^L)\) are polylogarithmic when \(D\) is. The finite quadratic budget therefore excludes polylogarithmic-degree refutations of this whole family for sufficiently large \(n\). No feature values are imposed as new axioms on PHP.

This positive control is an application of the existing map, not a new source-hardness theorem. It shows exactly why high cubic rank must not be mistaken for the absence of cheap common features.

5. Route assessment and next obligation

What the main goal needs. A complete-source reduction with an affordable degree/inventory ledger and a surviving old PHP target, ultimately composable over retained earlier coefficients. The old-only cubic endpoint is an intermediate test of a possible general mechanism; it is not itself the Frege theorem.

Assessment of this line. The present two-branch rank proxy is inadequate: its advertised low threshold and required high head count leave a concrete gap. The imported exponential common-feature bound also does not certify an affordable feature budget merely by raising its scalar-rank parameter to this head scale. This is a limitation of those available estimates, not a claim that the exponential bound is sharp. Common-factor spaces can have cheap branches despite that large scalar rank. The cubic program remains plausible as a structural route, but no complete dichotomy or retained-system induction has been established; another specially normalizable example would not close either gap.

Next step on general-step. Audit whether an available theorem for bounded-degree input spaces gives an affordable alternative based on actual common-feature complexity and exceptional input-space dimension, rather than only scalar rank. Require explicit small-characteristic hypotheses and bounds that fit the existing complete branch map. Stop at an applicable quantitative statement or a documented missing implication before developing a new family of examples. If no such structural input is available, compare this route with the direct complete-source moment obligation before further parameter refinements.

Process assessment. The general implication was falsified before any high-rank universality import or computational search, and the existing branch map supplied the positive control. The current bounded retrieval and falsification guidance was sufficient; no new framework rule is warranted. Restoration and initial navigation preceded instrumentation briefly; a mistyped anchor lookup was corrected during the measured reading window.

20 September 2026 — Polynomial tensor compression is available; binary integration is still missing

Imported finite-field tensor theorem and working input-space compression. This gives common factors for polarized tensors, not yet old polynomial features or a stronger PHP endpoint. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, audit a quantitative replacement for the failed scalar-rank versus many-heads shortcut. A polynomial common-feature bound would permit much larger low-complexity spaces than the currently imported exponential bound. Test published tensor structure theorems against characteristic two and the exact feature identity needed by the complete branch map. Stop at an applicable statement plus its actual consequence, identifying any unproved conversion.

1. The tensor theorem has the required field scope

Imported statement. For each fixed order \(d\) and finite field \(\mathbb F\), there are constants \(C_d,A_d\) such that a multilinear tensor \(T\) satisfies

\[ \operatorname{prank}(T)\le C_d\max(1,\operatorname{arank}(T))^{A_d}, \qquad \operatorname{arank}(T)=-\log_{|\mathbb F|}\mathbb E\chi(T). \tag{TA-rank} \]

Partition rank counts products of multilinear factors on complementary nonempty groups of slots. The constants are independent of the dimensions of those slots. The precise source used is Janzer, arXiv:1902.11207v1, Definitions 1.7–1.9 and Theorem 1.10, printed pp. 4–5. It allows \(\mathbb F_2\); its separate polynomial conclusions, Theorems 1.4–1.6, assume degree below the characteristic. The passage on p. 5 from tensors to polynomials divides a diagonal polarization by \(d!\). Those latter conclusions cannot be imported for binary cubics. The theorem is used as published input, not independently reproved here; no optimal constant or exponent is claimed.

Lovett, The Analytic Rank of Tensors and Its Applications, Theorem 1.7(i) and Claim 3.1, gives \(\operatorname{arank}\le\operatorname{prank}\) over finite fields. Its statement and the deduction from subadditivity were checked. For the particular cubic bound below, an elementary direct bias estimate suffices, so no extra rank-comparison dependency is needed.

2. Package the entire input space into one tensor

Working lemma. Let \(V=\mathbb F_2^v\), and let \(W\) be a vector space of polynomial functions on \(V\) of degree at most three. Assume every \(f\in W\) has \(\operatorname{rank}_3(f)\le r\), where \(r\ge1\), with the recorded linear-times-quadratic convention. Define

\[ \mathcal T(f,u_1,u_2,u_3) =D_{u_1}D_{u_2}D_{u_3}f(0),\qquad D_u f(x)=f(x+u)-f(x). \tag{TA-package} \]

This is a four-linear tensor on \(W\times V^3\), and

\[ \operatorname{arank}(\mathcal T)\le3r,\qquad \operatorname{prank}(\mathcal T)\le P:=C_4(3r)^{A_4}. \tag{TA-cost} \]

One may take an integer ceiling for \(P\). There is a subspace \(W_0\subseteq W\) of codimension at most \(P\) on which the polarized input family has a decomposition into at most \(P\) terms. Each term has a factor independent of \(f\) that is either a linear form in one copy of \(V\) or a bilinear form in two copies. These are common tensor factors; the statement does not yet give common polynomial features on one copy of the old Boolean variables.

Proof of the bias bound. Fix \(f\). A cubic monomial contributes the sum of its six assignments to three direction slots, and lower-degree monomials contribute zero, so its third derivative is trilinear and independent of the base point. This also proves linearity in \(f\). Write \(f=\sum_{i=1}^{r'}\lambda_iQ_i+Q_0\), with \(r'\le r\). If \(\ell_i\) is the homogeneous linear part of \(\lambda_i\) and \(B_i\) is the bilinear polarization of \(Q_i\), then

\[ T_f(u,v,w)=\sum_{i=1}^{r'}\bigl[ \ell_i(u)B_i(v,w)+\ell_i(v)B_i(u,w)+\ell_i(w)B_i(u,v)\bigr]. \]

Let \(K=\bigcap_i\ker\ell_i\); its codimension is at most \(r\). Independent uniform \(u,v\) belong to \(K\) with probability at least \(2^{-2r}\). For each fixed \(u\in K\), the further equations \(B_i(u,v)=0\) impose at most \(r\) homogeneous linear constraints on \(v\in K\), and hence retain at least a \(2^{-r}\) fraction. On this event \(T_f(u,v,w)=0\) for every \(w\). Averaging the binary character over \(w\) yields zero for every nonzero linear functional and one for the zero functional. Therefore

\[ \operatorname{bias}(T_f) =\Pr_{u,v}[T_f(u,v,-)=0]\ge2^{-3r}. \]

Averaging this nonnegative bias over uniform \(f\in W\) gives \(\operatorname{bias}(\mathcal T)\ge2^{-3r}\). Apply (TA-rank) with order four and field \(\mathbb F_2\).

Common factors and the exceptional subspace. Orient each partition-rank term so that its first factor contains the \(f\)-slot. If the other factor uses all three direction slots, the first factor is a linear functional of \(f\) alone. Intersect the kernels of these functionals to obtain \(W_0\), with codimension at most the number of such terms. Every remaining complementary factor uses one or two direction slots, and is therefore a common linear or bilinear form. There are at most \(P\) terms in total. This proves the claimed normal form without requiring the individual minimal-rank decompositions of different \(f\)'s to agree. \(\square\)

3. Why this does not yet improve the polynomial feature bound

Diagonal evaluation is identically zero: for every binary function, \(D_x^2=0\), hence \(\mathcal T(f,x,x,x)=0\). The cubic \(f=x_1x_2x_3\) gives an exact control: its polarized tensor is nonzero at \((e_1,e_2,e_3)\), although its diagonal is zero. Polarization still determines its cubic part; the failure is of the diagonal inverse, not loss of all cubic information.

In a fixed coordinate basis, that information can be recovered by the ordered coefficient formula

\[ f_3(x)=\sum_{i<j<k}T_f(e_i,e_j,e_k)x_ix_jx_k. \tag{TA-integrate} \]

However, this linear recovery operation has not been shown to preserve a small common-feature decomposition. For example, a term \(\ell_f(u)B(v,w)\), with fixed bilinear \(B\), contributes

\[ \sum_i\ell_f(e_i)x_iQ_i(x),\qquad Q_i(x)=\sum_{i<j<k}B(e_j,e_k)x_jx_k. \]

The direct formula exposes up to \(v\) common quadratics from a single tensor factor, rather than a number controlled just by \(P\). This is not a lower bound on a better integration method. It identifies the missing estimate: exploit the symmetry and alternation of the full polarized family, including cancellations between partition terms, to obtain a polynomial feature bound independent of \(v\), or establish a precise obstruction. Merely naming all these coordinate-dependent quadratics incurs an ambient-sized feature allowance, which does not certify the existing \(O(n^\varepsilon)\), \(\varepsilon<1/13\), branch budget.

A successful lift must produce actual old polynomial identities modulo degree-two Boolean equations, with controlled exceptional input dimension. Only then can the complete branch transfer charge selectors, companion images, fields and branch inventory. Independent tensor copies are not extra old variables that may be adjoined without a proof.

4. Scope of the other screened sources

Polishchuk–Wang, Linear subspaces in cubic hypersurfaces, Theorems A–B on p. 1, concerns a homogeneous cubic in the ordinary polynomial ring and intersections of linear ideals. Its quadratic bound on the span of minimal factor spaces pertains to one cubic. It is not a statement about a whole Boolean function space modulo quadratic remainders. No common-feature theorem for our input spaces is inferred from it.

Karam, ITCS 2024, Small Sunflowers and the Structure of Slice Rank Decompositions, Theorem 12, pp. 67:12–13, bounds possible minimal slice-factor spaces for one tensor over a finite field. Its Section 6 formulates further support and partition-rank questions. The inspected result does not provide our polynomial common-feature bound for a varying family. This is a scope assessment of that version, not a claim that no later improvement exists. The newer journal record was located but not used as a theorem dependency.

5. Outcome and the next exact test

For general-step, we now have a dimension-independent polynomial bound for a tensor encoding the whole bounded-cubic-rank space, including a controlled exceptional input codimension. This is a useful intermediate structural statement, but it neither improves the established logarithmic-rank PHP endpoint nor resolves the high-rank alternative or retained multilevel composition. The obstruction is now an explicit binary integration problem rather than an unspecified appeal to tensor rank.

Next bounded task. Test whether the alternating symmetric four-tensor normal form above can be lifted to polynomially many common old linear/quadratic features and polynomial exceptional input codimension in characteristic two. First check known symmetrization results and the shared-factor and diagonal controls. Stop at a valid costed lifting lemma or a counterexample; if this conversion remains unsupported, compare with direct source moments instead of elaborating more special cubic inputs.

20 September 2026 — Rank cleaning lifts the binary tensor structure to common polynomial features

Working common-feature lifting lemma and power-rank old-cubic source endpoint. The unrestricted high-rank alternative and retained multilevel composition remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, resolve the precise binary integration gap: turn a small partition decomposition of the whole polarized cubic space into common old polynomial features without an ambient-dimension factor. The proposed mechanism removes low-rank bilinear factors, then uses uniqueness across the three slot placements to exploit exact symmetry and alternation. Stop at a proved lifting statement and its complete-source budget, not an unrestricted cubic or Frege lower bound.

1. Exact statement

Working lemma. Let \(W\) be a space of degree-at-most-three polynomial functions on \(V=\mathbb F_2^v\). Suppose its tensor

\[ \mathcal T(f,u,v,w)=D_uD_vD_w f(0) \]

has a partition-rank decomposition of length at most an integer \(P\ge1\). Then there are a subspace \(W_0\subseteq W\), common homogeneous linear forms \(L_1,\ldots,L_s\), and common quadratic polynomials \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_b\), with

\[ \operatorname{codim}_W W_0\le P,\qquad s\le P+8P^2,\qquad b\le2P, \tag{BL-count} \]

such that every \(f\in W_0\) has a Boolean function identity

\[ f=\sum_{j=1}^b\lambda_{f,j}Q_j +\sum_{t=1}^s L_t H_{f,t}+R_f, \quad \deg\lambda_{f,j}\le1,\quad \deg H_{f,t},\deg R_f\le2. \tag{BL-identity} \]

These are actual polynomials in the old variables. Representatives of degree at most three differ by ordinary old Boolean certificates through three. If \(P=0\), every member of \(W\) is already quadratic and no features are needed. The numerical bounds are sufficient, not optimized.

2. Remove the low-rank matrix directions once for the whole space

Orient every partition term so that one factor contains the \(f\)-slot. Terms whose other factor uses all three old-direction slots have a scalar linear functional of \(f\) as their first factor. Intersect these kernels to obtain \(W_0\), losing at most \(P\) input dimensions. Terms with a one-slot old factor have a common old linear form. Restrict all three old directions to their common kernel \(U_1\), losing at most \(P\) old dimensions. What remains consists of terms with a common old bilinear factor and a factor bilinear in \(f\) and the remaining old direction.

Let \(\mathscr B\) be the span of these common bilinear forms on \(U_1\), together with their transposes. Its dimension is at most \(2P\), and it is transpose invariant. We now shrink the old-direction space repeatedly. If the current restricted matrix space has a nonzero member of rank at most \(4P\), restrict both matrix arguments to its left kernel. This costs at most \(4P\) dimensions and kills that nonzero member, so the dimension of the image matrix space drops by at least one. Its transpose is killed too, because both arguments lie in the same left kernel. Transpose invariance persists.

There are at most \(2P\) such steps. On the final subspace \(U\subseteq U_1\), the resulting space \(\mathscr B_U\) has dimension \(b_0\le2P\) and every nonzero member has rank greater than \(4P\). The total old codimension is

\[ \operatorname{codim}_V U\le P+8P^2. \]

This is a greedy rank reduction in a fixed common matrix space; it is independent of \(f\). It does not require low rank of every original matrix, an extension field, or a union over all input combinations.

3. High matrix rank forces the common factors to be alternating

Choose a basis \(B_1,\ldots,B_{b_0}\) of \(\mathscr B_U\). First note that the three spaces of tensors of the following respective forms are in direct sum:

\[ \sum_j a_j(u)B_j(v,w),\qquad \sum_j b_j(v)B_j(u,w),\qquad \sum_j c_j(w)B_j(u,v). \tag{BL-slots} \]

Indeed, if their sum is zero, fix \(u\). The first term, as a matrix in \((v,w)\), is a member of \(\mathscr B_U\). The other two terms are each sums of at most \(b_0\) rank-one matrices. Thus the first term has rank at most \(2b_0\le4P\), forcing it to be zero. Independence of the \(B_j\) makes every \(a_j(u)\) zero, for every \(u\). Fixing \(v\) in the remaining equality similarly makes every \(b_j\) zero; then the \(c_j\) vanish. This elementary comparison is the same rank-separation principle seen in Karam's Proposition 11; here the direct argument is supplied and no minimal-decomposition hypothesis is used.

For each \(f\in W_0\), the restriction \(T_f|_{U^3}\) has a representation by (BL-slots), and it is symmetric under every permutation of the three old slots. Since the common matrix space is transpose invariant, those permutations preserve the three summand spaces and their direct-sum uniqueness applies. Swapping the first two slots identifies the first and second coefficient maps; swapping the last two identifies the second and third. Moreover, swapping the two arguments inside any common-matrix position shows that each coefficient-weighted matrix is symmetric. Thus there is one linear map \(A_f:U\to\mathscr B_U\), taking values in its symmetric matrices, such that

\[ T_f(u,v,w)=A_f(u)(v,w)+A_f(v)(u,w)+A_f(w)(u,v). \tag{BL-symmetric} \]

The original classical polar form also satisfies \(T_f(u,u,w)=0\). In (BL-symmetric) the first two terms cancel, so \(A_f(w)(u,u)=0\) for all \(u,w\). Every matrix in the image of every \(A_f\) is therefore alternating. Let \(S_1,\ldots,S_b\) be a basis of the alternating subspace of \(\mathscr B_U\), with \(b\le2P\). We can write

\[ A_f(u)=\sum_{j=1}^b\lambda_{f,j}(u)S_j. \]

Consequently all the surviving cubic polar forms have the same alternating bilinear factors. The case \(\mathscr B_U=0\) has the empty sum and is included.

4. Integrate the alternating factors and restore the removed coordinates

In a basis of \(U\), every alternating binary bilinear form \(S_j\) is the polarization of the quadratic

\[ Q_j(x)=\sum_{i<k}S_j(e_i,e_k)x_ix_k. \]

The polarization of \(\lambda_{f,j}Q_j\) is precisely the cyclic three-term expression occurring in (BL-symmetric). Hence the third derivative of \(f-\sum_j\lambda_{f,j}Q_j\), restricted to \(U^3\), is zero. For a binary function of degree at most three, this means its restriction to \(U\) has degree at most two: a cubic coefficient is its third derivative on the corresponding three distinct basis directions.

Extend the chosen coordinates on \(U\) linearly to \(V\), and use the extensions to define all \(Q_j\) and \(\lambda_{f,j}\) on the old space. Choose independent linear forms \(L_1,\ldots,L_s\) defining \(U\). Together with the extended coordinates they give an invertible binary coordinate system. The multilinear representative of

\[ f-\sum_j\lambda_{f,j}Q_j \]

has no cubic monomial involving only the \(U\)-coordinates. Assign every remaining cubic monomial to one of its \(L_t\) factors. Its remaining two-variable product contributes to \(H_{f,t}\); put every term of degree at most two into \(R_f\). This gives (BL-identity) as a Boolean function identity. All polynomials involved have ordinary degree at most three after returning to old coordinates. Their difference vanishes on the entire old cube, so monic division by the old Boolean equations certifies the identity through degree three. No cubic diagonal inverse and no ambient-sized list of quadratic prefixes is used. \(\square\)

5. The complete branch map pays a polynomial cost

Choose a complementary basis \(F_1,\ldots,F_e\) for \(W/W_0\), with \(e\le P\). Every original input is a constant combination of these exceptional cubics plus a member of \(W_0\). Query the common features \(L_t,Q_j,F_c\). Their number and total ordinary degree are bounded by

\[ t\le s+b+e\le8P^2+4P,\qquad \kappa\le s+2b+3e\le8P^2+8P. \tag{BL-branch-cost} \]

On any feature-value branch, (BL-identity) replaces each \(Q_j\) and \(L_t\) by its value, leaving a quadratic polynomial, while each exceptional \(F_c\) becomes a scalar. This yields a quadratic branch input agreeing with the original input on the full old-domain branch. If an original input already has ordinary degree at most two, retain that input on every branch to preserve its individual degree ceiling. Zero and constant cleanup is unchanged.

The binary feature selectors are products of \(1-(z-\sigma)\), of degree at most \(\kappa\). The complete branch theorem therefore maps all companions and coefficient field equations at every original positive accuracy, with proof-degree factor \(\kappa+1\). For \(M\) blocks with uniform decomposition bound \(P\), total branch inventory is at most \(M2^t\). Different blocks may use different features and overlap in old variables. The original PHP base is unchanged; queries are not new base axioms. No later block using retained coefficients is implicitly covered.

6. A positive-power cubic-rank endpoint

Working theorem. There exists an absolute \(\eta>0\) such that complete binary old-only ENS families over compact PHP, with polynomial block inventory, arbitrary positive accuracies and original input degree at most three, have no polylogarithmic-degree ordinary NS or PC refutations for sufficiently large \(n\), provided every input combination in every block satisfies

\[ \operatorname{rank}_3(f)\le n^\eta. \tag{BL-power-rank} \]

Proof and accounting. The whole-space tensor bound, using the imported finite-field theorem at order four, gives \(P\le C(1+r)^A\) for absolute fixed \(C,A\), which we may take with \(A\ge1\). The lifting lemma gives

\[ \kappa,t=O((1+r)^{2A}),\qquad D_*=(\kappa+1)D,\qquad \ln M_*\le\ln M+t\ln2. \]

Choose any fixed \(0<\eta<1/(26A)\), and then choose \(\varepsilon\) strictly between \(2A\eta\) and \(1/13\). Under (BL-power-rank), \(\kappa=O(n^\varepsilon)\) and \(\ln M_*=O(n^\varepsilon)\). The finite quadratic budget excludes the transferred proof. This proves the theorem with an absolute positive exponent; no optimized numerical exponent is asserted. \(\square\)

This strengthens the earlier logarithmic-rank endpoint. Its hypothesis still concerns every combination, not just generators, and still excludes neither arbitrary cubic input spaces nor retained higher levels. The shared-factor control is consistent with the new bound: its logarithmic-power rank is now inside the generic sufficient range. The nonzero diagonal-cubic control is handled by alternating quadratic integration, not by the invalid cubic diagonal formula.

7. Outcome and next obligation

For general-step, the specific binary integration gap is closed by a working proof with dimension-independent polynomial bounds. This yields a real enlargement of the proved restricted endpoint, from logarithmic to a positive power of scalar cubic rank, without limiting input arity. It does not prove a general cubic dichotomy or a composable Frege source reduction.

Next bounded task. Revisit a full cubic input-space structural split using this polynomial low-complexity bound. Before importing a high-rank extraction theorem, write one complete common-weight degree/inventory ledger for both branches and determine the quantitative collective-rank hypothesis it can afford. The head count and scalar rank remain distinct; the shared-factor counterexample still rules out their naive identification. Stop if the combined estimates do not fit, rather than proving an unnecessarily strong structural convenience.

Significance and checks. The common-feature lift is a reusable structural candidate deserving an independent proof and prior-art review; novelty is not established and no publication claim is made. The proof was checked for zero residual matrix space, transpose closure during restriction, uniqueness of the three slots, alternation, Boolean certificate degrees and exceptional-input costs. No finite enumeration or Lean verification was run. Tidor's low-characteristic inverse-theorem introduction was screened for context; no theorem from it is a dependency of this proof.

Process assessment. Working directly with the exact common tensor decomposition avoided importing a stronger approximate-symmetrization theorem. The existing proof-review and source-scope rules sufficed; no new framework rule is needed. The measured reading window includes source interpretation and initial mathematical development before the mathematics marker; the categories are not retrospectively reassigned.

20 September 2026 — Polynomial cubic extraction would fit one complete common-weight ledger

Working finite source criterion and conditional general cubic endpoint. A polynomial collective-rank extraction theorem is sufficient but has not been established or imported here. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, cost the full cubic structural split before seeking a high-rank theorem. The polynomial feature lift repairs the low case, but its branch count must coexist with the high-case kernel and the lower-degree normalizers. Stop at a complete finite criterion and a feasible sufficient extraction threshold; do not treat the missing threshold as proved.

1. A finite criterion preserving complete source blocks

Work over compact binary PHP with \(n=2^\ell\), \(\ell\ge2\), and \(v=(n+1)\ell\). There are at most \(M\ge1\) complete old-only ENS blocks with actual input degrees at most three and arbitrary positive accuracies. Suppose each nonconstant input tuple has one of these two descriptions:

  • High cubic: \(a_3\) constant combinations of its actual inputs have disjoint squarefree cubic leading monomials under a degree-compatible order, after a supplied invertible binary affine coordinate change.
  • Quadratic branches: at most \(t\) binary polynomial features, with total ordinary degree at most \(\kappa\), give one-hot selectors on the full old cube. On every feature-value branch the tuple agrees with a specified tuple of old quadratics. Each branch input has degree no greater than its original input. Empty branches are allowed.

All features and branch polynomials involve old variables only. Let \(a_2\ge1\), \(k\ge3\), and put

\[ d=\lceil\log_2(v+1)\rceil,\quad t_2=16a_2^2d^2,\quad c_2=\lceil C_{\rm BR}(a_2+1)^4\rceil, \] \[ N_2=M2^t,\qquad N_1=M2^{t+t_2},\qquad T=\kappa+t_2+2k+2c_2+1,\qquad B=TD+k. \tag{CL-cost} \]

Working finite theorem. There is no degree-\(D\) ordinary NS or PC refutation if

\[ D\ge\max(\ell,7),\quad 3a_3\le v,\quad2a_2\le v,\quad k\le n/16,\quad\theta\le1/2,\quad B\le n/4, \] \[ \theta=\frac{16(n+1)}n\left[\left(1+\frac{3k}v\right)^\ell-1\right], \tag{CL-room} \] \[ M(v+1)e^{-a_3k^3/v^3}\le1/8,\quad N_2(v+1)e^{-a_2k^2/v^2}\le1/8,\quad N_1e^{-k^2/v}\le1/8. \tag{CL-images} \]

2. One old multiplier for all stages

The fixed leading-monomial reduction extends directly to disjoint cubic heads. Reduce by the monic multilinear representatives of the selected actual combinations and the old Boolean equations, always decreasing the supplied degree-compatible order. Standard monomials are squarefree and avoid every selected triple, so their count through degree \(k\) is at most

\[ J_3(v,a_3,k)=\sum_{j=0}^k[z^j] ((1+z)^3-z^3)^{a_3}(1+z)^{v-3a_3}. \]

The triple counting estimate bounds this by \(\binom vk(v+1)e^{-a_3k^3/v^3}\). No exact quotient-dimension or Gröbner-basis claim is needed. A kernel element has a representation \(f=\sum_i c_iq_i+E\), with \(\deg c_i\le k-3\) and \(E\) an old Boolean consequence through \(k\). Representatives of actual cubic combinations differ by Boolean certificates through three. Pulling back a binary affine coordinate change preserves these ceilings.

For every quadratic feature branch, apply the quadratic dichotomy with parameter \(a_2\). Its high branches contribute at most \(N_2\) pair-reduction maps. Each low quadratic branch has at most \(t_2\) linear probes and input codimension at most \(c_2\), yielding at most \(N_1\) affine branch spaces. For every proper affine space of rank at least \(2k+3\), impose the same flat-restriction kernel as in the general quadratic proof, of relative image dimension at most \(e^{-k^2/v}\).

The three image sums in (CL-images) consume at most \(3\binom vk/8\), below the dimension \(\binom vk/2\) available in the cube-volume space \(\mathcal S_k\). Hence there is one nonzero \(f\in\mathcal S_k\) in all the kernels. Every map acts on the original old polynomial space; branch values are not imposed on PHP. Including empty branches only enlarges the safe upper bounds on the number of maps.

3. Interpolate coefficients once, with additive degree cost

As in the quadratic proof, set all source coefficient rows after the first to zero. This is a degree-nonincreasing specialization. On a high cubic tuple use the kernel cofactors, so its product is \(1-f\) as a Boolean function and all companions vanish where \(f=1\).

On each quadratic feature branch, use the quadratic simultaneous coefficient construction with this same \(f\). A high pair case uses its kernel cofactors. A low case combines the high-affine clamp or low-affine flat indicator with the at most \(c_2\) exceptional quadratics, then interpolates the linear probes. Every branch coefficient has degree at most \(t_2+2k+2c_2+1\), and its branch companions vanish on all old Boolean points where \(f=1\). Unit and zero spaces use the recorded scalar cleanup.

Now interpolate these coefficients with the original nonlinear feature selectors:

\[ \beta_i=\sum_{\sigma}\chi_\sigma\beta_{\sigma,i},\qquad \deg\beta_i\le\kappa+t_2+2k+2c_2+1=T. \tag{CL-map} \]

At each Boolean point exactly one feature selector is one. The selected quadratic tuple agrees with the original tuple at that point, so all mapped original companions vanish wherever \(f=1\). Every original coefficient has an old-only image; there is no retained dependency between these maps. Degrees in (CL-map) add. In particular, this proof does not first transform the entire refutation by \(\kappa+1\) and then multiply that degree by a second normalization bound.

For a nonzero original input of degree \(d_i\), tuple maximum \(\delta\le3\), and original accuracy \(h\ge1\), its original companion cost is \(e_i=h(\delta+1)+d_i\). After the row specialization, its weighted image has ordinary degree at most

\[ k+T+\delta+d_i\le k+Te_i. \]

It vanishes on the entire old Boolean cube, and therefore has an old Boolean NS certificate at that ceiling. Weighted coefficient fields have certificates through \(k+2T\). Old generators are fixed and weighted by \(f\). An NS cofactor through \(D-e_i\) then gives total cost at most \(TD+k\). For PC, simulate each line as \(f\Phi(p)\); a multiplication predecessor has degree at most \(D-1\), and its variable image costs at most \(T\). The complete replay derives \(f\) in old PC through \(B\), contradicting cube-volume separation under (CL-room). This proves the finite theorem.

4. An exact sufficient structural obligation

Unproved extraction hypothesis. Suppose there are fixed constants \(C,s>0\) such that, for every \(a\ge1\), an \(a\)-dimensional binary cubic input-function space whose every nonzero member has cubic rank greater than

\[ H(a)=C(a+1)^s \tag{CL-extraction-hypothesis} \]

supplies \(a\) actual input combinations with disjoint cubic leading heads after a binary affine change. No theorem asserting this hypothesis is imported in this entry. Scalar cubic rank, tensor partition rank, and head count must be matched explicitly in any subsequent source audit.

Conditional working corollary. This polynomial extraction hypothesis, together with the recorded tools, suffices to exclude every polylogarithmic-degree NS or PC refutation of polynomial-inventory complete binary old-cubic sources.

Structural proof under the hypothesis. In an arbitrary input space \(W\), choose a maximal subspace \(C_0\) whose nonzero elements have rank greater than \(H(a_3)\). If \(\dim C_0\ge a_3\), the hypothesis gives the high cubic case. Otherwise let \(A_0=\{q\in W:\operatorname{rank}_3(q)\le H(a_3)\}\). Maximality implies \(W=C_0+A_0\): a missing coset with no low-rank member would enlarge \(C_0\). Thus \(A_0\) has density at least \(2^{-a_3}\).

The recorded binary Bogolyubov–Ruzsa input gives \(W_0\subseteq4A_0\) of codimension \(c_3\le\lceil C_{\rm BR}(a_3+1)^4\rceil\). Cubic function rank is subadditive, by concatenating linear-times-quadratic expressions modulo quadratics; hence every \(q\in W_0\) has rank at most \(4H(a_3)\). The tensor bound followed by the binary lift gives feature number and total degree polynomial in \(H(a_3)\). Query also the at most \(c_3\) exceptional cubic inputs from \(W/W_0\), adding at most \(c_3\) features and \(3c_3\) degree. Consequently

\[ t,\kappa\le C'(a_3+1)^K \tag{CL-polynomial-low-cost} \]

for fixed constants \(C',K\), and we may enlarge \(K\) to have \(K\ge4\). This produces exactly the two alternatives of the finite criterion. Lower-degree original inputs can be left unchanged on every branch; actual source costs are preserved.

5. The simultaneous asymptotic budget is feasible

For polynomial \(M\), choose

\[ \gamma=\frac1{16K},\quad a_3=\lfloor n^\gamma\rfloor,\quad a_2=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor, \] \[ k=\left\lceil\max\left\{3, v\left(\frac{\ln(16M(v+1))}{a_3}\right)^{1/3}, v\sqrt{\frac{\ln(16M(v+1))+t\ln2}{a_2}}, \sqrt{v\bigl(\ln(16M)+(t+t_2)\ln2\bigr)} \right\}\right\rceil. \tag{CL-choice} \]

Each image sum is at most \(1/16\). The parameters obey

\[ \kappa,t=O(n^{1/16}),\quad t_2=O(n^{1/4}(\log n)^2),\quad c_2=O(n^{1/2}), \] \[ k=O\!\left(n^{1-1/(48K)}\operatorname{polylog}n\right),\qquad T=O\!\left(n^{1-1/(48K)}\operatorname{polylog}n\right). \]

Indeed the three nonconstant choices for \(k\) have exponents respectively \(1-1/(48K)\), at most \(31/32\), and at most \(5/8\), with logarithmic factors absorbed. For \(K\ge4\) the first is largest. Thus \(k=o(n)\), \(\theta=o(1)\), and \(TD+k=o(n)\) for every fixed polylogarithmic \(D\). The support and room conditions eventually hold. This proves the conditional corollary and shows that some fixed polynomial extraction threshold would suffice; an optimal exponent is unnecessary.

6. Outcome and next step

For general-step, the high and low cases now have one complete ledger with a positive degree saving. This removes a quantitative uncertainty that would otherwise make a structural source import premature. It is a conditional endpoint: the polynomial collective-rank extraction hypothesis remains open in this record, and retained earlier coefficients remain outside the old-only theorem.

20 September 2026 — Quantitative universality completes the binary old-cubic endpoint

Working general old-cubic source theorem using an imported universality statement. No rank, arity or factor-shape restriction remains on old cubic inputs; retained levels and odd primes remain outside it. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, check a published theorem against the exact polynomial extraction obligation. The needed conclusion is a simultaneous family of disjoint cubic heads with polynomial dependence on family size. Audit the characteristic, rank convention, target dimension and injectivity of the affine map before applying the complete common-weight ledger.

1. Imported finite-field universality, with the quantitative convention

The source is Kazhdan–Ziegler, Properties of High Rank Subvarieties of Affine Spaces, arXiv:1902.00767v5, dated 17 July 2020. Definitions 2.1 and 2.6–2.7, Remark 2.8 and Theorem 2.9 are the relevant passages, printed pp. 4–5.

Imported statement used. For fixed maximum degree, sufficiently high non-classical rank of a polynomial family makes the pullback map from affine maps into its variable space to polynomial families on a prescribed target space \(q^{-t}\)-uniform. The required threshold is polynomial in target dimension, family size and \(t\). The statement covers every finite field, including \(\mathbb F_2\). For \(t=1\), uniformity implies surjectivity.

Here non-classical rank means the ordinary polynomial product rank of the highest additive-derivative tensor, minimized over nonzero family combinations. It is not silently identified with tensor partition rank. The rank definition and the proof's separate all-characteristic passage were checked; the full universality proof is imported, not independently reverified. No stronger high-characteristic geometric theorem is needed.

2. A direct comparison with our cubic function rank

Let \(f\) be a binary cubic function, represented by its ordinary multilinear polynomial, and let \(T_f(u,v,w)=D_uD_vD_wf(0)\). Let \(R\) be the source's ordinary polynomial product rank of this trilinear polynomial. We claim

\[ \operatorname{rank}_3(f)\le6R. \tag{GC-rank-bridge} \]

Proof. A product-rank expression writes \(T_f=\sum_{i=1}^R A_iB_i\), where the ordinary degrees of both factors are less than three. Take the homogeneous degree-three component of this identity in the three independent groups of direction variables. Since \(T_f\) is homogeneous of degree three, it becomes a sum of at most \(2R\) products of a homogeneous linear form and a homogeneous quadratic form:

\[ T_f=\sum_{i=1}^R\bigl((A_i)_1(B_i)_2+(A_i)_2(B_i)_1\bigr). \]

Each linear factor on \(V^3\) is the sum of three linear forms, one in each direction group. Let \(U\subseteq V\) be their common kernel over all these factors and groups. Its codimension is at most \(6R\), and \(T_f\) vanishes on \(U^3\). Therefore the restriction of \(f\) to \(U\) has Boolean function degree at most two. In linear coordinates adapted to \(U\), every remaining cubic monomial contains one of at most \(6R\) complementary coordinate forms. Group these monomials by such a form and collect lower terms into a quadratic remainder. This is a cubic-rank expression with at most \(6R\) terms. The case \(T_f=0\) has cubic rank zero. \(\square\)

This comparison uses ordinary polynomial degrees in the source rank expression and Boolean function rank only at the final integration step. It avoids relying on a small-field identification of ordinary product rank with partition rank, and needs neither division by six nor scalar-field extension.

3. The exact collective extraction hypothesis follows

Working extraction lemma. There are absolute constants \(C,s>0\) such that every \(a\)-dimensional binary cubic input-function space with

\[ \operatorname{rank}_3(f)>C(a+1)^s \quad\text{for every nonzero }f \]

has \(a\) actual input combinations with disjoint cubic leading monomials after an invertible binary affine coordinate change, under a degree-compatible order.

Proof. Choose a basis \(f_1,\ldots,f_a\) of the space. Every nonzero combination has degree exactly three. By (GC-rank-bridge), its source non-classical rank is at least its cubic function rank divided by six. Apply the imported theorem with family size \(a\), all degrees three, target dimension \(m=3a\), field \(\mathbb F_2\), and uniformity parameter one. Its threshold at these parameters is bounded by a fixed polynomial in \(a\), so enlarge \(C,s\) to absorb the factor six and that bound.

Surjectivity gives one affine map \(\phi:\mathbb F_2^{3a}\to V\) satisfying simultaneously

\[ f_i(\phi(y))=y_{3i-2}y_{3i-1}y_{3i},\qquad i=1,\ldots,a. \tag{GC-target} \]

To see explicitly why uniformity gives a nonempty fiber, if the finite domain and target sets have sizes \(A,B\), its definition gives \(|B\,|\kappa^{-1}(Q)|-A|\le A/2\); hence every target fiber has strictly positive size.

The affine map is injective. Write \(\phi(y)=b+Ly\). If \(Lh=0\), every target product in (GC-target) is invariant under translation by \(h\). The degree-two part of the difference of one target product under that translation is

\[ h_{3i-2}y_{3i-1}y_{3i} +h_{3i-1}y_{3i-2}y_{3i} +h_{3i}y_{3i-2}y_{3i-1}. \]

Its three monomials are distinct, so invariance forces all three corresponding coordinates of \(h\) to vanish. The target triples cover all \(3a\) coordinates; thus \(h=0\). Complete the independent columns of \(L\) to a basis of \(V\) and use origin \(b\). This makes \(\phi\) the coordinate subspace on the first \(3a\) variables.

In these coordinates each multilinear representative restricts to its single designated target product. Every other cubic monomial therefore contains a variable outside the first \(3a\). Compare monomials first by total degree, then by weight two on the first \(3a\) variables and weight one on the others, then by a fixed lexicographic tie break. The designated head has weight six, while every other cubic term has weight at most five. These are the required disjoint heads. The selected functions are constant combinations of the original inputs; any representative changes have old Boolean certificates through three. \(\square\)

4. Complete binary ENS on arbitrary old cubic inputs

Working theorem. Fix a polynomial block-inventory bound and a polylogarithmic proof-degree bound. For sufficiently large \(n=2^\ell\), compact binary PHP together with any family of complete ENS blocks having at most that many blocks, arbitrary positive accuracies and arbitrary inputs of ordinary degree at most three in the old bits alone has no ordinary NS or PC refutation within that degree bound.

Input arities and overlaps are unrestricted; inputs may be arbitrary sums. Every companion and every coefficient Booleanity equation is present and accounted for. There is no individual-factor, common-feature, collective-rank or leading-head hypothesis left on the input family.

End-to-end argument through the recorded dependencies. The extraction lemma discharges the sole unproved structural premise of the polynomial-extraction corollary. In each input span, its maximal high-minimum-rank split either gives cubic heads or a dense low-rank set. Binary Bogolyubov–Ruzsa then supplies the low-rank input subspace of polynomial codimension. The packed tensor bound and binary common-feature lift, with exceptional cubics queried, supply the quadratic feature branches.

The complete common-weight criterion constructs one old multiplier, simultaneous old-only coefficient maps, and certificates for every weighted original axiom. The recorded parameter choice gives \(B=TD+k=O(n^{1-1/(48K)}\operatorname{polylog}n)=o(n)\), for a fixed structural exponent \(K\). Its cube-volume separator forbids the resulting old consequence. This proves the theorem for every fixed polynomial inventory exponent and polylogarithmic degree exponent. Smaller degree bounds are covered by increasing the requested ceiling to include \(\max(\ell,7)\).

This enlarges the general quadratic endpoint and removes the rank restriction from the preceding cubic endpoint. Earlier sharper bounds on narrower classes remain valid. The proof is a working synthesis of the linked local arguments and imported theorems, not an independent verification of every published dependency.

5. What changed, and where the main gap remains

For general-step, the arbitrary binary old-cubic endpoint is now available as a working theorem. The structural route succeeded because the low case has polynomial common-feature cost and the high case has polynomial simultaneous universality; neither an isolated cubic example nor a qualitative extraction statement would have supplied the full bound.

This is still not a superpolynomial lower bound for ordinary PHP in \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege. Genuine later source inputs involve retained earlier coefficients and whole values. Treating them as extra old variables does not preserve the PHP separator or produce consistent images of those same coefficients. Nor does this binary theorem cover odd primes. The relative target-separation premise and the degree/inventory recurrence remain separate obligations.

Next step: route review. Identify the precise PHP-relative interface needed to use this structure on the actual retained source, and test it against the same-degree preservation and ambient-cost obstructions. Compare a sufficient simultaneous final-target construction with stronger intermediate stability demands. Do not proceed automatically to another old-only degree case; require a mechanism that addresses the main retained-source gap.

Checks and significance. Reviewed the source's field and quantitative conventions, the factor-six rank bridge, absence of a common translation period, head order, and applicability of the complete ledger. No new finite computation or Lean verification was run. The general endpoint and common-feature mechanism are flagged for independent mathematical and prior-art review; novelty and publication readiness are not asserted.

Process assessment. Costing the needed conclusion before the source import made the audit decisive: the published meaning of “effective” supplies exactly the required polynomial dependence. The direct rank bridge avoided a silent change of rank convention. Existing workflows suffice; no additional framework rule is needed.

The exact retrieved version, private-file hash and reading scope are in the source audit and provenance.
