20 September 2026 — Return to retained sources: private coefficients reveal old-only probes

Route review and working source-specific polar-rank lemma. The arbitrary old-cubic theorem is progress; a complete retained-source interface is still unproved. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

General claim under review. The compiled polynomial-inventory, fixed-depth complete PHP source should exclude its polylogarithmic ordinary NS degree, uniformly at each fixed prime and depth. A sufficient proof can construct one final separated target or normalized annihilator; it need not preserve every intermediate moment or every old consequence at the same degree. The new old-cubic theorem supplies a genuine nonlinear endpoint, but does not by itself address the earlier coefficients present in actual later inputs.

1. Why simply repeating the old-only argument fails

The existing relative criterion identifies the real extra premise: for an appropriate multiplier space \(S\), the map \(f\mapsto fq\) into the retained degree-\(B\) quotient must have rank exceeding the normalization maps' total image loss. Retained nonrefutability gives only one surviving class, not this quantitative rank. The cubic structural improvements do not supply that missing quotient estimate.

The recorded two controls still apply. A high input family supported in extra coefficient-like Boolean coordinates can have no nonzero old-only multiplier in its input ideal. Conversely, copying the full ambient-variable estimates costs at least the existing quadratic stage's \(V^{8/9}\)-scale factor and need not fit the old \(n\)-scale barrier when \(V\) is an arbitrary polynomial coefficient inventory. This rejects the unchanged ambient scheme, not every source-specific relative construction.

The same-degree counterexample also rejects universal interface preservation, but does not reject a costed final-target argument. The earlier PC elimination baseline already handles one upper parent and suitably bounded inventories; another one-parent example would not address the open polynomial-inventory case.

Parked alternatives. The weighted bottom deletion retains a valid product-only interface. Its survivors are flat indicators, whose rank need not be constant; the sharper affine cutoff can make the surviving width polylogarithmic in its stated feasible regime, but does not turn them into bounded-degree cubics. The joint value route needs a hard simultaneous value assignment and has an explicit literal-family obstruction. The local/wide moment corrections remain conditional on source compatibility. None can be declared solved by the recent tensor theorem.

2. A source-specific low case that avoids coefficient probes

Working lemma. Work over a prime field \(\mathbb F_p\). Let \(b\) be old variables, and let each bottom block have old-affine inputs \(g_{c,j}(b)=a_{c,j}+\ell_{c,j}(b)\), with \(\ell_{c,j}\) homogeneous linear. Its accuracy-one whole product is

\[ P_c=1-\sum_j r_{c,j}g_{c,j}(b). \]

The coefficient variables are private and disjoint between bottom blocks. Let \(A\subseteq\mathbb F_p^{\mathcal C}\) be a linear coefficient code and consider inputs

\[ q_\alpha(b,r)=L_\alpha(b)+\sum_c\alpha_cP_c, \qquad\alpha\in A, \tag{PR-source} \]

where each \(L_\alpha\) is old-affine. Write \(U_c=\operatorname{span}\{\ell_{c,j}\}_j\). The polar bilinear form of \(q_\alpha\), on all old and retained coefficient variables, has rank

\[ \operatorname{rank}\operatorname{Pol}(q_\alpha) =2\dim\left(\sum_{c:\alpha_c\ne0}U_c\right). \tag{PR-exact} \]

If that polar rank is at most \(2R\) for every \(\alpha\in A\), then the old direction space of all active bottom blocks satisfies

\[ U_*:=\sum_{c:\exists\alpha\in A,\ \alpha_c\ne0}U_c, \qquad \dim U_*\le\frac{p}{p-1}R\le2R. \tag{PR-old-probes} \]

Consequently at most \(\lfloor pR/(p-1)\rfloor\) common probes, involving old variables only, make every member of (PR-source) affine in the remaining old and coefficient variables on every value branch. No independence of the code coordinates is assumed.

Proof of the rank identity. Let \(C_\alpha\) be the matrix whose columns are the coefficient vectors of \(\alpha_c\ell_{c,j}\), with the columns indexed by the private variables \(r_{c,j}\). The quadratic part of the input is \(-b^{\mathsf T}C_\alpha r\); constants in bottom inputs and the old-affine term affect only its affine part. Thus its polar matrix has off-diagonal blocks \(-C_\alpha,-C_\alpha^{\mathsf T}\) and zero diagonal blocks. Its rank is \(2\operatorname{rank}C_\alpha\), by the dimensions of the two independent kernel equations. Distinct private columns prevent cancellation between different bottom blocks. Their column span is exactly the sum in (PR-exact).

Proof of the union bound. Choose a basis \(u_1,\ldots,u_s\) of \(U_*\) from the union of the individual spaces, and assign each basis vector an active block \(c(i)\) containing it. For uniform \(\alpha\in A\), an active coordinate \(\alpha_{c(i)}\) is nonzero with probability \(1-1/p\), since it is a nonzero linear functional on \(A\). Whenever it is nonzero, that basis vector lies in the selected sum of spaces. The selected basis vectors remain independent, so (PR-exact) and the hypothesis give

\[ (1-1/p)s =\mathbb E_\alpha\bigl|\{i:\alpha_{c(i)}\ne0\}\bigr| \le\mathbb E_\alpha\dim\sum_{c:\alpha_c\ne0}U_c \le R. \]

Linearity of expectation does not require independent activations. This proves (PR-old-probes). Query a basis of \(U_*\). On a branch every active \(g_{c,j}\) is constant, so each active \(P_c\) is affine in its private coefficients and each \(q_\alpha\) is affine in the remaining variables. The difference from this branch expression is a sum of probe equations times coefficient-linear polynomials, through ordinary degree two. The case \(R=0\) is immediate. \(\square\)

3. What this lemma does and does not transfer

For bottoms of larger accuracy, setting all coefficient rows after the first to zero is one degree-nonincreasing polynomial specialization of the whole source and proof. It produces the displayed products consistently in every later occurrence. It does not independently rename a reused product, discard a companion, or justify reducing carried original costs. Thus the private-column structure is available at this two-level stage. Binary coherent parent inputs that are affine combinations of genuine bottom products fit it, with their stated old-affine part. Arbitrary raw coefficient uses, products of bottom products, and non-affine old boundary terms are not included in (PR-source).

The lemma strengthens the location and size of the general bounded-polar-rank probe conclusion on this special source structure: its probes lie in the old variables and their count is independent of the full coefficient inventory. It does not prove that any selected probe branch preserves PHP hardness. A full transfer must keep all branches or otherwise justify its old target, handle shared bottoms consistently, and certify every original axiom. The high-rank side still requires a source-aware separator; (PR-exact) alone is not that separator.

4. Assessment and next bounded test

Assessment. The recent cycles advanced a real restricted endpoint and supplied a reusable polynomial common-feature argument. The main retained-source compatibility problem is still open. The new private-column calculation gives a concrete source-specific improvement over treating all retained variables as generic old coordinates. It is worth testing its complete low-case map before seeking another old-only degree theorem, but it does not yet supply a two-level lower bound under the new hypothesis.

Next task on general-step. For a polynomial two-level family with old-affine bottoms and parent inputs of form (PR-source), assume each parent's entire input space has polar rank at most a polylogarithmic bound. Test whether (PR-old-probes) yields a simultaneous complete map into the known old-affine endpoint, with polylogarithmic degree loss and affordable branch inventory. Normalize each shared bottom once, retain unused bottoms and all coefficient fields, and charge the original costs. Stop at a complete map or an explicit conflict. This tests the low side of a potential general retained-source split; the high side remains a separately named obligation.

Process assessment. The review distinguished genuine structural progress from the unchanged target-rank gap, then used the actual private-coefficient grammar to obtain an old-only probe bound. Existing indexed controls avoided rediscovering the value-clamping and ambient-dimension failures. No new framework rule or repeated numerical test was needed.

20 September 2026 — Low collective parent rank has a complete two-level affine image

Working all-prime complete transfer and restricted two-level PHP endpoint. Shared bottoms, unused blocks, all companions and fields are retained in the degree accounting. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, test the low side of an actual retained-source split. The private-column lemma supplies old-only probes, but a valid endpoint also needs a single substitution for each reused bottom coefficient and full certificates for all parent axioms. Stop at that complete map and its quantitative lower-bound application; do not assume the high-rank parent case.

1. Source, rank hypothesis and finite transfer

Fix a prime \(p\). An old base \(\Gamma(b)\) contains every old Boolean equation. Bottom blocks have old-affine input tuples \(g_{c,j}(b)\), private coefficients and arbitrary positive accuracies \(h_c\). Parents have inputs

\[ q_{a,i}=L_{a,i}(b)+\sum_c\alpha_{a,i;c}P_c, \qquad \alpha_{a,i;c}\in\mathbb F_p, \tag{LP-source} \]

where each \(L_{a,i}\) is old-affine and each \(P_c\) is the genuine whole bottom product. Parent accuracies \(h_a\) are arbitrary positive integers. There are no parents reading other parents, no raw bottom coefficient terms in (LP-source), and no products of bottom products. The source is complete: every companion and coefficient equation \(r^p-r\) is present.

For the rank hypothesis only, specialize every bottom coefficient row after the first to zero, consistently throughout all parent inputs. Require every constant combination in each resulting parent input space to have polar rank at most \(2R\), for an integer \(R\ge1\), on the old bits and retained first-row coefficients together. This does not replace the original costs carried by the proof.

Working transfer lemma. Put \(S=pR+1\). There is a simultaneous polynomial substitution, fixing \(b\), from the entire source to \(\Gamma\) plus a single level of complete old-affine ENS blocks. It transfers ordinary degree-\(D\) NS or PC refutations to degree at most \(SD\). Every used bottom is normalized once; unused bottoms remain as complete target blocks. If there are \(M_b\) bottoms and \(M_p\) parents, the target inventory is at most

\[ M_*\le M_b+M_p\,p^{\lfloor pR/(p-1)\rfloor}. \tag{LP-inventory} \]

Each parent branch keeps its parent's accuracy. Unused bottoms keep theirs. The statement is a complete map of a two-level source, not the selection of one supposedly hard feature branch.

2. Choose each shared bottom image once

Call a bottom used when its coefficient in at least one listed parent input is nonzero. The exact rank identity shows that every used bottom's homogeneous old input span has rank at most \(R\). Indeed a parent input activating that block has active old span containing it and polar rank at most \(2R\). For each parent separately, the union \(U_a\) of the old directions of all its active bottoms has dimension

\[ u_a:=\dim U_a\le\lfloor pR/(p-1)\rfloor. \]

Clean up zero and unit bottom input spans. A zero tuple maps to value one by setting coefficients zero; if one lies in the affine input span, a constant coefficient row makes the product identically zero. For each remaining used bottom choose once and for all an affine basis \(F_{c,1},\ldots,F_{c,r_c}\), with \(r_c\le R\), and define

\[ A_c(b)=\prod_{j=1}^{r_c}(1-F_{c,j}(b)^{p-1}). \tag{LP-bottom-value} \]

Use the ordinary telescoping identity

\[ 1-A_c=\sum_{j=1}^{r_c} F_{c,j}^{p-2}\prod_{t<j}(1-F_{c,t}^{p-1})\,F_{c,j} \]

and constant basis representations in the original inputs to assign its first coefficient row. Set the other rows to zero. The original product maps exactly to \(A_c\), with coefficient-image degree at most \((p-1)r_c-1\le S\). This is the one-bin case of the complete affine normalization. A nonzero original bottom companion maps to \(g_{c,i}A_c\), which vanishes on the full old Boolean cube and has degree at most \((p-1)r_c+1\le S(2h_c+1)\). Old Boolean division gives the certificate at that ceiling. Every bottom coefficient field image is likewise Boolean-zero through \(pS\).

All parents use this same \(A_c\) for a shared bottom. No parent-specific assignment to a reused coefficient is made. Coefficients of unused bottoms are fixed, so those blocks remain complete old-affine blocks in the target.

3. Parent branches use only old probes

Choose a homogeneous old-linear basis \(H_{a,1},\ldots,H_{a,u_a}\) of \(U_a\). On the branch \(H_a(b)=\sigma\in\mathbb F_p^{u_a}\), all old-affine inputs of every active bottom are constant. Hence its indicator \(A_c\) is constant, and the substituted parent tuple

\[ q'_{a,i}(b)=L_{a,i}(b)+\sum_c\alpha_{a,i;c}A_c(b) \]

agrees on that branch with a specified old-affine tuple \(q_{a,sigma,i}(b)\). Retain a globally constant substituted input as that constant on every branch when necessary; zero inputs cause no difficulty. For an original nonconstant input, these affine branches have degree at most its original degree. Original nonzero constant inputs may instead clean up their parent block by a constant coefficient row, before this construction.

Use selectors

\[ \chi_{a,sigma}(b)=\prod_{t=1}^{u_a} \bigl(1-(H_{a,t}(b)-\sigma_t)^{p-1}\bigr), \qquad\deg\chi_{a,sigma}\le\kappa_a=(p-1)u_a\le pR. \]

They are exactly one-hot on the entire old Boolean cube, including when some feature-value branches are empty. Give each affine branch a complete fresh block, with coefficients \(s_{a,\sigma,u,i}\), product \(B_{a,\sigma}\), all companions and fields. For every original parent coefficient set

\[ r_{a,u,i}\longmapsto \beta_{a,u,i}=\sum_\sigma\chi_{a,\sigma}s_{a,\sigma,u,i}. \tag{LP-parent-map} \]

Every image has degree at most \(\kappa_a+1\le S\). The same selector chooses the branch in every row and every input position of that parent. Different parents have independent target coefficients. Together with the bottom images, this is one substitution of maximum variable-image degree \(S\), not two whole-proof substitutions whose factors must be multiplied.

4. Complete original-degree certificates

Let \(d_{a,i}\) and \(\delta_a\) be the actual original input degree and its tuple maximum, before bottom normalization. For a nonzero parent companion its original degree is

\[ e_{a,i}=d_{a,i}+h_a(\delta_a+1). \]

Write \(\Phi\) for the full simultaneous map. Coefficientwise in the fresh target variables, the difference

\[ \Phi(q_{a,i}P_a) -\sum_\sigma\chi_{a,\sigma}q_{a,\sigma,i}B_{a,\sigma} \tag{LP-companion-difference} \]

vanishes on the full old Boolean cube. At an old point exactly one selector is one; the bottom images and branch inputs agree, and all rows use the same branch. This establishes the coefficientwise identity for formal target coefficients, without assuming any target companion equation.

The first term has ordinary degree at most \(Se_{a,i}\), since every variable image has degree at most \(S\). A branch companion has degree at most \(e_{a,i}\): it retains \(h_a\), while every nonconstant branch input is affine and respects the original individual degree ceiling. Thus its masked term has degree at most

\[ \kappa_a+e_{a,i}\le(\kappa_a+1)e_{a,i}\le Se_{a,i}. \]

Division by the old Boolean equations, coefficientwise in target variables and counting their degrees, gives an ordinary certificate for (LP-companion-difference) through \(Se_{a,i}\). The remaining terms are legal multiples of target companions at that same ceiling.

For each parent field equation, Frobenius gives

\[ \beta^p-\beta =\sum_\sigma\chi_\sigma^p(s_\sigma^p-s_\sigma) +\sum_\sigma(\chi_\sigma^p-\chi_\sigma)s_\sigma. \]

The first sum uses target field equations through \(p(\kappa_a+1)\le pS\); the second has old Boolean certificates within that bound. Used-bottom certificates were checked above. Unused bottoms, their fields and the old base are fixed. Every original generator of degree \(e\) therefore has a target certificate through \(Se\). Original NS cofactors through \(D-e\) map through \(S(D-e)\), and primitive PC multiplications replay at the same factor \(S\). This proves the complete transfer and (LP-inventory). No collected degree is substituted for an original carried cost.

5. A finite PHP endpoint and a power-sized rank range

Working theorem. Take \(\Gamma=\mathcal Q_{n,p}\), \(n=2^\ell\), and the two-level family above. Require every parent and every unused bottom to have accuracy at least \(h_0=3(p-1)\ell\); used bottom accuracies may be arbitrary positive integers. Let \(\widehat M\ge\max(1,M_*)\), \(D'=SD\), \(m=n+1\). If an integer \(k\) satisfies

\[ k\ge\max\{1,\lceil\sqrt{m\ln(4\widehat M)}\rceil\},\qquad k\le m,\qquad4(k-1)<n,\qquad n\ge2k(D'+1)-1, \tag{LP-PHP-range} \]

then the original source has no degree-\(D\) NS or PC refutation.

Proof. The complete map produces only old-affine blocks. If necessary, specialize surplus target rows to zero so that their accuracies all equal \(h_0\), without increasing degree. Apply the all-prime affine endpoint at target degree zero and proof ceiling \(D'\). Conditions (LP-PHP-range) are exactly its refutation range. \(\square\)

Asymptotic consequence. Fix \(p\) and \(0<\eta<1/3\). For polynomial \(M_b,M_p\), polylogarithmic \(D\), and \(R\le n^\eta\), all these inequalities hold for sufficiently large \(n\), with the stated accuracy lower bound. Indeed

\[ \ln\widehat M=O(R+\log n),\quad D'=O(RD+D),\quad k=O\!\left(n^{(1+\eta)/2}\operatorname{polylog}n\right), \] \[ k(D'+1)=O\!\left(n^{(1+3\eta)/2}\operatorname{polylog}n\right)=o(n). \]

The remaining room inequalities follow from \(k=o(n)\). In particular every polylogarithmic collective polar-rank bound is covered. This is a restriction on every parent input combination after the specified bottom first-row specialization, not merely on the individual listed inputs.

6. Outcome and remaining high case

For general-step, the low collective-rank two-level case now has a complete map that handles polynomially many parents, shared bottoms and every coefficient domain. Unlike the old-cubic result alone, this directly treats genuine parent readings of retained bottom values before mapping them away. The source-specific old probe bound, rather than the full retained-variable count, controls the cost.

The unrestricted high-rank parent family remains outside the theorem. So do additional levels, arbitrary raw coefficient input terms, products of products and non-affine old boundary terms. The stated accuracy condition is retained, not silently removed. An odd-prime source with nonlinear modular readings requires additional work; affine combinations of bottom products are the exact template here.

Next bounded task. Test whether the high-polar-rank side of this same private-bottom template admits a PHP-separated common weight compatible with the bottom companions. Use the exact active-old-span rank formula; do not reuse an ambient coefficient-space count or treat a raw high rank as source hardness. Stop at a complete costed high-case construction or a concrete obstruction to the proposed invariant, with the low-case theorem as the positive control.

Process assessment. Writing the simultaneous variable map before replaying the proof avoided a spurious product of degree losses and exposed every shared-bottom obligation. The symbolic axiom ledger is the relevant check; no enumeration or rendering audit was needed. The initial checkpoint window included preliminary map planning before the mathematics marker, and is left as measured rather than backfilled.

20 September 2026 — Multiplicity questions need a different invariant; one printed question follows from a standard lemma

Status: source-audit corollary of an imported theorem and exploratory route assessment; no novelty claim or new formalization. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question and stopping point. Can the heterogeneous scalar-profile frontier plausibly lead to one of the published covering questions from the preceding audit? This is a user-assigned side-significance review. The main general-step obligation remains unchanged. Stop after identifying the exact target, testing the direct transfer, and giving a concrete first unresolved step; do not launch an unrestricted new covering project.

A printed binary question is already implied by multiplicity Schwartz–Zippel

Source alignment. Question 4.3 in the published 2023 PDF asks whether a binary polynomial, vanishing to order at least \(k\) at every nonzero point and at most \(k-1\) at the origin, has degree at least \(2k-\lfloor k/2^{n-1}\rfloor\), for \(k\ge2^{n-2}\). This numbering is version-specific: the older arXiv version has a different Question 4.3. The journal HTML and PDF agree on the polynomial question.

Imported theorem. Dvir–Kopparty–Saraf–Sudan, Definition 2.2 and Lemma 2.7, uses Hasse multiplicity, equivalently the least total degree of a nonzero term in \(P(a+z)\). For every nonzero polynomial of total degree \(d\), over any field, and finite \(S\),

\[ \sum_{a\in S^n}\operatorname{mult}_a(P)\le d|S|^{n-1}. \]

The source's complete inductive proof was read: differentiate a leading coefficient to its first nonzero Hasse jet, apply the univariate multiplicity bound along the last coordinate, and sum using the lower-dimensional induction. There is no degree-versus-field-size hypothesis. This is an imported result, not a new proof of that lemma or a kernel verification.

Full deduction. The origin condition excludes the zero polynomial. For \(S=\mathbb F_2\), nonnegative multiplicity at zero and the \(2^n-1\) other points give

\[ k(2^n-1)\le\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_2^n}\operatorname{mult}_a(P) \le d\,2^{n-1}. \]

Therefore \(d\ge2k-k/2^{n-1}\). Since \(d\) is integral,

\[ d\ge\left\lceil2k-\frac{k}{2^{n-1}}\right\rceil =2k-\left\lfloor\frac{k}{2^{n-1}}\right\rfloor. \]

This proves the printed inequality for every positive \(n,k\), without the question's lower threshold on \(k\). The proof uses the frontier theorem nowhere. It is a direct consequence of prior literature, not evidence that our frontier newly resolves a major open problem. The exact application has not been independently reviewed, and whether the authors intended a stronger variant or have already noted this implication remains a specific source-clarification question. No author was contacted.

A closer extension target: odd-field double covers

For a future extension, Question 4.2 is more relevant. Its \(k=2,q=3\) case predicts \(f_3(n,2,1)=2n+2\) for sufficiently large \(n\): cover every nonzero ternary vector twice with affine hyperplanes, allowing the origin at most one covering. This review identifies a question posed in that source, not an exhaustive current-open-status certification.

What our existing endpoint supplies. The \(T=0\), two-nonzero-value specialization gives the classical \(2n\) lower bound for a single cover avoiding the origin. From a double cover remove its unique origin-covering plane, if present, or any plane otherwise. The remaining planes avoid the origin and still cover every nonzero point, so the original number is at least \(2n+1\). A \(2n+2\) construction takes \(x_i=1,2\) for every coordinate and adds \(\sum_i x_i=1,2\). A vector with at least two nonzero coordinates already has two coverings; a vector with one nonzero coordinate receives one more from the added pair; the origin is uncovered. Thus the first proposed all-dimension target is the one-hyperplane gap between these bounds, not another list of small examples. These elementary bounds are consistent with the source and are not claimed as new.

Why the frontier does not close that gap automatically. In its reduced state algebra, a successful product is an idempotent selector. Already over \(\mathbb F_2[x]/(x^2-x)\), the polynomials \(1-x\) and \((1-x)^r\) have the same class for every positive \(r\), but have multiplicities one and \(r\) at \(x=1\). Thus value-only reduction loses precisely the information needed for repeated covering. This refutes the proposed automatic inference from an unchanged selector to a multiplicity bound; it does not obstruct every extension of the method.

Plausible but unproved bridge. Retain local derivative data, for example modulo powers of the point maximal ideals, or retain an incidence-sensitive factor ledger. Then seek an analogue of the untouched-group lower bound for products of affine factors, preserving the original number of planes and the origin's permitted coverage. Ordinary quotient idempotence and degree-complete reductions do not transfer unchanged to these thicker local algebras. It is also invalid to replace the affine-factor optimization by arbitrary polynomials without proving that this relaxation preserves the desired bound. No such transfer is proved here.

Assessment. This is a plausible bounded exploratory direction because the base domain, distinguished point and factor-count objective agree, but our nonconstant-coefficient refinement supplies no demonstrated advantage yet. The decisive first milestone is an invariant that distinguishes one from two coverings and improves the general \(2n+1\) bound over \(\mathbb F_3\), or an explicit obstruction to that proposed invariant. It requires a substantial new argument, not routine substitution into the current theorem. The main route's high-rank cubic extraction/separation question remains the proposed next step; all four living sections were reviewed, and only the side-review pointer is refreshed. The existing working-context soft overage is retained with its essential hypotheses, within unchanged hard limits.

20 September 2026 — Cheap flat-partition relations defeat a raw high-rank clamp

Working high-case control and costed input-basis reduction. The failure concerns a zero-product shortcut, not complete source hardness or the established low-case map. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, test the proposed high side of the private-bottom two-level split: does high collective polar rank justify a common old weight on which every high parent's product can be set to zero? First quotienting identical bottom flats is already available; use a control with distinct flats. Stop at a verified obstruction to this particular invariant and a legal way to account for its short retained relations.

1. Distinct-flat comparisons have high raw polar rank

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\), with integers \(r,a,h\ge1\). Take independent old bits \(b_1,\ldots,b_r,x_1,\ldots,x_a\). Let \(G=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)\), and form complete accuracy-\(h\) bottom blocks, with private coefficients, for

\[ P=P_G,\qquad Q_{j,0}=P_{G\cup\{x_j\}},\qquad Q_{j,1}=P_{G\cup\{1-x_j\}}\quad(1\le j\le a). \]

The corresponding affine zero flats are all distinct and nonempty. Define parent input directions

\[ q_j=Q_{j,0}+Q_{j,1}-P. \tag{FH-directions} \]

These ordinary polynomials are linearly independent and each nonzero combination has actual degree \(2h\), because it retains a coefficient monomial belonging to a private child block that occurs in no other direction. After simultaneous first-row specialization, the private-column rank identity gives, for a combination with nonempty support \(J\subseteq[a]\),

\[ \operatorname{rank}\operatorname{Pol}\left(\sum_{j\in J}q_j^{(1)}\right) =2(r+|J|)\ge2(r+1). \tag{FH-rank} \]

The active old span contains \(G\) and precisely the chosen \(x_j\)'s, whether or not the coefficient of \(P\) cancels. Taking \(r\ge2a^2\) makes this an \(a\)-dimensional high-minimum-polar-rank family even at the threshold used by the generic quadratic head lemma. It embeds into the old PHP bits whenever \(r+a\le(n+1)\ell\). No essential occurrence in a short PHP proof is asserted.

2. Every direction already has a short retained certificate

Let \(\Gamma\) contain the old Boolean equations and all the displayed bottom companions and fields. The recorded codimension-one comparison identity gives

\[ Q_{j,0}-(1-x_j)P\in\mathcal I_{4h+1}(\Gamma),\qquad Q_{j,1}-x_jP\in\mathcal I_{4h+1}(\Gamma). \]

The second instance substitutes \(1-x_j\) for the added bit; its Boolean equation has the same degree-two old witness. Add the two certificates. Since \((1-x_j)+x_j=1\), this proves

\[ q_j\in\mathcal I_{4h+1}(\Gamma). \tag{FH-certificate} \]

This is an application of an existing comparison identity, not a new flat-partition theorem. Equal-flat canonicalization alone does not remove the example because the flats are distinct; its short partition relations do.

Complete positive control. Add arbitrarily many complete parent blocks whose inputs lie in the span of the \(q_j\)'s, at any positive accuracies \(H\). Set every parent coefficient to zero, so every parent product becomes one. A nonzero parent input has degree \(2h\), and its companion's original cost is

\[ e=H(2h+1)+2h\ge4h+1. \]

Its image is the input itself, certified by (FH-certificate) through that cost. Parent fields map to zero, and \(\Gamma\) is fixed. Thus the entire parent family can be removed without increasing ordinary NS or PC degree, independently of its raw polar rank. With the old compact PHP base, polynomial inventory and bottom accuracy at the recorded affine endpoint, its nonrefutability follows from that existing one-level theorem.

3. The zero-product shortcut is impossible for this control

Suppose all bottom and parent coefficient images are old-only polynomials, and a nonzero multilinear old weight \(f\) makes every mapped bottom companion vanish on the full old Boolean cube. At any old point with \(f=1\), each bottom product must equal its exact zero-flat indicator: if all its inputs vanish, its product is literally one; otherwise a nonzero input and its weighted companion force the product to zero.

The two child flats partition the base flat, so all mapped \(q_j\)'s vanish at such a point. Every parent product on these directions is then literally one, for any parent coefficient images. Therefore

\[ f\Phi(P_{\rm parent})=f \quad\text{as Boolean functions}. \]

Because a nonzero multilinear binary polynomial is not the zero Boolean function, this cannot be a Boolean-zero weighted product. The proposed uniform “high raw rank implies zero product” rule fails. The sufficient requirement that weighted companions vanish is not refuted; the degree-preserving positive control satisfies it with parent product one. Mixed retained-variable weights and PHP-relative certificates are not ruled out by this old-domain argument.

4. A legal quotient by supplied low-degree relations

Working reduction lemma. Let \(\Gamma(y)\) be a retained system with the relevant domains, and let a fresh complete level have inputs \(g_{a,i}\), accuracy \(h_a\), original input degrees \(d_{a,i}\), maximum \(\delta_a\), product degree \(w_a=h_a(\delta_a+1)\), and companion costs \(e_{a,i}=w_a+d_{a,i}\). Zero inputs may be omitted. Choose, for each block, a subset of its actual input positions \(f_{a,j}\), with constant expressions

\[ g_{a,i}=\sum_j\lambda_{a,i,j}f_{a,j}+u_{a,i},\qquad \deg f_{a,j}\le d_{a,i}\text{ when }\lambda_{a,i,j}\ne0, \qquad u_{a,i}\in\mathcal I_{c_{a,i}}(\Gamma). \tag{QB-data} \]

The residual memberships require supplied ordinary NS certificates. Put \(w'_a=h_a(1+\max_j\deg f_{a,j})\) for a nonempty selected tuple, and \(w'_a=0\) for the empty tuple. Define

\[ \Delta=\max_{a,i}\max\{0,c_{a,i}+w'_a-e_{a,i}\}. \tag{QB-loss} \]

Replacing each block by the complete block on its selected tuple, or omitting it when that tuple is empty, transfers degree-\(D\) ordinary NS or PC consequences of retained targets to degree at most \(D+\Delta\). The loss is a maximum over the whole fresh level, not a sum over blocks. This is a vector-space quotient backed by certificates, never a quotient by the unrestricted ideal of an unsatisfiable base.

Proof. Keep the coefficient positions of the selected inputs, rename them to fresh target coefficients, and set all other source coefficients to zero. The original product becomes exactly the selected product \(P'_a\), or one for an empty tuple. Old variables are fixed. Its original companion image is

\[ g_{a,i}P'_a=\sum_j\lambda_{a,i,j}(f_{a,j}P'_a)+u_{a,i}P'_a. \]

Each first summand is a target companion through \(w'_a+d_{a,i}\le e_{a,i}\), by degree adaptation and \(w'_a\le w_a\). The last term has a retained certificate through \(c_{a,i}+w'_a\le e_{a,i}+\Delta\). Coefficient fields either rename to target fields or vanish. Thus every source axiom has an image certificate within its original degree plus \(\Delta\), under a variable substitution of degree at most one. Original NS cofactors add at most \(D-e_{a,i}\), giving \(D+\Delta\). For PC, derive the axiom images with those certificates, then replay the specialized original proof with its linear substitutions; its own line degrees do not increase. This proves the reduction.

A degree-ordered greedy basis in the image of the input span modulo a supplied consequence space gives the degree-adapted subset in (QB-data). One must still supply the residual certificates with the stated ceilings. The literal zero-residual case is the existing degree-adapted input-basis reduction. The historical quotient batch lemma already uses supplied PC consequences for elimination; the present statement keeps smaller complete blocks and states an ordinary-NS residual ledger. It does not claim a general bound on the quotient dimension or on finding its certificates.

For (FH-directions), choose every selected tuple empty and use \(c_{a,i}=4h+1\). Then \(\Delta=0\), recovering the positive control above. The relation cost is not charged as though it were freely available at raw input degree \(2h\); the empty target product releases the original companion's product-degree allowance.

If all those input values are zero, every factor in the product is one. If some input value is nonzero, (SC-common-map) forces \(\widehat P_a=0\). In both cases this is exactly \(\chi_a\). The induction includes zero and empty input tuples and assigns a reused product the same value at every occurrence.

It follows that \(f\Phi(g_{a,i}P_a)\) vanishes on the full old Boolean cube: on \(X_f\) the companion is zero, and outside it the weight is zero. Each old-only coefficient image has values in \(\mathbb F_p\), so its field equation also vanishes on that cube. This proves compatibility for all blocks at once; choosing unrelated weights at different levels would not justify the induction.

3. Use original degrees, not the size of semantic expansions

For any original generator \(E\) of actual ordinary degree \(e\), substitution has \(\deg\Phi(E)\le Te\). Thus a weighted companion or coefficient field image has an old Boolean NS certificate through \(Te+k\), by monic Boolean division. No degree bound on the full expansion of \(\chi_a\) or \(\overline g_{a,i}\) was used in this certificate calculation. Those functions justify pointwise vanishing; the polynomial being divided is the actual \(f\Phi(E)\).

An old base generator is fixed and has weighted certificate \(fE\) through \(e+k\le Te+k\). In NS, an original cofactor of degree at most \(D-e\) maps to degree at most \(T(D-e)\), giving total ceiling \(TD+k\). In PC, simulate every line \(p\) by \(f\Phi(p)\). Addition is linear, and multiplying a predecessor of degree at most \(D-1\) by the degree-at-most-\(T\) image of its source variable stays within \(TD+k\). The last line is \(fq\), proving the lemma. \(\square\)

This does not claim that \(g_{a,i}-F_{a,i}\) has a cheap proof inside the retained source. It supplies a different, globally weighted proof map. Agreement only on models of the unsatisfiable PHP base would be vacuous and is not a permitted replacement for (SC-functions) or (SC-common-map).

4. Profile classes for which the normalizers are available

Working corollaries. Apply the lemma to the complete compact PHP source. All input degrees and proof ceilings below refer to the original expanded source, not to semantic representatives.

  • All-prime affine profiles. Suppose every induced input function has an old-affine representative on the whole Boolean cube and every block has accuracy at least \(3(p-1)\ell\). The coefficient maps and old weight in the all-prime affine proof can be chosen for the single old-affine family of all these representatives. With \(m=n+1\), \(M\) blocks, \(k\ge\max\{1,\lceil\sqrt{m\ln(4M)}\rceil\}\), \(k\le m\), \(4(k-1)<n\), and \(n\ge2k(D+1)-1\), they have \(T=k\) and an old-separated degree-\(k\) weight. The original leveled source therefore has no degree-\(D\) NS or PC refutation. Polynomial inventory and polylogarithmic \(D\) satisfy this range eventually.
  • Binary cubic profiles. Suppose \(p=2\) and every induced input function has old Boolean degree at most three. At arbitrary positive accuracies, the common old-only maps constructed in the general cubic proof apply to the family of these representatives. Its joint ledger provides one weight and coefficient maps with \(TD+k=o(n)\) for polynomial inventory and polylogarithmic original \(D\). Hence the original leveled source has no such refutations. This uses the maps and their full-cube compatibility from that proof, not a logical inference from one-level nonrefutability alone.

Scalar-normalizable semantic spans can be mixed in. Either corollary may also include blocks whose induced input-function span has dimension \(r_a\) with \((p-1)r_a\le h_a\), without a degree bound on those functions. Choose a basis of their function span and express it by constant combinations of the listed induced inputs. Use one coefficient row for each basis function and each nonzero field scalar, with the corresponding constant coefficient vector; set unused rows to zero. Its product is

\[ \prod_{j=1}^{r_a}\prod_{c\in\mathbb F_p^*}(1-cF_j) =\prod_{j=1}^{r_a}(1-F_j^{p-1}), \]

the exact common-zero indicator, so all its semantic companions vanish everywhere. These constant maps satisfy (SC-common-map) for any old weight. Choose the common weight using only the remaining affine or cubic profile blocks, and apply the same induction to the entire acyclic source. If every block is of this scalar type, take \(f=1,T=1\); the source transfers to its old base without increasing proof degree. This is the semantic-input version of the familiar scalar packing construction, not a claim that all actual sources satisfy its rank threshold.

5. Controls and the remaining coverage problem

The high raw polar-rank control now has a uniform interpretation: all of its parent input functions are zero, so those parent blocks are scalar-normalizable with product one. This respects the partition identity without enumerating a relation basis or forcing a zero product. The bottom input functions are affine, so the mixed affine-profile corollary applies at its stated accuracies.

A high-degree flat value can also be read by a scalar-span block: a single induced input may have large old degree while its span has dimension one. Thus the criterion does not demand that every whole product have small semantic degree. On the other hand, an unrestricted family of many affine-flat indicators can have both high input-function degree and large semantic span. Neither the old-cubic theorem nor scalar packing covers that family automatically. Proper internal subformulas do not become low-degree input functions just because proof lines are tautologies.

For general-step, there is now a direct leveled lifting mechanism for compatible semantic old profiles, preserving original proof costs and shared values. It gives actual sufficient classes and resolves the identified relation control. It does not prove that arbitrary compiled \(\mathrm{AC}^0[p]\)-Frege sources have these profiles or that a suitable common weight makes every exceptional input low-degree.

Next bounded task. Test the remaining coverage on polynomial families of affine-flat indicator inputs whose semantic span exceeds the scalar packing threshold and whose old degree exceeds three. Require an old-separated common weight and compatible low-degree profiles on its support. Use the existing high-flat cutoff and its exact degree budget, not just rarity of the exceptional set or an uncharged semantic replacement. Stop at an affordable new profile mechanism or a precise obstruction; do not call the criterion itself a general Frege lower bound.

Process assessment. A pointwise acyclic induction supplied the missing shared-value consistency once one common normalizer was available. This avoided treating semantic relations as free retained-ideal certificates. The existing input-profile and original-degree rules were sufficient; no new framework rule or finite computation was needed.

20 September 2026 — Compressing semantic offsets requires a costed old domain

Working common-weight compression theorem and weighted entropy obstruction. A one-column PHP domain meets the reduction hypothesis; unrestricted source coverage remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, extend the semantic common-weight lift beyond exact low-degree input profiles. Test whether a small number of offsets from such profiles can be interpolated at affordable cost. Stop at a complete transfer, a falsifying test of automatic smallness, and a proper PHP-domain control. Small offset images will be a hypothesis to verify, not a consequence of bounded source depth.

1. Proper domains with a quantified reduction cost

Let the old base \(\Gamma(b)\) over \(\mathbb F_p\) contain the Boolean equations in \(v\) old variables. Fix a nonempty \(\Omega\subseteq\{0,1\}^v\) and \(\lambda\ge0\) with the following property: every old polynomial \(A\) vanishing on \(\Omega\) has an ordinary NS certificate from \(\Gamma\) through degree \(\deg A+\lambda\). This is an explicit, uniform reduction hypothesis. It does not follow merely from membership in the full unsatisfiable PHP ideal.

The full cube has \(\lambda=0\). More generally, suppose \(\Omega\) is cut out inside the cube by squarefree forbidden monomials, each supplied with a \(\Gamma\)-certificate through its own degree plus \(\lambda\). Boolean reduction and deletion of monomials divisible by a forbidden monomial never increase degree. The surviving monomials are indexed by allowed supports, and evaluation at allowed Boolean supports is the subset-incidence matrix. Ordered by cardinality, this matrix is triangular with diagonal one. The remainder of a vanishing polynomial is therefore zero over every field. Substitution of the supplied certificates costs the maximum excess \(\lambda\), not a sum of excesses. This proves the stated domain property in this case. It extends the same monomial-normal-form mechanism used by the stable column ideal.

Consider a complete acyclic product-only source

\[ P_a=\prod_{u\le h_a}\left(1-\sum_i r_{a,u,i}g_{a,i}\right), \qquad g_{a,i}=H_{a,i}\bigl(b,(P_c)_{c<a}\bigr). \tag{OC-source} \]

The input identity is literal in the original polynomial ring. Coefficient variables are private to their blocks, all companions and field equations are present, and proof cofactors may use raw coefficients. Let the dependency depth be at most \(d\), counting a bottom block as depth one, and the actual expanded ordinary input degrees be at most \(L\). On \(\Omega\), define recursively the induced functions \(\overline g_{a,i}=H_{a,i}(b,(\chi_c)_{c<a})\), where \(\chi_a\) is one exactly when every induced input of block \(a\) is zero.

Choose old baseline polynomials \(Q_{a,i}\) of degree at most \(q\). Write

\[ \eta_a(b)=(\overline g_{a,i}(b)-Q_{a,i}(b))_i,\qquad V_a=\eta_a(\Omega),\qquad N_a=|V_a|\ge1. \]

For each offset \(v\in V_a\), a reference tuple is \((Q_{a,i}+v_i)_i\), with the original accuracy \(h_a\). Suppose the reference tuples have one common old weight \(f\), \(\deg f\le k\), and old-only coefficient normalizers of degree at most \(T_0\ge1\), making all their companions vanish on \(\Omega\cap\{f\ne0\}\). The same normalizer can be reused for repeated reference tuples. This is the concrete pointwise map property supplied by the earlier affine/cubic constructions, not just a one-level nonrefutability conclusion.

Working compression theorem. Put \(s_a=0\) when \(N_a=1\), and otherwise \(s_a=\lceil2\log_p N_a\rceil+1\). With

\[ s=\max_a s_a,\quad L_* =\max(1,L,q),\quad C=\bigl(1+(p-1)sL_*\bigr)^d, \qquad B=T_0CD+k+\lambda, \tag{OC-cost} \]

every degree-\(D\) ordinary NS or PC source proof of an old target \(u(b)\) transfers to an old proof of \(fu\) through degree \(B\). In particular, an old weight separated at that ceiling excludes a source refutation. It suffices to construct the common reference maps for at most \(M_0=\sum_a p^{s_a}\le p^2\sum_aN_a^2\) blocks. Zero/empty input tuples cause no exception.

2. Hash the offsets and interpolate coefficient maps

Proof. There is a linear map \(A_a:\mathbb F_p^{m_a}\to\mathbb F_p^{s_a}\) injective on \(V_a\), where \(m_a\) is the number of inputs. For \(N_a=1\), use the empty map. Otherwise a uniformly random linear map identifies a given pair with probability \(p^{-s_a}\); the union bound over fewer than \(N_a^2\) ordered pairs is strictly less than one. Also \(p^{s_a}\le p^2N_a^2\). Decode every used code to its unique offset, and every unused code to an arbitrary fixed member of \(V_a\). Introduce the corresponding reference tuple for every code \(\sigma\). Denote its degree-\(T_0\) coefficient maps by \(\alpha_{a,\sigma,u,i}\).

Construct a single substitution \(\Phi\) fixing the old variables, in dependency order. If earlier coefficient images have been defined, form

\[ K_a=A_a\bigl((\Phi_{<a}(g_{a,i})-Q_{a,i})_i\bigr),\qquad \theta_{a,\sigma}=\prod_{j\le s_a}\bigl[1-(K_{a,j}-\sigma_j)^{p-1}\bigr], \] \[ \Phi(r_{a,u,i})=\beta_{a,u,i} =\sum_{\sigma\in\mathbb F_p^{s_a}} \theta_{a,\sigma}\alpha_{a,\sigma,u,i}. \tag{OC-map} \]

The selectors are one-hot at every old Boolean point, since each \(K_{a,j}\) takes values in \(\mathbb F_p\). On \(\Omega\cap\{f\ne0\}\), induction gives \(\Phi(P_c)=\chi_c\) for all earlier blocks. Consequently \(K_a=A_a\eta_a\), so the selected reference tuple agrees with the actual current input tuple. Its reference companions vanish there. If the tuple is zero the actual product equals one; otherwise a nonzero input and its vanishing companion force the product to zero. Thus \(\Phi(P_a)=\chi_a\) on the same set, completing the induction. Every reused product has one image, and unused codes do not occur on this support.

This is related to historical common-feature conditioning. Here each block may have different offset features, and low-degree baseline inputs remain unfrozen. The one common reference weight replaces conditioning on a single cell of all features from every block; its existence still has to be supplied.

3. Charge the hash recursion and the old reduction once

If earlier coefficient images have degree at most \(U\ge1\), the original expanded-degree bound implies \(\deg K_a\le L_*U\). Therefore

\[ \deg\beta_{a,u,i}\le T_0+(p-1)sL_*U. \]

Starting at old degree one, induction on depth gives \(\deg\beta_{a,u,i}\le T_0C\). This charge uses actual expanded source inputs, not a new degree assigned to a simplified semantic expression. Each weighted actual companion \(f\Phi(E)\) vanishes on \(\Omega\), including points where \(f=0\); its ordinary degree is at most \(T_0C\deg E+k\). The domain hypothesis supplies a \(\Gamma\)-certificate through that degree plus \(\lambda\). Coefficient field images vanish on the full cube and need no larger bound. Old generators are fixed.

An NS cofactor of original degree at most \(D-\deg E\) adds at most \(T_0C(D-\deg E)\), so every resulting summand fits (OC-cost). For PC, simulate a line \(v\) by \(f\Phi(v)\): source axioms have the preceding certificates, linear combinations are preserved, and multiplication by a source variable is multiplication by a degree-at-most-\(T_0C\) polynomial. A multiplication predecessor of degree at most \(D-1\) has image degree at most \(T_0C(D-1)+k\); expansion of that multiplication fits \(T_0CD+k\). The extra \(\lambda\) is needed only in the old derivations of axiom images. This proves the bound for both proof systems. \(\square\)

4. The finite bounds give genuine PHP sufficient cases

In compact PHP, assume fixed \(p,d\), polynomial original block inventory, and polylogarithmic \(L,D,\lambda\) and \(\max_a\log N_a\). For a fixed baseline degree, both \(C\) and \(\log M_0\) are polylogarithmic. Take the reference proof ceiling \(D_0\ge CD+\lambda\), enlarged to the harmless minimum required by the endpoint. Then \(T_0CD+k+\lambda\le T_0D_0+k\). There are two supplied reference constructions:

  • Affine baselines, every fixed prime. For \(q\le1\) and every accuracy at least \(3(p-1)\ell\), the explicit affine normalizers have \(T_0=k=O(\sqrt n\operatorname{polylog}n)\). Their finite conditions, using \(M_0,D_0\), eventually hold. Their weight remains old-separated at the required ceiling.
  • Binary cubic baselines. For \(p=2,q\le3\) and arbitrary positive accuracies, use the cubic construction with its finite ledger. Although the earlier asymptotic statement used polynomial inventory, its parameter proof also covers \(\log M_0=\operatorname{polylog}n\): in (CL-choice), inventory enters only through \(\ln(16M_0(v+1))\). With the same \(a_3=\lfloor n^{1/(16K)}\rfloor\), \(a_2=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\), the three choices for \(k\) retain exponents at most \(1-1/(48K),31/32,5/8\), respectively, up to fixed polylogarithmic factors. Thus \(T_0D_0+k=o(n)\), and all three image-loss and room inequalities eventually hold. This uses the actual coefficient maps, not an unsupported extension of a black-box nonrefutability theorem.

Both give source exclusion under the stated domain and offset hypotheses. For ways to verify small images, if the coordinate functions of \(\eta_a\) span dimension \(r\), then \(N_a\le p^r\). If \(\eta_a\) is a fixed linear image of \(m\) Boolean child values and at most \(t\) are active at each domain point, then \(N_a\le\sum_{j\le t}\binom mj\le(m+1)^t\). These are sufficient structural facts to prove about a source; the source syntax does not establish them automatically.

5. A low-degree weight does not automatically compress independent flats

Working obstruction. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), take \(a\) disjoint groups of \(w\) bits and let \(Z_i\) be the product of the bits in group \(i\). Extra old variables are allowed. For arbitrary old polynomials \(Q_i\) of degree at most \(q<w\), and any nonzero multilinear old polynomial \(f\) of degree at most \(k\),

\[ \left|\left\{(Z_i(b)-Q_i(b))_{i\le a}:f(b)=1\right\}\right| \ge 2^{\max(0,a-k)}. \tag{OC-entropy} \]

Proof. Pick a monomial \(m\) of maximum degree \(t=\deg f\) in \(f\). At most \(t\) groups meet its support. Let \(J\) be the remaining groups, so \(|J|\ge a-k\). For every \(c\in\mathbb F_2^J\), consider

\[ R_c=f\prod_{j\in J}(1+Z_j+Q_j+c_j). \]

The squarefree monomial \(m\prod_{j\in J}Z_j\), of degree \(t+w|J|\), has coefficient one after Boolean reduction. To reach that degree a term must choose every \(Z_j\), because \(\deg Q_j<w\), and a degree-\(t\) monomial of \(f\). A different such monomial either overlaps a selected group, lowering its reduced degree, or is disjoint from them and produces a different monomial. Lower-degree monomials cannot contribute. Hence \(R_c\) is a nonzero Boolean function. At some point it equals one; there \(f=1\) and \(Z_j-Q_j=c_j\) for every \(j\in J\). Projection of the offset image onto \(J\) is therefore surjective, proving (OC-entropy). The case \(a-k<0\) uses that a nonzero Boolean \(f\) has nonempty support. \(\square\)

Take the first \(n\) rows of compact binary PHP, \(w=\ell\), and \(Z_i=\prod_t b_{it}\), the indicator of the all-one label. For any fixed baseline degree \(q\), eventually \(\ell>q\). Any nonzero weight of degree at most \(n/4\) leaves at least \(2^{3n/4}\) offset patterns on its support. A literal two-level source realizes these indicators as products of bottom affine literal tuples, with one parent reading all products. Thus full-cube small offset image fails even for a single high-arity parent, despite low source depth and polylogarithmic expanded degree.

This is a failure of the proposed representation criterion, not a proof-complexity lower bound or a counterexample to the transfer theorem. The historical one-parent PC elimination already handles that restricted source. Moreover, the obstruction concerns profiles on the full cube or the stated weight support; a properly costed PHP domain can change the conclusion.

6. One PHP column removes this entropy obstruction at zero excess

For the same binary full-row indicators, let \(\Omega\) consist of old Boolean assignments with at most one selected \(Z_i=1\). This domain is nonempty and is defined by forbidden squarefree monomials \(Z_iZ_j\), \(i\ne j\). Each has a compact-PHP certificate through its own degree \(2\ell\):

\[ E_{ij}=\prod_{t\le\ell}(1+b_{it}+b_{jt}),\qquad Z_iE_{ij}\equiv Z_iZ_j\pmod{\mathrm{BOOL}}, \qquad\deg(Z_iE_{ij})\le2\ell. \]

Indeed \(b_{it}(1+b_{it}+b_{jt})\equiv b_{it}b_{jt}\), and Boolean reduction costs at most the unreduced degree. The first part of this entry therefore proves the domain hypothesis with \(\lambda=0\). On this domain the vector \((Z_i)_i\) has only \(n+1\) possibilities. With zero parent baselines, its hash length is \(O(\log n)\); the bottom affine input baselines have zero offsets. The affine version of the compression theorem applies at its stated accuracy and fixed-depth budgets, including polynomially many parents reading linear combinations of these same indicators.

This is a proper-domain control tied to one fixed hole. It neither proves small offset images for arbitrary affine flats nor certifies a simultaneous reduction domain for every PHP collision. In particular, imposing all collisions on \(n+1\) fully assigned rows and \(n\) holes makes the domain empty, invalidating the hypothesis. The elementary example should not be confused with a new one-parent exclusion; its purpose is to locate the domain issue that the full-cube entropy calculation misses.

7. Outcome, next obligation and process

For general-step, a common-weight construction now tolerates block-dependent offset images of polylogarithmic logarithm, with a complete fixed-depth cost recurrence. The full-cube coverage hypothesis fails on independent flats even after multiplication by a low-degree weight. A proper PHP domain repairs the one-column control, but a general affordable domain and offset description for actual compiled sources is still unproved. The line remains useful as a sufficient mechanism, not as an unconditional route through arbitrary retained inputs.

Next bounded task. Review whether proper domains beyond the one-column example can provide enough compression while retaining uniform low-degree reductions and the old separator. Test any proposed domain against overlapping label cylinders, empty states under the unary decoder, and the full-unsatisfiable-domain trap before refining hash constants or studying another isolated old-only degree.

Checks and process assessment. Reviewed hash injectivity, the single shared-value induction, the additive domain excess, the finite cubic logarithmic-inventory range, and the leading-monomial entropy proof. No numerical or Lean verification is claimed. Targeted source extraction exposed the historical common-feature baseline and kept the work on its missing per-block coverage; no new framework rule is needed. The interrupted interval remained within the running research clock; no retrospective split of that interval is claimed.

20 September 2026 — Cheap proper domains do not give universal offset compression

Working PHP-relative entropy obstruction and route review. It applies to the current low-degree weight classes; it does not obstruct all simultaneous source normalizers. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

General claim under review. For general-step, the offset theorem would supply an affordable fixed-depth map if every relevant tuple had a small image after subtracting fixed-degree profiles on a proper old domain with cheap reductions. The one-column example showed that a full-cube counterexample need not survive this change of domain. This cycle tests the general coverage claim using the old signed-cube separator, before developing more domain examples.

1. A finite obstruction on costed PHP domains

Work over \(\mathbb F_2\) with compact PHP on \(m=n+1\) rows and \(n=2^\ell\) labels, \(\ell\ge2\). Let \(\Omega\ne\varnothing\) be any subset of the old Boolean cube such that every polynomial vanishing on \(\Omega\) has an ordinary NS certificate from the compact old base through its own degree plus \(\lambda\ge0\). Choose \(a\) distinct rows, and on each choose \(w\) bit positions, where \(1\le w\le\ell\). Let \(Z_i\) be the product of those \(w\) bits in row \(i\). Let \(Q_i\) be arbitrary old polynomials of degree at most \(q<w\); they may mix all rows.

Let \(f\ne0\) be multilinear of degree at most \(k\), possessing a nonzero monomial \(m_*\) of its actual maximum degree \(t\), with row-axis counts \(d_j\), such that

\[ k\le n/16,\qquad W(m_*)=\sum_j(4^{d_j}-1)\le n/16, \qquad a(4^w-1)\le n/16, \] \[ B=\max\{\ell,k+aw+\lceil\lambda\rceil\}\le n/4. \tag{DO-room} \]

Working obstruction theorem. On the common support \(\Omega\cap\{f=1\}\),

\[ \left|\left\{(Z_i(b)-Q_i(b))_{i\le a}: b\in\Omega,\ f(b)=1\right\}\right| \ge2^{\max(0,a-k)}. \tag{DO-entropy} \]

In particular, this common support is nonempty. The top-monomial budget holds for every nonzero weight in the recorded cube-volume space. It also holds eventually for the affine endpoint's row-linear weights of degree \(o(n)\), whose monomials use at most one bit per row and have \(W=3t\). Thus the conclusion covers the weight types actually supplied by the current affine and cubic reference constructions.

2. Missing patterns would give a forbidden old consequence

Proof. Let \(J\) consist of selected cylinder rows disjoint from the support of \(m_*\). At most \(t\le k\) selected rows are lost, so \(|J|\ge a-k\). For each pattern \(c\in\mathbb F_2^J\), consider

\[ R_c=f\prod_{i\in J}(1+Z_i+Q_i+c_i). \tag{DO-pattern} \]

This polynomial has a squarefree top monomial \(m_*\prod_{i\in J}Z_i\), of degree \(K=t+w|J|\), with coefficient one. To reach total degree \(K\), a term must use every \(Z_i\), since \(\deg Q_i<w\), and a degree-\(t\) monomial of \(f\). Another such monomial either overlaps selected bits and produces a nonsquarefree term, or gives a different monomial. Neither cancels the displayed squarefree coefficient. No Boolean reduction of the other terms is required.

The selected top monomial has row-cube cost at most \(n/8\), and \(K\le k+aw\le n/8\), because \(w\le4^w-1\). Let \(u\le K\) be its occupied-row count. Construct disjoint coordinate cubes with the prescribed free axes by decreasing axis count. For a new cube of dimension \(d\), the number of previously deleted labels satisfies

\[ 2^d N_{\rm used}\le\sum_{\rm earlier\ rows}4^{d_j} \le W+u\le n/4<n. \]

There are \(n/2^d\) cosets with these axes, and each used label forbids at most one coset. A disjoint cube therefore exists. The final number of deleted labels is

\[ F=\sum_j2^{d_j}\le\tfrac12\sum_j4^{d_j} =\tfrac12(W+u)\le n/8. \]

Consequently \(m\ge B\), and \(n-F\ge7n/8\ge2(B-u)-1\), with positive residual room. The signed multi-axis detector says that the affine unary decoding of \(R_c\) is not an old functional PC consequence through \(B\). That detector isolates exactly the chosen squarefree top coefficient and annihilates every other term, including lower-degree terms and nonsquarefree top terms. The degree-preserving compact decoder therefore excludes \(R_c\) from the compact old NS space through \(B\). If \(K=0\), the same conclusion for the nonzero constant uses a normalized old matching design in the stated room.

If pattern \(c\) were absent on \(\Omega\cap\{f=1\}\), (DO-pattern) would vanish on \(\Omega\): it is zero where \(f=0\), and otherwise its remaining factors are the indicator of exactly that offset pattern. The domain hypothesis would certify it from the old base through \(K+\lambda\le B\), a contradiction. Every pattern on \(J\) is therefore attained. Projection gives (DO-entropy), including the empty projection when \(J=\varnothing\). \(\square\)

This strengthens the full-cube entropy obstruction for the supplied weight classes. The new step is not a stronger elementary counting estimate: missing patterns are converted into old PHP consequences and excluded by a residual matching design. The proof uses ordinary NS reduction certificates, while old PC separation is available as a stronger endpoint.

3. The obstruction remains exponential in the relevant regime

Fix any baseline degree \(q\), take \(w=q+1\), and let

\[ a=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{32(4^w-1)}\right\rfloor. \]

For \(k=o(n)\), \(\lambda=\operatorname{polylog}n\), and an eligible top monomial of \(f\), all conditions in (DO-room) hold eventually. Moreover \(a-k=\Omega(n)\). Hence even after choosing an affordable proper domain, arbitrary degree-\(q\) profiles and one of the present reference weights, the offset image has size at least \(2^{\Omega(n)}\). The conclusion applies to fixed cubic baselines by taking width four, and to every other fixed baseline degree by the same single argument. Increasing a list of fixed-degree endpoints does not establish the missing uniform source coverage.

These cylinders arise as induced products of affine literal bottom tuples; a parent can read all of them. At logarithmic source accuracy, the source has fixed dependency depth and polylogarithmic original expanded degree. Its large semantic span exceeds scalar packing. Thus the test respects the relevant broad source syntax. It is not a claim that such a tuple is essential in a short Frege proof, and a single parent is already removable by the historical elimination theorem.

There is no conflict with the one-column positive control. There the full-row indicator has width \(w=\ell\), so reserving even one such row cube would cost \(4^\ell=n^2\), outside (DO-room). Narrow cylinders leave enough label room for many mutually compatible row cubes; all occupants of one full label do not. The two controls test genuinely different PHP geometry.

4. Route decision and an alternative already present in the record

Contribution to general-step. The sufficient offset theorem remains valid. The attempted universal coverage argument is now falsified on a proper-domain test, with the current weight classes and every fixed baseline degree. I am parking the effort to make every source tuple small by this representation. It can still be used when a source independently supplies small images. This is a method obstruction, not evidence that PHP has short Frege proofs, and not an obstruction to all old-weight normalizers.

A sharper alternative is to work directly with the tuple's common-zero ideal or its costed retained relations, instead of reconstructing its entire vector of values from a short code. The existing leading-head kernels already illustrate this distinction: a large input vector may have many values while a low-degree common weight lies in its input ideal. The costed basis reduction and historical additive elimination remain legitimate preprocessing tools; their total charges must be budgeted, not assumed small.

The actual label boundary also has a useful parked reduction. Full label parents reduce to unary-affine families without degree increase. Those are not the compact bit-affine families already solved: they allow sums of arbitrary within-pigeon functions, and the multiscale middle-rank inventory survives the old rank tests. The high-rank unary endpoint covers a constant fraction of the ambient cell dimension, not those intermediate ranks. Reopening that precise quotient-image problem is more relevant than repeating a cubic-to-quartic extrapolation.

Next bounded task. For general-step, test direct common-weight input-ideal normalization against the row-cylinder obstruction and the unary-affine middle-rank boundary. First derive what the existing leading-head reduction actually costs for cylinder width growing with \(\ell\); then compare with the already available label-to-unary map. Stop at a source-relevant improvement of the quotient-image bound or a precise failure of that bound. Do not infer full source coverage from a fixed-width positive control.

Process assessment. The restored signed-cube detector settled the domain proposal without a new numerical sweep, a sequence of degree-specific examples, or a new framework rule. This is the intended falsification-before-refinement discipline. The working overview is consolidated below its hard budget; the full negative argument remains in this unlimited record.

20 September 2026 — Direct semantic kernels tolerate growing width, but full rows need another map

Working variable-width leading-head endpoint and exact full-row kernel obstruction. The tuple structure is an additional hypothesis; arbitrary retained-source coverage is open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, test the direct input-ideal alternative selected by the proper-domain review. A large value image need not prevent a common weight from lying in every selected input ideal. Derive the complete width-dependent cost, then test its limit at full-row label indicators and compare the existing unary-affine boundary. Stop before treating a family of fixed-width examples as an all-source result.

1. A finite source theorem with variable-width leading heads

Use compact binary PHP with \(n=2^\ell\), \(v=(n+1)\ell\), and a complete acyclic product-only source as in the semantic transfer lemma. All original proof degrees are expanded ordinary degrees. Define the induced old input functions on the entire Boolean cube. Assume each block is either:

  • Affine type: every induced input has an old-affine representative; or
  • Head type: \(a_b\) constant combinations of its induced inputs have polynomial representatives of degree \(w_b\), with pairwise disjoint squarefree leading monomials of degree \(w_b\) under a supplied degree-compatible monomial order in the old bits.

Lower terms of the selected representatives may involve arbitrary old bits. Other inputs in a head-type tuple need not have degree \(w_b\) or smaller. Every accuracy is positive; it may differ between blocks. Let \(M_A\) be the number of affine-type blocks. Choose \(1\le k\le n/16\), with \(1\le w_b\le k\), \(a_bw_b\le v\), and let

\[ \theta=\frac{16(n+1)}n\left[\left(1+\frac{3k}{v}\right)^\ell-1\right], \quad T=2k+1,\quad B=TD+k. \]

Working finite theorem. There is no ordinary NS or PC source refutation through degree \(D\ge\max(\ell,2)\) if

\[ \theta\le\tfrac12,\qquad B\le n/4, \qquad M_Ae^{-k^2/v}\le\tfrac18, \qquad\sum_{b\text{ of head type}}(v+1) e^{-a_b(k/v)^{w_b}}\le\tfrac18. \tag{VH-room} \]

The statement gives one common weight and one global coefficient substitution. It does not sum a charge over the number of blocks or add a factor per dependency level.

2. The reduction image and common weight

Proof of the head bound. Generalize the fixed leading-monomial reduction and triple count. For \(a\) disjoint degree-\(w\) heads, reduce by the monic selected representatives and the old Boolean equations, always decreasing the fixed degree-compatible order. The resulting linear map has image dimension at most

\[ J_w(v,a,k)=\sum_{j=0}^k[z^j] \bigl((1+z)^w-z^w\bigr)^a(1+z)^{v-aw}. \tag{VH-count} \]

It need not be a Gröbner normal form: a fixed terminating linear reduction and its ordinary certificates suffice. A degree-at-most-\(k\) kernel element has a representation by the selected polynomials and Booleanity through degree \(k\), with selected-polynomial cofactors of degree at most \(k-w\).

For completeness, put \(t=k/(v-k)\le1\). The sum of coefficients through \(k\) of a nonnegative polynomial is at most \(t^{-k}\) times its value at \(t\). The largest term in \((1+t)^v\) is its degree-\(k\) term, so \((1+t)^v\le(v+1)\binom vk t^k\). Hence

\[ J_w(v,a,k)\le\binom vk(v+1) \left[1-(k/v)^w\right]^a \le\binom vk(v+1)e^{-a(k/v)^w}. \tag{VH-image} \]

For each proper affine-type input space of rank at least \(2k+3\), also impose the familiar restriction kernel to its affine zero flat. Its image dimension is at most \(\binom vk e^{-k^2/v}\), as in the existing common-weight proof. The two losses in (VH-room) sum to at most \(\binom vk/4\), whereas the cube-volume space \(\mathcal S_k\) has dimension at least \(\binom vk/2\). Therefore a nonzero homogeneous \(f\in\mathcal S_k\) lies in every required kernel.

3. Normalize the actual source, using its original degrees

For a head-type tuple, pull the reduction cofactors back along the constant combinations of its induced inputs. They give old coefficients \(\beta_i\) of degree at most \(k-w_b\) such that \(\sum_i\beta_i\overline g_i=f\) as a Boolean function. Put these coefficients in the first row and zero in later rows. Its induced product is \(1-f\), hence all induced companions vanish on \(f=1\), including companions of unselected inputs.

A proper high-rank affine tuple uses its flat-kernel cofactors. A proper affine tuple of rank \(r\le2k+2\) uses a basis \(F_1,\ldots,F_r\) and the exact identity

\[ 1-\prod_{j=1}^r(1-F_j) =\sum_{j=1}^r F_j\prod_{t<j}(1-F_t). \]

Constant pullback to the original inputs gives coefficients of degree at most \(r-1\le2k+1\); its product is the exact common-zero indicator. Unit spans use a constant representation of one, and zero tuples use zero coefficients. Thus all blocks have old-only coefficient maps of degree at most \(T\), normalizing their induced inputs on the same weight support.

Apply the acyclic common-weight transfer directly. Every weighted actual generator image has a Boolean certificate through \(T\) times its original degree plus \(k\), and a source refutation would derive \(f\) from the old base through \(TD+k\). Cube-volume separation contradicts (VH-room). The full semantic expansions justify pointwise compatibility but are not substituted as new source generators. This proves the theorem. \(\square\)

4. The head width can grow with the instance

Fix constants \(\alpha>0,c>0,b\ge1\). Suppose the total inventory is at most \(n^c\), the original requested degree satisfies \(D=O((\ln n)^b)\), and every head-type block has \(a_b\ge n^\alpha\). Subject to the disjoint-support hypotheses, suppose

\[ w_b\le\frac{\alpha\ln n}{2(b+4)\ln\ln n}. \tag{VH-width} \]

Choose \(k=\lfloor n/(\ln n)^{b+2}\rfloor\). For large \(n\), \(k/v\ge(\ln n)^{-(b+4)}\), and therefore

\[ a_b(k/v)^{w_b}\ge n^{\alpha/2},\qquad \frac{k^2}{v}=\Omega\!\left(\frac{n}{(\ln n)^{2b+5}}\right). \]

Both image-loss bounds beat the polynomial inventory. Also \(\theta=o(1)\), \(k\le n/16\), and \((2k+1)D+k=O(n/(\ln n)^2)=o(n)\). Thus the finite theorem gives a source endpoint in a genuinely growing-width range. This is a uniform width-dependent proof, not extrapolation from several fixed-degree examples.

In particular, polynomial families of large disjoint-cylinder tuples can satisfy this endpoint while having the exponential offset images established in the proper-domain obstruction. The simultaneous kernel method needs a small reduction image of low-degree polynomials modulo the input ideal; it does not need a small image of the entire input-value vector. It still requires the stated head structure for every block assigned to that case.

5. Full-row indicators show the exact limit of a zero-product clamp

Working obstruction. Let \(Z_i=\prod_{t\le\ell}b_{it}\) be any family of positive full-row label indicators. In the Boolean function ring, the ideal \((Z_i)_i\) is spanned by squarefree monomials divisible by at least one \(Z_i\): multiplication only adds variables, and Boolean reduction preserves such divisibility. Every monomial in \(\mathcal S_k\) has row-cube cost at most \(n/16\), whereas a monomial divisible by a full-row \(Z_i\) has cost at least \(4^\ell-1=n^2-1\). Therefore

\[ \mathcal S_k\cap (Z_i)_i=\{0\} \quad\text{in the full old Boolean function ring}. \tag{VH-full-row} \]

No nonzero weight from this space can give a global input-ideal certificate \(f=\sum_i\beta_i Z_i\) modulo Booleanity, regardless of the allowed coefficient degree. This concerns the particular zero-product construction, not all weighted companion normalizers: on a common-zero point the correct product may be one.

The elementary counting bound shows the same lack of coverage at the crude dimension level. Among degree-\(k\) squarefree monomials, at most \(a\binom{v-\ell}{k-\ell}\) are divisible by one of \(a\le n+1\) full-row heads. For \(k\le n/4\), their fraction is at most \(a(k/v)^\ell\le(n+1)(4\ell)^{-\ell}=o(1)\). Thus the ambient filtered image estimate removes essentially no top-degree dimension; the exact statement (VH-full-row) is stronger for the chosen multiplier space.

The one-column proper-domain map can nevertheless handle these full-label inputs. It is allowed to use old PHP collisions and to leave the product one when all inputs vanish. No source lower bound follows from (VH-full-row). More general label parents already have the degree-preserving map to unary-affine tuples, which should be used rather than treating their bit degree as an intrinsic obstacle.

6. What changes, and what remains

For general-step, the direct semantic method now has an explicit growing-width endpoint covering some high-entropy tuples that the offset method cannot compress. Its all-block head/affine dichotomy is not known for compiled sources. Full-row indicators rule out forcing every block into its zero-product case, even though those indicators can be easy by other maps. This gives useful sufficient structure, but neither a full retained-source normalization nor the fixed-depth prime-field recurrence.

Next bounded task. Reopen the specific unary-affine boundary, retaining the middle-rank control. Test whether the old matching quotient supplies a smaller image for restriction by those input equations than the ambient-cell estimate used in the high-rank endpoint. State and test the needed quotient-image inequality before building another degree-specific structural theory; a direct complete-source functional remains an alternative if that inequality fails.

Process assessment. Reusing the existing reduction and semantic-lift proofs exposed one uniform width parameter and an exact failure at full rows. No numerical enumeration, source download, rendering check or new workflow rule was needed. The record distinguishes the new growing-width bound from its previously available quadratic/cubic components.
