20 September 2026 — A nearly full quotient image can coexist with a small-support source endpoint

Working quotient-image counterfamily, support-sensitive separator and unary-affine endpoint. Large residual rank is retained; arbitrary dense middle-rank sources remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, revisit the unary-affine label boundary. Test whether passing from ambient polynomial restrictions to the old matching quotient forces a rank-proportional image drop. The existing full-base relative learning lemma already supplies the transfer: it is not a new result here. Stop at a falsifying image calculation or a proved improvement, and test whether the counterfamily itself has another affordable map.

1. The proposed inequality and the existing sufficient interface

Write \(\mathcal F=\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun}\), \(m=N+1\), \(v=N(N+1)\), and

\[ V_k=\mathcal P_{\le k}/\mathcal I_k(\mathcal F),\quad q_k=\dim V_k,\quad q_k(G)=\dim\bigl(\mathcal P_{\le k}/\mathcal I_k(\mathcal F\cup G)\bigr). \tag{SQ-quotient} \]

Here \(G\) is an affine input tuple treated as additional old equations. These are truncated ordinary NS quotients, not quotients by the full unsatisfiable ideal. The natural map from \(V_k\) to the latter quotient has kernel \(\mathcal I_k(\mathcal F\cup G)/\mathcal I_k(\mathcal F)\).

For a family \((G_b)_b\), the dimension inequality \(\sum_bq_k(G_b)<q_k\) gives a nonzero common relative class. The recorded relative-learning lemma and old filtration stability then exclude a source refutation when \(B=\max(1,k-1)D+k\) fits \(N\ge2B-1\). This is an application of those existing results. A tempting improvement over the ambient-cell bound would be a universal estimate resembling \(q_k(G)\le e^{-c rk/N}q_k\), where \(r\) is affine rank and \(c>0\) is fixed. At \(r=\Theta(N)\), it would make polynomial inventory affordable at polylogarithmic \(k\). The following counterfamily rules out that estimate, even with substantial row/column spread and robustness on large matching residuals.

2. Sparse cell support leaves almost the whole old quotient

Let \(F\) be any set of cells, and suppose every input in \(G\) is a homogeneous linear combination of the variables \(X_e\), \(e\in F\). For \(1\le k\le N/4\), set

\[ \Delta_k(F)=\binom k2\frac{2N-1}{v-1} +\frac{k|F|}{v} +\frac{(N+2)k}{v-2k+1}. \tag{SQ-loss} \]

Working image bound. If \(\Delta_k(F)<1\), then

\[ q_k(G)\ge\bigl(1-\Delta_k(F)\bigr)q_k. \tag{SQ-large-image} \]

Proof. Adjoining all equations \(X_e=0\), \(e\in F\), can only decrease the quotient dimension further. Before row equations are imposed, Booleanity, row/column exclusions and those zero cells have the degree-complete basis of matching monomials avoiding \(F\). Let \(u_j(F)\) count all such matchings of size at most \(j\). Row equations add at most \((N+1)u_{k-1}(F)\) spanning relations: reduce the multiplier first to a matching of size at most \(k-1\); its row product is zero when that row is already used, and otherwise is one marginal relation. Thus

\[ q_k(G)\ge u_k(F)-(N+1)u_{k-1}(F). \]

A uniform \(k\)-subset of all \(v\) cells contains a conflicting pair with probability at most \(\binom k2(2N-1)/(v-1)\). It hits \(F\) with probability at most \(k|F|/v\). Both are ordinary union bounds, with no independence assertion. Consequently

\[ u_k(F)\ge\binom vk\left(1-\binom k2\frac{2N-1}{v-1}-\frac{k|F|}{v}\right). \]

Put \(b_j(v)=\sum_{i\le j}\binom vi\). Successive binomial ratios give \(b_{k-1}(v)/\binom vk\le k/(v-2k+1)\), while \(b_k(v)/\binom vk\le1+k/(v-2k+1)\). Use \(u_{k-1}(F)\le b_{k-1}(v)\), \(q_k\le b_k(v)\), and the preceding positive lower bound to obtain (SQ-large-image). The old quotient is nonzero in this range by matching design extension. \(\square\)

In particular, if \(|F|\le512N\) and \(k=o(\sqrt N)\), then \(q_k(G)/q_k\ge1-O((k^2+k)/N)=1-o(1)\), irrespective of the input rank. This alone does not show that the relative common kernel is zero or that the source is hard. It does show that summing these individual image dimensions cannot prove a common class for even two blocks once \(\Delta_k(F)<1/2\).

3. The counterfamily can have wide, robust intermediate rank

For every sufficiently large even \(N\), there is a set \(F\) in the first \(N\) rows and all \(N\) columns such that

\[ 32N\le |F|\le512N,\qquad \max(\Delta_{ m row},\Delta_{ m col})\le\lceil(\ln N)^2\rceil, \] \[ |F\cap(U\times W)|\ge32N \quad\text{whenever }|U|=|W|=N/2. \tag{SQ-support} \]

Existence proof. Select cells independently with probability \(256/N\). A fixed half-by-half rectangle has expected count \(64N\); the elementary binomial lower-tail bound gives probability at most \(e^{-8N}\) of falling below \(32N\). There are at most \(4^N\) rectangles. The upper-tail bound for the total count gives probability at most \(e^{-256N/3}\) of exceeding \(512N\). For any row or column and \(L=\lceil(\ln N)^2\rceil\), the union bound over its \(L\)-subsets gives \(\Pr[\deg\ge L]\le(256e/L)^L\); the sum over \(2N\) vertices tends to zero. The three failure probabilities have sum below one for large \(N\), proving (SQ-support). The binomial estimates here follow from exponential Markov bounds for independent Bernoulli trials, not from an assumption about matching events.

Set \(r=\lfloor N/16\rfloor\). Choose \(N\) input spaces, each spanned by \(r\) independently uniform binary coefficient vectors on \(F\). With positive probability, every pair of these spaces has combined rank \(2r\) after restriction to every half-by-half rectangle. Indeed, for a fixed pair, rectangle and nonzero combination of its \(2r\) rows, the restricted coefficient vector is uniformly random on at least \(32N\) cells. A union bound makes the total failure probability at most

\[ N^2\,4^N\,2^{2r}\,2^{-32N}<1 \]

for large \(N\). Fix such a choice. Every nonzero vector in any pair span meets more than \(N/2\) rows and more than \(N/2\) columns: otherwise some half-by-half rectangle would see zero. Thus there is no nonzero row-local or column-local input vector.

Now take any matching restriction retaining an \((R+1)\times R\) board with \(R\ge N/2\). Its linear parts contain the restriction to some half-by-half rectangle in the first \(N\) rows, and retain rank \(r\) individually and \(2r\) pairwise. They also remain independent modulo residual row equations. Each residual row has an available cell outside \(F\), since its support degree is less than \(N/2\); comparing coefficients at such cells forces all coefficients of a putative row-sum combination to be zero. Constant offsets introduced by the matching restriction do not change this argument. In particular the proper input spans do not acquire one.

This gives polynomial inventory, intermediate rank proportional to the residual size on this large-residual range, and strong original row/column spread. Nevertheless (SQ-large-image) says that on the original board each actual relative quotient image is asymptotically the whole old quotient at \(k=o(\sqrt N)\). Taking, for example, \(k=\lceil(\ln N)^2\rceil\) refutes the proposed exponential rank-only decay, even with a fixed polynomial prefactor. This is not the earlier all-residual-size construction: robustness below \(N/2\) is not claimed. Nor is a refutation or hardness theorem inferred from the large quotient dimensions.

4. A weight space adapted to the support does survive

The preceding counterfamily has a different useful property. For any support graph \(F\) on the functional board, let \(U_{F,k}\) be the span of its matching monomials of degree at most \(k\). Let \(\Delta_{ m row}\) be its maximum row degree. Assume

\[ 1\le k\le B,\qquad N\ge2B-1,\qquad N\ge\Delta_{ m row}+2k. \tag{SQ-detector-room} \]

Working separation lemma. Every nonzero \(f\in U_{F,k}\) is outside \(\mathcal C_B(\mathcal F_N^{\rm fun})\), over every field.

Proof. Choose a maximum-degree matching monomial in \(f\), of degree \(t\le k\), with row set \(S\) and distinct selected labels \(j_i\). For every selected row choose an alternative label \(a_i\) outside that row's \(F\)-support, outside all \(t\) selected labels, and outside earlier alternatives. At the last step at most \(\Delta_{ m row}+2t-1<N\) labels are forbidden, so all choices exist. The pairs \(\{j_i,a_i\}\) are mutually disjoint.

Delete their \(2t\) labels and take a normalized residual matching design through \(B-t\), using \(N-2t\ge2(B-t)-1\). Put signs \(+1,-1\) on \(j_i,a_i\), respectively. As in the signed residual construction, set a matching moment to zero unless every selected row lies on its designated pair and every other row avoids all deleted labels; otherwise use the product of signs times the residual moment. Missing selected rows have zero marginal sum, and all remaining marginals are those of the residual design. This functional annihilates old NS through \(B\), and hence old PC by the recorded stability theorem.

A monomial of \(f\) missing a selected row is annihilated. Any remaining monomial has degree at least \(t\), so at degree at most \(t\) it uses exactly those rows. Because each alternative lies outside its row's support, the only such monomial with nonzero evaluation is the selected one. Its value is its nonzero coefficient. Constants use a normalized old design. This proves separation. \(\square\)

The statement is a unary support version of the existing signed-row detector. It requires alternative labels outside the chosen cell support; it does not say that all matching monomials on the full board are independent modulo row equations.

5. A complete endpoint measured in shared support size

Let a binary one-level complete affine ENS family of common accuracy \(h\ge1\) have all inputs supported in the same \(F\), with \(s=|F|\). Remove zero tuples and unit spans by their usual constant maps, and let the remaining ranks be \(r_b\). Define

\[ \varepsilon_k=\binom k2\frac{\Delta_{ m row}+\Delta_{ m col}-2}{s-1}, \qquad T=\max(1,k-1),\quad B=TD+k. \]

Take \(s\ge2\), \(1\le k\le s\), \(D\ge2h+1\), and the room conditions (SQ-detector-room). A sufficient exclusion criterion is

\[ \sum_b b_k(s-r_b)<(1-\varepsilon_k)\binom sk. \tag{SQ-endpoint} \]

Proof. A random \(k\)-subset of \(F\) has a conflicting row/column pair with probability at most \(\varepsilon_k\), by counting adjacent edge pairs. Hence \(\dim U_{F,k}\ge(1-\varepsilon_k)\binom sk\). Restriction to a proper input zero flat in the \(s\) supported coordinates, followed by Boolean reduction, has image rank at most \(b_k(s-r_b)\). Under (SQ-endpoint), the joint restriction kernel contains a nonzero \(f\in U_{F,k}\). The existing common-vanishing learning lemma would derive \(f\) through \(B\) from a source refutation. The new support-sensitive separator forbids that consequence. This proves both NS and PC exclusion, preserving complete original companions and their cofactor budgets.

In particular, polynomially many blocks are covered if \(s=\Theta(N)\), \(\Delta_{ m row},\Delta_{ m col}=\operatorname{polylog}N\), \(r_b\ge\rho s\) for a fixed \(0<\rho<1\), and \(D=\operatorname{polylog}N\). Choose \(k=C_\rho\ln(M+2)\), rounded up, with a sufficiently large constant. For large \(s\), binomial tail comparison gives \(b_k(s-r_b)/\binom sk\le2(1-\rho)^k\). Thus the image sum is less than \(\binom sk/4\), \(\varepsilon_k=o(1)\), and \(B\) and \(\Delta_{ m row}+2k\) are polylogarithmic. All room conditions hold eventually.

The robust counterfamily in Section 3 satisfies this endpoint: \(32N\le s\le512N\), \(r=\lfloor N/16\rfloor\ge s/16384\) eventually, and its support degrees are polylogarithmic. Consequently its complete one-level source has no polylogarithmic-degree refutation, despite failure of the sum-of-individual-relative-image criterion. When \(N=2^\ell\), the recorded label-parent map covers the corresponding compact two-level label source as well. This is a new support-sensitive sufficient class; the source itself was not used as evidence that all middle-rank families are hard.

6. Route assessment

For general-step, simple exponential decay of each full old quotient image is false, even for the stated wide robust middle-rank family. Yet a much smaller support-adapted weight space resolves that family simultaneously. The distinction is between losing a large fraction of the full old quotient and finding one separated common class inside a well-chosen subspace. The latter is sufficient and can succeed when the former fails.

Dense middle-rank unary families remain outside this endpoint: their shared support can be \(\Theta(N^2)\) while input rank is only \(\Theta(N)\), and full row support leaves no alternative labels for the displayed separator. The earlier dense multiscale control is not claimed to satisfy the new support condition. No universal decomposition into small-support packages is proved, and summing package costs would need a new budget.

Next bounded task. Test whether support-adapted weights can be chosen for different input spaces without losing one common separated weight, using the dense middle-rank control as the mandatory test. Compare this requirement with the existing relative-learning and mixed-moment interfaces before claiming another sufficient decomposition. Stop at a proved simultaneous mechanism or a precise incompatibility; do not infer density compression from rank or row/column distance alone.

Process assessment. Bounded index retrieval located the existing relative-learning interface before it was reinvented. Pairing a falsifying quotient calculation with a support-adapted positive construction kept the work on a complete source endpoint. The arguments use exact symbolic counts and explicit probability bounds; no numerical evidence, kernel verification or new framework rule is claimed.

20 September 2026 — Sparse graph restrictions synchronize unary-affine weights

Working general binary one-level unary-affine endpoint, using an imported graph-PC theorem and a new separated weight space. Independent review and downstream proof-system auditing remain necessary. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, remove the single shared-support hypothesis of the preceding endpoint. Restrict the complete board to one bounded-degree graph, eliminate one coordinate per row in the affine inputs, and seek a large separated weight space in the remaining coordinates. The old sparse-support detector cannot simply be reused: its alternative labels outside the support would have been deleted. The construction below replaces that step by signed restrictions to hard residual graph instances. Stop at a complete one-level source theorem; do not infer an unrestricted retained-source or Frege recurrence.

1. Imported degree bound and the linear-row encoding

Imported theorem. Mikša and Nordström, A Generalized Method for Proving Polynomial Calculus Degree Lower Bounds, arXiv:1505.01358v1, Definition 4.1 and Theorem 4.9: if a bipartite graph has left degree at most \(d\) and every left set of size at most \(s\) has at least \(\delta\) times its size uniquely adjacent right vertices, then its functional graph-PHP CNF requires PC degree greater than \(\delta s/(2d)\). The paper works over arbitrary fields. The source audit records the version, hash, pages and encoding transfer. This is an imported result, already noted in the earlier source context; the exact theorem and its application proof are checked here, while the general theorem underlying its Corollary 3.29 is used as a published dependency.

The CNF has pigeon, hole and functionality clauses (4.2a)–(4.2c), without onto clauses. The paper uses the opposite Boolean truth convention; the affine complement change gives our variables \(X_e=1\) for occupied edges. Its pigeon polynomial is \(\prod_{e\ni i}(1-X_e)\). Modulo the same-row exclusion generators, its difference from \(1-\sum_{e\ni i}X_e\) has a certificate through the row degree: every remaining product term contains a pair of distinct cells in that row. Thus the linear row equation is derivable in PC through degree at most \(d\). A PC refutation of the linear-row graph system through \(B\ge d\) would therefore give a refutation of the CNF through the same \(B\). This transfers the imported lower bound to the linear-row system in the range used below. No onto axiom is added.

2. Many monomials have a hard signed restriction

Working separated-space lemma. Let \(m=N+1\), let \(k\ge1\) be an integer with \(k=O(\sqrt{N\ln N})\), and let \(N\) be sufficiently large. There is a bipartite graph \(H\) on these rows and \(N\) holes, with exactly sixteen distinct neighbors per row and one distinguished neighbor \(p_i\) per row, for which the following holds. Write \(Y\) for the \(s=15(N+1)\) nondistinguished edge variables. There is a space \(W_k\) spanned by degree-\(k\) matching monomials in \(Y\), with

\[ \dim W_k\ge\tfrac12 e^{-5k^2/N}\binom sk, \qquad W_k\cap\mathcal C_B(\Gamma_H)=\{0\} \quad\text{for }\max(k,8)\le B\le N/10^6. \tag{GS-space} \]

Here \(\Gamma_H\) is the functional graph-PHP system with linear row equations. The same graph and monomial set work over every field; the later affine normalizers will be binary.

Random model. Independently in each row, choose an ordered list of sixteen distinct holes uniformly. The first is \(p_i\); the remaining fifteen index the coordinates of \(Y\). A candidate monomial chooses \(k\) distinct rows and one nondistinguished position in each. Call it good if its \(k\) chosen holes together with the \(k\) distinguished holes are all distinct, and deleting those rows and all those \(2k\) holes leaves a graph whose linear-row functional PHP has no PC refutation through \(N/10^6\).

3. The residual hardness event has probability tending to one

Condition on the distinct chosen pairs and on their deleted hole set \(D\). The remaining rows still have independent uniform sixteen-neighbor lists. A remaining row loses at least nine neighbors with probability at most \(\binom{16}{9}(2k/N)^9\), by a union bound over positions. The sum over at most \(N+1\) rows tends to zero in the stated range. Hence every remaining row retains at least eight neighbors with probability \(1-o(1)\).

Conditional on that event, take the first eight surviving neighbors in each row. These are independent uniform eight-subsets of the \(n'=N-2k\) surviving holes. There are \(m'=N+1-k\le2n'\) surviving rows eventually. We verify a boundary expansion bound directly. If a set of \(t\) rows has fewer than \(2t\) unique neighbors, then its total neighbor set has size at most \(5t\): with \(8t\) incident edges, nonunique neighbors consume at least two edges each. A union bound over the rows and a containing set of \(5t\) holes is at most

\[ \binom{m'}t\binom{n'}{5t} \left(\frac{5t}{n'}\right)^{8t} \le\left[C\left(\frac{t}{n'}\right)^2\right]^t, \qquad C=250e^6<182250. \tag{GS-expansion} \]

For \(1\le t\le n'/10000\), the sum tends to zero. Indeed, for \(t\le\sqrt{n'}\) it is bounded by a geometric series with ratio \(C/n'\), and for larger \(t\) the bracket is below \(1/4\), giving an exponentially small tail. Thus the eight-neighbor subgraph is a \((\lfloor n'/10000\rfloor,2)\)-boundary expander with probability \(1-o(1)\).

The imported theorem gives PC degree greater than \(\lfloor n'/10000\rfloor/8\), which exceeds \(N/10^6\) eventually, also for the linear-row encoding. Dropping extra edges is a Boolean restriction, so hardness of this eight-neighbor subgraph implies hardness of the full surviving graph. Adding edges is not being claimed to preserve boundary expansion. This proves the required residual hardness probability, uniformly over the identities of the deleted holes. It concerns a residual graph with \(k+1\) more rows than holes; Theorem 4.9 does not require deficiency one.

4. Count good monomials, then separate their whole span

For a fixed candidate, the probability that all selected pairs are distinct is exactly

\[ \frac{(N)_{2k}}{[N(N-1)]^k}. \]

There are \(\binom mk15^k\) candidates. For large \(N\), \(k\le N/4\); the elementary bound \(\ln(1-x)\ge-2x\) for \(0\le x\le1/2\) gives

\[ \frac{\binom mk15^k}{\binom{15m}k}\ge e^{-k^2/N}, \qquad \frac{(N)_{2k}}{[N(N-1)]^k}\ge e^{-4k^2/N}. \]

The residual event has conditional probability \(1-o(1)\), so the expected number of good monomials is at least the right side of (GS-space). Some graph has at least that many. Fix it and let \(W_k\) be the span of all its good monomials. Different candidates give different squarefree monomials.

For a good monomial \(M\), assign each selected row either to its chosen nondistinguished hole or to its distinguished hole, independently. Distinct pairs make all \(2^k\) choices collision-free. In every choice set every other cell in the selected rows to zero, and set every cell in the remaining rows on any of the \(2k\) deleted holes to zero. All these restrictions send \(\Gamma_H\) to the same hard residual graph system. Choose a normalized linear functional \(\lambda\) annihilating that system's degree-\(B\) PC consequence space; it exists because there is no refutation through \(B\).

Compose \(\lambda\) with each restriction, and sum with the product signs \(+1\) for a chosen nondistinguished hole and \(-1\) for a distinguished hole. Each composition annihilates \(\mathcal C_B(\Gamma_H)\), since Boolean restrictions preserve PC degree. Their signed sum does too. Its value on any degree-\(k\) monomial in \(Y\) is zero unless that monomial is exactly \(M\): a missing selected row cancels, and in a present row the distinguished variable never occurs in \(Y\), so only the chosen nondistinguished cell can contribute. On \(M\) its value is one.

These coefficient detectors separate every nonzero linear combination of good monomials. This proves (GS-space). In characteristic two the signs coincide, but the two missing-row contributions still sum to zero. Unlike the complete-board detector, this proof does not assert old graph-PC equals ordinary NS: each signed summand annihilates PC directly by restriction to a PC-hard residual system. \(\square\)

5. A general one-level binary unary-affine endpoint

Working theorem. Fix any polynomial block-inventory bound and any polylogarithmic proof-degree bound. For sufficiently large \(N\), the ordinary functional unary PHP base on \(N+1\) rows and \(N\) holes, augmented with any complete one-level ENS family whose inputs are affine in the old cell variables, has no ordinary NS or PC refutation within that degree bound. Accuracies are arbitrary positive integers; all coefficient Boolean equations and all original companions are retained. The same conclusion holds for the weak unary base, by explicitly adjoining the functional axioms.

Choose the common graph. Given an inventory bound \(M\ge1\), put

\[ k=\left\lceil\sqrt{N\ln(16(M+1))}\right\rceil, \quad R=300k,\quad T=300k,\quad B=TD+k. \tag{GS-choice} \]

For polynomial \(M\) and polylogarithmic \(D\), \(k=O(\sqrt{N\ln N})\) and \(B=o(N)\). Increase the requested degree bound to at least sixteen if necessary; this preserves the asymptotic assertion. Use the preceding lemma's graph and weight space, taking \(N\) large enough that \(B\le N/10^6\). Restrict every old cell outside \(H\) to zero throughout the supplied source and proof. This preserves the original proof-degree ceiling, complete blocks and coefficient domains. Affine inputs remain affine; their ranks need not be preserved.

Eliminate the distinguished coordinates only in the affine inputs. Replace each \(X_{i,p_i}\) in an input by \(1-\sum_{j\ne p_i:(i,j)\in H}X_{ij}\). Each new input \(g'_i(Y)\) differs from its old affine input by a constant combination of graph row equations. The degree-exact affine row-replacement lemma transfers the supplied proof to the new complete tuples at its original companion ceilings. Keep the old graph base and its variables; no claim that the row-projected base is a free cube is needed.

One weight for all high ranks. After zero/unit cleanup, classify a tuple as high if its proper affine rank in the \(s=15(N+1)\) coordinates \(Y\) exceeds \(R\). Its Boolean affine-flat restriction map on degree-at-most-\(k\) polynomials has image dimension at most \(b_k(s-r)\). Since \(k=o(s)\), monotonicity and the binomial-tail estimate give, uniformly in high ranks,

\[ b_k(s-r)\le2e^{-Rk/s}\binom sk \le2e^{-10k^2/N}\binom sk. \]

Here \(s\le30N\); if there are no high ranks, no image loss is charged. The sum over at most \(M\) high blocks is strictly less than \(\tfrac12e^{-5k^2/N}\binom sk\), since \(e^{5k^2/N}>4M\). Thus one nonzero \(f\in W_k\) vanishes on every high input flat.

Complete coefficient map. For a high tuple, Boolean affine-ideal membership expresses \(f\) by its inputs with coefficients of degree at most \(k-1\), modulo Booleanity in \(Y\). For a proper low tuple of rank \(r\le R\), use the exact basis-prefix common-zero indicator; its first-row coefficients have degree at most \(r-1\le T\). Unit spans have constant maps and zero tuples have zero maps. In every block set coefficient rows after the first to zero. All induced companions vanish at every old Boolean point where \(f=1\), and all coefficient maps have degree at most \(T\).

The original one-level proof now has a single weighted substitution. For every used nonconstant affine companion of original degree \(e=2h+1\ge3\), its actual weighted image has an old Boolean certificate through at most \(Te+k\). Weighted coefficient fields cost at most \(2T+k\); old graph generators are fixed and multiplied by \(f\). Original NS cofactors or PC multiplication steps then fit \(TD+k=B\), exactly as in the common-weight ledger. Unused high-degree companions incur no proof obligation, and smaller specialized degrees never enlarge the original cofactor spaces. A source refutation would derive \(f\) from \(\Gamma_H\) through \(B\), contradicting (GS-space). This proves the theorem. \(\square\)

6. Scope, controls and remaining route

This addresses the dense unary middle-rank boundary at one old-affine level: after the graph restriction, low ranks are normalized directly and high ranks share a kernel in the graph-adapted space. It does not require a simultaneous rank-preservation theorem, and it does not rely on the false exponential decay of each full old quotient image. The loss \(e^{-O(k^2/N)}\) in the number of separated monomials is explicitly paid by the stronger high-rank restriction loss.

The earlier large-image counterfamily is consistent with this theorem. The theorem chooses a different, separated subspace, not a large fractional drop in the full old quotient. The old multiscale inventory also causes no rank dichotomy failure here: all rank classes are tested after the same sparse graph restriction in only \(15(N+1)\) affine coordinates.

For general-step, this is a working general binary unary-affine one-level endpoint, and hence applies through the existing label-parent transfer to that specified compact two-level source class. The unrestricted deeper source has inputs depending on retained products, not merely old unary-affine coordinates. Graph restriction does not make those inputs affine. The general Frege compatibility step and the all-prime fixed-depth recurrence therefore remain open.

Review boundary and next task. The result depends on the imported graph-PC theorem; it is not Lean-verified or independently reviewed. Before treating any stronger proof-system lower bound as established, audit the graph-weight construction, the old encoding transfer, and the exact source compiler for that proposed application. In particular, do not infer an ordinary-PHP Res(\(\oplus\)) theorem here without checking its rule and initial-clause conventions end to end. Such a consequence would be a side result requiring its own significance and prior-art audit.

Process assessment. The prior shared-support theorem exposed the exact missing alternative-label step. Replacing it by direct signed restrictions preserved PC separation without asserting false graph filtration stability. One existing private paper supplied the needed theorem; no dependency installation, numerical stress test or notebook rendering check was needed.

20 September 2026 — All-prime affine coverage and the ordinary-PHP parity consequence

Working all-prime one-level extension and ordinary unary-PHP Res-parity theorem. The latter is an unreviewed publication candidate; retained-source iteration and novelty review remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Review question. For general-step, audit the exact scope of the graph-based affine endpoint. Check whether the field restriction is necessary, whether the generic clause compiler really yields an ordinary-PHP parity consequence, and where the argument stops at a retained layer. This is a boundary audit of the new line, not a claim that the Frege recurrence has been completed.

1. The unary-affine endpoint holds over every fixed prime

Working theorem. Fix a prime \(p\), a polynomial block-inventory bound, and a polylogarithmic proof-degree bound. For sufficiently large \(N\), the weak or functional linear-row unary PHP base on \(N+1\) rows and \(N\) holes, together with any complete one-level ENS family whose inputs are affine in the old cells over \(\mathbb F_p\), has no ordinary NS or PC refutation within that degree bound. Accuracies are arbitrary positive integers; own coefficient domains are \(r^p-r\).

Proof. The graph-separated monomial space and its imported residual-PC lower bound work over every field. Use the same sixteen-neighbor graph and distinguished row coordinates. The affine row-replacement identity also works over every field: for \(F_u=1-\sum_jr_{uj}g_j\), the difference of two companions is the outside input difference times \(\prod_uF_u\), plus the telescoping sum of one factor difference times the remaining factors and the new outside input. If each input difference is a constant combination of row equations, every summand still has its original ceiling \(2h+1\). No binary identity is used at this step.

Let \(s=15(N+1)\), take \(k=\lceil\sqrt{N\ln(16(M+1))}\rceil\), and split proper affine tuples at rank \(R=301k\). At odd primes use ordinary polynomial restriction to an affine zero flat over \(\mathbb F_p\), not Boolean reduction in arbitrary affine coordinates. The image dimension for rank \(r>R\) is at most \(\binom{s-r+k}{k}\). Directly,

\[ \frac{\binom{s-r+k}{k}}{\binom sk} =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\left(1-\frac{r-k}{s-j}\right) \le e^{-k(r-k)/s}\le e^{-10k^2/N}. \tag{APG-image} \]

The sum of all high images is below the graph space dimension \(\frac12e^{-5k^2/N}\binom sk\). Thus one nonzero \(f\in W_k\) lies in every high kernel. Literal affine-ideal membership gives \(f=\sum_i a_i g_i'\), with \(\deg a_i\le k-1\).

For a high tuple put \(\beta_i=f^{p-2}a_i\) in its first coefficient row. Its product is \(1-f^{p-1}\), which is zero wherever \(f\ne0\). For a low tuple take a basis \(F_1,\ldots,F_r\), and use

\[ 1-\prod_{j=1}^r(1-F_j^{p-1}) =\sum_{j=1}^r F_j\left[F_j^{p-2}\prod_{t<j}(1-F_t^{p-1})\right]. \tag{APG-prefix} \]

Constant pullback to the actual input tuple gives first-row coefficients of degree at most \((p-1)r-1\). Its product is the exact common-zero indicator on old Boolean assignments, since all basis values lie in \(\mathbb F_p\). The formula includes \(p=2\), where the zero power is the constant polynomial one. Set all other coefficient rows to zero; unit and zero spans retain their constant maps.

Every coefficient has degree at most \(T=(p-1)301k\). All weighted actual companions vanish on the full old Boolean cube and have Boolean NS certificates through their actual image degree, bounded by \(Te+k\) for original generator degree \(e\). The coefficient fields have weighted certificates through \(pT+k\), exactly matching their original degree \(p\). Old graph generators are fixed. Original cofactors and PC multiplication then fit \(B=TD+k=o(N)\), contradicting graph separation through \(N/10^6\). Harmlessly increasing \(D\) to at least \(\max(16,p)\) covers small requested ceilings. Functional strengthening for the weak base is explicit, as before. \(\square\)

The parameter \(p\) is fixed. No bound uniform in a growing prime is asserted. This extends one-level source coverage, not the proof-system compiler beyond its audited binary version.

2. End-to-end ordinary unary-PHP Res-parity theorem

Let \(\mathrm{PHP}^{N+1}_N\) be the ordinary unary CNF on variables \(X_{ij}\): each row has the clause \(\bigvee_jX_{ij}\), and each pair of distinct rows has the hole clauses \(\neg X_{ij}\lor\neg X_{i'j}\). The functional version additionally forbids two occupied cells in one row.

Working theorem; unreviewed publication candidate. For every real \(K>0\), all sufficiently large \(N\) have this property: every unrestricted DAG-like Res(\(\oplus\)) refutation of either of these CNFs has more than \(N^K\) nodes. The rule scope includes complementary-parity resolution with semantic weakening and, more strongly, the recorded arbitrary binary semantic affine-clause rule. There is no regularity, tree-likeness or proof-depth restriction.

Proof using the recorded dependencies. Suppose a refutation has \(S\le N^K\) nodes. Before any restriction or compilation choose the inventory bound

\[ M_* =\left\lceil3N^K+4N^3\right\rceil,\qquad k=\left\lceil\sqrt{N\ln(16(M_*+1))}\right\rceil. \]

Choose the graph \(H\), distinguished coordinates and space \(W_k\) from the separated-space lemma. This choice depends only on the displayed bounds, not on a rank-preservation assumption about the source. Use this same graph throughout the proof below.

Restrict every nonedge cell to zero in the given Res(\(\oplus\)) DAG. Affine equations remain affine; semantic implications remain valid, and the empty conclusion remains empty. A complementary pivot becoming constant is a permitted one-premise semantic weakening from the surviving premise. Thus the restricted proof fits the audited affine DAG calculus with at most \(S\) nodes. Initial clauses either become the graph's pigeon/hole/functionality clauses or become tautologies. A tautological initial is semantically covered by any graph pigeon clause; it need not introduce another initial slot.

Every graph row has sixteen neighbors. The nontrivial initial clauses have width at most sixteen, and their number is bounded by

\[ t_H\le(N+1)+N\binom{N+1}{2}+(N+1)\binom{16}{2} \le4N^3 \]

for large \(N\); omit the last term for the weak CNF. Apply the generic CNF-to-affine-registry transfer, specifically its transfer conclusion, with accuracy \(h=1\). It produces one complete old-affine ENS registry with \(M=3S+t_H\le M_*\), at most \(\max(16,16(N+1)+2)\) inputs per slot, and an ordinary PC refutation over the graph-CNF polynomial base through

\[ D=\max(2h+16,4h+1)=18. \tag{UP-transfer} \]

Replace the graph pigeon product axioms by their derivations from the linear row and functionality axioms, through degree sixteen. Hole and functionality polynomials and Booleanity are already graph-base axioms. Replaying the PC proof keeps the global ceiling eighteen. For the weak CNF this is an explicit addition of functionality to the algebraic base, which can only make refutation easier.

We now have exactly the fixed-graph affine family handled by the graph-normalization proof: replace distinguished coordinates only in its affine inputs, and use the same \(W_k\). Its high-rank image budget uses only the bound \(M_*\); low ranks have their exact prefix maps. Taking the all-prime construction above at \(p=2\) gives \(T=301k\), hence a nonzero \(f\in W_k\) would be derivable from \(\Gamma_H\) through

\[ TD+k=5419k=o(N)<N/10^6. \]

This contradicts graph separation. The contradiction proves the theorem for each fixed \(K\). \(\square\)

Why the order matters. Compiling the original unary row clauses first would retain their width \(N\), and the initial-value degree would be linear in \(N\). Restricting the actual proof first makes that width sixteen. Conversely, one cannot apply a theorem about a complete-board base to a graph-restricted source as though the additional zero-cell equations were free. The proof uses the graph-selected weight space and that graph's affine normalization directly, without a second graph restriction.

The recorded correction to the generic criterion concerns an explanatory sentence about satisfiable bases, not its verified transfer. That correction has been checked. The new graph theorem and this composition are not Lean-verified merely because the compiler is. The existing bit-PHP preprint is unchanged; its bit-to-unary implication was not assumed, since the usual substitution does not preserve affine Res(\(\oplus\)) queries.

3. Bounded prior-art check and publication status

The encoding-specific check found the unary-PHP bounds cited by Efremenko–Garlík–Itsykson, introduction, Sections 1.1.1–1.1.2, in the tree-like discussion. Their regular binary result is a different restriction. Byramji–Impagliazzo give depth-restricted bounds. Itsykson–Knop, ITCS 2026, and Itsykson–Podolskii–Shekhovtsov, TR26-018 still distinguish restricted superpolynomial bounds from unrestricted size bounds.

This targeted check did not identify a published unrestricted unary theorem matching the displayed endpoint. It is not an exhaustive literature review or a certification of novelty. The result is flagged as an independent candidate requiring expert correctness review and a fuller prior-art audit; no new whitepaper or formalization is started here. Primary-source locators and the checked compiler scope are preserved in the cycle's audit report.

4. The first retained layer still falls outside the theorem

Exact scope obstruction. Row elimination and graph sparsity do not keep a zero-test of an affine tuple affine. For two independent row coordinates \(x,y\), a bottom block with inputs \((x,y)\) has induced product

\[ \chi=(1-x)(1-y). \]

On the four row-state choices \((0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)\), its values are \((1,0,0,0)\). Their sum in \(\mathbb F_2\) is one, whereas the sum of any affine function over this rectangle is zero. Thus the next block reading this genuine product has a nonaffine induced input, even on the proper domain where each of these rows occupies exactly one of two allowed neighbors. This example is itself easy by scalar normalization; it witnesses failure of the affine hypothesis, not source hardness.

The graph proof uses a coefficient ceiling \(T=\Theta(\sqrt{N\log M})\) for polynomial inventory. Multiplying two such worst-case degree factors would already cost \(\Theta(N\log M)D\), above the old linear barrier. This is a warning about that automatic composition, not a lower bound on every possible simultaneous map: the semantic common-weight transfer can avoid repeated factors when suitable maps are supplied. What is missing is a construction for the actual nonaffine retained input family, compatible with the same separated old endpoint.

Contribution and next step. The one-level boundary is now covered over every fixed prime, and the binary compiler yields the stated ordinary-PHP side result. The main Frege route still needs a PHP-relative mechanism for the first genuinely retained layer and a valid fixed-depth recurrence. Next test that interface on the actual nonlinear input spaces after graph restriction, preserving the current sufficient bounds and the known relative target-rank and same-degree obstructions. Do not replace that task with polishing the publication side branch.

Existing compiler metadata and its explicit correction prevented redundant formalization or a source-system substitution. The all-prime extension came from the coefficient identity, without a prime-by-prime case list.

20 September 2026 — The graph degree budget handles larger inventories and a genuine two-level low case

Working quantitative affine endpoint, all-accuracy unary low-polar corollary and stronger parity candidate. Automatic nonlinear iteration still fails the available budget comparison. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping point. For general-step, determine whether the new endpoint tolerates the inventory and degree increase of an actual retained-source map. The previous asymptotic wording only covered polynomial inventory and polylogarithmic degree. Derive the full power range, apply it to the recorded complete two-level low-polar map, and test the available nonlinear kernel estimate before proposing iteration.

1. A uniform power budget

Working theorem. Fix a prime \(p\), exponents \(\alpha,\beta\ge0\) with \(2\alpha+\beta<1\), and fixed polylogarithmic factors. For sufficiently large \(N\), a complete one-level old-affine ENS family over weak or functional unary PHP has no ordinary NS or PC refutation of degree \(D\) if

\[ D\le N^\alpha\operatorname{polylog}N, \qquad \ln(M+1)\le N^\beta\operatorname{polylog}N, \tag{GP-range} \]

where \(M\) bounds the number of blocks. Constant multiplicative bounds are included in the notation. Accuracies are arbitrary positive integers, and the full coefficient domains are retained. The statement concerns existence and degree, not an efficient enumeration of an exponentially large target family.

Graph extension. In the separated-space construction, replace sixteen by a fixed integer \(d\ge16\), with one distinguished edge per row. There are \(s=(d-1)(N+1)\) remaining coordinates. Keep eight neighbors per unselected row after deleting the selected pairs. A row retains fewer than eight only if at least \(d-7\) of its original neighbors are deleted, so the total failure probability is at most

\[ (N+1)\binom d{d-7}\left(\frac{2k}{N}\right)^{d-7}. \tag{GP-survival} \]

Whenever \(k=o(N^{1-1/(d-7)})\), this tends to zero. Conditional on retaining eight neighbors in every row, their first eight surviving neighbors are still independent uniform eight-subsets. The same expansion proof and imported graph-PC theorem give residual hardness through \(N/10^6\). The expected good-monomial count is now

\[ \binom{N+1}k(d-1)^k \frac{(N)_{2k}}{[N(N-1)]^k}(1-o(1)) \ge\tfrac12e^{-5k^2/N}\binom sk. \]

The two elementary product bounds and the signed coefficient detectors are unchanged. Thus this space remains separated from graph PC through \(N/10^6\). This is a quantitative extension of the recorded graph lemma, with its additional condition (GP-survival) made explicit.

Choose the parameters. Pick a constant \(d\ge16\) so that

\[ d-7>\frac{2}{1-\beta},\qquad k=\left\lceil\sqrt{N\ln(16(M+1))}\right\rceil, \quad A_d=20(d-1)+1, \quad T=(p-1)A_dk. \]

Then \(k=O(N^{(1+\beta)/2}\operatorname{polylog}N)\), and (GP-survival) tends to zero by the strict choice of \(d\). Split proper affine ranks at \(A_dk\). Since \(s\le2(d-1)N\), ordinary flat restriction gives the same image ratio at most \(e^{-10k^2/N}\). The all-prime normalizers therefore supply one separated common weight and maps of degree at most \(T\).

The original-degree replay ceiling is

\[ TD+k=O\!\left(N^{\alpha+(1+\beta)/2} \operatorname{polylog}N\right)=o(N), \]

exactly because \(2\alpha+\beta<1\). It eventually fits the graph separation range. The same graph restriction and affine row replacement preserve the original source bookkeeping, proving (GP-range). \(\square\)

2. Apply the range to a complete two-level source

Take old-affine bottom inputs over the unary PHP cells, private bottom coefficients, and parent inputs of the precise form

\[ q_{a,i}=L_{a,i}(X)+\sum_c\alpha_{a,i;c}P_c, \]

with old-affine \(L_{a,i}\), no raw bottom coefficients, no parent-of-parent dependence, and no products of bottom products. Suppose that, after consistently setting every bottom coefficient row after the first to zero for the rank test, every constant combination of each parent tuple has polar rank at most \(2R\). All original degrees are measured before this specialization.

Working corollary. For every fixed prime and fixed \(0<\eta<1/3\), polynomially many such bottoms and parents with \(R\le N^\eta\) have no polylogarithmic-degree refutation, with arbitrary positive accuracies in every block.

Proof. The existing complete map fixes the old base and transforms the whole source into one old-affine level, at

\[ D'=(pR+1)D,\qquad M'\le M_b+M_p\,p^{\lfloor pR/(p-1)\rfloor}. \]

It chooses every shared bottom image once and preserves the parent and unused-bottom accuracies; its Boolean and field certificates retain the original generator degrees. Consequently \(D'\le N^\eta\operatorname{polylog}N\) and \(\ln(M'+1)\le N^\eta\operatorname{polylog}N\). Apply (GP-range) with \(\alpha=\beta=\eta\). The condition is \(3\eta<1\), proving the corollary. \(\square\)

This is an application of the prior two-level map, not a new rank-to-probe lemma. Compared with its earlier compact-bit endpoint, the old inputs here may be arbitrary unary-affine forms, and the target affine theorem requires no accuracy lower bound such as \(3(p-1)\ell\). The general high-polar-rank parent case is still outside the statement.

3. Quantitative consequence for the ordinary-PHP side theorem

Working refinement of the ordinary unary-PHP parity theorem. For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1\), sufficiently large \(N\) require more than

\[ \exp(N^{1-\epsilon}) \]

nodes in either recorded unrestricted DAG-like Res(\(\oplus\)) convention, for ordinary weak unary PHP and its functional variant. The exponent is measured in the number \(N\) of holes; the original unary encoding has \(N(N+1)\) variables. This remains an unreviewed publication candidate.

Proof. Repeat the same-graph compiler argument with an assumed node bound \(S\le\exp(N^{1-\epsilon})\). Choose a fixed graph degree \(d\ge16\) with \(d-7>2/\epsilon\), and choose its weight graph from the bound \(M_*=\lceil3\exp(N^{1-\epsilon})+4N^3\rceil\). The actual proof is restricted first. The resulting graph initial clauses have width at most \(d\) and still have at most \(4N^3\) nontrivial members for large \(N\), since \(d\) is fixed.

The verified generic compiler at accuracy one gives a complete affine registry of size at most \(M_*\) and PC degree \(D_0=\max(d+2,5)=d+2\). Its graph pigeon product axioms have linear-row/functionality proofs through \(d\), so replay preserves \(D_0\). The fixed-graph form of (GP-range), with \(\alpha=0\), \(\beta=1-\epsilon\), excludes that refutation: its ceiling is \(O_\epsilon(N^{1-\epsilon/2})=o(N)\). The graph is never changed after restricting the proof. This proves the bound. \(\square\)

This strengthens the quantitative candidate without changing the rule or encoding scope. It is not a claim of an exponential bound in all \(N^2\) original variables, and it does not supply independent review or a new novelty audit. The previous literature limitations remain in force.

4. Why this does not give automatic nonlinear iteration

The source range \(2\alpha+\beta<1\) quantifies the square-root issue in the previous review. A full affine normalization has coefficient degree of order \(\sqrt{N\log M}\). Treating that as a new proof-degree factor puts the next request at exponent at least one half, even before the next inventory cost; a second application cannot satisfy the strict range. A simultaneous map may avoid that multiplication, but none is provided by this calculation.

Working limitation of the available image comparison. Nor can the old absolute leading-head estimate simply be transplanted onto the graph weight space. For \(s=15(N+1)\), \(w\ge2\), \(aw\le s\), and \(w\le k\le s/2\), the existing reduction-image upper bound is

\[ U=\binom sk(s+1)e^{-a(k/s)^w}, \qquad L=\tfrac12e^{-5k^2/N}\binom sk \]

for the guaranteed graph-space dimension. Since

\[ a(k/s)^w\le\frac{s}{2}(k/s)^2 =\frac{k^2}{2s}\le\frac{k^2}{30N}, \]

we have \(U/L\ge2(s+1)\exp((5-1/30)k^2/N)>1\). Thus the sufficient comparison \(U<L\) cannot certify even one nonlinear head-type block, regardless of tuning \(k\) within these hypotheses. This is a failure of the present upper/lower estimates, not proof that the actual image is large, that the true weight space is small, or that every nonlinear normalizer fails.

For general-step, the complete low-polar retained case now works over the unary base without the former accuracy threshold, and the one-level parameter range is explicit. Arbitrary retained inputs still need a relative image/certificate argument, a correlated moment construction, or another simultaneous mechanism. The high parent case cannot be resolved by inserting the old cubic theorem or multiplying two one-level maps.

Next bounded task. Return to the actual first retained layer with the relative target and complete-source moment interfaces. Test a source-specific mechanism that accounts for the old graph relations before estimating image loss. Require a concrete compatibility construction or falsifying certificate, rather than another absolute old-polynomial dimension bound.

Process assessment. The inventory introduced by a real retained-source map forced the quantitative extension; the same calculation supplied the stronger side bound and exposed the failed nonlinear comparison. No large family was enumerated, and no numerical check or new framework rule was needed.
